Fresh tea and aged ham—a small token of my own respect.” Hu had no choice but to invite him in. Zhang insisted on paying his respects to both Hu's mother and wife. Ordinary families observed less strict separation between men and women than official households, so both women came out, exchanged greetings, and heard many pleasant words from him.

等坐定了谈入正题。他把王有龄突然来到信和，还清那笔款子的经过，细说了一遍，只把遗失了那张借据这一节，瞒着不提。讲了事实，再谈感想，“雪岩！”他问，“你猜猜着，王老爷这一来，我顶顶高兴的是啥子？““自然是趁此可以拉住一个大主顾。”这句话说到了张胖子的心里，但是他不肯承认：“不是。雪岩，并非我此刻卖好，要你见情，说实在的，当初那件事，东家大发脾气，我身为大伙，实在叫没法子，只好照店规行事。心里是这样在巴望，最好王老爷早早来还了这笔款子，或者让我发笔什么财，替你赔了那五百两头。这为什么？为来为去为的是你好重回信和。现在闲话少说喏，”他把预先备好的红封套取了出来，“他十十月的薪水，照补，四十两本票，收好了。走！”一面说，一面他用左手把红封套塞到胡雪岩手里，右手便来拉着他出门。

Once they were seated, Zhang came to the point. He described Wang's unexpected visit and repayment in detail, omitting only the loss of the original note. Then he turned from events to his feelings. “Xueyan, can you guess what pleased me most about His Honour's visit?” “The chance to secure an important customer, naturally.” That was precisely right, but Zhang would not admit it. “No. I'm not saying this to flatter you or make you grateful. The truth is that our employer was furious about that affair. As manager, I had no choice but to enforce the rules. All the while, I hoped Mr Wang would soon repay the money—or that I might come into a little fortune and cover the five hundred taels for you myself. Why? Simply so that you could return to Xinhe. Well, no more talk.” He produced the red envelope. “Here are ten months' back wages: a note for forty taels. Keep it safe. Come along!” As he spoke, he pressed the envelope into Hu's hand with his left and seized him with his right to lead him out.

“慢来，慢来！张先生。”胡雪岩问道：“怎的一桩事体，我还糊里糊涂。你说走，走到哪里去？”“还有哪里？信和。”胡雪岩是明知故问，听他说明白了，便使劲摇头：“张先生，‘好马不吃回头草’，盛情心领，谢谢了。”说着把红封套退了回去。张胖子双手推拒，责备似他说：“雪岩，这就是你的不是了……自此展开冗长的说服工作，他的口才虽好，胡雪岩的心肠也硬，随便他如何导之以理，动之以情，一个只是不肯松口。

“Wait a moment, Mr Zhang. I still don't understand what's happening. Where are we going?” “Where else? Xinhe.” Hu had asked deliberately. Once Zhang stated it plainly, he shook his head firmly. “A good horse doesn't turn back to graze the same patch. I appreciate your kindness, but no, thank you.” He handed the envelope back. Zhang pushed it away with both hands. “Now, Xueyan, that isn't right of you...” A long campaign of persuasion followed. Zhang's eloquence met Hu's resolve. However he appealed to reason or feeling, Hu would not yield.

磨到日已过午，主人家留客便饭，实在也有逐客的意思。哪知张胖子是抱定了破釜沉舟的决心，嬲往胡雪岩，再也不肯走的，“好，多时不见，正要叙叙，我来添茶！”他摸出块碎银子，大声唤那小徒弟：“小瘌痢，到巷口‘皇饭儿’，叫他们送四样菜来：木榔豆腐，件儿肉，响铃儿，荤素菜，另外打两斤‘竹叶青’！”胡雪岩夫妇要拦拦不住，只好由他。等一喝上酒，胡雪岩就不便“闷声大发财”，听他一个人去说，少不得要找出许许多多理由来推托。无奈张胖子那张嘴十分厉害，就象《封神榜》斗法似地，胡雪岩每祭一样法宝，他总有办法来破，倒是有样法宝，足可使他无法招架，但胡雪岩不肯说，如果肯说破跟王有龄的关系，现在要到海运局去“做官”了，难道张胖子还能一定叫他回信和去立柜台，当伙计？

By midday, the household invited him to stay for lunch, partly hoping that the offer would prompt him to leave. But Zhang had resolved to stake everything on success and would not let go. “Excellent! It's been so long since we talked properly. I'll add something to the meal.” He took out a piece of silver and shouted to the apprentice, “You little scamp! Go to the eating house at the end of the lane. Have them send four dishes: mulang tofu, sliced pork, crisp bean-curd rolls, and mixed meat and vegetables. And fetch two jin of Zhuyeqing wine.” Hu and his wife could not stop him. Once the wine was served, Hu could no longer remain silently on the defensive while Zhang did all the talking. He had to invent one reason after another for refusing. But Zhang's tongue was formidable. Like the magical duels in The Investiture of the Gods, every weapon Hu produced was met by a counterspell. There was one argument Zhang could not answer, but Hu was unwilling to use it. If he revealed his relationship with Wang and his forthcoming work at the bureau, could Zhang possibly insist that he return to stand behind a bank counter?

酒添了又添，话越说越多，连胡雪岩的妻子都有些不耐烦了，正在这不得开交的当儿，来了个不速之客。“咦！”张胖子把眼睛瞪得好大，“高二爷，你怎么寻到这里来了？”奉命来请胡雪岩的高升，机变虽快，却也一时无从回答，但他听出张胖子的语气有异，不知其中有何蹊跷？不敢贸然道破来意，愣在那里只拿双眼看着胡雪岩。看看是瞒不住了，其实也不必瞒，于是胡雪岩决定把他最后一样法宝拿出来。不过说来话长，先得把高升这里料理清楚。才能从容细叙。

More wine was brought, and the conversation grew longer. Even Hu's wife began to lose patience. Just as the situation seemed impossible to resolve, an unexpected visitor arrived. “Oh!” Zhang stared. “Second Master Gao! How did you find your way here?” Sent to fetch Hu, Gao was quick-witted but could not answer immediately. Something in Zhang's tone seemed strange. Unsure what lay behind it, he dared not announce his purpose and merely looked at Hu. The truth could no longer be concealed—and perhaps need not be. Hu decided to use his final argument. But it would take time to explain. First he must settle Gao's business, then tell the story at leisure.

“你吃了饭没有？”胡雪岩先很亲切地问，“现成的酒菜，坐下来‘摆’一杯！”“不敢当，谢谢您老！”高升答道：“胡少爷不知什么时候得空？”“我知道了。”他看一看桌上的自鸣钟说：“我准四点钟到。”“那么，请胡少爷到公馆个吃便饭好了。”把来意交代清楚，高升走了。胡雪岩才歉意地笑道：“实不相瞒，张先生，我已经跟王老爷先见过面了。我不陪他到信和去，其中自有道理，此刻也不必多说。王老爷约我到海运局帮忙，我已经答应了他，故而不好再回‘娘家‘。张先生你要体谅我的苦衷。“

“Have you eaten?” he asked warmly. “There's food and wine ready. Sit down and have a cup.” “Thank you, but I wouldn't presume. When will you be free, Young Master Hu?” “I understand.” Hu glanced at the clock on the table. “I'll be there at four precisely.” “Then please come to the residence for dinner.” With his message delivered, Gao left. Hu smiled apologetically. “To tell you the truth, Mr Zhang, I had already seen Mr Wang before he visited Xinhe. I had reasons for not accompanying him, though there's no need to discuss them now. He has invited me to help at the Sea Transport Bureau, and I've agreed. So I cannot return to my old home. You must understand my difficulty.”

“啊！”张胖子咧丑嘴拉长了声调，做出那意想不到而又惊喜莫名的神态，“雪岩，恭喜，恭喜！你真正是‘鲤鱼跳龙门’了。“跳了龙门，还是鲤鱼，为人不可忘本。我是学的钱庄生意，同行都是我一家。张先生，以后还要请你多照应。”“哪里话，哪里话！现在自然要请你照应。”张胖子忽然放低了声音说，“眼前就要靠你帮忙，我跟王老爷提过，想跟海运局做往来。现在银根松，摆在那里也可惜，你想个什么办法用它出去！回扣特别克己。”“好！”胡雪岩很慎重地点头，“我有数了。”

“Ah!” Zhang drew out the sound, opening his mouth in a display of astonished delight. “Congratulations, Xueyan! You truly are a carp that has leapt the Dragon Gate.” “Even after leaping the gate, I remain a carp. A man mustn't forget his beginnings. Banking is the trade I learned, and everyone in it is family to me. I shall still rely on your help.” “Not at all. It's we who must rely on you now.” Zhang suddenly lowered his voice. “In fact, there's something you can do at once. I told Mr Wang we'd like to do business with the bureau. Money is plentiful at present, and it's a pity to leave it idle. See if you can find a way to put ours to use. We'll be particularly generous about the commission.” “Very well.” Hu nodded seriously. “I'll bear it in mind.”

张胖子总算不虚此行，欣然告辞。胡雪岩也随即赶到王有龄公馆里。他把张胖子的神态语言形容了一番，两人拊掌大笑，都觉得是件很痛快的事。“闲话少说，我有件正事跟你商量。”王有龄把上院谒见抚台，以及与藩司、粮道会议的结果都告诉了胡雪岩，问他该如何办法？

Zhang left pleased that the visit had not been wasted. Hu then hurried to Wang's residence. His account of Zhang's expressions and speeches made both men clap their hands and laugh. They found the affair thoroughly satisfying. “Enough of that. There's important business to discuss.” Wang related his audience with the governor and the consultation with the treasurer and grain intendant, then asked what should be done.

“事情是有点麻烦。不过商人图利，只要划得来，刀头上的血也要去舐，风险总有人肯背的，要紧的是一定要有担保。”“怎么样担保呢？”“最好，当然是我们浙江有公事给他们，这一层怕办不到，那就只有另想别法，法子总有的，我先要请问，要垫的漕米有多少？”“我查过帐了，一共还缺十四万五千石。”“这数目也还不大。”胡雪岩说，“我来托钱庄保付，粮商总可以放心了。”“好极了。是托信和？”“请信和转托上海的钱庄，这一节一定可以办得到。不过抚台那里总要有句话，我劝你直接去看黄抚台，省得其中传话有周折。”

“It is a little complicated. But merchants seek profit. If the return is sufficient, they'll lick blood from a blade. Someone will accept the risk. What matters is having a guarantee.” “What sort of guarantee?” “An official undertaking from Zhejiang would be best, naturally. I doubt we can obtain that, so we must find another way. There will be one. First, how much grain must be advanced?” “I checked the accounts. The shortage is 145,000 shi.” “That isn't such a large amount,” Hu said. “I'll arrange for a bank to guarantee payment. That should put the grain merchant at ease.” “Excellent. Through Xinhe?” “Xinhe can arrange it with a Shanghai bank. That can certainly be done. But we must have a definite word from the governor. I advise you to see him directly, rather than let the message pass through others.”

“这个，”王有龄有些不以为然，“既然藩台、粮道去请示，当然有确实回话给我。似乎不必多此一举。”“其中另有道理。”胡雪岩放低了声音说，“作兴抚合另有交代，譬如说，什么开销要打在里头，他不便自己开口，更不便跟藩台说，全靠你识趣，提他一个头，他才会有话交下来！”“啊！”王有龄恍然大悟，不断点头。“还有一层，藩台跟粮道那里也要去安排好。就算他们自己清廉，手底下的人，个个眼红，谁不当你这一趟是可以‘吃饱’的好差使？没有好处，一定要出花样。”王有龄越发惊奇了，“真正想不到！雪岩，”他说，“你做官这么内行！”“做官跟做生意的道理是一样的。”

“Well...” Wang was not convinced. “Since the treasurer and grain intendant are asking for instructions, they'll surely give me a definite answer. Another visit seems unnecessary.” “There's another reason.” Hu lowered his voice. “The governor may have further instructions—some expense he wants included, for example. He can't conveniently raise it himself, still less discuss it with the treasurer. He needs you to understand and provide an opening. Then he can tell you what he wants.” “Ah!” Wang understood and nodded repeatedly. “There's more. You must make arrangements at the treasury and the grain intendant's office too. Even if the men themselves are honest, their subordinates will all be envious. Who won't suppose this assignment offers you a chance to fill your pockets? Without some benefit, they're certain to make difficulties.” Wang was more astonished than ever. “I would never have thought of it. Xueyan, you're an expert at official life!” “The principles of being an official and doing business are the same.”

听得这话，王有龄有些想笑。但仔细想一想，胡雪岩的话虽话得直率，却是鞭辟入里的实情。反正这件事一开头就走的是小路，既然走了小路，就索性把它走通。只要浙江的漕粮交足，不误朝廷正用，其他都好商量。如果小路走得半途而废，中间出了乱子，虽有上司在上面顶着，但出面的是自己，首当其冲，必受大害。这样一想，他就觉得胡雪岩的话，真个是“金玉良言”。这个人也是自己万万少不得的。“雪岩，我想这样，我马上替你报捐，有了‘实收’，谁也不能说你不是一个官。那一来，你在我局里的名义就好看了，起码是个委员，办事也方便些。““这慢慢来！等你这一趟差使弄好了再说。”

Wang almost laughed. On reflection, however, blunt as the remark was, it went straight to the truth. This affair had begun by taking a side path. Having chosen it, they might as well follow it through. So long as Zhejiang's full grain quota was delivered and the state's needs were not delayed, everything else could be arranged. If they faltered halfway and trouble arose, their superiors might stand above them, but Wang was the man acting openly. He would bear the first and heaviest blow. Seen in that light, Hu's advice was truly worth its weight in gold. He was a man Wang could not do without. “Xueyan, here's what I propose. I'll apply to purchase a title for you at once. Once you have the official receipt, no one can deny you're an official. Your position in the bureau will then be more presentable—at least that of a commissioner—and you'll find it easier to act.” “There's no hurry. Let's finish this assignment of yours first.”

王有龄懂他的意思。自己盘算着这一趟差使，总可以弄个三五千两银子，那时候替胡雪岩捐个官，可以捐大些。胡雪岩大概是这样在希望，自然要依他。“也许。”他把话说明了，“我有了钱，首先就替你办这件事。不过，眼前怎么样呢？总要有个名义，你才好替我出面。”“不必。”胡雪岩说，“我跟你的交情，有张胖子到外面去一说，大家都知道了，替你出面办什么事，人家自然相信。”“好，好，都随你！”就从这一刻起，王有龄对他便到了言听计从的地步。

Wang understood what he thought Hu meant. The assignment should yield three to five thousand taels, he reckoned. Then he could purchase a more substantial title for his friend. Presumably that was what Hu hoped for, and naturally he should oblige him. “Very well,” he said plainly. “Once I have the money, that will be the first thing I do for you. But what about now? You need some recognised position if you're to act for me.” “There's no need,” Hu replied. “Once Zhang has told people about our friendship, everyone will know. Whatever I undertake on your behalf, they'll naturally trust me.” “Very well. As you wish.” From that moment, Wang came to follow Hu's advice in everything.

当天夜里又把酒细谈，各抒抱负。王有龄幼聆庭训，深知州县官虽被视作“风尘俗吏”，其实颇可有所展布，而且读书不成，去而捐官，既然走上了这条路子，也就断了金马玉堂的想头，索性作个功名之士。胡雪岩的想法比他还要实际，一个还脱不了“做官”的念头，一个则以为“行行出状元”，而以发财为第一，发了财照样亦可以做官，不过捐班至多捐一个三品的道员，没有红顶子戴而已。因为气质相类，思路相近，所以越谈越投机，都觉得友朋之乐，胜过一切。当夜谈到三更过后，才由高升提着海运局的灯笼，送他回家。

That night, over more wine, they spoke at length of their ambitions. From his father's teaching, Wang knew that local magistrates, dismissed by some as ordinary officials immersed in worldly affairs, could in fact accomplish much. Since his studies had not brought success and he had purchased office, he had already abandoned dreams of the scholarly splendour of court. He would seek achievement and advancement along the practical path he had chosen. Hu's ideas were more practical still. One man remained attached to the ambition of official service; the other believed that excellence could be found in every trade and put making a fortune first. Wealth could bring office too. The only limitation was that purchased advancement reached no higher than a third-rank circuit intendancy, without the red hat button of a higher official. Their temperaments and outlooks were so alike that the longer they talked, the better they understood each other. Both felt that the pleasure of friendship surpassed everything else. It was after midnight when Gao finally escorted Hu home, carrying a lantern bearing the bureau's name.

胡雪岩精力过人，睡得虽迟，第二天依旧一早起身。这天要办的一件大事，就是到信和去看张胖子。他心里在想，空手上门，面子上不好看，总得有所点缀才好。胡雪岩又想，送礼也不能送张胖子一个人。他为人素来“四海”，而现在正要展布手面，所以决定要博得个信和上下，皆大欢喜。这又不是仅仅有钱便可了事。他很细心地考虑到他那些老同事的关系、境遇、爱好，替每人备一份礼，无不投其所好，这费了他一上午的工夫，然后雇一个挑伕，挑着这一担礼物，跟着他直到盐桥信和钱庄。这一下，就把信和上上下下都收服了。大家都有这佯一个感觉，胡雪岩倒霉时，不会找朋友的麻烦，他得意了，一定会照应朋友。

Hu had exceptional energy. Despite the late night, he rose early the next morning. His main task was to visit Zhang at Xinhe. He felt that arriving empty-handed would look poor; some appropriate gesture was needed. Nor should Zhang alone receive a present. Hu had always been generous in his dealings, and now that he had a chance to show it, he intended to please everyone at the bank. Money alone would not do. He carefully considered each former colleague's circumstances, relationships, and tastes, then chose a gift suited to each. This occupied the whole morning. Finally, he hired a porter to carry the load and followed him to Xinhe at Salt Bridge. That won the entire bank over. Everyone felt the same thing: when Hu was unfortunate, he did not trouble his friends; when he prospered, he would always remember them.

当然，最兴奋的是张胖子，昨天他从胡家出来，不回钱庄，先去拜访东家，自诩“慧眼识英雄”，早已看出胡雪岩不是池中物，因而平时相待极厚。胡雪岩所以当初去而无怨，以及现在仍旧不忘信和，都是为了他的情分。东家听了他这番“丑表功”，信以为真，着实嘉奖了他几句，而且也作了指示，海运局这个大主顾，一定要拉往，因为赚钱不赚钱在其次，声誉信用有关，这就是钱庄票号的资本，信和能够代理海运局的汇划，在上海的同行中，就要刮目相看了。

Zhang was naturally the most excited. After leaving Hu's house the previous day, he had gone to the proprietor before returning to the bank. He boasted of his ability to recognise exceptional men. He had long known that Hu was destined for greater things, he said, and had always treated him especially well. It was because of their bond that Hu had left without resentment and still remembered Xinhe with affection. The proprietor believed this shameless self-praise, commended Zhang warmly, and gave clear instructions: the bureau must be secured as a client. Profit was secondary. Reputation and credit were involved, and those were a bank's real capital. If Xinhe handled the bureau's remittances, its Shanghai counterparts would regard it with new respect.

张胖子和胡雪岩都是很厉害的角色，关起门来谈生意，都不肯泄漏真意，胡雪岩说：“今天我遇见王老爷，谈起跟信和往来的事。他告诉我，现在有两三家钱庄，都要放款给海运局，也不是放款，是垫拨，因为利息有上落，还没有谈定局，听说是我的来头，情形当然不同。张先生，你倒开个‘盘口’看！”张胖子先不答这句话，只问：“是哪两三家？”胡雪岩笑了：“这，人家怎么肯说？”“那么，你说，利息明的多少，暗的多少？”“现在不谈暗的，只谈明的好了。”“话是这么说，”张胖子放低了声音，“你自己呢？加多少帽子？”胡雪岩大摇其头：“王老爷托我的事，我怎么好落他的‘后手’？这也不必谈。”

Both Zhang and Hu were formidable men. Behind closed doors, neither would reveal his true intentions. Hu began, “When I saw Mr Wang today, we discussed doing business with Xinhe. He said two or three banks were offering loans to the bureau—or rather, advances. Nothing has been settled because the interest rates differ. Naturally, when he heard that I was speaking for you, the situation changed. Mr Zhang, what terms would you offer?” Zhang did not answer directly. “Which banks?” Hu smiled. “How would anyone be willing to tell me that?” “Then tell me this: what is the rate on paper, and what is the private arrangement?” “Let's leave private arrangements aside for now and discuss the stated rate.” “Certainly,” Zhang said, lowering his voice. “But what about you? How much do you want added for yourself?” Hu shook his head vigorously. “Mr Wang has entrusted this to me. How could I take a secret cut behind his back? There's nothing to discuss on that score.”

“你不要，我们总要意思意思。”张胖子又问，“要垫多少？期限是长是短，你先说了好筹划。”“总要二十万。”“二十万？”张胖子吃惊地说，“信和的底子你知道的，这要到外面去调。”到同行中去调头寸，利息就要高了，胡雪岩懂得他的用意，便笑笑说道：“那就不必谈下去了。”“不是这话，不是这话！”张胖子又急忙改口，“你的来头，信和一定要替你做面子，再多些也要想办法。这你不管了，你说，期限长短？”

“Even if you ask for nothing, we must show our appreciation.” Zhang continued, “How much is needed, and for how long? Tell me that first so I can make arrangements.” “At least two hundred thousand taels.” “Two hundred thousand?” Zhang was startled. “You know Xinhe's resources. We'd have to raise money elsewhere.” Obtaining funds from other banks would mean a higher interest rate. Hu understood the implication and smiled. “Then there's no point in discussing it further.” “That's not what I mean!” Zhang hastily corrected himself. “Since you bring us the business, we must do you credit. Even a larger sum could be managed. Leave that to us. Tell me the term.”

“你们喜欢长，还是喜欢短？”胡雪岩说，“长是长的办法，短是短的办法。”如果期限能够放长，胡雪岩预备移花接木，借信和的本钱，开自己的钱庄。张胖子自然不肯明白表示，只说：“主随客便，要你这里吩咐下来，我们才好去调度。”这一问胡雪岩无从回答，海运局现在还不需用现银，只要信和能够担保。而他自己呢，虽然灵机一动，想借信和的资本来开钱庄，但这件事到底要跟王有龄从长计议过了，才有动手，眼前也还说不出个所以然来。

“Would you prefer a long one or a short one? We can arrange either accordingly.” If the term could be extended, Hu intended to use a substitution of his own and open a bank with Xinhe's capital. Zhang naturally avoided stating a preference. “We follow the client's wishes. Once you tell us what is required, we can arrange our funds.” Hu could not answer that. The bureau did not yet need cash; it needed Xinhe's guarantee. As for his own sudden idea of using Xinhe's capital to establish a bank, he would have to discuss it thoroughly with Wang before acting. He had no definite plan to state.

他这样踌躇着，张胖子却误会了，以为胡雪岩还是想在利息上“戴帽子”，自己不便开口，所以他作了个暗示：“雪岩，我们先谈一句自己弟兄的私话，你现在做了官，排场总要的，有些用度，自己要垫，我开个折子给你，二千两的额子以内，随时支用，你有钱随时来归，利息不计。”胡雪岩明白，这是信和先送二千两银子，得人钱财，与人消灾，收了他这二千两，信和有什么要求，就非得替他办到不可。不过胡雪岩也不便峻拒，故意吹句牛：“这倒不必。信和是我‘娘家’，我有钱不存信和存哪里？过几天我有笔款子，大概五六千两，放在你们这里，先做个往来。”“那太好了。你拿来我替你放，包你利息好。”

Zhang misunderstood his hesitation, assuming that Hu did want a personal margin added to the interest but was embarrassed to say so. He offered a hint. “Xueyan, let us speak privately as friends. Now that you've entered official life, you must keep up appearances, and some expenses will have to be advanced from your own pocket. I'll open an account for you. Draw whatever you need up to two thousand taels and repay it whenever you have the money. No interest.” Hu understood: Xinhe was offering two thousand taels in advance. Accept a man's money, and you must solve his problems. If he took it, he would have to fulfil the bank's requests. But an outright refusal would be awkward. Instead, he deliberately boasted. “There's no need. Xinhe is my old home. Where else would I deposit my money? In a few days, I expect five or six thousand taels. I'll leave it here and begin an account.” “Excellent! Bring it in, and I'll lend it out for you. I guarantee a good return.”

“这再谈吧！”胡雪岩问道：“信和现在跟上海‘三大’往来多不多？”“还好。”这就是不多之意，胡雪岩心里有些嘀咕，考虑了一会，觉得不能再兜圈子了，尔虞我诈，大家不说实后，弄到头来，会出乱子。

“We can discuss that later. Do you have much business with Shanghai's Big Three at present?” “Fairly well.” That meant not much. Hu was uneasy. After considering it, he decided they could no longer circle around each other. If both continued bluffing and concealing the truth, the matter would end in trouble.

于是他换了副神态说：“我也知道你的意思，海运局跟你做了往来，信和这块牌子就格外响了。我总竭力拉拢。不过眼前海运局要信和帮忙。这个忙帮成功，好处不在少数。”一听这话，张胖子越发兴奋，连连答应：“一定效劳，一定效劳。”“话未说之先，我有句话要交代。”胡雪岩神色凛然地，“今天我跟你谈的事，是抚台交下来的，泄漏不得半点！倘或泄漏出去，闯出祸来，不要说我，王老爷也救不了你，做官的人不讲道理，那时抚台派兵来封信和的门，你不要怪我。”说得如此严重，把笑口常开的张胖子吓得脸色发青，“唷！”他说，“这不是当玩儿的。等我把门来关起来。“

His manner changed. “I understand what you want. A relationship with the bureau would make Xinhe's name more distinguished, and I'll do my best to bring it about. But first the bureau needs your help. If you can provide it, the benefits will be substantial.” Zhang grew still more eager. “Certainly. We shall do everything we can.” “Before I explain, there is one condition.” Hu's expression became stern. “What we discuss today comes from the governor. Not a word may leak out. If it does and trouble follows, neither I nor Mr Wang will be able to save you. Officials aren't reasonable when things go wrong. If the governor sends soldiers to seal Xinhe's doors, don't blame me.” The warning wiped the smile from Zhang's face and left him pale. “Oh! This is no joking matter. Let me close the door.”

关上房门，两个并坐在僻处，胡雪岩把那移花接木之计，约略说了一遍，问张胖子两点：第一，有没有熟识的粮商可以介绍。第二，肯不肯承诺保付。这风险太大了。张胖子一时答应不下，站起来绕室徘徊，心里不住盘算。胡雪岩见此光景，觉得有动之以利的必要，便把他拉住坐下，低声又说：“风险你自己去看，除非杭州到上海这一段水路上，出了纰漏，漕船沉掉，漕米无法归垫，不然不会有风险的。至于你们的好处，这样，好在日子不多，从承诺保付之日起，海运局就算借了信和的现银子，照日拆计息，一直到跟粮商交割清楚为止。你看如何？”

With the door shut, they sat together in a secluded corner. Hu outlined the substitution scheme and asked two questions: did Zhang know a grain merchant he could recommend, and would Xinhe guarantee payment? The risk seemed enormous. Zhang could not agree at once. He rose and walked about the room, calculating silently. Seeing this, Hu decided to appeal to his interest. He drew him back into a seat and spoke quietly. “Judge the risk for yourself. Unless something happens on the waterway between Hangzhou and Shanghai—unless the grain boats sink and the rice cannot be supplied in repayment—there should be no loss. As for your return, here's my proposal. The period won't be long. From the day you undertake the guarantee, the bureau will treat the sum as though it had borrowed cash from Xinhe, paying interest by the day until the merchant's account is fully settled. How does that sound?”

这一说，张胖子怦怦心动了，不须调动头寸，只凭一纸契约，就可以当作放出现款，收取利息，这是不用本钱的生意，加以还可借海运局来长自己的声势，岂不大妙？张胖子利害相权，心思已经活动、做生意原来就是靠眼光，有胆气，想到胡雪岩当初放那五百两银子给王有龄，还不是眼光独到，甚至连张“饭票子”都赔在里面，在他个人来说，是背了风险，但如今来看，这笔生意他是做对了。由于胡雪岩的现成的例子摆着，张胖子的胆便大了，心思也灵活了，他已决定接受胡雪岩的建议，但不便当时就作决定，还有一件事是非做不可的，到藩台衙门去摸一摸底，看看漕米运到上海的情形，藩台对王有龄是怎样一种态度？只有这两层上没有什么疑问，这笔生意就算做定了。

Zhang's heart stirred. Without moving any funds, a written undertaking would earn interest as though he had made a cash loan. It was business requiring no immediate capital, with the bureau's reputation to enhance his own. What could be better? Weighing advantage against danger, he began to yield. Business depended on judgement and courage. Hadn't Hu shown unusual judgement in lending those five hundred taels to Wang? He had even sacrificed his livelihood over it. Personally, he had borne a great risk. Yet now the transaction had proved sound. With Hu's example before him, Zhang grew bolder and more inventive. He had decided to accept, but could not commit immediately. There was one thing he must do first: inquire at the provincial treasury about the grain's progress towards Shanghai and the treasurer's attitude to Wang. If both points were satisfactory, the business was settled.

于是他说：“雪岩！我们自己弟兄，还有说不通、相信不过的地方？这就算八成帐了！不过象这样大的进出，我总要向东家说一声，准定明天午刻听回话，你看好不好？”“这有什么不好？不过我也有句话，大家都是替人家办事，身不由主。我老实说，也不必明天午刻，索性到后天好了，一过后灭，没有回话，我也就不必再来看你，省得白耽误工夫。“这就是说定了一个最后限期。张胖子觉得胡雪岩做事爽快而有担当，十分欣赏，连连点头答应。

“Xueyan, between friends like us, what cannot be discussed or trusted?” he said. “Consider it eight-tenths agreed. But for a transaction this size, I must consult my employer. I'll give you a definite answer by noon tomorrow. Will that do?” “Of course. But I have something to say too. We're both acting for others and cannot decide everything ourselves. To be frank, there's no need to insist on noon tomorrow. Take until the day after. If I hear nothing by then, I won't come back. That will save us both wasted time.” A final deadline had been set. Zhang admired Hu's decisiveness and willingness to take responsibility, and nodded repeatedly.

回到海运局跟王有龄见面，互道各人商谈的结果。王有龄十分兴奋，说这天上午非常顺利，先去看了麟桂，说抚台已有表示，差额由藩库先垫，今年新漕中如何加派来弥补这笔款子，到时候再定办法，不与王有龄相干。又去看了抚台，黄宗汉吩咐，只要事情办得快，多花点钱无所谓。他还拿出两道上谕来给王有龄看，一道是八旗京兵有十五万之多，须严加训练，欠饷要设法发清，通谕各省，从速解运漕米银两，以供正用。一道是酌减文武大臣“养廉”银，以充军饷。可见得朝廷在粮饷上调度困难，如能早日运到，黄宗汉答应特保王有龄升官。“照这一说，事情就差不多了。”胡雪岩心知张胖子要去打听情形，既然藩司有此确实表示，信和这方面当然可以放心，不必等张胖子正式回话，便可知事已定局，“该商量商量，好动身到上海去寻‘户头’了。”

Back at the bureau, Hu and Wang exchanged reports. Wang was delighted: his morning had gone very well. He had first seen Lingui, who said the governor had agreed that the treasury should advance the price difference. How it would later be recovered through additional levies on the new grain would be decided separately and was no concern of Wang's. He had then seen Huang, who told him that some extra expense did not matter provided the work was done quickly. The governor showed him two edicts. One stated that the capital's Eight Banner forces numbered 150,000, required strict training, and must receive their overdue pay; the provinces were to expedite grain and silver to meet the state's needs. The other ordered reductions in civil and military officials' integrity allowances to supply military funds. Clearly, the court was struggling to meet its requirements. Huang promised to recommend Wang for promotion if the grain arrived promptly. “Then the matter is almost settled.” Hu knew Zhang would make inquiries. With the treasury's undertaking so definite, Xinhe could feel secure. There was no need to await Zhang's formal reply to know the outcome. “We should discuss going to Shanghai to find the right merchant.”

“我想这样，请你陪了我去，局里当然要派两个人，那不过摆摆样子，事情全靠你来办。”胡雪岩想了想答道：“真的要我来办，得要听我的办法。”“好！”王有龄毫不迟疑地答就，“全听你的。”

“My thought is that you should accompany me. The bureau will naturally send two officials, but that will be largely for appearances. The real work will depend on you.” Hu considered. “If you truly want me to handle it, you must let me do it my way.” “Certainly,” Wang answered without hesitation. “I'll follow your lead.”

为了办事方便，王有龄到底下了一通“关书”，聘请胡雪岩当“司事”，在签押房旁边一个小房间办事，作幕后的策划。首先是从藩库提了十万两银子过来，等跟信和谈好了保付的办法，把这笔款子存入信和，先划三万两到上海大亨钱庄。这三万两银子，一万两作公费使用，二万两要替黄宗汉汇到家乡，当然那是极秘密的。

To make the work easier, Wang finally issued a formal letter engaging Hu as an administrative clerk. He occupied a small room beside the private office and planned matters behind the scenes. First, a hundred thousand taels were drawn from the provincial treasury. Once the guarantee terms with Xinhe had been settled, the sum was deposited there, and thirty thousand taels were remitted to Daheng Bank in Shanghai. Of that amount, ten thousand were for official expenses; twenty thousand were to be forwarded to Huang Zonghan's home district. The latter arrangement was, of course, strictly secret.

然后，胡雪岩在局里挑了两个委员，一个是麟桂的私人姓周，一个跟粮道有关系姓吴，请王有龄下条子，“派随赴沪”，同时每人额外先送二百两银子的旅费，周、吴二人原来有些敌视胡雪岩，等打听列这于排出于他的主张，立刻便倾心结交。胡雪岩又把张胖子也邀在一起，加上庶务、厨子、听差、上上下下一共十个人，雇了两只“无锡快”，随带大批准备送人的土产，从杭州城内第一座大桥“万安桥”下船，解缆出关，沿运河东行。

Hu then selected two bureau commissioners: Zhou, a follower of Lingui, and Wu, who had connections with the grain intendant. He asked Wang to issue orders assigning them to accompany him to Shanghai. Each also received an additional two hundred taels for travelling expenses. Both had initially regarded Hu with some hostility, but once they learned that this payment was his proposal, they immediately sought his friendship. Hu invited Zhang as well. With the general affairs officer, cook, attendants, and others, the party numbered ten. They hired two fast Wuxi boats and took a large supply of local products intended as gifts. Boarding at Wan'an Bridge, the first great bridge within Hangzhou, they cast off, passed the city barrier, and travelled east along the canal.

这时是三月天气，两岸平畴，绿油油的桑林，黄澄澄的菜花，深红浅绛的桃李，织成一幅锦绣平原。工有龄诗兴大发，倚舷闲眺，吟哦不绝。但别的人没有他那么雅兴，周、吴两委员，加上胡雪岩、张胖子正好凑成一桌麻将。打牌是张胖子所提议的，胡雪岩欣然附议。张胖子便要派人到头一条船上去请周、吴二人，一个说，“慢慢！摆好桌子再说。”胡雪岩早有准备的，打开箱子，取出簇新的一副竹背牙牌，极精致的一副筹码，雪白的牙牌，叫船家的女儿阿珠来铺好桌子，分好筹码。两面茶几，摆上果碟，泡上好茶，然后叫船家停一停船，搭上跳板，把周、吴两委员请了过来。

It was the third month. Flat fields, rich green mulberry groves, golden rapeseed flowers, and peach and plum blossoms in shades of red and pink spread along both banks like a brocade. Inspired to poetry, Wang leaned against the side of his boat, gazing and murmuring lines. The others had no such literary inclination. Zhou and Wu, together with Hu and Zhang, made exactly four for mahjong. Zhang proposed the game, and Hu readily agreed. Zhang was about to send to the leading boat for the two commissioners when Hu stopped him. “Wait. Let's have the table ready first.” Hu had come prepared. He opened a trunk and took out a new set of ivory mahjong tiles with bamboo backs and an exquisite set of counters. He called the boatman's daughter, A'zhu, to lay the table and divide the counters. Fruit dishes stood on side tables, and fine tea was brewed. Only then did he ask the boatman to pause alongside the other vessel, put out a gangplank, and invite Zhou and Wu over.

一看这场面，两人都是高兴得不得了，“有趣，有趣！”周委员笑着说道：“跟我们这位胡大哥在一起，实在有劲道。”“闲话少说，”吴委员更性急，“快坐下来。怎么打法？”于是四个人坐下来扳了位，张胖子提议，一百两银子一底的“幺半”，二十和底，三百和满贯。自摸一副“辣子”，三十两一家，便有九十两进帐。“太大了！”周委员说，“自己人小玩玩，打个对折吧！”“对，对，打对折。”吴委员也说，“我只带了三十两银子，不够输的。”

The two were delighted by the preparations. “Splendid!” Zhou laughed. “There's real pleasure in travelling with our friend Hu.” “Enough talk,” Wu said impatiently. “Let's sit down. What rules are we playing?” They took their seats and drew for positions. Zhang proposed a game with a hundred taels to a stake, using the yaoban scoring scale: a twenty-point base and a three-hundred-point limit. A self-drawn limit hand would bring thirty taels from each of the other players, ninety in all. “That's too high,” Zhou said. “We're friends playing for amusement. Let's halve it.” “Yes, halve it,” Wu agreed. “I've brought only thirty taels. I can't afford to lose at that rate.”

“不要紧，不要紧！有钱庄的人在这里，两位怕什么？”胡雪岩一面说，一面给张胖子递了个眼色。张胖子会意了，从身上摸出一叠银票来，取了两张一百两的放在周，吴二人面前，笑着说道，“我先垫本，赢了我提一成。”“输了呢？”吴委员问。“输了？”胡雪岩说，“等赢了再还。”这是有赢无输的牌，周、吴二人越发高兴。心里痛快，牌风也顺了，加以明慧可人的阿珠，一遍遍毛巾把子，一道道点心送了上来，这场牌打得实在舒服。

“No need to worry. With a banker here, what have you to fear?” As he spoke, Hu gave Zhang a meaningful glance. Zhang understood. Taking out a stack of bank drafts, he laid a hundred-tael note before each commissioner. “I'll provide the capital,” he said with a smile. “If you win, I take ten per cent.” “And if we lose?” Wu asked. “If you lose,” Hu said, “repay it when you win.” It was a game in which they could win without really losing. Zhou and Wu were happier still. Good spirits brought good luck, and the bright, charming A'zhu repeatedly supplied hot towels and refreshments. Nothing could have made the game more comfortable.

四圈打完，坐在胡雪岩下家的周委员，一家大赢，吴委员也还不错，输的是张胖子和胡雪岩，两个人的牌品都好，依旧笑嘻嘻地毫不在乎。等扳了位，吴委员的牌风又上去了，因为这四圈恰好是他坐在胡雪岩的下家。再下一家是周委员，吴委员只顾自己做大牌，张子出得松，所以周委员也还好，氽出去有限。八圈打完，船已泊岸，天也快黑了，自然歇手。算一算筹码，吴委员赢了一底半，周委员赢了一底，张胖子没有什么输赢。但有他们两家一成的贴补，也变成了赢家，只有胡雪岩一个人大输，连头钱在内，成了“四吃一”。

After four rounds, Zhou, sitting immediately after Hu, had won heavily. Wu had done fairly well too. The losers were Zhang and Hu, both cheerful and gracious, apparently unconcerned. After they changed places, Wu's luck improved. For these next four rounds, it was he who sat after Hu. Zhou followed Wu, whose concentration on making high-scoring hands led him to discard freely. Zhou therefore did reasonably well too and lost little of what he had won. By the end of eight rounds, the boats had moored and darkness was approaching, so they stopped. Counting the counters, Wu had won a stake and a half, Zhou one stake. Zhang had neither won nor lost much, but the ten per cent due from their winnings made him a winner too. Hu alone had lost heavily. Including the table fee, there were four claims upon a single loser's purse.

“摆着，摆着！”周委员很大方地说，“明天再打再算！”“赌钱赌个现！”胡雪岩说了句杭州的谚语，“而况是第一次，来，来兑筹码，兑筹码！”胡雪岩开“枕头箱”取出银票，一一照付，零数用现银子补足，只看他也不怎么细算，三把两把一抓，分配停当，各人自已再数一数，丝毫不差。吴委员大为倾服，翘起大拇指赞道：“雪岩兄，‘度支才也’！”他肚子里有些墨水，这句引自《新唐书》，唐明皇欣赏杨国忠替他管赌帐管得清楚的褒语，胡雪岩却听不懂，但他懂得藏拙，料想是句好话，只报以感谢的一笑，不多说什么！

“Leave it for now,” Zhou said generously. “We can play again tomorrow and settle then.” “Gambling debts are paid in cash,” Hu replied with a Hangzhou saying. “Besides, this is our first game together. Come, let's exchange the counters.” He opened his small bedside chest and took out bank drafts, paying each man and making up the odd amounts in silver. He seemed scarcely to calculate, merely taking a few handfuls and dividing them. Yet when the recipients checked, every payment was exact. Wu was greatly impressed and raised a thumb. “Brother Xueyan, you have the talent of a master of finance!” Wu had some literary learning. The phrase came from the New Book of Tang, in which Emperor Xuanzong praised Yang Guozhong for keeping his gambling accounts so clearly. Hu did not understand the allusion, but he knew how to conceal a gap in his knowledge. Assuming it was a compliment, he merely smiled his thanks.

最后算头钱，那是一副牌、一副牌打的，因为牌风甚大，打了十六七两银子，胡雪岩把筹码往自己面前一放，喊道：“阿珠！”阿珠正帮着她娘在船梢上做菜，听得招呼，娇滴滴答应一声：“来了！”接着便出现在船门口，她系一条青竹布围裙，一面擦着手，一面憨憨地笑着，一根乌油油的长辫子从肩上斜甩了过来，衬着她那张红白分明的鹅蛋脸，那番风韵，着实撩人。胡雪岩眼尖，眼角已瞟见周、吴二人盯着阿珠不放的神情，心里立刻又有了盘算，“来，阿珠，四两银子的头钱。”他说：“交给你娘！”“谢谢胡老爷！”阿珠福了福。

Last came the table fee, collected hand by hand. With such high stakes, it amounted to sixteen or seventeen taels. Hu placed the counters before him and called, “A'zhu!” She was helping her mother cook at the stern. At his call, she answered brightly, “Coming!” She appeared in the cabin doorway, wiping her hands on a blue cotton apron and smiling with simple good humour. Her long, glossy black plait had swung forward over one shoulder, setting off her oval face with its clear complexion and rosy colour. She was strikingly attractive. Hu's quick eyes noticed Zhou and Wu staring at her, and another calculation formed in his mind. “Come here, A'zhu. Four taels in table fees,” he said. “Give them to your mother.” “Thank you, Mr Hu.” She made a curtsy.

“你谢错人了！要谢周老爷、吴老爷。喏！”他拈起一张银票，招一招手，等阿珠走近桌子，他才低声又说：“头钱不止四两。周老爷、吴老爷格外有赏，补足二十两银子，是你的私房钱。”这一说，阿珠的双眼张得更大了，惊喜地不知所措，张胖子便笑道：“阿珠！周老爷、吴老爷替你办嫁妆。还不快道谢！”“张老爷最喜欢说笑话！”阿珠红云满面，旋即垂着眼替周、吴二人请安。“这倒不能不意思意思了！”吴委员向周委员说。于是每人又赏了十两。在阿珠，自出娘胎，何曾有过这么多钱？只看她道谢又道谢，站起身来晃荡着长辫子，碎步走向船梢，然后便是又喘又笑在说话的声音，想来是把这桩得意的快事在告诉她娘。

“You're thanking the wrong man. Thank Mr Zhou and Mr Wu. Here!” He picked up a bank draft and beckoned. When she came close to the table, he spoke softly. “The fees came to more than four taels. Mr Zhou and Mr Wu are adding a special reward to make twenty in all. It's money for you to keep yourself.” Her eyes opened wider, and she was too delighted and surprised to know what to do. Zhang laughed. “A'zhu, Mr Zhou and Mr Wu are helping with your dowry. Aren't you going to thank them?” “Mr Zhang is always joking!” She blushed deeply, then lowered her eyes and paid her respects to Zhou and Wu. “Now we must add something ourselves,” Wu said to Zhou. Each gave her another ten taels. Never in her life had A'zhu possessed so much money. She thanked them again and again, then rose and hurried towards the stern, her long plait swinging. A moment later they heard breathless, laughing speech. She was evidently telling her mother of her good fortune.

大家都听得十分有趣，相视微笑。就这时听得外面在搭跳板，接着是船家招呼：“王大老爷走好！”王有龄过船来了，大家一剂起身迎接，只见他手里拿着一个信笺，兴冲冲地走了进来，笑着问周、吴二人：“胜败如何？”属官听上司提起赌钱的事，未免不好意思，周委员红着脸答道：“托大人的福！”“好，好！”王有龄指着张胖子说，“想来是张老哥输了，饯庄大老板输几个不在乎。”“理当报效，理当报效。”

They all found it entertaining and exchanged smiles. Just then, a gangplank was laid outside, followed by the boatman's call: “Mind your step, Your Honour Wang!” Wang had crossed over from his boat. Everyone rose to greet him as he entered cheerfully with a sheet of writing paper in his hand. Smiling, he asked Zhou and Wu, “How did the battle go?” They were embarrassed to have their superior refer to the gambling. Zhou blushed. “Fortune favoured us, thanks to Your Excellency.” “Good, good.” Wang pointed to Zhang. “Then our banker must have lost. A few taels mean little to a man of his resources.” “A pleasure to contribute, a pleasure.”

说笑了一会，阿珠来摆桌子开饭。“无锡快”上的“船菜”是有名的，这天又特别巴结，自然更精致了。除此以外，各人都还带得有“路菜”，桌子上摆不下，另外端两张茶几来摆。胡雪岩早关照庶务多带陈年“竹叶青”，此时开了一坛，烫得恰到好处，斟在杯子里，糟香四溢，连一向不善饮的周委员，都忍不住想来一杯。这样的场合，再有活色生香的阿珠侍席，应该是淳于髡所说的“饮可八斗”的境界，无奈有王有龄在座，大家便都拘束了，他谈话的对象也只是一个吴委员，这天下午倚舷平眺，做了四首七绝，题名《春望》，十分得意，此时兴高采烈地跟吴委员谈论，什么“这个字不响”，“那个字该用去声”，大家听不大懂，也没有兴致去听，但礼貌上又非装得很喜欢听不可的样子，以致于变成喝闷酒，嘉肴醇醒，淡而无味，可餐的秀色，亦平白地糟蹋了，真是耳朵受罪，还连带了眼睛受屈！

After some joking, A'zhu laid the table for dinner. The cooking aboard the fast Wuxi boats was famous, and special efforts had been made that day, so the food was finer still. Everyone had also brought provisions for the journey. There was not enough room on the main table, and two side tables had to be added. Hu had instructed the general affairs officer to bring plenty of aged Zhuyeqing wine. A jar was opened and warmed to precisely the right temperature. Its rich aroma filled the air as it was poured. Even Zhou, ordinarily a poor drinker, could not resist a cup. With such a meal and the lively, attractive A'zhu serving them, it should have been an occasion on which, as the ancient wit Chunyu Kun said, a man could drink an astonishing amount. Unfortunately, Wang's presence made everyone restrained. He conversed only with Wu. That afternoon, gazing from his boat, he had composed four seven-character quatrains entitled “Spring Views” and was very proud of them. Now he enthusiastically discussed which word lacked resonance and which should carry a departing tone. The others understood little and cared less, yet courtesy required them to look fascinated. They drank in gloomy silence. Fine food and mellow wine lost their flavour; even the girl's charms were wasted. Their ears suffered, and their eyes were deprived as well.

胡雪岩看看不是路数，一番细心安排，都叫王有龄的酸气给冲掉了。好在有约在先，此行凡事得听他作主，所以他找了个空隙，丢过去一个眼色，意思请他早些回自己的船，好让大家自由些。王有龄倒是酒酣耳热，谈得正痛快，所以对胡雪岩的暗示，起初还不能领会，看一看大家的神态，再细一想，方始明白，心头随即浮起歉意。“我的酒差不多了！”他也很机警，“你们慢慢喝。”于是叫阿珠盛了小半碗饭，王有龄吃完离席。胡雪岩知道他的酒不曾够，特地关照船家，另外备四个碟子，烫一斤酒送到前面船上。

Hu saw that things were going wrong. His careful arrangements were being spoiled by Wang's pedantry. Fortunately, they had agreed that Hu should direct this journey. Seizing a pause, he gave Wang a glance, asking him to return early to his own boat and leave the others free to enjoy themselves. Warm with wine and delighted by his conversation, Wang at first missed the hint. Then he examined the others' expressions, thought a little, understood, and felt apologetic. “I've had enough wine,” he said tactfully. “You carry on.” He asked A'zhu for a small half-bowl of rice, ate it, and left the table. Hu knew that he had not really finished drinking, so he specially asked the boatman to prepare four dishes and warm a jin of wine to send to the leading boat.

“好了！”周委员挺一挺腰说，“这下可以好好喝两杯了。”略略清理了席面，洗盏更酌，人依旧是五个，去了一个王有龄，补上一个庶务，他姓赵，人很能干，不过，这几天的工夫，已经让胡雪岩收服了。“行个酒令，如何？”吴委贝提议。“我只会豁拳。”张胖子说。“豁拳我倒会。”周委员接口，“就不会喝酒。”“不要紧，我找个人来代。”胡雪岩便喊：“阿珠，你替周老爷代酒。”“嗯。”阿珠马上把个嘴撅得老高，上身摇两摇，就象小女孩似地撒娇。“好，好！”胡雪岩也是哄小孩似地哄她，“不代，不代！”阿珠嫣然一笔，自己觉得不好意思了：“这样，周老爷吃一杯，我代一杯！”“如果周老爷吃十杯呢？”赵庶务问。阿珠想了想，毅然答道：“我也吃十杯。”

“There!” Zhou said, straightening his back. “Now we can enjoy a proper drink.” The table was tidied, the cups rinsed, and more wine poured. There were still five at dinner: Wang had been replaced by Zhao, the general affairs officer, a capable man whom Hu had already won over in these few days. “How about a drinking game?” Wu suggested. “I only know finger-guessing,” Zhang said. “I can play that too,” Zhou put in. “It's the drinking I can't manage.” “Never mind. I'll find someone to drink for you.” Hu called out, “A'zhu, drink Mr Zhou's forfeits for him.” “Oh!” A'zhu immediately pushed out her lower lip and swayed her shoulders in a playful pout, like a little girl. “All right, all right!” Hu coaxed her as though soothing a child. “You needn't, you needn't!” She smiled prettily, then felt a little embarrassed. “How about this? For every cup Mr Zhou drinks, I'll drink one for him.” “And if he drinks ten?” Zhao asked. She considered, then declared firmly, “I'll drink ten too.”

大家都鼓掌称善，周委员便笑着摇手：“不行，不行！你们这是存心灌我酒。”说着便要逃席。赵庶务和阿珠，一面一个拉住了他，吴委员很威严地说：“我是令官，酒令大似军令，周公乱了我的令，先罚酒一杯！”！“我替他计个饶。”胡雪岩说。“不行！除非阿珠来求情。”“呀！吴老爷真正在说笑话了！”阿珠笑道：“这关我什么事啊？”“你不是替他代酒吗？既会你跟周老爷好，为什么不可以替他求情呢？”这算是哪一方的道理？阿珠让他缠糊除了，虽知他的话不对，却无法驳他。不过，说她跟周老爷“好”，她却不肯承认。

Everyone applauded. Zhou laughed and waved his hands. “No, no! You're deliberately trying to get me drunk.” He made to leave the table, but Zhao and A'zhu caught him, one on either side. Wu declared sternly, “I'm master of the drinking game. Its rules are stricter than military orders. Mr Zhou has disobeyed me: one penalty cup to begin with!” “Let me plead for him,” Hu said. “No! Unless A'zhu does the pleading.” “Oh, Mr Wu, you really are joking!” she said with a laugh. “What has this to do with me?” “Aren't you drinking for him? Since you're so fond of Mr Zhou, why shouldn't you plead for him too?” What sort of reasoning was that? He had talked her into a muddle. She knew his argument was wrong, but could not refute it. Still, she would not admit to being particularly fond of Zhou.

“我伺候各位老爷都是一样的，要好大家都好……”下面那半句话不能再出口，偏偏张胖子促狭，故意要拆穿：“要不好大家都不好，是不是？”“啊呀呀！不作兴这样子说的。”阿珠有些窘，面泛红晕，越发妩媚，“各位老爷都好，只有一位不好。”“哪一个？”“就是你张老板！”阿珠说了这一句，自己倒又笑了，接着把腰肢一扭，到船梢上去取热酒。取来热洒，吴委员开始打通关。个个逸兴遗飞，加以有阿珠如蛱蝶穿花般，周旋在席间，周、吴二人乐不可支，欢饮大醉。就这样天天打牌饮酒，跟阿珠调笑，船走得极慢，但船中的客人还嫌快！

“I serve all you gentlemen alike. If I'm fond of one, I'm fond of all...” She could not very well finish the thought, but the mischievous Zhang deliberately exposed it. “And if you dislike one, you dislike us all—is that it?” “Oh, no, no! You mustn't say that.” A'zhu looked flustered, her blush making her more charming still. “All the gentlemen are good, except one.” “Which one?” “You, Mr Zhang!” She laughed at her own retort, then turned with a swing of her waist and went to the stern for hot wine. When she returned, Wu began challenging each man in turn. They were all in high spirits, and with A'zhu moving among them like a butterfly among flowers, Zhou and Wu were beside themselves with pleasure. They drank until thoroughly drunk. So the days passed in cards, wine, and flirtation with A'zhu. The boats moved very slowly, but their passengers thought them too fast.

第四天才到嘉兴，吴委员向胡雪岩暗示，连日在船上，气闷之至，想到岸上走走。这是托词，实在是想多停留一天。胡雪岩自然明白，便跟王有龄说了，在嘉兴停一天。既到嘉兴，不能不逛南湖，连王有龄一起，在烟雨楼头品茗。那天恰好是个阴天，春阴漠漠，柳色迷离，王有龄的诗兴又发了。张胖子却坐不住，“找只船去划划？”他提议。“何必？”吴委员反对，“一路来都是坐船，也坐腻了。坐这里的船，倒不如坐自家的船。”自家的船上有阿珠，南湖的船上也有不少船娘，但未见得胜过阿珠，就算胜得过，片时邂逅，也没有什么主意好打。

They did not reach Jiaxing until the fourth day. Wu hinted to Hu that several days aboard had become unbearably confining: he would like a walk ashore. That was an excuse. He really wanted another day's delay. Hu understood perfectly, spoke to Wang, and arranged to stay a day in Jiaxing. A visit to Jiaxing necessarily meant an excursion to South Lake. Wang joined them for tea upstairs in the Tower of Mist and Rain. The day happened to be overcast; spring haze hung over the water, and the willows blurred in the dim light. Wang felt another poem coming on. Zhang, however, could not sit still. “Shall we hire a boat and row about?” he suggested. “What for?” Wu objected. “We've been sitting in boats all the way and have had enough of it. If we're going boating, we might as well use our own.” Their own boat had A'zhu. South Lake had plenty of boatwomen too, but none necessarily surpassed her; and even if one did, so brief an encounter offered little prospect of anything further.

“我倒有个主意了。”张胖子失声说了这一句，发觉王有龄在注意，不便再说，悄悄把胡雪岩一拉，到一旁去密语。张胖子是想去访“空门艳迹”，嘉兴有些玷辱佛门的花样，胡雪岩也知道，但王有龄的身分不便去，当时商定，张胖子带周、吴去结“欢喜缘”，胡雪岩陪着王有龄去闲逛。于是分道扬镳，胡雪岩掉了个花枪，陪着王有龄先走，两顶小轿到了闹市，下轿浏览，信步走进一家书坊。王有龄想买部诗集子，胡雪岩随手翻着新到的京报，看见一道上谕，上有黄宗汉的名字，便定睛看了下去。上面除了黄宗汉奏复椿寿自尽原因的原折，说“该司因库款不敷，漕务棘手，致肝疾举发，因而自尽，并无别情。”皇帝批的是，“知道了。”胡雪岩知道，黄宗汉的那个麻烦已经没有了。这是否何桂清的功劳呢。王有龄买了诗集子，胡雪岩也买了京报，无处可去，正好乘周、吴两人不在，回到船上去密谈。

“I have an idea!” Zhang blurted out. Then, noticing Wang's attention, he stopped, drew Hu aside, and spoke privately. He wanted to seek out the amorous diversions concealed behind monastic doors. Hu too knew of certain practices in Jiaxing that disgraced the Buddhist establishment, but Wang's official position made such a visit unsuitable. They agreed that Zhang should take Zhou and Wu to form these “blissful connections,” while Hu accompanied Wang on a stroll. They therefore separated. With a little manoeuvring, Hu took Wang away first. Two small sedan chairs carried them to the busy streets, where they got out to browse and wandered into a bookshop. Wang wanted a collection of poems. Hu idly leafed through a newly arrived Peking Gazette and, noticing Huang Zonghan's name in an imperial edict, read more closely. The entry included Huang's memorial in reply to the inquiry into Chunshou's suicide: “The treasurer, distressed by the shortage of treasury funds and the difficulties of grain transport, suffered a recurrence of liver illness and consequently took his own life. There were no other circumstances.” The emperor's response was, “Noted.” Hu knew that this particular trouble was now behind Huang. Was He Guiqing responsible for that? Wang bought his poems and Hu the gazette. With nowhere else to go, and Zhou and Wu conveniently absent, they returned to the boats for a private talk.

看完京报上那道上谕，王有龄的心情，可说是一则以喜，一则以惧，喜的是黄字汉脱然无累，圣眷正隆，今后浙江的公事，好办得多，惧的是久闻他刻薄奸狡，说不定过河拆桥，不再买何桂清的帐，那就失去了一座靠山。“雪公！”胡雪岩对他，新近改了这样一个公私两宜的称呼，“我说你是过虑。黄抚台想做事，要表功，我们照他的意思来做，做得比他自己所想的还要好，那还有什么话说？俗语说得好，‘师父领进门，修行在各人’，何学台把你领进门就够了，自己修行不到家，靠山再硬也不中用。你看！”

After reading the edict, Wang felt both pleased and afraid. He was pleased that Huang had emerged unencumbered and stood high in imperial favour: Zhejiang's affairs should now be much easier to manage. Yet he had long heard of the governor's harshness and cunning. Huang might discard a bridge once he had crossed it and cease to heed He Guiqing. That would cost Wang an important source of support. “Mr Xuexuan,” Hu said, using a form of address he had recently adopted as suitable for both public and private occasions, “I think you're worrying too much. Governor Huang wants things done and wants credit for doing them. If we follow his wishes and do better than he himself expects, what can he possibly complain of? As the saying goes, the master shows you through the gate, but the practice is your own. Education Commissioner He has done enough by bringing you in. If you don't develop your own abilities, even the strongest patron is no use. Look!”

他指着京报中的一道上谕让王有龄看，写的是：“谕内阁大学士、军机大臣会同刑部定拟徐广缙罪名一折，己革署湖广总督徐广缙，经朕简派钦差大臣，接办军务，沿途行走，已属迟延；迫贼由湖南下窜，汉阳、武昌相继失守，犹复株守岳州，一筹莫展，实属调度失机，徐广缙着即照裕诚等所拟，按定律为斩监候；秋后处决。”“这位徐大帅，皇帝特派的钦差大臣，靠山算得硬了！自己不好还是靠不住，还是要杀头。”胡雪岩似乎很感慨他说，“一切都是假的，靠自己是真的，人缘也是靠自己，自己是个半吊子，哪里来的朋友？”这番话听得王有龄连连点头，“雪岩，”他说：“不是我恭维你，你可惜少读两句书，不然一定比何根云、黄抚台还要得意。”“我不是这么想，做生意的见了官，好象委屈些，其实做生意有做生意的乐趣。做官许多拘束，做生意发达了才快活！”

He pointed out another edict in the gazette: “Concerning the memorial jointly submitted by the Grand Secretaries, the Grand Council, and the Board of Punishments, as instructed, proposing a sentence for Xu Guangjin: Xu Guangjin, formerly acting Governor-General of Huguang and since dismissed, was specially appointed by Us as imperial commissioner to take charge of military affairs, yet was already dilatory in his progress along the route. When the rebels descended from Hunan and Hanyang and Wuchang fell in succession, he still clung to Yuezhou without devising a single plan. He gravely mishandled the deployment of forces and lost his opportunity. Let Xu Guangjin be sentenced, in accordance with the recommendation of Yucheng and his colleagues and the established law, to beheading after detention, the sentence to be carried out after autumn.” “This Commander Xu was an imperial commissioner personally appointed by the emperor. You could hardly have a stronger patron! But when a man fails, even that support is unreliable. He still faces execution.” Hu sounded deeply moved. “Everything else is uncertain. You can truly depend only on yourself. Even good connections depend on what you are. What friends can a good-for-nothing expect?” Wang nodded repeatedly. “Xueyan, this is no flattery: it's a pity you haven't had more schooling. Otherwise you'd certainly do better than He Genyun or Governor Huang.” “I don't see it that way. A merchant may seem at a disadvantage before an official, but business has pleasures of its own. An official faces all sorts of restrictions. A prosperous merchant can really enjoy himself!”

“喔！”王有龄很感兴趣地说：“ ‘盍言尔志’！”这句话胡雪岩是懂的，“说到我的志向，与众不同，我喜欢钱多，越多越好！”他围拢两手，做了个搂钱的姿势，“不过我有了钱，不是拿银票糊墙壁，看看过瘾就算数，我有了钱要用出去！世界上顶顶痛快的一件事，就是看到人家穷途末路，几几乎一钱逼死英雄汉，刚好遇到我身上有钱，”他做了个挥手斥金的姿态，仿佛真有其事似他说：“拿去用！够不够？”王有龄大笑：“听你说说都痛快！”“还有一样，做生意发了财，尽管享用，盖一座大花园，计十七八个姨太太住在里面，没有人好说闲话。做官的发了财，对不起，不好这样子称心如意！不说别的，叫人背后指指点点，骂一声‘赃官’，这味道就不好过了。”“唉！”王有龄被他说动了心，“照此看来，我都想弃官从商了。”

“Oh?” Wang was interested. “Then let us hear your ambitions!” This was one classical phrase Hu understood. “My ambition is rather different from other men's. I like plenty of money—the more the better!” He brought both hands round as though gathering a heap towards him. “But once I have it, I don't mean to paper the walls with bank notes and be satisfied just looking at them. I mean to spend it! The finest pleasure in the world is to find someone at the end of his tether, some fine fellow whom the lack of a single coin is almost driving to his death, and happen to have money on me.” He flung out a hand as though scattering silver and, almost acting out the scene, exclaimed, “Take it! Is that enough?” Wang burst out laughing. “It's a pleasure even to hear you say it!” “There's something else. A merchant who makes a fortune can enjoy it freely. He can build a great garden and put seventeen or eighteen concubines in it, and nobody has any right to complain. But an official who grows rich—I'm sorry, he can't please himself so freely! Leave everything else aside: having people point behind your back and call you a corrupt official would be unpleasant enough.” “Ah!” Wang was tempted. “The way you put it, I feel like giving up office and going into business myself.”

“这也不是这么说。做官也有做官的乐趣，起码荣宗耀祖，父母心里就会高兴。象我，有朝一日发了大财，我老娘的日子自然会过得极舒服。不过一定美中不足，在她老人家心里，十来个丫头伺候，不如朝廷一道‘诰封’来得值钱！”“这也不是办下到的事。”王有龄安慰他说，“不过一品夫人的诰封请不到而已。”捐班可以捐到三品道员，自然也就有诰封。胡雪岩此时还不敢存此奢望，“请个诰封，自然不是太难的事，只是做官要做得名符其实，官派十足，那就不容易了。”他笑笑又说：“不是我菲薄做官的，有些候补老爷，好多年派下上一个差使，穷得来吃尽当光。这样子的官，不做也罢。”

“That's not quite what I mean. Office has its pleasures too. At the very least, it brings honour to your ancestors and makes your parents happy. If I make a great fortune one day, my mother will naturally live in tremendous comfort. Yet there'll always be something missing. In her eyes, ten or a dozen maidservants wouldn't be worth as much as an imperial patent granting her a title.” “That isn't impossible either,” Wang assured him. “You simply couldn't obtain a patent making her a lady of the first rank.” Purchased advancement could reach a third-rank circuit intendancy, which naturally carried eligibility for such a patent. Hu did not yet dare entertain that ambition. “Obtaining a patent wouldn't be too difficult, of course. But actually living up to an official title, with all the standing that ought to go with it—that isn't easy.” He smiled and added, “I'm not disparaging officials, but some expectant gentlemen go years without a single assignment, until poverty has made them eat through their resources and pawn everything they own. That sort of office is hardly worth having.”

这话，王有龄颇有感触，便越觉眼前的机会可贵。“雪岩，”他问，“周、吴二人，怎么说法？”什么事怎么说？胡雪岩无法回答，但他的意思是能够懂的：“雪公，你放心！这两位全在我手里，要他长就长，要他短就短，不必放在心上。我现在担心的是怕寻不着这么一位肯垫货的大粮商。”“是呀！”王有龄也上了心事，“我还怕找到了，他不肯相信。”“这……”胡雪岩摇摇头：“不要紧！只要他有实力，不怕他不听我们的话。”看到他这样有信心，再想到他笼络人的手段，王有龄果然放心了。

Wang felt the force of that remark from experience and valued his present opportunity all the more. “Xueyan,” he asked, “what about Zhou and Wu?” What about them in what respect? Hu could not answer so vague a question, but understood its intention. “Rest easy, Mr Xuexuan. Those two are completely in my hands. They'll do exactly as I wish. There's no need to worry about them. What concerns me now is whether we can find a large grain merchant willing to supply the rice in advance.” “Yes.” Wang too grew anxious. “I'm also afraid that, even if we find one, he won't trust us.” “That...” Hu shook his head. “That doesn't matter. Provided he has the resources, I can make him listen.” His confidence, together with what Wang had seen of his skill in winning people over, reassured Wang at once.

等闲谈到晚，张胖子带着周、吴两人兴尽归来。仔细看去，脸上都浮着诡秘的笑容。胡雪岩当着王有龄不便动问，心里明白，他们此行，必为平生所未历。“喔，喔，我想起件事。”张胖子忽然一本正经他说，“我今天遇到一个朋友，偶然谈起，松江有一家大粮行，跟漕帮的关系密切，他们有十几万石米想卖。倒不妨打听一下。”胡雪岩还未开口，王有龄大为兴奋：“这下对了路了！”“咦，雪公！”胡雪岩奇怪地，“事情不过刚刚一提，也不知内情如何？你何以晓得对了路了！““你也有不懂的事！”王有龄得意地笑了，为他讲解其中的道理。

They talked until evening, when Zhang returned with Zhou and Wu, all well satisfied with their outing. A closer look revealed secretive smiles on their faces. Hu could not ask questions in Wang's presence, but knew they must have experienced something quite new to them. “Oh, I've just remembered something,” Zhang suddenly said with an air of complete seriousness. “I met a friend today, and it came up in conversation that a large grain firm in Songjiang has close ties to the grain-transport association. They have a hundred thousand shi or more of rice to sell. It might be worth making inquiries.” Before Hu could speak, Wang exclaimed excitedly, “Now we're on the right track!” “Why, Mr Xuexuan,” Hu asked in surprise, “we've only just heard of it. We know nothing of the circumstances. How can you tell it's the right track?” “So there are things even you don't understand!” Wang smiled triumphantly and explained his reasoning.

他对于漕运已经下过一番功夫，知道松江出米，又当江浙交界，水路极便，所以松江的漕帮是个大帮，也应该是个富帮。但唯其既大且富，便成了一个俎上之肉。松江府知府所以与四川成都府、湖南长沙府，成为府缺中有名的三个肥缺，各有特殊的说法，松江府兼管水路夫隘，漕帮过闸讨夫，不能不买他的帐是一大原因。年深月久，饱受剥削，松江槽帮的公款亏空甚巨，成了“疲帮”。王有龄判断这家粮行，实际上就是漕帮所开，现在有粮食要卖，来源大成疑问，可能就是从漕米中侵独偷漏而来的，米质不会好，但是米价一定便宜，差额便可减少许多。“那好！”胡雪岩对此还未有过深入的研究，只听王有龄的话。

He had made a serious study of grain transport. Songjiang produced rice, lay at the boundary between Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and enjoyed excellent water communications. Its transport association was therefore large and ought also to have been rich. But its very size and wealth made it meat on the chopping board. The prefecture of Songjiang ranked with Chengdu in Sichuan and Changsha in Hunan as one of the three famously lucrative prefectural appointments, each for its own particular reasons. One important reason in Songjiang was the prefect's control of waterway labour and checkpoints. When the association needed passage through sluices or men to haul its boats, it had to accommodate him. After years of exploitation, the Songjiang association had accumulated an enormous deficit in its common funds and become an impoverished organisation. Wang judged that the grain firm was actually its own business. The origin of the rice now offered for sale was highly questionable: it might well have been siphoned off from the grain-tax shipments. The quality would be poor, but the price should certainly be low, greatly reducing the amount needed to cover the difference. “Excellent!” Hu had not studied these matters in depth and accepted Wang's account.

于是，张胖子重又上岸，去寻他的朋友，约定在松江与那粮商会面的时间，会面的地方就在船上，这是王有龄处事精细，怕上岸与粮商有所接洽，会引起猜疑。等张胖子回来，说是已经约好了，第三天到松江，舟泊城内秀野桥下，他那朋友自会约好粮行里的人来寻。而且他也证实了王有龄的判断，那家字号“通裕”的粮行，果然是松江漕帮的后台，不但经营米粮买卖，并且兼营票号，只是南方为钱庄的天下，跟北方通声气的票号，难与钱庄抗衡，张胖子也知道有这家通裕，素无往来，所以不知道信用如何？“你们明天再玩一天，”王有龄以一半体恤、一半告诫的语气说：“一到松江就要办正事了！”事实上这天夜里就已开始办正事，大家在王有龄的船上吃饭，席间便谈起漕运。王育龄在这方面的学问，是从书本上得来的，所以只晓得规制、政令和故事。周委员却是老手，久当押运委员，在运河上前后走过七八趟，漕运中的弊病，相当了解，他所说的琐碎细节，虽有些杂乱无章，不如王有龄言之成理，但出于本身经验，弥觉亲切。他们两个人的话，到胡雪岩脑子里一集中，便又不同了，一夜深谈，他成了一个既明规制，又懂实务的内行。

Zhang therefore went ashore again to find his friend and arrange a meeting with the merchant in Songjiang. It was to take place aboard their boats. Wang, attentive to such details, feared that going ashore to negotiate with a grain dealer would arouse suspicion. On returning, Zhang reported that everything was arranged. They would reach Songjiang on the third day and moor beneath Xiuye Bridge inside the city. His friend would bring someone from the grain firm to find them there. He also confirmed Wang's judgement. The firm, Tongyu, was indeed the financial backing of the Songjiang association. Besides trading grain, it operated a remittance bank. But the south was the domain of private banks, and remittance houses with northern connections found it hard to compete. Zhang had heard of Tongyu, but had never dealt with it and knew nothing of its credit. “Enjoy yourselves for one more day tomorrow,” Wang said, half indulgently and half in warning. “Once we reach Songjiang, there'll be serious work to do!” In fact, serious work began that very night. They dined aboard Wang's boat and discussed grain transport. Wang's knowledge came from books, so he knew the regulations, government orders, and precedents. Zhou, by contrast, was an experienced hand. As a convoy commissioner, he had made seven or eight journeys along the canal and knew a good deal about the abuses of the system. His scattered details were less orderly than Wang's account, but their basis in personal experience made them particularly vivid. When Hu brought the two accounts together in his mind, something new emerged. After a night's discussion, he understood both the regulations and their practical operation.

“我现在要请教，”他也还有些疑问，“怎么叫‘民折官办’？”“所谓‘民折官办’是如此……”王有龄为他解释，漕粮的征收，有五种花样，一种叫“正兑”，直接运到京城十三仓交纳。一种叫“改兑”，运到通州两仓交纳，这两处米仓简称为“京仓”、“通仓”。再有一种“白粮”，就是糯米，亦运“京仓”，供给祭祀及搭发王公官员俸米之用，规定由江苏的功州、松江、常州、太仓，以及浙江的嘉兴、湖州等五府一州缴纳。这三种名目都是征实物，应证实物，由于特殊的原因，征米的改为征杂粮，征杂粮的改为征银，都出于特旨，就称“改征”。最后一种是“折征”，以实物的征额，改征为银子，这又有四种花样，“民折官办”为其中之一，换句话说，老百姓纳粮，照价折算银子，由宫府代办漕米充“正兑”或“改兑”，就叫“民折官办。”

“There is something I should like to ask,” Hu said, for he still had questions. “What does ‘cash payment by the taxpayer, procurement by the authorities’ mean?” “The arrangement works as follows...” Wang explained that grain-tax collection took five forms. One, called “regular delivery,” required the grain to be taken directly to the thirteen granaries in the capital. Another, “redirected delivery,” sent it to the two granaries in Tongzhou. The two sets were known for short as the capital granaries and the Tongzhou granaries. A third category, “white grain,” consisted of glutinous rice, also delivered to the capital, for sacrificial offerings and as part of the grain salaries of princes and officials. This levy fell upon the five prefectures and one department of Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, and Taicang in Jiangsu, and Jiaxing and Huzhou in Zhejiang. All three required payment in kind. Where special circumstances led to rice being replaced by other grains, or other grains by silver, the change required a specific imperial order and was called “altered collection.” The final form was “commuted collection”: a quota originally assessed in produce was collected in silver instead. This had four variants, of which “cash payment by the taxpayer, procurement by the authorities” was one. In other words, the taxpayer paid the silver equivalent of his grain assessment, and the government bought the rice for regular or redirected delivery on his behalf.

“我懂了，再要请教。是怎么一种情形之下，可以‘民折官办’？”这细节上就要同委员来解答了，“那也没有一定。总之，为了官民两便。譬如说，朝廷有旨意，为了正用，赶催漕米，那就先动库款，买米运出，再改征银子，归还垫款，也有小户实在无米可交，情愿照市价折银，官府自然乐于代办。再有一种就是各地丰歉不同，丰收的地方，大家自然交米，正项以外，另外额定的‘漕耗’、‘船耗’的耗米，以及浮收的耗外之耗，也都是米，这些米运到歉收的地方，价钱比较便宜，老百姓可以买来交粮，只要帐面上做一道手续好了，也算‘民折官办’。“

“I understand. May I ask another question? Under what circumstances is that arrangement permitted?” Zhou was the man to answer this practical detail. “There is no fixed rule. In general, it is for the convenience of both officials and taxpayers. Suppose an imperial order presses for grain to meet government needs. Treasury money can first be used to buy and ship the rice; silver is then collected to reimburse the advance. Some small households have no rice to deliver and willingly pay its market value instead. Naturally, the authorities are glad to procure it for them. There is another case: harvests vary from place to place. In districts with a good harvest, people naturally deliver rice. Beyond the basic quota, the officially prescribed allowances for losses in transport and aboard ship are collected in rice too, as are the additional, unauthorised levies imposed on top of those allowances. When this rice is taken to districts with poor harvests, its price is comparatively low. The people there can buy it to discharge their grain tax. Only an entry in the accounts is required. That too counts as cash payment by the taxpayer and procurement by the authorities.”

“原来如此，那我们就用不着偷偷摸摸做了。”胡雪岩说，“现在军情紧急，赶催海运，我们动正项购运，有何不可？至于通裕这方面，既然是漕帮应得的耗米，而且准许‘民折官办’，那他卖米也不犯法。就算他们是偷盗来的赃货，我们只当他是应得的耗米好了！”“不错啊！” 一向口快的张胖子说，“麻袋上又没有写着字：”偷来的‘！“王有龄和周、吴二人都相视以目，微微点头，显然的，他们都有些困惑，这么浅显的道理，何以自己就没有想到？“话是不错。”王有龄说，“照这样子做，当然最好，但海运局只管运，‘民折官办’是征粮那时候的事，藩司、粮道两衙门，没有公事给我，我何能越俎代庖？

“So that is how it works! Then we needn't go about this in secret,” Hu said. “The military situation is urgent, and grain shipments by sea are being pressed forward. Why shouldn't we use the regular funds to buy and ship rice? As for Tongyu, if this is the association's legitimate allowance for transport losses, and official procurement against cash payments is permitted, selling it breaks no law. Even if the rice is stolen, we can treat it as their proper allowance.” “Exactly!” the ever-ready Zhang said. “The sacks don't have ‘Stolen’ written on them!” Wang, Zhou, and Wu exchanged glances and nodded slightly. They were plainly puzzled: why had so simple an argument never occurred to them? “That's true,” Wang said. “Of course it would be best to proceed that way. But the Sea Transport Bureau is responsible only for shipping. This arrangement belongs to the collection stage. Without an official communication from the provincial treasury and the grain intendant's office, how can I take over their duties?”

到这里就看出胡雪岩一路来，把周、吴二人伺候得服服帖帖的效验了，他俩争着开口，却又互相推让，不过看得出来，要说的话是相同的，有一个人说也就够了。周委员年纪长些，又是藩台麟桂的私人，所以还是由他答复：“这不要紧，藩台衙门要补怎么样一个公事？归我去接头。”“粮道衙门也一样，归我去办好。”“那就承情不尽了。”王有龄拱拱手说，“偏劳两位。”“分所当为。”周、吴二人异口同声地。

Now the effect of Hu's careful attentions to Zhou and Wu throughout the journey became clear. Both hurried to speak, then deferred to each other. Plainly they had the same thing to say; one could answer for both. Zhou was older and a personal follower of Treasurer Lingui, so he replied. “That needn't trouble you. Whatever supplementary document is required from the treasurer's office, I'll arrange it.” “And I'll do the same at the grain intendant's office.” “Then I am most grateful,” Wang said, clasping his hands. “I must trouble you both.” “It is our duty,” they answered together.

“慢来，慢来！”张胖子忽然插嘴，“这把如意算盘不见得打得通！”他说了其中的道理，确不为无见。通裕是想卖米，而自己这方面是想找人垫借，两个目标不同，未见得能谈出结果。“那也不见得，”胡雪岩说，“做生意不能光卖出，不买进。生意要谈，就看你谈得如何？”大家都点头称是，连张胖子也这样，“除非你去谈。”他笑道，“别人没这个本事。”虽是戏言，也是实话，周委员私下向王有龄献议，“当官的”出个面，证明确有其事，实际上都委托胡雪岩跟张胖子去谈，生意人在一起，比较投机。这番话恰中下怀，王有龄欣然接纳，而胡雪岩也当仁不让，到松江以后的行止，由他重新作了安排。本来只预备跟通裕那面的人，在舟上一晤，现在却要大张旗鼓，摆出一番声势，才便于谈事。

“Wait a moment!” Zhang suddenly interrupted. “This attractive calculation may not work out.” His reasoning was not without merit. Tongyu wanted to sell rice, while they wanted someone to advance it on loan. With different aims, the two sides might never reach an agreement. “Not necessarily,” Hu replied. “A business cannot go on selling without buying. Trade calls for negotiation. Everything depends on how you negotiate.” They all nodded, including Zhang. “Only if you do the talking,” he said with a smile. “Nobody else could manage it.” The remark was partly a joke, but true enough. Zhou privately suggested to Wang that the officials should appear briefly to establish the authenticity of the matter, then leave the actual negotiation to Hu and Zhang. Businessmen would find it easier to deal with one another. This was exactly what Wang wanted, and he readily agreed. Hu accepted the responsibility without demur and revised their plans for Songjiang. They had originally intended a single meeting aboard the boats with Tongyu's representatives. Now a conspicuous display of standing would make the negotiations easier.

一路顺风顺水，过嘉善到枫泾，就属于松江府华亭县的地界了。第二天进城，船泊在以出“巨口细鳞”的四鳃鲈闻名的秀野桥下。王有龄派庶务上岸，雇来一顶轿子，然后他和高升主仆二人，打扮得一身簇新，另外备了丰厚的土仪，叫人挑着，一起去拜客。先拜松江府，用手本谒见，再拜华亭县和娄县。化亭是首县，照例要尽地主之谊，随即便来回拜，面约赴宴，又派了人来照料。接着，知府又送了一桌“海菜席”，胡雪岩作主，厚犒来使，叫把菜仍旧挑回馆子里，如何处理，另有通知。“雪公！”胡雪岩说，“晚上你和周、吴二公去赴华亭县的席，知府的这桌菜，我有用处！”“好，好，随你。”

With wind and current in their favour, they passed Jiashan and reached Fengjing, entering Huating County in Songjiang Prefecture. The next day they entered the city and moored beneath Xiuye Bridge, famous for the four-gilled perch with its “great mouth and fine scales.” Wang sent the general affairs officer ashore to hire a sedan chair. Then, both dressed in fresh clothes, he and Gao set out to pay calls, accompanied by porters carrying generous gifts of local produce. He first visited the prefect of Songjiang, presenting the formal card appropriate to an official call, then called on the magistrates of Huating and Lou counties. Huating, as the county containing the prefectural seat, was expected to act as host. Its magistrate promptly returned the visit, invited Wang to dinner, and sent men to attend to his needs. The prefect then sent over a full seafood banquet. Hu took charge, tipped the bearers generously, and told them to carry it back to the restaurant, where further instructions would follow. “Mr Xuexuan,” he said, “you, Zhou, and Wu should go to the Huating magistrate's dinner tonight. I have a use for the prefect's banquet.” “Certainly. Do as you think best.”

话刚说完，张胖子的朋友，带着通裕的“老板”寻了来了，看见王有龄自然要请安。他受了胡雪岩的教，故意把官架子摆得十足。这两个人是张胖子的朋友姓刘、通裕的“老板”姓顾，王有龄请教了姓氏，略略敷衍几句，便站起身来说：“兄弟有个约会，失陪，失陪！”接着又向张胖子，“你们谈谈。凡事就跟我在场一样，说定规了就定规了。”等他一走，周、吴两人声明，要陪同王有龄赴华亭知具之约，也起身而去。于是宾主四人，开始深谈。

They had scarcely finished speaking when Zhang's friend arrived with the manager of Tongyu. On seeing Wang, both naturally paid their respects. Following Hu's advice, Wang deliberately assumed an imposing official manner. Zhang's friend was surnamed Liu; Tongyu's manager was Gu. Wang asked their names, exchanged a few civilities, then rose. “I have an engagement. You must excuse me.” Turning to Zhang, he added, “You gentlemen discuss matters. Treat everything exactly as though I were here. Whatever you agree shall stand.” Once he had left, Zhou and Wu explained that they were accompanying him to the Huating magistrate's dinner and departed too. The four remaining hosts and guests then settled down to a serious conversation.

深谈的还不是正题，是旁敲侧击地打听背景。顾老板坦率承认，通裕是松江漕帮的公产。接着，胡雪岩便打听漕帮的情形。他是“空子”，但漕帮中的规矩是懂的。所以要打听的话，都在要紧关节上，很快地弄清楚，松江漕帮中，行辈最高的是一个姓魏的旗丁，今年已经八十将近，瞎了一只眼，在家纳福。现在全帮管事的是他的一个“关山门”徒弟，名叫尤老五。

They did not yet tackle the main issue, but sounded out the circumstances around it. Gu freely acknowledged that Tongyu was the collective property of the Songjiang grain-transport association. Hu then asked about the association itself. Though an outsider, he understood its customs, and his questions all touched the important points. He soon learned that its most senior member was a boat-service soldier named Wei, nearly eighty, blind in one eye, and enjoying retirement at home. The man now managing its affairs was Wei's final admitted disciple, You Laowu.

“道理要紧！”胡雪岩对张胖子说，“我想请刘、顾两位老大哥领路，去给魏老太爷请安。”刘、顾二人一听这话，赶紧谦谢：“不敢当，不敢当！我把胡大哥的话带到就是。”“这不好。”胡雪岩说：“两位老哥不要把我当官面上的人看待。实在说，我虽是‘空子’，也常常冒充在帮，有道是‘准充不准赖’，不过今天当着真神面前，不好说假话。出门在外，不可自傲自大，就请两位老哥带路。再还有一说，等给魏老太爷请了安，我还想请他老人家出来吃一杯，有桌菜，不晓得好不好，不过是松江府送我们东家的，用这桌莱来请他老人家，略表敬意。“客人听得这一说，无不动容，觉得这姓胡的是“外场朋友”，大可交得，应该替他引见，欣然乐从，离舟登岸，安步当车，到了魏家。

“Proper respect comes first,” Hu said to Zhang. “I should like our friends Liu and Gu to take us to pay our respects to Old Master Wei.” Both guests hastened to decline the honour implied by his courteous address. “You are too kind. We can simply convey your message to him.” “That wouldn't do,” Hu said. “Please don't regard me as an official. To tell you the truth, though I'm an outsider, I often pass myself off as a member. As the saying goes, a man may claim membership, but a member may not deny it. Still, in the presence of the real thing today, I mustn't pretend. A man away from home ought never to put on airs. I ask you both to lead the way. And there's something else. After paying my respects, I should like to invite the old gentleman out for a drink. We have a banquet—I don't know how good it is, but the Songjiang prefect sent it to my employer. I should like to offer it to him as a small mark of respect.” Both guests were impressed. This Hu knew how to conduct himself in the wider world and was well worth befriending. They ought to introduce him. They readily agreed, and the party went ashore and walked to Wei's house.

魏老头子已经杜门谢客，所以一到他家，顾老板不敢冒昧，先跟他家的人说明，有浙江来的一个朋友，他愿不愿见？胡雪岩是早料到这样的处置，预先备好了全帖，自称“晚生”，交魏家的人，一起递了进去。在客厅里坐不多久，魏家的人来说，魏老头请客人到里面夫坐。刘、顾二人脸上顿时大放光彩，“老张，”姓刘的对他说，“我们老人爷很少在里面见客，说实话，我们也难得进去，今天沾你们两位贵客的光了！”一听这话，胡雪岩便知自己这着棋走对了。

Old Wei had withdrawn from social life and no longer received visitors. Gu therefore dared not announce them without preparation. He explained to the household that a friend from Zhejiang had come and asked whether the old man wished to see him. Hu had anticipated this. He had brought a formal visiting card describing himself as a junior and handed it over to be taken in with the message. They had not sat long in the reception room before a member of the household invited them into the inner quarters. Liu and Gu immediately brightened. “Zhang,” Liu said, “our old gentleman rarely receives anyone inside. To tell the truth, we scarcely ever get to go in ourselves. Today we owe the honour to you two distinguished guests!” Hearing that, Hu knew he had made the right move.

跟着到了里面，只见魏老头子又干瘦、又矮小，只是那仅存一目，张眼看人时，精光四射，令人下敢逼视，确有不凡之处。胡雪岩以后辈之礼谒见。魏老头子行动不便，就有些倚老卖老似地，口中连称“不敢当”，身子却不动。等坐定了，他把胡雪岩好好打量了一下，问道：“胡老哥今天来，必有见教？江湖上讲爽气，你直说好了。”“我是我们东家叫我来的，他说漕帮的老前辈一定要尊敬。他自己因为穿了一身公服不便来，特地要我来奉请老辈，借花献佛，有桌知府送的席，专请老前辈。”“喔！”魏老头很注意地问：“叫我吃酒？”“是！敝东家现在到华亭县应酬去了。回来还要请老前辈到他船上去玩玩。”“谢谢，可惜我行动不便。”“那就这样。”胡雪岩说，“我叫他们把这一桌席送过来。”“那更不敢当了。”魏老头说，“王大老爷有这番意思就够了。胡老哥，你倒说说看，到底有何见教，只要我办得到，一定帮忙。”

Inside, they found a thin, wizened little man. Yet when he opened his single eye to look at them, it flashed so fiercely that they could hardly meet his gaze. There was indeed something exceptional about him. Hu greeted him with the ceremony due from a junior to a senior. Wei had difficulty moving and, rather as though trading on his age, repeatedly protested that he did not deserve the honour without stirring from his seat. Once they were settled, he examined Hu closely. “You must have something to tell me, my friend. Among men of the world, plain speaking is valued. Say it directly.” “My employer sent me. He says the elders of the grain-transport association must be treated with respect. He could not conveniently come himself in official dress, so he specially asked me to invite you. We are borrowing flowers to make an offering: the prefect sent him a banquet, and he wishes to devote it entirely to you.” “Oh?” Wei asked attentively. “He wants me to dine?” “Yes. He is attending the Huating magistrate's dinner now. When he returns, he would also like you to visit his boat.” “Thank you. Unfortunately, I don't move about easily.” “Then let us do this,” Hu said. “I'll have the banquet brought here.” “That would be too much. His Honour Wang's kind intention is enough. Now tell me what you need. If there is anything I can do, I shall certainly help.”

“自然，到了这里，有难处不请你老人家帮忙，请哪个，不过，说实在的，敝东家诚心诚意叫我来向老前辈讨教，你老人家没有办不到的事，不过在我们这面总要自己识相，所以我倒有点不大好开口。”胡雪岩是故意这样以退为进。等他刚提到“海运”，魏老头独眼大张，炯炯逼人地看着他，而这也在他意料之中，他早就想过了，凭人情来推断、漕运一走海道，运河上漕帮的生存便大受影响，万众生计所关，一定会在明里暗里，拼命力争。现在看到魏老头的敌视态度，证实了他的判断不错。既然不错，事情就好办了。他依旧从从容容把来意说完。魏老头的态度又变了，眼光虽柔和了些，脸上却已没有初见面时，那种表示欢迎的神情，“胡老哥，你晓不晓得，”他慢条斯理地说：“我们漕帮要没饭吃了？”“我晓得。”“既然晓得，一定会体谅我的苦衷。”魏老头点点头，“通裕的事，我还不大情楚，不过做生意归生意，你胡老哥这方面有钱买米，如果通裕不肯卖，这道理讲到天下都讲不过去，我一定出来说公道话。倘或是垫一垫货色，做生意的人，将本求利，要敲一敲算盘，此刻我也说不出个所以然来。”

“Naturally, if we run into difficulties here, whom else could we ask? But, truly, my employer sent me to seek your advice in all sincerity. There is nothing beyond your powers. We, however, must know what it is proper to ask. That makes me a little reluctant to speak.” Hu was deliberately retreating in order to advance. At his first mention of sea transport, Wei's single eye opened wide and fixed him with a piercing stare. That too was expected. Hu had already reasoned that moving the grain shipments to sea would seriously threaten the canal associations' existence. With countless livelihoods at stake, they were bound to fight the change desperately, openly and in secret. Wei's hostility confirmed his judgement. Since the judgement was sound, the matter would be easier to handle. He calmly finished explaining his purpose. Wei's manner changed again. His gaze softened a little, but the welcome had gone from his face. “My friend,” he said slowly, “do you realise that our association is about to lose its livelihood?” “I do.” “Then you must understand my difficulty.” Wei nodded. “I don't know much about Tongyu's affairs now, but business is business. If you have money to buy rice and Tongyu refuses to sell, nobody anywhere could defend that. I would certainly speak for what is fair. But if you want an advance of goods, a merchant puts up his capital to earn a return and must make his calculations. I can't give you an answer to that now.”

这是拒绝之词，亦早在胡雪岩的估计之中，“老前辈！”他抗声答道，“你肯不肯听我多说几句？”“啊呀，胡老哥你这叫什么话？承你的情来看我，我起码要留你三天，好好叙一叙，交你这个朋友。你有指教，我求之不得，怎问我肯不肯听你多说几句？莫非嫌我骄狂？”“那是我失言了。”胡雪岩笑道，“敝东家这件事，说起来跟漕帮关系重大。打开天窗说亮话，漕米海运误期，当官的自然有处分，不过对漕帮更加不利。”接下来他为魏老头剖析利害，倘或误期，不是误在海运，而是误在沿运河到海口这段路上，追究责任，浙江的漕帮说不定会有赔累，漕帮的“海底”称为“通漕”，通同一体，休戚相关，松江的漕帮何忍坐视？先以帮里的义气相责，魏老头就象被击中了要害似地，顿时气馁了。

It was a refusal, and one Hu had anticipated. “Sir,” he answered firmly, “would you hear a little more from me?” “My dear friend, what are you saying? You've done me the kindness of visiting. I ought at least to keep you three days, talk things over properly, and make a friend of you. If you have advice, I could ask for nothing better. Why ask whether I'm willing to listen? Do you find me arrogant?” “Then I spoke badly.” Hu smiled. “My employer's business is actually of great consequence to your association. Let us speak plainly. If the sea shipment misses its deadline, the officials will naturally be punished. But the consequences for the association will be worse.” He went on to explain the balance of interests. Any delay would not have occurred at sea, but on the canal journey to the port. An inquiry into responsibility might leave Zhejiang's association liable for ruinous compensation. The associations' secret code was known as Tongcao—“all grain-transport men united.” They formed one body, sharing prosperity and adversity. How could the Songjiang association stand by and watch? This appeal to their obligation of brotherhood struck Wei at a vulnerable point. His resistance immediately weakened.

“再说海运，现在不过试办，将来究竟全改海运，还是维持旧规，再不然海运、河运并行，都还不晓得。老实说一句，现在漕帮不好帮反对河运、主张海运的人的忙。”“这话怎么说？”魏老头极注意地问。“老前辈要晓得，现在想帮漕帮说话的人很多，敝东家就是一个。但是忙要帮得上，倘或漕帮自己不争气，那些要改海运的人，越发嘴说得响了，你们看是不是，短短一截路都是困难重重！河帮实在不行了！现在反过来看，河运照样如期运到，毫不误限，出海以后，说不定一阵狂风、吹翻了两条沙船，那时候帮漕帮的人，说话就神气了！”魏老头听他说完，没有答复，只向他左右侍奉的人说：“你们把老五替我去叫来！”

“Besides, sea transport is only an experiment for now. Nobody knows whether it will eventually replace the canal altogether, whether the old arrangements will be kept, or whether both routes will be used. Frankly, the association ought not to help the people who oppose canal transport and advocate shipment by sea.” “What do you mean?” Wei asked with close attention. “You should know, sir, that plenty of people want to speak for the association. My employer is one. But they must have grounds on which to help. If the association lets itself down, those who want sea transport will argue all the louder: ‘Look! Even this short stretch is full of difficulties. The canal men are simply no use any more!’ Now consider the opposite. Suppose the canal shipment arrives on time, without the slightest delay. Once it has put to sea, a gale might overturn a couple of sand junks. Then the association's supporters would have something powerful to say!” Wei heard him out without answering. He merely told the attendants beside him, “Go and fetch Laowu.”

这就表示事情大有转机了，胡雪岩在这些地方最能把握分寸，知道话不必再多说，只需哄得魏老头高兴就是，因此谈过正题，反入寒暄。魏老头自言，一生到过杭州的次数，已经记不清楚，杭州是运河的起点，城外拱宸桥，跟漕帮有特殊渊源，魏老头常去杭州是无足为奇的。谈起许多杭州掌故，胡雪岩竟螳然不知所答，反殷殷向他请教，两个人谈得投机。谈兴正浓时，尤老五来了，约莫四十岁左右，生得矮小而沉静，在懂世故的人眼里，一望而知是个极厉害的人物。当时由魏老头亲自为他引见胡雪岩和张胖子。尤老五因为胡、张二人算是他“老头子”的朋友，所以非常客气，称胡雪岩为“胡先生”。“这位胡老哥是‘祖师爷’那里来的人。”漕帮中的秘密组织，“清帮”的翁、钱、潘三祖，据说都在杭州拱宸桥成道，所以魏老头这样说。

The affair had plainly taken a promising turn. Hu had an excellent sense of how far to go on such occasions. No further argument was needed; he had only to keep Wei happy. Their serious business concluded, they turned belatedly to social conversation. Wei said he had lost count of his visits to Hangzhou. That was hardly surprising: Hangzhou marked the beginning of the canal, and Gongchen Bridge outside the city had special associations with the boatmen. Wei recalled many old Hangzhou stories about which Hu knew so little that he could offer no answer. Instead, he eagerly asked for more, and they talked congenially. They were deep in conversation when You Laowu arrived. He was about forty, small and composed. Anyone experienced in the world would have recognised at a glance a formidable man. Wei himself introduced Hu and Zhang. Since they were friends of his master, You was exceedingly polite and addressed Hu as “Mr Hu.” “This friend of ours comes from the home of the patriarchs,” Wei said. The three founders of the Qing Brotherhood, the secret society within the grain-transport association—Weng, Qian, and Pan—were all said to have attained enlightenment at Gongchen Bridge in Hangzhou. That was what he meant.

“这就象一家人一样了。”尤老五说：“胡先生千万不必客气。”胡雪岩未曾答口，魏者头又说：“胡老哥是外场人物，这个朋友我们一定要交。老五，你要叫‘爷叔’，胡老哥好比‘门外小爷’一样。”尤老五立即改口，很亲热地叫了声：“爷叔！”这一下胡雪岩倒真是受宠若惊了！他懂得“门外小爷”这个典故，据说当初“三祖”之中的不知哪一们，有个贴身服侍的小童，极其忠诚可靠，三祖有所密议，都不避他。他虽跟自己人一样，但毕竟未曾入帮，在“门槛”外头，所以尊之为“门外小爷”。每逢“开香堂”，亦必有“门外小爷”的一份香火。现在魏老头以此相拟，是引为密友知交之意，特别是尊为“爷叔”，便与魏者头平辈，将来至少在松江地段，必为漕帮奉作上客。初涉江湖，有此一番成就，着实不易。当然，他要极力谦辞。无奈魏老头在他们帮里，话出必行，不管他怎么说，大家都只听魏老头的吩咐，口口声声喊他“爷叔”。连张胖子那个性刘的朋友，和通裕的顾老板也是如此。

“Then we're practically one family,” You said. “You mustn't stand on ceremony, Mr Hu.” Before Hu could reply, Wei continued, “Our friend Hu is a man who knows the world. We must make a friend of him. Laowu, call him Uncle. He is like the Little Master Outside the Gate.” You immediately changed his form of address, warmly calling him “Uncle.” Hu was genuinely overwhelmed by the honour. He knew the story of the Little Master Outside the Gate. One of the three founders—he could not remember which—was said to have had a young personal attendant of exceptional loyalty and trustworthiness. Even when the founders discussed secret matters, they did not exclude him. Yet although he was treated as one of them, he had never joined the brotherhood and technically remained outside its threshold. They therefore honoured him as the Little Master Outside the Gate. Whenever an incense-hall ceremony was held, he too received a share of the incense offerings. Wei's comparison meant that he was admitting Hu as a trusted intimate. Above all, to have him addressed as Uncle put him on Wei's own generational level. In future, at least in the Songjiang district, the association would treat him as an honoured guest. That was no small achievement for someone just entering this world. Naturally, he protested vigorously that he did not deserve it. But Wei's word was law among his people. Whatever Hu said, they obeyed the old man's instruction and called him Uncle, including Zhang's friend Liu and Tongyu's manager Gu.

“老五！浙江海运局的王大老爷，还送了一桌席，这桌席是我们松江府送的，王大老爷特为转送了我。难得的荣耀，不可不领情。”魏老头又说：‘ 人敬我一尺，我敬人一丈’，你先到船上替我去磕个头道谢。““不必，不必！我说到就是。”胡雪岩口里这样客气，心中却十分高兴，不过这话要先跟王有龄说明白，尤老五去了，便不好乱摆官架子，因而又接上一句：“而且敝东家赴贵县大老爷的席去了。”“那我就明天一早去。”于是胡雪岩请尤老五派人到馆子里，把那一桌海菜席送到魏家。魏老头已经茹素念佛，不肯入席，由尤老五代表。他跟胡雪岩两人变得都是半客半主的身分，结果由张胖子坐了首席。

“Laowu! His Honour Wang of the Zhejiang Sea Transport Bureau has also sent us a banquet. It was a gift from our own prefect, and he has specially passed it on to me. Such an unusual honour must be acknowledged.” Wei continued, “If a man gives me a foot of respect, I give him ten feet in return.
