She turned away and hurried along the side of the road. Watching her slender figure recede, he recalled her parting admonitions and found endless pleasure in their implications. His contentment was beyond words.

阿珠却跟他不同，心里乱糟糟的，不辨是何滋味？却又无法静下来想一想，因为一回去就让七姑奶奶缠住了。“你怎么这么快就回来了？”这第一句话就让她不容易回答，她嘴上不大肯让人，其实说不来假话，自己算一算，到船上来回一趟，这点辰光是不够的，因而疑心七姑奶奶已发觉她根本没有去见她父亲，只是借故溜出去跟陈世龙“讲私话”。于是象被人捉住了短处似地，她一张脸涨得退红，半晌说不出话来。七姑奶奶等于一个女光棍，那双眼睛看阿珠这样的人，表里俱澈。恍然大悟之余，心中好笑，真正是做贼心虚。但她虽口沿遮拦，对这句后到底还有顾忌，怕阿珠脸皮薄，一个挂不住，会伤了彼此情分，因此笑笑不响。这一笑在心思也极灵敏的阿珠，当然亦猜到了她的心理。掩饰不可，只有解释，索性把话说明了，倒也无所谓。

A’zhu felt very differently. Her thoughts were in turmoil, and she could not tell what she felt. Nor could she sit quietly to consider it, for the Seventh Lady caught her the moment she returned. “How did you get back so quickly?” The very first question was hard to answer. A’zhu seldom conceded anything in an argument, but she was a poor liar. A quick calculation showed that she had not been away long enough to go to the boat and back. She suspected the Seventh Lady had discovered that she had never visited her father at all, merely used him as an excuse to slip out for a private conversation with Chen. Feeling as though she had been caught doing something wrong, she flushed deeply and could not speak for some time. The Seventh Lady was as worldly as any hardened rogue. She could see straight through someone like A’zhu. Understanding suddenly, she was amused: a guilty conscience indeed! Yet, free as she was with her tongue, she hesitated to say this aloud. If she embarrassed the thin-skinned girl beyond endurance, she might damage their affection. She merely smiled. A’zhu was perceptive too and naturally guessed what lay behind the smile. Concealment was impossible; she could only explain. There was no harm in stating the matter openly.

“老实告诉你，”她的脸色反转为平静，“我也要托陈世龙买点东西，不好当着你们的面说。”“为啥？”“在府上打扰了好些日子，哪怕送点不值钱的东两，也是我一点心。我如果当了你们的面说，你们一定不肯，所以我要避开你们托他。”“原来这佯。你何必又破费。”“是不是？”阿珠理直气壮似地说，“我就晓得你们一定会拦住我。”“好了。我就不客气了。自己姐妹，老说客气话也没有意思。”七姑奶奶看一看桌上的自鸣钟说：“我要到书场去了。你去不去？”七姑奶奶喜欢听书。一部书听上了瘾，天天要听。阿珠总觉得女人抛头露面上书场，不象样子。而且有些“先生”，说到男女间事、看有“堂客”在座，比较含蓄，有些就毫无顾忌了，绘声绘影，春情十足，七姑奶奶不在乎，阿珠却窘不可言。她“上过一回当”，颇存戒心，七姑奶奶也不便勉强，只是每天去总要问她一声。她有时去，有时不去，要看那天说的是哪一回书。

“To tell you the truth,” A’zhu said, her expression becoming calm, “I wanted to ask Chen to buy some things too, and I couldn't say so in front of you.” “Why not?” “I've been troubling your household for so many days. Even a small present would show my gratitude. If I'd mentioned it before you, you would certainly have objected. That was why I had to ask him privately.” “So that was it. Why put yourself to more expense?” “You see?” A’zhu spoke as though fully vindicated. “I knew you would try to stop me.” “Very well. I won't stand on ceremony. We're sisters; there's no point in endlessly exchanging polite speeches.” The Seventh Lady glanced at the striking clock on the table. “I'm going to hear the storyteller. Are you coming?” She loved storytelling. Once absorbed in a tale, she had to hear it every day. A’zhu, however, felt that women made a poor show of themselves by appearing in public at storytelling houses. Besides, when describing affairs between men and women, some performers restrained themselves if ladies were present, while others had no scruples at all and told their amorous scenes with vivid abandon. The Seventh Lady did not mind; A’zhu found it unbearably embarrassing. Having been caught out once, she remained wary. The Seventh Lady could hardly insist, but always asked before going. Sometimes A’zhu went and sometimes she stayed, depending on which episode was to be told.

阿珠知道，她听上瘾的那部书是《玉晴蜓》，随即问道：“今天说到哪里？”“快要‘庵堂产子’了。”“庵堂产子”只有怀孕足月的小尼姑志贞，没有造孽缘的申贵升，听这回书不会受窘，阿珠便答应同去。有人做伴，七姑奶奶的兴致格外好，一面涂脂抹粉，细细打扮，一面把“庵堂产子”的情节和昨天的“关子”说到什么地方，都讲了给阿珠听。“到底是‘申大爷’，还是‘金大爷’？”“应该是‘申大爷’，说书先生都称‘金大爷’，因为苏州申家势力大，不敢得罪他们，这部书，从前是禁的。”“这样说来，真的有这回事了？”“那就不晓得了。不过，”七姑奶奶说：“申家上代出过状元，倒是真的。有年到苏州，走过一家人家，门口下马石、旗杆，有块匾‘状元及第’，气派大得很，别人说是申状元家。”“这个状元，就是小尼姑志贞的儿子？”“照《玉蜻蜓》说，志贞的儿子叫申元宰，后来中了状元，‘庵堂认母’，把她接回家里。”

Knowing that the tale which had captivated her was The Jade Dragonfly, A’zhu asked, “Where have they got to today?” “Almost to ‘The Birth in the Nunnery.’” In that episode, the young nun Zhizhen was at the end of her pregnancy, but Shen Guisheng, the man with whom she had formed the ill-fated attachment, did not appear. There would be nothing to embarrass her, so A’zhu agreed to go. Pleased to have company, the Seventh Lady carefully applied her rouge and powder and dressed, all the while explaining the episode and the point of suspense at which yesterday's performance had ended. “Is he really Master Shen or Master Jin?” A’zhu asked. “It ought to be Master Shen. The storytellers all call him Master Jin because the Shen family is powerful in Suzhou and they dare not offend them. This tale used to be forbidden.” “Then did it really happen?” “That I don't know. But it's true that an ancestor of the Shen family came first in the palace examination. One year in Suzhou, I passed a house with dismounting stones and flagpoles outside, and a plaque proclaiming its owner's first place in the examination. It was very grand. Someone said it was the home of the great scholar Shen.” “Was that scholar the nun Zhizhen's son?” “According to The Jade Dragonfly, her son's name was Shen Yuanzai. He later came first in the palace examination, acknowledged his mother at the nunnery, and took her home.”

“那么，”阿珠问道：“ ‘申大娘娘’呢？怎么说？”“这还有啥话说？儿子虽不是她生的、诰封总要先归她，再说申大爷老早痨病死在庵里，为死人吃醋也没有这个道理。”“这一下，志贞总算苦出头了。”阿珠感叹着说，“大概她做梦也不曾想到，儿子会中了状元。”“照我想想犯不着。”七姑奶奶很平静的说：“苦守苦熬多少年，才熬得儿子出了头，头发白了，眼睛花了，牙齿掉了，就算有福好享，也是枉然。倒不如觅个知心合意的，趁少年辰光，过几天写意日子。“这话不知是不是有意讽劝？反正阿珠的印象极深。等听了“庵堂产子”回来，感触越深，而且由志贞的伶仃无告，勾起她想家的念头，渴望着回到湖州，觉得只有在自己娘身边，这颗心才能定下来。

“What about Madam Shen?” A’zhu asked. “What did she say?” “What could she say? Although she hadn't given birth to him, any imperial title granted to his mother would go to her first, as the lawful wife. Besides, Master Shen had long since died of consumption in the nunnery. There was no sense in being jealous over a dead man.” “Then Zhizhen finally came to the end of her troubles.” A’zhu sighed. “She probably never dreamed her son would come first in the examination.” “To my mind, it wasn't worth it,” the Seventh Lady said calmly. “Years and years of suffering and waiting, until her son finally made his way. By then her hair would be white, her eyes dim, and her teeth gone. Even if there were good fortune to enjoy, it would be wasted. Better to find someone who understands you and suits you, and have a few happy days while you're young.” Whether or not this was intended as indirect advice, it left a deep impression on A’zhu. After hearing “The Birth in the Nunnery,” she felt it more keenly still. Zhizhen's loneliness and helplessness made her homesick. She longed to return to Huzhou and felt that only beside her own mother could her heart find peace.

乡思造成失眠，一直到四更天还不曾睡着。七姑奶奶跟她住东西两厢房、一觉睡醒，发觉对面还有灯光，心里有些不放心，便起床来敲她的房门。阿珠知道是七姑奶奶，除了她不会有第二个人。于是开门问道：“你怎么还不睡？”“我已经睡过一大觉了，看见你这里灯光亮着，过来看看。”她走进门来，发觉阿珠的两面帐门都未放下，便奇怪的问：“你一直都不曾睡吗？在做什么？”“什么都没有做，就是睡不着。”“在想哪个？”阿珠脸一红，“会想哪个？”她说，“自然是想娘。”“怪不得！”七姑奶奶捏着她的手臂问：“冷不冷？”“还好。”阿珠见她只穿着一件对襟短袖的褂子，胸前钮扣，不曾扣好，露出雪白的一块肉，褂子又小了些，鼓蓬蓬的凸出两大块。心里便想，七姑奶奶象花开到盛时，却形单影只的守了寡，似乎也可怜。这样想着，不由得伸手捏住了她的丰腴的手臂，“七姐，”她说，“这里来坐！”她拉着她并坐在床沿上，怔怔地看着她，眼中有些迷惘和优郁，把七姑奶奶看得莫名其妙，便即问道，“怎么回事？你有话说嘛！”

Homesickness kept her awake. Even during the fourth watch, she had not slept. She and the Seventh Lady occupied opposite wings of the house. Waking after a good sleep, the Seventh Lady noticed light across the way and became uneasy. She rose and knocked on A’zhu's door. A’zhu knew who it must be; nobody else would come. Opening the door, she asked, “Why aren't you asleep yet?” “I've already had a good sleep. I saw your lamp burning and came to look in.” Entering, she noticed that the bed curtains on both sides were still raised. “Haven't you slept at all? What have you been doing?” “Nothing. I simply can't sleep.” “Who are you thinking of?” A’zhu blushed. “Who should I be thinking of? My mother, naturally.” “No wonder!” The Seventh Lady held her arm. “Are you cold?” “Not very.” A’zhu saw that she wore only a short-sleeved, front-fastening blouse. The buttons had not all been done up, exposing a patch of pale skin, and the blouse was rather tight across her full bosom. A’zhu thought that the Seventh Lady was like a flower in full bloom, yet lived alone as a widow. It seemed pitiable. Almost involuntarily, she took the woman's full arm in turn. “Seventh Sister, come and sit here.” She drew her onto the edge of the bed and gazed at her with bewilderment and melancholy in her eyes. The Seventh Lady could not understand it. “What's the matter? If you have something to say, say it.”

“我在想，”阿珠缓慢而低沉地说，“俗语说‘家家有本难念的经’，这话还不对，实在是‘人人有本难念的经’。譬如七姐你，别人看起来，一天到晚，嘻嘻哈哈，好象没啥心事，仔细想一想，你一个人的日子也难过。”这两句话听来平淡无奇，谁知恰好触着了七姑奶奶的隐痛，连她兄嫂在内，从来没有人说过这话。午夜梦回，凄凉万状，那时的心境，只有自己知道。如今总算还有个人了解她的苦楚！七姑奶奶顿有知遇之感，那么刚强的人，竟忍不住眼圈一红，快要掉眼泪了。但是刚强的人总是刚强的，就在这时候，也不愿让人觉得她可怜，“你说得不对！”所以她装得很豁达地，“我倒不觉得日子难过。”“叫我，”阿珠摇摇头，“这种日子就过不下去。”“所以罗！”七姑奶奶为人的心又热了，接口劝她，“你过不惯这种一个人孤孤单单的日子，要趁早打主意。跟胡老板断了，这着棋走得一点不错，他是个做大生意的人，一会儿湖州，一会儿上海，说走就走，丢下你独守空房，这味道不大好受的。”“嗳！”阿珠皱眉摇手，“不要去讲他了。讲讲别人吧！”

“I was thinking,” A’zhu said slowly and quietly, “people say every household has a difficult scripture to recite. That isn't quite right. Really, every person has one. Take you, Seventh Sister. Others see you laughing and joking all day, as though you had no worries. But when I think about it, living alone must be hard for you.” The words sounded ordinary enough, yet they touched the Seventh Lady's hidden pain. No one, not even her brother or his wife, had ever said such a thing. Only she knew the desolation of waking from a dream in the middle of the night. At last someone understood her suffering. She felt profoundly recognised. Strong as she was, her eyes reddened and tears almost came. Yet a strong person remained strong: even now, she would not allow herself to be pitied. “You're wrong!” she said, affecting an easy spirit. “I don't find life hard at all.” “I couldn't bear it,” A’zhu said, shaking her head. “Precisely!” Her concern for others revived, and the Seventh Lady seized the opportunity to advise her. “If you can't endure a life of loneliness, you must decide what to do early. You were quite right to break with Mr Hu. He's a man with a great business: Huzhou one moment, Shanghai the next. He would leave at a moment's notice and let you keep watch over an empty room. That isn't a pleasant life.” “Oh, don't talk about him!” A’zhu frowned and waved a hand. “Let's talk about someone else.”

她是无心的一句话，七姑奶奶却大为兴奋，“来！”她拉着她倒下，“今天我陪你。我们姐妹也说说私话。”阿珠也是精神亢奋，毫无睡意，刚过了立秋的天气，后半夜非常舒服，她也愿意作个长夜之谈。不过七姑奶奶如不羁的野马，她买在有些怕她，便得要有句话“言明在先”。“说私话可以。”她笑道，“就是你哇啦、哇啦吃不消。”“傻妹子！”七姑奶奶捧着她的红馥馥的脸香了一下，“说到私话，怎么会哇啦、哇啦？自然只有你我两个人才听得见。”“这样才好，”阿珠问道，“你饿不饿？我有杭州带来的‘绍兴香糕’，要不要吃？”“ ‘绍兴香糕’哪有你们‘湖州酥糖’好吃。有没有‘沙核桃糖’？”“有，有！我倒忘记掉了。”阿珠从置放茶食用的可以收燥的石灰坛里，摸出一大包沙核桃糖，带到床上，两个人并头共枕，盖着一条薄薄的紫罗被，一面吃糖，一面谈私话。

She spoke without any particular intention, but the Seventh Lady became excited. “Come!” She drew A’zhu down beside her. “I'll stay with you tonight. We sisters can have a private talk.” A’zhu was wide awake too. The season had just passed the Beginning of Autumn, and the later hours of the night were very comfortable. She was willing to talk until dawn. But the Seventh Lady was like an unbridled horse, and A’zhu was rather afraid of her. A condition must be stated first. “A private talk is all right,” she said with a smile. “It's your shouting and carrying on that I can't stand.” “Silly girl!” The Seventh Lady took her flushed face in her hands and kissed her cheek. “How could I shout when we're talking privately? Naturally, only you and I will hear.” “That's all right, then. Are you hungry? I've some Shaoxing fragrant cakes I brought from Hangzhou. Would you like some?” “Those aren't as good as your Huzhou flaky sweets. Have you any walnut sweets?” “Yes, yes! I'd quite forgotten them.” From the jar in which snacks were kept dry with lime, A’zhu took a large packet of walnut sweets and brought it to bed. With their heads beside each other on the pillow and a thin purple gauze coverlet over them, the two ate sweets and talked confidentially.

“七姐，你守寡守了几年了？”“四年。”这四年的味道如何呢？阿珠很想问，又觉得碍口，只好扯些不相干的话，“想来你那婆婆很凶。”“凭良心说，倒也还好。就是脾气合不来，一天到晚罗嗦，实在也是好意，譬如说，天气热胃口总有不好的时候，只要一顿不吃，她老人家就问长问短，一刻不停了。一会儿是不是病了？要不要看医生？一会儿又说受凉了，晚上睡觉要小心。如果我不理她，她就哭儿子，我都想哭在那里，听见她哭，你想烦不烦？”“那么，回娘家来住，是哪个的意思呢？”“自然是我自己的意思，”七姑奶奶说，“哪个都做不得我的主。”“难道，”阿珠很谨慎地问： “在娘家住一辈子？”“住一辈子也不要紧。我五哥、五嫂，跟别家的兄嫂不同。”“这我看得出来的，说句良心话，五哥、五嫂待你是再也没话可说了。”“当然，自己同胞手足嘛！不过，”七姑奶奶又说，“其中还有个道理，说给你听听也不要紧。“

“Seventh Sister, how long have you been widowed?” “Four years.” What had those four years been like? A’zhu wanted to ask, but felt awkward. Instead, she ventured something less direct. “I suppose your mother-in-law was very fierce.” “To be fair, she was quite decent. We simply didn't get on. She fussed from morning to night, though she really meant well. In hot weather, for instance, everyone loses their appetite sometimes. But if I missed a single meal, she would ask questions without stopping. Was I ill? Did I need a doctor? Then she would say I'd caught cold and must be careful at night. If I ignored her, she began mourning her son. I felt like crying myself already. Imagine having to listen to her too! Wasn't that exasperating?” “Whose idea was it for you to come back to your own family?” “Mine, naturally. Nobody else can decide for me.” “But surely...” A’zhu asked cautiously, “you won't stay here for the rest of your life?” “It wouldn't matter if I did. My fifth brother and his wife aren't like other brothers and sisters-in-law.” “I can see that. Honestly, nobody could say anything against the way they treat you.” “Of course. We're flesh and blood. But there's another reason too. I may as well tell you.”

原来尤五在十几年前，是倔强到底，宁折不弯的脾气，有一次跟松江府知府的大少爷，在妓院里打架，被抓到了“班房”里。那知府倒也还明理，预备训斥一顿，放他走路。但尤五自觉道理上站得住，所以言语顶撞，不受责备，这一下知府动了真气，非办他个“目无官长”的罪名不可。“老太爷”托出许多人来求情，那知府是个书呆子，说什么也不行。“这时漕粮要起运了，船上不是我五哥，就吃不住，老太爷十分着急。后来是我出面去见知府。“七姑奶奶回忆着得意的往事，那双眼睛格外亮，格外显得一汪水似的，”我说：大老爷，我哥得罪了大少爷，又得罪大老爷，理当吃三年六个月的官司。不过现在他有公事，好不好我来做押头？把我关起来，放我哥哥出去当差，等漕船回空，他进监牢，我再出去。“

More than ten years earlier, You Laowu had been stubborn to the last degree: he would sooner break than bend. Once, after fighting in a brothel with the eldest son of the prefect of Songjiang, he had been taken into custody. The prefect was reasonably fair-minded and meant merely to reprimand him and let him go. But You believed himself in the right and answered back, refusing to accept blame. The prefect became genuinely angry and insisted on charging him with contempt for official authority. The old master enlisted many people to intercede, but the prefect was a bookish man who would listen to nothing. “The grain tribute was just about to sail,” the Seventh Lady continued. “Without my fifth brother, nobody could keep the boats under control. The old master was terribly worried. In the end, I went to see the prefect myself.” Recalling this proud episode, her eyes grew unusually bright and lustrous. “I said, ‘Your Honour, my brother has offended both your son and yourself. He deserves three years and six months in prison. But he has public duties to perform just now. Could I stand as security for him? Lock me up and let him go about his work. When the grain boats return empty, he can go to prison and I can leave.’”

“你倒想得出。”阿珠听得津津有味的笑道：“那知府大老爷，怎么说法？”“大家都说知府大老爷是书呆子，其实不呆。”七姑奶奶答道：“当时他跟我说：”你哥哥不讲道理。世界上只有老百姓怕官，照他这样子，莫非官要怕他？那不是没有王法了吗？我本来不但要重办，而且还要申详到上头，革他尖丁的差使。现在看你倒还讲道理，不过你也不要看得太容易，监狱里的罪不是好受的。‘我说：“我晓得。不过不是这样子，大老爷不能消气，说不得只好我咬咬牙关来受罪。’大老爷听我这一说，摇摇手：”罢了，罢了！看你这样子，我也不气了。你具个结，把你哥哥领了回去。‘“

“What an idea!” A’zhu listened with delighted interest. “What did the prefect say?” “Everyone called him a pedant, but he wasn't stupid. He told me, ‘Your brother is unreasonable. In this world, ordinary people fear officials. Does he expect officials to fear him? Where would the law be then? I meant not only to punish him severely but to report the matter to my superiors and have him dismissed from his post as a grain-transport headman. You seem more reasonable. But don't think this is easy. Prison is no pleasant place.’ I said, ‘I know. But unless I do this, Your Honour's anger cannot be appeased. I'll just have to grit my teeth and bear it.’ He waved his hand. ‘Enough, enough! Seeing you like this has taken away my anger. Sign a bond and take your brother home.’”

“这真正是新闻。”阿珠笑道：“还要你具结？”“是啊！硬是我盖手模具结。具了结，知府大老爷把五哥叫了去说‘你要改过自新！再是这样子横行霸道，我不办你，办具结的人。你要想想，倘或你连累你妹子吃官司，对不对得起你父母？’”“啊！这一着厉害。”阿珠倒懂得那知府的用意，“就算五哥自己天不怕，地怕，总要顾到你。这一来，脾气无论如何要改改了。”“就是这话罗！所以我说知府大老爷一点不呆。”七姑奶奶又说，“等堂上下来，老太爷亲自来接我，接到他家，摆开了十桌酒席，帮里弟兄都到了，老太爷叫我坐首座。他说：阿七可惜是女的，如果是男的，我要收了‘他’才‘关山门’。”“七姐！”阿珠听得出了神， “我倒没有想到，你出过这么大的风头？”“唉！”七姑奶奶长叹一声：“就是那次风头出坏了。”

“Now that is something new!” A’zhu laughed. “He actually made you sign a bond?” “Yes, and put my handprint on it. Afterwards he summoned my fifth brother and said, ‘You must mend your ways. If you behave like this again, I shan't punish you. I shall punish the person who stood surety. Think about it: if you land your sister in prison, how can you face your parents?’” “Ah! That was a powerful move.” A’zhu understood the prefect's purpose. “Even if your brother feared neither heaven nor earth, he'd have to think of you. Whatever happened, he'd have to improve his temper.” “Exactly! That is why I say the prefect wasn't stupid at all.” The Seventh Lady continued, “When we left the court, the old master came to fetch me himself. At his house he had laid on ten tables of food, and all the brothers in the association were there. He made me take the seat of honour. ‘It's a pity A’qi is a woman,’ he said. ‘If she were a man, I would take her as my disciple before closing my doors to any more pupils.’” “Seventh Sister!” A’zhu was absorbed. “I never imagined you had made such a name for yourself.” “Ah!” The Seventh Lady gave a long sigh. “It was making that name that ruined things.”

“怎么呢？”阿珠诧异地问。是老于世故的，就不会觉得诧异。以七姑奶奶的性情，出了这样一回风头，自不免得意非凡，从此以后，也象男子汉一样，伸手管事，“吃讲茶”常有她一份。豪情胜概，自然会把女孩儿家的温柔、消折殆尽。“女人总是女人。”七姑奶奶不胜悔怨地说：“女人不象女人，要女人做啥？象我这样子，弄到头来，吃亏的是自己。”这句话说得极深。七姑奶奶以过来人的资格，才有此“见道之言”。阿珠既警惕，又感动。警惕的是女人争强好胜，使得男人敬神而远之，实在欠聪明。感动的是七姑奶奶的这些话，真正是肺腑之言，对旁人是决不肯说的。“七姐！”阿珠也还报以真情，“你不说，我不敢说，你既然说了，我倒要劝你。你不开口坐在那里，真正是一尊观音菩萨，一开口就比申大娘娘还要厉害。如果申大娘娘不是雌老虎，申大爷不会迷上那几个‘师太’，一条命也不会送掉。我劝你，也要象五哥一样，把脾气好好改一改。““我何尝不想改？”七姑奶奶摇摇头，不说下去了。这是说改不掉？阿珠在想，改不掉就不会有男人敢要她。真的守一辈子寡？想守出一座贞节牌坊来？她疑心七姑奶奶守不住。但这话说出来会得罪人，所以几次想开口，终于还是忍住了。

“How?” A’zhu asked in surprise. Someone more experienced in the world would not have been surprised. Given the Seventh Lady's temperament, such a success was bound to make her exceedingly proud. From then on, she intervened in affairs like a man and often took part in the gatherings at tea houses where disputes were settled. Her boldness and high spirits gradually wore away the gentleness expected of a young woman. “A woman is still a woman,” she said regretfully. “If she doesn't behave like one, what is the use of being a woman? In the end, someone like me is the one who suffers.” There was deep meaning in this. Only experience had brought the Seventh Lady such insight. A’zhu felt both warned and moved. It was foolish, she thought, for a woman to be so fiercely competitive that men kept a respectful distance. Yet she was moved that the Seventh Lady should speak from her heart as she would never do to others. “Seventh Sister, I wouldn't have dared say it if you hadn't. But now you have, I must offer some advice. When you sit without speaking, you look just like the Goddess of Mercy. Once you open your mouth, you're more formidable than Madam Shen. If Madam Shen hadn't been such a tigress, Master Shen would never have become infatuated with those nuns and lost his life. I think you should do as your fifth brother did and try to change your temper.” “Do you suppose I haven't wanted to?” The Seventh Lady shook her head and said no more. Did she mean she could not change? A’zhu wondered. If she could not, no man would dare marry her. Would she truly remain a widow all her life, hoping to earn a memorial arch for chastity? A’zhu doubted that she could endure it. But saying so would offend her. Several times she was about to speak; each time she held back.

“我问你，”七姑奶奶突如其来地说：“你看阿龙这个人怎么样？”“又要提到他了。”阿珠想拦住她，因而持意装出不悦的神情，“你为啥这么关心他？”七姑奶奶笑了，略带些忸怩的神色，这样的神色，阿珠几乎还是第一次看见，在她的印象中，七姑奶奶从不知什么难为情，因而这一丝忸怩之色，便特别引人注意。阿珠想起她平日对陈世龙的殷勤，深悔失言，自己的这句话，可能在七姑奶奶听来刺耳。正想有所弥补时，七姑奶奶说出一番令人大吃一惊的话来：“不错，我关心他。老实跟你说了吧，我也想过好几回，要么不嫁，要嫁，现成有在那里！”“现成有在那里”的，自然是陈世龙。话说得如此赤裸裸，阿珠简直不能相信自己的耳朵，回忆一遍，并未听错。这一来，心里的滋味，便不好受了，脸上的神色，也不好看了，勉强笑着问了声：“你是说哪个？陈世龙？”“是啊，陈世龙。”七姑奶奶看了看她的脸色，又问，“你看我嫁他配不配？”

“Tell me,” the Seventh Lady asked abruptly, “what do you think of A’long?” “Back to him again!” Hoping to stop her, A’zhu deliberately looked displeased. “Why are you so interested in him?” The Seventh Lady smiled with a trace of shyness. A’zhu could hardly remember seeing such an expression on her before. In her experience, the woman never knew embarrassment, so even this hint of it was striking. Recalling the attention she usually paid Chen, A’zhu regretted her question. It might have sounded offensive. Just as she was trying to make amends, the Seventh Lady said something astonishing. “You're right. I am interested in him. I'll tell you honestly: I've thought several times that, if I ever marry again, there's someone ready to hand.” The man ready to hand was, of course, Chen Shilong. So blunt a declaration seemed incredible. A’zhu went over it in her mind, but she had heard correctly. Her feelings became unpleasant, and so did her expression. Forcing a smile, she asked, “Who do you mean? Chen Shilong?” “Yes, Chen Shilong.” The Seventh Lady studied her face. “Do you think he and I would make a suitable match?”

真正脸皮厚，居然问得出来！阿珠心想：你不怕难为情，我就胡胡你的调。因而点点头说：“配！怎么不配？”“你倒说说看，我跟他怎么样的相配？”“这话就奇怪了。”阿珠依然是很勉强的笑容，“怎么样的相配，你自己总想过，何用来问我？”“我跟你开开玩笑的。”七姑奶奶在她脸上轻轻拧了一把，“我怎么会跟他相配？第一，年纪不对，第二，身分不配，他没讨过亲，要娶自然娶个黄花闺女，第三，脾气不配，他的性子也是好胜的，两个人在一起，他不让我，我不让他，非天天吵架不可。”阿珠不知怎么，颇有如释重负之感，但因为她言语闪烁，一会儿象熬有介事，一会儿又说“开玩笑”，所以大起戒心，不敢轻易答话，只微笑着作出不甚关心的样子，同时很仔细地观察她的脸色。“你说，我的话对不对？”“也不见得对！”阿珠很谨慎地回答，反过来试探她：“七姐，陈世龙娶了你，也有很多好处。象你这样的人才，打了灯笼都没处去寻的，又漂亮，又能干，而且还有五哥的照应。再好都没有了。”“真的？”七姑奶奶有意相问。语气中听得出来，有说她作违心之论的意味在内。阿珠有些发窘，但不容不答，更不容改口，硬着头皮答道：“自然是真的。”

What nerve, to ask such a question! A’zhu thought that, if the Seventh Lady felt no embarrassment, she might as well humour her. She nodded. “Certainly. Why wouldn't you?” “Then tell me what makes us suitable.” “That's a strange question.” A’zhu's smile was still forced. “You must have considered that yourself. Why ask me?” “I'm only teasing you.” The Seventh Lady gently pinched her cheek. “How could we be suitable? First, our ages are wrong. Second, our circumstances don't match. He's never married. Naturally, he'll want a maiden. Third, our temperaments don't suit each other. He likes to have his own way too. If we lived together, he wouldn't yield to me and I wouldn't yield to him. We'd quarrel every day.” A’zhu felt unaccountably relieved. Yet the Seventh Lady's shifting words—serious one moment, a joke the next—made her wary. She dared not answer readily and merely smiled as though little concerned, while carefully studying the woman's expression. “Am I right?” “Not necessarily,” A’zhu replied cautiously, now testing her in turn. “There would be plenty of advantages for Chen if he married you. You could search with a lantern and not find another woman like you: pretty, capable, and with Brother Five to support you. He couldn't do better.” “Really?” The Seventh Lady asked with deliberate emphasis. Her tone suggested that A’zhu did not mean what she said. Embarrassed, A’zhu nevertheless had to answer and could not retract her words. She braced herself. “Of course.”

七姑奶奶笑一笑不答。随后又说：“话再拉回来，你看阿龙这个人怎么样？”第二次再问，如果依旧避而不答，便显得“有心”了。阿珠想了想说：“我跟他认识的日子也不久，只晓得他人很能干的。”“心呢？”七姑奶奶问，“你看他的心好不好？”“我看不出来。”阿珠说：“有道人心难测。”“别人的心思难测，阿龙的心，你总晓得的。”“又来说疯话了！”阿珠一半害羞、一半赌气，翻个身脸朝里，以背向人。过了一会，没有动静，她当七姑奶奶有些动气了，想回过身来敷衍两句，但外床的人比她快了一步，已经起身下床。“嗨！”她提高了声音喊，“你到哪里去？”

The Seventh Lady smiled without replying. Then she returned to her question. “But tell me, what do you think of A’long?” Asked a second time, A’zhu could not evade it again without revealing that she had something to conceal. After some thought, she said, “I haven't known him long. All I know is that he's very capable.” “And his heart? Do you think he has a good heart?” “I can't tell. As they say, the human heart is hard to fathom.” “Other people's hearts may be hard to fathom. Surely you know A’long's.” “There you go talking nonsense again!” Half embarrassed and half annoyed, A’zhu turned towards the wall, presenting her back. For a while there was no response. Thinking the Seventh Lady had taken offence, she meant to turn back and say something conciliatory. But the woman beside her moved first and got out of bed. “Hey!” A’zhu called. “Where are you going?”

“哪里也不去。”七姑奶奶吹灭灯，仍旧回到床上。她过分亲昵的举动让阿珠感到不自在。阿珠轻声抗议，要她让开一些，她才稍稍松开。“现在你用不着怕难为情了，”她说，“有话尽管讲。”“我没有什么话好讲。”七姑奶奶仍把话引向陈世龙，要阿珠想一想自己对他的感情。一再的逗弄使阿珠越发不好意思。“真不得了，从没有遇见过你这样的人！”七姑奶奶说，想象一下自己盼望的幸福又有什么要紧。阿珠回答，越想只怕越盼望。“这倒是真的。”七姑奶奶承认，却仍想从阿珠的陪伴中得到些安慰。

“Nowhere.” The Seventh Lady blew out the lamp and returned to bed. Her excessive familiarity made A’zhu uneasy. “Give me some room,” A’zhu protested softly, and the Seventh Lady eased back a little. “Now you needn't be embarrassed,” she said. “Say whatever you like.” “I have nothing to say.” The Seventh Lady kept steering the conversation towards Chen and urging A’zhu to consider her feelings for him. The persistent teasing only deepened her embarrassment. “Really! I've never met anyone like you!” The Seventh Lady suggested that there could be no harm in imagining the happiness one wanted. A’zhu answered that imagining it might only make the longing worse. “That's true,” the Seventh Lady admitted, though she continued to seek comfort in A’zhu's company.

阿珠不肯顺着她一再的要求。七姑奶奶随后吐露，自己心里想的是死去的丈夫。阿珠很意外，也生出不忍，便表示体谅，又拿明天谁来服侍谁、谁替谁洗脚开了个玩笑，想使气氛轻松些。“你正好说反了，从前是我们那口子服侍我洗脚。”“我不相信！男子汉大丈夫，做这种没体面的事，真正气数！”“你不懂。夫妻相处有许多意想不到的习惯，将来等你嫁了阿龙就知道了。”又是阿龙！阿珠不作声，争辩也无用，而且觉得越争辩似乎越认真，不如随她说去。她对夫妻间这些意想不到的相处方式感到好奇，却问不出口，只希望七姑奶奶自己说下去。七姑奶奶没有猜到她的心思，见她不响，自己也不开口，沉在自己的回忆里，渐渐困倦，一觉睡到天亮。

A’zhu resisted her insistence. The Seventh Lady then confided that she was thinking of her dead husband. This admission surprised A’zhu and softened her. She responded sympathetically, then tried to lighten the mood with a joke about being waited on and having her feet washed the next day. “You've got it the wrong way round,” the Seventh Lady answered. “My husband used to wash my feet.” “I don't believe it! A grown man doing such an undignified thing! What a sorry state of affairs.” “You don't understand. Married couples have all sorts of unexpected ways. You'll know when you marry A’long.” A’long again! A’zhu remained silent. Arguing would achieve nothing and might even make her seem too concerned. Better to let the woman say what she pleased. She was curious about these unexpected ways of married life, but could not bring herself to ask and hoped the Seventh Lady would explain without prompting. The Seventh Lady did not guess what she was thinking. Since A’zhu said nothing, she too fell silent. Absorbed in her own memories, she grew drowsy and slept until morning.

是阿珠先惊醒，只听见有人叫门：“阿七，阿七！”是尤五嫂的声音：“张家妹子！你醒醒！”“来了！”阿珠听得尤嫂的声音有异，急忙推醒七姑奶奶：“你听，五嫂在叫你，好象出了什么事似地。”七姑奶奶定定神，一骨碌下床，拔开门闩，只见尤五嫂的脸色有些惊惶。“怎么搞的！都叫不醒。”尤五嫂一脚跨进门来，拉住七姑奶奶的手，连摇撼：“小刀会造反，上海昨天失守了。”“喔！”七姑奶奶回身看了看阿珠，“不要把她吓一跳！到我房里去说。”这句话反而说坏了，阿珠的耳朵尖，已经听得清清楚楚，急急赶过来问道：“七姐，出了什么事？”“你慌啥？”七姑奶奶很沉着地指着她嫂子说：“我也是刚听她说，说上海失守了！”

A’zhu woke first to someone calling at the door. “A’qi! A’qi!” It was Mrs You. “Young Zhang sister, wake up!” “Coming!” Something unusual in her voice alarmed A’zhu. She hurriedly woke the Seventh Lady. “Listen, Fifth Sister-in-Law is calling you. It sounds as though something has happened.” Collecting herself, the Seventh Lady sprang from bed and unbolted the door. Mrs You stood outside looking frightened. “What's the matter with you? I couldn't wake either of you!” She stepped inside, seized the Seventh Lady's hand, and shook it repeatedly. “The Small Swords Society has risen. Shanghai fell yesterday.” “Oh!” The Seventh Lady glanced back at A’zhu. “Don't frighten her. Come to my room and tell me.” That only made matters worse. A’zhu's hearing was sharp, and she had already caught every word. Hurrying over, she asked, “Seventh Sister, what's happened?” “Why panic?” Calmly, the Seventh Lady pointed to her sister-in-law. “I've only just heard it from her myself. She says Shanghai has fallen.”

阿珠何能不慌？小刀会要起事的消息，事先她毫无所闻，只想到上海失守，她父亲便要陷在里面，还有陈世龙，还有胡雪岩，都是有关系的人，如今一起都有危险，因而急得快要哭了。“你怎么想不穿！”这些时候，就看出七姑奶奶的“本事”来了，说出话来，明白有力：“我五哥也在上海，难道我倒不急？”想想不错，尤五嫂似乎也不怎么着急，可见得事情不要紧，再想到尤五的手面，越发心宽。当然，关切还是关切，不过看她们姑嫂有正事要谈，只得暂时忍耐，回头再来打听。尤五嫂没有工夫来管她，拉着七姑奶奶的手说：“你快去穿衣服。嘉定有人来了，你去跟他见个面。”听她这一说，七姑奶奶拉着尤五嫂就走，到了她自己房里匆匆漱洗，拢一拢头发，穿裙着衫，走来走会地忙着。尤五嫂便跟来跟去，把嘉定来客的话，告诉了她。

How could A’zhu not panic? She had heard nothing beforehand about the Small Swords Society's intended rising. All she could think was that, with Shanghai lost, her father would be trapped there. Chen Shilong too, and Hu Xueyan—all of them mattered to her, and now all were in danger together. She was almost in tears. “Why can't you think it through?” At such moments, the Seventh Lady's ability showed itself. Her words were clear and forceful. “My fifth brother is in Shanghai too. Do you suppose I don't care?” On reflection, that was true. Mrs You did not seem excessively anxious either, so perhaps things were not very serious. Remembering You Laowu's influence and connections reassured A’zhu further. Naturally, she remained concerned. But the two women had urgent business to discuss, and she could only be patient for the moment and ask more later. Mrs You had no time to attend to her. Taking the Seventh Lady's hand, she said, “Quickly, go and dress. Someone has come from Jiading. You must see him.” At once the Seventh Lady drew her sister-in-law away to her own room, where she hurriedly washed, smoothed her hair, and put on her skirt and blouse, moving busily back and forth. Mrs You followed her about, repeating what the visitor from Jiading had said.

第十三章｜CHAPTER THIRTEEN

这个不速之客是嘉定的周立春派来的。周立春与刘丽川有联系，所以上海一起事，周立春预备在嘉定响应，事先曾经跟尤五接头，希望“有福同享，有难同当”，尤五不愿这浑水，但也不便得罪他们，所以一直采取敷衍的态度。但以前可以敷衍，此刻到了真刀真枪要上场的时候，那就敷衍不过去了。“我来跟他说。”七姑奶奶小声诅咒着，话又难听了：“他娘的！只有强奸，没有逼赌！造反又不是去吃花酒，还有啥硬拉牢了一起走的？”“你又来了！”尤五嫂又气又急，“求求你，姑奶奶！你要跟他去吵架，还是不要去的好。”“唉！五嫂，你又看得我那样子草包了！我不过在这里发发牢骚，见了面，人家总是客人，我无缘无故得罪他做什么？”七姑奶奶推着她说：“你先去应酬应酬，要特别客气，不要冷落人家。”“不要紧。我开了早饭，请他在吃酒。”尤五嫂说：“人家是连夜赶来的。”“那么，你看他吃好了，请他在五哥的那间房子里见面。”

The unexpected visitor had been sent by Zhou Lichun of Jiading. Zhou was in touch with Liu Lichuan and intended to rise in Jiading as soon as the uprising began in Shanghai. He had approached You Laowu beforehand, proposing that they “share good fortune and face hardship together.” You had no desire to enter these troubled waters, yet could not afford to offend them, so he had always put them off with agreeable words. That had been possible before. Now that the time had come for real swords and spears, agreeable words were no longer enough. “I shall speak to him,” the Seventh Lady said, swearing under her breath in her usual coarse fashion. “Damn it! There is such a thing as forced sex, but not forced gambling. Rebellion is not an evening with singing girls. How can they drag someone along against his will?” “There you go again!” Mrs You was both angry and anxious. “Please, my dear lady! If you mean to quarrel with him, you had better not go.” “Oh, Fifth Sister-in-Law, you still take me for such a fool! I am only grumbling here. Once we meet, he is a guest. Why should I offend him without cause?” She urged Mrs You towards the door. “Go and attend to him first. Be especially courteous; do not leave him feeling neglected.” “There is no need to worry. I have had breakfast served, and he is drinking some wine. He travelled all night to get here.” “Then, when he has finished, ask him to meet me in Brother Five’s room.”

尤五有间密室，看是孤零零一座院落，四外隔绝，其实有地道与外间相通。七姑奶奶为怕走漏风声，特意约在那里相会。那个人是周立春的本家兄弟，排行第六，七姑奶奶也认识，但谈这些事，非另有凭信不可，因而一见面，她先这样问说：“周六哥，你要寻我五哥有啥话说呢？”周六略略踌躇了一下答道：“七姑奶奶，立春有几句机密话……”“慢点！周六哥，”她拦着他说，“既然是周大哥的机密话，你总晓得规矩？”“喔，我倒忘记掉了。”周六歉意的笑着，伸手到腰上去掏摸。他掏摸出来一块汉玉，送到七姑奶奶手里，这是信物。周立春因为造反是要杀头的机密大事，往来接洽，不便形诸笔墨，而派人传话，却又口说无凭，便与尤五作了个约定，用这块汉玉作为凭证。无此信物，守口如瓶，七姑奶奶知道有这样一个约定，所以首先就要查问。验明无误，她把汉玉交了回去，接着便说：“周六哥，你晓得我们这里情形的，你有话跟我说也一样。”

You had a private meeting room in what appeared to be an isolated courtyard, cut off on every side, though in fact a tunnel connected it with the outside. Fearing that word might leak out, the Seventh Lady deliberately chose this place for their conversation. The visitor was a clansman of Zhou Lichun’s, sixth in his generation, and she knew him too. But for business of this kind, personal acquaintance was not enough; credentials were required. As soon as they met, she asked, “Brother Zhou Liu, what is it you wish to discuss with Brother Five?” Zhou Liu hesitated. “Seventh Lady, Lichun has a few confidential words...” “A moment, Brother Zhou Liu.” She stopped him. “If they are Brother Zhou Lichun’s confidential words, you know the rule?” “Ah, I had forgotten.” With an apologetic smile, he reached into his waistband and produced a piece of Han-dynasty jade. This was his credential. Planning rebellion was a secret matter that could cost a man his head, so Zhou Lichun could not commit their dealings to writing. Yet a messenger’s unsupported word was no proof. He and You had therefore agreed that this jade would authenticate any message. Without it, lips must remain sealed. The Seventh Lady knew the arrangement and had asked for it at once. Having verified the piece, she returned it. “Brother Zhou Liu, you know how things are managed here. You may speak to me just as you would to my brother.”

“是，是！我们也晓得七姑奶奶女中丈夫，令兄凡遇大事，都要跟你商量。”周六说到这里，不放心似的望外面看了一下，然后把声音放得极低：“上海方面的情形，七姑奶奶想必已有消息？”“我也是刚刚听说，详细情形还不晓得。”“上海已经成功了。刘大哥事情很顺手，以后还要顺手。苏州的绿营兵，湖州人居多，跟刘大哥是同乡，已经约定，就要起事。”周六顿了一下，很吃力地说：“立春也就要在这两三夭动手，以前跟尤五哥谈过，尤五答应到时候一定帮忙。我今天来，就是来谈这件事。”“喔，”七姑奶奶从从容容地答道：“你们谈过这件事，我是晓得的，不过我没有听我五哥说过一定帮忙的话。”这一下就谈不下去了，周六愣住在那里，一脸懊丧之色。

“Yes, yes. We know that the Seventh Lady has the mettle of a man and that your brother consults you in every important affair.” Zhou Liu glanced uneasily outside, then lowered his voice almost to a whisper. “You have heard the news from Shanghai, I suppose?” “Only just. I do not yet know the details.” “Shanghai has succeeded. Everything has gone smoothly for Brother Liu, and it will go more smoothly still. Most of the Green Standard soldiers at Suzhou are from Huzhou, his own home district. They have already agreed to rise. Lichun intends to act within the next two or three days.” Zhou paused, then continued with some difficulty. “He discussed it with Brother Five You before, and You promised to help when the time came. That is what I have come about.” “I know you discussed the matter,” she answered without haste. “But I never heard Brother Five promise that he would certainly help.” There was no obvious way to continue after that. Zhou sat dumbfounded, his face full of disappointment.

“周六哥，我五哥最讲义气，为朋友上刀山、下油锅，他都肯的。是不是？”“是啊！”周六连连点头，“就为此，立春才来请尤五哥帮忙的，大家‘有福同享，有难同当’。”“实不相瞒，我五哥眼前就是难关。”七姑奶奶正好接住他的话，“如果是前一两年，我五哥有啥推辞是孙子王八蛋，眼前真正叫有心无力。为啥呢？为来为去为的是，不晓得哪个赃官想出来的，断命的‘海运’呀！”“海运？”周六问道：“是说漕米改海运？”“是啊，漕米改了海运，挑沙船帮发财！走关东的沙船，本来一向是装了压舱石头到北边的，现在改装漕米，平白里赚一笔水脚银子，运到天津不出事，还有啥‘保举’，沙船帮老大也做官了，气数不气数！”七姑奶奶咽了口唾沫，接下去又说：“沙船帮交贼运，我们漕帮要没饭吃了。松江是疲帮，你也晓得的，我五哥当这个家，真正是黄连当饭，苦头吃足。转眼重阳节边，西北风起，漕帮弟兄的夹衣裳都还在当铺里，我五哥不能不想办法。现在陪了个‘空子’到上海去做丝生意了，多少想掏摸几个，贴补贴补。周六哥你倒想想，我五哥在江湖上的身份，倘不是穷极无奈，怎么肯去服侍一个空子？这样子泥菩萨过江，自身难保的时候，怎么帮得上周大哥的忙？“

“Brother Zhou Liu, no one values loyalty more than my brother. For a friend, he would climb a mountain of blades or plunge into boiling oil. Would he not?” “Indeed!” Zhou nodded repeatedly. “That is why Lichun asked for his help. We should share good fortune and face hardship together.” “To tell you the truth, my brother is facing hardship himself at this very moment.” She seized the opening. “A year or two ago, if he had made excuses, he would have been a contemptible bastard. Now he truly has the will but not the means. Why? It all comes back to that damned sea transport, dreamed up by some corrupt official!” “Sea transport? You mean sending the grain tax by sea?” “Exactly. It fattens the purse of the Sand-Boat Guild. Their vessels used to sail north towards Manchuria carrying nothing but stone ballast. Now they carry tax rice instead and earn freight money for what was once an empty voyage. If they reach Tianjin without mishap, there are recommendations for official rewards as well. Even the guild leaders are becoming officials. Is that not enough to make one furious?” She swallowed and continued. “The sand-boat men are enjoying their cursed good fortune, while our Grain Transport Brotherhood is losing its livelihood. You know Songjiang is one of the impoverished branches. Keeping this household of men going has been like eating bitter coptis root instead of rice for my brother—nothing but hardship. The Double Ninth Festival will soon be here, and the northwest winds will rise, yet the brothers’ lined coats are still in the pawnshops. He has to find some means of helping them. At present he has gone to Shanghai with an outsider to trade in silk, hoping to scrape together something to fill the gaps. Think of his standing in our world, Brother Zhou Liu! Would he attend on an outsider unless poverty left him no choice? He is like a clay Buddha crossing a river, unable even to save himself. How can he help Brother Zhou Lichun?”

一番话说得周六哑口无言，好半天才说了句：“既然如此，尤五哥为啥又说，到时候一定帮忙。”“这就是我五哥的为人。你现在跟他去说，他还是会答应帮忙。不过这个忙，照我看，是越帮越忙。”“噢！”周六深为诧异，“这是啥道理？”“啥道理？吃饭的道理。”七姑奶奶答得极其爽脆，“漕米为啥改为海运，说运河水浅，有时候漕船不通，这好想办法，时世一乱，漕船走不过去，那才是死路一条。帮里的弟兄，对‘长毛’都摇头，现在再要他们跟周大哥一起走，表面不说，心里另有打算。万一做出啥对不起人的事来，我五哥一定压不住。这不是越帮越忙吗？”周六听她这一说，打了个寒噤。果然要松江漕帮协同起事，说不定洋枪到手，枪口朝里，那岂是儿戏之事？

Zhou was left speechless. After a long pause, he managed to ask, “Then why did he promise to help when the time came?” “That is the sort of man he is. Ask him now, and he will still promise. But in my opinion, the more he helped, the more trouble he would cause.” “Oh?” Zhou was astonished. “Why should that be?” “Because men have to eat.” Her answer was crisp. “Why was the grain tax diverted to the sea? They say the canal is too shallow and the grain boats sometimes cannot pass. One can find a remedy for that. But if disorder makes the route impassable, that is a complete dead end. The brothers already shake their heads at the Longhairs. Ask them to follow Brother Zhou Lichun now, and they may say nothing openly while thinking something quite different. If they did something disloyal, my brother could certainly not hold them down. Would his help not make matters worse?” Zhou shuddered. If the Songjiang brotherhood joined the rising and, once it had foreign guns in its hands, turned them on its supposed allies, that would be no laughing matter.

不过，仔细想一想也不对。俗称“通草”的“通漕”，周六也见过，上面记着，陆祖命翁、钱、潘三祖下山行道，行的就是“反清复明”的道，陆祖说的两首偈子，第一首中的“前人世界后人收”，就指的是光复大明江山，第二首中“日月巍巍照玉壶”，日月合成“明”字，“壶”字谐音“胡”，指的是清，也有反清复明的意思在内。那么，现在起事反清，漕帮弟兄何能倒戈？他是想到就是，而七姑奶奶报以轻蔑说：“周六哥，这些道理不晓得是啥辰光留下来的？‘皇帝不差饿兵’，饭都没得吃了，现在想大明江山，不好笑？”再说下去，依然无用。这一趟完全白来。周六想了想，只好这样说：“那么，七姑奶奶，我今天这番话，算是没有说，你也当作不曾听见过好了。”这话她懂，“尽管请放心！我哪里会做这种半吊子的事？如果周六哥，你今天跟我说的话，漏一个字到外面，你尽管来寻我们兄妹说话。”她接下来又极诚恳地说：“周六哥，害你白来一趟，我心里真正过意不去。不过事情明摆在那里，实在力不从心。请你回去跟周大哥说，这一次真对不起他，别处有用得着我们的地方，尽管吩咐。话再说回来，我们也有请周大哥照应的时候，‘行得春风有夏雨’，只要力量够得到，帮朋友就是帮自己。”

On reflection, however, the argument did not seem right to him. Zhou had seen the brotherhood’s canonical text, the Tongcao, whose title was colloquially written with the similar-sounding character for “grass” in place of “grain transport.” It recorded how Patriarch Lu sent the three patriarchs Weng, Qian, and Pan down from the mountain to spread the Way—the Way of overthrowing the Qing and restoring the Ming. Of the two verses spoken by Lu, the first contained the line “The later generation shall recover the world of those before,” referring to the recovery of the Ming realm. In the second, “Sun and moon shine high upon the jade vessel,” the written characters for sun and moon combined to make Ming, while the word for vessel, hu, sounded like the word for the northern peoples and referred to the Qing. That too implied overthrowing the Qing and restoring the Ming. How, then, could the brotherhood turn against a rising directed against the Qing? He voiced his thoughts, only to receive a scornful reply. “Brother Zhou Liu, who knows how long ago those doctrines were handed down? Even an emperor cannot send hungry soldiers to fight. With no food to eat, is it not ridiculous to dream of the Ming realm now?” There was no point in pursuing the matter. His journey had been wasted. After thinking for a moment, Zhou said, “Then let us regard everything I have said today as unsaid, Seventh Lady. You may treat it as something you never heard.” She understood. “Set your mind at rest. I would never be such a bungler. If a single word of what you have told me escapes, come and call my brother and me to account.” She continued with great sincerity. “I truly regret that you have made this journey for nothing. But the situation is plain: we cannot do what we would wish. Please tell Brother Zhou Lichun that we are sorry to fail him this time. If there is anything else in which we can be useful, he has only to ask. We too may need his protection one day. Send a spring breeze, and summer rain will follow. As long as it is within our power, helping a friend is helping ourselves.”

周六暗暗点头，都说这位七姑奶奶办事跟男子汉一样，果然名不虚传。这几句话还有打招呼的意思在内，事情不成，朋友要交，索性买买她的帐。“这就是七姑奶奶的话了！尽管请放心！嘉定过来青浦，青浦过来松江，过几天到了贵宝地，有‘老太爷’在，决不敢惊动的！”“周六哥，你这句话值钱了。我替松江老百姓，谢谢你！”说着，她学男人的样子，抱拳作了个揖。总算不伤和气，把周六送出后门，七姑奶奶心里不免得意，笑嘻嘻地回到后面，尤五嫂迎着她问道：“怎么说法？”“没事了！”她守着给周六的诺言，“详细情形也不必说，总而言之一句话，五哥的麻烦，我统统把它扫干净了！”

Zhou nodded inwardly. People said that the Seventh Lady conducted affairs as capably as any man, and her reputation was justified. Her last words also carried an appeal. Even if the business had failed, the friendship should be maintained; he might as well show her the consideration she sought. “Since that is what you say, Seventh Lady, you may be entirely reassured. From Jiading one comes to Qingpu, and from Qingpu to Songjiang. If we reach your district in a few days, with the Old Master here, we would never presume to cause a disturbance.” “Brother Zhou Liu, those words are worth something. I thank you on behalf of the people of Songjiang.” She clasped her hands and bowed in the manner of a man. Harmony had at least been preserved. After seeing Zhou out through the back door, she could not help feeling pleased with herself and returned to the rear quarters smiling. Mrs You came to meet her. “What was said?” “It is all settled.” She kept her promise to Zhou. “There is no need to go into the details. In a word, I have swept away every one of Brother Five’s difficulties.”

“真正亏得你！”尤五嫂极欣慰他，“实在也要谢谢胡老板，不是他来，你五哥不会到上海去。叫他自己来应付，还不如你出面来得好。”“这话倒是真的。”七姑奶奶想了想说，“五嫂，我今天要到上海去一趟。”“应该去一趟。”尤五嫂说，“就怕路上不好走。”“怕什么？”七姑奶奶毫不在乎的，“他们闹事是在陆路上，我们坐船去，根本就碰不见，碰见也不要紧，凭我还会怕他们？”“那好，你就赶快去一趟，叫你五哥在那里躲一躲，省得那班‘神道’又来找麻烦。”“我晓得。我去收拾东西，五嫂，你关照他们，马上替我备船。”

“We are fortunate to have you!” Mrs You was deeply relieved. “We should thank Mr Hu too. Without him, your brother would never have gone to Shanghai. You have handled this better than he could have done himself.” “That is true.” After considering, the Seventh Lady said, “Fifth Sister-in-Law, I must go to Shanghai today.” “You ought to. I only fear the journey may be difficult.” “What is there to fear?” She was unconcerned. “They are making trouble on land. We shall go by boat and never encounter them. Even if we did, would I be afraid?” “Then go as soon as you can. Tell Brother Five to stay out of the way there for a while, so that those troublemakers do not come looking for him again.” “I understand. I shall pack. Please have a boat made ready at once.”

于是七姑奶奶回到自己卧室，匆匆收拾随身衣物，正在手忙脚乱的当儿，阿珠悄悄的走了进来，有所央告。“七姐！”她用耍赖的神态说道：“我不管，你一定要带我一起走。”“咦！”七姑奶奶有些诧异：“我又不是去玩儿。”“我也不是去玩儿。我要去看我爹，不然不放心。”“话是不错，走起来有难处，路上不平靖。”七姑奶奶郑重其事地说，“你想想看，造反的人，哪个不是无法无天？遇见了，不是好玩儿的。”“我不怕！”阿珠豁出去了，“大不了一条命。”“他不要你的命，要你的身子。”听这句话，阿珠不能不怕，愣了一会说：“那么你呢？”“我不要紧，跟他们‘滚钉板’，滚过明白。”七姑奶奶又说，“我再告诉你，我学过拳头，象阿龙这样的，三、五个人，我一样把他们‘摆平’！”说完，她拿起墙角的一枝青皮甘蔗，右掌平平的削过去，也不见她如何用力，甘蔗却已断成两截。这一说一试，效用恰好相反，阿珠对她本就信赖，现在看她“露了一手”，益发放心，轻松地笑道：“我有个女镖客保镖，还伯什么？我跟你走定了！我也会收拾东西。“

She returned to her bedroom and hurriedly gathered the clothes she would need. While she was busy, A’zhu slipped in with a request. “Seventh Sister, I do not care what you say—you must take me with you.” “Eh?” The Seventh Lady was surprised. “I am not going for an outing.” “Neither am I. I want to see Father. Otherwise I cannot feel easy.” “That is understandable, but the journey is difficult. The roads are unsettled.” She spoke gravely. “Think of it: what rebel has any respect for law or restraint? Meeting them would be no joke.” “I am not afraid!” A’zhu declared recklessly. “At worst, I have only one life to lose.” “They may spare your life and assault you instead.” That frightened her. After a pause, she asked, “What about you?” “I shall be all right. I can face them and settle things directly. Besides, I have trained in martial arts. Three or five fellows like A’long would be no match for me.” Taking a green sugar cane from the corner, she struck it with the edge of her right palm. She seemed to use scarcely any force, yet the cane broke in two. Her explanation and demonstration had exactly the opposite effect from the one intended. A’zhu already trusted her. Now, seeing this display of skill, she felt safer still. “With a woman bodyguard to protect me, what have I to fear?” she said lightly. “I am definitely coming. I shall pack too.”

“慢点，慢点。”七姑奶奶一把拖住她，想了又想，无奈点头：“你一定要去，我就依你。不过，说实话，象你这样人又漂亮，年纪又轻的人，我带了你走，责任很重。你要听我的话做，不然……”“听，听！”阿珠抢着表示态度：“不管你怎么说，我都听。”“那么，”七姑奶奶说，“你也不是没有在江湖上走过的，总晓得女人有女人的笨法子。你有没有粗布衬裤？”阿珠也听人说过这种“笨法子”，很愿意试一试，但是，“精布裤子倒没有。“她说。“那就多穿两条。”阿珠依言而行，穿了三条衬裤，两件紧身小马甲，到了七姑奶奶那里，关紧房门，拿针线把裤腰裤脚和小马甲的前襟，缝得死死地。这样子，遭到强暴，对方就很难得逞了。

“A moment, a moment.” The Seventh Lady caught her and thought it over again. Finally, with a helpless nod, she yielded. “If you insist, I shall take you. But frankly, bringing someone as young and pretty as you places a heavy responsibility on me. You must do as I say, or else...” “I will, I will!” A’zhu interrupted eagerly. “Whatever you say, I shall do.” “Then you have travelled enough to know that women have their own crude precautions. Have you any undertrousers of coarse cloth?” A’zhu had heard of this precaution and was quite willing to try it, but she had no coarse-cloth pair. “Then wear several pairs.” She obeyed, putting on three pairs of undertrousers and two close-fitting little waistcoats. Back in the Seventh Lady’s room, with the door firmly shut, they sewed the waistbands, trouser cuffs, and waistcoat fronts securely shut. The intention was to make it difficult for an attacker to get through the clothing.

到了饭后，正预备下船，突然来了个意想不到的人，是陈世龙，一身泥泞、十分狼狈，但精神抖擞，脸上充满了经历艰险，安然到达目标的快慰。这一到，立刻为尤家的人所包围，都要听他从上海带来的消息。七姑奶奶和阿珠也就停了下来，先听他了，再定行止。“你是怎么来的？”尤五嫂急急问道，“我们的人都好的吧？”“都好，都好！”陈世龙大声答道：“都住在夷场，安稳得很。”有这句话，大家都放心了，“那么，上海县城呢？”尤五嫂又问。“县城失守了。”陈世龙所了解的情形，相当完整，于是从头细说，“小刀会要起事，早有谣言了，坏在吴道台手里……”

After lunch, just as they were preparing to board, an unexpected visitor arrived: Chen Shilong. He was covered in mud and looked thoroughly bedraggled, but his spirits were high. His face showed the satisfaction of a man who had come through danger and reached his destination safely. The household immediately gathered around him, all eager for news of Shanghai. The Seventh Lady and A’zhu postponed their departure; they would hear what he had to say before deciding what to do. “How did you get here?” Mrs You asked urgently. “Our people are all well, I hope?” “All well, all well!” Chen answered loudly. “They are staying in the foreign settlement. Perfectly safe.” This reassured everyone. “And the county town?” she asked. “The town has fallen.” Chen had a fairly complete understanding of events and began at the beginning. “There had long been rumours that the Small Swords Society intended to rise. The trouble lay with Circuit Intendant Wu...”

吴道台是指苏松太兵备道吴健彰。他跟刘丽川是同乡旧识，而上海县的团练又多是广东、福建人，因此，吴健彰对于小刀会利用团练起事的流言，不以为意，在他的想法，小刀会起事，就是跟他过不去，有彼此的交情在，刘丽川不会做出什么对不起人的事来。谁知刘丽川已经跟太平天国的丞相罗大纲有联络，同时与英国领事温那治有所联系，决定于“丁祭”那天起事，先攻县衙门。上海县知县名叫袁祖惪，是袁子才的孙子，由捐班的宝山县丞，升任上海知县。这天一早整肃衣冠，预备坐轿到文庙去上祭，人刚走出大堂，拥进来一群红巾裹头的人，为头的叫小金子，曾经为袁祖惪把他当流氓抓来办过罪，仇人相见，分外眼红，雪亮一把刀立刻递到胸前。袁祖惪倒也是个硬汉，破口大骂，不屈而死，吴健彰得到消息，溜到了英国领事署，总算逃出一条命。于是道署、县署、海关，相继被袭。小刀会占据了小南门乔家滨、沙船帮巨擘郁馥山新起的大宅作据点。城内乱得很厉害，但“红巾”不敢入夷场一步，因此难民纷纷趋避，十里夷场反倒格外热闹了。

He meant Wu Jianzhang, the military intendant of the Suzhou-Songjiang-Taicang circuit. Wu and Liu Lichuan came from the same province and were old acquaintances. Moreover, many of the Shanghai county militia were men from Guangdong and Fujian. Wu therefore paid little attention to rumours that the Small Swords Society would use the militia to launch a rising. In his view, such a rising would be an act against him personally. Given their friendship, Liu would never do anything so disloyal. Yet Liu had already made contact with Luo Dagang, a chief minister of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, and with the British consul, Wen Nazhi. He decided to rise on the day of the Confucian sacrifice and attack the county yamen first. Shanghai’s magistrate was Yuan Zude, a grandson of Yuan Zicai. Having purchased office as deputy magistrate of Baoshan, he had risen to the Shanghai magistracy. Early that morning he dressed formally and prepared to take his sedan to the Confucian temple for the sacrifice. He had just emerged from the main hall when a band of men with red cloths wound around their heads burst in. Their leader, Little Jin, had once been arrested and punished by Yuan as a hooligan. At the sight of his old enemy, his anger blazed; a bright blade was thrust towards Yuan’s chest. Yuan was a man of courage. He cursed them bitterly and died without yielding. On hearing the news, Wu fled to the British consulate and escaped with his life. The circuit offices, county offices, and customs house were attacked in succession. The Small Swords men established themselves in a newly built mansion belonging to Yu Fushan, a magnate of the Sand-Boat Guild, at Qiaojiabin near the Little South Gate. The city was in great disorder, but the Red Turbans dared not set foot in the foreign settlement. Refugees poured there for safety, making its ten-li extent busier than ever.

“官兵呢？”七姑奶奶问道，“难道不打一打？”“官兵少得很，根本不敢打，带兵官是个守备，姓李，上吊死了。”“鸭屎臭！”七姑奶奶不屑地，“有得上吊，为啥不拚？”“不去管这些闲事了。”尤五嫂问，“你是怎么来的？”“我特地来送信，口信。”陈世龙看了看说，“可以不可以到里面去说？”这自是机密信息，引入内厅，陈世龙告诉尤五嫂说，尤五特地嘱咐，如果嘉定有人来，好好敷衍，千万不可得罪。“原来是这么一句话！”七姑奶奶问道，“怎么会叫你来的呢？”这话问得有理，尤五手下多的是人，传这样的信息，理当派自己人，何至于劳动来作客的陈世龙？

“What about the government troops?” the Seventh Lady asked. “Did they not even fight?” “There were very few of them. They did not dare fight at all. Their commander, a garrison officer surnamed Li, hanged himself.” “Duck dung!” she said contemptuously. “If he had the nerve to hang himself, why not fight?” “Let us leave these other people’s affairs alone,” Mrs You said. “How did you get here?” “I came specially with a message—a spoken message.” Chen looked around. “May we go inside to discuss it?” The information was plainly confidential. Once they had moved into the inner hall, he told Mrs You that You Laowu had particularly instructed them to deal courteously with anyone who came from Jiading and, above all, not to give offence. “So that is the message!” the Seventh Lady said. “Why did they send you?” It was a reasonable question. You had plenty of men of his own; a message of this kind should have been entrusted to one of them. Why trouble Chen, who was a guest?

“其中有个道理，”陈世龙道，“胡先生叫我把珠小姐送回湖州，顺便就要我带个口信。”“这……”七姑奶奶深感意外，“这是为啥？”“胡先生说兵荒马乱，还是回去的好。张老板也是这么说。”“这要问问她自己。”七姑奶奶忽然又说，“这样吧，我们已经约好一起到上海，船都备好了，你跟我们一起走，有啥话到上海再说。“

“There is a reason,” Chen explained. “Mr Hu asked me to take Miss Zhu back to Huzhou. As I was coming this way, I was to bring the message too.” “But...” The Seventh Lady was greatly surprised. “Why is that?” “Mr Hu says that with war and disorder everywhere, she would be better off at home. Mr Zhang says the same.” “We must ask her.” Then she suddenly added, “Here is what we shall do. We have already arranged to go to Shanghai together, and the boat is ready. Come with us. Whatever needs discussing can be discussed when we get there.”

“好的。啥时候走？”陈世龙看着身上说，“我一身烂污，总得先洗个澡。”等陈世龙到“混堂”里去洗澡的工夫，七姑奶奶才去找到因为他们要传机密口信而回避的阿珠，说了陈世龙此来的本意，以及她的决定，阿珠自然表示同意，但也不免奇怪，胡雪岩此刻正当用人之际，何以肯放陈世龙专程送她回湖州？七姑奶奶很快就看出，胡雪岩是在替陈世龙安排两人相处的机会。阿珠对自己的前途尚无着落，陈世龙又对她倾心，而且彼此已有些好感，漫长的旅程可能使两人的感情进一步发展。七姑奶奶却自觉比胡雪岩更了解他们，也有把握促成这桩婚事，因此自作主张，改变了他的安排。

“Very well. When do we leave?” Chen looked down at himself. “I am covered in mud. I must have a bath first.” While he was at the bathhouse, the Seventh Lady sought out A’zhu, who had withdrawn to let them discuss the confidential message. She explained the real purpose of Chen’s journey and her own decision. A’zhu naturally agreed, though she wondered why Hu, who must be badly in need of helpers just now, was willing to send Chen on a special journey to escort her home. The Seventh Lady was shrewd enough to understand at once that Hu was making an opportunity for Chen. A’zhu was uncertain of her future, Chen was deeply attached to her, and some affection had already grown between them. A long journey together might allow their feelings to develop further. Yet the Seventh Lady believed she understood the two better than Hu did and was confident that she could help bring about a suitable match. She therefore took it upon herself to change his arrangements.

* * *舟入吴淞江，顺风顺水，一夜工夫就到了上海。船不敢再泊小东门，在洋泾滨上岸，直接坐轿到了裕记丝栈。丝栈里乱得一团糟，连走廊上都打着地铺，全是县城里和浦东一带逃难来的，沾亲带故，半央求、半强占地住了下来。七姑奶奶也是第一次到这里来，一看这情形就喊了起来：“这里怎么住法？五哥他们住哪里？”不要吵，不要吵！有地方。“陈世龙引着她和阿珠，径自走到最后，另有道黑漆石库门，虚虚掩着，推开一看，别有天地，三开间一楼一底，堆满了丝包。“咦！阿珠。”阿珠抬头一看，是她父亲正开了楼窗在喊。“楼下堆丝，楼上住人。”陈世龙告诉七姑奶奶说：“上楼再说。”老张下楼把他们接到楼上，父女相见，因为有了一番变乱的缘故，所以多少有恍如隔世之感。坐定下来，七姑奶奶问道：“他们呢？”这是指尤五和胡雪岩。“洋人请他们吃番菜，谈生意，大概快要回来了。”老张又问她女儿，“我跟雪岩商量，叫世龙送你回湖州，你怎么跑到上海来了。”“是我的主意。”七姑奶奶抢着答道，“好在也方便得很，闲话少说，张老板，对不起你，请你楼下坐一坐，我们要房间用一用。”

Their boat entered the Wusong River and, favoured by both wind and current, reached Shanghai after a single night. They dared not moor at the Little East Gate this time. Landing at Yangjingbang, they took sedan chairs directly to the Yuji Silk Warehouse. The place was in chaos. Even the corridors were covered with makeshift bedding. Refugees from the county town and the Pudong area, all connected with the household by some tie of kinship or acquaintance, had half begged and half forced their way into lodging there. It was the Seventh Lady’s first visit too. At the sight of the crowd, she cried, “How can anyone live here? Where are Brother Five and the others?” “Do not worry. There is room.” Chen led the two women straight to the back, where another black-painted, stone-framed gate stood slightly ajar. Beyond it was quite a different world: a two-storey building three bays wide, stacked with bales of silk. “A’zhu!” She looked up and saw her father calling from an open upstairs window. “The silk is downstairs; the people sleep above,” Chen explained. “Let us go up first.” Zhang came down to meet them and led them upstairs. After the upheaval they had endured, father and daughter felt almost as though they were meeting in another lifetime. When they were seated, the Seventh Lady asked, “Where are they?” She meant You and Hu. “Some foreigners have invited them to a Western meal to discuss business. They should be back soon.” Zhang turned to his daughter. “Xueyan and I agreed that Shilong should take you to Huzhou. Why have you come to Shanghai instead?” “It was my idea,” the Seventh Lady answered quickly. “It was easy enough to arrange. But let us say no more for now. Mr Zhang, forgive me, but would you sit downstairs for a little while? We need to use the room.”

这话真说到了阿珠心里，自从用了那个“笨法子”，大不“方便”，她连茶都不敢多吃一口，急于解除束缚，轻松一下，所以帮着七姑奶奶催：“爹，你先请下去，快，快！”老张莫名其妙，但女人的事也不必多问，提着旱烟袋就走，陈世龙自然也要下楼，指一指左右说：“两间房都开着，随便你们用哪一间。”“阿龙，”七姑奶奶喊住了他，从来不晓得什么叫难为情的人，这时也不免有些忸怩，窘笑着说：“拜托你一件事，也不晓得他们这里有没有娘姨，大厨房在哪里？替我们提一桶热水来，好不好？”“怎么不好？”陈世龙也很机警，“胡先生房间有个新买的脚盆，你们用好了。”说着，“噔、噔、噔”一直下楼。“你看，”七姑奶奶低声对阿珠笑道：“阿龙替你提洗脚水去了！”阿珠无心理她的戏谑，匆匆奔进房去。七姑奶奶自然也跟着行动，两个人的手脚都很快，关紧门窗，相互帮忙，在黑头里摸索着，解除了束缚。不久，楼梯声响，是陈世龙提了水上楼，一壶热水、一桶凉水，交代明白，便待下楼。

This was exactly what A’zhu wanted. Since taking that “crude precaution,” she had found the restrictions most inconvenient and had scarcely dared drink any tea. She was eager to undo the fastenings and be comfortable again. “Father, please go down for a little while,” she urged. “Quickly!” Zhang was puzzled, but saw no need to inquire into women’s matters. He took his tobacco pipe and left. Chen naturally had to go too. Pointing to either side, he said, “Both rooms are open. Use whichever you please.” “A’long!” The Seventh Lady called him back. For once, even this woman who scarcely knew the meaning of embarrassment looked a little awkward. She smiled sheepishly. “May I trouble you with something? I do not know whether they have a maid here, or where the main kitchen is. Could you bring us a bucket of hot water?” “Of course.” Chen understood quickly. “There is a newly bought washbasin in Mr Hu’s room. You may use it.” He hurried downstairs. “Look,” the Seventh Lady whispered teasingly to A’zhu. “A’long has gone to fetch your washing water.” A’zhu had no attention to spare for jokes and hurried into the room. The Seventh Lady followed. Both worked quickly: they closed the doors and windows, helped each other in the darkness, and undid the protective stitching. Before long they heard Chen on the stairs, bringing a kettle of hot water and a bucket of cold. Having explained which was which, he prepared to go down again.

“阿龙慢一点！”七姑奶奶喊道：“黑咕隆咚的怎么办？要替我们拿盏灯来。”那间房正就是他跟老张的卧室，因而答道：“我桌上有洋蜡烛，还有包红头洋火，在我枕头下面。”“哪张床是你的？”“靠壁的那张。”陈世龙说“红头洋火，随便哪里一划就着，当心烧着手。”“晓得了！你不要走，我还有事情要你做。”

“A’long, wait!” the Seventh Lady called. “What are we to do in the dark? Bring us a light.” The room happened to be the one he shared with Old Zhang. “There is a foreign candle on my table and a packet of red-headed matches under my pillow,” he answered. “Which bed is yours?” “The one against the wall. The matches will light if you strike them anywhere. Be careful not to burn your hand.” “I understand. Do not go yet; there is something else I want you to do.”

七姑奶奶摸着洋火，取一根在地板上划亮。阿珠担心隔墙的缝隙让屋内失去隐私，立刻把火柴吹灭。七姑奶奶便问陈世龙在外面做什么。他说自己坐着等候，看她还有什么事要吩咐。她拿他守在外面打趣，又提醒他尊重她们的隐私。陈世龙笑笑没有回答，阿珠低声埋怨她不该特地提这件事，又请她别点蜡烛。陈世龙听见后，觉得还是守规矩要紧，便大声说没有事就先下楼。七姑奶奶也觉得应当让他回避，谢过他，并请他守着楼梯，别让旁人突然上来。有了他守候，两人可以放心。七姑奶奶到胡雪岩房里取来脚盆，提水进屋；两人洗漱后重新梳头、涂脂抹粉，换上干净衣服，才开门出来。

The Seventh Lady found the matches and struck one on the floor. A’zhu immediately blew it out, concerned that the gaps in the partition might compromise their privacy. The Seventh Lady called to Chen to ask what he was doing outside. “I am sitting here, waiting to see what else you need.” She teased him about lingering and told him to respect their privacy. He smiled without answering. A’zhu quietly reproached her for drawing attention to the matter and asked her not to light the candle. Chen heard this and decided that proper conduct mattered more than anything else. “If there is nothing more, I shall go downstairs,” he called. The Seventh Lady agreed that he should withdraw. “Thank you. Please watch the stairs and make sure nobody comes up unexpectedly.” With him guarding the staircase, they could feel secure. She fetched the washbasin from Hu’s room and brought in the water. After washing, they took out their grooming things, arranged their hair, put on their cosmetics, and changed into clean clothes. Only then did they open the door.

巧得很，正好裕记丝栈的老板娘，听说有“堂客”到了，带了一个粗做娘姨和一个丫头赶来。七姑奶奶是认得她的，招呼一声“陈太太”，接着便替阿珠引见。等娘姨在楼上替她们收拾了残局，宾主坐定寒暄，问了问路上的情形，陈太太邀她们到家去住。七姑奶奶怕拘束不肯去，转身跟阿珠商量，她也不愿住陈太太家，便以见了她父亲，马上就要回湖州，不必费事作推托。七姑奶奶也就设词力辞，陈太太只得由她们。坐了一会，邀客到她家吃晚饭，七姑奶奶答应等他们兄妹见过面，谈完正事再赴约。于是等陈太太一走，陈世龙动手替她们设榻，老张和他搬到楼下，在丝包旁边安设床位。原来的房间里一张大床，一张小床，七姑奶奶占大床，阿珠用小床，而这张小床，正就是陈世龙原来所睡的。

By coincidence, the proprietor’s wife had just heard that women guests had arrived and came over with a maid for heavy work and a younger maid. The Seventh Lady knew her and greeted her as Mrs Chen, then introduced A’zhu. While the older maid put their upstairs room in order, host and guests settled down to exchange courtesies and discuss the journey. Mrs Chen invited them to stay at her own house. The Seventh Lady feared the restrictions of being a guest and did not wish to go. When she consulted A’zhu, the girl agreed and offered the excuse that, having seen her father, she would soon return to Huzhou, so there was no need to make further arrangements. The Seventh Lady added her own polite refusals, and Mrs Chen had to accept them. After sitting a while, she invited them to dinner. The Seventh Lady agreed to come once she had seen her brother and finished their business. When Mrs Chen left, Chen Shilong arranged the beds for them. He and Old Zhang moved downstairs and made sleeping places beside the bales of silk. Their former room contained a large bed and a small one. The Seventh Lady took the large bed; A’zhu had the small one, which had previously been Chen’s.

刚刚安置停当，胡雪岩和尤五回到了裕记丝栈。时地相异，感觉不同，胡雪岩固然神态自若，阿珠也还显得从容。七姑奶奶略略道了决定到上海来的缘由，随即向尤五使个眼色，示意避人密谈，尤五因为跟胡雪岩已到了共机密的程序，所以顺手把他一拉，一起来听七姑奶奶的报告。“嘉定的人，昨天早晨来过了……”她把经过情形，细说了一遍。“这样应付也好！”尤五欣慰的。默默在一旁听着的胡雪岩，不曾想到七姑奶奶，如此能干，不免刮目相看。她发觉了他的眼色，心里觉得很舒服，便笑着问了句：“小爷叔，你看我说错了话没有？”“当然不错！”胡雪岩转脸对尤五说：“这下了掉一件心事，我们在上海可以好好动一动脑筋。”尤五先不答他的话，向他妹子低声叮嘱：“阿七，我一时不能回去，家里实在放不下心，趁这一两天，路上还不要紧，你赶紧回去吧！”

The arrangements had barely been completed when Hu and You returned to the depot. A different time and place produced different feelings: Hu was composed as ever, and A’zhu too seemed at ease. The Seventh Lady briefly explained why she had decided to come to Shanghai, then signalled to her brother that she wanted a private conversation. You now shared confidential matters with Hu and drew him along to hear her report. “The man from Jiading came yesterday morning...” She gave a detailed account. “That was a good way to handle it,” You said, relieved. Listening quietly, Hu had not expected the Seventh Lady to be so capable and regarded her with new respect. She noticed his look and was pleased. “Young Uncle,” she asked with a smile, “do you think I said anything wrong?” “Certainly not!” Hu turned to You. “That removes one worry. Now we can give proper thought to our affairs in Shanghai.” Before replying to him, You spoke quietly to his sister. “A’qi, I cannot return just yet, and I am anxious about things at home. The route should still be passable for a day or two. You had better go back at once.”

七姑奶奶点点头，问起他们在上海的情形：“ 生意怎么样？”这活在尤五就无从置答了，只是微微叹口气，见得不甚顺手。“生意蛮好！”胡雪岩却持乐观的态度，“正在谈，就要谈出结果来了。”事实上不容易谈得出结果，胡雪岩扳持不卖，洋行方面因为小刀会起事的关系，是在观望之中，所以最大的两项“洋庄”货色，茶和丝都变成有行无市，混沌一团。尤五因为生意方面不大在行，而局势甚乱，自不免悲观，因而才叹气不答。“阿七，”尤五又说，“你明天就回去吧！”

She nodded, then asked about their affairs in Shanghai. “How is business?” You had no ready answer. He merely sighed faintly, showing that matters were not going smoothly. Hu, however, remained optimistic. “Very good. We are negotiating and should have a result soon.” In fact, agreement would not be easy. Hu was holding firm and refusing to sell, while the foreign firms were waiting to see what would happen after the Small Swords uprising. Tea and silk, the two largest items in the export trade, still had quoted prices but scarcely any transactions; the whole market was in confusion. You knew little about commerce and, with the political situation so unsettled, naturally felt pessimistic. That was why he had sighed instead of answering. “A’qi,” he repeated, “go back tomorrow.”

“晓得了！”七姑奶奶不悦，“我会走的。不过张家妹子是我带到上海来的，总要把她作个交代。”“交代她爹就是了。”话是不错，但七姑奶奶一心要牵那条红线，巴不得当时就有个着落，这话又似乎不宜出口，因而沉默着。“七姐！”胡雪岩看出她的热心，安慰她说，“事情是一定会有个好好交代的，急也急不得。我想把她先送回湖州，叫世龙送了去，那也就算是有交代了。”“嗯，嗯。”七姑奶奶不置可否地，然后又说：“裕记老板娘，今天请我们一起去吃夜饭，也该走了。”“不行！”尤五摇头，“我们今天夜里约好一个要紧人在那里。你们去吧！”于是乍一相见，匆匆又别。尤五和胡雪岩不暇暖地，赶到一家“堂子”里去赴约会。

“I know!” the Seventh Lady replied with displeasure. “I shall go. But I brought our sister Zhang to Shanghai, and I must make some arrangement for her.” “Leave her in her father’s care.” That was reasonable, but the Seventh Lady was intent on tying the red thread of marriage and wanted a settlement at once. She could hardly say so openly and fell silent. Hu understood her enthusiasm. “Seventh Sister, there will certainly be a proper arrangement. It is no use hurrying. I mean to send her back to Huzhou with Shilong. That, too, would count as making provision for her.” “Mm, mm.” She committed herself to neither agreement nor disagreement. Then she said, “The proprietor’s wife has invited us all to dinner tonight. It is time to go.” “We cannot,” You replied, shaking his head. “We have arranged to meet an important man this evening. Go without us.” They had scarcely met before they parted again. Without even time to warm their seats, You and Hu hurried away to keep an appointment at a courtesan house.

第十四章｜CHAPTER FOURTEEN

要会的那个要紧人姓古，广东人，是个“通事”，结交的洋朋友极多，对英国人尤其熟悉，而在上海的英国人，自从洪秀全在江宁开国，便有许多花样。他们去会那姓古的，就是要打听这些花样。尤五在上海的路子也很广，辗转打听到，英国洋行已经跟洪军展开贸易。曾经有两只英国兵船，从上海开到下关。洪军起初以为是清军邀来助阵的，大起戒备。谁知英国人带了一名通事上岸，一开口就表明，此来特为通商。商品是枪械火药，以货易货。那家洋行，大获其利，而所带的通事，就是这个姓古的，名叫古应春。

The important man they were to meet was a Cantonese interpreter named Gu. He had many foreign friends and was particularly familiar with the British. Since Hong Xiuquan had established his kingdom at Jiangning, the British in Shanghai had been trying all manner of schemes. It was these schemes that Hu and You wanted to learn about. You Laowu had extensive connections in Shanghai, and through a succession of inquiries he had discovered that a British firm was already trading with Hong’s army. Two British warships had sailed from Shanghai to Xiaguan. At first the rebels had assumed that the Qing forces had invited them to help fight, and had taken elaborate precautions. But the British had brought an interpreter ashore, and his opening words made it clear that they had come expressly to trade. Their merchandise consisted of firearms and gunpowder, to be exchanged for other goods. The firm had made a handsome profit. The interpreter who had accompanied them was this very man, Gu Yingchun.

于是胡雪岩又有了新的主意，他跟尤五商量，最好能够跟古应春结交，在珍宝和枪械方面都有生意好做。尤五对胡雪岩已到了言听计从的地步，便设法托人，从中介绍，前一天已在吃花酒的场面上见过面，当时约定，这天是尤五回请，全班人马，一个不缺，其实主客只有一个古应春。设席的地点在宝善街怡情院。尤五是这家“长三堂子”的主政，怡情老二的恩客，所以连带胡雪宕亦有宾至如归之乐。到了那里，在“大房间”落座，刚刚卸去长衫，听“相帮”在喊客到，怡情老二亲自打开帘子，只见古应春步履轻快地踏上台阶了。“古大少，真真够交情。”怡情老二盈盈笑着，“第一个到。”“尤五哥请客不能不早点来。”古应春又说，“而且是在你这里请客，更不能不早到。”“这是我沾尤五少的光，谢谢，谢谢！”

This gave Hu Xueyan another idea. He told You that they ought to make Gu’s acquaintance: there would be business to do in both precious objects and arms. By now You followed Hu’s advice in everything. He arranged an introduction through a mutual acquaintance, and the previous day they had met over a banquet with courtesans. It had been agreed then that You would return the hospitality today, with the entire party invited again. In reality, there was only one guest who mattered: Gu Yingchun. The dinner was to be held at Yiqing House on Baoshan Street, an establishment of the prestigious changsan class. You was a favored patron of Yiqing’s Second Miss, the woman who ran the house, so Hu too enjoyed the pleasure of being received as one of the household. They had scarcely taken their seats in the main room and removed their long gowns when an attendant called out that a guest had arrived. Second Miss herself lifted the curtain, revealing Gu Yingchun coming briskly up the steps. “Young Master Gu, you really do honor your friends!” she said with a graceful smile. “The very first to arrive.” “When Brother You gives a dinner, I can hardly be late,” Gu replied. “And when he gives it at your house, I must certainly come early.” “Then I owe this honor to Fifth Master You. Thank you, thank you!”

“承情之至。”尤五也拱手致谢，接着向里一指，“要不要里头躺一会？”“我是过足了瘾来的。不过躺一会也可以。”一听这话，怡情老二便喊：“点灯！”接着把古应春的哔叽袍子接过来，引入里间。里间就是怡情老二的香闺，一色红木家具，却配了一张外国来的大铜床，雪白珠罗纱的帐子吊得高高地，床上已设着一副极精致的鸦片烟具。古应春略略客气了一下，先在上首躺下，对面的空位，尤五让胡雪岩，胡雪岩又让尤五，这是一番做作，胡雪岩是客，而且有话要问古应春，自然该他相陪。

“Much obliged,” You said, clasping his hands in thanks. Then he gestured toward the inner room. “Would you like to lie down for a while?” “I had my fill of opium before coming, but I wouldn’t mind lying down.” At this, Second Miss called, “Light the lamp!” She took Gu’s serge gown and led him inside. The inner room was her own bedchamber. Its furniture was all of rosewood, except for a large imported brass bed, whose snowy gauze curtains were drawn high. An exquisite set of opium implements had already been laid out on it. After a token show of reluctance, Gu reclined in the place of honor. You offered the opposite place to Hu, and Hu offered it back to You. These were formalities. Hu was the guest, and he had questions for Gu; naturally, he was the one to keep him company.

“香”过两筒烟，说过一番闲话，怡情老二要去招呼“台面”，尤五也另有客要陪，小屋间里便只剩下胡、古二人。胡雪岩已经看出，古应春也是个很“外场”的人物，不难对付，因而一上来便用请教的口气说：“应春兄，我总算运气不错，夷场上得有识途老马指点，以后要请你多多指教。”“不敢当。”古应春笑道，“尤五哥是我久已慕名的，他对你老兄特别推重，由此可见，足下必是个好朋友，我们以后要多亲近。”“是，是！四海之内皆弟兄，况且海禁已开，我们自己不亲近，更难对付洋人了。”“着！”古应春拿手指拍着烟盘，“雪岩兄，你这话真通达。说实在的、我们中国人，就是自己弄死自己，白白便宜洋人。”

After two pipefuls and some idle conversation, Second Miss went out to attend to the dinner, while You had other guests to entertain. Hu and Gu were left alone. Hu had already seen that Gu was a man well accustomed to society and would be easy to approach. He began in the tone of one seeking guidance. “Brother Yingchun, I count myself fortunate to have found an old hand to show me the way in the foreign settlement. I shall often have to ask your advice.” “You flatter me,” Gu said with a smile. “I have admired Brother You’s reputation for a long time. He speaks very highly of you, which tells me that you must be a friend worth having. We ought to see more of each other.” “Indeed! All men within the four seas are brothers. And now that the maritime prohibitions have been lifted, it will be harder still to deal with the foreigners unless we Chinese stick together.” “Exactly!” Gu tapped the opium tray with a finger. “Brother Xueyan, that is a thoroughly sensible remark. The truth is that we Chinese ruin one another and let the foreigners reap the benefit.”

这话就有意思了，胡雪岩心想，出言要谨慎，可以把他的话套出来。“现在新兴出来‘洋务’这两个字，官场上凡是漂亮人物，都会‘谈洋务’，最吃香的也是‘办洋务’，这些漂亮人物我见过不少，象应春兄你刚才这两句话，我却还是第一次听见。”“哼！”古应春冷笑着，对胡雪岩口中的“漂亮人物”，做了个鄙夷不屑的表情。“那些人是闭门造车谈洋务，一种是开口就是‘夷人’，把人家看做茹毛饮血的野人，再一种是听见‘洋人’二字，就恨不得先跪下来叫一声：”洋大人‘。这样子谈洋务、办洋务，无非自取其辱。““这话透彻得很。”胡雪岩把话绕回原来的话头上，“过与不及，就‘自己人弄死自己人’了。”“对了！”古应春拿烟签子在烟盘上比划着说：“恨洋人的，事事掣肘，怕洋人的，一味讨好，自己互相倾轧排挤，洋人脑筋快得很，有机可乘，决不会放过。这类人尤其可恶。”

There was something in that remark. Hu decided that, with a little care, he could draw Gu out. “These days everyone talks about ‘foreign affairs.’ All the fashionable figures in official circles discuss foreign affairs, and managing them is the most sought-after occupation of all. I have met plenty of those gentlemen, but this is the first time I have heard anyone say what you have just said.” “Hmph!” Gu gave a contemptuous smile at Hu’s mention of these fashionable figures. “They discuss foreign affairs shut up in their own rooms, knowing nothing of the world outside. One sort calls foreigners barbarians and treats them as savages who eat raw flesh and drink blood. The other can scarcely hear the word ‘foreigner’ without wanting to fall on his knees and cry, ‘Your Excellency!’ Discussing and managing foreign affairs in that spirit brings nothing but humiliation upon ourselves.” “You put it very clearly,” Hu said, steering the talk back to its original point. “Both extremes end in our own people ruining one another.” “Precisely!” Gu gestured over the tray with his opium pick. “Those who hate foreigners obstruct everything; those who fear them do nothing but curry favor. Meanwhile, we undermine and push out our own people. Foreigners are quick to see an opening, and they never let one slip. People of that sort are especially detestable.”

胡雪岩看他那愤慨的神情，知道他必是受过排挤，有感而发。“不遭人妒是庸才”，受倾轧排挤的人，大致能干的居多，看他说话，有条有理，见解亦颇深远，可以想见其人。于是胡雪岩心想，自己正缺少帮手，尤其是这方面的人才，倘或古应春能为己所用，岂不大妙？这个念头，几乎在他心里一出现，就已决定，但却不宜操之过急，想了想，他提出一个自信一定可以引起古应春兴趣的话题。“应春兄！”他矍然而起，从果碟子，抓了几粒杏仁放在嘴里大嚼，嘴唇动得起劲，说话便似乎格外显得有力，“我有点不大服气！我们自己人弄死自己人，叫洋人占了便宜，难道就不能自己人齐心一致，从洋人手里再把便宜占回来？”古应春听了他的话，只是翻眼，一要烟签子不断在烟盘戳着，好久，他说，“雪岩兄，从来没有人跟我说过这话。上次开了两条兵轮到下关去卖军火，价钱已经谈好，要成交了，有个王八蛋跑来见洋人，他会说洋文，直接告诉洋人，说洪军急需洋枪火药，多的是金银珠宝。说这句话，洋人翻悔了，重新议价，涨了一倍还不止。这就是洋人占的大便宜！我也一直不服气。能够把洋人的便宜占回来，哪怕我没有好处也干。于今照你所说，自己人要齐心一致，这句话要怎么样才能做到，我要请教。“

His indignation convinced Hu that he had himself been pushed aside and was speaking from experience. Only a mediocrity escaped envy; those who suffered from rivalry and exclusion were generally capable men. Gu spoke coherently, and his views showed considerable foresight. Hu felt that he could judge the man from his conversation. He was short of helpers, particularly of men with this kind of ability. How useful it would be to bring Gu into his service! The thought had scarcely occurred to him before he resolved to act on it, though he must not be too hasty. After a moment’s reflection, he raised a subject he felt certain would interest Gu. “Brother Yingchun!” He suddenly sat up, took a few almonds from a dish and chewed vigorously, which seemed to give his words added force. “There is something I cannot accept. If we ruin one another and let the foreigners gain at our expense, why can’t we unite and win the advantage back?” Gu looked up, poking repeatedly at the tray with his opium pick. At length he said, “Brother Xueyan, no one has ever said that to me before. The last time we took those two warships to Xiaguan to sell arms, the price had been settled and the bargain was almost concluded when a bastard who spoke their language came to see the foreigners. He told them directly that Hong’s army desperately needed guns and powder and had gold, silver and jewels in abundance. That was enough. The foreigners went back on their word, reopened negotiations and more than doubled the price. What a windfall they made! I have resented it ever since. If I could win that advantage back from them, I would do it even without a profit for myself. But you say our own people must unite. How are we to accomplish that? I should like your advice.”

“这话倒是把我问倒了。”胡雪岩说，“事情是要谈出来的，现在我还不大知道洋人的情形，说不出个所以然来。不过既说齐心一致，总要有个起头。譬如说，你、我，还有尤五哥，三个人在一起，至诚相见，遇事商量，哪个的主意好，照哪个的做，就象自己出的主意一样，这样子一步一步把人拉拢来，洋人不跟我们打交道则已，要打，就非听我们的话不可！”“好！”古应春也一仰身坐了起来：“三人同心、其利断金。就从你、我、尤五哥起头。我洋行里那个‘康白度’也不要做了。”洋行里管事的人叫“康白度”，是洋文的译音，地位又非仅仅负传译之责的通事可比。胡雪岩觉得他不须如此做法。“应春兄，”胡雪岩首先声明：“自己人说话，不妨老实。你洋行里的职位，仍旧要维持，不然跟洋人打交道不方便、而且这一来，洋人那里的消息也隔膜了。”古应春原是不假思索，想到就说的一句话，即使胡雪岩不点明，他回想一下，也会改变主意的。因而当然一迭连声的表示同意。

“Now you have put me on the spot,” Hu said. “Things have to be worked out through discussion. I know too little about the foreigners yet to offer a definite answer. Still, if we are to unite, we must make a beginning. Take you, me and Brother You: the three of us could deal with one another in complete sincerity and consult over everything. Whoever has the best idea, we follow it as readily as if it were our own. Then we bring more people together, step by step. The foreigners need not deal with us, but if they do, they will have to listen to us.” “Excellent!” Gu sat up too. “When three men are of one mind, their strength can cut through metal. Let it begin with you, me and Brother You. I’ll give up my job as comprador at the foreign firm.” Comprador was a foreign term for the man who managed a foreign firm’s business dealings. His position stood well above that of an interpreter responsible merely for translating. Hu saw no need for Gu to resign. “Brother Yingchun, between ourselves we should speak frankly. You ought to keep your position at the firm. Otherwise our dealings with foreigners would become inconvenient, and we would lose touch with what was happening among them.” Gu had spoken on impulse. Even without Hu’s reminder, a moment’s reflection would have made him change his mind. Naturally, he agreed at once and repeatedly.

“我在想，”胡雪岩踌躇满志的说，“你刚才所说的‘三人同心，其利断金’。这句话真正不假。我们三个人，各占一门，你是洋行方面，尤五哥是江湖上，我在官场中也还有点路子。这三方面一凑，有得混了！”古应春想一想，果然！受了胡雪岩的鼓舞，他也很起劲的说，“真的，巧得很！这三方面要凑在一起，说实在的，真还不大容易。我们明天好好谈一谈，想些也众不同的花样出来，大大做它一番市面。“因为有此契合，这顿花酒，吃得十分痛快，尤五的手面很大，请的客又都是场面上人，每人都叫了两三个局，莺莺燕燕，此去彼来，弦管嗷嘈，热闹非凡。吃到九点多钟，又有人“翻台”，一直闹到子夜过后，才回裕记丝栈。七姑奶奶和阿珠都已累了一天，早早入梦，老张是一向早睡早起，只有陈世龙一个人，泡了一壶好茶在等他们。

“I was thinking,” Hu said with satisfaction, “how true your saying is about three men of one mind cutting through metal. Each of us has his own field: you have the foreign firms, Brother You the brotherhood world, and I have a few connections in official circles. Put those three together and we ought to get somewhere!” Gu considered this and saw that it was so. Encouraged by Hu, he replied enthusiastically, “Indeed! What a fortunate combination. Bringing those three fields together is no easy matter. Let’s have a proper talk tomorrow, think of something different from everyone else and do some business on a grand scale.” Their understanding made the evening’s entertainment especially enjoyable. You was a generous host, and his guests were all men of the world. Each summoned two or three courtesans; the women came and went amid a clamor of strings and pipes. After nine, someone ordered another round of entertainment, and the festivities continued past midnight. When Hu and You returned to Yuji Silk Warehouse, the Seventh Lady and A’zhu, tired by the day’s events, were already asleep. Old Zhang always went to bed and rose early. Only Chen Shilong was waiting, with a pot of good tea ready for them.

“五哥，你困不困？”胡雪岩兴致勃勃的问。“不困。”尤五问道：“你有啥事情要谈？”“事情很多。”胡雪岩转脸说道：“世龙，你也一起听听，我今天替你找了个读洋文的先生。”这一说，尤五立即明白：“你是说古应春！你们谈得怎么样？”“谈得再好都没有了……”胡雪岩把他跟古应春在烟榻上的那一席对话，源源本本地说了给尤五听。尤五比较深沉，喜怒不大形于颜色，但就算如此，也可以发现他眉目轩豁，这几天来阴沉沉的脸色，似乎悄然消失了。“你的脑筋快，”他用徐缓而郑重的声音说，“倒想想看，跟他有什么事可以做联手的。”

“Brother You, are you sleepy?” Hu asked eagerly. “Not at all. What do you want to talk about?” “A great many things.” Hu turned to Chen. “Shilong, you should listen too. I found you a teacher of the foreigners’ language today.” You understood at once. “You mean Gu Yingchun! How did your talk go?” “It couldn’t have gone better.” Hu recounted their conversation on the opium couch from beginning to end. You was a reserved man who seldom showed his feelings, but even so, his features visibly brightened. The gloom of the past few days seemed quietly to have lifted. “You have a quick mind,” he said slowly and earnestly. “Think what sort of business we could do together with him.”

“眼前就有一样，不过……”胡雪岩的尾音拖得很长。“咦！”尤五诧异了，“有啥为难的话，说不出口？”“我不晓得你跟卯金刀，到底有没有交情？”“卯金刀”是指刘丽川，尤五当然明白，很快地答了句：“谈不上。”“我这么在想，英国人反正做生意，枪炮可以卖给太平军，当然也可以卖给官军。今天我在席面上听说，两江总督和江苏巡抚，郡为了卯金刀在伤脑筋，奏报出去，轻描淡写，好象是地方上闹事，其实是想多派兵，一仗把他打倒。既然如此，枪炮、火药是要紧的，我们好不好先替他们办个‘粮台’，等他们的兵一到，就好出队打仗。如果你认为这个办法可以，我马上到苏州去跑一趟，江苏巡抚许乃钊是我们杭州人，一定可以找得到路子见一见他。”

“There is one opportunity before us already, only…” Hu let the last word linger. “Why, what is so difficult that you can’t say it?” You asked in surprise. “I don’t know whether you have any friendship with ‘Mao, Metal and Knife.’” This was a coded way of writing the surname Liu and referred to Liu Lichuan. You understood immediately. “Nothing worth mentioning.” “Here is what I was thinking. The British are in business, after all. If they can sell guns and cannon to the Taiping forces, they can surely sell them to the government army. I heard at dinner that both the governor-general of Liangjiang and the governor of Jiangsu are worrying over Liu. Their reports play the affair down as a local disturbance, but in reality they mean to send in a large force and crush him in one battle. In that case, guns and powder will be essential. Could we establish a supply office for them in advance, so that when their troops arrive they can go straight into action? If you approve, I’ll go to Suzhou at once. Governor Xu Naizhao of Jiangsu is a fellow Hangzhou man. I can certainly find a way to see him.”

“主意倒是不错。不过我不能做。”“是因为‘圈吉’的关系？”胡雪岩问。“圈吉”周，是指周立春，尤五点点头说，“一点不错，不过你跟他没有交情，你可以做。”“那就算了。第一，要做，就是大家一起来，第二，人家也晓得我跟你的交情，如果你觉得有妨碍，我做了一样也有妨碍。”尤五听得这话，大感快慰，他心里是巴不得胡雪岩不要做，但“光棍不断财路”，明明是笔好生意，自己不能叫他罢手，所以那样言不由衷地说“你可以做”。

“The idea is good enough. But I can’t take part.” “Because of ‘Ji in a Box’?” Hu asked. The character ji enclosed in a frame made the surname Zhou: he meant Zhou Lichun. You nodded. “Exactly.
