But you have no ties to him. You could do it.” “Then let it drop. First, whatever we do, we do together. Second, people know how close we are. If it would put you in a difficult position, my doing it would cause the same difficulty.” You was deeply relieved to hear this. In his heart he had wanted Hu to abandon the scheme, but a man of the brotherhood did not cut off another man’s livelihood. It was plainly a profitable venture; he could not ask Hu to give it up. That was why he had said, against his own wishes, “You could do it.”

“我还有第二条路子，浙江现在正在办团练，湖州由一位姓赵，名叫赵景贤的绅士出面，此人极其通达能干，跟王雪公的公谊私交都不错，我一说就可以成功。”“那好！这笔军火生意，我们一起来做。”“就有一样麻烦，要尤五哥你有办法才能成功。”胡雪岩说，“英国人的兵船开不到湖州，只能在上海交货，上海运到湖州，路上怕有危险。抢掉了怎么办？”“危险也不过上海到嘉兴这一段，一进浙江境界，有官兵护送，哪个敢抢？至于这一段路，归我保险。”尤五又说，“反正我们漕帮弟兄现在都空在那里，要人要船都现成。借此让他们赚一笔水脚，事情再好都没有了。”“这一说，在我们两个人就算定局了。说做就做，你倒再想想看，你那面还有什么事要我做到的？”尤五仔细想了想说，“你请浙江方面，替我们这里的督粮道来封公事，说要用松江漕帮的船运军火。这样，我对官面上就算有了交代。”

“There is another course,” Hu continued. “Zhejiang is organizing militia forces. In Huzhou, a gentleman named Zhao Jingxian has taken the lead. He is an exceptionally capable, broad-minded man, and is on good terms with Prefect Wang both publicly and privately. A word from me should settle it.” “Good! Let’s undertake that arms business together.” “There is just one difficulty, and it will depend on you to solve it. British warships cannot reach Huzhou, so delivery would have to be made in Shanghai. The journey from Shanghai to Huzhou might be dangerous. What if the cargo were seized?” “The only dangerous stretch is between Shanghai and Jiaxing. Once it enters Zhejiang, government troops can escort it. Who would dare attack it then? As for the first stretch, I’ll guarantee its safety. Our grain-transport brothers are all idle now, with men and boats ready to hand. Giving them a chance to earn some freight money would be the best possible arrangement.” “Then as far as the two of us are concerned, it is settled. Let’s get on with it. Think again: is there anything else you need me to arrange?” You considered carefully. “Have the Zhejiang authorities send an official letter to our grain transport circuit intendant here, saying that they wish to use the Songjiang grain boats to carry arms. That will put my dealings with the authorities in order.”

“这一定办得到。”胡雪岩转脸对陈世龙说，“又要你辛苦跑一趟了。”“到杭州，还是到湖州？”“先到杭州。如果王大老爷已经回任，你就再到湖州，寻着他算数。不错，”胡雪岩忽然又说，“你正好把阿珠送了回去。”“好的。啥时候走？”“最多两三天，等我在这里接好头，写了信，马上就走。”

“That can certainly be done.” Hu turned to Chen. “I’m afraid I must send you on another journey.” “To Hangzhou or Huzhou?” “Hangzhou first. If Prefect Wang has already returned to his post, go on to Huzhou. You must find him wherever he is. And of course,” Hu added suddenly, “you can take A’zhu home at the same time.” “Very well. When do I leave?” “Within two or three days at most. As soon as I’ve made the arrangements here and written the letter.”

接头是跟古应春接头。第二天在怡情老二的香闺中，三个人又见了面，胡雪岩说了经过，问古应春，英国人肯不肯将枪炮、火药卖给这方面？“有啥不肯？他们是做生意，只要价钱谈得拢，什么都卖。”古应春问道，“你要些什么东西，我好去谈。”这下把胡雪岩难倒了，“这上面我一窍不通。”他说，“只要东西好就好。”“不光是东西好坏，还有数目多少。总要有个约数，才好去谈，譬如洋枪，应该多少支？”“总要一千支。”“一千支！”古应春笑道，“你当一千支是小数目？我看办团练，有五百支洋枪就蛮好了。还有，要不要请教习？洋枪不是人人会放的，不会用，容易坏，坏了怎么修，都要事先盘算过。”“应春兄，”胡雪岩拱拱手说，“你比我内行得太多了。索性你来弄个‘ 说帖’，岂不爽快？”

The arrangements were to be made with Gu Yingchun. The next day the three met again in Second Miss’s bedchamber at Yiqing House. Hu explained what they had discussed and asked whether the British would sell guns, cannon and powder to their side. “Why wouldn’t they? They are businessmen. If the price is right, they will sell anything. Tell me what you want, and I can negotiate.” This stumped Hu. “I know nothing about such things. So long as the goods are good, that is enough.” “Quality isn’t the only consideration. There is quantity too. I must have approximate figures before I can negotiate. How many foreign guns, for instance?” “A thousand, surely.” “A thousand!” Gu laughed. “Do you imagine that is a small number? Five hundred foreign guns would be quite a good supply for a militia force. And will you need instructors? Not everyone knows how to fire them. In inexperienced hands they are easily damaged. How will you repair them? All this must be considered beforehand.” Hu clasped his hands. “Brother Yingchun, you know far more about it than I do. Why don’t you draw up a memorandum yourself? That would settle everything.”

古应春慨然应诺，而且立刻功手。怡情老二亲自照料，移过“叫条子”用的笔砚来，磨浓了墨，却无纸可写，好在是草稿，不妨拿“局票”翻过来，将就着用。于是古应春一面提笔构思，一面过鸦片烟瘾，烟泡装上烟枪，枪嘴上接根橡皮管子，一直通到他嘴里。十六筒烟抽完，精神十足，文不加点，洋洋洒洒地写完，递到了胡雪岩手里。胡雪岩自己不能动笔，看却会看，不但会看，而且目光锐利，象这些“说帖”，最要紧的是简洁，要几句话就能把那些大官儿说动心，才是上品。古应春的笔下很来得，但流畅有余，不免枝蔓，他把洋枪、火药的好处，源源本本谈起，好虽好，看来却有些吃力。胡雪岩心想，这个说帖，王有龄、赵景贤一定会看完，但递到黄宗汉手中，他有没有看完的耐心，就难说了。

Gu readily agreed and began at once. Second Miss personally brought over the brush and inkstone used to write invitations to courtesans and ground a rich supply of ink. There was no blank paper, but since this was only a draft, the backs of the invitation slips would serve. Gu composed with his brush while indulging his opium habit. The prepared pellets were put into the pipe, with a rubber tube attached to the mouthpiece and reaching his lips. After sixteen pipefuls, he was in excellent spirits. His prose flowed freely, without a correction, and he handed the finished draft to Hu. Hu could not compose such a document himself, but he could read it—and judge it shrewdly. A memorandum of this kind had above all to be concise. The best would move a high official with a few sentences. Gu wrote fluently, but fluency had carried him into unnecessary elaboration. He explained the merits of foreign guns and gunpowder from their beginnings. The exposition was good, but somewhat laborious to read. Wang Youling and Zhao Jingxian would certainly finish it, Hu thought. Whether Huang Zonghan would have the patience was another question.

“高明之至！”胡雪岩先声色不动地把说帖递给尤五。“我不必看了。”尤五笑道，“看也是白看。”“雪岩兄，”古应春接口问道：“我是急就章，有不妥的地方你尽管说。”“好极了！不过，应春兄，对外行不好说内行话，说了，人家也不懂。我看，前面这一段，有些地方要割爱。““我懂！”古应春点点头，“现在谈洋务，都是些闭门造车，自说自话蒙人的玩意。那些谈枪、炮怎么样制造的道理，说句实话，也真没有几个人懂，我可以把它删节。删归删、添归添，你看，哪里还可以多说两句？““很好了。还有些地方不说也可以。”这显然是客气话，古应春便说：“我这个人做事，不做则已，一做一定要把它做好，何况是自己人，尽请直言。”“既如此，我说出来请你斟酌，第一，说道光年间，‘英、法犯我，不幸丧师，症结所在，厥为刀矛不敌火器’，这句话一针见血，不过还可以着力说两句。”“对！我自己也有这么个想法。”

“Excellent!” Hu said, keeping his expression unchanged as he passed the memorandum to You. “There’s no need for me to read it,” You said with a laugh. “I wouldn’t get anything out of it.” “Brother Xueyan,” Gu put in, “this was written in haste. If anything is unsuitable, please say so.” “It is very good. Only, Brother Yingchun, you cannot talk to outsiders in the language of an expert. They won’t understand. I think you may have to sacrifice some of the opening section.” “I understand.” Gu nodded. “So much talk of foreign affairs nowadays consists of people shutting themselves away and spinning their own tales to deceive others. To be frank, very few understand the principles behind the manufacture of guns and cannon. I can shorten those passages. But cutting is one thing and adding another. Where might I usefully say more?” “It is very good already. There are still places where you could say less.” Recognizing this as politeness, Gu replied, “When I undertake something, I mean to do it properly. Besides, we are among friends. Please speak plainly.” “Then let me offer this for your consideration. First, you say, ‘During the Daoguang reign, Britain and France attacked us, and our forces suffered defeat; the essential cause was that swords and spears could not withstand firearms.’ That goes straight to the point, but it could be emphasized further.” “Yes! I had the same thought.”

“再有一层，应春兄，是不是可以加这么一段……”胡雪岩所建议增加的是，说英国人运到上海的洋枪、火药有限，卖了给官军，就没有货色再卖给洪军及各地其他人，所以这方面多买一支，那方面就少得一支，出入之间，要以双倍计算。换句话说，官军花一支枪的钱，等于买了两支枪。“你这个算法倒很精明，无奈不合实情。英国人的军械，来了一批又一批，源源不绝，不会有什么卖给这个，就不能再卖给那个的道理。”“是的。应春兄，这种情形，我清楚，你更清楚，不过做官的清楚，京里的皇上和军机大臣，更不会清楚。我们只要说得动听就是。”古应春看着尤五笑了，尤五的话，很爽直：“应春兄，这些花样，我的这位小爷叔最在行，你听他的，包定不错。”“好！”古应春说，“我都懂了。如果没有别的话，我今天带回去，改好誊正，再连洋行里的估价单，一起开来交给你。”

“There is another point, Brother Yingchun. Could you add a passage along these lines?” Hu proposed saying that the supply of British guns and powder arriving in Shanghai was limited. What was sold to government forces would no longer be available to Hong’s army or other parties elsewhere. Every additional gun bought by the government would therefore mean one fewer in hostile hands, a difference that should count double. In other words, the government would obtain the benefit of two guns for the price of one. “That is a clever calculation,” Gu said, “but unfortunately it does not fit the facts. British arms arrive in one shipment after another, without interruption. Selling to one customer does not prevent them from selling to another.” “Of course. I know that, and you know it better still. But officials do not, and the emperor and the grand councillors in Beijing know even less. All we need is an argument they will like to hear.” Gu looked at You and smiled. You spoke bluntly. “Brother Yingchun, my young uncle here is an expert at these devices. Follow his advice and you won’t go wrong.” “Very well,” Gu said. “I understand. If there is nothing else, I will take this home today, revise it and make a fair copy. I’ll bring it back with a quotation from the firm.”

“慢来！”尤五插嘴问道：“估价单怎么开法？”“照例是二人回扣。”古应春答道：“如果要‘戴帽子’，我亦可以去说。”听他的口气，显然不主张浮报价款的“戴帽子”。胡雪岩也觉得一方面不能叫洋人看不起，另一方面对浙江官方要建立信用，不宜在两成回扣以外，另出花样。“对！”尤五很诚恳地接受，“我原是怕你们疏忽，提一句。既然都曾想过，那就怎么样都是不错的了。”

“Wait a moment,” You interrupted. “How will the quotation be drawn up?” “The usual arrangement is a twenty-percent rebate,” Gu answered. “If you want the price padded, I can discuss that too.” His tone made it plain that he did not favor inflating the quoted price. Hu agreed. They must avoid earning the foreigners’ contempt, and they needed to establish their credit with the Zhejiang authorities. They ought not to invent further devices beyond the twenty-percent rebate. “Quite right,” You said sincerely. “I only mentioned it in case you had overlooked the matter. Since you have considered it, whatever you decide will be all right.”

“不过，”古应春接下来问：“除了洋枪，还有大炮，要不要劝浙江买？”“这慢一点。浙江有个姓龚的，会造炮……”姓龚的福建人，名叫龚振麟，曾经做过嘉兴县的县丞，道光末年就在浙江主持“炮局”。从明朝中叶以来，一直在仿制的“红衣大将军炮”，都用生铁翻砂，龚振麟却发明了铸炮铁模，著成《图说》，还著了一本《枢机炮架新式图说》，在铸炮技术上，颇有改良。他的儿子名叫龚之棠，能得父传。父子二人、都很得浙江大吏的重用。“当然，打‘群子’的土造大炮，不及西洋的‘落地开花大炮’，但这话不能说！一说，炮局里的人当我们要敲他的饭碗，一定鸡蛋里挑骨头，多方挑剔，结果是连洋枪都不卖。”“雪岩兄，”古应春既感慨又佩服地，“你真正人情熟透，官场里的毛病，被你说尽了。”“官场、商场都一样！总而言之，‘同行相妒’，彼此能够不妒，什么事都可以成功！”

“But besides guns,” Gu continued, “there are cannon. Should we urge Zhejiang to buy those too?” “Let that wait. There is a man named Gong in Zhejiang who makes cannon.” Gong Zhenlin was a native of Fujian and had once served as deputy magistrate of Jiaxing. By the closing years of the Daoguang reign, he was directing Zhejiang’s cannon works. Since the middle of the Ming dynasty, the so-called Red-Robed General cannon had been copied by casting iron in sand molds. Gong had devised iron molds for casting cannon and had written an illustrated account of them. He had also written an Illustrated Account of a New Pivoted Gun Carriage, making significant improvements in cannon-making technology. His son, Gong Zhitang, had learned his craft from him. Both father and son were highly valued by Zhejiang’s senior officials. “Naturally, our locally made cannon firing clusters of shot cannot match the Western guns with shells that burst on impact. But we mustn’t say so! The men at the cannon works would think we were trying to take away their livelihood. They would find fault with everything, and we might end up unable to conclude even the purchase of guns.” “Brother Xueyan,” Gu said with mingled admiration and feeling, “you understand human affairs thoroughly. You have laid bare all the faults of official life.” “Business and official life are alike in that respect. People in the same trade envy one another. If only they could put envy aside, anything could be accomplished.”

古应春和尤五，都认为他这句话说得好，因此感情亦特别融洽。在怡情院中，浅斟低酌，谈了许多开展的计划，一直到午夜散席，约定第二天下午，仍旧在原处见面。古应春走了，尤五宿在怡情老二那里，因为还有事要谈，所以胡雪岩就在怡情院“借干铺”。尤五要谈的是，他这天中午，和胡雪岩分手以后，到怡情院重新见面以前，所得来的一个消息。听说，刘丽川跟英国人联系上了。夷场四周，英国人预备建筑围墙、不让官军进驻，也不准官军借道，但是英国人却预备开放陈家木桥，让刘丽川能够获得军火和粮食的接济。“照这样子，上海一年半载，不会光复。我们的丝生意，是不是做得下去？现在先要作个打算。”

Both Gu and You thought this well said, and their feelings toward one another grew warmer still. Over leisurely drinks at Yiqing House they discussed many plans for expanding their business. It was midnight before they parted, agreeing to meet there again the following afternoon. Gu left, while You stayed with Second Miss. Since there was more to discuss, Hu borrowed a bed at the house without engaging a companion. You had news acquired between their parting at noon and their meeting again at Yiqing House. Liu Lichuan had reportedly established contact with the British. The British intended to build a wall around the foreign settlement and allow neither government troops to be stationed inside nor government forces to pass through. Yet they planned to open Chenjia Wooden Bridge so that Liu could receive supplies of arms and food. “If that is so, Shanghai won’t be recovered for another six months or a year. Can we carry on our silk business? We had better consider it now.”

“这倒要好好想一想。”胡雪岩提出疑问，“上海的关税，是两江的命脉，总不会一直让英国人张牙舞爪，一定有对付的办法。”“这也听说了。”尤五答道，“两江总督怡大人怊良，因为洋人助逆，早就预备禁止内地跟夷场通商。来源一断，我们在上海还有什么发展？”“这话分两方面来说，来源一断，货价必高，对我们有利，没有货色，货价再高也无用，对我们无利。”胡雪岩说，“生意还是可以照常做，只要对我们不利的这方面，能够避掉。”“怎么避呢？就是避不掉！”有个办怯，就是走私。以尤五在水路上的势力。呼应灵活，走私亦非难事，但犯法的勾当，胡雪岩不敢做，而且目前事事顺利，也犯不着去干犯法的勾当。就这一转念间，他把到口的话，缩了回去。“小爷叔，我想只有这么样，”尤五自己提出了一个办法：“尽量调动现款，就在上海收货，囤一段时间脱手。另外除了军火以外，有啥生意好做，我们再商量。顶好是我们漕帮弟兄能够一起出力的事，一则大家有口苦饭吃，二则也免得游手好闲去闯祸。”胡雪岩听出尤五的话中，对漕帮生计日窘，情有隐忧，既成知己，休戚相关，应该替他分优，于是问起松江漕帮的困难，看有什么办法好想？这一谈就谈得深了，直到天色微明。方始归寝。

“We must think carefully,” Hu said. “Shanghai’s customs revenue is the lifeblood of Liangjiang. They cannot let the British have their own way indefinitely. There must be a way of dealing with them.” “I have heard something about that too,” You replied. “Governor-General Yiliang has long been preparing to prohibit trade between the interior and the foreign settlement because the foreigners are helping the rebels. Once supplies are cut off, what prospects will we have in Shanghai?” “There are two sides to that. Cutting off supplies will raise prices, which helps us. But without goods, even the highest prices are useless to us. We can carry on business as usual if we can avoid the disadvantageous side.” “How can we avoid it? We can’t!” There was one way: smuggling. With You’s influence over the waterways and his responsive network, it would not be difficult. But Hu did not dare undertake something illegal. Everything was going well at present; there was no need to break the law. The thought passed through his mind, and he swallowed the words before uttering them. “Young Uncle, I can see only one course,” You said. “Raise as much ready cash as possible, buy goods already in Shanghai, hold them for a while and then sell. As for other business besides arms, we can discuss that too. Best of all would be something our grain-transport brothers could work at together. It would give everyone a hard-earned living and keep them from getting into trouble through idleness.” Hu heard the concealed anxiety behind these words about the brotherhood’s worsening livelihood. They were now close friends, sharing good fortune and bad; he ought to help You bear his worries. He asked about the difficulties facing the Songjiang brotherhood and what might be done. The discussion grew so absorbing that they did not go to bed until dawn.

一觉睡到近午时分，胡雪岩为怪情院一个“大姐”喊醒，说有客来。起床一看是陈世龙，递上一封信，说是王有龄专程派人送了来的。启封细看，才知道新城县抗粮滋事案，大功已成，嵇鹤龄不负所望，协同地方绅士，设计擒获首要各犯。已经解到杭州审讯法办。报告喜讯以外，接着便谈冬漕，因为上海失守，浙江的漕米海运。决定改由浏河出口。这一来便多了周折，所以必须提早一个月启运，连带也就要提早催征、王有龄得要赶回湖州。同时又因为上海失守的缘故，浙江人心惶惶，各地团练，都在加紧办理，湖州亦不例外，虽说有赵景贤主持其事，地方官守土有责，不能不问。所苦的是，海运局的差使还不能摆脱，分身乏术，希望胡雪岩无论如何回浙江一趟，他有许多事要当面商量。看完信，胡雪岩又高兴、又为难，而且还有些困惑，高兴的是新城建功，为难的是他亦分身乏术，困惑的是嵇鹤龄应有酬庸、却未见提起。怎么办？他定神想了想、决定回去一趟，但不能“空手而回”，有两件事，可以光为王有龄做好。想停当了他告诉陈世龙说：“你回去收拾行李，我们明天就走，阿珠也一起走。”

Hu slept until nearly noon, when one of the senior female attendants at Yiqing House woke him to say that he had a visitor. It was Chen Shilong, bringing a letter delivered by a special messenger from Wang Youling. Hu opened it and read carefully. The affair of the grain-tax disturbances in Xincheng had been brought to a successful conclusion. Ji Heling had fulfilled their expectations: working with local gentlemen, he had devised a plan to capture the principal offenders, who had been sent to Hangzhou for trial and punishment. After the good news came the question of the winter grain shipment. Because Shanghai had fallen, Zhejiang’s tribute rice would now be shipped out to sea through Liuhe. The extra complications meant starting a month early, and the collection of the grain tax would also have to be advanced. Wang needed to hurry back to Huzhou. Shanghai’s fall had caused alarm throughout Zhejiang, and militia organization was being pressed forward everywhere, Huzhou included. Although Zhao Jingxian was directing the work, the local official was responsible for the defense of his territory and could not leave it unattended. Yet Wang could not extricate himself from his duties at the Sea Transport Bureau and could not be in two places at once. He hoped that Hu would return to Zhejiang at all costs: there were many things they needed to discuss in person. Hu finished the letter pleased, troubled and puzzled. He was pleased by the success at Xincheng, troubled because he too had more than he could attend to, and puzzled because there was no mention of the reward Ji Heling deserved. What should he do? He collected his thoughts and decided to go back, but not empty-handed. There were two things he could first arrange for Wang. Having made up his mind, he told Chen, “Go back and pack. We leave tomorrow. A’zhu will come with us.”

接着，他匆匆漱洗，去找尤五商量，一谈漕米由浏河出口，尤五皱着眉说：“这麻烦大了！”“怎么呢？”“浏河在嘉定北面……”“啊！”胡雪岩失声而呼，漕米驶运到浏河，由青浦、嘉定这一条路走，是不可能了。“那么，该怎么走呢？”“要兜圈子！”尤五蘸青茶在桌上画出路线：“从嘉兴往北，由吴江，昆山、太仓到浏河。”“这真是兜了个大圈子。”胡雪岩又问，“太仓是不是靠近嘉定？”“是啊，太仓在嘉定西北，四五十里路。”说着，他深深看了胡雪岩一眼，意思是要当心周立春劫漕米。胡雪岩心里明白，灵机一动，笑嘻嘻地说道：“尤五哥，你的生意来了，靠交情卖铜钿，浙江冬漕，最后到训河那段路，归你包运好不好？”

He hurried through his washing and went to consult You. At the mention of sending the tribute rice out through Liuhe, You frowned. “That will cause a great deal of trouble.” “Why?” “Liuhe lies north of Jiading.” “Ah!” Hu exclaimed. Sending the grain boats to Liuhe by way of Qingpu and Jiading would be impossible. “Then which way can they go?” “They must make a detour.” Dipping a finger in clear tea, You traced the route on the table. “North from Jiaxing, through Wujiang, Kunshan and Taicang to Liuhe.” “That is a considerable detour. Is Taicang near Jiading?” “Yes, forty or fifty li northwest of it.” You gave Hu a significant look: they must beware of Zhou Lichun seizing the grain. Hu understood. An idea struck him, and he smiled. “Brother You, here is business for you. Turn your connections into money! How would you like the contract to carry Zhejiang’s winter tribute grain over the final stretch to Liuhe?”

这是顺理成章，极妙的事，但尤五因为来之太易，反有天下哪有这种好事的感觉，一时竟茫然不知所答。“怎么样？”胡雪岩催促着说，“这件事我有把握，完全可以作主，只等你一句话，事情就算定局。”“不晓得‘那方面’头不买我的帐？”尤五踌躇着说。出入关系，就在这一点上，所谓“靠交情，卖铜钿”也就是这一点，胡雪岩说道：“尤五哥，别的我都可以替你出主意，这方面要你自己才有数，我不便说什么！”“是的。”尤五深深点头。“这要我自己定主意。说实话，既然答应下来，要有肩胛，不能做连累你和王知府的荒唐事。这样，为求稳当，我只能暂且答应你。好在日子也还早，我托人跟‘圈吉’去打个招呼看看，如果口气不妙，我立刻通知你，只当没有说过这回事。你看怎么样？”“你怎么说，怎么说。我们假定事在必成，先商量商量怎么个办法。”于是议定浙江清船到吴江，归尤五接驳转运，到浏河海口为止。因为包运要担风险，水脚自然不能照常例计算。胡雪岩答应为他力争，多一个好一个。

It was a natural and excellent proposal. Yet it had come so easily that You could scarcely believe such good fortune existed; for a moment he did not know what to say. “Well?” Hu urged. “I am confident about this. I can settle it myself. One word from you, and it is arranged.” “I don’t know whether the other side will honor my connections,” You said hesitantly. That was the decisive point, the very basis of turning friendship into money. “Brother You,” Hu replied, “I can advise you on everything else. But only you can judge that. I cannot speak for you.” “Yes.” You nodded solemnly. “That is for me to decide. If I undertake it, I must shoulder the responsibility. I cannot do anything foolish that would involve you and Prefect Wang in trouble. To be safe, I can only agree provisionally. There is still time. I’ll send someone to sound out our friend Zhou. If his response is unfavorable, I’ll notify you at once, and we will treat the whole proposal as though it had never been made. What do you think?” “Whatever you say. Let us assume it will succeed and first discuss the arrangements.” They agreed that, once Zhejiang’s grain boats reached Wujiang, You would take over the cargo and carry it onward to the sea outlet at Liuhe. Since the contract involved risk, the freight rate could not follow the ordinary scale. Hu promised to argue for the best possible terms: every extra payment would help.

谈完了一件谈第二件，这要去找古应春、胡雪岩估计情势，浙江当道不但一定会买洋枪，而且因为上海失守，人心惶惶，防务亟待加强，所以对洋枪的需要，会倍感急迫。看准了这一点，不妨双管齐下，一面带说帖回去，劝浙江当道大批购买，一面带着现货回杭州，如果团练不用洋枪，就劝王有龄买了，供他的亲军小队使用。找到古应春家，只见他正衣冠整齐地，顶备到恰情院赴约。等胡雪岩说明来意，古应春想了一下问道：“你想要买多少支？”“先买两百支。”胡雪岩说，“我带了一万两银子在身上。”“两百支，有现货。你怎么运法？”古应春提醒他说，“运军械，要有公事，不然关卡上一定会被扣。”“是的。我跟尤五哥商量好了，由上海运到松江，不会有麻烦。我一到杭州。立刻就请了公事迎上来接货，这样在日子上就不会有耽搁了。”“好！我此刻就陪你去看洋人，当面议价。”说着，古应春拉了胡雪岩就走。

With the first matter settled, Hu turned to the second, which required a visit to Gu. From his assessment of the situation, the Zhejiang authorities would certainly buy foreign guns. Indeed, the alarm caused by Shanghai’s fall and the urgent need to strengthen defenses would make their demand especially pressing. He could therefore proceed on two fronts: take the memorandum back and urge a large official purchase, while also bringing guns ready for use to Hangzhou. If the militia did not buy them, he could persuade Wang to purchase them for his personal guard detachment. When Hu reached Gu’s house, he found him dressed and ready for their appointment at Yiqing House. After hearing Hu’s purpose, Gu considered for a moment and asked, “How many do you want?” “Two hundred to begin with. I have ten thousand taels with me.” “There are two hundred in stock. How will you transport them? You need official papers to move arms, or they are certain to be detained at a checkpoint.” “Yes. I have discussed it with Brother You. Getting them from Shanghai to Songjiang will cause no trouble. As soon as I reach Hangzhou, I’ll obtain the official documents and send to meet the shipment. That will avoid any delay.” “Good! I’ll take you to see the foreigner now, and we can negotiate the price in person.” He took Hu by the arm and started out.

“慢点，慢点！”胡雪岩怯意地笑着，“跟洋人打交道，我还是第一回……”“你怕什么？”古应春打断他的话说，“洋人也是人，又不是野人生番，文明得很。”“不是说野蛮、文明，是有些啥洋规矩？你先说给我听听，省得我出洋相。”“这一时无从谈起。”古应春说，“中国人作揖，洋人握手，握右手。到屋子里要脱帽。洋人重堂客，回头你看见洋婆子要站起来，那个哈德逊太太很好客，最喜欢跟中国人问长问短，洋人的规矩是不大重男女大防的，你不必诧异。““这倒好，”胡雪岩笑道，“跟我们尤家那位七姑奶奶一样。”“你说谁？”“不相干的笑话，你不必理我。”胡雪岩摇摇手说，“我们走吧！”

“Wait, wait!” Hu said with a nervous smile. “This is my first time dealing with foreigners.” “What are you afraid of?” Gu interrupted. “Foreigners are human too. They are not wild savages. They are quite civilized.” “I don’t mean whether they are savage or civilized. What foreign rules of conduct should I know? Tell me beforehand so I don’t make a fool of myself.” “There is scarcely time to explain everything. We clasp our hands and bow; they shake hands—the right hand. Take off your hat indoors. They show respect to women, so stand when you see a foreign lady. Mrs Hudson is very hospitable and likes to ask Chinese visitors all sorts of questions. Their customs do not insist on a strict separation between men and women. Don’t be surprised.” “That sounds pleasant,” Hu said, laughing. “Like the Seventh Lady in the You household.” “Who do you mean?” “An irrelevant joke. Never mind me.” Hu waved it aside. “Let’s go.”

于是两乘肩舆，到了泥城桥一座小洋房，下轿投刺，被延入客厅，穿蓝布大褂的听差，也不奉茶，也不敬烟，关上房门就走了。隔不多久，靠里的一道门开启，长了满脸黄胡子的哈德逊大踏步走了出来。胡雪岩已打定主意，亦步亦趋跟着古应春，看他起身，他亦起身，看他握手，他亦握手，只有古应春跟洋人谈话时，他只能看他们脸上的表情。表情很不好，洋人只管耸肩摊手，而古应春大有恼怒之色，然后声音慢慢地高了，显然起了争执。“岂有此理！”古应春转过脸来，怒气冲冲地对胡雪岩说，“他明明跟我说过，贸易就是贸易，只要有钱，他什么能卖的东西都愿意卖，现在倒又翻悔了，说跟长毛有协议，卖了给他们就不能再卖给官军。我问他以前为什么不说，他说是他们领事最近才通知的。又说，他们也跟中国人一样，行动要受官府约束，所以身不由主。你说气人不气人？”“慢来！”胡雪岩问道：“什么叫协议，是不是条约的意思？”“大致就是这意思。”“那就不对了，朝廷跟英国人订了商约，开五口通商，反而我们不能跟他通商，朝廷讨伐的叛逆，倒能够跟他通商。这是啥道理！”

Two sedan chairs took them to a small Western house at Nicheng Bridge. They alighted, sent in their visiting cards and were shown into the drawing room. The servant, dressed in a long blue cotton gown, offered neither tea nor tobacco; he simply closed the door and went away. Before long an inner door opened, and Hudson, his face covered in a yellow beard, strode in. Hu had resolved to copy Gu exactly. When Gu rose, he rose; when Gu shook hands, he shook hands. But when conversation began, Hu could do nothing except watch their expressions. Those expressions were far from reassuring. The foreigner kept shrugging and spreading his hands, while Gu looked increasingly angry. Their voices gradually rose: plainly they were arguing. “Outrageous!” Gu turned to Hu in fury. “He told me clearly that business was business: if a customer had money, he would sell anything he was able to sell. Now he goes back on it. He says he has an agreement with the Long-Haired rebels and cannot sell to government troops after selling to them. I asked why he hadn’t said so before. He claims his consul only recently informed him of it. He says they are subject to their authorities just as we are to ours and cannot act as they please. Isn’t that infuriating?” “Wait,” Hu said. “What does he mean by an agreement? Something like a treaty?” “Roughly speaking, yes.” “Then it makes no sense. Our government made a commercial treaty with Britain, opening five ports to trade. Yet we cannot trade with him, while rebels whom our government is fighting can! What sort of reasoning is that?”

古应春大喜，“不错，不错。说得真有道理！等我问他。”于是古应春转脸跟哈德逊办交涉，胡雪岩虽然听不懂意思，却听得出语气，看得出神色，古应春一派理直气壮的声音，而哈德逊似乎有些词穷了。到最后只见洋人点头，古应春含笑，向胡雪岩说道：“成功了！他答应跟他们领事去申诉。看样子未必有什么协议，只因为我们的生意小，长毛的生意大，伯贪小失大而已。”“请你告诉他，眼前我们的生意小，将来生意会很大，眼光要放远些，在目前留些交情，将来才有见面的余地。”古应春便把他的话译了过去，洋人不断颔首，同时也不断看着胡雪岩，显然是心许其言。“雪岩兄，”古应春说：“他说，你的话很有意味，要交你一个朋友，想请你去喝杯酒。问你的意思怎么样？”“当然，应该叙叙，归我们做东好了。”“那倒不必。让他做东好了。等生意谈妥，我们再回请。”

Gu was delighted. “Exactly! That is a very good argument. Let me put it to him.” He turned back to negotiate. Hu could not understand the words, but he could hear the tone and read the expressions. Gu spoke with the confidence of a man who had right on his side; Hudson seemed at a loss for an answer. At last the foreigner nodded, and Gu turned to Hu with a smile. “We have done it! He has agreed to take the matter up with his consul. I suspect there may be no agreement at all. Our order is small and the rebels’ orders are large; he is merely afraid of losing the greater profit for the smaller.” “Tell him that our business is small now but will be large in the future. He should take the long view. If he cultivates our friendship today, we can continue dealing with him tomorrow.” Gu translated. Hudson nodded repeatedly and kept looking at Hu, plainly approving of what he had said. “Brother Xueyan, he finds your remarks very interesting and would like to make a friend of you. He wants to invite you for a drink. What do you say?” “Of course. We should get better acquainted. Let us be the hosts.” “There is no need. Let him entertain us this time. We can return the invitation once the business is settled.”

于是，等古应春转达了接受邀请的答复，哈德逊到屋角将一条在中国犯禁的“明黄”色丝绦一拉，外面叮叮当当的响了起来，接着便见原来的那个听差推门而入，这让胡雪岩学了个乖，洋人招呼听差，是打铃不是拉长了声音喊：“来呀！”哈德逊吩咐听差，是准备马车，亲自拉缰，把他们两人载到一家外国酒店，入门一看，胡雪岩觉得有些头晕，四面镜子，映出无数人影、灯烛、桌椅，赶紧顺手扶住一张椅子，立定了脚再说。“就是这里吧！”古应春喊住哈德逊，各拉一张椅子坐下来。于是胡雪岩也拉开椅子坐下，一抬眼，恰好看见镜子中出现的丽影，转脸来望，见是个金发碧眼的美女，真正是雪肤花貌，腰如一捻，露出一嘴雪白的牙齿，笑着在问话。于是哈德逊嘱咐了几句，那女侍转身走了。胡雪岩不便盯着她的背影看，只望着镜子。西洋女人见得还不多，这一望，眼睛使舍不得离开镜子，看到那刚健婀娜的行路姿态，不由得想起穿着“花盆底”的旗下大姑娘，一摇三摆的样子，觉得各擅胜场，都比三寸金莲、走路讲究裙幅不动的汉人妇女来得中看。正在这样想着，镜中的丽影又出现了，她手托银盘，盘中一瓶颜色象竹叶青的酒，三只水晶杯，又有一瓶凉水。摆设停当，哈德逊取了三块银洋，放在银盘里。

When Gu conveyed their acceptance, Hudson went to a corner and pulled a silk bell cord in the bright yellow reserved for imperial use in China. A jangling sounded outside, and the servant returned. Hu learned something: foreigners summoned servants by ringing a bell instead of drawing out a loud cry of “Come!” Hudson ordered the carriage, took the reins himself and drove them to a Western drinking establishment. As Hu entered, he felt dizzy. Mirrors on every side multiplied the people, lamps, tables and chairs without end. He quickly grasped a chair and steadied himself. “Let’s sit here,” Gu called to Hudson, and each drew up a chair. Hu sat down too. Looking up, he caught the reflection of a beautiful figure in a mirror. He turned and saw a blonde, blue-eyed woman with a snow-white complexion, lovely features and a slender waist. Her smile revealed white teeth as she asked a question. Hudson gave her an order, and she turned away. Hu could hardly stare openly after her, so he watched her in the mirror. He had seen few Western women, and now found it difficult to take his eyes from the reflection. Her vigorous yet graceful stride reminded him of the swaying walk of young Manchu women in their flowerpot-soled shoes. Each had its own charm; both seemed more attractive to him than Han women with tiny bound feet, whose ideal was to walk without disturbing the folds of their skirts. While he was thinking this, the waitress reappeared in the mirror carrying a silver tray. On it were a bottle of liquor resembling Bamboo Leaf Green in color, three crystal glasses and a bottle of cold water. Once she had set them down, Hudson placed three silver dollars on the tray.

“这酒也不便宜。”胡雪岩说，“一块银洋七钱二，三块银洋就合到二两一钱多银子。”“是啊！运费贵。”古应春答了他一句，帮着哈德逊倒酒，又加上凉水，然后彼此举一举杯。“怎么？”胡雪岩问：“这就吃了？有酒无肴！”“洋盘！”古应春用夷场中新近流行的谚语笑他，“洋人吃酒，没有菜的。”“这我倒还是第一回。”胡雪岩喝了一口，酒味倒还不坏，但加了水，觉得劲道不够，便又把杯子放下了。“我们谈生意吧！”古应春说了一声，跟哈德逊去交谈，然后又问胡雪岩说，“他问你货色什么时候要？”“最多三天就要起运。”“那价钱就不同了。”古应春说，“有一批货色，他已经答应了镇江一个姓罗的长毛，你要可以先给你，要三十两银子一支。如果你肯等半个月，他另有一批货色从英国运到，只要二十两一支。““三十两就三十两。货色要好。”

“This liquor isn’t cheap,” Hu remarked. “A silver dollar is worth seven qian and two fen. Three dollars come to more than two taels and one qian.” “Yes, freight is expensive,” Gu replied. He helped Hudson pour the liquor and add cold water; then they raised their glasses to one another. “What?” Hu asked. “We drink now? Wine without dishes?” “A novice in foreign ways!” Gu teased him with a new expression current in the settlement. “Foreigners drink without food.” “Well, that is a first for me.” Hu took a sip. The flavor was not bad, but diluted with water it lacked strength. He put down the glass. “Let’s talk business,” Gu said. After speaking with Hudson, he turned back. “He asks when you need the goods.” “They must be dispatched within three days at most.” “Then the price will be different. He has a shipment already promised to a rebel named Luo at Zhenjiang. He can let you have it first, but it will be thirty taels a gun. If you can wait half a month, another shipment will arrive from Britain, and those would be only twenty taels each.” “Thirty it is. The goods must be good.”

古应春点点头，又跟哈德逊去说。就这样由他居间口译，很快地谈妥了一切细节，两百支枪，一万发子药，总价一万一千两银子，二八回扣，实收八千八百两。另外由哈德逊派一名“铜匠”随货到浙江去照料，要二百两银子的酬劳。“贷款我带在身上，是不是此刻就交？”“不必。”古应春说，“明天到他洋行里去办手续。”“那就托你了。”胡雪岩取出银票，交了过去，“这里一万两，多的是你的。”“用不着。”古应春急忙摇手，“大家一起做，回扣列入公帐，将来再说。”“这话也对。那么，多的一千两算存在你的手里好了。”

Gu nodded and spoke to Hudson again. With him interpreting between them, they soon settled every detail: two hundred guns and ten thousand rounds of ammunition, at a total price of eleven thousand taels. After a twenty-percent rebate, the sum payable was eight thousand eight hundred. Hudson would also send a gunsmith with the shipment to Zhejiang to attend to the weapons, for a fee of two hundred taels. “I have the money with me. Shall I pay now?” “No need,” Gu replied. “We can complete the formalities at his firm tomorrow.” “Then I’ll leave it to you.” Hu took out his banknotes and handed them over. “Here are ten thousand taels. The surplus is yours.” “There is no need for that!” Gu hastily waved the suggestion aside. “We are all in this together. The rebate goes into our common accounts. We can settle our shares later.” “Quite right. Then consider the remaining thousand taels a deposit you are holding for me.”

古应春点点头，指着银票又跟哈德逊去谈，只见洋人笑容满面，很快的说了好些话，据古应春传译，哈德逊认为跟胡雪岩做生意，很痛快，他要额外送一支最新式的“后膛七响”，以表敬意。“ 请你替我说，谢谢！”胡雪岩又说，“再请你问问他，那种什么”后膛七响‘，可以不可以卖几支给我？我要带回去送人。“这有些困难，哈德逊在中国好几年，深知贪小便宜的人多，留着几支好枪要用来应酬人情，不肯出售。然而最后哈德逊却又让步了，愿意匀出两支来卖给胡雪岩，价钱是每支一百五十两银子，据他说，完全是照成本出让。每支枪另配一百粒子药，也是白送。

Gu nodded, pointed to the notes and spoke to Hudson, whose face broke into a broad smile. He said a great deal very quickly. According to Gu, Hudson found doing business with Hu so agreeable that he wished to present him with one of the latest breech-loading, seven-shot guns as an additional mark of esteem. “Please thank him for me,” Hu said. “And ask whether he could sell me a few of those—what are they called?—seven-shot breech-loaders. I should like to take some home as gifts.” This was less easy. Hudson had spent several years in China and knew how fond many people were of small favors. He was keeping a few fine guns for cultivating useful relationships and did not want to sell them. In the end, however, he yielded and agreed to spare two for Hu, at one hundred and fifty taels apiece, which he said was exactly the cost price. Each would come with a hundred rounds of ammunition, also given free.

做了额外的这笔小交易，哈德逊要开一瓶香摈酒庆祝。古应春心想，胡雪岩对那种带点酸味的淡酒，未见得会感兴趣，而开一瓶香摈很贵，让哈德逊破费还是小事，回头胡雪岩端起杯子一喝，皱眉摇头，浅尝即止，那就是件很不礼貌的事，不如辞谢了的好。于是他告诉哈德逊，说胡雪岩喝不惯洋酒，不能领受他的好意，表示抱歉，哈德逊厦问，胡雪岩是不是不会喝酒？及至听说他的酒量很好时，哈德逊使表示奇怪，说桌上那瓶酒，来自苏格兰，不但是最有名的牌子，而且窖藏甚久，为何胡雪岩不喝？又说，他跟好些中国人有过交往，凡是会喝酒的，都欣赏苏格兰的酒，何以胡雪岩独异？接着又表示，如果胡雪岩不介意，他很想知道其中的缘故。古应春想敷衍一下，就算过去。倒是胡雪岩看哈德逊不断指着酒瓶和他的酒杯。滔滔不绝地在说话，猜到是谈杯中物，便自己先问起此事。古应春自然照实回答。“饮食一道，萝卜、青菜，各人自爱，好象女人一样，情人眼里出西施，没有什么道理好讲的。”古应春把他这一段话译给哈德逊听，洋人大点其头，说饮食没有道理好讲，这就是道理。接着又说，外国酒种类很多，胡雪岩不喜欢英国酒，也许喜欢法国的白兰地，于是招一招手把那女侍叫了过来，指明要一种名牌的白兰地。

To celebrate this additional little transaction, Hudson proposed opening a bottle of champagne. Gu doubted that Hu would care for a light wine with a somewhat sour taste. Champagne was expensive, but putting Hudson to expense was the lesser concern. If Hu tasted it, frowned, shook his head and refused another sip, that would be distinctly rude. Better to decline. He therefore apologized on Hu’s behalf, saying that Hu was unaccustomed to foreign liquor and could not accept the kind offer. Hudson asked in return whether Hu was unable to drink. On learning that he had a considerable capacity, Hudson was astonished. The bottle on the table came from Scotland, he said; it was not only a celebrated brand but had been aged for a long time. Why would Hu not drink it? He knew many Chinese, and all who enjoyed liquor appreciated Scotch. What made Hu different? If Hu did not mind, he would very much like to know. Gu meant to give an evasive answer and let the matter pass. But Hu saw Hudson repeatedly indicating the bottle and his glass while talking at length. Guessing the subject, he asked about it, and Gu naturally told him the truth. “In eating and drinking, one man likes radishes and another likes greens. It is like women: to a lover, his beloved is as beautiful as Xi Shi. There is no explaining tastes.” Gu translated this, and Hudson nodded emphatically. Saying that tastes could not be explained was itself an explanation. There were many kinds of foreign liquor, he added. If Hu did not like British liquor, perhaps he would enjoy French brandy. He beckoned to the waitress and named a particular celebrated brand.

喝这种酒又是一种杯子，矮脚敞口大肚子，但酒例得不多，也不掺水。哈德逊通过古应春，教胡雪岩喝这种酒的方法，说要双手台捧酒杯，慢慢摇晃，等手心里的热气，传入酒中，香味自发，便益觉醇美。胡雪岩如法炮制，试一试果如其言。哈德逊告诉古应春说，他终于找到了一种为胡雪岩所喜爱的酒，觉得很高兴。接着便谈白兰地的制法，由采撷葡萄到装瓶出售，讲碍非常详细。最后指着标贴纸上的一个洋字，读出它的译名叫“可涅克”，说选白兰地，一定要注意这个字，它是地名，法国出酒最好的地方。“我懂了！”胡雪岩对古应春说，“好比中国的黄酒一样，一定要‘绍兴’才道地。”“对，就是这意思。”

Brandy required a different glass: short-stemmed, broad-mouthed and round-bowled. Only a little was poured, without water. Through Gu, Hudson taught Hu how to drink it. He should cradle the glass in both hands and swirl it gently; as warmth from his palms entered the liquor, its fragrance would rise and its mellow flavor become more apparent. Hu followed these directions and found them justified. Hudson told Gu how pleased he was to have found a liquor Hu enjoyed. He then described brandy-making in great detail, from harvesting grapes to bottling the finished drink. Finally, he pointed to a word on the label and pronounced it: “Cognac.” When choosing brandy, he said, one should always look for this word. It was a place-name, the finest liquor-producing district in France. “I understand!” Hu told Gu. “Just like our yellow wine: it has to be Shaoxing to be authentic.” “Exactly.”

“现在……”哈德逊接着便跟古应春说，他的洋行，刚刚取得这种法国酒的代理权，希望胡雪岩为他介绍买卖。“ 原来他是推销货色！”胡雪岩笑道，“怪不得这么起劲。不过我不懂，什么叫‘代理权’？”“就是归他包卖。”古应春为他解释，“这种俩在我们中华土地上，归他总经销，坐抽水子，这就叫代理权。“胡雪岩立刻就懂了，这种坐享其成的事，完全要靠信誉，牌号响，信用好，货色销得出去，货款收得进来，到时候结帐，不久分文，人家才肯赋予代理权。他心里在想，自己也大可这么做，不过那是将来的事，眼前怎么样也谈不到此，所以不再往下说了。

“Now…” Hudson went on to tell Gu that his firm had just obtained the agency for this French liquor, and he hoped Hu would introduce customers. “So he is promoting his merchandise!” Hu laughed. “No wonder he is so enthusiastic. But I don’t understand: what does an agency mean?” “He has the exclusive right to sell it,” Gu explained. “He is the general distributor of this liquor in China and takes a commission on the sales. That is what an agency means.” Hu understood at once. Such a business, earning its return from arranging sales, depended entirely on reputation and credit. A firm needed a respected name, sound credit, the ability to sell the goods and collect payment, and accounts settled punctually without a penny left owing. Only then would another company grant it an agency. He thought he might very well do the same himself. But that was for the future, beyond any immediate prospect, so he did not pursue the subject.

酒味甚美，只是有酒无肴，胡雪岩还不习惯这样的饮酒方式，所以喝得不多，但为了酬答雅意，也为了馈赠所需，他决定买五箱白兰地带回去。哈德逊也很会做生意，马上又给他一个很优惠的折扣，他的目的是在推广。杭州是浙江省城，除了总督，各式各样的衙门都有，又是运河起点，商业相当繁盛，这个码头在哈德逊看，是可以有所作为的，他希望得到胡雪岩的助力，能够把他所代理的各种洋货，推销到杭州。这番意思经由古应春表达以后，胡雪岩自然欢迎，但他跟古应春说了实话，他官商两方面，缠在手里的事情实在太多，一时无法给哈德逊任何确实的答复，看这话是如何说法？“那就直接回头他！”这里的“回头”是辞谢的意思，胡雪岩却又觉得这是个机会，弃之可惜，最好是拖延着，要能让哈德逊不找别人，为他保留着这个机会。脑筋一动，想到了一番话：“你这样跟他说，本来我马上可以答应他，为他在杭州策划，但目前局势不稳，上海到杭州的路会断，货源不继，变成白贴开销。等局势稍微稳定下来，我马上替他动手。”哈德逊认为他的看法很稳健，同意等一等再说，不过他要求胡雪岩在杭州先替他看看洋货的行情，预作准备，将来有任何代理承销的机会，答应让胡雪岩优先承揽。

The brandy tasted excellent, but Hu was still unused to drinking without food and took little. To acknowledge Hudson’s hospitality, and to supply himself with gifts, he decided to buy five cases to take home. Hudson was a shrewd businessman too and immediately offered a generous discount. His aim was to promote the product. Hangzhou was Zhejiang’s provincial capital, with every kind of government office except that of a governor-general. It was also the starting point of the canal and a flourishing commercial center. Hudson saw considerable potential in the port and hoped Hu would help sell there the various foreign goods for which his firm held agencies. When Gu explained this, Hu naturally welcomed the proposal. But he spoke frankly to Gu: he already had far too much official and commercial business on his hands to give Hudson a definite answer. How should they put that? “Then simply turn him down.” Hu felt, however, that this was an opportunity too valuable to discard. Better to delay in such a way that Hudson would keep the opportunity for him instead of approaching someone else. An idea occurred to him. “Tell him this: ordinarily I could agree at once to organize matters for him in Hangzhou. But conditions are unsettled. The route from Shanghai to Hangzhou may be cut, interrupting supplies and leaving us to pay expenses for nothing. As soon as the situation becomes a little more stable, I will get to work for him.” Hudson thought this a prudent judgment and agreed to wait. Meanwhile, he asked Hu to investigate the Hangzhou market for foreign goods and make preliminary preparations. He promised Hu the first opportunity to take up any future agency or distribution arrangement.

生意谈到这里为止，彼此都觉得很圆满。古、胡二人先起身告辞，安步当车，走回怡情院。一路走，一路谈，谈的却不是生意。胡雪岩问道：“怎么样？外国酒馆里的那个洋女人，算是啥名堂？”“卖酒的还有啥名堂！”古应春笑道，“你想她卖啥？”胡雪岩笑笑不答，不一会却又以抱憾的声音说：“可惜我不懂洋文。不然，跟她谈谈说说，一定是蛮有趣的一件事。”“我倒想不到，”古应春也笑了，“你会中意洋女人！”“女人总是女人，管她是华是洋，只要动人就好。”“慢慢来！”古应春说，“将来你在上海住长了，总有跟洋女人落个交情的时候。”

Their business discussions ended to everyone’s satisfaction. Gu and Hu took their leave and walked back to Yiqing House. They talked on the way, but no longer about business. “Tell me,” Hu asked, “what exactly is the position of that foreign woman in the drinking place?” “She sells liquor. What else?” Gu laughed. “What did you imagine she sold?” Hu smiled without answering. After a while he said regretfully, “It is a pity I don’t understand their language. Otherwise it would surely be interesting to talk with her.” “I wouldn’t have expected you to take a fancy to a foreign woman,” Gu said, laughing too. “A woman is a woman. Chinese or foreign makes no difference, so long as she is attractive.” “Give it time,” Gu replied. “Once you have lived in Shanghai longer, you will have opportunities to make friends with foreign women.”

就这样谈着夷场风月，不知不觉到了恰情院。一进门就见相帮、娘姨、大姐聚在一起，指指点点在小声说笑，似乎遇见了什么神秘而有趣的事，胡雪岩便好奇地问道：“你们在讲啥？”“胡老爷，有位堂客在里面，跟二小姐谈得好亲热。”“堂客！”胡雪岩诧异：“堂子里只住官客，哪来的堂客？”说着便站往了脚，因为有堂客在里面，虽未“放门帘”，也不便乱闯。“不要紧！胡老爷你请进去看了，就晓得了。”古应春比胡雪岩更好奇，听得“不要紧”三字，首先就拔脚进门，只觉眼前一亮，那位堂客如雪山皑皑，令人不可逼视。这位丰腴丰皙、艳光照人的少妇，正是七姑奶奶。看见闯来的那个陌生男子，长身如鹤，英气勃勃，不觉心中一动，五百年风流冤家，就此在不该相遇的地方遇到了。

Talking of romance in the foreign settlement, they reached Yiqing House almost without noticing. Inside the entrance, the male and female attendants and maids were gathered together, pointing and laughing quietly as though something mysterious and amusing had occurred. Curious, Hu asked, “What are you all talking about?” “Mr Hu, there's a lady inside, having a very friendly conversation with the Second Miss.” “A lady!” Hu was astonished. “A courtesan house receives gentlemen. Where has a lady come from?” He stopped. With a woman visiting, it would be improper to walk straight in, even though the curtain had not been lowered. “It's all right, Mr Hu. Go in and see, and you'll understand.” Gu Yingchun was even more curious. At the words “It's all right,” he stepped through the door ahead of Hu. His eyes were dazzled: the visitor was as radiantly fair as a snow-covered mountain, almost too brilliant to look upon. The full-figured, fair-skinned young woman, radiant with beauty, was the Seventh Lady. Seeing the stranger—tall as a crane and full of spirit—she felt an involuntary stirring. A pair of lovers destined for each other five hundred years before had met where they ought never to have met.

一半是不知如何招呼，一半是目炫心迷，正当他们错愕无语，而怡情老二也觉得为难之际，胡雪岩跟了进来，一看亦大感意外：“咦，七姐！是你。”有人搭腔，事情便好办了，七姑奶奶向来说话粗声大气，不堪领教，这时不知是受了恰情老二一口吴侬软语的感染，还是因为有古应春这个一见便生好感的陌生男客在，心存顾忌，居然斯斯文文地喊一声：“小爷叔，你想不到我在这里吧？”自然想不到，胡雪岩心想，兄弟一起逛堂子的事，听说过，兄妹一起逛堂子，却是天大的新闻。便点点头说：“我道是哪位堂客？怎么样也想不到是你。”“请坐，请坐！”怡情老二看古应春和七姑奶奶偷眼相望，随即说道：“胡老爷，你来引见吧！”于是胡雪岩为古应春及七姑奶奶作了介绍，一个盈盈含笑，把双手放在左腰上，福了一福，一个抱拳作揖说道：“原来是七姐！真正伉爽不让须眉。”七姑奶奶懂了他那句语，虽是恭维，却也有惊诧的意味在内，想想一个良家妇女，独闯娼门，说起来是有些不守妇道，所以很难得地害了羞，红着脸报以微笑。她的笑容最甜，虽是窘笑，依然妩媚。古应春心里在想：倒不曾料到，尤五有这样漂亮的一个妹妹！

Neither knew quite how to greet the other, and both were dazzled and bewildered. They stood in startled silence, while Yiqing's Second Miss wondered what to do. Then Hu came in and was equally surprised. “Why, Seventh Sister! It's you.” With someone to begin the conversation, things became easier. The Seventh Lady ordinarily spoke so loudly and roughly that she was difficult to endure. Now, whether influenced by the Second Miss's soft Suzhou speech or restrained by the presence of a stranger who had pleased her at first sight, she spoke with remarkable gentleness. “Young Uncle, you didn't expect to find me here, did you?” Certainly not. Hu had heard of brothers visiting courtesans together, but a brother and sister doing so was extraordinary news. He nodded. “I was wondering who the lady could be. I'd never have thought of you.” “Please sit down, both of you!” Noticing Gu and the Seventh Lady stealing glances at one another, the Second Miss added, “Mr Hu, do introduce them.” Hu did so. Smiling, the Seventh Lady placed both hands at her left waist and curtsied. Gu returned a clasped-hands bow. “So you are Seventh Sister! Your spirit is the equal of any man's.” She understood the compliment, but heard surprise in it too. A respectable woman coming alone into a courtesan house could hardly be called proper conduct. Unusually for her, she felt shy and answered with a blush and a smile. Her smile was exceptionally sweet; even an embarrassed one remained charming. Gu thought that he had never expected You Laowu to have such a beautiful sister.

等怡情老二招呼着坐定，胡雪岩自然要问来意，七姑奶奶坦率相告，因为尤五一夜不曾回家，而她回松江之前还有许多话要问他，心里焦急，所以找上门来。“你一个人来的？”“是啊！”七姑奶奶顽皮而得意地笑道，“我那位妹子不许我来，阿龙也不肯带路，我只好借故溜了出来，自己雇一顶小轿到这里。不曾遇着五哥，倒跟二小姐谈得好投机，”“啊呀！七姑奶奶，”怡情老二不安地笑着：“真正不敢当你这么的称呼，叫我老二好了。”“或者叫小五嫂。”胡雪岩打着趣问：“那么，人呢？”这是指尤五，怡情老二答道：“有朋友约了出去了。说八点钟一定回来，请胡老爷、古老爷务必等他。”“自然要等。”胡雪岩问七姑奶奶，“想来你也还没有吃饭，我们是上馆子，还是就在这里吃。”“自然是在这里吃。”怡情老二急忙接口，“我请七姑奶奶吃便饭，请你们两位作陪客。”“理当奉陪。”

Once the Second Miss had settled them in their seats, Hu naturally asked what had brought the Seventh Lady there. She answered frankly: her brother had stayed out all night, and she had much to ask him before returning to Songjiang. Growing anxious, she had come to find him. “Did you come alone?” “Yes!” She smiled with mischievous satisfaction. “Our young sister wouldn't let me come, and A’long wouldn't show me the way. I had to slip out on an excuse and hire a small sedan chair myself. I haven't found Brother Five, but I've had a splendid talk with the Second Miss.” “Oh, Seventh Lady!” Their hostess smiled uneasily. “Such a formal title is far too much for me. Just call me Second.” “Or Little Fifth Sister-in-Law,” Hu teased. “Well, where is he?” He meant You Laowu. “A friend invited him out,” the Second Miss replied. “He said he'd certainly be back at eight and asked both of you to wait.” “Of course we shall.” Hu turned to the Seventh Lady. “I suppose you haven't eaten either. Shall we go to a restaurant or eat here?” “Here, naturally!” the Second Miss interrupted eagerly. “I'm inviting the Seventh Lady to a simple meal, with you two gentlemen to keep her company.” “We shall be honoured to join you,” Gu replied.

古应春都答应了，胡雪岩还有什么话说？七姑奶奶却是外场人物，招招手把他叫到一边，悄悄问道：“小爷叔，这里的规矩，我不大懂。你看，这顿饭该不该吃？”“来都来了，还讲什么规矩？”七姑奶奶脸一红，“本来是没有这种规矩的，我大着胆子乱闯。只怕叫人笑死了！”说着，悄伶伶一双眼睛瞟了过去。胡雪岩顺着她的眼光看过去，恍炊大悟，怪不得“女张飞”这般斯文！当时只有一个念头，要成人之美。于是他轻轻一道：“七姐，你请过来，我有句话说。“怡情院的那个“大房间”甚大，西面用个“多宝格”隔开，他领着她到里面，在窗下红木太师椅上坐下，两人的脸都朝外，透过多宝格，只见古应春和怡情老二也正谈到起劲，不会注意到他们的谈后，于是胡雪岩才出言规劝。“七姐”他用兄妹般，极恳切的声音说，“你不开口，是尊观音，开出口来，说句实话，别人吃你不消！今天总算难得，替五哥做了面子。回头你自己再做忌些，那样子，人家就不会笑你了。”在平日，七姑奶奶对他这话，一定不服帖，这时却是窘笑着点一点头说：“我晓得了。就是这句话吗？”“就是这句话。”胡雪岩说：“你是玲珑七窍心，自己有数就是，何必还要我多说呢？”这话有言外之意，七姑奶奶想再问些什么，到底还不好意思出口，只很妩媚地笑着道谢：“谢谢你，小爷叔！”

Since Gu had accepted, what could Hu say? The Seventh Lady, however, was accustomed to dealing with people. She beckoned Hu aside and asked quietly, “Young Uncle, I don't know the customs here. Do you think I ought to stay for this meal?” “Now that you've come, why worry about customs?” She blushed. “There certainly isn't any custom of this kind. I simply took my courage in both hands and came. I'm afraid people will laugh themselves to death at me.” As she spoke, her lively eyes glanced across the room. Hu followed her gaze and understood. No wonder the female Zhang Fei had become so refined! His immediate impulse was to help a happy match along. “Seventh Sister, come over here,” he said softly. “There's something I want to tell you.” The large room at Yiqing House was spacious indeed. Open display shelves divided off the western side. He led her behind them, and they sat in rosewood armchairs beneath the window, both facing outwards. Through the shelves, they could see Gu and the Second Miss deep in conversation, unlikely to notice their own talk. Only then did Hu offer his advice. “Seventh Sister,” he said earnestly, as a brother might, “when you say nothing, you look like the Goddess of Mercy. But once you begin to speak, people frankly find you too much. Today, for once, you've done Brother Five credit. Keep a little more restraint as the evening goes on, and nobody will laugh at you.” Ordinarily, she would have resented this. Now she merely smiled awkwardly and nodded. “I understand. Is that all?” “That is all. You're clever enough to grasp the slightest hint. Once you understand, why should I say more?” There was meaning beneath the words. She wanted to ask further, but could not quite bring herself to do so. With a charming smile, she simply said, “Thank you, Young Uncle.”

两人走到外面，怡情老二迎上来说：“古老爷的话不错，这里大嘈杂，请到我‘小房了’去吃吧！”姑娘与恩客另营不虑人干扰的双宿双飞之处，叫做“小房子”。抬情老二的小房子就在这条弄堂的末尾，也是尤五每个月贴开销，但尤五的朋友多，在怡情院会客比较方便，所以难得到小房子去。想不到这时候倒派上了用场。胡雪岩自然赞成，回头对七姑奶奶说道：“那是老二住家的地方，比较清静，走吧！”于是怡情老二关照相帮，凡有“局票”来，只说病了，不能出“堂差”，又关照，等尤五一来，请到小房子去。这一下倒提醒七姑奶奶了，依然是把胡雪岩喊到一边，悄悄说道：“我是溜出来的。不见我的人，他们会发急。”这是指阿珠和陈世龙而言，“那好办！”他说，“叫人去通知一声就是了。”当时写了个便条，说七姑奶奶与尤五在一起，到时自回，不必着急。胡雪岩掏了个银角子做力钱，叫怡情院的相帮，立刻送交陈世龙。

When they emerged, the Second Miss came to meet them. “Mr Gu is right. It's too noisy here. Let's eat at my little house.” A courtesan's “little house” was a separate retreat where she and a favoured patron could be together undisturbed. Hers stood at the far end of the lane. You Laowu paid its monthly expenses too, but with so many friends to entertain, he found Yiqing House more convenient and seldom used the retreat. Unexpectedly, it now had a purpose. Hu naturally approved. Turning to the Seventh Lady, he said, “It's where she lives. Much quieter. Let's go.” The Second Miss instructed the male attendant that, if any invitations arrived, he must say she was ill and could not attend outside engagements. When You arrived, he was to be directed to the little house. This reminded the Seventh Lady of something. Calling Hu aside again, she said softly, “I slipped out. If they can't find me, they'll worry.” She meant A’zhu and Chen. “That's easily managed. We'll send someone to tell them.” He wrote a note saying that the Seventh Lady was with You Laowu and would return in due course; there was no need for anxiety. Taking out a small silver coin as a tip, he told the attendant to deliver it to Chen immediately.

办妥了这一切，一起走到怡情老二的小房子，是一楼一底的石库门房子，楼下是另一家，她住楼上，布置得楚楚有致，看上去是很舒服的地方。刚刚坐定，怡情院里自己做的酒菜。已经送到。怡情老二和古应春都要推七姑奶奶上座，她则一定不肯，结果是古应春首座，她和胡雪岩两对面，主人未座，正好各据一方。款客的是红葡萄酒，古应春送的洋酒。据说那是补血的，连宫里都经常饮用。怡情老二把它看得很珍贵，殷殷相劝。七姑奶奶的酒量，也还不坏，但一心只记着胡雪岩的忠告，强持着不肯多喝，也不多说话。席面上只听古应春在谈胡雪岩上外国酒馆的经过，七姑奶奶和怡情老二都听得只是笑。古应春这天的兴致很好，谈笑风生，滔滔不绝，一直到尤五出现，话锋才被打断。

With everything settled, they went to the Second Miss's little house. It was a two-storey building with a stone-framed gateway. Another household occupied the ground floor; she lived upstairs, where everything was arranged with taste and care. It looked very comfortable. They had barely sat down when the food and wine prepared at Yiqing House arrived. Both their hostess and Gu urged the Seventh Lady to take the seat of honour, but she firmly refused. In the end, Gu sat at the head, she and Hu faced one another, and their hostess took the lowest place, one person on each side of the table. The drink was a foreign red grape wine, a gift from Gu. It was said to nourish the blood and to be drunk regularly even at the imperial court. The Second Miss prized it highly and pressed it on her guests. The Seventh Lady could hold her liquor, but with Hu's advice firmly in mind, she made herself drink little and speak little. Gu did most of the talking, recounting Hu's visit to the foreign tavern and keeping both women laughing. He was in excellent spirits that day, witty and fluent, and his stream of conversation continued until You Laowu appeared.

兄妹相见，都有些不自然的表情，尤五的不悦，还可以想象得到，但对七姑奶奶的微现俱惮，胡雪岩却有些意外，在他的印象中，七姑奶奶行事任性，从不知什么叫害怕？平日只见尤五有些怕她，此刻为何她怕尤五？这就是为了有古应春在座的缘故。胡雪岩很快的想通了，她怕她哥哥责备她几句，当着古应春下不得台。既然如此，倒要小心防护她，因此，他首先就替她解释不能不来的缘故。接着便谈与哈德逊会面的经过，算是让尤五忘掉了对七姑奶奶的不快。自此开始，就没有工夫说笑了，许多正事要商量，头绪纷繁，一件事没有办妥，又扯到第二件。直到午夜，还未安排停当。“怎么办呢？我非早早赶回杭州不可。”胡雪岩有些着急，“一直都觉得人不够用，此刻越觉得摆布不开。”半天未曾开口的七七姑奶奶开口了：“也没有什么摆布不开！小爷叔你明天尽管动身，路上没有人送，我送，保你到了嘉兴，我再回松江。”“这倒也是个办法！”尤五点点头，“好在一路上，阿七都熟。就这样吧！你到了杭州，赶快派世龙拿了公事到松江来接洋枪。”他们兄妹这一番对答，使得古应春大为惊奇，“原来七姐是这么能干！”他自愧不如以外，也为她担忧，“这条路上，这几天很不好走，要当心！”“谢谢你！”她报以矜持的微笑，“不要紧的。”

Brother and sister greeted each other awkwardly. You's displeasure was understandable, but the slight fear in the Seventh Lady's manner surprised Hu. In his experience, she did exactly as she pleased and knew nothing of fear. Usually her brother seemed somewhat afraid of her. Why was she afraid of him now? Hu soon understood: Gu was present. She feared a reprimand from her brother that would embarrass her before him. Hu must protect her. He began by explaining why she had had to come, then recounted their meeting with Hudson, successfully diverting You from his displeasure. After that there was no time for jokes. Many practical matters needed discussion, so entangled that they passed to a second before resolving the first. By midnight, everything was still not arranged. “What are we to do? I must get back to Hangzhou soon.” Hu was anxious. “I've always felt short of people, but now I can hardly manage at all.” The Seventh Lady, silent for a long time, spoke up. “There's nothing so unmanageable about it. Go tomorrow, Young Uncle. If there's nobody to escort you, I'll do it. I'll see you safely to Jiaxing and then return to Songjiang.” “That would be a solution,” You said, nodding. “A’qi knows the whole route well. Let's settle it like that. Once you reach Hangzhou, send Shilong to Songjiang as quickly as possible with the official papers to collect the foreign guns.” Gu was astonished by the exchange. “So Seventh Sister is capable of all this!” He felt outdone, but worried for her too. “That route has been difficult these last few days. You must be careful.” “Thank you.” She gave him a restrained smile. “It will be quite all right.”

“真的不要紧！”到这时候，尤五总算找到机会，可以说她一句了，“我们家这位姑奶奶，一个人乱闯闯惯了的。”“也不是什么乱闯。”七姑奶奶觉得必须分辩，“有把握的地方我才敢去，摸不清路道的地方，我也不敢乱闯。象这里，我就晓得是不要紧的。”“对啊！”怡情老二接口说道，“要是不嫌弃，常常请过来，这里就跟自己家一样。”“听见没有，五哥！”七姑奶奶碍意地，“就跟自己家一样！”“只有一件，”古应春也凑趣说笑，“回去在五嫂面前瞒着点。”“这倒不碍事。我五嫂最贤慧，不管他这笔帐。”“好了，好了！”尤五看看钟说，“该走了。”

“Quite all right indeed!” At last You had found an opportunity to reprimand her. “Our lady here is used to rushing off anywhere by herself.” “I don't simply rush off anywhere.” She felt obliged to defend herself. “I go where I'm confident of things. I wouldn't venture where I didn't know my way. Here, for instance, I knew there was nothing to worry about.” “Exactly!” the Second Miss said. “If you don't think it beneath you, please come often. Treat this place as your own home.” “Did you hear, Brother Five?” the Seventh Lady asked triumphantly. “My own home!” “Only one thing,” Gu added playfully. “Keep it quiet before Fifth Sister-in-Law when you return.” “There's no need. She's exceedingly good-natured. She doesn't hold this sort of thing against him.” “Enough, enough!” You looked at the clock. “It's time to go.”

于是古应春首先告辞，却悄悄拉了胡雪岩一把。知道是有话说。胡雪岩便跟着古应春下楼出门，站定了脚笑道：“你可是要跟我打听一个人？”“咦！”古应春诧异：“你怎么知道？”“你别管！说吧，可是要问七姑奶奶？”“是的。”古应春说，“我听老二告诉我，她似乎居孀多年。可有这话？”“有的。不过也不算多年。”“倒守得住？”这是指七姑奶奶守节为何守不住，胡雪岩觉得他的话问得好笑，而且难以回答，只好半开玩笑地答道：“你何不自己去问她？”

Gu was the first to take leave, quietly giving Hu a tug. Understanding that he wished to speak, Hu followed him downstairs and outside. Stopping, he asked with a smile, “Do you want to inquire about someone?” “Why!” Gu was surprised. “How did you know?” “Never mind that. Tell me—is it the Seventh Lady?” “Yes. The Second Miss told me she has apparently been widowed for many years. Is that true?” “Yes, though it hasn't been so many years.” “And she's managed to remain a chaste widow?” He meant her fidelity to her late husband. Why should she not have managed it? Hu found the question amusing and difficult to answer. Half joking, he replied, “Why don't you ask her yourself?”

古应春也发觉自己失言，只好报以苦笑。就这时候看到尤五兄妹和怡情老二，已经走下楼来，古应春心想，明天胡雪岩就要走了，此一去又有多日暌隔，而自己有一番心事非要跟他商量不可，因而便向尤五说道：“五哥，你们先请。我跟胡雪岩还有些事要商量。”尤五还不曾开口，怡情老二便说：“何不请到我那里去谈？”这就是胡雪岩机警了，不等古应春开口，他先就搭话：“实在是我有点私事托应春兄，就在这里谈一谈好了，你们先请过去，我们马上就到。”“那么，快点来。”怡情老二说：“等你们来吃消夜。等他们走远了，胡雪岩便问：“应春兄，是在这里谈，还是找个地方坐坐呢？我看你要谈的事，不是三言两语所能变得清楚的。”“你大概也猜到了。”古应春说，“七姑奶奶的相貌、风度，很对我的劲。我托你做个媒。“

Gu realised that he had said the wrong thing and could only offer a rueful smile. Just then, he saw You, the Seventh Lady, and the Second Miss coming downstairs. Hu was leaving tomorrow and would be away for many days, yet Gu had something on his mind that he must discuss with him. “Brother Five, please go ahead,” he said. “Hu Xueyan and I have something to talk over.” Before You could answer, the Second Miss said, “Why not come and talk at my place?” Hu was quick enough to intervene before Gu spoke. “Actually, I have a little private business to ask Brother Yingchun about. We'll discuss it here. Please go ahead. We'll join you shortly.” “Then don't be long. We'll wait for you to have supper.” Once they were out of earshot, Hu asked, “Shall we talk here, Brother Yingchun, or find somewhere to sit? I suspect this isn't something that can be settled in a few words.” “You've probably guessed. The Seventh Lady's looks and manner suit me very well. I'd like you to act as matchmaker.”

胡雪岩想不到他这么开门见山，就说了出来，一时倒有些无从答复，愣在那里，半晌无声。“怎么样？”古应春很关切的问，“是不是有难处？”“有没有难处，还不知道。”胡雪岩说，“你总先把你的情形跟我说一说。”“对，对！这是我的疏忽……”古应春说了他的家庭，父母都在广东，也娶过亲，只是妻子已经过世，有个女儿，今年十六岁，随祖父母在乡，如此而已。“那倒好，没有什么罗嗦。”胡雪岩说：“七姑奶奶就因为跟她婆太太合不来，才回的娘家，照你府上这情形，如果不回广东，大概她也愿意。”“那……”古应春反倒迟疑了，“不回广东是办不到的。无论如何要回去见一见家父、家母。”“那自然。我是说不回广东乡下去住，你们夫妇在上海自立门户。这都是以后的事……”胡雪岩沉吟着说：“看样子，七姑奶奶对你，倒也还中意。不过，我有句话，一定要说在前面。““是，是。你说！我总尽力照办。”“不是要你什么‘照办’！是要你忍耐。你晓不晓得七姑奶奶有个外号，叫做‘女张飞’！”“是不是说她脾气暴躁？”古应春摇摇头，“我看倒不象‘女张飞’！”

Hu had not expected him to come straight to the point. For a while he could find no answer and stood silent. “Well?” Gu asked anxiously. “Is there some difficulty?” “I don't know yet whether there is. First, tell me about your own circumstances.” “Of course. How thoughtless of me.” Gu described his family. Both parents were in Guangdong. He had married, but his wife was dead. His daughter, now sixteen, lived with her grandparents in their home district. That was all. “Then there should be little complication,” Hu said. “The Seventh Lady returned to her own family because she couldn't get on with her mother-in-law. Given your circumstances, I imagine she might agree, provided she didn't have to return to Guangdong.” “But...” Now Gu hesitated. “Never going back to Guangdong would be impossible. Whatever happens, we must visit my father and mother.” “Naturally. I meant not settling in the countryside there. You and your wife would establish your own household in Shanghai. Those are matters for later.” Hu considered. “The Seventh Lady seems to like you too. But there's something I must say beforehand.” “Please do. I'll do my best to comply.” “It's patience you need, not compliance. Do you know that the Seventh Lady has a nickname—the female Zhang Fei?” “Do you mean she has a violent temper?” Gu shook his head. “She doesn't seem like a female Zhang Fei to me.”

这一半是“情人眼里出西施”，一半也是七姑奶奶特意收敛，看样子好事可谐，但情愿还是先把话说得深些，劝他慎重的好。“应春兄，”他说，“日子太浅，相知不深，好在以后见面的时候有得是，你何不看一看再说？”听语气是七姑奶奶有着不便说破的缺点，自己去看，当然最好。但古应春鳏居十年，一下子动了心，有如古井重波，心澜难平，急于要问个明白，所以接下来又说：“看归看，听归听！你多告诉我些。”胡雪岩不知该告诉他些什么？七姑奶奶的情形，他耳闻目见的很多，但不能一昧说好话，更不能一味说坏话。如果是寻常女子，品貌过得去，他一定尽说好话，促成美事，因为那可以断定，决不会成为怨偶。而七姑奶奶与众不同，做媒的责任甚重，真仿佛一言可兴邦，也可丧邦，谁能受得了她的脾气，她便一定是个贤内助，否则，感情会搞得极坏，媒人挨骂一辈子，于心何安？

Partly, beauty lay in the lover's eyes; partly, the Seventh Lady had deliberately restrained herself. A happy outcome seemed possible, but Hu preferred to speak frankly and urge caution. “Brother Yingchun, you've known each other too briefly. There will be plenty of opportunities to meet. Why not observe her for a while before deciding?” His tone suggested some fault that could not conveniently be stated. Seeing for himself would of course be best. But after ten years as a widower, he had suddenly been moved, like a long-still well stirred into waves. His heart would not settle, and he urgently wanted to understand. “I shall observe her, but I should like to hear about her too. Tell me more.” Hu did not know what to tell him. He had seen and heard a good deal about the Seventh Lady, yet he could neither praise her without reserve nor speak only of her faults. Had she been an ordinary woman of acceptable looks and character, he would certainly have praised her to bring about a happy match, confident that the pair would not become enemies. But the Seventh Lady was different. A matchmaker's responsibility was heavy: one word seemed capable of either bringing prosperity to a kingdom or destroying it. To a man who could bear her temper, she would be an excellent helpmate. Otherwise, the marriage would turn bitter, and the matchmaker would be cursed for life. How could he be easy in his conscience?

“说实话，你们都是一见钟情，瞒不过我，我也用不着你说，就已经想来做这个媒。应春兄，胡雪岩非常恳切的说，”你知道我的，我做事一向性子急，但这件事，实在急不得！为啥呢？七姑奶奶的好处，是别人没有的，她的叫人啼笑皆非的脾气，也是别人没有的，所以你要我说，我实在说不象。要你自己看，反正我总一定帮你的忙，做你的参赞。再透个信息给你，七姑奶奶的愿守不愿守，她兄嫂都做不得她的主。现在她似乎也看中你了，那你就请放心，好事迟早必成。“这番话对古应春是颗定心丸，而且启发甚多，大致七姑奶奶是个巾帼须眉，个性极强，遇事敢当。这样性格刚强的人，要看自己能不能驾驭得住她？驾驭得住，百炼钢化为绕指柔，闺房中仍有画盾之乐，驾驭不住，一辈子是她系在裤腰带上的裙下之囚。“多谢，多谢！就你这几句话，我已受惠非浅。走吧！”

“Honestly, you were both taken with each other at first sight. You couldn't conceal it from me. Before you said anything, I was already thinking of arranging the match. Brother Yingchun,” Hu said with great earnestness, “you know how impatient I usually am to get things done. But this is something that really cannot be hurried. Why? Because the Seventh Lady has good qualities nobody else possesses, and a temperament, unlike anyone else's, that can leave you unsure whether to laugh or cry. If you ask me to describe her, I simply can't do her justice. You must see for yourself. I shall certainly help and advise you. And here's something else: whether she remains a widow is entirely her own decision. Neither her brother nor his wife can decide for her. Now she seems to have taken a fancy to you, so you may rest assured. Sooner or later, the match is bound to succeed.” These words reassured Gu and gave him much to consider. Evidently, the Seventh Lady had the spirit of a man, a powerful will, and the courage to take responsibility. With such a strong character, the question was whether he could manage her. If he could, tempered steel might become soft enough to wind about his finger, and married life would still offer its tender pleasures, such as painting her brows. If he could not, he would be her prisoner for life, tied to her apron strings. “Thank you, thank you. Those few words have helped me greatly. Let's go.”

两个人一起回到怡情院，只见七姑奶奶跟怡情老二，并坐在床边，喁喁细语，亲热得象姐妹。尤五显然对此感到欣慰，含笑坐在一旁，神态显得很恬静。“来了，来了！”他站起来，兴致勃勃地：“有人送了我一篓蟹，刚才忘了拿到那里去吃了，尝一尝！”于是怡情老二急忙站起来招呼，七姑奶奶自己也要下手帮忙，做主人的一定不准她动手，这是堂子里，七姑奶奶是客，下手帮忙变得也成了主人，那不象话，但她想不到此，最后是胡雪岩递了个眼色，她才会过意来。这使得古应春又得了个极深的印象，他觉得她只是凡事热心。所以显得有些鲁莽。好在她也肯听人教导，绝不是那种蛮不讲理，死不认错的泼妇。这就没有可怕了。

They returned to Yiqing House and found the Seventh Lady and the Second Miss sitting together on the edge of the bed, talking confidentially, as intimate as sisters. You was plainly gratified and sat smiling beside them, looking very peaceful. “Here they are!” He rose with enthusiasm. “Someone sent me a basket of crabs. I forgot to take them over for our meal. Come and try them.” The Second Miss immediately rose to make arrangements. The Seventh Lady wanted to help, but her hostess firmly refused. This was a courtesan house, and the Seventh Lady was a guest. Helping would make her seem another hostess, which would be quite improper. This did not occur to her until Hu gave her a meaningful glance. Gu took a strong impression from the incident. He felt that she was simply eager to help in everything and therefore seemed somewhat rash. Fortunately, she was willing to listen to advice. She was certainly not one of those unreasonable shrews who would never admit a fault. So, he concluded, there was nothing to fear.

摆好桌子，娘姨端出两大盘热气腾腾，加紫苏蒸的阳澄湖大蟹，此是文人墨客笔下的天下第一名物，阳澄湖的尤其出名。特征是“金毛紫背”，通常每只八两，两只一斤，所以称为“对蟹”。七姑奶奶嗜蟹如命，但这时却很斯文，先挑了一只团脐送到尤五面前。“先敬客嘛！”尤五完全是做哥哥教导弟妹的派头。客是两位，论客气应该是古应春，七姑奶奶不知不觉地又有些着急，便拿那只蟹送到胡雪岩面前。“七姐，我们自己人。我自己来！”胡雪岩有些促狭，不但话里挤对她非把那只蟹送给古应春不可，而且还用手往外推谢。“那就你来！”七姑奶奶被逼到差不多的地步。“冲劲”就来了，大大方方地对古应春说，并且还把一小碗姜醋推到他面前。“谢谢！”古应春含着笑说，同时深深看了她一眼。七姑奶奶装作不见，只拿一只蟹在手，看胡雪岩已经自己动手，“便拿向她哥哥面前，然后自己也取一只，同时转眼去看怡情老二。

Once the table was ready, a female attendant brought two large plates of steaming Yangcheng Lake crabs, cooked with perilla. Crabs were celebrated by men of letters as the finest delicacy under heaven, and those from Yangcheng Lake were especially renowned. Their distinguishing features were golden hairs and purplish backs. They generally weighed eight liang apiece, so that two made a jin; hence the name “pair crabs.” The Seventh Lady adored them, but now behaved with great refinement, first choosing a female crab and placing it before her brother. “Guests first!” You spoke like an elder brother instructing his younger siblings. There were two guests; courtesy plainly required her to offer it to Gu. Growing flustered despite herself, she put the crab before Hu instead. “Seventh Sister, we're old friends. I'll help myself.” Mischievously, Hu not only used his words to press her into giving it to Gu, but pushed it away with his hand. “Then you take it!” Driven far enough, she recovered her boldness and addressed Gu openly, also placing a little bowl of ginger vinegar before him. “Thank you,” Gu said with a smile, giving her a long look. Pretending not to notice, she picked up another crab. Seeing that Hu had already helped himself, she gave it to her brother, took one for herself, and glanced towards their hostess.

怡情老二正取了一副吃蟹的家伙出来，纯银打造，小钳小锤子的，看来十分精巧。七姑奶奶觉得好玩，取过小锤子来，一下打在蟹螯上。在她自觉未曾用力，但那只蟹赘已被砸得甲碎肉烂，一塌糊涂了。大家都笑，七姑奶奶也笑，“这东西不是我用的。”她说，“还是用手方便。”她的那只手仿佛生来就是为剥蟹用的，手法熟练非凡，只用一根牙筷帮忙，须臾之间，把一只蟹吃得干干净净，蟹赘、蟹脚和那个“盖”拼凑在一起，看来仍旧是一只蟹。“这倒着实要点本事。”古应春颇为惊异，“我还是第一次见！”广东人的古应春，吃蟹自然没有苏锡嘉湖一带出蟹地方的人来得内行，表里不分，胡嚼一气，吐了一桌子的渣滓，七姑奶奶直性子，实在看不过去，便打趣他说：“你真是猪八戒吃人参果。看我来！”她取了一只蟹，依然只用一根筷子，很快地剥了一盖子的蟹肉，黄白杂陈，倒上姜醋，却不是自己享用，一推推到了古应春面前。这真叫古应春受宠若惊了，但也知不宜显示心中的感觉，所以只是接连说了两声：“多谢，多谢！”

The Second Miss was bringing out a set of crab-eating implements: tiny pincers and hammers made entirely of silver, exquisitely fashioned. Amused by them, the Seventh Lady took a little hammer and struck a claw. She felt that she had hardly used any force, yet the shell shattered and the flesh was mashed into a hopeless mess. Everyone laughed, and she joined them. “These things aren't meant for me. My hands are easier.” Her hands seemed made for shelling crabs. With astonishing skill and only one ivory chopstick to help her, she emptied a crab in moments. Claws, legs, and upper shell could be fitted back together so that it still looked whole. “That certainly takes skill,” Gu said in surprise. “I've never seen it before.” Coming from Guangdong, he naturally knew less about eating crabs than people from the crab-producing districts of Suzhou, Wuxi, Jiaxing, and Huzhou. He failed to distinguish shell from flesh, chewed indiscriminately, and spat debris all over the table. The forthright Seventh Lady could not bear to watch. “You're just like Zhu Bajie swallowing the ginseng fruit without tasting it. Watch me!” Taking another crab and again using only one chopstick, she quickly filled its shell with white flesh and yellow roe. She added ginger vinegar, then pushed the filled shell towards Gu instead of eating it herself. He was overwhelmed by her kindness, but knew better than to display his feelings. He merely said, “Thank you, thank you.”

巧得很，怡情老二正好也用小钳小锤子，敲敲打打，外带嘴咬手剥，也弄了一盖子蟹肉，送给尤五。于是胡雪岩笑道：“你们都有人代劳，只有我没有这份福气！“古应春知道他在打趣七姑奶奶，怕她脸上下不来，有意要把“美人之贻”这回事，看作无所谓，便将那蟹盖推过去说：“你来，你来！”“你舍得？”胡雪岩抓住题目，越发要开玩笑。这话很难回答，要说“舍得”，马上就会惹七姑奶奶在心里骂一句：没良心！想了想这样答道：“在别人，自然舍不得，你老兄又当别论。”“承情之至。不过，只怕你舍得，人家舍不得。”胡雪岩说，“人家辛辛苦苦剥了给你吃的，让我吃掉了，一定会心痛！”话还不曾完，七姑奶奶发急了，“小爷叔！”她用笑容掩饰窘态， “罚酒！你的话真正说得气人。”“是啊！”怡情老二在一旁帮腔，平她的气：“胡老爷话里有骨头，应该罚酒。”“好，好！”胡雪岩原是为古应春试探，看七姑奶奶虽然羞窘，并无温色，觉得试探的结果，大可满意，便欣然引杯，一饮而尽。

As it happened, the Second Miss had also been working with pincers and hammer, helped by her teeth and fingers, and had filled a shell with crabmeat for You. Hu laughed. “You both have someone to do the work for you. I'm the only one without such good fortune.” Gu knew he was teasing the Seventh Lady. Afraid she would be embarrassed, he tried to treat this gift from a beauty as nothing exceptional. Pushing the shell towards Hu, he said, “Here, you have it.” “Could you bear to part with it?” Hu seized the opening for more mischief. It was a difficult question. If Gu said yes, the Seventh Lady might immediately think him ungrateful. After a moment, he answered, “Not for anyone else, naturally. But you are another matter.” “I'm deeply obliged. Only, you may be willing to part with it when someone else is not. After all her hard work shelling it for you, she would surely be heartbroken if I ate it.” Before he finished, the Seventh Lady protested. “Young Uncle!” She hid her embarrassment behind a smile. “You must drink a forfeit. Your words are really exasperating.” “Quite right!” the Second Miss supported her, trying to soothe her feelings. “Mr Hu's words have sharp edges. He must drink.” “Very well, very well!” Hu had been testing the Seventh Lady's feelings on Gu's behalf. Seeing her embarrassed but not offended, he was thoroughly satisfied. He gladly raised his cup and emptied it.

一直坐在那里不说话的尤五，到这时才恍然大悟，他是做哥哥的想法，觉得七姑奶奶不些放浪形骸，心里便不大舒服。胡雪岩鉴貌辨色，看出风向不对，很知趣地把话题引了开去，同时也不肯再多作流连，找个机会，提议散席。时近午夜，而怡情院所在地的那条弄堂，却还热闹得很，卖熟食的小贩，往来如梭，吆喝不停，弄口停着许多小轿，流苏轿帘，玻璃小窗，十分精致，专做深宵寻芳倦客的生意，唯有这天抬着一位堂客——七姑奶奶。回到裕记丝栈，她第一个下轿，往后直奔，刚上楼梯，便扯开喉咙大喊：“张家妹子，你睡了没有？”阿珠还没有睡，先是不放心七姑奶奶，要为她等门，后来是跟陈世龙吃零食闲谈，谈上了劲，倒把要等的人忘掉了。这时听得楼下一喊，方始惊觉，赶紧起身迎了出去。两人在楼涕口相遇，只见七姑奶奶双颊如霞，眼波如水，一片春色，不觉大声而问：“你在哪里吃得这么醉醺醺地回来？”

Only now did You, who had been silent all this time, understand. Thinking as an elder brother, he felt that the Seventh Lady was behaving too freely and became uncomfortable. Reading his expression, Hu saw the change in the air and tactfully turned the conversation elsewhere. Nor did he wish to linger. At a suitable moment, he suggested ending the gathering. It was nearly midnight, but the lane outside Yiqing House was still lively. Food hawkers passed continually, calling their wares. At the entrance stood numerous little sedan chairs, finely made, with tasselled curtains and small glass windows. They catered especially to weary late-night seekers of pleasure. On this occasion alone, one carried a lady—the Seventh Lady. Back at the Yuji Silk Warehouse, she was first out of her chair and hurried towards the rear. Scarcely on the stairs, she called at the top of her voice, “Sister Zhang, are you asleep?” A’zhu was still awake. At first she had stayed up to let the Seventh Lady in, worried about her. Later, chatting and eating snacks with Chen, she had become so absorbed that she forgot whom she was waiting for. The call from below startled her, and she hurried out. They met at the head of the stairs. Seeing the Seventh Lady's rosy cheeks, sparkling eyes, and exuberant glow, A’zhu exclaimed, “Where have you been drinking to come back so tipsy?”

“你看，我带了什么好东西来给你吃！”七姑奶奶把一只细竹篮递了过去。这时胡雪岩和尤五亦已上楼，加上阿龙和闻声起床的老张，挤得满满的一屋子，却只听得七姑奶奶一个人的声音，大讲在怡情院消磨了这一晚上的经过。在老张父女是闻所未闻的奇事，就连陈世尤也觉得这位七姑奶奶胆大得惊人。“你们吃嘛！”最后她揭开了篮盖，里面是六只阳澄湖大蟹。她粗中有细，特别周到，连姜醋都是现成带着的。一则情不可却，再则那蟹也实在诱人，老张父女和陈世龙，便一面剥蟹，一面听七姑奶奶谈怡情院的风光。尤五却向胡雪岩使个眼色，两人避到里面谈心去了。

“Look what I've brought you!” The Seventh Lady handed her a finely woven bamboo basket. Hu and You had now come upstairs too. With Chen and Old Zhang, who had risen at the noise, the room was crowded, yet only the Seventh Lady's voice could be heard, recounting how she had spent the evening at Yiqing House. To Old Zhang and his daughter, it was an unheard-of adventure. Even Chen marvelled at her audacity. “Have some!” At last she lifted the basket lid, revealing six large Yangcheng Lake crabs. Beneath her rough manner, she was remarkably thoughtful: even the ginger vinegar was ready to hand. Her kindness could not be refused, and the crabs themselves were tempting. Old Zhang, A’zhu, and Chen began shelling them as they listened to her description of life at Yiqing House. You, meanwhile, signalled to Hu, and the two withdrew into the inner room for a private conversation.

“小爷叔，”尤五皱着眉头说：“你看我这个妹子越来越不象样，怎么得了？”“不要这么说！”胡雪岩笑嘻嘻地答道，“五哥，我要讨喜酒吃了。你晓得老古跟我怎么说？他要托我做媒！”尤五大为诧异，愣了好一会才问：“是想娶我们阿七。”“对！这才叫一见倾心。姻缘，姻缘，真正是缘分。”“什么缘分？”尤五的双眉皱得更深，“说起来是在堂子里见过面，那有多难听！”这个回答大出胡雪岩的意料，一时不知如何为他和七姑奶奶譬解？愣在那里，好半晌作声不得。“我倒不懂了，老古怎么会知道阿七此刻住在娘家？”尤五又问，“他当阿七还是大小姐？”“不”他晓得七姐居孀。是老二告诉他的，不对！是他跟老二打听的。“接着，胡雪岩便把古应春家里的情形说了一遍。

“Young Uncle,” You said with a frown, “my sister's behaviour grows more improper every day. What are we to do?” “Don't say that!” Hu replied cheerfully. “Brother Five, I shall be asking for wedding wine soon. Do you know what Gu said to me? He wants me to arrange a marriage.” You was astonished. After a long silence, he asked, “He wants to marry our A’qi?” “Exactly. Love at first sight! Marriage really is a matter of destiny.” “What destiny?” You frowned still more deeply. “Think how it would sound: they met in a courtesan house!” This response surprised Hu. He could not immediately think how to defend Gu and the Seventh Lady, and stood speechless for some time. “There's something I don't understand,” You continued. “How did Gu know that A’qi is living with her own family now? Does he think she's still an unmarried young lady?” “No. He knows she's a widow. The Second Miss told him—no, he asked her.” Hu then described Gu's family circumstances.

“那么，小爷叔，你怎么回答他的呢？”“我说，要他自己看。我看……他们有缘，这杯喜酒吃得成功的。”尤五不以为然，大摇其头：“算了，我看不要害人！”“你倒也不必把我们这位姑奶奶贬得太厉害！”胡雪岩以不平的语气说：“象她这样的人才，嫁给老古，照我看还是委屈的。至于说她脾气不好，这话要说回来，女人家心思最怪不过，只要她自己愿意，自然会改。看今天的样子，斯斯文文，大大方方，可见已经在改了！”话虽说得动听，却无结论，事实上婚姻大事，一时也不可能有什么结论，只有摆着再说，先料理第二天动身的事。

“Well, Young Uncle, what did you tell him?” “I told him to see for himself. I think they are destined for each other. We should be able to drink that wedding wine.” You shook his head emphatically. “Let it be. We shouldn't ruin a man's life.” “There's no need to put our lady down so harshly!” Hu spoke with indignation. “With her looks and abilities, I think even marrying Gu would scarcely do her justice. As for her temper, that cuts both ways. A woman's mind is a strange thing: if she herself wishes to, she will naturally change. Look at her today—refined and perfectly at ease. Clearly, she's changing already.” Persuasive though the words were, they led to no conclusion. A marriage could hardly be settled immediately in any case. They must leave it for later and first arrange the following day's departure.

下船是在中午，胡雪岩“师弟”，老张父女，加上七姑奶奶一共五个人，除去老张，各自只可促膝密谈，未便公然表露的心事，加以路上不太平，风吹草动，需要随时当心，所以就连七姑奶奶这样爱说话的人，也是保持沉默的时候居多。第二天快到松江了，胡雪岩该当作个决定，要不要七姑奶奶送到嘉兴？如果认为不需要，把她留在松江，扬帆而走，至多停泊半日，将他自己和阿珠寄在尤家的行李搬上船，否则，至少得在松江停一天，让七姑奶奶先打听消息，或者带个把可供奔走的人同行。“小爷叔！”等胡雪岩刚一提及，七姑奶奶便抢着说，“不管我送不送你，无论如何在我们那里住一天再走。”“杭州等得很急……”“急也不急在一天，我五嫂有话跟你说。”这倒奇了，尤五嫂会有什么话？就有话要说，七姑奶奶怎么会知道？凡是遇到艰难，胡雪岩总要先通前彻后想一遍，等自己想不通时再发问。

They went aboard at noon: Hu and his pupil, Old Zhang and his daughter, and the Seventh Lady—five in all. Apart from Old Zhang, each had private concerns that could be discussed only in close confidence, never openly. Moreover, the route was unsettled, and every disturbance required vigilance. Even the talkative Seventh Lady remained silent much of the time. As they approached Songjiang the following day, Hu had to decide whether she should escort them as far as Jiaxing. If unnecessary, they could leave her in Songjiang and sail on after stopping no more than half a day to collect the luggage he and A’zhu had left with the You family. Otherwise, they must stay at least a day while she gathered news and perhaps brought along someone to run errands. “Young Uncle!” As soon as he raised the matter, she interrupted. “Whether I escort you or not, you must stay a day at our house before leaving.” “They're waiting urgently in Hangzhou...” “One day won't make all the difference. Fifth Sister-in-Law has something to say to you.” That was strange. What could Mrs You want to say? And if she did have something to say, how could the Seventh Lady know? Whenever faced with a difficulty, Hu tried to reason it through from beginning to end before asking questions.

他的脑筋特别快，察言辨包，觉得只有一个可能，“七姐，”他问，“是不是你自己有话不便说，要请五嫂来问我？”七姑奶奶笑了，带些顽皮，也有些忸怩，“小爷叔，”她说：“你顶聪明。”“既然如此，你何不直接告诉我？”“还是等五嫂自己来问你的好。”这话倒象是关于尤五夫妇的事，胡雪岩有些困惑，细想一想，莫非是有关怡情老二的话？也许七姑奶奶多事，要到她嫂子那里去“告密”，所以尤五嫂会有些话要问。或者七姑奶奶倒是好心，与怡情老二投缘，在她嫂子面前下说词，劝她为夫纳妾，这样尤五嫂就更会有些话要问。同样是问，有的话可说，有的话不可说。到底是怎样的一问？先得把方向弄清楚，临事才不致窘迫。于是他问：“七姐，你晓不晓得五嫂要问我的话，是好事还是啥？”“自然是好事。”

His mind worked exceptionally quickly. Watching her expression, he could see only one possibility. “Seventh Sister, is there something you find awkward to say yourself and want Fifth Sister-in-Law to ask me?” She smiled, partly mischievous and partly shy. “Young Uncle, you are very clever.” “Then why not tell me directly?” “It would still be better to let her ask you herself.” That sounded as though it concerned You and his wife. Puzzled, Hu considered it further. Could it be about the Second Miss? Perhaps the Seventh Lady meant to meddle and report her brother's activities, giving Mrs You questions to ask. Or perhaps she intended kindness. Having taken to the Second Miss, she might persuade her sister-in-law to let her husband take the courtesan as a concubine. In that case, Mrs You would have even more to ask. Questions might be alike in form, yet some could be answered freely and others could not. What sort of inquiry awaited him? He must establish its direction beforehand, or risk being caught at a disadvantage. “Seventh Sister, do you know whether what she wants to ask concerns something good?” “Naturally.”

这下胡雪岩放心了。船抵松江，上岸直到尤家，歇一歇脚。他趁空去拜访了“老太爷”，在他那里吃了饭。再到尤家，谈不到三五句话，尤五嫂起身说道：“小爷叔，我有件事拜托你。”是拜托胡雪岩做媒，却不是为尤五娶怡情老二进门，是替七姑奶奶促成良缘。尤五嫂告诉他说，当他在裕记丝浅跟尤五密谈古应春时，七姑奶奶在外屋趁老张父女和陈世龙吃蟹吃得起劲时，悄悄在“听壁脚”，古应春的意思她已经知道了，表示非古应春不嫁。因为听出尤五似乎不赞成这头亲事，所以特为来跟嫂子谈。听完经过，胡雪岩失笑了。笑自己误解了七姑奶奶的语气，上了自己的当，如果是跟人做一笔出入甚巨的生意，也是这样子胡思乱猜，自以为是，那就非大蚀其本不可。

Hu was reassured. At Songjiang they went ashore and directly to the You house for a rest. Taking the opportunity, Hu paid a visit to the old master and dined with him. Back at the house, he had scarcely exchanged a few words when Mrs You rose. “Young Uncle, I have a favour to ask.” She wanted him to act as matchmaker. It was not, however, to bring the Second Miss into You's household, but to secure a happy marriage for the Seventh Lady. Mrs You explained that, while Hu and You had been discussing Gu privately at the Yuji Silk Warehouse, the Seventh Lady had taken advantage of the others' absorption in their crabs to listen at the wall. She knew Gu's intentions and had declared that she would marry nobody else. Having heard that her brother seemed opposed, she had come especially to discuss it with his wife. Hu laughed at himself. He had misread the Seventh Lady's tone and fallen victim to his own cleverness. If he approached a major business transaction with such wild guesses and self-assurance, he would surely lose heavily.

“小爷叔，”尤五嫂问道，“阿七怎么会认识那姓古的，好象是第一次见面，在哪里？”这一问就不易回答了，尤其是对她。诚然如尤五所说的，在堂子里见的面，这话提起来难听。再问下去：她怎么跑到了那种地方去？那又要牵涉到怡情老二，尤五这样的人，在花街柳巷走走，尤五嫂自然不会干涉，但如说是怡情老二的恩客，在外面置了“小房子”，就难保尤五嫂会不吃醋。于是他说：“在裕记丝栈。老古现在跟五哥，跟我，三个人合伙。这头亲事说起来倒也是顺理成章的事，郎有意姐有情，哪还有啥话说？至于做媒的话，不但义不容辞，而且是所谓非我莫属。不过，五嫂，我们有这样一个想法，说出来你看，对不对！”“你的话没有错的，小爷叔，你说。”

“Young Uncle,” Mrs You asked, “how did A’qi come to know this Mr Gu? It seems they had only just met. Where was it?” That was not easy to answer, especially to her. As You had said, meeting in a courtesan house sounded disgraceful. Her next question would be why the Seventh Lady had gone there, which would bring in the Second Miss. Mrs You would naturally not interfere with a man like her husband occasionally visiting the pleasure quarters. But knowing that he was the Second Miss's favoured patron and maintained a separate little house might well make her jealous. Hu therefore said, “At the Yuji Silk Warehouse. Gu, Brother Five, and I are now partners. The marriage would be quite natural. He is willing and so is she. What more is there to say? As for arranging it, I am not only bound to help; you might say nobody else is so well placed. But, Fifth Sister-in-Law, we have an idea.
