Still half in a dream, confronted by something beyond his imagining, he was utterly confused. He looked from her to the window and back again, first trying to establish whether he was awake at all.

“我盼望你好几天了！”阿七幽幽地说，同时走了过来，由暗处到亮处站住脚，拿一双水汪汪的眼睛，在陈世龙脸上瞟来瞟去。这下陈世龙才把她看清楚，脂粉未施，鬓发蓬松，但不假膏沐，却越显她的“真本钱”，白的雪白，黑的漆黑，一张嘴唇不知是不是上火的关系，红得象榴花。身上穿一件紧身黑缎夹袄，胸前鼓蓬蓬，大概连肚兜都未带。这触目惊心的一番打量，把他残余的睡意，驱除得干干净净，跳起身来，先把所有的窗子打开，然后大声说道：“你请外面坐！”“为啥？”“不方便！”“怕什么！”阿七答道，“我们规规矩矩说话，又没有做啥坏事。”“话不是这么说……”陈世龙心里十分着急，就无法跟她好好讲了，紧皱着眉，连连挥手，“你最好请回去！我这个地方你不要来。”这一说，阿七脸色大变，但愤怒多于羞惭，同时也不能期望她能够为这么一句话气走，不但不走，反倒坐了下来，冷笑说道：“小和尚，我晓得你已讨厌我了。”看样子，她要撒泼。如果换了几个月以前，他倒也不在乎她，对骂就对骂，对打就对打，如果她要哭、自己就甩手一走，反正没有她占的便宜。但现在情形不同了，这中间关碍着身分，脸面，而最要紧的是嫌疑，在郁四面前分辩不清楚，固然麻烦，若是风声传入阿珠耳中，更是件不得了的事，因而只好想办法敷衍。

“I’ve been waiting for you for days,” A’qi said plaintively. She came closer, stepping out of the shadow into the light, and let her liquid eyes move over his face. Now he could see her clearly. She wore no powder or rouge, and her hair was loose, but the lack of grooming only revealed her natural attractions more fully. The white of her skin was snowy, the black of her hair jet-black. Perhaps from excess inner heat, her lips were as red as pomegranate flowers. Her close-fitting black satin jacket swelled over her breasts; apparently she wore no bodice beneath it. This startling sight banished every remnant of sleep. He sprang up, opened all the windows and said loudly, “Please sit outside.” “Why?” “It isn’t convenient.” “What is there to fear? We’re talking properly. We haven’t done anything wrong.” “That isn’t the point...” In his anxiety, Chen could no longer explain patiently. Frowning, he waved his hand repeatedly. “You had better go home. Don’t come here.” Her face changed sharply, with more anger than shame. Nor could he expect one remark to drive her off. Instead of leaving, she sat down and sneered. “Little Monk, I know you’re tired of me now.” It looked as though she meant to make a scene. A few months earlier he would not have cared: he could answer abuse with abuse and blows with blows. If she cried, he could simply walk away. She would have gained nothing. Now matters were different. His standing and reputation were involved, and above all there was the danger of suspicion. Explaining himself to Yu Si would be troublesome enough; if word reached A’zhu, it would be disastrous. He must find some way to manage A’qi.

“不是讨厌你，是不敢惹你。”陈世龙这样答道，“你不想想你现在啥身分？我啥身分？”“你啥身分我不晓得！不过吃饭不要忘记种田人，不是我在胡老板面前替你说好话，你哪有今天？这话不是我丑表功，要你见我的情。我不过表表心，让你晓得，你老早把我抛到九霄云外，我总是时时刻刻想着你。”这番话叫陈世龙无以为答，唯有报以苦笑：“谢谢你！闲话少说，你有啥事情，灶王爷上天，直奏好了。”“不作兴来看看你，一定要有事才来？”“好了，好了！”陈世龙又不耐烦了，“你晓得郁四叔的脾气的。而且我……”他是要说，答应过胡雪岩，从此不跟她见面。但这话说出来，没意思，所以顿住了口，而阿七却毫不放松：“男了汉、大丈夫，该说就说！你有什么话说不出口。”“跟你不相干！总而言之，你来看我，我谢谢你。现在看过了，你好走了！”阿七一听这话，霍地站起身来，把脚顿两顿才骂道：“你死没良心！”她咬牙切齿的，“我偏偏不走！”

“It isn’t that I’m tired of you. I dare not get involved with you,” Chen replied. “Think of your position now, and mine.” “I don’t know what your position is! But when you eat, don’t forget the man who grew the rice. Where would you be today if I hadn’t spoken for you to Mr Hu? I’m not boasting of my services or demanding gratitude. I only want you to know what is in my heart. You forgot me long ago, but I’ve never stopped thinking of you.” Chen had no answer beyond a rueful smile. “Thank you. But enough of that. If you have business, be like the Kitchen God going up to Heaven: make your report directly.” “Can’t I come to see you? Must I have business?” “Enough!” His patience was failing again. “You know Uncle Four’s temper. Besides, I...” He had meant to say that he had promised Hu never to see her again. But there was no point in saying that, and he stopped. A’qi gave him no respite. “Be a man and say what you have to say! What can’t you bring yourself to tell me?” “Nothing that concerns you. In any case, thank you for coming to see me. Now you’ve seen me, you can leave.” At this she sprang up and stamped twice. “You heartless wretch!” she said through clenched teeth. “I won’t go!”

“你不走，我走！”陈世龙摘下衣架上的夹袍，往身上一披，低头拔鞋，连正眼都不看她。“好了，好了！”阿七软语赔罪，“何必生这么大的气？”陈世龙啼笑皆非，同时也不能再走了，因为这样要甩手一走，就会有人批评：第一欺侮女人，不算好汉，第二，说他连水晶阿七这样一个女人都应付不了。不走就得另打主意，陈世龙发过一阵脾气，此时冷静下来，觉得麻烦要找了来，推不掉就只有挺身应付，且看她说些什么？反正抱定宗旨，不理她，等她走后，再到郁四那里和盘托出，原来就要去看郁四，转达胡雪岩的口信，正好“烧香看和尚，一事两勾当”。于是他拔上鞋子再扣衣纽，阿七还来帮他的忙，低着头替他扣腋下的扣子，露出雪白了这一段头颈，正在陈世龙眼下，他把视线移了开去，但“元宝领”中的散发出来的甜甜、暖暖的香味，却叫他躲避不了。好在这只是片刻工夫，等把衣纽扣好，随即走到窗前一张凳子上坐下，预备好好应付麻烦。“我昨天刚刚到，胡先生有好些要紧的事情，叫我替他去办。县衙门里杨师爷在等我，”陈世龙先表白一段，然后提出要求说：“你有话，爽爽快快说！我实在没有工夫陪你。”

“If you won’t, I will!” Chen took his lined gown from the clothes stand and slipped it on, then bent to pull on his shoes without looking at her. “All right, all right!” She softened her voice and tried to make peace. “Why be so angry?” He did not know whether to laugh or cry. Nor could he now walk away. If he did, people would say, first, that bullying a woman was unworthy of a man, and second, that he could not even cope with Crystal A’qi. If he stayed, he must devise another approach. His fit of temper had passed. More calmly, he reflected that trouble had sought him out: if he could not push it away, he must face it and hear what she had to say. He would hold firmly to his resolve and give her no encouragement. When she left, he would tell Yu Si everything. He had to see him anyway with Hu’s message. As the saying went, burn incense and visit the monk—two errands accomplished together. Chen pulled on his shoes and began fastening his gown. A’qi came to help, lowering her head to fasten the buttons beneath his arm. A stretch of white neck lay directly under his eyes. He turned his gaze away, but could not escape the warm, sweet scent rising from her high, ingot-shaped collar. Fortunately it lasted only a moment. As soon as the buttons were fastened, he sat on a stool by the window, ready to deal with the difficulty. “I only arrived yesterday. Mr Hu has several urgent matters for me to attend to, and Secretary Yang at the county yamen is waiting for me.” Having stated his position, he made his request. “Say what you have to say plainly. I really haven’t time to keep you company.”

水晶阿七不即回答，想了好一会才说：“本来有一肚皮的话，要细细的告诉你，所以特为起个早来。既然你没有工夫，要我爽爽快快地说，我就说一句：三年前头，你跟我说过的那句话，算不算数？”提到三年前，陈世龙就知道麻烦不小，那时阿七还没有跟郁四，跟陈世尤有过一段情。情热如火时，什么话都说出来，陈世龙不知道她指的是哪句话？不过也可以想象得到，这句话在这时候来说，一定对自己不利。因此他先就来个“金钟罩”，概不认帐：“那时的话哪里好作数？”“什么？”阿七咄咄逼人地，“亏你说得出口，说了话不算数？难道你小和尚是这种没肩胛的人？”“肩胛要看摆在什么地方？”陈世龙说，“我也不知道你指的是啥？如果说，我答应过你什么，譬如买衣料、打镯子什么的，我自然有肩胛，倘或有些事情，当时做得到，现在做不到，再有肩胛的也没有办法。”“你自然做得到。”阿七说道：“你倒再想想看，你答应过我一句什么话？”“我想不起，你说好了。”“你说过，要我跟你。就是这句话！”

A’qi did not answer at once. She thought for a good while before saying, “I had a bellyful of things to tell you, every detail of them. That was why I got up specially early to come. Since you have no time, and want me to be quick and plain, I’ll ask just one thing. Three years ago you made me a promise. Does it still count?” At the mention of three years ago, Chen knew he was in serious trouble. Before A’qi had taken up with Yu Si, she and Chen had had a romance. When their passion burned hot, he had said all sorts of things. He had no idea which promise she meant, but any promise she brought up now was sure to tell against him. He therefore put on an armour of blanket denial. “How can anything said then still count?” “What?” she demanded fiercely. “Aren’t you ashamed to say that? Your word doesn’t count? Is Little Monk the sort of man who refuses to take responsibility?” “That depends on what I’m supposed to take responsibility for,” Chen said. “I don’t even know what you mean. If I promised to buy you cloth, say, or have bracelets made, of course I’ll stand by it. But if something was possible then and is impossible now, all the responsibility in the world won’t help.” “Of course it’s possible. Think again. What did you promise me?” “I can’t remember. Tell me.” “You said you wanted me to come and live with you. That was the promise!”

这句话却把陈世龙搞糊涂了，原来以为她只是想瞒着郁四来偷情，不道是这样一句话！“那怎么行！”他脱口答道，“你是郁四叔的人，怎么谈得到此？”这是陈世龙失言，他没有细想一想，如果她还是跟着郁四，怎么能说这话？阿七相当机警，捉住他这个漏洞，逼紧了问：“你是说，碍着郁老头？如果没有这重关碍，你当然还是有肩胛，说话一定算话！是不是？“话外有话，陈世龙再不敢造次，先把她前后两句话的意思细想了一遍问道：“是不是你跟郁四叔散伙了？”“对！我跟郁老头散伙了。”果有其事，陈世龙不免诧异，照他知道，郁四是一天都离不开阿七的，何以竟会散伙？莫非阿七做下什么不规矩的事，为郁四所不能容忍，赶出门去？“你奇怪是不是？”阿七神色泰然地说，“我先说一句，好叫你放心，我跟郁老头是好来好散的。”这就越发不能理解了！“是怎么回事？”他说，“我有点不大相信。”“不要说你不相信，连我自己都不大相信。不过，这也该当你我要走到这一步，真正运气来了，城墙都挡不住。”看她那种兴高采烈、一厢情愿的神气，陈世龙又好笑，又好气，本来想拦着不让她说，但这一来马上又要吵架，她如何跟郁四散伙的经过，就听不到了。因而很沉着地听她讲完，催促着说：“你闲话少说！就讲郁四叔为啥跟你散伙好了。”

This left Chen bewildered. He had assumed that she merely wanted a secret affair behind Yu Si’s back. He had never expected this. “How could that be?” he blurted out. “You’re Uncle Four’s woman. How can you even speak of it?” He had made a false step. He had not stopped to reflect that if she were still living with Yu Si she could hardly make such a proposal. A’qi was quick enough to seize the opening. “You mean Old Yu is the obstacle? Without that obstacle, of course you’d be a responsible man and keep your word. Isn’t that so?” There was something behind her words. Chen dared not answer rashly again. He considered her two remarks together, then asked, “Have you and Uncle Four parted company?” “Exactly. Old Yu and I have parted company.” So it was true. Chen was astonished. As far as he knew, Yu Si could not do without A’qi for a single day. Why should they have parted? Had she behaved so badly that he could not tolerate her and had driven her out? “You’re surprised, aren’t you?” she said calmly. “Let me put your mind at rest. Old Yu and I parted on good terms.” This was more incomprehensible still. “What happened? I find it rather hard to believe.” “Never mind you—I can hardly believe it myself. But it must have been fated that you and I should come to this. When good fortune arrives, even a city wall can’t keep it out.” Her cheerful certainty that everything would turn out as she wished both amused and irritated Chen. He wanted to cut her short, but that would start another quarrel, and he would never learn how she and Yu Si had separated. He listened patiently to the end, then urged, “Never mind all that. Just tell me why Uncle Four parted with you.”

“嗨！提起来，真是说书先生的口头禅：”六月里冻杀一只老绵羊，说来话长！‘“说到这里，阿七的神色忽显哀伤，”你晓不晓得，阿虎死掉了？“陈世龙大惊：“什么？阿虎死掉了，怎么死的？”“绞肠痧！可怜，八月十四下半天得的病，一夜工夫就‘翘’掉了，连个节都过不过！”陈世龙听得傻了，眼中慢慢流出两滴眼泪。郁四生一子一女，阿虎就是他的独子，今年才二十二岁，去年娶的亲。为人忠厚，极重义气，跟陈世龙也算是要好弟兄，尤其因为他父亲不准陈世龙上门，他似乎倒怀着歉意，所以对陈世龙格外另眼相看，三天两头不是来邀他听书、吃酒，就是来问问要不要铜钿用？这样一个好朋友，一别竟成永诀，陈世龙自然要伤心。但是，他的这两滴眼泪，在阿七看来，却别有会心，越觉得好事可成，因为这可以看出，陈世龙是有良心，重感情的。

“Ah! As the storytellers say, ‘An old ram froze to death in the sixth month—a long tale lies behind it!’” Her expression suddenly turned sorrowful. “Do you know that A’hu is dead?” Chen was horrified. “What? A’hu dead? How did he die?” “A sudden intestinal illness. Poor fellow! He fell ill on the afternoon of the fourteenth day of the eighth month and was gone overnight. He didn’t even live to see the festival.” Chen sat stunned, and slowly two tears rolled from his eyes. Yu Si had a daughter and one son. A’hu, his only boy, was just twenty-two and had married the year before. Honest, kind and deeply loyal to his friends, he and Chen had been close as brothers. Because his father forbade Chen to visit their house, A’hu had seemed almost apologetic and had treated him with particular consideration. Every few days he came to invite him to a storytelling performance or out for a drink, or simply to ask whether he needed spending money. To think that when they had last parted, he had been saying farewell for ever to such a friend! Naturally Chen grieved. A’qi, however, found another meaning in those two tears. They showed that he had a conscience and deep feelings, and made her all the more hopeful that her own wish would come true.

“你也不要难过。死了，死了，死啦就了掉了！”阿七停一下说，“我跟郁老头散伙，就是因为阿虎死了，才起的因头。阿虎不死，将来他老子的家当，归他独得，哪个也不能说话，阿虎一死，又没有留下一儿半女，你想想看，自然有人要动脑筋了。你晓得是哪个动脑筋？”陈世龙摇摇头，方在哀伤之际，懒得去想，也懒得说话。“一说破，你就不会奇怪了，是阿兰姐夫妇！”阿兰姐是郁四的大女儿，今年快三十了，是个极厉害的角色，年前，郁四跟他的同事，一个姓邢的刑房书办结了亲家。老书办是世袭的行当，老邢去世，小邢进衙门当差，比他老了干得还出色，又可知是如何厉害的角色呢？这对夫妇凑在一起，图谋回娘家来夺产，自是不足为奇之事。陈世龙因为跟阿虎的交情，此时便想到阿虎嫂的将来，不由得愤愤说道：“阿兰姐是嫁出去的人，她凭啥来动脑筋呢？”“就是这话罗！‘嫁出去的女儿，泼出去的水’，本来没啥脑筋好动，说来说去，是阿兰姐和她男人厉害，没事找事，脑筋动到了我头上。”“怎么呢？”陈世龙有些想不通，“跟你啥相干？”“怎么不相干？如果我替郁老头养个儿子，他们还有啥脑筋好动，所以把我看成眼中钉。你懂了吧？”“懂是懂了！”陈世龙摇摇头，“我就不懂郁四叔，怎么肯放你走？”

“Don’t take it so hard. Dead is dead, and once you’re dead, it’s all over.” A’qi paused. “It was A’hu’s death that led to my parting with Old Yu. If A’hu had lived, he alone would have inherited everything, and nobody could have said a word. But he died without leaving a child. Think of it! Naturally somebody began to scheme. Do you know who?” Chen shook his head. In his grief he had no wish either to think or to talk. “Once I tell you, you won’t be surprised. Sister A’lan and her husband!” A’lan was Yu Si’s eldest daughter, nearly thirty and a formidable woman. Earlier, Yu Si had married her to the son of a colleague named Xing, a clerk in the criminal office. The old clerks passed their occupation from father to son. When Old Xing died, Young Xing entered the yamen and proved still more capable than his father. One could imagine what a formidable character he was too. It was hardly surprising that this pair should scheme to seize the property of her family. Remembering his friendship with A’hu, Chen began to worry about the young widow’s future. “Sister A’lan has married out of the family,” he said indignantly. “What right has she to scheme for it?” “Exactly! ‘A married daughter is like water poured away.’ There was nothing for her to get. But she and her husband are clever. They invented a problem and turned their schemes on me.” “How?” Chen could not understand. “What had it to do with you?” “How could it have nothing to do with me? If I bore Old Yu a son, what could they hope to get? That made me a thorn in their eyes. Do you see?” “I see that,” Chen said, shaking his head. “What I don’t see is why Uncle Four was willing to let you go.”

“哼！”阿七冷笑道，“你当郁老头是什么有良心的人？年纪一大把，‘色’得比哪个都厉害。你道他那宝贝女儿怎么跟他说？”“我想不出。总归是郁四叔听得进去的话。”“自然罗！说给他另外买人，又年轻、又漂亮，老色鬼还有啥听不进去。”照阿七打听来的消息是如此：阿兰姐劝她父亲，说阿七过了两三年，没有喜信，就不会有喜信了，风尘出身的，“凉药”吃得多，根本不能生育。没有儿子，只能在族中替阿虎嫂过继一个，偌大家产，将来白白便宜了别人。最好的办法，莫如买两个宜男之相的年轻女人做侍妾，必有得子之望。讲到这里，陈世龙插了一句嘴：“什么，还要买两个？”“是啊，怕一个不保险，多弄一个。”阿七用讥嘲的口风说：“有这样孝顺的女儿，做老子的，当然艳福不浅！”“我懂了。买这两个人，一定归阿兰姐经手，他们夫妇就从这上头一步一步踏进来，把持一切。不过，”陈世龙说，“又何必把你看成眼中钉？”“他们怕我坏她的事。在郁老头面前说，我会吃醋，搅得家宅不安。最最气不过的是，”阿七咬牙切齿地说，“自己做贼，赖人做贼，说我一定会勾引了外面的野汉子，来谋他郁家的财产，小和尚你想想，这种女人，心毒不毒？”

“Hmph!” A’qi sneered. “Do you imagine Old Yu has a conscience? At his age he’s more lustful than anyone. Do you know what his precious daughter told him?” “I can’t imagine. Something he wanted to hear, no doubt.” “Of course! She would buy him other women, young and pretty. What was there in that for the lecherous old man to object to?” According to what A’qi had learned, A’lan had told her father that, since A’qi had failed to become pregnant in two or three years, she never would. Women from the pleasure quarters took so much ‘cooling medicine’ that they could not bear children. Without a son, they would have to adopt a boy from the clan as an heir for A’hu’s widow, and all that property would eventually enrich someone else. The best course was to buy two young concubines whose appearance promised sons. Then there would surely be hope of an heir. At this point Chen interrupted. “What? Two of them?” “Yes. One might not be enough, so he must have another for insurance.” Her voice was mocking. “With such a dutiful daughter, a father can certainly expect plenty of female favours!” “I understand. Sister A’lan would choose and buy them, of course. From there, she and her husband could move in step by step and take control of everything. But why did they have to make an enemy of you?” “They were afraid I’d spoil their plans. They told Old Yu I’d be jealous and turn the household upside down. And the most infuriating thing of all,” she added through clenched teeth, “was that the thieves called someone else a thief! They said I’d be sure to seduce some lover outside and bring him in to steal the Yu family fortune. Little Monk, tell me—could any woman be more vicious?”

话说到这里，全盘情况，皆已了解，郁四听了女儿的话，决定跟阿七散伙。既说“好来好散”自然有一笔钱可拿，照郁四的手面，这笔钱还不会少，没有五千，也有三千。只不知道阿七自郁家下堂以后，是不是重张艳帜？不过，他心里虽然存疑，而且好奇心驱使，得问个明白，却终于不曾开口，因为他要表示出事不干已，不闻不问的态度，好让阿七自己识趣，知难而退。阿七却决不会如他的愿，“现在谈到正事上头来了。”她说：“小和尚，我随郁老头唱了半出‘乌龙院’，他走他的清秋大路，我也没有什么麻烦好找他的。走的时候，总算客客气气，房子是他买的，早已过户到我名下，所以该他搬出，另外给了我一个他钱庄里的折子，数目是五千两，只能取息，不能动本，这以后再说了，是我名下的铜钿，我当然要提出来。他识相的，拉倒，不识相我要打官司，好在王大老爷跟胡老板是好朋友……““慢慢！”陈世龙当头泼她的冷水：“你不要做梦！人家胡老板跟郁四叔等于弟兄一样，打到官司，一定帮他不帮你！”“那就不要他帮！”阿七答得极爽利，“我自己到堂上去告，说他那爿钱庄要‘倒灶’了，我不相信他，可以不可以？”陈世龙为她那种自说自话的神态逗得笑了，“都随你！”他说，“你跟阿兰姐一样，都算是厉害角色！”

The whole picture was now clear. Yu Si had listened to his daughter and decided to part with A’qi. Since they had parted on good terms, she must have received a settlement, and, given his generous habits, it could hardly have been small: if not five thousand taels, then at least three thousand. Chen wondered whether, after leaving Yu, she intended to return to her former profession. Curious as he was, he refrained from asking. He wanted to appear wholly unconcerned, neither asking nor listening, so that she would take the hint and withdraw. But A’qi had no intention of obliging him. “Now we come to the real business,” she said. “Little Monk, Old Yu and I have acted out half of The Black Dragon Courtyard. He can go his own open road, and I have no quarrel to pursue with him. We parted quite civilly. He bought the house, but he had already transferred it to my name, so he was the one who had to move out. He also gave me a passbook for five thousand taels at his bank. I can draw the interest, but not the principal. We’ll see about that later. It’s money in my name, and naturally I mean to withdraw it. If he sees sense, well and good. If not, I’ll sue. Luckily, Prefect Wang and Mr Hu are close friends...” “Wait!” Chen threw cold water over this at once. “Don’t dream of it! Mr Hu and Uncle Four are practically brothers. If you sue, he’ll help him, not you.” “Then I don’t need his help!” she answered readily. “I’ll go into court myself and say his bank is about to fail and I don’t trust him. Can I withdraw it then or can’t I?” Her confidence that everything would happen just as she wished made Chen laugh. “Have it your own way! You and Sister A’lan are both formidable women.”

“我啥厉害？做人全靠心好！象阿兰姐，哼，也是到现在没有儿子，将来有苦头吃。这都不去说它了。”话到此处，阿七的神情变得郑重而兴奋，“小和尚，从我跟郁老头分手，就有好些上门来打我的主意，都叫我回绝掉了，不识相的，我就爽爽快快的把他骂了出去。我平日都不出门，出门就是去打听你的消息。我一直在守你，今天总算守到了。你先搬到我那里去住，有话我们慢慢再说，”长篇大套，自说自话完了，一只手就搭了过来，按在陈世龙肩膀上，同时一双俏伶伶的眼睛瞟着，是恨不得弄碗水来，把他一口吞了下去的神气。陈世龙并不觉得好笑，是着急，没有想到她一厢情愿到痴的程度！照此看来，只怕她跟郁四过了两三年日子，心里是对他想了两三年，牵丝攀藤这么多日子下来，要想好好摆脱是无论如何办不到的事。那么怎么办呢？“说嘛！”她又催促，“啥辰光搬？我那里通通现成，不象你这里，一早起来，要茶要水，什么都没。洗个脸都要到茶店里去。这种光棍打流的日子，你自己想想看，苦不苦？”不对了！就这片刻工夫，又是结结实实的一根藤缠了上来，这样下去，非让她捆得动弹不得不可。陈世龙心想，只有快刀一挥，才能斩断纠葛，这在她自己受不了，但为了自保，不能不下辣手。“阿七！我骗你我天诛地灭！”他先罚个咒，让她知道决非设词推托：“小和尚老早有小厄姑了！”

“What’s formidable about me? All that matters is having a good heart. As for A’lan—hmph! She has no son herself yet. She’ll have trouble enough in years to come. But never mind all that.” A’qi grew earnest and excited. “Little Monk, since Old Yu and I parted, plenty of men have come with designs on me. I turned them all away. If they wouldn’t take the hint, I simply cursed them out of the house. I hardly ever go out. When I do, it’s to ask for news of you. I’ve been waiting and waiting, and today I’ve finally found you. Move in with me first. We can talk everything over at leisure.” Having settled the matter to her own satisfaction in this long speech, she reached out and laid a hand on Chen’s shoulder. Her lively eyes played over him, as though she longed for a bowl of water to wash him down whole. Chen found nothing amusing in this. He was alarmed. He had never imagined her wishful thinking could reach such a pitch of obsession. Perhaps throughout her two or three years with Yu Si she had been thinking of Chen all the time. If she had been winding these tendrils around him for so long, there could be no gentle way to break free. What was he to do? “Tell me!” she urged. “When will you move? Everything’s ready at my place. Not like here, where you get up in the morning and there’s neither tea nor water. You even have to go to a teashop to wash your face. Think what a miserable life it is, drifting about as a bachelor!” This would never do. In those few moments another stout vine had wrapped itself around him. At this rate she would bind him so tightly he could not move. Only one swift cut could sever the tangle. It would hurt her badly, but to save himself he must be ruthless. “A’qi, may Heaven destroy me if I’m lying!” He began with an oath, to show that this was no excuse. “Little Monk already has his Little Nun!”

阿七的脸色大变，眼猜倒还是水汪汪的，不过象含了两泡泪水，脸上一阵青、一阵白，摇摇头说：“我不相信！是哪个？”“张家的阿珠。”“哪个张家的阿珠？”“原来摇船，现在开大经丝行的……”“你在说啥！”阿七打断了他的话，显得十分困惑地，愣了好半天才说：“我还是不相信，摇船老张的女儿，不是胡老板的人吗？”“你完全弄错了！人家是把阿珠当女儿看，哪里有啥别的意思？”陈世龙又说，“就是这趟到上海，胡老板替我定下的亲事。聘礼都送过去，四样首饰，也是胡老板买的。总在今年年底，就要请大家吃喜酒。”言之凿凿，不象撒谎，把阿七听得目瞪口呆，背脊上一阵阵发凉，颓然坐倒，只是喃喃地说，“有这种事情？想都想不到的！”“就是罗！”陈世龙此时如释重负，“就象你跟郁四叔散伙一样，也是想都想不到的。”“不过……”阿七霍地站了起来，仿佛犹不死心，最后还想跟阿珠争夺一番似地，但是力不从心，终于气馁。

A’qi’s face changed completely. Her eyes were still liquid, but now they seemed full of tears. Her face turned pale and ashen by turns. She shook her head. “I don’t believe it. Who?” “A’zhu, from the Zhang family.” “Which Zhang family?” “The one who used to work a boat and now runs the Dajing Silk Firm...” “What are you saying?” She broke in, utterly bewildered, and stared for a long moment before continuing. “I still don’t believe it. Isn’t the old boatman Zhang’s daughter Mr Hu’s woman?” “You’ve got it all wrong. He treats A’zhu as a daughter. He never meant anything else.” Chen went on, “He arranged the match for me on this trip to Shanghai. The betrothal gifts have already been sent—four kinds of jewellery, bought by Mr Hu himself. We’ll be inviting everyone to the wedding feast before the year is out.” He spoke with such assurance that it did not sound like a lie. A’qi was dumbfounded. Chills ran down her back, and she sank into a chair, muttering, “Such a thing! I could never have imagined it.” “Exactly.” Chen felt an enormous weight lift from him. “Just like you and Uncle Four parting. Nobody could have imagined that either.” “But...” A’qi suddenly rose, as though she still refused to admit defeat and meant to make one last attempt to wrest him from A’zhu. Yet she had no strength for it, and her courage failed.

“阿七！”陈世龙安慰她说，“人都是缘分。我们缘分不到，没有话说。你也不要难过，象你这样的人，不怕没人要。“他又说：”你的心好，好心自有好报。你请回去吧，我送你回去。“阿七象斗败了的公鸡似地，垂头不语，慢慢站起身来，脸上浑不似初来时那种芍药带露、艳光逼人的神采，气色灰暗，倒象一下子老了十年。陈世龙瞻念旧情，不能无动于衷，但怜念一生，马上又感到双肩都有沉重的压力，一只肩上是与阿珠偕老的盟约，想到在船上跪在她面前求婚所许下的诺言，一只肩膀上是胡雪岩的情分，想到他提携爱护，待自己嫡亲的子弟，亦不过如此，自己何能去找这种一沾上便摆不开的麻烦，以致耗神废业，辜负了他的期望？这样一转念，他的心肠便又硬了。对阿七的神情，视如不见，走出巷，招手喊过一顶小轿来，同时早就拈了块只多不少的碎银子在手里，等轿子抬到，他把碎银子递了过去，交代了阿七的住处，使往旁边一站，意思是等她上轿。“小和尚！”阿七这样喊了一声，欲言又止，只拿忧郁而惶惑的眼色看着他。“你回去吧！”陈世龙觉得要有句话，哪怕是敷衍的话，也得说一句，才能叫她上轿，因而顺口又说：“有空我来看你！”阿七点点头，脸上有着感激的意味，移步从放倒的轿杠上跨了进去，回身倒退着进轿时，又是深深地一瞥，为陈世龙留下来无数幽怨。

“A’qi,” Chen said soothingly, “everything depends on fate. We weren’t meant for each other, and there’s nothing to be done. Don’t be unhappy. A woman like you need never fear that nobody will want her. You have a good heart, and a good heart gets its reward. Go home now. I’ll see you off.” She hung her head like a defeated fighting cock and slowly rose without a word. None of the dazzling freshness of her arrival, like a peony wet with dew, remained. Her face was dull and grey; she seemed to have aged ten years in an instant. Remembering their old affection, Chen could not remain unmoved. But as soon as pity stirred, he felt a heavy weight on each shoulder. On one rested his pledge to grow old with A’zhu, the promises he had made as he knelt before her on the boat and asked her to marry him. On the other rested his debt to Hu Xueyan, who had encouraged and protected him as generously as if he had been his own flesh and blood. How could he seek out a trouble that, once entangled in it, he would never shake off, wasting his energies, neglecting his work and disappointing Hu’s hopes? At this thought his heart hardened again. Ignoring A’qi’s dejection, he went out of the alley and hailed a small sedan chair. He already had a piece of silver in his hand, more than enough for the fare. When the chair arrived, he gave it to the bearers, told them her address and stood aside, waiting for her to get in. “Little Monk!” she said, then stopped, looking at him in melancholy bewilderment. “Go home.” He felt that he must say something, however empty, to persuade her to enter, and added without thinking, “I’ll come and see you when I have time.” She nodded gratefully and stepped over the lowered poles. Turning to back into the chair, she gave him one last deep look, leaving him burdened with all her unspoken sorrow.

这时太阳已经很高了，十月小阳春，阳光明亮，照得人有些目，陈世龙觉得有些晕淘淘，信步踏进一爿小茶店，洗脸喝茶点心，静静坐了一会，脑子才算完全清醒。想想这天该做的事，第一件就是到阿虎灵前一拜，同时把胡雪岩的话交代了郁四。于是他取钱托茶博士办来一份素烛清香，往北门郁四的老家走了去。进门就淌眼泪，一路淌到灵前，焚烛上香，拜罢起身，只见阿兰头上簪一朵白花，手扶在一个小丫头的肩上，袅袅婷婷地走了出来。一见了面少不得又是“流泪眼观流眼泪”，阿兰姐一面抹眼泪，一面为陈世龙说阿虎得病的经过。接着又说她父亲晚年丧子，家门如何不幸，然后再谈阿七，指她不安于室，又说阿七日夜吵着要进郁家的门，不但进门，还要做阿虎嫂的婆婆，要给她磕头。“小和尚，你想想看！这是做不做得到的事情？”阿兰姐说，“明晓得做不列，天天又哭又闹，她打的是什么主意？还不是一想就明白！所以大家都劝爹，放她走路算了，这件事提来鸭屎臭，你见了我爹，不必说起。免得他老人家心里不舒服。”照她说来，是阿七不对。不过陈世龙也不尽相信她的话，只觉得事不关己。不必多问，所以点点头说：“我晓得了。四叔是不是在茶店里？”“是啊！”阿兰说，“你昨天叫人送了胡老板的礼来，他才晓得你回来了。一早就要到碧浪春去等你。你就到那里去看他吧！”

The sun was high by now. In this brief return of spring in the tenth month, its bright light was almost dazzling, and Chen felt rather dazed. He wandered into a little teashop, washed his face and had tea and something to eat. Only after sitting quietly for a while did his mind become fully clear. He considered the day’s business. First he must pay his respects before A’hu’s spirit tablet and deliver Hu’s message to Yu Si. He gave the tea attendant money to buy plain candles and incense, then walked to Yu Si’s family home near the north gate. Tears began to flow as he entered, and continued all the way to the mourning altar. He lit the candles and incense and bowed. As he rose, A’lan appeared, a white flower pinned in her hair, walking gracefully with one hand resting on a little maid’s shoulder. At their meeting, each looked through tears at the other’s tearful face. Wiping her eyes, A’lan told him how A’hu had fallen ill. She spoke of their family’s misfortune, and of her father losing his son in old age. Then she turned to A’qi, accusing her of being restless and unfaithful. A’qi, she said, had clamoured day and night to enter the Yu family household. Nor was that all: she wanted to become A’hu’s widow’s mother-in-law and have the young woman kowtow to her. “Little Monk, think! Was such a thing possible? She knew perfectly well it wasn’t, yet every day she cried and made scenes. What was she after? One moment’s thought makes it plain. We all urged Father to let her go. The whole affair stinks of duck dung. Don’t mention it when you see him. It will only upset him.” In her account, A’qi was to blame. Chen did not entirely believe her, but it was no affair of his and there was no need to ask further. He nodded. “I understand. Is Uncle Four at the teahouse?” “Yes. When you sent over Mr Hu’s gifts yesterday, he learned you were back. He went to Bilangchun early this morning to wait for you. Go and see him there.”

到了碧浪春，只见郁四仍旧坐在马头桌子上，人瘦了不少。陈世龙叫过一声：“四叔”，相顾黯然。“你昨天到的？”郁四有气没力地说。“是的。昨天下半天到的。”说了这一句话，陈世龙忽然转到一个念头，在“家门”里，他的“前人”跟郁四是“同参”，师父一死，郁四就算嫡亲的长辈，为了阿七不准自己上门，并不是不照应自己，起码胡雪岩这条路子就是从这位长辈身上来的，“家门”里讲究饮水思源，“引见”之恩不可忘。照此说来，昨天一到，应该先去看他，自己是走错了一步，尤其这天早晨，阿七又来密访，“光棍心多，麻布筋多”，如果郁四把这两件事摆在一起想一想，搞出什么误会来，那就“跳到黄河洗不清”了！所以正好趁此刻先作一个不着痕迹的解释。于是他说：“四叔！昨天一到，我就先要给你老人家来请安的，哪晓得一到了老丈人那里，硬给他们留住了。”这段话有两层用意，一是解释他所以昨天一到未去看郁四的原因，二是表示他已经定了亲，决不会再跟阿七搅七念三。然而郁四却有些莫名其妙，“你说啥？”他问“啥个老丈人？你几时定的亲，怎么我不晓得？”“湖州还没有人晓得，是这趟胡先生作主替我定下的。”“噢！”郁四显然自这喜讯中，受到了鼓舞，失神的双眼，有了闪闪的亮光，“好极！是哪一家的姑娘？”“这话说来很长，也很有趣，四叔万万想不到的。”陈世龙先宕开一句：“ 胡先生还有他自己的事情，要我跟四叔谈。”这话郁四明白，自然是头寸上的事，于是他站起身来说：“这里人来人往，静不下来。走，到聚成去！”

At Bilangchun, Yu Si sat at his usual horse-head table. He had grown much thinner. Chen greeted him as “Uncle Four,” and they looked at one another sadly. “You arrived yesterday?” Yu asked listlessly. “Yes. Yesterday afternoon.” As he said this, a thought struck Chen. Within their brotherhood, his initiating master had been Yu Si’s fellow initiate. Since the master’s death, Yu counted as his closest elder. Forbidding him to visit because of A’qi did not mean that Yu had ceased to look after him. At the very least, it was through this elder that he had come to know Hu Xueyan. In the brotherhood, a man must remember the spring from which he drank: the favour of an introduction must never be forgotten. He should therefore have called on Yu as soon as he arrived yesterday. That had been a mistake. Worse still, A’qi had paid him a secret visit this morning. ‘A crafty fellow has as many suspicions as hemp has fibres.’ If Yu put the two things together and misunderstood, Chen could never wash himself clean, even in the Yellow River. Here was his chance to explain without appearing to do so. “Uncle Four, the moment I arrived yesterday I meant to come and pay my respects. But once I reached my father-in-law’s, they insisted on keeping me.” This served two purposes: it explained his failure to visit the previous day, and announced that he was engaged and would no longer become entangled with A’qi. Yu, however, was bewildered. “What are you saying? What father-in-law? When did you get engaged? Why didn’t I know?” “Nobody in Huzhou knows yet. Mr Hu arranged it for me on this trip.” “Oh!” The good news visibly heartened Yu. His dull eyes began to shine. “Splendid! Whose daughter is she?” “It’s a long story, and an interesting one. You’d never guess, Uncle Four.” Chen put him off for the moment. “Mr Hu also has some business of his own for me to discuss with you.” Yu understood: naturally, it concerned funds. He stood up. “People are always coming and going here. There’s no peace. Come along to Jucheng.”

聚成钱庄中，特为给郁四预备了一个房间，他有许多衙门里的公事，都在这里处理。这天却是清闲无事，陈世龙从容细谈，先把胡雪岩在上海、杭州的情形，大致说了一遍，最后谈到他头寸的话。郁四跟胡雪岩是有约定的，阜康代为放款，比同行拆息还便宜，照一般放款利息折半计算，当然也不需要什么担保。郁四把聚成的档手喊了进来，一问可以调拨三万银子，便即关照，马上汇到杭州阜康。

Jucheng Bank kept a room especially for Yu Si, and he dealt with much of his official business there. Today, however, he was free. Chen Shilong could talk at leisure. He first gave a general account of Hu Xueyan's affairs in Shanghai and Hangzhou, then came to his need for funds. Yu and Hu already had an arrangement: Fukang lent out Yu's money and paid him half the interest charged to its borrowers—a cost lower even than the interbank rate—and naturally no security was required. Yu called in Jucheng's manager. On learning that thirty thousand taels could be made available, he instructed him to remit the money to Fukang in Hangzhou immediately.

谈完“公事”，陈世龙谈私事，把胡雪岩对阿珠的用心及处置，从头细叙。郁四觉得比听书还要有味，从烟榻听到饭桌上，再由饭桌听到烟榻上。听完说道：“老胡这个人，真要佩服他！做出来的事，别出心裁，真正漂亮！”“四叔，”陈世龙说，“喜事总在年底，那时候发帖子，要你老人家替我出面。”“那当然！”说到这里，长叹一声：“你倒好了……”这自是触景生情，想起阿虎，陈世龙赶紧说道：“四叔，你老人家不要难过！阿虎不在了，还有我侍奉你老人家。”一听这话，郁四的眼圈红了，也不知是伤子还是为陈世龙而感动？但终于强自振作起来，“小和尚！”他说，“你晓得的，我这个做四叔的，也有对不起你的地方，现在事情过去了，也不必多说了。你现在成家立业，朝正路上走去，我高兴得很，亲事自然我来出面，一切都是我的。那四样首饰，你打听打听看，老胡是花多少银子办的，我来还他。有我在，这笔聘礼不好叫他出。”

Their business concluded, Chen turned to his private affairs and recounted, from the beginning, Hu's intentions and arrangements concerning A’zhu. Yu found it more entertaining than a storyteller's performance. He listened on the opium couch, continued listening at the dining table, and returned to the couch for more. When Chen finished, he said, “You have to admire Old Hu! The things he does are so original, and so beautifully managed.” “Uncle Four, the wedding should be towards the end of the year. When we send out invitations, I'll need you to represent me.” “Naturally!” He gave a long sigh. “Things have turned out well for you...” The occasion had evidently brought A’hu to mind. Chen hastened to say, “Don't grieve, Uncle Four. A’hu is gone, but I'm still here to look after you.” Yu's eyes reddened. Whether from grief for his son or gratitude to Chen, it was hard to tell. At last he forced himself to rally. “Little Monk, you know I've wronged you in some ways. That's past, and we needn't say more. Now you're establishing a home and a livelihood and taking the proper road. I'm delighted. Of course I'll represent you in the marriage, and I'll take responsibility for everything. Find out how much Old Hu paid for those four kinds of jewellery. I'll repay him. With me here, he ought not to pay for your betrothal gifts.”

陈世龙自然感激。但他虽只跟了胡雪岩短短一段日子，因为人既聪明灵活，又是衷心受教，人情世故的阅历上，大非昔比，此时心里在想，自己是出于一番至诚，安慰长辈，而郁四居然拿自己当亲人看待，原是好事，但郁家迟早要闹家务，阿兰姐正在动娘家的脑筋，自己再受郁四的好处，叫别人看来，仿佛他也是乘虚而入，在打郁四的主意，这个嫌疑不可不避。避嫌疑犹是小事，眼前看样子是阿兰姐在替郁四当家，买那四样首饰也要千两银子，由郁四捧出来还给胡雪岩，阿兰姐知道了，心里先将不舒服，闲话可就多了！“怎么？”郁四见他不作声，倒真有困惑了，“那还有什么话说？”陈世龙已决定辞谢郁四的好意，不过这话不知如何措词？经他一逼，只好这样答道：“四叔！不是我不识拾举，我是想争口气，这件事我要自己来办。为来为去也是为四叔争气，说起来，四叔可以告诉人家，小和尚是自己讨的亲，我要替他出聘礼，他用不着。这不是四叔也有面子。”

Naturally Chen was grateful. Yet, brief as his time with Hu had been, his intelligence, adaptability, and wholehearted willingness to learn had greatly advanced his understanding of the world. He had sincerely meant to comfort an elder; now Yu was treating him as family. That was good in itself. But trouble would come sooner or later within Yu's household, and Sister A’lan was already scheming about her parents' property. If he accepted benefits now, people might think he too was taking advantage of Yu's vulnerability. He must avoid that suspicion. Even that was a lesser concern. A’lan appeared to be managing Yu's household now. The four kinds of jewellery would cost a thousand taels; if Yu paid that sum back to Hu, A’lan would be displeased as soon as she heard, and there would be no end of talk. “Well?” Yu was puzzled by his silence. “What is there to say about it?” Chen had decided to decline but could not find the words. Pressed, he answered, “Uncle Four, it isn't that I fail to appreciate your kindness. I want to prove myself and manage this myself. Ultimately, that will do you credit too. You'll be able to tell people that Little Monk paid for his own marriage. You offered to provide the betrothal gifts, but he didn't need it. Won't that give you something to be proud of?”

江湖上讲究面子，也看重“人贵自立”这句话，尤其是做长辈的，听他这样说，自然要嘉许，“你这两句话，我听了倒高兴。不过，”郁四又以告诫的语气说，“你刚刚出道，不要别的本事没有学会，先学会说大话。那就不对了！”“我是实实在在的话。尤其是在四叔面前，说大话算哪一出？”“那么，我倒问你。”郁四很认真地，“你哪里来的钱讨亲？你不是说四样首饰是老胡替你买的吗？”“是啊！胡先生替我垫银子买的，将来我分了花红可以还他。如果是四叔替我出了这笔钱，将来我说拿了来还四叔，不是要挨骂了吗？”“那也一样。你有了钱也可以孝敬孝敬我的！”“那还用说？我有了钱不孝敬四叔，把哪个用？不过眼前要请四叔，帮我做过面子争口气，一切让我自己来。”听了他的话，郁四又高兴、又困扰，高兴的是他前面那两句话，就算是米汤，心里也舒服。困扰的是后面那两句话，不管他，让他自己去料理，是帮他争气做面子，出钱替他办喜事，反倒不是！这成何话说。

In their world, standing mattered, and so did the saying that a man should support himself. An elder could hardly withhold approval. “I'm pleased to hear you say that. But...” Yu's tone became admonitory. “You're only just starting out. Don't learn to boast before you learn anything else. That wouldn't do.” “I'm speaking honestly. What would be the point of boasting, especially before you?” “Then let me ask you seriously: where will you get the money to marry? Didn't you say Old Hu bought the jewellery for you?” “Yes. Mr Hu advanced the money. I can repay him from my share of the profits later. If you provided the money, wouldn't you scold me when I tried to pay you back?” “It's all the same. When you have money, you can show your respect for me too.” “Of course! If I don't honour you with it, whom should I spend it on? For now, though, please help me keep my pride and prove myself. Let me manage everything.” Yu was both pleased and perplexed. The first part delighted him: even if it was flattery, it felt good. The second troubled him. Leaving Chen to his own devices would help him prove himself and preserve his standing; paying for his wedding would apparently do the opposite! What sort of reasoning was that?

虽不成话，却驳不倒！郁四把头往后仰一仰，打量了陈世龙一番，拿签子指指点点地说：“两三个月不见，我看你是变过了！长衫上身，倒也蛮象个‘大二先生’的样子，说两句话，异出异样，比上头的‘官腔’还要难应付。这都是你从老胡那里学来的？”其词若憾，其实深喜，陈世龙笑笑不答，站起身来说：“四叔，我还有几桩事情，等着要去接头。明天再来看你老人家。”“明天到我家来，北门！”郁四特地交代明白，接着又叹口气，“唉，这一阵的日子，不是人过的，今天见了你，心里好过得多。你晚上有空，最好再来一趟，我还有些话要告诉你，如果今天晚上没空，明天上午一定来，茶店里我这一向也少去，今天是为了等你，不然我也就在家里孵孵算了，衙门里的差使，我都想辞掉。没有意思！”说着，摇头不止。郁四居然连世袭的差使，都不想要了，可知心境灰恶。陈世龙于心不忍，颇想再陪他坐一会，说些夷场上有趣的见闻，为他遣愁破闷，无奈这一夭，从水晶阿七来访开始，已经耽误了太多的工夫，不得不走，去办正事。

Unreasonable though it sounded, Yu could not refute it. Leaning back, he studied Chen and pointed at him with the opium needle. “I haven't seen you for two or three months, and you've changed! In that long gown, you look quite like a senior business clerk. And the things you say are so extraordinary that they're harder to answer than an official pronouncement from above. Did you learn all this from Old Hu?” He sounded regretful but was secretly delighted. Chen merely smiled, then stood. “Uncle Four, I have several matters to attend to. I'll come and see you again tomorrow.” “Come to my house tomorrow—the North Gate house.” Yu made the address quite clear, then sighed again. “These days have been unbearable. Seeing you today has made me feel much better. If you're free tonight, do come again. I have more to tell you. If you can't come tonight, you must come tomorrow morning. I seldom go to the tea shop now. I went today only to wait for you. Otherwise I'd have stayed brooding at home. I even think of giving up my post at the yamen. There's no point!” He shook his head repeatedly. That Yu could contemplate abandoning even his hereditary position showed how despondent he had become. Chen felt sorry for him and wanted to stay, entertaining him with interesting stories of the foreign settlement. But the day had already been delayed too long, beginning with Crystal A’qi's visit. He had to leave and attend to business.

等一个圈子兜下来，把胡雪岩交代的事情办妥，已是近夕照黄昏，匆匆赶到大经丝行，只见黄仪迎着他说道：“你丈母娘刚走，把你的房间铺陈好，还等了好一歇辰光，看看你不来，只好回去。临走千叮万嘱，一定要你到家吃饭。丈母娘待女婿，真正是没话说。”“我心里也急。”陈世龙有些不安。“实在是分不开身，现在也还不能去，我想先给胡先生写封信，好趁早叫航船带出。”“晚上回来写也不迟。好在你今天总要住在这里。”“不！”陈世龙觉得住在大经，便好似“入赘”一般，有骨气的男子汉是不肯做赘婿住在岳家的，因而很坚决地表示：“我还是住在我自己那里。”黄仪了解他的用心，点点头说：“这也随你。不过我劝你早点到张家，信到那里去写也一样。”

By the time he completed his rounds and finished the tasks Hu had entrusted to him, the evening light was fading. He hurried to Dajing Silk Firm, where Huang Yi came forward to greet him. “Your mother-in-law has just left. She made up your room and waited quite a while, but when you didn't come, she had to go home. Before leaving, she told me over and over to send you there for supper. Nobody could fault the way she treats her son-in-law!” “I've been anxious too.” Chen felt uneasy. “I simply couldn't get away. Even now I can't go immediately. I want to write to Mr Hu first and send the letter on the regular boat as soon as possible.” “You can write when you come back tonight. You're staying here anyway.” “No!” Living at Dajing seemed to Chen much like marrying into his wife's household. A man with backbone would not live as a dependent son-in-law in his wife's family home. He therefore said firmly, “I'm still staying at my own place.” Huang understood. “That's up to you. But I'd advise you to go to the Zhangs soon. You can write the letter there just as well.”

这个建议，陈世龙接受了。赶到张家，正好是阿珠来开的门。这一次不象昨天那样不好意思了，她用微带埋怨的口吻说，“怎么到这时候才来？”“遇以好些意想不到的事。唉！”陈世龙摇摇头。“一进门就叹气，”阿珠十分关切地，“为啥？”“不是我的事。”陈世龙怕她误会，先这样说一句，好叫她放心，“一个要好弟兄，想不到死掉了。真正天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福。”看他神情不怡，阿珠也郁郁地不开心。关上大门，把他带到客堂说道：“爹吃喜酒去了。没有人陪你。要不要到厨房里来？”“要来的！”陈世龙说，“等我到厨房里去打个招呼，抽空给胡先生写信。”这个招呼一打就是好半天工夫，阿珠的娘一面炒菜，一面问长问短问陈世龙这天做了些什么？于是谈阿虎就谈不完，自然水晶阿七那一段，他只字不会提的。“好了！”阿珠等要开饭时笑道，“信也写不成了。”“吃了饭写，今天非写不可。”

Chen accepted that suggestion. When he reached the Zhang house, A’zhu herself opened the door. This time she was not as embarrassed as she had been the day before. “Why have you come so late?” she asked with a trace of reproach. “Several unexpected things happened. Ah!” He shook his head. “Sighing as soon as you come in! Why?” She was deeply concerned. “It isn't anything that's happened to me,” he said first, lest she misunderstand and worry. “A close friend has died unexpectedly. Truly, storms come without warning, and a person's fortune can change overnight.” His unhappy expression saddened her too. Closing the front gate, she led him into the sitting room. “Father has gone to a wedding feast, so there's nobody to keep you company. Would you like to come into the kitchen?” “Certainly. I'll greet your mother there, then find a moment to write to Mr Hu.” The greeting took a long time. As she cooked, A’zhu's mother asked question after question about what Chen had done that day. Once they began discussing A’hu, there was no end to it. Naturally, he said nothing whatever about Crystal A’qi. “Well,” A’zhu said with a smile when the meal was ready, “you haven't managed to write your letter after all.” “I'll write after supper. It must be done today.”

这是正事，阿珠的娘把它看得很重要，吃完饭，忙着收桌子，泡上茶来，摆出笔砚，阿珠又替他铺纸磨墨，连陈世龙自己都觉得这样子未免太郑重，便自嘲似地说，“不象写信，倒象给皇帝写奏折。”“闲话少说，快点写好了，送到航船上。晚上，人家都睡了，那就得明天起个大早才赶得上。”明天有明天的事，陈世龙感恩图报，决心要好好巴结，守定今日事今日毕的宗旨，当时定一定心，把胡雪岩交代的事，办得如何，逐项写明。最后提到郁四，说他独子病故，而且要闹家务，精神颓唐，当然，也提到了他的喜事。写完看一看钟，已经九点敲过，匆匆告辞，自己送到去杭州的航船上。然后径自回家。

This was proper business, and A’zhu's mother regarded it as important. After the meal, she hurried to clear the table, make tea, and set out brush and inkstone. A’zhu spread the paper and ground the ink for him. Even Chen felt that they were making too much of it. “This looks less like a letter than a memorial to the emperor,” he said with a self-mocking smile. “Less chatter! Finish it quickly and take it to the boat. If they've gone to sleep, you'll have to get up very early tomorrow to catch them.” Tomorrow would have its own business. Determined to repay kindness through diligent work, Chen held to the rule of finishing today's tasks today. He collected his thoughts and reported, item by item, how he had carried out Hu's instructions. At the end, he mentioned Yu: his only son's death, the threatened family troubles, and his low spirits. Naturally, Chen included news of his own marriage arrangements. When he finished and looked at the clock, it had already struck nine. He hurriedly took his leave and delivered the letter himself to the boat bound for Hangzhou, then went straight home.

未曾进门就已发现了怪事，他屋里亮着灯，而且不止一盏灯亮。陈世龙出门向来不上锁，因为没有什么东西好偷，而钥匙忘记带出来，或者虽带出来而遗失反倒麻烦，好在同一个大门里的邻居会替他照看，不锁更不要紧。有时朋友来访，见他不在家径自推门入内坐等，事或有之，但都在白天，象这样的情形，还是头一回，不免令人诧异，同时也逗人的好奇心，陈世龙心想，倒要看看是哪一个？这样转着念头，就不肯直接推门去看，蹑手蹑脚走到窗下，找个窗纸破了的洞洞，凑眼过去张望。一望就知道麻烦大了。里面是水晶阿七，对着一盏擦得雪亮的油灯在喝茶，两眼怔怔地望着另一张桌上的油灯，仿佛有无数心事在盘算。看她身上穿一件紫红宁绸的小夹袄，领子上的纽扣未扣，敞得极大，一股系肚兜的金链子，隐约可见，这副样子让人看见了，不说“水晶阿七跟小和尚有一腿”，那才真叫有鬼！陈世龙十分火冒，走到房门口，提脚就踢，但就在拉起脚的刹那，心中自语，慢来！看样子阿七不知安着什么心？他知道她的为人，心是不坏，但吃了那碗饭，脸皮就撕破了，什么好刁泼辣的事，都做得出来。也许她是故意的，好说不行，存心来撩拨得自己跟她吵架，传到阿珠耳朵里，这饥荒有得打。万一吵散，阿七就得其所哉了！念头转到这里，自觉是“小人之心”，但记起黄仪常说的两句话：“害人之心不可有，防人之心不可无”，象阿七这种人不可不防，只看眼前的情形，就是自己防不到的。

Before he reached his door, he noticed something strange. There was light inside—and more than one lamp was burning. Chen never locked his door when he went out. There was nothing worth stealing, and forgetting or losing a key would be a nuisance. Besides, neighbours who shared the entrance could keep an eye on the place. Sometimes a visiting friend, finding him absent, would push open the door and sit down to wait. But that happened by day. This was the first such occasion at night, and it surprised and intrigued him. Who could it be? Instead of entering directly, he crept beneath the window and peered through a hole in the paper. One look told him he was in serious trouble. Crystal A’qi sat drinking tea by a lamp polished bright, her eyes fixed on another lamp across the room, as though turning over countless worries. She wore a purplish-red, lined jacket of Ning silk. Its collar was unfastened and spread wide, revealing glimpses of the gold chain that held her underbodice. Anyone seeing her like this would certainly say that Crystal A’qi and Little Monk were having an affair. Furious, Chen went to the door and raised his foot to kick it. At that instant, he checked himself. Wait! Who knew what she intended? Her heart was not bad, but her former occupation had stripped away her inhibitions, and she could be as wilful and defiant as anyone. Perhaps, having failed by persuasion, she deliberately meant to provoke a quarrel. If word reached A’zhu, there would be trouble enough. Should the engagement break off, A’qi would have got just what she wanted. Chen felt that this suspicion was mean-minded. Yet he remembered Huang's saying: never intend harm, but never fail to guard against it. He must be cautious with someone like A’qi. Her presence here already showed what he had failed to foresee.

想停当了，气也平了，伸手把门一推，阿七似乎猝不及防，霍地站起身来，两眼睁得极大，看见陈世龙才拍拍胸说：“咄！吓得我来！”“你倒不说我吓一跳！”陈世龙平静地答道，“你这样子，象不象半夜里跑出一只狐狸精来？”“你骂好了！”阿七泰然地笑着，“好在我自己晓得，我不是来迷你的。”“那你来做啥？”“想想你光棍可怜，我又没啥事情好做，替你这间狗窝样的房子收拾收拾，这总不犯啥法？”这一说，陈世龙才把视线扫了一遍。屋子里收拾得象个样子了，尤其使他触目的是，那张床不象自己的床，他是从来不叠被的，此刻叠好了被一看，仿佛那张床大了许多。“难为你！”陈世龙坐了下来。“刚刚泡的茶。”阿七倒了一杯茶给他，“廊沿上我替你炖了一锅鸭粥在那里。”“哪里来的锅灶？”“买的。”阿七数着手指说，“风炉、茶壶、砂锅，还有炭，一共用了两千铜钱。”

Once he had thought it through, his anger subsided. He pushed open the door. Apparently taken by surprise, A’qi sprang up with wide eyes. Seeing Chen, she patted her chest. “Oh! You frightened me!” “What about the fright you gave me?” he answered calmly. “Don't you look like a fox spirit appearing in the middle of the night?” “Scold away!” She smiled untroubled. “At least I know I haven't come to bewitch you.” “Then what have you come for?” “I thought your bachelor's life looked pitiful. With nothing else to do, I came to tidy this kennel of yours. Surely there's no law against that?” Only then did Chen look round. The room had been put in order. The bed particularly caught his eye: it hardly seemed his own. He never folded his bedding, and with it folded now, the bed looked much larger. “You've gone to a great deal of trouble.” He sat down. “Freshly made tea.” She poured him a cup. “I've a pot of duck congee simmering for you on the veranda.” “Where did the stove and pot come from?” “I bought them.” She counted on her fingers. “A portable stove, teapot, earthenware pot, and charcoal: two thousand copper cash altogether.”

“还替我买了啥东西，一共垫了多少？”“你要还我？”“当然！”陈世龙说，“我又不跟你‘做人家’，没有要你来买的道理。”看他的神气倒还平静，但话中摸不到一丝热气，阿七心里便自怨，何苦来自讨没趣？但一则不甘于就此一走，二则是觉得良家妇女好做，凄凉和寂寞难耐。秋宵冷雨，独对孤灯，把棉被咬破了都没用，还不如在陈世龙这里的好，虽说他没有好脸嘴给人看，到底是两个人呀！这样转着念头，陈世龙就落下风了，他原来是想她自觉没趣，不如归去。谁知她虽觉没趣而不走，是他再也猜不到的，所以谈话依旧是一句顶一句，毫不放松。

“What else did you buy for me? How much have you spent in all?” “Do you mean to pay me back?” “Naturally. We aren't setting up house together. There's no reason for you to buy these things.” His manner was calm, but there was no warmth in his words. A’qi reproached herself inwardly. Why come here to be snubbed? Yet she could not bear simply to leave. Living respectably was one thing; enduring desolation and loneliness was another. Alone beside a lamp on an autumn night of cold rain, she could bite her quilt to pieces and gain nothing. Better to stay here. Chen might show her no kindness, but at least there were two of them! With this resolution, she gained the advantage. Chen had hoped that embarrassment would send her home. He had never imagined that she might feel unwelcome and stay anyway. Not knowing this, he continued to meet every remark with an uncompromising rejoinder.

阿七行所无事，走到廊沿下去把一锅鸭粥端了进来，放在地上，接着又奔了出去，只听乒乒乓乓的响声，不知在搞些什么？陈世龙忍不住也走出去张望，这才发现廊沿转角上已安下一个小小的厨房，一张白木方桌，靠壁置着一具竹子碗橱，“乒乒乓乓”正就是她在取碗筷弄出来的响声。她倒是真的想打算跟自己“做人家”了。陈世龙又好气，又好笑，却不能说什么，他回身坐定，阿七已跟着走了进来，手里一个托盘，两副碗筷以外，还有两碟小菜，一碟是糟“吐瓞”，一碟是酱萝卜。“我不要吃！”陈世龙先来个拒人于千里之外。“你不吃我吃！”阿七答得异常爽脆。她自盛了一碗鸭粥坐下来吃，也不知是真的饿了，还是有意气他？只见她唏哩呼噜，吃得好香。鸭粥熬得火候够了，香味浓郁，不断飘到他的鼻下，再看她挟块绷脆的酱萝卜放在嘴里，咬得“嘎吱嘎吱”地响，越使得陈世龙要咽唾沫。

A’qi went about her business. She brought in the pot of congee, set it on the floor, and hurried out again. Clattering sounds followed. Unable to imagine what she was doing, Chen went to look and discovered a little kitchen installed round the corner of the veranda: a plain wooden table and a bamboo cupboard against the wall. The noise came from her taking out bowls and chopsticks. She really seemed intent on setting up house with him! He was both annoyed and amused but could say nothing. Returning to his seat, he was followed by A’qi with a tray. Besides two sets of bowls and chopsticks, it held two side dishes: tudie preserved in wine lees, and radish pickled in sauce. “I don't want any,” he said, determined to keep her at a distance. “Then I'll eat!” she answered briskly. She served herself congee and sat down. Whether she was truly hungry or meant to annoy him, she ate with noisy relish. The congee had simmered to perfection, and its rich aroma drifted continually towards him. Watching her bite into crisp pickled radish with an audible crunch made him swallow with longing.

想想有点不甘心，“你这个人倒好！”他说，“真的当这里是你的家了？”“有交情的嘛！”阿七毫不在乎地说，“你到我那里，还不是一样？”“我是不会这样子不识相的。”“你是说我不识相？”“有一点。”陈世龙说，“天晚了，我要睡觉了。”“小和尚，你气量真小！”阿七的声调幽幽地，“你就让我把这碗粥吃完了，再赶我走，也还不迟。”这话说得很够分量，陈世龙大为懊悔，堂堂男子汉，在江湖上辈分虽低，倒也从来没有哪个敢当面藐视过，不过今天“吃瘪”在她这两句话上！于是他要“找场”了！“什么气量小，气量小？谈不到！”他说，“我是为你好，不是啥‘赶你走，！随你喜欢到啥辰光，我不在乎。不过我要少陪了。”

He began to feel aggrieved. “You've made yourself comfortable! Do you really think this is your home?” “We're friends, aren't we?” she answered without concern. “Wouldn't you do the same at my place?” “I wouldn't be so insensitive.” “You mean I'm insensitive?” “A little. It's late. I want to go to bed.” “Little Monk, you're terribly small-minded,” she said quietly. “You could at least let me finish this bowl before driving me away.” The rebuke struck home. Chen regretted his words. He was a grown man; low as his standing in their world might be, nobody had ever dared openly slight him. Yet today her two remarks had put him completely in the wrong. He must recover his ground. “Small-minded? That has nothing to do with it! I'm thinking of you, not driving you away. Stay as long as you please. I don't mind. But you'll have to excuse me.”

说着脱下长衫，往椅背上一搭，坐到床沿上去换拖鞋。哪知早晨刚刚穿过的拖鞋，此时已不在床下，心知是阿七不知摆到哪里去了？懒得跟她搭话，使把鞋子一甩，身子往床上一倒。“拖鞋在这里。”阿七从床头方凳下拖出一双拖鞋来，回身又把他的长衫挂到衣架上，接着又去收拾桌子。陈世龙看在眼里不响，但身子却睡不宁帖，倒象背上长了根刺在那里似地。他此时唯一的希望是，阿七早早离去，从此不来。“小和尚！”阿七收拾完毕，坐下来说，“我有句话要问你。”不理不好意思，陈世龙只得冷冷地答道：“你说好了。”“说实话，我从来没有烧过这么入味的鸭粥，你吃一碗好不好？”想不到是这么一句话！陈世龙大出意外，“人心都是肉做的”，她辛辛苦苦烧好，还要哀求别人来享用，仿佛吃她一碗鸭粥，就是帮了她什么大忙似的。这叫人无论如何硬不起心肠来峻拒，只好这样推托：“已经都收拾好了，何必再费事……”

He took off his long gown, laid it across a chair, and sat on the edge of the bed to change into slippers. The slippers he had worn that morning were no longer underneath it. A’qi must have moved them. Unwilling to speak to her, he kicked off his shoes and flung himself onto the bed. “Your slippers are here.” She drew them from beneath a square stool at the head of the bed, then hung his gown on the clothes stand and cleared the table. Chen watched in silence, but could not lie comfortably. He felt as though a thorn were sticking into his back. His only wish was that she would leave soon and never return. When she had finished, she sat down. “Little Monk, there's something I want to ask you.” Too embarrassed to ignore her, he answered coldly, “Go ahead.” “Honestly, I've never made such well-flavoured duck congee. Won't you have a bowl?” He had never expected that. Nobody's heart was made of stone. She had worked hard to prepare it, and now must beg him to enjoy it, as though eating a bowl would do her some great favour. He could not bring himself to refuse harshly. “You've cleared everything away. Why go to more trouble...?”

一句话没有完，阿七已站起身来，连连说道：“不费事，不费事！”说着，就走了出去。陈世龙无法阻拦。心里有着说不出的懊恼，是恨自己无用，连个阿七都对付不了！于是自己跟自己赌气，一面从床上仰身坐了起来，一面心中自语：何必象见了一条毒蛇似地怕她？越是这样躲她，她越要缠住不放。等阿七笑嘻嘻地盛了粥来，他也不说一声“谢谢”，扶起筷子就吃，也象她一样，把酱萝卜咬得“嘎吱嘎吱”地响，吃完一碗，再来一碗。“味道不错吧？”阿七得意地问。“不见得怎么样。”“哼！”她撇一撇嘴，笑他言不由衷，“我烧的粥是不好，不过你的胃口还不错。”“我的胃口是不好，不过不吃你不开心。”陈世龙学着她的语气说。阿七不作声，静静地在咀嚼他这句话的滋味。

Before he could finish, she was on her feet. “No trouble at all!” She hurried out, and he could not stop her. Chen felt an indescribable vexation with himself. How useless he was, unable even to deal with A’qi! Sitting up, he argued inwardly with his own weakness. Why fear her like a poisonous snake? The more he avoided her, the more tightly she would cling. When she brought the congee with a smile, he offered no thanks, merely took his chopsticks and began to eat, crunching the radish as loudly as she had. He finished one bowl, then had another. “Tastes good, doesn't it?” she asked proudly. “Nothing remarkable.” “Hmph!” She curled her lip at his insincerity. “My congee may be poor, but your appetite seems good.” “My appetite is poor, but you wouldn't be happy if I didn't eat.” Chen imitated her phrasing. A’qi said nothing, quietly savouring his words.

“现在该论到我问句话了。”陈世龙放下空碗说：“你到底要我怎么样？”“没有啥！说实话，我回去也没有事，一个人躺在床上想东想西，一夜到天亮都睡不着。跟你谈谈，心里好过些，谈到差不多辰光了，你睡你的觉，我回我的家。”所望不奢，而且陈世龙对她的观感，跟刚进门时，已有不同，于是点点头答应：“好嘛！大不了陪你坐到天亮。”阿七嫣然一笑，先把碗筷收了出去，重新沏了一壶茶来，就隔着一盏剔亮了的油灯，跟陈世龙闲谈，自然是她的话多，谈郁四的待人接物，说他“还算是有良心的”，只是耳朵软，喜欢听女儿的话。又说她本来已经死心塌地的预备跟郁四一辈子，哪知道中途出此变故？因而便发牢骚，说大家只骂风尘中人下贱，去不知从良也不是件容易事。谈到这里就不是闲话了，“小和尚！”她说，“我今天下午去打听过了，你跟张家的亲事不假，我晚了一步！那么，你倒替我想想，我以后的日子怎么过法？”看她的神情是诚恳求教，陈世龙不能推托，想一想答道：“你自己总要有几句话摆出来，人家才好替你留意，譬如说，你吃不吃得苦，肯不肯做小？要怎么样的人品？说清楚了，我替你去找。这件事说难很难，说容易很容易，胡老板在这两三个月中，就做了三个媒。在这上面，就跟他的做生意一样，顶有办法。我把你的事情托他，包你三个月之内，就有好消息。“

“Now it's my turn to ask a question.” Chen set down his empty bowl. “What exactly do you want from me?” “Nothing much. Honestly, there's nothing for me to do at home. I lie alone in bed, thinking of everything, unable to sleep till morning. Talking to you makes me feel better. When it's time, you can go to bed and I'll go home.” It was a modest request, and Chen's view of her had changed since he came in. He nodded. “Very well. At worst, I'll sit with you till dawn.” She smiled, cleared away the bowls, and made fresh tea. Across the newly brightened lamp, they chatted, though she did most of the talking. Yu Si, she said, was fairly decent in his dealings with people, but too easily influenced, especially by his daughter. She had truly meant to spend her life with him. Who could have foreseen this change? People called women of her former profession low and contemptible, she complained, but knew nothing of how hard it was to leave that life. At this point, the talk became serious. “Little Monk, I made inquiries this afternoon. Your engagement to the Zhang girl is real. I'm a step too late. Then tell me, how am I to live from now on?” Her request for advice was sincere, and Chen could not evade it. After thinking, he replied, “You must first say what you want, so that others can look for you. Could you endure hardship? Would you accept being a concubine? What sort of man do you want? Make it clear, and I'll look. Such a matter can be very difficult or very easy. Mr Hu has arranged three matches in the past two or three months. He's as resourceful at it as at business. I'll entrust your case to him and guarantee good news within three months.”

阿七不响，只是眨眼，仿佛连她自己都弄不清楚，该“从”怎么样的一个“良人”？“终身大事急不得！”陈世龙趁机劝她走路，“你回去好好想一想。已经吃过一次亏，不能再吃第二次。”语气很诚恳，阿七觉得他说得很中听，便站起身来有告辞的模样。陈世龙的动作很快，把他从大经丝行带来的钉在亭柱上的一盏灯笼，取了下来，点了蜡烛，交在阿七手里。“那么明朝会了！”“明朝会，明朗会！”陈世龙灵机一动，下个伏笔：“不过这两天你怕不容易寻得着我。”“怎么呢？”阿七问道，“这样子忙法？”“是啊！说来你不相信，连知府衙门里的公事，我都要管。”这也没有什么不能相信，阿七知道胡雪岩跟王大老爷是分不开的，既然陈世龙是胡雪岩的亲信。附带办些知府衙门的公事，也是情理中事。好在公事总在白天，晚上亦总要回家睡觉，不怕寻不着他。

A’qi merely blinked, as though she herself could not decide what sort of respectable man she should settle with. “Marriage can't be rushed,” Chen said, seizing the chance to encourage her departure. “Go home and think it over. You've suffered once. You mustn't suffer twice.” His earnest tone persuaded her, and she rose as though to leave. Chen moved quickly. He took down the lantern he had brought from Dajing, which hung on a nail in a post, lit its candle, and placed it in her hand. “Then I'll see you tomorrow!” she said. “Tomorrow, tomorrow!” An idea struck him, and he laid the groundwork. “Though you may find it hard to catch me these next two days.” “Why? Are you that busy?” “Yes. You may not believe it, but I even have business from the prefectural yamen to attend to.” There was nothing unbelievable about that. A’qi knew Hu and Prefect Wang were inseparable. As Hu's trusted man, Chen might naturally handle some official matters as well. But official business was done by day, and he must return home to sleep at night. She need not fear being unable to find him.

陈世龙要避她的，正在晚上。看阿七现在的样子，硬的吓不走她，软的磨不过她，三十六计，走为上策，当然不能离开湖州，那就是两个办法，第一个是另外找房子搬家，第二个是住到大经丝行去。细想一想，其实只有一个办法，搬到大经丝行，因为另外找房子搬家，别人问起来，总得有个说法，说是为了避阿七，则变成自己心虚，无私有弊了。同时，阿七说不定会到大经去找，自己在那里，比较好应付，否则，阿七在那里说两句不知轻重出入的话，引起嫌疑，就跳到黄河也洗不清了。打定了主意，安然入梦。第二天一早出门去看了几个素日有来往的小弟兄，一顿酒吃到下午三点钟，回家收拾随身衣服，带到大经丝行。

Night was precisely when Chen wanted to avoid her. As matters stood, sternness would not frighten her away, and he could not outlast her gentle persistence. Of all strategies, retreat was best. He could not leave Huzhou, so there were two possibilities: find another house, or move into Dajing. On reflection, only the second would do. If he found a new place, he would have to explain himself when people asked. Saying he wished to avoid A’qi would look like a guilty conscience and make an innocent matter seem suspicious. Besides, she might call at Dajing. If he lived there, he could handle her more easily. Otherwise, a few careless words from her could arouse suspicions that even the Yellow River could not wash away. His mind settled, he slept peacefully. Early next morning he went to see several younger friends he knew well. Their drinking lasted until three in the afternoon. Then he went home, packed his clothes, and took them to Dajing.

“来，来！”黄仪从屋里奔了出来，招手喊道：“今天我这个媒人有话跟你说了。”邀他到房间里，一谈经过，陈世龙大出意外。据说郁四在这天早晨，特地到大经丝行来看老张，口称“亲家”，说陈世龙是他的小辈，现在当儿子一样看待，将来办喜事，男家归他主持，同时送了一千两银子的聘金。“你丈人老实，有点手足无措，不知道怎么办？特地来问我，这还有啥话说？我叫你老丈人认了亲家。”黄仪很高兴地说，“到底是占码头的人物，做事漂亮之至，送了我二百两银子，算是谢媒，不收他会不高兴，我也就老实，叨你老弟的光了。“陈世龙听这一说，觉得面子十足，心里非常高兴，但不肯在脸上摆出来，怕黄仪发觉他并不知道这件事。“这一来，日子就急得不得了。”黄仪说道：“你丈母娘请我去吃中饭，当面跟我说，她要替女儿办嫁妆，起码要半年工夫，年底下来不及。看你的意思怎么佯？我们先谈好了，再跟郁四叔去说。”

“Come along!” Huang hurried from his room, beckoning. “Your matchmaker has something to tell you today.” Once inside, Chen heard a wholly unexpected story. That morning Yu had come to Dajing especially to see Old Zhang, addressing him as his fellow parent-in-law. Chen, he explained, was his junior, but he now regarded him as a son. At the wedding, Yu would head the bridegroom's family. He had also brought a thousand taels in betrothal money. “Your father-in-law is an honest fellow and didn't know what to do. He came to ask me. What was there to discuss? I told him to acknowledge the relationship.” Huang was delighted. “That's a man of standing for you! He does things magnificently. He gave me two hundred taels as thanks for arranging the match. Refusing would have offended him, so I frankly accepted. I've benefited through you, my young friend.” Chen felt greatly honoured and was very pleased, but hid it lest Huang discover that he had known nothing of the arrangement. “This makes the timing terribly tight,” Huang continued. “Your mother-in-law invited me to lunch and told me she needs at least six months to prepare her daughter's dowry. There isn't time before the year's end. What do you think? Let's settle it between ourselves, then speak to Uncle Four.”

陈世龙有些不太愿意，想了想问道：“不晓得阿珠怎么说？”“你问这话真没道理！她会怎么说，难道说越早出阁越好？”想想不错，陈世龙失笑了，“这件事我做不来主。”他说，“要跟郁四叔、胡先生商量了再说。”“难道你自己作不得你自己的主？”黄仪拿了郁四的、吃了张家的，不能不把情况弄清楚，“说句实话，你父母双亡，人家虽帮你的忙，到底不是‘父母之命’。”“父母之命，媒妁之言”这两句话，陈世龙也听到过，但他的这头亲事，真所谓“如人饮水，冷暖自知”，成家立业是一事的两面，为胡雪岩想，是要提拔陈世龙，也为了他自己的事业，要觅个得力的帮手，引替陈世龙促成良缘，此刻各样生意，都在着春进展之中，到什么时候，需要陈世龙出力，只有胡雪岩心里才有数，倘或正要用人的时候，他在忙着办喜事，岂不耽误了生意，那就不是胡雪岩的本意了。除此以外，陈世龙还有一份感恩的心情，自从跟了胡雪岩，叫他“先生”，陈世龙才知道“师父，师父”，师真如父，为了尊敬“胡先生”，哪怕就没有耽误生意的顾虑，他也愿意请命而行。见他沉吟不语，黄仪明白了，陈世龙必有他的难处，但女家也有女家的难处，要先让陈世龙明白，否则做媒人的两头传话，南辕北辙，就吃力而不讨好了。

Chen was reluctant. After some thought, he asked, “What does A’zhu say?” “What an unreasonable question! What could she say? That the sooner she leaves home to marry, the better?” Seeing the point, Chen laughed. “I can't decide this. I must discuss it with Uncle Four and Mr Hu.” “Can't you decide your own affairs?” Having accepted Yu's money and the Zhangs' hospitality, Huang had to understand the situation. “Frankly, both your parents are dead. Others may help, but their wishes aren't your parents' commands.” Chen had heard the saying about parental commands and a matchmaker's words. Yet his own marriage was like water whose warmth only the drinker knew. Establishing a home and establishing a livelihood were two sides of the same matter. Hu had arranged the match both to advance Chen and to secure an able assistant for his own enterprises. All those ventures were now being actively developed, and only Hu knew when Chen would be needed. If he were busy with a wedding precisely when his help was required, business would suffer. That could not be Hu's intention. Besides, Chen felt grateful. Only after following Hu and calling him “sir” had he understood how a teacher could truly be like a father. Out of respect, he would willingly seek Hu's approval even without any risk of disrupting business. Seeing him silent in thought, Huang understood that he had difficulties. But the bride's family had difficulties too, and Chen must first understand them. Otherwise, carrying messages between two sides pulling in opposite directions would be thankless work.

“世龙，”他用劝告的语气说，“洞房花烛，一个人一生只一回，女家又是独养女儿，人家要好好预备嫁妆，因此耽误日子，我们做男家的要体谅。大户人家的小姐，一到了十二三岁就在办嫁妆了，一办五、六年，不足为奇。现在人家只要五、六个月，不算多。你跟胡老板去说，他的人情世故熟透熟透，一定会答应。““我也晓得他十之八九会答应，不过我不能不先跟他说一声。”“那就行了。”黄仪指着他随身的衣包又问，“你主意改过了？觉得还是住到这里来方便，是不是？”陈世尤灵机一动，阿七的事，不便对别人说，“媒人”这里正好说清楚，万一将来发生误会，有个有力的见证，于是叹口气说：“我是来‘逃难’！”“咦！”黄仪大为惊异，而且颇为关切，“ 你有了什么麻烦，自己家里都不能住了！是不是欠了哪个的债？”“债倒是债，不是钱债……”

“Shilong,” Huang said persuasively, “a person has only one wedding night, and she's her family's only daughter. If preparing her dowry delays the wedding, we on the bridegroom's side must be considerate. Great families begin preparing a daughter's dowry when she's twelve or thirteen. Taking five or six years is nothing unusual. Here they ask for only five or six months. That's not much. Tell Mr Hu. He understands human affairs thoroughly and will certainly agree.” “I know he's very likely to agree. But I must tell him first.” “Then that's settled.” Huang pointed to Chen's bundle of clothes. “You've changed your mind? You think it would be more convenient to stay here after all?” An idea struck Chen. He could not tell other people about A’qi, but the matchmaker was precisely the person who should know. If a misunderstanding arose later, he would have an influential witness. He sighed. “I've come to take refuge!” “Why?” Huang was both surprised and concerned. “What trouble prevents you from staying in your own home? Do you owe someone money?” “A debt, yes, but not a money debt...”

听他说完经过，黄仪笑道：“真正是风流债！世龙，你倒是艳福不浅。”接着又用不胜羡慕的语气说：“到底是小伙子，有办法！”“你还要拿人开胃！这件事，没有第二个人知道，黄先生，你要帮我的忙。”“你做得对，步子踏得很稳。不要紧，不要紧！”黄仪拍胸说道：“只要你自己把握得定，不受她的诱惑，一切有我。如果她寻上门来，我有绝妙一计对付她，包你一点麻烦都没有。“听他说得如此有把握，陈世龙关切以外，不免好奇，笑嘻嘻地问道：“黄先生，你这条妙计，可以不可以先跟我讲一讲？”“天机不可泄漏！”黄仪定神想了一会，忽然问道：“有句话我再问一声，你确确实实晓得她跟郁四叔是好好分手的？不是吵散的？”“看样子是这样。不然郁四叔也不是好说话的人。”“等她来了，你躲起来，千万不要露面。我自有‘退敌，之方。”

After hearing the story, Huang laughed. “A debt of love, indeed! Shilong, fortune certainly favours you with women.” His tone turned envious. “Young fellows know how to manage these things!” “And you still tease me! Nobody else knows about this. Mr Huang, you must help.” “You've acted correctly and kept your footing. Don't worry!” Huang struck his chest. “As long as you hold firm and resist her temptation, leave everything to me. If she comes here, I've a splendid plan for dealing with her. I guarantee you won't have the least trouble.” Such confidence aroused Chen's curiosity as well as his interest. Smiling, he asked, “Could you tell me this wonderful plan beforehand?” “Heaven's secrets mustn't be revealed!” Huang paused to consider, then asked suddenly, “One more thing. Are you absolutely certain she and Uncle Four parted amicably? They didn't quarrel?” “So it appears. Otherwise Uncle Four isn't easy to deal with either.” “When she comes, hide yourself. Whatever happens, don't appear. I have my own way of driving off the enemy.”

陈世龙实在不知道他葫芦里卖的什么药？好在有了这块挡箭牌，诸事无碍，宽心一放。当时便住入他丈母娘替他布置的卧室。略略睡了片刻，复又出门去向郁四叔道谢，陪着他说了些闲话，再到张家，阿珠的娘对他是越发亲热了，但也象是越发客气了。“我住到行里去了。”他这样告诉她，不说任何原因。“原该这样。”阿珠的娘当然高兴，“以后你每天回家来吃饭，行里的伙食也还好，不过总没有在家里吃得舒服。”他们这样在谈，阿珠一直躲在自己的屋中，她有许多话要问陈世龙，只是越来越觉得不好意思。陈世龙也是一样，不便闯进屋去，只不住遥望雪白纸窗中的一盏明灯、一条黑影，看看已无话可说，起身告辞，阿珠的娘没有留他，也没有提到阿珠，让他怏怏然地离去。陈世龙一路走，一路在想。觉得他丈母娘仿佛有把他与阿珠隔绝开来的意思？这是为了什么？费人猜疑。当然，他不愿往不好的地方去猜，然而实在也无法说它是个好现象，只好自譬自解，当作一件偶然之事。

Chen had no idea what Huang was planning. Still, with this shield in place, he could feel at ease. He moved into the bedroom his mother-in-law had prepared, slept briefly, then went out again to thank Yu and keep him company for a while. Afterwards he visited the Zhangs. A’zhu's mother was warmer towards him than ever, yet also seemed more formal. “I've moved into the firm,” he told her, without giving any reason. “As you should.” Naturally she was pleased. “Come home for your meals every day. The food at the firm is quite good, but it can't be as comfortable as eating at home.” While they talked, A’zhu remained in her room. She had many questions for Chen, but felt increasingly shy. He felt the same. Unable to intrude, he kept looking towards the lamp and dark silhouette behind her white paper window. At last, with nothing more to say, he rose to leave. Her mother neither detained him nor mentioned A’zhu, and he departed disconsolately. As he walked, he wondered whether his mother-in-law meant to keep them apart. Why would she? It was puzzling. Naturally, he did not want to suspect anything bad, yet could hardly call it a good sign. He could only reassure himself that it was an isolated occurrence.

第二天一早起身，神清气爽，思虑敏锐而周密，觉得在湖州要找件正经事做，如果湖州无事，就当赶回杭州，看胡雪岩有何差遣？无所事事，坐享“清福”，决不是善策。于是他粑整个情况细细思考一遍，发觉有件事情可以做，去打听打听丝的行情。这个行情是胡雪岩所急于想知道的，他在杭州一直也在打听，但销洋庄的丝，大部分出在湖州，在杭州打听湖州的行情，不一定准确，闲着无事，正好替胡雪岩在这方面出点力。转念一想，这件事是黄仪熟悉。行情如有变化，他一定会写信给胡雪岩，自己何必白忙？倒是到县衙门里去看看那两位师爷，打听打听官场有什么消息，倘或平静无事，不如回杭州去的好。结果是扑了个空，也可以说是碰了一鼻子的灰。刑、钱两师爷的住处，关防甚严，向来不准闲杂人等乱闯，陈世龙跟杨用之他们并不熟悉，所以托听差通报进去，都挡驾不见。陈世龙心里很不高兴，但想想是自己冒昧，又算长了一次经验。回到大经，枯坐无聊，想回自己住处去看看，刚踏出门，只见行里的一个小徒弟，匆匆赶来告诉他，说黄仪叫他来通知，让陈世龙赶紧从后门避开。

Next morning he rose clear-headed, able to think sharply and thoroughly. He must find useful work in Huzhou. If there was none, he should return to Hangzhou and ask for Hu's instructions. Idling in comfort was no sound policy. Reviewing the situation, he found something he could do: investigate silk prices. Hu urgently wanted this information and had been making inquiries in Hangzhou. But most silk intended for export came from Huzhou, and reports gathered elsewhere might be inaccurate. With nothing else to do, Chen could help him directly. Then he reconsidered. Huang knew that business well. If prices changed, he would surely write to Hu. Why duplicate the work? Better to call on the two advisers at the county yamen and inquire about official developments. If all was quiet, he might as well return to Hangzhou. The visit came to nothing; indeed, it was a rebuff. Access to the quarters of the legal and financial advisers was strictly controlled, and casual visitors were never allowed to wander in. Chen did not know Yang Yongzhi and the other adviser well. When he sent his name through their attendants, both refused to receive him. He was displeased, but admitted that he had been presumptuous and had learned another lesson. Back at Dajing, he sat about bored and decided to visit his own rooms. He had barely stepped out when an apprentice hurried up with Huang's message: he must leave by the back door immediately.

这是阿七寻上门来了。陈世龙好奇心起，反倒不肯走，只问：“可是有个堂客来看黄先生？”“是的。”“黄先生怎么跟她说？”“黄先生笑嘻嘻地请她到里头坐。叫她‘七阿姐’。”听这一说，陈世龙决定会窥探一番，遣走了那小徒弟，从侧门溜到黄仪那里。他的房间旁边就是楼梯，楼梯下面是堆储杂物之处，有一道门锁着，陈世龙悄悄开了锁，就躲在这里偷听。“七阿姐！”他听见黄仪在说，“我倒不晓得你跟世龙相熟。”“我们认识多年了。”“这样说起来，你们是‘老相好’？”黄仪的话过于率直，近平粗鲁，听壁脚的陈世龙大为皱眉。就这时一线光亮穿壁而入，壁上本来有个洞，刚才是为黄仪的背脊所挡住了，此刻他换了个地方坐，所以光线得以透过。陈世龙凭此指引，悄悄移步凑眼，阿七和黄仪恰好都在视界之中。阿七打扮得很朴素，穿一件铁灰线春的薄棉袄，系着玄色洋绉的裙子，脂粉不施，只在鬓边替一朵红花。这样打扮，在庄重中又显得很俏丽，徐娘风韵，着实迷人。她的神色也很庄重，但一双眼睛不能动，一动便如波光潋滟，令人目炫。陈世龙顾得看，便顾不得听，想不起刚逝的这片刻工夫，两个人又对答了几句什么话？只见阿七略有愠色，必是黄仪说话太不客气的缘故。

A’qi had come looking for him. Curiosity made Chen unwilling to leave. “Has a lady come to see Mr Huang?” “Yes.” “What did he say to her?” “He smiled and invited her inside, calling her Sister A’qi.” Chen decided to investigate. Dismissing the apprentice, he slipped through a side door towards Huang's room. Beside it was a staircase, with a locked storeroom beneath. Chen quietly unlocked it and hid there to listen. “Sister A’qi,” he heard Huang say, “I didn't know you were acquainted with Shilong.” “We've known each other for years.” “Then you're old sweethearts?” Huang's bluntness bordered on rudeness, and Chen frowned. Just then, a ray of light entered through the partition. There was a hole which Huang's back had previously blocked. He had changed seats, letting the light through. Guided by it, Chen moved silently and put his eye to the opening. Both were in view. A’qi was plainly dressed in a lightly padded jacket of iron-grey xianchun fabric and a black skirt of imported crepe. She wore no rouge or powder, only a red flower at her temple. The effect was both dignified and pretty, with the captivating charm of a mature woman. Her expression was dignified too, provided her eyes remained still. Once they moved, they glittered like sunlight on water, dazzling the observer. Absorbed in looking, Chen forgot to listen and missed whatever had been said in the interval. A’qi now looked slightly angry. Huang must have been speaking too discourteously.

“七阿姐！”黄仪在说，“既然你们规规矩矩，没啥纠葛，那么你来看世龙是为啥？”“我有笔小小的款子，托他代为放息。现在要钱用，想请他替我抽回来。”一听这话，陈世龙先是诧异，从而恼怒！这不是诬赖？她何尝有什么款子托自己放息，然而稍为多想一想，便即恍然，这是“烟熏鼠穴”之计，目的是要把自己逼出来跟她见面。这一计想得甚绝！怕黄仪难以应付了。不然！黄仪听陈世龙谈过她跟郁四的情形，以前陈世龙连跟她见面的机会都没有，怎会替她经手银钱？而况郁四自己跟人合股开着聚成钱庄，如果阿七有私房，何不存在聚成生息，要来托陈世龙代放？明知道她是假话，黄仪却不肯戳穿，只问：“你那笔钱是多少，要抽回多少？”“不多，几百两银子，能抽回多少是多少。”“好的。我替你转告。”

“Sister A’qi,” Huang was saying, “if your relationship is entirely proper and there's nothing between you, why have you come to see Shilong?” “I entrusted a small sum to him to lend at interest. Now I need money and want him to call it back.” Chen was first astonished, then angry. Wasn't this a false accusation? She had never given him money to lend. A little thought made her purpose clear: she was smoking a rat out of its hole. She meant to force him to appear. It was a brilliant scheme, and he feared Huang would be unable to answer it. But Huang understood. Chen had told him about her relations with Yu. Previously, Chen had scarcely been able to meet her, so how could he have handled her money? Besides, Yu owned Jucheng with partners. If A’qi had savings, why not deposit them there for interest instead of asking Chen to lend them? Knowing she was lying, Huang chose not to expose her. “How much is it, and how much do you need back?” “Not much. A few hundred taels. As much as he can recover.” “Very well. I'll tell him.”

“谢谢你！”阿七略停一停又说，“不过我想要当面跟他算一算帐。黄先生你看，我啥辰光来，可以见得着他的面？”“说句实话，啥时光也见不着！”“为啥？”“为了他一见你七阿姐要着迷，我的责任有关。”这句话很厉害！厉害在骤出不意，如当头霹雳一般，把盘算得好好地，预备一步一步逼出陈世龙来的阿七，震得七荤八素，枪法大乱，有些气馁了。望着笑嘻嘻地，似乎不怀好意的黄仪，阿七很不服气，挺一挺腰，凸出了她那个鼓蓬蓬的胸脯说：“着迷不着迷，不去说它，我倒要请教黄先生，什么叫‘责任有关’？我要跟陈世龙见一见面，谈正经事，你为啥从中作梗？”“陈世龙要讨亲了，是我做的媒，我对女家有责任，新郎官看见你着了迷，到时候出了什么花样，女家找我说话，我怎么交代？”黄仪又换了个位子，坐到她下首一张椅子上，隔着茶几凑过脸去问道：“七阿姐，你想呢，我这话在不在道理上？”阿七气得脸色发白，冷笑连声：“有道理，有道理！”陈世龙看在眼里，又觉得好笑，又有些不忍，他心里在想，黄仪如果是打算着把她气走，这一计便不高明了。因为他深知阿七的脾气，服软不服硬，越是如此，越惹得她心中不平，什么撒泼的花样都耍得出来，岂不是把事情搞得更糟？

“Thank you.” After a pause, A’qi continued, “But I'd like to settle the account with him personally. When should I come to find him?” “To tell you the truth, you won't find him at any time.” “Why?” “Because seeing you would bewitch him, and I have a responsibility.” The force lay in its unexpectedness. Like a thunderclap, it shattered her carefully calculated plan to draw Chen out step by step, leaving her bewildered and discouraged. Huang was smiling as though he meant mischief. Resenting him, A’qi straightened her back and thrust out her full bosom. “Never mind whether he's bewitched. I'd like to ask what you mean by responsibility. I want to discuss proper business with Chen Shilong. Why are you obstructing me?” “He's engaged to be married. I arranged the match and am responsible to the bride's family. If the bridegroom sees you, loses his head, and does something foolish, they'll come to me. What could I tell them?” Huang changed seats again, moving to a lower chair beside her and leaning towards her across the tea table. “Think about it, Sister A’qi. Isn't that reasonable?” Her face whitened with anger. “Very reasonable!” she answered with repeated cold laughs. Watching, Chen was amused but also sorry for her. If Huang meant to anger her into leaving, it was a poor plan. Chen knew her temper: kindness persuaded her, force did not. Resentment could provoke any sort of outrageous scene. Wouldn't that make matters worse?

正在有些失悔着急，只见黄仪又换了副神色，满脸疚歉，一片小心，“七阿姐，”他低声下气地说，“我言语冒犯，你在生我的气，是不是？”“哼，”阿七微微冷笑，“我怎么敢生你黄先生的气？”“啊呀！”黄仪抓抓头皮，作出那万分伤脑筋的神气，“听这话，生气生得大了。七阿姐，我替你赔罪，你千万不要生气。”听他这样说，阿七不好意思了，把脸色放缓和了说：“没有。我生什么气。”“真的不生气？”黄仪带着些逗弄的意味：“真的不生气，你就笑一笑。”这怎么笑得出？阿七觉得这个人，颇为难缠。定睛一看，只见黄仪的一双色眼瞪在自己胸前，恍然大悟，原来这家伙不怀好意！想起他的可恶，阿七决定要请他吃点苦头。这样一转念，便先浮起一阵报复的快意，心境开朗，不觉嫣然一笑，秋波流转，站起身来，走了几步，回身斜睨着黄仪，欲语不语地，真有烟视媚行之致。黄仪心里痒得仿佛有十七八只小手在搔抓似地，他原来的盘算，就是挺身自代，既替陈世龙解了围，自己又捡了个便宜，所以一上来不惜言语开罪，好叫她对陈世龙先死了心，然后用“潘驴邓小闲”的“小”字诀，来叫她化嗔为喜。自己估量，这是着实要费一番精神的事，不想收功如此之速，因有喜出望外之感。

While Chen was beginning to regret the arrangement, Huang changed his expression. All apology and caution, he said humbly, “Sister A’qi, I've offended you. You're angry with me, aren't you?” “Hmph!” She smiled coldly. “How would I dare be angry with you?” “Oh dear!” Huang scratched his head, looking desperately troubled. “That sounds very angry indeed. I apologise. Please don't be offended.” This made her uncomfortable, and she softened. “I'm not angry. Why should I be?” “Truly?” His tone became playful. “If you aren't angry, give me a smile.” How could she? He was proving difficult to handle. Looking closely, she saw his lustful eyes fixed on her breast and suddenly understood. So that was what he wanted! Recalling his offensiveness, she resolved to teach him a lesson. The anticipated pleasure of revenge brightened her mood. She smiled, her eyes sparkling, then rose and walked a few steps before turning to glance sideways at him, as though about to speak. Her lowered gaze and seductive movements were artful indeed. Huang felt as though seventeen or eighteen little hands were tickling his heart. His plan had been to offer himself in Chen's place, rescuing the young man and gaining an advantage for himself. He had begun by deliberately offending her, to end her hopes of Chen, then intended to win her over through the deference prescribed in the old seducer's formula of looks, virility, wealth, humility, and leisure. He had expected this to require considerable effort. Such swift success delighted him beyond expectation.

“七阿姐，”他开始挑逗，“我听世龙说过，你一个人孤孤单单，寂寞得很。可有这话？”“是啊！”阿七把眼望着别处，似乎不好意思正视黄仪，“不然我还不会来寻陈世龙。”“你现在就寻看他也没用了。陈世龙得新忘旧，一片心都在张家的阿珠小姐身上。”听得这话，阿七的妒心又起，冷笑说道：“哼，阿珠我也见过，黄毛丫头也叫‘小姐’了，真正气数！”“这都不去说它了，提起来你不开心。阿七姐，”黄仪试探着问，“你住哪里？”“就住郁老头原来往的地方。现在是我一个人。”“怪不得！一个住是太寂寞了些。”黄仪说道，“用个小大姐陪陪你嘛！”“有一个。”阿七答道，“笨得象牛，蠢得象猪，一吃过夜饭就要打瞌盹，上了床象死人一样。”

“Sister A’qi,” he began insinuatingly, “Shilong told me you're alone and very lonely. Is that true?” “Yes.” She looked elsewhere, seemingly too shy to meet his eyes. “Otherwise I wouldn't have come looking for him.” “Finding him won't help now. Chen Shilong forgets old affections for new ones. His whole heart is set on Miss Zhu of the Zhang family.” Jealousy stirred again. “Hmph! I've seen A’zhu. Even a mere slip of a girl gets called ‘Miss’ now. What a world!” “Let's leave that. It only makes you unhappy. Tell me, Sister A’qi, where do you live?” “Where Old Yu used to live. I'm alone there now.” “No wonder! Living alone is too lonely. Why not hire a maid for company?” “I have one. As stupid as an ox and as dull as a pig. After supper she starts dozing, and once in bed she's like a dead person.”

“这样子，夜里就寂寞了。也没有人来看看你？”“有哪个？鬼都没有得上门。”“那么，”黄仪涎着脸说：“我来做‘鬼’好不好？”“这，这叫什么话？”“你说鬼都没得上门，我就做‘鬼’上你的门！”“啊唷！”阿七双手环抱在胸前，作出不胜战栗的样子，“你来嘛就来！啥叫‘做鬼上门’，说得人吓兮兮地！“这副神态虽是做作，却也可喜，而黄仪特感会心的是，她那第一句话，认为无意流露，最见真情，只要能够上门，象她这种出身，自然不愁不能入幕。

“Then your nights must be lonely. Doesn't anyone come to see you?” “Who would? Not even a ghost crosses my threshold.” “Then,” Huang asked with an ingratiating smile, “may I be the ghost?” “What sort of talk is that?” “You said not even a ghost comes. I'll be the ghost at your door!” “Oh!” Folding her arms across her chest, A’qi pretended to shudder. “Come if you like! Why talk of ghosts at the door? You make it sound frightening.” Her manner was affected but charming. Huang particularly relished her first words, taking them as an unguarded revelation of her true feelings. Once he could visit her house, with a woman of her background, he felt sure of being admitted to her bed.

心里这么在想，手上就随便了，“不要吓，不要吓！”他很自然的拉往了她的手：“说说笑笑。”阿七凝睇含笑，象是心里有什么不易为人知的高兴事在想，突然间，将手一夺，懔然说道：“不要动手动脚！”说着还转脸望了一下。这在黄仪又有会心了，“动手动脚”不要紧，就怕让人看见。那容易！“怎么搞的呢？叫学生子去买点心，到现在还不来？”他这样自言自语着，奔了出去。间壁的陈世龙却不免诧异，不懂阿七是什么意思？莫非真个孤衾难耐，有意接受黄仪的勾引？他想仔细看一看阿七的表情，无奈她背着身子，正朝窗外在望。就这时候，听得黄仪的脚步声，接着是关门声和落闩声。原来如此！陈世龙心想，黄仪心也太急了些，这下真有场“隔壁戏”好看了。

The thought made his hands less restrained. “Don't be frightened. We're only joking.” He took her hand quite naturally. She gazed at him with a smile, as though enjoying some secret thought. Suddenly she snatched her hand away and said sternly, “Keep your hands to yourself!” As she spoke, she glanced behind her. Huang thought he understood again: touching was acceptable; being seen was the danger. That was easy to remedy. “What's going on? I sent the apprentice to buy refreshments, and he still hasn't returned!” Muttering this, he hurried outside. In the adjoining space, Chen was puzzled. What did A’qi mean? Could loneliness truly have made her willing to accept Huang's advances? He tried to study her expression, but her back was turned as she looked out of the window. Then came Huang's footsteps, followed by the sound of a door closing and a bolt sliding home. So that was it! Huang was far too impatient. There would certainly be a performance worth watching from next door.

“你看我这地方怎么样？”黄仪走回来笑嘻嘻地说，“一门关紧，连只苍蝇都飞不进来。”“我晓得了！”阿七慢慢点着头，伸出一只用凤仙花染红了指甲的食指，指指戳戳地说：“你好坏！”“坏！怎么坏法？”“问你自己啊！”“我倒不晓得。”黄仪又拉住了她的手，涎着脸说：“你倒说给我听听。”“何必我说？”阿七把眼睛望着别处，“说出来就没有意思了。”“对，说出来没意思。只要心里有数就是。”一面说，一面把脸凑过去闻她。阿七只把脸往侧面仰了仰。但一双手被他拉着，就躲也躲不远，到底让他闻到了。“好香！”黄仪仰脸闭眼，向空嗅了两下，同时一只手从她膀子上慢慢摸了上去。

“What do you think of my room?” Huang returned smiling. “Once the door is shut, not even a fly can get in.” “I understand!” A’qi nodded slowly, pointing at him with an index finger whose nail was stained red with balsam. “You're wicked!” “Wicked? How?” “Ask yourself!” “I don't know.” He took her hand again and smiled ingratiatingly. “Tell me.” “Why should I?” She looked away. “Saying it aloud would spoil it.” “Exactly. No need to say it. Understanding is enough.” As he spoke, he leaned close and inhaled her scent. She tilted her face aside, but with both hands held, she could not move far enough to avoid him. “How fragrant!” Tilting back his head and closing his eyes, Huang sniffed the air twice. Meanwhile, one hand began moving slowly up her arm.

他还在不胜陶醉，陈世龙却在替他担心了。因为阿七已经变态，眼睛渐渐睁圆，眉毛渐渐上竖，嘴巴渐渐闭紧，最后扬起她那只多肉的手，使劲一掌，打在黄仪脸上。“啊！”黄仪大喊一声，睁开眼来，看到阿七的脸色，才知道是怎么回事？“你为什么打我？”他捂着脸问。“打你个调戏良家妇女！”阿七很沉着地说。“你！”黄仪象打雷似地暴喝一声，跳脚骂道：“你个臭婊子一声没有骂完，脸上又着了一掌，这时才显出阿七的泼辣，抢步过去，从桌上拿起把剪刀扬起来，咬牙切齿地骂：”你嘴里再不干不净，我一剪刀扎出你的眼乌珠！“不得了！陈世龙大为着急，要出人命了。幸好黄仪识趣，窘笑着说，“何必呢！这样子认真。早晓得你开不起玩笑，哪个孙子忘八蛋跟你罗嗦！”“哼！”阿七把剪刀往桌上一抛，板着脸叱斥：“走！开门。我要走了。”

While Huang remained entranced, Chen began to worry for him. A’qi's expression was changing: her eyes widened, her brows rose, and her mouth tightened. At last she raised her fleshy hand and struck him hard across the face. “Ah!” Huang shouted. Opening his eyes and seeing her expression, he finally understood. “Why did you hit me?” he demanded, holding his cheek. “For molesting a respectable woman,” she replied calmly. “You!” He roared and stamped. “You filthy whore...” Before he finished, another slap struck his face. Now A’qi showed her fierce spirit. She darted to the table, snatched up a pair of scissors, and raised them. Through clenched teeth she said, “Use that filthy language again, and I'll jab out your eyes!” Chen was alarmed. Someone might be killed! Fortunately, Huang knew when to retreat. With an embarrassed smile, he said, “Why take it so seriously?
