Just as a basket’s framework could not hold together without bamboo strips, a grand social establishment needed such men. Hu too could use a few to help with entertaining and social obligations. If Liu Bucai was not bad at heart, merely prone to making a mess of things, it might be worth finding a way to win him over as an assistant. “Here they are!” Chen suddenly tugged at Hu’s clothes and spoke softly. Hu collected himself and looked up. At once he felt something unusual. The young widow was a dark-complexioned beauty. Apart from her complexion, he could find nothing to criticize. Her waist was extremely slender, and as she walked she swayed like a willow in the breeze. Yet there was none of the calculated display of a courtesan; her grace was natural. Alighting from her chair, she rested a hand on a maid of eleven or twelve and walked past the stall. Hu’s face followed her until his back was turned to Chen. Chen had already paid. He gave Hu a quiet tug, and they followed the women through the temple gate. A’qi had noticed them long before. Now she dropped back a step, turned slightly and made a small warning gesture with her hand.

“她什么意思？”胡雪岩问。“大概是关照不是靠得太近。”听这一说，胡雪岩便站住了脚，尽自盯着她的背影看。从头到脚，一身玄色，头上簪一朵穿孝的白绒花，显得格外触目。“胡先生，”陈世龙轻声问道：“怎么样？”“就是皮肤黑一点。”“有名的‘黑芙蓉’嘛！”陈世龙说。“怎么叫黑芙蓉？只听说过黑牡丹。”“她的名字就叫芙蓉。”“芙蓉！”胡雪岩偏着头，皱着眉想，“好象什么地方听说过个名字？”就这样不断念着“芙蓉、芙蓉”，皱眉苦思，到底起起来了。“原来在这里！”他把刚才求的那张签，拿给陈世龙看。“巧了！”陈世龙极感兴趣的笑着，“看起来是前世注定的姻缘。”“不见得！‘美人何处采芙蓉’，是采不到的意思。”胡雪岩摇摇头，大为快怏之意。陈世龙从未见过他有这样患得患失、近乎沮丧的神情，心里有些好笑。但随即想到，胡雪岩对芙蓉，可说是一见钟情，无论如何得把她“采”来供养，才是报答之道。

“What does she mean?” Hu asked. “Probably that we should not follow too closely.” Hu stopped and stared after the widow. She wore black from head to foot, with a soft white mourning flower in her hair that stood out strikingly. “What do you think, Mr Hu?” Chen asked softly. “Only that her complexion is a little dark.” “She is famous as Black Lotus.” “Why Black Lotus? I have only heard of Black Peony.” “Her name is Furong—Lotus.” “Furong!” Hu tilted his head and frowned. “Where have I heard that name?” He repeated it, thinking hard, until at last he remembered. “Here!” He showed Chen the fortune slip. “What a coincidence!” Chen laughed with interest. “It looks like a marriage destined in a former life.” “Not necessarily. ‘Where does the beauty gather lotus blooms?’ means that the lotus cannot be gathered.” Hu shook his head in disappointment. Chen had never seen him so anxious about gaining or losing something, almost dejected, and was secretly amused. Then he reflected that Hu had plainly fallen in love at first sight. Whatever happened, he must help gather this lotus for Hu. That would be a way to repay his kindness.

“再进去看看！”胡雪岩说。“胡先生，你一个人去好了，她有点认识我的，见面不大方便，我先避开为妙。”等陈世龙一走，胡雪岩一个在大殿前面那只高可及人的大香炉旁边，七上八下想心里，又想闯进殿去细看一看，又怕不依阿七的暗示，会把好事搞坏，左思右想只是打不定主意，自己都觉得有些好笑，几万银子上落的生意，都是当机立断，毫无悔尤，偏偏这么点事会大为作难！辰光就这样空耗着，耗到阿七和芙蓉出殿，他不能再没行动了，“嗐！”他自己对自己不满，这有什么大不了的！成也罢，不成也罢，何必看得那样认真？这一转念，犹豫和怯意一扫而空，同时也把阿七的约定和暗示，都抛到九霄云外，踏着从容潇洒的步子迎了上去，清清朗朗地喊一声：“郁四嫂！”

“Let us go farther in and have another look,” Hu said. “You had better go alone, Mr Hu. She knows me a little, and meeting her might be awkward. I should keep out of the way.” Once Chen left, Hu stood beside the great incense burner, as tall as a man, in front of the main hall. His thoughts rose and fell. He wanted to go inside for a closer look, yet feared that disregarding A’qi’s warning would spoil the affair. He could not make up his mind. It seemed ridiculous even to him: in transactions involving tens of thousands of taels, he decided instantly and felt no regret. Yet such a small matter left him at a loss. Time slipped away until A’qi and Furong emerged from the hall. He could not remain inactive. “Bah!” he said to himself in annoyance. What was so important? Whether it succeeded or failed, why take it so seriously? The thought swept away his hesitation and timidity. It also sent A’qi’s agreement and warning clean out of his mind. With an easy, confident step he went forward and called clearly, “Sister-in-Law Yu!”

既然叫出来了，阿七不能不理，装出略如惊喜的神态说道：“啊，胡老板，是你！怎么有空？来烧香，还是啥？”“偶然路过，进来逛一逛。”胡雪岩一面说，一面打量芙蓉。她那双眼睛很活，但也很静，在初见胡雪岩，视线飞快地一绕之后，一直垂着眼皮，看着地下。阿七心想，一不做，二不休，既然胡雪岩自己要出头，索性彰明较著替他们拉拢，让他自己来显显本事，倒省了许多心。于是她说：“胡老板，我要敲你的竹杠，好好请一请我们……”一说到“我们”两字，芙蓉便推一推她的手埋怨：“你这个人！哪里有这样子的？”“怕啥！”阿七一副理直气壮的态度，“胡老板又不是外人，是我们老头子的要好弟兄！”“正是这话。这位……”胡雪岩微笑着说：“这位小姐，不必见外！”“喔，”阿七趁机说道，“胡老板，我来引见，这是我的小姐妹，娘家姓刘，夫家姓何，小名叫芙蓉。你叫她名字好了。”听这番介绍，芙蓉只是皱眉，胡雪岩不知道她因何不满，不敢鲁莽，“没有这个道理！至少该尊称一声小姐。”说着作了个揖，“芙蓉小姐！”“不敢当。”芙蓉带着羞意，还了礼，接着转脸对阿七说：“我先走一步了！”

Since he had called, A’qi had to answer. She assumed an expression of mild surprise and pleasure. “Ah, Boss Hu! How do you find the time? Have you come to burn incense, or what?” “I happened to be passing and came in for a stroll.” As he spoke, Hu studied Furong. Her eyes were lively yet composed. On first seeing him, she had glanced swiftly at him; ever since, she had kept them lowered toward the ground. A’qi decided that, since Hu had chosen to show himself, she might as well bring them together openly and let him display his own abilities. It would save her a great deal of trouble. “Boss Hu, I mean to take advantage of you. You must give us a proper treat.” At the word “us,” Furong nudged her hand and protested. “Really! How can you behave like that?” “What is there to fear?” A’qi answered as though her conduct were perfectly justified. “Boss Hu is no stranger. He is my old man’s close friend.” “Exactly,” Hu said with a smile. “This young lady need not stand on ceremony.” “Oh, let me introduce you,” A’qi went on. “This is a young friend of mine. Her maiden surname is Liu, and she married into the He family. Her personal name is Furong. You may call her that.” Furong frowned at the introduction. Hu did not know what displeased her and dared not be rash. “Certainly not! I must at least address her respectfully as Miss.” He bowed. “Miss Furong.” “You are too kind.” Blushing, she returned the greeting, then turned to A’qi. “I must leave you now.”

“你不要扫我的兴！”阿七一把拉住她，“我老早想到白衣庵去吃素斋，难得今天凑巧，又有人做东道，又有人陪我。”芙蓉不响，自是默许了。胡雪岩便一叠连声地说：“好，好！我做个小东。不过白衣奄在哪里？在它那里吃素斋是怎么个规矩？我都不知道。”“我知道！”阿七接口答说，“不过，胡老板，这个东道倒不是小东道！白衣奄的素菜，湖州有名的，吃一顿斋，缘簿上总要写五两银子才够面子。““只要你吃得中意，五两银子算啥？”胡雪岩避开一步问道：“轿子可是在山门外？”“已经打发走了。胡老板，拜托你到山门口去雇两顶，白衣庵在西门城脚下，轿伕都知道的。“胡雪岩答应着，抢步先行，等阿七和芙蓉一出山门口，轿子已经倾倒轿杠在等着了。但事情起了变化，芙蓉原已默许了的，突然变卦，说她的小兄弟在发烧，甚不放心，一定要回家。阿七自然不肯，无奈芙蓉的主意也很坚决。众目睽睽之下，不便拖拖拉拉地争持，于是胡雪岩反帮着她阿七，说不必勉强，改天还有相叙的机会。“哪里还有相叙的机会？”等芙蓉坐上轿子回家，阿七这样埋怨胡雪岩，“我关照你不要叫我，你不听！好好一头姻缘，让你自己搅散了！”此时此地，不宜细谈此事，胡雪岩自己认错：“都怪我不好。回家去说。”

“Don’t spoil my pleasure!” A’qi caught hold of her. “I have long wanted a vegetarian meal at Baiyi Nunnery. Today, by good fortune, I have someone to treat me and someone to keep me company.” Furong said nothing, which amounted to assent. Hu eagerly agreed. “Very well! Let me offer a modest meal. But where is Baiyi Nunnery, and how does one arrange to eat there? I know nothing about it.” “I know. But this will be no modest treat, Boss Hu! Its vegetarian dishes are famous in Huzhou. To keep up appearances, a guest must enter at least five taels in the donation book.” “If the food pleases you, what are five taels?” Hu stepped aside and asked, “Are your chairs outside the gate?” “We sent them away. Please hire two for us at the gate. Baiyi Nunnery is at the foot of the city wall by the West Gate. Every bearer knows it.” Hu agreed and hurried ahead. By the time the women came out, the chairs were waiting with their shafts lowered. But matters had changed. Furong, who had tacitly agreed, suddenly said that her younger brother had a fever. She was too worried to stay and must go home. A’qi resisted, but Furong was firm. With so many eyes upon them, they could not argue or pull one another about. Hu therefore helped persuade A’qi not to press her: there would be another occasion to meet. Once Furong had departed in her chair, A’qi reproached him. “What other occasion? I told you not to greet me, and you wouldn’t listen. You have spoiled a perfectly good match yourself!” This was no place for a detailed discussion. Hu admitted fault. “It was all my doing. Let us go home and talk.”

一回到家，说郁四到沂园“孵混堂”去了。好在通家之好，不避形迹，阿七便留胡雪岩吃午饭，谈芙蓉的事。“我已经露口风给她了，虽然没有指出人来，不过你一露面，也就很清楚了。”阿七又说：“她跟我的交情很够，等我慢慢来说，一定可以成功。哪晓得你心这么急？现在事情弄僵了！““也不见得。”胡雪岩说，“也许是她心里有数，所以不好意思。你不妨去探探她的口气看！”“当然！总不能就此算数。不过，很难！”阿七摇摇头说，“我懂她的脾气。”“她的脾气怎么样？”“她也是很爽快的人，一肯就肯，说不肯就不肯。”“我倒不相信！”胡雪岩心想，本来也还无所谓，照现在看，非要把芙蓉弄到手不可！不然传出去便成了一个话柄。不过这一趟是无论如何来不及了！且等年下有空，好好来动一番脑筋。心里存了这么个主意，便暂且抛开了芙蓉，自去知府衙门访杨、秦两位老夫子辞行，准备再住一天就带着黄仪回杭州。

Back at the house, they learned that Yu had gone to spend a leisurely spell at Yiyuan Bathhouse. As Hu was a close family friend, there was no need for formal reserve. A’qi kept him to lunch and discussed Furong. “I had already hinted at the matter to her. I didn’t name the man, but once you appeared it was obvious. She and I are very close. If I had been allowed to work on her gradually, it would certainly have succeeded. Who would have thought you were in such a hurry? Now things are at an impasse.” “Not necessarily,” Hu replied. “Perhaps she understood and felt embarrassed. You might sound her out.” “Of course. We cannot simply abandon it. But it will be difficult.” A’qi shook her head. “I know her temperament.” “What is it like?” “She is straightforward too. When she agrees, she agrees; when she refuses, she refuses.” “I don’t believe it.” Hu had initially been indifferent enough, but now felt he must win Furong. Otherwise, if the story spread, it would become a subject of gossip. There was certainly no time on this visit. He would wait until he was free near the year’s end and give the matter serious thought. Having settled on that, he put Furong aside for the moment and went to the prefectural yamen to call on the two secretaries, Yang and Qin, and take his leave. He intended to stay one more day and then return to Hangzhou with Huang Yi.

“来一趟不容易，何妨多住几天。”郁四挽留他说，“你不是要在上海打局面，我有几个南得的朋友，不可不文。”这一说胡雪岩心思活动了。他一直想到南浔去一趟，因为做洋庄的丝商，南浔最多，一则应该联络一气，以便对付洋人，再则洋庄方面还有许多奥妙，非局外人所知，他们也不肯随便透露，现在有郁四介绍，正好叨教。于是他欣然答道：“好的！我就多留两天。”“两天？”郁四慢吞吞地答道：“也够了。不过，我这两天衙门里有事，不能陪你，我另外找个人陪你去，就同我去一样。”“好的。什么时候动身？”“随便你。明天一早动身好了。晚上我把陪你去的人找来，你们先见一见面。”那人是郁四手下的一个帮手，沉默寡言，但人头极熟，交游极广。他姓刘，单名一个权字，原是南浔人。南浔刘家是大族，刘权以同族的关系，包收南得刘家的钱粮。以这样的关系，陪着胡雪岩同行引路，可说是最适当的人选。

“You seldom come. Why not stay a few more days?” Yu urged. “You want to establish yourself in Shanghai. I have several friends in Nanxun whom you ought to know.” This interested Hu. He had long wanted to visit Nanxun, which had more silk merchants engaged in the export trade than anywhere else. They ought to build connections and act together in dealing with foreigners. Besides, there were many intricacies of the export business that outsiders did not know and insiders would not readily disclose. With Yu’s introduction, he could learn from them. “Very well,” he answered gladly. “I’ll stay another two days.” “Two days?” Yu replied slowly. “That should be enough. But I have business at the yamen and cannot accompany you. I’ll find someone else to go with you. It will be just as good as going with me.” “When do we leave?” “Whenever you like. Tomorrow morning would do. I’ll bring your companion here tonight so that you can meet.” The man was one of Yu’s assistants, quiet and sparing of words but widely acquainted and well connected. His surname was Liu and his given name Quan. He was a native of Nanxun, where the Liu clan was a great family. Through his clan connections, he had contracted to collect its taxes. This made him an ideal companion and guide for Hu.

“你哪一天回湖州？”郁四问道，“我们把它说定规！”“我想两天工夫总够了。”“明天，后天，好！你准定大后天回来，我有事要请个客，你一定要赶到。““一定！”胡雪岩毫不迟疑地应承。“那就拜托你了。”郁四向刘权说，“老刘，你晓得的，胡老板是王大老爷的好朋友。”这是指点刘权，要把胡雪岩的这种特殊关系说出去，好增加声势，果然，“不怕官，只怕管”，就因为王有龄的关系，胡雪岩在南浔的两天，极受优礼，到第三天东道主还挽留，胡雪岩因为郁四有事请客，不能失约，坚辞而回。早晨上船，过午到湖州，陈世龙在码头迎接，告诉他说，郁四在沂园等他。“好，我正要淴个浴。”“我也晓得胡先生一定要淴浴。”陈世龙把手里的包裹一扬，“我把胡先生的干净小褂裤、袜子都带来了。”这虽是一件小事，显得陈世龙肯在自己身上用心，胡雪岩相当高兴。一路谈着南浔的情形，走到沂园。跟郁四见面招呼过，随即解衣磅礴，一洗征尘，顿觉满身轻快，加以此行极其顺利，所以精神抖擞，特别显得有劲。

“Which day will you return to Huzhou?” Yu asked. “Let us fix it.” “I should think two days will be enough.” “Tomorrow and the next day. Good. Then be sure to return the day after that. I am giving a dinner for a particular occasion, and you must be there.” “Certainly,” Hu agreed without hesitation. “Then I leave it to you,” Yu told Liu Quan. “Old Liu, you know that Boss Hu is Prefect Wang’s good friend.” He meant Liu to make this special relationship known and add weight to Hu’s standing. As the saying went, people feared not officials in general but the official who had authority over them. Through his connection with Wang, Hu received exceptional courtesy during his two days in Nanxun. On the third day his hosts still urged him to remain, but he could not break his promise to Yu and firmly took his leave. Boarding in the morning, he reached Huzhou after noon. Chen met him at the landing and said that Yu was waiting at Yiyuan. “Good. I was just wanting a bath.” “I knew you would, Mr Hu.” Chen raised the bundle in his hand. “I have brought your clean underclothes and socks.” It was a small matter, but it showed Chen’s thoughtful attention to him, and Hu was pleased. They walked to Yiyuan, talking of Nanxun on the way. After greeting Yu, Hu undressed and washed away the dust of travel, feeling light and refreshed. The success of his journey added to his spirits, and he seemed especially energetic.

谈了好些在南浔的经过，看看天色将晚，胡雪岩便问：“四哥，你今天请哪个？是啥事？”“很客气的一位客人。”郁四说着，便向放在软榻前面的胡雪岩的那双鞋子，看了一眼。胡雪岩是极机警的人，立刻便说：“我这双鞋子走过长路，不大干净，恐怕在生客面前，不大好看吧！”“自己人说老实话，是不大光鲜。不要紧，”郁四叫过跑堂来说，“你到我那里去一趟，跟四奶奶说，把我新做的那件宁绸衬绒袍子，直贡呢马褂拿来。另外再带一双新鞋子。”“何必？”胡雪岩说，“你新做的袍子怎么拿来我穿？我的这身衣服也还有八成新，叫他们刷刷干净，也还可以将就。鞋子也不必去拿，回头走出去现买一双好了。”郁四没有理他，挥挥手示意跑堂照办，然后才说：“你也太见外了，套把衣服算得了什么？还要客气！”听这一说，胡雪岩还能有何表示？丢开此事，谈到他预备第二天就回杭州。郁四还要留他，胡雪岩不肯，两人翻覆争执，没有结果，而跑堂的已把衣服取来了。“走吧！”郁四说，“时间不早了。你到底哪天动身，回头再说。”

After much talk of Nanxun, Hu noticed that evening was approaching. “Brother Yu, whom are you entertaining today? What is the occasion?” “A guest who requires special courtesy,” Yu replied, glancing at the shoes in front of Hu’s couch. Hu was quick to understand. “These shoes have traveled a long way and are rather dirty. They might not make a good impression on a guest I haven’t met.” “Between ourselves, they are not very presentable. Never mind.” Yu called an attendant. “Go to my house and ask Fourth Mistress for my new ning-silk robe with its plush lining and my gong-cloth riding jacket. Bring a pair of new shoes too.” “Why should I wear your new robe?” Hu protested. “My clothes are still almost new. Have them brushed, and they will do. There is no need to fetch shoes either. I can buy a pair when we go out.” Yu ignored him and waved the attendant away to carry out the order. Then he said, “You are standing far too much on ceremony. What is a suit of clothes between friends?” Hu could hardly object further. He changed the subject to his plan to return to Hangzhou the following day. Yu urged him to stay; Hu refused. They argued back and forth without reaching a decision, until the attendant returned with the clothes. “Let us go,” Yu said. “It is getting late. We can discuss your departure later.”

“慢点！”胡雪岩看着那双双梁缎鞋和一身新衣服，摸着脸说，“要剃个头才好，不知道辰光够不够？”“够，够！你尽管剃！”于是唤了个剃头担子来，胡雪岩剃头修脸，重新打过辫子，才穿上新袍新鞋，里里外外，焕然一新，跑堂的打趣说道：“胡老爷象个新郎官！”“我呢？”郁四接口问道：“你看我象不象个‘大冰老爷’？”郁四也是上下簇新，喜气洋洋，很象个吃喜酒的冰人。跑堂的还不曾接口，又出现了一个衣帽鲜洁，象个贺客佯的人，那是陈世龙。胡雪岩不觉诧异，“你怎么又来了？”他问，“是找我有话说？”陈世龙笑笑不响，只看着郁四。于是郁四说道：“我请客也有他一个。走吧！“

“Wait.” Looking at the double-ridged satin shoes and the new clothes, Hu touched his face. “I ought to have a shave. Is there time?” “Plenty. Go ahead.” A traveling barber was called. Hu had his head and face shaved and his queue redressed before putting on the new robe and shoes. He was transformed from head to foot. The attendant joked, “Master Hu looks like a bridegroom!” “And I?” Yu asked. “Do I look like an honored matchmaker?” He too was dressed in new clothes and beaming, very much like a matchmaker attending a wedding feast. Before the attendant could answer, another man appeared in fresh clothes and a clean hat, looking like a guest come to offer congratulations. It was Chen Shilong. Hu was surprised. “Why have you come back? Is there something you need to tell me?” Chen only smiled and looked at Yu. “He is invited too,” Yu said. “Let us go.”

第十八章｜CHAPTER EIGHTEEN

走了沂园，坐上轿子，陈世龙吩咐了一个地名，是胡雪岩所不曾听说过的，只觉得曲曲折折，穿过好儿子长巷，到了一处已近城脚，相当冷僻的地方，下轿一看，是一座很整齐的石库房子，黑漆双扉洞开，一直望到大厅，灯火通明，人影幢幢，再细看时，檐前挂着宫灯，厅内烧着红烛，似是有何喜庆的模样。“这是哪里？”胡雪岩问。“是我的房子。”“幄！”胡雪岩灵机一动，“四哥，莫非今朝是你的生日？怎么不先告诉我！”郁四微笑着点点头说：“你进去看了就知道了。”走到里面一看，有杨、秦两位老夫子，黄仪、老张，还有胡雪岩所认识的钱庄里的朋友，看见他们进来，一齐拱手，连称“恭喜”。胡雪岩只当是给郁四道贺，与己无干，悄悄退到一边去打量这所房子的格局，心里盘算，倘或地方够宽敞，风水也不错，倒不妨跟郁四谈谈，或买或典，在湖州安个家。这一打量发现了怪事，正中披了红桌围的条桌上，红烛双辉，有喜庆是不错，但做寿该有“糕桃烛面”，供的应该是寿头寿脑的“南极仙翁”，现在不但看不到寿桃寿面，而且供的是一幅五色缂丝的“和台二仙”。这不是做寿，是娶亲嫁女儿的喜事。“咦！”胡雪岩摸着报脑说：“真正‘丈二金刚摸不着头’！怎么回事？”

They left Yiyuan and entered their sedan chairs. Chen Shilong gave the bearers a place-name Hu had never heard. After winding through several long lanes, they reached a quiet, out-of-the-way spot near the city wall. Hu alighted before a neat stone-gated house. Both black lacquered doors stood open, giving a view straight through to a brightly lit hall full of moving figures. Palace lanterns hung beneath the eaves, and red candles burned inside. There seemed to be some celebration. “Where are we?” Hu asked. “At a house of mine,” Yu replied. An idea struck Hu. “Brother Yu, is it your birthday? Why didn’t you tell me?” Yu smiled and nodded. “Go in and you will see.” Inside were the two secretaries, Yang and Qin, Huang Yi, Old Zhang, and friends from the banks whom Hu knew. As they entered, everyone clasped hands and offered congratulations. Hu assumed these were meant for Yu and had nothing to do with him. He stepped quietly aside to inspect the house, thinking that, if it was spacious and favorably situated, he might discuss buying it or taking possession under a redeemable property pledge and establish a home in Huzhou. Then he noticed something odd. Two red candles shone on the central table, which was draped in red. It was certainly a celebration, but a birthday should have cakes, longevity peaches, candles and noodles, with an image of the venerable God of Longevity. There were no peaches or noodles. Instead, a five-colored silk tapestry depicted the Two Immortals of Harmony. This was a wedding celebration. “Why!” Hu rubbed the back of his head. “This is like trying to reach the head of a twelve-foot guardian deity—I can make neither head nor tail of it! What is going on?”

这一回引得哄堂大笑，笑声中出现一位堂客，是阿珠的娘，梳得极光的头，簪着红花，身上是缎袄罗裙。胡雪岩从未见她如此盛装过，不由得又愣住了。“胡先生！”阿珠的娘笑道：“恭喜，恭喜！”胡雪岩恍然大悟，回身以歉意的声音说道：“对不起，对不起！原来各位刚才是跟我道喜。我倒失礼了！”说着，连连拱手。这一来又引得大家发笑。胡雪岩倒又发觉一桩疑问，一把拉住郁四问道：“郁四嫂呢？”“大概在里头陪新人。”“对了！”阿珠的娘笑得异常愉悦，“真正好人才！胡先生，你好福气，还不快来看？”于是一拥而进，都要来看胡雪岩的新宠。而他本人反倒脚步趑趄了，心想，世人有这种怪事，自己娶妾，别人都知道，就是本人被瞒在鼓里！现在既已揭晓，总也得问问清楚，不然言语之间接不上头，岂不是处处要闹笑话。

The room burst into laughter. Through it came a woman: A’zhu’s mother, her hair smoothly dressed and adorned with a red flower, wearing a satin jacket and gauze skirt. Hu had never seen her so splendidly attired and stared again. “Mr Hu!” she said, smiling. “Congratulations!” At last he understood. Turning to the company, he apologized. “Forgive me! So it was me you were congratulating. How discourteous I have been!” He clasped his hands repeatedly, provoking another burst of laughter. Then a new question occurred to him. He caught Yu by the arm. “Where is Sister-in-Law Yu?” “Probably inside with the bride.” “Exactly!” A’zhu’s mother smiled delightedly. “Such a fine young woman! You are fortunate, Mr Hu. Come and see her.” Everyone surged toward the inner rooms to look at Hu’s new concubine. Only Hu himself hesitated. What a strange affair: everyone knew he was taking a concubine except the man concerned! Now that the secret was out, he must at least learn the details, or he would make a fool of himself at every turn.

于是，他落后两步，拉住陈世龙说：“到底怎么回事？你先告诉我。”“四叔都说好了，就请胡先生做现成的新郎官。”这两句话要言不烦，胡雪岩完全明白，今天的局面，是郁四一手的经营，劝自己到南得去走一趟，原是“调虎离山”，好趁这两天的辰光办喜事。虽说他在湖州很够面子，时间到底太匆促，好比喝杯茶的工夫要拿生米煮成熟饭，近乎不可思议。刘不才又是个很难惹的家伙，郁四能在短短两天之内，让他就范，大概威胁利诱，软硬齐来，不知花了多少气力！转念到此，胡雪岩不由得想到了“盛情可感”这句话，钱是小事，难得的是他的这片心、这番力！交朋友交到这样，实在有些味道了。

He fell back a step or two and detained Chen. “Tell me what has happened.” “Uncle Four has arranged everything. All you need do is be the bridegroom.” Those few words explained it. Yu had organized the whole scene. Encouraging Hu to visit Nanxun had been a stratagem to lure the tiger away from its mountain, giving Yu two days to arrange the marriage. Influential as he was in Huzhou, the time had been desperately short. It was almost like cooking raw rice in the time it took to drink a cup of tea—hard to imagine. Liu Bucai was also difficult to deal with. To bring him to terms in two days, Yu had probably used threats and inducements, persuasion and pressure together. Who knew how much effort it had cost? Hu was deeply moved by such generosity. Money was a small matter. What was rare was the thought and effort behind it. There was real savor in friendship carried to such lengths.

“嗨！”郁四回身喊道，“你怎么回事？”这一喊才让胡雪岩警省，抬眼望去，恰好看到珠翠满头的阿七，红裙红袄，浓妆艳抹，从东首一间屋里，喜气洋洋地迎了出来。郁四这时候特别高兴，先拿阿七打趣，“唷！”他将她上下一看：“你倒象煞个新娘子！”阿七不理他，冲着胡雪岩改口喊做：“胡大哥！”她得意地问道：“你怎么谢我？”“承情之至！”胡雪岩拱手说，“我早晚一炉香，祝你早生贵子。”这是善颂善祷，阿七越发笑容满面，接着便以居停主人的身分，招待宾客，一个个都应酬到，显得八面玲玫，而郁四却有些不耐烦了。“好了，好了！”他拦着她说，“办正经要紧。请出来见礼吧！”娶妾见礼，照规矩只是向主人主母磕头，主母不在，只有主人，胡雪岩觉得此举大可不必。无奈贺客们众口一词，礼不可废，把他强按在正中太师椅上。然后只见东首那道门帘掀开，阿七权充伴娘，把芙蓉扶了出来，向上磕了个头，轻轻喊了声：“老爷！”芙蓉忸怩，胡雪岩也觉得忸怩，贺客们则大为高兴，尤其是杨、秦两位老夫子，评头品足，毫无顾忌。阿珠的娘便来解围，连声催促，邀客入席。

“Hey! What are you doing?” Yu called back. This brought Hu to himself. Looking up, he saw A’qi coming joyfully from a room on the east side, dressed in a red jacket and skirt, heavily made up and glittering with pearls and jade. Yu was particularly happy and began by teasing her. “Well!” He looked her up and down. “You look just like the bride yourself.” Ignoring him, she addressed Hu by a new title. “Brother Hu! How will you thank me?” she asked triumphantly. “I am deeply obliged.” Hu clasped his hands. “I shall burn incense morning and evening and pray that you soon bear a fine son.” This auspicious wish made her smile still more broadly. Assuming the role of hostess, she attended to every guest with easy social skill, until Yu grew impatient. “Enough! The proper ceremony comes first. Bring her out to pay her respects.” When a concubine entered a household, custom required only that she kowtow to its master and mistress. The mistress was absent, leaving Hu alone. He thought the ceremony quite unnecessary, but the guests unanimously insisted that propriety must be observed and pressed him into the principal armchair. The eastern curtain lifted. A’qi, acting as attendant to the bride, brought Furong out. She bowed to the floor and softly addressed him as “Master.” Both Furong and Hu felt embarrassed, while the guests were delighted. Secretaries Yang and Qin, in particular, appraised her appearance without restraint. A’zhu’s mother came to the rescue by urging everyone to take their places at dinner.

喜筵只有一席，设在厅上，都是男客，猜拳行令，闹到二更天方散。贺客告辞，只郁四和陈世龙留了下来。“到里面去吧！”郁四说，“看看你的新居，是阿七一手料理的，不晓得中不中你的意？”说着，他拉着胡雪岩就走。“慢点，慢点！”胡雪岩说，“四哥，你这么费心，我不知道怎么说才好？一共替我垫了多少？”“这时候算什么帐？明天再说。”“好，明天再说。不过，有件事我不明白。”胡雪岩问：“她那个叔叔呢？”“你是说刘不才？”郁四略停一下说道，“你想，他怎么好意思来？”侄女儿与人做妾，做叔叔的自不好意思来吃喜酒。胡雪岩心想，照此看来，刘不才倒还是一个要脸面的人。“不过今天不来，迟早要上门的。这个人有点麻烦，明天我再跟你谈。”胡雪岩本想把他预备收服刘不才做个帮手的话，说给郁四听，但郁四不容他如此从容、一叠连声地催着，便只好先丢开“叔叔”，去看他的“侄女儿”。

There was only one banquet table, set in the hall, and all those seated at it were men. Finger-guessing drinking games and other revelry continued until the second watch. The guests then took their leave, except for Yu and Chen. “Come inside,” Yu said, taking Hu by the arm. “See your new home. A’qi arranged it all. I hope it pleases you.” “Wait, Brother Yu! You have taken such trouble that I don’t know how to thank you. How much have you advanced for me altogether?” “Why discuss accounts now? We can do that tomorrow.” “Very well. But there is something I don’t understand. What about her uncle?” “Liu Bucai?” Yu paused. “How could he have the face to come?” An uncle could scarcely attend a wedding feast at which his niece became a concubine. Hu reflected that Liu evidently retained some sense of dignity. “He has not come today,” Yu added, “but he will appear sooner or later. He is troublesome. I’ll tell you about him tomorrow.” Hu wanted to explain his plan to win Liu over as an assistant, but Yu would not let him linger and kept urging him onward. He had to put the uncle aside and go to see the niece.

一踏进新房，看得眼都花了，触目是一片大红大绿，裱得雪亮的房间里，家具器物，床帐衾褥，无不全新，当然，在他感觉中，最新的是芙蓉那个人！新人正由阿珠的娘和阿七陪着吃饭，听见脚步声响，她先就站了起来，有些手足无措似地。胡雪岩也觉得不无僵窘之感，只连声说道：“请坐，请坐！你们吃你们的。我看看！”借故搭讪，看到壁上悬着一幅红绫裱的虎皮笺，是黄仪写的字，胡雪岩腹中墨水不多，但这幅字，却能读得断句，因为是他熟悉的一首诗——签上的那首诗，只最后一句改了两个字，原来是“美人何处采芙蓉”，黄仪却写成“美人江上采芙蓉”。胡雪岩笑了，回头看到陈世龙，他也笑了。显然的，这是他跟黄仪两个人搞的把戏。别人却不明白，不知他们笑些什么？阿七最性急，首先追问，陈世龙便将胡雪岩的如何求签，又如何因“何处”二字而失望的故事，笑着讲了一遍。大家都感觉这件事很有趣，特别是芙蓉本人，一面听，一面不断拾起头来看一看，每一看便如流光闪电般，那眼神在胡雪岩觉得异常明亮。“那就没有话说了！”阿七对芙蓉说，“ 你天生该姓胡！”“是啊，真正姻缘前定。”郁四也说，“我从没有办过这样顺利的事。”

The bridal chamber dazzled him. Everywhere he looked were brilliant reds and greens. In the freshly papered room, the furniture, utensils, bed curtains and bedding were all new. To Hu, of course, the newest thing of all was Furong herself. She was eating with A’zhu’s mother and A’qi. At the sound of footsteps she rose, looking rather at a loss. Hu felt awkward too. “Please sit. Go on eating. I am only looking round.” Searching for something to say, he noticed a sheet of tiger-patterned paper mounted in red silk on the wall. Huang Yi had written the calligraphy. Hu had little literary learning, but could make out its phrasing because he knew the poem: it was the verse on his fortune slip. Only two characters in the final line had changed. Instead of “Where does the beauty gather lotus blooms?” Huang had written, “Upon the river the beauty gathers lotus blooms.” Hu smiled and looked back at Chen, who smiled too. Plainly this was a trick the two of them had devised. The others did not understand their amusement. Impatient A’qi asked first, and Chen laughingly told how Hu had drawn the slip and been disappointed by the words “where does.” Everyone found the story entertaining, especially Furong. As she listened, she repeatedly raised her eyes to look at Hu. Each glance seemed to him as bright as a flash of light. “Then there is no more to say!” A’qi told her. “You were born to join the Hu family.” “Indeed, a match ordained beforehand,” Yu agreed. “I have never arranged anything so smoothly.”

“话虽如此，到底是两位的成全。借花献佛，我敬四哥四嫂一杯酒。”阿珠的娘手快，听胡雪岩这一说，已把两杯酒递了过来，一杯给她，一杯给郁四。“慢来，慢来！不是这样。”阿七用指挥的语气说，“你们索性也坐了下来再说。”于是阿七亲自安排席次，上首两位，胡雪岩和芙蓉，阿珠的娘和陈世龙东西相对，然后她和郁四说：“老头子，我们坐下首，做主人。”大家都坐定了，只有芙蓉畏畏缩缩，仿佛怕礼节僭越，不敢跟“老爷”并坐似地，胡雪岩就毫不迟疑地伸手一拉，芙蓉才红着脸坐了下来。“你们先吃交杯盏，再双双谢媒。”由这里开始，阿七想出花样来闹，笑声不断，她自己也醉了。胡雪岩酒吃得不少，但心里很清楚，怕阿七醉后出丑，万一跟陈世龙说几句不三不四的话，那就是无可弥补的憾事，所以不断跟阿珠的娘使眼色，要他们劝阻。

“Even so, we owe it to you both,” Hu said. “Let me borrow another’s flowers to make an offering and drink a toast to Brother Yu and his wife.” Quick-handed A’zhu’s mother immediately brought two cups, one for A’qi and one for Yu. “Wait! That is not the way,” A’qi directed. “You had better all sit down first.” She arranged the seats herself. Hu and Furong took the two places of honor; A’zhu’s mother and Chen faced one another on the east and west. “Old man,” A’qi told Yu, “we will sit at the lower end and act as hosts.” Everyone sat except Furong, who hesitated as though afraid that sitting beside her master would overstep her rank. Hu took her hand without hesitation, and she blushed and sat. “First drink the bridal cross-cup toast, then thank your matchmakers together.” From this beginning A’qi devised one amusement after another. Laughter never ceased, and she herself became drunk. Hu had drunk a good deal too, but his mind was clear. He feared that A’qi might disgrace herself. If she said something improper to Chen, the damage might be irreparable. He kept signaling to A’zhu’s mother to intervene.

“好了！我们也该散散了，让新人早早安置。”阿珠的娘说到这里，回头看了看便问：“咦！世龙呢？”陈世尤见机，早已逃席溜走。胡雪岩心里有些着急，怕她一追问，正好惹得阿七注意，便赶紧乱以他语：“郁四嫂酒喝得不少，先抉她躺一躺吧！”一句话未完，阿七张口就吐，狼藉满地，把簇新的洞房，搞得一塌糊涂，气得郁四连连叹气。自然，胡雪岩不会介意，芙蓉更是殷勤，忘却羞涩矜持，也顾不得一身盛装，亲自下手照料，同时指挥新用的一名女仆和她自己带来的一个小大姐，收拾残局。等呕吐过后，阿七的酒便醒了，老大过意下去，连声道歉。郁四又骂她“现世”，旁人再夹在中间劝解，倒显得异常热闹。乱过一阵，贺客纷纷告辞，芙蓉送到中门，胡雪岩送出大门，在郁四上轿以前，执着他的手说：“四哥，这一来你倒是给我出了一个难题。湖州怕还要住几天了。”郁四笑笑不响，陈世龙却接上了话，“胡先生！”他说，“如果杭州有事要办，我去跑一趟。”“对呀！”阿珠的娘说，“尽管叫世龙去！”“等我想一想，明天再说。”

“We ought to leave and let the newlyweds retire early,” A’zhu’s mother said. Turning round, she asked, “Why, where is Shilong?” Chen had seen the danger and slipped away long before. Hu grew anxious that pursuing the question would draw A’qi’s attention. He hurriedly changed the subject. “Sister-in-Law Yu has had quite a lot. Help her lie down for a while.” Before he finished, A’qi vomited all over the floor, leaving the brand-new bridal chamber in a dreadful mess. Yu sighed repeatedly in exasperation. Hu naturally took no offense. Furong was even more attentive: forgetting her embarrassment and reserve, and heedless of her splendid clothes, she personally cared for A’qi while directing a newly engaged maid and the young maid she had brought with her to clean up. Once she had been sick, A’qi sobered. She was terribly ashamed and apologized over and over. Yu scolded her for making an exhibition of herself, while the others intervened to soothe them. The commotion was considerable. Eventually the visitors departed. Furong saw them to the inner gate, and Hu accompanied them to the street. Before Yu entered his chair, Hu took his hand. “Brother Yu, you have set me a problem. I fear I shall have to stay in Huzhou a few more days.” Yu smiled without answering. Chen spoke instead. “Mr Hu, if there is business in Hangzhou, I can go for you.” “Certainly!” A’zhu’s mother agreed. “Send Shilong wherever he is needed.” “Let me think. We will discuss it tomorrow.”

回进门来亲自关了大门，走进大厅，喜烛犹在，红艳艳的光晕闪耀着，给胡雪岩带来了梦幻似的感觉。“真正象做梦！”他自语着，在一张新椅子上坐了下来，看着扶手，识得那木料，在广东名叫“酸枝”，样子也是广式，在杭州地方要觅这样一堂新家具，都不容易，何况是在湖州？见得郁四花的心血，真正可感。由郁四想到阿七，再想到老张和他的妻儿女婿，还有黄仪和衙门里的两位老夫子，最后想到这天的场面，胡雪岩十分激动——世界上实在是好人多，坏人少，只看今天，就可明白，不但成全自己的好事，而且为了让自己有一番意外的惊喜，事先还花了许多心血“调虎离山”。这完全是感情，不是从利害关系生出来的势利。正想得出神，咀嚼得有味，听见有人轻轻喊道：“老爷！转脸一看是芙蓉，正捧了一盏盖碗茶来，她已卸了晚妆，唇红齿白，梳个又光又黑的新样宫署，这时含羞带笑地站在胡雪岩面前，那双眼中荡漾着别样深情，使得胡雪岩从心底泛起从未经验过的兴奋，咽了两口唾沫，润湿了干燥的喉咙，方能开口答话。

Hu returned and closed the main gate himself. In the hall the wedding candles still burned, their glowing red light giving everything a dreamlike air. “It really is like a dream,” he murmured, sitting in a new chair. Looking at the armrest, he recognized the wood known in Guangdong as suanzhi rosewood. The design was Cantonese too. Finding a whole new suite of such furniture would be difficult even in Hangzhou, let alone Huzhou. Yu’s painstaking care deeply moved him. From Yu he thought of A’qi, then of Old Zhang and his wife, daughter and son-in-law-to-be, of Huang Yi and the two secretaries, and finally of the day’s gathering. His feelings rose. There were, after all, more good people than bad in the world. Today alone proved it. They had not merely brought about his happiness; they had taken elaborate pains to send him away beforehand so that it would come as an unexpected delight. This was affection, not favor calculated from advantage. While he sat absorbed, savoring the thought, someone called softly, “Master.” He turned. Furong stood there holding a covered teacup. She had removed her evening makeup; her lips were red and her teeth white, and her glossy black hair was dressed in a new court-style bun. Smiling shyly before him, with a different depth of feeling in her eyes, she stirred an excitement he had never known. He swallowed twice to moisten his dry throat before he could speak.

“谢谢！”他一只手接过茶碗，一只手捏住她的左臂。“索性在外面坐一坐再进去吧！”芙蓉说，“我熏了一炉香在那里，气味怕还没有散尽。”“郁四嫂真有趣。”胡雪岩问道：“你们是很熟的人？”“认识不过两年，从她嫁了郁四爷，有一次应酬……”芙蓉笑笑不说下去了。“怎么呢？”胡雪岩奇怪，“又是闹了什么笑话？”“不是闹笑话。”芙蓉语声从容地答道，“那夭别人都不大跟她说话，想来是嫌她的出身。我不晓得她是什么人？只觉得她很爽朗，跟她谈了好些时候。就此做成了好朋友。”“原来如此！”胡雪岩很欣赏芙蓉的态度，同时又想到她刚才不嫌龌龊，亲自照料呕吐狼藉的阿七的情形，庆幸自己娶了个很贤慧的妇人。这一转念间，胡雪岩对芙蓉的想法不同了。在一个男人来说，妻妾之间的区别甚多，最主要的是“娶妻娶德，娶妾娶色”。胡雪岩看中芙蓉，也就是倾心于她的翦水双瞳，柳腰一捻，此刻虽然矜持庄重，而那风流体态，依然能令人如灯蛾扑火般，甘死无悔。但是，光有这样的想法，胡雪岩觉得可惜，就好比他表链上所系的那个英国金洋钱一样，英镑诚然比什么外国钱都来得贵重，但拿来当作表坠，别致有趣，比它本身的价值高得多。这样，如果只当它一个可以折算多少银子的外国钱来用，岂不是有点儿糟蹋了它？要娶芙蓉这样一个美妾，也还不算是太难的事，但有色又有德，却是可遇而不可求的事，应该格外珍惜。这样想着，他的心思又变过了，刚才是一味兴奋，所想到的是“携手入罗帏”，此刻是满足的欣悦，如对名花，如品醇酒，要慢慢的欣赏。

“Thank you.” He accepted the cup with one hand and gently held her left arm with the other. “Let us sit outside a little longer before going in,” Furong said. “I have burned some incense in there, but the smell from earlier may not have cleared yet.” “Sister-in-Law Yu is very amusing. Have you known each other long?” “Only two years. After she married Master Yu, we met at a gathering.” Furong smiled and stopped. “What happened? Another amusing incident?” “No.” She answered calmly. “The others scarcely spoke to her that day, probably because they disapproved of her background. I did not know who she was. I only thought her frank and lively and talked with her for a long time. That is how we became friends.” “I see.” Hu admired her attitude. Remembering how she had cared for A’qi without shrinking from the mess, he congratulated himself on having taken such a kind and capable woman into his household. His view of Furong changed. A man saw many distinctions between wife and concubine, the chief one expressed in the saying that a wife was chosen for virtue, a concubine for beauty. Hu himself had been captivated by Furong’s clear eyes and slender waist. Though she was now composed and dignified, her graceful figure could still draw a man like a moth to a flame, willing to perish without regret. But to think of her only that way would be a waste. It was like the British gold coin attached to his watch chain. A sovereign was worth more than other foreign coins, but used as an unusual and attractive ornament, it had a value beyond its silver equivalent. To treat it merely as money would diminish it. Finding a beautiful concubine like Furong was not so difficult; finding beauty joined with virtue was a rare good fortune that could not be commanded. She deserved special care. His mood changed again. A moment before, he had been absorbed in excitement and thoughts of leading her behind the gauze bed curtains. Now he felt a contented joy, as though contemplating a rare flower or savoring mellow wine, to be enjoyed slowly.

看他未曾说话，只是一会儿眨眼，一会儿微笑，芙蓉很想知道，他想什么想得这么有趣？然而陌生之感，到底还浓，只有尽自己的礼法。便试探育说道：“请到里面去坐吧！”“好！你先请。”这样客气，越使她有拘束之感，退后一步说：“老爷先请！我还有事。“她分内之事，就是尽一个主妇的责任，吹灭烛火，关上门窗，又到厨房里去，检点了一番，才回人“洞房”。胡雪岩一个人在屋里小饮，四碟小菜、一壶酒是早就预备在那里的，把杯回想这天的经过，心里有无数急待解答的疑问，所以看见她一进来就又忙忙碌碌地整理衾枕，便即说道：“芙蓉，你来！我们先谈谈。”“嗯！好。”芙蓉走了过来，拉开椅子坐下，顺手便把一碟火腿，换到他面前，接着又替他斟满了酒。他把酒杯递到她唇边，她喝了一口，又夹了一片火腿来，她也吃了。

He said nothing, only blinking or smiling from time to time. Furong wanted to know what gave him such pleasure, but the sense of being strangers was still strong, and she could only observe proper courtesy. “Shall we go inside?” she ventured. “Certainly. After you.” His politeness made her more constrained. Stepping back, she said, “Please go first, Master. I have things to attend to.” Her task was to fulfill a housewife’s responsibilities. She extinguished the candles, closed the doors and windows, and checked the kitchen before returning to the bridal chamber. Hu was drinking alone. Four small dishes and a pot of wine had been prepared. As he raised his cup and recalled the day, countless questions pressed for answers. Seeing her immediately begin arranging the bedding, he called, “Furong, come here. Let us talk first.” “Yes, of course.” She came over and sat, moving a dish of ham within his reach and filling his cup. He held it to her lips; she took a sip. He offered her a slice of ham, and she ate that too.

“你晓不晓得我今天闹个大笑话？”这个开始很好，似乎一下子就变得很熟了，芙蓉以极感兴趣和关切的眼色看着他，“怎么呢？”她问。“我跟郁老四一起进门，大家都说‘恭喜’，我莫知莫觉，只当是郁老四做生日，大家是跟他道喜，你想想，世界上有这种事！”芙蓉忍俊不禁，“噗”地一声笑了出来，却又赶紧抿着嘴。摆出正经样子：“难道你自己事先一点都不知道？”“一点都不知道。为了瞒着我，他们还特地把我弄到南浔去玩了一趟。”“那……”芙蓉迟疑了一会，双目炯炯地看着他问，“要我，不是你的意思？”“哪有这话！”胡雪岩赶紧分辩，“我是求之不得！”芙蓉点点头，神色和缓了，“我也不曾想到。”她低着头说：“我实在有点怕！”“怕什么？”“伯我自己笨手笨脚，又不会说话，将来惹老太太、太太讨厌。”“那是决不会有的事！你千万放心好了。”得到这样的保证，芙蓉立刻绽开了笑容，笑容很淡，但看起来却根深，她是那种天生具有魔力的女人，不论怎么一个淡淡的表情，受者都会得到极深的感受。“我的情形，你大概总听郁四嫂说过了。”胡雪岩问道，“她是怎么说我？”“话很多。”芙蓉把那许多话，凝成一句：“总之，劝我进你们胡府上的门。”“那么你呢？乐意不乐意？”这话在芙蓉似乎很难回答，好半晌，她垂着眼说：“我夭生是这样的命！”话中带着无限的凄楚，可知这句话后面隐藏着无限波折坎坷。胡雪岩怜惜之余，不能不问，但又怕触及她什么身世隐痛，不愿多说。所以踌躇着不知如何启齿？

“Do you know what a fool I made of myself today?” It was a good beginning, seeming to make them familiar at once. She looked at him with interested concern. “How?” “When I came in with Yu, everyone said ‘Congratulations.’ I knew nothing and thought it was his birthday and they were congratulating him. Imagine such a thing!” Furong burst into laughter, then quickly pressed her lips together and tried to look serious. “Did you really know nothing beforehand?” “Nothing at all. To keep it from me, they even sent me on a visit to Nanxun.” “Then…” She hesitated, looking intently at him. “Was taking me not your wish?” “How could you think that?” Hu hastened to explain. “I could not have wished for anything better.” She nodded, and her expression softened. “I never expected it either,” she said with lowered eyes. “I am rather afraid.” “Afraid of what?” “That I am clumsy and do not know how to speak properly, and will eventually displease the old mistress and your wife.” “That will never happen. You may be completely at ease.” At this reassurance, she smiled immediately. The smile was faint but seemed rooted deep. She was one of those naturally compelling women whose slightest expression made a profound impression. “Sister-in-Law Yu has probably told you about me,” Hu said. “What did she say?” “A great deal.” Furong compressed it all into one sentence. “In short, she urged me to enter your household.” “And you? Were you willing?” This seemed difficult to answer. After a long silence, she lowered her eyes and said, “It is the fate I was born to.” Her voice held infinite sadness, suggesting many hidden hardships. Hu felt tender concern and wanted to ask, yet feared touching some painful secret she did not wish to tell. He hesitated, unsure how to begin.

一个念头转到她的亲属，立刻觉得有话可说了，“你不是有个兄弟吗？”他问，“今天怎么不见？”“在我叔叔那里。”芙蓉抬起头来，很郑重地，“我要先跟老爷说了，看老爷的意思，再来安排我兄弟。”“我不晓得你预备怎么安排？”胡雪岩说，“当初郁四嫂告诉过我，说你要带在身边。这是用不着问我的，你愿意怎么样，就怎么样，将来教养成人，当然是我的责任！”听到最后一句，芙蓉的不断眨动的眼中，终于滚出来两颗晶莹的泪珠，咬一咬嘴唇，强止住眼泪说：“我父母在阴世，也感激的。”“不要这样说！”胡雪岩顺手取一块手巾递了给她，“不但你兄弟，就是你叔叔，我都想拉他一把，既然做了一家人，能照应一定要照应。日子一长，你就晓得我的脾气了。”“我晓得，我听阿七姐说过。”芙蓉叹口气：“唉！我不知道该怎么说？”“我也听说过，你的叔叔，外号叫做‘刘不才’，这不要紧！别人不敢用，我敢用，就怕他没有本事。”说到这里，胡雪岩便急转直下地加了一句：“你家是怎么个情形，我一点都不晓得。”芙蓉点点头：“我当然要告诉你。”

Thinking of her relatives gave him a way forward. “Don’t you have a younger brother? Why wasn’t he here today?” “He is with my uncle.” Furong raised her head and spoke earnestly. “I wanted to ask your wishes before making arrangements for him.” “What arrangements had you in mind? Sister-in-Law Yu told me from the beginning that you wanted him with you. You need not ask me. Do as you wish. Raising and educating him will naturally be my responsibility.” At those last words, two bright tears rolled from her constantly blinking eyes. She bit her lip and forced the tears back. “Even my parents in the next world would be grateful.” “Don’t say that.” Hu handed her a handkerchief. “I want to help not only your brother but your uncle too. Now that we are one family, I must look after them if I can. In time you will learn what I am like.” “I know. Sister A’qi told me.” Furong sighed. “I don’t know what to say.” “I have heard that your uncle is nicknamed Liu the Good-for-Nothing. That does not matter. Others may not dare employ him; I do. My only concern is whether he has ability.” Then he abruptly added, “I know nothing of your family’s circumstances.” She nodded. “Of course I must tell you.”

刘家也是生意人家，芙蓉的祖父开一家很大的药材店，牌号叫做“刘敬德堂”。祖父有三个儿子，老大就是芙蓉的父亲，老二早夭，老三便是刘不才。刘不才绝顶聪明，但从小就是个纨袴，芙蓉的父亲是个极忠厚老实的人，无力管教小兄弟，又怕亲友说他刻薄，便尽量供应刘不才挥霍。因此，刘敬德堂的生意虽做得很大，却并不殷实。不幸地，十年前出了一个极大的变故，芙蓉的父亲到四川去采办药材，舟下三峡，在新滩遇险，船碎人亡，一船的贵重药材，漂失无遗。刘不才赶到川中去料理后事，大少爷的脾气，处处摆阔，光是雇人捞尸首，就花了好几百银子，结果尸首还是没有捞到，便在当地做法事超度，又花了好些钱。“你想想，我三叔这样子的弄法，生意怎么做得好？一年工夫不到，维护不下去了，人欠欠人清算下来，还差七千银子。那时我三叔的脾气还很硬，把店给了人家，房子、生财、存货，一塌刮子折价一万，找了三千银子回来。”三千银子，下到一年就让刘不才花得光光。于是，先是上当铺，再是卖家具什物，当无可当、卖无可卖，就只好以贷借为生。“救急容易救穷难”，最后连借部没处借了。谈到这里，芙蓉摇摇头，不再说下去，那不堪的光景，尽在不言，墒雪岩想了想问：“你娘呢？”

The Lius had been a business family too. Furong’s grandfather owned a large medicinal-goods shop called Liu Jingde Hall. He had three sons. The eldest was Furong’s father; the second had died young; the youngest was Liu Bucai. Liu was exceptionally clever, but had been a spoiled spendthrift from childhood. Furong’s father was an extremely honest, kindly man, unable to discipline his younger brother. Afraid that friends and relatives would call him harsh, he supplied money as generously as possible for Liu’s extravagance. Thus, although Liu Jingde Hall did a large trade, the family was not solidly prosperous. Then, ten years earlier, a terrible disaster struck. Furong’s father had gone to Sichuan to buy medicinal ingredients. Sailing down through the Three Gorges, his boat was wrecked at Xintan. He died, and an entire cargo of valuable medicines was lost in the river. Liu hurried to Sichuan to handle the aftermath, behaving everywhere like a grand young gentleman and spending lavishly. Hiring men to recover the body alone cost several hundred taels. They never found it, so he held rites for the dead locally, spending still more. “Think of it,” Furong said. “How could the business prosper with Third Uncle behaving like that? Within a year it could no longer be kept going. After reckoning what others owed us and what we owed them, there was still a debt of seven thousand taels. Third Uncle was proud then. He handed over the whole shop—the building, fittings and stock—at a valuation of ten thousand, receiving three thousand as the balance.” He spent those three thousand within another year. Then came pawning possessions, followed by selling furniture and utensils. When nothing remained to pawn or sell, they lived by borrowing. People could help in an emergency, but not support endless poverty. At last there was nowhere left to borrow. Furong shook her head and stopped. The misery needed no further description. After reflecting, Hu asked, “What about your mother?”

“娘早就死了，我兄弟是遗腹子，我娘是难产。”芙蓉又说，“到我十五岁那年，我三婶也让我三叔把她活活气杀！我也不知道我三叔哪里学来的本事？家里米缸，天天是空的，他倒是天天吃得醉醺醺回来，就靠我替人绣花，养我兄弟，想积几两银子下来，将来好叫我兄弟有书读，哪晓得？妄想！”“怎么是妄想？”“我三叔啊！”芙蓉是那种又好气，又好笑，出于绝望的豁达的神情：“不管把钱藏在什么地方，他都能寻得着！真正是气数。”胡雪岩也失笑了，“这也是一种本事。”他说，“那样下去也不是一回事。你怎么办呢？”“就是这话罗！我想了又想，下定决心。”芙蓉略停一停，挺一挺胸说，“我十二岁的时候批过一张八字，说我天生偏房的命，如果不信，一定会克夫家。所以我跟我三叔说，既然命该如此，不如把我卖掉，能够弄个二三百两银子，重新干本行，开个小药店，带着我兄弟过日子，将来也有个指望。

“She died long ago. My brother was born after my father’s death, and Mother died in childbirth. When I was fifteen, Third Aunt too was driven to her death by my uncle’s behavior. I don’t know how he managed it: our rice jar was empty every day, yet every day he came home drunk. I supported my brother by embroidering for other people. I hoped to save a few taels so that he could go to school. But that was a dream!” “Why?” “Third Uncle!” Her expression mingled anger and amusement with a resignation born of despair. “Wherever I hid the money, he found it. Fate, surely!” Hu could not help smiling. “A kind of ability in itself. But it could not go on. What did you do?” “Exactly. I thought and thought, then made up my mind.” She paused and straightened herself. “When I was twelve, a fortune-teller read my birth details and said I was destined to be a secondary wife. If I refused to believe it, I would bring disaster upon my husband’s family. So I told Third Uncle: since that was my fate, he might as well sell me as a concubine. Two or three hundred taels would let him resume the family trade, open a small medicine shop and support my brother. There would be some hope for the future.”

你晓得我三叔怎么说？“胡雪岩对刘不才这样的人，了如指掌，所好的就是虚面子，所以这样答道：“他一定不肯，怕失脸面。”“一点不错！他说，我们这样的人家，穷虽穷，底子是在的，那有把女儿与人做偏房的道理？别的好谈，这一点万万办不到。”芙蓉说，“我也就是在这一点上，看出我三叔还有出息。”前后话锋，不大相符，胡雪岩心中不无疑问，但亦不便打断她的话去追问，只点点头说：“以后呢？”“以后就嫁了我死去的那个。”芙蓉黯然说道：“一年多工夫，果然，八字上的话应了！”胡雪岩这才明白，她现在愿意做人的偏房，是“认命”。但是，刘不才呢？可是依旧象从前那样，郁四是用了什么手腕，才能使他就范？这些情形是趁此时问芙蓉，还是明天问郁四？他正在这样考虑，芙蓉却又开口了，“有件事，我不甘心！”她说，“我前头那个是死在时疫上。初起并不重，只要有点藿香正气丸，诸葛行军散这种极普通的药，就可以保得住命，偏偏是在船上，又是半夜里，连这些药都弄不到。我常常在想，我家那爿药店如果还开着，这些药一定随处都是，他出门我一定会塞些在他衣箱里，那就不会要用的时候不凑手。应该不死偏偏死，我不甘心的就是这一点！”

“Do you know what he said?” Hu understood men like Liu perfectly. What they prized was empty dignity. “He refused, for fear of losing face.” “Exactly. He said, ‘A family like ours may be poor, but its foundations remain. How could we give a daughter to be someone’s concubine? Anything else can be discussed, but never that.’ That was one thing that made me feel there was still hope for him.” Her tone did not quite accord with what she had said earlier. Hu had questions, but would not interrupt. He nodded. “And afterward?” “Afterward I married the man who is now dead.” Her voice darkened. “In little more than a year, the prediction came true.” Hu now understood: she was willing to become a concubine because she accepted what she believed to be her fate. But what about Liu? Had he remained as stubborn as before? What means had Yu used to bring him round? Should Hu ask Furong now or Yu tomorrow? While he considered, Furong spoke again. “There is one thing I cannot reconcile myself to. My first husband died of an epidemic disease. At the beginning it was not severe. Even ordinary medicines such as Huoxiang Zhengqi Pills or Zhuge Marching Powder would have saved him. But he was on a boat, in the middle of the night, and could not obtain even those. I often think that, if our shop had still been open, such medicines would have been everywhere. I would certainly have put some in his traveling chest before he left, and they would have been ready when needed. He ought not to have died, yet he did. That is what I cannot accept.”

胡雪岩不作声。芙蓉的话对他是一种启发，他需要好好盘算。就在这默然相对之中，只听“扑”地一声，抬眼看时，红烛上好大的一个灯花爆了。“时候不早了！”芙蓉柔声问道：“你恐怕累了？”“你也累了吧！”胡雪岩握着她的手，又捏一捏她的手臂，隔着紫缎的小夹袄，仍能清楚地感觉到，她臂上的肌肉很软，却非松弛无力，便又说道：“你不瘦嘛！”英蓉的眼珠灵活地一转，装作不经意地同道：“你喜欢瘦，还是喜欢胖？”“不瘦也不胖，就象你这样子。”芙蓉不响，但脸上是欣慰的表情，“太太呢？”她问，“瘦还是胖？”“原来跟你也差不多，生产以后就发胖了。”胡雪岩忽然提起一句要紧话：“你有孩子没有？”“没有！”芙蓉又说，“算命的说，我命里该有两个儿子。”听得这话，胡雪岩相当高兴，捧着她的脸说，“我也会看相，让我细看一看。”这样四目相视，一点腾挪闪转的余地都没有，芙蓉非常不惯，窘笑着夺去他的手，“没有什么好看！”说着，她躲了开去。

Hu said nothing. Her story had given him an idea that required careful thought. As they sat facing each other in silence, there was a soft crack. He looked up: a large bright tuft had burst from the red candlewick. “It is late,” Furong asked gently. “You must be tired?” “You must be too.” He held her hand and lightly squeezed her arm. Even through the purple satin jacket, he could feel that it was soft without being weak or slack. “You are not thin, after all.” Her eyes shifted playfully. Pretending indifference, she asked, “Do you like women thin or plump?” “Neither thin nor plump—just as you are.” She said nothing, but looked pleased. “What about your wife? Is she thin or plump?” “She was much like you, but grew plump after childbirth.” An important question suddenly occurred to him. “Have you any children?” “No. The fortune-teller said I was destined to have two sons.” This pleased Hu considerably. Cupping her face, he said, “I can read faces too. Let me have a good look.” With their eyes meeting directly and no room to evade his gaze, Furong felt deeply ill at ease. Smiling in embarrassment, she pulled his hands away. “There is nothing to look at.” She moved aside.

“我问你的话，”胡雪岩携着她的手，并坐在床沿上说，“那天你先答应去吃素斋，一出天圣寺的山门，怎么又忽然变了卦？”“我有点怕！”“怕什么？”芙蓉诡秘地笑了一下，尽自摇头，不肯答话。“说呀！”胡雪岩问道，“有什么不便出口的？”迟疑了一下，她到底开了口：“我怕上你的当！”“上什么当？”胡雪岩笑道：“莫非怕我在吃的东西里面放毒药？”“倒不是伯你放毒药，是伯你放迷魂药！”说着，她自己笑了，随即一扭身，伏在一床白缎绣春丹凤朝阳花样的夹被上，羞得抬不起头来。不管她这话是真是假，胡雪岩只觉得十分够味，因而也伏身下去，吻着她的颈项头发，随后双脚一甩，把那双簇新的双梁缎鞋，甩得老远。

Taking her hand, Hu sat with her on the edge of the bed. “Tell me something. The other day you agreed to the vegetarian meal. Why did you change your mind as soon as we left Tiansheng Temple?” “I was a little afraid.” “Of what?” She gave a secretive smile and kept shaking her head, unwilling to answer. “Tell me. What is so difficult to say?” After hesitating, she finally spoke. “I was afraid of being taken in by you.” “Taken in how?” Hu laughed. “Did you think I would put poison in the food?” “Not poison—I was afraid you would slip me a bewitching potion!” She laughed herself, then turned and buried her face in a white satin quilt embroidered with a phoenix greeting the rising sun, too embarrassed to look up. Whether or not she meant it, Hu found the answer delightful. He bent over her, kissing her neck and hair, then kicked both feet and sent his brand-new satin shoes flying far away.

第二天早晨，他睡到钟打十点才起身，掀开帐子一看，芙蓉已经打扮得整整齐齐，正在收拾妆台。听得帐钩响动，她回过头来，先是娇羞地一笑，然后柔声说道：“你不再睡一息？”“不睡了！”胡雪岩赤着脚走下地来，“人逢喜事精神爽，还睡什么？”“你看你！”芙蓉着急地说，“砖地上的寒气，都从脚心钻进去了，快上床去！”说着，取了一件薄棉袄披在他身上，推着他在床沿上坐定，替他穿袜子、穿套裤、穿鞋，然后又拉着他站起身来，系裤带，穿长袍。胡雪岩从来没有这样为人伺候过，心里有种异样的感受，“怪不得叫妾侍！“他不由得自语，” ‘侍，是这么个解释！““你在说啥？”芙蓉没有听清楚他的话，仰着脸问。“我说我真的享福了！”胡雪岩又说，“我们谈谈正经！”

The next morning he did not rise until the clock struck ten. Drawing back the bed curtains, he saw Furong already neatly dressed and tidying her dressing table. At the sound of the curtain hook, she turned, smiled shyly and asked softly, “Won’t you sleep a little longer?” “No.” Hu stepped down barefoot. “A happy occasion refreshes the spirit. Why sleep?” “Look at you!” she said anxiously. “The chill of the brick floor will rise through your feet. Get back on the bed.” She draped a lightly padded jacket over him, pushed him onto the bed’s edge and put on his socks, leggings and shoes. Then she drew him to his feet, tied his waistband and helped him into his long robe. Hu had never been attended to like this and felt a strange new pleasure. “No wonder they call a concubine an attendant,” he murmured. “So that is what the word means.” She had not heard clearly and looked up. “What did you say?” “That I really am enjoying a fortunate life. Now let us talk about serious matters.”

胡雪岩的“正经事”无其数，但与芙蓉佰共的只有两桩，也可以说，只有一桩，胡雪岩要安置她的一叔一弟。“你兄弟名字叫啥？”“我小弟是卯年生的，小名就叫小兔儿。”“今天就去接了他来！你叔叔不会不放吧？”胡雪岩人情透熟，君子小人的用心，无不深知，刘不才在此刻来说，还不能当他君子，所以胡雪岩以“小人之心”去猜度，怕他会把小兔儿当作奇货，因而有些一问。这一问还真是问对了，芙蓉顿有忧色，“说不定！”她委委屈屈地说，“我跟我三叔提过。他说，刘家的骨血，不便，不便……”芙蓉不知如何措词，脸涨得通红，话说出来屈辱了自己，也屈辱了娘家。刘三才的话说得很难听，“你说你命中注定要做偏房，自己情愿，我也没话说。郁四有势力，我也搞不过他。不过小兔儿是我们刘家的骨血，你带到姓胡的那里，算啥名堂？你自己已经低三下四了，莫非叫你兄弟再去给人家做小跟班？”当时自己气得要掉眼泪，但也无法去争，原来打算慢慢再想办法，此刻胡雪岩先提到，就不知道怎么说了！不便什么？胡雪岩的心思快，稍微想一想就明白，自然是名分上的事。那好办！他说：“你们刘家的骨血，自然让他姓刘。我现在算是姐夫资格，难道就不能管你的同胞骨肉？”

Hu had countless serious matters, but only two concerned Furong—or, in a sense, only one: making provision for her uncle and brother. “What is your brother’s name?” “He was born in the Year of the Rabbit. His childhood name is Little Rabbit.” “Send for him today. Your uncle won’t refuse to let him come, will he?” Hu understood human motives thoroughly, those of decent men and scoundrels alike. At present Liu could not be treated as a gentleman. Judging him by a less generous standard, Hu feared that he might use the boy as something valuable to bargain with. Hence the question. It was well founded. Furong immediately looked worried. “He might. I mentioned it to Third Uncle. He said that, as the boy was of the Liu bloodline, it would be improper—improper…” She did not know how to continue. Her face reddened: repeating the words would humiliate both herself and her family. Liu had spoken harshly. “You say you are destined to be a concubine and choose it yourself. I have nothing more to say. Yu is influential, and I cannot stand against him. But Little Rabbit is of our family’s blood. What would taking him to that man Hu mean? You have already lowered yourself. Must your brother become someone’s little servant too?” She had been near tears with anger, yet could not argue. She had intended to find a solution gradually. Now Hu had raised the matter first, and she did not know how to explain. Improper in what way? Hu quickly understood: it was a question of status. That was easily settled. “Naturally, a child of the Liu family will retain the surname Liu. I am his brother-in-law now. Surely I can look after your own flesh and blood?”

芙蓉怕是自己听错了，回想一遍，是听得清清楚楚，有“姐夫”二字，惊喜感激之余，却仍有些不大相信，世界上没有这样的好事！“还有啥难处？你说出来商量。”这还有什么难处？就怕他的话靠不住！芙蓉在要紧关头上不放松，特意问一句，“你说小兔儿叫你‘姐夫’？”“不叫我姐夫叫啥？难道也象你一样，叫我老爷？”芙蓉叫“老爷”是宫称，就是正室也如此叫法，身分的差别不显，小兔儿就不能这么叫。 难得胡雪岩这等宽宏大量，体贴入微，芙蓉真个心满意足，凝眸含笑，好半天说不出话来。这翻衷情，让胡雪岩发觉，自己的猜测，完全对了，“这一来，你叔叔该没话说了吧！”他问。“当然！”芙蓉的声音很响亮，“我自己去接我小弟。”

Furong wondered whether she had heard correctly. Thinking it over, she was certain he had said “brother-in-law.” Surprise and gratitude filled her, yet she could scarcely believe that such good fortune existed. “What other difficulty is there?” Hu asked. “Tell me, and we can discuss it.” What difficulty remained except the fear that he might not mean it? She would not let the crucial point slip. “You mean Little Rabbit may call you Brother-in-Law?” “What else should he call me? Master, as you do?” Furong’s use of “Master” was conventional; a principal wife used it too, so it did not openly mark a difference in status. But for Little Rabbit, calling him Master would mean something different. Hu’s generosity and delicate consideration left her completely content. She gazed at him with a smile, unable to speak for a long time. Her emotion confirmed that his guess had been right. “Then your uncle should have nothing more to say?” “Certainly!” she answered brightly. “I will go and fetch my little brother myself.”

胡雪岩先不答她这话，只说：“我想跟你叔叔见个面。你看是我去拜会他，还是请他到我们这里来？”“他怕不肯来，你暂时也不必理他。”芙蓉一大半是为胡雪岩打算，“我叔叔，说实在的，能避他还是避开他的好。”“我倒问你，他对本行生意，到底怎么样？”没有料到他会提起这句话，而且意义也不明显，芙蓉不知如何作答？细细想一想，才略略猜出他的意思，大概是要给她三叔荐到什么药材行去做事。论本事倒还不差，就是银钱上头，不能叫人放心，将来一走连累保人。然而人家既有这番好意，自己这面又是嫡亲的叔叔，也不能说有机会不要，左恩右想，十分为难，就越发无话可答了。“我是说他的本事。对本行是不是在行？”“怎么不在行？祖传的行当，从小看也看会了。”芙蓉说到这里，突生灵感，“老爷，”她说，“我倒有个主意，不晓得办不办得到？”这个主意是这样，刘不才千里有几张家传的丸散膏丹的秘方，是根据明朝大内的“宫方”，加以斟酌损益而成，“刘敬德堂”的生意，一半要靠这几张方子。生意“倒灶”，清算帐目时，还差七千银子，有人提议拿这几张秘方作价了清。刘不才却是宁愿不要店面和生财，要留着那几张方子，当时他倒是“人穷志不穷”，对债主表示：“刘敬德堂从我手里败掉的，自然还要从我手里恢复。将来‘老店新开’，这几张方子，我自己要用。”

Hu did not immediately answer that. “I should like to meet your uncle. Do you think I should call on him, or invite him here?” “He may not come. You need not trouble with him yet.” She was thinking chiefly of Hu. “To be honest, it is best to avoid him if you can.” “Tell me, how well does he know the family trade?” She had not expected the question, and its purpose was unclear. After thinking carefully, she guessed that Hu meant to recommend him for employment at a medicinal-goods firm. His skill was not poor, but he could not be trusted with money; if trouble arose, it could implicate whoever had guaranteed him. Yet Hu was offering help, and the man was her own uncle. She could hardly reject an opportunity for him. Torn between these considerations, she found it still harder to answer. “I mean his ability,” Hu clarified. “Does he know the trade?” “How could he not? It is the family business. He could have learned it simply by watching from childhood.” An idea suddenly occurred to her. “Master, I have a suggestion, though I don’t know whether it can be carried out.” Liu possessed several secret family formulas for pills, powders, ointments and medicinal preparations. They had been adapted from prescriptions used at the Ming court, and half the business of Liu Jingde Hall had depended on them. When the shop failed and its accounts still showed a debt of seven thousand taels, someone had proposed accepting the formulas in settlement. Liu had preferred to give up the premises and fittings and keep them. Poor as he was, he had retained his ambition. He told the creditors, “Liu Jingde Hall failed in my hands, and it must be restored in my hands. When the old shop opens anew, I shall need these formulas myself.”

“老店新开，看来是痴心妄想！”芙蓉说道，“小兔儿倚靠得着你，我也可以放心了。我三叔，照我看，除掉一样吃鸦片，没出息的事，都做绝了。我做侄女儿的，不管他怎么对不起我，总没有眼看他没饭吃，不拉他一把的道理。不过，我也不敢请你替他想办法，害你受累，岂不是变成我自讨苦吃？所以我这样在想，要劝他把那几张秘方卖掉。从前有人出过七千银子，现在不晓得能不能卖到一万银子？有一万银子，随他去狂嫖烂赌，总也还有几年好混，倘或他倒回心向善了，拿这一万银子做做生意，真个安分守己，省吃俭用，变得可以靠得住，那时候你也自然肯提拔他。这才真正是我们刘家祖上的阴功积德！“听她长篇大论说这一套，胡雪岩对芙蓉越发爱中生敬，因为她不但明白事理，而且秉性淳厚，再从她的话中，对刘不才又多了一番认识，此人不但有本事，也还有志气，人虽烂污，只要不抽鸦片，就不是无药可救。这样转着念头，心中立刻作了个决定，他对自己的这个决定很兴奋，但一切都要等与刘不才见了面，才能定局，此时还不宜对芙蓉细谈实话。

“Reopening it now looks like a foolish dream,” Furong said. “I can be at ease about Little Rabbit, since he can depend on you. As for Third Uncle, except for smoking opium, he has committed every disreputable act I can think of. But I am his niece. However badly he has treated me, I cannot watch him go hungry without helping. Nor dare I ask you to find a way for him and bring trouble on you. That would only make trouble for myself. So I thought of persuading him to sell the formulas. Someone once offered seven thousand taels. Might they fetch ten thousand now? With ten thousand, he could squander money on women and gambling and still live for several years. Or perhaps he would reform, use it in business, behave decently, live frugally and become dependable. Then you would naturally be willing to help him. That would truly show the hidden merit accumulated by our ancestors.” Listening to this long explanation, Hu felt respect deepen within his affection. She was both sensible and naturally kind. Her words also gave him a clearer view of Liu: the man had ability and retained ambition. Disreputable though he was, so long as he did not smoke opium, he was not beyond recovery. Hu immediately made a decision and felt excited by it. But nothing could be settled until he met Liu. It was too early to tell Furong the whole truth.

“你的打算真不错。那几张秘方值不值一万银子，不去管它，只要他肯拿出来，我一定可以替他卖到这个价钱。这样子，”胡雪岩说，“今天下午我们一道去看你三叔。你穿了红裙子去好了！”向来明媒正娶的正室，才有穿红裙的资格，所以听得胡雪岩这一说，芙蓉既感激又高兴。虽然只有胡太太不在这里，权且僭越，但总是有面子的事。不过从而一想，又不免犯愁，天生是偏房的命，做了正室，便要克夫。这条红裙穿得穿不得？还得要请教算命先生才能决定。因此，她便不谢，只含含糊糊地点一点头。就在这时候，阿珠的娘和阿七不约同至，而且还有不约而同的一件事，都叫人挑了食盒，送了菜和点心来。相见之下，自然有一番取笑，阿珠的娘还比较客气，阿七则是肆无忌惮，连房筛燕好的活都问得出来，把芙蓉搞得其窘无比。幸好又来了两个男客，一个是郁四，一个是陈世龙，这才打断了阿七的恶谑。

“Your plan is excellent. Never mind whether the formulas are worth ten thousand taels. If he is willing to part with them, I can certainly get that price for him. Let us visit Third Uncle together this afternoon. You may wear a red skirt.” Traditionally, only a principal wife married through the proper ceremonies was entitled to wear red. Furong was grateful and delighted. Even if she could overstep the rule only temporarily because Mrs Hu was absent, it gave her dignity. Then another worry arose. If she was destined to be a concubine and assuming a principal wife’s position would bring harm to her husband, could she wear that red skirt? She must consult a fortune-teller before deciding. Instead of thanking him, she merely nodded vaguely. Just then A’zhu’s mother and A’qi arrived independently, each having had the same thought: both had sent bearers carrying food boxes with dishes and refreshments. Naturally, their meeting brought teasing. A’zhu’s mother was comparatively restrained; A’qi had no such limits and even asked about the pleasures of the bridal chamber, embarrassing Furong terribly. Fortunately, Yu and Chen soon arrived and interrupted her outrageous jokes.

一桌吃过了午饭，男客和女客分做两起，芙蓉拉着阿珠的娘和阿七去请教，那条红裙穿得穿不得？胡雪岩邀了郁四在外面厅上坐，有话要谈。谈的是刘不才。郁四也正感到这是桩未了之事；游说芙蓉，是阿七建的功，何家早就表示过，愿意放她自主，自然不会留难。刘不才那里，郁四原预备让他“开价”，只要不是太离谱，一定照办，不想刘不才的话说得很硬气：“穷虽穷，还下到卖侄女儿的地步。初嫁由父，再嫁由己，她愿意做胡家的偏房，我没话说。不过我也不想认胡家这门亲戚。”“这不象他平日的行为。也不知道他打的什么主意？”郁四又说，“事情总要料理清楚，留下个尾巴也讨厌，我正要跟你商量，还是得想个办法，送他一笔钱！”“四哥，你费心得多了，这件事不必再劳你的神。芙蓉已经阳我仔细谈过，”胡雪岩笑道，“他不想认我这门亲，我却非认他不可！”“怎么个认法？”陈世龙颇有童心，“刘不才难惹得很，我倒要看胡先生怎么跟他打交道？”“我要请你先替我去做个开路先锋！”于是他把芙蓉所谈的情形，扼要谈了些，又嘱咐了陈世龙几句话，让他先去探路。

After lunch together, the men and women separated. Furong took A’zhu’s mother and A’qi aside to ask whether she might wear the red skirt, while Hu invited Yu into the outer hall to talk. The subject was Liu Bucai. Yu too felt that this remained unfinished business. A’qi had persuaded Furong, and the He family had long said she could decide for herself, so they had raised no obstacle. With Liu, Yu had intended to let him name a price and meet it unless it was absurd. Instead, Liu had answered with unexpected pride. “Poor as I am, I have not sunk to selling my niece. A first marriage is for the father to arrange; remarriage is the woman’s own affair. If she chooses to become a concubine of the Hu family, I have nothing to say. But I do not intend to acknowledge the Hu family as my relatives.” “That is unlike his usual behavior,” Yu said. “I don’t know what he is planning. We ought to settle matters cleanly. Leaving a loose end is tiresome. I was about to suggest finding some way to give him money.” “You have taken more than enough trouble, Brother Yu. This need not concern you further. Furong has explained everything.” Hu smiled. “He may refuse to acknowledge me, but I am determined to acknowledge him.” “How?” Chen asked with youthful curiosity. “Liu Bucai is very difficult. I should like to see how you deal with him.” “I shall ask you to go ahead and clear the way.” Hu briefly recounted what Furong had told him, gave Chen a few instructions and sent him to sound out the ground.

陈世龙打听到了刘不才的住处，一径就寻上门去，他跟嵇鹤龄一样，也是祖了一家式微世家的余屋住，不过另外开了个门，敲了两下，有个眉清目秀，但十分瘦的孩子来开门，转着乌黑的一双眼珠问道：“你找谁？”陈世龙听胡雪岩谈过，猜想他必是芙蓉的弟弟，随即说道：“小兔儿，你三叔呢？”“在里头。”等陈世龙要踏进去，他却堵着门不放，“你不要进来，先告诉我，你姓啥？”“怎么？”陈世龙答道，“你怕是我跟你三叔来讨债的？不是，不是！我姓陈，送钱来给你三叔的。“小兔儿有些将信将疑，但毕竟还是让步了。陈世龙一进门就觉得香味扑鼻，不由得咽了口唾沫，仔细辨一辨味道，是炖火腿的香味。“这家伙，真会享福！”一句话未完，看见刘不才的影子，哼着戏踱了出来，身上穿一件旧湖绪棉袄。下面是黑洋绉扎脚裤，两只裤脚扎得极其挺括，显得极有精神。

Chen Shilong found out where Liu Bucai lived and went straight there. Like Ji Heling, Liu had rented spare rooms in the house of an old family fallen on hard times, though his quarters had a separate entrance. After two knocks, a fine-featured but very thin boy opened the door. His dark eyes turned towards Chen. “Who are you looking for?” Remembering Hu Xueyan's account, Chen guessed that this must be Furong's brother. “Little Rabbit, where is your Third Uncle?” “Inside.” But when Chen tried to enter, the boy blocked the doorway. “Don't come in. Tell me your name first.” “Why? Are you afraid I've come to collect a debt from your uncle? No, no! My name is Chen. I've come to bring him money.” Little Rabbit remained doubtful, but at last let him through. At once a delicious aroma made Chen swallow. He recognised the scent of stewing ham. “The fellow certainly knows how to enjoy himself!” Before he had finished, Liu appeared, strolling out and humming an operatic tune. He wore an old padded jacket of Hu silk and black imported-crepe trousers, their ankles tied with such neat precision that he looked remarkably brisk.

“小和尚！想不到是你。”“刘三爷！待为来跟你老人家请安。”过于谦恭，反成戏谑，刘不才便骂：“去你的，寻什么穷开心！”“不是这话。”陈世龙答道，“从前叫你刘不才，如今不同了，你变成我的长辈，规矩不能不讲。”“咦！”刘不才眨着眼说，“我倒没有想到，忽然爆出来的这么个晚辈！是怎么来的，你说来听听！““你跟我先生结成亲戚，不就是我的长辈？”刘不才愣了一下，换了副傲慢的神色：“我不晓得你的先生是哪个？反正我最近没有跟什么人结亲，谦称奉壁，蜗居也不足以容大驾，请！”说着将手向外一指，竟下了逐客令。陈世龙有些发窘，但当然不能翻脸，在平时，翻脸就翻脸，也无所谓，此刻是奉命差遣，不能不忍一忍，同时还得想办法让刘三才取消逐客令。

“Little Monk! I didn't expect you.” “Third Master Liu, I've come especially to pay my respects.” Excessive humility turned the greeting into mockery, and Liu retorted, “Away with you! Why make fun of a poor man?” “That isn't what I mean. I used to call you Liu Bucai. Now things are different. You've become my elder, and I must observe the proper forms.” “Well!” Liu blinked. “I never expected a younger relation to spring up so suddenly. Tell me, where have you come from?” “You've become related to my teacher. Doesn't that make you my elder?” Liu paused, then assumed an arrogant expression. “I don't know who your teacher is. In any case, I haven't recently formed a marriage connection with anyone. I return the honour you offer. My humble dwelling cannot accommodate your distinguished presence. This way, please!” Pointing outside, he ordered his guest to leave. Chen felt embarrassed, but could hardly quarrel. Ordinarily he might have done so without concern. Today he had been sent on a mission. He must endure it and find some way to make Liu Sancai withdraw the dismissal.

于是他尽量装出自然的笑容，“刘三爷，你真不够朋友，炖着那么好吃的东西，一个人享用，好意思？莫非，”他说，“你不想在赌场里见面了？”提到赌场，刘三才的气焰一挫。彼此的交情虽不深，但输了就顾不到体面、曾有两三次向陈世龙伸手借过赌本，想起这点情分，也是话柄，他的脸板不成了。“要怪你自己不知趣！‘哪壶水不开，偏提哪一壶’，你晓得我讨厌我那个侄女儿，你偏要拿她来触我的心境，叫人光火不光火？”“好了，好了，说过算数。如果你留我吃饭，你出菜，我出酒。小兔儿，你来！”陈世龙摸出块五六钱的碎银子问道：“你会不会上街买东西？”“你要买什么？”刘不才问。“巷口那家酒店的‘绍烧，我吃过，不坏，叫他们送两斤来，把酒钱带去给他。”说着，他把银子塞到小兔儿子里，“多下的送你买梨膏糖吃！”“没有要你破费的道理！”刘不才赶上来插在他跟小兔儿中间，一只手到他侄儿手里去夺银子，一只手又推陈世龙，仿佛不让他给钱似地。这就象下馆子抢着惠帐，只拉住了别人的不管用的左手一样，完全是“障眼法”。结果是那块碎银子到了刘不才手里，却叫小兔儿到酒店里去赊帐。从这个行为上，陈世龙看透了他；骨头硬不到哪里去！他跟芙蓉也决不会决裂。

He forced the most natural smile he could. “Third Master Liu, you're no friend! Stewing something so delicious and keeping it all to yourself—aren't you ashamed? Or don't you expect to meet me at the gambling table again?” Mention of gambling weakened Liu's defiance. They were not close friends, but after losing, he had forgotten his dignity and borrowed gambling money from Chen two or three times. Remembering the obligation—and the hold it gave Chen—he could no longer maintain his stern face. “Blame your own tactlessness! You always pick up the kettle that won't boil. You know I can't stand that niece of mine, yet you bring her up to provoke me. How could I help being angry?” “Very well. Let that be the end of it. If you'll keep me to dinner, you provide the food and I'll provide the drink. Little Rabbit, come here!” Chen took out a scrap of silver weighing five or six qian. “Can you go shopping?” “What do you want to buy?” Liu asked. “I've tried the Shaoxing spirit at the shop by the lane entrance. It's good. Ask them to send two jin and take the money.” He put the silver into the boy's hand. “Keep the change for pear-syrup sweets!” “There's no reason for you to spend money!” Liu hurried between them, reaching with one hand for the silver and pushing Chen with the other, as though preventing payment. It was pure sleight of hand, like pretending to fight over a restaurant bill while holding only the other man's unoccupied left hand. The silver ended up in Liu's possession, while Little Rabbit was sent to obtain the liquor on credit. Chen saw through him. His backbone was not so stiff after all! He would never truly break with Furong either.

“来，来！”刘不才的兴致又很好了，把沙锅盖一揭，鼻子闻了两下，得意的笑道：“ ‘走得着，谢双脚’，你的口福不坏！陈火腿全靠收拾得干净，整整搞了一上午，才把上面的毛钳干净。”“刘三爷！”陈世龙趁机说道，“你的陈火腿吃不光！我今天来拉拢一桩生意。”“生意？”刘不才不信他，“怎么找到我头上？跟我有啥生意好谈？”自然有！等下我再告诉你。“等酒杯一端上手，陈世龙才道明来意，他说他有个朋友，预备在杭州开一家极大的药店，知道“刘敬德堂”的名气，也知道刘不才是行家，特地托他来探问一下，想邀刘不才合伙。“合伙？怎么合法？”刘不才摇着头说，“别的事都好谈，这件事谈不拢，我哪里有股本？”“你不是有几张祖传的药方子？”这话一说出口，刘不才的脸色顿时就很难看了，笑容尽敛，冷冷笑道：“原来是打我这个主意！怪道，我说世界上还有这样子的好人，不嫌我穷，来邀我台伙！”

“Come along!” Liu's spirits had recovered. Lifting the earthenware pot's lid, he sniffed twice and smiled proudly. “‘Thank your feet for bringing you here.’ You're fortunate in your food! With aged ham, everything depends on cleaning it properly. I've spent the whole morning plucking every hair from it.” “Third Master Liu,” Chen seized the opening, “you'll have more aged ham than you can eat. I've come to bring you a business opportunity.” “Business?” Liu was unconvinced. “Why come to me? What business could we discuss?” “There is some. I'll tell you shortly.” Only when they had their cups in hand did Chen explain. A friend intended to open a very large medicine shop in Hangzhou. Knowing Liu Jingde Hall's reputation and Liu's expertise, he had asked Chen to inquire whether Liu would become his partner. “A partner? On what terms?” Liu shook his head. “We can discuss anything else, but this won't work. Where would I find capital?” “Haven't you several medicinal formulas handed down in your family?” Liu's expression darkened immediately. His smile vanished. “So that's what you're after! No wonder! I thought it strange that someone should be kind enough to overlook my poverty and invite me into partnership.”

话和神色，都让陈世龙忍不住心头火发，“咦！”他也很不客气地回敬：“怪道叫你刘不才！‘狗咬吕侗宾，不识好人心’，怎见得人家打你那几张药方的主意？你晓得人家是怎么说？”“且慢！”刘不才的态度变得受商量了，“我先问一声，想跟我合伙的是哪一个？是不是姓胡的？”陈世龙很机警，趁机反问一句：“你见过我那位胡先生没有？”“从来不曾见过。”“那我告诉你，”陈世龙既不说破，也不否认，“此人是个候补知县，在官场中很红，本人虽不出面，却有好些差使跟他有关系。他要开药店也不光是为了做生意，是存心济世……”“好了，好了！”刘不才不屑地，“ ‘修合虽无人见，存心自有天知’，药店里挂的这副对子，是啥花样，难道我还不知道？何必到我面前来卖这种膏药？”“不是我在你面前卖膏药，人家这么告诉我，我照本宣科，信不信在你！”“闲话少说，他做生意也好，存心济世也好，与我无关。如说要邀我合伙，看中我那几张祖传秘方，请他趁早少打主意。”“你为来为去是怕方子落在人家手里，你要晓得，人家并不要你的什么宝贝方子！”“那……”刘不才愕然，不知这话从何说起了。

His words and manner angered Chen. “Well!” he replied just as sharply. “No wonder people call you Liu Bucai! Like the dog that bit Lü Dongbin, you don't recognise kindness. What makes you think he wants to steal your formulas? Do you know what he actually proposes?” “Wait.” Liu became more amenable. “First, who is this would-be partner? Is his surname Hu?” Chen promptly turned the question back on him. “Have you ever met my Mr Hu?” “Never.” “Then let me tell you.” Chen neither confirmed nor denied the identity. “This man is an expectant county magistrate, very well regarded in official circles. Though he doesn't appear in person, he is connected with many public appointments. He wants a medicine shop for more than trade. His intention is to help the world...” “Enough!” Liu said scornfully. “‘Though none see the compounding, Heaven knows the heart.’ Do you think I don't understand that couplet hanging in medicine shops? Why try to sell me that remedy?” “I'm not selling you anything. I'm merely repeating what I was told. Believe it or not, as you please.” “Spare me the talk. Whether he wants profit or to help the world is nothing to me. If the partnership means getting hold of my family's secret formulas, tell him to abandon the idea.” “It all comes down to your fear of the formulas falling into someone else's hands. You should know that he doesn't want possession of your precious recipes!” “Then...” Liu was astonished and could not understand.

于是陈世龙转述了合伙的办法，刘不才的祖传秘方，当然要用，可是不要求他把方子公开，将来开了药店，清他以股东的身分在店里坐镇，这几张方子上的药，请他自己修合。“君臣佐使”是哪几味药？分量多少？如何炮制？只有他自己知道，何虑秘方泄漏？原来人家不是来图谋自己的秘方，刘不才倒觉得刚才的态度，未免鲁莽，因而歉意地点点头：“这倒还可以谈谈！”“我再告诉你，人家提出来的条件，合情合理，药归你去台，价钱由人家来定，你抽成头。你的药灵，销得好，你的成头就多，你的药不灵，没人要，那就对不起，请你带了你的宝贝方子卷铺盖！”“药怎么会不灵？尤其是一种‘狗皮膏药，明朝的一个皇帝，靠了它才生的太子，真正是无价之宝！”“吹什么牛！”陈世龙笑道：“刘敬德堂的狗皮膏药，哪个不晓得，完全是骗人的东西！”“这你就不懂了！老实告诉你，方于是真的，药太贵重，而合起来交关麻烦，只好马马虎虎，效验当然就差了。这且不去说它！”刘不才把腰挺一挺，双手靠在桌上，凑近陈世龙，显得相当认真地说：“这位老朋友说的话很上路，看起来决不是半吊子。他的办法在我有益无损，可进可退，只要成头谈得拢，我就跟他合伙。”

Chen explained the arrangement. Naturally the inherited formulas would be used, but Liu would not have to disclose them. Once the shop opened, he would work there as a partner and compound those medicines himself. Which ingredients served as sovereign, minister, assistant, and envoy, their quantities, and the methods of preparation would be known to him alone. Why fear the secrets leaking out? Realising that nobody meant to take his formulas, Liu felt he had been rash. He nodded apologetically. “That is something we could discuss.” “And the terms are reasonable. You compound the medicines; he sets the prices; you receive a percentage. If your medicines work and sell well, your share increases. If they don't work and nobody wants them, then, I'm sorry, you take your precious formulas and pack your bags.” “How could they fail to work? There's one dogskin plaster that enabled a Ming emperor to father a crown prince. It's priceless!” “What boasting!” Chen laughed. “Everyone knows Liu Jingde Hall's dogskin plaster. It's a complete fraud!” “You don't understand. Honestly, the formula is genuine, but the ingredients are terribly costly and the preparation very troublesome. We had to cut corners, so naturally its effects were poorer. Never mind that now.” Liu straightened, braced his hands on the table, and leaned earnestly towards Chen. “Your friend speaks like someone who knows his way about. He's no fool. His proposal benefits me without harming me. I can go forward or withdraw. If we agree on my percentage, I'll join him.”

“那么你说，你想怎么抽法？”“我先要问一句，价钱为啥要归他定？应该大家商量商量。”“这没有商量的余地，因为你想定得高，人家既然为了济世，自然要定得低。”陈世龙觉得这话说得不好，便又补了一句：“再说，薄利多卖，生意才会好，竹杠把人家敲怕了，不上你的门，药再好也无用。”“这话也对。不过既然薄利，我的成头要多抽些。”陈世龙也很精明，“既然是薄利多卖，你名下的也不会少，怎么说要多抽？”接着他又自下转语，“不过，这都好商量，等你们碰了头，当面再谈，一定会谈得很投机。”刘不才点点头，用手抓着一块火腿脚爪在嘴里啃，同时一双眼珠骨碌碌地转着，见得他在心里有极周详的盘算，陈世龙也不催他答话，只是冷眼旁观，看他的神态，打自己的主意。“就这样了！”刘不才把火腿骨头一丢，使劲擦着手说：“我决定交这个人！小和尚，你说，哪天跟他碰头？事情既然决定了，就不必耽搁，越快越好！”

“Then tell me what share you want.” “First, why should he set the prices? We ought to discuss them together.” “There's no room for discussion there. You would want them high. Since he wants to help people, he'll naturally keep them low.” Feeling that this was not well put, Chen added, “Besides, small profits and large sales make good business. If you frighten customers away by overcharging, even the best medicine is useless.” “That's true. But if profits are small, my percentage should be higher.” Chen was shrewd too. “With small profits and large sales, your total won't be small either. Why should the percentage increase?” Then he softened his position. “Still, all that can be discussed. Settle it face to face when you meet. I'm sure you'll get on very well.” Liu nodded. Gnawing a piece of ham trotter held in his hand, he rolled his eyes about in a way that showed how carefully he was calculating. Chen did not press him, merely watched coolly and considered his own next move. “That's settled!” Liu threw down the bone and wiped his hands vigorously. “I've decided to make this man's acquaintance. Little Monk, when shall we meet? Once a thing is decided, there's no point delaying. The sooner the better!”

看他心思如此活动，陈世龙便进一步逗引他：“刘三爷！你还有什么话，自己不便说，我可以替你转达。你们没有见面前，你有什么难处，我可以替你想办法，等你们见了面，有话自己谈，就没有我的事了。”刘不才原就想开口，听陈世龙这一说，恰中下怀，当即定一定神答道：“小和尚，承你的好意，我也不必瞒你，我的境况，你是晓得的，他要请我到杭州去跟他合伙，谈妥当了，也要我动得成身才行！”“我晓得。”陈世尤问道：“你身上有多少债务？”“也不过几百两银子。”“嗯！”陈世龙又问，“你的傈儿呢？要托人照应啊！”“不必！我带到杭州去。”“喔！”陈世龙站起身来说，“那么，我先去告诉人家，什么时候碰头，我明天一早来给你回音。”

Seeing his eagerness, Chen encouraged him further. “Third Master Liu, is there anything you find awkward to say? I can pass it on. Before you meet, I can help with any difficulties. Afterwards you'll talk directly, and it will no longer be my affair.” Liu had wanted just such an opening. Collecting himself, he said, “Little Monk, since you're kind enough, I needn't conceal anything. You know my circumstances. If he wants me to join him in Hangzhou, even after we agree, I must be able to leave.” “I understand. How much debt do you have?” “Only a few hundred taels.” “And your nephew? Someone must look after him.” “No need. I'll take him to Hangzhou.” “I see.” Chen stood. “Then I'll report to him first. I'll bring word early tomorrow about when you can meet.”

一夜过去，刘不才起来得特别早。他家里不象样，“出客”的衣服，依旧很漂亮，不但料子，连花样都有讲究，一件铁灰摹本缎的袍子，松竹梅的暗花，梅花还只含苞初放，因为这是早晨，倘或下午穿出去，还有一件，那梅花就开得极盛了。打扮好了，在家坐等陈世龙的回音。到了九点钟只听有人敲门，刘不才亲自去开门一看，不由得愣住了，门外两顶轿子四个人，一个老妈子，一个丫头，一个是极艳丽的少妇，还有一个是自己的侄女儿！“三叔！”穿着红裙的芙容，叫了一声，不等他应声，便回身为那少妇引见：“这位是郁太太，这是我三叔！”郁太太自然是阿七，当时盈盈含笑地喊道：“刘三爷！”刘不才有些发急。他好面子，而家里乱六八糟，如何好意思接待这位珠翠满头、艳光照人的郁太太？一时有些手足无措，拚命在想，怎么样得能挡驾，不让她们进门？而就在这时候，从他胁下钻出来一个人，是小兔儿！

Next morning Liu rose unusually early. His home might be shabby, but his visiting clothes remained splendid. Not only their material but even their patterns were carefully chosen. His iron-grey robe of moben satin had a subtle design of pine, bamboo, and plum. The plum blossoms were only just opening, appropriate to the morning. For an afternoon outing, he had another robe on which they were in full bloom. Dressed, he sat waiting for Chen's message. At nine, someone knocked. Opening the door himself, he was astonished to find two sedan chairs and four people: an older woman servant, a maid, an exceptionally beautiful young woman, and his own niece. “Third Uncle!” Furong, wearing a red skirt, called to him. Without waiting for his reply, she turned to introduce her companion. “This is Mrs Yu. This is my Third Uncle.” Mrs Yu was naturally A’qi. With a graceful smile, she greeted him. “Third Master Liu!” He grew anxious. He cared about appearances, and his home was in chaos. How could he receive this radiant Mrs Yu, her hair resplendent with jewels? Flustered, he desperately sought some way to keep them from entering. Just then, Little Rabbit slipped beneath his arm.

“姐姐！”“小免儿！”芙蓉一把将她兄弟揽在怀里，接着便捧着他的脸端详了一下，痛心地埋怨：“看你，脏得这个样子！两个鼻孔象烟囱，只怕三天没有洗过脸了！”一面说，一面扯下衣纽上的绣花手帕，毫无顾惜地为小兔儿去擦鼻子。“刘三爷！冒昧得很，我送我这个妹妹来见叔太爷，请到里面坐了，好行礼！”这一下反客为主，刘不才枪法大乱，而芙蓉已经搀着小兔儿走了进去。到此地步，刘不才已经毫无主张，芙蓉的一切，暂时也无从去考虑，觉得眼前的唯一大事，是要打点精神来应酬这位艳丽的郁太太。于是他赔笑说道：“劳动郁太太，真正过意不去。请里面坐！地方又小又脏，实在委屈了贵客。”“不必客气！”阿七嫣然一笑，索性改了称呼：“刘三叔，都是自己人，用不着叙什么客套。”“是，是！郁太太说得是。请，我来领路。”

“Sister!” “Little Rabbit!” Furong caught her brother in her arms, then held his face to inspect it. “Look how dirty you are! Your nostrils are like chimneys. I don't suppose you've washed your face for three days!” Distressed, she pulled the embroidered handkerchief from her button and wiped his nose without a thought for the cloth. “Third Master Liu, forgive the intrusion,” A’qi said. “I've brought my younger sister to pay respects to her uncle. Please sit inside so that she can make her bow.” Suddenly the visitor had taken command. Liu lost his bearings, while Furong had already led Little Rabbit indoors. Now he had no course of his own. Whatever concerned Furong must wait. His sole immediate task was to receive the beautiful Mrs Yu properly. Smiling apologetically, he said, “I'm terribly sorry to trouble you. Please come in. Such a small, dirty place is unworthy of distinguished guests.” “No formalities!” A’qi smiled and changed her form of address. “Third Uncle Liu, we're all family. There's no need for ceremony.” “Yes, yes! Quite right, Mrs Yu. This way. I'll show you in.”

刘不才甩着衣袖，走几步路着实潇洒，进了他那间起坐兼饭厅的客堂，亲自端了他的唯一象样的一样家具，那张红木的骨牌凳，抽出雪白的手绢，拂了两下，请阿七落座。接着又找茶叶、洗茶碗，口中还要跟客人寒暄，一个人唱独脚戏似地在那里忙个不停，仿佛忘掉了还有个芙蓉在。芙蓉跟阿七对看了一眼，都觉得有点好笑，同时也都感到安慰，因为看样子，刘不才是很好说话的了。“刘三叔！你不必费心！请坐下来，我有几句正经话说。”“好！恭敬不如从命。郁太太有什么吩咐？”刘不才等坐了下来才发觉，小兔儿不但脸洗得极干净，而且已换上了一件新罩袍，安安静静偎倚着他姐姐坐着。“刘三叔，”阿七问道，“你前天怎么不来吃喜酒？”这第一句话就问得刘不才发窘，只能故意装作讶异地问：“喜酒？”

With a graceful swing of his sleeves, Liu led them into the room that served as both sitting room and dining room. He fetched his only respectable piece of furniture, a rectangular rosewood stool, and dusted it with his spotless handkerchief before inviting A’qi to sit. Then he searched for tea, washed cups, and kept up polite conversation, bustling about like a performer in a one-man show. He seemed to have forgotten Furong entirely. The two women exchanged a glance, amused and reassured. He now appeared quite easy to deal with. “Third Uncle Liu, don't trouble yourself. Sit down. I have something serious to say.” “Very well. Obedience is better than ceremony. What are your instructions?” Only after sitting did he notice that Little Rabbit's face was perfectly clean and that he wore a new outer robe, sitting quietly against his sister. “Why didn't you come to the wedding feast the day before yesterday?” A’qi's first question embarrassed him. He could only pretend surprise. “Wedding feast?”

“是啊，我芙蓉妹子的喜酒。”阿七紧接着把话挑明，“刘三叔，你心里一定有误会。你看看，芙蓉穿的啥裙子？那位胡老爷是三房合一子，照规矩可以娶三房家小，芙蓉是他的‘湖州太太’，跟他的‘杭州太太’又不见面。人家抬举芙蓉，你这个做亲叔叔的，先把侄女儿贬得不是人！好日子都不到，叫人家看起来，真当我们芙蓉妹子，是怎么样的低三下四。你想想看，哪有这个道理？“阿七的言词爽利，表情又来得丰富，斜睨正视，眼风如电，这番兴师问罪的话，把刘不才说得服服帖帖，赔笑答道：“郁太太说得是！是我不对。”接着又转脸看着芙蓉说：“我哪里知道，是这么回事？早知如此，我自然出面替你办喜事。现在只有这样，我发帖子，请大家补吃喜酒。”“这是一桩！”阿七紧接着他的话说，“还有一桩，刘三叔！刘三婶过去了，你也不续弦，孤家寡人一个，带着侄儿也不方便。不如让芙蓉把她兄弟领了去！”“这一层……”刘不才终于答应了：“也好！”阿七很高兴地笑了，“多谢刘三叔！”她说，“总算给我面子。不过，还有件事，我要请问，你们什么时候会亲？”这是指的跟胡雪岩见面，刘不才心想，当然是侄女婿先来拜叔岳。不过家里实在不象样，最好晚几天，等把药店合伙的事情谈好，先弄几文钱到手，略略铺排一下，面子比较好看。于是他说：“这要挑个好日子。我也要预备预备，能不能稍停两天再说？”

“Yes, Furong's wedding feast.” A’qi made her meaning plain. “Third Uncle Liu, there must be some misunderstanding. Look at the skirt she's wearing! Mr Hu is the sole son carrying on three family branches. By custom, he may take a wife for each branch. Furong is his Huzhou wife and won't even meet his Hangzhou wife. Others honour her, yet her own uncle treats her as though she were worthless! You stayed away even on her happy day, making people think she was some low creature. Tell me, how can that be right?” Her words were brisk and her expression vivid; whether glancing sideways or directly at him, her eyes flashed. The accusation brought Liu entirely to submission. Smiling apologetically, he said, “You're right, Mrs Yu. I was wrong.” Turning to Furong, he added, “How was I to know? If I'd understood, I'd naturally have arranged your wedding myself. There's only one thing now: I'll send invitations and give a belated feast.” “That's one matter,” A’qi continued. “Here's another. Your wife has died, and you haven't remarried.
