Added to the ten thousand and more he had won the previous day, it would provide enough capital to restore Liu Jingde Hall. So much was at stake that the decision was agonising. There was no time for leisurely reflection. Gritting his teeth, he told himself that silver and copper could be spent to the last coin; another chance to make friends like Hu and Pang might never come.

于是他做出为难而歉然的神色，笑一笑说道：“庞二哥，你出手之阔是有名的，这等于送了我三万二千银子。我不收是不识抬举，收了心里实在不安。我想这样，做朋友不在一日。以后无论是在一起玩，还是干啥正经，总还有合伙的机会。这笔钱，我存在你这里。”说着，把那个信封放回庞二面前。“你……”庞二搔搔头皮，“没有这个道理！我们一笔了一笔，以后再说，无论一起玩，还是干啥正经，总有你一份就是了。”刘不才急忙拱手：“庞二哥说到这话，当我一个朋友，这就尽够了！来来，吃饭去！”一面说，一面走了出去。庞二无可奈何，只好在那个信封上写了“刘存”二字，藏入抽斗。

With an awkward, apologetic expression, Liu smiled. “Brother Pang, everyone knows how generous you are. This is as good as giving me thirty-two thousand taels. To refuse would be ungrateful, but to accept would leave me very uneasy. Let me suggest this. Friendship isn't a matter of one day. Whether we play together again or undertake some proper business, we'll have other chances to be partners. I'll leave this money on deposit with you.” He put the envelope back before Pang. “You...” Pang scratched his head. “That won't do! Let's settle one account at a time. Whatever we do later, gambling or business, there'll always be a share for you.” Liu hastily clasped his hands. “If you say that and regard me as a friend, Brother Pang, that's more than enough. Come, let's eat.” Speaking as he went, he walked out. Pang could only write “Liu's deposit” on the envelope and put it in the drawer.

等吃了饭再赌，刘不才觉得刚才那样做法，对胡雪岩的委托来说，已经做到，所以心无牵挂，全副精神摆在赌上，用“冷、准、狠”的三字诀，在周五所摇的二十摊中，只下了三次注，看准了“老宝”打两千银子的孤丁，赢了六千，连本带利再扑一记，变成一万八。第三记收起一万打八千，如果赢了，就是两千变成三万四，除去本钱，恰好是那辞谢未受的三万二千银子。结果吃掉了，周五的庄也做完了，刘不才赢了八千银子。以后换了推牌九，赌到天亮，没有什么进出，而刘不才觉得三四天工夫就赢了两万银子，大可知足。

When play resumed after dinner, Liu felt that his conduct had fulfilled Hu's commission. With that concern removed, he gave his whole mind to gambling, following the three rules of coolness, precision, and ruthlessness. During Zhou's twenty rounds, he bet only three times. Judging Old Treasure to be the right number, he staked two thousand taels on it alone and won six thousand. He put down capital and winnings together once more, and the sum became eighteen thousand. On the third bet, he set aside ten thousand and wagered eight thousand. If he won, his original two thousand would have become thirty-four thousand; after deducting the capital, the profit would exactly equal the thirty-two thousand he had declined. Instead, the stake was taken, and Zhou's turn as banker ended. Liu had won eight thousand taels. They changed to pai gow and played until dawn without any substantial change in his fortunes. Having won twenty thousand taels in three or four days, Liu felt he had every reason to be satisfied.

伸个懒腰，离开牌桌，走到窗前把窗帘拉开，顿觉强光炫目，闭一闭眼，再从那难得几家有的外国玻璃窗望出去，不由得讶然失声：“好大的雪！”“真是！赌得昏天黑地，”高四也说，“外面下这么大的雪都不知道。”“雪景倒真不坏！”刘不才望着弥望皆白的西湖说，“庞二哥这个庄子的地势真好，真正是洞天福地。”“你说好就不要走。”周五赌兴未已，“多的是客房，睡一觉起来，我们再盘肠大战。”刘不才遇到赌是从不推辞的，但此时想到胡雪岩的正事，而他本人又早已回城，必得跟他碰个头才谈得到其他，所以推说有个紧要约会，宁可回了城再来。“再来就不必了。”庞二说道，“今天歇一天吧！如果有兴，倒不妨逛一逛西湖，我派船到涌金门码头去等你们。”一听这话，周五先就将脖子一缩，“我可没有这个雅兴，”他说，“不如到我那里去吃火锅，吃完再赌一场。”“不行！”庞二笑道，“我这个地方，就是赏雪最好，我也学一学高人雅士，今天不想进城。”高四也说有事，还有几位客，都不开口，周五的提议，就此打消。在庞家吃了丰盛的早饭，各自坐轿进城。刘不才不回钱庄，直接到一家招牌叫“华清池”的澡堂，在滚烫的“大汤”中泡了一会，躺在软榻上叫人捶着腿便睡着了。

Stretching, he left the card table and drew back a window curtain. The sudden brightness dazzled him. He closed his eyes for a moment, then looked through the foreign glass, a luxury few households possessed. “What a snowfall!” he exclaimed. “Indeed!” Gao said. “We've gambled ourselves blind to the world. We didn't even know it was snowing so heavily.” “The view is magnificent.” Liu looked over West Lake, white as far as he could see. “Brother Pang's villa is wonderfully situated—a paradise.” “Then don't leave,” said Zhou, whose appetite for gambling remained unsatisfied. “There are plenty of guest rooms. Sleep a while, and we'll return to battle.” Ordinarily, Liu never refused a game. But now he remembered Hu's business. Hu had long since returned to the city, and he must meet him before considering anything else. He therefore pleaded an important appointment: he would rather return to town and come out again. “There's no need to come again,” Pang said. “Let's rest today. If you're interested, we could tour West Lake. I'll send a boat to wait at the Yongjin Gate wharf.” Zhou drew in his neck at once. “I haven't that refined taste. Better come to my place for hotpot, then another game.” “No!” Pang laughed. “This is the best place to admire the snow. I'll imitate the elegant scholars for once and stay out of town today.” Gao too said he had business, and several other guests said nothing. Zhou's proposal came to nothing. After a plentiful breakfast, they each took a sedan chair into the city. Liu went directly to a bathhouse called Huaqing Pool instead of returning to the bank. He soaked in its scalding communal bath, then lay on a padded couch and fell asleep while an attendant pounded his legs.

这一觉睡到下午两点才醒，还不想离开澡堂子，喊来一名跑堂，到馆子里，叫菜来吃饭，同时写了张条子，吩咐送到胡雪岩家，说明行踪，请来相会。等他说着一只十景生片火锅，喝完四两白干，正在吃饭时，胡雪岩到了，一见他便很注意的说：“ 你今天的气色特别好。想来得意？”“还不错。一切都很顺利。等我吃完这碗饭，再细谈。”刘不才说，“天气太冷，你先到池子里泡一泡。”于是胡雪岩解衣入池，等他回到座位，刘不才已很悠闲的在喝着茶等。炕几上摆着个信封，看上面写着两行字：“拜烦袖致雪岩老哥。”

He did not wake until two in the afternoon and still felt no wish to leave the bathhouse. He called an attendant to order dishes from a restaurant and, at the same time, wrote a note for delivery to Hu's house, giving his whereabouts and asking Hu to meet him. By the time Hu arrived, Liu had been enjoying a hotpot of ten varieties of sliced raw ingredients, had drunk four liang of strong clear spirits, and was eating his rice. Looking at him closely, Hu said, “You look particularly well today. Things must have gone your way.” “Quite well. Everything went smoothly. Let me finish this bowl of rice, then I'll tell you all about it. It's bitterly cold. Go and have a soak first.” Hu undressed and entered the pool. When he returned to his place, Liu was waiting at ease over his tea. An envelope lay on the low table, bearing two lines of writing: “Kindly deliver by hand to my elder friend Xueyan.”

“你昨天怎么不等庞二把摊摇完，就走了？”“我自然要先走，不然，到晚上‘叫城门’就麻烦了。”胡雪岩说，“我开了两张票子，带在身上，交是交了给庞二，号子里有没有这么多存款，还不知道，必得赶进城来布置好。”“亏得庞二不曾输掉，否则就麻烦了。”刘不才这时倒有不寒而栗之感，“你想，我说了跟他四六成合伙，倘或连你这十万一起输光，就是二十万。我派四成，得要八万，划个帐，找两万银子。十万剩了两万，险呀！这种事下次做不得了。““你也知道做不得！”胡雪岩笑道，“你在场上赌，等于我在场外赌。不过我这场外赌，无论输赢，都是合算的。““赢了是格外合算。你看！”刘不才把信封推了给他，说明经过。

“Why did you leave yesterday before Pang finished his turn?” Liu asked. “Naturally, I had to leave early. Getting the city gate opened at night would have been troublesome. I had two notes drawn up and carried them with me. I'd handed them to Pang, but I didn't know whether the bank had enough deposits to cover them. I had to hurry back into town and make the arrangements.” “Fortunately, Pang didn't lose the money. Otherwise, there would have been trouble.” Liu shuddered at the thought. “I'd agreed to a forty-sixty partnership. If he had lost everything, including your hundred thousand, that would have been two hundred thousand. My forty per cent would be eighty thousand. After offsetting the accounts, there would be only twenty thousand to give back. A hundred thousand reduced to twenty thousand! What a risk. We must never do that again.” “So you know it shouldn't be done!” Hu laughed. “You were gambling at the table, and I was gambling outside it. But my gamble would have been worthwhile whether you won or lost.” “Winning made it especially worthwhile. Look!” Liu pushed the envelope towards him and explained what had happened.

胡雪岩这时才打开信封，把他自己的两张银票收了起来，扬着庞二的那张五千两的银票说：“我当然不能要他这五千银子，但也不便退回。只有一个办法，用他的名义，捐给善堂。昨天夜里一场大雪，起码有二三十具‘倒路尸’，我钱庄里已经舍了四口棺材了。”“ ‘做好事’应该！我也捐一千银子。”“算了，算了！”胡雪岩不便说他有了钱，“大少爷脾气”就会发作，只这样阻止：“你要做好事，也该到湖州去做！杭州有我，不劳你费心。”刘不才有些发觉了，略显窘色地笑道：“其实我也要别人来做好事，自己哪里有这个资格。”“闲话少说。”胡雪岩说，“这里不是说话的地方，到舍间去谈。”

Only then did Hu open the envelope. He put away his own two banknotes and held up Pang's note for five thousand taels. “Naturally, I can't take this five thousand. But it would be awkward to return it. There's only one course: donate it to a charitable institution in his name. After last night's heavy snow, there must be at least twenty or thirty bodies lying in the roads. My bank has already given four coffins.” “Good works are only right. I'll give a thousand taels too.” “No, no!” Hu could hardly say that, once Liu had money, his wealthy young master's habits would return. Instead he checked him with, “If you want to do good works, you should do them in Huzhou. Hangzhou has me; you needn't trouble yourself.” Liu sensed something of his meaning and smiled a little awkwardly. “In truth, I need other people to do good works for me. What standing have I to do them myself?” “Enough of that. This isn't the place to talk. Let's go to my house.”

于是两个人穿衣起身。刘不才是第一次到胡家，想到他侄女儿，有些心事重重的模样，他不知道胡雪岩在湖州另立门户，胡太太是不是知道？倘或知道，自己的身分不免尴尬，因而便有畏缩之意。但转念又觉得这是机会，可以看看胡太太为人如何？将来跟芙蓉是不是相处得来？就这样踌躇着，走出华清池时，脚步就懒了。胡雪岩回身一望，从他的脸色，猜到他的心里，觉得必须交代一句。“三叔，”他说，“在湖州的事，见了内人，不必提起。”这句话解消了刘不才心里的一个疙瘩，脑筋就变得灵活了。“那么，”他提醒他说：“你也不能叫我三叔！脱口出来，就露了马脚。”“不要紧。倘或内人问起来，我只说我先认识你侄儿，跟着小辈叫，也是有的。”“算了，你叫我别样。我也不想做你的长辈，宁愿做朋友。”“是的！刘三爷。”这是“官称”，刘不才欣然同意。一起坐轿到了胡家，拜见胡雪岩的母亲和妻子，刘不才口称“伯母”、“大嫂”。看这位“胡大嫂”人虽精明，极顾“外场”，不是那种蛮不讲理的悍泼妇人，刘不才替芙蓉放了一半心。

They dressed and got up to leave. This would be Liu's first visit to Hu's home, and the thought of his niece made him uneasy. Did Mrs Hu know that her husband had established another household in Huzhou? If she did, Liu's position would be awkward. He felt apprehensive. Then he reflected that this was an opportunity to see what sort of woman she was and whether she and Furong might get on in future. Torn between these thoughts, he lagged as they left Huaqing Pool. Hu looked back, read his expression, and realised that he must say something. “Third Uncle, when you meet my wife, there's no need to mention Huzhou.” This removed one obstacle from Liu's mind, and his thoughts began to move freely again. “Then you mustn't call me Third Uncle either. If it slips out, you'll give yourself away.” “That doesn't matter. If she asks, I'll say I knew your nephew first and followed the younger generation's form of address. That happens often enough.” “Never mind. Call me something else. I don't want to be your elder anyway. I'd rather be your friend.” “Certainly, Third Master Liu.” This was his formal social title, and he readily accepted it. They took sedan chairs to Hu's house and paid their respects to his mother and wife. Liu addressed them as Auntie and Sister-in-Law. He found that Mrs Hu, though shrewd, had a proper regard for social appearances and was no unreasonable shrew. Half his anxiety on Furong's behalf disappeared.

于是围炉把酒，胡雪岩开始谈到庞二，“你晓得的，我现在顶要紧的一笔生意，是上海的丝。”他说，“我既然托了你，以后也还要共事，我不必瞒你，年关快到了，各处的帐目要结，应该开销的要开销，上海那批丝，非脱手不可。““嗯，嗯！”刘不才生长在湖州，耳濡目染，对销洋庄的丝，自然也颇了解，“现在价钱不错呀！不如早早脱手。摆到明年，丝一变黄，再加新丝上市，你就要吃大亏了。”“是的，眼前的价钱虽不错，不过还可以卖得好，说句你不相信的话，价钱可以由我开。”“有这样的好事！”刘不才真的有些不信，反问一句，“那你还在这里做啥？赶紧到上海去呀！”“对！就这几天，我一定要动身。现在只等庞二的一句话。”这一句话就是要取得庞二的承诺，他在上海跟洋商做丝的交易，跟胡雪岩采取同样的步骤，胡雪岩已经得到极机密的消息，江苏的督抚，已经联衔出奏，因为在上海租界中的洋人，不断以军械粮食接济刘丽川，决定采取封锁的措施，断绝内地也洋人的贸易，迫使其转向“助顺”。这一来，丝茶两项，来源都会断绝，在上海的存货，洋人一定会尽量搜购，只要能够“垄断”，自然可以“居奇”。

Sitting round the brazier with wine, Hu began to discuss Pang. “As you know, the most important business before me is the silk in Shanghai. Since I've entrusted this matter to you and we shall be working together, there's no need to conceal anything. The year's end is approaching. Accounts must be settled everywhere, and expenses must be met. That silk in Shanghai has to be sold.” “Yes, yes.” Growing up in Huzhou had naturally given Liu considerable knowledge of silk for the foreign market. “Prices are good now. Better sell early. If you keep it until next year, the silk will yellow, and the new crop will come on the market. You'll lose heavily.” “Exactly. Prices are good now, but they could be better. You may not believe this, but I can name my own price.” “As good as that?” Liu was indeed doubtful. “Then what are you doing here? Get to Shanghai at once!” “Quite right. I must leave within the next few days. I'm only waiting for Pang's word.” That word was a promise that, in selling silk to foreign merchants in Shanghai, Pang would follow the same course as Hu. Hu had received highly confidential news: Jiangsu's governor-general and governor had submitted a joint memorial. Because foreigners in the Shanghai settlement were continually supplying Liu Lichuan with arms and provisions, they had decided on a blockade, cutting off trade between the interior and the foreigners to force them to support the imperial side. Supplies of both silk and tea would then cease. Foreigners would buy as much of the stock in Shanghai as possible. Whoever could control the supply could naturally hold it for an exceptional price.

“原来如此！”刘不才很有把握地说，“这庞二一定会答应的，挑他赚钱，何乐而不为？”“话不是这么说。”胡雪岩大摇其头，“你不要把事情看得太容易！”刘不才是不大肯买帐的性格，“我倒不相信！”他说，“宠二没有不答应的道理。”“凭交情，自然会答应。交情不够就难说了。你要晓得。第一，他跟洋人做了多年的交易，自然也有交情，有时不能不迁就，第二，在商场上，这有面子的关系，说起来庞二做丝生意，要听我胡某人的指挥。象他这样的身分，这句话怎么肯受？”想想果然！刘不才又服帖了，笑着说道：“你的脑筋是与众不同。这样一说，我倒还真得小心才好。”“对了！话有个说法。”胡雪岩接下来便教了他一套话。

“So that's it!” Liu said confidently. “Pang will certainly agree. You're helping him make money. Why wouldn't he?” “It isn't as simple as that.” Hu shook his head emphatically. “Don't take it too lightly.” Liu was not easily convinced. “I don't believe it. There's no reason for him to refuse.” “With enough friendship, naturally he'll agree. Without it, one can't be sure. First, he's traded with foreigners for years and has friendships among them. Sometimes he must accommodate them. Second, there's his standing in business. People would say Pang has to take instructions from me about his silk. How could a man in his position accept that?” On reflection, this was true. Liu yielded again and smiled. “Your mind works differently from other people's. Put like that, I really must be careful.” “Exactly. There's a way of saying things.” Hu then taught him how to put the proposal.

刘不才心领神会的点头，因为休戚相关的缘故，不免又问：“万一你倒扳价不放，洋人看看不划算，做不成交易，岂非枉做恶人？而且对庞二也不好交代！”“不会的！”胡雪岩答道，“外国的丝，本来出在叫做意大利的一个国度，法兰西也有。前个六八年，这两个国度里的蚕，起了蚕瘟，蚕种死了一大半，所以全要靠中国运丝去。原料不够，外国的丝厂、机坊都要关门，多少人的生计在那里！他们非买我们的丝不可，羊毛出在羊身上，水涨船高，又不亏洋丝商的本，怕什么！”“你连外国的行情都晓得！”刘不才颇有闻所未闻之感，“怪不得人家的生意做不过你。”“好了，好了！你不要恭维我了。”胡雪岩笑道，“这些话留着跟庞二去说。”

Liu nodded with full understanding. Since their fortunes were linked, however, he could not help asking, “What if you hold firmly to your price and the foreigners decide it isn't worth their while? If no sale takes place, won't you have made yourself unpleasant for nothing? And how would you explain it to Pang?” “That won't happen. Foreign silk originally came from a country called Italy, and from France too. Six or eight years ago, a disease struck their silkworms and killed more than half their stock. So they depend entirely on silk shipped from China. Without enough raw material, their silk mills and weaving workshops must close. Think how many people's livelihoods depend on them! They have to buy our silk. The wool comes from the sheep, and boats rise with the water: the foreign silk merchants won't lose their own capital. What is there to fear?” “You even know the foreign market!” Much of this was entirely new to Liu. “No wonder other people can't compete with you.” “Enough! Stop flattering me,” Hu laughed. “Save those words for Pang.”

刘不才如言受教，第二夭专诚去访庞二，一见面先拿他恭维一顿，说他做生意有魄力，手段厉害。接着便谈到胡雪岩愿意拥护他做个“头脑”的话。“雪岩的意思是，洋人这几年越来越精明，越来越刁，看准有些户头急于脱货求现，故意杀价。一家价钱做低了，别家要想抬价不容易，所以，想请你出来登高一呼，号召同行，齐心来对付洋人！”“是啊！我也想到过，就是心不齐。原是为大家好，哪晓得人家倒象是求他似地。”庞二摇摇头，叹口气。“唉！我何苦舒服日子不过，要吃力不讨好，自己给自己找气来受！”“你是大少爷出身，从出娘胎，也没有受过气，自然做不来这种仰面求人的事。雪岩也知道，他只请你出面为头，靠你的地位号召，事情归他去做。”“这也不敢当！”庞二答道，“老胡这样捧我，实在当不起。”这话就要辨辨味道了，可能是真心话，也可能是推托。如果是推托，原因何在？刘不才这样想着，一面口中恭维，一面在细察庞二的脸色。这是刘不才有阅历的地方！庞二果然是假客气的话，他对胡雪岩虽颇欣赏，但相知不深，对于胡雪岩一下子如跳龙门似地，由穷小子闯出这样的手面，其间的传奇，也听人约略谈过，认为他实力毕竟有限，深恐他弄什么玄虚，存着戒心。

Following Hu's advice, Liu made a special call on Pang the next day. He began by praising Pang's boldness and ability in business, then explained that Hu wished to support him as their leader. “Xueyan thinks the foreigners have grown shrewder and more difficult these last few years. They see that some dealers need to sell quickly for cash and deliberately force down prices. Once one firm's price falls, it's hard for the others to raise theirs. So he'd like you to give the call and bring the trade together to deal with the foreigners.” “Yes, I've thought of that myself. The trouble is that people won't act together. I mean it for everyone's benefit, but they behave as though I were begging a favour.” Pang shook his head and sighed. “Why should I give up a comfortable life for thankless work and invite vexation?” “You were born a young master and have never had to put up with an insult. Naturally, you can't go humbly begging others. Xueyan understands that. He asks only that you stand at the head and lend the movement your prestige. He'll do the work.” “I couldn't accept such an honour,” Pang answered. “Old Hu gives me far too much credit.” The words needed careful interpretation. They might be sincere, or merely an excuse. If an excuse, why? As he continued to flatter Pang, Liu studied his expression closely. Here his experience proved useful. Pang's modesty was indeed a pretence. He admired Hu, but they did not know each other well. He had heard something of the remarkable story of Hu's rise, like a leap through the Dragon Gate, from a poor young fellow to a man who could operate on such a scale. Yet he thought Hu's real resources must still be limited. Afraid there might be some trick behind the proposal, he remained on his guard.

说到后来，刘不才有些着急了，“庞二哥，承蒙你看得起我，一见如故，所以雪岩托我这件事，我一口答应。现在你一再谦虚，似乎当我外人看待。”说到这里，发觉自己的态度，有些过分，便笑一笑说，“好了，好了！庞二哥，我不管这桩闲事了，我请你到‘江山船’上吃花酒去。”最后这一转很好，庞二觉得刘不才很够朋友，自己虽存着猜疑之心，他却依旧当自己好朋友，这很难得。就一转念之间，心便软了，觉得无论如何要有个交代，于是这样笑道：“老刘，你不要气急！不看僧面看佛面，你第一趟跟我谈正经事，又是为彼此的利益，我怎么能不买你的帐？不过，我也说句实话，象这样的事，做好了没有人感激，做坏了，同行的闲话很多。中国人的脑筋比外国人好，就是私心太重，所以我不敢冒昧出头。现在这样，我跟老胡先谈一谈再说，能做我一定做，决不会狗皮倒灶。你看好不好？”“哪还有不好的道理？你说，你们在哪里谈？”“今天我还有一个约，没有空了，就明天吧。”庞二又说，“你不是要请我吃花酒吗？我们就在江山船上谈好了。”“一言为定。明天请你江山船上吃花酒，我发帖子来。”

As the conversation continued, Liu grew anxious. “Brother Pang, you've been kind enough to take to me as an old friend from the moment we met. That's why I immediately agreed when Xueyan asked me to undertake this. Now you keep declining so modestly that you seem to regard me as an outsider.” Realising that he had gone a little too far, he smiled. “Never mind! I won't meddle in this any longer. Let me invite you to drink with the courtesans on a Jiangshan pleasure boat.” The final turn was well judged. Pang felt that Liu was a true friend. Though Pang had remained suspicious, Liu still treated him warmly. That was rare. The thought softened him, and he felt he must give some definite answer. “Old Liu, don't be impatient. If not for the monk, then for the Buddha: this is the first time you've brought me a business proposal, and it benefits both sides. How could I refuse you consideration? But let me speak frankly. If such a scheme succeeds, nobody thanks you. If it fails, the trade will have plenty to say. Chinese minds are sharper than foreign ones; the trouble is excessive self-interest. That's why I dare not rush to take the lead. Let me talk to Old Hu first. If it can be done, I'll certainly do it. I won't be a tiresome obstruction. Will that suit you?” “How could it not? Where shall you meet?” “I've another appointment today and no time. Tomorrow, then. Didn't you offer me a courtesans' drinking party? We can talk on the Jiangshan boat.” “Agreed. Tomorrow I'll entertain you there. I'll send an invitation.”

“这不必了。你是用哪家的船？”庞二对此道也很熟悉，“顶好的是小金桂的船，只怕定出去了。其次就是‘何仙姑’的船。”“好，不是小金桂，就是何仙姑。事不宜迟，我马上去办。定好了船，还是发帖子来。”“好，好，我听你招呼。”庞二又说，“人不宜太多，略微清静些，好谈正事。”刘不才答应着告辞而去。进城直接去找胡雪岩，细说了经过，表示佩服胡雪岩有先见之明，果然事情不那么容易，又说他未能圆满达成任务，深感歉疚。“这是哪里的话！”胡雪岩安慰他说，“有这样一个结果，依我看，已经非常好了。”“那么，预备怎么跟他谈呢？”“那自然要临机应变。看样子，他是跟我初次共事，还不大能够相信。”胡雪岩又说，“这件事即使做不成功，我以后跟他合作的日子还有。所以，三爷，倘或事情谈不拢，你不必摆在心上，好象觉得对不起我，他不够朋友。你要一切照常，一点不在乎。你懂我意思不懂？““当然懂！”刘不才深深点头，“这个朋友是长朋友。”“对了！”胡雪岩极欣慰的，“说这话，你是真的懂了。”

“No need for that. Whose boat will you use?” Pang knew this world well too. “Xiao Jingui's is the best, but it may already be booked. Next best is He Xiangu's.” “Then one of those two. There's no time to lose. I'll arrange it now. Once I've secured the boat, I'll send an invitation all the same.” “Very well. I'll await your word. But don't invite too many people. We want some quiet to discuss business.” Liu agreed and took his leave. Returning to the city, he went directly to Hu and recounted the conversation. He admired Hu's foresight: the business had indeed proved difficult. He also apologised deeply for failing to complete his mission satisfactorily. “What are you saying?” Hu reassured him. “To my mind, this is already an excellent result.” “How will you approach him, then?” “Naturally, I'll adapt as we talk. It seems he doesn't quite trust me yet, since this would be our first undertaking together. Even if this one doesn't succeed, there will be other opportunities for us to work together. So, Third Master, if we can't agree, don't take it to heart as though you'd failed me or he weren't a good friend. Treat everything as usual and think nothing of it. Do you understand?” “Of course.” Liu nodded earnestly. “This is a friendship for the long term.” “Exactly!” Hu was deeply pleased. “That shows you truly understand.”

于是，刘不才告辞回去，托刘庆生派人定了小金桂的船，又发帖子，整整忙了一下午，才算诸事就绪。哪知到了夜里，突然接到庞二的信，说他接到家报，第二天必须赶回甫浔，花酒之约，只得辞谢，胡雪岩的事，希望即晚谈一谈，在何处见面，立等回音。信是由庞家的听差送来的，刘不才打听了一下，才知道庞二闹家务，看起来他的心境不会好，对胡雪岩的事，自然也不会感觉兴趣，谈与不谈已经无关宏旨了。不过想到“长朋友”这句话，刘不才觉得对庞二应有一番慰问之意，因此告诉庞家的听差，说他马上约了胡雪岩去拜访。等庞家的听差一走，刘不才接着也赶到了胡家，相见之下，说了经过，胡雪岩大为皱眉，沉吟了好半晌，倏地起身，成竹在胸似地说：“走吧！船到桥头自然直。”坐轿出城，见着了庞二，胡雪岩发觉他眉宇之间，隐然有忧色，便不谈自己的事，只问庞二有何急事，要赶回家去？“我叫人告到官里了！”庞二很坦率地回答，“这一趟回去，说不定要对簿公堂。”“不幸之至。”胡雪岩问道，“到底为了什么？”“ 这话说来太长，总之，族中有人见我境遇还过得去，无理取闹。花几个钱倒不在乎，这口气忍不下去。”

Liu took his leave and asked Liu Qingsheng to send someone to book Xiao Jingui's boat. He also sent the invitations. The preparations occupied the whole afternoon. That night, unexpectedly, a letter arrived from Pang. He had received news from home and must return to Nanxun the following day, so he could no longer attend the party. He hoped to discuss Hu's business that very evening and was waiting for an immediate reply about where they should meet. The letter came by Pang's servant. After a few inquiries, Liu learned that there was trouble within Pang's family. He would hardly be in good spirits or interested in Hu's affairs; whether they discussed the proposal now seemed to matter little. But remembering their “friendship for the long term,” Liu felt he should offer some sympathy. He told the servant that he would fetch Hu and call on Pang immediately. As soon as the servant left, Liu hurried to Hu's house and explained. Hu frowned deeply and considered for some time, then suddenly rose as though his plan were settled. “Let's go. The boat will straighten itself when it reaches the bridge.” They took chairs out of the city. On seeing Pang, Hu detected worry in his expression. Instead of raising his own business, he asked what urgent matter required Pang to return home. “Someone has brought a case against me,” Pang answered frankly. “I may have to appear in court.” “Most unfortunate. What is it about?” “That's a long story. In short, some members of my clan see that I'm fairly comfortably off and are making unreasonable trouble. I don't mind spending money. It's the insult I can't swallow.”

一听这话，就知道无非族人夺产，事由不明，无法为他出什么主意，只好这样相劝：“庞二哥，讼则终凶，惟和为贵。”“和也要和得下来。”庞二摇摇头，“唉！不必谈了。”庞二不谈，胡雪岩却不能不谈，也不可不谈，因为他可以帮庞二的忙，“如果你愿意和，我包你和得下来。”胡雪岩说，“庞二哥，打官司你不必担心！只要理直，包赢不输，不过俗话说得好：富不跟穷斗。你的官司就打赢了也没有什么意思。”“啊！”庞二突然双眼发亮，“对了，你跟王大老爷是好朋友。这个忙可以帮我。”“当然。”胡雪岩说，“我先陪你走一趟。你的事要紧，我上海的事只好摆着再说了。”这是以退为进的说法，庞二被提醒了，他是阔少的作风，遇到这些地方，最拿得出决断，“老胡！”他说，“你上海的事不要紧，都在我身上。你说，要我怎么样？”

Hu understood at once that the clansmen were after Pang's property. Without the particulars, he could offer no specific advice. He could only urge, “Brother Pang, lawsuits end badly. Peace is best.” “Peace must be possible first.” Pang shook his head. “Never mind. Let's not discuss it.” But Hu could not let the subject drop, nor should he: he could help. “If you're willing to settle, I guarantee a settlement. You needn't fear a lawsuit, Brother Pang. If right is on your side, I guarantee you'll win. But the saying is sound: the rich shouldn't fight the poor. Even winning your case would bring little satisfaction.” “Ah!” Pang's eyes suddenly brightened. “Of course! You're a close friend of Prefect Wang. You can help me.” “Naturally. I'll go with you first. Your affairs are urgent. My business in Shanghai will have to wait.” This was a retreat intended to gain ground. Reminded of Hu's business, Pang showed the decisiveness of a wealthy young master. “Old Hu, don't worry about Shanghai. Leave it all to me. Tell me what you want me to do.”

“刘三爷跟你大致已经谈过了。我就是想庞二哥来出面，我劝同行齐心一致，由我陪你去跟洋人谈判。”“我是没有空来办这件事了。”庞二问道，“你在上海有多少丝？”“我有两万包。”“那就行了。我跟你加在一起，已经占到百分之七十，实力尽够了。你跟洋人会谈，我把我的栈单交了给你，委托你代我去做交易，你说怎么就怎么。这样总行了吧？”得到这样一个结果，胡雪岩喜出望外。有庞二的全权委托，不但对洋商的交易，可以顺利达成，而且自己的声望，立刻就会升高。但好事来得太容易，反令人有不安之感，他不敢有得意的神色，“庞二哥，你这个委任重了！”他戒慎恐惧的说：“我怕万一搞得灰头土脸，对你不好交代。”“不会的！”庞二答道：“我听老刘谈过了，你对丝不外行。就请你记住一句话，‘顺风旗不要扯得太足’，自然万无一失。”“是的，”胡雪岩衷心受教，“我照你的话去做。价钱方面，我总还要跟你商量的，不会独断独行。”

“Third Master Liu has told you the general idea. I'd like you to take the lead. I'll persuade the trade to act together, then accompany you to negotiate with the foreigners.” “I won't have time to handle it myself. How much silk have you in Shanghai?” “Twenty thousand bales.” “Then that's enough. Yours and mine together already account for seventy per cent. We have ample strength. You negotiate with the foreigners. I'll hand you my warehouse receipts and authorise you to sell on my behalf. Whatever you decide goes. Surely that will do?” The result surpassed Hu's hopes. With Pang's full authority, he could not only bring the transaction with the foreign merchants to a successful conclusion but immediately raise his own standing. Yet such easily won good fortune made him uneasy. He dared show no triumph. “Brother Pang, you're placing a heavy responsibility on me. I'm afraid that if I make a mess of it, I shan't know how to face you.” “You won't. Old Liu has told me about you. You know the silk trade. Remember just one thing: don't stretch your banner too far in a favourable wind. Then nothing can go wrong.” “Yes,” Hu answered with sincere respect. “I'll follow your advice. As for the price, I shall still consult you. I won't decide everything on my own.”

“不必，你看着办好了。至于回扣……”“不，不！”胡雪岩急忙摇手，“你这么捧我，我决不能再要回扣。原是你自己可以谈的事，怎么好损失回扣？我晓得你为人大方，不过你手下也有一般‘朋友’，叫他们背后说你的闲后，变得我对不起你了。”听这一说，庞二越觉得胡雪岩“落门落槛”，是做生意可以倾心合作的人。别人漂亮，他更不肯马虎，坚持一定要送，胡雪岩也作了很肯定的表示，倘或庞二一定要送，他不能不收，只是除了必要的开支以外，余数他要送庞二手下的“朋友”。“那随你，我就不管了。”庞二又说，“今天晚上我就写信通知上海，把栈单给你送去，送到哪里？”“不是这么做法，只请你写封委托信给我，同时请你通知宝号的档手，说明经过。栈单不必交给我。”

“No need. Use your own judgement. As for your commission...” “No, no!” Hu hastily waved his hands. “After such support, I couldn't take a commission as well. You could have handled the transaction yourself. Why should you lose that amount? I know you're generous, but you have ‘friends’ working under you. If they criticised you behind your back, I should have done you a disservice.” Pang felt still more strongly that Hu understood how things should be done and was a man with whom he could cooperate wholeheartedly. If the other man behaved handsomely, he would not be careless in return. He insisted on paying. Hu was equally definite: if Pang insisted, he could not refuse, but after deducting necessary expenses, he would give the balance to Pang's “friends.” “That's up to you. I won't interfere. I'll write to Shanghai tonight and have the warehouse receipts sent to you. Where should they go?” “Not that way. Please just give me a letter of authorisation and notify your firm's manager of the arrangement. The receipts needn't be handed to me.”

这样做，亦无不可。谈完胡雪岩的事，庞二谈他自己的事。照胡雪岩的想法，上海那方面的生意，他可以托人代办，自己该陪着庞二到湖州，去替他料理官司。刘不才也在旁边帮腔，说胡雪岩对这种徘难解纷的事，最为擅长，此行少不得他。但唯其如此，庞二反倒顾虑了。“老胡！有你出大力帮忙，这件事，我现在就可以放心，至多惹几天麻烦，花几吊银子，没有什么大不了的。不过，我不愿意落个仗势欺人的名声。你陪了我去，好是好，就只一样不妥，湖州好些人都知道你跟王大老爷是知交，看你出面，明明王大老爷秉公办理，别人说起来，总是我走了门路。“庞二停了一下又说，“这一来不但我不愿意，对王大老爷的官声也不好。”听了这番话，胡雪岩心想，谁说庞二是不懂事的纨袴，谁就是有眼无珠的草包，因而心悦诚服的答说：“庞二哥看事情，真正透彻！既然如此，我全听吩咐。”“不敢当！”庞二说道：“我只请你切切实实的替我写封信，我也是备而不用。”“好的。我的信要写两封，一封给王雪公，一封给刑幕秦老夫子，此人我也是有交情的，庞二哥有什么难处，尽管跟他商量。”

That arrangement was equally acceptable. With Hu's business settled, they returned to Pang's. Hu thought he could entrust the Shanghai transaction to someone else and accompany Pang to Huzhou to help with the lawsuit. Liu supported him, saying that Hu excelled at resolving disputes and was indispensable to the journey. Yet this very argument made Pang hesitate. “Old Hu, with your full help, I can already set my mind at rest. At worst there'll be a few troublesome days and a few strings of cash to spend. Nothing very serious. But I don't want a reputation for using influence to bully people. It would be good to have you with me, except for one thing. Many people in Huzhou know you're a close friend of Prefect Wang. If you appear, they'll say I used connections even if he handles the case with complete impartiality.” After a pause, Pang added, “I wouldn't like that, and it would harm his official reputation too.” Hearing this, Hu thought that anyone who called Pang an ignorant rich idler was a blind fool himself. With heartfelt admiration, he replied, “You see matters very clearly indeed, Brother Pang. In that case, I'll do as you wish.” “You flatter me. All I ask is that you write me a proper, substantial letter, to keep in reserve rather than use.” “Certainly. I'll write two: one to Prefect Wang and one to Secretary Qin, his legal secretary. I'm friendly with him too. If you have any difficulty, consult him freely.”

“这是文的一面，还有武的一面。”刘不才插嘴问庞二：“郁四，你认不认识？”“认是认得，交情不深。”庞二答道：“说句实话，这些江湖朋友，我不大敢惹。”“这个人也是‘备而不用’好了。”胡雪岩说，“信我也是照写，其实不写也不要紧，郁四听见是庞二哥的事，不敢不尽心。”这是胡雪岩拿高帽子往庞二头上戴，意思是以庞家的名望，郁四自然要巴结。只是恭维得不肉麻，庞二听了非常舒服，心里在想，他们杭州人的俗语，“花花轿儿人抬人”，胡雪岩越是如此说，就越要买他的面子。“老胡，听你这一说，郁四跟你的交情一定不错。你的朋友就是我的朋友，我这趟回湖州，倒要交他一交，请你替我写介绍信。”“一句话！”胡雪岩起身告辞，“你就要走了，总还有些事要料理，我不耽搁你的工夫，明天一早，我把信送来。”这天晚上胡雪岩备下三封极其切实的信，第二天一早带到庞二那里。投桃报李，他交给胡雪岩的两封信也很实在，一封是委托书，一封是写给他在上海的管事的，特意不封口，请胡雪岩代发，意思是让他过了目，好放心。这使得胡雪岩对庞二又有深一层的了解，做事不但豪爽，而且过节上的交代，一丝不苟，十分漂亮。

“That's the formal side. There's the forceful side too.” Liu asked Pang, “Do you know Yu Si?” “I know him, but not well. Frankly, I don't much care to get involved with such men of the streets and waterways.” “Keep him in reserve too,” Hu said. “I'll write him a letter as well, though it scarcely matters. Once Yu hears that it's your business, Brother Pang, he won't dare spare any effort.” Hu was flattering him, implying that the Pang family's prestige would naturally make Yu eager to oblige. The compliment was subtle enough to give Pang great pleasure. He thought of the Hangzhou saying: people take turns carrying one another's decorated chairs. The more Hu spoke like this, the more Pang ought to honour him. “Old Hu, from what you say, you and Yu must be good friends. Your friends are mine. When I return to Huzhou, I should like to get to know him. Please write me an introduction.” “Consider it done.” Hu rose to leave. “You're going tomorrow and must still have things to arrange. I won't take up your time. I'll bring the letters early in the morning.” That night, Hu prepared three letters, all giving firm and practical support, and took them to Pang the next morning. Returning favour for favour, Pang gave him two equally substantial letters: one was an authorisation; the other was addressed to his manager in Shanghai. He had deliberately left the latter unsealed and asked Hu to send it, meaning that Hu should read it first and be reassured. This gave Hu a deeper understanding of Pang. He was not only generous and forthright; in attending to every detail of an arrangement, he was scrupulous and admirable.

第二十章｜CHAPTER TWENTY

有了这封委托书，胡雪岩要好好的动脑筋了。他不断跟古应春有书信往来，上海方面的生意，是托古应春代为接头，尤五的一切情形，也是由古应春代达。所以庞二这面谈成功，他第一件事，就是写信告诉古应春，然后料理杭州这方面所经手的事务，预备在十二月初动身到上海，尽月半以前把丝卖出去，好应付公私帐目。然后开了年，另外再推出新的计划，大干一番。不多几天，古应春的回信来了，让胡雪岩大出意外的是，洋人那方面变了卦，表示年关以前，无意买丝。表面是说，他们国内来信，存货已多，可以暂停。实际上照古应春的了解，外国人也学得门槛精了，知道中国商场的规矩，三节结帐，年下归总，需要大笔头寸。有意想“杀年猪”。如果胡雪岩价钱不是扳得太高，则洋人为了以后的生意，也下会赶尽杀绝。“事情麻烦了！”胡雪岩跟刘不才说，“我自己要头寸在其次，还有许多小户，不能过关，一定会倒过来恳求洋商，虽然他们这点小数，不至于影响整个行情，但中国人的面子是丢掉了！”“那就只有一个办法，”刘不才已经把胡雪岩佩服得五体投地，认为世上没有难得倒他的麻烦，所以语气非常轻松，“你调一笔头寸帮小户的忙，或者买他们的货，或者做押款，叫他们不要上洋人的圈套，不就完了吗？”胡雪岩最初的计议就是如此，难就难在缺头寸，所以听了他的话，唯有报以苦笑。这一下，刘不才也看出意思来了，“老胡，”他说，“我看庞二也是吃软不吃硬的脾气，听见洋人这样可恶，一定不服帖，你何不跟他商量一下看？他的实力雄厚，如果愿意照这个办法做，岂不就过关了？“话是说得不错，但自己有许多公私帐务，一定要有个交代，那又如何说法？这非得细细地通盘筹划一番不可。

Now that he had the letter of authorisation, Hu Xueyan needed to think carefully. He had kept up a steady correspondence with Gu Yingchun, who handled his business contacts in Shanghai and passed on all news of You Laowu. Once the agreement with Pang Er was settled, his first act was to write to Gu. Then he attended to the affairs in his charge in Hangzhou, intending to leave for Shanghai early in the twelfth month and sell the silk before mid-month to meet his public and private obligations. After the New Year, he would launch fresh plans and make a great effort. Gu's reply arrived a few days later with an unpleasant surprise: the foreign merchants had changed their minds and had no intention of buying silk before the year ended. They claimed that letters from home reported ample stocks and advised suspending purchases. In Gu's view, however, they had grown shrewd. They knew the Chinese business custom of settling accounts at the three major festivals and making a final reckoning at year-end, when large sums of ready money were needed. They meant to “slaughter the New Year pig.” Yet if Hu did not hold out for too high a price, their interest in future dealings would keep them from driving him entirely to the wall. “This makes things difficult!” Hu told Liu Bucai. “My own need for funds is secondary. Many small dealers won't get through the year. They'll have to turn round and beg the foreigners. Their small quantities won't affect the whole market, but we Chinese will lose face!” Liu now admired him so completely that he thought no difficulty could defeat him. His answer was therefore quite casual. “There's only one solution. Raise some money to help the small dealers: buy their goods or lend against them. Keep them out of the foreigners' trap, and the problem is solved.” That had been Hu's original plan. The difficulty was the lack of money. He could only smile bitterly. Liu understood. “Old Hu, I think Pang Er responds to persuasion but resists pressure. He won't swallow such behaviour from the foreigners. Why not discuss it with him? He has ample resources. If he agrees to your plan, won't that see you through?” True enough. But Hu also had many public and private accounts of his own to settle. What was he to say about those? The whole matter required careful consideration.

这天晚上，胡雪岩跟刘庆生算了一夜的帐，各处应付款项，能展期的展期，能拖一拖的拖一拖，无论如何要三十万两银子才能过关。而应收及可以调动的款子，不到十五万，头寸还缺一半，更不用说替丝商小户张罗过年的现款。这就到了必须向洋商屈服的时候了。胡雪岩想想实在于心不甘，多少时间心血花在上面，就为的是要弄成“一把抓”的优势，如今有庞二的支持，优势已经出现，但“一把抓”抓不住，仍旧输在洋商手里，这是从何说起？一方面不甘屈服，一方面急景调年，时不我待，胡雪岩彻夜彷徨，想不出善策。急得鬓边见了白发。而刘庆生却又提出警告，该付的不付，面子要弄得很难看了！这个警告的意味，他很了解，万一传出风声，说胡某人的周转不灵，阜康的存户纷纷的提存，这样一“挤兑”，雪上加霜，非倒闭不可。于是他又想到刘不才的话，觉得庞二是个可共患难的人，与其便宜洋商，不如便宜自己人！向庞二去开口，当然是件失面子的事，然而，这是同样的道理，与其丢面子丢给洋人，倒不如丢给自己人。“三爷！你陪我到湖州去一趟。”他这样跟刘不才说，“这一趟去要看我的运气，如果庞二闹家务，已经顺顺利利了结，我说话也就容易了。不然，他自己都弄得‘头盔倒挂’，我怎么还开得出口？”“好的。”刘不才说，“我看我们直接赶到南浔去吧，不必先到湖州，再走回头路就耽误工夫了。“胡雪岩点点头，未置可否，心里在盘算杭州跟上海两方面的交代，细想一想，就是三、五天的工夫也不容易抽出来，年底下的商场，虽不是瞬息万变，却往往会出意外，万一有何变化，自己措手不及，岂不误了大事，刘不才看他踌躇不决，知道他必须坐镇在杭州，因而试探着说：“雪岩，你看是不是我代你去走一趟？”

That night Hu and Liu Qingsheng worked over the accounts until morning. They extended whatever payments could be extended and postponed whatever could be postponed, but still needed three hundred thousand taels to get through the year. Receivables and funds that could be mobilised amounted to less than a hundred and fifty thousand. Half the required sum was still missing, even before finding year-end cash for the small silk dealers. He had reached the point of having to submit to the foreign merchants. The thought was intolerable. So much time and effort had gone into securing the advantage of a unified grip on the business. With Pang's support, that advantage was finally taking shape. Yet he could not maintain his grip and would still lose to the foreigners. How could this be? Unwilling to yield, with the year's end fast approaching and time running out, he worried through the night without finding an answer. Anxiety brought grey hairs to his temples. Liu Qingsheng added a warning: failure to pay what was due would look very bad. Hu understood what that meant. If word spread that he was short of working funds, Fukang's depositors would rush to withdraw their money. Such a run would make matters worse and force the bank to close. He thought again of Liu Bucai's suggestion. Pang Er seemed a man with whom one could share adversity. Better to let one of their own profit than the foreigners. Asking him for help would certainly cost face, but the same principle applied: better to lose face before one of their own. “Third Master, come with me to Huzhou,” he said. “This journey will depend on my luck. If Pang's family dispute has been settled smoothly, I can speak more easily. If his own affairs are in a muddle, how can I open my mouth?” “Very well. I think we should go straight to Nanxun. Going to Huzhou first and then doubling back would waste time.” Hu nodded without committing himself. He was considering the arrangements needed in both Hangzhou and Shanghai. On reflection, even three or five days were hard to spare. Business at year-end might not change every instant, but unexpected developments were frequent. If something happened while he was unprepared, it could ruin everything. Seeing his hesitation and understanding that he must remain in charge in Hangzhou, Liu ventured, “Xueyan, why don't I go in your place?”

这倒是个办法。刘不才的才干，办这样一件事，可以胜任。但他还有一件事不放心，“三爷！”他说，“你去了不能露出急吼吼的样子……”“这何消说得？”刘不才抢着说，“我不能连这一点都不懂。”“不是！我还有话。”胡雪岩说，“既然不是急如星火的事，那就可以从从容容来。大少爷的脾气，你是最明白不过的，”他模拟着庞二的态度说：“ ‘好了，好了，凡事有我。先赌一场再说。’那时候你怎么样？”刘不才想想不错，这一赌下来，说不定就耽误了胡雪岩的工夫，千万赌不得！“我这样跟他说：我自己在杭州还有许多事，要赶回去料理，到年三十，我赶到南浔来，陪你好好赌几场。”“对！就是这么说。”胡雪岩又郑重的加了一句：“三爷，你可不能拆我的烂污！”“你不相信我，就不要叫我去。”说到这话，胡雪岩不能再多提一句，当时写了信，雇了一只船，加班添人，星夜赶到南浔去会庞二，约定无论事成与否，三天以后，必定回来。

That offered a solution. Liu had the ability to handle such a mission, but one concern remained. “Third Master, when you arrive, you mustn't look desperate...” “Surely you don't need to tell me that!” Liu interrupted. “I understand that much.” “No, there's more. If it doesn't seem desperately urgent, there will seem to be time to spare. You know that rich young master's temper better than anyone.” Imitating Pang, Hu said, “‘All right, all right. Leave everything to me. Let's have a game first.’ What will you do then?” Liu saw the point. Once they started gambling, he might delay Hu's business. He must not play. “I'll tell him I have a great deal to attend to in Hangzhou and must hurry back. On New Year's Eve I'll come to Nanxun and play as many games as he likes.” “Exactly. Say just that.” Hu added solemnly, “Third Master, you mustn't let me down!” “If you don't trust me, don't send me.” After that, Hu could say no more. He wrote the letter and hired a boat, adding extra hands to speed it on its way through the night to Nanxun. They agreed that, successful or not, Liu must return in three days.

这三天自是度日如年的光景，但胡雪岩决不会独坐愁城，听天由命，他要作万一的打算，所以依然每天一早，坐镇阜康，不断派出人去联络试探，希望能找出一条得以筹集这笔巨款的路子来。第一天第二天都毫无结果，到了第三天，他就有些沉不住气了，正在攒眉苦思时，嵇鹤龄到阜康钱庄来相访，一见面便讶然说道：“雪岩，几天不见，你何以清瘦如此？”异姓手足，无需掩饰，胡雪岩老实答道：“还差三十万银子，怎么不急得人瘦？”听这话，嵇鹤龄大吃一惊，“你怎不跟我说？那天我问你，你不是说可以‘摆平’吗？”他带些责备语气地问。“跟你说了，害你着急，何苦？”胡雪岩改用宽慰的语气说，“只要海运局的那笔宕帐，你能给我维持住，别的也还不要紧。”怎么又说不要紧？显见得他是故意叫人宽心。嵇鹤龄想了想问道：“你总得想办法罗！”“是的。”他说了遣刘不才到南浔乞援的事，“我给庞二的信上说，我愿意照市价卖多少包丝给他，便宜不落外方。我这样吃亏还卸面子，他应该可以帮我这个忙。”“年底下一下子要调动三十万的头寸，不是件容易的事。”“其实，有一半也可以过关了。”“十五万也不是少数。”嵇鹤龄招招手说，“你来，我跟你句话。”

Those three days naturally seemed like years. But Hu would never sit helplessly with his troubles and leave everything to fate. He needed a fallback. Each morning he took his place at Fukang and kept sending people out to make contacts and test possibilities, hoping to find some means of raising the large sum. The first two days produced nothing. On the third he was beginning to lose his composure. While he sat frowning in thought, Ji Heling called at the bank. “Xueyan!” Ji exclaimed. “It's only been a few days since I saw you. How have you grown so thin?” There was no need to conceal anything from a sworn brother. “I'm still three hundred thousand taels short,” Hu said frankly. “How could I help worrying myself thin?” Ji was shocked. “Why didn't you tell me? When I asked the other day, didn't you say you could put everything in order?” There was reproach in his voice. “What good would it do to make you anxious too?” Hu adopted a reassuring tone. “As long as you can keep that outstanding Sea Transport Bureau account from being pressed, the rest isn't too serious.” Not serious? Plainly he was trying to put Ji at ease. After thinking a moment, Ji asked, “But you must be doing something?” “Yes.” Hu explained Liu's mission to Nanxun. “In my letter, I offered to sell Pang a quantity of silk at the current market price, so the benefit would stay among ourselves. Since I'm accepting a loss and swallowing my pride, he ought to help.” “Raising three hundred thousand at once at the year's end is no easy matter.” “Actually, half would see me through.” “A hundred and fifty thousand is no small sum either.” Ji beckoned. “Come here. I have something to tell you.”

到得僻处密谈，嵇鹤龄告诉他一个消息，是裘丰言谈起的，说有个洋商走了“炮局”龚振麟、龚之棠父子的路子，龚家父子又走了黄抚台三姨太的路子，决定跟洋商买一万五千支洋枪，每支三十二两银子，价款先发六成，就在这两天要立约付款了。听得这个消息，胡雪岩大为诧异，买洋枪是他的创议，如果试用满意，大量购置，当然是他原经手来办，何以中途易手，变成龚家父子居间？当然，这是不用说的，其中必有花佯，胡雪岩问道：“可晓得那洋商叫什么名字？”“不知道。听说是个普鲁士人。”“那就不是哈德逊了。”胡雪岩说，“这笔生意，每支枪起码有十二两的虚头，一万五千支枪是十八万，回扣还不算。这样子办公事，良心未免太黑了一点。”“这不去说它了。我告诉你这个消息，是提醒你想一想，这笔款子，能不能在你手里过一过，能够办得到，岂不是眼前的难关，可以过去？”这倒是个很新鲜的意见。胡雪岩对任何他不曾想到的主意，都有兴趣，于是扳着手指数道：“一万五千乘三十二，总价四十八万银子，先付六成就是二十八万八，弄它一升半就差不多了。”“你跟龚家父子认识不认识？我倒有个朋友，跟小龚很熟，可以为你先容。”“好极了！等我想一想。这条路子一定有用的。”

In a secluded spot, Ji passed on news from Qiu Fengyan. A foreign merchant had approached Gong Zhenlin of the Cannon Bureau and his son Gong Zhitang. They in turn had approached Governor Huang's third concubine, and a purchase of fifteen thousand foreign guns had been agreed at thirty-two taels apiece, with sixty per cent paid in advance. The contract was to be signed and the money paid within the next day or two. Hu was astonished. Buying foreign guns had been his own initiative. If the trial proved satisfactory and a large purchase followed, surely he, as the original agent, should handle it. Why had the business changed hands, with the Gongs acting as intermediaries? Obviously there must be some trick behind it. “Do you know the merchant's name?” he asked. “No. I hear he's Prussian.” “Then it isn't Hudson. There's at least twelve taels of padding in the price of each gun. On fifteen thousand guns, that's a hundred and eighty thousand, before counting any commission. Their consciences must be very black to handle public business like this.” “Leave that aside. I'm telling you so that you can consider whether the money might pass through your hands. If that could be arranged, wouldn't it solve your immediate difficulty?” It was a fresh suggestion. Hu always took an interest in an idea that had not occurred to him. Counting on his fingers, he said, “Fifteen thousand times thirty-two makes four hundred and eighty thousand taels. Sixty per cent in advance is two hundred and eighty-eight thousand. If I could get roughly half of that, it would be about enough.” “Do you know the Gongs? A friend of mine knows the younger Gong well and could introduce you.” “Excellent! Let me think. This avenue is bound to be useful.”

胡雪岩略为一想，就看出了这桩交易之中的不妥之处，一万五千支洋枪，是一批极惹人注目的军火，近则上海的小刀会，远则金陵的太平军，一定都会眼红，如果在上海起运，不管陆路水路，中途都难免会出纰漏。“怎么样能把合同打听出来就好了。”胡雪岩自语似地说，“我看这件事，怕有点靠不住！”“怎么靠不住，千真万确有些事。”“我不是说没有这件事，是说这笔生意，怕要出乱子，龚家父子会惹极大的麻烦。”接着，胡雪岩将他的顾虑，跟嵇鹤龄细谈了一遍。“我懂了！”嵇鹤龄说，“症结在交货的地方，如果是在上海交货，黄抚台得派重兵护运。这倒是很麻烦的事。”“有了！”胡雪岩当时便把刘庆生找了来问说：“抚台衙门刘二爷的节敬送了没有？”“还早啊！”“要提前送了。”胡雪岩说，“我记得是每节一百两，过年二百两，请你另外封四百两，连例规一起送去，说我拜托他务心帮个忙！”要刘二帮忙的，就是把合同的原底子设法抄了来。刘二看在两个红封，总计六百两银票的面上，这个忙非帮不可，又因为龚家父子越过他这一关，以同乡内眷，经常来往的便利，直接搭上了三姨太的线，心里原就有气，这时猜测胡雪岩的用意。大概要动脑筋打消这笔买卖，自所乐见，格外巴结，当天就用五十两银子买通了黄宗汉的娈童兼值签押房的小听差，把合同的底稿偷了出来，刘二关上民门，亲自录了个副本，神不知鬼不觉地送到了胡雪岩手里。

A little thought revealed a weakness in the transaction. Fifteen thousand foreign guns were a consignment of arms that would attract enormous attention. The Small Swords Society nearby in Shanghai and the Taiping forces farther away in Jinling would certainly covet them. Whether sent from Shanghai by land or water, they would be vulnerable along the route. “If only we could discover what the contract says,” Hu murmured. “I suspect something isn't sound here.” “Not sound? The information is absolutely certain.” “I don't doubt that the transaction exists. I mean it may go wrong and land the Gongs in serious trouble.” He explained his concerns. “I see,” Ji said. “The crucial point is where delivery takes place. If it's Shanghai, Governor Huang will have to send a strong escort. That would be troublesome.” “I have it!” Hu summoned Liu Qingsheng. “Have we sent Second Master Liu at the governor's yamen his festival gift?” “It's still early.” “Send it ahead of time. I recall it's a hundred taels at each festival and two hundred at New Year. Put another four hundred in a separate envelope and send both. Tell him I have a favour to ask and beg him to take special care.” The favour was to obtain a copy of the original draft contract. For two red envelopes containing banknotes worth six hundred taels, Liu Er could hardly refuse. Besides, he resented the Gongs for bypassing him. As people from the same native place, their womenfolk called frequently on the governor's household, and they had used that advantage to approach the third concubine directly. Liu guessed that Hu meant to find a way to stop the purchase, a prospect he welcomed. He was particularly obliging. That same day, fifty taels bought the cooperation of Huang Zonghan's young male favourite, who also served as a junior attendant in the official signing room. The attendant stole out the draft. Liu shut the door, copied it himself, and delivered the copy to Hu in complete secrecy.

合同上写的是由船运在浙江边境交货。胡雪岩倒弄不明白。这个名叫鲁道夫的普鲁士人，具何神通？能够安然通过上海到嘉善的这一段水路？倘或中途出险，不能如约交货，又将如何？细看合同，果然有个绝大的漏洞，这笔买卖，在卖主方面自然有保人，由上海的两家钱庄承保，但保的是“交货短少”及“货样不符”，又特为规定一样：“卖方将枪支自外洋运抵上海后，禀请浙江抚台衙门委派委员，即就海关眼同检验，须验得式样数目相符，始得提领交运。”看起来好象公事认真，完全为了维护买方的利益，实际上是正好为卖方脱卸责任。“好刀笔！”在一起细看合约的嵇鹤龄，书生积习，不免愤慨，“公家办事，就是如此！自作聪明，反上了别人的当。”“恐怕不是自作聪明，是故作聪明。”胡雪岩说，“照这个合约来看，卖方只要把洋枪运到上海，在海关经过浙江的委员眼同检验，数量式样相符，卖方就已尽了责任，如果中途遇劫，那就好比当票上的条规：”天灾人祸，与典无涉。‘保人是不保兵险的。真的闹将开来，洋人只要说一句：在你们中国地方被抢的。你们自己不能维持地方平靖，与外人什么相干？这话驳不到，还只能捏着鼻子受他的！“嵇鹤龄也是才气横溢，料事极透的人，听了胡雪岩的话，连连点头，嘴角中现出极深沉诡秘的笑容，眼睛不断眨动，似乎别有深奥的领悟似地。

The contract specified delivery by boat at the Zhejiang border. Hu was puzzled. What remarkable powers did this Prussian, Rudolf, possess that would let him pass safely along the waterway from Shanghai to Jiashan? If trouble prevented delivery, what would happen? A closer reading revealed a tremendous loophole. The seller had guarantors, two Shanghai banks, but their guarantee covered only shortages in quantity and discrepancies in specifications. There was also a special clause: “After the seller has transported the guns from overseas to Shanghai, the Zhejiang governor's yamen shall be requested to appoint commissioners to inspect them jointly at the customs house. Only after the specifications and quantities have been verified as conforming may the goods be released for onward shipment.” It looked like careful administration, wholly intended to protect the buyer. In reality, it provided precisely the means for the seller to escape responsibility. “What skilful legal drafting!” Ji, studying the contract beside him, could not suppress a scholar's indignation. “This is how public business is done! They think themselves clever and fall into someone else's trap.” “Perhaps they're pretending to be clever,” Hu replied. “Under this contract, once the guns reach Shanghai and the Zhejiang commissioners have verified their quantity and specifications at customs, the seller has discharged his responsibility. If they're robbed on the way, it's like the rule on a pawn ticket: ‘The pawnbroker is not liable for natural or human disasters.’ The guarantors don't cover war risks. If a dispute arises, the foreigner need only say, ‘They were stolen in your country. If you can't maintain order in your own territory, what has that to do with us?’ We couldn't refute him. We'd have to hold our noses and swallow it.” Ji, himself exceptionally able and perceptive, nodded repeatedly. A deep, cryptic smile appeared at the corners of his mouth. His eyes kept blinking, as though he had reached some further understanding.

“大哥！”胡雪岩问道：“你另有看法？”“我是拿你的话，进一步去想。也许是‘小人之心’，但是，人家未必是君子，所以我的猜测也不见得不对。”说了半天，到底是指什么呢？胡雪岩有些不耐，催促着说：“大哥！你快说吧，这件事上，也许可以生发出什么办法来，如今时间不多了，我们得要快动脑筋，快动手。”于是嵇鹤龄提纲挈领的只问了一句，胡雪岩就懂了，所问这一句是：“这会不会是个骗局？”如果要行骗，根据合约来说，并不是不可能：洋枪运到上海关，浙江所派的委员验明了数目式样，无不相符，但交运中途，说是遇到劫盗，意外灾祸，不负责任。至于是不是真的抢走了洋枪，无可究诘，那就可以造成骗局。倘或事先有勾结，浙江的委员虚应故事，数目既不够，式样也不符，而以“相符”禀报，及至被动，亦是无可究诘，这个骗局就更厉害了。“我看，”胡雪岩毕竟是商人，迟疑着问道：“这，我看他们不至于如此大胆吧？”“哈！”嵇鹤龄冷笑，“你不知官场的龌龊！事实俱在，这合约中有漏洞，人之才智，谁不如我？我们一看就看出来了，他们经过那么多人看，说是不曾看出来，其谁能信？”“是的。”胡雪岩点点头，转问出一句极要紧的话：“既然我们看出来了，该怎么办？”嵇鹤龄笑了，“以你的聪明，何需问我？”他说，“你定策，我看我能不能帮你的忙！”胡雪岩觉得嵇鹤龄这个人不失为君子，在这样异姓手足之亲，时不我待之迫，有了机会还不肯出“坏主意”，就算很难得了。

“Elder Brother, have you another thought?” Hu asked. “I'm taking your argument a step further. Perhaps it's a base suspicion, but the others may not be honourable men. My guess needn't be wrong.” What, after all that, did he mean? Hu grew impatient. “Tell me quickly! There may be some way forward in this. Time is short. We must think and act fast.” Ji needed only one question to make his point. “Could it be a fraud?” Under the contract, fraud was certainly possible. The guns would reach Shanghai customs, and Zhejiang's commissioners would report the quantity and specifications correct. During onward shipment, the seller could claim robbery, an unforeseen calamity for which he bore no responsibility. Whether the guns had actually been stolen would be impossible to establish. That opened the way to a swindle. With collusion arranged beforehand, the commissioners might merely go through the motions. Even if the quantity were short and the specifications wrong, they could report conformity. Once the goods were said to have been stolen, investigation would be equally impossible. That would be an even greater fraud. Hu was, after all, a businessman. Hesitantly he said, “Surely they wouldn't dare go that far?” “Ha!” Ji sneered. “You don't know how filthy official life is! Here are the facts: there's a loophole in the contract. Why should everyone else be less intelligent than we are? We saw it at a glance. So many people have examined it. Who could believe none of them noticed?” “Yes.” Hu nodded, then asked the essential question. “Now that we've seen it, what should we do?” Ji smiled. “With your intelligence, why ask me? Decide on a plan, and I'll see how I can help.” Hu thought Ji remained a gentleman. Even with the closeness of sworn brotherhood between them and time pressing so urgently, he would not suggest an underhanded scheme when the opportunity arose. That was rare indeed.

“办法当然很多。”胡雪岩想了想说，“光棍不断财路，只要他们不是行骗，生意仍旧让他们去做。不过，我觉得黄抚台不作兴这样，我也帮过他好些忙，买洋枪又是我开的路子，现在叫别人去做这笔生意，想想于心不甘。”嵇鹤龄听他的话一脚进、一脚出，便知道他的意思了，反正只要能对他眼前的难关有帮助，他也不愿多事，照此宗旨替他设想，觉得有跟龚家父子开个谈判的必要。“请谁去谈判呢？”胡雪岩问，“托你的朋友？”“不！这件事你我先都还不便出面，叫裘丰言去！”“妙！妙！”胡雪岩抚掌称善，“我们马上找他来谈。”于是就借嵇鹤龄的地方，由瑞云设炉置酒，叫人去请裘丰言。时已深夜，天气已冷，裘丰言黄昏时分喝得醺醺然，早已上了床，但听说嵇、胡二人请他围炉消夜，立刻披衣起床，冒着凛冽的西北风，兴冲冲地赶到嵇家。一进门他就把“寒夜客来茶当酒”这句诗改了一下，朗然而吟：“寒夜客来酒当茶！”不但嵇鹤龄和胡雪岩相视莞尔，连隔室的瑞云都笑了，只见小丫头把门帘一掀，她一手提个酒瓶，一手提把酒壶，扬一扬笑道：“裘老爷，有的是酒，中国酒、外国酒都有，你尽管喝！”

“There are plenty of ways,” Hu said after a little thought. “A man of the world doesn't cut off another's livelihood. If they aren't committing fraud, let them keep the business. Still, Governor Huang shouldn't treat me this way. I've helped him often enough, and I opened the way to buying foreign guns. To see someone else given the transaction now—it's hard to accept.” Ji understood the way Hu's words advanced and retreated. So long as the matter helped him through his immediate difficulty, he did not want further trouble. On that basis, Ji thought they ought to negotiate with the Gongs. “Who should negotiate?” Hu asked. “Your friend?” “No. Neither of us should appear at this stage. Send Qiu Fengyan.” “Excellent!” Hu clapped his hands. “Let's get him here at once.” They used Ji's house, where Ruiyun set out a brazier and wine, and sent for Qiu. It was late and cold. Having drunk himself pleasantly tipsy at dusk, Qiu had long since gone to bed. But the invitation to a late supper round the brazier brought him up at once. He dressed and hurried eagerly to Ji's through the bitter north-westerly wind. On entering, he altered the poetic line “On a cold night, a guest arrives; tea takes the place of wine,” and declaimed, “On a cold night, a guest arrives; wine takes the place of tea!” Ji and Hu exchanged smiles. Even Ruiyun in the next room laughed. A little maid lifted the door curtain, and Ruiyun appeared with a bottle in one hand and a wine pot in the other. Raising them, she said, “Mr Qiu, there's plenty! Chinese wine and foreign wine—drink all you please!”

“多谢如嫂夫人！”裘丰言兜头一揖，然后接过一瓶白兰地，拔开寒头，先就嘴对嘴喝了一口。这一下惹得瑞云又笑，“裘老爷喝酒倒省事，”她说，“用不着备菜！”“这话在别处可以这么说，在府上我就不肯这么说了。”“为什么呢？”“说了是我的损失。说句不怕人见笑的话，我这几天想吃府上的响螺跟红糟鸡，想得流涎不止。”“那真正是裘老爷的口福，今天正好有这两样东西。”瑞云笑道，“不过，不好意思拿出来待客，因为吃残了！”“怕什么，怕什么！来到府上，我就象回到舍下，没有说嫌自己家里的东西吃残的。”于是瑞云将现成的菜，办了一个火锅、四只碟子为他们主客三人消夜，嵇鹤龄一面劝酒，一面为裘丰言谈那张购枪合同的毛病。他虽未提到胡雪岩，而有了几分酒意，并且一向与胡雪岩交好的裘丰言却很替他不平。“是可忍，孰不可忍！这件事非得好好评理不可。”

“My thanks, Madam!” Qiu bowed deeply, took a bottle of brandy, pulled out the stopper, and drank straight from its mouth. Ruiyun laughed again. “Mr Qiu makes drinking so easy. There's no need to prepare food!” “You might say that elsewhere, but I won't let you say it here.” “Why not?” “Because I'd lose by it. At the risk of being laughed at, I've spent the last few days positively drooling over the thought of your sea conch and chicken in red wine lees.” “Then you are fortunate. We happen to have both today.” She smiled. “Only I'm ashamed to serve them to guests. They've already been eaten from.” “What does that matter? Coming here is like coming home. Nobody objects to leftovers in his own house.” Using what was ready, Ruiyun prepared a hotpot and four small dishes for the three men's supper. As Ji urged Qiu to drink, he explained the faults in the gun contract. Though he said nothing of Hu, Qiu, already a little tipsy and always friendly towards him, felt indignant on his behalf. “If this can be tolerated, what cannot? We must have the rights and wrongs of this properly argued!”

“少安毋躁！”嵇鹤龄拉着他的手说，“今天请你来就是要跟你商量个打抱不平的办法。毛病捉住了，但‘没有金刚钻，不揽碎瓷器’，龚家父子也不是好相与的人，这件事还得平心静气来谈。”“好，好！”裘丰言喝口酒，夹块红糟鸡放在口中咀嚼着，含含糊糊他说，“有你们两位在，没有我的主意，你们商量，我喝着酒听。”嵇胡两人对看一眼，都觉得老实人也不易对付，他们原先有过约定，预备一搭一档，旁敲侧击，让裘丰言自告奋勇，现在他是“唯君所命”的态度，说话就不能再绕圈子，否则便显得不够朋友，所以反觉得为难。当然，还是得嵇鹤龄开口，他想了一下看着胡雪岩说：“做倒有个做法，比较厉害，不过盘马弯弓，不能收立竿见影之效。”“不管它！你先说你的。”“我想，老裘办过一回提运洋枪的差使，也可以说是内行，不妨上他一个说帖，就说有英商接头，愿意卖枪给浙江，条件完全跟他们一佯，就是价钱便宜，每支只要二十五两银子。看他们怎么说？”“此计大妙！”说不开口的裘丰言，到底忍不住开口，“有此说帖，黄抚台就不能包庇了，不然言官参上一本，朝廷派大员密查，我来出头，看他如何搪塞？”“不至于到此地步。这个说帖一上，龚家父子一定会来找你说话，那时就有得谈了。”嵇鹤龄转眼看着胡雪岩说，“有好处也在年后。”裘丰言不明用意，接口又说：“年后就年后，反正不多几天就过年了。”嵇鹤龄听得这话，慢慢抬眼看着胡雪岩，是征询及催促的眼色，意思是让他对裘丰言有所表白。胡雪岩会意，但不想说破真意，因为这对袭丰言无用，此人样样都好，就是办到正事，头绪不能太多，跟他说了他也许反嫌麻烦，答一句：“长话短说，我记不住那么多！”岂不是自己找钉子碰？因此，胡雪岩只这样说，“不管什么时候收效，这件事对老裘有益无害，我看先上了说帖再作道理。”“那也好。”嵇鹤龄转脸问道：“老裘，你看怎么样？”

“Calm yourself.” Ji took his hand. “We invited you precisely to discuss how to put this injustice right. We've found the weakness, but you don't undertake to mend porcelain without a diamond drill. The Gongs aren't easy men to deal with. We must discuss it calmly.” “Very well!” Qiu drank, put a piece of chicken in his mouth, and said indistinctly as he chewed, “With you two here, I've no opinion to offer. You discuss it. I'll drink and listen.” Ji and Hu exchanged a glance. Even an honest fellow could be hard to manage. They had planned to play off one another, approaching the matter indirectly until Qiu volunteered. Now that he was placing himself entirely at their disposal, further circumlocution would be unfriendly. It left them in an awkward position. Naturally Ji had to speak. After a moment's thought, he looked at Hu. “There is one rather forceful approach. But it's a matter of drawing the bow and holding the threat. It won't produce an immediate result.” “Never mind. Tell us.” “Qiu has already handled the collection and transport of foreign guns, so he can claim experience. He might submit a memorandum saying that a British merchant has approached him and is willing to sell guns to Zhejiang on exactly the same terms, but at only twenty-five taels apiece. Let's see what they say.” “An excellent plan!” Qiu, despite his promise of silence, could not contain himself. “With that memorandum before him, Governor Huang couldn't shield them. Otherwise a censor might impeach him and the court send a high official to investigate secretly. I'd come forward then and see how he explained himself!” “It won't go that far. Once the memorandum is submitted, the Gongs are certain to approach you. Then there'll be something to discuss.” Ji turned to Hu. “Any benefit will come after the New Year.” Not understanding the purpose, Qiu said, “After the New Year, then! It's only a few days away.” Ji slowly raised his eyes to Hu, questioning and prompting him to make some explanation. Hu understood but did not want to reveal his real purpose. It would do no good with Qiu. An excellent fellow in other ways, he could not manage too many threads in serious business. If told, he might only find it troublesome and say, “Make it short! I can't remember all that.” Why invite a rebuff? Hu therefore said only, “Whenever it produces results, this can only benefit Qiu. Let's submit it first and see.” “Very well.” Ji turned back. “What do you think?”

“除却酒杯莫问我！”醉眼迷离的裘丰言，答了这样一句诗样的话，一只手又去抓酒瓶。“你不能喝了！”嵇鹤龄夺住他的手，“要办正事就不能喝醉。等办完了事，我让你带一瓶回去。”裘丰言恋恋不舍的松了手，瑞云在隔室很见机，立刻进来收拾残肴剩酒，另外端来一锅“烧鸭壳子”熬的粥，四样吃粥小菜。裘丰言就着象牙色的“冬腌菜”，连吃三碗，“好舒服！”他摸着肚子说：“酒醉饭饱，该办正事了。是不是拟说帖？““对了！”嵇鹤龄问道：“你还能动笔不能？”“有何不能，‘太白斗酒诗百篇’，何况平铺直叙一说帖？”“那好！你先喝着茶，抽两袋烟休息。我跟雪岩商量一下。”于是两个人移坐窗前，悄悄的商议，因为有些话不便当着裘丰言说，首先就要考虑他个人的利害。

“Ask me nothing beyond the wine cup!” Qiu answered in something like a line of verse, his drunken eyes misty as he reached again for the bottle. “No more!” Ji caught his hand. “You mustn't get drunk when there's work to do. Once it's finished, I'll give you a bottle to take home.” Reluctantly Qiu let go. Ruiyun, alert to the situation from the next room, promptly cleared away the remaining food and wine. She brought a pot of rice gruel simmered with a roast-duck carcass and four accompaniments. With ivory-coloured winter-pickled vegetables, Qiu ate three bowls. “How comfortable!” he said, rubbing his stomach. “Full of wine and food—now for business. Are we drafting the memorandum?” “Exactly. Can you still wield a brush?” “Why not? ‘A measure of wine, a hundred poems from Li Bai.’ Surely I can manage one plain memorandum!” “Good. Have some tea, smoke a couple of pipes, and rest while Xueyan and I discuss it.” They moved to the window and spoke quietly. Some things could not be said before Qiu. First they must consider the consequences for him personally.

“这个说帖一上，黄抚台自然把裘丰言恨得牙痒，将来或许会有吃亏的时候，我们做朋友的，不能不替他想到。”“这当然要顾虑。不过，大哥，我跟你的看法有点西洋，黄抚台这个人，向来敬酒不吃吃罚酒，说不定这一来反倒对老裘另眼相看。”嵇鹤龄想了想说：“这一层暂且不管，只是这个说帖，要弄得象真的一样才好。”“本来就要有这个打算。真的这笔生意能够拿过来，二十五两银子一支一定可以买得到，而且包定有钱赚。”等这一点弄明白了，说帖便不难拟，移砚向灯，他们两个人斟酌着一条一条地说，裘丰言便一条一条地写。写完再从头斟酌，作成定稿，说好由裘丰言找人去分缮三份，一份送抚台，一份送藩台。这件事明天上午就得去妥。“好！这都归我。现在问下一步，说帖送了上去，黄抚台要找我，我该怎么说？”“黄抚台不会找你！”嵇鹤龄极有把握地答道：“要找一定是龚家父子来找你。”“那总也要有话说啊！”“这不忙！他来找你，你来找我。”“等我来找你，你的‘过年东道’就有着落了。”胡雪岩觉得这话不妥，因而紧接着笑道，“这是我说笑话，不管怎么样，你今年过年不必发愁，一切有我！”“多谢，多谢！”裘丰言满脸是笑，“说实话，交上你们两位朋友，我本来就不用愁。”说到这里，裘丰言站起身来告辞，胡雪岩亦不再留，一起离了槛家，约定第二天晚饭时分，不管消息如何，仍在嵇家碰头。

“Once the memorandum goes in, Governor Huang will hate Qiu. He may suffer for it later. As his friends, we must consider that.” “Of course. But, Elder Brother, I see it a little differently. Governor Huang has always responded to pressure better than courtesy. This might even make him regard Qiu with new respect.” Ji reflected. “Leave that aside for now. The memorandum must at least look genuine.” “We must be prepared to make it genuine. If we actually take over the transaction, we can certainly supply guns at twenty-five taels each and still make a profit.” Once that was clear, drafting was easy. They moved the inkstone towards the lamp. Ji and Hu considered each point and dictated it, and Qiu wrote each one down. Then they reviewed the whole and settled on a final text. Qiu would have three fair copies made, one for the governor and one for the provincial treasurer. This must be done the next morning. “Very well. Leave all that to me. Now, the next step: once it's submitted, what should I say if Governor Huang sends for me?” “He won't,” Ji replied with complete confidence. “It will be the Gongs who come.” “I still need something to say.” “There's no hurry. When they come to you, come to me.” “By the time I come to you, your New Year expenses will be provided for,” Hu added. Feeling this was ill-judged, he immediately laughed. “I'm joking. Whatever happens, don't worry about this New Year. Leave everything to me!” “Thank you, thank you!” Qiu beamed. “To tell the truth, with friends like you two, I had no need to worry anyway.” He rose to leave. Hu did not detain him and left Ji's house with him. They agreed to meet there again at supper the following evening, whether there was news or not.

裘丰言感于知遇，特别实力，回家以后，就不再睡，好在洋酒容易发散，洗过一把脸，喝过两杯浓茶，神思便已清醒，于是挑灯磨墨，决定把这通说帖抄好了它，一早“上院”去递。这一番折腾，把他的胖太太吵得不能安眠，“死鬼！她在帐子里”娇嗔“：”半夜三更，又是这么冷的天气，不死到床上来，在搞啥鬼！“你睡你的，我有公事。”这真是新闻了，裘丰言一天到晚无事忙，从未动笔办过公。事，而况又是如此深宵，说有公事，岂非奇谈！“你骗鬼！什么公事？一定又是搞什么‘花样’，穷开心！”胖太太又说，“快过年了，也不动动脑筋，看你年三十怎么过？”“就是为了年三十好过关，不能不拼老命。你少跟我罗嗦，我早早弄完了，还要上院。”听说上院，就决不是搞什么“花样”，胖太太一则有些不信，二则也舍不得“老伴”一个人“拼老命”，于是从床上起身，走来一看，白折子封面写着“说帖”二字，这才相信他真的是在忙公事。“你去睡嘛！”裘丰言搓一搓手说，“何苦陪在这里受冻。”“你在这里办公事，我一个人怎么睡得着？”听得这话，裘丰言的骨头奇轻，伸手到她的脸上，将她那象泻粉似的皮肉轻轻拧了一把，然后提起笔来，埋头疾书。他的一笔小楷，又快又好，抄完不过五更时分，胖太太劝他先睡一会，裘丰言不肯，吃过一杯早酒，挡挡寒气，趁着酒兴，步行到了巡抚衙门，找着刘二，道明来意。

Moved by their appreciation, Qiu exerted himself unusually hard. Back home, he did not return to bed. Fortunately, the effects of the foreign liquor wore off readily. After washing his face and drinking two cups of strong tea, he felt clear-headed. He trimmed the lamp, rubbed the ink, and resolved to copy the memorandum properly so that he could take it to the governor's yamen first thing in the morning. His activity disturbed his stout wife's sleep. “You wretch!” she scolded affectionately from behind the bed curtains. “In the middle of the night, in weather this cold, why don't you drag yourself to bed? What are you up to?” “Go back to sleep. I have official business.” This was news indeed. Qiu spent his days being busy about nothing and had never put brush to paper on official work. To claim it at such an hour was extraordinary. “Tell that to the ghosts! What official business? You're playing some foolish trick for amusement again. New Year's nearly here. Think about that! How are you going to get through New Year's Eve?” “It's precisely to get through it that I'm working myself to death. Stop bothering me. Once I finish, I still have to go to the governor's yamen.” That could hardly be a prank. Half disbelieving, and unwilling to let her old companion work himself to death alone, she rose and came over. Seeing “Memorandum” on the cover of the plain folded paper, she finally believed him. “Go to bed,” he said, rubbing his hands. “Why stand here freezing with me?” “How could I sleep alone while you're doing official work?” Her words made him feel delightfully light. He reached out and gently pinched her cheek, soft as starch paste, then took up his brush and wrote rapidly with his head bent. His small regular script was both swift and elegant. He finished by the fifth watch. His wife urged him to sleep a little, but he refused. After an early cup of liquor to keep out the cold, he walked, fortified by it, to the governor's yamen, found Liu Er, and explained his errand.

由于裘丰言为人和气，所以人缘极好，刘二跟他是开玩笑惯了的，把“裘老爷”叫成：“舅老爷！”他笑着说道，“已经冬天了，‘秋风’早就过去了，你这两个说帖没得用！”“难道上说帖就是想打秋风？”裘丰言答道：“今年还没有找过你的麻烦，这件事无论如何要帮我的忙。”“怎么帮法？”“马上送到抚台手里，不但送到，还要请他老人家马上就看。”“有这么紧要？”刘二倒怀疑了，“什么事，你先跟我说一说。”裘丰言已听嵇鹤龄和胡雪岩谈过，知道刘二对龚家父子亦颇不满，心想，这件事不必瞒他，便招一招手把他拉到僻处，悄悄说道：“我有个户头要推销洋枪，这件事成功了，回扣当然有你一份。”“推销洋枪！”刘二细想一想，从裘丰言跟胡雪岩的关系上去猜测，就知道了是怎么回事？便毫不迟疑地答道：“我有数了。倘有信息送哪里？”这句话把裘丰言问住了，他得先想一想，是什么“信息”？如果是黄抚台的约见，则嵇鹤龄已经说过，不会有这样的情形。看起来，这个推断还是不确，得要预备一下。“你是说抚台会找我？”裘丰言想了想答道，“你寻我不易，这样吧，我下午再来一趟。”“也好！如果有信息，而我又不在，必定留下信，否则就是没有消息，你请回好了。”这样约定以后，裘丰言方始回家补觉，一睡睡到午后两点才醒，只见胖太太递给他一封信，是胡雪岩写来的，约他下午三点在阜康钱庄见面。原来说好了，晚上仍旧在嵇家相会，如今提前约晤，必有缘故。裘丰言不敢怠慢，匆匆漱洗，出门赴约。

Qiu's amiability made him well liked. Liu Er was accustomed to joking with him, punning on “Master Qiu” by calling him “Uncle.” “It's winter already,” he laughed. “The autumn wind has long passed. These two memoranda of yours won't do any good!” “Does submitting a memorandum always mean coming to cadge money? I haven't troubled you once this year. You must help me this time.” “How?” “Put it into the governor's hands at once—and ask him to read it at once too.” “Is it that urgent?” Liu was doubtful. “Tell me what it's about first.” From Ji and Hu, Qiu knew that Liu resented the Gongs. There was no need to conceal this from him. He beckoned him aside and whispered, “I have a client who wants to sell foreign guns. If it succeeds, there'll naturally be a share of the commission for you.” “Foreign guns!” Thinking it over and taking Qiu's connection with Hu into account, Liu understood. He answered without hesitation, “I see. Where shall I send word if there's news?” That stumped Qiu. What sort of news? If it meant a summons from Governor Huang, Ji had said none would come. Perhaps the prediction was uncertain after all, and he ought to prepare. “You mean the governor might send for me?” he asked after a moment. “I'm hard to find. I'll come again this afternoon.” “Very well. If there's news and I'm out, I'll leave a message. If there's none, you can go home.” With that settled, Qiu returned to make up his lost sleep. He did not wake until two in the afternoon, when his wife handed him a letter from Hu asking him to come to Fukang at three. They had agreed to meet at Ji's that evening. There must be a reason for the earlier appointment. Qiu hurriedly washed, rinsed his mouth, and went out.

一到阜康钱庄，头一个就遇见陈世龙，彼此是熟识的，寒暄了几句，去见胡雪岩，只见他神采焕发，喜气洋洋，不由得诧异：“咦！你今天象个新郎官！”胡雪岩笑一笑，不理他的话，只问：“那东西递上去了？”“昨天晚上回去……”他倒也不是“丑表功”，只要说明替好朋友办事的诚意，所以把整个经过情形讲了一遍。“好极！事缓则圆。回头你就再辛苦一趟，看看有什么信息，打听过了，晚上我们在嵇家喝酒。”“好，好，我这就去。”裘丰言又问，“不过有件事我不明白，你特为约我此刻见面，就是问这句话？”“是的！我的意思，怕你说帖还不曾送出去，就摆一摆，等我到了上海，把那个普鲁士人的底细摸清楚了再说。既然已送了出去，那也很好。”这一说裘丰言更为困惑，“怎么，一下子想到要去上海？”他问：“哪天动身？”“日子还没有定，总在这两天。喔，”胡雪岩想起一件事，从口袋里取出一个红封袋，塞到裘丰言手里，笑着说道，“赶快回去跟你胖太太交帐，好让她早早筹划打年货！”裘丰言抽开封套看，是一张四百两银子的银票，心里愧感交集，眼圈有些发红。胡雪岩不肯让他说出什么来，推着他说：“请吧，请吧，我不留你了，回头嵇家见。”

The first person he met at Fukang was Chen Shilong, an old acquaintance. After a few words of greeting, he went to Hu and found him looking radiant and delighted. “Well!” Qiu exclaimed. “You look like a bridegroom today!” Hu smiled, ignored the remark, and asked only, “Has that thing been submitted?” “When I got home last night...” Qiu described the whole business, with no intention of boasting, simply to show how sincerely he had worked for his friends. “Excellent! Matters settle better when we take our time. Trouble yourself to go once more and see whether there's news. After that, we'll drink at Ji's this evening.” “Certainly. I'll go now. But there's something I don't understand. Did you specially ask me here now just to ask that?” “Yes. If you hadn't sent it in, I meant to hold it back until I'd been to Shanghai and learned more about that Prussian. Since it's already gone, that's fine too.” Qiu was more puzzled. “Why this sudden thought of Shanghai? When are you leaving?” “No date is fixed, but within the next day or two. Oh!” Remembering something, Hu took a red envelope from his pocket and pushed it into Qiu's hand. “Hurry home and report to your stout wife, so she can start buying for the New Year.” Qiu opened it and found a banknote for four hundred taels. Gratitude mingled with a sense of unworthiness, and his eyes reddened. Hu would not let him say anything. Gently urging him away, he said, “Off you go! I won't keep you. See you at Ji's later.”

陈世龙的不速而至，在胡雪岩颇感意外，但说穿了就不希奇，是刘不才“抓差”。到庞家的交涉，还算顺利，主要的还是靠胡雪岩自己，由于他那两封信，王有龄对庞二自然另眼相看。嘱咐刑名老夫子替他们调解争产的纠纷。原告是庞二的一个远房叔叔，看见知府出面调停，知道这场这司打下去得不到便宜，那时“敬酒不吃吃罚酒”，未免不智，所以愿意接受调解。庞二早就有过表示。花几个钱不在乎，能够不打官司不上堂，心里就安逸了。因此，看了胡雪岩的信，听了刘不才的叙述，一口答应帮忙。只是年近岁逼，人又在南浔，一下子要凑一大笔现银出来，倒也有些吃力。“我来想办法！一定可以想得出。你就不必管了，先玩一玩再说。”果然是胡雪岩预先猜到的情形出现了，刘不才心想，如果辞谢，必惹庞二不快，说不定好事就会变卦，但坐下来先赌一场，又耽误了胡雪岩的正事。灵机一动，想到个两全其美的办法。“庞二哥，我受人之托，要忠人之事，本来应该赶回去，不过你留我陪着你玩，我也实在舍不得走。要玩玩个痛快，不要叫我牵肠挂肚。这样，”他略作沉吟之态，然后用那种事事不无可疑，非如此办不可的语气说：“庞二哥，你把雪岩托你的事筹划好，我到湖州找个人回去送信！”“好！”庞二很爽快地答应，“你坐一下，我到帐房里去问一问看。”他一走，刘不才也不愿白耽误工夫，立刻就写了一封信，请庞家派个人到湖州，把陈世龙找来待命。

Chen's unexpected arrival had surprised Hu, but the explanation was simple: Liu Bucai had pressed him into service. Negotiations at the Pang household had gone fairly smoothly, largely because of Hu's own earlier efforts. His two letters had naturally led Wang Youling to treat Pang with special consideration and instruct his legal secretary to mediate the inheritance dispute. The plaintiff, a distant uncle of Pang's, saw that with the prefect intervening, continuing the lawsuit would bring him no advantage. It would be foolish to reject a cup offered courteously only to drink one imposed as punishment, so he accepted mediation. Pang had already said that he did not mind spending a little, provided he could avoid litigation and appearing in court. That would put his mind at rest. After reading Hu's letter and hearing Liu's explanation, he agreed at once to help. But with the year's end so close, and himself in Nanxun, assembling a large sum in cash immediately was difficult. “I'll find a way. I certainly will! Don't trouble yourself. Let's enjoy a game first.” Exactly as Hu had predicted. Liu thought that refusal would offend Pang and might undo the good result. Yet sitting down to gamble would delay Hu's business. Then he hit upon a way to satisfy both. “Brother Pang, I've been entrusted with something and must see it through. I ought to hurry back. But since you want me to stay and play, I'm reluctant to leave too. Let me enjoy it properly, without something weighing on my mind. How about this...” He paused as though considering, then spoke as though nothing could be taken on trust and this was the only arrangement that would do. “Settle what Xueyan asked you to do, and I'll get someone from Huzhou to take the news back!” “Good!” Pang agreed readily. “Sit here. I'll ask in the counting house.” Liu would not waste time while he was away. He wrote at once and asked the Pang household to send someone to Huzhou for Chen Shilong, who was to come and await instructions.

“家里倒有点现银，过年要留着做赌本，也防着穷朋友穷亲戚来告贷，不能给老胡。”庞二说道，“我在上海有好几十万帐好收，划出二十五万给老胡，不过要他自己去收，有两笔帐或许收不到，看他自己的本事。”“好的，好的！”刘不才觉得有此结果，大可满足、“你帮雪岩这么一个大忙，我代表他谢谢。不过，这笔款子，怎么算法，你是要货色，还是怎么样？请吩咐了，我好通知雪岩照办。”“要什么货色？算我借给老胡的，等他把那票丝脱手了还我。”“是！那么，利息呢？”“免息！”“这不好意思吧……”刘不才迟疑着。“老刘！”庞二放低了声音，“我跟你投缘，说老实话吧，其中有两笔帐，大概七八万银子上下，不大好收。听好老胡跟松漕帮的尤老五，交情很够，这两笔帐托尤老五去收，虽不能十足回笼，七成帐是有的。能够这样，我已经承情不尽，尤老五那里，我自然另有谢意，这都等我跟老胡见了面再谈。”

“There is some silver in the house,” Pang said, “but I must keep it for New Year gambling and for poor friends and relations who come to borrow. I can't give that to Old Hu. I have several hundred thousand owing to me in Shanghai. I'll assign him two hundred and fifty thousand, but he'll have to collect it himself. Two debts may prove uncollectable. That will depend on his ability.” “Excellent!” Liu was thoroughly satisfied. “On his behalf, thank you for such a great favour. But how is this money to be treated? Do you want goods for it, or something else? Tell me so that I can notify Xueyan.” “What goods? It's a loan. He can repay me when he's sold that consignment of silk.” “Yes. And the interest?” “None!” “Surely that's too much to ask...” Liu hesitated. Pang lowered his voice. “Old Liu, we get on well, so I'll speak frankly. Two of those debts, amounting to perhaps seventy or eighty thousand, will be hard to collect. I hear Old Hu is very close to You Laowu of the Songjiang Grain Transport Brotherhood. If he asks You to collect them, we should recover seventy per cent, even if we can't get it all. I'd be deeply grateful for that. I'll thank You separately, of course. I'll discuss it all with Hu when we meet.”

陈世龙非常巴结，接信立刻到南浔。刘不才已经在牌九桌上了，抽不出空写信，把他找到一边，连话带庞二的收帐凭证，一一交代明白，陈世龙随即坐了刘不才包雇的快船，连夜赶到杭州。胡雪岩一块石头落地。不过事情也还相当麻烦，非得亲自到上海去一趟不可，而杭州还有杂条要料理。尤其是意外发现的买洋枪这件事，搞得好是笔大生意，由此跟洋人进一步的交往，对他的丝生意也有帮助，而搞不好则会得罪了黄抚台和龚家父子，倘或迁怒到王有龄和嵇鹤龄身上，关系甚重，更加放不下心。看他左右为难，陈世龙便自告奋勇：“胡先生！”他说，“如果我能办得了，就让我去一趟好了。”胡雪岩想了想，这倒也是个办法，“你一个是办不了的，要托尤五！”他断然决然的作了决定：“你先到松江，无论如何要拖着他在一起。其余的事，我托老古。”于是整整谈了一晚上，指点得明明白白。第二天一早，陈世龙就动身走了。就在这天，裘丰言所上的说帖有了反应，一大早便有一顶蓝呢大轿，抬到裘家门口，跟班在拜匣里取了张名帖，投到裘家“门上”。

Chen Shilong was eager to oblige. The moment he received the letter, he went to Nanxun. Liu Bucai was already at the pai gow table and could spare no time to write. Drawing Chen aside, he explained everything, gave him Pang Er's documents authorizing collection of the debts, and made sure he understood every detail. Chen then took the fast boat Liu had hired and travelled through the night to Hangzhou. A weight lifted from Hu Xueyan's heart. Yet matters were still complicated enough to require a journey to Shanghai, while miscellaneous business in Hangzhou also needed his attention. The unexpected discovery of the foreign gun transaction was a particular concern. Properly handled, it could become a substantial piece of business, and closer dealings with the foreigners would help his silk trade. Handled badly, it could offend Governor Huang and the Gongs. If their resentment spread to Wang Youling and Ji Heling, the consequences would be grave. He could hardly leave it unattended. Seeing his dilemma, Chen volunteered. “Mr Hu, if it's something I can manage, let me make the journey.” Hu considered this. It was a possible solution. “You couldn't do it alone. You'll have to ask You Laowu.” His decision made, he continued firmly, “Go to Songjiang first. Whatever happens, get him to stay with you and help. I'll entrust the other business to Old Gu.” They talked throughout the evening, until Hu had made every instruction clear. Chen left early the next morning. That same day, Qiu Fengyan's memorandum produced a response. Early in the morning, a large sedan chair covered in blue woollen cloth arrived outside Qiu's house. An attendant took a visiting card from his card case and handed it to the doorkeeper.

看门的是早就受了嘱咐，一看帖子便回说主人出门了，其实裘丰言刚刚起身。客是走了，名帖却留了下来，是炮局坐办龚振麟来拜访过了。裘丰言大为兴奋，一直赶到阜康钱庄，见了胡雪岩就说：“鹤龄好准的阴阳八卦！你看，老龚果然移樽就教来了。”“你见了他没有？”“自然不见。一见便万事全休，他要一问，我什么也不知道，真正是‘若要盘驳，性命交脱’！”“没有那样子不得了，你别害怕。走，我们到鹤龄那里去。”海运局年底清闲无事，嵇鹤龄在家纳福，冬日晴窗之下，正在教小儿子认字号。看到裘丰言的脸色，便即笑道：“必是有消息了。”“是啊！”裘丰言答道：“一路上我在嘀咕，从来不曾干过这种‘戳空枪’的把戏，不知道应付得下来不能？”他担心的是本无其事，亦无其人，问到洋人在何处，先就难得回答。然而在胡雪岩和嵇鹤龄策划之下，也很容易应付，细细教了他一套话。裘丰言才真的有了笑容。

The doorkeeper had already been instructed. One glance at the card, and he replied that his master was out, although Qiu had only just risen. The visitor left, but his card remained: Gong Zhenlin, executive director of the Cannon Bureau, had called. Highly excited, Qiu hurried straight to Fukang Bank. “Heling reads the signs like a master diviner!” he told Hu. “Look—the elder Gong has come to seek my counsel, just as he predicted.” “Did you see him?” “Of course not. One meeting would have ruined everything. If he had asked me anything, I wouldn't have known what to say. Truly, ‘Let them question me, and my life is forfeit!’” “It isn't as terrible as all that. Don't be frightened. Come, let's go to Heling's.” There was little to do at the Sea Transport Bureau at the end of the year, so Ji was enjoying a quiet time at home. Seated by a sunny window on this winter day, he was teaching his little son to recognize characters. At the sight of Qiu's expression, he smiled. “There must be news.” “Indeed there is! All the way here I've been worrying. I've never tried a bluff like this before. I don't know whether I can carry it off.” His concern was that neither the proposed transaction nor the supposed merchant behind it actually existed. A question about the foreigner's whereabouts would be enough to put him in difficulty. Under Hu and Ji's guidance, however, this was easy enough to manage. They carefully coached him in what to say, and at last a real smile appeared on his face.

“我要去回拜，得借你的轿子和贵管家一用。”“不好！”嵇鹤龄未置可否，胡雪岩先就表示异议，“那一下就露马脚了。”“不错，不错！不要紧，我可以将就。”裘丰言朋友也很多，另借一顶轿子，拿他的门上充跟班，将就着到炮局去回拜，名帖一递进去，龚振麟开中门迎接。他家就住在炮局后面，为示亲切，延入私第，先叫他儿子龚之棠来拜见，一口一个“老伯”，异常恭敬。“丰言兄，久仰你的‘酒中仙’，我也是一向贪杯，颇有佳酿，今天酒逢知己，不醉无归。”“一定要叨扰，未免不成话！”“老兄说这话就见外了。”龚振麟嘱咐儿子：“你去看看裘老伯的管家在哪里？把衣包取了来。”“不必，不必！”裘丰言说，“原来是打算着稍微坐一坐就告辞，不曾带便衣来。”“既如此，”龚振麟看看客人，又看看儿子：“之棠，你的身材跟裘老伯相仿，取一件你的皮袍子来。伺候裘老伯替换。”裘丰言心想，穿着官服喝酒，也嫌拘束，就不作假客气，等龚之棠叫个丫头把皮袍子取了来，随即换上，是件俗称“萝卜丝”的新羊皮袍，极轻极暖，刚刚合身。

“I must return his call. I'll need to borrow your chair and your steward.” Ji had yet to answer when Hu objected. “No! That would give the game away.” “Quite right, quite right. Never mind. I'll manage.” Qiu had plenty of friends himself. He borrowed a chair elsewhere, took his own doorkeeper along as an attendant, and thus equipped went to return the call at the Cannon Bureau. As soon as his card was presented, Gong Zhenlin opened the main gate to receive him. Gong's home lay behind the bureau. To show his friendliness, he conducted Qiu into his private quarters and first summoned his son, Gong Zhitang, to pay his respects. The young man addressed Qiu repeatedly as “Uncle” and behaved with the greatest deference. “Brother Fengyan, I've long admired your fame as an immortal of the wine cup. I'm fond of a drink myself and have some excellent vintages. Now that two kindred drinkers have met, you mustn't leave sober.” “I really ought not to impose on you like this!” “You're treating me as a stranger.” Gong told his son, “Go and see where Uncle Qiu's steward is. Have his bundle of clothes brought in.” “No need, no need. I'd intended to stay only a moment, so I brought no informal clothes.” “In that case...” Gong glanced from his guest to his son. “Zhitang, you're much the same size as Uncle Qiu. Fetch one of your fur robes and help him change.” Drinking in official dress would be rather stiff, Qiu reflected, so he dispensed with polite refusals. When Zhitang had a maid bring the robe, he put it on. It was a new lambskin robe of the kind commonly called ‘shredded radish’, exceptionally light and warm, and it fitted perfectly.

未摆酒，先设茶，福建的武夷茶，器具精洁，烹制得恰到好处。裘丰言是随遇而安的性格，跟点头之交的龚振麟虽是初次交往，却象熟客一样，一面品茗，一面鉴赏茶具，显得极其舒适随便。而龚振父子也是故意不谈正事，只全力周旋着想在片刻之间，结成“深交”。品茗未毕，只见龚家两个听差，抬进一坛酒来，龚振麟便说：“老兄对此道是大行家，请过来看看。”裘丰言见此光景，意料必是一坛名贵的佳酿，便欣然离座，跟龚振磷一起走到廊下，只见是一坛二十五斤的花雕，坛子上的彩画，已经非常黯淡，泥头尘封，变成灰色，隐约现得有字。拂尘一看，上面写着：道光十三年嘉平月造。“哟！”裘丰言说：“整整二十年了！”“是的。在我手里也有五六年了。一共是两坛，前年家母七十整寿，开了一坛，这一坛是‘ 尊因吾辈到时开’！”裘丰言自然感动，长揖致谢，心里却有些不安，这番隆情厚意，不在胡、嵇估计之中、以后投桃报李，倒下不了辣手了。

Before the wine came tea: Wuyi tea from Fujian, prepared to perfection and served in exquisite, spotless utensils. Qiu was at ease wherever he found himself. Though he and Gong had previously been no more than nodding acquaintances and this was his first visit, he behaved like an old guest, tasting the tea and admiring the utensils in complete comfort. Father and son deliberately avoided business, concentrating instead on their attentions to him, as though they could become intimate friends in a few moments. Before they had finished their tea, two servants carried in a jar of wine. “You're a great connoisseur,” Gong said. “Come and have a look.” Judging from the ceremony, Qiu expected a rare vintage.
