He rose gladly and accompanied Gong into the corridor. It was a twenty-five-jin jar of huadiao wine. The painted designs had faded badly, and dust had turned the clay seal grey. A faint inscription appeared beneath the dust. When this was brushed away, it read: “Made in the twelfth month of the thirteenth year of Daoguang.” “Oh!” Qiu exclaimed. “A full twenty years!” “Yes. I've had it myself for five or six. There were two jars altogether. We opened one for my mother's seventieth birthday the year before last. This one has waited for a guest worthy of its opening.” Naturally touched, Qiu bowed deeply in thanks. Yet he felt uneasy. Hu and Ji had not anticipated such lavish kindness. Once he owed a return for all this generosity, it would be difficult to deal harshly with his host.

就在这沉吟之际，龚家听差已经将泥头揭开，取下封口的竹著说：“裘老爷，你倒看一看！”探头一看，坛口正好有光直射，只见一坛酒剩了一半，而且满长着白毛，这就证明了确是极陈的陈酒，裘丰言果然是内行，点点头说：“是这样子的。”于是，龚家听差拿个铜久，极小心地撇净了白花，然后又极小心地把酒倒在一个绿瓷大坛中，留下沉淀的不要，又开了十斤一坛的新酒，注入瓷坛，顿时糟香扑鼻，裘丰言不自觉地在喉间咽下一口口水。回屋入座，但见龚家的福建菜，比王有龄家的更讲究，裘丰言得其所载，在他们父子双双相劝之下，一连就干了三杯，顿觉胸隔之间，春意拂拂而生，通身都舒泰了。等小龚还要劝千第四杯时，裘丰言不肯，“这酒上口淡，后劲足，不宜喝得过猛。”他说，“喝醉了不好！”“老伯太谦虚了！无论如何再干一杯。先干为敬。”说着龚之棠“啯、啯”的，一口气喝干了酒，侧杯向客人一照。裘丰言也只好照干不误。自然，他的意思，龚家父子明白，是要趁未醉之前，先谈正事。事实上也确是到了开谈的时候了。

While he hesitated, the servants removed the clay seal and the bamboo covering beneath it. “Have a look, Mr Qiu.” He leaned forward. Light fell directly into the jar, revealing that only half the wine remained and that its surface was covered with white growth. This confirmed how old it was. Qiu knew his wine: he nodded. “That's how it should be.” With a copper ladle, a servant carefully skimmed away the white growth, then poured the wine with equal care into a large green porcelain jar, leaving the sediment behind. He opened a ten-jin jar of new wine and added it. Immediately, the fragrance of fermented grain filled the air, and Qiu swallowed involuntarily. They went back inside and took their places. The Gong household's Fujian dishes were even more elaborate than those served at Wang Youling's. Qiu was in his element. Encouraged by father and son together, he drained three cups in succession. A springlike warmth stirred within his chest, and comfort spread through his whole body. When young Gong urged a fourth cup upon him, he declined. “It tastes mild, but it has a powerful kick. One shouldn't drink it too quickly. It wouldn't do to get drunk.” “You're far too modest, Uncle. You must have one more. I'll drink first, as a mark of respect.” Zhitang gulped down his wine in one draught and tilted the empty cup towards his guest. Qiu had no choice but to follow suit. The Gongs understood what he meant, of course: he wanted to discuss business before he became drunk. And it was indeed time to begin.

“昨天我上院，听抚台谈起，老兄有个说帖，”龚振麟闲闲提起，“抚台嘉赏不已！说如今官场中，象老兄这样的热心又能干的人，真正是凤毛麟角了。”“那是抚台谬奖。”裘丰言从容答道：“抚台是肯做事的人，不然，我也不肯冒昧。”“是啊！抚台总算是有魄力的。不过做事也很难，象这趟买的洋枪，是京里的大来头，不晓得那普鲁士人具何手眼、力量居然达得到大军机？价钱当然就不同了，简直是狮子大开口！抚台把这桩吃力不讨好的差使委了我，好不容易才磨到这个价钱。我做了恶人，外面还有人说闲话，变得里外不是人，这份委展，别人不知道，你老兄一定体谅！”裘丰言心想，他拿大帽子压下来，也不知是真是假，此时犯不着去硬顶。好在胡雪岩已授已四字妙诀：不置可否！于是他点点头答了一个字：“哦！”连这大军机是谁都不问。

“Yesterday, when I called at the governor's yamen, His Excellency mentioned a memorandum of yours,” Gong began casually. “He praised it most warmly. Men as zealous and capable as you, he said, are exceedingly rare in official life these days.” “His Excellency is too generous,” Qiu answered calmly. “He is a man willing to get things done. Otherwise, I shouldn't have ventured to submit it.” “Quite so. Our governor certainly has determination. But accomplishing anything is difficult. Take this gun purchase: it comes with powerful backing from the capital. Who knows what connections that Prussian has, to reach a Grand Councillor himself? Naturally, that makes a difference to the price. His demands were outrageous. The governor entrusted this thankless commission to me, and it took endless bargaining to bring the price down to its present level. I've made myself the villain, and people outside still criticize me. Neither side is pleased. Others may not understand what I've suffered, but you surely will.” Qiu reflected that Gong was trying to overawe him with a great name. Whether the story was true he could not tell, and there was no point in challenging it now. Fortunately, Hu had given him a simple guiding principle: neither agree nor disagree. He nodded and answered with a single “Oh!” He did not even ask which Grand Councillor was involved.

“我现在要请教老兄，你说帖中所说的英商，是不是哈德逊？”这不能不答：“是的。”“这就有点奇怪了！”龚振麟看看他的儿子说：“不是哈德逊回国了？”这话是说给裘丰言听的，他一听大惊，心想智者千虑，必有一失，胡雪岩本事再大，也不会想到哈德逊已不在中国。这一下，谎话全盘拆穿，岂不大伤脑筋？幸好，第一，襄丰言酒已上脸，羞愧之色被掩盖着，不易发现，第二，裘丰言押运过一次洋枪，也到过上海，跟洋人打过交道，不是茫无所知，第三，最后还有一句托词。“这怕是张冠李戴了！”他这样接口，“洋人同名同姓的甚多，大概是另外一个洋商哈德逊。至于我，这趟倒没有跟哈德逊碰头，是一个‘康白度’的来头。”“康白度”是译音，洋人雇用中国人作总管，代为接洽买卖，就叫“康白度”，是个极漂亮的“文明辙儿”，龚家父子听他也懂这个，不觉肃然起敬。“也许是的。”龚之棠到底年纪轻，说话比较老实，“是那个普鲁士人，同行相妒，故意这么说的。”

“Now, may I ask whether the British merchant named in your memorandum is Hudson?” This required an answer. “Yes.” “That's rather curious.” Gong looked at his son. “Hasn't Hudson gone home?” The remark was meant for Qiu, and it alarmed him. Even the wisest man could overlook something; for all Hu's ability, he would never have guessed that Hudson was no longer in China. If the whole invention were exposed at one stroke, what a predicament he would be in! Fortunately, three things helped him. First, wine had already reddened his face, concealing his embarrassment. Second, he had escorted a shipment of guns, visited Shanghai and dealt with foreigners; he was not wholly ignorant of the subject. Third, there remained one excuse he could use. “There must be some confusion,” he replied. “Many foreigners have the same first and last names. It was probably another merchant called Hudson. As for me, I haven't actually met Hudson over this transaction. The approach came through a comprador.” The word was a foreign borrowing. Chinese managers employed by foreigners to negotiate business on their behalf were called compradors. It was an impressively fashionable expression, and hearing that Qiu knew it made the Gongs regard him with new respect. “Perhaps so,” Zhitang said. Being younger, he was more candid. “It was the Prussian who told us. He must have said it deliberately, out of jealousy of a rival.”

“对了！”龚振麟转脸跟裘丰言解释，“跟现在这个洋人议价的时候，我自然要拿哈德逊来作比，想杀他的价。如果他肯跟哈德逊的出价一样，那么，既买了上头的面子，公事上也有了交代。其中唯一的顾虑，是胡雪翁费心费力，介绍了一个哈德逊来，照规矩，应该让他优先，现在机会给了别人，说起来道理上是不对的。不过，军机上的来头不能不买帐，事出无奈，所以我曾经跟抚台特为提到。抚台当时就说，胡某人深明大义，最肯体谅人，这一次虽有点对不起他，将来还有别的机会补报。军兴之际，采买军人的案子很多，下一次一定调剂他。又说：“胡某人的买卖很多，或许别样案子，也可以作成他的生意，总而言之，不必争在一时。”龚振麟长篇大套，从容细叙，裘丰言则酒在口中，事在心里，只字不遗地听着，一面听，一面想，原是想跟洋商讲价，结果扯到胡雪岩身上。这篇文章做得离题了！黄抚台是否说过那些话，莫可究诘，但意在安抚胡雪岩，则意思极明。自己不便有所表示，依然只能守住“不置可否”的宗旨，唯唯称是而已！

“Exactly.” Gong turned back to Qiu. “When bargaining with this foreigner, I naturally cited Hudson's price to try to beat him down. If he would match Hudson, we could both oblige our superiors and justify the purchase on its merits. My only concern was Mr Hu. He had taken such trouble to introduce Hudson, and by the rules his offer ought to have had priority. Giving the opportunity to someone else wasn't right. But backing from the Grand Council cannot be ignored. We had no choice, so I made a particular point of mentioning this to the governor. His Excellency said at once that Mr Hu understood the larger interests involved and was always considerate of other people's difficulties. Though this occasion might do him a slight wrong, there would be others on which to make it up to him. In wartime there are many military procurement contracts; he must be accommodated next time. His Excellency also said, ‘Mr Hu has many business interests. Perhaps some other project could provide him with a transaction. In any case, there's no need to contest this particular opportunity.’” Gong expounded his account at leisurely length. Qiu drank, but his thoughts stayed on the matter at hand; he missed not a word. The supposed subject was bargaining with a foreign merchant, yet they had ended up talking about Hu Xueyan. Quite a departure from the point! There was no way to establish whether the governor had actually said these things, but the intention to placate Hu was unmistakable. Qiu could make no commitment himself. He could only keep to his rule of neither agreeing nor disagreeing, murmuring polite acknowledgements.

“所以我现在又要请教，老兄所认识的这个哈德逊，与胡雪岩上次买枪的卖主哈德逊，可是一个人？”这句话是无可闪避的，裘丰言觉得承认比不承认好，所以点点头说：“ 是的！”“那么上次卖三十两银子一支，此刻何以又跌价了呢？”“上次是我们向他买，这次是他自己来兜生意，当然不能居奇。”裘车言自觉这话答得极好，一得意之下，索性放他一把野火：“再说句实话，我还可以杀他个三、五两银子！”“喔，喔！”龚振麟一直显得很从容，听到这一句，却有些穷于应付的模样了。龚振麟大概也发觉到自己的神态，落入裘丰言眼中，不是一件好事，所以极力振作起来，恢复原来的从容，喝口酒说道：“我有句不中听的话，不能不说与老兄听，哈德逊的货色，并不见得好，炮局曾拿老兄上次押运回来的洋枪试放过，准头不好。不知道这一次哈德逊来兜销的货色，是不是跟上次的一样？”说“准头不好”，到底是确有其事，还是他有意这么说，裘丰言无法分辨，但后半段的话，却不难回答，“我的说帖上写得很明白，”他说，“照那个普鲁士人同样的货色。”“这反而有点不大台龙了。”龚振麟说，“那批货色除他，别人是买不到的。”

“So may I ask again: is this Hudson you know the same Hudson who sold Mr Hu the guns last time?” There was no evading that question. Qiu decided that admission was better than denial and nodded. “Yes.” “Then why has the price fallen, when last time he charged thirty taels apiece?” “Last time we approached him. This time he's coming to us for business. Naturally, he can't hold out for a scarcity price.” Pleased with his answer, Qiu decided to add fuel to the fire. “To tell you the truth, I could bargain him down another three or five taels.” “Oh! Oh!” Gong had maintained his composure throughout, but this remark seemed to leave him at a loss. Apparently realizing that it was unwise to let Qiu see his discomfiture, he rallied, recovered his calm and took a sip of wine. “There's something you may not like hearing, but I must tell you. Hudson's goods aren't necessarily very good. The bureau tested the guns you escorted back last time, and their aim was poor. I wonder whether the guns he's offering now are the same.” Qiu could not judge whether the allegation about poor aim was true or deliberately invented, but the latter part was easy to answer. “My memorandum states it quite clearly: goods identical to the Prussian's.” “That makes it harder to understand,” Gong replied. “No one else can obtain that particular stock.”

不妙！裘丰言心想，这样谈下去，马脚尽露，再有好戏也唱不下去了。于是他不答这话，单刀直入地问：“我要请教贤乔梓，那个普鲁士人在不在这里？好不好我当面跟他谈一谈？”这是裘丰言的缓兵之计，用意是不想跟龚家父子多谈，哪知龚振麟却认为他真的想跟洋人见面盘问，心里有些着慌，因为其中有许多花样，见洋人一谈，西洋镜就都拆穿了。于是他这样答道：“洋人此刻在上海。老兄有何见教，不妨跟我说了，我一定转达。”裘丰言多喝了几杯酒，大声说道：“我想问问他，凭什么开价这么高！”这语气和声音，咄咄逼人，龚振麟不觉脸色微变，“刚才已经跟老兄说过了，有京里的大来头，此间办事甚难。”他用情商的口吻说，“凡事总求老兄和胡雪翁体谅。”说到这后，便无可再谈。裘丰言既不便应承，亦不便拒绝，只点点头说：“老兄的意思，我知道了。”局面变得有些僵，龚振麟当然不便硬逼，非要裘丰言打消本意，收回说帖不可，唯有尽主人的情意，殷殷酬劝，希望裘丰言能够欢饮而归。

This was dangerous. Qiu thought that if they continued, every flaw in his story would show, and however good the performance, he could not keep it going. Instead of answering, he put a direct question to father and son. “May I ask whether the Prussian is here? Could I speak with him face to face?” This was a delaying tactic; Qiu merely wanted to stop discussing the matter with the Gongs. Gong, however, thought he really intended to question the foreigner, and grew anxious. There were so many concealed tricks in the business that one conversation would expose the whole deception. “The foreigner is in Shanghai at present,” he replied. “If you have anything to say, tell me and I'll certainly pass it on.” After a few more cups, Qiu declared loudly, “I want to ask what entitles him to demand such a price!” His words and tone were aggressive enough to make Gong's expression change. “As I told you, there is powerful backing in the capital. That makes things very difficult here.” His voice became conciliatory. “In everything, I can only ask for your understanding and Mr Hu's.” There was little more to say. Qiu could neither accept nor refuse. He simply nodded. “I understand what you mean.” They had reached something of an impasse. Gong could hardly compel him to abandon his plan and withdraw the memorandum. All he could do was play the attentive host, repeatedly urging wine upon him in the hope that he would depart in good spirits.

一顿酒吃了四个钟头，裘丰言带着八分酒意，到了嵇家。胡雪岩正好在那里，听他细谈经过，不免有意外之感。“原来是京里大军机的来头，怪不得敢这样明目张胆地做！大哥，”胡雪岩问嵇鹤龄，“你看这件事该怎么办？”官场中的情形，嵇鹤龄自然比胡雪岩了解得多，“不见得是大来头，是顶大帽子。”他说，“你先不要让他给压倒了！”“对！”裘丰言也说：“我就不大相信，堂堂军机大臣，会替洋商介绍买卖。”“再退一步说，就算有大来头，也不能这么乱来！他有大来头，我们也有对付的办法，不过那一来是真刀真枪地干了！”“怎么呢？大哥你有啥办法？”“最直截了当的是，托御史参他一本，看他还敢说什么大来头不敢？”这是极狠的一着，只要言官有这么个折子，即令黄宗汉有京里的照应，可以无事，至少那桩买卖是一定可以打消的。但这一来就结成了不可解的冤家，只要黄宗汉在浙江一天，就有一天的麻烦。而且必然连累王有龄在浙江也无法混了。

The drinking lasted four hours. Well advanced towards drunkenness, Qiu arrived at Ji's house, where Hu happened to be. His detailed account surprised Hu. “So a Grand Councillor is behind it! No wonder they dare act so openly. Elder Brother, what do you think we should do?” Ji knew official life far better than Hu. “There may be no powerful patron at all—only a powerful name to intimidate us. Don't let it crush you before we begin.” “Exactly,” Qiu agreed. “I find it hard to believe that a dignified Grand Councillor would introduce business for a foreign merchant.” “Even supposing there is such a patron, they can't behave as they please. We have ways of dealing with powerful backing, too, though then we'd be fighting in earnest.” “How, Elder Brother? What means have you in mind?” “The most direct is to have a censor submit an impeachment memorial. Then let's see whether they still dare talk about their powerful patron.” This was a ruthless move. Once such a memorial had been submitted, even if Huang Zonghan's connections in the capital protected him personally, the transaction would at least be certain to collapse. But it would also create an irreconcilable enmity. For as long as Huang remained in Zhejiang, there would be trouble. Wang Youling, too, would inevitably be implicated and could no longer get along in the province.

当然，桩鹤龄也不过这样说说，聊且快意而已。反倒是裘丰言由此触机，出了个极妙的“点子”。“我想我们可以这么做，‘只拉弓，不放箭’，托个人去问一问，就说有这么一回事，不知其详，可否见告？看龚振麟怎么说。”嵇鹤龄有些不解：“托什么人去问？”“自然是托出一位‘都老爷’来。”这一说嵇、胡二人都明白了，所谓“只拉弓，不放箭”，就是做出预备查究其事的姿态，叫龚振麟和黄宗汉心里害怕，自然便有确切的表示。“好是好！哪里去寻这么一位都老爷？从京里写信来问，缓不济急。”裘丰言当然是有这么一个人在，才说那样的话，有个监察御史姓谢，请假回籍葬亲，假期已满，只等一开了年便要动身，这位谢都老爷是裘丰言的文酒之友，感情极好，一托无有不成之理。

Of course, Ji was only saying this for the momentary satisfaction it gave him. It was Qiu who drew inspiration from it and produced an excellent idea. “We might ‘draw the bow without loosing the arrow’. Have someone make an inquiry: we've heard of such a matter but don't know the details—could you enlighten us? Then see what Gong says.” Ji was puzzled. “Whom would we ask to inquire?” “Why, a censor, naturally.” Now Ji and Hu understood. Drawing the bow without loosing the arrow meant appearing ready to investigate. Gong and Huang would be frightened into making a definite offer. “An excellent idea. But where shall we find a censor? A letter from the capital would come too late.” Qiu would not have proposed it without a man in mind. An investigating censor surnamed Xie had taken leave to return home for a parent's burial. His leave had expired, and he was waiting only for the New Year to set off again. He and Qiu were close friends through literature and wine. There was every reason to expect that he would oblige.

“你看怎么样？”嵇鹤龄向胡雪岩说，“我是不服龚家父子的气，肆无忌惮，竟似看准了没有人敢说话似地。”“我不是怄这个闲气，也不想在这上头赚一笔。只是我现在正跟洋人打交道，面子有关。”嵇鹤龄懂胡雪岩的意思，心里在想，能把抚台作主的已有成议的买卖推翻，另找洋商，这消息传到夷场上去，足以大大地增加胡雪岩的声势。但另一方面，无疑地，黄宗汉和龚家父子都会不快。所以此事不干则已，一干就必定结了冤家。“我想这样子，”胡雪岩在这片刻间，打走了主意，“这件事做还是做，有好处归老裘，一则他出的力多，二则也替他弄几文养老，或者加捐个实缺的‘大花样’，也会过一过官瘾。只是将来事情要做得和平。”“再和平也不行！”嵇鹤龄说，“你从人家口去夺食，岂能无怨！”“这我当然想到，”胡雪岩说，“光棍不断财路，我们这票生意倘能做成功，除了老裘得一份，龚家父子和黄抚台的好处，当然也要替他们顾到。”“这还差不多！”

“What do you think?” Ji asked Hu. “I resent the Gongs' behaviour. They act without the least restraint, as though certain that no one would dare speak.” “I'm not nursing an idle grievance, and I'm not trying to make money out of this. But I'm dealing with foreigners now. My standing is involved.” Ji understood. He reflected that if Hu could overturn a transaction already settled with the governor's approval and bring in a different foreign merchant, the news would enormously enhance his influence in the foreign settlement. On the other hand, it would undoubtedly displease Huang and the Gongs. Once they acted, they were bound to make enemies. In those few moments, Hu had decided. “This is what I suggest. We go ahead, and the profit goes to Qiu. First, he's done most of the work. Second, it will put something aside for his old age. Or he might pay an additional contribution for an actual official appointment—a grander title with a real post—and satisfy his taste for office. Only we must settle things amicably when the time comes.” “You can't, however amicable you try to be,” Ji said. “Snatch food from someone's mouth, and how can he not resent it?” “I've considered that, of course. A man of the world doesn't cut off another's livelihood. If we succeed in doing this business, besides Qiu's share we must naturally look after the Gongs and Governor Huang.” “That's more like it.”

事情就此谈定局。实际上等于是裘丰言的事，所以由他去奔走，胡雪岩只是忙自己的事。由于尤五的帮忙和古应春的手腕，上海方面的情形，相当顺利，杭州方面亦都“摆平”，到了腊月二十，几乎诸事就绪，可以腾出工夫来忙过年了。就在送灶的那一天，裘车言兴冲冲地到阜康来看胡雪岩，带来一个好消息，说龚振麟已经跟他开诚布公谈过，那笔洋枪生意，预备双方合作。龚振麟提出来的办法是，这一批洋枪分做两张合同，划出五千支由哈德逊承售，也就是裘丰言经手，抚台衙门每支拿二两银子作开销，此外都是裘丰言的好处。胡雪岩算了一下，原来每支枪有十二两银子的虚头，如今只取了一个零数，换句话说，让出五千支就是损失了五万两银子。这不是笔小数，龚振麟岂甘拱手让人？只是为势所迫，不能不忍痛牺牲，心里当然记着仇恨，以后俟机报复，自己要替裘丰言挡灾，未免太划不来。当然，即上了这个说帖，龚振麟不能不敷衍，他自己吃肉，别人喝汤，应该不会介意，照现在这样，变成剜了他的心头肉，那就太过分了。但当初已经说过，有好处都归裘丰言，那么如今替龚振麟的利益着想，便又是剜裘丰言的心头肉，怕他会不高兴。这样想，左右为难，觉得这件事做得太轻率了。

The matter was settled. In practice, it had become Qiu's affair, and he did the running about while Hu attended to his own business. Thanks to You Laowu's help and Gu Yingchun's skill, matters in Shanghai went fairly smoothly. Hangzhou's affairs were also brought into order. By the twentieth day of the twelfth month, almost everything was ready, and Hu could spare time for New Year preparations. On the day the Kitchen God was sent off to heaven, Qiu came eagerly to Fukang with good news. Gong had spoken frankly with him: the gun transaction would be handled jointly. His proposal was to divide the purchase between two contracts. Five thousand guns would be supplied by Hudson, with Qiu handling the transaction. The governor's yamen would take two taels per gun for expenses; the remaining benefit would be Qiu's. Hu calculated. There had originally been twelve taels of padding on each gun. Now they were retaining only the odd two taels. In other words, surrendering five thousand guns meant sacrificing fifty thousand taels. This was no small sum. How could Gong willingly hand it over? He was yielding under pressure and making a painful sacrifice. Surely he would bear a grudge and wait for a chance to retaliate. Having to shield Qiu from the consequences would hardly be worthwhile for Hu. With the memorandum already submitted, Gong had to offer something. He could hardly object to letting others drink the broth while he ate the meat. But this proposal cut into his very flesh; it went too far. Yet Hu had promised Qiu all the benefit. To protect Gong's interests now would be to cut into Qiu's flesh instead, and Qiu might resent it. Caught between the two, Hu felt that they had acted too lightly.

“怎么回事？”裘丰言见他神色有异，困惑地问。“老裘，”胡雪岩试探着说，“恭喜你发笔财！”“那都是你挑我的。”裘丰言答道，“这笔好处，当然大家有份，将来听你分派。”这个表示，使得胡雪岩很安慰，只要裘丰言未曾存着“吃独食”的打算，事情就好办了。“我跟鹤龄决不要！不过，老裘，钱要拿得舒服，烫手的钱不能用。哈德逊的这张合同，大有研究。”胡雪岩想了一下问道，“说实话，老裘，你想用多少钱？”这话使人很难回答，裘丰言不解所谓，也不知道能用多少钱，唯有这样答道：“我说过，归你分派，你给我多少，就是多少。”“是这样，我不能不从头说起。”胡雪岩说：“他们让出五千支来，就要损失五万银子，但是从哈德逊那里，弄不到这个数目，为啥呢？我算结你听……”说帖上说，照同样的货色，每支只要二十五两银子，实际上每支二十两，只有五两银子的虚头，所以一共也只有二万五千银子的好处，除掉抚台衙门一万，还剩下一万五千银子。

“What's the matter?” Qiu asked, puzzled by his expression. “Congratulations on your windfall,” Hu said tentatively. “I owe it all to your support. Naturally, everyone has a share. I'll leave the distribution to you.” This reassured Hu. So long as Qiu had no intention of keeping everything to himself, matters would be manageable. “Heling and I won't take anything. But money must be comfortable to hold. Money that burns the hand is no use. We need to consider Hudson's contract very carefully.” After a moment's thought, he asked, “Tell me honestly, Qiu: how much money would you like?” It was a difficult question. Qiu did not understand what Hu meant and had no idea how much he might have. “As I said, I'll leave it to you. Whatever you give me will be enough.” “Then I must explain from the beginning. They're sacrificing fifty thousand taels by giving up those five thousand guns, but we can't make that much from Hudson. Why not? Let me show you the figures.” The memorandum offered identical guns at twenty-five taels each. Their actual cost was twenty, leaving only five taels of padding per gun, or twenty-five thousand altogether. After deducting ten thousand for the governor's yamen, fifteen thousand remained.

“一万五千银子三股派，”胡雪岩说到这里，襄丰言自动表示，“每人五千。”所望不奢，胡雪岩反倒过意不去，“你忙了一场，五千也太少了，你拿一万。”他说，“我跟鹤龄不要。”“那么，还有五千呢，莫非送给龚振麟？”“不错，不但这五千送他，还要问他，愿意戴多少‘帽子’？要这样，你的钱才不烫手。”裘丰言先还不服气，经过胡雪岩反复譬解，总算想通了，答应照他的意思跟龚振麟会谈。当然，这有个说法，说是哈德逊愿意每支枪再减一两银子。加上另外的二两，一共三两，这就是说每支枪以二十二两银子算。实收是这个数目，如果“上头还有别的开销，要加帽子也不妨”。

“Fifteen thousand divided three ways,” Qiu volunteered when Hu had explained this much. “Five thousand each.” His expectations were so modest that Hu felt almost guilty. “Five thousand would be too little after all your trouble. Take ten thousand. Heling and I want nothing.” “And the other five thousand? Surely you don't mean to give it to Gong?” “Exactly. And besides giving him that five thousand, we must ask how much more he wishes to add on top. Only then will your money cease to burn your hand.” At first Qiu objected, but after Hu had explained his reasoning repeatedly, he saw the point and agreed to discuss it with Gong on those terms. Naturally, they needed a way to present the arrangement. Hudson, they would say, was willing to reduce his price by another tael per gun. Together with the two taels already allowed for the governor's yamen, that made a deduction of three from the quoted twenty-five: the guns would thus be reckoned at twenty-two taels apiece. This was the net amount their side would receive. If “the higher authorities have other expenses and need to add something on top, that is quite acceptable.”

一听这个说法，龚振麟的观感一变。裘丰言背后有胡雪岩，他是知道的，原来以为胡雪岩太辣手，现在才发觉是“极漂亮”的一个人。除了交情以外，当然更要紧的是估量利害关系。龚振麟对胡雪岩一派的势力，相当了解，王有龄已有能员之名，在抚台面前很吃得开，嵇鹤龄也是浙江官场中一块很响的牌子，而此两人都倚胡雪岩为“谋主”，此人手腕灵活，足智多谋，尤其不可及的是人人乐为所用。象这样的人物，有机会可以结交而交臂失之，未免可惜。打定了这个主意，龚振麟便对裘丰言这样表示：“不瞒老兄说，这件事我的处境，实在为难，其中委曲，不必细表。以老兄及胡雪翁的眼力，自然能识得透，言而总之一句话，多蒙情让，必有所报。”这几句话听得裘丰言大为舒服，便也很慷慨他说：“交个朋友嘛！无所谓。”“是，是！俗语说得一点不错，‘在家靠父母，出外靠朋友’，朋友能交得上，一定要交。”龚振麟说：“事完以后，老兄这里，我另有谢意，至于胡雪翁那里，我当然也要致敬，想请教老兄，你看我该怎么办？”“如果你有所馈赠，他是一定不肯收的。”裘丰言说到这里，灵机一动，“我为老兄设想，有个惠而不费的办法。”

Hearing these terms, Gong's view changed. He knew Hu stood behind Qiu. He had thought Hu excessively ruthless; now he discovered a man who handled matters most handsomely. Friendship mattered, but weighing interests mattered more. Gong understood the strength of Hu's circle quite well. Wang Youling had earned a reputation as an able official and enjoyed considerable favour with the governor. Ji Heling, too, was a name that carried weight in Zhejiang official circles. Both relied on Hu as their principal adviser. Hu was adaptable and resourceful, and his greatest advantage was that everyone gladly worked for him. To miss an opportunity to befriend such a man would be a pity. Having made up his mind, Gong told Qiu, “To be frank, this affair has put me in a very difficult position. I needn't explain all the complications. You and Mr Hu are perceptive enough to understand them. In a word, I am deeply obliged for your consideration and concessions, and shall certainly repay them.” Qiu found this very gratifying. “We're making friends,” he replied generously. “There's no need to speak of repayment.” “Indeed, indeed! The proverb is perfectly true: ‘At home, rely on your parents; away from home, on your friends.’ Whenever one can make a friend, one should. When this is settled, I shall thank you separately. And naturally I must also pay my respects to Mr Hu. What would you advise?” “If you offer him a gift, he'll certainly refuse.” An idea occurred to Qiu. “I can suggest a kindness that will cost you nothing.”

“好极了！请指教。”“阜康钱庄，你总知道，是杭州钱庄大同行中，响当当的字号，老兄大可跟阜康做个往来，也算是捧捧他的场。”“这容易得紧，容易得紧！”龚振麟一叠连声的说，“此外，我想奉屈胡雪翁小叙，请老兄为我先谷。”“好，好！胡雪岩很爱朋友的，一定会叨扰。”“事情就这样说了。”龚振麟重又回到公事上，“哈德逊这方面的事，谨遵台命办理。上头有什么开销，我要上院请求了才能奉告。”说到这里，他又放低声音，作出自己人密诉肺腑的神态，“替黄抚台想想也不得了！一个年过下来，从京里到本省、将军、学政那里，处处打点，没有三十万银子过不了关。真正是‘只见和尚吃粥，不见和尚受戒’！”听这口风，便知加的帽子不会小。裘丰言也不多说，回到阜康钱庄跟胡雪岩细谈经过，话还未完，刘庆生笑嘻嘻地走了进来，显然是有什么得意的事要说。

“Excellent. Please tell me.” “You know Fukang Bank, of course—a name of real standing among Hangzhou's major banks. You could do business with Fukang and give him your support.” “Nothing could be easier!” Gong repeated eagerly. “I'd also like to invite Mr Hu for a visit. Would you kindly make the introduction?” “Certainly. Hu loves making friends. He'll be glad to accept.” “Then that's settled.” Gong returned to the official business. “We'll handle Hudson's side as you propose. As for any expenses above us, I must consult the governor before I can tell you.” He lowered his voice, assuming the air of a man confiding in an intimate. “Think what the governor faces! At New Year he must attend to everyone, from the capital down to our own province, the garrison general and the education commissioner among them. He can't get through it on less than three hundred thousand taels. People truly ‘see the monk eating his porridge, but never see him enduring his vows’!” From this, Qiu knew that the amount added on top would not be small. He said no more and returned to Fukang to give Hu a detailed account. Before he had finished, Liu Qingsheng came in smiling, evidently with something pleasing to report.

“胡先生，来了一笔意外的头寸，过年无论如何不愁了。”他说，“炮局龚老爷要立个折子，存八万银子！”这一下裘丰言也得意了。笑着问道：“如何？”“你慢高兴。”胡雪岩却有戒慎恐惧之感，对刘庆生说：“这笔头寸，不算意外，随时来提，随时要有，派不着用场。”“不！说了的，存三个月，利息随意。”“那倒也罢了！”胡雪岩想了想说，“利息自然从优。这样，你先打张收条给来人，就说：我马上去拜会龚老爷，存折我自己带去。”刘庆生答应着管自己去料理。胡雪岩这时才有喜色，踌躇满志地跟裘丰言表示，这件事得有此结束，是意外地圆满。因为原来他最顾虑的是“治一经，损一经”，怕因为这件事，把王有龄跟黄抚台的关系搞坏，而照现在看，关系不但未坏，反倒添上一层渊源，岂不可喜？

“Mr Hu, an unexpected sum has come our way. There's no need to worry about New Year now. Mr Gong of the Cannon Bureau wants to open an account and deposit eighty thousand taels!” Qiu, too, was delighted. “Well?” he asked with a smile. “Don't celebrate yet.” Hu felt caution rather than pleasure. He told Liu, “This money isn't unexpected. If he wants it back at any moment, we must have it ready. We can't put it to use.” “No! He's specified three months, with the interest left to us.” “Then that's another matter.” Hu considered. “Naturally, we'll give him favourable interest. Issue a receipt to the person who brought it and say that I'll call on Mr Gong at once, bringing the passbook myself.” Liu agreed and went to see to it. Only now did Hu's pleasure show. With evident satisfaction, he told Qiu that the outcome was unexpectedly complete. His greatest fear had been that mending one thing would damage another: this affair might spoil Wang Youling's relationship with Governor Huang. Now, instead of damaging that relationship, they had added another bond. How could he not be pleased?

“不过，也不能大兴头。”胡雪岩又说，“现在连‘买空卖空，都谈不到，只能说是’卖空‘，大包大揽答应了下来，哈德逊那里还不知道怎么说呢！”“不要紧！你不是说哈德逊答应二十两一支？现在有个二两头的富余在那里，大不了我白当一次差，二十二两一支，总敲得下来。”裘丰言这番表白，很够昧道，胡雪岩笑笑拍一拍他的肩。然后，带着存折到炮局去拜访龚振麟。一见面当然各道仰慕，十分投机，入座待茶，胡雪岩首先交代了存折，申明谢意，接着便谈王有龄的近况，套到这层关系上，更觉亲热，真正是“一见如故”了。“这次裘丰翁上的说帖，多蒙雪岩兄斡旋，体谅苦衷，承情之至。”龚振麟说道：“我已经面禀抚台，抚台亦很欣慰，特地嘱我致意。”如何致意没有说，意思是黄宗汉也很见情。胡雪岩矜持地笑了笑，没有多说什么。

“Still, we mustn't get carried away,” Hu added. “We can't even call this speculative buying and selling. We've only been selling what we haven't got! We've undertaken everything, and still don't know what Hudson will say.” “Never mind. Didn't you say Hudson had agreed to twenty taels a gun? We now have two taels' leeway. At worst, I'll do the job for nothing. Surely we can settle at twenty-two.” It was a generous declaration. Hu smiled and patted his shoulder, then took the passbook to the Cannon Bureau to call on Gong. Naturally, they began with mutual expressions of admiration and found themselves in perfect accord. After they sat down and tea was served, Hu first handed over the passbook and expressed his thanks. He then spoke of Wang Youling's recent circumstances. Once this connection had been established, they felt closer still, truly like old friends at their first meeting. “Over Mr Qiu's memorandum, you've shown such understanding of our difficulties and done so much to help resolve them,” Gong said. “I'm deeply obliged. I've reported to the governor in person. He, too, was very gratified and specifically asked me to convey his regards.” Gong did not say precisely what those regards were, but he meant that Huang appreciated the favour as well. Hu smiled with reserve and said little.

“我虽承乏炮局，对洋务上所知并不多，以后还要请雪岩兄多指教！”“不敢当。”胡雪岩急转直下地问道，“我想请教，跟普鲁士人订的那张合同，不知定在什么地方交货？”“定在杭州。”龚振麟答道，“他答应包运的。”“振麟兄！由上海过来，路上的情形，你估量过情形没有？”“也晓得不大平靖，所以我已经面禀抚台，将来要派兵到边境上去接。”“能入浙江境界，就不要紧了。”“喔！”龚振麟很注意地问，“你是说江苏那段水路不平靖？”“是的。小刀会看了这批枪，一定会眼红。”胡雪岩说，“不是我危言耸听，洋人包运靠不住。”龚振麟吸着气，显然有所疑惧，望着胡雪岩，半晌说不出话。“振麟兄，”胡雪岩很率直他说，“万一出事，洋人可以推托；或者禀请官厅缉捕。那场官司怎么打？”“啊！”龚振麟满头大汗，站起身来，深深一揖：“多蒙指点，险险乎犯下大错。合同非修改不可，不能叫洋人包运，他也包不了。”

“Though I hold this post at the Cannon Bureau, my knowledge of foreign affairs is limited. I shall need much guidance from you.” “You flatter me.” Hu abruptly turned to the point. “May I ask where delivery is specified in your contract with the Prussian?” “Hangzhou. He's undertaken to arrange the transport.” “Brother Zhenlin, have you considered conditions along the route from Shanghai?” “I know it isn't very peaceful, so I've already asked the governor to send troops to meet the shipment at the border.” “Once it reaches Zhejiang, there'll be nothing to worry about.” “Oh!” Gong's attention sharpened. “You mean the waterway through Jiangsu is unsafe?” “Yes. The Small Sword Society will certainly covet that shipment. I'm not trying to alarm you, but the foreigner's undertaking to transport it cannot be relied upon.” Gong drew in his breath, plainly troubled by doubts. He stared at Hu for some time without speaking. “Brother Zhenlin,” Hu said frankly, “if anything happens, the foreigner can disclaim responsibility, or ask the authorities to pursue the robbers. How would you fight that case?” “Ah!” Sweat covered Gong's forehead. Rising, he bowed deeply. “Thank you for pointing this out. I nearly made a grave mistake. The contract must be amended. We cannot leave transport to the foreigner. He cannot guarantee it.”

“是的！振麟兄明白了。”“明白是明白了，怎么个办法，还要雪岩兄指点。”龚振麟又说：“这件事恐怕还要请教裘丰翁，他押运过一趟，路上的情形比较熟悉。”“不须请教他。此事我可以效劳。”“那太好了！”龚振麟又是一揖。胡雪岩赶紧还了礼。到此地步，自不需再作迂回，他直截了当地把跟尤五的交情说了出来，表示如果龚振麟有用得着的地方，可以帮忙。“自然要仰仗！”龚振麟喜不可言，感激之情，溢于言表，“多亏得雪岩兄，不然真是不了之事了！”接着，龚振麟要人。官场中讲交情关系，谈到这一点，就是最切实的表示，无奈胡雪岩自己也是人手不足，便只有谨谢不敏了。不过，他还是替龚振麟出了一个主意，两方面的枪支不妨合在一起运，仍旧请黄抚台下委札，派裘丰言当“押运委员”，跟尤五的联络，自然也归裘丰言负责，驾轻就熟，可保无虑。这个办法既省时，又省运费，龚振麟自然依从。两人越谈越投机，直到深夜方散。第二天龚振麟又到胡家回拜，硬要把胡老太大请出堂前，为她磕头，到了下午又是龚太太携礼来见。两家很快地成了通家之好。

“Exactly. You understand now.” “I understand, but I'll still need your guidance on what to do. We may also have to consult Mr Qiu. He's escorted a shipment and knows the route better.” “There's no need to ask him. I can be of service.” “Excellent!” Gong bowed again. Hu hastily returned the courtesy. At this point, there was no need for further circumlocution. He explained his friendship with You Laowu directly and offered help if Gong could use it. “I certainly must rely on you!” Gong's joy and gratitude were unmistakable. “Without you, this could have become an endless disaster.” He next asked Hu to provide someone to work for him. In official circles, a request of this kind was the most concrete expression of a relationship. Unfortunately, Hu was short of men himself and had to decline with thanks. He did, however, offer another suggestion. The guns supplied by both merchants could travel together. Governor Huang could issue a commission appointing Qiu as escort commissioner again, with responsibility for liaising with You as well. Qiu would be doing familiar work, and they could rest easy. This arrangement would save both time and freight charges, so Gong naturally agreed. They found more and more common ground and talked until late into the night. The following day, Gong returned the visit at Hu's home and insisted that Old Mrs Hu be invited into the main hall so he could kowtow to her. That afternoon, Mrs Gong arrived with gifts. The two families quickly became close enough to visit one another's private households.

不过胡雪岩对龚振麟是“另眼相看”的，这“另眼”不是青眼，他察言观色，看出龚振麟这个人的性情，利害重于感情，如俗语所说的“有事有人，无事无人”，所以不能与王有龄、尤五、郁四、嵇鹤龄等量齐观。也因此，他嘱咐妻子，与龚家交往要特别当心，礼数不可缺，而有出入关系的话，不可多说，免得生出是非。果然，从龚家惹来一场是非！年三十晚上，祭过祖吃“团圆夜饭”。胡老太太穿着新制的大毛皮袄，高高上坐，看着儿媳，又欢喜、又感慨他说：“我也想不到有今天！虽说祖宗积德，也靠‘家和万事兴’，雪岩，你总要记着一句老古话：”糟糠之妻不可忘‘，良心摆在当中。“大年三十怎么说到这话，胡雪岩心里觉得不是味道，但只好答应一声：“我晓得！”

Hu did, however, see Gong in a different light, and not a favourable one. From his words and manner, Hu judged that self-interest mattered more to him than affection. As the saying went, he knew a man when he needed him and forgot him when he did not. Gong could not be placed alongside Wang Youling, You Laowu, Yu Si or Ji Heling. Hu therefore warned his wife to take particular care in dealing with the Gongs. No courtesy should be omitted, but anything with consequences for their affairs should be left unsaid, lest it cause trouble. And trouble did indeed come through the Gong household. On New Year's Eve, after the ancestral rites, the family sat down to their reunion dinner. Wearing a newly made coat of thick fur, Old Mrs Hu occupied the place of honour. As she looked at her daughter-in-law, she spoke with mingled happiness and emotion. “I never imagined we'd see a day like this! We owe it to our ancestors' virtue, but also to the truth that harmony in a family makes everything prosper. Xueyan, you must always remember the old saying: ‘Never forget the wife who shared your poverty.’ Keep your conscience in its proper place.” Hu found it unpleasant to hear this on New Year's Eve, but could only answer, “I know.”

胡太太不响，照料一家老小吃完，才问她丈夫：“你要不要出去？”“不出去！”胡雪岩说，“今天晚上自然在家守岁。”听得这话，胡太太使备了几个精致的碟子，供胡雪岩消夜。夫妇俩围炉小饮，看看房中无人，做妻子的说出一句话来，让胡雪岩大为惊疑。“娘说的话，你总听见了。雪岩，你良心要摆在当中！”“奇怪了！”胡雪岩说，“我哪里做了对不起你的事？”“好！这话是你自己说的。”胡大大说，“一过了年，湖州那个人，叫她走！”这句话说得胡雪岩心中一跳，镇静着装傻：“你说的是哪个？”“哼！你还要‘装羊’？可见得要把我骗到底。”胡太太说：“要不要我说出名字来？”“你说嘛！”“芙蓉！”

His wife said nothing. She attended to everyone, old and young, until they had finished eating, then asked her husband, “Are you going out?” “No. Naturally, I'll stay at home to see the New Year in.” At this, Mrs Hu had a few delicate dishes prepared for his late supper. Husband and wife sat drinking quietly beside the brazier. When she saw that no one else was in the room, she said something that startled and alarmed him. “You heard what Mother said. Xueyan, you must keep your conscience in its proper place.” “This is extraordinary. What have I done to wrong you?” “Very well. Those are your own words. Once New Year is over, dismiss that woman in Huzhou.” Hu's heart gave a jump. He steadied himself and played the fool. “Which woman do you mean?” “Hmph! Still pretending innocence? So you intend to deceive me to the end. Must I say her name?” “Go on, then.” “Furong!”

“噢……”胡雪岩装得久已忘却其事，直到她提起，方始想到的神情，“逢场作戏，总也有的。过去的事了，提她作啥？我问你，你这话听谁说的？”“自然有人！”胡太太追紧了问，“你说啥逢场作戏，过去的事？是不是说这个人不在湖州了？”“在不在湖州，我怎么晓得？”胡雪岩一面这样说，一面在心里一个个的数，数她妻子平日往来的亲友，谁会知道芙蓉其人？想来想去只有一个人知道，王有龄的太太。但是，王太太能干而稳重，说什么也不会多嘴去告诉胡太太，除非……胡雪岩蓦然醒悟，王龚两家同乡，内眷常有往来，一定是王太太在闲谈中泄漏了秘密，而胡太太是从龚太太那里听来。由于做丈夫的坚决不认，做妻子的也只得暂且抛开。但夫妇俩就此有了心病，这个年也过得不如想象中那么痛快。

“Oh...” Hu assumed the air of a man reminded of something long forgotten. “One has the occasional passing amusement. It's all in the past. Why bring her up? Tell me, who said this to you?” “Someone did, naturally!” His wife pressed him. “What do you mean, a passing amusement, all in the past? Are you saying she's no longer in Huzhou?” “How should I know whether she's in Huzhou?” Even as he spoke, Hu ran through his wife's usual relatives and friends one by one. Who among them could know of Furong? After considering them all, he could think of only one: Wang Youling's wife. Yet Mrs Wang was capable and discreet. Nothing would induce her to tell Mrs Hu out of mere gossip, unless... Suddenly he saw it. The Wangs and the Gongs came from the same home district, and their womenfolk often visited one another. Mrs Wang must have let the secret slip in casual conversation, and Mrs Hu had heard it from Mrs Gong. With her husband resolute in his denials, his wife could only let the subject drop for the time being. But an uneasiness now lay between them, and the New Year was less happy than they had imagined.

第二十一章｜CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE

年初四夜里“接财神”。胡雪岩因为这一年顺利非凡，真象遇见了财神菩萨似地，所以这天夜里“烧财神纸”，他的心情异常虔诚，照规矩，凡是敬神的仪节，妇女都得回避，胡雪岩一个人孤零零地上香磕头，既鲜兄弟，又无儿子，忽然感从中来，觉得身后茫茫，就算财神菩萨垂青，发上几千万两银子的大财，有何用处。等把财神“接”回来，全家在后厅“散福饮胙”，胡老太太倒很高兴，胡雪岩却神情忧郁，勉强吃了两杯酒、半碗鸡汤面，放下筷子就回卧房去了。“怎么了？”胡老太太很不安地低声问儿媳妇：“接财神的日子，而且吃夜饭辰光，还是有说有笑的，忽然变成这副样子，是不是你又跟他说了啥？”“没有！我什么话也没有说。”胡太太说，“新年新岁，一家要图个吉利，我不会跟他淘闲气的。”他婆婆的连连点头，显得十分欣慰，“我晓得你贤惠，雪岩有今天，也全亏你。”她抚慰着说，“不过，他外面事情多，应酬也是免不了的。你的气量要放宽来！”前面的话都好，最后一句说坏了，胡太太对婆婆大起反感，想答一句：“我的气量已经够大了！”但话到口边，到底又咽了下去。

On the night of the fourth day of the New Year, the household welcomed the God of Wealth. Hu Xueyan’s extraordinary success during the past year had made him feel as though he had indeed encountered the god, and he burned the ritual paper offerings with unusual devotion. According to custom, women withdrew from ceremonies honouring the gods. As he stood alone offering incense and kowtowing, with neither brothers nor a son beside him, he was suddenly overcome by sadness. What lay beyond him seemed utterly empty. Even if the God of Wealth favoured him with a fortune of tens of millions of taels, what use would it be? When the god had been welcomed, the family gathered in the rear hall to share the blessed offerings. Old Mrs Hu was delighted, but her son looked melancholy. Forcing down two cups of wine and half a bowl of noodles in chicken broth, he put down his chopsticks and returned to his bedroom. “What is wrong?” his mother asked her daughter-in-law anxiously in a low voice. “On the very day we welcome the God of Wealth! He was still laughing and talking at dinner. Why the sudden change? Have you said something to him again?” “No. I haven’t said a word,” Mrs Hu replied. “At the beginning of a new year, we all want good fortune for the household. I wouldn’t pick a quarrel with him.” Her mother-in-law nodded repeatedly, much comforted. “I know how good you are. He owes his success to you too. But he has so much business outside, and entertaining is unavoidable. You must be more broad-minded.” All had been well until that last remark. It provoked a sharp resentment in Mrs Hu. She wanted to say that she was broad-minded enough already, but swallowed the words.

回到卧房，只见胡雪岩一个人在灯下想心事，胡太太想起婆婆的话，忘掉了那令人不怡的一句，只记着“他外面事多”这句话，心便软了，也亏他一个赤手空拳，打出这片天下，在家里，凡事总要让他。于是她问：“你好象没有吃饭，有红枣莲子粥在那里，要不要吃点甜的？”胡雪岩摇摇头，两眼依旧望着那盏水晶玻璃的“洋灯”。“那么，睡吧！”“你不要管我！”胡雪岩不耐烦他说，“你睡你的。”一片热心换他的冷气，胡太太心里很不舒服，“他在想啥？”她暗中自问自答：“自然是想湖州的那个狐狸精！”这一下，只觉得酸味直冲脑门，忍了又忍，噙着眼泪管自己铺床，而胡雪岩却发了话。“喂！”他说：“我看你要找个妇产医生去看看！”听这一说，朝太太大为诧异，“为啥？”她问，不敢转过脸去，怕丈夫发现她的泪痕。“为啥？”胡雪岩说，“ ‘屁股后头光塌塌’，你倒不着急？”这是指她未生儿子。胡太太又气又恼，倏地转过身来瞪着她丈夫。

Back in the bedroom she found Hu sitting alone under the lamp, lost in thought. Remembering his mother’s words, she forgot the offending sentence and thought only of his many affairs outside. Her heart softened. He had built all this from nothing, with his own hands. At home she ought to give way to him. “You hardly ate,” she said. “There is rice porridge with red dates and lotus seeds. Would you like something sweet?” Hu shook his head, his eyes still fixed on the clear glass of the foreign lamp. “Then come to bed.” “Leave me alone,” he answered impatiently. “Go to bed yourself.” His cold response to her kindness hurt her. What was he thinking of? Naturally, that fox-spirit in Huzhou! Jealousy rushed straight to her head. Controlling herself with difficulty, she made the bed with tears in her eyes. Then Hu spoke. “Listen. I think you ought to consult a physician about childbearing.” She was astonished. “Why?” She dared not turn round, lest he see the traces of tears. “Why? There is nothing behind us but emptiness. Doesn’t that worry you?” He meant that she had borne him no son. Angry and distressed, she turned abruptly and stared at him.

“没有儿子是犯‘七出之条’的。”胡太太瞪了一会，爆出这么句话来。这句话很重，胡雪岩也愣了，“怎么说得上这话？”他实在有些困惑，原也知道妻子胸有丘壑，不是等闲的女流，却想不到说出话来比刀口还锋利。“我怎么不要说？”胡太太微微冷笑着：“生儿育女是两个人的事，莫非天底下有那等人，只会生女儿，不会生儿子？你既然要这样说，自然是我退让，你好去另请高明。”为来为去为的是芙蓉，胡雪岩听出因头，不由得笑了，“你也蛮高明的。”他说：“ ‘先开花，后结果’，我的意思是不妨请教请教妇科医生，配一服‘种子调经丸’试试看。”胡太太实在厉害，不肯无理取闹，态度也变得平静了，但话很扎实，掌握机会，谈到要紧关头上：“试得不灵呢？”她问。胡雪岩已具戒心，不敢逞强，“不灵只好不灵，”他带点委屈的声音，“命中注定无子，还说点啥？”有道是“柔能克刚”，他这两句仿佛自怨自艾的话，倒把胡太太的嘴堵住了。这一夜夫妇同床异梦，胡太太通前彻后想了一遍，打定了一个主意。

“Bearing no son is one of the seven grounds for putting away a wife.” After staring a moment, she burst out with this. It was a heavy accusation, and Hu too was taken aback. “How can you say such a thing?” He was genuinely bewildered. He knew his wife had a mind of her own and was no ordinary woman, but had not expected words sharper than a knife. “Why shouldn’t I?” she asked with a faint, cold smile. “Having children concerns two people. Is there anyone in the world who can bear only daughters and never sons? Since that is what you say, naturally I must give way, and you can seek someone more capable.” It all came back to Furong. Recognising the cause, Hu could not help smiling. “You are capable enough yourself. First the blossom, then the fruit. I only meant that we might consult a physician who treats women and try a course of Fertility and Menstrual-Regulating Pills.” His wife was formidable indeed. She would not quarrel without reason, and now grew calm, but her words remained firm. Seizing the opportunity, she came to the crucial point. “And if they don’t work?” Hu was on his guard and dared not press his advantage. “Then they don’t work,” he said, sounding a little aggrieved. “If fate has decreed that I shall have no son, what is there to say?” Softness overcomes strength: those two apparently self-pitying remarks left her with no answer. That night they shared a bed but followed different thoughts. Mrs Hu considered the whole matter from beginning to end and made up her mind.

于是第二天胡老太太问儿子：“你打算哪一天到上海去？”“到上灯就走。”“今天初五，上灯还有八天。”胡老太太说，“也还来得及。”“娘！”胡雪岩诧异的问道：“什么来得及来不及？”胡老太太告诉他，胡太太要回娘家，得要算一算日子，趁胡雪岩未走之前，赶回家来。胡太太娘家在杭州附近的一个水乡塘栖，往返跋涉，也辛苦得很，如果日子局促，一去就要回来，便犯不着吃这一趟辛苦了。“那倒奇怪了，她怎么不先跟我谈？”“我也问她，说你晓得不晓得？她说先要我答应了，再告诉你。”话是说得礼与理都占到了，而其实不是那么一回事，每一次归宁都是夫妇俩先商量好了，方始禀告堂上的，何以这一次例外？同时一接了财神，商场上便得请吃春酒，胡雪岩要趁这几天大请其客，不能没有人照料，此刻怎抽得出工夫回娘家？他把这一层意思一说，胡老太太答道：“ 我也提到了。她说你请客是在店里，用不着她，她也帮不上忙。请几家亲眷吃春酒，日子也定了，就是明天。”“岂有此理！”胡雪岩不悦，“怎么不先告诉我？”

The next morning his mother asked, “When do you intend to leave for Shanghai?” “When the lanterns go up.” “Today is the fifth. There are eight days before then. There is still time.” “Mother!” Hu asked in surprise. “Time for what?” She explained that his wife wanted to visit her own family. They must count the days so that she could return before he left. Her family lived in Tangqi, a water town near Hangzhou. The journey there and back was tiring. If time was so short that she had to turn round almost as soon as she arrived, it would hardly be worth the trouble. “How strange! Why didn’t she discuss it with me first?” “I asked whether you knew. She said she must have my consent before telling you.” That explanation satisfied both courtesy and reason, but it was not how things usually happened. On every previous visit, husband and wife had agreed first and then informed their elders. Why was this time different? Besides, once the God of Wealth had been welcomed, merchants began giving their New Year dinners. Hu intended to entertain extensively over the next few days and needed someone to manage matters. How could she leave just now? When he explained this, his mother answered, “I mentioned that too. She said you would entertain at the shop and wouldn’t need her; she could be of no help there. As for the family dinner, the date has already been fixed. It is tomorrow.” “This is absurd!” Hu was annoyed. “Why wasn’t I told first?”

胡老太太因为已经知道芙蓉的事，觉得儿媳妇受了委屈，不免袒护，所以这时候便“揽是非”，说是她的主意，与胡太太无关。看这样子，胡雪岩认为以少开口为妙，冷笑一声答道：“随便她！反正在家里是她大！”这句话的言外之意，做娘的自然听得出来，“这个家也亏得她撑恃，”她警告儿子：“你不要以为你在外头，就没有人管你，高兴怎么样就怎么样！如果你真的存了这个念头，将来苦头有得你吃！“知子莫若母，一句话说到胡雪岩心里，他也颇生警惕，不过事情多想一想也不能无怨，“娘！”他说，“ ‘不孝有三，无后为大’，难道你老人家就不想抱孙子？”“我怎么不想？”胡老太太平静他说，“这件事我们婆媳已经商量过了。媳妇不是不明事理的人，我做婆婆的，自然要依从她的打算。““她是怎么样打算？”“你先不要问。”胡老太太笑道，“总于你有好处就是了。”胡雪岩猜不透她们婆媳葫芦里卖的是什么药，也就只好暂且丢开。

His mother already knew about Furong and felt her daughter-in-law had been wronged, so she was inclined to protect her. Taking the blame, she said the arrangement was her own idea and had nothing to do with Mrs Hu. Seeing how matters stood, Hu thought it best to say little. He gave a cold laugh. “Let her please herself. At home she is the one in command, anyway.” His mother naturally understood the implication. “This household depends on her,” she warned him. “Don’t imagine that because you are outside, nobody can control you and you can do whatever you please. If that is what you think, there is trouble in store for you.” Nobody knows a son like his mother. Her words went straight to his thoughts and made him wary. Yet on reflection he could not entirely suppress his grievance. “Mother, of the three failures in filial duty, leaving no heir is the greatest. Don’t you want a grandson?” “Of course I do,” she answered calmly. “Your wife and I have discussed it. She is a reasonable woman. As her mother-in-law, naturally I should follow her plan.” “What is her plan?” “Don’t ask yet.” His mother smiled. “It will be to your benefit.” Unable to guess what the two women were plotting, Hu could only leave the matter for the time being.

第二天在家请过了春酒。胡太太便带着八岁的小女儿，雇了一只专船回塘栖，这一去只去了五天，正月十一回杭州。他们夫妇感情本来不坏，虽然略有龃龋，经此小别，似乎各已忘怀，仍旧高高兴兴地有说有笑。胡雪岩打算正月十四动身，所以胡太太一到家，使得替丈夫打点行李，他个人的行李不多，多的是带到松江、上海去送人的土产，“四杭”以外，吃的、用的，样数很不少，一份一份料理，着实累人。土产都是凭折子大批取了来的，送礼以外，当然也留坐自用，胡雪岩打开一包桂花猪油麻酥糖，吃了一块不想再吃，便喊者他的小女儿说：“荷珠，你来吃了它。”拿起酥糖咬了一口，荷珠直摇头：“我不要吃！”“咦！你不是顶喜欢吃酥糖？”“不好吃！”荷珠说，“没有湖州的好吃。”“你在哪里吃的湖州酥糖？”这句话其实问得多余，自然是在外婆家吃的，但“一滴水恰好溶入油瓶里”，略懂人事的荷珠，忽然有所顾忌，竟答不上来，涨红了脸望着他父亲，仿佛做错了什么事伯受责似地。

The next day they gave the family New Year dinner. Then Mrs Hu took her younger daughter, aged eight, and hired a boat for the journey to Tangqi. She was away only five days, returning to Hangzhou on the eleventh of the first month. The couple’s relationship had always been fairly good. After this short separation, their slight disagreement seemed forgotten, and they laughed and talked happily as before. Hu intended to leave on the fourteenth, so as soon as his wife returned she had to pack for him. He needed little personal luggage. The bulk consisted of local products to be given away in Songjiang and Shanghai. Besides Hangzhou’s “four specialities,” there were many kinds of food and useful articles. Sorting each gift separately was tiring work. These local goods had been obtained in bulk on account. Naturally, some were kept for the household. Hu opened a packet of crumbly sesame sweets made with lard and scented with osmanthus. After one piece he wanted no more. “Hezhu,” he called to his younger daughter, “come and finish these.” She picked one up, took a bite and shook her head. “I don’t want it.” “Why? Aren’t these your favourite sweets?” “They don’t taste nice. The ones from Huzhou are better.” “Where did you have sweets from Huzhou?” The question was really unnecessary: obviously, at her grandmother’s house. Yet it was like a drop of water falling into an oil bottle. Hezhu was old enough to understand a little of grown-up affairs. Suddenly she grew cautious, could not answer, and looked at her father with a flushed face, as though expecting punishment for some wrongdoing.

这一来胡雪岩疑云大起，看妻子不在旁边，便拉着荷珠的手，走到窗前，悄悄问道：“你告诉爸爸，哪里来的湖州酥糖？我上海回来，买个洋囡囡给你。”荷珠不知怎么回答？想了半天说：“我不晓得！”做父亲的听这回答，不免生气，但也不愿吓得她哭，只说：“好！你不肯告诉我，随便你！等我上海回来，姐姐有新衣裳，洋囡囡，你呢，什么没有！”威胁利诱之下，荷珠到底说了实话：“娘带回来的。”“娘到湖州去过了？”“嗯。”荷珠委屈他说，“我也要去，娘不许！”“噢！去了几天？”“一天去，一天回来。”“那么是两天。”胡雪岩想了想又问，“你娘回来以后，跟外婆说了些什么？”“我不晓得。我走过去要听。娘叫我走开。娘又说，不准我说，娘到湖州去过。”荷珠说到这里，才感觉事态严重，“爸爸，爸爸，你千万不要跟娘去说，说我告诉你，娘到湖州去过。”“不会，不会！”胡雪岩把她搂在怀里，“我买洋囡囡给你。”

Hu’s suspicions rose at once. Seeing that his wife was not nearby, he took Hezhu to the window and asked quietly, “Tell Papa where those Huzhou sweets came from. When I return from Shanghai, I’ll bring you a foreign doll.” She did not know what to say. After thinking for a long while, she answered, “I don’t know.” This annoyed him, though he did not want to frighten her into tears. “Very well. If you won’t tell me, please yourself. When I return from Shanghai, your sister will have new clothes and a foreign doll. You will have nothing.” Between the threat and the reward, Hezhu finally told the truth. “Mother brought them back.” “Mother went to Huzhou?” “Mm.” She sounded aggrieved. “I wanted to go too, but she wouldn’t let me.” “Oh! How many days was she away?” “One day to go, one day to come back.” “Two days, then.” Hu thought a moment. “When she came back, what did she say to Grandmother?” “I don’t know. I went over to listen, and she sent me away. She also said I mustn’t tell anyone she had been to Huzhou.” Only now did Hezhu realise how serious this was. “Papa, Papa, you mustn’t tell Mother that I told you she went to Huzhou.” “I won’t, I won’t.” He gathered her into his arms. “I’ll buy you the foreign doll.”

安抚了荷珠，胡雪岩大上心事。他妻子的湖州之行，不用说，自然是为了芙蓉，但她干了些什么，却难以揣恻，是去打听了一番，还是另有什么作为？照他的了解，她做事极有分寸，决不是蛮横无理的悍泼之妇可比。意识到这一点，他越觉得自己不可鲁莽，必须谋定后动，或者说，兵来将挡，水来土掩，看她是用的什么办法，再来设计破她。只要知道了她的用意和行动，一定有办法应付，这一点胡雪岩是有信心的。不过他也有警惕，自己所遭遇的“对手”太强，不可造次，同时估量形势，在家里他非常不利，上有老母，下有一双女儿，都站在他妻子这面，自己以一敌四，孤掌难鸣。所以眼前的当务之急，是要争取优势，而这个工作只能在暗地里做，让妻子知道了，只要稍加安抚，“地盘”就会非常稳固。于是他首先还是找到荷珠，告诫她不可将他所问的话，告诉她母亲。然后又找他的大女儿，十五岁的梅王。梅玉很懂人事了，虽是她母亲的“死党”，却很崇拜父亲，因而胡雪岩跟她说话，另有一套计算，一开口就说：“梅王，你跟爸爸一起到上海去，好不好？”这话让梅玉又惊又喜。能出去开一开眼界，又听说十里夷场有数不尽的新奇花样，自然向往万分，但离开母亲，又仿佛觉调不能令人安心，所以只骨碌碌地转着一对黑眼珠，半晌答不出话来。

Having reassured Hezhu, Hu was deeply troubled. Naturally his wife’s journey to Huzhou concerned Furong, but what she had done was hard to guess. Had she merely made inquiries, or taken some other action? He knew she had an excellent sense of measure and was nothing like a violent, unreasonable shrew. That made it all the more necessary for him to avoid rashness. He must plan before acting—or, as the saying went, meet soldiers with generals and floodwater with earth: discover her move and devise the proper answer. Once he knew her purpose and actions, he was confident he could deal with them. But this was a powerful opponent, and he must be careful. At home the odds were against him. His mother above and his two daughters below all stood on his wife’s side. One against four, he could hardly prevail. His immediate task was therefore to gain an advantage, and he could do it only in secret. If his wife learned of it, a little reassurance from her would make her position unshakable. First he sought Hezhu out again and warned her not to tell her mother what he had asked. Then he approached his elder daughter, fifteen-year-old Meiyu. She understood a good deal of the world. Though firmly her mother’s ally, she admired her father, so he adopted a different approach. “Meiyu, would you like to come to Shanghai with Papa?” The proposal surprised and delighted her. She longed to see something of the world, especially the foreign settlement with its countless novelties. Yet leaving her mother seemed unsettling. Her dark eyes moved to and fro, and for a while she could not answer.

“你的意思怎么样？不愿意？”“哪个说不愿意？”梅玉说，“我有点怕。”“怕？那完了！”胡雪岩说，“爸爸还想靠你，你先怕了！”“靠我！”梅玉大惑不解，怎么样也不能接受这话，“爸爸，你靠我什么？”“靠你替我写写、算算。”胡雪岩郑重其事他说，“我在外面的生意做得很大，总要有个帮手，这个帮手一定要自己人，因为有些帐目，是不能让别人知道的。哪怕刘庆生刘叔叔、陈世尤陈叔叔，都不能让他们知道。想来想去，只有靠你帮忙。”这一套鬼话，改变了梅王的心情，原来一直当目己是个文弱的女孩子，在外面百无一用，只有帮着操持家务，现在才知道自己还肯派得上紧要用场的地方，顿觉自己变了一个“大人”，而且也不再想到母亲，自觉胆子甚大，出去闯一闯也无所谓。但是，这只是一鼓作气，多想一想不免气馁，“爸爸，”她说，“我怕我算不来帐。”“那么，你帮你娘记家用帐，是怎么记的呢？”“家用帐是家用帐。爸爸的帐是上千上万的进出。”“帐目不管大小，算法是一样的，家用帐琐琐碎碎，我的帐只有几样东西，还比家用帐好记。”梅平接受了鼓励，“雄心”又起，毅然决然的说：“那我就跟了爸爸去，不过我要把阿彩带了去。”阿彩是专门照料她的一个丫头，胡雪岩当然答应。事情就这样说定局了。

“What do you think? Don’t you want to go?” “Who says I don’t?” Meiyu replied. “I’m a little afraid.” “Afraid? Then that settles it! I was hoping to rely on you, and you are afraid already.” “Rely on me?” She was utterly bewildered. “Papa, what could you rely on me for?” “To write things down and do calculations for me.” Hu sounded thoroughly serious. “My business outside has grown very large. I need someone to help, and it must be one of our own family. There are accounts nobody else can know about—not even Uncle Liu Qingsheng or Uncle Chen Shilong. I have thought it over, and you are the only person I can rely on.” This fabrication changed her feelings completely. Until now she had regarded herself as a frail girl, useless outside the home and fit only to help with household affairs. Suddenly she discovered that she could perform an important service. She felt grown-up at once. She stopped thinking of her mother, became bold, and saw no harm in venturing out into the world. But the first burst of courage faded under further reflection. “Papa, I’m afraid I won’t know how to keep the accounts.” “How do you keep the household accounts for your mother, then?” “Those are household accounts. Your money comes and goes in thousands and tens of thousands.” “Large or small, the method is the same. Household accounts are full of little items. Mine concern only a few things. They are easier to keep.” Encouraged, Meiyu’s ambition rose again. “Then I’ll go with you,” she declared. “But I must take A’cai.” A’cai was the maid who looked after her. Naturally Hu agreed, and the matter was settled.

这一来，全家大小都知道了这回事，而胡太太只当丈夫说笑话。“你要把梅玉带到上海去啊？”她问她丈夫。“对！”胡雪岩说，“女儿大了，带她出去阅历阅历。”“阅历！”胡太太诧异之至，“听说夷场上的风气不好，有啥好阅历？学了些坏样子回来，你害了她！“胡雪岩笑笑不作声。这有何可笑？女孩子学坏学好，有关终身，不是好笑的事，那自然是笑自己的话没见识！胡太太倒有些不服气了。“我的话说锗了？”她平静而固执地，“而且听说路上不平靖，梅玉不要去！”“路上不平靖，那么我呢？你倒放心得下？”“你跟梅玉不同。”胡太太说，“又有尤五爷照应，我自然放心。”“那就对了，梅王跟我在一起，你还有啥不放心？”夫妇俩的交谈，针锋相对，而且是“绵里针”，劲道暗藏着，但毕竟还是胡雪岩占了上风，胡太太争不过他，还有一着棋，拿老太太搬了出来。

Soon everyone in the household knew, though Mrs Hu supposed her husband was joking. “Are you taking Meiyu to Shanghai?” she asked. “Yes. She is growing up. I want her to gain some experience.” “Experience!” His wife was astonished. “They say the foreign settlement has bad ways. What experience is there to gain? If she comes home with bad habits, you will have ruined her.” Hu only smiled. What was amusing? A girl’s conduct affected her whole future. It was no laughing matter. He must be laughing at her ignorance! Mrs Hu resented it. “Am I wrong?” she asked, calmly but stubbornly. “Besides, they say the roads are unsafe. Meiyu is not to go.” “If the roads are unsafe, what about me? Aren’t you worried?” “You and Meiyu are different. With Master You looking after you, naturally I feel easy.” “Exactly. If she is with me, what is there to worry about?” Their words met point against point, needles hidden in silk, with all their force concealed. Yet Hu had gained the upper hand. Unable to defeat him in argument, his wife made one last move: she brought his mother into it.

对母亲说话，自然不能那样子一句钉一句，胡雪岩依旧是对梅玉的那套说法，说要有个亲信的人替他管帐，不过一套假话，比对梅玉说的还要详细，他说有些交际应酬的帐目，没有凭证，如果不是当时记下来，事后就搞不清楚。而这些帐目，无论如何是不能让外人知道的，所以要把梅王带去帮忙。说到这里，他叹口气：“如果有男孩子，何必要带梅玉出去？哪怕有个亲侄儿也好了！苦的就是没有。“这是胡雪岩灵机一动的攻心之计。胡老太太果然在想，梅玉如果是个男孩，十五岁便可以跟他父亲出去“学生意”，有五六年下来，足可以成为你父亲的一个得力帮手，生意做得发达了，不患后继无人。如今就算马上有了孩子，要到十几年以后，才能成人，缓不济急，对胡家来说，是吃了亏了，不免有些怨儿媳妇，耽误了这十几年的大好时光。这一下胡太太又落了下风，胡雪岩则甚为得意，但再想进一步打听他妻子到了湖州的情形，却是失望，听梅玉的口气，她母亲根本没有跟她说过。

With his mother he could not answer every objection so sharply. He returned to the story he had told Meiyu: he needed someone he could trust to keep accounts. This time the fabrication was more detailed. Some expenses for entertaining and social dealings had no receipts. Unless they were recorded at once, they became impossible to disentangle later. Nobody outside the family could be allowed to know these accounts, so he needed Meiyu’s help. Then he sighed. “If I had a boy, why should I have to take Meiyu? Even a nephew of my own would do. The trouble is that I have neither.” This was an inspired appeal to his mother’s feelings. She immediately began to think that, had Meiyu been a boy, at fifteen he could have gone out with his father to learn business. In five or six years he would be a capable assistant, and the growing enterprise would have someone to inherit it. Even if a boy were born now, more than ten years must pass before he grew up. That could not meet their present need. The Hu family had lost an opportunity. She could not help blaming her daughter-in-law for wasting all these good years. Once again Mrs Hu was at a disadvantage, and her husband was pleased with himself. But when he tried to discover more about her visit to Huzhou, he was disappointed. From what Meiyu said, her mother had told her nothing of it.

就在这天晚上，钱庄里派人来通知，说刘不才已经从湖州回来，请胡雪岩去有话说，可想而知的，必是关于芙蓉的事，否则刘不才也是熟客，何不到家来谈？估量到这一层，他首先就要注意他妻子的态度：“奇怪！”他试探着说：“刘不才怎么不来？反要我去看他。”“你管他呢！”胡太太夷然不以为意，“你去了再说。”胡太太的沉着实在厉害了！等跟刘不才见了面，才知道她跟芙蓉已经见过面，只说她是跟胡雪岩共患难的糟糠之妻，然后留下一张五千两银票，就告辞了。“有这样的事！”胡雪岩说，“我实在想不到。”“谁也没有想到。”刘不才很尴尬的说：“芙蓉要我来问你的意思，才好作去留之计。”于是胡雪岩又改回原来的称呼：“三叔！”他说，“请你仍旧回湖州，叫芙蓉不必着急。我自有办法。”“是什么办法呢？”“这一时说不清楚。”胡雪岩这样答道：“三叔，反正我一定对得起芙蓉就是了。”这话恰好是刘不才听不进去的，照他的私心打算，最好胡雪岩再给个三两万银子，让芙蓉下堂，别求归宿，省得自己沾上这点不十分光彩的裙带亲。而现在听他的口气，适得其反，刘不才虽然失望，却不便多说什么。

That evening a messenger came from the bank. Liu Bucai had returned from Huzhou and wanted Hu to come and speak with him. Obviously it concerned Furong. Otherwise, Liu was familiar enough with the household to call there himself. Having worked this out, Hu first watched his wife’s reaction. “How strange,” he said, sounding her out. “Why doesn’t Liu come here? Why must I go to him?” “Never mind that,” she answered with complete unconcern. “Go and find out.” Her composure was formidable indeed. Only when Hu met Liu did he learn that she had already seen Furong. She had simply introduced herself as the wife who had shared Hu’s hardships, left a five-thousand-tael banknote and taken her leave. “Such a thing!” Hu exclaimed. “I never imagined it.” “Nobody did.” Liu was embarrassed. “Furong sent me to ask your wishes before she decides whether to stay or go.” Hu returned to his former mode of address. “Third Uncle, please go back to Huzhou and tell Furong not to worry. I shall find a way.” “What way?” “I cannot explain just now. Whatever happens, I shall deal honourably with her.” This was precisely what Liu did not want to hear. Privately, he hoped Hu would give another twenty or thirty thousand taels, release Furong to find another home, and spare him this not altogether creditable connection through his niece. Hu’s words suggested the opposite. Disappointed, Liu could say little.

“你新年里的手气如何？”胡雪岩故作闲豫地问。这一问，刘不才又高兴了，“实在不错！”他笑得合不拢口，“所向披靡，斩获甚丰。”大概是赢得不少。胡雪岩心想，趁这时候得要规劝几句。“三叔！”他说，“ ‘瓦罐不离井上破，将军难免阵前亡’你见过哪个是在赌上发迹的，现在你手上很有几文了，应该做点正事。”“我的帐都还清了。”刘不才说，“还赢进一张田契，我已经托郁四去替我过户营业。”说到这里，他又感慨他说，“一个人真是穷不得！手头有几个钱，别人马上不同，就在这几天，有好几个人来替我做媒，劝我续弦。”“那是好事啊！”“不忙！”刘不才摇摇头，“让我潇潇洒洒，先过几年清闲日子再说。”“这就不对了！未曾发财，先想纳福，吃苦在后头。”胡雪岩说：“三叔，我劝你把世德堂恢复起来。”“咦！”刘不才诧异，“你不是要我帮你开庆余堂吗？”这件事几乎连胡雪岩自己都已忘记了，“自己人我说实话，这要慢慢再说了。就是开起来，我也要另外请人，三叔，”他说，“你的长处不在这上面。“

“How has your luck been over the New Year?” Hu asked, feigning leisure. This cheered Liu at once. “Excellent!” he said, grinning. “Victorious everywhere, with rich spoils.” He must have won a good deal. Hu thought this a suitable moment for advice. “Third Uncle, the pitcher is bound to break at the well, and the general is bound to die on the battlefield. Have you ever known anyone make his way in the world through gambling? You have a little money now. You ought to turn to serious work.” “All my debts are paid,” Liu replied. “I even won a deed to some land. I have asked Yu Si to arrange the transfer and put me in possession.” Then he grew reflective. “A man really cannot afford to be poor. Once he has a little money, people change towards him at once. In these last few days several people have offered to arrange a marriage for me, urging me to take another wife.” “That would be a good thing.” “There is no hurry.” Liu shook his head. “Let me enjoy a few carefree years first.” “That is wrong. Think of comfort before you have made your fortune, and hardship will come later. Third Uncle, I advise you to restore Shide Hall.” “What?” Liu was surprised. “Weren’t you going to have me help open Hu Qingyu Hall?” Hu had almost forgotten the undertaking himself. “Between ourselves, I shall tell you frankly. That must wait. Even if I open it, I shall have to find someone else. Third Uncle, your strengths lie elsewhere.”

一听是这样的答话，刘不才不免有些伤心，“雪岩，”他怨艾他说：“你看看我只会赌钱？”“不是这话，不是这话！”胡雪岩倒觉歉然，极力安慰他说，“你的长处我都知道，将来我有大大仰仗你的地方。”“那么眼前呢？”“眼前要看你自己的意思，你的志向是把祖传的基业恢复起来，所以我那样劝你，而且可以帮你的忙。”“我的想法变过了，世德堂就算恢复了，也没有啥意思，叫我守在店里，更加办不到。我想想，还是跟你一起去闯一闯的好。”“那好！”胡雪岩说，“你先回湖州，叫芙蓉放心，关起门来过日子，什么事也不必管，等我上海回来，自有安排。这话说到了，请你跟世龙一起赶到上海来。”

This hurt Liu. “Xueyan,” he said reproachfully, “do you think gambling is all I can do?” “Not at all!” Hu felt apologetic and did his best to reassure him. “I know your abilities. There will be important matters in which I must depend on you.” “What about now?” “For now, it depends on your wishes. Your ambition was to restore the family business. That is why I advised it, and I can help you.” “My mind has changed. Even restoring Shide Hall would mean little. I certainly couldn’t stay behind a shop counter. I think I would rather go out into the world with you.” “Very well. First return to Huzhou and put Furong’s mind at rest. Tell her to live quietly at home and concern herself with nothing else. When I return from Shanghai, I shall make arrangements. Once you have delivered that message, come to Shanghai with Shilong.”

这样说定了，各自分手。胡雪岩已出钱庄，灵机一动，开了张五千两的银票，带在身上，一到家，正好在书房里遇着他妻子，便把那张银票递了过去。胡太太装作不解地问道：“这是啥？”“你白送了五千银子！我贴还你的私房。”胡雪岩又说，“有私房钱，放到钱庄里去生息倒不好？压在箱子底下，大钱不会生小钱的。”看他是这种态度，胡太太倒有些莫测高深了。夫妇俩暗中较劲，到了这样的地步，至矣尽矣，胡太太自然有些不安，心想既然西洋镜已经折穿，就不如敞开来谈了。于是她先表示歉意，“雪岩，你不要怪我事先没有跟你商量！我也是万般无奈，为了一家大小，我们苦了这么多年，你刚刚转运，千万沾染不得‘桃花’，我这样做，是为你好。十几年夫妻，你总晓得我的心。”她停了一下又说，“当然，我另外有打算的，跟娘也讲过，将来你就可以晓得了，我不是不讲道理，乱吃醋的人。”

They parted with this agreed. Hu had already left the bank when an idea struck him. He had a five-thousand-tael note drawn and took it home. Finding his wife in the study, he handed it to her. “What is this?” she asked, pretending not to understand. “You gave away five thousand taels for nothing. I am replacing your private savings. Wouldn’t it be better to put your money in the bank and earn interest? Kept at the bottom of a chest, big money won’t breed little money.” His manner left her unable to fathom him. Their silent contest had reached its utmost limit. Uneasy, she thought that, since the secret was out, they had better speak openly. She began with an apology. “Xueyan, don’t blame me for not discussing it with you first. I had no choice. I did it for the whole family. We suffered for so many years, and now that your fortune has only just turned, you must not become entangled in love affairs. It was for your own good. After more than ten years of marriage, you know my heart.” She paused. “Of course, I have another plan, which I have discussed with Mother. You will understand in time. I am not an unreasonable woman consumed by jealousy.”

最后这几句话，让胡雪岩看穿了她妻子的用心。只要是小康之家，三十一过，尚乏子息，堂上老亲。便会动替儿子置妾的念头，再过五六年，依然有“后顾之忧”，则乡党宗亲都会出来“说公话”，再悍泼的大妇，也得屈服于“不孝有三，无后为大”的“道理”之下，忍气吞声让丈夫另辟偏房。因此，会吃醋的人便作未雨绸缪之计，表面绝不露温色，而且为丈夫置妾之念，表现得非常热切，三天两头找媒婆上门，里外串通，托词宜男之相，找来个粗脚大手，其蠢如牛的女孩子，作为丈夫金屋中的阿娇。同时一进门便立下许多规矩，阃令大如军令，偏房有如敌国，戒备森严，把丈夫摆布得动弹不得。胡雪岩认为他妻子就是这类厉害的角色，所以立刻表示“敬谢不敏”！“你不必瞎打算，我也不会领你的情。”他接着提到芙蓉：“你这趟到湖州去，做错了，大错特错！我跟你说过，是逢场作戏，认不得真，以后我自有摆脱的办法。现在你这一来，倒叫我为难了，如果照你的想头，给个几千银子，让人家走路，说出去是我胡雪岩怕老婆！不要说我面子上下不来，而且人家要想，胡雪岩凡事自己做不得主，你倒说人家还信任不信任我？”

Those last words revealed her purpose to Hu. In any reasonably prosperous family, once a son passed thirty without a male heir, his parents began thinking of finding him a concubine. If another five or six years passed and the future remained uncertain, neighbours and clansmen would speak out in the name of fairness. Even the fiercest principal wife had to submit to the argument that leaving no heir was the greatest failure of filial duty, swallow her anger and let her husband take a second woman. Cleverly jealous wives therefore prepared in advance. They showed no anger and seemed positively eager to obtain a concubine, calling matchmakers in every few days. In collusion with them, on the pretext of selecting a woman whose appearance promised sons, they found a girl with broad feet and large hands, as stupid as an ox, to serve as the A’jiao of their husband’s golden house. As soon as she entered, they laid down countless rules. Commands within the women’s quarters were as strict as military orders; the concubine was treated like an enemy state, under such close guard that the husband could scarcely move. Hu considered his wife just such a formidable strategist and immediately declined the favour. “Don’t waste your plans. I shan’t thank you for them.” Then he turned to Furong. “Your journey to Huzhou was a mistake—a very great mistake. I told you it was a passing amusement, nothing to take seriously. I had my own way of extricating myself later. Now you have put me in a difficulty. If I follow your idea, give her a few thousand taels and send her away, everyone will say Hu Xueyan is afraid of his wife. Besides losing face, I shall make people think I cannot decide anything for myself. Tell me, will they still trust me?”

这番道理把胡太太说得愣住了！她虽精明，到底世面见得少，商场中的习惯和顾忌，哪里懂得透？只好这样辩解：“我一个人去，一个人来，一共只见了一面，谈不到一盏茶的工夫，真正是人不知鬼不觉，哪个会晓得？”“是不是‘鬼不觉’，我不晓得，若要‘人不知’，除非己莫为。不说别的，就说我，先就晓得了。”胡雪岩故意跌足嗟叹：“现在湖州已经在笑话我了！你晓得庞二怎么说？他说，做大生意就象皇帝治天下一样，该杀的杀，该放的放，全靠当机立断，所以切忌女人轧脚。胡雪岩原来要听太太的话！如果说有笔生意来了，发大财或者本钱蚀光，都在当时一句话上，而胡某人说要回去跟太太商量一下看。你们说，这样子怎么合得拢淘来做大生意？”这番编出来的话，把胡太太说得青一阵，红一阵，心里又急又悔，好半晌说不出话来。“你也不要急！”胡雪岩倒过来安慰她，“事情已经做错了，懊悔也无用，眼前只有让他们去笑我，等我上海回来再说。”越是如此，越不能让胡太太安心。夫妇之间为了妾侍，没有不吵得天翻地覆的，即令丈夫脾气好，也不能这样丝毫不带愠色。其中一定有什么花样！同时芙蓉到底怎么样了呢，是知难而退，还是恋恋不舍，也得从丈夫口中讨出一个确实信息来，才好处置。总而言之，事情到此地步，由暗而明，使得干干净净有个了结，如果听任丈夫从上海回来再办，且不说夜长梦多，光是这许多日子他心中怀着不满，就足以使夫妇的感情起变化。

This argument left Mrs Hu stunned. Clever as she was, she had seen little of the world. How could she fully understand the habits and anxieties of business? She could only protest, “I went alone and came back alone. We met once, for less time than it takes to drink a cup of tea. Nobody could have known. Who would find out?” “Whether the spirits knew, I cannot say. But if you don’t want people to know of something, don’t do it. Never mind anyone else—I know already.” Hu deliberately stamped and sighed. “They are laughing at me in Huzhou now! Do you know what Pang said? ‘Running a great business is like an emperor ruling the realm. Execute whom you must, spare whom you should—everything depends on deciding at once. Above all, you must not let women hamper your steps. Yet it turns out Hu Xueyan must obey his wife! Suppose an opportunity arises and one immediate word decides between a fortune and the loss of all the capital. Then Hu says he must go home and consult his wife. Tell me, how can anyone join such a man in serious business?’” This invented speech made her turn pale and red by turns. Anxious and remorseful, she could not speak for a long time. Now Hu comforted her. “Don’t distress yourself. What is done is done. Regret will not help. For the moment, let them laugh. We will see when I return from Shanghai.” The more he spoke like this, the less reassured she felt. Disputes between husband and wife over a concubine invariably produced a storm. Even a good-tempered husband could not show absolutely no resentment. There must be some design behind it. And what had become of Furong? Had she withdrawn in the face of difficulty, or was she unwilling to let go? Mrs Hu needed a definite answer before deciding what to do. Now that the matter was out in the open, it ought to be settled cleanly. Waiting until his return from Shanghai invited further complications. Worse still, the resentment he might nurse throughout those days could change their relationship.

想到这里，胡太太认为丈夫的生意虽然要紧，但这件事更显得紧迫，说不得只好留了下来。“你晚几天走好不好？”她问。真是俗语说的“开口见喉咙”，一听这话，胡雪岩便看透底蕴，却明知故问他说：“为啥？”“梅玉第一趟出远门，总要替她多做点衣服。”胡太太这样托词，“晚个两三天走，也不碍吧？”“你说不碍就不碍。”胡雪岩隐约提出警告：“不过这几天当中，你不要替我惹什么麻烦，弄得我走不成，那就要了我半条命锣。”“有啥麻烦？”胡太太想到自己处处落下风，不免怨恨，便发牢骚似他说，“啥麻烦也难不倒你！反正各凭天良就是了。”说着，眼圈便有些红了。性格刚毅的女子，有此软弱的表示，最易感人，胡雪岩倒觉得心里酸酸地，一伸手扶着她的肩头说：“十几年夫妻，你难道还不晓得我？你有良心，我也有良心，不然我们不会有今天这样的日子。”想到眼前的日子，胡太太又生警惕，也越觉得留住丈夫是个一点不错的做法，她的做法是预备请嵇鹤龄出面来谈判，能让步一定让步。胡雪岩只知道她一定会有动作，却不知道她是打的这个主意。冷静地想一想，发觉到这重纠纷，主客已经易势，原来是自己怀着个鬼胎，深怕妻子进一步追究，此刻变成她急自己不急，以逸待劳，看她使出什么招数，再来设法破它，也还不迟。

His business was important, Mrs Hu decided, but this was more urgent. She must ask him to remain. “Could you leave a few days later?” The moment she opened her mouth, as the saying went, he could see straight down her throat. He understood completely, but asked as though he did not, “Why?” “It is Meiyu’s first long journey. We must make her some more clothes,” she said by way of a pretext. “Two or three days’ delay would not matter, would it?” “If you say it won’t matter, it won’t.” He added an indirect warning. “But don’t cause me any trouble in those few days and make it impossible for me to leave. That would take half my life.” “What trouble?” Resenting her constant defeats, she complained, “No trouble can defeat you. Let each of us act according to conscience, that is all.” Her eyes reddened. Such weakness in a strong-minded woman is particularly moving. Hu felt a pang and put a hand on her shoulder. “After more than ten years together, don’t you know me? You have a conscience, and so do I. Otherwise we would not have reached the life we have today.” Thinking of that life made her more watchful and more certain she was right to keep him at home. She intended to ask Ji Heling to mediate and would concede whatever she could. Hu knew she meant to act, but not that this was her plan. Calm reflection showed him that their positions had reversed. At first he had carried a guilty secret and dreaded further questions. Now she was anxious and he was not. He could wait at ease, see what move she made and devise an answer in good time.

有此闲豫的心情，而且有了多出来的两三天工夫，他忽发雅兴，特地约嵇鹤龄和裘丰言，白天逛湖，晚上吃“皇饭儿”，吃完上城隍山去看灯。裘丰言一诺无辞，嵇鹤龄则辞了逛湖之约，来赴饭局。酒到半酣，话题落到芙蓉身上，一个是异姓手足，一个是无话不谈的好朋友，有了几分酒意的胡雪岩想起对付他妻子的手腕，自觉得意，忍不住大谈特谈。就是这天上午，嵇鹤龄已受了胡太太之托，要来调停此事，便落得听他“自供。裘丰言却不知就里，附和着胡雪岩说：”胡大嫂果然精明，只怕是读过‘妒律’的。“胡雪岩没有听懂，追问一句：“你说啥？”“ ‘妒律’，妒忌之妒，律例之律！”“吃了酒又来信口开河，杜撰故事了。”嵇鹤龄笑道：“从未听说过有此一部律例。”“自然是游戏笔墨，但也不无道理。把大妇的妒心，刻画得无微不至。”裘丰言笑道：“天下凡想纳宠的男子，都当一读。”“那么，”胡雪岩很感兴趣的说，“你倒讲讲这部妒律，是怎么回事？”“分吏、户、礼、兵、刑、工，另加‘各例’、‘督捕律’等，一共八章。有引有判，是绝妙好词。”

In this leisurely mood, with two or three extra days at his disposal, Hu suddenly felt like an outing. He invited Ji Heling and Qiu Fengyan to tour the lake by day, dine at Huangfan’er and then climb City God Hill to see the lanterns. Qiu accepted without hesitation. Ji declined the lake excursion but came to dinner. When the wine had warmed them, the conversation turned to Furong. One man was his sworn brother, the other a close friend with whom he could discuss anything. A little tipsy, Hu recalled his handling of his wife, felt pleased with himself and could not resist talking at length. That very morning Ji had been asked by Mrs Hu to mediate, so he was content to hear Hu make his own confession. Qiu knew nothing of this. Agreeing with Hu, he said, “Sister-in-Law Hu is indeed clever. She must have read the Code of Jealousy.” Hu had not understood. “What did you say?” “The Code of Jealousy—jealousy, as in envy; code, as in statutes.” “Wine has set you inventing stories again,” Ji said with a smile. “I have never heard of such a code.” “Naturally it is a literary jest, but not without reason. It depicts a principal wife’s jealous heart in the finest detail. Every man thinking of taking a concubine ought to read it.” Hu was interested. “Then tell us about this code.” “It has eight chapters: Personnel, Revenue, Rites, War, Punishments and Works, with Additional Regulations and the Statutes for Apprehending Offenders. There are citations and judgments. Admirable writing!”

“我念几条来听听！”裘丰言点点头，喝了口酒，来了一个“响铃儿”在嘴里咀嚼得“嘎吱、嘎吱”的响，念念有词的默诵了一会，忽然笑道：“想起来了，你念两条你听，是兵部的军律：”凡妇见夫人妾房言语，即假借公事，突入冲散，拟坐以擅闯辕门律。如止挥扰，不作嗔状，引例未减，笞五十，免供。判曰：翡翠床前，方调鹦鹉之舌，水晶帘外，忽来狮吼之声。不徒花上晒衣，未免腹中藏剑！有心心术不端，无心见识不到。‘“这几句四六是胡雪岩听得懂的，“判得好！‘花上晒衣’，大煞风景，”他说：“真个该打手心！”

“Recite a few provisions for us.” Qiu nodded, drank some wine and took a crisp “ringing-bell” roll, crunching it as he silently rehearsed the words. Then he suddenly laughed. “I remember! Here are two for you, from the military statutes: ‘Any wife who sees her husband enter a concubine’s room to converse and, on the pretext of household business, bursts in and breaks up their meeting shall be charged under the statute against unauthorised entry into a military headquarters. If she merely disturbs them without showing anger, the provision for mitigation shall apply: fifty strokes of the light bamboo, with no confession required. The judgment states: Before the jade-green bed, the parrot’s tongue is just being coaxed to speech; beyond the crystal curtain, suddenly comes the roaring of a lion. This is more than hanging washing over flowers: it suggests a sword concealed in the belly. If deliberate, the intentions are improper; if unintentional, the understanding is deficient.’” Hu understood these balanced phrases. “A fine judgment! Hanging washing over flowers—what a way to spoil the scene. She really deserves a beating on the palms.”

“再有一种罪名，就不轻了！”裘丰言又拉长了声调念：“凡妇度与夫正值绸缨之际，忽唤妾起，嘱以他事，拟坐以‘擅调官军’律……”一句话未完；胡雪岩大笑：“好个‘擅调官军’，应得何罪？”“杖一百，发边远充军。”“这未免太重。”嵇鹤龄也笑了。“你说太重，人家以为‘宥以生命，犹为宽曲’。”襄丰言接着念判词：“酣战方深，浪子春风一度，金牌忽召，夫人号令三申，既撤白登之围，讵有黄龙之望？”“想想也是。”胡雪岩问道：“象内人那样，不晓得犯什么‘律’？”裘丰言想了想说：“有这么一条，‘凡妇蓄妾，原非得已，乃自夸贤德，冀人赞美。拟坐现任官辄自立碑律，杖一百。徒三年’。此由‘事因情近，名与实违’，‘盗名有禁，功令宜遵’！”

“There is another offence whose penalty is far from light.” Drawing out his voice, Qiu continued: “‘Any wife who judges that her husband and concubine are at a tender moment together, and suddenly calls the concubine away on another errand, shall be charged with unauthorised deployment of government troops...’” Before he finished, Hu burst out laughing. “Excellent! Unauthorised deployment of troops! What is the punishment?” “A hundred strokes of the heavy bamboo and military service on a distant frontier.” “Rather severe,” Ji said, laughing too. “You call it severe, but the author says, ‘To spare her life is already excessive leniency.’” Qiu went on with the judgment: “‘The battle is at its height, the rake enjoying a moment of spring; suddenly a golden tally recalls the troops, and the lady repeats her command three times. Once the siege of Baideng has been lifted, what hope remains of reaching Huanglong?’” “There is something in that,” Hu said. “What statute would a woman like my wife offend against?” Qiu considered. “There is this one: ‘Any wife who agrees to a concubine only because she has no choice, yet boasts of her virtue in hope of praise, shall be charged under the statute against an incumbent official erecting a monument to himself: one hundred strokes of the heavy bamboo and three years’ penal servitude.’ The circumstances are comparable, while the reputation contradicts the reality. ‘Usurping a reputation is prohibited; the regulations must be obeyed.’”

“你不要瞎说！”嵇鹤龄觉得裘丰言的玩笑之谈，有碍他的调停之职，所以阻止他再说下去，“我那位弟妇，决不是那种人，要替雪岩置妾，既非‘名与实违’，更不是‘盗各’。你说的妒律，全不适用。”裘丰言听出他的言外之意，极其见机，“原是不经之谈，”他说，“胡大嫂的贤德，不必自夸，亲友无不深知。”“家家有本难念经……”“雪岩！”嵇鹤龄抢着问道：“你那位新宠，如今怎么样了？”胡雪岩当然没有骗他的道理，老实答道：“好好在湖州。”“还顶着你的姓？”“当然。”胡雪岩忽然发觉嵇鹤龄的态度，与自己不尽符合，便问了一句：“大哥，你说我该怎么办？”“千言并一句，不可因此在家庭中生出意见，否则就是大不幸。”“对，对！”裘丰言又在旁边帮腔，“家和万事兴！雪岩兄鸿运当头，方兴未艾，此时最要得内助的力。”

“Stop talking nonsense!” Ji felt that Qiu’s jokes were obstructing his work as mediator and prevented him from continuing. “My sister-in-law is nothing of the kind. Her wish to find Xueyan a concubine neither contradicts her real intentions nor usurps a reputation. Your Code of Jealousy does not apply.” Qiu caught the implication and adapted at once. “It is all fanciful nonsense, of course. Sister-in-Law Hu need not boast of her goodness. All her friends and relations know it.” “Every household has a difficult scripture to recite...” “Xueyan!” Ji interrupted. “What has become of your new favourite?” Hu had no reason to deceive him. “She is living quietly in Huzhou.” “Still under your name?” “Naturally.” Suddenly realising that Ji’s attitude did not entirely agree with his own, Hu asked, “Elder Brother, what do you think I should do?” “A thousand words come to one point: do not let this sow discord in your family. That would be a great misfortune.” “Exactly!” Qiu chimed in. “When the family is harmonious, everything prospers. Brother Xueyan, your good fortune is still rising. Now above all you need your wife’s help.”

胡雪岩把他们两人一看，笑着说道：“双拳难敌四手，看样子我今天说不过你们了。”“老裘不是外人。我说老实话，我受托调停，即此可以看出弟妇的贤德。”嵇鹤龄又说：“今天上午，我也拜见了伯母，面奉慈谕，要我以长兄的资格，料理这件‘风流官司’。”“高堂之命、贤妻之托、长兄之尊，”裘丰言拍掌笑道：“雪岩兄，你可真要唯命是从了。”嵇鹤龄赶紧摇手阻止，“不是这话，不是这话！大家都是为雪岩。我先问你的意思，弟妇有句话给我，只要在情理上，一定可以如你的愿。”说到这后，胡雪岩觉得不必再玩弄什么手腕，便很率直他说道：“我不是什么荒唐的人，而且也还没有到可以荒唐的时候。没有儿子是一层，各地来去，要有个歇脚的地方，又是一层。所以我不觉得在湖州立个门户，就是对不起内人。我是尊重她，所以不让她知道，她偏偏要戳穿西洋镜，这出戏就很难唱得下去了。”“唱总要唱下去，顶了石臼也要唱。”嵇鹤龄说：“家庭之间和为贵，要和就得忍。弟妇算是忍耐了，你呢？”

Hu looked from one to the other and smiled. “Two fists cannot fight four hands. It seems I shall lose the argument today.” “Qiu is one of us, so I shall speak plainly. I have been asked to mediate. That alone shows your wife’s good sense. This morning I also paid my respects to your mother and received her personal instructions to settle this romantic lawsuit as your elder brother.” “Your mother’s command, your good wife’s request and your elder brother’s authority!” Qiu clapped his hands and laughed. “Brother Xueyan, you must surely obey.” Ji hastily waved him down. “That is not what I mean. Everyone is acting for Xueyan’s sake. First I want to know his wishes. His wife has told me that, provided they accord with reason and propriety, she will certainly meet them.” At this point Hu felt there was no need for further manoeuvres and spoke frankly. “I am not a dissolute man, nor have I reached a point where I can afford to be one. Having no son is one consideration; needing somewhere to rest as I travel is another. I therefore do not think that establishing a household in Huzhou wrongs my wife. I kept it from her out of respect. But she insisted on exposing the illusion, and now the play has become difficult to continue.” “It must continue even if you have to act with a stone mortar balanced on your head,” Ji replied. “Harmony matters most in a family. To achieve harmony, there must be forbearance. Your wife has shown it. What about you?”

“我不是也在忍吗？凡事将就，不跟她吵，也算对得起她了。”“是的。我也知道。不过芙蓉呢？总得有个着落才好。”“目前的情形，就是着落。”“这就谈不下去了。”照此看来，胡太太提得有条件，胡雪岩心想，莫非他妻子还是坚持要遣走芙蓉？果然如此，可真的是谈不下去了。就在这显现僵局之际，裘丰言说了句很公平的话：“彼此都要让步。雪岩兄如果坚持目前的情形，似乎不对！”“对了！我也是这话。”“不坚持目前的情形又如何？莫非真的叫大家笑话我胡某人怕老婆？”“当然不是这样子。”嵇鹤龄说，“我已经听出意思来了，弟妇的想法是，你讨小纳妾都可以，不过一定要住在一起。”“这就不错了！”裘丰言说，“胡大嫂这个意思在情理上。”“情理固然说得过去，无奈还有法——妒律！”

“Haven’t I shown it too? I give way in everything and don’t quarrel with her. Surely I have treated her fairly.” “Yes, I know. But what about Furong? There must be some settled arrangement.” “The present situation is the arrangement.” “Then we cannot get any further.” Evidently Mrs Hu had imposed a condition. Was she still insisting that Furong be sent away? If so, there really was nothing to discuss. As they reached this deadlock, Qiu made a fair remark. “Both sides must yield something. It hardly seems right for Brother Xueyan to insist that everything remain as it is.” “Exactly! That is what I mean.” “And if it doesn’t remain as it is? Am I really to let everyone laugh at Hu Xueyan for being afraid of his wife?” “Certainly not,” Ji said. “I have understood your wife’s meaning. You may take a concubine, but she insists that you all live together.” “That is reasonable,” Qiu agreed. “Sister-in-Law Hu is within the bounds of propriety.” “It may satisfy reason and propriety,” Hu replied, “but there is still the law—the Code of Jealousy!”
