On this journey to the capital, I shall need someone close to look after me. Could you find a suitable woman for me in Shanghai or Hangzhou?” “Nothing could be easier. Tell me what sort of woman you like.” “Someone like A’qiao would be ideal,” He answered without thinking.

胡雪岩一愣，细看一看他的脸色，不象饰词巧索，心里使好过些了，“我知道了。”他点点头，“总在云公动身以前，我必有以报命。”“拜托，拜托！”何桂清说，“回头我先送五百两银子过来。请雪岩兄在这个数目之内替我办。”“用不了这么多。”胡雪岩说：“云公也不必送来，办成了，我跟云公一起算，顺便还要讨赏。”“言重，言重！该我谢媒。”答应是答应下来了，回到金阊栈，细想一想，要找象阿巧姐这样的人，却真还不大容易。“嗐！我傻了！”胡雪岩突破心头的蔽境，解决了难题，却带来怅然若失的情怀。何必再去寻阿巧姐这样的人？阿巧姐不就在眼前？然而胡雪岩这一次撒手，跟放弃阿珠的感觉不大相同，当时移花接木将阿珠与陈世龙之间的那条红丝联系起来，不但心安理得，而且有快心惬意之感，如今要将阿巧姐送入别人的怀抱，心里却是酸溜溜的，很不好受。因此一个人徘徊又徘徊，翻来覆去的在想，除此以外可还有更好的办法？

Hu started. Studying He's expression, he concluded that this did not seem to be a disguised request for A’qiao herself, and felt somewhat better. “I understand,” he said, nodding. “Before you leave, I shall certainly have something to report.” “Thank you! I'll send five hundred taels over presently. Please arrange it within that sum.” “It won't cost so much. Nor need you send the money. Once it's settled, we'll reckon everything together. I'll even ask for a reward.” “You put it too strongly. I ought to thank my matchmaker.” Hu had agreed, but back at Jinchang Inn he realized that finding another woman like A’qiao would be no easy matter. “Ah! How foolish I've been!” Breaking through the obstruction in his mind, he solved the difficulty, only to be left with a sense of loss. Why seek someone like A’qiao when A’qiao herself was already there? Yet letting her go felt different from giving up A’zhu. When he had redirected the match, joining A’zhu's red thread of marriage to Chen Shilong's, his conscience had been clear and he had felt positively pleased. Now, at the thought of sending A’qiao into another man's arms, his heart was sour with unhappiness. He paced back and forth, turning the matter over repeatedly. Was there no better way?

这样蚁旋磨转的一直到天快黑，听得外面有人在喊：“胡大老爷！”声音很熟，却一时想不起是谁？出门一看，才影绰绰的辨清楚，是周一鸣。“中午我来伺候，胡大老爷出去了？”“喔，对不起，失迎！”胡雪岩答道：“何学台约我逛狮子林。”“姨太太也不在？”“她回木渎去了。”胡雪岩又补了一句：“那不是小妾，你的称呼用不着。”这也算是碰了一个钉子，周一鸣答不上来了，没话找话说了句：“胡大老爷怎不点灯？”“啊！”胡雪岩这时才醒悟，自己也觉得好笑，说了一半实话：“我大想一件心事，想得出神了。老周，我们吃酒去。”“是！”周一鸣赔笑说道：“我本来就打算做个小东，请胡大老爷喝杯酒。只怕胡大老爷不肯赏脸，不敢说。”“笑话！啥叫不肯赏脸？你说得太客气了。”胡雪岩很中意周一鸣，想跟他谈谈，便很恳切的说：“我扰你的。不过，下馆子我可不去，不是怕你多花饯。第一，中午油腻吃得太多，第二，想看看苏州的小酒店是怎么个光景，跟我们杭州有什么不同。”“胡大老爷这样说，我就恭敬不如从命了。这种专门吃酒的酒店，玄妙观前多得很，地方很干净，可以坐一坐。““那好，我们就走吧！”

His thoughts went round and round like an ant circling a millstone until it was almost dark. Then someone called from outside, “Mr Hu!” The voice was familiar, though for a moment he could not place it. Going out, he dimly made out Zhou Yiming. “When I called at noon, you were out?” “Oh, I'm sorry to have missed you. Education Commissioner He invited me to the Lion Grove.” “And the young mistress is away too?” “She's gone home to Mudu. She isn't my concubine, by the way. There's no need to call her that.” This was something of a rebuff. Zhou could find no answer and said, merely to fill the silence, “Why haven't you lit a lamp?” “Ah!” Only now did Hu notice. Amused at himself, he gave half the truth. “I've been so absorbed in something on my mind that I forgot. Old Zhou, let's go for a drink.” “Certainly.” Zhou smiled ingratiatingly. “I'd been hoping to act as host and offer you a cup, but I was afraid you wouldn't honour me and didn't dare suggest it.” “Nonsense! Why wouldn't I? You're far too polite.” Hu liked him and wanted to talk, so he added earnestly, “I'll be your guest. But I won't go to a restaurant. It isn't that I'm afraid of making you spend too much. First, I've had too much rich food at lunch. Second, I'd like to see what Suzhou's little taverns are like and how they differ from Hangzhou's.” “Then I'll do as you say. There are plenty of places devoted to drinking in front of Xuanmiao Temple. They're clean, and we could sit awhile.” “Good. Let's go.”

胡雪岩随手套上一件马褂，关照店伙计锁了门，与周一鸣雇了一辆马车进城。玄妙观前灯火辉煌，十分热闹，江宁失守，苏州成了全省的首善之区，文武官员，平空添了数百，大多不曾带家眷，公余无处可去，多集中在玄妙观前，闲逛的闲逛，买醉的买醉，市面要到二更才罢。酒店家家客满，最后在一家字号叫“元大昌”的。找到了一副临街的座头，两个人坐下来，要了绍兴花雕，随即便有两三个青布衣衫，收拾得十分干净挺括的上了年纪的妇人，挽着篮来卖下酒的卤菜。那些鸭头和鸭翅膀，看样子很不坏，但味道不怎么样，好在胡雪岩旨在领略苏州酒店的情趣，不在口腹，倒也不甚介意。等坐定了，吃过一巡酒，他放眼四顾，开始观察，苏州本地人雍容揖让，文文气气，一望而知，他们问壁一桌就是，两个都是白须老者，但一口道地的苏州话，却是其软无比，只听他们高谈阔论，也是一种乐趣。四外烽火连天，这“元大昌”中却是酒温语软，充满了逸兴闲情，隔座那两位白须老者，谈的是嘉庆年问的旧话，谈砚台、谈宜兴的“供春壶”、谈竹雕，都是太平盛世、文人墨客的雅玩。

Hu slipped on an outer jacket, told an inn servant to lock his door and hired a carriage with Zhou to go into the city. The area before Xuanmiao Temple blazed with lights and bustled with people. Since Jiangning had fallen, Suzhou had become the province's foremost city. Several hundred civil and military officials had appeared almost overnight. Most had not brought their families and had nowhere to go when work was done. They congregated here, some strolling, others drinking themselves tipsy, and the market remained busy until the second watch. Every tavern was full. At last they found seats facing the street in one called Yuandachang. They sat down and ordered Shaoxing huadiao. Two or three older women, neatly and cleanly dressed in blue cotton, promptly approached with baskets of braised snacks to accompany the wine. The duck heads and wings looked good enough, though their flavour was unremarkable. But Hu had come to savour the atmosphere of a Suzhou tavern, not its food, and did not much mind. Once settled, after their first round of wine, he looked about him and began to observe. Suzhou natives were easily recognized by their composed manners, courteous deference and scholarly air. The two men at the next table were examples: both white-bearded, both speaking the local dialect in wonderfully soft voices. Merely listening to their animated conversation was a pleasure. War blazed on every side, yet Yuandachang was full of warm wine, gentle voices and leisurely enjoyment. The two old men were recalling the Jiaqing years, discussing inkstones, Yixing Gongchun teapots and bamboo carvings—the elegant playthings of scholars in a peaceful, prosperous age.

“人生在世，为什么？”胡雪岩忽生感慨，“就是吃吃喝喝过一生？”这句话问得周一鸣直着眼好愣，不但不能回答，甚至也无从了解他的意思。“我是说，象隔壁那两位老太爷，”胡雪岩放低了声音说：“大概是靠收租过日子的乡绅。这样的人家，我们杭州也很多，祖上做过官，挣下一批田地，如果不是出了个败家精，安分度日，总有一两代好吃。本身也总有个把功名，好一点是进过学的秀才，不然就是二三十两银子捐来的监生，也算场面上的人物。一年到头无事忙，白天孵茶馆，晚上‘摆一碗’，逍遥自在到六七十岁，一口气不来，回老家见阎王，说是我阳世里走过一遭了。问他阳世里做点啥？啥也不做！象这样的人，做鬼都没有意思。“这番不知是自嘲，还是调侃他人的话，周一鸣倒是听懂了，此人也算是有志向的人，所以对胡雪岩的话，颇有同感，“是阿！”他说，“人生在世，总要做一番事业，才对得起父母。”

“What is a man alive for?” Hu asked, suddenly moved. “Simply to eat and drink his way through life?” Zhou stared blankly. He could not answer; he could scarcely even understand the question. “I mean people like those two old gentlemen,” Hu explained, lowering his voice. “They're probably country gentry living on rents. We have plenty of such families in Hangzhou. An ancestor held office and acquired some land. Unless a spendthrift appears, quiet living leaves enough to feed a generation or two. The men themselves generally have some examination standing. The better ones are licentiates admitted to the schools; otherwise they've paid twenty or thirty taels for the status of an Imperial Academy student. They count as people of standing too. All year round they're busy doing nothing: they sit in teahouses by day and have a bowl of wine at night. They drift pleasantly on until sixty or seventy, then stop breathing and go home to meet the King of Hell. ‘I've had my turn in the world of the living,’ they say. Ask what they did there, and the answer is nothing! Even being a ghost would be meaningless for someone like that.” Whether he was mocking himself or teasing others was unclear, but Zhou understood this much. He too had ambitions and felt considerable sympathy. “Quite so. A man should accomplish something in his lifetime, if only to do right by his parents.”

有这句话，胡雪岩觉得可以跟他谈谈了，“老周，”他问，“听说你在水师，也是蛮有名的人物。”“名是谈不到，人缘是不错。”周一鸣喝了口酒，满腹牢骚地说，“从前船户都叫我‘老总’，见了客气得很，现在都叫我老周，啥跑腿的事都要干。想想真不是味道。”“你的意思，仍旧想回水师？”“想也不行！”周一鸣摇摇头，“从前我那个长官，现在官更大了，听了他娘的小舅子的话，把我恨得要死。要想再回去补个名字，除非移名改姓，从小兵干起，那要干到什么时候才得出头？想想只好算了。”“果真你要回去，我倒可以帮你的忙。”胡雪岩说，“想来水师管带，官也不会大到哪里去，我替你请何学台写封信，你看怎么样？”“求得到何学台的信，我又不必回原地方了，何学台跟江苏巡抚许大人是同年，有何学台的信，我投到‘抚标’去当差，比原来的差使好得多。”“那好！”胡雪岩说，“这上头我不大懂。明天我带你去见何学台，你当面跟他说。”听得这话，再想到何桂清对胡雪岩的客气，料知他们交情极深，事必有济，所以他极其兴奋，连连道谢，应酬得格外殷勤了。

At that, Hu felt they could talk. “Old Zhou, I hear you were quite a figure in the navy.” “I wouldn't say I had a name, but I got on well with people.” Zhou took a drink and poured out his grievance. “Boatmen used to call me ‘Officer’ and treat me with great respect. Now it's ‘Old Zhou’, and I have to run every kind of errand. It leaves a bitter taste.” “You'd like to return to the navy, then?” “Wishing won't help.” He shook his head. “My old commanding officer has risen higher still. He listened to that damned brother-in-law of his and hates me like poison. The only way to get back on the rolls would be to change my name and start again as a common soldier. How long would it take to get anywhere? I can only give it up.” “If you really want to go back, I could help. A naval commander can hardly be so very high an official. What if I asked Education Commissioner He to write a letter for you?” “With a letter from him, I wouldn't have to return to my old place. He and Governor Xu of Jiangsu passed the metropolitan examination in the same year. I could enter the troops under the governor's direct command. That would be far better than my old post.” “Very well. I don't know much about these things. Tomorrow I'll take you to see the commissioner, and you can tell him yourself.” Remembering how courteously He had treated Hu, Zhou concluded that they must be close friends and that success was assured. He was intensely excited, thanked Hu repeatedly and became still more attentive as host.

酒吃到六分，胡雪岩不想再喝，叫了两碗“双浇面”，一碗是焖得稀烂的大肉面，一碗是熏鱼面，两下对换，有鱼有肉，吃得酒醉饭饱，花不到五钱银子，胡雪岩深为满意。“钱不在多，只要会用。”他说，“吃得象今天这么舒服的日子，我还不多。”“这是因为胡大老爷晓得我做东，没有好东西吃，心里先就有打算了，所以说好。”“这就叫‘知足常乐’。”胡雪岩说，“凡事能够退一步想，就没有烦恼了。”这天晚上他再想阿巧姐的去留，就是持着这种态度，譬如不曾遇见她，譬如她香消玉殒了，譬如她为豪客所夺，这样每自譬一次，便将阿巧姐看得谈了些，最后终于下了决心，自己说一声：“君子成人之美！”然后叹口气，蒙头大睡。

When Hu had reached a comfortable degree of tipsiness, he wanted no more wine. They ordered two bowls of noodles with a double topping between them: one came with pork braised until meltingly tender, the other with smoked fish. By exchanging toppings, they each had fish and meat. They ate and drank to their hearts' content for less than half a tael. Hu was thoroughly pleased. “It isn't how much money you have, but how you use it. I've seldom enjoyed a meal as much as this.” “That's because you knew I was treating you and expected nothing fine. You'd prepared yourself, so it seems good.” “That's what they mean by ‘contentment brings lasting happiness’. If you can step back a little in your thinking, there's nothing to trouble you.” That night, he approached the question of letting A’qiao go in this same spirit. Suppose he had never met her. Suppose she had died. Suppose some powerful patron had taken her from him. Each such reflection loosened his attachment a little. At last he made up his mind. “A gentleman helps others attain their happiness,” he told himself. Then he sighed, pulled the quilt over his head and went to sleep.

第二天一早起身，周一鸣已经在等着了，临时客串听差，替他奔走招呼，所以阿巧姐虽不在身边，胡雪岩亦觉得并无不便。同时心里在想，自己一向为求使捷爽利，不喜欢带个听差在身边，看来若有象同一鸣这样的人，带在身边，亦自不妨，这一趟回去，或在杭州，或在上海，倒要好好物色一个。等他漱洗完毕，周一鸣又要请他进城去喝早茶。胡雪岩心里有数，便连声答道：“好的，好的！吃完早茶，我带你去见何学台，当面求他替你写信。”于是进了城在“吴苑”茶店吃早茶。苏州的茶店跟杭州的又不同，杭州的茶店，大都是敞厅，一视同仁，不管是缙绅先生，还是贩夫走卒，入座都是顾客，苏州的茶店，分出等级，各不相淆，胡雪岩好热闹，与周一鸣只在最外面那间厅上坐，一面喝茶，一面吃各式各样的点心，消磨到十点钟，看看是时候了，算了帐，安步当车到苏州府学去见何桂清。由于爱屋及乌的缘故，何桂清对周一鸣也很客气，再三让坐，周一鸣守着官场的规矩，只是垂手肃立，最后却不过意，才屁股沾着椅子边，仿佛蹲着似地坐了下来。看他这局促的光景，胡雪岩倒觉得于心不忍，便要言不烦他说明来意，何桂清当时答道：“许大人亲自到上海督师去了。”接着转脸问胡雪岩：“现在倒有个好机会，是去收税，不知道这位周君愿意不愿意屈就。”“屈就这两个字言重了。不知是哪一处税卡？”“现在新创一种‘厘金’，你总晓得。”“这听说过。”胡雪岩答道，“到底怎么回事，却还不十分清楚。”

When he rose early the next morning, Zhou was already waiting. Acting as a temporary servant, he ran about attending to Hu's needs, so that even without A’qiao Hu felt no inconvenience. He had always preferred travelling without a servant for the sake of freedom and efficiency. But a man like Zhou might be useful to have beside him. On his return, whether in Hangzhou or Shanghai, he ought to look carefully for someone suitable. After Hu had washed, Zhou invited him into the city for morning tea. Understanding what was on his mind, Hu readily agreed. “Yes, yes. Afterwards, I'll take you to the commissioner and ask him in person for a letter.” They went to the Wuyuan teahouse. Suzhou teahouses differed from Hangzhou's. In Hangzhou, most had open halls and treated everyone alike. Gentry, pedlars and labourers were all customers once seated. In Suzhou, the different classes were separated and did not mingle. Hu enjoyed a crowd, so he and Zhou sat in the outermost hall, drinking tea and sampling the various pastries until ten. Judging the time right, they paid and strolled to the prefectural school to see He Guiqing. Out of regard for Hu, He treated Zhou courteously too, repeatedly asking him to sit. Zhou observed official etiquette, standing respectfully with his hands at his sides. At last he could not refuse and perched on the edge of a chair as though squatting. Hu felt sorry for his discomfort and explained their purpose briefly. “Governor Xu has gone to Shanghai to direct the troops in person,” He replied. Then he turned to Hu. “There is a good opening at present, though. It's tax collection. I wonder whether Mr Zhou would consider it beneath him.” “You flatter him. At which tax station?” “You've heard of the new levy called lijin?” “I've heard of it, but I don't yet know exactly how it works.”

“是你们浙江的一个奇士的策划。此人算来是雪轩的部民，湖州府长兴人，名叫钱江……”钱江字东平，是浙江长兴的一名监生，好大言，多奇计，仿佛战国的策士一流人物。鸦片战争一起，协办大学士吏部尚书，宗室奕经，奉旨以“杨威将军”的名义，到浙江督办军务，钱江叩辕献计，招募壮士，奇袭英军，擒其首脑。畏葸的奕经，如何敢用这样的奇计？敬谢不敏。后来林则徐得罪遣戍，而钱江在广州主张拒英，亦充军到伊犁，在戍所相遇，林则徐对他深为赏识。当林则徐遇赦进关时，设法将他洗脱了罪，带入关内，在京城里为他揄扬于公卿之间，声名鹊起，不幸地，林则徐不久病殁，钱江顿失凭依，于是挟策游于江淮之间，在扬州遇到了雷以诚。献上两策，第一策是预领空白捐照，随时填发，第二策就是开办厘金。

“It was devised by a remarkable man from your own Zhejiang. Indeed, he comes from Xuexuan's jurisdiction: Changxing County in Huzhou Prefecture. His name is Qian Jiang.” Qian Jiang, courtesy name Dongping, was an Imperial Academy student from Changxing. Fond of bold talk and ingenious schemes, he resembled the wandering strategists of the Warring States. When the Opium War began, Yijing, an imperial clansman who was assistant grand secretary and president of the Board of Civil Appointments, received orders to direct military affairs in Zhejiang as General Who Spreads Awe. Qian presented himself at his headquarters with a plan: recruit brave men, surprise the British and capture their leaders. Timid Yijing dared not attempt such an extraordinary scheme and politely declined. Later, Lin Zexu fell into disgrace and was sent into exile. Qian, having advocated resistance to the British in Guangzhou, was likewise sentenced to military exile in Ili. They met there, and Lin greatly admired him. When Lin was pardoned and allowed to return within the passes, he arranged to clear Qian's conviction and brought him back. In the capital, Lin praised him among the high officials, and his reputation rapidly grew. Unfortunately, Lin died not long afterwards, leaving Qian without support. He then travelled with his schemes through the country between the Yangtze and Huai rivers. In Yangzhou, he met Lei Yixian and proposed two measures. The first was to obtain blank certificates for purchased ranks in advance, to be filled in and issued on the spot. The second was to introduce lijin.

穷了想富，富了想贵，人之常情，所以做生意发了财的，尤其是两淮的那班盐商，最喜欢捐官，捐到三品道员还觉得戴蓝顶子不够威风，总想找机会，如报效军需，捐助河工，花大把银子买个“特保”，弄个二品顶戴的红顶子才肯罢休。但是捐官的手续甚为繁复，吏部书办的花样百出，往往“上兑”一两年，一张证明几品官员身分的“部照”还拿不到，这一来自然影响捐官的兴趣。钱江的办法就是专为想过官瘾的富商打算，一手交钱，一手交货，上了兑，立刻填发部照，爽快无比。雷以諴认为此策极妙，便托钱江上了个奏折，细陈其事，照他的办法，部里的书办就没有好处了，所以起初部议不准。无奈国库空虚，乾嘉年间积下的上千万银子，从道光年间鸦片战争以来，以奕经、耆英、琦善以及赛尚阿等总领师干的钦差大臣，花得光光，现在朝廷为对付洪杨起义，“既要马儿好，又要马儿不吃草”，如果马儿自己觅草去吃，犹复不准，如何说得过去？因此，钱江的妙策，到底被批准了。部里领来大批的空白捐照，现款交易，而且没有层出不穷的小费，既快又便宜，捐官的人，自然趋之若鹜。雷以諴就靠了这笔收入，招募乡勇，才得扼守扬州、镇江一带。然而捐官只是一趟头的买卖，细水长流，还得另想别法，于是而有厘金。

The poor long to be rich, and the rich to be honoured: that is human nature. Merchants who had made fortunes, particularly the salt merchants of the Two Huai districts, were therefore especially fond of purchasing official rank. Even after contributing enough to become third-rank circuit intendants, they felt a blue finial insufficiently imposing. They were always seeking opportunities—funding military supplies, for instance, or contributing to river works—to spend large sums on a special recommendation. Only a second-rank red finial would satisfy them. Yet buying rank involved complicated procedures. Clerks at the Board of Civil Appointments had endless tricks. A man might remit his payment and still wait a year or two for the board's certificate establishing his rank. Naturally, this diminished enthusiasm. Qian's scheme catered precisely to wealthy merchants eager to taste official distinction: money in one hand, goods in the other. As soon as payment was made, the certificate would be completed and issued. Nothing could be more straightforward. Lei thought the proposal excellent and had Qian submit a memorial setting it out in detail. Since the scheme would deprive the board's clerks of their profits, the board initially rejected it. But the treasury was empty. The more than ten million taels accumulated under Qianlong and Jiaqing had been exhausted since the Opium War in the Daoguang reign by imperial commissioners commanding armies—Yijing, Qiying, Qishan, Saishang’a and others. Now, in confronting the uprising of Hong and Yang, the court wanted a good horse without having to feed it. If it forbade the horse even to find its own fodder, how could that be justified? Qian's ingenious proposal was therefore approved at last. Large quantities of blank certificates arrived from the board. Transactions were immediate and required none of the endless incidental fees. Quicker and cheaper, the new arrangement naturally drew crowds of buyers. With this revenue, Lei recruited local volunteers and was able to hold the Yangzhou–Zhenjiang area. But each sale of rank brought payment only once. A continuing stream required another source. Hence lijin.

清朝的行商税，本来只有关税一种。大宗税收是钱粮地丁，因为失地太多而收额大减，两淮的盐税，亦因为兵火的影响，销场不旺，弥补之道，就靠厘金，一钱抽一厘，看起来税额甚轻，但积少成多，为数可观。最先是由雷以諴在扬州仙女庙、邵伯镇等运河码头，设卡试办，成效不坏，朝廷因而正式降旨，命两江总督怡良、江苏巡抚许乃钊、漕运总督杨以增，在江南、江北各地试行捐厘助饷，以裕军需。听罢何桂清的陈述，胡雪岩对钱江其人，深为仰慕，颇想一见，但这是一时办不到的事，只好丢开，先替周一鸣作打算。“他是水师出身，运河、长江各码头，都是熟人。若得云公栽培，当差决不致误事，坍云公的台。”“我知道，我知道，看周君也是很能干的人，而况又是你的举荐，一定赏识不虚。”何桂清说，“我马上写信，请坐一坐！”说罢，他退入书房，亲笔写了一封信。何洼清虽未做到封疆大吏，督抚的派头已经很足，两张八行笺，写着胡桃大的字，按科名先后，称雷以諴为“前辈”。胡雪岩接了信代周一鸣道谢，周一鸣自己则叩头相谢。

Previously, the Qing had imposed only customs duties on travelling merchants. Its principal tax revenue came from the land and poll levy, but so much territory had been lost that receipts had fallen sharply. War had also depressed sales in the Two Huai salt market and reduced its tax yield. Lijin was to make up the shortfall: one li collected on every qian. The rate appeared slight, but small sums accumulated into a considerable amount. Lei first tried it at canal wharves such as Xiannümiao and Shaobo near Yangzhou. The results were good. The court then formally ordered Yiliang, Governor-General of Liangjiang, Xu Naizhao, Governor of Jiangsu, and Yang Yizeng, Director-General of Grain Transport, to introduce contributions of lijin for military funds in various places north and south of the Yangtze. After hearing He's account, Hu greatly admired Qian and longed to meet him. That was impossible for the moment, however, so he set the thought aside and returned to Zhou's prospects. “He served in the navy and knows people at wharves all along the canal and the Yangtze. If you give him this opportunity, he certainly won't neglect his duties or let you down.” “I know. Mr Zhou looks very capable, and with your recommendation I'm sure your confidence is justified. I'll write at once. Please sit awhile.” He withdrew to his study and wrote the letter himself. Though not yet a provincial ruler, he already had all the manner of a governor or governor-general. His characters, as large as walnuts, filled two sheets of eight-line letter paper. In keeping with the order of their examination success, he addressed Lei as his senior. Hu received the letter and thanked He for Zhou, who himself expressed his gratitude by kowtowing.

“你先回去吧！”胡雪岩对周一鸣说，“我还要陪何大人谈谈。”等周一鸣一走，何桂清告诉胡雪岩一个消息，说江苏巡抚许乃钊有调动的消息，“今天一早，接到京里的密信。”他说，“我想等一等再说。”许乃钊调动，何以他要等候？细想一想，胡雪岩明白了，必是何桂清有接此任的可能，不妨静以观变。这个主意的变化，胡雪岩觉得对自己这方面大为不利，因而颇想劝他仍照原来的计划，先活动调任仓场侍郎，然后放到浙江去当巡抚，那一来，对王有龄，对自己，对嵇鹤龄便有左右逢源、诸事顺手之乐了。暗中的猜测，不便明劝，万一猜得不对，变成无的放矢，是件可笑的事，叫何桂清看轻了自己，而且凡事明说不如暗示，旁敲侧击的效果最好，这是胡雪岩所深知的。于是略想一想，有了一套说词。“江苏巡抚这个缺，从前是天下第一，现在，我看是最末等的了。”他忽然发了这样一段议论。何桂清当然要注意，“苏抚的缺分，不如以前是真的，”他说，“但亦不至于沧为末等。”“我是瞎说说的，跟云公请教。”胡雪岩徐徐而言，想着末等的理由，想到一条说一条：“第一是大乱在江苏，地方少了，钱粮也就少了。”

“Go back first,” Hu told Zhou. “I'll stay and talk with His Excellency.” Once Zhou had left, He told Hu that Xu Naizhao might be transferred from the governorship of Jiangsu. “A confidential letter from the capital arrived early this morning. I think I shall wait and see.” Why should Xu's transfer make him wait? After a moment, Hu understood: He must have a chance of succeeding him and wanted to observe developments. This change of plan would be decidedly unfavourable to Hu's side. He wanted to urge He to keep to the original course: first arrange a transfer as granary vice-minister, then seek appointment as governor of Zhejiang. That would make everything convenient for Wang Youling, Ji Heling and Hu himself, with helpful connections on every side. But he could not openly argue against something he had only guessed. If the guess was wrong, he would be shooting at no target and make himself ridiculous in He's eyes. Besides, Hu knew that hints and indirect approaches worked better than plain statements. After a little thought, he found his line of argument. “The governorship of Jiangsu used to be the finest post in the empire,” he suddenly remarked. “Now I should call it the very worst.” He naturally paid attention. “It's true that the post is no longer what it was, but hardly that it has fallen to the bottom.” “I'm only talking at random and seeking your advice.” Speaking slowly, Hu thought of reasons one at a time and offered them as they came. “First, the worst disorder is in Jiangsu. Less territory means less tax revenue.”

“还好，苏松膏腴之地，还在我们手里。”胡雪岩不便说苏松难保，“要保住，也很吃力，刘丽川至今还在上海。这且不去说它，第二，江苏的官太多。“他说，”浙江好的是巡抚独尊！““啊！”何桂清深深点头，“你这话有道理，督抚同城，确是麻烦，不是东风压倒西风，就是西风压倒东风。”“巡抚要压倒总督，怕不大容易，这也不去说它，第三，”胡雪岩又说：“江南大营的向大人，听说很难伺候。云公，有这话没有？”这话当然有的。何桂清心想，江南大营的骄兵悍将，不知凡几，向茶的难侍候，犹其余事。于是本来想在江苏等机会，打算着能接许乃钊的遗缺的心思动摇了。看他默然不语，胡雪岩猜到了他的心思，益发动以危言：“地方官要与城共存亡。我替我们杭州同乡许大人说句私话，如果能够调动一个缺，真正是‘塞翁失马，焉知非福’了。”这句话才真的打动了何桂清，他最胆小，虽然纸上谈兵，豪气万丈，其实最怕打仗。看起来，江苏真的成了末等的缺，何必自讨苦吃，还是进京去吧！主意打定了，却不便明说，只连连点头：“高论极是，佩服之至。”

“Not so bad. We still hold the fertile Suzhou–Songjiang country.” Hu could hardly say that even Suzhou and Songjiang might be lost. “Holding it is hard enough. Liu Lichuan is still in Shanghai. But leave that aside. Second, Jiangsu has too many officials. The advantage of Zhejiang is that the governor stands supreme.” “Ah!” He nodded deeply. “There's sense in that. A governor and governor-general in the same city are indeed troublesome. Either the east wind overcomes the west or the west overcomes the east.” “It can hardly be easy for a governor to overcome a governor-general. But leave that aside too. Third, I've heard that General Xiang at the Jiangnan Grand Camp is difficult to serve. Is that true?” Of course it was. He reflected that the camp was full of arrogant troops and unruly commanders; Xiang Rong's difficult temper was the least of it. His intention of waiting in Jiangsu for a chance to succeed Xu began to waver. Seeing him silent, Hu guessed what he was thinking and pressed him with a further warning. “A local official must live or die with his city. Speaking privately on behalf of Governor Xu, my fellow native of Hangzhou, if he could be transferred elsewhere, it might truly be a case of the frontier old man's lost horse proving a blessing in disguise.” This struck home. He was extremely timid. However boldly he discussed warfare on paper, he was terrified of actual fighting. Jiangsu did seem to have become the worst of posts. Why seek trouble? Better go to the capital after all. Having decided, he could not say so openly. He merely nodded repeatedly. “Your argument is entirely right. I admire your insight.”

“我哪里懂什么，不过俗语道得好：”旁观者清。‘不在其位，不关得失，看事情比较清楚。““说得一点不错。”何桂清答道：“我就正要老兄这样的人，多多指点。”“云公这话说得太过分，真叫我脸红。”他趁势站了起来，“我就此告辞了，顺便跟云公辞行。”“怎么？”何桂清顿现怅然之色，“你就这样走了？”“是的，我预备明天一早动身回上海。”“那么……”何桂清沉吟了好半晌说：“我们上海见面吧！那不会太久的。”“是！我一回上海就把款子预备好，随时等云公的招呼。”“还有件事，无论如何，奉托费心。”胡雪岩一愣，随即会意，事实上此事已成功了一半，所以很有把握他说：“云公请放心，一到上海，必有喜信。”何桂清自然高兴。而过分的欣悦，反生感慨，“真想不到，这一次无端与雪岩兄结成知交。”他摇摇头说，“人生在世，都是一个缘字，想想真是不可思议。”胡雪岩跟他的境遇，约略相似，再加上王有龄，三个人天南地北，不知冥冥中是什么力量的驱使？得能聚在一起，象七巧板一样，看似毫不相干，居然拼出一副花样，实在巧妙之至。所以对他的话，深具同感。“云公，说到缘字，还有让你想不到的事。”他紧接着又说，“眼前我不说破，说破了不好玩了。只盼你早则节前，晚则节后，到了上海，我们再叙。”听他如此说法，何桂清便不肯多问，只说：“好，好！我们再叙。良晤非遥，我就不送你了。”“不敢当，我也就不再来辞行了。”他站起身作揖。

“What do I know? But as the saying goes, a bystander sees clearly. Without holding the post or having a personal stake in its gains and losses, one can see more plainly.” “Quite true. I need more guidance from men like you.” “You flatter me so much that you make me blush.” Hu took the opportunity to rise. “I must leave now, and take my leave of you before my journey as well.” “What?” He looked disappointed at once. “Are you going already?” “Yes. I mean to return to Shanghai early tomorrow.” “Then...” He considered for a long while. “We'll meet in Shanghai. It won't be very long.” “Certainly. As soon as I'm back, I'll have the money ready and wait for your instructions.” “There is also that other matter. I must ask you, whatever happens, to give it your attention.” Hu was momentarily puzzled, then understood. In fact, half the work was already done, and he could answer confidently. “Don't worry. Once I reach Shanghai, I shall have good news.” He was naturally delighted, and his excessive pleasure turned reflective. “To think that this visit should unexpectedly have made such close friends of us! Life is all a matter of affinity. It's truly beyond understanding.” Hu's circumstances resembled his in some degree. With Wang Youling, they were three men from distant corners of the country, brought together by some unseen force. Like the pieces of a tangram, apparently unrelated, they had combined into a pattern. It was wonderfully ingenious, and Hu felt deep sympathy with He's words. “Speaking of affinity, there's something else that will surprise you. I won't reveal it yet; that would spoil the pleasure. I only hope you'll reach Shanghai before the festival if possible, and shortly after if not. Then we'll talk again.” Hearing this, He would not press. “Very well. We'll talk then. Our next meeting is not far off, so I won't see you off on your journey.” “You needn't trouble yourself. Nor shall I call again to take leave.” Hu rose and bowed.

“你请等一等。”何桂清说完，匆匆又走入书斋，好久，都不见再露面。他是亲笔在写名帖，写信来不及了，只好用名帖，一共七、八张，从苏州到上海，沿路掌管一方的文武官员，都有他的名帖致意，致意是门面话，其实是为胡雪岩作先容。“你备而不用吧！”何桂清把一叠名帖交了过去，“交情深浅，都在措词上看得出来，该用不该用，怎么用法？你自己斟酌。”“有云公这几张名帖，就等于派了百把兵保护，一路上可以睡到上海，多谢，多谢！”“雪轩那里，我另外复信，这里跟浙江，每天都有驿差，方便得很。我就不必麻烦你转信了。”何桂清一面说，一面亲自送客，体制所关，送到二门为止。等胡雪岩回到客栈，他跟着又派人送了四样路菜，一部他新刻的诗槁，另外一个沉甸甸的小木箱，打开来一看，是一只“汽锅”。“难为你家大人想到。”“我家大人交代，”那个叫何福的听差说：“胡大老爷的交情，与众不同，叫我跟胡大老爷请示，若还有事，我就在这里侍候胡大老爷上了船再回去。““不必，不必！我有人，你请回去吧，替我道谢。”说完，在阿巧姐的梳头匣里取了个红封套，红封套甚多，备着赏人用的，轻重不等，最重的是五两一张银票，给何福的就是这一种。

“Wait a moment.” He hurried back into his study and did not reappear for some time. He was writing on visiting cards himself. There was no time for letters, so he used seven or eight cards, one for each of the civil and military officials controlling the districts along the route from Suzhou to Shanghai. Ostensibly, they conveyed his regards; in reality, they introduced Hu. “Keep these in reserve,” he said, handing over the little stack. “The wording will tell you how close I am to each man. Judge for yourself which to use, whether to use them and how.” “These cards are as good as sending a hundred soldiers to protect me. I can sleep all the way to Shanghai. Thank you!” “I'll answer Xuexuan separately. Couriers travel between here and Zhejiang every day, so it's easy enough. I needn't trouble you to carry the letter.” As he spoke, He accompanied his guest out. Official propriety allowed him to go no farther than the second gate. After Hu returned to the inn, He sent four dishes for the journey, a copy of his newly printed poems and a small, heavy wooden box. On opening it, Hu found a steam pot. “How thoughtful of your master!” “My master said,” replied the attendant He Fu, “that his friendship with you is unlike any other. He told me to ask whether you need anything. If so, I'm to stay and attend to you until you've boarded your boat.” “No need. I have someone. Please go back and thank him for me.” From A’qiao's dressing case, Hu took a red envelope. There were many there, prepared for tips of varying amounts. The largest contained a five-tael banknote. He gave He Fu one of these.

这一下，胡雪岩就只有一件事了，等阿巧姐回来。原说午间可到，结果等到日落西山，不见芳踪，反倒是周一鸣又来相伴了。“胡大老爷，真是多亏你栽培。我去请教过人了，说何大人这封八行的力量很够，一定会得个好差使。”他笑嘻嘻地说。“那很好！”胡雪岩也替他高兴，“你得赶快到扬州才好。迟了就没有好差使了。”“不碍。沿运河、长江两岸都要设卡子，差使多得很，抢不光的。我伺候了胡大老爷回上海，再到扬州，最多耽误十天的工夫，不要紧。”看他意思甚诚，而且路上也还要他招呼，胡雪岩就点点头不再多说了。于是又闲谈了一会，同一鸣看胡雪岩有点心神不定的模样，但有些踌躇，再坐下去，怕惹他的厌，如果告辞，丢下他一个人在客栈，更为不妥，想了想又劝他出去喝酒散心。“谢谢，今天不行了。我得等人。”“喔，”周一鸣知道他心神不定的由来了，“是等阿巧姐？”“是啊！她回木渎娘家去，说了中午回来的，至今人面不见，不知是怎么回事？”“此刻不来，今天不会回来了。木渎的航船，早就到了。”“不是搭的航船，自己雇了一只船来回。”“那这样，”周一鸣站起身来，“我到阎门码头上去打听打听看。”“不晓得是哪一条船，怎么打听？”“不要紧！我到那里，一问便知。”“对了！你码头上最熟。”胡雪岩欣然答道，“那就拜托了。”

Now Hu had only one thing left to do: wait for A’qiao. She had said she would arrive at noon, but the sun sank without any sign of her. Instead, Zhou returned to keep him company. “Mr Hu, I owe you so much for helping me. I've consulted someone who says His Excellency's letter carries great weight. I'm certain to get a good post.” He was smiling broadly. “Excellent!” Hu was pleased for him. “You ought to get to Yangzhou quickly. Wait too long, and the good posts will be gone.” “Never fear. There'll be stations all along the canal and both banks of the Yangtze. There are too many posts for others to snap them all up. I'll see you back to Shanghai first, then go to Yangzhou. It'll delay me ten days at most. That's nothing.” He was clearly sincere, and Hu would still need his help on the journey, so he nodded and said no more. They talked for a while. Seeing Hu restless, Zhou hesitated. Staying might annoy him, but leaving him alone at the inn would be worse. After considering, he suggested going out for a drink to take his mind off things. “Thank you, but not today. I'm waiting for someone.” “Oh—A’qiao?” Now Zhou understood his uneasiness. “Yes. She went to her parents' home in Mudu and promised to return at noon. There's still no sign of her. I don't know what's happened.” “If she isn't here now, she won't be back today. The regular passenger boat from Mudu arrived long ago.” “She didn't take the regular boat. She hired one for the return journey.” “Then I'll inquire at the Chang Gate wharves.” Zhou stood up. “How can you inquire when we don't know which boat?” “Never mind. Once I'm there, a question will tell me.” “Of course! You know everyone at the wharves. Thank you.”

等周一鸣走不多时，忽然有个十五六岁的小后生，由金阊栈的店伙领了来见胡雪岩，自道他是潘家跑上房的书僮，奉了他家姨太太之命，“请胡老爷过去，有位堂客，要见胡老爷。”又是姨太太，又是堂客，当着店伙在那里，胡雪岩倒有些尴尬，怕引起误会，传出谣言去，总是烦恼，所以不跟那小后生答话，只向店伙说道：“你们这里，另外有位胡老爷吧？他弄错了！”“不错！”店伙答道，“他说了胡大老爷的官印，上雪下岩，我才领了来了。”“那就奇怪了。”胡雪岩对那小后生说，“苏州我没有姓潘的朋友，更不认得你家姨太太。”“原是木渎来的那位堂客要见胡老爷。”小后生说，“那位堂客是我们姨太太的要好姐妹。”“原来是阿巧姐！”胡雪岩大惑不解，“怎么不回客栈，到了你家？”“那就不清楚了。只说请胡老爷过去见面。”胡雪岩为难了。素昧平生，应人家内眷的邀请，这算是怎么回来？同时阿巧姐有何理由到了潘家？而又叫自己去相会？凡此都是疑窦。以不去为妙。

Not long after Zhou left, an inn servant brought in a boy of fifteen or sixteen. He said he was a young attendant who carried messages to the inner quarters of the Pan household. Their mistress had sent him. “Please come over, Mr Hu. A lady would like to see you.” All this talk of mistresses and ladies, with the inn servant listening, embarrassed Hu. It might cause misunderstandings and gossip—always a nuisance. Instead of answering the boy, he addressed the servant. “There's another Mr Hu staying here, isn't there? He has the wrong man.” “No mistake, sir. He gave your name, Xueyan. That's why I brought him in.” “How strange.” Hu turned to the boy. “I have no friend in Suzhou called Pan, and I certainly don't know your mistress.” “It's the lady from Mudu who wants to see you. She's a close friend of our mistress.” “So it's A’qiao!” Hu was utterly puzzled. “Why did she go to your house instead of coming back to the inn?” “I don't know. She only said to ask you to come and see her.” Hu was in a quandary. How could he accept an invitation from the womenfolk of a complete stranger? Why had A’qiao gone to the Pans', and why was she asking him to meet her there? Everything raised doubts. Better not go.

话虽如此，事情却要弄清楚，真假之间，首先要问阿巧姐，“那位木渎来的堂客，你看见了没有？”他问。“见了的。”“是怎么个样子？”那小后生把阿巧姐的身材、容貌、服饰形容了一遍，果然不错。阿巧姐在潘家这话，看来不假。有了这个了解，事情就好办了，“好的，你到外面等一下。或者去逛一逛再来，我要等个人回来见了面，才能跟你去。”说着，胡雪岩随手在茶几上抓了些零钱给他，“你去买糖吃！”“谢谢胡老爷！”小后生问道，“我歇多少时候再来？”“歇半个时辰。”

Even so, he must find out what had happened. To establish whether the story was true, the first thing was to ask about A’qiao. “Have you seen this lady from Mudu?” “Yes.” “What does she look like?” The boy described her figure, features and clothes correctly. It seemed true, then, that A’qiao was at the Pan house. With that established, the next step was easy. “Very well. Wait outside, or go for a walk and come back. I must see someone I'm expecting before I can go with you.” Hu took some small change from the tea table and gave it to him. “Go and buy yourself some sweets.” “Thank you, Mr Hu. When should I come back?” “In an hour.”

未到半个时辰，等的人到了，是周一鸣，据他打听的结果，阿巧姐的那条船，早在下午三点钟，就已到达。“这有点意思了！看起来不假。”接着，胡雪岩便将那个突如其来的邀请，说了给周一鸣听。“这其中一定有道理。阿巧姐必有不便回来的理由，胡大老爷，我陪了你去。”“你的话不错。不过我不想去，一个人不怕一万，独怕万一。”胡雪岩低声说道，“人心多险，一步错走不得。我平日做人，极为小心，不愿得罪人，但难免遭妒，有人暗中在算计我，亦未可知。别样事都好分辩，就是这种牵涉人家闺阁的事，最要远避。所以，我想请你替我去一趟。”周一鸣久历江湖，各种稀奇古怪的事都经过，心想他是怕着了“仙人跳”，顾虑得倒也有道理。自己替他去走一趟，一样也要小心，当时便点点头说：“我去！去了只把阿巧姐请出来，看她是何话说？”“对了！你问明了立刻来告诉我。”正在谈着，那小后生已转了回来。胡雪岩随便找了个不能分身的理由，来人自无话说，带着周一鸣走了。

Before the hour was up, the man he was waiting for returned. It was Zhou. His inquiries showed that A’qiao's boat had arrived as early as three that afternoon. “This is interesting. It seems the story is true.” Hu then told him about the unexpected invitation. “There must be a reason. A’qiao must have some difficulty about returning here. I'll go with you.” “You're right, but I don't want to go. It's the one chance in ten thousand that a man must fear.” Lowering his voice, Hu continued, “People can be treacherous. One wrong step may ruin everything. I'm always careful and try to offend no one, but I can't avoid jealousy. Someone may be plotting against me. Other matters can be explained. Anything involving the women's quarters of another household is best kept far away from. I'd like you to go for me.” Zhou had long experience of the world and had seen every kind of strange affair. Hu was afraid of an extortion trap involving a woman, he thought, and the concern was reasonable. He too must be careful if he went in Hu's place. He nodded. “I'll go. I'll simply ask A’qiao to come out and hear what she has to say.” “Exactly. Find out and come straight back to tell me.” As they spoke, the boy returned. Hu gave some convenient reason why he could not leave. The messenger could hardly object and took Zhou away.

这一走，过了个把时辰，才见他回来，“阿巧姐的话很多，有些事，我也弄不清楚。”周一鸣略停一停，整理一下思绪，要言不烦地说：“阿巧姐夫家派了人，从木渎跟了她到这里，看样子是来找麻烦。阿巧姐不愿回这里，就是不愿意让他们发现她落脚的地方。阿巧姐说有好些话一定要跟胡大老爷你当面谈。她怕跟来的人，在潘家附近守着，此刻不敢出门，到半夜里叫我去接了她来。”“喔！”胡雪岩深为诧异，“据我知道，她夫家老实得很。怎有此事？”这话在周一鸣无可赞一词，只这样说，“反正见了面就知道了。”“慢点！”胡雪岩双目炯炯，神色凛然，“不能去接她！万一为人跟踪，明天告我个拐带良家妇女，这个面子我丢不起。老周，我问你，那潘家是怎么回事？”“苏州潘家有两潘，一潘是‘贵潘’，一潘是‘富潘’，阿巧姐的那一家，是富潘的同族。阿巧姐的小姐妹，是他家的姨太太，太太故世了，姨太太当家，所以能够作主，把阿巧姐留了下来往。”“潘家的男主人，叫啥？你晓得不晓得。”“不晓得。”“不晓得也不碍。”胡雪岩说，“等我去拜他家男主人，当面说明经过，把阿巧姐找了出来，就当着他家男主人谈好了。不过，这一下，要委屈你了。“这话周一鸣明白，是要他权且充任报帖的家人，这也无所谓，他很爽快地答应：“我伺候胡大老爷去。”于是雇好一顶轿子，周一鸣持着拜匣，跟随胡雪岩到了潘家。帖子一投进去，潘家的男主人莫名其妙，但他的姨太太心里明白，说了经过，方始恍然，立刻吩咐接见。

It was some two hours before Zhou returned. “A’qiao had a great deal to say. There are things I don't fully understand.” He paused to collect his thoughts, then explained briefly. “Her husband's family sent someone who followed her here from Mudu. They seem to be looking for trouble. She didn't come back because she didn't want them to discover where she's staying. She says there are many things she must discuss with you in person. She's afraid the people following her are watching near the Pans', so she dare not leave now. She wants me to fetch her at midnight.” “Oh!” Hu was deeply surprised. “As far as I know, her husband's family are very docile. How can this be?” Zhou could offer no opinion. “You'll know when you see her.” “Wait!” Hu's eyes flashed, and his expression became stern. “You mustn't fetch her. If someone follows and accuses me tomorrow of abducting a respectable married woman, I can't afford that disgrace. Old Zhou, tell me about this Pan family.” “There are two prominent Pan families in Suzhou: the ‘Noble Pans’ and the ‘Rich Pans’. This household belongs to the same clan as the Rich Pans. A’qiao's friend is the master's concubine. His principal wife has died, so the concubine runs the household. That's why she can decide to let A’qiao stay.” “What's the master's name? Do you know?” “No.” “That doesn't matter. I'll call on him and explain what has happened. Then we can ask A’qiao to come out and talk in his presence. But this will mean asking you to accept a humble role.” Zhou understood: he was to act for the moment as a servant presenting Hu's visiting card. He did not mind and readily agreed. “I'll attend you.” They hired a sedan chair. Carrying the card case, Zhou accompanied Hu to the Pan house. When the card was brought in, the master was bewildered. His concubine understood, however, and explained. Once he grasped the situation, he immediately ordered that the visitor be received.

“来得冒昧之至，”胡雪岩长揖问道：“还不曾请教台甫。”“草字叔雅。”潘叔雅说，“老兄的来意，我已经知道了。我把人请出来，你们当面谈。”“是！是！承情不尽。只是深夜打搅，万分不安。”于是潘叔雅道声：“暂且失陪。”转身入内。趁这片刻工夫，胡雪岩将潘家的客厅，打量了一番，这才讶然发现，潘家的里外大不相同，大门残旧狭隘，象个破落户，客厅中的陈设却是名贵非凡，光是壁上的字画，就让胡雪岩目眩不止，这面一堂屏条山水，四幅恰好就是“四王”，那面一堂屏条书法，四幅也恰好就是文微明的真草隶篆“四体”。另有一幅中堂，顶天立地，写的是碗大的狂草，胡雪岩除了个“一”字，其余一字不识，但这么两丈多长，七、八尺宽的一张大宣纸，就够他发半天的愣了。

“This is a most presumptuous visit,” Hu Xueyan said with a deep bow. “May I have the honour of your name?” “My courtesy name is Shuya,” Pan replied. “I already know why you have come. I'll ask her to join you so that you can speak face to face.” “Thank you, thank you. I'm most grateful, and very sorry to disturb you so late.” “Excuse me for a moment.” Pan Shuya turned and went inside. Hu took the opportunity to examine the reception room and was astonished by the difference between the house's exterior and interior. The narrow, worn entrance suggested a family in decline, yet the furnishings were extraordinarily valuable. The pictures and calligraphy alone dazzled him. A set of four landscape scrolls on one wall represented the “Four Wangs,” one apiece. On another wall hung four calligraphic scrolls by Wen Zhengming, covering all four scripts: regular, cursive, clerical, and seal. There was also an enormous central scroll stretching from ceiling to floor, covered in wild cursive characters as big as bowls. Apart from the character for “one,” Hu could not read a thing. But the sheer size of the sheet of xuan paper, over two zhang long and seven or eight chi wide, was enough to leave him staring.

“胡老爷，请用点心！”一个穿着极整洁的蓝布大褂的听差，捧来了一只银盒，盒子凿成一朵梅花，花蒂就是把手。揭开来看，里面是五只细瓷碟子，盛着五样点心，红、绿、黄、黑、白俱备，颜色极艳，胡雪岩只认得红的是玫瑰年糕，拿起银镶牙筷，拈了一块放在嘴里，滑糯香甜，其味弥甘，但却不是玫瑰的味道。“这是拿啥做的？”“是拿桃子汁在粉里蒸的。”这在胡雪岩可说闻所未闻，只有叹一声：“你们府上真讲究！”听差矜持的微笑着，退后两步，悄悄侍立。胡雪岩一面进食，一面在想：等将来发了大财，总要比这潘家更讲究，做人才有意思。

“Mr Hu, please have some refreshments.” A servant in an exceptionally neat blue cotton gown brought a silver box wrought in the shape of a plum blossom, its stalk forming the handle. Beneath the lid were five fine porcelain dishes, each with a different delicacy. Red, green, yellow, black, and white were all represented in brilliant colour. Hu recognised only the red one, which he took for rose-flavoured New Year cake. Using ivory chopsticks mounted in silver, he lifted a piece to his mouth. Smooth, glutinous, fragrant, and sweet, it grew more delicious as he tasted it—but the flavour was not rose. “What is this made with?” “Peach juice mixed into the flour and steamed.” Hu had never heard of such a thing. “Your household certainly knows how to do things finely!” The servant smiled with restraint, stepped back two paces, and stood silently by. As Hu ate, he thought that when he made a great fortune, he must live even more exquisitely than the Pans. That would make life worth living.

正在仰慕不已，胡思乱想的当儿。 听得屏风后面，有了人声，抬眼看时，正是阿巧姐由个丫头陪着走了出来。一见面就说：“我等你好久了。”请这面坐吧！“听差十分知趣，将他们两人引到靠里的炕床上，端来了盖碗茶，随即向那丫头使个眼色，都退到了廊下。“怎么回事？”胡雪岩问，“回一趟娘家，搞出很大的麻烦！早知如此，倒不如我叫老周陪了你去。”“陪了去也没用。事情很奇怪……”奇的是就在阿巧姐回去的前一天，有人寻到阿巧姐的夫家，直言相告，说是受阿巧姐的委托，来谈如何了结他们这层名存实亡的夫妇关系。如果愿意休妻另娶，可以好好送一笔钱。阿巧姐的丈夫很老实，不知何以为答，但他有个堂房哥哥，名叫小狗子，却是个喜欢搅是非的坏蛋，一看奇货可居，当时便表示：一切都好谈。但要阿巧姐亲自出面料理。来人一再探询口风，小狗子说是只想要个两三百银子。“是假话！小狗子的打算，是要骗我到家，好敲人家的竹杠。偏偏我第二天就回家，亏得消息来得早，所以小狗子来叫我，我不肯回去。我娘也叫我早早走。”阿巧姐接着又说：“哪知道小狗子带了两个地痞，弄了只船跟了下来。我一看这情形，不敢回客栈，同时关照船老大，不可说破是金阊栈代雇的船。上了岸，雇顶小轿，一直抬到这潘府上，还不晓得小狗子知道不知道我在这里？“

In the midst of his admiration and wandering thoughts, he heard voices behind the screen. Looking up, he saw A’qiao approaching with a maid. “I've been waiting so long for you,” she said at once. “Please sit over here.” The tactful servant led them to a couch farther inside, brought covered bowls of tea, and gave the maid a glance. Both withdrew to the veranda. “What's happened?” Hu asked. “One visit to your family, and all this trouble! If I'd known, I'd have sent Zhou with you.” “That wouldn't have helped. It's very strange...” The strange thing was that on the day before A’qiao returned, someone had called at her husband's home and announced openly that she had sent him to discuss ending their marriage, which now existed only in name. If her husband was willing to divorce her and marry again, he could receive a substantial payment. Her husband was an honest, simple man and did not know what to say. But an elder cousin on his father's side, called Xiaogouzi, was a scoundrel who enjoyed stirring up trouble. Seeing a valuable opportunity, he immediately said that everything could be discussed, but A’qiao must come and settle it herself. The visitor repeatedly sounded him out, and Xiaogouzi said that he wanted only two or three hundred taels. “A lie! He meant to lure me home and use me to extort money from someone. As luck would have it, I came back the very next day. Fortunately, word reached me in time. When he came to fetch me, I refused to go. My mother told me to leave quickly too. Who would have thought he'd get a boat and follow me down with two local ruffians? When I saw that, I daren't return to the inn. I warned the boatman not to reveal that Jinchang Inn had hired his boat for me. I went ashore, hired a little sedan chair, and came straight here. I still don't know whether Xiaogouzi knows I'm here.”

胡雪岩一面听，一面深深点头，等她说完，主意也就定了，“你做得好！”他说，“不要紧，我来料理。”“你怎么样料理？”“这家的姨太太，跟你的交情厚不厚？”“从小在一起的姐妹。‘阿巧姐答道：”交情不厚，我也不会投到这里来了。“那好！”胡雪岩欣慰地，“你就先住在这里。多住几日。”阿巧姐大感意外，“多住几日？”她皱眉问道：“住到几时？”胡雪岩的意思，最好住到何桂清动身北上的时节。但这话此时不便说，而且一时也说不清楚。再又想到，虽然阿巧姐跟人家的交情甚厚，只是当居停的，到底不是正主人，作客的身分也有些尴尬，主客双方，都有难处，短时勾留，还无所谓，住长了要防人说闲话。“这样吧！”胡雪岩说，“见事行事。你在这里打搅人家，我自然有一番意思。明天就备一笔礼来，若是她家男主人好意相留，你就住下去，不然另想别法。”

Hu nodded gravely as he listened. By the time she finished, his mind was made up. “You did the right thing. Don't worry. I'll handle it.” “How?” “Are you very close to the concubine in this house?” “We've been friends since we were children. I wouldn't have come to her if we weren't close.” “Good!” Hu was relieved. “Then stay here for the present. Stay a few more days.” A’qiao was surprised. “A few more days?” She frowned. “Until when?” Hu would have preferred her to remain until He Guiqing left for the north, but this was neither the moment to say so nor something he could easily explain. Then he considered that, close though the women were, her hostess was not the household's principal mistress. A’qiao's position as a guest was awkward too. Both sides had their difficulties. A brief visit was harmless; a long stay might invite gossip. “Let's proceed as circumstances suggest,” he said. “If you're imposing on them here, naturally I must show my appreciation. I'll send a gift tomorrow. If the master of the house kindly invites you to remain, stay on. Otherwise we'll find another way.”

“住下去倒没有什么。我只是问你，要住到哪一天？”阿巧姐又说，“我也知道你上海事情多，最多三两天就要回去，莫非把我一个人撇在这里？”“当然不会！”胡雪岩说，“我另有安排……”“啥安排？”阿巧姐抢着问，神气极其认真。若是别人，看她这样咄咄逼人，会觉得招架不住，胡雪岩自然不会，“你不要着急，自然是极妥当的安排。”他接着又说：“长话短说，我让你住在这里，不让你回客栈，就是不想落把柄在小狗子手里。回头我就要去打听，到那里去的人是什么人？”“对！这要去打听。”阿巧姐说，“在船上我一直想不通，为啥要冒我的名，说我托他们去谈的？莫非是我认识的人？”这句话提醒了胡雪岩，念头象闪电一般从心里划过，十有八、九是尤五和古应春搞的把戏，自己曾经跟他们说过，请他们听自己的招呼行事，暂时不必插手，果然，不听自己的话，弄巧成拙，反惹出意外的麻烦。不过，他也知道阿巧姐此时心神不定，不宜多说，便即答道：“你不必瞎猜。一切有我。这件事办得顺利的话也很快，说不定明后天就可以水落石出。你先安心在这里玩几天，我把你的衣箱送过来。”

“There's no difficulty about staying. I only want to know until what day. You've so much to do in Shanghai that you'll have to go back in two or three days at most. Surely you don't mean to leave me here alone?” “Of course not. I have other arrangements...” “What arrangements?” she interrupted, intensely serious. Another man might have felt unable to withstand her persistent questioning, but not Hu. “Don't be anxious. Naturally, the arrangements will be perfectly satisfactory.” He continued, “To put it briefly, I'm keeping you here rather than bringing you back to the inn because I don't want to give Xiaogouzi anything to use against us. Next I'll find out who visited your husband's family.” “Yes, you must find out. All the way on the boat I kept wondering why they had used my name and said I'd asked them to negotiate. Could it have been someone I know?” Her words struck Hu like a flash of lightning. Almost certainly this was You and Gu's doing. He had told them to wait for his instructions and keep out of the matter for the present. They must have disregarded him, and their cleverness had backfired, producing unexpected trouble. But he knew A’qiao was unsettled and ought not to be told too much just then. “Don't go guessing. Leave everything to me. If this goes smoothly, it may be settled very quickly. Perhaps everything will be clear by tomorrow or the day after. Stay here a few days with an easy mind. I'll send your clothes trunk over.”

“那倒不必。我跟我那小姐妹，身材相仿，她的衣服多得穿不完，不过，”阿巧姐又提到那话：“这总也要说个日子，到底住多少天？我也好安心，人家问起来，我也有话好答。”“那……”胡雪岩心想，看样子到端午前后，何桂清动身的那时候，是不可能的了，既然如此，就早些了结这事，所以盘算了一会，很爽快地答道：“三天！第四天我准定来接你。”阿巧姐很满意，却又叮嘱了一句：“你可记在心里！”“不会忘忆！”说着，他从身上摇出一大叠银票来，捡了几张小数目的递了过去，“这里二百两银子，你留着用。在人家这里作客，小钱不要省，下人该当开发的，都要开发。出手也不可以小气。懂吧？”阿巧姐如何不懂？点点头说：“你放心好了，我不会丢你的面子。”

“There's no need. My friend and I are much the same size, and she has more clothes than she can wear. But...” A’qiao returned to her point. “You must give me a day. How long exactly am I to stay? Then I can be at ease and have an answer if they ask.” “Well...” Hu saw that keeping her here until He Guiqing left, around the Dragon Boat Festival, would be impossible. In that case, he should settle the matter sooner. After considering briefly, he answered decisively, “Three days. On the fourth day I'll certainly come to fetch you.” She was satisfied, but added, “Do remember!” “I won't forget.” He took out a thick sheaf of banknotes and selected several of smaller denominations. “Here are two hundred taels for your expenses. While you're a guest here, don't stint over small sums. Give the servants whatever gratuities are appropriate, and don't be mean about it. Understand?” Of course she understood. She nodded. “Don't worry. I won't let you lose face.”

于是胡雪岩请见主人，道谢告辞，等周一鸣陪着回到金阊栈，他把他留了下来，细谈究竟。这段经过，前因后果，相当曲折，即令胡雪岩把不必说出的话，隐去了许多，仍旧使周一鸣听得津津有味，而且磨拳擦掌，大有跃跃欲试之意。“乡下土流氓搞不出什么把戏，等我打发他们走。”“人都还不知道在哪里，你先别忙！”胡雪岩说，“我们商量好再动手。只是摆脱这两个人，事情好办，我要跟小狗子打交道。““喔！”周一鸣把心定下来，因为看样子还有许多花样，且等听了再说。“我现在又要叫小狗子晓得厉害，又要他感激。你倒想个办法看。”这是个难题，胡雪岩原有借此考一考周一鸣的意思。他好好考虑了一会，出了一个主意，胡雪岩认为可行，当天就开始动手。

Hu then asked to see the host, thanked him, and took his leave. Back at Jinchang Inn, he kept Zhou Yiming with him and explained the situation in detail. The story was complicated, with many twists of cause and consequence. Even though Hu omitted much that did not need telling, Zhou listened with relish and rubbed his hands, eager to take part. “Country ruffians can't manage much. Let me send them packing.” “We don't even know where they are. Don't rush,” Hu said. “Let's agree on a plan before acting. Getting rid of those two fellows would be easy enough. It's Xiaogouzi I want to deal with.” “Oh!” Zhou settled down to listen. Apparently, there was more to come. “I want to teach Xiaogouzi a lesson and make him grateful to me as well. See if you can think of a way.” This was a difficult problem, and Hu had partly intended it as a test. After careful thought, Zhou proposed a plan. Hu considered it workable, and they began preparations that day.

第一步是去打听这两个人，乡下人到底是乡下人，不脱泥土气，所以第二天一早，周一鸣很快地在潘家附近找到了。潘家的巷口就是一爿俗称“老虎灶”的小茶店，光顾这里的茶客，大多是附近的平民，一到先自己取了木脸盆舀水洗脸漱口，相互招呼，然后吃茶吃点心，高谈阔论，只有坐在门口饶饼摊子后面那张桌子上，土里土气，贼头贼脑的两个茶客，不但不跟人招呼，而且两双眼睛只盯着过往行人，特别是看见堂客，更为注意，这就相当明显了。“小狗子！”周一鸣冒叫一声。小狗子哪知道“螳螂捕蝉，黄雀在后”，听得声音，转脸来看，看到同一鸣含笑注视，便即问道：“是你叫我？”“是啊！哪一天进城来的？”“昨……昨天。”小狗子嗫嚅着说，“我不认识你。”“怎么会不认得我？”周一鸣也做出困惑的神色，“我倒请问，你是不是家住木渎？”“是的。”“那就对了！”周一鸣以极有把握的声音说：“你贵人多忘事，认不得我，我是不会记错的。我们上一次吃过‘讲茶’，我那朋友多亏你帮忙。”这又是周一鸣瞎扯，料准象小狗子这样的人，少不得有吃讲茶、讲斤头的行径，所以放心大胆撒谎。小狗子不知是计，想了想问：“你的朋友是哪个？”“姓王。”“喔，”小狗子说：“想来是王胖子的朋友。不错，王胖子调戏刘二寡妇，挨了耳光，是我帮他叫开的。王胖子现在还好吧！”“还不错，还不错！”周一鸣顺口回答，“他常常提到你，说你小狗子够朋友。来，来，我做个吃点心的小东。”说着便向烧饼摊子高声吩咐：“拿蟹壳黄、油包来！”

The first step was to locate the two men. Country people were country people, with a rustic air they could not shed, and early the next morning Zhou found them near the Pan house without much difficulty. At the mouth of the Pans' lane stood a little tea shop of the kind popularly called a “tiger stove.” Its customers were mostly ordinary people from the neighbourhood. On arriving, they took a wooden basin and scooped up water to wash their faces and rinse their mouths, greeted one another, then drank tea, ate snacks, and talked loudly. Only two furtive, rustic-looking customers, sitting at the table behind the flatbread stall by the entrance, greeted no one. Their eyes followed every passer-by, paying particular attention to women. The signs were plain enough. “Xiaogouzi!” Zhou called out on a guess. Xiaogouzi had no idea that, while the mantis stalked the cicada, an oriole waited behind it. He turned and found Zhou smiling at him. “Were you calling me?” “Yes. When did you come into town?” “Yester... yesterday.” Xiaogouzi faltered. “I don't know you.” “How can you not know me?” Zhou looked puzzled too. “Let me ask: don't you live in Mudu?” “Yes.” “Then that's right.” Zhou sounded utterly certain. “An important man forgets easily. You may not recognise me, but I can't be mistaken. We once attended a dispute-settling tea meeting together. You were a great help to my friend.” This was another fabrication. Zhou reckoned that a man like Xiaogouzi was bound to have taken part in such meetings and settlements, so he lied boldly. Suspecting no trick, Xiaogouzi considered. “Which friend?” “His surname is Wang.” “Oh! You must be Fat Wang's friend. Yes, he got slapped for making advances to Widow Liu, and I intervened for him. How is he now?” “Quite well, quite well,” Zhou answered readily. “He often mentions you and says what a loyal friend you are. Come, let me treat you to a little breakfast.” He called to the stall, “Bring some crab-shell pastries and oil buns!”

“不好意思，不好意思。”小狗子一面说话，一面眼睛朝外看，街上走过一个女人，后影极俏，象极了阿巧姐。这等于自画供状，周一鸣心里好笑，便根本不拿他当个对手，等那条俏影消失，小狗子怏怏地收拢目光，脸上并现懊恼与疑惑之色，周一鸣便单刀直入问道：“小狗子，你在等人？”“不是，不是！”“那个女的，”周一鸣遥遥一指，“后影好熟，好象在哪里见过？”小狗子怎想得到是有意逗他？惊喜交集地问：“你……啊，说了半天，看我荒唐不荒唐？还没有请教你老哥尊姓？”周一鸣因为藐视他的缘故，便懒得改姓，照实答道：“敝姓周。”“喔，周大哥，刚才过去的那个女人，你也觉得象是认识的？”“是啊！”周一鸣说：“好象木渎见过，也好象在上海见过。”他摇摇头：“记不得了！”这番做作，把小狗子骗得死心塌地，当时先不忙跟周一鸣答话，向他的同伴叫了声：“老吴！”接着向外努一努嘴。那个老吴便飞奔而去，周一鸣越发匿笑不已。“小狗子，”他放低了声音说：“你们在钉人的梢？”他又用关切的神色，提出警告：“苏州城里，不比乡下，尤其是这年把，总督、巡抚、总兵，多少红顶子大官儿在这里，你们要当心。”“这……”小狗子嗫嚅着，“不要紧的！是熟人。”“什么熟人？说刚才那个女的是熟人？”“是的。”小狗子觉得周一鸣见多识广，而且也说了相熟，便不再隐瞒：“周大哥，你说在木渎，在上海见过都不错。说起名字，你恐怕晓得，叫阿巧！”

“You shouldn't trouble yourself,” Xiaogouzi said, but his eyes kept turning outside. A woman was passing whose graceful figure from behind looked very much like A’qiao's. It was as good as writing his own confession. Zhou laughed inwardly and ceased to regard him as any sort of opponent. When the figure disappeared, Xiaogouzi reluctantly looked back, his face showing both annoyance and doubt. Zhou went straight to the point. “Are you waiting for someone?” “No, no!” “That woman...” Zhou pointed into the distance. “Her back looks so familiar. Where have I seen her?” Xiaogouzi could not imagine that he was being deliberately baited. Surprised and delighted, he began, “You... Ah, how foolish of me! We've been talking all this time and I haven't asked your surname.” Holding him in such contempt, Zhou could not even be bothered to invent one. “Zhou.” “Brother Zhou, you too thought you recognised that woman who just passed?” “Yes. I seem to have seen her in Mudu, and perhaps in Shanghai too.” He shook his head. “I can't remember.” This performance deceived Xiaogouzi completely. Rather than reply, he called to his companion, “Old Wu!” and jerked his chin towards the street. Old Wu dashed off, leaving Zhou still more amused. Lowering his voice, Zhou asked, “Are you following someone?” With an air of concern, he warned him, “Suzhou isn't the countryside, especially this past year or so. The governor-general, governor, military commander—there are any number of great officials with red hat buttons here. You'd better be careful.” “Well...” Xiaogouzi faltered. “It's nothing. Someone we know.” “Who? Do you mean that woman?” “Yes.” Thinking Zhou worldly and experienced, and remembering his claim to know her too, Xiaogouzi stopped concealing the truth. “You're right about both Mudu and Shanghai. Perhaps you'll know her name. She's called A’qiao.”

听得这话，周一鸣又有番做作，把腰一直，脸微微向后，眼略略下垂，好半晌才说：“我道是哪个，是在长三堂子里的阿巧！怪不得背影好熟。”“对，对！周大哥，你也晓得的，她在堂子里。”小狗子更觉需要解释，赶紧又说：“那都是她娘家不好，她是私下从夫家逃出的，做出这种事来，害得夫家没面子，真正气数。”“那你现在钉她的梢，所为何来？想捉她回去？”“也不是捉她，她不守妇道，想劝她回去。”“这，小狗子，不是我说一句，真正你们苏州人的俗语：”鼻头上挂咸鱼——臭鲞，‘这种人怎么劝得醒？“小狗子点点头，想开口却又把话咽了回去。周一鸣明白，这就到了要紧关头了。他原来定的计划是，找好“班房”里一个跑腿的小伙计，托他找个同事，两个人弄条链子，弄副手铐，等自己探明了小狗子的住处，“硬装榫头”，随便安上他一个罪名，先抓到班房里，然后胡雪岩拿着何桂清留经他的致长洲知县的名片去保他出来。这就是既叫小狗子知道厉害，又要他感激的手法。而照现在来看，根本无需这样子大动干戈，直截了当谈判就行了。对小狗子这面，毫无疑问，周一鸣认为“搓得圆、拉得长”，要他成什么样子，就什么样子，极有把握，但在胡雪岩那方面不能没有顾忌，他觉得自己无论就身分、交情来说，替他办事，还没有能够到自作主张，独断独行的程度。自己只不过为胡雪岩奔走，他怎么说，自己怎么做，能把他的交代完全办到，便是最圆满的事。不听他的话做，即使效果超过预期，依然会使得胡雪岩有“此人不可靠”的感觉，因为不听话即是不易控驭。

Zhou put on another performance. Straightening his back, drawing his face a little away, and lowering his eyes, he paused for some time. “So that's who it is! A’qiao from the high-class courtesan house. No wonder her back looked familiar.” “Yes, yes! Brother Zhou, you know she's at one of those houses.” Feeling a further explanation necessary, Xiaogouzi hurried on. “It's all her own family's fault. She ran away secretly from her husband's home. Carrying on like that has disgraced his family. What rotten luck!” “Why are you following her now? To catch her and take her back?” “Not catch her. She's neglected her duties as a wife. We want to persuade her to return.” “Xiaogouzi, if I may say so, this is just like your Suzhou saying: ‘Hang a salted fish under your nose—smell it, but forget your hopes.’ How can you expect to talk sense into someone like that?” Xiaogouzi nodded, opened his mouth, then swallowed his words. Zhou knew they had reached the critical point. His original plan had been to find a young runner from the detention quarters and have him recruit a colleague. With a chain and a pair of handcuffs, they would wait until Zhou discovered Xiaogouzi's lodging, then pin some arbitrary charge on him and haul him into custody. Hu would then use the visiting card He Guiqing had given him for the magistrate of Changzhou County to secure Xiaogouzi's release. That was how they meant to frighten him and make him grateful as well. Now it seemed there was no need for such elaborate measures: direct negotiation would suffice. Zhou had no doubt he could mould Xiaogouzi like dough, round or long, into whatever shape he wanted. But he had to consider Hu. Neither his standing nor the closeness of their acquaintance entitled him to act independently. He was merely running errands: Hu gave instructions, and he followed them. Carrying them out exactly was the best possible result. If he disobeyed, even an outcome better than expected could make Hu think him unreliable, because a man who would not obey was a man difficult to control.

为此，他改了主意，“小狗子，各人有各人的事，我也不来多问。”他略停一停说，“今天也是凑巧，我有个机会可以发笔小财，不过这件事我自己一个人做不成，正好路过看见你，想邀你做个帮手，不知道你有空没空。”话甚突兀，小狗子一时不知如何回答？有钱进帐的事，自然求之不得，但第一要看他的话靠得靠不住，第二要看自己做得了做不了？所以先要问个清楚才能打主意。“周大哥，你挑我，我自然没话说。是怎么回事，好不好请你先说一说？”“说来话长。看你现在心神不定，我也还有点事要去办，这样，”周一鸣故意做个沉吟的神情，然后语声很急地问道：“你住在哪里，中午我来看你。”“我住在阊门外一个朋友那里。”小狗子又说，“中午不见得回去。”“那么，我们中午约在哪里碰头好了。我请你吃酒，把你的朋友老吴也带来。”“好的。”小狗子毫不迟疑地答道：“你约地方好了。哪个请哪个，自己弟兄都一样的。”“对！我们准定中午在观前街元大昌碰头。先到先等，不见不散。”说定了，周一鸣先走，他很细心，没有忘了先到烧饼摊上付了点心钱。

For this reason, Zhou changed course. “Everyone has his own affairs, Xiaogouzi. I won't ask any more.” He paused. “It's a coincidence, but I have a chance to make a little money today. I can't manage it alone. Passing by and seeing you, I thought I'd ask you to help. Have you any time?” The proposal came so abruptly that Xiaogouzi did not know how to answer. Of course he welcomed any chance to make money. But first he must decide whether Zhou could be trusted, and second whether he could do the job. He needed an explanation before making up his mind. “If you've chosen me, Brother Zhou, naturally I'm willing. But what's involved? Could you tell me first?” “It's a long story. You're distracted at the moment, and I have something else to do. Let's see...” Zhou pretended to consider, then asked urgently, “Where are you staying? I'll call at noon.” “With a friend outside Chang Gate. But I may not go back at noon.” “Then let's arrange somewhere to meet. I'll invite you for a drink. Bring your friend Old Wu.” “Good.” Xiaogouzi agreed without hesitation. “You choose the place. We're brothers; it makes no difference who treats whom.” “Exactly. Yuandachang on Guanqian Street, at noon sharp. Whoever arrives first waits. We must meet.” With this settled, Zhou left first. He was careful enough not to forget to pay the stall for their breakfast.

然后匆匆奔到吴苑茶店，这是昨晚上约好了的，胡雪岩在那里等他。“这个小狗子，两眼墨黑，啥也不懂！居然想来寻这种外快，真正叫自不量力！”周一鸣得意地细讲了发现小狗子的经过，然后又说：“杀鸡焉用牛刀？”这种样子，胡大老爷你也犯不着费心了，有话跟他实说就是。本来我就想跟他打开天窗说亮话的，不过是胡大老爷的事，我不敢擅专。““不敢，不敢！”胡雪岩对周一鸣很满意，所以也很客气，拱着手说；“你帮我的这个忙，帮得不小。”“哪里的话？胡大老爷，你不必说客气话。”周一鸣很恳切地答道，“该当怎么办，你尽管吩咐，我去跑。”“你的办法已经很好了。能够就在这一两天内办妥当了，说句实话，是意想不到的顺利。你中午去赴约，约了他到我客栈里，我们一起跟他谈。不过，那个姓吴的，最好把他撇开。”“这容易。我自有法子。”“还有件事，很要紧。”胡雪岩略想一想说：“不管它了，我自己去办，你就只管约了小狗子来，只要约到，以下都是我的事。”“只要约到”四个字，等于提醒周一鸣，小狗子可能心生疑惑，有意爽约。那在胡雪岩面上就不好交代了。

He hurried to Wuyuan Tea House, where Hu was waiting by arrangement from the previous night. “That Xiaogouzi is completely in the dark. He knows nothing! To think he'd try making money this way—he has no idea of his own limits.” Zhou proudly described how he had found him, then added, “Why use an ox-cleaver to kill a chicken? A fellow like that isn't worth your trouble. We need only tell him straight. I'd meant to speak plainly on the spot, but since it was your business, I didn't dare take the decision myself.” “You do me too much honour.” Well pleased, Hu responded with equal courtesy, clasping his hands. “You've done me a great favour.” “Not at all. No need for formalities, Mr Hu,” Zhou answered earnestly. “Just tell me what should be done, and I'll do the legwork.” “Your method is excellent already. To settle it within a day or two would be easier than I could have expected, to tell the truth. Keep your noon appointment, then bring him to my inn so we can talk together. It would be best to leave the man named Wu out of it.” “Easy enough. I'll find a way.” “There's one more thing, and it's important.” Hu thought briefly. “Never mind. I'll do it myself. Just bring Xiaogouzi. Once you've got him there, leave the rest to me.” Those words reminded Zhou that Xiaogouzi might grow suspicious and deliberately fail to appear. Then he would have no satisfactory account to give Hu.

于是周一鸣不暇多说，匆匆出了金阊栈，为求快速，赁了一匹供游客逛山用的马，认镫扳鞍，跨上马背，将缰绳一带朝城里走。“喂，喂，客人，你到哪里？”赁马的马伕赶紧抢着嚼环，仰脸问说。这些马照例有马伕带路，而马是跑熟了路的，出行之时，一步踏一步，到归途回槽，撒开四蹄，却又不大相同。马都是上了岁数的，实在也快不到哪里去，而且除却逛山，从不进城，所以马伕要那样诧异地问。周一鸣原晓得这些规矩，一看不能通融，便很简捷地说：“我要进城，你赁不赁？不赁我就下来。”“做生意哪有不赁之理。不过……”周一鸣没有工夫跟他多磨，跳下马来将缰绳一丢，掉头就走。这态度就不大好了，而那马伕也是有脾气的，当时便吐一口唾沫，自言自语的骂道：“真叫气数！碰着‘老爷’哉！”苏州话的“老爷”，用在这里当鬼解释，周一鸣正因赁马不成，惹了一肚子气，此时怒不可遏，转过身来，抢上两步，戟指喝道：“你骂谁？”那马伕一看来势汹汹，便有惧意，但“苏州人打架”的那副工架是出了名的，一面用怎么样也硬不起来的苏州话，连声警告：“耐要那哼？耐要那哼？”一面倒退着揎拳捋袖、捞衣襟、盘辫子，仿佛要拼个你死我活似地。苏州人又最好看热闹，顿时围了一圈人，那马伕有本地人助威，声音便高了，用极快的苏州话指责周一鸣不通人性，即令是吵架，也忘不了说几句俏皮话，于是看热闹的人丛中，便有了笑声。周一鸣此时处境甚窘，他倒不是畏惧，而是怕闹得不可开交，误了小狗子的约会，便误了胡雪岩的要紧事，心里颇为失悔，却苦干找不到一个台阶可下。

Without further talk, Zhou hurried out of Jinchang Inn. To save time, he hired one of the horses used for excursions into the hills, set his foot in the stirrup, swung into the saddle, and turned it towards the city. “Hey, sir! Where are you going?” The groom hurried to catch the bridle and looked up at him. These horses normally went out with a groom leading the way, and knew the route thoroughly. They advanced one slow step at a time on the outward journey, but moved very differently when home and their feed troughs were in sight. All were old, so none could go particularly fast. They were used only for hill excursions and never entered the city. Hence the groom's astonishment. Zhou knew the rules. Seeing that no exception would be made, he said curtly, “I'm going into town. Will you hire it to me or not? If not, I'll get down.” “I'm in business. Why wouldn't I? Only...” With no time for discussion, Zhou jumped down, tossed away the reins, and turned to go. His manner was poor, and the groom had a temper too. Spitting on the ground, he muttered, “Rotten luck! I've met a ‘master’ today.” In this use of Suzhou speech, “master” meant a ghost or devil. Zhou was already furious at failing to hire the horse. Now he could contain himself no longer. Turning, he strode back two paces and pointed. “Who are you cursing?” Alarmed by this menacing approach, the groom was afraid. Yet the elaborate preparations of Suzhou men for a fight were famous. In a dialect that would never sound fierce, he repeatedly demanded, “What d'you want? What d'you want?” while backing away, baring his fists, rolling his sleeves, gathering his skirts, and winding up his queue as though preparing for a fight to the death. Suzhou people also loved a spectacle, and a ring of onlookers soon formed. Encouraged by the support of his fellow townsmen, the groom raised his voice and accused Zhou of behaving unreasonably in rapid Suzhou speech. Even in a quarrel he remembered to add a few witticisms, which drew laughter from the crowd. Zhou was now in an awkward position. He was not afraid, but feared becoming so entangled that he would miss Xiaogouzi and spoil Hu's important business. He regretted his conduct but could find no way to retreat with dignity.

幸好，有了救星，是胡雪岩，“老周，”他从人背后挤了出来，问道，“跟他吵什么？”“为了赶辰光，想赁匹马进城，这家伙的马，要拣地方走的，那就算了！‘买卖不成仁义在’，用不着骂人。““哪个骂人？”马伕也抢上来分辩，却让胡雪岩止住了。“ ‘相骂无好口’，谁是谁非，不必再辩。我只问你，耽误了你的生意没有。”“就耽误了生意，也只好我认倒霉。”“那就没话可说了。”胡雪岩说：“你赶快招呼你的生意去吧！”说着，他把周一鸣一拉，掉臂而出，也不必劝解，更不必追问，两个人雇了两顶轿子抬进城，在观前下轿，重新约一约时间，准定正午在金阊栈见面，然后分手，各去干各的。

Fortunately, help arrived in the shape of Hu. Pushing through the spectators, he asked, “Zhou, why are you quarrelling with him?” “I wanted a horse to get into town quickly. His horses are particular about where they'll go. Very well! Even if a bargain falls through, civility remains. There's no need to curse me.” “Who cursed you?” The groom hurried forward to argue, but Hu stopped him. “No one speaks pleasantly in a quarrel. There's no need to debate who's right. I ask only this: has he cost you any business?” “Even if he has, I'll have to put it down to bad luck.” “Then there's nothing more to say. Go and attend to your customers.” Taking Zhou by the arm, Hu walked away. There was no need for further soothing or questions. They hired two sedan chairs into the city, got out at Guanqian, fixed their meeting at Jinchang Inn for noon precisely, and separated to attend to their respective tasks.

胡雪岩本想去找“炉房”，一打听地方远得很，只好找钱庄，踏进一家门面很象样的“永兴盛”，开口便问：“有没有刚出炉的‘官宝’。”官宝就是五十两一个的大元宝，由藩库监视熔铸，专备解京及其他公用，所以称作“官宝”。钱庄不见得有刚出炉的官宝，但可以到炉房去兑换，甚至现铸，只要顾客愿意“贴水”，无不办到。永兴盛有个伙计，架子甚大，双手分开成个八字，撑在柜台上，歪着头问：“要多少？”“要二十个。”二十个就是一千两银子，那伙计拿过算盘来，滴沥搭拉打了几下，算出贴水的银数，然后说道：“要下午才有。”“我有急用，另贴车费，拜托代办一办。”于是又说定所贴的车费，胡雪岩付出一大一小两张阜康的“即票”，那伙计斜睨着说：“这票子我们不收。”“为什么？”“信用靠不住。”如果说跟阜康没有往来，不知道它的虚实，不便收受，胡雪岩倒也无话可说。说阜康“信用靠不住”，近于诬蔑，他不由得气往上冲，伸手入怀，取出一大叠银票，其中有鼎鼎大名的京师“四大恒”，以及总号设在汉口、分号二十余处的“日升昌”的票子，预备拿到柜台上，叫他自己挑一张。手已经摸到银票了，转念一想，不必如此，便忍住了怒气问道：“宝号可出银票？”“当然。”“那好。”胡雪岩问道：“如果是宝号的本票，自然是顶靠得住了？”“那还用说吗？你有多少，我们兑多少。”“我没有。既然宝号不肯收阜康的票子，我只好到别家了。”胡雪岩拱拱手说：“对不起，对不起！”

Hu had intended to find a silver foundry, but inquiries showed it was too far away. He would have to use a bank instead. Entering Yongxingsheng, whose premises looked suitably imposing, he asked at once, “Have you any official ingots fresh from the mould?” These were large ingots of fifty taels each, cast under the supervision of the provincial treasury for remittances to the capital and other official purposes, hence their name. A bank might not have newly cast ones on hand, but could exchange for them at a foundry or even have them made. Anything was possible if the customer would pay the premium. A clerk at Yongxingsheng, full of his own importance, braced his hands wide apart on the counter, tilted his head, and asked, “How many?” “Twenty.” Twenty meant a thousand taels. The clerk pulled over an abacus, rattled through the calculation of the premium, and said, “Not until this afternoon.” “I need them urgently. I'll pay extra for transport. Please arrange it.” They agreed on that charge too, and Hu handed over two Fukang notes payable on demand, one large and one small. The clerk gave them a sidelong look. “We don't accept those notes.” “Why?” “Their credit is unreliable.” Had he said they had no dealings with Fukang and could not accept its notes because they knew nothing of its position, Hu would have had no objection. But to call its credit unreliable was close to slander. Anger rose in him. He reached inside his gown for his thick sheaf of notes, which included those of the capital's celebrated “Four Hengs” and Rishengchang, with its head office in Hankou and more than twenty branches. He meant to put them on the counter and let the man choose. His hand had already touched them when he reconsidered. There was no need. Suppressing his anger, he asked, “Does your bank issue notes?” “Of course.” “Good. Its own notes must be perfectly reliable, then?” “Need you ask? Bring as many as you like. We'll redeem them all.” “I have none. Since you won't accept Fukang's, I must go elsewhere.” Hu clasped his hands. “My apologies.”

出了永兴盛，觉得这口气真咽不下去，最好马上就能报复，但这不是咄嗟可办的事，只得暂且丢开，先另找一家钱号，兑换了二十个官宝，托那家钱庄派一名“出店”送到了金阊栈。也不过刚刚把银子堆好，周一鸣陪着小狗子到了，引见以后，胡雪岩开门见山地说：“我是阿巧姐的客人，她托我替她来说句话，如果他夫家肯放她，她愿意出一千两银子，让她丈夫另外攀亲，还可以买几亩田，日子很可以过得去了。我听老周说，这件事有你‘轧脚’在内，‘皇帝不差饿兵’，我替阿巧姐作主送你一百两银子。你看如何？”这番话说得很明白，而小狗子仍有突兀之感，最叫他困惑的是，这个自称是王胖子的朋友、曾经一起吃过讲茶的“周大哥”，何以会把自己的底细，摸得这么清楚？因此，看看周一鸣，又看看胡雪岩，翻着一双白多黑少的三角眼，竟无从作答。就在他这迟疑不语之际，突然觉得眼前一亮——胡雪岩把张被单一揭，下面盖着的二十个大元宝，尽皆揭露，簇簇全新，银光闪亮，着实可爱，另外又有一堆银子，几个“中锭”，一些“元丝”，估计是百把两上下，这不消说是，是预备送自己的谢礼。俗语道得好：“财帛动人心”，胡雪岩是钱眼里不知翻过多少跟斗的，最懂得这句俗语，所以特地要换官宝，好来打动小狗子的心。这是胡雪岩熟透世故、参透人生、驾驭世人的一帖万应灵药，小狗子心里也知道，阿巧姐真正成了奇货。说书的常说：美人无价，若是咬定牙关不放松，弄个一万八千的也容易得很，这区区一千两银子算得了什么？无奈心里是这样想，那双眼睛却不听话，盯住了叠得老高，耀眼生花的大元宝不肯放。当然口中无话。周一鸣要催他，嘴唇刚一动，让胡雪岩摇手止住了。

Outside Yongxingsheng, Hu found the insult hard to swallow. He would have liked to retaliate immediately, but that could not be arranged in a moment. Putting it aside, he found another bank, obtained twenty official ingots, and had one of its outside clerks deliver them to Jinchang Inn. The silver had scarcely been stacked when Zhou arrived with Xiaogouzi. Once they were introduced, Hu came straight to the point. “I'm a patron of Sister A’qiao's. She has asked me to speak for her. If her husband's family will release her, she's willing to pay a thousand taels so that her husband can marry again and buy a few mu of land. He could live comfortably enough. Zhou tells me you're involved in the matter. An emperor doesn't send hungry soldiers on a mission. On Sister A’qiao's behalf, I'll give you a hundred taels. What do you say?” The proposal was plain, yet Xiaogouzi found it abrupt. What puzzled him most was how this “Brother Zhou,” who claimed to be Fat Wang's friend and to have attended a tea settlement with him, could know so much about his affairs. Looking first at Zhou and then at Hu, he rolled his triangular eyes, which showed more white than black, and could find no answer. As he hesitated, a flash of brightness struck him. Hu had pulled away a sheet, revealing twenty large ingots beneath, all brand-new and glittering with silver light: a truly lovely sight. Beside them lay another pile, several medium-sized ingots and some pieces of refined silver, perhaps a hundred taels in all. Plainly, that was the reward intended for him. “Money moves the heart,” as the saying went. Hu, who had turned countless somersaults through the eye of a coin, understood this better than anyone. That was why he had gone out of his way to obtain official ingots. Knowledge of the world, insight into human nature, and command over other men had given him this unfailing prescription. Xiaogouzi knew, too, that A’qiao had become a valuable commodity. Storytellers always said a beauty was beyond price. If he held firm, eighteen thousand taels would be easy enough to get. What was a mere thousand? Such were his thoughts, yet his eyes refused to obey. They would not leave the gleaming pile of ingots. Naturally, he said nothing. Zhou moved his lips to press him, but Hu stopped him with a gesture.

他很有耐心，尽让小狗子去想。银子如美色，“不见可欲，其心不乱”，或者刚看一眼，硬生生被隔开，倒也罢了，就是这可望而不可即的境况之下，一定越看越动心，小狗子此时的心情，就慢慢变成这个样子了。“凡事不必勉强。”胡雪岩开口了，再不开口，小狗子开不得口，会成僵局，“你如有难处，不妨直说。”“难处？”小狗子茫然地问。胡雪岩看他有点财迷心窍的模样，便象变戏法似地，拎起被单的一角，往上一抖，被单飞展，正好又把元宝覆住。这一来，小狗子的一颗心，才又回到了腔子里。“我也晓得你老哥是在外头跑跑的，做事‘落门落槛’，所以爽爽快快跟你说。”胡雪岩说，“我是受人之托，事情成不成，在我毫无关系，只要讨你一句回话，我就有交代了。”银子等于已经收起来了，似乎只等自己一句话，事情便成罢论。这样一个局面，轻易放弃，总觉得“于心不忍”，因此不译言地答了句：“我来想办法。”“这就是了。”胡雪岩接着他的话说，“我们都是居间的人，有话尽不妨实说，有难处大家商量着办。你老哥是何办法？我要请教。”“事情我做不得主，我只有尽力去说。成不成，不敢包。”小狗子又说，“如果数目上有上落，应该怎么说法？要请胡老爷给我一句话，我心里好有个数。”

Hu was patient and let Xiaogouzi think. Silver was like beauty: “Let a man see nothing to desire, and his mind remains untroubled.” Even if he caught a glimpse and was abruptly cut off from it, that could be endured. But when it remained visible and just beyond his reach, each look intensified his longing. Xiaogouzi was gradually reaching precisely that state. “Nothing need be forced,” Hu said at last. If he did not speak, Xiaogouzi could not, and they would be deadlocked. “If there's a difficulty on your side, say so.” “A difficulty?” Xiaogouzi asked blankly. Seeing how the money had bewitched him, Hu lifted a corner of the sheet and flicked it upwards like a conjuror. It spread through the air and settled exactly over the ingots. Only then did Xiaogouzi recover his senses. “I know you're a man of the world who understands how things are done,” Hu continued. “That's why I've spoken plainly. I'm acting for someone else. Whether it succeeds or fails makes no difference to me. I only need an answer to take back.” The money had effectively been put away. One word from him, it seemed, and the whole matter would be dropped. Such an opportunity was too painful to surrender lightly. “I'll find a way,” he answered involuntarily. “That's the spirit. We're both intermediaries. We can speak frankly and discuss any difficulties together. What way do you have in mind?” “I can't decide it myself. I can only do my best to persuade them. I can't guarantee success.” Xiaogouzi added, “And if there's some difference over the amount, what should I say? Please give me something to go on, Mr Hu.”

这到了讨价还价的时候，可说大事已定，胡雪岩略想一想说：“我在苏州很忙，实在没有闲工夫来磨，这样，予人方便，自己方便，如果不耽误我的工夫，我花钱买个痛快。明天一早，能够立笔据，我自己贴四个大元宝。”“明天一早怕来不及。”“至迟明天中午，中午不成，这件享就免谈了。一千两银子有人想用。”这话是什么意思？小狗子方在猜疑，周一鸣便桴鼓相应地说了句：“刑房的张书办，我是约了明天中午吃酒。”两句话加在一起，表示这一千两银子，可能送给张书办，送钱给刑房书办用，自然是要打官司，小狗子越发心存警惕，于是连连点头：“好的，好的。我准定明天中午，把‘原主’带了来，要立笔据，我就是中人。”“我们这方面，请老周做中人。”胡雪岩把那一百两银子取了来，放在小狗子面前，“这个，你先收了。”小狗子喜出望外，但口头还自要客气两句：“没有这个规矩！”“规矩是人立的，我的规矩一向如此，你先把你的一百两银子拿了去，跑起腿来也有劲。”胡雪岩还附带奉送了一块簇新的绸面布里的包袱，将银子亲手包好，交了过去。小狗子算一算，这件事办成功了，那一千二百两银子中，明的中人钱，暗的二八回扣，还有三百两银子好进帐，平白撞出这一炷财香，也多亏周一鸣，所以向胡雪岩道了谢，招招手说：“周大哥，请你陪我出去。”

They had reached the bargaining stage, which meant the main issue was effectively settled. Hu considered briefly. “I'm very busy in Suzhou and have no spare time for haggling. Make things easy for others, and they're easier for you too. If you don't waste my time, I'll pay for promptness. If the documents can be signed first thing tomorrow, I'll add four large ingots myself.” “Tomorrow morning may be too soon.” “Noon tomorrow at the latest. If it can't be done by noon, there's nothing more to discuss. Someone else has a use for a thousand taels.” As Xiaogouzi wondered what this meant, Zhou supplied the perfectly timed response: “I've invited Clerk Zhang of the criminal office to drink with me tomorrow at noon.” Together, the two remarks implied that the thousand taels might go to Zhang. Money for a clerk in the criminal office naturally meant a lawsuit. Xiaogouzi grew still more alert. “Yes, yes,” he said, nodding repeatedly. “I'll certainly bring the husband here by noon tomorrow. I'll act as intermediary for the documents.” “Zhou will act for our side.” Hu took the hundred taels and put them before Xiaogouzi. “Take this now.” Xiaogouzi was delighted beyond expectation, though he offered the required polite objection. “That isn't the custom.” “People make customs. This has always been mine. Take your hundred taels first. It'll give you more energy for running about.” Hu added a brand-new wrapping cloth, silk outside and cotton within, bundled up the silver himself, and handed it over. Xiaogouzi calculated that if the affair succeeded, the twelve hundred taels would yield him another three hundred through the open intermediary's fee and the concealed twenty-per-cent kickback. Such a windfall had dropped out of nowhere, and he owed it to Zhou. After thanking Hu, he beckoned. “Brother Zhou, please come outside with me.”

周一鸣陪他出了门，等走回来时，手里托着两个“中锭”，笑嘻嘻地说：“这家伙倒还有良心，说饮水思源，是我身上来的路子，要送二十两银子给我，我乐得收下来，物归原主。”说着，把两锭银子摆在胡雪岩面前。“笑话，他送你的，跟我啥相干？你收下好了！明天‘写纸’，我们照买卖不动产的规矩，‘成三败二’，中人钱五厘，你们‘南北开’，还有三十两银子，是你应得的好处。”周一鸣也平白进帐了五十两银子，高兴得不得了，自然也把胡雪岩奉若神明，敬重得不得了，自告奋勇，要去接阿巧姐回来。“不忙，不忙，让她在潘家住两天。”胡雪岩说：“我倒有两件事跟你商量。”这两件事，第一件是他这天早上在永兴盛受的气要出，问周一鸣有何妙计？“心思好不过胡大老爷。”周一鸣答道，“你老想出法子来，跑腿归我。”“法子倒有一个，我怕手段太辣。我先讲个票号的故事你听……”

Zhou accompanied him out. When he returned, he carried two medium-sized ingots and was smiling broadly. “The fellow has a conscience after all. He said one should remember the source when drinking water, and since the opportunity had come through me, he wanted to give me twenty taels. I was happy to accept, so I could return them to their rightful owner.” He set the ingots before Hu. “Nonsense. He gave them to you. What have they to do with me? Keep them. Tomorrow, when the papers are signed, we'll follow the custom for property transactions: ‘three from the buyer, two from the seller.’ The intermediary's commission is five li, divided between the two sides. You'll have another thirty taels. That's your rightful benefit.” Zhou had thus gained fifty taels out of nowhere. Overjoyed, he revered Hu as though he were a god and volunteered to fetch A’qiao. “No hurry. Let her stay at the Pans' a couple of days,” Hu replied. “There are two other matters I'd like to discuss.” The first was the insult he had suffered at Yongxingsheng that morning. He wanted redress. Did Zhou have a clever suggestion? “No mind is better than yours, Mr Hu. You think of the plan, and I'll do the legwork.” “I do have a plan, but I'm afraid it may be too harsh. Let me tell you a story about a remittance house first.”

京师的票号，最大的四家，招牌都有个“恒”字，通称“四大恒”。行大欺客，也欺同行，有家异军突起的票号，字号“义源”，专发钱票，因为做生意迁就和气，信用又好，营业蒸蒸日上。而且发钱票专跟市井细民打交道，这口碑一立，一传十，十传百，市面上传得很快，连官场中都晓得义源的信誉了。四大恒一看这情形，同行相妒，就要想法打击义源，于是一面暗地里收义源所出的票子，收了去兑现，一面放出谣言，说义源快要倒闭了，这一来造成了挤兑的风潮。哪知一连三天，义源见票即兑，连等都不用等，第四天，风平浪静，义源的名气反倒越加响了。四大恒见此光景，自然要去打听它的实力，一打听才晓得遇上了不倒的劲敌，义源有实钱四百万，出了一张票子，照数提一笔另行存贮，从来不发空票，所以不致受窘。这个故事一说，周一鸣就懂了，“胡大老爷，”他问，“你的意思也是想收‘义源’的票子，去‘整’它一家伙？”“对了！不过我又怕象‘四大恒’跟‘义源’一样。”胡雪岩说：“你做初一，人家做初二，弄‘义源’不倒，‘义源’来整我的阜康，岂不是自讨苦吃？”“是的。这一点不可不妨。”周一鸣说，“等我去打听打听‘义源’的实力看。实力不厚，不妨‘将他一军’，不然，还得另想别法。”“我就是这个意思，你去打听了再说。好在这件事不忙。我讲另外一件。”

The four largest remittance houses in the capital all had the character Heng in their names and were commonly called the “Four Hengs.” Great businesses could bully their customers, and their competitors too. A rising house called Yiyuan specialised in copper-cash notes. Courteous and accommodating in its business, and sound in credit, it prospered rapidly. Its notes circulated chiefly among ordinary townspeople. Once its good name was established, word spread from one to ten and ten to a hundred, until even official circles knew its reputation. Jealous of a competitor, the Four Hengs set out to damage it. They secretly collected its notes and presented them for redemption while spreading rumours that it was about to fail. A run followed. Yet for three days Yiyuan redeemed every note on sight, without even making people wait. On the fourth day calm returned, and its reputation was stronger than before. The Four Hengs naturally investigated its resources, only to discover an unshakable opponent. Yiyuan had four million in cash reserves. Whenever it issued a note, it set aside the full corresponding amount in a separate reserve. It never issued an unbacked note, so it could not be embarrassed. Zhou understood the point. “Mr Hu, you mean to collect Yongxingsheng's notes and give it a lesson?” “Exactly. But I'm afraid of repeating what happened between the Four Hengs and Yiyuan. One man makes a move today, and the other answers tomorrow. If I fail to bring Yongxingsheng down and it turns on Fukang, wouldn't I be asking for trouble?” “Yes, we must guard against that. Let me find out how strong it is. If its resources are thin, we can put it in check. Otherwise we'll need another method.” “Just what I mean. Make inquiries first. Fortunately, there's no hurry. Now for the other matter.”

另一件事是要送潘叔雅一笔礼，一则酬谢他暂作阿巧姐居停的情谊，再则是胡雪岩觉得象这样的人，大可做个朋友，有心想结纳。如果说，仅仅是还人情债，这笔礼很容易送，反正花上几十两银子，买四色礼物，情意就算到了。但要谈结纳，则必须使潘叔雅对这笔礼重视，甚至见情，他家大富，再贵重的礼物，也未见得放在心上。或者是杭州的土产，物稀为贵，倒也留下一个印象，无奈人在苏州，无法办到。这番意思说了出来，等于又替周一鸣出了个难题，“送礼总要送人家求之不得的东西。”他说，“潘家有钱，少的是面子。能不能送他个面子？”“这话说得妙！”胡雪岩抚掌称赏，“我们就动脑筋，寻个面子来送他。”这两句话对周一鸣是极大的鼓励，凝神眨眼，动足脑筋，果有所得，“我倒有个主意，你老看行不行？”他说，“何学台跟你老的交情够了，托他出面，送潘家一个面子。”“这个主意的意思很好。”胡雪岩深深点头，“不过，我倒想不出，这个面子怎么送法？”“可以这样子办，你老写封信给何学台，事情要不要说清楚，请你老自己斟酌，如果不愿意细说，含含糊糊也可以，就说，这趟很承潘某人帮忙，请何学台代为去拜访潘某人道谢。”周一鸣说，“二品大员，全副导子去拜访他，不是蛮有面子的事？”“好极，好极。这个主意高明之至，高明得……老周，你自己都不晓得高明在哪里？”这是什么怪话？周一鸣大为困惑，自然也无法赞一词，只望着胡雪岩翻眼。胡雪岩也不作解释，还没有到可以说破的时候，他已经决定照官场中通行的风气，买妾以赠，安排阿巧姐做何桂清的侧室。这一来，阿巧姐在潘家作客，何桂清亦应见情，所以代胡雪岩道谢，实在也就是他自己道谢。周一鸣的主意，隐含着这一重意义，便显得极外高明，只是他自己不明白而已。

The other matter was a gift for Pan Shuya. Hu wanted both to thank him for lodging A’qiao and to cultivate his friendship, for a man like that was well worth knowing. If he merely wished to discharge a debt of courtesy, the gift would be easy: spend a few dozen taels on four kinds of presents, and the obligation would be met. Friendship required something Pan would value, even something that would touch him. The family was rich; no costly object was likely to impress it. Local products from Hangzhou might have left an impression through their rarity, but Hu was in Suzhou and could not obtain them.
