Already pleased with himself, Yu grew more excited at the praise. Without thinking, he announced, “Let's do another fine, decisive thing today. Once I say it, everyone will agree. But Old Hu mustn't speak.” “Why not?” Hu protested with a smile. “You might spoil the occasion.” Gu had already guessed his intention. Afraid that Yu would speak and Hu refuse, turning a happy plan into a deadlock, he hurried to intervene. “Elder Yu, come here a moment.” Drawing him aside, he found he was right. Yu meant to unite Hu and Miaozhu at once. The banquet was ready to serve as their wedding feast; the guests and gifts were there too. With the marriage settled, Hu could return to Suzhou tomorrow and attend to business. “Little Uncle will certainly appreciate your kindness. But every household has its own difficult scripture. We don't yet know his troubles. Your word carries great weight. Once you've spoken, he cannot refuse. Yet you wouldn't want him to harbour private misgivings. Friends should leave one another no cause for regret. Don't you agree?” Yu did not understand the formal phrase, but grasped the meaning readily. On reflection, he had been rash. Once spoken, the words could not be recalled; if matters went wrong, his own dignity would suffer. He felt a new respect for Gu. “Quite right. You've thought it through. What should we do?” Gu knew Yu's love of excitement, and his spoilt young master's belief that a well-meant offer must never be refused. Reflecting that Hu had softened towards Miaozhu and a happy outcome seemed possible, he agreed to inquire privately.

私下一谈，胡雪岩的答复是古应春再也想下到的，“我已经叫老周接妙珍来了。”他说：“俞老一开口，我就懂了，既然如此，回头就烦你们两位跟妙珍谈一谈，什么都好答应，只有一样：不能老住在外面。”“小爷叔！”古应春楞了一下说：“我晓得你意思已经活动了，不想变得这么快？是怎么想了一想？”男女间事，无理可喻，胡雪岩的改变心意，是决定于重新贴上“胡寓”门牌的那一刻，而到底又是什么原因让他决定贴上“胡寓”的门牌，是为了妙珠忽作悬崖勒马之计而受了感动，还是一时兴起？已莫可究诘。不过，他是个不肯欺心的人，既然有此决定，即令不为人知，亦不可相负。至于趁今天纳宠，无非不愿辜负朋友的好意，乐得“凑兴”。感到兴趣的，自然不止俞武成和古应春，未吃喜酒，先闹新房，都挤在妙珠屋中，欢然谐笑。等妙珍一到，俞武成和古应春“做媒”，代为谈判条件，问她有何要求？“我没有要求，这是件好事，我只有高兴。不过，我总得问问妙珠的意思。”这是理所当然的，便让她们姐妹密谈。妙珍的意思，怕胡雪岩将来会变心，要他拿出一笔钱来，以防人老珠黄，后半辈子的衣食可以无忧。“你心里要放明白，不是我在打什么主意。初出来那两年的债务，总算弄清楚了，我不想一个钱的好处，他那笔钱拿出来，用你的户名去存去放，折子仍旧交给你。”妙珍又说，“我们姐妹一场，我完全是为你着想。”“那就跟他要三千银子好了。”妙珠的身价，应该不止三千两。不过这桩喜事，与一般情形不同，妙珍也就不便再多劝。把话转到古应春那里，他不需征询胡雪岩的意见，便代为答应了下来，当时向这一晌掌管着胡雪岩的财务的刘不才，如数要足银票，用个红封袋套好，封签上写明“奁仪”，交了给妙珍。妙珍再转交妙珠，她却不肯收，送给姐姐，作为敬意。妙珍无论如何不要，姐妹俩推让了半天，最后作为妙珠托她代为放息，妙珍才收下那个“红包”。

Hu's answer astonished him. “I've already sent Zhou to fetch Miaozhen. As soon as Elder Yu spoke, I understood. Since things have reached this point, you two can discuss it with her when she comes. I'll agree to anything, with one exception: she cannot be left living away from me indefinitely.” “Little Uncle!” Gu paused in surprise. “I knew you were wavering, but not that you'd change so quickly. What made you decide?” There was no reasoning out affairs between men and women. Hu had made his choice when he replaced the ‘Hu Residence’ notice. Why he had done that—whether moved by Miaozhu's sudden drawing back, or by a passing impulse—could no longer be disentangled. But he would not deceive his own conscience. Having decided, he could not betray that decision even if nobody knew of it. Taking her as his concubine today merely meant accepting his friends' goodwill and joining in the pleasure of the occasion. Yu and Gu were not the only delighted ones. Before the wedding wine was drunk, the guests were already crowding into Miaozhu's room with cheerful bridal jokes. When Miaozhen arrived, Yu and Gu acted as matchmakers and asked what terms she required. “None. It's a good thing, and I'm only happy. But I must ask Miaozhu what she wants.” Naturally, the sisters were allowed a private talk. Miaozhen feared that Hu might one day tire of her sister. He should provide money now to secure her later years, when youth and beauty had gone. “Understand me: I'm not scheming for myself. The debts from our first two years in the trade are finally cleared. I don't want a single coin. His money can be deposited or lent out in your name, and you keep the passbook. You're my sister. I'm thinking only of you.” “Then ask for three thousand taels.” Miaozhu's value should have been greater, but this marriage differed from the usual arrangement, and Miaozhen would not press her. Gu accepted the request without consulting Hu. He obtained the full amount in banknotes from Liu, who had lately been managing Hu's funds, put them in a red envelope labelled ‘Bridal Gift’, and handed it to Miaozhen. When she passed it to Miaozhu, the younger sister refused it and offered it to her elder sister in gratitude. Miaozhen would not accept. After much mutual insistence, she finally took it on the understanding that she would lend it at interest on Miaozhu's behalf.

酒阑人散，妙珠方得有机会跟胡雪岩说话。只是原有无数语言，迫不及待地想倾吐，而到了此时，反觉无从说起。望着高烧的红烛，回想这两天的波折，心里不辨是悲，是喜，是感慨，还是感激——感激日日在念经礼拜的白衣大士，菩萨有灵，终于如愿以偿。胡雪岩的心思也跟她差不多，在绯色的光晕中，有着如梦似幻的感觉，凝视着镜中的宜喜宜嗔春风面，自不免兴奋而得意，但想到在苏州的芙蓉，不由得又生歉意。就这样心潮起伏，便想不起该怎么找两句话来跟妙珠说了。“洞房”中是出奇地沉寂，寂静得灯花爆裂的声音都听得见。这使得炒珠大起警觉，也可以说是大起疑虑，如此良宵，决不该有这样清冷的光景，于是觉得有句话非说不可。“你懊侮了是不是？”她问。胡雪岩很诧异，“懊悔什么？”他反问一句。“懊悔不该自己贴上‘胡寓’那张条子？”“没有这话！我做事从来不懊悔的。”妙珠默然。这总算是一种安慰，但究不知他真心如何？也许口中否认，心里真有悔意。那样子倒是自己该懊悔孟浪了。生米已经煮成熟饭，却还未了咽。她心里在想，错了一步，错不得第二步，宁可落下笑柄，也不能自误一辈子，无论如何得要试出他的真心来。一念到此，立刻有了计较。要试别人的真心，先得自己表示真心，她毫不迟疑地打开一只描金皮箱，从箱底取出首饰箱来，开锁揭盖，送到胡雪岩面前。

Only when the drinking ended and the guests dispersed could Miaozhu speak with Hu. She had countless things to say, yet now did not know where to begin. Watching the tall red candles, she thought of the past two days' upheavals. Was she sad, joyful, moved or grateful? Grateful, surely, to the White-Robed Bodhisattva before whom she prayed every day. The compassionate power had answered her wish at last. Hu's feelings were much the same. In the crimson glow, everything seemed dreamlike. The lively face reflected in the mirror, equally lovely in pleasure and displeasure, filled him with excitement and pride. Then he thought of Furong in Suzhou and felt guilty. His emotions shifted so much that he too could find nothing to say. The bridal chamber was extraordinarily quiet; even the crackling candlewicks could be heard. Miaozhu became alert, then suspicious. Such a night should not be so cold and silent. She had to ask. “You regret it, don't you?” “Regret what?” he asked in surprise. “Putting up ‘Hu Residence’ yourself.” “Nothing of the sort. I never regret what I do.” She fell silent. It was some comfort, but what were his true feelings? Perhaps he denied regret while feeling it. Then she ought to regret her own rashness. The rice was cooked, but not yet swallowed. One false step must not lead to another. Better become a laughingstock than ruin her whole life. She must test his heart. The way came to her at once: to test another's sincerity, she must first show her own. Without hesitation, she opened a gilded leather trunk, took the jewel box from its bottom, unlocked it and brought it to Hu.

箱子里有玉镯、宝石、戒指、珠花、金镑、珈南香手串，都用新棉花包着，此时一样一样揭开来放在桌上，五光十色，令人目眩。胡雪岩不解所谓，忍不住问道：“你这样献宝干什么？”“我的私房都在这里。喏，你看！”她捡起一扣存折，递给胡雪岩。“你自己的东西，用不着给我看！”他不着存折，顺手抛在首饰箱里。“这些首饰，我自己估一估，值两万银子。你看呢？”“我不大懂。”胡雪岩说：“快收起来！财不露白。如果这时候外面有个贼在偷看，以后就危险了。”“ 不要紧的！这房子严密得很，围墙极高，不怕贼来。”妙珠略停一下，回入正题：“我留着这些东西无用，说不定如你所说，叫贼偷了去，反害得我心疼，不如交了给你。”“交给我做什么？”“咦！那还不是随便你，做生意派点本钱也是好的。”听得这两句话，胡雪岩的感想极多，但最后却是笑了出来，想到“唱本”上的故事：公子落难，花园赠金，大魁天下，奉旨归娶。看起来，妙珠多少也有这样子的想法。

Inside were jade bangles, gems, rings, pearl ornaments, gold sovereigns and fragrant aloeswood beads, each wrapped in fresh cotton. As she uncovered them one by one and placed them on the table, their colours dazzled the eye. Hu did not understand. “Why are you showing off your treasures?” “These are all my private savings. Look.” She picked up a passbook and handed it to him. “Your own belongings needn't be shown to me.” Without looking, he tossed it back into the jewel box. “I estimate the jewellery at twenty thousand taels. What do you think?” “I'm no expert. Put it away quickly. Wealth shouldn't be displayed. If a thief were watching outside, there could be trouble later.” “Don't worry. The house is secure and the walls very high.” After a pause she came to the point. “I have no use for these things. Perhaps, as you say, a thief will steal them and leave me heartbroken. Better give them to you.” “What for?” “Whatever you like. They could provide some capital for your business.” Hu had many feelings at this, but finally laughed. He thought of the stories in songbooks: a young gentleman fallen on hard times, a gift of gold in a garden, triumph in the examinations, then an imperial command to return and marry his benefactress. Miaozhu seemed to harbour some such notion.

这一笑，显得有些轻侮，妙珠微感不悦，正色说道：“我是诚心诚意的正经话。”“我晓得你是诚心诚意。可惜，”胡雪岩想了想，还是将那句话说了出来：“你这番诚心，用错了地方。”“怎么呢？诚心待人还会错？”“本心不错，用得不得当。你要遇见一个肯上进的穷书生就好了，将来不说中状元，进京赶考中个进士好了，明媒正娶，还挣副诰封给你。那有多好？”“我不稀罕。只要……”“只要怎么样？”“只要……”妙珠很吃力地说：“只要你不变心就好了。”胡雪岩默然。觉得所遇到过的几个女子，以妙珠用心最苦，胁之以死，动之以利，先怕嫁不成，嫁成了又怕人变心，心眼儿这么多，将来怕难得相处。他的心里很矛盾，有畏惧也有怜惜，因而既想设法将刚结上的红丝剪断，却又觉得割舍不下，就这踌躇莫决之际，听得妙珠幽幽地叹了口气。“唉！嫁鸡随鸡，嫁狗随狗，我也跟你一样，做事不会懊悔的。将来都看你！反正不管怎么样，我姓胡是姓定了。”听得出来，这是从心底掏出来的真话。她有这样的表示，自己便再无别的主意好打。但是胡雪岩也警觉到，此时不宜轻许诺言，宜乎硬起心肠来，言明在先。

The laugh seemed slightly contemptuous. A little hurt, she said seriously, “I mean it sincerely.” “I know. Unfortunately...” He considered, then said what he had been thinking. “Your sincerity has found the wrong object.” “How can sincerity towards someone be wrong?” “The intention is good; its use is mistaken. You should have met an ambitious, poor scholar. Even if he didn't finish first in the empire, he might go to the capital and gain the jinshi degree. Then he could marry you properly as his wife and earn you an imperial title. How fine that would be.” “I don't care for that. All I want...” “What?” With difficulty, she answered, “For you not to change your heart.” Hu was silent. Of all the women he had known, Miaozhu had taken the greatest pains: first threatening death, then appealing with wealth; first fearing she could not marry him, then fearing that he would change once she had. With so many calculations, she might be hard to live with. He felt both apprehension and pity. Part of him wanted to cut the red thread they had just tied, yet he could not bear to part with her. While he hesitated, she sighed softly. “Marry a cock, follow the cock; marry a dog, follow the dog. Like you, I won't regret what I've done. The future rests with you. Whatever happens, my name is Hu now.” The words came from her heart. After that declaration, he could entertain no other plan. Yet he realized that easy promises would be unwise. He must harden himself and speak plainly first.

“你这样一片诚心待我，我怎么肯变心。不过，我有为难之处，你也该体谅。将来有不得不让你委屈的地方，你肯不肯咬起牙关来承受？”妙珠咬一咬牙，答了一个字：“肯！”“那就好了。什么委屈，这时候也不必去说它，总之将心比心，到时候你肯为我设想，就晓得我要你受那种委屈，也是无奈。”这番话暧昧难明，妙珠认为必须问个清楚：“你倒说说看，是啥委屈？让我心里也好有个预备。““譬如说，我明天一早就要走了，丢下你一个人在这里，岂不是委屈了你？”“象这样，不算委屈。”妙珠又问：“还有呢？”“还有？”胡雪岩摇摇头，“一时无比说起。反正都是这种事出无奈的情形。我们先谈明天，我起了以后，你怎么样？”“自然是关起门来过日子。”这样的答复，是可以意料得到的。但说出口来，有声音灌入耳中，少不得要想一想，这一想，便有疑问了。“你是过惯了热闹日子的，一个人清清冷冷，熬得下来吗？”话问得很坦率，也很实在，可是妙珠却觉得不中听，因而语声中便有不服气的意味：“你看着好了，看我熬得下来，熬不下来？”熬不下来又如何？胡雪岩心里在想，将来红杏出墙丢了自己的面子。这件事非同小可，必得好好想个办法。生米已经煮成熟饭，说不算也不行，那就只有一条路好走。

“With such sincerity towards me, how could I change? But I have difficulties too, and you must understand them. If circumstances force me to make you bear some hardship, will you grit your teeth and accept it?” Miaozhu clenched her teeth and gave one word: “Yes.” “Good. We needn't discuss what hardships now. Put yourself in my place when the time comes, and you'll understand that I have no choice.” The words were too vague. She had to ask. “Tell me what you mean, so I can prepare myself.” “For instance, I must leave early tomorrow and leave you alone here. Won't that be hard on you?” “That doesn't count. What else?” He shook his head. “I can't list everything now. They will be things beyond my control. Let's talk about tomorrow. Once I've left, what will you do?” “Close my doors and live quietly, of course.” He could have predicted that answer. Hearing it aloud, however, made him consider it, and a question followed. “You're used to a lively life. Can you endure the loneliness?” It was a frank, practical question, but she disliked it. Defiance entered her voice. “Wait and see whether I can.” And if she could not? Hu thought. An affair would disgrace him. This was serious; he must find a sound arrangement. The rice was already cooked. He could not pretend otherwise. There was only one course.

对这一重姻缘，一直优柔寡断、访煌游移、自己都不知道如何是好的胡雪岩，恢复了他的明快果断的性格，“妙珠！”他用毫不含糊的语气说：“这些东西你自己先收起来，有机会我替你做点‘小货’，是你的私房，我决不来动你，至于丢你一个人在这里，我也不放心，你等我明天一走，就收拾收拾行李，我再来接你，我想把你摆在上海。”到底有了个明确的了断！转弯抹角，终于逼出了他心里的话，妙珠大为欣慰。但是，他还有个芙蓉在那里，又将作何处置？“此刻在苏州的‘那一个’呢？”“你是说芙蓉？”胡雪岩毫不迟疑地答道：“我拿她摆在湖州。”这就很容易明白了，他预备立三个“门口”，除了杭州在老家，上海、湖州各一处。上海是繁华之地，而且要做生意，就碍常住上海，比较上以自己的处境最优越。妙珠苦心设计，做作得太久，这时候再也不愿掩饰她的真情，收好她的首饰箱往床里枕头边一放，随即便贴住他的身子坐下，两手环抱，抱住他的上半身，将脸偎依在他肩头，深深地吸着气，显得极其满足恬适似地。

After all his indecision over this marriage, Hu recovered his usual clarity and firmness. “Miaozhu, put these things away for now. When there's an opportunity, I'll do some small trading for you. They are your private assets; I won't touch them for myself. As for leaving you here alone, I can't feel easy about that either. Once I go tomorrow, begin packing. I'll come back for you. I mean to settle you in Shanghai.” At last there was a definite decision. After so many twists, she had drawn out his real intention, and was deeply relieved. But there was still Furong. What would become of her? “And the one in Suzhou?” “You mean Furong?” He answered without hesitation. “I'll settle her in Huzhou.” It was plain enough to her. He meant to establish three households: the old family home in Hangzhou, and others in Shanghai and Huzhou. Shanghai was prosperous, and business would keep him there often. Her position was the best of the three. She had schemed and acted for too long to conceal her true feelings any more. Putting away her jewel box beside the pillows, she sat close against him, wrapped both arms round his upper body, laid her face against his shoulder and drew a deep breath, looking utterly content and at peace.

第三十章｜CHAPTER THIRTY

第二天一早便有人敲门，妙珠惊醒了问道：“是不是阿金？做啥？”“是我。”阿金高声相答：“古老爷来了。说有要紧事情，要跟胡老爷说。”于是妙珠推醒胡雪岩说知究竟。他披衣起床，开出门来，古应春歉然说道：“对不起！吵醒了你们的好梦。有个消息，非马上来告诉你不可。”胡雪岩睡意犹在，定定神问道：“什么消息？不见得是好事吧？来，来，进来坐了谈。”“不必！我直截了当说吧！五哥派了专人送信来，上海洋商那里，事情怕有变化，庞二那里的档手出了花样……”“是那个性朱的吗？”胡雪岩打断他的话问。“是的。就是那个外号‘猪八戒’的朱观宗。”“这个人我早已看出他难弄。”胡雪岩摇摇头，“你说，他出了什么花样？”“五哥派来的那个人很能干，讲得很详细。是这么一回事……”

Early the next morning, someone knocked. Miaozhu woke with a start. “Is that A’jin? What is it?” “Yes, it’s me,” A’jin called. “Mr Gu is here. He says he has urgent business to discuss with Master Hu.” Miaozhu shook Hu awake and told him. He threw on a robe, rose, and opened the door. Gu greeted him apologetically. “Forgive me for disturbing your pleasant dreams. There is news I must tell you at once.” Still sleepy, Hu collected himself. “What news? Not good, I suppose. Come in and sit down.” “No need. I shall come straight to the point. Brother Five has sent a special messenger. There may be trouble over the deal with the foreign merchant in Shanghai. Pang Er’s manager has been up to something...” “The fellow named Zhu?” Hu interrupted. “Yes. Zhu Guanzong, the man they call Pigsy.” “I could see from the start that he would be difficult.” Hu shook his head. “What has he done?” “The man Brother Five sent is very capable and explained everything in detail. This is what happened...”

原来“猪八戒”野心勃勃，想借庞二的实力，在上海夷场上做江浙丝帮的头脑，因而对胡雪岩表面上“看东家的面子”，不能不敷衍，暗地里却是处心积虑要打倒胡雪岩。自从古应春跟洋商的生意谈成功，由于事先有庞二的关照，猪八戒不能不跟着一起走。坏在胡雪岩不在上海，一时不能签约，而古应春又到了同里，造成可乘之隙。据尤五打听来的消息，猪八戒预备出卖胡雪岩，他已跟洋商接过头，劝洋商以他为交涉的对手，他也愿意订约保证，以后三年的丝，都归此洋商收买，而眼前的货色则愿以低于胡雪岩的价格，卖给洋商。“这家伙是跟洋商这么说：你不必担心杀了价，胡某人不肯卖给你！你不知道他在实力，我知道，他是空架子，资本都是别处地方挪来的，本钱搁熬在那里，还要吃拆息，这把算盘怎么打得通？不要说杀了价，他还有钱可赚，就是没有钱赚，只要能保本，他已经求之不得。再说，新丝一上市，陈丝一定跌价，更卖不掉。”古应春越说越气，声音提得很高，象吵架似地：“你看，这个忘八蛋的猪八戒，是不是汉奸？”“你不必生气。我自有治汉奸的法子。”胡雪岩好整以暇地喊道，“妙珠：你叫阿金先弄些点心来给古老爷呢。”

Pigsy was fiercely ambitious. He wanted to use Pang Er’s resources to become the leader of the Jiangsu and Zhejiang silk merchants in Shanghai’s foreign settlement. Outwardly, out of consideration for his employer, he had to accommodate Hu; in secret, he had long been plotting to bring him down. Once Gu negotiated the sale to the foreign merchant, Pang’s prior instructions obliged Pigsy to follow suit. Unfortunately, Hu was away from Shanghai and could not immediately sign the contract. Gu’s departure for Tongli created a further opening. According to You Laowu’s information, Pigsy was preparing to betray Hu. He had already approached the foreign merchant and urged him to negotiate through himself instead. He too was willing to guarantee by contract that the merchant could buy all their silk for the next three years, while offering the present stock below Hu’s price. “This is what the fellow told him: ‘You needn’t worry that Hu will refuse to sell if you force down the price. You don’t know his real resources; I do. He is an empty shell. His capital has all been brought in from elsewhere. While it lies tied up in stock, he has to pay short-term interest. How can that calculation work? Never mind that he would still make a profit at a lower price—even if there were no profit, he would be thankful merely to recover his capital. Besides, once the new silk comes onto the market, old stock is bound to fall in price and become harder to sell.’” Gu grew angrier as he spoke, raising his voice as though in an argument. “Tell me, isn’t that bastard Pigsy a traitor to his own people?” “There is no need to be angry. I have my own ways of dealing with traitors.” Entirely unhurried, Hu called, “Miaozhu! Ask A’jin to bring Mr Gu something to eat.”

“不必，不必！我吃不下，气都气饱了。小爷叔，”古应春说，“我看只有一个法子，一面你或者请刘三爷，赶到南浔去一趟，请庞二出来说话，一面我赶回上海，联络散户对付猪八戒。”“庞二是孙悟空，治猪八戒倒是一帖药。不过，还没有到要搬请齐天大圣出来的时候。”胡雪岩又说：“至于联络散户对付猪八戒，打狗要看主人面，庞二面上不好交代，”“小爷叔！”古应春真的有点着急，“你处处请交情，爱面子，你不想想人家跟你不讲交情，不讲面子，”胡雪岩想了想，笑了，“我已经有了法子。”他说，“猪八戒识相的，我们善罢干休，他如果不识相，那就真正是‘猪八戒照镜子’，我要搞得他‘里外不是人’。”“好啊！小爷叔，你说！”“不忙，不忙，先坐下来。”等胡雪岩拖他进了“新房”，妙珠已经草草妆成，一夜之隔，身分不同，古应春笑嘻嘻地叫一声：“阿姨，恭喜，恭喜！”“不敢当。”妙珠娇羞满面，“古老爷请坐，啥事体生气？听你喉咙好晌。”“现在不气了。”胡雪岩接口说：“快弄点茶水来，我渴得要命。”于是妙珠唤来阿金，一面伺候胡雪岩漱洗，一面张罗着招待客人。胡雪岩说“有了法子”是宽古应春的心的话，直到慢慢洗完了脸，才真的筹划出一个办法。

“No, no! I couldn’t eat. I am full of anger already. Little Uncle, I see only one solution. You, or perhaps Third Master Liu, must hurry to Nanxun and ask Pang Er to intervene. Meanwhile I shall return to Shanghai and organize the small dealers against Pigsy.” “Pang Er is Sun Wukong, and certainly knows how to bring Pigsy to heel. But we have not yet reached the point of summoning the Great Sage Equal to Heaven. As for organizing the small dealers against him, even when beating a dog you must consider its master. We should have difficulty explaining that to Pang.” “Little Uncle!” Gu was genuinely anxious. “You consider friendship and face at every turn. Haven’t you noticed that the other man considers neither when dealing with you?” Hu thought for a moment, then smiled. “I have a plan. If Pigsy knows what is good for him, we can let the matter drop. If he does not, he will find himself like Pigsy looking in a mirror—no human being on either side. I shall make him unacceptable to everyone!” “Excellent! Tell me, Little Uncle.” “No hurry. Sit down first.” Hu drew him into the bridal chamber. Miaozhu had hastily finished dressing. One night had changed her status, and Gu greeted her with a smile. “Auntie, congratulations!” Blushing, she answered, “You are too kind. Please sit down, Mr Gu. What has made you angry? I could hear you raising your voice.” “He is not angry now,” Hu put in. “Bring us some tea quickly. I am desperately thirsty.” Miaozhu summoned A’jin and attended to Hu’s washing while arranging refreshments for the visitor. Hu had said he had a plan merely to reassure Gu. Only after leisurely finishing his wash did he actually devise one.

于是胡雪岩一面陪着古应春吃早点，一面授以对付“猪八戒”的秘计。古应春心领神会，不断称是。等谈妥当，古应春即时动身，赶回上海，照计行事。依照预定的步骤，他首先去看洋商，怡和洋行的大班吉伯特，那个原在东印度公司任职的英国人，极善于做作，一见古应春的面，首先表示惋惜，当初谈成交后，不曾先签下一张草约，于今接到欧洲的信息，丝价已跌，所以不能照原定的价格成交，他个人表示非常抱歉。又说：如果当初订下草约，则此刻照约行事，总公司明知亏本，亦无可奈何。怪来怪去怪古应春自己耽误。“是的，草约不曾订，是我自误。不过，中国人做生意，讲究信义，话说出口，便跟书面契约一样有效。”古应春从容问道：“欧洲的丝价，是否已跌，我们无法求证。我只想问一问：你是不是仍旧愿意照原价买我们的丝？”“抱歉！我已经说得很清楚了。”吉伯特答道：“如果你愿意减价百分之十五，我们依旧可以交易。”“不行！”古应春答：“你向任何一个中国商人买丝，都需要这个价钱。”

Over breakfast, Hu explained his secret plan for dealing with Pigsy. Gu grasped it thoroughly and repeatedly expressed his agreement. As soon as they had settled everything, he left for Shanghai to carry it out. Following the agreed sequence, he first called on the foreign merchant. Gilbert, the head of Jardine Matheson, was an Englishman formerly employed by the East India Company, and a highly accomplished actor. The moment he saw Gu, he expressed regret that they had not signed a preliminary agreement when they first settled the sale. News had now arrived from Europe that silk prices had fallen, so the transaction could not proceed at the original price. He was personally very sorry. Had they signed a preliminary contract, he added, it would have had to be honored; even knowing that it would lose money, the head office could have done nothing about it. In short, Gu had only his own delay to blame. “Yes, failing to sign a preliminary agreement was my mistake. But Chinese merchants value good faith. Once we have given our word, it is as binding as a written contract.” Gu asked calmly, “We have no means of verifying whether silk prices in Europe have fallen. I want to ask only this: are you still willing to buy our silk at the agreed price?” “I am sorry. I have made myself quite clear,” Gilbert replied. “If you will reduce the price by fifteen percent, we can still do business.” “Impossible. You will have to pay our price, whichever Chinese merchant supplies your silk.”

谈判决裂是在意中。古应春离开抬和洋行，立即赶到二马路一家同兴钱庄，取出一张五千两的银票，存入“福记”这个户头。“好的！”同兴的伙计说，“请你把折子给我。”“没有折子。”古应春答道，“我们是裕记丝栈，跟福记有往来，收了我的款子，请你打一张收条给我。”生意上往来，原有这种规矩，同兴钱庄便开出一张收据，写明“裕记丝栈交存福记名下银五千两整”，付与古应春。同时又通知了福记，有这样一笔款子存入。“福记”就是“猪八戒”的户头，他的名字叫朱福年。一接到同兴的通知，深为诧异，因此等古应春去拜访他时；首先但提到这件事，“老兄，”他问，“我们并无银钱上落，你怎么存了五千银子在我户头里？”“这是胡先生的一点意思。”古应春答道：“胡先生说，平常麻烦你的地方很多，早想有所表示，现在丝上赚了一笔，当然要送红利。”

The breakdown in negotiations was expected. Leaving Jardine Matheson, Gu went straight to Tongxing Bank on Second Road, produced a five-thousand-tael banknote, and deposited it in an account called Fuji. “Very good,” said the clerk. “May I have your passbook?” “I have no passbook. We are Yuji Silk Warehouse and have business dealings with Fuji. Accept the money and give me a receipt.” This was a customary business procedure. Tongxing issued a receipt stating, “Received from Yuji Silk Warehouse, for deposit to the account of Fuji, exactly five thousand taels of silver,” and handed it to Gu. It also notified Fuji of the deposit. Fuji was Pigsy’s account; his name was Zhu Funian. The notice from Tongxing astonished him, so it was the first thing he mentioned when Gu called. “My dear fellow, there are no payments due between us. Why have you put five thousand taels into my account?” “A small token from Mr Hu. He says we often put you to trouble and he has long wished to show his appreciation. Now that he has made a profit on silk, he must naturally send you a share.”

“不敢当，不敢当。”朱福年忽然装得忧形于色地，“应春兄，你是刚回上海？”“是的。”“那么，怡和洋行的吉大班你碰过头没有？”“碰过头了。”我就是为这件事，来向你老兄讨教的。吉伯特说欧洲的丝价跌了，要杀我们的价。你看，该怎么办？““这……我正也为这一层在伤脑筋。洋人坏得很，我们要齐了心对付他。他要杀价，我们就不卖。““你这里实力充足，搁一搁不要紧，我们是小本钱，搁不起。”“好说，好说。”朱福年试探着问，“应春兄，你那里的货色，是不是急于想脱手？”古应春点点头，面色凝重而诚恳，“实不相瞒，”他说，“这票丝生意，如果先没有成议，各处的款子都还可以缀一缓，因为十拿九稳了，所以都许了人家最近料理清楚。想不到煮熟了的鸭子又飞掉，只好请老兄帮忙，让我们过一过关。”“不敢当，只怕我力量有限，作不得主……”“当然不会让老兄为难，”古应春抢在前面说，“跟洋人做生意，不是这一回，再困难也不能走绝路。老兄也是内行，晓得洋人的厉害，所以我们这票丝，跌价卖给洋人，无论如何不肯。我跟吉伯特已经说过了，不管向哪个中国人买丝，都非照原议的价钱不可。只要大家齐心，不怕洋人不就范。我想这样，便宜不落外方，我们少赚几个，老兄帮了我们的忙，总也要有点好处。“

“You are too generous, too generous.” Zhu suddenly assumed an anxious expression. “Brother Yingchun, have you only just returned to Shanghai?” “Yes.” “Then have you met Mr Gilbert of Jardine Matheson?” “I have. That is precisely why I have come for your advice. Gilbert says silk prices have fallen in Europe and wants to force down our price. What should we do?” “Well... that has been worrying me too. These foreigners are dreadful. We must stand together against him. If he demands a reduction, we must refuse to sell.” “You have ample resources and can afford to wait. Our capital is small; we cannot.” “You are too modest.” Zhu probed further. “Are you anxious to dispose of your stock, Brother Yingchun?” Gu nodded, his expression grave and sincere. “To tell you the truth, before the sale was agreed, we could still have delayed payments elsewhere. But once it seemed certain, we promised everyone that their money would soon be settled. Now the cooked duck has flown away. We can only ask you to help us through this difficulty.” “I hardly deserve such confidence. My powers are limited, and I cannot decide on my own...” “Naturally, we would not put you in a difficult position,” Gu interrupted. “This will not be our last transaction with the foreigners. However hard things are, we cannot destroy our future. You know the trade and understand how formidable they are. Whatever happens, we will not sell this silk to them at a reduced price. I have already told Gilbert that whichever Chinese merchant he buys from, he must pay the agreed price. If we all stand together, he will have to yield. Here is my idea: keep the advantage on our own side. We can take a little less profit, while you gain something for helping us.”

接着古应春便说了办法，拿他们的丝卖给朱福年，照吉伯特的原价打个九五折，换句话说是，给朱福年五厘的好处，算起来有一万六千银子。古应春的神态，看来恳切，其实是安排下一个陷阱，如果朱福年知趣，收下那五千银子的“红包”，高抬贵手，仍旧照原议，让古应春代表同业跟吉伯特去打交道，订约成交，利益均沾，则万事全休。无奈此人利令智昏，一只手如意，一只手算盘，心里在想，一转手之间，有一万多银子好赚，而且归自己出面订约，马上就变成同业的头脑，这样名利双收的机会，岂可错过？“只是心花虽已怒放，表面还不能不做作一番，“应春兄，只要我力量够得上，无有不效劳的。不过，我是依人作嫁，这件事做是可以做，照规矩总碍先跟东家说一声。歇个三、四天，给你回音好不好？”这两句托词，早在胡雪岩意料之中，古应春心里好笑，一1165 只脚已经被拉住了，他还在鼓里！当时答道：“是的。规矩应该如此，不过总要拜托老兄格外上紧。”

Gu then explained his proposal. They would sell their silk to Zhu at ninety-five percent of the original price agreed with Gilbert. In other words, Zhu would receive a five-percent advantage, amounting to sixteen thousand taels. Gu appeared earnest, but was actually setting a trap. Had Zhu understood the situation, accepted the five-thousand-tael gift, and stopped obstructing them, all could have ended well. Gu would still represent the trade in negotiations with Gilbert, as originally arranged; the contract would be signed, the sale concluded, and everyone would share the benefits. But greed clouded Zhu’s judgment. With a wish-fulfilling scepter in one hand and an abacus in the other, so to speak, he reflected that a single resale would bring him more than ten thousand taels. By signing the contract himself, he would also immediately become the leader of the trade. How could he pass up such a chance to gain both money and standing? Delighted though he was, he had to maintain appearances. “Brother Yingchun, I shall do everything within my power. But I am working for another man. This can be done, though the rules require me to consult my employer first. May I give you an answer in three or four days?” Hu had anticipated this excuse. Gu laughed inwardly: one of the fellow’s feet was already caught, and he still knew nothing of the trap. Aloud he said, “Certainly. That is the proper procedure. But please give it your most urgent attention.”

“我晓得，我晓得，最多四天工夫，一定有确实回信。”朱福年又说：“那五千银子，决不敢领，请你带了回去。”接着便拿钥匙要开外国银箱取银票。“不！”古应春将他那只拿钥匙的手按住，放低了声音说：“老兄，我们迟早要付的，四天以后有了确实回信，我再把余数补足。”“嗯，嗯！”朱福年还不大懂他的话。“老兄，”古应春的声音放得更低，“这笔生意，怎么样一个折扣、怎么样出帐，完全听你老兄的。如果是照原价出让，我们再补一万一千银子到福记。”这是叫朱福年作弊，意思是他大可跟庞二去说，为了帮胡雪岩的忙，照吉伯特的原价，先行垫付，帐上十足照给，暗中收下一万六千银子的回扣，这也是做法之一。朱福年一时无从决定，当然是先保留着这条路，所以点点头说：“那也好！我们到时候再结帐。”于是欢然辞别。回到裕记丝栈，古应春找着尤五，不曾开口，先就得意大笑。

“I understand. Within four days at most, you shall have a definite answer. As for those five thousand taels, I really cannot accept them. Please take them back.” Zhu reached for his keys to open the foreign-made safe and fetch banknotes. “No!” Gu stopped the hand holding the keys and lowered his voice. “Sooner or later, we have to pay it. Once we have a definite answer in four days, I shall make up the balance.” “Yes, yes...” Zhu had not quite understood. Gu spoke still more quietly. “How the discount is arranged and how the transaction is entered in the accounts is entirely up to you. If the sale is recorded at the original price, we shall pay another eleven thousand taels into Fuji.” This was an invitation to dishonesty. Zhu could tell Pang that, to help Hu, he had advanced the full original price agreed with Gilbert, entering that entire amount in the books while secretly receiving a sixteen-thousand-tael kickback. It was one possible method. Unable to decide immediately, Zhu naturally kept that option open. He nodded. “Very well. We can settle the account when the time comes.” They parted on excellent terms. Back at Yuji Silk Warehouse, Gu found You Laowu and burst into triumphant laughter before speaking a word.

由于古应春一到上海就忙着跟洋人与“猪八戒”打交道，匆匆一晤，尤五只知道胡雪岩已授以“锦囊妙计”，却不知其详，所以这时看他得意大笑，虽觉欣慰，更多困惑，急于要问个明白。古应春说了经过，他还是不明白，“这里头有啥‘窍槛，？我倒不懂，”尤五问道，“四天以后，照你的价钱卖给猪八戒，无非白白让他得一万六千银子的好处，外带捧他做个‘老大，。”“哪里有这么便宜的事？等我修起一封书信来，刘三爷一到，直投雪得，那时候就要叫‘猪八戒照镜子，里外不是人’了！”“啊，啊！”尤五被点醒了，却还不曾点透，“庞二是大少爷脾气，要面子的，跟小爷叔的交情也够。不过……”他说，“照我来说，猪八戒帮东家赚钱，他也不能说他错。”“不然！”古应春问道：“五哥，你算是朱福年，设身处地想一想，他有几个做法？”尤五想了一会答道：“他有三个做法，一个是自己‘做小货’，赚钱归自己，蚀本归东家。帮人做伙计，这是最犯忌的事。第二，他照你教他的办法，跟庞二说是帮我们的忙，十足垫付，暗地里收了个九五回扣，这也是开花帐，对不起东家的事。但是，他如果老老实实，替庞二打九五折收我们的货，赚进一万六千银子归入公帐，那就一点不错了。”

Since arriving in Shanghai, Gu had been occupied with the foreign merchant and Pigsy. During their brief encounter, You had learned only that Hu had supplied an ingenious plan, without hearing its details. Gu’s delighted laughter therefore pleased but puzzled him, and he was eager for an explanation. Even after hearing the account, he still failed to understand. “What is the trick? I don’t see it. Four days from now, if you sell to Pigsy at your proposed price, you will simply hand him sixteen thousand taels and promote him to leader of the trade into the bargain.” “It will not be that easy for him. Wait until I have written a letter. As soon as Third Master Liu arrives, he will take it straight to Nanxun. Then Pigsy will find himself facing that mirror, with neither side willing to call him human!” “Ah!” You had been shown the way, but did not yet see it clearly. “Pang has a rich young gentleman’s pride and cares about appearances. His friendship with Little Uncle is sound too. But if Pigsy is making money for his employer, surely Pang cannot call that wrong?” “Can’t he? Brother Five, put yourself in Zhu’s place. How many courses are open to him?” You considered. “Three. He could trade privately on his own account, keeping any profit and charging any loss to his employer. That is the gravest offense an employee can commit. Second, he could follow your suggestion, tell Pang that he is helping you by advancing the full price, and secretly pocket the five-percent rebate. That would be falsifying the accounts and cheating his employer too. But if he honestly buys your silk for Pang at ninety-five percent of the price and enters the sixteen-thousand-tael gain in the business accounts, there is nothing wrong with it.”

“说得不错，可惜还有一样把柄在我们手里。”古应春将同兴钱庄所掣的那张收据一扬。“这……”尤五疑惑地，“这也好算是把柄？”“怎么不是把柄？就看话怎么说！”古应春得意洋洋地，“不说他借东家的势力敲竹杠，只说他吃里扒外，如果不是送了五千银子，我们的丝卖不到这个价钱！”“我懂了，我懂了。”尤五恍然大悟，“意思是说，吉伯特要打八五折，我们跟猪八戒串通好，提高到九五折？”“对！不然我们为什么要送他五千银子？银子多得发霉了是不是？”“这咬他一口，倒也厉害。不过，他要退了回来呢？岂不是嫌疑洗刷干净了？”“怎么洗刷得干净？他要今天硬不肯收那五千银子，而且自己先跟他东家说明白：人家送我五千银子，我不要！那才算他硬气，这一步错过，嫌疑洗刷不干净了。”尤五想一想，果然！“小爷叔想条把计策，也蛮毒的。”他笑说道，“当然，只怪猪八戒心大狠，这五千银子本来是‘人参果’，现在变成蜜糖裹的砒霜，看它啥时候发作？”“信一到就会发作。”古应春说，“这封信很要紧，我得快点动手。”

“Quite right. Unfortunately for him, we have something else against him.” Gu flourished the receipt issued by Tongxing. “That?” You looked doubtful. “Can that count as evidence against him?” “Why not? It depends how the story is told.” Gu was thoroughly pleased with himself. “We need not say he used his employer’s power to extort money from us. We need only say that he took an outsider’s money to betray his employer: without paying him five thousand taels, we could never have obtained such a price for our silk.” “I understand!” You exclaimed. “You mean Gilbert offered eighty-five percent, but we conspired with Pigsy to raise it to ninety-five?” “Exactly! Why else would we have given him five thousand taels? Because we had so much money it was going moldy?” “That is a vicious bite. But what if he gives it back? Wouldn’t that clear him?” “How could it? If he had absolutely refused the money today and immediately told his employer, ‘They offered me five thousand taels, but I refused,’ he could stand his ground. He has missed that chance. The suspicion will not wash away.” You thought it over. Quite true! “Little Uncle can devise a poisonous scheme when he chooses,” he said with a laugh. “Of course, Pigsy has only his own greed to blame. Those five thousand taels began as ginseng fruit; now they are arsenic wrapped in sugar. I wonder when the poison will act.” “As soon as the letter arrives. It is a very important letter. I must begin at once.”

于是他精心构思，用胡雪岩的语气，给庞二写了一封求援的信。信上第一段说，吉伯特要杀他的价，而他急于脱货求现，跟朱福年已经谈过。第二段是引用朱福年自己的话，也道出了写这封信的缘故，因为朱福年表示不敢作主，要请东家决定，所以他特地向庞二请求，希望“鼎力赐援，俾济眉急”。第三段最难措词，要在惭愧中有感慨，感慨中寓不满，意思是说：回想当初，承庞二全力支持，原以为可以借重他的实力，有一番作为，不想落到今日的地步，当然是自己才具不胜，辜负了好朋友的厚爱，这是惭愧中有感慨。然而又何以落到这步田地呢？当然是猪八戒从中捣乱的缘故，但这话决不宜说破，而又不能太隐晦，明暗之间要恰恰能引起庞二的关切怀疑，不能不加以追究为度，过与不及，皆非所宜，是相当费斟酌的事。好在古应春英文虽佳，中文也不坏，改了又改，又征询尤五的意见，毕竟写得了恰到好处的程度。等誊清校对，看明只字不误，这就要等刘不才了。尤五的意见，认为不管朱福年是真的要请求东家，还是别有用心，这封信却必须尽快递到南浔，无论如何要在朱福年之前“抢个原告”，才有效验。古应春认为这个看法很实在，但刘不才不到，没有第二个人认识庞二，也是枉然。

Gu composed it with great care, writing to Pang in Hu’s voice to ask for help. The first paragraph explained that Gilbert was demanding a lower price and that Hu, urgently needing to turn his stock into cash, had already spoken to Zhu. The second quoted Zhu’s own words and explained the reason for writing: Zhu had said that he dared not decide without his employer’s approval, so Hu was appealing directly to Pang, hoping that he would “extend your fullest assistance and relieve my pressing difficulty.” The third paragraph was hardest to frame. It had to convey regret within an expression of shame, and dissatisfaction within the regret. With Pang’s wholehearted support at the outset, Hu had expected to accomplish something by drawing on his resources. Instead, matters had reached this unfortunate pass. Naturally, Hu’s own inadequacy was to blame; he had disappointed a good friend’s generosity. That supplied the shame and regret. But why had matters reached such a pass? Because Pigsy had been interfering. This could not be stated outright, yet neither could it be too obscure. Between explicit statement and suggestion, the wording had to arouse just enough concern and suspicion in Pang to compel an inquiry. Too much or too little would spoil the effect. Fortunately, Gu’s Chinese was good as well as his English. He revised repeatedly and consulted You until the balance was exactly right. Once the letter had been copied and checked word by word, they had only to wait for Liu. You thought it must reach Nanxun as quickly as possible, whether Zhu truly intended to consult his employer or had some other purpose. They must get their version before Pang first. Gu agreed, but without Liu, the only available man who knew Pang, they could do nothing.

“这样，我们迎了上去，如果能在松江截住刘三爷，转舵直奔南得，起码可以省出来一天的工夫。”“也好！”古应春说，“我顺便到府上去等七姐，说不定小爷叔也到了，有啥话，我们在松江细谈，也是一样。”于是在裕记丝栈留下话，万一中途错过，刘不才到了上海，让他即刻翻回松江。当然，水路上一路而去，尤五处处皆熟，逢人打听，是很少会有错失可能的。到了松江，才知道这一着真是走对了。他们是一早到家的，进门就遇见刘不才在客厅上喝早酒，问起来才知道他是前一天晚上到的，护送七姑奶奶和芙蓉在尤家暂住，他自己预备中午下船回上海。“小爷叔呢？”尤五问。“他跟何学使还有点要紧事谈。大概一两天回上海。”“暂时不管他。”古应春说：“三爷，事不宜迟，你的酒带到船上去喝。”“可以。”于是尤五替他准备船只，古应春交代此行的任务，将其间的作用关键，细细说完，千叮万嘱：“说话要当心，言多必失。”“是了。你放心。”刘不才说，“问起来，我只说我在同里，不清楚就是了。”

“Let us go to meet him. If we can intercept Third Master Liu at Songjiang and send his boat straight to Nanxun, we shall save at least a day.” “Very well,” Gu said. “I can wait for Seventh Sister at your house. Little Uncle may have arrived too. Whatever we need to discuss can be discussed in Songjiang just as well.” They left instructions at Yuji: if they missed Liu on the way and he reached Shanghai, he was to return to Songjiang immediately. In fact, You knew people everywhere along the water route and asked as they traveled, so there was little chance of missing him. Their arrival in Songjiang proved the wisdom of the move. They reached home early in the morning and found Liu in the sitting room, drinking his morning wine. He had arrived the previous evening, escorting the Seventh Lady and Furong to stay with the You family, and intended to leave by boat for Shanghai at noon. “Where is Little Uncle?” You asked. “He still has important business to discuss with Education Commissioner He. He should be back in Shanghai in a day or two.” “Never mind him for now,” Gu said. “Third Master, there is no time to lose. Take your wine aboard and drink it there.” “Certainly.” You arranged a boat while Gu explained the mission in detail, dwelling on every crucial point. His repeated warning was, “Be careful what you say. The more you talk, the more likely you are to make a mistake.” “Understood. Don’t worry. If anyone asks, I shall simply say I was in Tongli and know nothing about it.”

* * *一条“无锡快”分班摇橹，日夜不停，赶到南浔，刘不才上岸雇桥，直奔庞家。来得不巧，也来得很巧，不巧的是庞二的老太太正做六十大寿，巧的是嘉宾云集，象刘不才这副清客材料，正好派上用场。到寿堂磕过了头，庞二一把拉住他说：“刘三哥，你来得好极。有帮客人，要你替我招呼。”不用说，当然是赌客，刘不才的心跟手都痒了，但办正事要紧。这天是寿诞正日，前一天暖寿，下一天补寿，一共三天。远道来的贸客，余兴未尽，少不得还要赌几天，所以刘不才打算着，总得五天以后才能回上海。两天过去，他已结交了好些朋友。这两天当中，他也确实卖力，根据客人的兴趣，组合赌局，各得其所，皆大欢喜，大家都夸奖刘不才；主人也有面子，所以庞二对刘不才大生好感。第三天上午，赌局还未开场以前，特地到他下榻的小花厅来道劳。

A Wuxi fast boat, its oarsmen working in shifts without stopping day or night, carried Liu to Nanxun. He hired a sedan chair on landing and went straight to the Pang residence. His timing was both unfortunate and fortunate. Unfortunate, because Pang’s mother was celebrating her sixtieth birthday; fortunate, because distinguished guests had gathered, and a companion of Liu’s talents was exactly what was needed. After Liu had kowtowed in the birthday hall, Pang caught him by the arm. “Third Brother Liu, you could not have come at a better time. I have some guests I need you to entertain.” Gamblers, naturally. Liu’s heart and hands both itched to begin, though the serious business must come first. This was the birthday itself. There had been a preliminary celebration the day before, and a further celebration would follow the next, making three days in all. Guests from afar, still eager for diversion, would doubtless gamble for several more days. Liu reckoned that he could not return to Shanghai for at least five days. Two days passed, and he had made many new friends. He worked hard, arranging games according to the guests’ tastes so that everyone was satisfied. They praised him freely, which reflected well on their host. Pang consequently took a great liking to him. On the third morning, before the gaming began, he came especially to the small reception pavilion where Liu was lodging to thank him for his trouble.

道过谢，说些闲话，庞二提了胡雪岩，“老胡的礼数真周到。”他说，“昨天特为派了人来送礼，真正盛情可感，”“应该的。”刘不才也很机警，答得十分漂亮：“若不是那票丝弄得他焦头烂额，照他跟二哥你的交情，一定还要赶来替我伯母磕头拜寿。”这一下倒提醒了庞二，皱着眉头说：“老胡长袖善舞，我最佩服他。何至于弄得如此！而且我也不懂，他是怎么跟洋人搞决裂的？照朱福年说，他心太急了些，让洋人看透他的实力，趁机‘拿跷’，不知道有没有这话？”“这我就不大清楚了。他跟洋人打交道，都是一位姓古的经手，所以这方面的情形，我隔膜得很。”“你是说古应春？这个人我也知道，极能干的，洋人那里的信用也很好。老胡有他，如虎添翼，所以越发叫人弄不懂了。“话要入港了，刘不才暗暗高兴，表面上却还是装洋，“怎么弄不懂？”他问。

After expressing his thanks and exchanging a few remarks, Pang mentioned Hu. “Old Hu is wonderfully attentive to courtesy. He sent someone specially with gifts yesterday. I am deeply touched.” Liu was alert and answered gracefully. “It was only right. Had that silk not left him at his wits’ end, he would surely have come himself to kowtow and wish your mother a happy birthday, considering his friendship with you.” This reminded Pang of the business. Frowning, he said, “I have the greatest admiration for Hu’s skill at making the most of his resources. How could things have come to this? Nor do I understand how he fell out with the foreigners. According to Zhu Funian, he was too impatient and let them see the true extent of his resources, so they took the opportunity to put pressure on him. Is that what happened?” “I do not really know. A man named Gu handles all his dealings with the foreigners, so I know very little of that side.” “You mean Gu Yingchun? I know of him too. Extremely capable, and well trusted by the foreigners. With him, Hu is like a tiger given wings. That makes it still harder to understand.” The conversation was approaching the point Liu wanted. Secretly pleased, he continued to feign ignorance. “What is hard to understand?”

于是刘不才不慌不忙他说道：“老伯母的大寿，理当效劳，只要用得着我，十天八天都要伺候。不过，我是雪岩特地派来的，有封信，请二哥先过目。”庞二拆开信，一目十行，匆匆看去，还未看完，就连声答说：“小事，小事，朱福年今天也要来的，我关照他就是。”这封信是要从容寻味，才能看出名堂，照眼前的情形，庞二哪里有心思细琢磨？看起来古应春的这番精心构思，变成“俏媚眼做给瞎子看”。自己虽守着“言多必失”之诫，未便多说，但这意外的情形，应该通知古应春，好作个准备。打算停当，便即摆出欣然的颜色：“二哥肯这样帮忙，我的差使也好交代了。上海还在等我的回音，我写封信叫原船带回去，回头再来帮你招呼客人。”“何必你亲自去跑。”庞二说道：“船在哪里？你写好了信，我派人替你送去。”“不必，不必！”刘不才答道：“我本来是打算原船回去的，现在总还得住两天，船上的东西，要收拾收拾，还是我自己去一趟的好。”听他这样说法，庞二只得由他，派了一名佣工，又派了轿子，送他到码头。刘不才先在船上收拾好行李，关照庞家的听差押着走，然后在舱中写好一封信，叮嘱船家即时赶回松江，送交尤五。

Quite unhurried, Liu said, “It is only right that I should help with your mother’s birthday. If you need me, I shall gladly stay eight or ten days. But Xueyan sent me here especially with a letter. May I ask you to read it first?” Pang opened it and glanced rapidly down the page. Before he had finished, he said repeatedly, “A small matter, a small matter! Zhu Funian is coming today too. I shall give him instructions.” The letter required leisurely reflection before its full meaning could emerge. In the present circumstances, Pang had no time to study it. Gu’s painstaking composition seemed to have become a coquettish glance thrown at a blind man. Bound by the warning against talking too much, Liu could say little, but he ought to inform Gu of this unexpected development so that Gu could prepare. Having decided, he assumed a delighted air. “With your help, I can give a satisfactory account of my mission. They are waiting for news in Shanghai. I shall write a letter and send my boat back with it, then return to help entertain your guests.” “Why trouble to go yourself? Where is the boat? Write the letter and I shall have someone take it.” “No need, no need. I had meant to return in the same boat. Since I must now stay another couple of days, I ought to collect my belongings from it. I had better go myself.” Pang could only let him. He provided a servant and a sedan chair to take Liu to the landing. Liu first packed his luggage aboard and sent it away under the Pang servant’s care. Then he wrote his letter in the cabin and instructed the boatman to return immediately to Songjiang and deliver it to You Laowu.

“应该可以做得极出色的事，为啥弄得这样子狼狈，我就不懂。我想，以老胡和姓古的手腕，加上老胡跟我的实力，我真不相信搞不过洋人！”“是啊！”刘不才做出被提醒的神气，眨着眼，皱着眉说：“照规矩说，不应该如此。到底啥道理，这趟我回上海倒要问问他。”“我们一起走。”庞二立即相邀，“我早就要走了。只为家母的整生日，分不开身，还有几位比较客气的朋友，明天都要走了，快的话，我们后天就可以动身。”案头正好有本皇历，刘不才随手一翻，看到后天那一行，一个大“宜，字下，密密麻麻的小字，不问可知是黄道吉日。看皇历有句俗语，叫做”呆人看长行“，长行的都是宜什么，宜什么，如果是个”破日“，只有短短一行，四个大字：”诸事不宜“。“后天宜乎出门。”他正好怂恿，“过了后天，就得隔五天才有好日子，我常在外面跑，无所谓，你好久不出门了，该挑个好日子。”“那，”庞二略一沉吟，毅然作了决定：“准定后天走。”

“What should have been a brilliant success has become this wretched muddle. That is what I cannot understand. With Hu’s skill and Gu’s, backed by Hu’s resources and mine, I cannot believe they would fail to get the better of the foreigners!” “Exactly!” Liu looked as though the thought had only just been suggested to him. Blinking and frowning, he said, “By rights, it should not have happened. When I return to Shanghai, I must ask him why.” “We shall go together,” Pang promptly offered. “I have wanted to go for some time, but could not leave because of my mother’s birthday. There are still a few guests to whom I owe particular attention. They will all leave tomorrow, so we could set out the day after.” An almanac happened to lie on the desk. Liu opened it and found the entry for the day after tomorrow. Beneath a large “Auspicious” was a dense row of small characters. Plainly it was a lucky day. There was a saying about almanacs: “A fool looks for the long entry.” Long entries listed the many activities favored that day. An unlucky “broken day” had only the short warning, “Nothing should be undertaken.” “The day after tomorrow favors travel,” Liu urged. “After that, there is no good day for another five days. I travel so often that it makes no difference to me, but you have not been away for some time. You ought to choose a lucky day.” Pang considered briefly, then decided. “Very well. We shall definitely leave the day after tomorrow.”

于是，刘不才陪客，庞二料理出门的杂物。纨袴子弟好面子，送人的礼物就装了半船，除了南浔的土产以外，还有两箱瓷器，是景德镇定烧的，庞老太太“六秩华诞”的寿碗，预备分送那种礼到人不到的亲友。五月底的天气，又闷又热，出门是一大苦事，但庞二有庞二的办法，在水路上“放夜站”，白天找浓密的柳荫下将船泊下，船是两条，一条装行李，住佣人，一条是他跟刘不才的客船，十分宽敞，听差的以外，随带一位十分伶俐的小丫头服侍，纳凉、品茗、喝酒、闲谈，十分逍遥自在。谈风月、谈赌经以外，少不得也谈到胡雪岩。庞二虽是纨袴，但出身生意人家，与做官人家那种昏天黑地、骄恣狂妄的“大少爷”毕竟不同，不但在生意买卖上相当精通，而且颇能识好坏、辨是非，加以刘不才处处小心，说到胡雪岩这一次的受窘，总是旁敲侧击，以逗人的怀疑和好奇为主。因此，庞二不能不拿古应春的信重新出来，再看一遍。这一看，使得他大为不安。当时因为家里正在做寿，贺客盈门，忙得不可开交，无暇细思，朱福年来了以后，也只是匆匆的交代一番，说照胡雪岩的意思办就是。这话乍看不错，其实错了，以自己与胡雪岩的交情，如何去赚他这个九五扣一万六千银子？当然是照洋人的原价收买。

Liu attended to the guests while Pang prepared for the journey. A wealthy young gentleman cared about appearances: the gifts he meant to distribute filled half a boat. Besides Nanxun specialties, there were two chests of porcelain birthday bowls, specially commissioned at Jingdezhen to commemorate his mother’s sixtieth birthday. These were for relatives and friends who had sent gifts but had not attended. The end of the fifth lunar month was oppressively hot, and traveling was a misery. Pang had his own solution. They made the water journey at night, mooring by day beneath thick willow shade. There were two boats: one for the luggage and servants, the other a spacious passenger boat for Pang and Liu. Besides his personal attendants, Pang had brought a particularly clever young maid. Enjoying the cool, drinking tea and wine, and chatting, they passed the time very pleasantly. Along with women and gambling, they naturally discussed Hu. Pang was a pampered son of wealth, but he came from a business family. He was quite different from the heedless, arrogant young masters of official households. He understood trade and could distinguish good from bad and right from wrong. Liu, moreover, was careful at every turn. Whenever Hu’s present difficulty arose, he approached it obliquely, chiefly to awaken suspicion and curiosity. Pang was thus led to take out Gu’s letter and read it again. This time it made him deeply uneasy. During the birthday festivities, with guests crowding the house, he had had no leisure to think. When Zhu arrived, he had merely told him in haste to do as Hu requested. That had seemed right, but was actually wrong. Given his friendship with Hu, how could he take sixteen thousand taels from him by buying at a five-percent discount? Naturally, he ought to buy at the full price originally offered by the foreigner.

“糟了！糟了！”他不胜懊丧地说：“老胡心里一定骂我不够朋友！刘三哥，你要替我解释。”接着，他把他的疏忽，说了给刘不才听。“庞二哥，你也太过虑了，老胡绝不是那种人！感激你帮忙还来不及，哪里会多心？”“这叫什么帮忙？要帮忙就该……”庞二突然顿住，心里涌起好些疑问。道理是很明白地摆在那里，要讲“帮忙”，就得跟胡雪岩采取一致的态度，迫使洋人就范。论彼此的交情，应该这么办，况且过去又有约定，更应当这么办。而目前的情形是，显而易见的各行其是了。到底是胡雪岩自己知难而退，解消了齐心一致对付洋人的约定，还是另有其他原故？必须弄个清楚。纨袴子弟都是有了疑问，渴望立即求得解答的脾气，所以庞二吩咐船家，彻夜赶路，兼程而进，到了上海，邀刘不才一起在“一品香”客栈住下，随即命他的贴身跟班庞义，去找朱福年来见面。在路上，刘不才已隐约听庞二谈起他的困惑，心里在想，这一见上面，说不定有一顿声色俱厉的斥责，自己是外人，夹在中间，诸多不便，因而表示要先去看胡雪岩，庞二亦不坚留，只说等下请他约了胡雪岩一起来，大家好好叙一叙。

“Terrible, terrible!” Pang exclaimed in distress. “Hu must be cursing me for being a poor friend. Third Brother Liu, you must explain for me.” He told Liu how he had been careless. “Brother Pang, you worry too much. Hu is not that sort of man. He can scarcely thank you enough for helping him. Why should he take offense?” “What sort of help is that? To help him properly, I should...” Pang stopped abruptly, his mind filling with questions. The answer was plain. Helping Hu meant standing with him and forcing the foreign merchant to yield. Their friendship required it; their earlier agreement made it still more necessary. Yet they were plainly pursuing separate courses. Had Hu himself retreated before the difficulty and abandoned their agreement to stand together, or was there some other reason? Pang must find out. Like other pampered young gentlemen, once a question arose he wanted an immediate answer. He ordered the boatmen to travel all night and press on at full speed. On reaching Shanghai, he invited Liu to stay with him at the Yipinxiang Inn, then immediately sent his personal attendant, Pang Yi, to summon Zhu Funian. During the journey Liu had heard enough of Pang’s doubts to suspect that their meeting might bring a furious reprimand. As an outsider, he would be awkwardly placed between them. He therefore said that he must go and see Hu first. Pang did not insist on his staying, but asked him to bring Hu back afterward so that they could have a proper talk.

* * *“这下要‘猪八戒，的好看了！”听刘不才说了经过，古应春兴奋地看着胡雪岩说，“我们照计行事吧！”朱福年的底细已经摸清楚了，他本来是想“做小货”的，亏得有庞老太太做寿一事，到了南得，庞二先提胡雪岩的信，他见机改口，说是“正为这件事、要跟二少爷来请示”。这下，就如尤五所预料的，变成为东家赚钱，无可为非。古应春亦就针对这情形作了布置，有个丝商也是南浔人，生意不大，人却活跃，跟庞二极熟，与古应春也是好朋友，预备通过他的关系，将胡雪岩与朱福年的秘密交涉，透露给庞二。这个“秘密交涉”已经了结，五千银子已经退了回来。古应春“存心不良”，另外打张收条给他，将同兴钱庄的笔据，捏在手里，作为把柄。但是胡雪岩却不愿意这样做了。“不必，不必！一则庞二很讲交情，必定有句话给我，二则朱福年也知道厉害了，何必敲他的饭碗？”他说，“我们还是从正路上去走最好。”所谓“正路”就是将交情拉得格外近，当时决定，借怡情老二的地方，为庞二接风。本来想即时去看他，当面邀约，怕他正跟朱福年谈话，诸多不便，决定先发请帖。“有个人要请他作陪客。”古应春笑嘻嘻他说，是不怀好意的神气。“你是说朱福年？”胡雪岩说，“照道理应该。不过，我看他不会来。”“不管他来不来？发了再说！”

“Now Pigsy is in for it!” Having heard Liu’s account, Gu turned excitedly to Hu. “Let us proceed as planned!” They had established what Zhu was doing. He had originally intended to trade on his own account. But the celebration of Pang’s mother’s birthday had intervened. At Nanxun, Pang mentioned Hu’s letter first, and Zhu promptly changed his story, saying that this was precisely the matter on which he had come to ask the Second Young Master’s instructions. As You had foreseen, it had thus become a legitimate transaction to make money for his employer. Gu had made arrangements to meet this development. A lively, small-scale silk merchant from Nanxun knew Pang well and was also Gu’s good friend. Through him, Gu intended to disclose Hu’s secret dealings with Zhu to Pang. That private arrangement had already been brought to an end: the five thousand taels had been returned. With deliberate malice, Gu had issued a separate receipt to Zhu and kept Tongxing’s original document as evidence against him. Hu, however, no longer wished to pursue this course. “No need. Pang values friendship and is sure to give me some satisfaction. Besides, Zhu has learned his lesson. Why break his rice bowl? We had better take the proper course.” By the proper course, Hu meant drawing his friendship with Pang still closer. They decided to give him a welcoming dinner at Second Miss’s rooms in Yiqing House. Hu had meant to call at once and invite him personally, but the possibility that Pang was talking to Zhu made a visit inconvenient. He would send an invitation first. “There is someone else we should invite,” Gu said with a smile that suggested no good intentions. “You mean Zhu? Strictly speaking, we ought to. But I doubt he will come.” “Whether he comes or not, send it!”

请帖送到一品香，带回来一网篮的东西，有寿碗，有土产，另外还有庞二的一封信，道谢以外，表明准时践约。时刻定的是“西正”，也就是傍晚六点钟，庞二却是五点半钟就到了。欢然道故之余，胡雪岩为他引见了尤五和古应春。庞二对古应春慕名已久，此时见他是个举止漂亮、衣饰时新的外场人物，越有好感。至于对尤五，听说他是漕帮中的顶儿尖儿，先就浮起一层神秘之感，因而看他朴实拙讷，更为好奇。纨袴子弟常喜结交江湖人物，尤五又是忠厚可亲的样子，自然一见如故。觉得这天来赴胡雪岩的邀约，大有所得。“你那里的那位朱先生呢？”胡雪岩问道：“怎么不跟你一起来。”一提到朱福年，庞二的笑容尽敛，代之而起的神色，不仅歉仄，还有恼怒。“ 老胡，”他略一踌躇，“还是我们私底下谈的好。”他又转脸问怡情老二：“二阿姐，可有清静房间，让我们谈一歇？”“有的，请过来。”怡情老二带他们到了尤五平时烧酒的小房间，红木炕床上摆着现成的烟盘，她一面点上那盏“太谷灯”，一面问道：“庞二少，要不要烧一口白相？”庞二喜欢躺烟盘，但并没有瘾，眼时有正事要谈，无心烧烟来玩，便摇摇头，表示不要。怡情老二也知道他们讲的是“私话”，便悄悄退了出去，顺手掩上了房门。

The invitation sent to the Yipinxiang Inn brought back a basket of gifts: birthday bowls, local specialties, and a letter in which Pang thanked Hu and promised to arrive punctually. Dinner was set for six in the evening, but Pang came at half past five. After a cheerful exchange of greetings and recollections, Hu introduced You and Gu. Pang had long known Gu by reputation. Finding him a man of polished manners, fashionable clothes, and easy social presence increased his liking. As for You, hearing that he was a leading figure in the Grain Transport Brotherhood lent him an immediate air of mystery. His plain, awkward manner only sharpened Pang’s curiosity. Wealthy young gentlemen often enjoyed knowing men of the brotherhoods, and You seemed honest and approachable. They were soon as friendly as old acquaintances. Pang felt that accepting Hu’s invitation had brought him much. “Where is your Mr Zhu?” Hu asked. “Why did he not come with you?” At the mention of Zhu, Pang’s smile disappeared. His expression showed not only embarrassment but anger. “Old Hu,” he said after a pause, “we had better discuss this privately.” Turning to Second Miss, he asked, “Second Sister, is there a quiet room where we can talk?” “Certainly. This way, please.” She led them to the little room where You usually smoked opium. A smoking tray stood ready on the rosewood couch. As she lit the Taigu lamp, she asked, “Second Young Master Pang, would you like a pipe?” Pang enjoyed reclining by an opium tray but had no habit. With serious business to discuss, he had no inclination to smoke for amusement and shook his head. Knowing that their conversation was private, Second Miss withdrew quietly and closed the door.

“老胡，”庞二的声音很奇怪，是充满着忧虑，“你看我那个性朱的，人怎么样？”胡雪岩略一沉吟答说：“我跟他不熟。”“人虽不熟，你跟他有过交往。你的这双眼睛，象电火一样，什么都瞒不过你。我们是好朋友，而且说句老实话，我佩服的人也没有几个，你就应该知无不言、言无不尽。”这番话说得太恳切了，使胡雪岩在感动以外，更有不安，拿他的话细细玩味了一番，似乎是他对朱福年起了绝大的怀疑。莫非……“姓朱的拆了你的什么烂污？”他忍不住问出口来。“现在还不敢说。”庞二点点头，“我一直当他忠心耿耿，人也能干。现在才知道不是这么回事。““怎么呢？”“事情就是从你身上起的。我在想，既然我答应了你，请你全权去跟洋人打交道，何以会搞成这个样子。所以一到就找了朱福年来问，越问越不对，一时也说不清楚，我只觉得他好象不知道我跟你的交情，跟你不大合作。老胡，”庞二加强语气问：“是不是这样？”胡雪岩不肯马上回答，有意踌躇了一会才说：“事情已经过去了，不必再谈它。”

“Old Hu,” Pang began in a strange, anxious voice, “what do you think of that man Zhu?” Hu considered briefly. “I do not know him well.” “Perhaps not, but you have had dealings with him. Those eyes of yours are like lightning. Nothing escapes them. We are good friends, and to tell you the truth, there are few men I admire. You must tell me everything you know, without holding anything back.” His sincerity moved Hu and also made him uneasy. Considering the words carefully, he felt that Pang must have developed grave suspicions of Zhu. Could it be...? “Has Zhu been making a mess of your affairs?” he could not help asking. “I cannot yet be certain.” Pang nodded. “I always thought him utterly loyal as well as capable. Now I find that things are not as I supposed.” “How so?” “It all began with your business. I wondered why matters had turned out this way when I had agreed to give you full authority to deal with the foreigners. So as soon as I arrived, I sent for Zhu and questioned him. The more I asked, the less satisfactory his answers became. It would take too long to explain everything. I felt that he hardly seemed to understand our friendship and had not cooperated with you. Old Hu,” he asked emphatically, “is that true?” Hu chose not to answer at once. After a deliberate hesitation, he said, “It is over. There is no need to discuss it further.”

“这样说来是有的！可见我的想法不错。接下来我问我自己的生意。”庞二咽了口唾沫，很吃力他说：“人与人之间，不能起疑心，一起疑心，处处都是毛病……”“这话也不尽然。”胡雪岩插了句嘴。“我不是冤枉他，确确实实有毛病。”“是不是帐上有毛病？”“帐还没有看，不过大致问了几笔帐，我已经发现有讲不通的地方。譬如说你这面吧，我在南浔就关照他：照人家胡老板的意思办。今天问他，他说货价还没有送过来，这就不对了。”“这没有什么不对。”胡雪岩要表示风度，便得回护朱福年，“照交易的规矩，应该由我们这面跟他去接头，我们因为货色先要盘一盘，算清楚确数，才能结帐，所以耽搁下来了。”“不然！”庞二大摇其头，“信义通商，你我的交情，他不是不晓得，既然我这样说了，他应该先把贷款送过来，帐随后再结不要紧。现在他的做法，替我得罪朋友，可以说是得罪同业，我要他做啥。”听庞二的口气，预备撤换朱福年。这原是胡雪岩的本意，现在他的想法不同了，庞二够朋友，他为庞二设想，不能杂以私意，因此他也大摇其头。

“Then it is true! My suspicions were right. After that I asked about my own business.” Pang swallowed and continued with difficulty. “Once you begin to suspect someone, you find faults everywhere...” “That is not always so,” Hu interjected. “I am not wronging him. There really are faults.” “In the accounts?” “I have not examined the books yet, but I asked about a few transactions and already found things that made no sense. Take your affair. In Nanxun I told him to do as Mr Hu wished. When I asked today, he said that payment for the goods had not yet been sent to you. That is wrong.” “There is nothing wrong with it.” To behave generously, Hu had to defend Zhu. “Under the usual procedure, we should contact him first. We need to check our stock and establish the exact quantity before settling the account. That has caused the delay.” “No!” Pang shook his head vigorously. “Business rests on good faith. He knows our friendship. Once I had given those instructions, he should have sent the payment first; we could settle the precise account afterward. Instead, his conduct makes enemies of my friends—of my fellow merchants, you might say. What use have I for him?” His tone suggested that he meant to dismiss Zhu. That had originally been Hu’s intention, but now his thinking had changed. Pang had proved a true friend. Hu must consider Pang’s interests without allowing private motives to intrude, so he too shook his head.

“庞二哥，光是为这件事，你大光其火，是说不通的……”“当然，还有别的。”庞二抢着说，“譬如，泥城桥有块地皮，也是他来跟我说的，预备买下来造市房出租。这话有两个月了，我总以为他已经成交，今天一问，说是让人家捷足先登了。问买主是哪个，他又说不出来。老胡，你想，既然晓得人家捷足先登，怎么会不晓得人家姓啥？为啥不问一问买主？所以我要去查一查，看看是不是他自己在捣鬼？此外还有好些前言不搭后语的地方，从前我相信他，都忽略了，现在听起来，处处是毛病。这个人决不能再用。你说是不是？”胡雪岩对那方面的情形，不甚明了，不肯轻作断语，未答之前，先问一句：“你那面‘抓总’的是哪个？”“就是他！我那样子信任他，他对不起我，这个人真是丧尽天良。”庞二愤愤地答说。其实这是无足为奇的事，豪门巨室的帐户，明欺暗骗，东家跌倒，西宾吃饱的情形，比比皆是。看样子朱福年也是心狠手辣的人，照庞二这种态度，说不定他一不做，二不休，反会出大毛病。

“Brother Pang, if this alone has made you so angry, I cannot agree...” “There is more, of course,” Pang interrupted. “For example, a piece of land at Nicheng Bridge. He brought it to my attention, and we intended to buy it and build commercial premises to let. That was two months ago. I always assumed the purchase had been completed. Today, when I asked, he said that someone else had got there first. But when I asked who the buyer was, he could not tell me. Think of it, Hu: if he knew someone had bought it first, how could he not know the buyer’s name? Why had he not asked? I mean to investigate and see whether he has been playing some trick himself. There are many other contradictions in what he says. I trusted him before and overlooked them; now everything sounds wrong. I cannot keep employing this man. Don’t you agree?” Hu knew too little of Pang’s affairs to give a hasty judgment. Before answering, he asked, “Who is in overall charge on your side?” “He is! I trusted him so completely, and he has betrayed me. The man has no conscience!” Pang replied angrily. There was nothing unusual in this. Open and concealed fraud in the finances of wealthy households was commonplace: when the master fell, his retainers grew fat. Zhu appeared to be a ruthless man. Faced with an employer in Pang’s present mood, he might decide to go to extremes, and serious trouble could follow.

因此他压容警告：“庞二哥，你千万动不得！他现在搞了些啥花样，你还不清楚，你在明里，他在暗里，你的形势就不利。大家不破面子，他还不敢明目张胆出大毛病。一听说你有动他的意思，先下手为强，拆你个大烂污，你怎么收拾？”这话说得庞二一愣，好半天答不出话来。“不说别的，一本总帐在他手里，交易往来，人欠欠人，只有他最清楚，帐里出点毛病，等你弄清楚，已是一两个月以后的事，他早就布置好了。你又能奈其何？”“老胡，亏得你提醒我！现在没有别的好说了，你我的交情，你不能不帮我这个大忙。”“当然。只要帮得上，你说，怎么帮法？”“他的毛病，一定瞒不过你，我不说请他走路的话，只请你接管我的帐，替我仔仔细细查一查他的毛病。”“这件事，我不敢从命。做不到！”庞二大为沮丧：“我晓得的，你待人宽厚，不肯得罪人。”“这不是这么说法！庞二哥你的事，为你得罪人，我也认了，不过这洋做法要有用才行，徒然得罪人，没有益处，何必去做它？你听我说……”

Hu therefore grew grave and warned him, “Brother Pang, you must not act against him yet. You still do not know what tricks he has been playing. You are in the open while he is in the dark; that puts you at a disadvantage. So long as neither of you breaks openly with the other, he will not dare cause flagrant trouble. But if he hears that you mean to move against him, he may strike first and leave you with a terrible mess. How will you put it right?” Pang was taken aback and could not answer for some time. “To take just one thing, he has the general ledger. He knows better than anyone who owes you money and whom you owe. If something goes wrong in the accounts, it may take you a month or two to discover it. By then he will have made all his arrangements. What could you do to him?” “Old Hu, thank goodness you reminded me! There is nothing more to say. With our friendship, you must help me out of this.” “Of course. If I can help, tell me how.” “He could never hide his tricks from you. I shall say nothing about dismissing him. I shall merely ask you to take charge of my accounts and examine them carefully for any wrongdoing.” “I cannot oblige you in that. It would not work.” Pang was deeply disappointed. “I know. You are generous to people and do not like to offend them.” “That is not the point. For your sake, Brother Pang, I would willingly offend someone. But it must achieve something. Why offend a man for no benefit? Hear me out.”

胡雪岩有三点理由，第一，怕打草惊蛇，反逼得朱福年去舞弊使坏，第二，庞二手下用的人很多，就算要换朱福年，也该从伙计当中去挑选替手，徐图整顿，此刻弄个不相干的人去查帐，仿佛看大家都靠不住，是跟朱福年走在一条路上，通同作弊，岂不令人寒心？第三，胡雪岩也实在抽不出那许多工夫替他专办这件事。“而况，我对你那方面的情形又不清楚，贸贸然下手，一年半载不能完事，在我有没有工夫，且不去说它，就怕一年半载下来，查不出名堂，那时你做东家的，对伙计如何交代？”“这没有什么！我现在可以断定，朱福年一定有毛病。”“毛病可以弥补的……”“对啊！”庞二抢着说道：“只要你一去，他看见厉害的人来了，赶紧想法子把他的毛病弥补起来，你不就帮了我的大忙了吗？”这话倒也驳他不倒。胡雪岩想了一会，总觉得庞二的做法，不甚妥当，就算将朱福年的毛病查出来了，甚至于照庞二的如意算盘，把胡雪岩三个字抬了出去，就能叫朱福年敛迹，弥补弊病，然而以后还用不用他呢？这样想着，便问出口来：“庞二哥，这朱某人的本事到底怎么样？”“本事是有的。”“如果他肯改过，实实在在替你办事，你还用不用他？”“如果是这佯，当然可以用。不过……”他摇摇头，觉得说下去就没有味道了。

Hu had three reasons. First, he feared that raising the alarm would drive Zhu Funian into fraud or deliberate mischief. Second, Pang employed many men. Even if Zhu were to be replaced, a successor should be chosen from among the staff and improvements made gradually. To bring in an outsider to inspect the accounts would suggest that everyone was untrustworthy and in league with Zhu. Would that not dishearten them? Third, Hu really could not spare the time to devote himself to the task. “Besides, I know nothing of the circumstances of your business. If I plunge in unprepared, it might take six months or a year. Leave aside whether I can spare the time. Suppose that after all those months I find nothing definite. How would you, as their employer, explain yourself to the staff?” “That does not matter. I am now certain there is something wrong with Zhu.” “Irregularities can be made good—” “Exactly!” Pang interrupted. “Once you arrive, he will see that a formidable man has come and hurry to put his irregularities right. Would that not be a great service to me?” It was difficult to refute this. Hu thought for a while, but still felt that Pang’s approach was unsatisfactory. Even if he uncovered Zhu’s misconduct—or if, as Pang hoped, merely invoking Hu Xueyan’s name made Zhu mend his ways and repair the damage—would Pang continue to employ him afterwards? He put the question aloud. “Brother Pang, how capable is this man Zhu?” “He has ability.” “If he were willing to reform and serve you honestly, would you still employ him?” “In that case, of course. But—” Pang shook his head, feeling that there was little point in continuing.

“我懂你的意思。”胡雪岩停了一下说，“人不对，请他走路。这是普通人的做法，你庞二哥要么不出马，一出马就要叫人晓得厉害，佩服你确是有一套。”这两句话，最配争强好胜的纨绔脾气，所以庞二精神一振，有了笑容。“老胡，你这两句话我交关听得进。你倒再说说看，应该怎么做法？”“要象诸葛亮‘七擒孟获’那样，‘火烧藤甲兵’不足为奇，要烧得他服帖，死心塌地替你出力，才算本事。”“话是一点都不错，不过，”庞二踌躇着说，“我实在没有这份本事。”说到这里，突然眼睛一亮，拍着自己的后脑勺：“我真糊涂了！现成的诸葛亮在这里。老胡，”他停了一下，喜逐颜开地又说，“我送你股份，你算是跟我台伙，也是老板的身分，名正言顺来管事，不就可以收服朱福年了吗？”胡雪岩的打算就是如此，不过自己说不出口，难得庞二的想法相同。光就是这一点，使值得替他出一番力了。胡雪岩有项过人的长处，能在心血来潮之际，作出重要而正确的决定，思路快不足为奇，能快又能细致深刻，就只有他有此本事。

“I understand what you mean.” Hu paused. “If a man is no good, dismiss him: that is the ordinary way. But you, Brother Pang, should either stay out of the field or, once you enter it, make everyone recognize your strength and admire your methods.” This appealed perfectly to the competitive pride of a wealthy young gentleman. Pang brightened and smiled. “Old Hu, that is exactly the sort of thing I like to hear. Tell me more. What should I do?” “Be like Zhuge Liang, capturing Meng Huo seven times. Burning the troops in rattan armour was nothing remarkable. The real achievement was to make him submit wholeheartedly and serve with complete devotion.” “You are quite right. But I really have no such ability.” Suddenly Pang’s eyes lit up. He slapped the back of his head. “What a fool I am! Here is Zhuge Liang, ready to hand. Old Hu”—he paused, then continued with a delighted smile—“I shall give you shares. You will be my partner, an owner yourself, with every right to take charge. Then you can bring Zhu Funian to heel!” This was precisely what Hu had intended, though he could hardly propose it himself. That Pang had reached the same idea was reason enough to make a considerable effort on his behalf. Hu possessed an exceptional gift: on the spur of the moment, he could make important decisions and make them correctly. Quick thinking alone was nothing extraordinary. To think quickly while remaining thorough and penetrating was his particular strength.

此刻便是这样。因为庞二先作提议，就是个极好的机会，他抓住了题目的精义，立即使有一篇好文章交卷。“庞二哥，”他正色说道，“生意是生意！分花红彼此礼让，是交朋友的情分、义气，不可一概而论。我是不赞成吃干股这一套花佯的，如果你看得起我，愿意让我搭点股份，我交现银出来。““好啊！”庞二欣然同意，因为这一来，胡雪岩就更加出力。他问：“你想要多少股子？”“我的实力比你差得远，只能来个两成。”“一句话！我们重新盘过，你十万，我四十万，我们五十万银子下手，上海的市面，可以捏在手里了。”“准定如此，庞二哥，”胡雪岩带点兴奋的神色，“我的钱庄，你也来点股子。索性大家滚在一起，有福同享，有难同当，人看好不好？”“怎么不好！礼尚往来，再好不过！而且便宜不落外方，你在上海立一爿分号起来，我们自己的款了存在自己的钱庄里，岂不方便？”胡雪岩的打算就是如此，他还有进一步的打算，此刻却不宜先露，只是连连称“是”。接着又说定庞二的股份，真个礼尚往来，他也是十万，彼此只要立个合伙的合同，划一笔帐，都不必另拨现银。

So it was now. Pang’s own proposal had presented an excellent opportunity. Hu grasped its essential point and immediately had his response ready. “Brother Pang, business is business,” he said seriously. “Giving one another a share of profits is a matter of friendship and loyalty. The two must not be confused. I do not approve of holding shares without putting in capital. If you think well enough of me to let me take a stake, I shall pay for it in silver.” “Excellent!” Pang readily agreed: this would give Hu still more reason to work hard. “How large a stake would you like?” “My means are far below yours. I could manage only two tenths.” “Agreed! We shall make a fresh reckoning. You put in a hundred thousand taels and I four hundred thousand. Starting with half a million, we can hold the Shanghai market in our hands.” “Then that is settled.” Hu looked a little excited. “Brother Pang, you must take a stake in my bank too. Let us join our interests completely, sharing good fortune and hardship alike. What do you say?” “Why not? Reciprocity could not be better. And the benefit will stay among ourselves. Establish a branch in Shanghai, and we can keep our own money in our own bank. How convenient!” This was exactly Hu’s plan. He had something further in mind, but it was too early to reveal it, so he merely agreed repeatedly. They then settled Pang’s contribution: in true reciprocity, it would also be a hundred thousand taels. All they needed was a partnership agreement and a transfer in the books; neither would have to send over additional cash.

他们谈得津津有味，外面却等得心急了，酒已经回烫过两遍，再烫就要走味，怡情老二推门望到第三遍，看他们还没有住口的样子，忍不住便轻轻咳嗽了一声。这下才惊醒了庞二，歉然说道：“对不起，对不起，害他们久等了，我们出去吧！”等坐定下来，第一件事是叫局。怡情老二亲自捧过一只长方红木托盘，里面是笔砚局票，拈笔在手，先问庞二。“我好久没有到上海来了，市面不灵。”他想了想说：“叫宝琴老三吧？”“是怡红院的宝琴老三吗？”怡情老二问。“对了。怡红院。”“这一节不做了。”怡情老二说，“节前嫁了个道台，做官太太去了。”于是庞二又想了两个人，非常不巧，不是从良，便是开了码头，他不免怅惘，说一声：“随便找好了！”“你替庞二少做个媒吧。”尤五对怡情老二说了这一句，便又转脸问庞二：“喜欢啥样子的？”“脾气爽快的好。”“有了！”怡情老二喜滋滋他说，“我替庞二少保荐一个，包管中意。”这个人叫怡云老七，就在怡情院“铺房间”，她怕庞二以为她有意照应小姐妹，不管好歹，硬塞给他，所以只说名字，不说地方。刘不才会意，也不多问，将一叠局票写好，交给“相帮”发了出去。

They were absorbed in their talk, but the people outside were growing impatient. The wine had already been warmed twice; another warming would spoil its flavour. When Second Miss opened the door for the third time and saw no sign of their stopping, she could not resist a discreet cough. Only then did Pang come to himself. “My apologies! We have kept everyone waiting. Let us go out.” Once they were seated, the first business was to summon the courtesans. Second Miss personally brought a long rosewood tray holding brush, inkstone, and invitation cards. Taking up the brush, she asked Pang first. “I have not been to Shanghai for a long time and am out of touch.” He thought for a moment. “Shall we ask for Third Miss Baoqin?” “Third Miss Baoqin of Yihong House?” “Yes, Yihong House.” “She is no longer working this season. Before the festival she married a circuit intendant and became an official’s wife.” Pang thought of two more women, but his luck was poor: they had either married out of the profession or moved elsewhere to work. A little wistfully, he said, “Find anyone you like.” “Make a match for Second Master Pang,” You Laowu told Second Miss, then turned to Pang. “What sort do you like?” “Someone with a frank, easy temper.” “I have just the one!” Second Miss said happily. “Let me recommend someone. I guarantee you will like her.” The woman was called Seventh Miss Yiyun and had rooms at Yiqing House itself. Second Miss feared Pang might suppose she was pushing a sister of the house on him merely to help her, regardless of suitability. She therefore gave only the name, not the address. Liu understood and asked no questions. He filled out a stack of invitations and gave them to an attendant to dispatch.

隔不多久，莲步姗姗进来一个丽人，鹅蛋脸，高身材，长眉入鬓，神采飞扬，是那种一见便能令人目眩神移的尤物。在座的人都没有见过她，她却全认得，含笑一一招呼，最后才在庞二身后坐下，未曾开口，先抛媚眼，然后轻声说道：“二少，长远不见了！”“原来你们是老相好！”刘不才起哄，“庞二哥怎不早说？罚酒，罚酒。”“你看！”庞二对怡云老七说，“你一来就害我罚酒。我们啥地方见过？我怎么想不起来？““在怡红院。二少，你自然想不起了，一则贵人多忘事，二则也看我不上眼。”庞二将牙一龇，故意说道：“好酸！”“庞二哥，你不要假惺惺装不认识。这杯酒非罚不可！”刘不才将一杯酒端了过来。庞二顺手就端向怡云老七，意思是要她代酒，怡云老七毫无难色，一仰脸干了那杯酒。“谢谢！”庞二开始有了笑容。于是怡云老七执壶敬酒，酒量很好，一个个都照了杯，最后是自己喝了半杯酒，剩下的半杯敬庞二，却又温柔地问：“嫌不嫌脏？”杯沿脂痕宛然，美人余泽，脏之何有？庞二笑嘻嘻地干了酒，大家也都相视而笑，笑庞二是如此容易地掉入怡云老七的罗网中。

Before long a beauty entered with graceful steps: tall, with an oval face, long eyebrows sweeping towards her temples, and a radiant liveliness that could dazzle a man at first sight. None of those present had seen her before, yet she knew them all and greeted each with a smile. Finally she sat behind Pang. Before speaking, she cast him an enticing glance, then said softly, “Second Master, it has been such a long time!” “So you are old sweethearts!” Liu raised a clamour. “Why did you not tell us, Brother Pang? A penalty cup!” “You see?” Pang told Yiyun. “You have only just arrived, and already you have landed me with a drinking penalty. Where have we met? Why can I not remember?” “At Yihong House. Naturally you would not remember. Important men have short memories, and besides, you never thought me worth a glance.” Pang bared his teeth deliberately. “How sour!” “Brother Pang, stop pretending not to recognize her. You must drink this cup.” Liu brought him the wine. Pang promptly held it out to Yiyun, asking her to drink on his behalf. Without the least reluctance, she tipped back her head and emptied it. “Thank you!” Pang began to smile. She then took the wine pot and toasted the company. Her capacity was excellent; she drank with each man in turn, showing her empty cup. Finally she drank half a cup herself and offered the remaining half to Pang, asking tenderly, “Do you mind its being soiled?” Rouge marked the rim: what could be dirty about a beauty’s lingering traces? Pang drank it with a delighted smile. The others exchanged smiles too, amused at how easily he had fallen into her net.

“你住在哪里？”庞二悄然相问。“ 等下告诉你。”他还想说什么，只听门帘响动，胡雪岩和刘不才叫的局，陆续到了。为求热闹，叫得不少，片刻之间，莺莺燕燕，翩然群集，猜拳的猜拳，唱戏的唱戏，因为庞二是主客，自然都应酬他，左顾右应，忙得不可开交。叫的局来了又去，川流不息，怡云老七却始终不动，娘姨拿进一叠局票，悄悄塞了过来，她看都不看、就交了回去，只说得一声：“随它去！”这一下反倒使得庞二过意不去了，“你管你出局去！”他说，“回头我们‘翻台，过来。你住得远不远？”“是真的要翻台过来？”“这，我骗你干什么？”怡云老七笑一笑不响，却依然坐着不动。“你先回去，预备预备，我们就过去。”“叫我回哪里去？”怡云老七用手一指，“喏，前厢房就是我的房间。”“原来你也在这里！”庞二顿觉意外，“为啥早不说？”“现在说也不晚。”怡云老七越发坐近了，手扳着他的肩，低声说道：“翻来翻去，都在一处地方。尤五少的面子，你就在这里多坐一会。回头到我那里去消夜好不好？”这便是一种暗示，有身分的“红棺人”，通常是不肯作此露骨的表示的，所以庞二颇为高兴。

“Where do you live?” Pang asked quietly. “I shall tell you later.” He wanted to say more, but the door curtain stirred. The women summoned by Hu and Liu began arriving one after another. To make the party lively, they had invited quite a number. Soon the room was filled with graceful, chattering beauties: some played drinking games, others sang opera. Pang was the guest of honour, so all attended to him, and he scarcely knew which way to turn. The summoned women came and went in an endless stream, but Yiyun remained. A maid slipped her a stack of invitation cards. Without looking at them, she handed them back. “Never mind them.” This made Pang feel guilty. “Do go to your engagements,” he said. “We shall move the party to your place afterwards. Is it far away?” “Do you really mean to come?” “Why should I deceive you?” She smiled without answering and remained seated. “Go back and make your preparations. We shall follow.” “Where do you want me to go?” She pointed. “Those rooms in the front wing are mine.” “So you live here too!” Pang was surprised. “Why did you not say so?” “It is not too late to say it now.” She moved closer, rested a hand on his shoulder, and lowered her voice. “Wherever we move, it is all the same house. For Fifth Master You’s sake, stay here a little longer. Afterwards, will you come to my rooms for supper?” This was a hint of the kind that a sought-after courtesan with a reputation to maintain would not ordinarily make so openly. Pang was therefore particularly pleased.

他们低眉垂眼，款款深谈的神情，都落入旁人眼中，也猜得到他们已有密约，所以为了予人方便，作主人的竟一反常例，提议早早散席，理由是因为怕庞二在路上辛苦了，需要早早休息。“多谢关切！”庞二指着怡云老七说，“我答应到她那里宵夜。大家一起过去坐一息。”怡云老七唯恐客人推辞，抢着先拜托怡情老二：“二阿姐，你替我讲一声，请各位老爷，赏我个面子。”直待大家都答应了，怡云老七方始匆匆赶回自己房间去准备。等庞二陪春客人一到，已经准备停当，虽是消夜，依然丰盛，还特地用了一副“银家伙”，开了一小坛十年陈的“竹叶青”，此外果盘茶烟，无不精美，这又合了庞二的脾胃，脸上飞了金似地，相当得意。“明天原班人马在这里，我不发帖子了。”“好的。”刘不才说，“后天该我……”“不行！刘三哥！你再让我两天，后天、大后天仍旧应该是我的，还是在这里。”阔客捧场，也要有个规矩，所以刘不才问道：“明天算是庞二哥还席，后天、大后天算是啥名堂？““我跟老胡的交情，还席可以摆在后头……”照庞二的说法，明天是他诚意结交新朋友，专请尤五和古应春，后天则是酬谢刘不才，在南浔替他照料宾客，大后天才是不胡雪岩的席，花丛哄饮，能够说得出道理，没有不凑兴的道理，因而大家都答应了，然后又徘定次序，接下来是刘、古、尤三人做主人。庞二的兴致极好，还要叫局，只是大家都说良朋良夜，清谈最好，只把抬情老二找了来，浅斟低酌，又消磨了一个时辰，方始兴尽而散。当然，这一夜的庞二是不会再回一品香了。

Their lowered eyes and intimate conversation had not escaped the others, who could guess that they had made a private arrangement. To oblige them, their hosts departed from the usual practice and proposed ending the banquet early, on the grounds that Pang must be tired from his journey and needed rest. “Thank you for your concern!” Pang pointed to Yiyun. “I have promised to take supper at her place. Come over with me and sit a while.” Afraid that the guests might decline, Yiyun quickly appealed to Second Miss. “Second Sister, please speak for me. Ask the gentlemen to honour me.” Only when all had agreed did she hurry back to her rooms to prepare. By the time Pang arrived with his friends, everything was ready. Though it was only supper, the spread was lavish. She had brought out a set of silverware and opened a little jar of ten-year-old Zhuyeqing wine. The fruit, tea, and tobacco were all of the finest quality. This suited Pang perfectly. His face seemed to shine with gold, so pleased was he. “The same company here tomorrow. I shall send no formal invitations.” “Very well,” Liu said. “The day after tomorrow is my turn—” “No, Brother Liu! Give me another two days. The day after tomorrow and the following day must still be mine, and here again.” Even a wealthy patron’s generosity needed a proper form, so Liu asked, “Tomorrow can be your return banquet. But what are the next two occasions?” “With Old Hu and me, returning his hospitality can wait.” Pang’s explanation was that tomorrow he wished sincerely to cultivate new friends, so You and Gu would be his particular guests. The next day he would thank Liu for entertaining his visitors at Nanxun. Only on the third day would he return Hu’s hospitality. At a drinking party among the flowers, any plausible reason deserved support. Everyone agreed, then fixed the order afterwards: Liu, Gu, and You would host in turn. Pang was in excellent spirits and wanted to summon more women, but the others said that with good friends on such a fine night, quiet conversation was best. They brought in only Second Miss, sipped their wine, and passed another two hours before dispersing at last. Naturally, Pang would not return to the Yipinxiang Inn that night.

第二天午后，刘不才听从胡雪岩的指挥，特地去陪伴庞二。胡雪岩则与古庆春和尤五在裕记丝栈谈了一下午，听说了庞二与他昨天所谈的话，尤、古二人大为兴奋。能够与庞二合作，无论讲声势、讲实力，都是十分有利的事，尤其是在上海设一爿钱庄，现成有五十万银子这么个大户头作往来，这个局面的开展，是件非同小可的事。不过障碍也不是没有，“朱福年多年耕耘，视庞二的事业如禁膏，肯拱手上让人吗？”古应春怀着浓重的疑惑。“小爷叔，”尤五也说，“你在庞二面前已夸下口了，要‘七擒孟获’，我倒要问问，怎么个擒法？”“用不着七擒！”胡雪岩说：“昨天我在床上就想好了办法，要下一着狠棋。五哥，同兴的档手你熟不熟？”“你是说同兴钱庄？”尤五答道：“档手姓邵，镇江人，我不熟，不过我可以托朋友去说话。”“说要我自己来说，不有让第三者知道。你能不能托人介绍，大家见一面？”“这不难。你想要啥时候见面？”“越快越好。”“今天晚上就可以。应春，”尤五转脸说道，“你替我写封信给华佩卿。”

The following afternoon, at Hu’s direction, Liu went specially to keep Pang company. Hu spent the afternoon at Yuji Silk Warehouse with Gu and You. Both were greatly excited to hear what Pang and Hu had discussed. Cooperation with Pang would bring substantial advantages in influence and resources alike. In particular, opening a bank in Shanghai with a half-million-tael business ready to become a major customer would create an opportunity of immense consequence. There were obstacles, however. “Zhu Funian has worked at this for years and regards Pang’s business as his private preserve. Will he hand it over meekly?” Gu was deeply doubtful. “Little Uncle,” You added, “you have already promised Pang that you will capture Meng Huo seven times. How do you mean to do it?” “There is no need for seven captures. I worked out a method in bed last night. We must make a ruthless move. Brother Five, do you know the manager at Tongxing?” “You mean Tongxing Bank? His name is Shao, and he comes from Zhenjiang. I do not know him, but I can ask friends to approach him.” “I must speak to him myself. No third person can know about it. Can you get someone to introduce us?” “That is easy enough. When would you like to meet?” “The sooner the better.” “This evening would be possible.” You turned to Gu. “Yingchun, write a letter to Hua Peiqing for me.”

古应春也认识华佩卿，他是个书贾，跟北京的琉璃厂有联络，以前在江南旧家收买了善本古书，总是搭松江帮的漕船进京，所以跟尤五颇有交情。古应春跟他相识，就是从尤五的关系上来的。“今天晚上要应酬庞二。请他约一约，明天中午见面如何？”“随便你。”于是古应春用尤五的名义给华佩卿写了信，立即派“出店”送去。信上注明：“即晚候玉”，而回信在他们到怡情院赴约以前就收到了。华佩卿很热心，回信中说，接到信他立即照办，找到了同兴的档手邵仲甫，说明经过。邵仲甫也知道有胡雪岩这么一位同业，仰慕已久，乐于相交。不过他明天中午有个“非践不可之约”，所以华佩卿已经跟他约好，第二天上午吃早茶，由华佩卿作东。介绍认识以后，胡雪岩要跟邵仲甫单独相谈，“自行面约可也”。

Gu knew Hua Peiqing too. He was a bookseller with connections in Beijing’s Liulichang district. In the past, when he bought rare old editions from established Jiangnan families, he had always sent them to the capital on the Songjiang brotherhood’s grain boats. He was therefore on friendly terms with You, through whom Gu had met him. “We have to entertain Pang this evening. Could you ask Hua to arrange a meeting for tomorrow at noon?” “As you please.” Gu wrote in You’s name, and a messenger was sent off at once. The letter said, “Your reply is awaited this evening,” and it arrived before they left for the banquet at Yiqing House. Hua had been most obliging. On receiving the letter he had immediately sought out Tongxing’s manager, Shao Zhongfu, and explained the request. Shao already knew of Hu as a fellow banker and had long admired him; he would gladly make his acquaintance. Unfortunately, he had an engagement at noon the next day that he could not fail to keep. Hua had therefore arranged to host morning tea instead. Once they had been introduced, Hu could make his own appointment for a private conversation with Shao.

* * *名为“吃早茶”，其实是约在一家扬帮馆子里。扬州人早晨这一顿很讲究，先拿肴肉、干丝来吃酒，然后点过桥面，“浇头”也先炒出来下酒。主客一共四个人，胡雪岩是由尤五陪着去的，四碗面两样花色，炒出来两大盘浇头，一盘虾腰，一盘“马鞍桥”，华佩卿不断劝客，十分殷勤。彼此都是“外场人物”，做生意又讲究和气亲热，不似官场中人矜持，所以胡雪岩跟邵仲甫第一遭相见，就很熟了。尤五看华佩卿健谈而又健啖，这顿早酒，着实要消磨些工夫，便向胡雪岩使个眼色：“你跟邵先生有话，就这里借个地方谈谈，岂不省事？”“对，对！你们两位尽管请便，我跟尤五哥好久不见，也要叙叙。”于是一桌化做两桌，胡雪岩跟邵仲甫另外在僻静角落坐定，喝茶密谈。在这一顿点心的工夫中，胡雪岩对邵仲甫的性情，已有了解，不善言词而是心有丘壑的人，这路人物比较讲实际，动以利害则自能分辨，所以他决定开门见山，实话直说。

Though called “morning tea,” the meeting was at a restaurant serving Yangzhou food. Yangzhou people took considerable care over their morning meal. They began by drinking wine with jellied meat and finely shredded bean curd, then ordered guoqiao noodles. The toppings were cooked first and also served to accompany the wine. There were four men in all, for You had come with Hu. Their four bowls of noodles had two different toppings, brought on two large platters: shrimps and kidneys on one, and a dish called “Saddle Bridges” on the other. Hua urged them to eat with great hospitality. They were all men accustomed to dealing with the world, and business encouraged warmth and friendliness rather than the reserve of officials.
