Hu and Shao therefore felt at ease together at this first meeting. Seeing that Hua was as hearty an eater as he was a talker, You realized that the morning drinking would occupy some time. He signalled to Hu. “You have something to discuss with Mr Shao. Why not find a place here? It would save trouble.” “Yes, by all means!” Hua agreed. “Brother You and I have not met for ages. We have plenty to talk about too.” One table thus became two. Hu and Shao settled in a quiet corner to talk privately over tea. During the meal Hu had already formed an idea of Shao’s character. He was no eloquent talker, but a man with well-considered plans of his own. Such men were practical and could judge their interests clearly. Hu decided to come straight to the point.

“仲甫兄，”他问，“宝号跟宠家的‘恒记，有往来？”“是的。”邵仲甫答道，“我们做往来，不是一年了。”“那以后还要请你多帮忙。”胡雪岩说，“庞家二少爷已经到了上海，你总见过面了。”“还没有。约了今天中午见面。”胡雪岩心里明白，所谓“非践不可之约”，就是跟庞二见面。照此看来，他对庞二的重视，又不言可知，然则自己动以利害的打算，越显得不错，不过，胡雪岩灵机一动，改变了主意，“这样说，我们中午还要见面。”他说，“我有几句话，不妨明后天再谈。”邵仲甫跟恒记有多年的关系，所以跟恒记有往来的客户，大致也都了解，就没有听说过有胡雪岩在内。然而照他此刻的话来看，似乎跟庞二很熟，与恒记在生意上有密切的牵连，岂不费解？既为了生意上的关切，也为了好奇，邵仲甫何能置而不问，“雪岩兄，我们一见如故，有话尽说不妨！”他用套交情的方式来套话，“何必等到明后天？”在胡雪岩原是盘马弯弓，有意要引起邵仲甫的注意，见他这副神情，便知已经入彀，不妨略为透露，于是很快地答道：“原是一见如故，我才跟仲甫兄谈到深处。庞二哥是我的好朋友，最近进一步谈到彼此合伙。当然，恒记是以他为主，听他跟你老兄是怎么说，我们再细谈。彼此同业，要讲义气，没有不好谈的。”

“Brother Zhongfu,” he asked, “does your bank do business with the Pang family’s Hengji?” “Yes. We have dealt with them for years.” “Then I shall need your help in future too. Second Master Pang has reached Shanghai. I imagine you have seen him?” “Not yet. I am meeting him at noon today.” Hu understood: this was the engagement that could not be missed. The importance Shao attached to Pang was plain, confirming Hu’s judgment that an appeal to his interests would be effective. Then an idea struck him, and he changed his approach. “In that case we shall meet again at noon. What I have to say can wait until tomorrow or the next day.” Through his long connection with Hengji, Shao knew most of the people with whom it did business, but had never heard of Hu among them. Yet Hu now spoke as though he were close to Pang and intimately concerned with Hengji’s affairs. It was puzzling. Both his business interests and his curiosity made it impossible to let the matter rest. “Brother Xueyan, we feel like old friends at our first meeting. Speak freely.” He used a profession of friendship to draw Hu out. “Why wait until tomorrow or the next day?” Hu had deliberately held his bow drawn to attract Shao’s attention. Seeing his expression, he knew that the bait had taken and could reveal a little. “It is precisely because we feel like old friends that I am speaking to you so intimately. Brother Pang is a good friend of mine, and recently we have gone a step further and discussed a partnership. Naturally, he remains the principal man in Hengji. Once I know what he has said to you, we can talk in detail. As fellow bankers, we must honour our obligations to one another. There is nothing we cannot discuss.”

这几句话闪闪烁烁，越引人关切，邵仲甫拿他的话，一个字一个字地体味了一遍，有些明白了，既然他们合伙，则庞二跟钱城有银钱往来，自然要问问做钱庄的胡雪岩的意见，最后讲的两句话，就是这个意思。恒记是同兴的大户，也是一根台柱，如果这根台柱一抽走，后果不堪设想。虽然胡雪岩的话，靠得住靠不住，尚待求证，但宁可信其有，不可信其无，难得他有讲同业义气的善意表示，不正好拉近了交情？“好极了！庞二少有你搭档，将来做出来的市面不得了，雪岩兄，”他急转直下他说，“我是久仰大才，也久仰阜康的信誉，大树底下好乘凉，想沾你老兄一点光，不晓得肯不肯照应照应我们？”“好说，好说，请吩咐！只要力量够得上，决不推辞。”“我是想，同兴跟阜康做个联号，不晓是高攀得上，高攀不上？”对这个提议，胡雪岩倒有些意外之感，暗暗佩服邵仲甫的手腕也不坏，做成联号，则恒记跟同兴的往来，也就等于跟阜康往来，他考虑了一下答道：“只怕阜康高攀不上。仲甫兄，我说句实话，现在丝生意是我自己管，钱庄都托了一个刘姓朋友，你老兄晓得的，东家未见得都了解，全盘情形，都在档手肚子里。彼此联手，我完全赞成，不过先要问一问我那个刘朋友，我写信叫他上来，大家一起谈好不好？““是的。做事情是应该如此。”“就这样说了。”胡雪岩假意掏出表来看了一下：“我还有个约会，先走一步，中午再碰头。”

These elusive remarks made Shao still more attentive. He weighed every word and began to understand. If Hu and Pang became partners, Pang would naturally consult Hu, himself a banker, about Hengji’s banking arrangements. That was the meaning of the last two sentences. Hengji was a major customer and one of Tongxing’s main supports. Losing it would have unthinkable consequences. Whether Hu’s claims could be trusted still needed confirmation, but it was safer to believe them than not. And since he had expressed goodwill towards a fellow banker, was this not a chance to draw closer? “Excellent! With you as his partner, Second Master Pang will build an extraordinary business. Brother Xueyan”—Shao abruptly changed direction—“I have long admired your ability and Fukang’s reputation. It is pleasant to sit in the shade of a great tree. I should like to share a little of your good fortune. Might you be willing to look after us?” “You are too kind. Tell me what you wish. If it is within my power, I shall certainly not refuse.” “I wondered whether Tongxing might become an associate bank of Fukang. I do not know whether we could aspire to such a connection.” The proposal took Hu somewhat by surprise, and he privately admired Shao’s skill. If the banks became associates, Hengji’s dealings with Tongxing would effectively be dealings with Fukang too. After considering it, he answered, “It is Fukang that may not be worthy of the connection. To tell you frankly, brother, I manage the silk business myself, but have entrusted the bank to a friend named Liu. You know how it is: an owner may not understand everything. The manager has the whole business in his head. I thoroughly approve of our joining forces, but I must first consult my friend Liu. Shall I write and ask him to come up, so that we can all discuss it?” “Certainly. That is the proper way to conduct business.” “Then we shall leave it at that.” Hu made a show of taking out his watch. “I have another appointment and must go. We shall meet again at noon.”

于是胡雪岩站起身来，向华佩卿道了谢，与尤五告辞出门，一起赶到怡情院，庞二刚穿好衣服，预备到一品香去会见约好了的人。“二哥！”胡雪岩将他拉到一边，悄然问道：“你今天中午是不是约了同兴的邵仲甫见面？”“是啊！你怎么知道？”“我跟他刚见了面。”胡雪岩以郑重的神色，低声说道：“恒记跟同兴的往来，都由朱福年经手，我先要拿同兴方面稳往，以防万一。”“不错，不错！你的心思真细。”庞二说道：“谈得怎么样？”“没有深谈，因为恒记到底是你的事业，要你作主。我告诉他，要先听你怎么说，我才能跟他进一步谈。”这两句话中，一方面表示尊重庞二，一方面也是为他自己表白，并无喧宾夺主的意思。同时也在暗示，需将双方的关系，公开向邵仲甫说明。措词相当巧妙，而丝毫不着痕迹。庞二深为满意，不知不党中便由胡雪岩牵着鼻子走了。

Hu rose, thanked Hua, and took his leave with You. Together they hurried to Yiqing House. Pang had just dressed and was preparing to go to the Yipinxiang Inn to meet the people he had invited. “Brother Pang!” Hu drew him aside. “Are you meeting Shao Zhongfu of Tongxing at noon?” “Yes. How did you know?” “I have just seen him.” Hu lowered his voice and grew serious. “All Hengji’s dealings with Tongxing pass through Zhu Funian. I must first make sure of Tongxing’s position, as a precaution.” “Quite right! You think of everything. How did the talk go?” “We did not go into detail. Hengji is your business, after all, and you must decide. I told him I had to hear what you said before I could discuss it further.” These two sentences both showed respect for Pang and assured him that Hu had no intention of usurping his authority. They also hinted that Pang needed to make their new relationship clear to Shao. The wording was skilful without showing any trace of artifice. Pang was delighted and, without realizing it, allowed Hu to lead him by the nose.

“好的。回头我们一起吃饭，我当面跟邵仲甫说。时候不早了，一起走吧。”到了一品香，已有好些人在等。包括朱福年在内，一见胡雪岩跟庞二在一起，他的脸色一变。庞二不曾发觉，胡雪岩是见如不见，神色不动地跟他寒暄，说前天请他作陪，未见赏光，深为遗憾。朱福年当然也有几句致歉的话，只是神色之间，不免忸怩。由这一番周旋，便看出朱福年其实不是什么厉害角色，因而越有自信必可将他收服。“福年！”庞二打发走了一些不相干的访客，招招手说：“你请过来，我有件事告诉你。”庞二住的是一进五间屋子，将朱福年找到最东面那一间，谈了好半天，才见朱福年出来，脸上的气色越发难看了，但对胡雪岩却又不能不敷衍。“胡先生，刚才二少爷跟我说了，说胡先生有大股份加到恒记来。”他极力装出欣幸的神情，“好极，好极！以后要请胡先生多教导。”“不敢当，不敢当。”胡雪岩很恳切地，但说话已有老板的味道：“老兄在恒记多年，将来着实还要借重。”听得这一说，朱福年的脸色好看了些，赔着笑敷衍了一会。胡雪岩以话套话，将庞二跟他说的话，都打听了出来，果然说的是“大股份”。显然的，这是为了让他好受恒记的同人着重，有意这么说，庞二真的很够交情。

“Very well. We shall have lunch together, and I shall tell Shao myself. It is getting late. Let us go.” At the Yipinxiang Inn, several people were already waiting, Zhu among them. At the sight of Hu beside Pang, his expression changed. Pang did not notice; Hu noticed but behaved as though he had not. He greeted Zhu calmly and said how sorry he had been that Zhu could not join them at dinner the day before yesterday. Zhu naturally offered apologies, though he could not conceal his awkwardness. This exchange showed Hu that Zhu was not really such a formidable man after all, strengthening his confidence that he could bring him to heel. After dismissing some unrelated visitors, Pang beckoned. “Funian, come here. I have something to tell you.” Pang occupied a suite of five rooms. He took Zhu into the easternmost one, and they talked for a considerable time. When Zhu emerged, his colour was worse than ever, though he still had to be polite to Hu. “Mr Hu, Second Master has just told me that you are bringing a substantial stake into Hengji.” He strained to look delighted. “Excellent! In future I shall depend on your guidance.” “You are too kind.” Hu sounded sincere, but already spoke as an owner. “You have been at Hengji for years, brother. We shall have much to rely on you for.” Zhu’s expression eased a little, and he continued the courtesies with a conciliatory smile. Drawing one remark out of another, Hu learnt what Pang had said. He had indeed spoken of a “substantial stake.” Clearly Pang had deliberately put it that way so that Hengji’s staff would give Hu due weight. He was a loyal friend indeed.

* * *由邵仲甫作东，吃了一顿丰盛的“番菜”，庞二要陪怡云老七到洋行里去买首饰衣料，匆匆走了，主人留胡雪岩在原处喝“英国红茶”，有话要谈。在邵仲甫面前，庞二也说胡雪岩在恒记有大股份，因而他的神态也显得跟第一次见面不同，连称呼也改过了，不是称兄道弟，而是叫“胡先生”。“胡先生！”他说，“我有句话请教，刚刚庞二少爷关照，以后恒记跟同兴往来，归胡先生你经手，那么，朱福年来说的话，算不算数？“一下子问到要害上，胡雪岩不敢轻率回答，先反问一句：“是什么话？”“恒记跟同兴的往来，本来都归朱福年一个人接头，上十万银子的出入，或者调拨户头，都听他一句话。以后，我们听不听呢？”这“调拨户头”四个字，正就是胡雪岩要弄明白的，当然往下追问：“恒记在宝号有几个户头？”“三个。”邵仲甫答道：“恒记、继嘉堂、福记。”“继嘉堂”是庞家的堂名，“福记”当然是朱福年，这个都算是私人户头，但恒记与继嘉堂不可分，福记的私人户头如何可以跟恒记混在一起？这其间，不言可知有了弊病。于是胡雪岩不但不答邵仲甫的询问，而且提出要求：“请同兴先将福记历年进出的数目，抄个单子给我。”

Shao hosted a sumptuous Western meal. Pang, who was to accompany Yiyun to the foreign shops to buy jewellery and dress fabrics, left in haste. Their host detained Hu over “English black tea”; he had something to discuss. Pang had told Shao too that Hu held a substantial stake in Hengji. Shao’s manner had consequently changed since their first meeting, as had his form of address. Instead of calling him brother, he now called him “Mr Hu.” “Mr Hu, there is something I must ask. Second Master Pang has just instructed us that you will henceforth handle Hengji’s dealings with Tongxing. Does that mean we should still act on Zhu Funian’s instructions?” The question went straight to the heart of the matter. Hu would not answer hastily. “What sort of instructions?” “Until now, Zhu alone has dealt with us for Hengji. Payments and receipts of over a hundred thousand taels, or transfers between accounts—we have acted on his word. Should we continue to do so?” “Transfers between accounts” was exactly what Hu wished to understand. He followed it up. “How many accounts does Hengji have with your bank?” “Three: Hengji, Jijia Hall, and Fuji.” Jijia Hall was the Pang family’s hall name, while Fuji was, of course, Zhu Funian’s account. The latter two were private accounts. Hengji and Jijia Hall could not be separated, but how could Zhu’s own account properly be mixed with Hengji’s? The existence of irregularities was plain. Instead of answering Shao, Hu made a request. “First have Tongxing copy out a statement of all Fuji’s receipts and payments over the past years for me.”

邵仲甫一听吓一跳。这是钱庄的大忌，有钱的人，守着“财不露白”的古训，在钱庄里存款是决不肯告诉人的，用堂名或用个什么“记”的户名，就是为了隐藏真相，而钱庄里也有义务为客户守机密，如今将福记存款进出的数目，泄漏给第三者，这话一传出去，信用一失，人人白危，都来提存，岂不把同兴挤垮。“胡先生，你是内行。”他哭丧着脸说：“这件事实在不敢从命。”他的难处，胡雪岩完全了解，所以早就想好了的，这时便即问道，“仲甫兄，我跟你有没有仇？”“哪里来的仇？”“那不就是了！我跟你无冤无仇，何必来害你？福记是纯粹的私人户头，我没有资格查他的帐，既然跟恒记混在一起，当然我要弄弄清楚。就是在同兴来说，也有义务拿福记的进出开给我看。”胡雪岩又说：“你放心好了！我不会坏同业的规矩的。这件事，无知地知，你知我知，连庞老二我都不告诉他，你还怕什么？“邵仲甫想了想问道：“胡先生，你要这张单子做啥用场，是不是跟朱福年去算帐？”“不是！”胡雪岩说：“朱福年也不会晓得有这件事，我是根据你开的单子，盘恒记的帐。”邵仲甫真的为难了，“英国红茶”喝了一杯又一杯，只是答不出来。

Shao was startled. This was a grave taboo in banking. Wealthy people followed the old rule of never displaying their riches and would not tell others what they had deposited. They used a family hall name or an account name ending in ji precisely to conceal the truth. Banks, in turn, were obliged to keep their customers’ affairs secret. To disclose Fuji’s deposits and withdrawals to a third person—if word of it spread, confidence would collapse. Every customer would fear for himself and withdraw his money. Tongxing would be ruined by a run. “Mr Hu, you know our business,” Shao said miserably. “I really cannot comply.” Hu understood his difficulty perfectly and had already considered it. “Brother Zhongfu, is there any enmity between us?” “Why should there be?” “Exactly. Since we have no grievance against one another, why should I wish to harm you? If Fuji were a purely private account, I should have no right to inspect it. But since it has been mixed with Hengji’s, naturally I must find out what has happened. Tongxing too has an obligation to show me its transactions. Set your mind at rest. I shall not break the rules of our profession. Heaven knows, Earth knows, you know, and I know. I shall not tell even Pang. What is there to fear?” Shao considered this. “Mr Hu, what will you use the statement for? To settle accounts with Zhu?” “No. He will not even know it exists. I shall use the figures you give me to examine Hengji’s books.” Shao was in a genuine quandary. He drank cup after cup of “English black tea,” unable to give an answer.

胡雪岩也知道这是件极严重的事，不加点压力，邵仲甫决不肯就范，所以用相当冷峻的声音说道：“庞老二本有意叫我在上海立阜康的分号，我因为你老兄有言在先，没有答应他。现在在看来，只有自己有钱庄，帐目才能弄得清楚。”说着，便有起身告辞的模样。阜康一设分号，同兴当然再也做不成恒记的生意，这一着棋是“将”邵仲甫的“军”，他不能不着急。“胡先生，胡先生，有话好商量。你能不能让我明天答你的话。”“那自然可以。不过有一层，仲甫兄你千万记住，无论你答应也好，不答应也好，这件事只有你我两个人晓得。”意思是不可泄露其事给朱福年。邵仲甫当然意会得到，连连答说：“我知道，我知道。”

Hu knew that this was a matter of the utmost seriousness. Without pressure, Shao would never agree. He therefore said in a rather cold voice, “Pang wanted me to establish a Fukang branch in Shanghai. Because of what you had already said to me, I did not agree. Now it seems that only by having a bank of my own can I get a clear view of the accounts.” He made as though to rise and leave. If Fukang opened a branch, Tongxing would naturally lose Hengji’s business. The move put Shao in check, and he could not help growing anxious. “Mr Hu, let us discuss this. Could you allow me until tomorrow to answer?” “Certainly. But remember one thing, brother. Whether you agree or refuse, this must remain known only to the two of us.” He meant that Zhu must hear nothing of it. Shao understood perfectly and repeatedly assured him, “I know.”

到了第二天一早，同兴钱庄派人送了信来，邵仲甫约胡雪岩，中午仍旧在那家番菜馆见面。准时赴约，点好了菜，等“仆欧”迟了出去，做主人的取出一个信封，摆在面前，跟他先有番话要交代。邵仲甫提出了“约法三章”：第一，这份清单不得泄漏给任何人，第二，不得以此作为对付朱福年的根据，第三，不管胡雪岩是不是在上海设阜康的分号，恒记不能与同兴断绝往来。第三点其实是请求，只是邵仲甫的措词不甚恰当，有些近乎要挟的意味。胡雪岩颇为不悦，“仲甫兄，”他这样答道：“第一、第二两点，我谨遵台命，第三点，我只能这么说，我一定讲同业的义气。恒记如果是我一个人的事业，老兄吩咐，闲话一句，无奈大老板是庞老二，他又是大少爷脾气，如果恼了他，翻脸不认人，我说的话，他也未见得听。所以这一点，完全要看你自己的做法，我在旁边总替同兴说好话就是。”这是暗示邵仲甫，如果同兴是这种近乎要侠的做法，庞二首先就会着恼，邵仲甫也是极老到的人，一听他这话，自知失态，很见机地道歉。“胡先生，我不会说话，请你不要见怪。将来仰仗的地方还多，一切心照。我也不多说了，总而言之，听你的吩咐就是。”

Early the next morning a messenger came from Tongxing with a letter. Shao asked Hu to meet him at noon at the same Western restaurant. Hu arrived on time. Once they had ordered and the waiter had withdrawn, Shao took out an envelope, laid it before him, and said that there were some points he must first make clear. He proposed three conditions. First, the statement must not be disclosed to anyone. Second, it must not be used as evidence against Zhu. Third, whether or not Hu opened a Fukang branch in Shanghai, Hengji must not break off its dealings with Tongxing. The third point was really a request, but Shao’s unfortunate wording made it sound almost like coercion. Hu was displeased. “Brother Zhongfu, I shall observe the first two conditions. On the third, I can only say that I shall honour my obligations to a fellow banker. If Hengji were mine alone, a word from you would settle it. Unfortunately, the principal owner is Pang, and he has a young gentleman’s temper. Anger him and he may turn his back on you; he will not necessarily listen to me. So that depends entirely on your own conduct. I shall always speak well of Tongxing at his side.” The implication was that if Tongxing adopted this almost coercive manner, Pang would be the first to take offence. Shao was experienced enough to recognize his mistake at once and tactfully apologized. “Mr Hu, I have expressed myself badly. Please do not hold it against me. I shall have much to depend on you for in future, and we understand one another. There is no need to say more. In short, I shall follow your instructions.”

胡雪岩的度量宽，有他这两句话，不满之意，随即消失。等邵仲甫将他面前的信封移了过来，便即抽出里面的单子来看，只见开头写的是“福记名下收付清单”，后面盖着“同兴协记钱庄”的书柬图章。他不暇细看内容，将前后折起，用桌上现成的餐，裁下“福记”字样及同兴图章，各约一指宽的两张纸条，交回邵仲甫。这个小小的动作，使得邵仲甫大为服帖，一则见得胡雪岩的诚意，不会拿这张清单作为对付朱福年的把柄，二则也见得他心细，邵仲甫发觉自己做错了，本来就不必写明“福记”字样，更不必盖上书柬图章，纵然胡雪岩无他，万一遗失了这张清单，落入旁人手中，依然是件极不妥的事。幸好，他的这个错误，为胡雪岩及时纠正了。“胡先生，”他由衷地表示佩服，“有魄力的人，粗枝大叶，心细的人，手面放不开。只有你胡先生，这两样长处都有，实在是没话可说了。”“谬奖，谬奖！”胡雪岩亦颇欣慰，因为邵仲甫言出至诚，看起来自己是在事业上结交了一个很有用的朋友。

Hu was generous in temper, and those words dispelled his displeasure. When Shao pushed the envelope across the table, he drew out the statement. At the top it read “Statement of Receipts and Payments under the Fuji Account”; at the end was the correspondence seal of “Tongxing Xieji Bank.” Without pausing to examine the figures, Hu folded back the top and bottom, took the table knife lying ready to hand, and cut off the account name “Fuji” and Tongxing’s seal. He returned the two strips, each about a finger’s width, to Shao. This small act won Shao over completely. First, it demonstrated Hu’s sincerity: he would not use the statement as evidence against Zhu. Second, it revealed his care for detail. Shao realized that he himself had made a mistake. There had been no need to write the name Fuji, still less to stamp the paper with the bank’s seal. Even if Hu intended no harm, the statement might be lost and fall into someone else’s hands, which would be highly undesirable. Fortunately, Hu had corrected the mistake in time. “Mr Hu,” Shao said with heartfelt admiration, “bold men tend to overlook details, while careful men lack breadth of action. You alone possess both qualities. There is really nothing more to be said.” “You praise me too highly!” Hu too was pleased. Shao spoke with complete sincerity, and it seemed that Hu had gained a very useful friend in business.

第三十一章｜CHAPTER THIRTY-ONE

朱福年的“把柄”虽已入手，胡雪岩却反丢开了，他做事一向往好的方面走，眼前的唯一大事是与庞二谈判合伙的细节。由于彼此都具诚意，谈判相当顺利，胡雪岩在恒记不居任何名义，但先要为恒记作一番整顿，等到有了头绪，再进行筹设阜康钱庄上海分号。对这方面，庞二表示概不过问，又说，如果胡雪岩资金不足，他可以拉一批长期存款的户头来，变相地为阜康增添资本。于是，双方找了见证人来写台伙的契约，胡雪岩请的是尤五，庞二找了一个他的父执，专做桐油出口的孙大存，合同签押好了，庞二大张筵席，请见证人，也请恒记管事的人，包括朱福年在内，即席宣布，赋胡雪岩以盘查银钱货色、考查同人、重新改组的大权。胡雪岩接着又站起来说了话，表示决不轻易更动，请大家照常办事，不必三心两意，话不多而扼要，每人都象服了颗定心丸。当然，只有朱福年是例外。到了第二天，朱福年来请胡雪岩到恒记去“视事”。他早就打好了主意，到了恒记在帐户中坐定，管事的人一个个来见过，他问了问各人的经历，随即起身辞别，朱福年请他看帐，他回说：“不忙。慢慢儿来好了。”这一半是放朱福年一马，看他是不是自己去弥补他的“花帐”，一半也是实话，因为眼前先有件与他切身利害有关的大事要办。

Although Hu now held evidence against Zhu Funian, he put it aside. He always preferred to turn affairs towards a favourable outcome, and his one immediate concern was to settle the details of his partnership with Pang Er. Since both were sincere, their negotiations went smoothly. Hu would hold no formal title at Hengji, but would first put its affairs in order. Once that work had taken shape, he would proceed with preparations for a Shanghai branch of Fukang Bank. Pang said he would leave that entirely to Hu. If Hu lacked funds, he could introduce customers willing to make long-term deposits, thereby increasing Fukang's working capital indirectly. They then invited witnesses to draw up the partnership agreement. Hu asked You Laowu; Pang chose Sun Dacun, a friend of his father's who specialized in exporting tung oil. Once the agreement had been signed and sealed, Pang gave a grand banquet for the witnesses and Hengji's managers, Zhu included. There he announced that Hu had full authority to examine the firm's money and merchandise, assess its staff and reorganize its operations. Hu rose in turn and assured everyone that he would make no changes lightly. They should carry on as usual, without doubts or divided minds. His few concise words reassured them all—except Zhu. Next day Zhu came to invite Hu to Hengji to assume his duties. Hu had already decided how to proceed. Once seated in the countinghouse, he received the managers one by one, asked about their experience, then rose to leave. Zhu invited him to examine the accounts. “There is no hurry. We can take our time.” Partly he was giving Zhu a chance to repair his irregular accounts himself; partly he meant exactly what he said. Another urgent matter directly affecting his own interests came first.

恒记人事上的变动，朱福年已经告诉了怡和洋行的大班吉伯特。这个意外的变化，自然是一大打击，但朱福年还不服气，怂恿吉伯特说：胡雪岩实力不足，只要吉伯特坚持原议，必可迫他杀价脱手。因此，当古应春跟吉伯恃再度会面，说明恒记的丝亦归他经手，要求照最初的议价成交时，吉伯特断然拒绝，依旧以欧洲丝价大跌为托词，只肯照八五折收买。事情成了僵局，胡雪岩相当为难，如果坚持原价，万一不能成交，不但自己的本钱搁不起，丝也会变质，而且对庞二这方面也难以交代，倘或委曲，则更不能求全，不但为宠二所笑，在商场上辛辛苦苦建立起来的名声，亦会大打折扣。同时还有一层顾虑，也许朱福年已经跟庞二说过，他那里的货色，可以照原定的价钱卖给吉伯特，由自己来经手，反打了个八五折，即或庞二了解其中的苦衷，为了划一步骤，以后易于控制全局，眼前不能不吃点亏，但心里总不会舒服，那就要影响彼此合伙的关系了。

Zhu had told Gilbert, the head of Jardine Matheson, about the changes at Hengji. This unexpected development was naturally a serious blow. But Zhu remained defiant. He urged Gilbert to remember that Hu lacked sufficient resources: by holding to his proposal, Gilbert could force Hu to sell at a reduced price. When Gu Yingchun met Gilbert again, explained that Hengji's silk was now also in his hands, and requested a sale at the price originally negotiated, Gilbert therefore refused outright. Still pleading a sharp fall in European silk prices, he would offer only eighty-five per cent of that price. The business was deadlocked, and Hu faced a real dilemma. If he held to the original price and no sale resulted, he could not afford to leave his capital tied up, the silk would deteriorate, and he would have difficulty explaining matters to Pang. Yet yielding would bring no satisfactory solution either. Pang would laugh at him, and the commercial reputation he had built with such effort would suffer badly. He had another concern. Perhaps Zhu had already told Pang that he could sell Hengji's goods to Gilbert at the agreed price. If Hu took over and obtained only eighty-five per cent, Pang might understand the difficulty—that a unified course of action and future control of the whole business required an immediate sacrifice—but he could hardly feel pleased. Their partnership would suffer.

“我在想，吉伯特恐怕也是‘嘴硬骨头酥’，莫非他买不成我们中国的丝，外国那些绸厂就拿织机停下来，不同绸缎？我想总没有这样的道理吧？”这一说，触发了古应春的灵感，“有了，”他喜滋滋地说，“我有个办法，打听他的虚实！”“那太好了。”胡雪岩精神一振，“我就是想要晓得他手里的牌，看样子‘三副落地’，到底是不是清一色呢？如果不是，我们死扣着那张牌，不是自己害自己？”“就是这话。我马上去打听”““慢来！”胡雪岩拉住他说，“你怎么样下手，先说来我听听！”“吉伯特听了朱福年的话，自然以为千稳万妥，买不成我们的货色，至少可以买恒记的，有了货色，当然要定轮船舱位装货。我就从轮船公司方面去打听，看他定了舱位没有？“古应春又说，”货色不在少数，一两条船还装不下，非先预定不可。所以一定打听得出来的。“

“I wonder whether Gilbert is all hard words and soft bones. If he cannot buy our Chinese silk, will the foreign silk mills stop their looms and cease weaving? Surely that cannot be so?” This gave Gu an inspiration. “I have it!” he said delightedly. “I know a way to discover how he really stands.” “Excellent!” Hu brightened. “That is just what I want: to see his hand. He seems to have three sets exposed already, but is he really playing for a hand all of one suit? If he isn't, aren't we hurting ourselves by holding back that one tile?” “Exactly. I shall find out at once.” “Wait.” Hu caught his arm. “Tell me how you mean to go about it.” “After listening to Zhu, Gilbert must think himself perfectly secure. Even if he cannot buy our goods, he can at least buy Hengji's. With goods in prospect, he will naturally have booked space aboard steamships. I shall ask the shipping company whether he has made a reservation. This is a substantial shipment. One or two ships cannot take it all; space must be booked in advance. We are certain to find something out.”

“对！这个办法好。”胡雪岩的脑筋极快，当时便说：“除非他真的不想做这票生意，要做这票生意，不但要他照我们的价钱，额外还要他破费。”古应春笑了。由于心情由沉重转为轻松，所以戏谑地挖苦胡雪岩：“小爷叔，你也真是，得着风就是雨！给不得你三分颜色，就要开大红染坊了。”“我说个道理你听，你就晓得我不是胡言乱说。”照他的判断，吉伯特以为自己这方面迟早总会就范，所以轮船的舱位定好了不会退掉，如果能够跟轮船公司接洽，以高价将吉伯特所定的舱位抢过来，则洋人买下了丝运不出去，又会来跟自己这方面情商转让，岂不又可以赚他一笔。“这是如意算盘。”古应春说，“不过也不妨试试。”说到这里，他触类旁通，仍旧觉得胡雪岩的话极有用，“小爷叔，你说的办法，恐怕行不通，不过我倒想到了，大可借这个说法，逼他一逼。”“嗯，嗯！”胡雪岩意会了，点点头说：“你请吧！我等你的回音。”

“Good! An excellent idea.” Hu's mind moved quickly. “Unless he truly means to abandon this transaction, we shall make him pay our price—and something extra besides.” Gu laughed. Relieved of his earlier heaviness, he teased Hu. “Little Uncle, you hear a breeze and call it rain! Give you a little colour and you open a great scarlet dyehouse.” “Let me explain my reasoning, and you will see that I am not talking nonsense.” Hu thought Gilbert believed they would eventually submit, so he would not cancel the shipping space he had booked. If they approached the shipping company and offered a higher price to take that space themselves, the foreigner might buy the silk only to find he could not ship it. He would then have to negotiate with them for the space, allowing them to make another profit. “That is a very hopeful calculation,” Gu said. “Still, we might try.” The suggestion gave him another idea, and he again found Hu's words useful. “Your plan may not work, Little Uncle, but we could certainly use the threat of it to put pressure on him.” Hu understood and nodded. “Go, then. I shall wait for your news.”

于是古应春去寻一个名叫陈顺生的朋友，此人是他的同乡，在太古轮船公司做买办，专门负责招揽客货承运。太古也是英国人的资本，怡和有货色交运，当然委托太古。一问果然，“不错，有这回事。”陈顺生答道：“先是定了两班轮船的舱位，到期说货色还不齐，要延到下两班，贴了四百两银子的损失。”“那么下两班什么时候到？”“一班十天以后，还有一班要半个月。到埠卸货装货，要十天工夫。”陈顺生问，“你打听它是为什么？”托人办事，当然要相见以诚，而且是同乡好友，也不必顾虑他会“泄底”，所以古应春将跟吉伯特斗法的经过，源源本本说了一遍，接着便托陈顺生去“逼他一逼”。“延过一次期，话就更好说了。”古应春低声说道：“我拜托你问一问吉伯特，货色齐了没有？到时候能不能装船？如果不能，要趁早说，好让太古另外去招揽客户。”“懂了。这个忙我可以帮你。”“多谢，多谢。今天晚上我请你吃花酒，顺便听你的消息。”“这么急？”“拜托，拜托！”古应春长揖恳求，“务必请你就跑一趟。”

Gu went to see a friend named Chen Shunsheng, a fellow townsman who worked as a comprador for the Swire Steamship Company, responsible for securing passenger and freight business. Swire was also British-owned, so Jardine Matheson naturally entrusted its shipments to it. His inquiry confirmed the guess. “Yes, that is right,” Chen said. “He first booked space on two sailings. When the time came, he said the goods were not ready and asked to postpone to the next two. He paid four hundred taels to cover the loss.” “When do the next two arrive?” “One in ten days, the other in half a month. Unloading and loading in port will take ten days. Why are you asking?” When requesting help, one ought to speak frankly. Chen was both a fellow townsman and a close friend, so Gu had no reason to fear that he would disclose their position. He explained the contest with Gilbert from beginning to end, then asked Chen to put some pressure on him. “Since he has already postponed once, you have all the more reason to ask,” Gu said quietly. “Please find out whether his goods are ready and can be loaded on time. If not, he should say so early, allowing Swire to seek other customers.” “Understood. I can help you with that.” “Thank you. I shall entertain you at a courtesan house tonight and hear your news.” “So urgent?” Gu bowed deeply. “I beg you to go at once.”

情面难却，陈顺生真的丢下了自己的事，去为古应春奔走。到了晚上在估情院见面，他带来了吉伯特的消息。“他说等三夭看。如果三天当中没有回话再谈。”“怎么叫‘再谈，？”古应春问，“是谈班期顺延，还是根本就不要舱位了？”“怎么不要？当然要的！”古应春听得这个回音，十分满意。足见怡和洋和非买丝不可，而且在三天以内就会来谈判。这个看法，胡雪岩也认为不错，但主张再逼一逼。这就是请陈顺生再跟吉伯特去说，有客户求货运舱位甚急，请他在三天以内，必须提出确实答复，否则，吉伯特就得照约履行，即使放弃不用，亦要照全价收费。

Unable to refuse his friend's appeal, Chen set aside his own affairs and went on Gu's errand. When they met at Yiqing House that evening, he brought Gilbert's answer. “He asks us to wait three days. If he has not replied by then, we can discuss it again.” “Discuss what?” Gu asked. “Postponing to another sailing, or giving up the space altogether?” “Why would he give it up? Of course he still wants it.” Gu was thoroughly satisfied. This showed, he thought, that Jardine Matheson had to buy the silk and would come to negotiate within three days. Hu agreed with this assessment, but favoured applying still more pressure. Chen should tell Gilbert that another customer urgently wanted freight space. Gilbert must give a definite answer within three days; otherwise, he would have to fulfil the contract and pay the full charge even if he chose not to use the space.

“这一逼还不够。”胡雪岩又说，“我们还要想个办法，让吉伯特以为我们不愿意跟他再做生意，他才会着慌，你看，我们是不是能够另外找洋人接头，虚张声势一番？”“不行！洋人比我们团结，彼此都通声气的，而且哪个洋行做哪项买卖，完全听他们国内指挥，不会突然之间改做别项生意。虚张声势瞒不过吉伯特。”古应春又说：“倒是有个办法，我们放个风声出去，预备立一间号子，专做洋庄，直接写信给外国厂家交涉。看吉伯特怎么说？”“这也是一个办法。不过，”胡雪岩沉吟了一会说：“俗语说得好：”前半夜想想自己，后半夜想想人家。‘吉伯特就算愿意回头，总也要有个’落场话‘。大家的话都很硬，自己转不来弯，我们要替吉伯特开条路子出来。你说是不是？““我也想到过。就怕我们想转圜，他以为我们软弱，越发搭架子，岂非僵上加僵？”对这个顾虑，胡雪岩无法作判断了，因为洋人做生意的规矩，以及吉伯特的性情，他都不太了解。只是将心比心，自己不肯低头，谅来吉伯特也是如此，如果从中有个穿针引线的人，搭一搭桥，事情使容易办通了。“小爷叔！”古应春看他犹豫的神色，提醒他说：“洋人做生意，讲利益，也讲道理，只要我们道理站得住，态度坚决，洋人倒是不讲面子的，自会笑嘻嘻来跟你说好话。所以你不要三心二意，让洋人看穿了，事情格外难办。”

“That is still not enough,” Hu added. “We must make Gilbert think we no longer wish to do business with him. Then he will become anxious. Could we approach another foreigner and make a show of it?” “No. The foreigners are more united than we are and exchange information. Besides, each firm's line of business is determined by instructions from home. They do not suddenly change to something else. Such a display would not deceive Gilbert. But there is another possibility: spread word that we intend to establish a firm dealing directly with foreign markets and write to manufacturers overseas ourselves. Then see what Gilbert says.” “That is one way. Still...” Hu reflected. “As the saying goes, think of yourself for the first half of the night, and of others for the second. Even if Gilbert is willing to reconsider, he needs a way to retreat with dignity. Both sides have spoken so firmly that neither can turn back easily. We must leave him a way out. Don't you agree?” “I have thought of that too. But if we seek a compromise, he may mistake it for weakness and grow more overbearing. Wouldn't that only deepen the deadlock?” Hu could not judge this concern. He knew too little about foreign business practices or Gilbert's character. Putting himself in the other man's place, he merely felt that since he was unwilling to bow first, Gilbert probably felt the same. An intermediary to bring them together would make matters easier. Seeing his hesitation, Gu reminded him, “Little Uncle, foreigners care about profit, but also about reason. If our case is sound and our position firm, they will not stand on dignity; they will come smiling to speak pleasantly to us. So do not waver. If they see through you, matters will become still harder.”

胡雪岩最尊重行家的意见，古应春跟洋人的交道打得多，自然听他的，“那好！”他说，“我们就做一番态度坚决的表示给他看，请尤五哥弄两条船，我们拿货色装上去。”“这，这表示，绝不卖给他了？”“对了！对外头说，我们的丝改内销了，预备卖给杭州织造衙门。”“那么，恒记的货色呢？”“这我会跟庞二说，让庞二关照朱福年，也是雇船运杭州。”古应春闭着嘴，脸色郑重地考虑好一会，毅然决然地答道：“可以！我们就这么做。不过，庞二对朱福年说的话很要紧。”“那当然！我知道。”胡雪岩说，“朱福年自然要劝他，不必受我们这方面的牵累拿丝卖给吉伯特。庞二只要说一句：”胡某人怎么样，我们怎么样，吉伯特要买丝跟胡某人去接头。‘那就成功了。“照胡雪岩的估计，朱福年当然会将庞二的态度告诉吉伯特，吉伯特一定会回头。如果不理，那么僵局就真的不能化解了。自己这方面固然损失惨重，怡和洋行从此也就不用再想在中国买丝。

Hu always respected expert opinion. Gu had dealt extensively with foreigners, so he naturally followed his advice. “Very well. Let us show Gilbert how firm we are. Ask Brother You to find two boats; we shall load our goods aboard.” “To show that we absolutely will not sell to him?” “Exactly. Say we are turning to the domestic market and intend to sell the silk to the Hangzhou Imperial Weaving Office.” “And Hengji's goods?” “I shall speak to Pang and have him tell Zhu to hire boats for Hangzhou too.” Gu considered this silently for some time, his expression grave. Then he answered decisively, “Yes. Let us do it. But what Pang says to Zhu will be crucial.” “Of course. I understand. Zhu will advise him to avoid being dragged into our difficulties and sell his silk to Gilbert. Pang need only say, ‘We shall do whatever Hu does. If Gilbert wants silk, let him approach Hu.’ That will settle it.” Hu reckoned that Zhu would certainly report Pang's attitude to Gilbert, who would then reconsider. If he ignored it, the deadlock would indeed become insoluble. Their own losses would be heavy, but Jardine Matheson need never again expect to buy silk in China.

想到就做，而且象煞有介事，裕记线栈开了仓，一包包的丝，用板车送到内河码头上去装船。另一方面，庞二听了胡雪岩的话，照计行事。他做生意多少有点公子哥儿的脾气，喜欢发发“骠劲”，把朱福年找了来，叫他雇船装丝运杭州，一言不合，拿朱福年训了一顿。“二少爷！”朱福年问，“这是为啥？”“丝不卖给洋人了！可以不可以？”“那也不用运杭州。运到杭州卖给哪个？”“卖给织造衙门。”“二少爷，这不对吧！”他说，“从一闹长毛，京里就有圣旨。各织造衙门的贡品都减少了。怎么会买我们的丝？这点道理，难道二少爷都不懂？”“我不懂你懂！”庞二的声音粗了，“除非有人吃里扒外，不然洋人怎么会晓得我们的情形？你跟洋人去说，他有洋钱是他的，我不希罕。他到中国来做生意，三翻四覆，处处想占便宜，当我们中国人好欺负？滚他娘的蛋！”

They acted at once, with every appearance of earnest purpose. Yuji Silk Warehouse opened its store, and carts carried bundle after bundle of silk to the inland-waterway wharf for loading. Meanwhile, Pang followed Hu's plan. In business he retained something of a rich young gentleman's temperament and enjoyed an occasional display of defiance. Summoning Zhu, he ordered him to hire boats and load the silk for Hangzhou. At the first disagreement, he gave Zhu a scolding. “Second Master,” Zhu asked, “why are we doing this?” “Because we are not selling to the foreigners! May we not choose?” “But there is no need to send it to Hangzhou. Who will buy it there?” “The Imperial Weaving Office.” “That cannot be right, Second Master. Ever since the Taiping troubles began, imperial orders from the capital have reduced the tribute goods required of all the weaving offices. Why would they buy our silk? Surely you understand that much?” “You understand everything, and I understand nothing!” Pang's voice grew harsh. “Unless someone was betraying us from within, how would the foreigners know our circumstances? Tell the foreigner that his silver is his own; I care nothing for it. He comes to China to trade, changes his position again and again, and tries to take advantage at every turn. Does he think we Chinese are easily bullied? To hell with him!”

这种情形，遇到过不止一次，朱福年也知道他不过一时之气，做伙计的遇上有脾气的东家，当不得真，否则不如早早卷铺盖走路。而况，庞二虽有脾气，御下相当宽厚，象恒记这种职位是“金饭碗”，丢掉了不易再找。所以想一想，宁可挨骂，该说的话还是要说，才显得自己是“忠心耿耿”。“二少爷，难怪你发脾气，洋人是不大对，不过，他既然是来做生意，当然没有空手而回的道理，我看，丝是一定要买的，就是价钱上有上落……”“免谈。少一个‘沙壳子’都办不到。就算现在照我的价钱，卖不卖也要看我的高兴。”“二少爷，生意到底是生意。”他试探着说：“要不要我再跟洋人去谈谈？如果肯依我们的价钱，不如早早脱手，钱也赚了，麻烦也没有。”“我不管。你跟胡先生去谈，看他怎么说就怎么说。”听得这一句话，朱福年只觉得酸味直味脑顶，顿时改了主意，回到帐房里，自己在咕哝：“他娘的，随他去。看他这票货色能摆到啥辰光？”这话是什对胡雪岩而说的，原来是“忠心耿耿”对东家，此时决定牺牲东家的利益，变相打击胡雪岩，真的雇了船，连夜装货，预备直驶杭州。但是，吉伯特却沉不住气了，一面是陈顺生来催，一面是对方的丝真有改为内销的迹象，不由得便软化了，急于想找个人来转圜。

Zhu had encountered such scenes before. He knew this was merely a passing fit of temper. An employee with a hot-tempered master could not take everything seriously; otherwise, he might as well pack up and leave. Besides, for all his temper, Pang treated his staff generously. A post at Hengji was a golden rice bowl, hard to replace once lost. Zhu therefore decided to endure the abuse and say what needed saying, demonstrating his “unswerving loyalty.” “You have reason to be angry, Second Master. The foreigner has behaved badly. But he came to do business and can hardly return empty-handed. I believe he must buy the silk. The only question is the price.” “No discussion. I will not take a single copper less. Even if he offers my price now, whether I sell depends on my mood.” “Business is business, after all,” Zhu ventured. “Shall I speak to him again? If he accepts our price, we might as well sell quickly, make our profit and end the trouble.” “I am not dealing with it. Speak to Mr Hu and follow whatever he says.” At these words, bitterness seemed to rise to the top of Zhu's head. He changed his mind at once. Back in the countinghouse, he muttered, “Damn him, let him do as he likes. We shall see how long he can sit on that silk.” He meant Hu. His earlier “loyalty” to his employer gave way to a decision to sacrifice that employer's interests in order to strike indirectly at Hu. He actually hired boats, loaded them through the night and prepared to send them straight to Hangzhou. Gilbert, however, was losing his composure. With Chen pressing him on one side, and real signs that the silk might be diverted to the domestic market on the other, he began to yield and urgently sought someone to arrange a compromise.

* * *这些情形胡雪岩不知道，他只听庞二说过，朱福年自告奋勇，愿跟吉伯特去重开谈判。又说已告诉朱福年，一切都听自己作主。既如此，则朱福年不论谈判得如何，都该跟自己来接头。何以不见他的踪影，反倒真的雇船装货？显见得其中起了变化。“如果朱福年肯去说，倒是最适当的人选。”古应春也说，“不过现在对他弄僵了，我们不便在他面前示弱，只有再请庞二去问他。”胡雪岩沉吟未答，古应春看的是一面，他要看两面，一面容易找出办法，要兼顾两面，就煞费周章了。“庞二以东家的身分，问他一声，这件事办得怎么了，有何不可。”“自无不可，不过那是不得已的办法，套句你们文绉绉的话，是下策。”“怎么样才是上策呢？”胡雪岩有些答非所问地：“象猪八戒这种样子，我们杭州话，叫做‘不入调’。现在好比唱出戏，我跟庞二唱的是‘乙字调’，他唱的是”扒字调‘，根本搭配不拢。我们调门高的，唱到半路拉不低，就算拉低了来迁就他，这出戏也好听不到哪里去了。“古应春把他这个比方，体味了一会，恍然大悟，“我懂了！”他说，“上策是叫朱福年将调门提高，让它入调！”“一点都不错。”“想倒想得不错。”古应春看一看胡雪岩的脸色，猜不透他葫芦里卖的什么药，只好老实问道：“计将安出？”

Hu knew none of this. Pang had merely told him that Zhu had volunteered to reopen negotiations with Gilbert, and that he had instructed Zhu to leave all decisions to Hu. In that case, whatever the result, Zhu should have approached him. Why had he vanished instead, actually hiring boats and loading the goods? Something had plainly changed. “If Zhu were willing to speak to him, he would be the best intermediary,” Gu said. “But now that our relations with him are strained, we cannot appear weak before him. We can only ask Pang to inquire.” Hu reflected without answering. Gu was considering one side; he had to consider two. Finding a remedy for one side was easy. Providing for both required much more care. “As his employer, Pang can surely ask how the business is progressing,” Gu continued. “Of course. But that is a last resort—the inferior strategy, to borrow your scholarly language.” “What would be the superior strategy?” Hu answered somewhat indirectly. “A man like Pigsy is what we in Hangzhou call ‘out of tune.’ Imagine that we are performing an opera. Pang and I are singing in a high key, and he in a low one. We cannot fit together. Halfway through, we cannot lower our key; even if we did, the performance would not be worth hearing.” Gu considered the comparison and suddenly understood. “I see! The superior strategy is to make Zhu raise his key and sing in tune.” “Exactly.” “A fine idea.” Gu studied Hu's expression, unable to guess his concealed purpose. He could only ask plainly, “But how?”

“喏！就靠这个。”他从身上掏出一张纸来一扬，古应春认出是同兴抄来的那张“福记”收付清单。“你倒看看，这里面有啥毛病？”古应春仔细看了一遍，实在找不出毛病，“我看不出。”他摇摇头，“钱庄生意，我是外行。”“用不着行家，照普通清理，就可以看得出来的。他一个做伙计的人，就算在恒记是头脑，进出数目，充其量万把银子，至矣尽矣。所以，”胡雪岩指着单子说：“这几笔大数目，都有毛病，尤其是这一笔，收五万、付五万，收的哪一个的，付的哪一个的？如果说是恒记的生意，头寸一时兜不转，他有款子，先代垫五万，这倒也说得过去。现在明明是转一个手，我可以断定收的五万是从恒记来的。如果恒记要付偿款，直接支付好了，为啥在要福记的户头里打个转？”他这样一说，古应春也觉得大有疑问，“那么，”他问，“小爷叔，你就当面拆穿他，让他不能不买你的帐？”要当面拆穿，我早就动手了，为的是要顾他的面子。我自有道理，明天上午你在这里等我消息。“

“With this.” Hu produced a sheet of paper and waved it. Gu recognized the statement of receipts and payments for the Fuji account copied from Tongxing's records. “Look at it. What is wrong here?” Gu examined it carefully but could find nothing. “I cannot see it. Banking is outside my trade.” “You need no special knowledge. Ordinary reasoning will do. He is an employee, even if he is Hengji's chief manager. At the very most, his own transactions could amount to ten thousand taels or so. These large entries must therefore be wrong. Especially this one: fifty thousand received, fifty thousand paid out. From whom, and to whom? If Hengji were temporarily short of funds and he had fifty thousand to advance, that might make sense. But here the money simply passes through his hands. I am certain the fifty thousand came from Hengji. If Hengji had a payment to make, why not make it directly? Why pass it through the Fuji account?” Gu now found it highly suspicious too. “Then will you expose him to his face and force him to respect your wishes?” “If I meant to expose him, I would have acted long ago. I am considering his dignity. I have my reasons. Wait here for word from me tomorrow morning.”

* * *第二天上午，胡雪岩到恒记说要看看帐，朱福年自然无话可说，硬着头皮，亲自开锁，从柜子里捧出一大叠总帐来。“总帐不必看，我看看流水。你的帐不会错的，我随便挑几天看看好了。”接着，胡雪岩便说，“请你拿咸丰三年七月、十月、十一月的流水帐给我。”听这样交代，朱福年大放其心，以为他真的不过随便抽查，便依言将这三个月的流水帐找了出来，捧到他的面前。胡雪岩翻到七月初八那一天细看，果然，有一笔五万两银子的现款，送于同兴。“福年兄。”他说，“请你拿‘恒记’户头的存折我看看。”朱福年的一颗心，陡地提了起来：“是不是现在在用的那一个？”这句话便是个老大的漏洞。按常理而论，应该就是目前在用的那一个，何消问得？问到这话，便表示他是“哑子吃馄饨，肚里有数”，胡雪岩的不是这一个。这见得朱福年不是什么老奸巨滑，只因为庞二到底是大少爷，只要对了他的脾气，什么都好说话。意会到此，胡雪岩越发打定了将朱福年收为己用的主意，因而在表面上越对他尊重，和颜悦色地说：“不晓得找起来方便不方便？我想拿这两年的存折，大略看一遍。”越是这样，越使朱福年有莫测高深之感，喏喏连声地说：“方便，方便。”

Next morning Hu went to Hengji and asked to examine the accounts. Zhu had no grounds to refuse. Bracing himself, he unlocked a cabinet and brought out a great stack of general ledgers. “No need for the general ledgers. Let me see the daybooks. Your accounts will be correct; I shall merely choose a few days at random.” Hu then requested the daybooks for the seventh, tenth and eleventh lunar months of the third year of Xianfeng's reign. Greatly relieved, Zhu assumed that Hu really intended only a casual spot check and brought him the three months' books. Hu turned to the eighth day of the seventh month and examined it closely. Sure enough, fifty thousand taels in cash had been sent to Tongxing. “Brother Funian, let me see the passbook for the Hengji account.” Zhu's heart suddenly rose into his throat. “The one currently in use?” The question exposed a serious weakness. Ordinarily, that would naturally be the book required; why ask? His question showed that, like a mute man eating wontons, he knew the count in his own stomach. He knew Hu wanted a different book. This suggested that Zhu was no hardened master of deception. Pang was, after all, a pampered young gentleman: humour him properly and everything was easy. Recognizing this, Hu became still more determined to win Zhu over for his own use. Outwardly, he treated him with greater respect and asked pleasantly, “Would they be easy to find? I should like to glance through the passbooks for the last two years.” The more considerate he was, the less Zhu could fathom him. “Quite easy, quite easy,” he answered repeatedly.

一把存折送了过来，胡雪岩慢条斯理地随意浏览，一面说着闲话，根不不象查帐的样子。朱福年却没有他那份闲豫情致，惴惴然坐在帐桌对面，表面是准备接受询问，其实一双眼只瞪在存折上。“朱先生！”小徒弟走来通报，“船老大有事来接头。”这“船老大”就是承揽装丝运杭州的船家。朱福年不能不去接头。趁这空档，胡雪岩在存折上翻到咸丰三年七月初八那一天。那里有同兴收银五万两的记载。胆子倒真大！胡雪岩心里在想，莫非硬吞五万银子？这盘帐倒要细看了。他是这一行的好手，如今虽因不大管帐打算盘，但要算起帐来，还是眼明手快，帐薄与存折一对，再看一看总帐，便弄清楚了，朱福年硬吞五万银子还不敢，只是挪用了公款，以后在半个月中，分四次归还了。然而这已是做伙计的大忌。胡雪岩认为不必细看，将翻开的帐簿、存折都收好，静等朱福年来答话。

A bundle of passbooks was brought over. Hu browsed through them at leisure, chatting as he did so, with nothing in his manner to suggest an audit. Zhu had no such ease. He sat anxiously across the desk, ostensibly ready to answer questions, while his eyes remained fixed on the books. “Mr Zhu,” a young apprentice came to announce, “the boatmaster has come on business.” This was the man engaged to carry the silk to Hangzhou, and Zhu had to see him. During his absence, Hu turned in the passbook to the eighth day of the seventh month in Xianfeng's third year. There was a record of Tongxing receiving fifty thousand taels. What nerve! Had he actually pocketed fifty thousand? Hu must examine this transaction closely. He was an expert in the trade. Though he seldom kept accounts or worked an abacus now, his eyes and hands were still quick. Comparing the account book with the passbook, then consulting the general ledger, he soon understood. Zhu had not dared to steal fifty thousand outright. He had diverted the firm's money to his own use, then repaid it in four instalments over the following half month. Even this, however, was a grave offence for an employee. Hu felt no need to examine further. He closed the books and passbooks he had opened and waited quietly for Zhu's return.

“船老大来问，货都装齐了，问啥时候开船？”朱福年说，“我告诉他，跟胡先生的货色搭帮走，比较有照应。不晓得胡先生的丝船，啥时候开？”很显然地，就这样一查帐，还未有何结果，就已让他感到威胁，不能不来周旋示好。胡雪岩便将计就计地说：“我们那票货色，是我的朋友古应春在料理。如果福年兄有空，中午我们一起吃饭，当面谈一谈这件事。你看好不好。”“好，好！”朱福年急忙答应，“我做个小东，请胡先生吃徽馆。”“哪个做东都一样。请你拿帐薄、存折收一收，我们就走吧。”看样子太平无事了，朱福年顿觉步履轻快，浑身是劲，收拾一切，陪着胡雪岩出了恒记的大门。

“The boatmaster says everything is loaded and asks when to sail,” Zhu reported. “I told him to travel with your shipment so that the boats could look after one another. When will your silk boats leave?” Plainly, the mere examination of the accounts, before any result had been announced, had threatened him enough to make him seek friendly relations. Hu took advantage of the opening. “My friend Gu Yingchun is handling our shipment. If you are free, Brother Funian, why not lunch together and discuss it with him? What do you say?” “Certainly!” Zhu agreed eagerly. “Allow me to offer a modest lunch at a Huizhou restaurant.” “It makes no difference who is host. Put away the books and passbooks, and let us go.” Everything seemed to have passed without incident. Zhu suddenly felt light on his feet and full of energy. After putting everything away, he accompanied Hu out of Hengji.

“就是后马路，有家徽馆，叫做福源楼，做几样我们家乡菜，着实道地。请胡先生尝尝看。““原来你是徽州人，口音倒听不出。”“我原籍徽州。”朱福年说，“在外多年，口音变过了。”“既是徽州，对典当自然熟悉？”“怎么不熟悉？我也劝过二少爷开典当。他说，穷人的钱不忍心赚。怎么也不肯。”“开典当是为了方便穷人，穷人出点利息，也是心甘情愿的。”“我也是这样说，二少爷听不进去，也是枉然。”就这样一路谈着典当，不知不觉地走到了福源楼。坐定下来，胡雪岩先写张条子，交柜上派人送到裕记丝栈去请古应春，然后点了菜，趁这等客等菜的工夫，他跟朱福年谈到了帐务。

“There is a Huizhou restaurant on Houmalu, called Fuyuanlou. Some of its dishes taste exactly as they do at home. Do try them.” “So you are from Huizhou? I could not tell from your accent.” “My family comes from there. After so many years away, my accent has changed.” “Then you must know the pawnshop business?” “Of course. I have urged Second Master to open a pawnshop. He says he cannot bear to make money from the poor and refuses.” “Pawnshops provide a service to the poor. They pay a little interest willingly.” “That is what I told him, but it is useless if he will not listen.” Talking of pawnshops, they reached Fuyuanlou almost without noticing. Once seated, Hu wrote a note and asked the restaurant to send someone with it to Yuji Silk Warehouse to invite Gu. He ordered the dishes, then, while waiting for their guest and the food, returned to the accounts.

“福年兄，刚才我看的那笔五万银子的帐，恐怕有点错了。”“喔。”因为胡雪岩语气缓和，所以朱福年也能沉得住气，平静地问道：“我倒还不清楚。日子久了，不大记得起来。”“帐上有送存同兴的一笔帐，存折上没有。”“是说恒记这个折子？”朱福年答道，“恒记在同兴有三个折子。”“我知道。”胡雪岩接着便问，“福记是你老兄的户头吧？”这就是所谓作贼心虚了，朱福年脸上的颜色，立刻就不大自然，勉强答说，“是的。”“我做钱庄也多年了，这种情形，倒还少见。”“各处地方不一样。”朱福年说，“为了调度方便，二少爷叫我也立一个户头。”“喔，”胡雪岩抓住他“调度方便”这四个字追问：“是不是说，有时候要向外头调动头寸，恒记不便出面，用你福记的名义？”这话，朱福年就答不出来了，因为庞二财大势雄，从不向外面调动头雨，如果应声“是”，胡雪岩跟庞二一谈，西洋镜马上拆穿，金饭碗也就要不翼而飞了。因此，他只能含含糊糊地答说：“不是这意思。”“那么是什么意思呢？”胡雪岩若无其事地问，声音中不带丝毫诘质的意味。而朱福年却已急得满头大汗，结结巴巴地不知道说些什么。

“Brother Funian, there may be a slight error in that fifty-thousand-tael transaction I looked at.” “Oh?” Hu's mild tone allowed Zhu to remain composed. “I am not quite sure. It was some time ago; I cannot remember it clearly.” “The account book records a deposit at Tongxing, but the passbook does not.” “You mean the Hengji passbook? Hengji has three passbooks at Tongxing.” “I know. Fuji is your own account, is it not?” A guilty conscience betrayed Zhu at once. His expression changed, and he forced out a “Yes.” “I have been in banking for years, but have seldom seen this arrangement.” “Customs differ from place to place. Second Master told me to open an account too, for convenience in managing funds.” Hu seized on those words. “Do you mean that when funds must be raised outside and Hengji cannot conveniently appear in the transaction, you use the name of Fuji?” Zhu could not answer. Pang was immensely wealthy and influential and never needed to raise funds outside. If he said yes and Hu mentioned it to Pang, the deception would be exposed at once, and his golden rice bowl would vanish. He could only answer vaguely, “That is not what I mean.” “What do you mean, then?” Hu asked casually, without the slightest interrogatory edge. Zhu, however, was sweating with anxiety and could only stammer incoherently.

“那也不必说它了！”胡雪岩不再侧面相逼，正面指出他的错，“那五万银子，细看前后帐，分毫不少……”“是啊！”朱福年急忙抢着辩白，“帐是决不会错的。”“错不错，要看怎么个看法，什么人来看？”胡雪岩答得极快，“我看是不错，因为以前的帐目，跟我到底没有啥关系，叫你们二少爷来看，就错了。你说是不是呢？”最后这一问，使得朱福年又大受其窘，只得先虚晃一枪：“我倒还不明白胡先生你的话？”“再明白都没有，五万银子说存恒记，结果存入福记，福记再分四次归还。前后数目不错，起码拆息上，恒记吃亏了。不过，这在我看，是小事，你倒拿我前后的话，仔细想一想！”他以前说过什么话？朱福年茫然不辨，定定心细想，才意会到他有句话，大有深意。这句话就是：“我看是不错，因为以前的帐目，跟我到底没有啥关系！”这就是暗示，以前的帐目他不会顶真，但以后他是恒记的股东，帐目便不能说无关，当然也就要认真了。意会到此，朱福年才知道自己不是“猪八戒”，倒是“孙悟空”，跳不出胡雪岩这尊“如来佛”的手掌心，乖乖儿认输，表示服帖，是上上大吉。

“Let us leave that aside.” Abandoning indirect pressure, Hu pointed out his fault plainly. “Looking carefully at the accounts before and after that fifty thousand, not a fraction is missing.” “Exactly!” Zhu hastened to defend himself. “The figures cannot be wrong.” “Whether they are wrong depends on how—and by whom—they are examined,” Hu answered at once. “To my eyes they are correct, since the earlier accounts have nothing to do with me. To Second Master's eyes, they would be wrong. Don't you agree?” Again cornered by the final question, Zhu tried an evasion. “I still do not quite understand you.” “It could not be clearer. Fifty thousand was said to have been deposited under Hengji, but went into Fuji. Fuji then repaid it in four instalments. The totals agree, but at the very least Hengji lost the interest. Still, I regard it as a small matter. Think carefully about everything I have said.” What had he said? Zhu was confused. Collecting himself, he finally grasped the significance of one sentence: “To my eyes they are correct, since the earlier accounts have nothing to do with me.” Hu was indicating that he would not insist on pursuing the old accounts. From now on, however, he would be a partner in Hengji. Its accounts would concern him, and he would examine them seriously. Zhu realized that he was not Pigsy after all, but Sun Wukong, unable to escape from Hu Xueyan’s palm, as though Hu were the Buddha himself. His best course was to admit defeat and submit.

“胡先生，我在恒记年数久了，手续上难免有疏忽的地方，一切要请胡先生包涵指教。将来怎么个做法，请胡先生吩咐，我无不遵办。”这是递了“降表”。到此地步，胡雪岩无需用旁敲侧击的办法，更用不着假客气，直接提出他的意见：“福年兄，受人之托，忠人之事，你们二少爷既然请我来看看帐，我当然对他要有个交代。你是抓总的，我只要跟你谈就是了，下面各人的帐目，你自己去查，用不着我插手。”“是。”朱福年说，“我从明天就清查各处的帐目，日夜赶办，有半个月的工夫，一定可以盘清楚。”“好的。你经手的总帐，我暂时也不看，等半个月以后再说。”“是！”“这半个月之中，你也不妨自己检点一下，如果还有疏忽的地方，想法子自己弥补。我将来也不过看几笔帐，”接着，胡雪岩清清楚楚他说了几个日子，这是从同兴送来的福记收支清单中挑出来的，都是有疑问的日子。朱福年暗暗心惊，自己的毛病自己知道，却不明白胡雪岩何以了如指掌，莫非他在恒记中已经埋伏了眼线？照此看来，此人高深莫测，真要步步小心才是。

“Mr Hu, I have been at Hengji for many years, and there may have been oversights in procedure. I ask your understanding and guidance. Tell me how to proceed in future, and I shall follow every instruction.” This was his declaration of surrender. Hu no longer needed hints or false politeness. He stated his wishes directly. “Brother Funian, when entrusted with a man's affairs, one must serve him faithfully. Since Second Master has asked me to examine the accounts, I must give him an explanation. You are in overall charge, so I need speak only to you. Examine the accounts of those beneath you yourself. I need not interfere.” “Yes. I shall begin checking every department tomorrow and work day and night. Within half a month, I shall have everything reconciled.” “Good. For the moment, I shall leave the general ledger in your hands unexamined too. We can discuss it in half a month.” “Yes.” “Meanwhile, review your own work. If there are any further oversights, find a way to put them right yourself. Later, I shall look at only a few transactions.” He then named several dates clearly and precisely, chosen from the statement of Fuji's receipts and payments supplied by Tongxing. Every one was questionable. Zhu was secretly alarmed. He knew his own irregularities, but could not understand how Hu knew them so thoroughly. Had he already planted informants at Hengji? The man was unfathomable. He must be careful at every step.

他的疑惧都流露在脸上，胡雪岩使索性开诚布公地说：“福年兄，你我相交的日子还浅，恐怕你还不大晓得我的为人。我一向的宗旨是：有饭大家吃，不但吃得饱，还要吃得好。所以，我决不肯敲碎人家的饭碗。不过做生意跟打仗一样，总要同心协力，人人肯拼命，才会成功。过去的都不必说了，以后看你自己，你只要肯尽心尽力，不管心血花在明处还是暗处？说句我自负的话，我一定看得到，也一定不会抹煞你的功劳，在你们二少爷面前会帮你说话。或者，你倒看得起我，将来愿意跟我一道来打天下，只要你们二少爷肯放你，我欢迎之至。““胡先生，胡先生！”朱福年激动不已，“你说到这样的金玉良言，我朱某人再不肯尽心尽力，就不是人了。胡先生，我敬一杯，表表我的心。”说罢，满斟一杯，仰脸饮尽。胡雪岩当然高兴，陪了一满杯，然后笑道：“福年兄，从此我们是一家人了，有啥说啥，不要见外。”

His fear and suspicion showed on his face, so Hu decided to speak openly. “Brother Funian, we have known each other only a short time. Perhaps you do not yet understand my character. My principle has always been that everyone should eat—not merely enough, but well. I would never willingly smash another man's rice bowl. Yet business is like war: success requires everyone to work together and give all their strength. Let us say no more about the past. The future depends on you. If you serve wholeheartedly, whether your efforts are visible or hidden, I venture to say that I shall see them. I shall never deny you the credit, and I shall speak for you before Second Master. Or, if you think well enough of me to wish to build a business at my side one day, I shall welcome you warmly, provided Second Master is willing to release you.” “Mr Hu!” Zhu was deeply moved. “After such precious words, I should scarcely deserve to be called a man if I failed to give my best. Let me drink to show my feelings.” He filled a cup and drained it. Hu gladly drank a full cup with him, then smiled. “Brother Funian, from now on we belong to one family. Speak freely. There is no need for ceremony.”

“是的。”朱福年想一想说，“胡先生，以后恒记的跟同兴的往来，只用两个户头，公款用恒记，二少爷私人收支用继嘉堂。我在同兴的户头，决定结了它。”“结了它也不必。”胡雪岩说，“不必让外头人猜测，以为我们内部生了啥意见。”这更见得胡雪岩的体恤，顾到自己的面子，当然乐受这番好意，“是！”他很恭敬地回答：“我懂胡先生的意思，找机会，我要告诉下面的‘朋友’们，恒记是一家，总要让外头人看得我们上下一心，不敢来动我们的歪脑筋才好。”“就是这话！‘打落牙齿往肚里咽’，方算好汉。”

“Yes.” Zhu considered. “Mr Hu, in future our dealings with Tongxing should use only two accounts: Hengji for the firm's money, Jijia Hall for Second Master's personal receipts and payments. I have decided to close my own account there.” “There is no need,” Hu replied. “We need not set outsiders wondering whether there has been a disagreement within the firm.” This showed still greater consideration for Zhu's dignity, and he gladly accepted it. “Yes, I understand,” he answered respectfully. “I shall find an opportunity to tell the men under me that Hengji is one family. Outsiders must see that we are united from top to bottom, so that they dare not plot against us.” “Exactly. A man must be able to swallow his broken teeth without a word.”

说到这里，只见古应春步履安详地踏了进来，朱福年起身让坐。极其殷勤。在右应春的心目中，此人自视甚高，加以东家“弹硬”，所以平日总在无意间流露出“架子大”“的味道，此刻一反常态，不用说，是对胡雪岩服帖了，才有这番连带尊敬的表示。意会到此，他的神情越发从容，说着闲话，不提正事。倒是朱福年忍不住了，“胡先生，应春兄来了，我们拿丝上的事说个定规。”他略停了一下又说：“ 照我看，‘只拉弓，不放箭’也就够了。”胡、古二人，目视而笑。然后是胡雪岩回答他的话，反问一句：“我们在‘打弓’，吉伯特晓不晓得？”“我想他是晓得的。我们真的‘放箭’他也会着急。”“当然罗！”古应春接口，极有信心地说：“他万里迢迢跑了来为啥？不是为了生意？生意做不成，他的盘缠开销哪里来？““话虽如此，事情有点弄僵！”胡雪岩问古应春：“你肯不肯向他去低头？”“我不去了！洋人是‘蜡烛脾气’，越迁就他，他越摆架子。”“为来为去，只为了我是当事人。如果这票货色不是我的，替双方拉场，话就好说了。而且双方也都一定感激此人。”

At this point Gu entered with an unhurried step. Zhu rose and offered him a seat with great attentiveness. Gu had always thought Zhu full of self-importance. Backed by a powerful employer, he habitually revealed an overbearing air. His changed manner could only mean that he had submitted to Hu and was extending the respect to Hu's friend. Understanding this, Gu grew still more composed. He chatted without mentioning business. Zhu finally could bear it no longer. “Mr Hu, now Brother Yingchun is here, let us settle what to do about the silk.” After a pause he added, “In my opinion, drawing the bow without loosing the arrow will be enough.” Hu and Gu exchanged a smile. “We are drawing the bow,” Hu replied, “but does Gilbert know it?” “I think so. If we really loose the arrow, he will be anxious.” “Of course!” Gu said confidently. “Why did he travel all these thousands of miles? For business. If no business is done, where will the money for his expenses come from?” “True, but things have become rather strained.” Hu turned to Gu. “Are you willing to bow to him?” “I shall not go again. Foreigners have a candle's temper: the more you indulge them, the more airs they put on.” “The difficulty is simply that I am a party to the transaction. If the silk were not mine, it would be easy to mediate—and both sides would surely be grateful to whoever did.”

“这个人很难。”古应春会意，故意不去看朱福年，尽自摇头：“不容易找！”他们这样一拉一唱。 暗中拉住了朱福年，他终于忍不住：“胡先生！你看，我跟吉伯特去谈一谈，是不是有用？”“噢！”胡雪岩一拍前额，做出茅塞顿开的姿态，“有你老兄出面，再好都没有了。有用，有用，一定有用。”受了鼓励的朱福年，越发兴致勃勃，自告奋勇：“吃完饭，我就去看他。我要吓他一吓，他不照原议买我们的这票货色，劝他趁早回国，他在这里永远买不到我们的丝！““对。就这么说。这倒也不完全是吓他，反正这票生意做不到，我们就斗气不斗财了！”朱福年倒真是赤胆忠心，即时就要去办事。胡雪岩当然要留住他，劝他从容些，把话想停当了再说。接着便设想吉伯特可能会有反响，他这么说便那么回答，那么说便这么回答，一一商量妥帖，还要先约个时间，从容不迫地谈，才能收效。

“Such a man would be hard to find.” Understanding Hu's meaning, Gu deliberately avoided looking at Zhu and kept shaking his head. “Very hard.” Between them they drew Zhu in. At last he could not resist. “Mr Hu, do you think it would help if I spoke to Gilbert?” “Ah!” Hu slapped his forehead as though suddenly enlightened. “Nothing could be better than having you act for us. It would help enormously.” Encouraged, Zhu grew more eager. “I shall see him after lunch. I shall give him a fright: if he will not buy our silk on the original terms, he had better go home. He will never buy our silk here.” “Yes. Say that. Nor would it be entirely an empty threat. If this transaction falls through, we shall fight for our pride instead of our profit.” Zhu was now wholly devoted to the cause and wanted to leave immediately. Hu naturally detained him, urging him to take his time and prepare what to say. They considered Gilbert's possible responses, deciding how to answer each one. They should also arrange an appointment first. Only a calm, unhurried discussion would achieve the desired result.

正事谈毕，酒兴未已，胡雪岩一直对典当有兴趣，此时正好讨教，“福年兄，”他先问：“你是不是典当出身？”“不是。不过我懂，我故世的三叔是朝奉，我在他那里住过一年。”接下来，朱福年便谈了典当中的许多行规和弊端，娓娓道来，闻所未闻。最后似感叹，又似遗憾地说，“当初未曾入典当，自己都不知道是得计，还是失策？因为‘吃典当饭’与众不同，是三百六十行生意中，最舒服的一行，住得好、吃得好，入息优厚，工作轻松，因此吃过这碗饭，别的饭就难吃了！”“照你这样说，如果开爿典当，要寻好手还不容易。”胡雪岩问，“典业中的好手，宾主相得，一动不如一静，轻易不肯他就。是这样吗？”“大致是这样子。不过人材是不断在冒出来的，本典无可位置，另求发展，也是有的。”“那么，我倒要请你留意，有这样的人，我想见见。”这表示胡雪岩也有创办典当的打算，朱福年欣然应诺，而且跃跃欲试地，颇有以半内行作内行，下手一试，以补少年未曾入此业之憾的意思。

Their business was settled, but they were still in the mood for drinking. Hu had always been interested in pawnshops, and this was a good opportunity to learn. “Brother Funian,” he began, “did you start out in the pawnbroking trade?” “No, but I know something about it. My late third uncle was a pawnshop appraiser, and I lived with him for a year.” Zhu went on to describe many of the trade’s rules and abuses, speaking so engagingly that Hu heard one thing after another entirely new to him. At last, with something between a sigh and an expression of regret, he said, “I never entered the trade. Even now I cannot tell whether that was a wise decision or a mistake. Earning your living in a pawnshop is unlike any other occupation. Of all the three hundred and sixty trades, it is the most comfortable: good accommodation, good food, generous pay, and light work. Once you have eaten from that bowl, it is hard to stomach any other.” “From what you say, finding good staff to open a pawnshop cannot be easy. An able man who gets on well with his employer is better off staying where he is. He will not readily take another position. Is that right?” “Broadly speaking, yes. But new talent keeps emerging. Sometimes there is no room for advancement in a man’s own shop, and he seeks an opportunity elsewhere.” “Then keep an eye out for me. I should like to meet someone of that sort.” Clearly Hu was considering opening a pawnshop himself. Zhu readily agreed and seemed eager to try his hand, treating his partial knowledge as full expertise and making up for the opportunity he had missed in his youth.

* * *朱福年是在第二天跟吉伯特见面的，那是陈顺生来探问运货舱位消息的时候，也正是由东印度公司转来伦敦总公司发出的何以今年的丝，至今未曾起运的质问之时，所以，吉伯特一见他的面，便先追问恒记和裕记两处的货色，可曾运离上海？“明天就要开船了。”朱福年用英语答说，“吉伯特先生，我觉得我对你有种道义上的责任，必须为你争取最后一个机会。最近商场上有一个大消息，不知道你听说了没有？”“我不知道你指的是什么？”“恒记的东家，也就是我的雇主庞先生，跟胡雪岩在事业上达成了合作的协议，胡雪岩的实力并不充足，但他是商场上一个非常特殊的人物，主要的是他在各方面都有极好的关系，而且他的手腕十分灵活。这两项就是他最大的资本，他所缺少的是现金，而这个缺点，由于跟庞先生的合作而充分弥补了。因此，我可以这样说：胡雪岩是无敌的，没有任何人能够在商场上击败他，包括你吉伯特先生在内。”“我不需要击败他，我只为我的公司的利益打算。最初是我采纳了你的建议，否则，也不至于有今天的僵局。”“吉伯特先生！” 朱福年放下脸来问：“你是不是要讨论这件事的责任？”“不！”吉伯特摇摇头，“那是没有用的。我又不能向你要求赔偿，哪里来的责任可言？你觉得对我有种道义上的责任，足见得你对我还存着友谊，我希望我们仍旧是朋友。”

Zhu met Gilbert the next day, just as Chen Shunsheng was enquiring about the shipping space and a demand had arrived from the London head office, forwarded by the East India Company, asking why this year’s silk had still not been shipped. The moment Gilbert saw him, he asked whether Hengji’s and Yuji’s consignments had left Shanghai. “The boats sail tomorrow,” Zhu replied in English. “Mr Gilbert, I feel a moral obligation towards you. I must try to secure one last opportunity for you. There has been important news in the business world lately. Have you heard it?” “I do not know what you mean.” “Hengji’s proprietor, my employer Mr Pang, has entered into a business partnership with Hu Xueyan. Hu’s resources were insufficient, but he is a most unusual figure in business. Above all, he has excellent connections in every quarter and is exceptionally resourceful. Those are his greatest assets. What he lacked was cash, and his partnership with Mr Pang has fully remedied that deficiency. I can therefore say this: Hu Xueyan is invincible. No one can defeat him in business, including you, Mr Gilbert.” “I have no need to defeat him. I am concerned only with my company’s interests. It was your advice I followed in the first place. Otherwise we should never have reached this impasse.” Zhu’s face hardened. “Mr Gilbert, do you wish to discuss who is responsible?” “No.” Gilbert shook his head. “That would serve no purpose. I cannot demand compensation from you, so what is the point of talking about responsibility? Your feeling of moral obligation shows that you still have some friendship for me. I hope we remain friends.”

听他这一番话，朱福年报之以诚恳的神色，“就因为如此，我要尽我的友谊。”他停了一下，用平静但很坚定的声音说：“吉伯特先生，你并没有失败，一切都可以照你原来的计划实现。但你如果错过此这个最后的机会，那么，你的失败不止于这一次，是明年及以后的日子。用最简单的话说：你将不能在上海买到你所需要的丝。”“照你看，丝价是不是能够减少若干？”吉伯特说，“如果你办得到，我们当然会付你应得的佣金。““不！”朱福年斩钉截铁地说，“决无可能！你应该知道，胡雪岩做生意的精明，是无人可及的，现在他不向你提出延期损失的赔偿，已经是很宽大了。”“好！”吉伯特终于低头了，“我一切照办，只希望赶快订约。”

Zhu responded with a look of sincerity. “That is precisely why I want to do what friendship requires.” He paused, then continued in a calm but firm voice. “Mr Gilbert, you have not been defeated. Everything can still go according to your original plan. But if you miss this final opportunity, your failure will extend beyond this one occasion, into next year and the years that follow. To put it simply, you will be unable to buy the silk you need in Shanghai.” “Do you think the price could be reduced at all?” Gilbert asked. “If you can arrange that, we shall of course pay you the commission you deserve.” “No!” Zhu was emphatic. “It is absolutely impossible. You should know that Hu Xueyan’s shrewdness in business is unequalled. He is already being very generous in not claiming compensation for the losses caused by the delay.” “Very well.” Gilbert finally yielded. “I agree to everything. I ask only that we sign the contract quickly.”

订了约，收银交货，胡雪岩如释重负。但经过一整夜的计算，却又爽然若失，自己都不知道为谁辛苦为谁忙。赚是赚了十八万银子，然而，不过说来好听，甚至于连帐面上的“虚好看”都没有。因为合伙的关系太多，开支也太大。跟尤五、古应春分了红利以外，还要跟郁四再分，付了各处的利息，还要为王有龄弥补海运局的亏空，加上裘丰言和嵇鹤龄那里都要点缀。这一下已经所余无几，却还有开销杭州、湖州、同里三个“门口”所拉下来的“宕帐”，细看一算，除了阜康钱庄的本钱，依旧是一整笔债务以外，还有万把银子的亏空。万把银子在他当然不必发愁，要愁的是这样子费心费力，到头来还闹了一笔亏空，则所谓“创业”也者，岂非缘木求鱼？照道理不应该如此！落到这样的地步，总有个道理在内，当然是自己的做法有了毛病。这个毛病不找出来，令人寝食难安。为此，他虽然一整夜未睡，脑子里昏昏沉沉地，但精神有种异样的亢奋，怎么样也不想上床。

Once the contract was signed, payment collected, and the silk delivered, Hu felt a great weight lift from him. Yet after a whole night’s calculations he was left strangely empty, scarcely knowing for whom he had worked and worried so hard. The profit was indeed a hundred and eighty thousand taels, but it only sounded impressive: not even a handsome figure on paper survived. There were too many partners and too many expenses. The profits had to be shared with You Laowu and Gu Yingchun, and then with Yu Si. Interest had to be paid in various quarters; Wang Youling’s deficit at the Sea Transport Bureau had to be made good; Qiu Fengyan and Ji Heling also had to receive their tokens of appreciation. That left very little. There were still the outstanding bills from his three households in Hangzhou, Huzhou, and Tongli. A close reckoning showed that, apart from the capital of Fukang Bank, which remained entirely a debt, he was another ten thousand taels or so short. Ten thousand taels in itself did not worry him. What troubled him was that so much thought and effort should end in a deficit. If that was how he meant to build a business, was he not climbing a tree to catch fish? It ought not to have worked out this way. There must be a reason, some fault in his own methods. Until he found it, he could neither eat nor sleep in peace. Although he had been awake all night and his head was heavy, a peculiar nervous excitement kept him from wanting to go to bed.

到了快中午时，古应春和刘不才相偕来访，一见了面，古应春失声说道：“小爷叔，你的气色好难看！是不是病了？”刘不才开过药店，对于伤风发烧之类的毛病，也能诊察，当时伸手一探他的额头，又叫他伸舌头出来看了舌苔，很准确地作了判断：“睡得太少，用心过度，是虚火上升。好好吃一顿，舒舒服服睡一觉，精神马上就好了。”“一点不错。”胡雪岩有意将他遣开：“请你替我去约一约庞二，晚上在哪里叙一叙。回头四、五点钟，你到浴德池来找我。”等刘不才一走，胡雪岩将预先一张张计算好的单子，取了出来，捡出古应春的一张交了给他，照胡雪岩的算法，古应春应该分一万五千多银子的盈余。“小爷叔！”古应春略看了一看，将单子推了回去，“第一，你分得我多了，第二，现在不要分，我们仍旧在一起做，商量商量以后怎么个做法，才是正经。”胡雪岩脱口答道：“我正就是不晓得以后怎么个做法？”接着便皱起了眉不断摇头。这态度很奇怪，古应春大为惊疑，“小爷叔！”他很吃力地说，“你好象有啥难言之隐似地。大家自己人，你尽吩咐，有啥‘摆不平’，我的一份不必计算在内。”

Towards noon, Gu Yingchun and Liu Bucai came together. The moment Gu saw him, he exclaimed, “Little Uncle, you look dreadful! Are you ill?” Liu had once run a pharmacy and could diagnose such ordinary ailments as colds and fevers. He felt Hu’s forehead, asked him to put out his tongue, examined its coating, and gave a very accurate diagnosis. “Too little sleep and too much mental exertion. Deficiency heat is rising. Eat a good meal and have a comfortable sleep, and you will feel yourself again.” “Exactly.” Hu deliberately found a reason to send him away. “Please arrange for me to meet Pang somewhere this evening. Come and find me at Yudechi Bathhouse at four or five.” Once Liu had left, Hu brought out the individual statements he had calculated beforehand and handed Gu his. According to Hu’s reckoning, Gu was entitled to a profit of more than fifteen thousand taels. Gu glanced through it and pushed it back. “Little Uncle, first, you have allotted me too much. Second, let us make no distribution now. We shall go on working together. What matters is to discuss how we should proceed.” “That is precisely what I do not know!” Hu blurted out, frowning and shaking his head repeatedly. His strange manner startled Gu. With some difficulty, he said, “Little Uncle, you seem to have some trouble you find hard to speak about. We are all friends. Tell me what you need. If there is anything you cannot settle, leave my share out of the reckoning.”

“应春兄！”胡雪岩相当感动，率直答道：“我一无所得，就是朋友的情分义气，千金不换。”“岂止于千金不换？小爷叔，你不要说一无所得，在我看，所得正多。不说别的，只说朱福年好了，庞二虽有些大少爷的脾气，有时讲话不给人留情面，到底御下宽厚，非别的东家好比，可是朱福年还是有二心，只有遇到小爷叔你，化敌为友，服服帖帖，这就是你的大本事，也就是你的大本钱。“由于说得中肯，不是一般泛泛的恭维可比，所以胡雪岩听了这几句话，深受鼓舞，“老古，”他便索性问道：“你直言谈相，看我做生意有啥毛病要改？”

Deeply moved, Hu answered frankly, “Brother Yingchun, I have gained nothing—except the loyalty and affection of friends, which a fortune could never buy.” “Worth more than any fortune! But do not say you have gained nothing, Little Uncle. To my mind you have gained a great deal. Take Zhu Funian alone. Pang has something of a pampered young gentleman’s temper and sometimes speaks without sparing anyone’s feelings, but he is generous to his staff in a way few employers are. Yet Zhu still harboured disloyal intentions. Only when he encountered you did an enemy become a friend and submit completely. That is your great ability and your great capital.” These observations went to the heart of the matter; they were far more than empty compliments. Hu was greatly encouraged. “Old Gu,” he asked outright, “speak frankly. What faults do you see in the way I do business? What should I change?”

“毛病是谈不到。不过，小爷叔，中国人有句话，叫做‘业精于勤，荒于嬉’，这个‘勤’字照我讲，应该当做敬业的敬，反过来‘嬉’字不作懒惰解释，要当作浮而不实的不敬来讲。敬则专，专心一志，自然精益求精。小爷叔，如果说你有失策之处，我直言谈相，就是不专心。“古应春又说，”人的精力到底有限，你经手的事情到底太多了，眼前来看，好象面面俱到，未出纰漏，其实是不是漏了许多好机会，谁也不得而知。“他一路说，胡雪岩一路点头，等他说完，随即答道：“有好几位都这样劝过我，不过没有你说得透彻。我刚才在想，忙了半天，两手空空，总有个毛病在那里，你说我不专心，这就是我的毛病。不过，也不能说两手空空……”他没有再说下去，说下去怕古应春多心，他本人两手空空，还亏下了帐，但相交合作的朋友，都有好处。这盘帐要扯过来算，还是有成就的。

“I would not call them faults. But there is a Chinese saying: ‘A calling is mastered through diligence and ruined by play.’ I take ‘diligence’ to mean respect for one’s calling. And ‘play’, in turn, means not laziness but a shallow lack of seriousness. Respect brings concentration; single-minded concentration brings continual improvement. Little Uncle, if you have made a mistake, I must tell you plainly that it is a lack of concentration. A man’s energy is limited, after all, and you have far too many affairs in hand. For the moment, everything seems to be attended to and nothing has gone wrong. Yet who can say how many good opportunities you may have missed?” Hu nodded throughout. When Gu had finished, he immediately replied, “Several people have advised me along these lines, but none has explained it as clearly as you. Just now I was thinking that after all this effort I was left empty-handed. There must be something wrong. You say I lack concentration. That is my fault. Still, I cannot really say I am empty-handed…” He stopped, afraid that saying more might make Gu uneasy. He himself had nothing to show for his work and was even in debt, but all the friends who had worked with him had benefited. Viewed from that side of the ledger, he had achieved something after all.

这样转念，更觉精神一振，“走，走，”他站起身来说：“照刘三爷的话，好好吃它一顿，睡它一觉。有没有什么好番菜？吃完了到浴德池去泡它一下午。”“好番菜是有，只怕你吃不来。”“怎么吃不来？”“夏天讲究吃‘色白大菜’，生冷清淡，半生不熟，吃不惯的会倒胃口。”“那就算了。还是……”“还是到我这里去吃饭吧！七姐现在返璞归真了，到处跟人学做菜，今天在做粉蒸鸡，还有你们西湖上的莼菜……”“你不要再说了。”胡雪岩咽了口唾沫答道，“再说下去，我真要流口水了。”于是一起到古应春那里。七姑奶奶果然卷起衣袖，在厨房里大忙特忙，汗水蒸润，她那张银盆似的脸，和两条藕也似的手臂，格外显得红白分明，看见胡雪岩在厨房门口探头一望，赶紧喊道，“厨房里象火焰山一样，小爷叔，快不要进来！”“我饿了！”胡雪岩老实答说，“有啥吃的，先弄点来喂喂我。”“我先下碗米粉干，让你点点饥。回头慢慢吃酒。”等一碗鸡汤火腿笋干米粉下肚，接着便摆桌子喝酒，恰好尤五也到了，胡雪岩越有兴致。

The thought revived him further. “Come, come!” He rose. “We shall follow Third Master Liu’s advice: a good meal and a good sleep. Is there any good Western food to be had? Afterwards we can spend the afternoon soaking at Yudechi.” “There is, but I am afraid you might not like it.” “Why should I not?” “In summer the fashionable thing is a se-bai Western dinner: cold, lightly flavoured food, raw or only half cooked. It can turn your stomach if you are not used to it.” “Then forget it. We had better…” “We had better eat at my place. Seventh Sister has returned to simpler ways. She is learning to cook from everyone she meets. Today she is making chicken steamed with rice meal, and there is water shield from your own West Lake…” “Say no more!” Hu swallowed. “If you go on, I shall start drooling.” They went together to Gu’s house. Sure enough, the Seventh Lady had rolled up her sleeves and was busy in the kitchen. The heat had brought a sheen of perspiration to her round, silver-basin face and her lotus-root arms, making their pink and white all the more vivid. Seeing Hu peer through the kitchen doorway, she called at once, “It is like the Flaming Mountain in here! Do not come in, Little Uncle!” “I am hungry,” he replied honestly. “Whatever you have, give me something to eat first.” “I shall cook a bowl of rice noodles to take the edge off your hunger. Then we can have a leisurely drink.” He finished a bowl of rice noodles in chicken broth with ham and dried bamboo shoots, and the table was set for wine. You Laowu happened to arrive as well, putting Hu in still better spirits.

席间当然要问他今后的打算，胡雪岩却反问尤五和古应春，要怎么样打算，才能于大家有益？“这话就是很难说了。”尤五答说，“照我的心思，最好你别人的闲事都不管。”“五哥也是！”七姑奶奶性子直，马上就补了一句他未曾说出来的话：“别人的闲事不要管，只管你的事。是不是？”大家都笑了。“这当然是一厢情愿。不过，”尤五正色说道，“我们漕帮方面，生路越来越狭，小爷叔，你答应过的，总要替我们想个办法。”“当然，当然。我一定当我自己的事来办。”胡雪岩又问古应春：“你看呢，我以后该怎么做法？”“我刚才就说过了。”胡雪岩点点头，重新回想他上午所作的那番劝告。那些话，尤五和七姑奶奶并不知道，尤其是七姑奶奶性子急，便追问首，胡雪岩将古应春劝他专心的话，说了给她听，并且盛赞古应春看得深，识得透。

Naturally they asked about his plans, but he put the question back to You and Gu: what course would benefit everyone? “That is difficult to say,” You replied. “If I had my way, you would leave everyone else’s affairs alone.” “Just listen to Brother Five!” The Seventh Lady was direct by nature and at once supplied the words he had left unsaid. “Leave everyone else’s affairs alone and attend only to yours. Is that it?” Everyone laughed. “Of course that is only wishful thinking on my part,” You said. Then he grew serious. “But the ways of earning a living are narrowing for our grain-transport brotherhoods. You promised, Little Uncle. You must find a way for us.” “Certainly, certainly. I shall treat it as my own business.” Hu turned to Gu. “And what do you think I should do?” “I told you just now.” Hu nodded, recalling the advice Gu had given him that morning. You and the Seventh Lady had not heard it. Impatient as ever, she pressed him for an explanation, and he repeated Gu’s counsel about concentrating his efforts, warmly praising its insight and clarity.

“谢谢一家门！”七姑奶奶撇着嘴说，“小爷叔，他是狗头军师，你不要听他的话。”古应春不服气，但也不敢跟她争辩，只说：“小爷叔，‘妇人之言，慎不可听’。”“啥叫‘妇人之言’？”七姑奶奶的反应快得很，“场面总是越大越好。照你的说法，有皇帝做也不要做了，因为管的事太多太杂？“一句话驳得古应春哑口无言，摇摇头轻轻说了句：“歪理十八条。”胡雪岩看他那无奈七姑奶奶之何的尴尬神态，未免好笑，但一向不以他那个“宝贝妹子”为然的尤五，却帮着她说话：“阿七说的倒也不是歪理。事情不怕多，要有人管，皇帝好做，难的是用不着一个好宰相。小爷叔，我想，考古的话也不错，阿七的比喻也有道理，你是聪明人，不妨拿他们两个人的话好好想一想，作一番打算。““是的！”胡雪岩深深点头。于是他一面吃喝闲谈，一面在心中盘算，等酒醉饭饱，他的盘算也大致停当了。

“Thanks to him and his entire family!” The Seventh Lady curled her lip. “Little Uncle, he is a bungling strategist. Do not listen to him.” Gu disagreed but dared not argue with her. He merely said, “Little Uncle, ‘Take care never to heed a woman’s words.’” “What do you mean, ‘a woman’s words’?” she retorted instantly. “Surely the larger your sphere of activity, the better. By your reasoning, a man should refuse to be emperor because he would have too many different affairs to manage!” That left Gu without an answer. He shook his head and murmured, “Eighteen varieties of crooked reasoning.” Hu was amused by Gu’s helpless embarrassment. You, however, who usually took a dim view of his precious younger sister, now supported her. “What Seventh Sister says is not altogether unreasonable. There is no harm in having many affairs, provided there are people to manage them. Being emperor is easy; the difficulty is finding a good chief minister. Little Uncle, I think Old Gu is right, but Seventh Sister’s comparison also makes sense. You are a clever man. Think over what they have both said and work out a plan.” “Yes.” Hu nodded gravely. As he ate, drank, and chatted, he kept turning the matter over. By the time he had enjoyed enough wine and food, his plan was largely settled.

“五哥，老古！”他说，“我们先把帐分了……”“不必分！”尤五抢着说，他的意思跟古应春一样，主张就原来的资本和盈余，听候胡雪岩全权运用，能够“利上滚利”。“我懂你们的意思。”胡雪岩说，“我要重起炉灶，做几样事业，大家分开来管，我只抓个总。就好比做皇帝一样，要宰相大臣分开来办事，用不着我亲自下手。”“嗯，嗯！”在座的三个人，不约而同地颔首表示同意。“第一样是钱庄，这方面是我的根本，我也内行，恐怕还是要亲自下手。第二样是丝，在湖州，我交给陈世龙，在上海，我交给老古。““好的！”古应春说，“我当仁不让，无需客气。将来茶叶、桐油也好做洋庄，慢慢儿再说。”“将来销洋庄都归你一手担当。茶叶、桐油我也想过，只要你认为可以做，我无不赞成。不过眼前新丝就要上市了，所以要请你赶紧筹划，专心一致，百事不管。不过……”胡雪岩看一看七姑奶奶，笑笑不再说下去。

“Brother Five, Old Gu,” he began, “first let us divide up the accounts…” “There is no need!” You interrupted. His view was the same as Gu’s: the original capital and the profits should remain entirely at Hu’s disposal, to earn profit upon profit. “I understand,” Hu said. “But I want to make a fresh start, with several businesses managed separately by different people, while I take overall charge. Like an emperor, I shall have ministers handling their own affairs without needing to do everything myself.” All three listeners nodded their agreement. “First comes banking. That is my foundation, and I know the trade, so I shall probably still have to attend to it myself. Second comes silk. In Huzhou I shall put Chen Shilong in charge; in Shanghai, Old Gu.” “Good,” Gu replied. “I shall accept that responsibility without standing on ceremony. Later we can also export tea and tung oil. We can discuss those in due course.” “All our exports will be in your hands. I have thought about tea and tung oil too. If you think they are worth doing, I shall support you. But the new silk will soon be on the market, so you must begin planning at once. Concentrate entirely on that and leave everything else alone. Except…” He glanced at the Seventh Lady and stopped with a smile.

这大有皮里阳秋的意味，七姑奶奶免不了要问：“小爷叔，不过什么？”“不过，”胡雪岩笑道，“百事不管，你们的终身大事是非管不可的。我也是这样子，别样闲事不能再管，你的这桩大事，非效劳到底不可。当着五哥在这里，我做大媒的说一句，你们挑日子、办喜事，乾坤两宅，自己商量，不必我来传话。古家老族长那里的归我疏通，一定不会办不通，你们放心好了。““是的。”尤五点点头说，“这件事，我就这几天要好好谈一谈。现在且不去说它，小爷叔你再讲你的打算。”

There was plainly something behind the remark, and the Seventh Lady could not help asking, “Except what, Little Uncle?” “Except,” Hu answered, laughing, “that however much you leave everything else alone, your marriage must be attended to. The same goes for me. I can no longer concern myself with every other matter, but I must see this one through for you. With Brother Five here, let me say this as your chief matchmaker: choose a day and arrange the wedding. The bride’s and bridegroom’s families can discuss it directly without having me carry messages between them. I shall bring the Gu family’s old clan head round. I am certain it can be done, so set your minds at rest.” “Yes,” You said, nodding. “We must have a proper talk about it in the next few days. But let us leave it for now. Go on with your plans, Little Uncle.”

“我还打算办两样事业，一样是典当，一样是药店。药店请刘三爷来做，典当，我想跟庞二谈一谈，请朱福年帮我的忙。”对他的这番打算，尤五和古应春默然不置可否，这意思就是不以为然，在古应春觉得他不宜做此自己不懂的事业，而刘不才的本性，也不宜于苦干创业，朱福年则相交未几，虽说“南蛮不复反矣”，但他究竟有几许本事，尚未明了，何以轻付以重任？尤五也略有这样的想法，此外他还有疑虑，率直问道：“小爷叔，一样钱庄，一样丝，都是大本钱，你哪里还有余力开当铺、开药店？”“五哥说到要害上来了。”胡雪岩很起劲地，“自然我都有打算。”胡雪岩的打算，是凭他的信誉、本领，因人成事。阜康设分号，是庞二有过承诺，愿意支持的，做丝生意，仍旧是大家集股。开典当的本钱，他看中了苏州潘叔雅那班富家公子，开药店则预备在江浙官场上动脑筋。

“I also intend to start two other businesses: a pawnshop and a pharmacy. I shall ask Third Master Liu to run the pharmacy. As for the pawnshop, I want to speak to Pang and ask for Zhu Funian’s help.” You and Gu offered neither approval nor objection. Their silence meant that they did not agree. Gu thought Hu should not enter trades he did not understand. Liu Bucai’s temperament was also ill suited to the hard work of establishing a new business. As for Zhu, they had known him only a short time. Though they might now say of him, “The southern barbarians will never rebel again,” his actual abilities were still uncertain. How could such important responsibilities be entrusted to him so readily? You had similar thoughts and another doubt besides, which he expressed frankly. “Little Uncle, banking needs a great deal of capital, and so does silk. Where will you find the means to open a pawnshop and a pharmacy as well?” “Brother Five has put his finger on the point,” Hu said eagerly. “Naturally I have made plans.” His plan was to use his reputation and ability to enlist other people’s help. Pang had promised support for a Fukang branch, while the silk business would continue to be financed by pooled shares. For the pawnshop’s capital, he had his eye on Pan Shuya and the other wealthy young gentlemen of Suzhou. For the pharmacy, he intended to find a way through official circles in Jiangsu and Zhejiang.

“我再说，为啥要开典当、开药店？这两样事业，一时都无利可图，完全是为了公益，我开典当是为方便穷人。胡雪岩三个字，晓得的人，也不算少了，但只有做官的和做生意的晓得，我以后要让老百姓都晓得，提起胡雪岩，说一声：这个人不错！事业就会越做越大。为此，我要开药店，这是扬名的最好办法。再说，乱世多病痛，大乱之后，必有瘟疫，将来药店的生意，利人利己，是一等一的好事业。“听得这一说，七姑奶奶首先就钦佩不止，“你听听，”她带点教训意味地对古应春说：“小爷叔的眼光，才真叫眼光！看到大乱以后了。你要学学小爷叔。”“本来就跟小爷叔在学。”古应春转脸问道，“小爷叔，你说开药店的本钱，出在公家，是怎么个办法？”“ 这要靠关系了。军营里自然要用药，我要跟刘三爷商量，弄两张好方子，真材实料修合起来，譬如刀伤药、诸葛行军散、辟瘟丹之类，要一服见效，与众不同。这样子就好禀请各路粮台，先定我们多少，领下价款来做本钱。”“真是！”七姑奶奶听得眉飞色舞，“我看世界上，没有小爷叔没有办法的事！”“七姐，”胡雪岩有些惶恐，“这话捧得我太过分了。一个人的力量到底有限，就算三头六臂，也办得了多少事？要成大事，全靠和衷共济，说起来我一无所有，有的只是朋友。要拿朋友的事当自己的事，朋友才会拿你的事当自己的事。没有朋友，就是有天大的本事，也还是没有办法。”

“Let me explain why I want a pawnshop and a pharmacy. Neither will make a profit immediately. I mean them entirely for the public good. A pawnshop will help poor people. Quite a few people already know the name Hu Xueyan, but they are all officials and businessmen. In future I want ordinary people to know it too. When they hear my name, I want them to say, ‘That is a decent man!’ Then my businesses will keep growing. That is why I want a pharmacy: it is the best way to make a name. Besides, troubled times bring illness, and great upheavals are always followed by epidemics. A pharmacy will benefit others and ourselves. It is one of the best businesses there is.” The Seventh Lady was the first to express her admiration. “Listen to him,” she told Gu, with a touch of admonition. “That is real foresight! Little Uncle is already looking beyond the war. You ought to learn from him.” “I am learning from him.” Gu turned to Hu. “You said the pharmacy’s capital would come from public funds. How would that work?” “Through our connections. The army must have medicines.
