Xiao was accustomed to life afloat, but steamships had none of these taboos, and Kong cared even less about them. Li Qingshan and Li Delong knew which subjects to avoid; they refrained from saying what ought not to be said but otherwise talked as usual. Beside them, Hu, normally so lively and entertaining, seemed weighed down by cares and sunk in the deepest gloom.

于是姓孔的提议打麻将，萧家骥为了替胡雪岩解除寂寞，特地去请他入局。『五个人怎么打。除非一个人做——。』说到『做』字，胡雪岩缩住了口；他记起坐过『水路班子』的船，『梦』是忌讳的，要说『黄粱子』，便接下去∶『除非一个人做黄粱子。』萧家骥一楞，想了一下才明白，『用不着。』他说，『我不想打。胡先生你来，解解厌气。』于是胡雪岩无可无不可地入了局。打到一半，风浪大作，被迫终止；胡雪岩又回到铺上去睡觉，心里不免忐忑不安，加以不惯风涛之险，大呕大吐，心里那份不宁帖，真有求生不得，求死不能之感。『胡先生，不要紧的！』萧家骥一遍一遍地来安慰他。不光是语言安慰，还有起居上的照料，对待胡雪岩真象对待古应春一样，尊敬而亲热。胡雪岩十分感动，心里有许多话，只是精神不佳，懒得去说。

Kong suggested mahjong. Hoping to relieve Hu’s loneliness, Xiao went specially to invite him to join them. “How can five of us play? Unless one man has a—” Hu stopped short. He remembered travelling on a floating pleasure boat, where the word “dream” was taboo and had to be replaced by “golden millet”. “Unless one man has his golden millet,” he finished. Xiao stared, then understood. “There is no need,” he said. “I do not wish to play. Come, Mr Hu. It will relieve the tedium.” Indifferent either way, Hu joined the game. Halfway through, a gale and heavy seas forced them to stop. He returned to his bunk to sleep. He was anxious enough already; now, unused to the violence of the wind and waves, he began vomiting miserably. His whole being was so unsettled that life seemed intolerable, while death offered no escape. “There is nothing to worry about, Mr Hu!” Xiao came again and again to comfort him. Nor did he offer words alone: he attended to all Hu’s needs, with the same affectionate respect he showed Gu Yingchun. Hu was deeply touched. There was much he wanted to say, but he felt too ill to make the effort.

入夜风平浪静，海上涌出一轮明月，胡雪岩晕船的毛病，不药而愈，只是腹饥难忍，记得七姑奶奶曾亲手放了一盒外国饼干在网篮，起床摸索，惊醒了熟睡中的萧家骥。『是我！』他歉然说道∶『想寻点干点心吃。』『胡先生人舒服了！』萧家骥欣然说道∶『尾舱原留了粥在那里，我替你去拿来。』于是萧家骥点上了盏马灯，到尾舱去端了粥米，另外是一碟盐鱼，一个盐蛋；胡雪岩吃得一干二净，抹一抹嘴笑道∶『世乱年荒，做人就讲究不到哪里去了。』

By nightfall the wind and waves had subsided. A bright moon rose out of the sea, and Hu’s seasickness vanished without medicine. Now, however, hunger tormented him. He remembered the box of foreign biscuits that the Seventh Lady had put into his mesh basket with her own hands. He got up to search for it and woke Xiao, who had been sleeping soundly. “It is only me,” he said apologetically. “I was looking for something dry to eat.” “You feel better, Mr Hu!” Xiao said delightedly. “They kept some congee for you in the stern cabin. I shall fetch it.” He lit a storm lantern and went aft, returning with the congee, a plate of salted fish and a salted egg. Hu ate everything, wiped his mouth and smiled. “In times of war and famine, one cannot be too particular about how one lives.”

『做人不在这上面，讲究的是心。』萧家骥说，『王抚台交胡先生这样的朋友，总算是有眼光的。』『没有用！』胡雪岩黯然，『尽人事，听天命。就算到了杭州，也还不知道怎么个情形；说不定就在这一刻，杭州城已经破了。』『不会的。』萧家骥安慰他说∶『我们总要朝好的地方去想。』『对！』胡雪岩很容易受鼓舞，『人，就活在希望里面。家骥，我倒问你，你将来有什么打算？』这话使萧家骥有如逢知音之感。连古应春都没有问过他这句话。所以满腹大志，无从诉说；不想这时候倒有了倾诉的机会。『我将来要跟外国人一较短长。我总是在想，他们能做的，我们为什么不能做？中国人的脑筋，不比外国人差，就是不团结；所以我要找几个志同道合的人，联合起来，跟外国人比一比。』『有志气！』胡雪岩脱口赞道∶『我算一个。你倒说说看，怎么样跟他们比？』『自然是做生意。他到我们这里来做生意，我们也可以到他那里去做生意。在眼前来说，中国人的生意应该中国人做；中国人的钱也要中国人来赚。只要便宜不落外方，不必一定要我发达。』胡雪岩将他的话细想了一会，赞叹着说∶『你的胸襟了不起。我一定要帮你，你看，眼前有啥要从外国人那里抢过来的生意——。』『第一个就是轮船——。』

“What matters in a man’s life is not that sort of thing, but his heart,” Xiao said. “Governor Wang showed sound judgement in choosing a friend like you.” “It is no use!” Hu’s face darkened. “We do what we can and leave the rest to Heaven. Even if we reach Hangzhou, who knows what we shall find? The city may be falling at this very moment.” “No,” Xiao said consolingly. “We must always look towards the brighter possibility.” “True!” Hu was easily encouraged. “Hope is what keeps a man alive. Jiaji, tell me: what do you mean to do in the future?” Xiao felt that at last he had found someone who understood him. Not even Gu had ever asked him that question. All his great ambitions had remained unspoken; now, unexpectedly, he had a chance to pour them out. “One day I mean to compete with the foreigners. I am always asking myself: why should we not do what they can do? Chinese minds are no worse than theirs. We simply fail to work together. I want to find a few men who share my aims, join forces with them and see how we measure up against the foreigners.” “That is ambition!” Hu exclaimed in admiration. “Count me in. Tell me how you propose to compete.” “In business, naturally. They come here to trade; we can go to their countries and do the same. For the present, Chinese business ought to be conducted by Chinese, and Chinese money earned by Chinese. So long as the advantage stays in our hands, I need not be the one to prosper.” Hu considered this for a moment. “What breadth of spirit! I shall certainly help you. What business could we begin taking from foreign hands now?” “Steamships, first of all—”

于是，从这天起，胡雪岩就跟萧家骥谈开办轮船公司的计划；直到沙船将进鳖子门，方台停了下来。依照预定的计划，黑夜偷渡，越过狭处，便算脱险，沿钱塘江往西南方向走；正遇着东北风，很快地到了杭州；停泊在江心。但是，胡雪岩却不知道如何跟城里取得联络；从江心遥望，凤山门外，长毛猬集，仿佛数十里连绵不断，谁也不敢贸然上岸。『原来约定，是王雪公派人来跟我联络；关照我千万不要上岸。』胡雪岩说∶『我只有等、等、等！』王有龄预计胡雪岩的粮船，也快到了，此时全力所谋求的，就是打通一线之路，直通江边，可以运粮入城。无奈十城紧围，战守俱穷，因而忧愤成疾，肝火上升；不时吐血，一吐就是一碗，失血太多，头昏目眩，脸如金纸，然而他不肯下城休息，因为休息亦归于无用，倒不如勉力支撑，反倒可收激励士气的效用。

From that day, Hu and Xiao discussed plans for establishing a steamship company. Only when the junks were about to enter Biezimen did their discussions cease. According to their plan, they slipped through under cover of darkness. Once through the narrows, they were out of danger and sailed southwest along the Qiantang. A favourable northeasterly wind soon brought them to Hangzhou, where they anchored in midstream. But Hu did not know how to communicate with the city. Looking from the river towards Fengshan Gate, they saw the Longhairs massed outside it, apparently stretching unbroken for tens of li. No one dared go ashore rashly. “The arrangement was that Governor Wang would send someone to contact me. He warned me on no account to land,” Hu said. “All I can do is wait, and wait, and wait!” Wang Youling expected the grain boats to arrive shortly. His whole effort now went into opening a passage to the riverbank through which the provisions could enter the city. But all ten gates were tightly besieged, and the defenders had exhausted their resources for both attack and defence. Anxiety and anger made him ill. His liver fire rose, and he repeatedly vomited blood, a bowlful at a time. The loss left him dizzy and faint, his face as yellow as gold paper. Yet he would not leave the wall to rest. Rest would do no good; better to force himself to hold on, and at least encourage the troops by his presence.

哀兵的士气，倒还不坏；但俗语道得好∶『皇帝不差饿兵』；打仗是费气力的事，枵腹操戈，连跑都跑不动，哪谈得到杀敌？所以每天出城攻击，长毛一退，官军亦随即鸣金收兵。这样僵持了好久，一无成就，而城里饿死的人，却是越来越多了；先还有做好事的人，不忍见尸骨骨露，掘地掩埋，到后来埋不胜埋，只好听其自然；大街小巷『路倒尸』不计其数，幸好时值冬天，还不致发生疫疠，但一城的尸臭，也熏得人够受的了。到了十月底，城外官军的营盘，都为长毛攻破；硕果仅存的，只有候潮门外，副将曾得胜一营，屹然不动。这一营的不倒，是个奇迹；但说穿了不希奇，城外比较容易找粮食，真的找不到了，到长毛营盘里去找。反正打仗阵亡也是死，绝粮坐毙也是死；既然如此，不如去夺长毛的粮食，反倒是死中求活的一条生路。因此，曾军打起仗来，真有视死如归之概。说也奇怪，长毛望见『曾』字旗帜，先就心慌，往往不战而遁；但是，这一营也只能自保，要想进击破敌，实力悬殊过甚。到底无能为力。

The defenders’ spirit, born of desperation, was not bad. Yet the saying was sound: even an emperor does not send hungry soldiers on a mission. Fighting requires strength. With empty bellies and weapons in their hands, the men could scarcely run, let alone kill an enemy. Each day they sallied out, but the moment the Longhairs drew back, the imperial troops sounded the gong to recall their own men. This stalemate continued for a long time without achieving anything, while more and more people starved inside the city. At first, charitable souls who could not bear to see the bodies exposed dug graves and buried them. Eventually the dead were too numerous to bury, and they had to leave them where they lay. Bodies beyond counting filled the streets and alleys. Fortunately it was winter, so no epidemic had yet broken out, but the stench throughout the city was torment enough. By the end of the tenth month, the Longhairs had overrun all the imperial camps outside the walls except one: Deputy Commander Zeng Desheng’s battalion stood firm outside Houchao Gate. Its survival seemed a miracle, though the explanation was simple. Food was easier to find outside the city; when none could be found elsewhere, the men sought it in the Longhairs’ camps. Death in battle and death from starvation were equally death. Better, then, to seize the enemy’s provisions and seek a chance of life in mortal danger. Zeng’s men accordingly fought with a courage that made them appear to welcome death as a homecoming. Strangely enough, the Longhairs lost heart at the sight of the flag bearing the character “Zeng” and often fled without fighting. Yet this single battalion could do no more than preserve itself. The disparity in strength was too great for it to launch an offensive and break the enemy. It was powerless to do more.

只是王有龄却对这一营寄以莫大的期望，特别下令仁和知县吴保丰，将安置在城隍山上的一尊三千斤重的大炮，费尽力量，移运到曾得胜营里，对准长毛的壁垒，大轰特轰。这一带长毛倒是绝迹了，但仍无法直通江边，因为大炮射程以外，长毛仍如牛毛，重重隔阻，处处填塞，始终杀不开重围。就在这时候，抓住一名奸细——奸细极易分别，因为城里的人，不是面目浮肿，就是骨瘦如柴，走路挪不了三寸，说话有气无力；如果遇到一个气色正常，行动舒徐，说话不必侧耳就可以听得清楚的，必是从城外混进来的；这样一座人间地狱，还有人跳了进来，其意何居？不问可知。果然，抓住了一顿打，立刻打出了实话，此人自道是长毛所派，送一封信来给饶廷选部下的一外营官，约定里应外合的日期。同时也从他口中得到一个消息，说钱塘江中，停泊了十几号大船，满装粮食。这不问可知，是胡雪岩的粮船到了；王有龄陡觉精神一振，当即去看杭州将军瑞昌，商量如何杀开一条血路，能让江中的粮食运入城内？不须多作商量，便有了结果，决定请副都统杰纯，当此重任。事实上怕也只有此人堪当重任——杰纯是蒙古人，他祖先驻防杭州，早有好几代；杰纯本人是正六品骁骑校出身，武艺娴熟，深得军心，积功升到正四品的协领，颇为瑞昌所倚重。

Wang nonetheless placed enormous hopes in it. He specially ordered Wu Baofeng, magistrate of Renhe, to move a cannon weighing three thousand jin from City God Hill to Zeng’s camp, at immense effort. Trained on the Longhairs’ fortifications, it thundered away until no enemy remained in that immediate area. Still they could not reach the riverbank. Beyond the cannon’s range the Longhairs remained as numerous as hairs on an ox, blocking every approach in layer upon layer. The encirclement could not be broken. Just then a spy was caught. Spies were easy to recognise: the people inside the city were either bloated in the face or wasted to skin and bone; they could scarcely shuffle a few inches and spoke in voices too weak to hear. Anyone of normal complexion who walked easily and could be heard without straining one’s ears must have slipped in from outside. What purpose could draw a man into such a hell on earth? There was no need to ask. Sure enough, a beating soon brought out the truth. The man admitted that the Longhairs had sent him with a letter for a battalion commander under Rao Tingxuan, fixing a date for a coordinated attack from within and without. He also revealed that more than a dozen large vessels, laden with provisions, lay in the Qiantang. Plainly Hu’s grain boats had arrived. Wang’s spirits revived at once. He went immediately to Ruichang, the garrison general of Hangzhou, to discuss how to force a bloody passage through which the grain might be brought into the city. Little discussion was needed. They decided to entrust the task to Deputy Lieutenant-General Jiechun. Indeed, there was probably no one else equal to it. Jiechun was a Mongol whose ancestors had served in the Hangzhou garrison for generations. He had begun as a cavalry officer of the senior sixth rank. Highly skilled in arms and deeply trusted by his men, he had risen through service to the senior fourth rank as a banner commander, and Ruichang relied heavily upon him.

咸丰十年春天，杭州城第一次为长毛轰破，瑞昌预备自刎殉国；杰纯劝他不必轻生，认为安徽广德来的敌军，轻骑疾进，未有后继，不足为忧，不妨固守待援。瑞昌听了他的话，退守满营；营盘在西湖边上，实际是一座子城，俗称满城。因为防御得法，长毛连攻六天，劳而无功；杰纯的长子守城阵亡，杰纯殓而不哭，认为长子死得其所，死得其时。到了第七天，张玉良的援兵到了；杰纯怒马突出，当者披靡，配合援军，大举反攻，将长毛逐出城外十几里。以此功劳，赏戴花翎，升任为宁夏副都统，但仍旧留在杭州，成了瑞昌的左右手。这次杭州再度吃紧，杰纯战功卓著，赐号巴图鲁，调任乍浦副都统，这是海防上的一个要缺；但乍浦已落入长毛手中，所以仍旧留防省城。杭州十城，最关紧要的就是北面的武林门和南门的凤山门；凤山门原由王有龄亲自坐镇，这一阵因为呕血过多，气衰力竭，才改由杰纯防守——胡雪岩的粮船，就泊在凤山门外的江面；让杰纯去杀开一条血路，亦正是人和地理，两皆相合的顺理成章 之事。

In the spring of the tenth year of Xianfeng, when the Longhairs first breached Hangzhou, Ruichang had prepared to cut his throat and die for his country. Jiechun urged him not to throw away his life. The enemy had advanced rapidly with light cavalry from Guangde in Anhui and had no reinforcements behind them; there was no cause for despair. They should hold their ground and await relief. Ruichang accepted his advice and withdrew into the Manchu garrison beside West Lake. In effect it was a city within the city, commonly called the Manchu City. Its defences were so skilfully managed that six days of Longhair attacks achieved nothing. Jiechun’s eldest son died defending the walls. His father laid out the body without tears, believing that his son had died as a man should, at the proper moment. On the seventh day Zhang Yuliang’s reinforcements arrived. Jiechun burst forth on a charging horse, sweeping aside all opposition. In concert with the relieving army, he launched a great counterattack and drove the Longhairs more than ten li beyond the city. For this service he received the right to wear a peacock feather and was promoted to deputy lieutenant-general of Ningxia, though he remained in Hangzhou as Ruichang’s right-hand man. During the present crisis his distinguished services earned him the title Baturu, “the Brave”, and a transfer to the deputy lieutenant-generalship of Zhapu, an important coastal-defence post. But Zhapu had fallen to the Longhairs, so he stayed to defend the provincial capital. Of Hangzhou’s ten gates, Wulin in the north and Fengshan in the south were the most important. Wang had originally commanded at Fengshan in person. Only recently, exhausted by vomiting blood, had he handed its defence to Jiechun. Hu’s grain ships lay in the river outside that very gate. To send Jiechun to force a passage was therefore the obvious choice, both for the man and for the position he held.

围凤山门的长毛主将叫做陈炳文，照太平天国的爵位，封号称为『朗天义』。他本来要走了——长毛的军粮，亦渐感不敷；李秀成已经拟定行定计划，回苏州度岁，预备明年春天，卷土重来。但陈炳文已从城里逃出来的难民口中，得知城内绝粮，已到了人吃人的地步；所以翻然变计，坚持不走；同时也知道城内防守，以凤山门为重点，因而又厚集兵力，一层夹一层，直到江边，弹丸之地，集结了四万人之多。等到粮船一到，遥遥望见，陈炳文越发眼红，一方面防备城内会冲出来接粮；一方面千方百计想攻夺粮船，无奈江面辽阔，而华尔的部下防守严密，小划子只要稍稍接近，便是一排抢过来，就算船打不沉，人却非打死打伤不可。一连三日，无以为计；最后有人献策，依照赤壁鏖兵，大破曹军的办法，用小船满载茅柴，浇上油脂，从上游顺流而下，火攻粮船。陈炳文认为此计可行。但上游不是自己的战区，需要派人联络；又要禀报忠王裁夺，不是一两天所能安排停当的。同时天气回暖，风向不定，江面上有自己的许多小划子；万一弄巧成拙，惹火烧身，岂不糟糕？因而迟疑未发。就在这时候，粮船上却等不得了。

The Longhair commander besieging Fengshan Gate was Chen Bingwen, whose title in the Taiping hierarchy was Langtianyi. He had been about to leave: the Longhairs too were beginning to run short of provisions. Li Xiucheng had already drawn up plans to return to Suzhou for the New Year and resume the campaign the following spring. But Chen learnt from refugees escaping the city that its food was gone and its inhabitants had begun eating one another. He abruptly changed his mind and insisted on staying. Knowing also that Fengshan Gate was the key to the city’s defence, he massed his forces there in layer after layer all the way to the river, concentrating as many as forty thousand men in that tiny area. When he saw the grain boats in the distance, his eagerness to seize them grew fiercer. He prepared against a sortie from the city to collect the provisions while trying every means of capturing the vessels. But the river was broad and Ward’s men guarded them closely. Whenever a small boat drew near, a volley met it. Even if the boat did not sink, its occupants could scarcely escape death or injury. Three days passed without success. Finally someone proposed copying the method by which Cao Cao’s army had been destroyed at Red Cliffs: load small boats with brushwood, soak it in oil and send them downstream from above to burn the grain ships. Chen thought the scheme feasible. But the upper reaches were outside his sector, so he had to make contact with the commanders there and submit the proposal to the Loyal King for a decision. Such arrangements could not be completed in a day or two. Moreover, the weather had grown warmer, the wind was changeable, and many of their own small boats were on the river. What if the clever plan backfired and they burned themselves instead? He hesitated to act. Meanwhile, the men aboard the grain ships could wait no longer.

因为一连三天的等待，胡雪岩度日如年，眠食俱废。而护航洋兵的孔联络官，认为身处危地，如果不速作鼾，后果不堪设想，不断催促胡雪岩，倘或粮食无法运上陆地，就应依照原说，改航宁波。沙船帮的李庆山口中不言，神色之间亦颇为焦急，这使得胡雪岩越发集躁，双眼发红，终日喃喃自语，不知说些什么，看样子快要发疯了。『得隆哥，』萧家骥对胡雪岩劝慰无效，只好跟李得隆商议，『我看，事情不能不想办法了。这样「屏」下去要出事。』『是啊！我也是这样在想。不过有啥办法呢？困在江心动弹不得。』李得隆指着岸上说∶『长毛象蚂蚁一样；将一座杭州城，围得铁桶似的，城里的人，怎么出得来？』『就是为了这一点。我想，城里的人出不来，只有我们想法子进城去，讨个确实口信；行就行，不行的话，胡先生也好早作打算。这样痴汉等老婆一船，等到哪一天为止？』李得隆也是年轻性急，而且敢冒险的人，当然赞成萧家骥的办法；而且自告奋勇，愿意泅水上岸，进城去通消息。『得隆哥，』萧家骥很平静地说∶『这件事倒不是讲义气，更不是讲客气的。事情要办得通；你去我去都一样，只看哪个去合适？你水性比我好，人比我灵活，手上的功夫，更不是我比得了的——。』『好了，好了！』李得隆笑道，『你少捧我！前面捧得越高，后面的话越加难所；你老实说，我能不能去？』『不是我有意绕弯子说话，这种时候，杂不得一点感情意气，自己好弟兄，为啥不平心静气把话说清楚。我现在先请问你，得隆哥，你杭州去过没有？你晓得我们前面的那个城门叫啥？』

For Hu, the three days had felt like years. He could neither eat nor sleep. Kong, liaison officer with the foreign escort, believed they were in a dangerous position and that failure to decide quickly might have disastrous consequences. He kept urging Hu to sail for Ningbo, as originally agreed, if the provisions could not be landed. Li Qingshan of the Sea-Junk Guild said nothing, but his face betrayed considerable anxiety. This made Hu still more frantic. His eyes reddened, and he muttered unintelligibly to himself all day. He looked close to madness. Unable to comfort him, Xiao turned to Li Delong. “Brother Delong, we must find some way out of this. Something will go wrong if we remain bottled up like this.” “Yes, I have been thinking the same thing. But what can we do? We are trapped in the middle of the river.” Li pointed ashore. “The Longhairs are like ants. They have sealed Hangzhou as tight as an iron barrel. How can anyone get out?” “That is precisely the point. If the people inside cannot get out, we must find a way in and obtain a definite answer. If it can be done, good; if it cannot, Mr Hu can make other plans at once. We are waiting like a fool for a wife. How long can this go on?” Li too was young, impatient and willing to take risks. He naturally approved of Xiao’s proposal and volunteered to swim ashore and carry a message into the city. “Brother Delong,” Xiao said calmly, “this is not a question of proving our loyalty, still less of making polite offers to one another. We have to get the task done. Whether you go or I go makes no difference; what matters is which of us is better suited. You swim better than I do, you are more agile, and your skill in a fight is far beyond mine—” “Enough, enough!” Li laughed. “Stop flattering me. The higher you praise me now, the harsher the words that follow. Tell me plainly: can I go or not?” “I am not trying to be roundabout. At a time like this we must not allow feeling or pride to interfere. We are good brothers; why should we not discuss it calmly and frankly? Let me first ask you this, Brother Delong: have you ever been to Hangzhou? Do you know the name of the gate in front of us?”

『不晓得。我杭州没有去过。』『这就不大相宜了。杭州做过宋朝的京城，城里地方也蛮大的。不熟，寻不着；这还在其次，最要紧的一点是，你不是听胡先生说过，杭州城里盘查奸细严得很；而且因为饿火中烧，不讲道理。得隆哥，』萧家骥停了一下说∶『我说实话，你不动气。你的脾气暴躁；口才不如我。你去不大相宜！』李得隆性子直爽，服善而肯讲道理，听萧家骥说得不错，例即答道∶『好！你去。』于是两个人又商量了如何上岸；如何混过长毛的阵地；到了城下，如何联络进城，种种细了，大致妥当，才跟胡雪岩去说明其事。『胡先生！』是由李得隆开口，『有件事禀告你老人家，事情我们都商量好了，辰光也不容我们再拖下去了，我说了，请你老人家照办，不要驳回。请你写封信给王抚台，由家骥进城去送。』李得隆其实是将胡雪岩看错了。他早就想过，自己必须坐守，免得城里千辛万苦派出人来，接不上头，造成无可挽救的错失；此外，只要可能，任何人都不妨进城通消息。所以一听这话，神态马上变过了。

“No. I have never been to Hangzhou.” “Then you are not quite the right man. Hangzhou was the capital of the Song dynasty. It is a large city, and without knowing it you will have trouble finding your way. But that is the lesser difficulty. The chief point is this: you heard Mr Hu say how strictly they are hunting spies inside the walls. Hunger has inflamed people’s tempers, and they will not listen to reason.” Xiao paused. “Brother Delong, do not be angry if I speak frankly. You have a quick temper, and you are not as ready with words as I am. It would not be wise to send you.” Li was straightforward, willing to listen to reason and accept sound advice. Recognising the truth of Xiao’s words, he answered at once, “Very well. You go.” The two then discussed how Xiao should land, pass through the Longhairs’ positions and make contact beneath the walls to enter the city. Only when these details were largely settled did they take their proposal to Hu. “Mr Hu,” Li began, “there is something we must report. We have worked it all out, and we cannot afford any more delay. Once I have told you, I beg you to agree and not refuse. Please write a letter to Governor Wang. Jiaji will take it into the city.” In fact, Li had misjudged Hu. Hu had long understood that he himself must stay where he was, lest someone from the city should reach the boats after terrible hardships only to miss him, with irreparable consequences. Apart from that, anyone who could possibly carry a message into the city ought to go. At Li’s words, his whole manner changed.

『慢慢来！』他又恢复了临大事从容不乱的态度；比起他这两天的坐卧不宁来，判若两人，『你先说给我听听，怎么去法？』『泅水上去——。』『不是，不是！』第一句话就让他大摇其头，『湿淋淋一身，就不冻出病来，上了岸怎么办？难道还有客栈好投，让你烤干衣服？』『原是要见机行事。』『这时候做事，不能说碰运气了。要想停当再动手。』胡雪岩说，『你听我告诉你。』他也实在没有什么腹案，不过一向机变快，一路想，一路说，居然就有了一套办法——整套办法中，最主要的一点是，遇到长毛，如何应付？胡雪岩教了他一条计策∶冒充上海英商的代表，向长毛兜售军火。

“Steady!” He had recovered his customary calm in the face of great affairs, utterly different from the restless man of the past two days. “First tell me how you intend to get there.” “Swim ashore—” “No, no!” Hu shook his head at the very first sentence. “What will you do once you land, soaked to the skin, even if you do not fall ill from the cold? Do you imagine there is an inn where you can dry your clothes by a fire?” “We meant to act as circumstances required.” “At a time like this we cannot simply trust to luck. We must think everything through before acting,” Hu said. “Listen to me.” He had no prepared plan himself. But he had always been quick-witted; thinking as he spoke, he soon worked out a complete scheme. Its most important point was how to deal with any Longhairs Xiao encountered. Hu suggested a stratagem: pose as the representative of a British merchant in Shanghai and offer to sell them arms.

『好在你会说英文，上海洋行的情形也熟；人又聪明，一定装得象。』胡雪岩说∶『你要记住，长毛也是土里土气的，要拿外国人唬他。』——交代停当，却不曾写信；这也是胡雪岩细心之处，怕搜到了这封信，大事不成，反惹来杀身之祸。但见了王有龄，必须有一样信物为凭；手上那个金戒指本来是最真确的，又怕长毛起眼劫掠，胡雪岩想了半天，只有用话来交代了。『我临走的时候，王抚台跟我谈了好些时候，他的后事都托了我。他最钟爱的小儿子，名叫苕云，今年才五岁，要寄在我名下；我说等我上海回来再说。这些话，没有第三个人晓得，你跟他说了，他自然会相信是我请你去的。』这是最好的征信办法，萧家骥问清楚了『苕云』二字的写法，紧记在心。但是，一时还不能走；先要想办法找只小船。

“You speak English, and you know the foreign firms in Shanghai. You are clever too. You will certainly make a convincing show,” Hu said. “Remember, the Longhairs are provincial fellows as well. Use the foreigners to overawe them.” Once his instructions were given, however, he wrote no letter. This too showed his care: if a letter were found in a search, the whole undertaking would fail and Xiao would lose his life. Yet Xiao needed some token to prove his credentials when he met Wang Youling. The gold ring on Hu’s hand would have been unmistakable, but he feared it would catch a Longhair’s eye and be stolen. After long consideration, he could think of nothing but an oral message. “Before I left, Governor Wang talked with me for a long time. He entrusted all his affairs after his death to me. His youngest son, whom he loves most dearly, is called Tiaoyun and is only five this year. He wanted to place the boy under my name. I said we should discuss it after I returned from Shanghai. No third person knows of this conversation. Tell him, and he will know that I sent you.” This was the best possible proof. Xiao asked exactly how the two characters of Tiaoyun’s name were written and committed them to memory. But he could not yet leave: first they had to find a small boat.

小船是有，过往载运逃难的人的渡船，时有所见，但洋兵荷枪实弹，在沙船上往来侦伺，没有谁敢驶近。这就要靠李得隆了，借了孔联络官的望远镜，看准远远一只空船；泅水迎了上去，把着船舷，探头见了船老大，先不说话，身上摸出水淋淋的一块马蹄银，递了过去；真是『重赏之下，必有勇夫』，很顺利地雇到了船。这是天色将暮，视界不明，却更易混上岸去；胡雪岩亲自指点了方向，就在将要开船时，他忽然想到了一件事。『喂，喂，船老大，你贵姓？』船老大指指水面∶『我就姓江。』『老江，亲苦你了。』胡雪岩说∶『你拿我这位朋友送到岸，回来通个信给我，我再送你十两银子。决不骗你；如果骗你，教我马上掉在钱塘江里，不得好死。』听他罚得这么重的咒，江老大似乎颇为动容，『你老爷贵姓？』他问。

There were boats about. Ferries carrying refugees passed from time to time, but with the foreign soldiers patrolling the junks, loaded guns in hand, none dared approach. Here they needed Li Delong. Borrowing Kong’s telescope, he picked out an empty boat in the distance and swam towards it. He caught hold of its side and raised his head to face the boatman. Before saying a word, he drew a dripping horseshoe-shaped silver ingot from his clothing and handed it up. Truly, a handsome reward will always find a brave man: he hired the boat without difficulty. Dusk was falling and visibility was poor, making it easier to slip ashore. Hu pointed out the direction himself. Just as they were about to cast off, another thought struck him. “Wait, boatman! What is your surname?” The man pointed at the water. “Jiang—River.” “Old Jiang, thank you for your trouble,” Hu said. “Take my friend ashore, then come back and bring me word. I shall give you another ten taels. I will not deceive you. If I do, may I fall straight into the Qiantang and die a dreadful death.” Such a terrible oath seemed to move the boatman. “What is your honourable surname, sir?” he asked.

『我姓王。』『王老爷，你老人家请放心；我拿这位少爷送到了，一定来报信。』『拜托、拜托！』胡雪岩在沙船上作揖，『我备好银子在这里等你，哪怕半夜里都不要紧，你一定要来！你船上有没有灯笼？』『灯笼是有的。』江老大也很灵活，知道他的用意，『晚上如果挂出来，江风一吹，马上就灭了。』『说得有理。来，来，索性「六指头搔痒」，格外奉承你了。』胡雪岩另外送他一盏燃用『美孚油』的马灯，作为报信时挂在船头的信号，免得到时洋兵不明就里，误伤了他。

“Wang.” “Rest assured, Mr Wang. Once I have landed this young gentleman, I shall certainly come back and report.” “I am relying on you!” Hu bowed from the junk. “I shall have the silver ready and wait for you here. Even if it is the middle of the night, come back without fail. Have you a lantern on your boat?” “A lantern, yes.” Jiang was quick-witted too and understood his purpose. “But if I hang it outside at night, the wind off the river will blow it out at once.” “Quite right. Come, then! I shall scratch your back with six fingers—an extra favour for you.” Hu gave him a storm lantern burning Mobil kerosene. He was to hang it at the bow as a signal when returning with news, lest the foreign soldiers, unaware of his purpose, fire on him by mistake.

等萧家骥一走，李得隆忍不住要问，何以要这样对待江老大，甚至赌神罚咒，唯恐他不信似的。是不是不放心萧家骥？『已经放他出去了，没有什么不放心。』胡雪岩说，『我是防这个船老大；要防他将人送到了，又到长毛那里去密告讨赏。所以用十两银子拴住他的脚，好教他早早回来。这当然要罚咒，不然他不相信。』『胡先生，实在服了你了，真正算无遗策。不过，胡先生，你为啥又说姓王呢？』『这另外有个缘故，钱塘江摆渡的都恨我；说了真姓要坏事。你听我说那个缘故给你听；二十年前——。』二十年前的胡雪岩，还在钱庄里学生意，有一次奉命到钱塘江南岸的萧山县去收一笔帐款；帐款没有收到，有限的几个盘缠，却在小菜馆里掷骰子输得只剩十个摆渡所需的小钱。『船到江心，收钱了。』胡雪岩说，『到我面前，我手一伸进衣袋里，拿不出来了。』『怎么呢？』李得隆问。『也叫祸不单行，衣袋破了个沿；十个小钱不知道什么时候漏得光光。钱塘江的渡船，出了名的凶，听说真有付不出摆渡钱，被推到江里的事。当时我自然大窘，只好实话实说，答应上岸到钱庄拿了钱来照补。叫啥说破了嘴都无用，硬要剥我的衣服。』『这么可恶！』李得隆大为不平，『不过，难道一船的人，都袖手旁观？』

Once Xiao had gone, Li Delong could not help asking why Hu had treated the boatman in that manner, even swearing by the gods as though afraid of being disbelieved. Was he worried about Xiao? “Once I have let him go, there is no point worrying,” Hu replied. “It is the boatman I am guarding against. He might land our man and then go to the Longhairs to inform on him for a reward. I tied his feet with ten taels so that he would come straight back. Naturally I had to swear an oath, or he would not believe me.” “Mr Hu, I truly admire you. You leave nothing to chance. But why did you tell him your surname was Wang?” “That has another cause. The Qiantang ferrymen all hate me. My real name would have caused trouble. Let me tell you why. Twenty years ago—” Twenty years before, Hu had still been an apprentice in a bank. On one occasion he was sent to Xiaoshan County on the south bank of the Qiantang to collect a debt. He failed to collect it, and in a little eating house he lost almost all his scant travelling money at dice, keeping only the ten copper coins needed for the ferry. “When the boat reached midstream, they collected the fares,” he said. “The man came to me, and I put my hand in my pocket—but could bring nothing out.” “Why?” Li asked. “Misfortunes never come singly. A hole had worn in the pocket, and all ten coins had slipped out without my noticing. The Qiantang ferrymen were notoriously fierce. I had heard of people actually being pushed into the river because they could not pay. Naturally I was desperately embarrassed. I could only tell the truth and promise to fetch the money from my bank as soon as we landed. I might as well have talked my mouth off. They insisted on stripping off my clothes.” “The villains!” Li exclaimed indignantly. “But surely the whole boat did not just stand by and watch?”

当然不致于，有人借了十文钱给他，方得免褫衣之辱。但胡雪岩经此刺激，上岸就发誓∶只要有一天得意，力所能及，一定买两只船；雇几个船夫，设置来往两岸不费分文的义渡。『我这个愿望，说实话，老早就可以达到。哪知道做好事都不行！得隆，你倒想想看，是啥道理？』『这道理好懂。有人做好事，就有人没饭吃了。』『对！为此钱塘江摆渡的，联起来来反对我，不准我设义渡。后来幸亏王抚台帮忙。』那时王有龄已调杭州知府，不但私人交情，帮胡雪岩的忙义不容辞；就是以地方官的身分，为民造福，奖励善举，亦是责无旁贷的事。所以一方面出告示不准告摆渡为生的人，阻挠这件好事；一面还为胡雪岩请奖。自设义渡，受惠的人，不知凡几；胡雪岩纵非沽钓誉，而声名洋溢，就此博得了一个『胡善人』的美名。只是钱塘江里的船家，提起『胡善人』，大多咬牙切齿，此所以他不肯对江老大透露真姓。小小的一个故事，由于胡雪岩心情已比较开朗，恢复了他原有的口才，讲得颇为风趣，所以李得隆听得津津有味，同时也更佩服了。

Of course not. Someone lent him ten cash, sparing him the humiliation of being stripped. Yet the experience stung him so deeply that, once ashore, he swore that if he ever prospered and had the means, he would buy two boats, engage some boatmen and establish a charitable ferry to carry passengers between the banks without charging a single coin. “To tell the truth, I could have fulfilled that wish long before I did. Who would have thought one could be prevented from doing good? Delong, what do you suppose the reason was?” “Easy enough. When one man does good, another loses his livelihood.” “Exactly. The Qiantang ferrymen joined forces against me and would not let me establish the free crossing. Fortunately Governor Wang helped me in the end.” At the time Wang had been transferred to the post of prefect of Hangzhou. His personal friendship made helping Hu a duty; equally, as the local official, he was bound to benefit the people and encourage charitable acts. He issued a proclamation forbidding those who earned their living by ferrying passengers to obstruct the scheme, and also applied for an official reward for Hu. Countless people benefited from the free ferry. Even though Hu had not set out to fish for praise, his reputation spread everywhere, and he became known as “Hu the Benefactor”. But most Qiantang boatmen gnashed their teeth at the mention of that name. That was why he had concealed his true surname from Jiang. Now that his spirits had lifted, Hu had recovered his usual gift for telling a story. He made this little incident so entertaining that Li listened with delight—and with growing admiration.

『胡先生，因果报应到底是有的。就凭胡先生你在这条江上，做下这么一桩好事；应该决不会在这条江上出什么风险。我们大家都要托你的福。』这两句话说得很中听，胡雪岩喜逐颜开地说∶『谢谢！谢谢！一定如你金口。』不但胡雪岩自己，船上别的人，也都受了李得隆那几句话的鼓舞，认为有善人在船，必可逢凶化吉。因而也就一下子改变了前两天那种坐困愁城，忧郁不安，令人仿佛透不过气来的味道；晚饭桌上，兴致很好，连不会喝酒的李得隆也愿意来一杯。

“Mr Hu, there must be such a thing as moral recompense. After the good you have done on this river, you surely cannot come to harm upon it. We shall all share in your good fortune.” This was exactly what Hu wished to hear. His face lit up. “Thank you, thank you! May your gracious words come true.” Nor was he the only one encouraged. Everyone aboard took heart from Li’s remarks, believing that with a good man among them, calamity would turn to blessing. At once the oppressive atmosphere of the past two days—their sense of being trapped, their anxiety and despondency—lifted. Dinner was a cheerful affair. Even Li, who was no drinker, agreed to take a cup.

『说起来鬼神真不可不信。』孔联络官举杯在手，悠闲地说，『不过行善要不教人晓得，才是真正做好事；为了善人的名声做好事，不足为奇。』『不然。人人肯为了善人的名声，去做好事，这个世界就好了。有的人简直是「善棍」。』胡雪岩说，『这就叫「三代以下，唯恐不好名」。』『什么叫「善棍」？』李得隆笑道，『这个名目则是第一次听见。』『善棍就是骗子。借行善为名行骗，这类骗子顶顶难防。不过日子一久，总归瞒不过人。』胡雪岩说，『什么事，一颗心假不了；有些人自以为聪明绝顶，人人都会上他的当；其实到头来原形毕露，自己毁了自己。一个人值不值钱，就看他自己说的话算数不算数；象王抚台，在我们浙江的官声，说实话，并不是怎么样顶好；可是现在他说不走，就不走，要跟杭州人同祸福，共存亡，就这一点上他比何制台值钱得多。』话到这里，大家不期而然地想到了萧家骥，推测他何时能够进城？王有龄得到消息，会有什么举动？船上该如何接应？『举动是一定会有举动的。不过——，』胡雪岩忽然停杯不饮，容颜惨淡，好久，才叹口气说∶『我实在想不出，怎样才能将这批米运上岸；就算杀开一条血路，又哪里能够保得住这条粮道畅通？』

“One really cannot disbelieve in spirits and gods,” Kong observed comfortably, cup in hand. “But true goodness is doing good without letting anyone know. There is nothing remarkable in charity performed merely to gain a reputation for virtue.” “I disagree. If everyone would do good for the sake of a good name, this world would be a fine place. Some people are simply charity swindlers,” Hu said. “As the saying goes, ‘Since the Three Dynasties, the fear should be that men care too little for a good name.’” “Charity swindlers?” Li laughed. “That is a new name to me.” “It means cheats who use charity as a cover. They are the hardest sort of swindler to guard against, though in time people always see through them. In anything a man does, he cannot counterfeit his heart for ever. Some imagine themselves so clever that everyone will fall into their trap. In the end their true nature shows, and they ruin themselves. A man’s worth depends on whether he keeps his word. Take Governor Wang. To speak frankly, his reputation as an official in Zhejiang was not among the very best. But now he says he will not leave, and he stays. He means to share the fortunes of Hangzhou’s people, to live or die with them. In that alone he is worth far more than Governor-General He.” At this, everyone’s thoughts turned naturally to Xiao. When would he enter the city? What would Wang do on receiving the news? How should the boats respond? “He is certain to take action. But—” Hu suddenly held his cup without drinking. His face grew bleak. After a long silence he sighed. “I really cannot see how we are to get this rice ashore. Even if they fight a passage through, how can they keep the supply route open?”

『胡先生，有个办法不晓得行不行？』李得隆说∶『杭州不是有水城门吗？好不好弄几条小船，拿米分开来偷运进城？』『只怕不行——。』话刚说得半句，只听一声枪响；随即有人喊道∶『不能开枪，不能开枪；是报信的来了。』于是胡雪岩、李得隆纷纷出舱探望，果然，一点星火，冉冉而来；渐行渐近，看出船头上挂的是盏马灯。等小船靠近，李得隆喊一声∶『江老大！』『是我。』江老大答应着，将一根缆索抛了过来。李得隆伸手接着，系住小船，将江老大接了上来，延入船舱；胡雪岩已将白花花一锭银子摆在桌上了。『那位少爷上岸了。』江老大说，『我来交差。』『费你的心。』胡雪岩将银子往前一推，『送你做个过年东道。』

“Mr Hu, I wonder whether this might work,” Li said. “Does Hangzhou not have water gates? Could we get a few little boats, divide the rice among them and smuggle it into the city?” “I fear not—” Hu had scarcely begun when a shot rang out. Immediately someone shouted, “Do not fire! Do not fire! The messenger is coming back!” Hu and Li hurried out of the cabin. Sure enough, a point of light was slowly approaching. As it drew nearer they could see a storm lantern hanging at the bow. When the boat came alongside, Li called, “Boatman Jiang!” “It is I!” Jiang answered, throwing up a rope. Li caught it, made the boat fast, helped him aboard and invited him into the cabin. Hu had already placed a gleaming silver ingot on the table. “The young gentleman has gone ashore,” Jiang said. “I have come to report.” “Thank you for your trouble.” Hu pushed the silver towards him. “A little something for your New Year’s entertainment.”

『多谢，多谢。』江老大将银子接到手里，略略迟疑了一下才说∶『王老爷，有句话想想还是要告诉你∶那位少爷一上岸，就教长毛捉了去了。』捉去不怕，要看如何捉法？胡雪岩很沉着地问∶『长毛是不是很凶？』『那倒还好。』江老大说，『这位少爷胆子大，见了长毛不逃；长毛对他就客气点了。』胡雪岩先就放了一半心，顺口问道∶『城里有啥消息？』『不晓得，』江老大摇摇头，面容顿见愁苦，『城里城外象两个世界。』『那末城外呢？』『城外？王老爷，你是说长毛？』『是啊！长毛这方面有啥消息？』『也不大清楚。前几天说要回苏州了；有些长毛摆地摊卖抢来的东西，三文不值两文，好象急于脱货求现；这两天又不听见说起了。』胡雪岩心里明白，长毛的军粮亦有难乎为继之势∶现在是跟守军僵持着，如果城里有粮食接济，能再守一两个月，长毛可以不战自退。但从另一方面看，长毛既然缺粮，那末这十几船粮食摆在江面上，必启其觊觎之心，如果调集小船，不顾死命来扑，实在是件很危险的事。因此，这晚上他又急得睡不着，心心念念只望萧家骥能够混进城去，王有龄能够调集人马杀开一条血路，保住粮道；只要争到一天的工夫，就可以将沙船撑到岸边，卸粮进城。

“Thank you, thank you.” Jiang took the silver, then hesitated before speaking. “Mr Wang, there is something I think I had better tell you. As soon as the young gentleman landed, the Longhairs took him.” Capture itself was nothing to fear; what mattered was how he had been taken. Hu asked calmly, “Were they very rough with him?” “No, not particularly. He is a brave young gentleman. He did not try to run when he saw them, so they treated him rather politely.” Half relieved already, Hu asked casually, “Is there any news from inside the city?” “I do not know.” Jiang shook his head, his face suddenly full of distress. “Inside and outside are two different worlds.” “Then what about outside?” “Outside? You mean the Longhairs, Mr Wang?” “Yes. What news is there on their side?” “I do not know much. A few days ago they were saying they would return to Suzhou. Some of them were selling their plunder from roadside stalls for next to nothing, as though anxious to turn it into cash. But these last two days I have heard no more about leaving.” Hu understood. The Longhairs too were finding their provisions hard to maintain. For the moment they were locked in a stalemate with the defenders. If the city could be supplied and hold out for another month or two, the enemy might retreat without a fight. Yet there was another side to it: since the Longhairs were short of food, the dozen or more grain-laden boats lying on the river must tempt them greatly. If they massed small craft and attacked regardless of their lives, the danger would be severe. That night Hu was once more too anxious to sleep. His every thought was a hope that Xiao would get into the city and Wang would assemble enough men to fight a passage through and hold the supply route. A single day would suffice: they could bring the junks alongside the bank, unload the grain and carry it into the city.

萧家骥果然混进城了。被捕之时，长毛就对他『另眼相看』；因为凡是被掳的百姓，没有不吓得瑟瑟发抖的。只有这个『新家伙』——长毛对刚被掳的百姓的通称——与众不同。因此别的『新家伙』照例双手被缚，这个的辫子跟那个的辫子结在一起，防他们『逃长毛』；对萧家骥却如江老大所说的，相当『客气』，押着到了『公馆』，问话的语气亦颇有礼貌。『看你样子，是外路来的。你叫什么名字，干什么行当？』一个黄衣黄帽，说湖北话的小头目问。『我姓萧，从上海来。』萧家骥从容答道∶『说实话，我想来做笔大生意。这笔生意做成功，杭州城就再也守不住了。』那小头目听他口气不凡，顿时肃然起敬，改口称他∶『萧先生，请问是什么大生意？怎么说这笔生意成功，他们杭州就会守不住？』

Xiao did indeed find his way inside. From the moment of his capture, the Longhairs had regarded him differently. Every civilian they seized ordinarily trembled with terror. Only this “new fellow”—their usual term for a newly captured civilian—was different. The others had their hands bound, and one man’s queue was tied to the next man’s to prevent them escaping. Xiao, however, was treated with considerable courtesy, just as Jiang had reported. They escorted him to the officer’s “residence”, where even the questioning was polite. “You look as though you come from elsewhere. What is your name, and what is your business?” asked a minor commander in a yellow robe and cap, speaking with a Hubei accent. “My name is Xiao. I have come from Shanghai,” Xiao answered calmly. “To tell you the truth, I hope to conclude a large piece of business. If it succeeds, Hangzhou will be unable to hold out any longer.” The breadth of his claim instantly impressed the commander, who changed his form of address. “Mr Xiao, what great business is this? Why should Hangzhou become unable to hold out once it succeeds?”

『这话我实在不能跟你说。』萧家骥道∶『请你送我去见忠王。』『忠王不知道驻驾在哪里？我也见不着他，只好拿你往上送。不过，萧先生，』那小头目踌躇着说∶『你不会害我吧？』『怎么害我？』『如果你说的话不实在，岂不都是我的罪过？』萧家骥笑了。见此人老实可欺，有意装出轻视的神色，『你的话真教人好笑？你怎么知道我的话不实在；我在上海住得好好的，路远迢迢跑到这里来干什么？跟你实说吧，我是英国人委托我来的，要见忠王，有大事奉陈。』他突然问道∶『请问尊姓大名？』『我叫陆德义。』『见了忠王，我替你说好话，包有重赏。』李秀成治军与其他洪杨将领，本自不同，一向注重招贤纳士；所以陆德义听了他这话，越发不敢怠慢，『萧先生，』他很诚恳地答道∶『多蒙你好意，我先谢谢。不过，今天已经晚了，你先住一夜；我一面派人禀报上头，上头派人来接。你看好不好？』

“I really cannot discuss it with you,” Xiao said. “Please send me to see the Loyal King.” “I do not know where His Highness is stationed, and I cannot gain an audience with him myself. I can only refer you to my superiors. But, Mr Xiao—” The man hesitated. “You will not get me into trouble, will you?” “How could I?” “If what you say is untrue, will not all the blame fall on me?” Xiao laughed. Seeing that the man was simple and easily deceived, he deliberately assumed a look of contempt. “What an amusing thing to say! Why should you suppose I am not telling the truth? I was living very comfortably in Shanghai. Why else would I travel all this way? Let me be frank: the British have commissioned me to come here. I must see the Loyal King and lay an important matter before him.” Suddenly he asked, “May I know your name?” “Lu Deyi.” “When I see the Loyal King, I shall put in a good word for you. You are certain to receive a handsome reward.” Li Xiucheng managed his army differently from the other Taiping commanders. He had always set great store by attracting able men. At Xiao’s words, Lu was more anxious than ever to show him proper attention. “Mr Xiao,” he answered sincerely, “thank you for your kindness. But it is late today. Stay the night while I send a report to my superiors. They will send someone to fetch you. Would that suit you?”

这也不便操之过急，萧家骥心想，先住一夜，趁这陆德义好相与，打听打听情形，行事岂不是更有把握？便即欣慰答道∶『那也好。我就住一夜。』于是陆德义奉之为上宾，设酒款待。萧家骥跑惯长江码头，而陆德义是汉阳人；因而以湖北近况为话题，谈得相当投机。最后谈到杭州城内的情状，那陆德义倒真不失为忠厚人，愀然不乐，『真正是劫数！』

It would not do to press too hard. Xiao thought that a night’s stay would allow him to question this obliging man and learn more about the situation, giving him a firmer basis for action. He therefore replied with apparent satisfaction, “Very well. I shall stay the night.” Lu treated him as an honoured guest and entertained him with wine. Xiao knew the Yangtze ports well, and Lu came from Hanyang. Recent events in Hubei supplied a topic, and they soon fell into congenial conversation. Eventually they came to conditions inside Hangzhou. Lu showed himself a man of genuine kindness. His face fell. “Truly a calamity!”

他叹口气说∶『一想起来，教人连饭都吃不下。但愿早早破城，杭州的百姓，还有生路；再这样围困着，只怕杭州的百姓都要死光了。』『是啊！』萧家骥趁机说道，『我来做这笔大生意，当然是帮你们，实在也是为杭州百姓好。不过，我也不懂，忠王破苏州，大仁大义，百姓无不感戴。既然如此，何不放杭州百姓一条生路。』『现在是骑虎难下了。』陆德义答道∶『听说忠王射箭进城，箭上有封招降的书信，说得极其恳切；无奈城里没有回音。』『喔！』萧家骥问道∶『招降的书信怎么说？』『说是不分军民满汉，愿投降的投降，不愿投降的遣散。忠王已经具本奏报「天京」，请天王准赦满军回北，从这里到「天京」往返要二十几日，「御批」还没有因来。一等「御批」发回，就要派人跟瑞昌议和。那时说不定又是一番场面了。』陆德义说∶『我到过好多地方，看起来，杭州的满兵顶厉害。』这使得萧家骥又想起胡雪岩的话，杭州只要有存粮，一年半载都守得住，因而也越发感到自己的责任重大，所以这一夜睡在陆德义的『公馆』里，一遍一遍设想各种情况，盘算着如何能够取信于李秀成，脱出监视；如何遇到官军以后，能够使得他们相信他不是奸细，带他进城去见王有龄？这样辗转反侧，直到听打四更，方始朦胧睡去；也不知睡了多少时候，突然惊醒，只听得人声嘈杂，脚步匆遽，仿佛出现了极大的变故。萧家骥一惊之下，睡意全消，倏然坐起，凝神静听；听出一句话∶『妖风发了，妖风发了！』这句话似乎在哪里听过，萧家骥咬紧了牙，苦苦思索，终于想到了，是沙船上无事，听胡雪岩谈过，长毛称清军为『妖』，『妖风发了』就是清军打过来了。

He sighed. “The thought of it spoils one’s appetite. I only hope the city falls soon, so that its people may have a chance to live. If this siege goes on, I fear they will all perish.” “Yes,” Xiao said, seizing his opportunity. “Naturally, the great business I have come to arrange will help your side, but it will really benefit Hangzhou’s people too. Yet there is something I do not understand. When the Loyal King took Suzhou, his humanity and generosity won everyone’s gratitude. Why, then, does he not give the people here a way to survive?” “It is hard to dismount once one has mounted a tiger,” Lu replied. “I hear the Loyal King had an arrow shot into the city with a letter urging surrender. It was most earnestly expressed, but no answer came.” “Oh? What did the letter say?” “That soldiers and civilians, Manchus and Han alike, might surrender if they wished, and those who did not wish to surrender would be allowed to leave. The Loyal King has already sent a memorial to the Heavenly Capital, asking the Heavenly King to pardon the Manchu troops and let them return north. The journey there and back takes more than twenty days, and the imperial rescript has not yet arrived. Once it comes, someone will be sent to negotiate peace with Ruichang. Things may look very different then. I have been to many places,” Lu added, “but the Manchu soldiers in Hangzhou seem to be the fiercest of all.” This recalled Hu’s words to Xiao: with food in store, Hangzhou could hold out for six months or a year. He felt the weight of his responsibility more keenly than ever. Lying that night in Lu’s “residence”, he imagined every possible turn of events again and again. How could he gain Li Xiucheng’s trust and free himself from surveillance? Once he encountered the imperial troops, how could he convince them that he was no spy and have them take him into the city to see Wang? He tossed and turned until he heard the fourth watch being called, and only then drifted into an uneasy sleep. He had no idea how long he had slept before he woke with a start. Voices clamoured and footsteps hurried outside, as though something momentous had happened. All sleep vanished. He sat bolt upright and listened intently, catching a cry: “The demon wind is up! The demon wind is up!” He seemed to have heard the expression somewhere. Clenching his teeth, he searched his memory until at last he remembered: in an idle moment aboard the junk, Hu had told them that the Longhairs called the Qing troops “demons”. “The demon wind is up” meant that imperial troops were attacking.

一想到此，又惊又喜，急忙起床，扎束停当；却还不敢造次，推开一条门缝，往外张望，只见长毛蜂拥而出，手中的武器，种类不一，有红缨枪、有白蜡杆、有大砍刀、也有洋枪——枪声已经起了；杂着呼啸之声，忽远忽近，忽东忽西，随着风势大小在变化，似乎清军颇不少。

Alarmed and delighted at once, Xiao hurried out of bed and dressed himself securely. Still he dared not act rashly. Opening the door a crack, he peered out. Longhairs were pouring outside with weapons of every kind—red-tasselled spears, ash-wood staffs, great chopping swords and foreign firearms. Gunfire had begun already, mingled with shouts that seemed now near, now far, now east, now west as the wind rose and fell. The attacking imperial force appeared considerable.

怎么样？萧家骥在心中自问；要脱身，此时是大好机会，但外面的情况不清楚，糊里糊涂投入枪林弹雨中，死了都只怕没人知道，岂不冤枉？然而不走呢？别的不说，起码要见李秀成，就不是一下子办得到的；耽误了工夫不说，也许陆德义就死在这一仗中，再没有这样一个讲理的人可以打交道，后果更不堪设想。就在这样左右为难之际，只见院子外面又闪过一群人，脚步轻，语声也轻，但很急促，『快，快！』有人催促，『快「逃长毛」，逃到哪里算哪里？』『逃长毛』是句很流行的话，萧家骥听胡雪岩也常将这三个字挂在口头，意思是从长毛那里逃走；而『逃到哪里算哪里』，更是一大启示。『逃！』他对自己说，『不逃，难道真的要跟李秀成做军火生意？』

What should he do? Xiao Jiaji asked himself. If he meant to escape, this was an excellent opportunity. But he knew nothing of conditions outside. To blunder into a hail of bullets and die without anyone even knowing what had happened—what a senseless end that would be! Yet if he stayed, there was at least one obvious difficulty: he could hardly expect to meet Li Xiucheng at once. Apart from the time he would lose, Lu Deyi might be killed in this very battle, leaving him without such a reasonable man to deal with. The consequences did not bear thinking about. While he wavered, another group hurried past outside the courtyard. Their footsteps and voices were light, but urgent. “Quick, quick!” someone urged. “Get away from the Longhairs! It does not matter where we end up!” “Getting away from the Longhairs” was a common expression; Xiao had often heard Hu use it. It meant escaping from their hands. But “it does not matter where we end up” was a revelation. “Escape!” he told himself. “If I do not, am I really going to sell arms to Li Xiucheng?”

打字主意，更不怠慢；不过虽快不急，看清楚无人，一溜烟出了夹弄，豁然开朗，同时闻到饭香，抬头一看，是个厨房。厨房很大，但似乎没有人。萧家骥仔细察看着，一步一步走过院落，直到灶前，才发现有个人生在灶下烤火；人极瘦，眼睛大，骤见之下，形容格外可怖，吓得他倒退了两步。那人却似一个傻子，一双虽大而失神的眼，瞅着萧家骥，什么表情都没有。『你是什么人？』他问。『你不要来问我！』那人用微弱的声音答道∶『我不逃！逃来逃去逃不出他们的手；听天由命了。』听得这话，萧家骥的心凉了一半，怔怔地望着他，半晌无语。

His mind made up, he wasted no time, though he moved quickly rather than rashly. Making sure no one was about, he slipped down the narrow passage and emerged into an open space. The smell of cooking reached him. He looked up: a kitchen. It was large and apparently deserted. He examined it carefully, crossing the courtyard a step at a time. Only when he reached the stove did he discover a man sitting beside its base, warming himself. The man was terribly thin, with enormous eyes; coming upon him so suddenly, Xiao found his appearance frightening and recoiled two paces. The man merely stared, as if half-witted, his large, lifeless eyes showing no expression. “Who are you?” Xiao asked. “Do not bother asking me,” the man replied feebly. “I am not running away. Run where you will, you never get out of their hands. I shall leave it to fate.” Half of Xiao’s courage ebbed away. He stared at the man, unable to speak for some time.

『看你这样子，不是本地人；哪里逃来的？』看他相貌和善、而且说话有气无力，生趣索然似的，萧家骥便消除一恐怕戒备之心，老实答道∶『我从上海来。』『上海不是有夷场吗？大家逃难都要逃到那里去，你怎么反投到这里来？』那人用听起来空落落的绝望的声音说∶『天堂有路你不走，地狱无门闯进来！何苦？』『我也是无法，』萧家骥借机试探，却又不便说真话，『我有个生死至交，陷在杭州，我想进城去看他。』『你发疯了！』那人说道，『杭州城里人吃人，你那朋友，只怕早饿死了；你到哪里去看他？就算看到了，你又不能救他；自己陷在里头，活活饿死。这打的是什么算盘？真正气数。』话中责备，正显得本心是好的，萧家骥决定跟他说实话，先问一句∶『你老人家贵姓？』

“By the look of you, you are not from here. Where have you escaped from?” The man had a kindly face. His voice was weak, as though life held no interest for him, and Xiao’s fear and suspicion subsided. “I have come from Shanghai,” he answered truthfully. “Is there not a foreign settlement in Shanghai? Everyone fleeing the troubles wants to get there. Why have you come into this place instead?” His voice sounded hollow with despair. “Heaven’s road lay open, and you would not take it; hell had no gate, yet you forced your way in. Why bring such trouble on yourself?” “I had no choice.” Xiao used the opportunity to sound him out, though he dared not yet tell the truth. “I have a friend in Hangzhou, a man bound to me for life and death. I wanted to go into the city to see him.” “You are mad! People are eating each other inside Hangzhou. Your friend is probably dead of starvation already. Where would you go to see him? And even if you found him, you could not save him. You would be trapped yourself and starve to death. What sort of reckoning is that? Truly, it must be fate.” His reproaches revealed a good heart. Xiao decided to tell him the truth, first asking, “May I know your name, sir?”

『人家都叫我老何。』『老何，我姓萧，跟你老人家老实说吧，我是来救杭州百姓的——也不是我，是你们杭州城里鼎鼎大名的一位善人做好事；带了大批粮食，由上海赶来。教我到城里见王抚台送信。』萧家骥略停一下，摆出一切都豁出去的神态说∶『老何，我把我心里的话都告诉你，你如果是长毛一伙，算我命该如此，今年今月今日今时，要死在这里。如果不是，请你指点我条路子。』老何听他说完，沉思不语，好久，才抬起头来；萧家骥发觉他的眼神不同了，不再是那黯然无光，近乎垂死的人的神色，是闪耀着坚毅的光芒，仿佛一身的力量都集中在那方寸眸子中似的。

“Everyone calls me Old He.” “Old He, my name is Xiao. I shall be honest with you. I have come to save the people of Hangzhou—or rather, it is not I, but a philanthropist of great renown in your city who is doing this good deed. He has brought a large quantity of grain from Shanghai and sent me to see Governor Wang with a message.” Xiao paused briefly, then assumed the manner of a man staking everything on a single throw. “I have told you what is in my heart. If you belong to the Longhairs, then it is my fate to die here, in this year, this month, this day, and this hour. If you do not, please show me a way through.” Old He listened and sat in thought without speaking. After a long time he raised his head. Xiao saw that his eyes had changed. They no longer had the dull, almost dying look of before. They shone with determination, as though all the strength in his body had gathered within them.

他将手一伸∶『信呢？』萧家骥愕然∶『什么信？』『你不是说，那位大善人托你送信给王抚台吗？』『是的。是口信。』萧家骥说，『白纸写黑字，万一落在长毛手里，岂不糟糕？』『口信？』老何踌躇着，『口信倒不大好带。』『怎么？老何，』萧家骥了解了他的意思∶『你是预备代我去送信？』『是啊？我去比你去总多几分把握。不过，凭我这副样子，说要带口信给王抚台，没有人肯相信的。』『那这样，』萧家骥一揖到地，『请老何你带我进城。』『不容易。我一个人还好混；象你这样子，混不进去。』『那末，要怎样才混得进去？』

He held out his hand. “Where is the letter?” Xiao was taken aback. “What letter?” “Did you not say that this great benefactor had sent you with a message for Governor Wang?” “Yes, but it is a spoken message. If there were black words on white paper and they fell into the Longhairs’ hands, would that not be disastrous?” “A spoken message?” Old He hesitated. “That would be rather difficult to carry.” “What do you mean, Old He?” Xiao understood him. “Were you intending to take it for me?” “Yes. I should have a better chance than you. But looking as I do, no one would believe me if I said I had an oral message for the governor.” “Then let me ask you”—Xiao bowed to the ground—“to take me into the city.” “It will not be easy. I might slip through alone, but someone who looks like you could never get in.” “Then what must I do?”

『第一、你这副脸色，又红又白，就象天天吃大鱼大肉的样子，混进城里，就是麻烦。如果，你真想进城，要好好受点委屈。『』不要紧！什么委屈，我都受。『『那好！』老何点点头，『反正我也半截入土的了，能做这么一件事，也值！先看看外头。』于是静心细看，人声依旧相当嘈杂，但枪声却稀了。『官军打败了。』老何很有把握地说，『这时走，正好。』

“First of all, your face is pink and white, as if you ate fish and meat every day. If you got inside looking like that, there would be trouble. If you really mean to enter the city, you must put up with some unpleasantness.” “That does not matter. I shall put up with anything.” “Very well.” Old He nodded. “I have one foot in the grave already. If I can do something like this first, it will have been worthwhile. Let us see what is happening outside.” They observed quietly. The voices were still noisy, but the gunfire had slackened. “The government troops have been beaten,” Old He said confidently. “This is the right time to leave.”

萧家骥觉得这是件不可思议的事，听一听声音，就能判断胜负，未免过于神奇。眼前是重要关头，一步走错不得，所以忍不住问了一句∶『老何，你怎么知道？』『我早就知道了。』老何答道∶『官军饿得两眼发黑，哪里还打得动仗？无非冲一阵而已。』这就是枪声所以稀下来的缘故了。萧家骥想想也有道理，便放心大胆地跟着老何从边门出了长毛的公馆。果然，长毛已经收队，满街如蚁，且行且谈且笑，一副打了胜仗的样子。幸好长毛走的是大街，而老何路径甚熟，尽从小巷子里穿来穿去，最后到了一处破败的财神庙，里面是七八个乞儿，正围在一起掷骰子赌钱。

Xiao found it extraordinary that the man could judge the outcome of a battle merely by listening. This was a crucial moment; a single wrong step might be fatal. He could not help asking, “How do you know, Old He?” “I knew it from the beginning. The government troops are so hungry that their sight is going black. How can they fight? All they can do is make one charge.” That explained the dwindling gunfire. On reflection, Xiao found it reasonable, and followed Old He out through a side gate of the Longhairs’ headquarters with renewed confidence. Sure enough, the rebels were returning to their quarters. They filled the main streets like ants, walking, talking, and laughing with all the air of victors. Fortunately, Old He knew the neighborhood intimately. Keeping clear of the main streets, he led Xiao through one narrow lane after another until they reached a dilapidated temple to the God of Wealth. Inside, seven or eight beggars were huddled together, gambling with dice.

『老何，』其中有一个说，『你到没有死！』老何不理他，向一个衣衫略为整齐些的人说∶『阿毛，把你的破棉袄脱下来。』『干什么？』『借给这位朋友穿一穿。』『借了给他，我穿啥？』『他把他的衣服换给你。』这一说便有好些人争着要换，『我来，我来！』乱糟糟地喊着。

“So you are not dead yet, Old He!” one of them said. Old He ignored him and addressed a man whose clothes were slightly less ragged than the others’. “A’mao, take off that tattered padded jacket.” “What for?” “Lend it to this friend.” “And what am I to wear?” “He will give you his clothes in exchange.” At that, several men clamored to make the exchange themselves. “Me! Me!” they cried in confusion.

老何打定主意，只要跟阿毛换；他的一件破棉袄虽说略为整齐些，但厚厚一层垢腻，如屠夫的作裙，已经让萧家骥要作呕了。『没有办法。』老何说道∶「不如此就叫不成功。不但不成功，走出去还有危险。不要说你，我也要换。『听这一说，萧家骥无奈，只好咬紧牙关，换上那件棉袄，还有破鞋破袜。萧家骥只觉满身虫行蚁走般肉麻，自出娘胎，不曾吃过这样的苦头，只是已穿上身，就决没有脱下来的道理。再看老何也找人换了一身衣服，比自己的更破更脏，别人没来由也受这样一分罪，所为何来？这样想着，便觉得容易忍受了。

Old He had made up his mind to deal only with A’mao. Though the padded jacket was a little more presentable than the rest, it was coated in such a thick layer of grease and filth that it looked like a butcher’s apron. The sight alone made Xiao nauseous. “There is no other way,” Old He said. “Without this, we cannot succeed. Worse than that, we shall be in danger as soon as we go out. And it is not just you: I must change too.” Xiao had no choice. Gritting his teeth, he put on the jacket, along with torn shoes and socks. His whole body crawled as if insects and ants were moving over his skin. Never in his life had he endured anything like it. Yet now that the clothes were on, there could be no question of taking them off. Looking at Old He, he saw that the man too had exchanged clothes with someone and was wearing garments even dirtier and more ragged than his own. Why was another man, with no obligation to him, taking on this misery as well? Thinking of that made it easier to bear.

『阿毛！』老何又说∶『今天是啥口令？』『我不晓得。』『我晓得。』有人响亮地回答，『老何，你问它做啥？』『自然有用处。』老何回头问萧家骥∶『你有没有大洋钱，摸一块出来。』萧家骥如言照办；老何用那块银洋买得了一个口令。但是，『这是什么口令呢？』萧家骥问。

“A’mao,” Old He asked, “what is today’s password?” “I do not know.” “I know,” someone answered loudly. “What do you want it for, Old He?” “I have a use for it, naturally.” Old He turned to Xiao. “Have you any silver dollars? Take one out.” Xiao did as he was told, and Old He bought a password with the coin. “But what is this password for?” Xiao asked.

『进城的口令。』老何答道，『城虽闭了，城里还是弄些要饭的出来打探军情，一点用处都没有。』在萧家骥却太有用了；同时也恍然大悟，为何非受这样的罪不可？走不多远，遥遥发现一道木城；萧家骥知道离城门还有一半路程。他听胡雪岩谈过杭州十城被围以后，王有龄全力企图打开一条江路，但兵力众寡悬殊，有心无力。正好张玉良自富阳撤退；王有龄立即派人跟他联络，采取步步为营的办法，张玉良从江干往城里扎营；城里往江干扎营，扎住一座，坚守一座，不求速效而稳扎稳打，总有水到渠成，联成一气打开一线生路的时候。

“For entering the city,” Old He replied. “The gates may be closed, but they still send a few beggars out to gather intelligence. Not that it does any good.” To Xiao it was immensely useful. Now he also understood why he had had to submit to this ordeal. They had not gone far when a timber fort came into view in the distance. Xiao knew they were still only halfway to the city gate. Hu had told him how, after Hangzhou’s ten gates were surrounded, Wang Youling had strained every effort to open a route to the river. Vastly outnumbered, he had lacked the strength to do it. Just then Zhang Yuliang had withdrawn from Fuyang. Wang immediately sent men to contact him and proposed an advance by fortified stages: Zhang would build camps inward from the riverbank, while the defenders built outward from the city. Each position, once established, would be held firmly. They would seek no quick result, but proceed methodically until the two lines eventually joined and a route to survival opened.

由于王有龄的亲笔信，写得极其恳切，说『杭城存亡，视此一举，不可失机误事，』所以张玉良不敢怠慢，从江干外堤塘一面打、一面扎营，扎了十几座，遭到一条河，成了障碍，张玉良派人夺围进城，要求王有龄派兵夹击；同时将他扎营的位置，画成明明白白的图，一并送上。王有龄即时通知饶廷选调派大队进城；谁知饶廷选一夜耽误，泄潜心机密，李秀成连夜兴工，在半路上筑成一座木城，城上架炮。城外又筑土墙，墙上凿眼架枪，隔绝了张玉良与饶廷选的两支人马；而且张玉良因此中炮阵亡。这是胡雪岩离开杭州的情形，如今木城依旧，自然无法通过；老何带着萧着骥，避开长毛，远远绕过木城，终于见了城门。

Wang’s handwritten appeal had been exceptionally urgent: “The survival of Hangzhou depends upon this one undertaking. We must not lose the opportunity and ruin the attempt.” Zhang Yuliang had therefore dared not delay. Fighting as he advanced, he built more than a dozen camps from the outer embankment by the river, until another waterway barred his way. He sent men through the siege lines into the city, asking Wang to launch a coordinated attack and enclosing a clear map of his positions. Wang immediately instructed Rao Tingxuan to dispatch a large body of troops into the city. But Rao delayed for a night, and the secret leaked out. Li Xiucheng set his men to work overnight and erected a timber fort halfway along the route, with cannon mounted on it. Outside stood an earthen wall pierced with firing holes for muskets. This cut off Zhang’s forces from Rao’s, and Zhang himself was killed by cannon fire. That was the position when Hu left Hangzhou. The timber fort still stood and was plainly impassable. Old He led Xiao well around it, keeping clear of the Longhairs, until at last they saw a city gate.

『这是候潮门。』『我晓得。』萧家骥念道∶『「候潮」听得「清波」响，「涌金」「钱塘」定「太平」。』这两句诗中，嵌着杭州五个城门的名称，只有本地人才知道；所以老何听他一念，浮起异常亲切之感，枯干瘦皱，望之不似人形的脸上，第一次出现了笑容，『你倒懂！』他说，『哪里听来的？』萧家骥笑笑答道∶『杭州我虽第一次来，杭州的典故我倒晓得很多。』『你跟杭州有缘。』老何很欣慰地说，『一定顺利。』

“This is Houchao Gate.” “I know.” Xiao recited, “‘Awaiting the Tide’, one hears the ‘Clear Waves’ sound; ‘Surging Gold’ and ‘Qiantang’ make ‘Great Peace’ secure.” The couplet wove together the names of five of Hangzhou’s gates, a piece of lore known only to local people. Hearing it, Old He felt a sudden warmth toward him. For the first time, a smile appeared on the withered, shrunken, wrinkled face that scarcely seemed human. “So you know that! Where did you hear it?” Xiao smiled in return. “This may be my first visit to Hangzhou, but I know a good many of its stories.” “You have a bond with Hangzhou,” Old He said, much comforted. “Everything is sure to go well.”

说着话，已走近壕沟；沟内有些巡逻，沟外却有人伏地贴耳，不知在干什事？萧家骥不免诧异却步。『这些是什么人？』『是瞎子。』老何答道，『瞎子的耳朵特别灵；地下再埋着酒坛子，如有啥声音听得格外清楚。』『噢！我懂了。』萧家骥恍然大悟，『这就是所谓「瓮器」，是怕长毛挖地道，埋炸药。』『对了！快走吧，那面的兵在端枪了。』说着，老何双手高举急步而行；萧家骥如法而施，走到壕沟边才住脚。

As they spoke, they approached a ditch. Men were patrolling on its inner side; on the outer side, others lay with their ears pressed to the ground. Xiao did not know what they were doing and stopped in surprise. “Who are those men?” “They are blind,” Old He replied. “Blind men have particularly keen hearing. Wine jars are buried underground too, so they can hear any noise all the more clearly.” “Ah, I understand!” It dawned on Xiao. “These are the listening jars I have heard of. They are afraid the Longhairs will dig tunnels and plant explosives.” “Exactly. Come along—the soldier opposite is raising his gun.” Old He lifted both hands and hurried forward. Xiao copied him, stopping only when they reached the edge of the ditch.

『口令！』对面的兵喝问。『日月光明。』那个兵不作声了，走向一座轴驴，摇动把手，将一条矗立着的跳板放了下来，横搁在壕沟上，算是一道吊桥。

“Password!” the soldier challenged them from the other side. “The sun and moon shine bright.” Without another word, the soldier went over to a windlass and turned its handle. A plank that had been standing upright came down across the ditch to form a drawbridge.

萧家骥觉得这个士兵，虽然形容憔悴，有气无力，仿佛连话也懒得说似的，但依然忠于职守，也就很可敬了；由此便想∶官军的纪律，并不如传说中那样糟不可言。既然如此，何必自找麻烦，要混进城去。想到就说∶『老何！我看我说明来意，请这里驻守的军官，派弟兄送我进去，岂不省事？』老何沉吟了一下答道∶『守候潮门的曾副将，大家都说他不错的；不妨试一试。不过，』老何提出警告∶『秀才遇着兵，有理说不清，也是实话。到底怎么回事，你自己晓得；不要前言不搭后语，自讨苦吃。』『不会，不会！我的话，货真价实；那许多白米停在江心里，这是假得来的吗？』

Though the soldier looked haggard and exhausted, as if even speaking demanded too much effort, Xiao thought his continued devotion to duty worthy of respect. Perhaps the government troops’ discipline was not quite as dreadful as people said. If so, why make trouble for himself by trying to slip into the city? He spoke as soon as the thought occurred. “Old He, would it not be easier if I explained my purpose and asked the officer commanding here to send some men to escort me inside?” Old He considered. “Everyone says Deputy Commander Zeng, who guards Houchao Gate, is a good man. You might try. But remember”—he added a warning—“a scholar confronted with soldiers may find that reason gets him nowhere. You know the facts yourself. Do not contradict yourself and invite trouble.” “I shall not. Every word I say is true. All that white rice is waiting in the middle of the river. Could anyone invent that?”

听这一说，老何翻然改计，跟守卫的兵士略说经过，求见官长；于是由把总到千总，到守备，一层层带上去，终于候潮门见到了饶廷选的副将曾得胜。『胡道台到上海买米，我们是晓得的。』曾得胜得知缘由以后，这样问道∶『不过你既没有书信，又是外路口音，到底怎么回事，倒弄不明白；怎么领你去见王抚台？』萧家骥懂他的意思，叫声∶『曾老爷！请你搜我身子，我不是刺客；公然求见，当然也不是奸细。只为穿越敌阵，实在不能带什么书信，见了王抚台，我有话说，自然会让他相信我是胡道台派来的。如果王抚台不相信，请曾老爷杀我的头。我立一张军令状在你这里。』『立什么军令状？这是小说书上的话。我带你去就是。』曾得胜被萧家骥逗得笑了；不过他的笑容比哭还难看。『是！』萧家骥响亮地答应一声，立即提出一个要求，『请曾老爷给我一身弟兄的棉军服穿！』他急于脱卸那身又破又脏的衣服；但轻快不过片刻，一进了城，尸臭蒸熏，几乎让他昏倒。

Hearing this, Old He changed his plan. He gave the sentry a brief account and asked to see an officer. They were passed up the chain from a bazong to a qianzong, then to a garrison officer, until at last, at Houchao Gate, they met Zeng Desheng, a deputy commander under Rao Tingxuan. “We know Circuit Intendant Hu went to Shanghai to buy rice,” Zeng said after hearing the story. “But you have no letter, and you speak with an outsider’s accent. I cannot make out exactly who you are. How can I take you to Governor Wang?” Xiao understood his concern. “Sir, search me. I am no assassin, and a man openly asking for an audience is surely no spy. I could not risk carrying a letter through the enemy’s lines. Once I see Governor Wang, I can tell him something that will prove Hu sent me. If he does not believe me, you may have my head. I shall leave a written military pledge with you.” “A military pledge? That is something out of a novel. I shall take you.” Xiao had made Zeng laugh, though the smile looked more painful than weeping. “Thank you, sir!” Xiao answered briskly, then immediately made a request. “Please give me a padded uniform like your soldiers’ to wear.” He was desperate to shed those filthy rags. But his relief lasted only a moment. Once inside the city, the reek of corpses rose about him so powerfully that he nearly fainted.

王有龄已经绝望了！一清早，杰纯冲过一阵——就是萧家骥听到枪声的那时刻；十几船活命的白米等着去运，这样的彭励，还不能激出士兵的力量来，又还有什么人能开粮通道，求得一线生路？因此，他决定要写遗折了∶窃臣有龄前将杭城四面被围，江路阻绝，城中兵民受困各情形，托江苏抚臣薛焕，据情代奏，不识能否达到？现在十门围紧，贼众愈聚愈多，迭次督同饥军，并密约江干各营会合夹击，计大小昼夜数十战，竟不能开通一线饷道。城内粮食净尽，杀马饷军，继以猫鼠，食草根树皮，饿殍载道，日多一日，兵弁忍饥固守，无力操戈。

Wang Youling had lost hope. Jiechun had launched an attack early that morning—the very moment when Xiao had heard the gunfire. More than a dozen boats of life-saving white rice lay waiting to be unloaded. If even that incentive could not summon the soldiers’ strength, who could possibly open the supply route and win them a chance of survival? Wang therefore decided to write his final memorial to the throne: “Your servant Youling previously entrusted Governor Xue Huan of Jiangsu with the task of reporting on my behalf that Hangzhou was surrounded on all sides, the route to the river blocked, and the troops and people trapped within the city. I do not know whether that report has reached Your Majesty. All ten gates are now closely besieged, and the rebel host grows ever larger. Repeatedly we have led our starving troops into battle and secretly arranged coordinated attacks with the camps along the riverbank. In several dozen engagements, great and small, by day and night, we have failed to open even a single supply route. The city’s food is entirely exhausted. Horses have been slaughtered to feed the soldiers, followed by cats and rats; roots and tree bark are eaten. The roads are strewn with the starved dead, whose numbers increase daily. Officers and men endure hunger and hold their posts, but they no longer have the strength to wield their weapons.”

初虞粮尽内变，经臣等涕泣拊循，均效死相从，绝无二志，臣等奉职无状，致军民坐以待毙，久已痛不欲生。

“At first we feared that the exhaustion of supplies would bring mutiny within. But after we pleaded with the men in tears and sought to comfort them, all pledged to follow us to the death, without a disloyal thought. We have discharged our duties so poorly that troops and people must sit awaiting death. Long have we suffered such anguish that life is unbearable.”

写到这里，王有龄眼痛如割，不能不停下笔来。他这眼疾已经整一年了，先是『心血过亏，肝肠上逼，脾经受克，肺气不好』，转为『风火上炎』而又没有一刻能安心的时候，以致眼肿如疣，用手一按，血随泪下；见到的人，无不大骇。后来遇到一位眼科名医，刀圭与药石兼施，才有起色；但自围城以来，旧疾复发，日重一日，王有龄深以为恨，性命他倒是早已置之度外，就这双眼睛不得力，大是苦事。

At this point the pain in Wang’s eyes became so sharp that he had to lay down his brush. He had suffered from the ailment for a whole year. At first it had been described as “an excessive depletion of the heart’s blood, upward pressure from the liver and bowels, affliction of the spleen channel, and weakness of the lung’s qi.” It had then developed into “wind and fire flaming upward.” Without a moment’s peace of mind, his eyes had swollen into wartlike lumps; when pressed, they shed blood with the tears. Everyone who saw them was horrified. Later, a renowned eye physician had treated him with medicines and other remedies, and there had been some improvement. Since the siege began, however, the old trouble had returned, worsening day by day. Wang bitterly resented it. He had long ceased to care about his life, but the failure of his eyes was a cruel affliction.

如果是其他文报，可以口授给幕友子侄代笔，但这通遗折，王有龄不愿为人所见，所以强睁如针刺般疼痛的双眼，继续往下写∶第残喘尚存，总以多杀一贼，多持一日为念，泣思杭城经去年兵燹之后，户鲜盖藏，米粮一切，均由绍贩运；军饷以资该处接济为多。金、兰这法后，臣等早经筹计，须重防以固宁绍一线饷源，乃始则饬宁绍台道张景渠，继又迭饬运司庄焕文，记名道彭斯举，各带兵勇设防，均经王履廉议格不行；又复袒庇绅富，因之捐借俱穷，固执已见，诸事掣肘。臣等犹思设防堵御，查有廖守元与湖绅赵景贤，历守危城，一载有余，调署绍兴府，竭筹布置。乃违大绅不愿设防之意，诬以通贼痛殴，履谦从旁袖手；比及城陷而走，卒致廖宗元城亡与亡，从此宁绍各属，相继失陷，而杭城已为孤注，无可解救矣！

Other official papers could have been dictated to a secretary, a son, or a nephew. But Wang did not wish anyone to see this last memorial. Forcing open eyes that felt as though needles pierced them, he continued: “While a breath remains in us, our sole thought is to kill one more rebel and hold out one more day. We reflect with tears that, after last year’s devastation by war, few households in Hangzhou retained any reserves. Rice and other provisions were all brought from Shaoxing, and much of our military funding came from there as well. After the fall of Jin and Lan, we planned at once to defend the Ningbo–Shaoxing supply line in strength. First we ordered Zhang Jingqu, intendant of the Ningbo–Shaoxing–Taizhou circuit, and later repeatedly directed Salt Commissioner Zhuang Huanwen and the nominated circuit intendant Peng Siju to lead troops and militia to establish defenses. Wang Lüqian opposed and obstructed every measure. He also shielded the wealthy gentry, exhausting all possibilities of obtaining contributions or loans. Clinging obstinately to his own views, he thwarted us at every turn. Still intent upon making defensive preparations, we noted that Liao Zongyuan, together with Zhao Jingxian of the Huzhou gentry, had held a city in peril for more than a year. We transferred Liao to act as prefect of Shaoxing and had him devote every effort to organizing its defense. But he went against the wishes of the great local gentry, who did not want defenses established. They falsely accused him of colluding with the rebels and beat him savagely, while Lüqian stood by without intervening. When the city fell, Lüqian fled; Liao Zongyuan ultimately died with the city. Thereafter, the districts of Ningbo and Shaoxing fell one after another, leaving Hangzhou an isolated last stake, beyond all hope of rescue.”

写到这里，王有龄一口怨气不出，想到王履谦携带家眷辎重，由宁波出海到福建，远走高飞，逍遥自在，而杭州全城百姓，受此亘古所无的浩劫；自己与驻防将军瑞昌，纵能拼得一死报君主，却无补于大局，因而又奋笔写道∶王履谦贻误全局，臣死不瞑目。眼下饷绝援穷，危在旦夕，辜负圣恩，罪无可逭。惟求皇上简发重兵，迅图扫荡，则臣等虽死之日，犹生之年。现在折报不通，以后更难偷达，谨将杭城决裂情形，合词备兵折稿，密递上海江苏抚臣薛焕代缮具奏。仰圣瞻天，无任痛切悚惶之至。

Wang could not release the resentment that filled him. He thought of Wang Lüqian taking his family and baggage out to sea from Ningbo and sailing away to Fujian, free and at ease, while the entire population of Hangzhou endured a catastrophe without precedent. Even if he and the garrison general, Ruichang, died to repay their sovereign, their deaths could do nothing to remedy the situation. He pressed on furiously with his brush: “Wang Lüqian has ruined the whole undertaking. I shall die unable to close my eyes. Our funds are exhausted and all hope of relief is gone; destruction may come at any moment. We have betrayed Your Majesty’s gracious trust, and our guilt admits of no pardon. We beg only that Your Majesty select and dispatch a mighty army to sweep away the rebels without delay. Then the day of our death will be as though we lived again. At present our memorials cannot pass through, and it will be still harder to smuggle them out hereafter. We therefore set forth jointly in this draft memorial the circumstances of Hangzhou’s impending collapse, for secret delivery to Shanghai, where Governor Xue Huan of Jiangsu may have it transcribed and submitted to the throne on our behalf. Looking up toward Your Sacred Majesty as toward Heaven, we are overwhelmed by anguish and fearful awe.”

遗折尚未写完，家人已经闻声环集∶王有龄看着奶妈抱着的五岁小儿子，肤色黄黑，骨瘦如柴，越发心如刀割，一恸而绝。等救醒过来，只见他的大儿子橘云含着泪强展笑容，『爹！』他说，『胡大叔派人来了。』『喔，』这无论如何是个喜信，王有龄顿觉有了精神。『在哪里？』『在花厅上等着。』橘云说道∶『爹也不必出去了，就请他上房来见吧！』『也好。』王有龄说，『这时候还谈什么体制？再说，胡大叔派的人，就是自己人。请他进来好了。』他又问∶『来人姓什么？』『姓萧！年纪很轻，他说他是古应春的学生。』

Before Wang could finish the memorial, his family had heard his grief and gathered about him. He looked at his five-year-old son in the nurse’s arms, his skin sallow and dark, his body thin as a bundle of sticks. The sight cut him to the heart. He gave a cry of anguish and lost consciousness. When they revived him, his eldest son, Juyun, stood before him, forcing a smile through his tears. “Father, Uncle Hu has sent someone.” “Oh!” Whatever else might happen, this was good news. Wang felt his strength return. “Where is he?” “Waiting in the reception room. There is no need for you to go out, Father. Let him come to your room.” “Very well. What use is ceremony at a time like this? Besides, anyone Uncle Hu sends is one of our own. Ask him in. What is his name?” “Xiao. He is very young, and he says he is Gu Yingchun’s pupil.”

进上房，萧家骥以大礼拜见。王有龄力弱不能还礼，只叫∶『萧义士，萧义士，万不敢当。』萧家骥敬重他的孤苦忠节，依旧恭恭敬敬地一跪三叩首；只有由橘云在一旁还了礼，然后端张椅子，请他在王有龄床前坐下。『王大人！』萧家骥只叫得这一声，下面的话就说不出来了。这倒不是怯官，只为一路而来，所见所闻，是梦想不到的惊心惨目；特别是此一刻，王家上下，一个个半死不活，看他们有气无力地飘来飘去，真如鬼影幢幢，以致于连他自己都不知道此身究竟是在人间，还是在地狱？因而有些神志恍惚，一时竟想不起话从哪里开头？于是反主为客，王有龄先问起古应春∶『令师我也见过，我们还算是干亲。想来他近况很好？』『是，是。托福，托福！』

Entering the inner room, Xiao Jiaji offered the full ceremonial obeisance. Wang was too weak to return it and could only protest, “Gallant Mr Xiao! Gallant Mr Xiao! I cannot possibly accept such an honor.” Respecting his lonely suffering and steadfast loyalty, Xiao nevertheless knelt reverently and touched his forehead to the floor three times. Juyun returned the courtesy on his father’s behalf, then brought a chair and asked the visitor to sit beside the bed. “Governor Wang!” Xiao got no further. It was not awe of an official that silenced him. Everything he had seen and heard along the way had been more appalling than he could ever have imagined. Now, above all, every member of the Wang household seemed half dead. They drifted weakly about like wavering ghosts, until he could no longer tell whether he was still among the living or already in hell. His mind grew dazed, and for a moment he did not know where to begin. Wang therefore took the initiative and asked about Gu. “I have met your teacher. We are, in fact, connected by an adopted family relationship. I trust he has been doing well?” “Yes, yes. Thanks to your good fortune, sir!”

等话出口，萧家骥才发觉一开口就错；王有龄眼前是这般光景，还有何福可托？说这话，岂不近乎讥讽？这样想着，急图掩饰失言，便紧接着说∶『王大人大忠大义，知道杭州情形的人，没有一个不感动的。都拿王大人跟何制台相比——。』这又失言了！何桂清弃地而逃，拿他相比，自是对照；然仿佛责以与杭州共亡似的。萧家骥既悔且愧又自恨，所以语声突住；平日伶牙利齿的人，这时变得笨嘴拙舌，不敢开口了。谁知道这话倒是发生了意想不到的效用，王有龄不但不以为忤；脸上反而有了笑容，『上海五方杂处，议论最多。』他问∶『他们是怎么拿我跟何制军相比？』

Only after the words escaped did Xiao realize that he had begun badly. With Wang in such a state, what good fortune could anyone borrow from him? It almost sounded like mockery. Anxious to cover his mistake, he hurried on. “Your loyalty and righteousness are known to all, Governor Wang. No one who knows the situation in Hangzhou can fail to be moved. Everyone compares you with Governor-General He—” Another blunder! He Guiqing had abandoned his territory and fled; the comparison was naturally intended as a contrast, yet it seemed to demand that Wang perish with Hangzhou. Ashamed, remorseful, and angry with himself, Xiao broke off. Normally so fluent, he had become tongue-tied and hardly dared speak again. Yet his words produced an unexpected result. Far from being offended, Wang smiled. “Shanghai gathers people from every quarter, and everyone has an opinion. How do they compare me with Governor-General He?”

既然追问，不能不说，萧家骥定定神答道∶『都说王大人才是大大的忠臣。跟何制台一比，贤愚不肖，更加分明了。大家都在保佑王大人，逢凶化吉，遇难成祥了。』『唉！』王有龄长长地舒了口气，『有这番舆论，可见得公道自在人心。』他略停一下又问∶『雪岩总有信给我？』『怕路上遇到长毛，胡先生没有写信，只有口信。』萧家骥心想，胡雪岩所说，王有龄向他托孤的话，原是为了征信之用；现在王有龄既已相信自己的身分，这话就不必再提，免得惹他伤心，所以接下来便谈正题∶『采办的米，四天前就到了，停在江心；胡先生因为王大人曾交代，米船一到，自会派人跟他联络，所以不敢离开。一直等到昨天，并无消息；胡先生焦躁得食不甘味，夜不安枕，特为派我冒险上岸来送信，请王大人赶快派兵，打通粮道，搬运上岸。』话还未完，王有龄双泪直流，不断摇头，哽咽着说∶『昨天就得到消息，今天也派兵出城了。没有用！叫长毛困死了；困得一点气力都没有了。可望而不可即；有饭吃不到口，真教我死不瞑目。』说到这里，放声一恸；王家大小，亦无不抢天呼地，跟着痛哭。萧家骥心头一酸，眼泪汨汨而下，也夹在一起号啕。『流泪眼看流泪眼』，相互劝慰着收住了眼泪；萧家骥重拾中断话头，要讨个确实主意。

Since Wang pressed him, Xiao had to answer. He composed himself. “They all say that you are a truly loyal servant of the throne. Set beside Governor-General He, the difference between worth and unworthiness becomes all the clearer. Everyone prays that danger will turn to safety for you and misfortune to good.” “Ah!” Wang let out a long breath. “If that is what people say, then justice does indeed live in human hearts.” After a pause he asked, “Xueyan must have sent a letter?” “Mr Hu feared that I might encounter the Longhairs on the road, so he wrote nothing. He entrusted me with a spoken message.” Xiao remembered the private conversation Hu had described, in which Wang had asked him to care for his child after his death. Its purpose had been to establish Xiao’s credentials. Now that Wang already accepted his identity, he need not mention it and cause further grief. He went straight to the business. “The rice we bought arrived four days ago and is lying in the middle of the river. Because you told Mr Hu that you would send someone to contact him as soon as the grain boats arrived, he has not dared leave them. He waited until yesterday without news. Anxiety has robbed him of his appetite and his sleep. He therefore sent me ashore at great risk to bring this message: please dispatch troops quickly to open the supply route so that the rice can be landed.” Before he had finished, tears were streaming down Wang’s face. He shook his head repeatedly and sobbed, “We learned of it yesterday. We sent troops out this morning. It was no use! The Longhairs have penned us in until we have not a scrap of strength left. We can see it, but cannot reach it. Food is there, yet we cannot put it into our mouths. How can I close my eyes in death?” He broke into a great cry of anguish. Everyone in the household, old and young, wept with him, calling upon Heaven and earth. Xiao’s heart ached; tears poured down his cheeks, and he too sobbed aloud. Tearful eyes met tearful eyes as they comforted one another and at last brought their grief under control. Xiao then returned to the interrupted discussion. He needed a definite decision.

问到这话，又惹王有龄伤心；这是唯一的一条生路，关乎全城数十万生灵，明知可望而不可即，却又怎么能具此大决断，说一声∶『算了！你们走吧！』不走等机会又如何？能办得到这一点，自然最好；虽然画饼不能充饥，但是望梅或可止渴，有这许多米停泊在钱塘江心，或者能激励军心，发现奇迹——王有龄见过这样的奇迹，幼时见邻家失火，有个病足在床的人，居然能健步冲出火窟。人到绝处想求生时，那份潜力的发生，常常是不可思议的。然而这到底是可遇而不可求的事。这许多米摆在那里，长毛必起觊觎之心∶就算他们自己不绝粮，但为了陷敌于绝境，亦必千方百计动脑筋不可，或明攻、或暗袭，只要有一于此，胡雪岩十之八九会葬身在钱塘江中，追随伍子胥于地下，呜咽朝夕，含恨千古。转念到此，王有龄凄然下泪，摇头长叹∶『何苦「临死还拉个垫背的」？萧义士，你跟雪岩说∶心余力绌，坐以待毙。请他快走吧！』其实这倒是萧家骥想讨到的一句话；但听王有龄说出口来，他反答应不下了。

The question brought Wang fresh anguish. This was the only road to survival for hundreds of thousands of people. Even knowing that it lay beyond their reach, how could he take the terrible decision to say, “There is no hope. Go”? And what if the boats stayed and waited for a chance? If that were possible, it would naturally be best. A painted cake could not satisfy hunger, but the thought of plums might ease thirst. With so much rice lying in the Qiantang, the troops might find fresh courage and work a miracle. Wang had seen such a miracle in childhood: when a neighbor’s house caught fire, a man who had been bedridden with crippled legs somehow leaped up and ran out of the flames. The hidden strength summoned by a desperate will to live could be astonishing. Yet such things might occur; they could not be commanded. All that rice was sure to tempt the Longhairs. Even if they had enough food themselves, they would devise every possible means of depriving the besieged of their last hope. Whether by open assault or a secret raid, one attack might very well send Hu Xueyan to his death in the Qiantang. He would join Wu Zixu beneath its waters, his bitter grief sounding in the tides morning and evening for a thousand years. At the thought, Wang wept sorrowfully, shook his head, and sighed. “Why drag another man down with me when I die? Mr Xiao, tell Xueyan that our will outstrips our strength. We can only sit and await death. Ask him to leave at once.” This was, in fact, the answer Xiao had come hoping to obtain. But now that Wang had spoken it, he could not bring himself to assent.

『王大人！再筹划筹划看！』『不用筹划了。日日盼望，夜夜盘算；连想派个人跟雪岩联络，都不容易办得到。唉，『王有龄痛心欲绝地说∶』我什么都不错，只错了两件事，一件是当初有人劝我从城上筑一条斜坡，直到江边，派重兵把守，以保粮路，我怕深累民力，而且工程浩大，担心半途而废，枉抛民力，不曾采纳。如今想来，大错特错。『这实在是个好办法，有了这条路，当然也难免遭长毛的袭击；但九次失败，一次成功，城内亦可暂延残喘，决不会象现在这样被困得一点点生路都找不到。

“Governor Wang, think it over once more. There may be a way.” “There is nothing left to think over. I hope all day and plan all night. Even sending someone to contact Xueyan is almost beyond us. Ah!” Wang was in mortal anguish. “I did nothing wrong except in two matters. First, someone advised me at the beginning to build a ramp from the city wall down to the riverbank and guard it with a strong force to secure our supply route. I feared the burden on the people. The undertaking was so vast that I worried we might have to abandon it halfway, wasting all their labor. I did not accept the proposal. Now I see how terribly wrong I was.” It really had been an excellent plan. Such a route would naturally have been attacked by the Longhairs, but even if nine attempts failed and one succeeded, the city could have prolonged its existence a little. It could never have been trapped as completely as it was now, without the smallest opening toward life.

当然，这话要说出来，会更使王有龄伤心，所以只好反过来说，『那也不见得。』他说，『照我一路看到的情形，长毛太多，就有这条斜坡，也怕守不住。』『这不去说他了。第二件事最错！』王有龄黠然说道∶『被围之初，有人说该闭城，有人说要开城放百姓，聚讼纷纭，莫衷一是。我不该听了主张闭城的人的话，当初该十门大开，放百姓去逃生才是正办。』『王大人，你老也不必懊悔了。说不定当初城门一开，长毛趁机会一冲，杭州早就不保。』『原来顾虑的也就是这一点。总当解围是十天半个月的事，大家不妨守一守；开城放百姓，会动摇军心。哪知道，结果还是守不住。既有今日，何必当初？我对不起杭州的百姓啊！』说到这道，又是一场号啕大哭；萧家骥再次陪泪，而心里却已有了打算，哽咽着喊道∶『王大人，王大人，请你听我说一句。』

To say so, however, would only deepen Wang’s grief. Xiao therefore argued the opposite. “Not necessarily.
