I have already asked the Seventh Lady to plead with my wife when she arrives, to say a few kind words for us and persuade her to make a special exception.” “That is strange!” A’qiao sounded angry. “She urged me to go back instead—the exact opposite of what you asked. Why?”

胡雪岩深为失悔，自己太疏忽了！明知道七姑奶奶劝她的话是什么；不该再说实话，显得七姑奶奶为人谋而不忠。同时也被提醒了，真的，七三奶奶这样做是什么意思，倒费人猜疑。然而，不论如何，眼前却必须为七姑奶奶辩白，『也许她是先探探你的口气。』他问∶『她怎么说？』『她说∶』妇道人家总要有个归宿，还是正式姓了胡，进门磕了头的好。不然，就不如拿个决断出来！「『』何谓」拿个决断出来「？『『你去问她。』阿巧姐这懒得说的语气，可知所谓『决断』，是一种她绝不能同意的办法。胡雪岩将前后语言，合起来作一个推敲，懂了七姑奶奶的心思；只不懂她为何有那样的心思？『七姑奶奶做事，常有教人猜想不到的手段。你先不必气急，静下心来看一看再说。

Hu deeply regretted his carelessness. Knowing what the Seventh Lady had advised, he should not have told the truth and made her seem disloyal to the task entrusted to her. At the same time, A’qiao’s question alerted him to something. Yes—what did the Seventh Lady mean by acting so? It was puzzling. Whatever the reason, he must defend her now. “Perhaps she was only trying to discover your attitude. What did she say?” “She said, ‘A woman must have a proper settled place. Better to join the Hu family formally and kowtow upon entering the household. Otherwise you should make a firm decision.’” “What did she mean by a firm decision?” “Ask her.” The weariness of A’qiao’s tone showed that this “decision” meant a course she could not possibly accept. Putting her remarks together, Hu understood the Seventh Lady’s intention, but not why she had formed it. “She often takes unexpected measures. Do not be angry yet. Calm yourself and wait to see what happens.”

『要看到什么时候？』阿巧姐突然咆哮，声音又尖又高∶『你晓不晓得七姑奶奶怎么说你？说你滑头；说你没有常性，见一个爱一个！这种人的良心让狗吃掉了，劝我早早分手；不然将来有苦头吃。我看啊，她的话一点不错。哼！骗死人不偿命。』这样夹枪带棒一顿乱骂，拿胡雪岩搞得晕头转向，几乎不相信自己的耳朵。心里当然也很生气；气的不是阿巧姐，而是七姑奶奶，不但为人谋而不忠，简直是出卖朋友。彼此这样的交情，而竟出此阴险的鬼蜮伎俩！这口气实在教人咽不下。胡雪岩从来没有这样生气过；气得脸青唇白，刚要发作，突然警觉，七姑奶奶号称『女中丈夫』，胸中不是没有丘壑的人，更不是不懂朋友义气的人，她这样说法，当然有她的道理在内——这层道理一定极深；深得连自己都猜不透。这样一转念间，脸色立刻缓和了，先问一句∶『七姑奶奶还说点啥？』『说点啥？』阿巧姐岂仅余怒不息，竟是越想越恨，『不是你有口风给她，打算不要我了，她会说这样的话！死没良心的——。』苏州女人受骂『杀千刀』；而阿巧姐毕竟余情犹在，把这三个字硬咽了回去。胡雪岩不作辩白∶因为不知道七姑奶奶是何道理，怕一辩就会破坏了她的用意。然而不辩白又不行；只好含含混混地说∶『你何必听她的？』

“How long must I wait?” A’qiao suddenly cried, her voice high and shrill. “Do you know what she said about you? That you are slippery! That you have no constancy and fall in love with every woman you see! Dogs have eaten the conscience of a man like that. She urged me to part from you soon, or I should suffer for it later. Well, I think she was right in every word. Hmph! You could deceive a person to death and never pay for it.” The barrage, striking both directly and by insinuation, left Hu bewildered. He could scarcely believe his ears. Naturally he was angry too—not with A’qiao, but with the Seventh Lady. She had not merely failed to act loyally for him: she had betrayed a friend. With such friendship between them, how could she resort to so underhand a trick? It was more than he could swallow. He had never been so angry. His face turned livid and his lips pale. Just as he was about to erupt, a thought warned him. The Seventh Lady was called a hero among women. She was neither without judgement nor ignorant of loyalty between friends. There must be a reason for what she had said—a very deep reason, too deep even for him to fathom. At that thought his expression softened at once. “What else did she say?” he asked. “What else?” A’qiao’s anger was not merely lingering; it grew as she thought. “Unless you had given her some hint that you meant to abandon me, would she have said such things? You heartless—” Suzhou women were fond of the curse “may you be cut into a thousand pieces”, but some tenderness remained in A’qiao, and she swallowed the words. Hu offered no defence. Until he understood the Seventh Lady’s purpose, he feared that defending himself might spoil it. Yet he could not say nothing at all. He answered vaguely, “Why must you listen to her?”

『那末，我听谁？听你的？』阿巧姐索性逼迫∶『你说，你倒扎扎实实说一句我听。』何谓『扎扎实实说一句』？胡雪岩倒有些困惑了，『你说！』他问，『你要我怎么说一句？』『你看你！我就晓得你变心了。』阿巧姐踩着脚恨声说道∶『你难道不晓得怎么说？不过不肯说而已！好了，好了，我总算认识你了。』静夜娇叱，惊起了丫头娘姨；窗外人影幢幢，是想进来解劝而不敢的模样，胡雪岩自觉无趣，站起身来劝道∶『夜深了，睡吧！』说完，他悄悄举步，走向套间；那里也有张床，是偶尔歇午觉用的，此时正好用来逃避狮吼，一个人捻亮了灯，枯坐沉思。丫头姨娘看看无事，各自退去；阿巧姐赌气不理胡雪岩，一俱上床睡下。胡雪岩见此光景，也不敢去招惹她，将就睡了一夜。第二天起身，走出套间，阿巧且倒已经坐在梳妆台前了，不言不语；脸儿黄黄，益显得纤瘦；仔细看去，似有泪痕，只怕夜来将枕头都哭湿了。

“Then whom should I listen to? You?” A’qiao pressed him harder. “Speak! Give me one plain, firm assurance.” What assurance did she mean? He was genuinely puzzled. “Tell me what you want me to say.” “There! I knew your heart had changed.” She stamped her foot and spoke bitterly. “Do you really not know what to say? You simply refuse to say it. Enough, enough! At last I know you.” Her angry cries in the quiet night roused the maids and older servants. Shadows gathered outside the window; they seemed to want to enter and mediate but dared not. Hu felt thoroughly uncomfortable. He rose and urged, “It is late. Let us sleep.” Then he quietly made his way into the adjoining room, where there was another bed used occasionally for afternoon naps. It offered a convenient refuge from the lioness’s roar. He turned up a lamp and sat alone, lost in thought. Seeing no further disturbance, the servants withdrew. A’qiao, offended, ignored him and went to bed by herself. Hu did not dare provoke her again and made do with a night apart. The next morning, when he came out of the adjoining room, she was already sitting at the dressing table. Silent and pale, she looked thinner than ever. On closer inspection he thought he saw tear marks. Perhaps she had wept enough in the night to soak her pillow.

『何苦！』他说∶『自己糟蹋身子。』『我想过了。』阿巧姐木然地说∶『总归不是一个了局。你呢，我也弄不过你。算了，算了！』一面说，一面摆手，而且将头扭到一边，大有一切撒手之意。胡雪岩心里自不免难过，但却想不出什么适当的话去安慰她。『今天中午要请郁老大吃饭。』他说，意思是要早点出门。『你去好了。』阿巧姐说；声音中带着些冷漠的意味。胡雪岩有些踌躇，很想再说一两句什么安抚的话，但实在没有适当的意思可以表白，也就只好算了。到古家才十点钟，七姑奶奶已经起身；精神抖擞地在指挥男佣女仆，准备款客。大厅上的一堂花梨木机智椅，全部铺上了大红缎子平金绣花的椅披；花瓶中新换了花；八个擦得雪高的高脚银盘，摆好了干湿果子。这天的云气很好，阳光满院，又没有风，所以屏门窗子全部打开，格外显得开阔爽朗。

“Why do this to yourself?” he said. “You are ruining your health.” “I have thought it over,” she said dully. “This cannot come to a proper end. And I cannot match you. Enough, enough.” She waved her hand and turned her head aside, as though relinquishing everything. Naturally he felt distressed, but could think of nothing suitable to comfort her. “I am giving Chief Yu lunch today,” he said, meaning that he must go out early. “Go, then.” There was coldness in her voice. He hesitated, longing to say another word or two of reassurance. Yet he had no adequate assurance to give and could only abandon the attempt. It was barely ten when he reached Gu’s house. The Seventh Lady was already up and vigorously directing the servants in preparing to receive their guests. The rosewood chairs in the main hall all wore bright red satin covers embroidered in gold. Fresh flowers stood in the vases, and eight tall silver dishes, polished to a brilliant shine, held fresh and dried fruit. The weather was fine, sunlight filled the courtyard and there was no wind. All the doors in the screen and the windows stood open, making the house especially spacious and cheerful.

『小爷叔倒来得早！点心吃了没有』『七姑奶奶忽然发觉∶』小爷叔，你的气色很不好；是不是身子不舒服？『』不是！『胡雪岩说∶』昨晚上一夜没有睡好。『』为啥？『七姑奶奶又补了一句∶』就一夜不睡，也不致于弄成这个样子，总有道理吧？『『对。其中有个缘故。』胡雪岩问道∶『老古呢？』『到号子里去了。十一点半回来。』『客来还早。七姐有没有事？没有事我有几句话想跟你说。』七姑奶奶的眼睛眨了几下，很沉着地回答说∶『没有事。我们到应春书房里去谈。』到得书房，胡雪岩却又不开心口；捧着一碗茶，只是出神。七姑奶奶已经有点猜到他的心事；如果是那样的话，发作得未免太快，自己该说些什么，需要好好想一想。所以他不说话，她也乐得沉默。

“You are early, Little Uncle! Have you eaten?” Suddenly she noticed his appearance. “You look very unwell. Are you ill?” “No. I scarcely slept last night.” “Why?” She added, “Even one sleepless night should not leave you looking like this. There must be a reason.” “There is. Where is Old Gu?” “At the firm. He will be back at half past eleven.” “It is still early for the guests. Are you busy, Seventh Sister? If not, I should like a few words.” Her eyes blinked several times. Calmly she answered, “I am free. Let us talk in Yingchun’s study.” Once there, Hu could not begin. He held his tea and stared into space. She already had some idea of his trouble. If she was right, the effect had come rather quickly. She needed time to consider what to say. His silence therefore suited her, and she remained silent too.

终于开口了∶『七姐，昨天晚上，阿巧跟我大吵一架？』他问∶『你到底跟她说了些啥？』七姑奶奶不即回答，反问一句∶『她怎么跟你吵？』『她说∶我有口风给你，打算不要她了。七姐，这不是无影无踪的事？』七姑奶奶笑一笑，『还有呢？』她再问。『还有，』胡雪岩很吃力地说∶『说你骂我滑头，良心让狗吃掉了。又说我是见一个爱一个。』七姑奶奶又笑了，这一笑似乎有点不好意思，『小爷叔，』她带点逗弄的意味，『你气不气？』『先是有点气。后来转念想一想，不气了∶我想，你也不是没有丘壑的人，这样子说法，总有道理吧？』

At last he spoke. “Seventh Sister, A’qiao had a terrible quarrel with me last night. What exactly did you say to her?” Instead of answering, she asked, “How did she quarrel with you?” “She said I had hinted to you that I meant to abandon her. There is no truth in that, is there?” She smiled. “What else?” With difficulty he answered, “She said you called me slippery, said dogs had eaten my conscience, and said I fell in love with every woman I saw.” She smiled again, this time with a trace of embarrassment. “Little Uncle,” she asked almost teasingly, “were you angry?” “A little at first. Then I thought again and ceased to be angry. You are not a woman without judgement. There must be a reason for speaking that way.”

听到这话，七姑奶奶脸上顿时浮起欣慰而感激的神色，『小爷叔，就因为你晓得我的本心，我才敢那样子冒失——其实也不是冒失，事先我跟人商量过，也好好想过，觉得只有这样子做最好。不过，不能先跟你说，说了就做不成了。』她撇开这一段，又问阿巧姐∶『她怎么个说法？为啥跟你吵？是不是因为信了我的话？』『她是相信我给了你口风，打算不要她了；所以你才会跟她说这些话。』胡雪岩说，『换了我，也会这样子想，不然，我们这样的交情，你怎么会在她面前，骂得我一文不值？』『不错；完全不错。』七姑奶奶很在意地问∶『小爷叔，那末你呢，你有没有辩白？』『没有。』胡雪岩说，『看这光景，辩亦无用。』由于胡雪岩是这样无形中桴鼓相应的态度，便和七姑奶奶的决心无可改变了。她是接受了刘不才的劝告，以胡家的和睦着眼，来考虑阿巧姐跟胡雪岩之间的尴尬局面，认为只有快刀斩乱麻，才是上策。但话虽如此，到底不能一个操纵局面；同时也不能先向胡雪岩说破，那就只有见机行事，到什么地步说什么话了。

Relief and gratitude spread over her face. “Little Uncle, it was only because I knew you understood my intentions that I dared act so rashly. In fact, it was not rash. I discussed it with someone beforehand and thought it through carefully. I concluded that this was the best course. But I could not tell you first. Had I done so, it would not have worked.” Setting that aside, she asked again about A’qiao. “What did she say? Why did she quarrel with you? Because she believed me?” “She believes I hinted that I meant to leave her, and that you said those things for that reason. I should have thought the same in her place. With our friendship as it is, why else would you run me down so completely before her?” “Quite right. Entirely right.” She asked with great concern, “And you, Little Uncle—did you defend yourself?” “No. From the way things stood, there seemed little use.” His unwitting cooperation, like drum and drumstick answering one another, fixed her resolve beyond alteration. She had accepted Liu Bucai’s advice and considered the awkward situation between Hu and A’qiao from the standpoint of the whole family’s harmony. A clean cut through the tangle seemed the best solution. Yet she could not control matters single-handed, nor could she explain her intention to Hu in advance. She could only act as opportunity offered, saying as much as each stage allowed.

第一步实在是试探。如果阿巧姐不信她只信胡雪岩∶拿她批评胡雪岩用情不专，迹近薄幸的种种『背后之言』，付之一笑，听过丢开；这出戏就很难唱得下去了。或者，胡雪岩对阿巧姐迷恋已深，极力辩白，决无其事，取得阿巧姐的谅解；这出戏就更难唱得下去了。谁知阿巧姐疑心她的话，出于胡雪岩的授意；而胡雪岩居然是默认的模样，这个机会若是轻轻放过，岂不大负本心？于是，她正一正脸色，显得极郑重地相劝∶『小爷叔！阿巧姐你不能要了。旁观者清，我替你想过，如果你一定不肯撒手，受累无穷——。』照七姑奶奶的说法，胡雪岩对阿巧姐有『四不可要』∶第一、阿巧姐如果一定要在外面『立门户』，坏了胡太太的家法，会搞得夫妇反目。第二、即令阿巧姐肯『回去』，亦是很勉强的事，心中有了芥蒂，妻妾之间会失和。第三、阿巧姐既由何家下堂，而且当初是由胡雪岩撮合，如今就该避嫌疑；不然，保不定会有人说他当初不过『献美求荣』，这是个极丑的名声。第四、阿巧姐出身青楼，又在总督衙门见过大世面；这样的人，是不是能够跟着胡雪岩从良到底，实在大成疑问。『小爷叔！』最后七姑奶奶又恳切地劝说，『杭州一失守，王雪公一殉难；你的老根断掉了，靠山倒掉了。以后等于要重起炉灶，着实得下一番功夫，才能恢复从前那种场面。如果说，你是象张胖子那样肯守的，只要一家吃饱穿暖就心满意足，那我没有话说；想要创一番事业，小爷叔，你这个时候千万闹不得家务。不但闹不得家务，还要婶娘切切实实助你一臂之力才行。这当中的利害关系，你倒仔细想一想！』前面的『四不可要』，胡雪岩觉得也不过『想当然耳』的危言耸听；最后一句『这个时候千万闹不得家务』，却真的让他悚然心惊了。『七姐，你晓得的，我不是张胖子那种人，我不但要重起炉灶创一番事业；而且要大大创它一番事业。你提醒了我，这个时候心无二用，哪里有功夫来闹家务——。』『是啊！』七姑奶奶抢着说∶『你不想闹家务；家务会闹到你头上来！推不开，摔不掉，那才叫苦恼。『』我就是怕这个！看样子，非听你的不可了。『』这才是！谢天谢地，小爷叔，你总算想通了。『七姑奶奶高兴地说，』阿巧姐自然是好的；不过也不是天下独一无二就是她！将来有的是。『』将来！『胡雪岩顿一顿足∶』就看在将来上面。七姐，我们好好来谈一谈。『

Her first step had really been a test. If A’qiao had trusted Hu alone, laughed off the Seventh Lady’s remarks behind his back about his inconstancy and apparent heartlessness, and forgotten them, the play would have been difficult to continue. If Hu’s infatuation had been so deep that he strenuously denied every charge and won A’qiao’s understanding, it would have been harder still. Instead, A’qiao suspected that Hu had authorised the remarks, while Hu seemed to accept the accusation in silence. To let such a chance slip would betray the Seventh Lady’s own purpose. She therefore composed her face and spoke with great earnestness. “Little Uncle, you must give A’qiao up. An onlooker sees clearly. I have considered it for you: if you refuse to let go, there will be no end to the trouble.” She advanced four reasons. First, if A’qiao insisted on establishing a separate household, breaking Mrs Hu’s rule would set husband and wife against each other. Second, even if she agreed to join the family, she would do so unwillingly; the grievance in her heart would destroy harmony between wife and concubine. Third, since she had left He Guiqing, and Hu himself had arranged that union, he ought now to avoid suspicion. Otherwise people might say he had originally offered a beauty in exchange for advancement—a profoundly ugly reputation. Fourth, she had come from the pleasure quarters and had seen the great world in a governor-general’s residence. Whether such a woman could settle permanently into respectable life with Hu was very doubtful. “Little Uncle,” she urged finally, “when Hangzhou fell and Governor Wang died, your roots were cut and your support collapsed. You must begin again. It will take real effort to recover your former position. If you were like Fatty Zhang, content to hold what you have and keep the family fed and clothed, I should have nothing to say. But if you mean to build a career, this is the one time when you must not have domestic trouble. More than that, you need your wife’s solid support. Think carefully what you stand to gain or lose.” Hu thought the first four reasons little more than alarming suppositions. But the last warning—that this was no time for domestic trouble—truly startled him. “Seventh Sister, you know I am not like Fatty Zhang. I mean not merely to begin again and build a career, but to build a great one. You have reminded me: my mind cannot be in two places at once. Where have I the time for family quarrels?” “Exactly!” she broke in. “You may not want domestic trouble, but domestic trouble will come looking for you. You cannot push it away or throw it off. That is when you will suffer.” “That is just what I fear. It seems I must listen to you.” “At last! Thank Heaven, Little Uncle, you have come to see it!” she said joyfully. “A’qiao is a fine woman, of course, but she is not the only one in the world. There will be others in the future.” “The future!” Hu stamped his foot. “Let it be for the sake of the future. Seventh Sister, let us discuss this properly.”

要谈的是如何处置阿巧姐。提到这一层，七姑奶奶不免踌躇∶『说实话，』她说，『我还要动脑筋！』『七姐，』胡雪岩似乎很不放心，『我现在有句话，你一定要答应我。你动出啥脑筋来，要先跟我说明白。』这话使得七姑奶奶微觉不安，也微有反感∶『哟！哟！你这样子说法，倒象我会瞒着你，拿她推到火炕里去似的。』她很费劲地分辩，『我跟阿巧姐一向处得很好，现在为了你小爷叔，抹熬良心做事；你好象反倒埋怨我独断独行——。』『七姐，七姐！』胡雪岩不容她再往下说，兜头长揖，『我不能「狗咬吕洞宾，不识好人心」，无非我自己觉得对不起她，要想好好补报她一番而已。』『我还不是这样？你放心好了，我决不会动她的坏脑筋。』说到这里，七姑奶奶的眼睛突然发亮；同时绽开笑靥，望空出神。这是动到了极好的脑筋。胡雪岩不敢打搅她；但心里却急得很！渴望她揭开谜底。七姑奶奶却似有意报复∶『我想得差不多了。不过，小爷对不起，我现在不没有动手，到开始做的时候，一定跟你说明白；你也一定会赞成。』『七姐！』胡雪岩陪笑说道∶『你何妨先跟我说说？』『不行，起码要等我想妥当，才能告诉你。』七姑奶奶又说，『不是我故意卖关子，实在是还没有把握，不如暂且不说的好。』听她言词闪烁，竟不知她葫芦里卖的什么药？以她的性情，再问亦无用，胡雪岩只好叹口气算了。

They needed to decide what to do for A’qiao. Here the Seventh Lady hesitated. “To be honest, I must still think of a way.” Hu seemed uneasy. “There is one thing you must promise me. Whatever plan you devise, explain it to me first.” This made her a little uncomfortable and a little resentful. “Oh, listen to you! You make it sound as though I might secretly push her into some dreadful fate.” She defended herself with considerable feeling. “A’qiao and I have always got on well. Now, for your sake, I am acting against my conscience, and you seem to blame me for taking too much upon myself—” “Seventh Sister, Seventh Sister!” Hu stopped her with a deep bow. “I must not be the dog that bites Lü Dongbin and fails to recognise a benefactor. I merely feel I have wronged her and want to compensate her properly.” “Do I feel otherwise? Rest assured. I shall never devise anything to harm her.” Suddenly her eyes brightened. A smile broke over her face as she gazed into space. A very good idea had occurred to her. Hu dared not interrupt, though he was impatient to hear it. She, however, seemed determined to take a little revenge. “I have most of it worked out. But forgive me, Little Uncle: I have not begun yet. When I do, I shall explain it clearly, and you will certainly approve.” “Why not tell me first?” he asked with an ingratiating smile. “No. At least let me think it through before I tell you. I am not deliberately keeping you in suspense. I am simply not yet sure of it, so I had better say nothing for the moment.” Her evasions left him entirely uncertain what she was planning. Knowing her temperament, he realised further questions were useless and gave up with a sigh.

到了第二天，胡雪岩又去看七姑奶奶，恰好古应春也在，谈起家眷将到，另外要找房子，置家具，备办日用物品，本来可以关照阿巧姐动手的，此刻似乎不便麻烦她了。『不要紧！』七姑奶奶在这些事上最热心，也最有兴趣，慨然应承∶『都交给我好了。』在一旁静听的古应春，不免困惑，『为啥不能请阿巧姐帮忙？』他问。『其中自然有道理。』七姑奶奶抢着说∶『回头告诉你。』『又是什么花样？』古应春跟他妻子提忠告∶『你可不要替小爷叔乱出主意。现在这个辰光，顶要紧的就是安静二字。』『正是为了安静两个字。』七姑奶奶不愿丈夫打搅，催着他说∶『不是说，有人请你吃花酒；可以走了。』『吃花酒要等人来催请，哪有这么早，自己赶了去的？』古应春看出妻子的意思，觉得还是顺从为妙；所以又自己搭讪着说∶『也好！我先去看个朋友。』『慢点！』七姑奶奶说，『我想起来了，有次秦先生说起，他的亲戚有幢房子在三马路，或卖或典都可以，你不妨替小爷叔去问一问。』秦先生是她家号子里的帐房。古应春恪遵阃令，答应立刻去看秦先生细问；请胡雪岩第二天来听消息。『这样吧，』七姑奶奶说，『你索性请秦先生明天一早来一趟。』『大概又是请他写信。』古应春说，『如果今天晚上有空，我就叫他来。』

The next day Hu called again. Gu was there too. They discussed the approaching arrival of Hu’s family and the need to find a house, furnish it and obtain everyday necessities. Normally A’qiao could have been asked to see to these things, but now it seemed awkward to trouble her. “Never mind!” The Seventh Lady was always most enthusiastic about such matters and enjoyed them greatly. “Leave it all to me.” Listening beside them, Gu was puzzled. “Why can A’qiao not help?” “There is a reason,” his wife interrupted. “I shall tell you later.” “What new device is this?” He warned her, “Do not give Little Uncle ill-considered advice. At this moment, peace is what matters most.” “Peace is precisely the purpose.” She did not want her husband interfering and hurried him along. “Were you not invited to a courtesan banquet? You can go now.” “One waits for a reminder before going to such a banquet. Who hurries off on his own at this hour?” Gu saw what she meant and thought it best to comply. Finding his own way out, he added, “Still, I can visit a friend first.” “Wait!” she said. “I remember Mr Qin once mentioning that a relative of his had a house on Third Road, available either for sale or under a redeemable property pledge. Ask about it for Little Uncle.” Mr Qin was the accountant at their firm. Obedient to his wife’s command, Gu agreed to question him at once and asked Hu to return for news the following day. “Better still,” she said, “ask Mr Qin to come here early tomorrow.” “You probably want him to write another letter,” Gu observed. “If he is free tonight, I shall send him over then.”

于是七姑奶奶等丈夫一走，便又跟胡雪岩谈阿巧姐，『小爷叔，』他问∶『你的主意打定了？将来不会懊悔，背后埋怨我棒打鸳鸯两分离？』『哪有这样的事？七姐在现在还不明白我的脾气？』『我晓得，小爷叔是说到做到、做了不悔的脾气。不过，我还是问一声的好，既然小爷叔主意打定，明天我就要动手了。你只装不知道，看出什么异样，放在肚子里就是。』『我懂！』胡雪岩问∶『她如果要逼着我问，我怎么样？』『不会逼着你问的，一切照旧，毫无变动，她问什么？』『好的！那就是我们杭州人说的那句话∶』城隍山上看火烧！「我只等着看热闹了。『如果不是极深的交情，这句话就有讽刺意味的语病了。不过七姑奶奶还是提醒他，不可自以为已经置身事外；一旦火烧了起来，也许会惊心动魄，身不由主，那时一定要有定方，视如不见，切忌临时沉不住气，横身插入，那一来，她说∶『就会引火烧身；我也要受连累，总而言之一句话，不管阿巧姐说什么，你不要理她！』原来七姑奶奶由胡雪岩要买房子，想到一个主意，决定借这个机会刺激阿巧姐，能把她气走了，一了百了。但也可能会发生极大的风波，所以特意提出警告。

Once her husband had gone, the Seventh Lady returned to A’qiao’s affairs. “Little Uncle, is your mind made up? You will not regret it later and complain behind my back that I struck apart a pair of loving mandarin ducks?” “How could I? Do you still not know my temper?” “I know: you do what you say, and do not regret what you have done. Still, I had better ask. Since you are determined, I shall begin tomorrow. You must merely pretend to know nothing. Whatever unusual thing you notice, keep it to yourself.” “I understand. But what if she presses me with questions?” “She will not. Everything will continue as before, without a change. What would she ask?” “Very well. As we say in Hangzhou, I shall watch the fire from City God Hill. I shall wait and enjoy the spectacle.” Between less intimate friends, this might have sounded offensive or sarcastic. Even so, she warned him not to suppose that he had removed himself from the affair. Once the fire began, events might alarm him and draw him in despite himself. He must remain firm, act as though he saw nothing and above all avoid losing his composure and intervening. “Otherwise you will bring the fire upon yourself, and I shall suffer too. In a word, whatever A’qiao says, pay no attention.” Hu’s need to buy a house had given her an idea. She would use it to provoke A’qiao into leaving of her own accord and settle the matter once for all. But there might also be a great storm, hence her special warning.

购屋之事，相当顺利；秦先生所介绍的那幢房子，在三马路靠近有名的画锦里，虽是闹事，但屋宇宏深，关紧大门，就可以隔绝市嚣，等于闹中取静。胡雪岩深为中意，问价钱也不贵，只有鹰洋两千五百元；所以当天就成交了。七姑奶奶奶非常热心，『小爷叔，』她说，『你再拿一千块钱给我；一切都归我包办。这三天你去干你的事；到第四天你来看，是啥样子？』『这还有啥好说的？不过，七姐，太费你的心了！』胡雪岩知道她的脾气，这样说句客气话就行了。如果觉得她过于劳累，于心不安，要派人去为她分劳，反使得她不高兴，所以交了一千银洋给她，不闻不问。趁这三天功夫，在自己钱庄里盘一盘帐，问一问业务，倒是切切实实做了些事。第三天从集贤里阜康钱庄回家，只见阿巧姐头光面滑，点唇涂脂，是打扮过了；但身上却穿的是家常衣衫，不知是正要出门，还是从外面回来？『我刚回来。我去看七姑奶奶了。』阿巧姐说，『三马路的房子，弄得很漂亮啊！』

The purchase went smoothly. The house Mr Qin recommended stood on Third Road near the famous Huajin Lane. Though the neighbourhood was busy, the house was spacious and deep; closing its great door shut out the clamour and created quiet amid the bustle. Hu liked it very much. The price was modest too—only two thousand five hundred eagle silver dollars—so he completed the purchase that day. The Seventh Lady was full of zeal. “Little Uncle, give me another thousand dollars and leave everything to me. Attend to your own affairs for three days. On the fourth, come and see what I have made of it.” “What more could I ask? But it is so much trouble for you, Seventh Sister.” He knew her ways. That polite acknowledgement was enough. If he worried that she was overworking and sent someone to share the burden, he would only displease her. He gave her a thousand silver dollars and neither asked nor interfered. During the three days he examined the accounts at his own bank and enquired into its business, accomplishing some solid work. On the third day he came home from Fukang Bank in Jixian Lane and found A’qiao with her hair dressed, her face carefully powdered and her lips coloured. Yet she wore informal clothes. Was she about to go out or had she just returned? “I have only just come back. I went to see the Seventh Lady,” she said. “The house on Third Road has been made very handsome.”

语气很平静，但在胡雪岩听来，似有怨责他瞒着她的味道；因而讪讪地有些无从接口。『七姑奶奶问我∶房子好不好？我自然说好。她又问我想不想去住；你道我怎么回答她？我说∶我没有这份福气。』胡雪岩本来想答一句∶只怕是我没有这份福气。话到口边，忽又缩住；用漫不经意的口吻答道∶『住这种夷场上的所谓「弄堂房子」，算啥福气？将来杭州光复，在西湖上好好造一座庄子；住那种洞天福地，可真就要前世修一修了。』阿巧姐不作声，坐到梳妆台前去卸头面首饰；胡雪岩便由丫头伺候着，脱掉马褂，换上便鞋，坐在窗前喝茶。『我看，』阿巧姐突然说道∶『我修修来世吧！』『来世我们做夫妻。』胡雪岩脱口相答。阿巧姐颜色大变——在胡雪岩的意思，既然她今生不肯嫁胡家的偏房；那就只好期望来世一夫一妻，白头到老。而阿巧姐误会了！『我原在奇怪，七姑奶奶为啥说那些话？果不其然，你是变心了！有话你很可以自己说，何必转弯抹角去托人？』

Her tone was calm, but Hu thought he heard a reproach for keeping it from her. Embarrassed, he hardly knew how to answer. “She asked whether I liked the house. Naturally I said yes. Then she asked if I wanted to live there. Do you know what I told her? That I was not so fortunate.” Hu almost replied, “I fear I am the one without that good fortune,” but checked the words. Casually he said, “What good fortune is there in one of these so-called lane houses in the foreign settlement? When Hangzhou is recovered, I shall build a proper estate beside West Lake. To live in such a paradise would indeed require merit accumulated in a former life.” A’qiao said nothing. She went to the dressing table to remove her ornaments, while a maid helped Hu take off his riding jacket and change into slippers. He sat by the window with his tea. “I think I had better accumulate merit for the next life,” she said suddenly. “In the next life we shall be husband and wife,” he answered without thinking. Her face changed dramatically. He meant that, since she would not become his concubine in this life, he could only hope that in the next they might be one husband and one wife, growing old together. But she misunderstood. “I wondered why the Seventh Lady said those things. So your heart really has changed! If you have something to say, say it yourself. Why go round corners and get someone else to do it?”

胡雪岩知道自己失言了。然而也实在不能怪自己；那天原就问过七姑奶奶，如果阿巧姐逼着要问她的归宿？如何作答。七姑奶奶认为『一切照旧，毫无变动』，她不会问。照现在看，情形不同了！新居既已为她所见，『变动』便已开始，以后她不断会问；总不能每次一问，便象此刻一样，惹得她怨气冲天。看来还是要靠自己动脑筋应付！他这样对自己说；而且马上很用心地去体察她的态度。为什么她不自己想一想，她这样不肯与大妇同住，悖乎常情，强人所准；而偏偏一再要指责他变心？莫非她自己有下堂求去之意，只是说不出口，有意这样诿过，这样逼迫；想把决裂的责任，加在他头上？这是个看来近乎荒诞的想法。胡雪岩自问∶果真自己是小人之心？不见得！阿巧姐当初对何桂清亦曾倾心过，到后来不管怎么说，总是负心；而且是在何桂清倒霉的时候负心。这样看起来，将她看成一个『君子』，似乎也太天真了些。就这一念之间，他自己觉得心肠硬了；用不大带感情的、平静得近乎冷漠的声音说∶『我没有什么话好说。你愿意修修来世，我当然也只好希望来世再做夫妻。』『你的意思是，今生今世不要我了？』阿巧姐转过脸过来，逼视着他问。他将视线避了开去，『我没有说这话，不过——。』他没有再说下去。

Hu knew he had spoken wrongly. Yet he could hardly be blamed. He had asked the Seventh Lady what to say if A’qiao pressed him about her future. She had assured him that, with everything unchanged, no questions would arise. But things were different now. A’qiao had seen the new house; the change had begun. She would keep asking, and he could not have her fly into a rage every time, as she had now. It seemed he must rely on his own ingenuity after all. He began studying her attitude closely. Why did she not consider her own refusal to live with his principal wife? She was defying accepted practice and asking the impossible, yet repeatedly accused him of a change of heart. Could it be that she herself wished to leave but could not say so, and was pressing him and shifting blame in order to make him responsible for the break? The thought seemed almost absurd. Was he judging her with a petty mind? Not necessarily. She had once given her heart to He Guiqing too. Whatever might be said, in the end she had failed him—and when he was in misfortune. Was it not rather naive to regard her as a paragon? In that moment Hu felt his own heart harden. In a quiet voice, almost cold, he said, “I have nothing to say. If you wish to cultivate good fortune for another life, I can only hope that we shall be husband and wife then.” She turned and looked directly at him. “You mean you do not want me in this life?” He avoided her eyes. “I did not say that. Only—” He stopped.

『说啊！男子汉大丈夫，说话不要吞吞吐吐！』遇到他这种口吻语气，如果她是愿意委屈息事的，至多流泪，不会追问，既然追问，便有不惜破脸的打算。胡雪岩觉得了解她的态度就够了；此时犯不着跟她破脸——最好永不破脸，好来好散！于是他笑笑说道∶『我们都不是三岁两岁的小孩，这个样子教底下人笑话，何必呢？』『哼！』阿巧姐冷笑了一下，依然回过脸去，对镜卸妆。胡雪岩觉得无聊得很。这种感觉是以前所从不曾有过的；他在家的时候不多，所以一回到家，只要看见阿巧姐的影子，便觉得世界上只有这个家最舒服，非万不得已，不肯再出门。而此刻，却想到哪里去走走；哪怕就在街上逛逛也好。此念一动，不可抑制；站起身来说∶『我还要出去一趟。』说了这话，又觉歉然，因而问道∶『你想吃点啥？我替你带回来。』阿巧姐只摇摇头，似乎连话也懒得说。胡雪岩觉得背上一阵一阵发冷；拔步就走，就穿着那双便鞋，也不着马褂，径自下楼而去。

“Say it! A grown man should not mumble and hesitate.” If she had been willing to yield for the sake of peace, she might have wept at his tone, but would not have pursued the question. By pressing him, she showed that she was prepared for an open break. Hu felt it was enough to understand her position. There was no need to quarrel now—better never to quarrel, but to part amicably. He smiled. “Neither of us is a two- or three-year-old child. Why make ourselves ridiculous before the servants?” “Hmph!” She gave a cold laugh and turned back to the mirror to remove her make-up. Hu felt thoroughly weary of the place, a feeling he had never known before. He spent little time at home, but whenever he returned, the mere sight of A’qiao had made it seem the most comfortable place in the world. Only absolute necessity could draw him out again. Now he wanted to go somewhere—anywhere, even for a walk in the street. The impulse grew irresistible. Rising, he said, “I must go out again.” Then, feeling apologetic, he asked, “Is there anything you would like to eat? I shall bring it back.” She merely shook her head, as though even speech were too much trouble. A chill passed repeatedly down his back. He left at once, going straight downstairs in his slippers, without putting on his riding jacket.

走出大门，不免茫然∶『轿班』阿福赶来问道∶『老爷要到哪里去？我去叫人。』轿班一共四个人；因为胡雪岩回家时曾经说过，这夜不再出门，所以那三个住在阜康钱庄的都已走了，只剩下阿福在家。『不必！』胡雪岩摆一摆手，径自出弄堂而去。茫然闲步，意兴阑珊；心里要想些有趣的事，偏偏抛不开的是阿巧姐。美目盼兮，巧笑倩兮，那些影子都在眼前；其美如莺的吴枕软语亦清清楚楚地响在耳际。突然间，胡雪岩有着浓重的悔意；掉头就走，而且脚步极快。

Outside the door he felt at a loss. A’fu, one of his sedan-chair bearers, hurried after him. “Where are you going, sir? I shall fetch the men.” There were four bearers. Hu had said on returning that he would not go out again that evening, so the other three, who lodged at Fukang Bank, had already left. Only A’fu remained. “No need!” Hu waved a hand and went out of the lane alone. He wandered without purpose, dispirited. He tried to think of something pleasant, but could not put A’qiao out of his mind. Her lovely, expressive eyes and enchanting smile remained before him; her soft Wu voice, sweet as an oriole’s, sounded clearly in his ears. Suddenly he was seized by overwhelming regret. He turned and walked home at great speed.

到家只见石库墙门已经关上了，叩了几下铜环，来开门的仍是阿福；胡雪岩踏进门便上楼，一眼望去，心先凉了！『奶奶呢？』他指着漆黑的卧室；向从另一间屋里迎出来的丫头素香问说。『奶奶出去了。』『到哪里？』『没有说。』『什么时候走的？』『老爷一走，奶奶就说要出去。』素香答说∶『我问了一声，奶奶骂我∶少管闲事。』『那，怎么走的呢？』胡雪岩问∶『为什么没有要你跟去？』『奶奶不要我跟去；说是等一息就回来。我说∶要不要雇顶轿子？她说，她自己到弄堂口会雇的。』胡雪岩大为失望，而且疑虑重重，原来想跟阿巧姐来说∶『一切照旧，毫无变动』；不管胡太太怎么说，他决意维持这个外室。除非阿巧姐愿意另外择人而事，他是决不会变心的。这一番热念，此刻全都沉入深渊。而且觉得阿巧姐的行踪，深为可疑；素香是她贴身的丫头，出门总是伴随的，而竟撇下不带，可知所去的这个地方，是素香去不得的，或者说，是她连素香都要瞒住的。

The stone-framed outer door was already shut. He knocked several times with the bronze ring. A’fu opened it, and Hu went straight upstairs. One glance chilled his heart. “Where is your mistress?” Pointing to the dark bedroom, he questioned Suxiang, the maid who had come out of another room to meet him. “She has gone out.” “Where?” “She did not say.” “When did she leave?” “As soon as you had gone, she said she was going out. I asked her a question and she scolded me: ‘Mind your own business.’” “How did she go? Why did she not take you?” “She would not have me with her. She said she would be back shortly. I asked if I should hire a chair, and she said she could get one herself at the entrance to the lane.” Hu was deeply disappointed and full of misgivings. He had returned to tell her that everything would remain as before, without a change. Whatever his wife might say, he had resolved to maintain this separate household. Unless A’qiao herself wished to choose another man, he would never change his heart. Now all that warmth sank into an abyss. Her movements seemed deeply suspicious. Suxiang was her personal maid and always accompanied her outside. If she had left the girl behind, she must have gone somewhere the maid could not go—or somewhere she wished to conceal even from Suxiang.

意会到此，心中泛起难以言宣的酸苦抑郁；站在客堂中，久久无语。这使得素香有些害怕，怯怯地问道∶『老爷！是不是在家吃饭？我去关照厨房。』『我不饿！』胡雪岩问∶『阿祥呢？』『阿祥，出去了。』『出去了！到哪里？』『要——，』素香吞吞吐吐地说∶『要问阿福。』

With that thought, an inexpressible bitterness and despondency filled him. He stood in the sitting room without speaking for a long time. Suxiang grew frightened. “Sir,” she asked timidly, “will you dine at home? I shall tell the kitchen.” “I am not hungry. Where is A’xiang?” “A’xiang has gone out.” “Out? Where?” “You would have to—” Suxiang faltered. “You would have to ask A’fu.”

这神态亦颇为可疑，胡雪岩忍不住要发怒；但一转念间冷静了，『你叫阿福来！』他说。等把阿福喊来一回，才知究竟，阿祥是在附近的一家小杂货店『白相』。那家杂货店老夫妇两个，只有一个十七岁的女儿；胡雪岩也见过，生得象『无锡大阿福』，圆圆胖胖的一张脸，笑口常开。阿祥情有所钟，只等胡雪岩一出门，便到那家杂货店去盘桓；是他家不支薪工饭食的伙计兼跑街。『老爷要喊他，我去把他叫回来。』『不必！』胡雪岩听得这段『新闻』；心里舒服了些，索性丢下阿巧姐来管阿祥的闲事，『照这样说，蛮有意思了！那家的女儿，叫啥名字？』『跟——，』阿福很吃力地说∶『跟奶奶的小名一样。』原来也叫阿巧，『那倒真是巧了！』胡雪岩兴味盎然地笑着。

Her manner too seemed suspicious, and Hu nearly lost his temper. Then he steadied himself. “Fetch A’fu.” Once the bearer had been called and questioned, the truth emerged. A’xiang was “amusing himself” at a little grocery nearby. Its elderly owners had only one child, a daughter of seventeen. Hu had seen her: she resembled a cheerful Wuxi clay doll, with a plump, round face and a smile that never left it. A’xiang had set his heart on her. As soon as Hu went out, he would linger in the shop, acting as an unpaid assistant and errand boy, without even receiving his meals. “If you want him, sir, I shall fetch him.” “No need.” The news made Hu feel rather better. He might as well leave A’qiao aside and concern himself with A’xiang’s affairs. “That sounds promising. What is the girl’s name?” “The same as—” A’fu struggled to get the words out. “The same familiar name as our mistress.” So she too was called A’qiao. “A coincidence indeed!” Hu laughed with interest.

『我跟阿祥说，你叫人家的时候，不要直呼直令地叫人家的名字；那样子犯了奶奶的讳。做下人的不好这样子没规矩。』这是知书识礼的人才会有的见解，不想出现在两条烂泥腿的轿班身上，胡雪岩既惊异又高兴；但口中问的还是阿祥。『他不叫人家小名叫啥？』胡雪岩问∶『莫非叫姐姐、妹妹？那不是太麻肉了。』『是啊！那也太肉麻。阿祥告诉我说，他跟人家根本彼此都不叫名字，两个人都是「喂」呀「喂」的。在她父母面前提起来，阿祥是说「你们家大小姐」。』『这倒妙！』胡雪岩心想男女之间，彼此都用『喂』字称呼，辨声知人，就决不是泛泛的情分了；只不知道∶『她父母对阿祥怎么样？』『她家父母对阿祥蛮中意的。』『怎么叫蛮中意？』胡雪岩问∶『莫非当他「毛脚女婿」看待？』『也差不多有那么点意思。』『既然如此，你们应该出来管管闲事，吃他一杯喜酒啊！』『阿祥是老爷买来的，凡事要听老爷作主；我们怎么敢管这桩闲事，再说，这桩闲事也管不了。』『怎么呢？』『办喜事要——。』胡雪岩会意，点点头说∶『我知道了。你把阿祥替我去叫回来。』

“I told A’xiang not to call her directly by her name. It is our mistress’s name too, and a servant ought not to be so disrespectful.” This was the sort of observation one expected from a man versed in books and propriety. Hearing it from a muddy-legged chairbearer surprised and pleased Hu. But his questions remained about A’xiang. “What does he call her, then? Sister? Little Sister? That would be rather sickly.” “Yes, far too sickly. He told me they never use each other’s names. They simply say ‘Hey!’ to one another. When he speaks of her to her parents, he calls her ‘your young lady’.” “Excellent!” Hu thought that when a young man and woman needed only “Hey!” and recognised each other by their voices, theirs was no ordinary acquaintance. But how did her parents feel? “They are very pleased with him.” “How pleased? Do they regard him as a prospective son-in-law?” “Something like that.” “Then you ought to lend a hand and earn a cup of wedding wine.” “A’xiang was bought into your household, sir. Everything must be decided by you. We would not dare interfere. Besides, we could not arrange it.” “Why not?” “A wedding needs—” Hu understood and nodded. “I see. Fetch him for me.”

用不到一盏茶的功夫，阿祥被找了回来。脸上讪讪地，有些不大好意思；显然的，他在路上就已听阿福说过，知道是怎么一回事了。『你今年十几？』『十七。』『十七！』胡雪岩略有些踌躇似的，『是早了些。』他停了一下又问∶『「他们家大小姐」几岁？』这句对阿巧的称呼，是学着阿祥说的；自是玩笑，听来却有讥嘲之意，阿祥大窘，嗫嚅着说∶『比我大两月，我是九月里生的，她的生日是七月七。』『连人家的时辰八字都晓得了！』胡雪岩有此忍俊不禁；但为了维持尊严，不得不忍笑问道∶『那家人家姓啥？』『姓魏。』『魏老板对你怎么样？』胡雪岩说，『不是预备拿女儿给你？你不要难为情，跟我说实话。』『我跟老爷当然说实话。』阿祥答道∶『魏老板倒没有说什么；老板娘有口风透露了，她说∶他们老夫妇只有一个女儿，舍不得分开。要娶她女儿就要入赘。』『你怎么说呢？』『我装糊涂。』『为啥？』胡雪岩说∶『是不肯入赘到魏家？』『我肯也没有用。我改姓了主人家的姓，怎么再去姓魏？』『你倒也算是有良心的。』胡雪岩满意地点点头，『我自有道理。』这当然是好事可谐了！阿祥满心欢喜；但脸皮到底还薄，明知是个极好的机会，却不敢开口相求，就此『敲打转脚』拿好事弄定了它。

Before a cup of tea could have been drunk, A’xiang was back. His embarrassed expression showed that A’fu had explained the matter on the way. “How old are you?” “Seventeen.” “Seventeen!” Hu hesitated slightly. “Rather early.” After a pause he asked, “And how old is ‘their young lady’?” He was playfully repeating A’xiang’s own phrase, but it sounded like mockery to the boy, who grew painfully embarrassed. “Two months older than I am. I was born in the ninth month; her birthday is the seventh of the seventh month.” “You even know her birth particulars!” Hu could scarcely keep from laughing, but restrained himself to preserve his dignity. “What is the family’s surname?” “Wei.” “How does Mr Wei treat you? Is he thinking of giving you his daughter? Do not be shy. Tell me the truth.” “Of course I would tell you the truth, sir. Mr Wei has said nothing, but his wife has dropped a hint. She says they have only one daughter and cannot bear to part with her. Whoever marries her must join their household.” “What did you say?” “I pretended not to understand.” “Why? Are you unwilling to marry into the Wei family?” “It would be no use if I were willing. I have taken my master’s surname. How could I change it again to Wei?” “You have a conscience, at least.” Hu nodded approvingly. “I shall see what can be done.” That plainly meant the happy outcome was possible. A’xiang was delighted. Yet he was still shy. He knew this was an excellent opportunity, but could not bring himself to ask and settle the matter while the chance was before him.

不说话却又感到僵手僵脚，一身不自在；于是搭讪着问道∶『老爷恐怕还没有吃饭？我来关照他们！』接着便喊∶『素香，素香！』素香从下房里闪了出来，正眼都不看阿祥；走过他面前，低低咕哝了一句∶『叫魂一样叫！』然后到胡雪岩面前问道∶『老爷叫我？』做主人的看在眼里，恍然大悟；怪不得问她阿祥在哪里？她有点懒得答理的模样！原来阿祥跟魏阿巧好了，她在吃醋。照此说来，落花有意，流水无情；阿祥倒辜负她了。这样想着，便有些替素香委屈。不过事到如今，没有胡乱干预，扰乱已成之局的道理，惟有装作不解；找件事差遣素香去做。

Saying nothing left him awkward and uncomfortable, so he found an excuse to speak. “You have probably not eaten, sir. I shall tell them.” He called, “Suxiang! Suxiang!” She emerged from the servants’ room without looking him in the face. Passing him, she muttered, “Must you call as though summoning a soul?” Then she asked Hu, “Did you call me, sir?” He saw it all and understood. No wonder she had seemed reluctant to answer when he asked where A’xiang was. She was jealous of his attachment to the Wei girl. The falling blossom was willing, but the flowing water felt nothing: A’xiang had disappointed her. Hu felt sorry for her. Yet there was no reason to interfere blindly and upset what was already taking shape. He could only pretend not to understand and find her something to do.

『我不在家吃饭了。』他嘱咐阿祥∶『你马上到张老板那里去，说我请他吃酒。弄堂口那家酒店叫啥字号？』『叫王宝和。』『我在王宝和等他。你去快点，请他马上来。』『是！』阿祥如奉了将军令一般，高声答应，急步下楼。等他一走，胡雪岩喝完一杯素香倒来的茶，也就出门了。走到王宝和，朝里一望；王老板眼尖，急忙迎了出来，哈腰曲背地连连招呼∶『胡大人怎么有空来？是不是寻啥人？』『不是！到你这里来吃酒。』王老板顿时有受宠若惊之感∶『请！请！正好雅座有空。胡大人来得巧了。』所谓雅座是凸出的一块方丈之地，一张条案配着一张八仙桌；条案上还供着一座神龛，内中一方『王氏昭穆宗亲之位』的神牌。胡雪岩看这陈设，越发勾起乡思；仿佛置身在杭州盐桥附近的小酒店中，记起与张胖子闲来买醉的那些日子了。『胡大人，我开一坛如假包换的绍兴花雕；您老人家尝尝看。』『随你。』胡雪岩问∶『有啥下酒菜？』『蛏子刚上市。还有鞭笋；嫩得很。再就是酱鸭，糟鸡。』『都拿来好了。另外要两样东西，「独脚蟹」，油炸臭豆腐干。』『独脚蟹』就是发芽豆，大小酒店必备；油炸臭豆腐干就难了，『这时候，担子都过去了。』王老板说，『还不知有没有？』『一定要！』胡雪岩固执地说，『你叫个人，多走两步路去找，一定要买来！』『是，是！一定买来，一定买来！』王老板一叠连声地答应，叫个小徒弟遍处去找，还特地关照一句∶『快去快回。』

“I shall not dine at home.” He told A’xiang, “Go straight to Mr Zhang and say I invite him for wine. What is the name of the tavern at the entrance to the lane?” “Wang Baohe.” “I shall wait for him there. Be quick, and ask him to come at once.” “Yes, sir!” The boy answered as loudly as though he had received a general’s command, then hurried downstairs. After he had gone, Hu finished the tea Suxiang had poured and went out too. As he looked into Wang Baohe, the sharp-eyed proprietor hurried forward, bowing repeatedly. “What brings Your Excellency here? Are you looking for someone?” “No. I have come for a drink.” Mr Wang was overwhelmed by the honour. “Please come in! The private table is free. You have chosen just the right moment.” The private space was a small projecting recess, about a square zhang, furnished with a narrow side table and a square dining table. On the side table stood a shrine containing a tablet to the ancestors of the Wang family. The setting deepened Hu’s homesickness. He seemed to be in a little tavern near Salt Bridge in Hangzhou, remembering the days when he and Fatty Zhang would drink together in their leisure. “Your Excellency, I shall open a jar of genuine Shaoxing Huadiao—guaranteed. Try it.” “As you please. What have you to eat with it?” “Razor clams have just come into season. There are tender whip bamboo shoots too, as well as soy-braised duck and chicken in wine lees.” “Bring them all. And two other things: one-legged crabs and fried stinking bean curd.” “One-legged crabs” meant sprouted beans, available in every tavern, large or small. The bean curd was harder. “The vendors have all passed by at this hour,” Mr Wang said. “I do not know whether any can still be found.” “I must have it,” Hu insisted. “Send someone a little farther to look. He must bring some back.” “Certainly, certainly! We shall find it.” Mr Wang sent a young apprentice searching, with particular orders to hurry back.

于是，胡雪岩先独酌。一桌子的酒菜，他单取一样发芽豆；咀嚼的不是豆子，而是寒微辰光那份苦中作乐的滋味。心里是说不出的那种既辛酸、又安慰的隽永向往的感觉。一抬眼突然发觉，张胖子笑嘻嘻地站在面前；才知道自己是想得出神了。定定神问道∶『吃了饭没有？』『正在吃酒，阿祥来到。』阿胖子坐下来问道∶『今天倒清闲；居然想到这里来吃酒？』『不是清闲，是无聊。』张胖子从未听他说过这种泄气的话，不由得张大了眼想问∶但烫来的酒，糟香扑鼻，就顾不得说话先要喝酒了。『好酒！』他喝了一口说；啧啧地咂着嘴唇，『嫡路绍兴花雕。』『酒再好，也比不上我们在盐桥吃烧酒的味道好。』『呕！』张胖子抬头四顾，『倒有点象我们常常去光顾的那家「纯号」酒店。』『现在也不晓得怎么样了？』胡雪岩微微叹息着；一仰脸，干了一碗。『你这个酒，不能这样子喝！要吃醉的。』张胖子停杯不饮，愁眉苦脸地说∶『啥事情不开心？』『没有啥！有点想杭州，有点想从前的日子。老张，「贫贱之交不可忘，糟糠之妻不下堂」；来，我敬你！』张胖了不知他是何感触？惴惴然看着他说∶『少吃点，少吃点！慢慢来。』还好，胡雪岩是心胸开阔的人，酒德甚好；两碗酒下肚，只想高兴的事。想到阿祥，便即问道∶『老张，前面有家杂货店，老板姓魏，你认不认识？』

Hu began drinking alone. Of all the dishes on the table, he touched only the sprouted beans. What he savoured was not the beans, but the little pleasures wrested from hardship in his humble days. An inexpressible mixture of pain, comfort and lingering longing filled him. Suddenly he looked up and saw Fatty Zhang smiling before him. Only then did he realise how far his thoughts had wandered. Collecting himself, he asked, “Have you eaten?” “I was just having a drink when A’xiang arrived.” Zhang sat down. “You must be at leisure today, to think of drinking here.” “Not at leisure. At a loose end.” Zhang had never heard such dispirited words from him. His eyes widened and he was about to ask, but the fragrance of the warmed wine reached him, and drinking took precedence. “Fine wine!” he declared after a sip, smacking his lips. “True Shaoxing Huadiao.” “However fine it is, it cannot taste as good as the spirits we drank at Salt Bridge.” “Oh!” Zhang looked around. “This does resemble the Chunhao tavern we used to frequent.” “Who knows what has become of it?” Hu sighed faintly and drained a bowl. “You must not drink like that. You will be drunk.” Zhang set down his own cup, looking troubled. “What has upset you?” “Nothing. I miss Hangzhou, and the old days. Old Zhang, ‘Never forget friends made in poverty; never cast out the wife who shared your bran and chaff.’ Here, I drink to you.” Zhang did not know what had stirred him and watched uneasily. “Less, less! Take it slowly.” Fortunately, Hu was broad-minded and well behaved in drink. After two bowls he wanted to think only of pleasant things. Remembering A’xiang, he asked, “Old Zhang, do you know the owner of the grocery up ahead? His name is Wei.”

『我们是同行，怎么不认识？你问起他，总有缘故吧？』『他有个女儿，也叫阿巧，长得圆圆的脸，倒是宜男之相。你总也很熟？』听这一说，张胖子的兴致来了，精神抖擞地坐直了身了，睁了眼睛看着胡雪岩，一面点头，一面慢吞吞地答道∶『我很熟，十天、八天总要到我店里来一趟。』『为啥？』『她老子进货，到我这里来拆头寸；总是她来。』『这样说，他这个杂货店也可怜巴巴的。』『是啊，本来是小本经营。』张胖子说，『就要他这样才好。如果是殷实的话，铜钾银子上不在乎；做父母的就未必肯了。』『肯什么？』胡雪岩不懂他的话。『问你啊！不是说她宜男之相？』胡雪岩楞了一下，突然意会；一口酒直喷了出来，赶紧转过脸去，一面呛，一面笑。将个张胖子搞得丈二金刚摸不着头。『啊老张，你一辈子就是喜欢自作聪明；你想到哪里去了？』『你，』张胖子嗫嚅着说，『你不是想讨个会养儿子的小？』『所以说，你是自作聪明。哪有这回事？不过，谈的倒也是喜事；媒人也还是要请你去做。』接着，胡雪岩便将阿祥与阿巧的那一段情，都说给了张胖子听。

“We are in the same trade. Of course I know him. You must have a reason for asking.” “He has a daughter called A’qiao, with a round face—the sort of face that promises sons. You must know her well too?” Zhang’s interest awakened. He sat up briskly and looked at Hu, nodding as he answered slowly, “Very well. She comes to my shop every week or so.” “Why?” “When her father needs money to restock, he borrows from me. She is always the one he sends.” “Then his little grocery must be rather hard pressed.” “Yes. He has always had very little capital. That is just what you want. If the family were comfortably off and cared little for money, her parents might not agree.” “Agree to what?” Hu did not understand. “You tell me! Did you not say she had a face that promised sons?” Hu stared, then suddenly understood. He sprayed out a mouthful of wine and hastily turned aside, coughing and laughing, while Zhang was left completely bewildered. “Old Zhang, you have spent your whole life thinking yourself clever. Where has your imagination taken you?” “Were you not thinking of taking a concubine who could bear you sons?” Zhang asked hesitantly. “That is why I say you are too clever by half. Nothing of the sort! But there is a marriage to arrange, and I still want you to be the matchmaker.” He then told Zhang the whole story of A’xiang and the Wei girl’s affection.

『好啊！』张胖子秀高兴地，『这个媒做来包定不会「春梅浆」！』『春梅浆』是杭州的俗语，做媒做成一对怨偶，男女两家都嗔怨媒人，有了纠纷，责成媒人去办交涉，搞得受累无穷，就叫『春梅浆』。老张说这话，就表示他对这头姻缘，亦很满意；使得胡雪岩越发感到此事做得惬意称心。一高兴之下，又将条件放宽了。

“Excellent!” Zhang said delightedly. “This match certainly will not become a bowl of ‘spring-plum pulp’.” That was a Hangzhou expression. If a matchmaker brought together an unhappy couple, both families blamed him. Every dispute was referred back to him for negotiation, burdening him without end; such a predicament was called “spring-plum pulp”. Zhang’s words showed that he approved of the match, which made Hu feel still more satisfied with what he was doing. In his good humour, he made the terms more generous.

『你跟魏老板去说，入赘可以，改姓不可以；既然他女儿是宜男之相，不怕儿子不多，将来他自己挑一个顶他们魏家的香烟好了。至于阿祥，我叫他也做杂货生意；我借一千银洋给他做本钱。』『既然这样，也就不必谈聘金不聘金了。嫁妆、酒席，一切都是男家包办；拜了堂，两家并作一家。魏老板不费分文，有个女婿养他们的老，有这样便宜的好事，他也该心满意足了。你看我，明天一说就成功；马上挑日子办喜事。』『那就重重拜托。我封好谢媒的红包，等你来拿。』『谢什么媒！你帮我的忙还帮得少了不成？』

“Tell Mr Wei that A’xiang may marry into his household, but may not change his surname. With her son-bearing looks, there should be no shortage of sons. Mr Wei can choose one to continue his family line. I shall put A’xiang into the grocery trade too, lending him a thousand silver dollars as capital.” “Then there is no need to discuss a separate betrothal payment. The groom’s side can provide everything—the trousseau, the feast and the rest. Once the marriage ceremony is held, the two households will become one. Mr Wei need spend nothing, and he will have a son-in-law to support them in old age. Such favourable terms should satisfy him completely. You will see: I shall settle it tomorrow, and we can choose a day for the wedding at once.” “Then I entrust it to you. I shall have a red packet ready to thank the matchmaker.” “Thank me? Have you not helped me often enough already?”

谈到这里，小徒弟捧来一大盘油炸臭豆腐干；胡雪岩不暇多说，一连吃了三块，有些狼吞虎咽的模样，便又惹得爱说话的张胖子要开口了。『看你别的菜不吃，发芽豆跟臭豆腐干倒吃得起劲！』胡雪岩点点头，停箸答道∶『我那位老把兄嵇鹤龄，讲过一个故事给我听∶从前有个穷书生，去庙里住；跟一个老和尚做了朋友。老和尚常常掘些芋头，煨在热灰里；穷书生吃得津津有味。到后来穷书生十年寒窗无人问，一举成名天下知，飞黄腾达，做了大官。衣锦还乡，想到煨芋头的滋味，特地去拜访老和尚，要尝一尝，一尝之下，说不好吃。老和尚答他一句∶芋头没有变，你人变了！我今天要吃发芽豆跟臭豆腐干，也就仿佛是这样一种意思。』『原来如此！你倒还记得，当初我们在纯号「摆一碗」，总是这两样东西下酒。』张胖子接着又问∶『现在你尝过了，是不是从前的滋味？』『是的。』『那倒难得！』张胖子有点笑他言不由衷的意味，『鱼翅海参没有拿你那张嘴吃刁？』『你弄错了，我不是说它们好吃！从前不好吃，现在还是不好吃。』『这话我就不懂了！不好吃何必去吃它？』张胖子说。『从前也不晓得吃过多少回，从来没有听你说过，发芽豆、臭豆腐干不好吃。』『不好吃，不必说；想法子去弄好吃的来吃。空口说白话，一点用都没有；反而害得人家都不肯吃苦了！』这几句话说得张胖子楞住了，怔怔地看了他好半天，方始开口∶『老胡，我们相交不是三年、五年；到今天我才晓得你的本性。这就难怪了！你由学生意爬到今天大老板的地位；我从钱庄大伙计弄到开小杂货店，都是有道理的。』一向笑嘻嘻的张胖子，忽然大生感触，面有抑郁之色。胡雪岩从他的牢骚话中，了解他不得意的心情；多年的患难贫贱之交，心里自然也很难过。

Just then the apprentice arrived with a great plate of fried stinking bean curd. Hu had no time for further talk. He ate three pieces in succession, almost wolfing them down, which gave the talkative Zhang another opening. “You leave the other dishes alone, but how you enjoy those sprouted beans and that bean curd!” Hu nodded and set down his chopsticks. “My old sworn brother Ji Heling once told me a story. A poor scholar went to live in a temple and became friends with an old monk. The monk would dig up taro roots and roast them in hot ashes, and the scholar ate them with delight. Later, after ten years of study in obscurity, the scholar won fame at a single stroke, rose rapidly and became a great official. Returning home in glory, he remembered the flavour of those taros and went specially to visit the monk and taste them again. This time he said they were no good. The monk answered, ‘The taros have not changed. You have.’ My wish for beans and stinking bean curd today means something rather like that.” “So that is it! You remember how those were always the two things we ate with a bowl of wine at Chunhao.” Zhang asked, “Now you have tasted them, do they taste as they did before?” “Yes.” “That is remarkable!” His tone suggested he doubted Hu’s sincerity. “Shark’s fin and sea cucumber have not spoiled your palate?” “You misunderstand. I did not say they tasted good. They did not then, and they do not now.” “I do not understand that! Why eat what you do not like? We ate them countless times in the old days, and I never heard you say they were no good.” “There is no need to say it. Find a way to get better things to eat. Empty talk achieves nothing; it only makes others unwilling to endure hardship.” These words left Zhang staring for a long time before he could speak. “Old Hu, we have been friends far longer than three or five years, but only today have I understood your nature. No wonder! You have climbed from apprentice to great proprietor, while I have gone from senior bank clerk to owner of a tiny grocery. There is a reason for both.” The habitually cheerful Zhang was suddenly overcome by feeling, and his face grew gloomy. Hu understood the disappointment beneath his complaint. They had shared poverty and adversity for so many years that he too felt distressed.

他真想安慰他。因而想到跟刘不才与古应春所商量的计划，不久联络好了杭州的小张和嘉兴的孙祥太，预备大举贩卖洋广杂货，不正好让张胖子也凑一股？股本当然是自己替他垫；只要他下手帮忙；无论如何比株守一爿小杂货店来得有出息。话已经要说出口了，想想不妥；张胖子嘴不紧，而这个贩卖洋广杂货的计划，是有作用的，不宜让他与闻。要帮他的忙，不如另打主意。想了一下，倒是有个主意，『老张，』他说，『我也晓得你现在委屈。不过时世不对，暂时要守一守。我的钱庄，你晓得的，杭州的老根一断，就没有源头活水了！现在也是苦撑在那里的局面。希望是一定有的；要摆功夫下去。你肯不肯来帮帮我的忙？』『你我的交情，谈不到肯不肯。不过，老胡，实在对不起，饭庄饭我吃得寒心了；你想想，我从前那个东家，我那样子替他卖力，弄到临了，翻脸不认人。如果不是你帮我一个大忙，吃官司都有份。从那时候起，我就罚过咒，再不吃钱庄饭！自己小本经营，不管怎么样，也是个老板。』说到这里，张胖子自觉失言；赶紧又作补充∶『至于对你，情形当然不同。不过我罚过咒，不帮人家做饭庄；这个咒是跪在关帝菩萨面前罚的，不好当耍。老胡，千言万语并一句∶对不对你！』说完，举杯表示道歉。

He wanted sincerely to comfort his friend. He thought of the plan he had discussed with Liu Bucai and Gu Yingchun. Once they had made contact with Little Zhang of Hangzhou and Sun Xiangtai of Jiaxing, they intended to trade on a large scale in imported and southern goods. Why not give Fatty Zhang a share? Naturally Hu would advance the capital. Zhang need only lend a hand; it would certainly offer more promise than clinging to a little grocery. He was about to speak when he thought better of it. Zhang could not keep his mouth shut, and the trading scheme served a particular purpose. He ought not to know of it. Better to find another way of helping him. After a moment, an idea came. “Old Zhang, I know that your present position is beneath you. But the times are wrong. You must hold on for a while. You know my bank: with its old roots in Hangzhou cut off, its living source of funds is gone. We too are struggling to keep it going. There is certainly hope, but work must be put into it. Would you come and help me?” “Between us, willingness does not enter into it. But forgive me, Old Hu: I have had my heart chilled by banking. Think of my former employer. I worked so hard for him, and in the end he turned against me. Without your great help, I might have faced a lawsuit. From that day I swore never to earn my living in a bank again. However small my own business, at least I am its proprietor.” Realising he had spoken awkwardly, he hurried to qualify it. “With you, naturally, it would be different. But I swore not to work in another man’s bank, and I made that oath kneeling before Lord Guan. It is not a thing to treat lightly. A thousand words come to one: I am sorry, Old Hu.” He raised his cup in apology.

『这杯酒，我不能吃。我有两句话请问你，你罚咒，是不帮人家做钱庄？』『是的。』『就是说，不给人家做伙计？』『是的！』张胖子重重地回答。『那末，老张，你先要弄清楚，我不是请你做阜康的伙计。』『做啥？』张胖子愕然相问。『做股东。等于你自己做老板！这样子，随便你罚多重的咒，都不会应了。』『做股东！』张胖子心动了，『不过，我没有本钱。』『本钱我借你。我划一万银子，算你的股份；你来管事，另外开一份薪水。』胡雪岩说，『你那家小杂货店，我也替你想好了出路；盘给阿祥，他自然并到他丈人那里。你看，这不是顺理成章 的事？』

“I cannot drink to that. Let me ask you two questions. Your oath was that you would not work in someone else’s bank?” “Yes.” “That is, you would not be another man’s clerk?” “Exactly!” Zhang answered emphatically. “Then understand this first, Old Zhang: I am not asking you to become a clerk at Fukang.” “What, then?” Zhang asked in surprise. “A shareholder. In effect, your own proprietor. However solemn your oath, that cannot violate it.” “A shareholder!” He was tempted. “But I have no capital.” “I shall lend it to you. I shall assign ten thousand taels as your share. You will manage the business and draw a separate salary. I have thought of a solution for your grocery too: transfer it to A’xiang, and he will naturally combine it with his father-in-law’s. Does that not all follow neatly?”

这样的条件，这样的交情，照常理说，张胖子应该一诺无辞；但他仍在踌躇，因为第一，钱庄这一行，他受过打击，确实有些寒心；第二，交朋友将心换心，惟其胡雪岩如此厚爱，自己就更得忖量一下，倘或接手以后，没有把握打开局面，整顿内部，让好朋友失望，倒不如此刻辞谢，还可以保全交情。当然，他说不出辞绝的话，而且也舍不得辞绝；考虑了又考虑，说了句∶『让我先看一看再说。』『看？你用不着看了！』胡雪岩说∶『阜康的情形比起从前王雪公在世的时候那样热闹，自然显得差了。跟上海的同行比一比，老实说一句，比上不足，比下着实有余。阜康决没有亏空，放款出去的户头，都是靠得住的；几个大存户亦都殷实得很，不至于一下子都来提款。毛病是我不能拿全副精神摆在上头；原来请的那个大伙，人既老实，身子又不好，所以弄得死气沉沉，没有起色。你去了，当然会不同；等我来出两个主意，请你一手去做，同心协力拿阜康这块招牌再刷得它金光闪亮。』照这样说，大可一干；不过，『我到底是啥身分到阜康呢？』他说，『钱庄的规矩，你是晓得的。』钱庄的规矩，大权都在大伙手里，股东不得过问；胡雪岩原就有打算的，毫不迟疑地答道∶『对我来说，你是股东；对阜康来说，你是大伙。你不是替人家做伙计，是替自己做。』这个解释很圆满，张胖子表示满意，毅然决然地答道∶『那就一言为定。主意你来出，事情我来做；对外是你出面，在内归我负责。』『好极！我正就是这个意思——。』

With such terms and such friendship behind them, Fatty Zhang ought, by all ordinary reasoning, to have accepted without hesitation. Yet he still wavered. For one thing, the blow he had suffered in banking had truly chilled his heart. For another, friendship required feeling to be repaid with feeling: precisely because Hu Xueyan treated him so generously, he must consider whether he could open up new business and put the bank in order. If he could not be sure of doing so, it would be better to decline now and preserve their friendship than to disappoint his friend later. Of course, he could neither bring himself to refuse nor bear to let the opportunity go. After thinking it over and over, he said, “Let me look into it first.” “Look into it? There is no need!” Hu replied. “Fukang is naturally less lively than it was when Governor Wang was alive. Compared with the other Shanghai banks, I can honestly say that we fall short of the best but stand well above the worst. There is absolutely no deficit. Our borrowers are reliable, and the few large depositors are all substantial men. They will not all descend on us to withdraw their money at once. The trouble is that I cannot give it my whole attention. The chief clerk I engaged is a straightforward fellow, but his health is poor; the place has become lifeless and never gets ahead. With you there, things would certainly be different. Let me provide an idea or two and you carry them through. Working together, we shall polish Fukang’s signboard until it shines like gold again.” Put that way, the venture was worth undertaking. Still, Zhang asked, “In exactly what capacity am I to join Fukang? You know the rules of banking.” By those rules, authority rested entirely with the chief clerk; shareholders were not to interfere. Hu had already thought this through. “In relation to me, you are a shareholder,” he answered without hesitation. “In relation to Fukang, you are the chief clerk. You will be working for yourself, not serving another man.” The explanation was complete, and Zhang was satisfied. “Then it is settled,” he said firmly. “You supply the ideas; I carry them out. You represent us outside; I take charge within.” “Excellent! That is exactly what I mean—”

『慢来。』张胖子突然想到，迫不及待地问∶『原来的那位老兄呢？』『这你不必担心。他身体不好，而且儿子已经出道；在美国人的洋行里做「康白度」，老早就劝他回家享福。他因为我待他不错，虽然辞过几次，我不放他，也就不好意思走。现在有你去接手，在他真正求之不得。』张胖子释然了，『我就怕敲了人家饭碗！』他又生感慨，『我的东家不好；不能让他也在背后骂东家不好。』『你想想我是不是那种人？』胡雪岩问道，『老张，君子一言，驷马难追；从此刻起，我们就算合伙了！倒谈谈生意经；你看，我们应该怎么个做法？』这一下，将张胖子问住了。他是钱庄学徒出身，按部就班做到大伙，讲内部管理，要看实际情形而定；谈到外面的发展，也要先了解了解市面。如要他凭空想个主意出来，可就抓瞎了。想了好一会，他说∶『现在的银价上落很大；如果消息灵通，兑进兑出一转手之间，利息不小。』『这当然。归你自己去办，用不着商量。』胡雪岩说∶『我们要商量的是，长线放远鹞，看到三年以后，大局一定，怎么样能够飞黄腾达，一下子窜了起来。』『这——』张胖子笑道，『我就没有这份本事了。』

“Wait!” A sudden thought struck Zhang, and he asked urgently, “What about the man already there?” “You need not worry about him. His health is poor, and his son has made his way in the world. He is a comprador with an American trading firm and has long urged his father to retire and enjoy life. The old fellow is grateful for my treatment of him. He has offered his resignation several times, but when I refused to let him go he felt ashamed to insist. He could wish for nothing better than to have you take over.” Zhang was relieved. “I was afraid of breaking another man’s rice bowl.” Once more he grew reflective. “My own employer treated me badly. We must not make him say behind our backs that his employer treated him badly too.” “Do you think I am that sort of man?” Hu asked. “Old Zhang, once a gentleman gives his word, four horses cannot overtake it. From this moment, we are partners. Now let us talk business. How do you think we should proceed?” That stumped Zhang. He had begun as an apprentice and risen step by step to chief clerk. Before advising on internal management he would have to examine the actual position, and before discussing expansion he would have to study the market. Asked to produce an idea out of thin air, he was helpless. At last he said, “The price of silver fluctuates sharply nowadays. With prompt information, we could make a handsome profit simply buying and selling.” “Certainly. You can deal with that yourself; there is no need to consult me. What we must discuss is how to let out a long line and fly our kite far ahead: three years from now, once affairs have settled down, how can we make a sudden leap into prosperity?” “That,” Zhang said with a laugh, “is beyond my abilities.”

谈生意经，胡雪岩一向最起劲；又正当微醺之时，兴致更佳，『今天难得有空，我们索性好好儿筹划一番。』他问∶『老张，山西票号的规矩，你总熟悉的吧？』『隔行如隔山；钱庄、票号看来是同行，做法不同。』张胖子在胡雪岩面前不敢不说老实话，『而且，票号的势力不过长江以南；他们的内幕，实在没有机会见识。』『我们做钱庄，唯一的劲敌就是山西票号。知己知彼，百战百胜；所以这方面，我平时很肯留心。现在，不妨先说点给你听。』照胡雪岩的了解，山西票号原以经营汇兑为主；而以京师为中心。这几年干戈扰攘，道路艰难，公款解京，诸多不便；因而票号无形中代理了一部分部库与省库的职司，公款并不计息，汇水尤为可观，自然大获其利。还有各省的巨商显宦，认为天下最安稳的地方，莫如京师；所以多将现款，汇到京里，实际上就是存款。这些存款的目的不是生利，而是保本，所以利息极轻。

Business talk always roused Hu’s enthusiasm. Now, pleasantly warmed by wine, he was more eager than ever. “We seldom have time to ourselves. Let us make some proper plans today. Old Zhang, you must know the practices of the Shanxi remittance houses?” “Different trades are mountains apart. Banks and remittance houses may look like the same business, but their methods differ.” Before Hu, Zhang dared give nothing but an honest answer. “Besides, their influence does not extend south of the Yangtze. I have had no opportunity to see their inner workings.” “For us bankers, the Shanxi houses are the only formidable rivals. Know yourself and your enemy, and you can win a hundred battles. That is why I always pay close attention to them. Let me tell you something about them first.” As Hu understood it, the Shanxi houses had originally dealt chiefly in remittances, with the capital as their centre. In recent years, war and difficult roads had made it inconvenient to transport government funds to Beijing. Almost without a formal arrangement, the houses had taken over some of the duties of the central and provincial treasuries. They paid no interest on government balances, while their remittance charges were substantial: naturally, the profits were great. Moreover, wealthy merchants and high officials in the provinces considered the capital the safest place under heaven. They therefore sent much of their ready cash there, which in practice meant depositing it with the houses. Such deposits were intended to preserve capital, not earn income, so the interest paid was very low.

『有了存款要找出路。头寸烂在那里，大元宝不会生小元宝的。』胡雪岩说，『山西票号近年来通行放款给做京官的，名为「放京债」；听说一万两的借据，实付七千——』『什么？』张胖子大声打断，『这是什么债，比印子钱还要凶！』『你说比印子钱还要凶，借的人倒是心甘情愿；反正羊毛出在羊身上，老百姓倒霉！』『怎么呢？』『你想，做官借债，拿什么来还？自然是老百姓替他还。譬如某人放了你们浙江藩司，京里打点，上任盘费；到任以后置公馆、买轿马、用底下人，哪一样不用钱？于是乎先借一笔京债；到了任想法子先挪一笔款子还掉，随后慢慢儿弥补；不在老百姓头上动脑筋，岂不是就要闹亏空了？』『这样子做法难道没有风险！譬如说，到了任不认帐？』『不会的。第一、有保人；保人一定也是京官。第二、有借据；如果赖债，到都察院递呈子，御史一参，赖债的人要丢官。第三、自有人帮票号的忙，不准人赖债。为啥呢，一班穷翰林平时都靠借债度日；就盼望放出去当考官，当学政，收了门生的「贽敬」来还债；还了再借，日子依旧可以过得下去。倘若有人赖了债，票号联合起来，说做官的没有信用，从此不借；穷翰林当然大起恐慌，会帮票号讨债。』胡雪岩略停一下又说∶『要论风险，只有一样；新官上任，中途出了事，或者死掉，或者丢官。不过也要看情形而定，保人硬气的，照样会一肩担承。』『怪不得！』张胖子说∶『这几年祁、太、平三帮票号，在各省大设分号。原来有这样的好处！』他跃跃欲试地，『我们何不学人家一学？』『着啊！』胡雪岩干了一杯酒，『我正就是这个意思。』

“Once you have deposits, you must find an outlet for them. Leave funds to rot, and large ingots will never give birth to little ones,” Hu said. “In recent years, the Shanxi houses have commonly lent to officials in the capital. They call it making ‘capital loans’. I hear that against a note for ten thousand taels they actually advance seven thousand—” “What?” Zhang interrupted loudly. “What sort of loan is that? Worse than the usurers who collect their instalments every day!” “You think it worse, but the borrowers agree willingly enough. The wool comes off the sheep’s back in the end. It is the common people who suffer.” “How so?” “Think about it. When an official borrows, what can he repay with? Naturally, the people repay for him. Suppose someone is appointed provincial treasurer of your Zhejiang. He must make payments in the capital and pay for his journey. Once he arrives, he needs a residence, chairs and horses, servants—what does not cost money? So he first takes a capital loan. After assuming office, he finds some public money to divert and pays it off, then gradually makes up the sum. Unless he devises ways to extract it from the people, he will be left with a deficit in his accounts.” “But is that not risky? Suppose he refuses to acknowledge the debt once he takes office?” “He will not. First, there is a guarantor, who must also be an official in the capital. Second, there is a signed note. If he repudiates the debt, a petition can be lodged with the Censorate. One impeachment from a censor, and the debtor loses his post. Third, others will help the houses and prevent defaults. Why? The poor Hanlin scholars live on loans. They hope to be sent out as examiners or education commissioners, collect ceremonial gifts from their pupils and repay their debts. Having repaid, they can borrow again and keep going. If anyone defaults, the houses may act together, declare officials untrustworthy and stop lending. The poor scholars would panic. They will help recover the money.” Hu paused, then went on. “There is only one real risk: something may happen to a newly appointed official on his journey. He may die or lose his appointment. Even then, it depends. A sound guarantor will shoulder the whole obligation.” “No wonder!” Zhang exclaimed. “These past few years the Qi, Tai and Ping groups of remittance houses have been opening branches all over the provinces. So this is the advantage!” Eager to try it himself, he asked, “Why should we not learn from them?” “Exactly!” Hu drained his cup. “That is just what I have in mind.”

胡雪岩的意思是，仿照票号的办法，办两项放款。第一是放给做官的。由于南北道路艰难，时世不同，这几年官员调补升迁，多不按常规；所谓『送部引见』的制度，虽未废除，却多变通办理；尤其是军功上保升的文武官员，尽有当到藩司、皋司，主持一省钱谷、司法的大员，而未曾进过京的。由京里补缺放出来，自然可以借京债；如果在江南升调，譬如江苏知县，调升湖北的知府，没有一笔盘缠与安家银子就『行不得也』！胡雪岩打算仿照京债的办法，帮帮这些人的忙。『这当然是有风险的。但要通扯扯算，以有余补不足。自从开办厘金以来，不晓得多少人发了财；象这种得了税差的，早一天到差，多一天好处，再高的利息，他也要借；而且不会吃倒帐。我们的做法是要在这些户头上多赚他些，来弥补倒帐。话不妨先说明白，我们是「劫富济贫」的做法。』『劫富济贫！』张胖子念一两遍，点点头说∶『这个道理我懂了。第二项呢？『

Hu intended to follow their example with two kinds of loan. The first would go to officials. With travel between north and south so difficult and circumstances so altered, transfers and promotions in recent years had often departed from normal procedure. The requirement that officials be sent to the appropriate ministry and presented for an imperial audience had not been abolished, but exceptions were commonly made. In particular, among civil and military officials recommended for promotion on the strength of wartime service, there were even provincial treasurers and judicial commissioners—men responsible for the finances or justice of an entire province—who had never been to Beijing. A man appointed from the capital could, of course, take a capital loan. But an official promoted within the lower Yangtze region—a Jiangsu magistrate made prefect in Hubei, for instance—could not move without money for the journey and for establishing his household. Hu proposed to help such men with loans on the same model. “There is risk, of course. But we must reckon the whole account, using the surplus here to cover the shortfall there. Since the likin taxes began, goodness knows how many men have grown rich. Someone given a tax post gains an extra day’s profit for every day earlier he arrives. However high the interest, he will borrow, and we shall not suffer a bad debt. Our method is to earn more from these accounts to make up for losses on others. We can say it plainly from the start: we shall ‘take from the rich to help the poor’.” “Take from the rich to help the poor!” Zhang repeated the phrase once or twice and nodded. “I understand the principle. What is the second kind?”

『第二项放款是放给逃难到上海来的内地乡绅人家。这些人家在原籍，多是靠收租过日子的，一早拎只鸟笼泡茶店；下午到澡塘子睡一觉；晚上「摆一碗」，吃得醉醺醺回家。一年三百六十天，起码三百天是这样子。这种人，恭维他，说他是做大少爷；讲得难听点，就是无业游民。如果不是祖宗积德，留下大把家私，一定做「伸手大将军」了。当初逃难来的时候，总有些现款细软在手里，一时还不会「落难」；日久天长，坐吃山空，又是在这个花天酒地的夷场上，所以这几年下来，很有些赫赫有名的大少爷，快要讨饭了！』这话不是过甚其词，张胖子就遭遇到几个；境况最凄惨的，甚至倚妻女卖笑为生。因此，胡雪岩的话，在他深具同感；只是放款给这些人，他不以为然，『救急容易教穷难！』他说，『非吃倒帐不可！』『不会的。』胡雪岩说，『这就要放开眼光来看；长毛的气数快尽了！江浙两省一光复，逃难的回家乡，大片田地长毛抢不走；他们苦一两年，仍旧是大少爷。怎么会吃倒帐？』『啊！』张胖子深深吸了口气，『这一层我倒还没有想到。照你的说法，我倒有个做法。』『你说！』『叫他们拿地契来抵押。没有地契的，写借据，言明如果欠款不还，甘愿以某处某处田地作价抵还。』『对！这样做法，就更加牢靠了。』

“The second is for families of the inland gentry who have fled to Shanghai. At home, most lived on rents. In the morning they carried a birdcage to the teahouse; in the afternoon they slept at the bathhouse; in the evening they sat down to a drinking party and went home tipsy. Of the three hundred and sixty days of the year, at least three hundred passed like that. To flatter such men, you call them young gentlemen of leisure. Less politely, they are idle vagabonds. Had their ancestors not earned merit and left them great estates, they would certainly have become generals of the outstretched hand. When they first fled here, they had some cash and valuables, so they did not immediately fall on hard times. But spend without earning, and even a mountain is exhausted—especially in this foreign settlement, with its feasting and pleasure. After these few years, a good many once-famous young gentlemen are close to begging.” This was no exaggeration. Zhang had encountered several himself; the most wretched even depended on their wives and daughters to earn a living entertaining men. He therefore sympathised deeply with Hu’s account, but disapproved of lending to such people. “It is easy to relieve an emergency and hard to rescue poverty. We should be certain to lose the money.” “No,” Hu said. “We must look further ahead. The Longhairs’ allotted days are almost over. Once Jiangsu and Zhejiang are recovered, the refugees will go home. The rebels cannot carry off their great tracts of farmland. After a year or two of hardship, they will be gentlemen of leisure again. Why should the loans be lost?” “Ah!” Zhang drew a deep breath. “That had not occurred to me. On that basis, I have a method to suggest.” “Let us hear it.” “Require their title deeds as security. If they have no deeds with them, have them sign a note stating that, if they fail to repay, specified land shall be valued and surrendered in settlement.” “Quite right! That makes it safer still.”

『还有！』张胖子跟胡雪岩一席长谈，启发良多，也变得聪明了；他说∶『既然是救穷，就要看远一点。那班大少爷出身的，有一万用一万，不顾死活的；所以第一次来抵押，不可以押足，预备他不得过门的时候来加押。』这就完全谈得对路了，越谈越多，也越谈越深；然而仅谈放款，又哪里来的款子可放？张胖子心里一直有着这样一个疑问，却不肯问出来；因为在他意料中，心思细密的胡雪岩，一定会自己先提到，无须动问。而胡雪岩却始终不提这一层，这就逼得他不能不问了∶『老胡，这两项放款，期限都是长的；尤其是放给有田地的人家，要等光复了，才有收回的确期，只怕不是三两年的事。这笔头寸不在少数，你打算过没有？』『当然打算过。只有放款，没有存款的生意，怎么做法？我倒有个吸收存款的办法；只怕你不赞成。』『何见以得我不赞成？做生意嘛，有存款进来，难道还推出去不要？』胡雪岩不即回答，笑一笑，喝口酒，神态显得很诡秘；这让张胖子又无法捉摸了。他心里的感觉很复杂，又佩服，又有些戒心；觉得胡雪岩花样多得莫测高深，与这样的人相处，实在不能掉以轻心。

“One thing more!” Their long conversation had taught Zhang a great deal and sharpened his wits. “Since we are relieving poverty, we must look ahead. These men brought up as young masters spend ten thousand if they have ten thousand, regardless of the consequences. We should not advance the full amount on a property at the first application. Leave something in reserve for an additional advance when they cannot make ends meet.” Now they were thinking along exactly the same lines. Their discussion grew wider and deeper. Yet they spoke only of lending. Where were the funds to come from? The question had been in Zhang’s mind all along, but he had held it back, expecting so meticulous a man as Hu to raise it without prompting. Hu never did, however, and Zhang was obliged to ask. “Old Hu, both these kinds of loan are long-term. Those secured on land, especially, cannot have a definite prospect of repayment until the country is recovered. That may take more than two or three years. It will require a great deal of capital. Have you considered that?” “Of course. How can we do business with loans going out and no deposits coming in? I have a way of attracting deposits, but I fear you may not approve.” “Why should you think so? We are in business. If deposits come our way, surely we shall not turn them down?” Hu did not answer at once. He smiled and sipped his wine with a mysterious air that once more left Zhang unable to fathom him. Zhang’s feelings were mixed: admiration, but also wariness. Hu’s resources were so unpredictable that one could never safely let down one’s guard with him.

终于开口了；胡雪岩问出来一句令人意料不到的话∶『老张，譬如说∶我是长毛，有笔款子化名存到你这里，你敢不敢收？』『这——，』张胖子答∶『这有啥不敢？』『如果有条件的呢？』『什么条件？』『他不要利息，也不是活期；三年或者五年，到期来提，只有一个条件，不管怎么样，要如数照付。』『当然如数照付；还能怎么样？』『老张，你没有听懂我的意思，也还不明白其中的利害。抄家你总晓得的，被抄的人，倘或有私财寄顿在别处，照例是要追的。现在就是说，这笔存款，即使将来让官府追了去；你也要照付。请问你敢不敢担这个风险？』这一说，张胖子方始恍然，『我不敢！』他大摇其头，『如果有这样的情形，官府来追，不敢不报，不然就是隐匿逆产，不得了的罪名。等一追了去，人家到年限来提款，你怎么应付？』

At last Hu spoke, asking a wholly unexpected question. “Old Zhang, suppose I were a Longhair and wanted to deposit money with you under an assumed name. Would you dare accept it?” “Well—why should I not?” “What if there were conditions?” “What conditions?” “He asks no interest, and it is not a demand deposit. He will withdraw it after three years or five. There is only one condition: whatever happens, you must repay the full amount.” “Of course we repay the full amount. What else could we do?” “Old Zhang, you have not understood what I mean, nor what is at stake. You know what happens when a household’s property is confiscated. Any private assets entrusted elsewhere are ordinarily pursued as well. What I mean is that, even if the authorities recover this deposit from you, you must still repay the depositor. Would you dare accept that risk?” Only now did Zhang see. “I would not!” he said, shaking his head vigorously. “If the authorities came looking for the money, we would have to disclose it. Otherwise we should be guilty of concealing rebel property—a terrible charge. Once they had taken it away, how could we pay the man when his deposit matured?”

『我晓得你不敢！』胡雪岩说∶『我敢！为啥呢？我料定将来不会追。』『喔，何以见得？你倒说个道理我听所。』『何用说道理？打长毛打了好几年了，活捉的长毛头子也不少；几时看官府追过。』胡雪岩放低了声音又说∶『你再看看，官军捉着长毛，自然搜括一空，根本就不报的，如果要追，先从搜括的官军追起；那不是自己找自己麻烦？我说过，长毛的气数快尽了！好些人都在暗底下盘算；他们还有一场劫，只要逃过这场劫，后半辈子就可以衣食无忧了。』『是怎么样一场劫？』『这场劫就是太平天国垮台。一垮台，长毛自然变成「过街老鼠」，人人喊打，在那一阵乱的时候最危险；只要局面一定，朝廷自然降旨；首恶必惩，胁从不问，更不用说追他们的私产。所以说，只要逃过这场劫，后半辈子就可以衣食无忧。』谈到这里，张胖子恍然大悟。搜括饱了的长毛，要逃这场劫有个逃法，一是保命，二是保产。大劫来时即令逃得了命，也逃不了财产。换句话说，保命容易保产难；所以要早作安排。

“I knew you would not dare,” Hu said. “I would. Why? Because I am certain they will not pursue it.” “Oh? What makes you so sure? Let me hear your reasoning.” “What reasoning is needed? We have been fighting the Longhairs for years and have taken plenty of their leaders alive. When have you seen the authorities trace their assets?” He lowered his voice. “Look at the imperial troops. Once they catch a Longhair, they strip him of everything and never report it. If anyone traced the property, they would have to begin with the troops who plundered it. Would that not be making trouble for themselves? As I said, the Longhairs’ days are nearly over. Many are laying secret plans. There is still one catastrophe for them to survive; once through it, they can live in comfort for the rest of their days.” “What catastrophe?” “The fall of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom. Once it collapses, the Longhairs will be like rats crossing the street, with everyone shouting to strike them down. That first confusion will be the most dangerous time. Once order is restored, the court will naturally issue an edict: punish the ringleaders, spare those forced to follow. Still less will it pursue their private property. That is why I say that, if they survive that catastrophe, they can live free of want for the rest of their lives.” Now Zhang understood everything. The Longhairs who had gorged themselves on plunder needed two kinds of protection against the coming disaster: protection for their lives and for their wealth. When it came, they might escape alive but lose their property. In other words, saving their lives was easier than saving their wealth. Hence the need to arrange matters early.

想通了，不由得连连称『妙！』但张胖子不是点头，而是摇头，『老胡，』他带着些杞人忧天的味道∶『你这种脑筋动出来，要遭天忌的！』『这也不足为奇！我并没有害人的心思为啥遭天之忌？』『那末，犯不犯法呢？』张胖子自觉这话说得太率直；赶紧又解释∶『老胡，我实在因为这个法子太好了。俗语说的是∶好事多磨！深怕其中有办不通的地方；有点不大放心。』『你这话问得不错的。犯法的事，我们不能做；不过，朝廷的王法是有板有眼的东西，他怎么说，我们怎么做，这就是守法。他没有说，我们就可以照我们自己的意思做。隐匿罪犯的财产，固然犯法；但要论法，我们也有一句话说∶人家来存款的时候，额头上没有写着字∶我是长毛。化名来存，哪个晓得他的身分？『『其实我们晓得的，良心上总说不过去！』

Once he saw the scheme, Zhang could not help exclaiming, “Excellent! Excellent!” Yet he shook his head instead of nodding. “Old Hu,” he said, with something of the man who feared the sky might fall, “such ingenuity may provoke Heaven’s jealousy!” “There is nothing so extraordinary about it. I mean no one harm. Why should Heaven be jealous?” “But is it against the law?” Feeling he had spoken too bluntly, Zhang hurried to explain. “Old Hu, it is because the scheme is so good. As the saying goes, good things meet many obstacles. I am afraid there may be something that makes it unworkable. I cannot feel quite at ease.” “You are right to ask. We cannot break the law. But the court’s laws are definite things: we do what they say, and that is obeying the law. Where they say nothing, we may follow our own wishes. Concealing a criminal’s property is certainly illegal. But if it is a question of law, we have an answer: when a man comes to make a deposit, he does not have ‘I am a Longhair’ written on his forehead. If he deposits under an assumed name, who knows his identity?” “In fact, we do know. Our consciences cannot accept that.”

『老张，老张！』胡雪岩喝口酒，又感叹，又欢喜地说∶『我没有看错人，你本性厚道，实在不错。然而要讲到良心；生意人的良心，就只有对主顾来讲。公平交易，老少无欺，就是我们的良心。至于对朝廷，要做官的讲良心。这实在也跟做生意跟主顾讲良心是一样的道理，「学成文武艺，卖与帝王家」，朝廷是文武官儿的主顾，是他们的衣食父母，不能不讲良心。在我们就可以不讲了。』『不讲良心讲啥？』『讲法，对朝廷守法，就是对朝廷讲良心。』张胖子点点头，喝着酒沉思；好一会才欣然开口∶『老胡，我算是想通了。多少年来我就弄不懂，士农工商，为啥没好奸士、奸农、奸工、只有奸商？可见得做生意的人的良心，别有讲究；不过要怎么个讲究，我想不明白。现在明白了！对朝廷守法、对主顾讲公平，就是讲良心；就不是奸商！』『一点不错！老实说一句∶做生意的守朝廷的法，做官的对朝廷有良心，一定天下太平。再说一句∶只要做官的对朝廷讲良心，做生意的就不敢不守法。如果做官的对朝廷没有良心，要我们来对朝廷讲良心，未免迂腐。』『嗯，嗯；你这句话，再让我来想一想。』张胖子一面想，一面说∶『譬如，有长毛头子抓住了，抄家；做官的抹煞良心，侵吞这个人的财产，那就是不讲良心。如果我们讲良心呢？长毛化名来存款，说是应该充分的款子，我们不能收。结果呢？白白便宜赃官；仍旧让他侵吞了。对！』他一拍桌子，大声说道∶『光是做生意的对朝廷讲良心，没有用处。我们只要守法就够了！』『老张啊！』胡雪岩也欣然引杯，『这样才算是真正想通。』

“Old Zhang, Old Zhang!” Hu took a sip, at once moved and pleased. “I was not mistaken in you. You are good-hearted by nature. That is excellent. But as for conscience, a merchant’s conscience concerns his customers. Fair dealings, cheating neither young nor old—that is our conscience. Officials must have a conscience towards the court. It is really the same principle as a merchant’s duty to his customers. ‘Master the arts of letters and arms, then sell them to the imperial house.’ The court is the customer of civil and military officials; it feeds and clothes them. They cannot disregard their consciences towards it. We need not consider conscience in that way.” “What should we consider, then?” “The law. To obey the court’s laws is to satisfy our conscience towards the court.” Zhang nodded and drank in thought. After a long while, he spoke with pleasure. “Old Hu, I think I understand at last. For years I have wondered: among the four callings—scholar, farmer, craftsman and merchant—why does one hear of dishonest merchants, but not dishonest scholars, farmers or craftsmen? Evidently, a merchant’s conscience needs a different explanation. I could never work out what it was. Now I understand. Obey the court’s laws and treat customers fairly: that is conscience, and that keeps one from being a dishonest merchant.” “Exactly! To speak plainly, if merchants obeyed the court’s laws and officials were conscientious towards it, the world would certainly be at peace. More than that: if officials were conscientious, merchants would not dare disobey the law. When officials have no conscience towards the court, to demand that merchants supply it is mere pedantry.” “Yes, yes. Let me think that through.” Zhang spoke as he reflected. “Suppose a Longhair leader is captured and his household’s property confiscated. An official stifles his conscience and pockets the property. That is acting without conscience. But if we act conscientiously? A Longhair offers a deposit under an assumed name, and we refuse because the money ought to be confiscated. What is the result? We simply benefit a corrupt official, who pockets it all the same. Exactly!” He slapped the table and raised his voice. “It is no use for merchants alone to be conscientious towards the court. Obeying the law is enough!” “Old Zhang!” Hu too raised his cup with pleasure. “Now you have truly understood.”

这一顿酒吃得非常痛快；最后是张胖子抢着做的东。分手之时，胡雪岩特别关照，他要趁眷属未到上海来的这两天，将钱庄和阿祥的事安排好；因为全家劫后重聚，他打算好好陪一陪老母，那时什么紧要的大事都得搁下来。张胖子诺诺连声；一回到家先跟妻子商议，那爿小杂货店如何收束？他妻了倒也是有些见识的，听了丈夫的话，又高兴，又伤感；走进卧房，开箱子取出一个棉纸包，打开来给张胖子看，是一支不甚值钱的银镶风藤镯子。做丈夫的莫名其妙，这支镯子与所谈的事有何相干？而张太太却是要从这上头谈一件往事，『这支镯子是雪岩的！就在这支镯子上，我看出他要发达。』她说，『这还是他没有遇到王抚台的时候的话；那时他钱庄里的饭碗敲破了。日子很难过。有一天来跟我说，他有个好朋友从金华到杭州来谋事，病在客栈里；房饭钱已经欠了半个月，还要请医生看病；没有五两银子不能过门，问我能不能帮他一个忙？我看雪岩虽然落魄，那副神气不象倒霉的样子；一件竹布长衫，虽然褪了色，也打过补钉，照样浆洗得蛮挺括，见得他家小也是贤慧能帮男人的。就为了这一点，我「嗯顿」都不打一个，借了五两银子给他。』『咦！』张胖子大感兴趣，『还有这么一段故事，倒没听你说过。钱，后来还你没有？』

They thoroughly enjoyed their drinking, and in the end Zhang insisted on paying. Before they parted, Hu gave him a particular reminder: he wanted the bank and A’xiang’s affairs settled during the next few days, before his family reached Shanghai. Once they were reunited after their ordeals, he meant to spend proper time with his aged mother. Even the most pressing business would have to be put aside. Zhang agreed repeatedly. On arriving home, he first consulted his wife about winding up their little grocery. She had some judgement of her own. His account made her both happy and wistful. Going into the bedroom, she opened a chest and took out a packet of soft cotton paper. She unwrapped it to show him a cheap vine bracelet mounted in silver. Her husband was puzzled. What could it have to do with their discussion? But Mrs Zhang wished to tell an old story. “This bracelet is Xueyan’s. It was this that showed me he would prosper. It happened before he met Governor Wang. He had lost his job at the bank and was having a very hard time. One day he told me that a good friend had come from Jinhua to seek work in Hangzhou and fallen ill at an inn. He owed a fortnight’s room and board and still needed a doctor. Without five taels he could not get through. Could I help? Though Xueyan was down in the world, he did not have the air of a beaten man. His cotton gown was faded and patched, but washed and starched as neatly as ever. That showed he had a capable, virtuous wife to support him. For that reason, I lent him five taels without a moment’s hesitation.” “Really!” Zhang was fascinated. “There was such a story, and you never told me! Did he repay you?”

『你不要打岔，听我说！』张太太说∶『当时雪岩对我说∶』现在我境况不好。这五两银子不知道啥时候能还；不过我一定会还。「说老实话，我肯借给他，自然也不打算他一时会还，所以我说∶『不要紧！等你有了还我。」他就从膀子上勒下这只风藤镯子，交到我手里∶』镯子连一两银子都不值。不能算押头；不过这只镯子是我娘的东西，我看得很贵重。这样子做，是提醒我自己，不要忘记掉还人家的钱。「我不肯要，他一定不肯收回，就摆了下来。『』这不象雪岩的为人，他说了话一定算数的。『』你以为镯子摆在我这里，就是他没有还我那五两银子？不是的！老早就还了。『』什么时候？『『就在他脱运交运，王抚台放到浙江来做官，没有多少时候的事。』『那末镯子怎么还在你手里呢？』

“Do not interrupt. Listen!” Mrs Zhang continued. “Xueyan told me, ‘I am in poor circumstances now. I do not know when I can repay these five taels, but I certainly shall.’ To be honest, since I was willing to lend, I naturally did not expect repayment at once. So I said, ‘Never mind. Repay me when you have it.’ Then he pulled this vine bracelet off his arm and put it in my hand. ‘It is not worth even one tael,’ he said. ‘It cannot count as security.
