Zuo had waited until after Cixi’s birthday before leaving Beijing, with permission to visit his ancestral graves. He reached Changsha, the Hunan provincial capital, on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His first act was to call on Guo Songtao. Their relations were tangled with old favors and grievances. In the eighth year of Xianfeng, when Zuo served on Governor Luo Bingzhang’s staff in Hunan, he decided everything for himself. One day Luo was reading in his office when a gun sounded at the outer gate. As it was not time for the regular noon gun, he asked what had happened. “Adviser Zuo is ceremonially dispatching a memorial,” a servant replied. Luo had not even known that a memorial was being sent. Zuo was virtually the governor of Hunan himself and acquired the nickname “Left Censor-in-Chief.” Governors normally carried the concurrent title of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief: the nickname implied that Zuo exercised still greater power.

其时有个湖南永州镇总兵樊燮，湖北恩施人，声名不佳，有一次去见左宗棠，谈到永州的防务情形，樊燮一问三不知，而且礼貌上不大周到，左宗棠大为光火，当时甩了他一个大嘴巴，而且立即办了个奏稿，痛劾樊燮“贪纵不法，声名恶劣”，其中有“目不识丁”的考语，也不告诉骆秉章就发出去了。樊燮是否“贪纵不法”，犹待查明，但“目不识丁”何能当总兵官？当下光革职，后查办。这“目不识丁”四字，在樊燮心里，比烙铁烫出来的还要深刻，“解甲归田”以后，好在克扣下来的军饷很不少，当下延聘名师教他的独子读书，书房里“天地君亲师”的木牌旁边，贴一张梅红笺，写的就是“目不识丁”四字。他告诉他的儿子说：“左宗棠不过是个举子，就这么样的神气，你将来不中进士，不是我的儿子。”他这个儿子倒也很争气，后来不但中了迸士，而且点了翰林，早年就是名士，此人就是樊增祥。一方面教子，一方面还要报仇。樊熨走门路，告到骆秉章的上司，两广总督官文那里，又派人进京，在都察院递呈鸣冤。官文为此案出奏，有一句很厉害的话，叫做“一官两印”，意思是说有两个人在做湖南巡抚。名器不可假人，而况是封疆大吏，这件事便很严重了。

At that time Fan Xie, brigade commander of Yongzhou in Hunan, was a man of poor reputation from Enshi in Hubei. On one visit, Zuo questioned him about Yongzhou’s defenses. Fan could answer nothing and was less than respectful. Furious, Zuo slapped him hard across the face and immediately drafted a memorial denouncing him as “corrupt, unrestrained, lawless, and notorious.” Among its judgments was “unable to recognize a single written character.” He sent it without informing Luo. Whether Fan was corrupt and lawless remained to be investigated, but how could a wholly illiterate man command a brigade? He was dismissed first and investigated afterward. Those words burned more deeply into him than a branding iron. Once retired, he used the considerable military funds he had withheld to engage distinguished teachers for his only son. Beside the study’s tablet honoring Heaven, Earth, the Sovereign, Parents, and Teachers, he pasted red paper bearing the charge of illiteracy. “Zuo is only a provincial graduate, yet he puts on such airs. Unless you become a jinshi, you are no son of mine.” The son justified his hopes: he not only became a jinshi but entered the Hanlin Academy, winning literary distinction early. He was Fan Zengxiang. While educating his son, Fan also sought revenge. Through influence he appealed to Luo’s superior, Guanwen, described as Governor-General of Liangguang, and sent men to present his grievance at the Censorate in Beijing. Guanwen’s memorial used the formidable phrase “one office, two seals,” meaning that two men were acting as governor of Hunan. Official authority could not be lent to private hands, least of all the authority of a great provincial governor. The matter was serious.

其时郭嵩焘是南书房翰林，他跟左宗棠的胞兄左宗植是儿女亲家，与左宗棠当然很熟，深知他才气过人，便跟同为南书房的翰林潘祖荫说：“左季高如果不在湖南，一走保不住，东南大局，不夏可问。我跟他同乡，又是姻亲，不便进言，老兄何妨上个摺子。”潘祖荫听他的话，果然上了个摺子，铺叙他的功绩以后，作了个结论：“国家不可一日无湖南，即湖南不可一日无左宗棠。”咸丰一看，为之动容，当即传旨问曾国藩，左宗棠是仍旧在湖南好呢？还是调到曾国藩大营中，以便尽其所长。曾国藩回奏，左宗棠“刚明耐苦，晓畅兵机”。于是奉旨随同曾国藩襄办军务。左宗棠因祸得福，多亏得藩祖荫、郭嵩焘，但他对潘、郭的态度，大不相同。对潘祖荫除了“三节两寿”必送一份极厚的礼金以外，知道潘祖荫好收藏金石碑版，当陕甘总督时，凡是关中有新出土的碑，初拓本一走专差送潘祖荫，有时甚至连原碑都送到潘家。

Guo Songtao was then a Hanlin scholar serving in the Southern Study. His child had married a child of Zuo’s elder brother Zuo Zongzhi, so he knew Zuo well and understood his exceptional ability. He approached Pan Zuyin, another Southern Study scholar. “Without Zuo Jigao, Hunan cannot possibly hold out. There would then be no hope for the situation in the southeast. I am his fellow provincial and a relative by marriage; it would be improper for me to speak. Why not submit a memorial yourself?” Pan did so. After recounting Zuo’s achievements, he concluded, “The state cannot do without Hunan for a single day, and Hunan cannot do without Zuo Zongtang for a single day.” Moved, the Xianfeng Emperor asked Zeng Guofan whether Zuo should remain in Hunan or be transferred to his headquarters, where his abilities could be fully used. Zeng replied that Zuo was “firm, clear-sighted, able to endure hardship, and thoroughly versed in military affairs.” An edict assigned him to assist Zeng. Misfortune had become good fortune, thanks largely to Pan and Guo, but Zuo treated the two men very differently. For Pan, he sent generous gifts of money on the customary three festivals and two birthdays. Knowing Pan’s interest in ancient inscriptions and stone monuments, he also sent the first rubbings of newly unearthed Guanzhong steles by special messenger while serving as Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu. Sometimes he sent the original stones themselves.

郭嵩焘是在洪杨失败后，奉旨出任广东巡抚。两广总督名瑞麟，与巡抚同驻广州，“督抚同城”，常不和睦，瑞麟贪而无能，但为内务府出身，有事可直接诉诸两宫太后，靠山很硬，所以郭嵩焘深受其掣肘之苦而无可如何。那知处境本已很难的郭嵩焘，万想不到多年好友。且曾加以援手的左宗棠会跟他为难，为了协饷，除致函指南以外，且四次上奉祈，指摘郭嵩焘，措施如何不然。郭、左失和的原因，有仲付传说，流传最盛的一个说法是，当郭嵩焘放广东巡抚时，湘阴文庙忽产灵芝，郭嵩焘的胞弟郭昆焘写信给老兄，以为是他开府的吉兆。左宗棠得知其事，大为不悦，说“文庙产灵芝。如果是吉兆，亦当应在我封爵一事上面，与郭家何干？“由此生了意见。其实，湘阴文庙产灵芝，是常有之事，左宗棠亦不至于小气到连这种事都要争，真正的原因是，洪杨军兴以后，带兵大员，就地筹饷，真所谓“有土斯有财”。李鸿章最懂得这个道理，所以始终霸住江苏，尤其是上海这个地盘不放，左宗棠却只得浙江一省，每苦不足，看出广东是大有生发之地。所以狠狠心不顾感情友谊，一再攻讦郭嵩焘。最后终于如愿以偿，由他的大将蒋益澧接了郭嵩焘的手。不过蒋益澧的广东巡抚，干不多久就被调走了。

After the Taiping defeat, Guo had been appointed Governor of Guangdong. Ruilin, Governor-General of Liangguang, also resided in Guangzhou. A governor and governor-general in the same city often failed to agree. Ruilin was greedy and incompetent, but his Imperial Household background gave him direct access to both empress dowagers and powerful protection. Guo suffered badly from his obstruction and could do little about it. Difficult though his position already was, he never expected Zuo, an old friend whom he had once helped, to turn against him as well. Over supplementary military contributions, Zuo sent reproachful letters and submitted four memorials criticizing Guo’s administration. Various stories explained their estrangement. The most widespread was that an auspicious lingzhi fungus had appeared in the Confucian temple at Xiangyin when Guo was appointed to Guangdong. His younger brother Guo Kuntao wrote that this foretold good fortune for his new governorship. Zuo supposedly took offense: “If lingzhi in the temple is an omen, it must refer to my ennoblement. What has it to do with the Guo family?” In fact, lingzhi appeared there often, and Zuo was not petty enough to quarrel over such a thing. The real reason lay in military finance. Since the Taiping wars, commanders had raised their own funds: possession of territory meant possession of revenue. Li Hongzhang understood this best and never loosened his grip on Jiangsu, especially Shanghai. Zuo had only Zhejiang, whose resources frequently fell short. Seeing Guangdong’s possibilities, he hardened his heart against friendship and repeatedly attacked Guo. At last his own general, Jiang Yili, replaced him. Jiang’s tenure as Governor of Guangdong, however, was brief; he too was soon transferred.

郭嵩焘因此郁郁不得志。光绪建元，起用在籍大员，他跟曾国荃同被征召至京，曾国荃放了陕西巡抚，因为不愿与陕甘总督左宗棠共事，改任河东河道总督，郭嵩焘则奉派为福建按察史。这在当过巡抚的人来说，是很委屈的，不过他还是接了事。不久，诏命开缺，以侍郎候补，充任出使英国钦差大臣。其时云南发生英国公使翻译马嘉理，越滇缅边境接应英国武装“探路队”，为中国军民所杀，因而引起的很严重的交涉。英国公使咸妥玛表示，郭嵩焘出使英国，如果在国书上表明中国认错字样，可即赴任，否则应候云南案结后再赴英国。总署诸大臣都认为中国不能认错，郭嵩焘亦就不能出国，奉旨署理兵部侍郎，并在总署行走。

Guo remained depressed by his frustrated career. At the beginning of the Guangxu reign, senior officials living in retirement were recalled, and he and Zeng Guoquan were summoned to Beijing. Zeng was appointed Governor of Shaanxi, but, unwilling to serve with Zuo, was transferred to the governor-generalship of the Hedong River Conservancy. Guo became Judicial Commissioner of Fujian. For a former governor, this was humiliating, but he accepted it. Soon afterward he was released from the post, placed on the expectant list for a vice-ministership, and appointed imperial envoy to Britain. At that time the British minister’s interpreter, Margary, had crossed the Yunnan–Burma frontier to meet a British armed surveying party and been killed by Chinese troops and civilians. A serious diplomatic dispute followed. The British minister, Wade, said Guo could leave at once if his credentials acknowledged China’s fault; otherwise he must wait until the Yunnan case was settled. The Zongli Yamen ministers refused such an admission, so Guo could not sail. He was made acting Vice-Minister of War and assigned to the Yamen.

郭嵩焘对办洋务，一面主张公平合理，认为非此不足以析服洋人。他认为马嘉理被杀一案，云南巡抚岑毓英不能说没有责任，当案发以后，意存掩护，又不查明击杀情由，据实奏报，一味倭罪于深山中的野人。而朝中士大夫又因为官兵所杀的是洋人，群起袒护岑毓英，以至于英国更觉不平，态度亦日趋强硬。郭嵩焘以为，这件纠纷固结不解，全由不讲公平、不讲事理之故，因而奉命入总署之日，便单衔上奏，请旨“将岑毓英先后酿成事端之处，交部严加议处，以为恃虚骄之气，而不务沉心观理、考察详情，以贻累国家者戒。”郭嵩焘平时讲洋务，本已为守旧的“卫道君子”所不满，如今居然参劾杀洋人的岑毓英，在他们看，显然是私通外国，因而引起了公愤，连他平素往来密切的朋友、门生，对他亦很不谅解，湖南则有许多人不认他是同乡。此外京师有人做了一副对联骂他：“出乎其类，拔乎其萃，不容于尧舜之世。未能事人，焉能事鬼，何必去父母之邦？“到得第二年七月底，中英订立《烟台条约》，“滇案”解决。郭嵩焘可以启程赴英国了，当时称为“放洋”，而“放洋”以前又发生了一件很不愉快的事。

Guo believed foreign affairs required fairness and reason, without which foreigners could not be persuaded. In his view, Governor Cen Yuying of Yunnan could not disclaim responsibility. After the killing, Cen had sought to protect those involved, failing to establish the circumstances and report them truthfully, and simply blaming remote mountain tribes. Officials at court defended him because the man killed by the troops was a foreigner, making the British feel more wronged and increasingly intransigent. Guo attributed the deadlock entirely to this absence of fairness and reason. On entering the Yamen, he submitted a memorial under his sole name, requesting a strict disciplinary review by the ministry of Cen’s part in provoking the affair, “as a warning to those who rely on empty arrogance instead of calmly examining principles and circumstances, and thereby burden the state.” Conservative defenders of orthodoxy already resented Guo’s views. To impeach a man who had killed foreigners now seemed clear proof of collusion with foreign powers. His action provoked general indignation. Even his close friends and former pupils could not understand him; many Hunan men would no longer acknowledge him as a fellow provincial. In Beijing, someone wrote a mocking couplet: “Outstanding among his kind, surpassing all his fellows—yet unwelcome in an age of Yao and Shun. Unable even to serve men, how can he serve devils? Why must he leave his parents’ land?” At the end of the seventh lunar month of the following year, the Chefoo Convention settled the Yunnan dispute. Guo could finally sail for Britain, but another unhappy incident occurred before his departure.

有个广东人叫刘锡鸿，原任刑部员外郎，此人是郭嵩焘在广东的旧识，谈起洋务来，颇为投机。此时希望跟郭嵩焘一起放洋。但谈洋务是一回事，办洋务又是一回事，郭嵩焘认为刘锡鸿脾气太刚、好意气用事，而办洋务是“水磨工夫”，颇不相宜。哪知刘锡鸿不死心，托出郭嵩焘的一个好友朱孙治来关说。朱孙治向郭嵩焘说：“你批评他不宜办洋务的话，我都跟他说了，他亦很有自知之明，表示一切不问，你只当带一个可以谈谈，以解异国寂寞的朋友好了。”听得这样说，郭嵩焘可怜刘锡鸿穷困不得意，便上奏保他充任参赞。刘锡鸿是个司员，而且只是六品的员外郎，论资格只能当参赞。不过上谕下来，竟是“刑部员外郎刘锡鸿着即开缺，以五品京堂候补，并加三品衔，充出使英国副使”。这种例子，殊为少见，其中有个内幕，军机大臣李鸿藻对郭嵩焘的态度，有此怀疑，怕他出使后，处处帮英国人讲话，因而提拔刘锡鸿，以副使的身分去钳制正使。这刘锡鸿是个不明事理的人，以为李鸿藻派他去当“打手”，所以谢恩以后，便去看郭嵩焘，责问他为何不保他当副使而当参赞？说他不够朋友，另外还有很难听的话，等于是骂了郭嵩焘一顿。

Liu Xihong, a Cantonese formerly serving as an assistant departmental director in the Ministry of Punishments, was an old Guangdong acquaintance with whom Guo had enjoyed discussing foreign affairs. He wanted to accompany him. Talking was one thing, however, and conducting diplomacy another. Guo thought Liu too rigid and impulsive for work requiring patient, delicate effort. Liu persisted, enlisting Guo’s friend Zhu Sunzhi to intercede. Zhu said he had repeated Guo’s criticisms to Liu, who recognized his faults and promised not to meddle: Guo should simply take him as a friend with whom to talk and relieve the loneliness of a foreign country. Moved by Liu’s poverty and lack of prospects, Guo recommended him as a counselor. A mere sixth-rank departmental official, Liu qualified for no higher diplomatic appointment. Yet the edict released him from the Ministry of Punishments, made him an expectant fifth-rank metropolitan court official, added an honorary third-rank title, and appointed him deputy envoy to Britain. Such a precedent was rare. Behind it lay Grand Councillor Li Hongzao’s mistrust of Guo. Fearing that Guo would always take Britain’s side, he had raised Liu to deputy rank to restrain the chief envoy. Liu misunderstood his mission as that of an enforcer. After thanking the throne, he visited Guo and demanded to know why Guo had proposed him only as counselor, rather than deputy envoy. He accused him of failing a friend and added much abusive language.

郭嵩焘气得半死，总是遇到这种恩将仇报的人，只好自怨命中注定。后来刘锡鸿果然处处跟他为难，而且大吵大闹，不顾体统，郭嵩焘写信给李鸿章，形容共事为“鬼嗥于室，狐啸于梁”，公使馆的上下不安，可想而知。其时刘锡鸿已调充驻德公使，可以单衔上奏，彼此互劾，而由于刘锡鸿有李鸿藻撑腰，占了上风。李鸿藻的门下，赫赫有名的“翰林四谏”之一张佩纶，上奏“请撤回驻英使臣”。郭嵩焘大为泄气，一再求去，终于在光绪五年七月改派曾国藩的长子曾纪泽接替郭嵩焘，不过刘锡鸿亦同时垮台，改派郭嵩焘所欣赏的李凤苞使德。这是李鸿章力争的结果。

Guo was furious, but could only blame fate for continually bringing him people who repaid kindness with hostility. Liu indeed obstructed him at every turn and made disgraceful scenes. In a letter to Li Hongzhang, Guo described their service together as “ghosts howling in the rooms, foxes screeching among the rafters.” The unrest throughout the legation was easy to imagine. By then Liu had become minister to Germany and could submit memorials independently. They impeached one another, and Liu’s backing from Li Hongzao gave him the advantage. Zhang Peilun, one of the celebrated Four Hanlin Remonstrants and a follower of Li Hongzao, called for the envoy to Britain to be recalled. Discouraged, Guo repeatedly asked to leave. In the seventh lunar month of Guangxu’s fifth year, Zeng Guofan’s eldest son, Zeng Jize, was appointed to replace him. Liu fell at the same time, however, and Li Fengbao, whom Guo admired, succeeded him in Germany. This was the result of Li Hongzhang’s vigorous intervention.

郭嵩焘在英国博得极好的声望，所以于郭之去，多表惋惜。郭嵩焘原配早死，继室下堂，只带了个姓梁的姨太太赵英，照她的身分是不能觐见维多利亚女王的，竟亦破例特许。但在英国如此，回国后郭嵩焘自知李鸿藻这班人不会放过他，而且已六十二岁，因而决意引退，一到上海即称病，不回京复命，而请开缺，终得如愿以偿，回湖南后住在长沙。身虽在野，并不消极，关于时政，特别是洋务方面，常跟李鸿章、曾国荃书信往米，细作讨论。日子过得也还闲适。这一年，光绪七年，郭嵩焘年初年尾有两件比较快意之事，一件是二月间，调回国充任通政使司参议的刘锡鸿，因为李鸿章敲掉了他的“洋饭碗”记恨在心，奏劾李鸿章跋扈不臣，俨然帝制。李鸿章正在红的时候，刘锡鸿自不量力，出以此举，自然是自讨没趣，上谕斥责其“信口诬蔑，交部议处”。结果竟落得个革职的处分。

Guo had won an excellent reputation in Britain, where his departure was widely regretted. His first wife had long been dead, and his second had been put aside. He had taken only a concubine surnamed Liang to Britain. Her status should have barred an audience with Queen Victoria, yet an exception had been made for her. However well he had been treated there, Guo knew that Li Hongzao’s party would not leave him in peace at home. Already sixty-two, he resolved to retire. On reaching Shanghai he pleaded illness rather than returning to Beijing to report, and requested release from office. His wish was eventually granted, and he settled in Changsha. Retirement did not mean indifference to public affairs. He corresponded frequently with Li Hongzhang and Zeng Guoquan, discussing current policy, especially foreign affairs, in detail. His days were fairly tranquil. In the seventh year of Guangxu, two events, one early and one late, gave him particular satisfaction. In the second lunar month, Liu Xihong, recalled to serve as a councillor in the Office of Transmission, denounced Li Hongzhang as overbearing, disloyal, and practically assuming imperial powers. He resented Li for having broken his diplomatic rice bowl. Li was then at the height of favor, and Liu’s ill-judged attack merely invited humiliation. An edict condemned his “reckless slander” and referred him for disciplinary review. The result was dismissal.

再一件就是左宗棠来拜访。排场阔极，顶马、跟马高脚牌，前听后拥一顶绿呢大轿，内中坐的是头戴宝石顶、双眼花翎、身穿四开褉袍黄马褂，鼻架一副大墨晶镜的东阁大学士烙靖候。首府长沙知府及首县长沙县，早就在郭嵩焘家附近，清道等候。湖南省的藩、两司、候补道等等，亦来站班。可是郭家双扉紧闭，拒而不纳，左宗棠只好在大门口下轿，由戴红顶子的“材官”上门投帖。“不敢当，不敢当！”郭家门上到左宗棠面前，打千说道：“请大人回驾。”左宗棠早已料到有此一着。一点都不生气，和颜悦色地答说：“你跟你家老爷去回，说我是来看五十年的故人，便衣不恭敬，所以穿了官服来的。”门上一进去，久无消息。首县看“爵相”下不了台，硬闯进去跟郭嵩焘打躬作揖，说是“如果不见，全城文武亦都僵在那里了。”请他体恤下情。总算说动了郭嵩焘，开正门迎接，不过他自己只是站在大厅上等候。“老哥！”左宗棠见面便说：“宗棠无状，特来请罪。”接着，拂一拂马蹄袖，捞起四开褉袍下摆，跪了下去。“不敢，不敢！”郭嵩煮也只好下跪答礼。随从官员，将主客二人都搀扶了起来，左宗棠便自责当年的不是，也不解释是为了军饷，“有土斯有财”的缘故，只连声：“是我该死，是我荒唐。”

The other satisfaction was Zuo’s visit. His procession was magnificent: horses before and behind, lofty boards displaying his titles, and crowds of attendants around a great green-covered chair. Within sat the Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and Marquis Kejing, wearing a jeweled hat button, a double-eyed peacock feather, a four-slit robe, and a yellow riding jacket, with large dark crystal spectacles on his nose. The prefect and county magistrate of Changsha had already cleared the streets near Guo’s house and stood waiting. Hunan’s two provincial commissioners, expectant intendants, and other officials also attended. Yet Guo’s double doors remained firmly shut. Zuo had to alight outside and send a red-buttoned military aide with his visiting card. Guo’s doorkeeper came out, made a formal obeisance, and said, “We cannot presume to receive such an honor. Please have Your Excellency’s chair turn back.” Zuo had expected this and showed no anger. “Tell your master that I have come to see a friend of fifty years. Informal clothes would not show sufficient respect, so I have worn my official robes.” The servant went in, and no answer came. Seeing the marquis-grand secretary left in this embarrassing position, the county magistrate forced his way inside and pleaded with Guo: unless he admitted Zuo, all the civil and military officials in the city would remain stranded outside. He begged consideration for their predicament. At last Guo agreed to open the main gate, though he himself waited in the hall. “My old friend,” Zuo said on meeting him, “I behaved disgracefully. I have come expressly to ask your pardon.” He brushed back his horseshoe cuffs, gathered the skirt of his robe, and knelt. “I dare not accept this!” Guo had no choice but to kneel in return. The accompanying officials helped both men up. Zuo reproached himself for his former conduct, making no attempt to explain it by military funding or the need for territory and revenue. He merely repeated, “I deserved to die. I behaved outrageously.”

左宗棠一向健谈，谈西征、谈边防、谈京里的新闻，又从曾国藩谈起往事，一直到中午都没有告辞的意思，郭嵩焘也不便象督抚会客那样“端茶碗送客”，便只好留饭。随从倒是有首县办差，从长沙第一家大馆子玉楼东去叫了酒席来，在附近的关帝庙接待。左宗棠却必须是郭嵩煮的家庖，才是待客之道。好在湘军出身的达官，除了胡林翼以外，都不甚讲究饮食。左宗棠喜欢吃狗肉，称之为“地羊”，有些一味，加上腊味，再炒一盘去骨的东安鸡，在他便是盛馔了。一顿饭吃到未末申初，左宗棠开始兴尽告辞。临行时做个手势，材官递上一个红封套，左宗棠双手奉上，口中说道：“不腆之仪，聊肋卒岁，务请赏收。”郭嵩焘不肯收，左宗棠非送不可。当着好些湖南的文武官儿，郭嵩焘觉得起了争执，有失体统，便收了下来，不过，心里已经打算好了，拆开封套一看，是阜康钱庄所出的一万两银票，当即提起笔来批上“注销”二字，拿个信封装了，送到左宗棠的行辕。照道理是要回拜的，郭嵩焘也免了这套俗礼。左宗棠到头来，还是讨了个没趣。

Zuo was always talkative. He discussed the western campaign, frontier defenses, and news from Beijing, then turned from Zeng Guofan to old times. Noon arrived with no sign of his leaving. Guo could hardly dismiss him by lifting a teacup, as governors did with visitors, and had to invite him to lunch. The county magistrate provided for the attendants, ordering a banquet from Yuloudong, Changsha’s foremost restaurant, to be served at a nearby temple of Guan Di. Zuo, however, must be fed from Guo’s own kitchen if hospitality were to be properly observed. Fortunately, senior men from the Hunan Army, apart from Hu Linyi, were undemanding about food. Zuo liked dog meat, which he called “earth mutton.” A dish of that, some cured meats, and a plate of boned Dong’an chicken made a feast for him. The meal lasted until about three in the afternoon. Only then did his enthusiasm ebb enough for him to leave. At the door he gestured, and a military aide handed him a red envelope. Offering it in both hands, he said, “A modest token to help you through the year’s end. I earnestly beg you to accept it.” Guo refused; Zuo insisted. Before so many Hunan officials, Guo considered a dispute undignified and accepted, having already decided what to do. Inside was a Fukang banknote for ten thousand taels. He immediately wrote “Canceled” across it, put it in another envelope, and sent it to Zuo’s temporary headquarters. Courtesy required a return visit, but Guo dispensed with that convention too. In the end, Zuo had still met with a rebuff.

十二月初二到湘阴，当天晚上，就收到一道由湖南巡抚衙门派专差送来的军机处的“廷寄”。廷寄中说，有人参劾湖广总督李瀚章“任用私人，纵容劣员，该省防军缺额，虚糜帑金，贻害地方，李瀚章本人默货无套，民怨日深。”原奏肿列了李瀚章许多劣迹，其中情节重大者四款：一，湖北全省厘金，岁收三四百万，报部则仅四万。二，竹木税年收百万，报部仅三万。湖广总督衙门每日用银七百五十两，即在此中开支，年耗帑银二十七万余两。三，以公家轮船，载运私货，公然贩卖。四，李瀚章在扬州、芜湖均设有当铺。清朝的规制，凡是督抚被参，视情节轻重作不同的处置。情节较重者，常由京里特派大员，至少是尚书，且须资格较被参督抚为深的，前往查办。为了防备被参督抚事先湮灭证据，所以明发上谕中只说派某人往某地出差，所谓“某地”决非被参督抚所管的省份，譬如说派到四川出差，湖北是必经之地，一到武昌，立即传旨，随带司员马上动手，封库的封库，查帐的查帐、来他一个措手不及。情节轻微，或者有意把案情看得不重，便就近派官阶资格较高音查办或查夏。左宗棠奉到的上谕是：“将所奏各节，确切查明，据实具奏。”这是查夏，不是查办，可是左宗棠不理这一套。

On the second day of the twelfth lunar month, Zuo reached Xiangyin. That evening a special messenger from the governor’s office delivered a confidential dispatch from the Grand Council. It reported an impeachment of Li Hanzhang, Governor-General of Huguang, for employing favorites, indulging corrupt officials, maintaining defense units below their authorized strength while wasting public funds, harming the people, and amassing wealth without restraint. Popular resentment was deepening. Four charges were particularly serious. First, Hubei’s likin revenue amounted to three or four million taels annually, but only forty thousand was reported to the ministry. Second, bamboo and timber duties yielded a million a year, while only thirty thousand was reported. The governor-general’s office spent seven hundred and fifty taels a day from this source, consuming over two hundred and seventy thousand annually. Third, public steamers carried private merchandise for open sale. Fourth, Li owned pawnshops in both Yangzhou and Wuhu. Qing procedure varied according to the gravity of an impeachment against a governor or governor-general. A serious case usually brought a special investigator from Beijing, at least a minister and senior in standing to the accused. To prevent the destruction of evidence, the public edict named another province as his destination. An assignment to Sichuan, for example, required passage through Hubei. On reaching Wuchang, the investigator would proclaim the actual order, and his staff would immediately seal the treasury and inspect the books, taking the accused by surprise. In a minor case, or one the court intended to treat lightly, a nearby official of superior rank and seniority would be appointed to investigate formally or simply ascertain the facts and report. Zuo’s order read, “Establish the truth of each allegation and report the facts.” This was an inquiry for a report, not a formal disciplinary investigation. Zuo disregarded the distinction.

十二月十三到武昌时，李瀚章已经接到李鸿章的通知，知道左宗棠要来查案，需先示意布政使衔候补道杨宗濂告假回籍。此人在成丰末年，以户部员外郎在原籍江苏金坛办团练。同治元年，江苏土绅凑集了十八万银子，雇用英国轮船到安庆，接淮军到上海打太平军时，杨宗濂就是往来奔走接头的人，以此渊源，与李鸿章的关系很深，李鸿章镇压捻军那两年，杨宗濂替他管过营务处，以后一直在湖北当道员。李氏兄弟相继督鄂，李宗濂由“李二先生”的部属变为“李大先生”的部属，管理汉口“新关”。“关差”一向是好差使，汉口是长江的第一个大码头，收入以竹木税为大宗。西南深山中的木材，以湘西辰州为集散地成“木排”，由阮江入洞庭湖，经岳阳入长江，在汉口交易。宗棠早就听湘西的“排客”谈过，汉口“新关”收竹木税的种种弊端，所以一到武昌，就要找杨宗濂。

By the time he reached Wuchang on the thirteenth, Li Hanzhang had been warned by Li Hongzhang that Zuo was coming to investigate. He had prompted Yang Zonglian, an expectant circuit intendant with the honorary title of provincial treasurer, to take leave and return home. In the closing years of Xianfeng, Yang had organized militia in his native Jintan, Jiangsu, while holding rank as an assistant departmental director in the Ministry of Revenue. In Tongzhi’s first year, when Jiangsu gentry raised a hundred and eighty thousand taels to hire British steamers to bring the Anhui Army from Anqing to fight the Taipings at Shanghai, Yang had gone back and forth making the arrangements. This gave him a close connection with Li Hongzhang. During Li’s two years fighting the Nian, Yang had managed his army administration; afterward he remained a circuit intendant in Hubei. As the Li brothers successively governed the province, he passed from the service of “Second Master Li” to that of “Eldest Master Li,” managing Hankou’s New Customs. A customs assignment was always lucrative. Hankou was the Yangtze’s foremost commercial port, and bamboo and timber duties formed its principal customs revenue. Timber from the southwestern mountains was assembled into rafts at Chenzhou in western Hunan, floated down the Ruan River into Dongting Lake, then through Yueyang to the Yangtze for sale at Hankou. Zuo had long heard western Hunan raft merchants describe abuses at the New Customs. On reaching Wuchang, he immediately sought Yang.

由于奉旨查案，所以左宗棠跟李瀚章不作私人的交往，在行辕以一角公文咨湖广总督衙门，“请饬杨宗濂到案备询”，而夏文是“该员业已告假回籍，无从传饬”。这一下左宗棠大为光火，用“札子”下给汉黄德道及武昌府，“催令杨宗濂迅赴江宁问话“。一面出奏：”臣前次回湘，路过新关，杨宗濂避而未见，此次又先朗告假回籍，是否有意规避，虽未可知，而查询杨宗濂素日声名平常、性情浮动，则众论相同，无代其剖白者。“至于经收竹木税有无弊端，”应俟查取票根底薄，传杨宗濂到到案质询，方昭核实“。接着声明：因为须赴两江接任，所以传杨宗濂到江宁备询，同时以”贪鄙狄诈“的考语，请旨将杨宗濂”先行革职，听候查办“。此外汉黄德道何维键、候补知府李谦，都是李瀚章的私人，左宗棠亦毫不客气，对何维键以“庸软无能”四字考语，奏请“开缺送部引见”，意思是请慈禧太后亲自考查，对李谦则谓之“性善圆通、难期振作”，请旨交湖北巡抚彭祖贤“察看”。

Acting under an imperial commission, Zuo avoided private dealings with Li Hanzhang. From his temporary headquarters he sent the governor-general’s office a formal request that Yang be ordered to attend for questioning. The reply stated that Yang had already taken leave and returned home, and could not be summoned. Zuo was furious. He issued directives to the Han–Huang–De circuit intendant and the prefect of Wuchang, requiring them to have Yang proceed promptly to Jiangning for questioning. He also memorialized: “On my previous journey home through the New Customs, Yang Zonglian avoided meeting me. On this occasion he again obtained leave in advance and returned home. Whether this was deliberate evasion cannot yet be known. Inquiries into his ordinary reputation, however, agree that it is undistinguished and his disposition unstable. No one speaks in his defense.” Whether there had been fraud in the bamboo and timber duties must await examination of the receipt counterfoils and original ledgers, together with Yang’s personal interrogation. Zuo explained that, as he had to assume office in Liangjiang, Yang was being summoned to Jiangning. Describing him as “greedy, mean, and deceitful,” he requested Yang’s immediate dismissal pending investigation. He Weijian, the circuit intendant, and Li Qian, an expectant prefect, were also Li Hanzhang’s clients. Zuo spared neither. Calling He “weak and incompetent,” he requested removal from his post and presentation through the ministry for an imperial audience—in other words, examination by Cixi herself. Li Qian was “adept at accommodating himself to others, unlikely to show vigor.” Zuo asked that Governor Peng Zuxian of Hubei keep him under observation.

奏折中还将李瀚章训了一顿，他说：李瀚章一门，遭逢圣时，功名大显，亲党交游，能自立的亦颇不乏人。不过依附者亦很多，当时随从立功，身致富贵者，又各有其亲友，辗转依附，久而久之，恃势妄为，官府处置为难，不能不作姑息，乡里受其欺凌，亦惟有敢怒而不敢言。由于“贤者不肯规之以正，懦者畏其忌嫉，谣诼纷兴、事端叠起，洵非家门之福。宜以身作则，毋与乡邦人士争势竟利，遇事敛抑，免为怨府。其李鸿章、李瀚章所难尽言者，臣等忝仕疆圻，亦当尽心化诲，俾知以义为利，如思保世承家，为报国之本，则李氏亲友之福，亦李鸿章、李瀚章一门之福也”。话说得很不客气，但左宗棠自以为对李瀚章多所开脱，帮了他很大的忙。十二月十九拜发奏折以后，随即坐长江轮船，鼓悼东下，到江宁拜印接任。因为如此，使得胡雪岩扑了个空。原来左宗棠原先的计划是：回湖南原籍祭祖扫墓以后，南下由广东至福建，自厦门坐特派的南洋兵舰到上海，再转江宁接任。这是为了一履旧日百战立功之地，同时还有“南洋大臣”巡海之意。不想一到湘阴，有奉旨查夏李瀚章纵容劣员一案，前后耽误了十一天，不能不走捷径，在年前赶到江宁接任。

The memorial also lectured Li Hanzhang. The Li family, Zuo wrote, had enjoyed an enlightened reign and risen to great distinction. Many relatives and associates could support themselves, but many others lived through dependence. Those who had earned wealth and rank in the brothers’ service had their own friends and relations, creating successive chains of patronage. In time such people abused their influence. Officials found them difficult to punish and tolerated them; local people endured their bullying, angry but afraid to speak. “The worthy will not correct them, while the timid fear their resentment. Slanders multiply and troubles arise one after another. This can scarcely benefit the family. They should lead by example, refrain from contending with their fellow provincials for power and profit, and exercise restraint, lest they become a focus of resentment. Where Li Hongzhang and Li Hanzhang cannot say everything necessary, we who have the honor to hold provincial office should earnestly instruct these people, so they may understand that righteousness is their true advantage. Preserving the family across generations is the foundation of service to the state. Such conduct would benefit both the Li brothers’ relatives and friends and the family itself.” The language was far from gentle, yet Zuo believed he had largely exonerated Li and done him a great service. After ceremonially dispatching the memorial on the nineteenth day of the twelfth month, he took a Yangtze steamer east to Jiangning to receive the seal and assume office. Thus Hu’s journey to meet him came to nothing. Zuo’s original plan had been to visit the ancestral graves, then travel south through Guangdong to Fujian, take a specially dispatched Nanyang warship from Xiamen to Shanghai, and proceed to Jiangning. Besides revisiting the ground of his old campaigns, he intended a coastal inspection in his capacity as Nanyang Minister. The imperial inquiry received at Xiangyin delayed him eleven days, forcing him to take the direct route if he was to assume office before the new year.

“既在如此，小爷叔你回杭州过年吧。”古应春说：“过了年，我陪小爷叔专程到南京去一趟。”“也只好这样子。不过，七姐的病，我实在不放心。”“不要紧的。人是醒过来了，只要慢慢调养，逐渐会好的。医生说：中风这种病，全靠调理。将来总归带病延年了。”胡雪岩跟七姑奶奶情如兄妹，看她人虽醒了，却还不能说话，不过人是认得的，一见双泪交流，嘴唇翕动，不知多少有苦难言，胡雪岩忍不住也掉眼泪。“小爷叔，小爷叔，千万不要如此。”古应春劝道：“这样子反让病人心里难过。”胡雪岩点点头，抹掉眼泪，强作欢颜，坐在病榻前向七姑奶奶说道：“七姐，年底下事情太多，我不能不走。你慢慢调养，我记得你的八字上，说你四十四岁有一关，来势虽凶，凶而不险，过了这一关，寿至七十八。今年年内春，算壬午年，你正好四十四，你这一关应过了，明年秋天，老太太等你来吃寿酒。”七姑奶奶口不能言，却听得懂，只在枕上摆头，表示会意。“还有句，七姐，那种荒唐事情，偶尔一回，以后决不会再做了。”七姑奶奶致疾之由，便是由于气恼胡雪岩的荒唐，所以这句对她是最好的安慰，居然含着泪笑了。

“In that case, Little Uncle, go home to Hangzhou for the new year,” Gu said. “Afterward I shall accompany you on a special visit to Nanjing.” “There seems no other choice. But I cannot stop worrying about Seventh Sister.” “She will be all right. She has regained consciousness; with patient nursing she will gradually improve. The doctor says a stroke depends above all on aftercare. She will have to live on with the illness.” Hu and the Seventh Lady were as close as brother and sister. Though awake, she still could not speak. She recognized him, and tears streamed down her face as her lips moved, full of things she could not say. Hu could not hold back his own tears. “Little Uncle, please do not,” Gu urged. “That only makes her feel worse.” Hu nodded, wiped his eyes, and forced a cheerful expression. Sitting beside the bed, he said, “Seventh Sister, there is so much business at year’s end that I must leave. Take time to recover. I remember your horoscope said you would meet a crisis at forty-four: fierce in its onset, but not truly dangerous. Once past it, you would live to seventy-eight. This year the Beginning of Spring falls before the lunar year ends, so the reckoning is already the renwu year, when you turn forty-four. You have passed the crisis. Next autumn Mother will be waiting for you at her birthday feast.” Unable to speak but understanding him, she moved her head on the pillow to acknowledge his words. “One more thing, Seventh Sister. That foolish conduct was a single lapse. It will never happen again.” Anger at his behavior had brought on her illness, and this was the best comfort he could offer. She even smiled through her tears.

离了病榻，打点回乡。当天晚上，古应春为胡雪岩饯行，只为七姑奶奶在病中，所以在家由厨娘备了几味精致的肴馔，也不邀陪客，只是两人对酌。在餐桌上，采运局的司事送来了一封信，是左宗棠自湘阴所发，告诉胡雪岩因为奉旨赴武昌办案，原来的行程取消，武昌事毕，径赴江宁，约胡雪岩灯节以后，在江宁相会。此外又托胡雪岩查一件事，说是“江苏司关厘局，及鄂湘皖西的督销局，每月均有专拨之饷。其细数如何，乞为密访见示。”胡雪岩看完信，沉吟了好一会说：“我看，左大人对李合肥要动手了。”“喔，小爷叔看出苗头来了？”古应春问道：“怎么样动手法？”“这还言之过早。而且动手也要看机会，不过左大人现在已经有这个意思了。”

Leaving her bedside, Hu prepared to return home. Gu gave him a farewell dinner that evening. With the Seventh Lady ill, they stayed at home, where the cook prepared a few delicate dishes. No other guests were invited; the two men drank alone. During dinner a clerk from the Purchasing and Transport Bureau brought a letter from Zuo, written at Xiangyin. It explained that the imperial order to investigate at Wuchang had canceled his original itinerary. When that business was finished, he would go straight to Jiangning, and wished to meet Hu there after the Lantern Festival. He also requested a discreet inquiry: “The treasury, customs, likin and other bureaus in Jiangsu, together with the salt-sales supervision bureaus in Hubei, Hunan, Anhui and the province abbreviated as Xi, all make earmarked monthly military remittances. What are the exact amounts? Pray inquire confidentially and let me know.” Hu considered the letter for some time. “I believe His Excellency means to move against Li of Hefei.” “You see a sign of it, Little Uncle? How will he act?” “It is too early to say, and action will depend on opportunity. But he already has the intention.”

原来李鸿章的准军有好些部队，驻扎在江苏，湘淮军都是子弟兵，行命将，后招募，募兵成营，即以统率将官之名命名。吴长庆所部名“庆字营”，有一营在江苏，“刘六麻子”刘铭传虽已挟其宦囊，在合肥原籍构筑“大潜山房”，饮酒赋诗，大过儒将的瘾，但“铭字营”的番号依旧，不过由李鸿章拿他们一分为二，一部分由记名提督刘盛休统带，驻山东张秋一带，防守运河要口，一部分交福建提督唐定奎率领，驻防江苏、靖江两县，另有铭字先锋马队之营，驻扎江苏宿迁，主要的任务，亦是防运河沿岸一带有警，可以迅速赴援。李鸿章的淮军中。亦有原为湘军的将领，此人名叫郭松林，他的旧部名为“武毅军”，有十营为江防军，亦驻江阴、靖江境内，有五营为海防军，驻扎上海、宝山两县境内。这些部队，都由江苏发饷。所谓“司关厘局”，司指藩局，关指海关，厘指厘金，局指捐局、税局以及淮盐督销局。两淮出盐，盐课收入为两江一大财源。但上江安徽、下江江苏两省的人吃不完两淮的盐，所以淮盐有指定的销售地区，称为“引局”，分布在鄂、湘、西、皖四个省份，西非山西而是江西。这四省都有淮盐督销局，收入亦归两江。

Several units of Li’s Anhui Army were stationed in Jiangsu. Like the Hunan Army, it consisted of men recruited through personal and local ties. A commander was appointed first and then raised his men; the resulting camps took his name. Wu Changqing’s forces were the Qing camps, one of which was stationed in Jiangsu. Although “Sixth Pockmarked Liu,” Liu Mingchuan, had already carried home his official fortune and built the Daqian Mountain Retreat at Hefei, where he drank, wrote poetry, and thoroughly enjoyed playing the scholarly general, the Ming camps retained their designation. Li had divided them. One part, under Liu Shengxiu, a registered candidate for provincial military command, guarded important canal points around Zhangqiu in Shandong. Another, under Tang Dingkui, the provincial military commander of Fujian, was stationed in two counties named in the text as Jiangsu and Jingjiang. A mounted vanguard camp of the Ming forces stood at Suqian in Jiangsu, chiefly to rush to the aid of places along the canal at the first alarm. The Anhui Army also included a former Hunan Army commander, Guo Songlin. His old forces were known as the Wuyi Army. Ten camps formed river-defense units in Jiangyin and Jingjiang, while five served coastal defense in Shanghai and Baoshan. Jiangsu paid all these troops. The expression “treasury, customs, likin and bureaus” meant the provincial treasury, customs offices, likin administration, contribution and tax bureaus, and the Huai Salt Sales Supervision Bureau. Salt from Lianghuai was an important source of revenue for Liangjiang. Anhui and Jiangsu could not consume the entire output, so designated sales areas, known as salt-certificate districts, extended into Hubei, Hunan, Jiangxi, and Anhui. Here Xi meant Jiangxi, not Shanxi. Each of the four provinces had a Huai Salt Sales Supervision Bureau, whose revenue also belonged to Liangjiang.

“也不回杭州查，也不叫采运局去办，我有个极方便的法子叫老宓写信到各处问一问，就差不多了。”胡雪岩口中的“老宓”，名叫宓本常，宁波人，他是阜丰雪记沪庄的档手。沪庄是阜丰总号，由他分函各地阜丰联号一查“司关厘局”近几个月汇款到淮军后路粮台的数目，每个月的负担，大致就可以算出来了，确是个很方便的办法。“不过，”古应春说：“既然左大人是要攻李合肥，这件事就是隐秘，这样子做法，会不会有风声传出去？”“ 有啥风声传出去？”胡雪岩说：“譬如，你是南昌阜丰的档手，我问你江西淮盐督销局每个月汇到江宁淮军后路粮台的款子有多少？你怎么会想到这是左大人要查了有作用的？”“不错，不错。我是知道了有这么件事，才会顾虑，不知道，我做梦也想不到的。不过，小爷叔，既然各处都是汇到江宁，那又何必费事，只要江宁阜丰查一查，总帐不就出来了？”“啊！啊！”胡雪岩在自己额头上拍了一下，“脑筋不灵了！‘脱裤子放屁’，真是多余的。“于是第二天在上船之前，胡雪岩就办好了这件事，只不过写两封信，一封是写给左宗棠，说江苏各处解交淮军后路粮台的款项，似乎除了委托阜丰以外，另无更简易的通汇之法，所以已函江宁阜丰开单径呈辕门，如有缺漏，另再设法查报。此外叙明，准明年灯节以后，到江宁叩遏。一封是写给江宁阜丰的档手，照办其事。

“There is no need to investigate in Hangzhou or set the Purchasing and Transport Bureau to work,” Hu said. “I have a much easier way. Let Old Mi write to the various places and ask. That should tell us nearly everything.” Old Mi was Mi Benchang of Ningbo, manager of the Shanghai establishment of Fufeng Xueji Bank. Shanghai was Fufeng’s headquarters. If he wrote to its affiliated banks in the various places, asking how much the treasury, customs, and other offices had remitted in recent months to the Anhui Army’s Rear Commissariat, the approximate monthly burden could readily be calculated. It was indeed convenient. “But if His Excellency intends to attack Li, the inquiry must be secret,” Gu said. “Might word of it get out?” “What word? Suppose you managed Fufeng at Nanchang. If I asked how much the Jiangxi Huai Salt Sales Supervision Bureau sent each month to the Rear Commissariat at Jiangning, why would you imagine that Zuo wanted the figures for a particular purpose?” “Quite right. I worry only because I know what lies behind it. Otherwise I should never dream of it. But if all the money goes to Jiangning, why take so much trouble? Have the Fufeng bank there look it up. Would that not give us the total account?” “Ah!” Hu slapped his forehead. “My brain is failing me. Taking off my trousers to fart—quite unnecessary!” Before boarding the boat next morning, he had set the matter in motion with just two letters. One informed Zuo that there seemed to be no simpler way of remitting the Jiangsu offices’ military contributions than through Fufeng. Hu had therefore asked its Jiangning manager to prepare a statement and send it directly to Zuo’s headquarters; any omissions could be investigated and reported afterward. He also confirmed that he would come after the Lantern Festival. The second letter instructed the Jiangning manager to carry this out.

“小爷叔，”古应春问：“开年什么时候来？”“总在上灯前后。”“好！到时候我陪小爷叔一起到南京。”“我当然巴不得你陪了我去，不过，也要看七姐的情形。”“那时候一定不要紧了。”古应春又说：“阿七得病，小爷叔回去了不必提。过年了，何必让老太太记挂。”胡雪岩不答，沉吟了好一会，叹口气说：“我实在没有想到，七姐为了我，会这样子在意。”古应春欲言又止，考虑了一会，终于说了出来，“小爷叔，既然你看出来了，我索性就说吧！阿七为小爷叔担心，也不是一天两天的事了。她常说：树大招风。小爷叔无心结下的怨家，大概不少。这倒还在其次，这几年小爷叔用的人，大不如前，有的本事有限，有的品性不好。她说，她还真不知道小爷叔的眼光，为啥不大灵了？是事情太多太杂，还是精神不济，照顾不到，或者是别有缘故？”胡雪岩脸一红，心知道“别有缘故”四字，是古应春说得含蓄，这“缘故”，说来说去总由于狗皮膏药在作怪。“七姐为我好，我晓得。不过，她实在也担心得稍微过头了。”胡雪岩又说：“等七姐稍微好一点，你同她说：她说我的毛病，我要仔仔细细想一想，结结实实拿它改掉。”“小爷叔这么说，阿七心里一定宽得多。”古应春欣然答说。

“When will you come back after the new year, Little Uncle?” Gu asked. “Around the time the lanterns go up.” “Good. I shall go to Nanjing with you then.” “Nothing would please me better, but it depends on Seventh Sister’s condition.” “She is sure to be well enough by then. And when you go home, do not mention A’qi’s illness. With the new year coming, why make your mother worry?” Hu was silent for some time. At last he sighed. “I truly never imagined Seventh Sister would care so deeply about what happened to me.” Gu hesitated, then decided to speak. “Since you have seen it, Little Uncle, I may as well say so. A’qi has been worrying about you for a long time. She often says a tall tree catches the wind. You must have made many enemies without intending to. That is the lesser concern. In recent years, the people you employ have been much poorer than before: some lack ability, others character. She cannot understand why your judgment has grown less sharp. Is your business too extensive and complicated? Have you less energy to oversee it? Or is there some other reason?” Hu flushed. He knew “some other reason” was Gu’s discreet way of putting it. In the end, the trouble came back to the dogskin plasters. “I know Seventh Sister means well. But she does worry rather more than she need. When she is a little better, tell her I shall think very carefully about every fault she has pointed out and make a thorough effort to correct it.” “That will put A’qi’s mind much more at ease,” Gu replied with pleasure.

第五章 “螺蛳太太”｜CHAPTER FIVE: MADAM LUOSI

胡雪岩这年过年的心境，不如往年，自然是由于七姑奶奶中风，使他有一种难以自解的歉疚之故。不过，在表面上是看不出来的，胡家的年景，依旧花团锦簇，繁华热闹，其中最忙的要数“螺蛳太太”。这个称呼，由来已久，她本姓罗，行四，未嫁以前，是个极能干的小家碧玉，认识她的人，不管老少，都叫她“罗四姐”，算是个尊称。这罗四组慧眼识英雄，在胡雪岩潦倒的时候，接济过他。可惜胡雪岩已经娶了妻子，彼此虽都有爱慕之意，却无从结合。不久，太平军起事，他们纷纷逃去，音信不通，一别九年，方始重逢。胡雪岩记得很清楚，那年是同治六年，他已经奉委主持西征采运局，长驻上海。清明之后不久，胡雪岩的旧侣张胖子去世，在静安寺作佛事，他跟古应春夫妇去祭吊时，看见有个在烧香的淡妆少妇，异常面善，却怎么样也想不起来是在哪里见过。那少妇烧完香，带着个十三四岁的小大姐走了。胡雪岩不死心，悄悄跟在后面，一路走，一路想，到底是什么人？

Hu Xueyan did not enter the New Year in quite the spirits of former years. The Seventh Lady’s stroke had left him with a sense of guilt he could not shake off. Nothing of this showed on the surface, however. The Hu household celebrated with its customary splendor and bustle, and no one was busier than Madam Luosi. The name was of long standing. Her surname was Luo, and she was the fourth in her family. Before her marriage she had been an exceptionally capable young woman of modest background. Everyone who knew her, old or young, called her Luo Sijie—Sister Four Luo—as a mark of respect. She had recognized Hu’s promise while he was still down on his luck and had helped him through his difficulties. Unfortunately, he already had a wife. Though they were fond of each other, they could not marry. Before long the Taiping uprising sent them fleeing in different directions. They lost all news of each other and did not meet again for nine years. Hu remembered their reunion clearly. It was the sixth year of Tongzhi. He had already been appointed to direct the Purchasing and Transport Bureau for the western campaign and spent most of his time in Shanghai. Shortly after Qingming, his old associate Fat Zhang died. Buddhist services were held at Jing’an Temple, and Hu went with Gu Yingchun and the Seventh Lady to pay his respects. There he saw a young married woman, lightly made up, offering incense. Her face was extraordinarily familiar, yet he could not remember where he had seen her. When she had finished, she left with a maid of thirteen or fourteen. Unwilling to let the matter rest, Hu quietly followed, wondering all the way who she could be.

静安寺是上海第一古刹，建于吴大帝赤乌十年，地方很大，原有“静安八景”之称，但那时已只剩下“涌泉”一景，涌泉又称沸井，井中之水终年翻翻滚滚，有如水沸，上海人说它是个海眼。初礼静安寺的人，少不得都要去望一望。那少妇亦不例外，胡雪岩亦步亦趋地跟了过去，装作来看沸井的旅客，驻足不行，以观动静。“阿华，当心，当心，跌到井里，把你小命送掉！”原来那小大姐探头下望沸井，走得很近，身子又往前倾，这个动作很危险，所以那少妇大声警告，一口杭州话帮胡雪岩敲开了记忆之门，又惊又喜地在想：这不是罗四姐？本想冒叫一声，证实了再上前招呼。但游客甚多，而上海的风气虽然比较开通，也还不到西洋人男女可以在稠人广众间公然招呼的程度，因而考虑了一下，回头关照书僮桂生，赶快将七姑奶奶所带来的小大姐叫一个来，越快越好。桂生飞奔而去，他亦不必先告诉七姑奶奶，在七姑奶奶带来的两个小大姐中，找到跟他比较好的彩凤，说一声：“跟我来，有要紧事，快，快！”彩凤只当他闯了什么祸，急急忙忙跟在他身后，桂生等看到胡雪岩的影子，方始停住脚。

Jing’an was Shanghai’s foremost ancient Buddhist temple, founded in the tenth year of Chiwu under the Wu emperor. Its grounds were extensive. Once celebrated for its Eight Views, it now retained only one, the Gushing Spring, also called the Boiling Well. The water churned throughout the year as though boiling, and Shanghai people called it an opening into the sea. A first-time visitor could hardly fail to go and look. The woman was no exception. Hu followed closely, then stopped nearby, pretending to be a traveler examining the well while he watched what she did. “A’hua, be careful! If you fall in, you’ll lose your life!” The maid had gone too close to the edge and was leaning forward to peer down. The danger made her mistress call out loudly. Her Hangzhou accent unlocked Hu’s memory. Could this be Luo Sijie? He was astonished and delighted. At first he thought of calling her name to make sure before approaching. But there were many visitors about. Shanghai might be comparatively liberal, yet it had not reached the Western custom of allowing men and women to greet each other openly in a crowd. After a moment’s thought, he turned to his page Guisheng and told him to fetch one of the Seventh Lady’s maids as quickly as possible. Guisheng ran off. Without first consulting the Seventh Lady, he found Caifeng, the more friendly toward him of the two maids she had brought. “Come with me. Something important. Quick!” Thinking he had got himself into trouble, she hurried after him. Only when Hu came into sight did Guisheng stop.

“是我们老爷要叫你。”“彩凤，”胡雪岩悄悄指点：“你上去问她，是不是杭州的罗四姐？如果她说是，你就说我们奶奶是胡老爷的亲戚，请她跟你们奶奶去见一见。”彩凤很伶俐，想了一下问：“如果她不肯去呢？”“你就回过头来看我，她就一定肯去了。”果然，一如胡雪岩的估计，只见彩凤上前搭话时，仿佛有难以沟通的情状，然后是彩凤先回头来看胡雪岩，接着是那少妇随着她的视线所示来搜索，遥遥望去，显得相当震动似地。胡雪岩知道成功了，赶紧转身直奔作为堂客休憩之地的一座禅房，找到七姑奶奶的另一个小大姐，关照请她的主母出来叙话。“七姐，我同你谈过的罗四姐，你还记得记不得？”七姑奶奶想了一下，点点头说：“记得。”“她今天在这里，我叫彩凤‘假传圣旨’，说你同我是亲戚，请她来见面。马上就要来了。七姐，你请她到你那里去，仔仔细细问问她，她好象居孀在那里。”“好，好！”七姑奶奶连连答应，又问，“小爷叔，你呢？”“我到钱庄里、有桩要紧事情料理好了，马上来。”

“It’s our master who wants you.” Hu pointed the woman out discreetly. “Caifeng, go and ask whether she is Sister Luo from Hangzhou. If she says yes, tell her that your mistress is a relative of Mr Hu’s and would like her to come over and meet her.” Caifeng was quick-witted. She considered this and asked, “What if she refuses?” “Just turn and look at me. Then she will certainly agree.” Events followed his prediction. When Caifeng approached the woman, there seemed at first to be some difficulty in making herself understood. Then she looked back at Hu. The woman followed her gaze, searching until she found him in the distance, and appeared deeply shaken. Hu knew that his plan had worked. He immediately turned and hurried to a monastic room set aside for the women guests. Finding the Seventh Lady’s other maid, he asked her to bring her mistress out for a word. “Seventh Sister, do you remember the Sister Luo I told you about?” After a moment she nodded. “I do.” “She is here today. I have had Caifeng issue a false imperial decree in your name: she has told her we are relatives and you want to meet her. She’ll be here any moment. Invite her home, Seventh Sister, and ask her carefully about her circumstances. She seems to be living as a widow.” “Of course, of course! And what about you, Little Uncle?” “I must go to the bank. As soon as I have dealt with something important, I’ll come straight over.”

等胡雪岩走了好一会，才看到彩凤领着莲步姗姗一个俏括括的素服少妇，扶着小大姐的肩头，冉冉而来。七姑奶奶性子急，撇开一双大脚，迎了上去。“是不是罗四姐？”“不敢当。我姓罗，尊姓？”“我夫家姓古，娘家姓尤，行七，我们小爷叔叫我‘七姐’。罗四姐你也这样叫我好了。”七姑奶奶是直性子，一古脑儿都说了出来。在罗四姐听，却有些牛头不对马嘴，既是“小爷叔”，何以又叫她“七姐”？但这个疑团，还在其次，眼前有句最要紧的话先要问清楚，才谈得到其他。“请问，古太太你的‘小爷叔’是哪个？”“还有哪个？不就是你老早认识的胡雪岩，鼎鼎大名阜康钱庄的老板。”罗四姐又惊又喜。她也曾听说过，阜康钱庄的老板，就是从前在张胖子那里做伙计的胡雪岩，一直想打听，苦无机会。不想真的有这回事。“罗四姐，”七姑奶奶说，“你听我叫他小爷叔，就晓得我们是自己人。你一定要请到我那里去坐一歇。你当年待我们小爷叔的好处，他也跟我说过。等下他也要来的。“罗四姐心想：胡雪岩倒真是有良心的！就这一转念间，心里顿时七上八下在翻动了。“罗四姐，”七姑奶奶催问着：“你肯不肯赏面子。”“唷，古太太，你的话太客气了。真正不敢当。”

Hu had been gone some time before Caifeng appeared with an attractive young woman in plain mourning clothes. Resting a hand on her maid’s shoulder, she advanced slowly with delicate steps. The impatient Seventh Lady strode forward on her unbound feet to meet her. “Are you Sister Luo?” “You are too kind. My name is Luo. May I ask yours?” “My husband’s name is Gu, my maiden name You, and I am the seventh in my family. Our Little Uncle calls me Seventh Sister. Please call me that too.” Frank as ever, she poured everything out at once. To Luo, it did not quite make sense. Why should someone she called Little Uncle call her Seventh Sister? That puzzle could wait. One more pressing question had to be settled first. “May I ask, Mrs Gu, who is this Little Uncle of yours?” “Who else but your old acquaintance Hu Xueyan, owner of the famous Fukang Bank?” Luo was both surprised and delighted. She had heard that Fukang’s proprietor was the Hu Xueyan who had once worked for Fat Zhang. She had long wanted to inquire but had found no opportunity. So it really was true. “You can tell from my calling him Little Uncle that we are close, Sister Luo. You must come and sit with me at home. He has told me how kind you were to him in the old days. He will be coming over shortly.” Hu had not forgotten her kindness after all! The thought set Luo’s heart in a turmoil. “Will you do me the honor, Sister Luo?” the Seventh Lady urged. “Oh, Mrs Gu, you are far too courteous. I really don’t deserve it.”

于是七姑奶奶向丧家致意告辞，将罗四姐主婢二人带回家。一看她家的气派，七姑奶奶又热心伉爽，罗四姐决心要结交，因而改了称呼，同时深谈身世。原来罗四姐当年随父母逃避战乱，转徒千里，流离途中，父母双亡，不然一身，不是了局，只有择人而事，结伴同行，一共有三家，其中两家都有个尚未婚娶的二十来岁的儿子，当然亦都时时在找机会向她献殷勤。这两家一富一穷，而罗四姐挑了穷的那家，姓程，是独子。“七姐，我是因为他虽穷，肯上进，只要他肯上进，我就有把握帮他出头。再说，上头只有一个老娘，不比另外一家，父母双全，还有三个兄弟，两个妹妹，嫁过去做媳妇，一定象顶石臼做戏，吃力不讨好。”“罗四姐，换了我，也会象你一样，宁愿挑这一位。”七姑奶奶早就发现她鬓边戴一朵白头绳结的菊花，却故意问说：“我们程姐夫呢？几时请过来见一见。”“不在了。”罗四姐凄然说道：“是前年这个时候去世的。”“可怜，可怜！”七姑奶奶紧握着她的手，但有无言的慰藉。

After taking leave of the bereaved family, the Seventh Lady brought Luo and her maid home. The style of the household, together with her hostess’s warmth and generosity, convinced Luo that she wanted to cultivate this friendship. She adopted the more intimate form of address and began to speak freely of her life. She had fled the fighting with her parents, traveling a thousand li in their wanderings, and both had died on the road. Remaining entirely alone was no solution; she had to choose someone to marry. They had been traveling in a party of three families. Two of the other families had unmarried sons in their twenties, both continually looking for opportunities to show her attentions. One family was rich and the other poor. Luo chose the poor family’s son, an only child named Cheng. “Seventh Sister, I chose him because, poor as he was, he wanted to make something of himself. So long as he had that ambition, I was confident I could help him rise. Besides, he had only an old mother. The other man had both parents, three brothers, and two sisters. Marrying into that household would have been like performing a play with a stone mortar on my head—all effort and no thanks.” “I would have chosen as you did, Sister Luo.” The Seventh Lady had already noticed the chrysanthemum made from white hair cord at her temple, but deliberately asked, “And where is Brother-in-Law Cheng? When will you bring him to meet us?” “He is gone,” Luo answered sadly. “He died at this time the year before last.” “Poor thing. Poor thing.” The Seventh Lady clasped her hand, offering the comfort for which there were no words.

“说起来也怪我不好。”罗叫姐说：“他学的是刻字匠手艺。有一回他跟我谈起，说是长毛打到杭州的前两年，乡试考举人，他跟他师父一起到考场里去刻题目纸，熬夜熬到天亮，心里在想：我也读过书，一样是熬夜，为啥不是去考举人，坐在这里当个低三下四的刻字匠，人家举子写借了字，顶多贴出‘蓝榜’，我刻错一个字要打手心，‘吃生活’？我就说：“你果然有心，把招牌收起来，好好儿读书。开门七件事都是我管，用不着你费心。‘他真的就听我的话，三更打灯五更鸡，闷倒头读书……”“罗四姐”，七姑奶奶打断她的话问：“你这开门七件事，怎么管法？”“我绣花，不光是绣花，还替绣庄去收件，到后来做‘小包’，一批绣货包下来，再分给人家去做，日子过得很舒服。七姐，上海滩繁华地方，遍地银子，只要你肯花工夫去捡。不瞒你说，我就不相信，世界上有饿死的人。饿死的人是有，那是因为有钱买不到米，不是没有铜钱买米。这不一样的。七姐，你说是不是？““怎么不是？”七姑奶奶笑道：“你的说法，倒跟小爷叔很象。”她紧接着又问：“后来呢？”

“In a way, it was my fault,” Luo said. “He had learned the woodblock cutter’s trade. Once he told me that, two years before the Longhairs reached Hangzhou, he and his master went into the examination compound to cut the blocks for the provincial examination papers. He worked through the night until dawn, thinking: ‘I have studied too. If I must stay up all night, why shouldn’t I be sitting the examination for a juren degree, instead of working here as a lowly block cutter? If a candidate writes a wrong character, at worst there is a notice on blue paper. If I cut one wrong character, they beat my palms. I get a thrashing!’ So I told him, ‘If you really mean it, take down your shop sign and devote yourself to your books. Leave all seven daily household necessities to me. You needn’t worry about them.’ He took me at my word and studied with his head down, burning his lamp in the third watch and rising with the cock in the fifth…” “Sister Luo,” the Seventh Lady interrupted, “how did you provide those household necessities?” “I embroidered. And not only that: I collected work for embroidery shops. Later I became a small contractor, taking on a whole batch and distributing it among other women. We lived very comfortably. Shanghai is a prosperous place, Seventh Sister. There is silver lying everywhere, if only you are willing to take the trouble to pick it up. To tell you the truth, I don’t believe anyone need starve. People do starve, of course, but because there is no rice to be bought, even with money—not because they have no cash to buy it. That is a different matter. Wouldn’t you say so?” “Certainly!” The Seventh Lady smiled. “You sound very much like Little Uncle. What happened then?”

“后来杭州光复了。他同我说，考秀才要到杭州去考，将来举人也是杭州考，家一搬到杭州，你的这点基础，就要抛掉了。不如捐个监生，下回直接进京去考举人，头一年秋天考中了，第二年春天再考进士。如果在浙江考中了举人，考进土还是要进京。一番手续两番做，反而不划算。我想想不错，凑了二百两银子，替他捐了个监生，他就更加用功了。唉！”罗四姐叹口气，说不下去了。“用功用出毛病来了？”练达人情的七姑奶奶问说。“先是吐血。”罗四奶用低幽但很平静的声音说。 “他还瞒着我，吐血吐到手帕里，手帕自己去洗。脸色越来越白，到了下半天，颧骨上倒象搽了胭脂，我懵懵懂懂，还不当它一回事。有一天他有应酬回来，我替他脱袍子，随手在口袋里一摸，摸出一条上有血迹的手帕，才晓得他是痨病。”“痨病？”七姑奶奶神色紧张，“后来呢，照样还是赶考去了？”“没有。他这样子怎么能赶考？”“以后呢？”以后自然是养病。痨病俗称“馋痨病”，想吃这个，想吃那个，罗四姐总依着他的性子去办，办来了，却又浅尝即止，剩下来的不仅是食物，还有他的歉疚。“我听人说，痨病只要胃口好，还不要紧，象他那样子，馋是馋得要命，胃口一点都没有。人一天比一天瘦，不过三个月的工夫。唉！”罗四姐又是一声长叹。

“After Hangzhou was recovered, he told me he would have to go back there to take the examination for a xiucai degree, and later the provincial examination as well. If we moved, all I had built up here would be lost. It would be better to purchase Imperial Academy student status and go straight to Beijing next time to sit for the juren degree. If he passed in the autumn, he could take the jinshi examination the following spring. Even if he won his juren in Zhejiang, he would still have to go to Beijing for the jinshi. Doing in two stages what could be done in one would be less economical. I thought he was right and scraped together two hundred taels to purchase the qualification for him. Then he studied harder than ever. Ah…” She sighed and could not continue. “Did the studying damage his health?” asked the Seventh Lady, who understood the ways of the world. “First he began coughing blood,” Luo said, quietly but calmly. “He hid it from me. He coughed into his handkerchief and washed it himself. His face grew paler and paler, yet in the afternoons his cheekbones looked as though he had put rouge on them. I was foolish and thought nothing of it. One day he came home from an engagement. I helped him take off his robe and happened to put my hand into a pocket. There was a bloodstained handkerchief. Only then did I realize he had consumption.” “Consumption?” The Seventh Lady looked alarmed. “Did he still go to the examinations?” “No. How could he, in that condition?” “What happened afterward?” Afterward, naturally, he tried to recover. People called consumption the craving sickness: the sufferer longed for one thing after another. Luo always procured whatever he wanted, but once it arrived, he took only a taste. What remained was not merely uneaten food, but his guilt. “I had heard that with a good appetite, consumption was not too serious. But he had terrible cravings and no appetite at all. He grew thinner every day. In only three months… Ah!” She sighed again.

七姑奶奶不必再谈她的丈夫，觉得要关心的是罗四姐，“你现在住在哪里？”她问。“南市。天主教堂后面。”“日子过得很艰难吧？”“也还好。”罗四姐淡淡地答说。“有没有伢儿？”“没有。”罗四姐口中干脆，内心不免抱歉。“既无儿女，年纪也离‘老’字还早……”七姑奶奶突然咽住。毕竟还是第一次见面，哪里能谈得那么深。看看没有话了，罗四姐便即告辞：“七姐，我要走了。”一面说，一面站了起来，“明天我再来看你。”“不，不！”七姑奶奶急忙拦阻，“何必等到明天？我们一见如故，你不要见外，在我这里吃了饭，我再拿马车送你回去。”罗四姐原是没话找话，并没有想走的意思，见她留客之意甚殷，落得将顺。“七姐的话，一点不错。”她复又坐了下来，“我也觉得我们一见如故，大概是前世的缘分。”“罗四姐，你说到‘前世的缘分’，我就更不肯放你回去了。”七姑奶奶的心又热了，“你这个样子不是个了局。守寡这回事，看起来容易，其买很难，我劝你……”她的话没有说完，但要劝的是什么，却无需明言，就会知道。于是，罗四姐很坦率地答说：“我也不想造‘节孝坊’，不过，这回是要好好挑一挑了。”

There was no need to ask more about her husband. The Seventh Lady felt it was Luo herself who now needed concern. “Where are you living?” “In the southern city, behind the Catholic church.” “Life must be very difficult?” “I manage,” Luo answered without emphasis. “Any children?” “No.” Her answer was brisk, though inwardly she could not help feeling apologetic. “With no children, and still a long way from being old…” The Seventh Lady stopped short. This was their first meeting, after all; she could hardly go so far. As the conversation faltered, Luo rose. “Seventh Sister, I must leave. I’ll come to see you again tomorrow.” “No, no!” Her hostess stopped her at once. “Why wait until tomorrow? We have taken to each other like old friends. Don’t stand on ceremony. Stay for dinner, and I’ll send you home in the carriage.” Luo had only been saying something to fill the silence; she had no real wish to leave. With so warm an invitation, she was happy to comply. “You are quite right, Seventh Sister.” She sat down again. “I feel we have known each other forever. Perhaps we were connected in a former life.” “If you speak of a bond from a former life, I’m still less willing to let you go.” The Seventh Lady’s heart warmed further. “You cannot go on like this. Remaining a widow looks easy, but it is very hard. My advice is…” She did not finish, but there was no need to explain what she meant. Luo answered frankly, “I have no ambition to have a chastity arch raised in my honor. But this time I must choose very carefully.”

正在谈着，胡雪岩来了，“果然是罗四姐！”他怔怔地望着她，心中百感交集，有无数的话要说，但都堵在喉头，竟不知说哪一句好。相形之下，罗四姐反显得比较沉着，站起来说道：“从前我叫你的名字，现在不晓得叫你啥好？”“你仍旧叫我雪岩好了。”“这不象样。你现在是大老板，哪里好直来直去叫名字，也忒嫌没分寸。”“这样好了，”七姑奶奶插嘴说道：“大家都叫他胡大先生，或者大先生，罗四姐，你也这样叫好了。”“好的，好的。这是禀称。大先生，我们没有见面有九年了吧？”胡雪岩默默算了一下，“九年！”他说，“虽说九年，同隔世一样。杭州光复之后，左大人叫我办善后，我叫人到处访你，音信毫无，那时候你在哪里？”“我已经在上海了。”“喔，怎么会到了上海了呢？”“这话说起来就长了。”七姑奶奶心想，罗四姐这一谈身世遭遇，要费好些辰光，她是已听说过了，不必在此白耗工夫，便即起身说道：“罗四姐，小爷叔，你们都在这里便饭，我去料理一下，你们慢慢谈。”所谓料理，只是交代几句话的事，一是到馆子里叫菜，二是通知古应春，家中有客，胡雪岩也在，晚上有饭局最好辞掉。回家来陪客。然后坐在客厅间壁的小房间中，打开了房门，一面闭目养神，一面听他们叙旧。

While they were talking, Hu arrived. “It really is Sister Luo!” He gazed at her, overwhelmed by conflicting feelings. Countless things he wished to say crowded his throat, and he could not decide where to begin. Luo seemed the more composed of the two. Rising, she said, “I used to call you by your name. Now I don’t know what to call you.” “Go on calling me Xueyan.” “That would hardly be proper. You are a great proprietor now. To keep calling you by your name would show no sense of what is fitting.” The Seventh Lady intervened. “Everyone calls him Mr Hu, or simply Sir. You may do the same, Sister Luo.” “Very well. That is a respectful form. Sir, it must be nine years since we last met?” Hu calculated silently. “Nine years! Yet it feels like another lifetime. After Hangzhou was recovered, Governor-General Zuo put me in charge of relief and restoration. I had people inquire for you everywhere, without the slightest news. Where were you then?” “Already in Shanghai.” “How did you come to Shanghai?” “That is a long story.” The Seventh Lady thought the account would take some time. Having heard it already, she need not sit there idly. She stood up. “Sister Luo, Little Uncle, you are both staying for dinner. I’ll see to it. Take your time talking.” All she needed to do was give a few instructions: order dishes from a restaurant and send word to Gu that there was a guest, Hu was there too, and he should cancel any dinner engagement if he could and come home to help entertain them. Then she sat in a small room adjoining the sitting room, with the door open, resting her eyes and listening to the old friends reminisce.

“罗四姐，”她听见胡雪岩在说，“你从前帮过我许多忙。现在我总算立直了，不晓得不啥地方可以帮你的忙，请你尽管说。”“多谢你。你也还混得落，到我混不落去的时候，再请你大先生帮忙。”“你一个人这样混也不是一个了局。”听得这话，七姑奶奶心中一动，悄悄起身，遥遥相望，只见胡雪岩与罗四姐四目凝视，心里在想：他们那一段旧情，又挑起来了。她猜得不错。胡雪岩觉得九年不见，罗四姐变了，从前是一根长辫子甩来甩去，走路腰扭得很厉害，左顾右盼，见了陌生人不会脸红的小家碧玉，如今沉静得多了，皮肤也白净得多了，瓜子形的清水脸上，那一双黑白分明的眼睛，不似从前那么灵活，但偶尔瞟他一眼，仿佛有无数心事要倾诉似地。最动人的是堕马髻旁戴一朵白头绳结成的菊花。胡雪岩选色，喜欢年轻孀妇，所以这朵带孝白菊花，最逗人遐思。“这样好不好，”胡雪岩说：“我帮你在杭州开一家绣庄。”“不！我不想回杭州。”“为啥呢？”“在上海住惯了。”“那么，绣庄就开在上海？”“多谢你。”罗四姐说，“等我想一想。”

“Sister Luo,” she heard Hu say, “you helped me so much in the old days. Now I can at last stand on my own feet. If there is anything I can do for you, please say so.” “Thank you. I can still get along. When I can no longer manage, I shall ask for your help, Sir.” “But living alone like this is no lasting solution.” The Seventh Lady’s interest stirred. She rose quietly and looked in from a distance. Hu and Luo were gazing into each other’s eyes. Their old affection had been rekindled, she thought. She was right. Hu felt that Luo had changed during their nine years apart. In the old days she had been a young woman of modest means whose long braid swung to and fro, whose waist swayed briskly as she walked, and whose eyes were always glancing about. Strangers never made her blush. Now she was much quieter, and her complexion had grown fairer and clearer. The sharply contrasted black and white of her eyes, set in an unpainted oval face, no longer moved about as restlessly as before. Yet an occasional glance at him seemed charged with countless things she wished to tell. Most touching of all was the chrysanthemum of white cord beside her loose, drooping hair knot. Hu had a particular taste for young widows, and this white flower of mourning stirred his imagination more than anything. “What do you think of this?” he asked. “Let me help you open an embroidery shop in Hangzhou.” “No. I don’t want to return to Hangzhou.” “Why?” “I am used to living in Shanghai.” “Then open it in Shanghai?” “Thank you,” she said. “Let me think it over.”

七姑奶奶很想再听下去，但古应春回来了，不能不抢先一步截住他，略略说了生客的来历，方始带他到客厅，与罗四姐见面。“喔，”罗四姐很大方地捡袄为礼，口中叫一声：“七姐夫。”是这样亲近的称呼，使得古应春很快地消失了陌生感，象跟熟人那洋谈了起来。不久，馆子里送了菜来，相将入席，大家都尊罗四姐上坐，她说什么也不肯，结果依旧是胡雪岩首座一张八仙桌，主客四人，各占一方。“罗四姐会吃酒的。”胡雪岩对七姑奶奶说，“而且酒量好得很。”“这样说，葡萄酒是太淡了。”七姑奶奶问说：“罗四姐，你喜欢哪种酒，烫花雕来好不好？”“谢谢。我现在酒不吃了。”“为啥要戒酒？”七姑奶奶说：“你一个人，正要吃酒，一醉解千愁。”“你看你！”古应春埋怨地说：“你没有吃酒，倒在说醉话了。人家罗四姐日子过得好好地，何必借酒浇愁？”“好！算我说错了。”七姑奶奶让步，复又劝客人：“你为我开戒，我陪你吃两杯。”“不敢当，不敢当。七姐一定要我吃，我就吃。”“守和好。你说，吃啥酒？”“你吃啥，我吃啥。”“我是吃了好玩儿的。只怕你不喜欢。”

The Seventh Lady would have liked to listen longer, but Gu had returned. She had to intercept him, explain briefly who their new guest was, and then bring him into the sitting room. “Ah, Brother-in-Law Gu.” Luo gathered her jacket neatly and made her greeting with easy grace. The intimate form of address soon dispelled Gu’s feeling of unfamiliarity, and he talked to her as he would to an old acquaintance. Before long the restaurant dishes arrived and they went in to dine. Everyone urged Luo to take the place of honor, but she would not hear of it. In the end Hu occupied it as usual. The four of them sat one on each side of a square table. “Sister Luo can drink,” Hu told the Seventh Lady. “And she has an excellent capacity.” “Then grape wine will be too light. What do you prefer, Sister Luo? Shall we warm some Huadiao?” “Thank you. I no longer drink.” “Why give it up? Living by yourself, you need a little wine. One good bout of drinking dissolves a thousand sorrows.” “Listen to yourself!” Gu reproached her. “You sound drunk before you have touched a drop. Sister Luo is managing perfectly well. Why should she drown her sorrows?” “Very well, I spoke out of turn.” The Seventh Lady yielded, then urged her guest again. “Break your rule for me. I’ll have a couple of cups with you.” “You are too kind. If you insist, I will.” “Then that is settled. What shall we have?” “Whatever you have.” “I only drink for amusement. I’m afraid you may not like it.”

七姑奶奶到柜子里取来一瓶薄荷酒，葫芦形的瓶子，碧绿的酒，非常可爱，倒将罗四姐的酒兴引发了。“我也吃杯薄荷酒。”胡雪岩凑趣，举杯在手，看着七姑奶奶说：“我劝罗四姐开一家绣庄，你们看好不好？”“大先生，我想过了”。罗四姐接口说道：“多谢你的好意，我是力不从心。本钱虽归你出，也要人手，我一个人照应不过来。”“那怕什么？请七姐帮你的忙，外场请应春照应。另外我再派两个老成靠得住的伙计给你。你做现成的老板好了。”“吃现成饭也没啥意思。”言语有点谈不拢。古应春觉得这件事暂时以不谈为妙，便将话扯了开去，作主人的当然要拣客人熟悉或感兴趣的话题，所以自然而然地谈到了“顾绣”。中国的刺绣分三派，湖南湘绣、苏州苏绣以外，上海独称“顾绣”，其中源远流长，很有一段掌故，罗四姐居然能谈得很清楚。“大家都晓得的，顾绣是从露香园顾家的一个姨太太传下来的。我现在住的地方，听他们说就是露香园的基址……”

The Seventh Lady fetched a bottle of mint liqueur from a cabinet. Its gourd-shaped bottle and emerald-green contents were so attractive that Luo’s appetite for a drink revived. “I’ll have some too,” Hu said, joining in the spirit of the occasion. With his glass in hand, he looked at the Seventh Lady. “I have been urging Sister Luo to open an embroidery shop. What do you think?” “Sir, I have considered it,” Luo interposed. “Thank you for your kindness, but it is beyond my strength. Even if you supply the capital, there must be people to do the work. I could not oversee it all alone.” “Why worry about that? Ask Seventh Sister to help, and let Yingchun look after outside business. I’ll send you two reliable, experienced assistants as well. You need only be the proprietor of a business ready-made for you.” “There is not much satisfaction in having everything handed to me.” The conversation was beginning to go awry. Gu thought it better to leave the matter for the time being and changed the subject. As host, he naturally chose something familiar or interesting to the guest, and so they came to Gu embroidery. Chinese embroidery fell into three schools: Hunan’s Xiang embroidery, Suzhou’s Su embroidery, and the Shanghai style uniquely called Gu embroidery. The last had a long history and a considerable tradition behind it. Luo proved surprisingly well able to explain it. “Everyone knows that it was handed down by a concubine of the Gu family at Luxiang Garden. They tell me the place where I now live stands on the garden’s old grounds…”

露香园在上海城内西北角，先是明朝道州知府顾名儒所建，本名“万竹山居“。顾名儒的胞弟叫顾名世，嘉靖三十八年的进士，官拜尚宝丞，告老还乡，宦囊甚丰，看万竹山居东面的空地尚多，于是拓宽来开辟一座池塘，哪知此地本来就是池，有掘出来的一块石碑为证。碑上刻的是”露香池“三字，而且是赵子昂的手笔。因此，顾名世将万竹山居改名”露香园“，那座池塘当然一仍其旧，依然叫做”露香池“。顾名世的姬妾很多，其中有一个姓缨，她在京城的时候，学会了刺绣，而且是宫中传出来的诀窍，缨姨娘在这方面有天才，更加改良，益见精妙。五色丝线孽，细针密缕，颜色由浅入深，浑然一体，配色之美，更不在话下。最见特色的是，顾绣以针代笔，以丝钱作丹青，以名迹作蓝本，山水、人物、花鸟，无不气韵生动，工细无匹，当时称为“画绣”。缨姨娘曾经仿绣赵子昂的《八骏图》，董其昌认为即使是赵子昂本人用笔，亦未见得能胜过她。又绣过一幅《停针图》，真是穷态极研，而且无法分辨是画，是绣。后来由扬州的一位监商，拿一个汉玉连环，及南唐名家周昉作画的一幅美人图交换了去。由于缨姨娘的教导，露香园的女眷，下至丫头，都会刺绣，而且极精，“画绣”之名大著，顾名世本人的名字，反而不为人所知，以至于顾名世有一次酒后大发牢骚，说他“寄名于汝辈十指之间”。

Luxiang Garden stood in the northwestern corner of the walled city. Gu Mingru, a Ming prefect of Daozhou, had originally built it under the name Retreat of Ten Thousand Bamboos. His younger brother Gu Mingshi became a jinshi in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing and rose to Assistant Director of the Imperial Seals Office. Retiring home with a substantial fortune from his official career, he saw that much ground remained vacant east of the retreat and enlarged it, digging a pond. The site proved to have held a pond before: an unearthed stone inscription supplied the evidence. It bore the words “Dew-Fragrance Pond,” in Zhao Zi’ang’s own calligraphy. Gu Mingshi therefore renamed the retreat Luxiang Garden, the Garden of Dew Fragrance, and naturally restored the pond’s old name. Among his many concubines was one surnamed Ying. While in Beijing she had learned embroidery, including techniques passed down from the palace. Gifted in the craft, she improved on them until her work became still more exquisite. With fine needles and close stitches, her silks of five colors blended seamlessly from light to dark; the beauty of her color combinations went without saying. Above all, Gu embroidery used the needle for a brush and silk thread for pigment, taking famous paintings as models. Landscapes, figures, flowers, and birds all possessed a living spirit and unrivaled delicacy. It was then known as “painted embroidery.” Mistress Ying once embroidered a version of Zhao Zi’ang’s Eight Steeds. Dong Qichang declared that even Zhao himself, working with a brush, might not surpass her. She also made a Pausing the Needle, extraordinarily expressive and beautiful, in which painting and embroidery were indistinguishable. A Yangzhou salt merchant later obtained it in exchange for a set of linked jade rings from the Han dynasty and a painting of a beauty by the celebrated Southern Tang artist Zhou Fang. Under Mistress Ying’s instruction, all the women of Luxiang Garden, down to the maids, became highly accomplished embroiderers. Their fame overshadowed Gu Mingshi’s own name, until one day, after drinking, he complained that his reputation hung between their ten fingers.

不过称为“顾绣”是入清以后的事。顾名世有个孙女儿，嫁夫姓张，二十四岁居孀，有个一岁的儿子。抚孤守节，全靠纤纤十指，绣件不输于缨姨娘，但除绣画以外还绣普通的花样，生意很好，“顾绣”便取“画绣”之名而代之，传遍南北。同时“顾绣”也成了上海的一佯名产，家学户习，甚至男子也有学刺绣的。罗四姐讲得头头是道，胡雪岩与七姑奶奶也听得津津有味。不过古应春却有些心不在焉，他关心的是胡雪岩这天在长三堂子中有六七处应酬，每处坐半点钟，连路上的工夫，至少亦要四个钟头，所以等罗四姐谈得告一段落，便提醒他说：“应该去了。”一听这话，胡雪岩便皱起了眉，“可以不去的，有哪些地方？”他问。“最好都去。万不得已，那么，有两处非去不可。”“好吧！就去这两处。”胡雪岩问道：“罗四姐呢？应该有人送。”“不要了。”七姑奶奶说：“城里这么远，又是晚上。”七姑奶奶是不由分说要留客过夜了。罗四姐也想留下来，不过家里只有一个老苍头看门，她一夜不回去，害老苍头着急，亦觉于心不忍。

The name “Gu embroidery,” however, came into use only after the beginning of the Qing. Gu Mingshi had a granddaughter who married a man named Zhang. Widowed at twenty-four with a year-old son, she supported the orphan and maintained her widowhood entirely through the work of her slender fingers. Her embroidery equaled Mistress Ying’s. Besides pictures, she embroidered ordinary designs, and business flourished. “Gu embroidery” replaced “painted embroidery” as the name of the craft and became known throughout the country. It was now one of Shanghai’s celebrated products, practiced in household after household; even men learned to embroider. Luo told the story with such command that Hu and the Seventh Lady listened with keen enjoyment. Gu was somewhat distracted, however. Hu had six or seven engagements at changsan houses that evening. At half an hour in each, plus travel, they would take at least four hours. As soon as Luo reached a pause, he reminded Hu, “We ought to go.” Hu frowned. “Which can we miss?” “Best to go to all of them. If you absolutely cannot, there are two you must attend.” “Very well. We’ll go to those two. What about Sister Luo? Someone ought to see her home.” “There is no need,” the Seventh Lady said. “It is such a long way into the city, and at night too.” Clearly, she meant to keep her guest overnight and would accept no argument. Luo wanted to stay, but only an old manservant was at home to watch the house. If she did not return, he would worry, and she could not bear to cause him that anxiety.

“这倒容易。”古应春说：“请罗四姐把府上的地址告诉我，我派人去通知。”于是胡、古二人先行离席，七姑奶奶陪着罗四姐吃完饭，领她到专为留堂客的客房，检点了补褥用具，请罗四姐卸了妆，再舒舒服服喝茶闲谈。一谈谈到午夜，古家照例每天必有消夜，正在吃粥时，古应春回来了，同行的还有胡雪岩。“小爷叔没有回去？”七姑奶奶信口说了一句。“我想来吃粥。”胡雪岩也信口回答。其实，大家都明白，他是特为来看罗四姐。卸了妆的她，梳一条松松的大辫子，穿的是散脚裤、小夹袄，照规矩是卧室中的打扮，见不得“官客”的。不过既然让官客撞见了，也就只好大大方方地，视如无事。“你们走了哪两家？”七姑奶奶问。“会乐里雅君老五家。还有昼锦秋月楼老四家。”古应春答说。“秋月楼老四不是从良了吗？”七姑奶奶问说：“莫非‘淴了个浴’又出来了？”“倒不是她要‘淴浴’，”胡雪岩答说：“是让邱家的大太太赶出来的。”“喔。”七姑奶奶问：“老四还是那么瘦？”“稍微发福了。”“那好，她是要胖一点才好看。”

“That is easily settled,” Gu said. “Give me your address, Sister Luo, and I’ll send someone to let him know.” The two men left the table first. When the women had finished, the Seventh Lady took Luo to a room reserved for female guests, checked the bedding and other necessities, and invited her to remove her makeup and settle comfortably over tea and conversation. They talked until midnight. A late supper was a daily custom in the Gu household, and while they were eating congee, Gu returned—with Hu beside him. “You didn’t go home, Little Uncle?” the Seventh Lady remarked casually. “I felt like some congee,” Hu answered just as casually. Everyone understood that he had come expressly to see Luo. With her makeup removed, she wore her hair in a loose, thick braid, and had put on wide-legged trousers and a little lined jacket. By convention this was bedroom dress, unsuitable for receiving male visitors. But since they had come upon her in it, she could only behave naturally, as though nothing were amiss. “Which two houses did you visit?” the Seventh Lady asked. “Yajun’s Fifth Miss in Huile Lane, and Qiuyuelou’s Fourth Miss in Zhoujin Lane.” “Hadn’t Fourth Miss left the profession to marry? Has she merely ‘taken a bath’ and come back?” “It wasn’t that she meant it to be just a bath,” Hu replied. “The Qiu family’s senior wife drove her out.” “Is she still so thin?” “She has filled out a little.” “That’s good. She needs a little more flesh to look her best.”

他们在交谈时，罗四姐的眼光不断扫来扫去，露出诧异的神色，七姑奶奶觉察到了，“罗四姐，”她问：“你逛过堂子没有？”“没有。”罗四姐答说：“听都没有听说过。”“女人逛堂子，只有我们这位太太。”古应春有点不好意思地说：“罗四姐，要不要让她带你去开开眼界？”“ 谢谢， 谢谢！” 罗四姐一面笑， 一面瑟缩…… 手， “我不敢。”“怕啥？”七姑奶奶鼓励她说：“不经一事，不长一智，你要到堂子里去过，才晓得为啥五六十岁的老头子，会交墓库运？你懂了其中的道理，你家老爷也就不会交墓库运了。”“这又是啥道理呢？”“因为你懂了，女人家要怎么个样子，才能收男人的心？他不喜欢的事情，你不要逼了他去做，他不喜欢听的话，你少说。他喜欢的事情，你也要当自己的事情那样子放在心上。到了这个地步，你尽管放他出去逛堂子，吃花酒，他一颗心还是在你身上的。”“怪不得！”罗四姐笑道：“七姐夫这样子听你的话。”“听她的话倒不见得。”古应春解嘲似地说：“不过大概不至于交墓库运。”“是不是？”七姑奶奶怂恿着说：“我们去打个茶围，有兴致再吃它一台酒，你也长长见识。又不跟他们男人家在一起，怕啥？”“我用不着长这个见识了。孤家寡人一个，这番见识也用不着。”说着，抬起头来，视线恰好跟胡雪岩碰个正着。赶紧避开，却又跟七姑奶奶对上了，看她似笑非笑的神情，罗四姐无缘无故地心虚脸红，竟有些手足无措了。

As they talked, Luo kept glancing from one to another in surprise. The Seventh Lady noticed. “Have you ever visited a courtesan house, Sister Luo?” “Never. I have never even heard of such a thing.” “Among women, only this wife of mine goes visiting them,” Gu said, a little embarrassed. “Would you like her to take you and broaden your experience?” “Thank you, thank you!” Luo laughed and made a hesitant movement with her hand. “I wouldn’t dare.” “What is there to fear?” the Seventh Lady encouraged her. “You learn something from every experience. Once you have visited those houses, you will understand why men in their fifties and sixties enter a ruinous turn in their fortunes. And once you understand, your own husband won’t suffer that fate.” “How does that follow?” “Because you will know how a woman can hold a man’s heart. Don’t force him to do things he dislikes. Say less of what he doesn’t want to hear. Whatever he cares about, take it to heart as though it concerned you yourself. Once you can do that, let him visit courtesans and drink with them as much as he pleases. His heart will still belong to you.” “No wonder Brother-in-Law Gu is so obedient!” Luo said with a smile. “Obedient may not be the word,” Gu answered, trying to save face. “But I probably won’t suffer that turn of fortune.” “There you are!” the Seventh Lady urged. “We’ll go for tea and conversation, and if we feel like it, order a whole banquet. You’ll learn something. We won’t be going with the men, so what is there to fear?” “I have no need to learn about that. I am alone in the world. Such knowledge would be no use to me.” Raising her head as she spoke, she met Hu’s eyes squarely. She looked away at once, only to encounter the Seventh Lady’s half-smiling gaze. For no reason she could explain, she felt guilty and blushed, hardly knowing what to do with herself.

于是胡雪岩便叫一声：“七姐，应春！”接着谈一件不相干的事，目的是将他们夫妇俩的视线吸引开去，为罗四姐解围。“我的酒不能再吃了。”罗四姐找个谈话的空隙，摸着微微发烧的脸说：“再吃要醉了。”“不会的。酒量好坏一看就看出来了。”七姑奶奶说：“只怕是酒不对你的胃口。”“大概是。薄荷酒带甜味，酒量好的人，都不喜欢甜味道。”古应春问道：“罗四姐，你吃两杯白兰地好不好？”“吃两种酒会醉。”“不会，不会！”七姑奶奶接口，“外国人一顿饭要吃好几种酒，有的酒在饭前，有的酒在饭后，杂七杂八都吃在肚皮里，也没有看他们有啥不对。”“真的？”看样子并不坚拒，古应春便起身去取了一瓶三星白兰地，拿着螺丝钻在开瓶塞时，罗四姐开口了。“我听人家说，这种酒上面那块月牙形招头纸，拿湿手巾擦一擦，会有三个蓝印子出来。没有蓝印子的就是假酒。”“这我们还是第一回听说，试试看。”叫人拿块湿手中来擦了又擦，毫无反应，罗四姐从从容容地说：“可见得听来的话靠不住。府上的酒，哪里会有假的？”

“Seventh Sister! Yingchun!” Hu began talking about something quite unrelated, drawing their attention away to rescue Luo from her embarrassment. Finding an opening in the conversation, she touched her faintly burning cheeks and said, “I mustn’t drink any more. Another glass and I shall be drunk.” “Not at all. One can tell at a glance whether someone can hold her drink. Perhaps the wine is not to your taste.” “Probably,” Gu agreed. “Mint liqueur is sweet. People who drink well generally dislike sweet flavors. Would you care for a couple of glasses of brandy, Sister Luo?” “Mixing two kinds will make me drunk.” “No, no!” the Seventh Lady put in. “Foreigners drink several kinds at one meal, some before it and some afterward. They put all those different drinks into their stomachs, and I’ve never seen anything wrong with them.” “Really?” Since Luo did not seem firmly opposed, Gu fetched a bottle of three-star brandy. As he worked at the cork with a corkscrew, she spoke again. “I have heard that if you rub the crescent-shaped label at the top with a damp cloth, three blue marks appear. Without those marks, the brandy is counterfeit.” “That is new to us. Let us try.” A damp handkerchief was brought, and they rubbed and rubbed, without the least result. Luo said calmly, “That shows how little one can trust hearsay. There could hardly be counterfeit wine in your house.”

“这也不见得，要尝过才算数。”七姑奶奶起身去拿了两个水晶酒杯来，向她丈夫说：“只有你陪罗四姐了。”“胡大先生，你呢？”罗四姐问。“我酒量浅，你请。”“罗四姐，”七姑奶奶又提逛堂子的事了，“怎么样，哪一天？”“七姐，”胡雪岩玩笑似地插嘴：“帮衬我打个‘镶边茶围’好不好？”“哪个要你‘镶边’，不但不要你镶边，我们还要‘剪’你的‘边’呢！”罗四姐看他们这样随意开玩笑，彼此都没有丝毫做作或不自然的神色，知道他们的交情够深了。而且看七姑奶奶不但爽朗热心，似乎胡雪岩很听她的话。她心里在想，如果对胡雪岩有什么盘算，一定先要将七姑奶奶这一关打通。于是，她的语气改变了，先是提到“堂子”就觉得是个不正经的地方，谈都不愿谈，这时候却自动地问道：“七姐，什么叫‘剪你的边’？”“ ‘剪边’就是把人家的相好夺过来。”七姑奶奶凑过去，以一种顽皮好奇的神态，略略放低了声音说：“我带你去看看小爷叔的相好，真正苏州人，光是听她说说话，你坐下来就不想走了。”“真正苏州人？”罗四姐不懂了，“莫非还有假的苏州人？”“怎么没有？问起来都说是苏州木渎人，实在不过学了一口‘堂子腔’的苏白而已。”“苏白就是苏白，什么叫堂子腔的苏白？”“我不会说，你去听了就知道了。”“好啊！”一直坚拒的罗四姐，趁此转圜，“几时跟七姐去开开眼界。”

“That is not certain either. We must taste it to decide.” The Seventh Lady fetched two crystal glasses and said to her husband, “You will have to keep Sister Luo company.” “What about you, Mr Hu?” Luo asked. “I have little capacity. Please go ahead.” The Seventh Lady returned to the proposed visit. “Well, Sister Luo, what day shall it be?” Hu interposed with a joking air. “Seventh Sister, how about helping me arrange a tea visit with a little ‘border’ added?” “Who wants you adding a border? We want none of your ‘border’—and we mean to snip your border away as well!” Watching them joke so freely, without the slightest affectation or awkwardness, Luo understood how close they were. The Seventh Lady was not merely warm and frank; Hu evidently listened to her. If Luo intended anything with Hu, she thought, she would first have to win the Seventh Lady over. Her tone changed accordingly. She had regarded courtesan houses as disreputable places and refused even to discuss them. Now she asked of her own accord, “Seventh Sister, what does ‘snip your border away’ mean?” “Steal someone’s sweetheart.” Leaning toward her with playful curiosity, the Seventh Lady lowered her voice a little. “I’ll take you to see Little Uncle’s favorite. A true Suzhou woman! Once you sit down and hear her speak, you won’t want to leave.” “A true Suzhou woman?” Luo was puzzled. “Can there be false ones?” “Of course. Ask them, and they all say they come from Mudu in Suzhou. In fact, they have merely learned a courtesan-house version of the Suzhou dialect.” “Suzhou speech is Suzhou speech. What do you mean by a courtesan-house version?” “I can’t imitate it. Come and listen, and you’ll understand.” “Very well!” Having resisted so firmly, Luo used this opening to change her position. “I’ll go with you one day and broaden my experience.”

“你们去是去，”古应春半真半假地警告：“当心《申报》登你们的新闻。”“喔，”胡雪岩突然提高了声音说：“应春提到《申报》，我倒想起一件事来了。从去年冬天天津到上海的电报通了以后，我看《申报》上有些新闻是打电报回来的。盛杏荪当电报局总办，消息格外灵通，有些生意上头，我们消息比人家晚，哪怕只不过晚一步，亏就吃得很大了。所以，我有个念头，应春，你看能不能托《申报》的访员帮忙？”“是报行情过来？”“是啊。”“那，我们自己派人在天津，每天用密码发过来好了。”“那没有多少用处。”胡雪岩说：“有的行情，只有访员才打听得到。而且，也不光是市面上的行情，还有朝廷里的行情。象去年冬天，李大先生的参案……“

“You may go,” Gu warned, half in jest, “but take care that your adventures do not appear in the Shen Bao.” “Ah!” Hu suddenly raised his voice. “That mention of the Shen Bao reminds me of something. Since the Tianjin–Shanghai telegraph opened last winter, I have noticed that some of its news arrives by wire. With Sheng Xingsun directing the telegraph administration, he is exceptionally well informed. In certain kinds of business, if our news comes later than his—even one step later—we can suffer a serious loss. I have been wondering, Yingchun, whether we could obtain help from the newspaper's reporters.” “To telegraph market quotations?” “Yes.” “Then why not station someone of our own in Tianjin and have him send a daily report in cipher?” “That would be of limited use. There are things only reporters can discover. Besides, I do not mean merely conditions in the market. I mean conditions at court too. Take the impeachment of the elder Mr Li last winter…”

“李大先生，”是指李瀚章。七姑奶奶的性情，外粗内细，一听谈到这些当朝大老的宦海风波，深知有许多有关系的话，不宜为不相干的人听见，传出去会惹是非，对胡雪岩及古应春都没有好处，所以悄悄拉了罗四姐，同时还做了个示意离席的眼色。“他们这一谈就谈不完了，我们到旁边来谈我们的。”罗四姐极其知趣，立刻迎合着七姑奶奶的意向说：“我也正有些话，不便当着他们谈。七姐，我心里头有点发慌。”“为啥？”罗四姐不即回答，将七姑奶奶拉到一边，在红丝绒的长安乐椅上并排坐了下来，一只手执着七姑奶奶的手，一只手只是摸着因酒而现红晕的脸。“是不是身子不舒服？”七姑奶奶不安地问：“怎么好端端地，心里会发慌？”“不是身子不舒服。”罗四姐仿佛很吃力他说：“我做梦也没有想到，忽然会有象今天这样子一天，又遇见雪岩，又结识了七姐你，好比买‘把儿柴’的人家，说道有一天中了‘白鸽票’，不晓得怎么好了。”七姑奶奶虽是松江人，但由于胡雪岩的关系，也憧杭州话，罗四姐的意思是，升斗小民突然中了奖券，也就是拿穷儿暴富的譬喻，来形容她自己的心境。七姑奶奶觉得她的话很中听，原来就觉得她很好，这下便更对劲了。不过要找一句适当的话来回答倒很难，所以她只是笑嘻嘻地说：“怎么会呢？怎么会呢？”

The elder Mr Li was Li Hanzhang. For all her outward bluntness, the Seventh Lady was inwardly perceptive. Once the conversation turned to the political fortunes of senior statesmen, she knew that many consequential remarks ought not to be overheard by people unconnected with the matter. If repeated, they might cause trouble for both Hu and Gu. She quietly drew Luo Sijie aside, signalling with her eyes that they should leave the table. “Once they begin, they will talk for ever. Let us go over there and have our own conversation.” Luo immediately understood and cooperated. “I have things to say that I would rather not discuss before them.
