If she truly refuses to become a concubine, there is nothing to be done. Everyone has their own aspirations; we cannot force them. But then there is no need to examine the Wealth, Officer and Food God in the earlier part of the horoscope.” “Why not?” “What use are they if the person is no longer alive?” Luo was badly startled. “Mr Wu, do you mean I shall die if I refuse to become a concubine?” “Certainly. Wei-Earth overcomes one zi-Water after another. Suppose jia-Wood refuses to retreat and confronts it. Very well: Wood controls Earth, and jia-Wood has assistance, so its strength is considerable. But look at wei-Earth. The ji-Earth in the year pillar supports it. That is not even the most important thing: the greatest power is si-Fire, for Fire generates Earth, supplying it without end. Which side is stronger? In the interaction of the Five Elements, what fails to overcome its opponent is overcome in turn. This wei-Earth is hard as rock, on which nothing can grow. If jia-Wood challenges it, it is like trying to split a mountain with a piece of timber. The timber breaks; the mountain remains.” Luo looked like a defeated fighting cock. Her fierce insistence on being a principal wife had vanished completely, although inwardly she still resented becoming a concubine.

于是七姑奶奶便要从正面来谈了，“那么，做了小就不要紧了。”她问“不是不要紧，是要做了小，就是说肯拿辛金当夫星，然后才能谈得到前面那四个字的好处。”“你是说，年上月上那四个字？”“是啊！土生金好比母子，木既嫁了金，就是一家眷属，没有再克的道理……”“吴先生，”七姑奶奶打断他的话说：“我是问那四个字的好处。”“好处说不尽。这个八字顶好的是已火那个‘食神’，八字不管男女，有食神一定聪明漂亮。食神足我所生，食神生己、未两土之财，财生辛官，这就是帮夫运。换句话说，夫星显耀，全靠我生的这个食神。”“高明，高明。”七姑奶奶转脸说道：“四姐，你还有什么话要请教吴先生。”

The Seventh Lady now turned to the favourable side. “Then she will be all right if she becomes a concubine?” “It is not merely a matter of being all right. Only by becoming a concubine—that is, by accepting xin-Metal as her Husband Star—can we begin to discuss the benefits of those four characters at the beginning.” “You mean the four characters of the year and month pillars?” “Yes. Earth generating Metal is like a mother and child. Once Wood has married Metal, they belong to the same family. There is no reason for further conflict…” “Mr Wu,” the Seventh Lady interrupted, “I was asking about the benefits of those four characters.” “They are endless. The finest feature of this horoscope is the Food God represented by si-Fire. In a horoscope, male or female, the Food God always means intelligence and good looks. It is what the self produces. Here the Food God generates Wealth in the two Earth signs, ji and wei; Wealth generates the xin-Officer. That is the fortune of a woman who advances her husband. In other words, the brilliance of the Husband Star depends entirely on this Food God that she produces.” “Most enlightening!” The Seventh Lady turned to Luo. “Sister Luo, is there anything else you would like to ask Mr Wu?”

罗四姐迟疑了一下，使个眼色，七姑奶奶知道她要说悄悄话，随即起身走向一边，罗四姐低声说道：“七姐，你倒问他，哪种命跟我合得来的。”“我晓得。”七姑奶奶回到座位上问道：“ 吴先生，如果要嫁，哪种命的人最好？”“自然是金命。”“土命呢？”说着，七姑奶奶微示眼色。吴铁口机变极快，应声而答：“土生金更好。”“喔。”七姑奶奶无所措意似地应声，然后转脸问道：“四姐，还有啥要问？”“一时也想不起。”说这话就表示她已经相信吴铁口是“铁口”，而且要问的心事还多。七姑奶奶觉得到此为止，自己的设计，至少已有七，八分把握，应该适可而止，便招招手叫小大姐将拜金递上来，预备取银票付润金。

Luo hesitated, then gave her a look. Understanding that she wanted a private word, the Seventh Lady rose and went aside with her. Luo whispered, “Seventh Sister, ask him what sort of destiny would suit mine.” “I understand.” Returning to her seat, the Seventh Lady asked, “If she marries, Mr Wu, what sort of destiny should the man have?” “Metal, naturally.” “What about Earth?” She gave him the faintest signal with her eyes. Wu was extremely quick-witted. “Earth generates Metal. Better still,” he replied at once. “Oh.” She sounded as though she attached no particular importance to it, then turned to Luo. “Anything else?” “Nothing comes to mind just now.” That answer showed that Luo already believed Wu's pronouncements to be infallible, and that she had much more on her mind to ask him. The Seventh Lady felt that her plan now had at least a seventy or eighty per cent chance of success. It was time to stop. She beckoned her maid to bring her purse, preparing to take out a banknote to pay his fee.

“吴先生，今天真谢谢你，不过还要请你费心，细批一个终身。”“这……”吴铁口面有难色，“这怕一时没有工夫。”“你少吃两顿花酒，工夫就有了。”吴铁口笑了，“这也是我命里注定的。”他半开玩笑地说：“ ‘满路桃花’的命，不吃花酒，就要赴阎罗王的席，划不来。”“哼！”六姑奶奶撇撇嘴，作个不屑的神情，接着说道：“我也知道你忙，慢一点倒不要紧，批一定要批得仔细。”“只要不限辰光，‘慢工出细货’一定的道理。”“那好。”七姑奶奶一面捡银票，一面问道：“吴先生该酬谢多少？”“古太太，你知道我这里的规矩的，全靠托贵人的福，命不好，多送我也不算，命好，我又不好意思多要，随古太太打发好了，总归不会让我白送的。”“白送变成‘送命’了。”七姑奶奶取了一张五十两银票，放在桌上说道：“吴先生，你不要嫌少。”“少是少了一点。不过，我决不嫌。”“我也晓得依罗四姐的八字，送这点钱是不够的。好在总还有来请教你的时候，将来补报。”

“Thank you very much for today, Mr Wu. But I must trouble you to write out a detailed reading of her whole life.” “Well…” Wu looked reluctant. “I am afraid I may not have time just now.” “Miss a couple of dinners with courtesans, and you will have time.” He laughed. “That too is ordained by my destiny. With peach blossoms all along my path, if I don't dine with courtesans, I shall have to dine with the King of Hell. It would be a poor bargain.” He was half joking. The Seventh Lady pursed her lips in disdain. “I know you are busy. A delay doesn't matter, but the reading must be very thorough.” “As long as there is no time limit, careful work is certain to produce a fine result.” “Good.” Sorting through her banknotes, she asked, “How much should we pay you?” “You know my rules, Mrs Gu. I depend entirely on the good fortune of my distinguished clients. If a destiny is bad, I won't read it however much I am offered. If it is good, I am too embarrassed to ask much. Give whatever you please. You would never let me give my work away.” “Giving away a destiny would be giving away a life!” She laid a fifty-tael note on the desk. “I hope you won't think it too little.” “It is a little on the low side. But I certainly shan't object.” “I know that for a horoscope like Sister Luo's, this is not enough. We are bound to consult you again. We shall make it up to you later.”

告辞出门，七姑奶奶邀罗四姐去吃大菜、看东洋戏法。罗四姐托辞头疼，一定要回家。七姑奶奶心里明白，吴铁口的那番斩钉截铁的论断，已勾起了她无穷的心事，要回去好好细想，因而并不坚邀，一起坐上她家的马车，到家以后，关照车夫送罗四姐回去。到了晚上十点多钟，古应春与胡雪岩相偕从宝善街妓家应酬而回。胡雪岩知道七姑奶奶这天陪罗四姐去算命，是特为来听消息的。“这个吴铁口，实在有点本事。说得连我都相信了。”要说罗四姐非“做小”不可，原是七姑奶奶对吴铁口的要求，自己编造的假话，出于他人之口，居然信其为真，这吴铁口的一套说法，必是其妙无比。这就不但胡雪岩，连古应春亦要先闻为快了。“想起来都要好笑。吴铁口的话很不客气，开口克夫，闭口做小，罗四姐动真气了。哪知到头来，你们晓得怎么样？”“你不要问了。”古应春说，“只管你讲就是。”“到头来，她私底下要我问吴铁口，应该配什么命好？吴铁口说，自然是金命。我说土命呢？”七姑奶奶说：“这种地方就真要佩服吴铁口，他懂我的意思倒不稀奇，厉害的是脱口而出，说土生金，更加好。”“小爷叔，”古应春笑道：“看起来要好事成双了。”“都靠七姐成全。”胡雪岩笑嘻嘻地答说。“你听见了？”古应春对他妻子说：“一切都要看你的了。”

As they took their leave, the Seventh Lady invited Luo to have a Western meal and watch Japanese conjuring tricks. Luo pleaded a headache and insisted on going home. Her friend understood: Wu's categorical pronouncements had stirred up endless thoughts, and Luo wanted to consider them privately. She did not press the invitation. They rode together in the Gu carriage, and on reaching her own house she told the coachman to take Luo home. After ten that evening, Gu Yingchun and Hu Xueyan returned together from an engagement at a courtesan's house in Baoshan Street. Knowing that the Seventh Lady had taken Luo to have her fortune told that day, Hu had come expressly for the news. “This Wu Tiekou really has some ability. He made even me believe him.” It was the Seventh Lady herself who had instructed him to say that Luo must become a concubine. If she could accept her own invention as truth when she heard it from someone else, his argument must have been extraordinary. Gu was now as eager as Hu to hear it. “It makes me laugh to think of it. Wu was most blunt. Every other word was either ‘bring death to your husband’ or ‘become a concubine.’ Sister Luo was truly angry. But do you know what happened in the end?” “Don't ask us,” Gu said. “Just tell the story.” “In the end she privately asked me to find out what destiny would make a good match for her. Wu said Metal, naturally. I asked, ‘What about Earth?’ That is where I really admire him. It was nothing remarkable that he understood my meaning; what was clever was his instant answer: ‘Earth generates Metal. Better still.’” “Little Uncle,” Gu said with a smile, “it looks as though happy events will come in pairs.” “It all depends on Seventh Sister's help,” Hu replied, beaming. “Did you hear?” Gu said to his wife. “Everything is in your hands.”

“事情包在我身上！不过急不得。罗四姐的心思，比哪个都灵，如果拔出苗头来，当我们在骗她，那一来，她什么话都听不进去了。所以，这件事我要等她来跟我谈，不能我跟她去谈，不然，只怕会露马脚。”“说得不错。”胡雪岩深深点头，“我不急。”“既然不急，小爷叔索性先回杭州，甩她一甩，事情反倒会快。”胡雪岩略想一想答说：“我回杭州，过了节再来。”“对！”七姑奶奶又说：“小爷叔，你不妨先预备起来，先禀告老太太。”“老太太也晓得罗四姐的，一定会答应。”“婶娘呢？”“她原说过的，要寻一个帮手。”“小爷叔，你一定要说好。”七姑奶奶郑重叮嘱，“如果婶娘不赞成，这件事我不会做的。多年的交情，为此生意见，我划不来。”七姑奶奶能跟胡家上下都处得极好，而且深受尊敬，就因为在这些有出入的事情上，极有分寸。胡雪岩并不嫌她的话率直，保证跟婶娘说实话，决不会害她将来为难。“即么，我等你的信。”“好的。我大概过三、四天就要走了。”胡雪岩说：“你看，我要不要再跟她见一次面？”“怎么不要？不要说一次，你天天去看她也不要紧。不过千万不要提算命的话。”一直不大开口的古应春提醒他妻子说：“ ‘满饭好吃，满话难说’。你也不要自以为有十足的把握。如果罗四姐对她的终身，真的有什么打算，一定也急于想跟你商量，不过，她不好意思移蹲就教，应该你去看她，这才是体谅朋友的道理。”

“Leave it to me! But we must not rush. Sister Luo is shrewder than anyone. If she detects a clue and decides we are deceiving her, she will refuse to listen to another word. I must wait for her to speak to me about it. If I raise it myself, I may give the game away.” “Quite right.” Hu nodded earnestly. “I am in no hurry.” “In that case, Little Uncle, you might as well return to Hangzhou first. Leave her alone for a while, and things may move faster.” Hu thought briefly. “I shall go back and return after the festival.” “Good. You can make some preparations there. Tell your mother first.” “She knows Sister Luo too. She is sure to agree.” “And Aunt?” “She has said herself that she needs someone to help her.” “You must make quite sure of her agreement,” the Seventh Lady urged solemnly. “If Aunt disapproves, I shan't arrange this. I have known her for years. It would not be worth creating ill feeling between us.” The Seventh Lady got on extremely well with everyone in Hu's household and was deeply respected because she knew exactly how to conduct herself in such delicate matters. Hu did not resent her frankness. He promised to tell his wife the truth and never leave the Seventh Lady in an awkward position later. “Then I shall wait for your letter.” “Good. I expect to leave in three or four days. Do you think I ought to see her again first?” “Of course. You can visit her every day if you like. Only be sure not to mention the fortune-telling.” Gu, who had said little, reminded his wife, “A full bowl of rice is easily eaten; a sweeping promise is hard to fulfil. Don't imagine you are absolutely certain. If Sister Luo really has plans for her future, she must be anxious to discuss them with you. But she may be embarrassed to come seeking your advice. You ought to visit her. That is how to show consideration for a friend.”

七姑奶奶欣然接受了丈夫的建议，第二天上午坐车去看罗四姐，到得那里，已经十点多钟，只见客堂中还坐着好些绣户。却只有老马一个人在应付。“你们东家呢？”“说身子不舒服，没有下楼。”老马苦笑着说：“我一个人在抓瞎。”“我来帮忙。”七姑奶奶在罗四姐平日所坐的位子上坐了下来，来过几次。也曾参与其事，发料发钱、验收货色，还不算外行。有疑难之处，唤小大姐上楼问清楚了再发落。不过半个钟头，便已毕事。“我上楼去看看。”七姑奶奶问小大姐：“哪里不舒服？”“不是身子不舒服。”小大姐悄悄说道：“我们奶奶昨天哭了一晚上，眼睛都哭肿了。”七姑奶奶大吃一惊，急急问道：“是啥缘故？”“不晓得，我也不敢问。”七姑奶奶也就不再多说，撩起裙幅上楼，只见罗四姐卧室中一片漆黑。心知她是眼睛红肿畏光，便站住了脚，这时帐子中有声音了。

The Seventh Lady willingly accepted her husband's suggestion and drove over the following morning. It was already after ten when she arrived. Quite a few embroidery workers were still sitting in the reception room, but Old Ma alone was attending to them. “Where is your mistress?” “She says she is unwell and hasn't come downstairs.” Old Ma smiled helplessly. “I am all at sea on my own.” “I shall help.” The Seventh Lady sat in Luo's usual place. Having visited several times and taken a hand before, she was not entirely unfamiliar with issuing materials and payments and inspecting finished work. Whenever a difficulty arose, she sent the maid upstairs to ask before deciding. Everything was settled within half an hour. “I shall go up and see her. What is wrong with her?” she asked the maid. “She is not ill,” the girl whispered. “She cried all last night, until her eyes were swollen.” Startled, the Seventh Lady asked quickly, “Why?” “I don't know. I didn't dare ask.” She said no more, lifted her skirt and went upstairs. Luo's bedroom was completely dark. Guessing that the light hurt her red, swollen eyes, she stopped in the doorway. A voice came from behind the bed curtains.

“是不是七姐？”“是啊！”“七姐：你不要动。等我起来扶你。”“不要，不要！我已经有点看得清楚了。”七姑奶奶扶着门框，慢慢举步。“当心，当心！”罗四姐已经起来，拉开窗帘一角，让光线透入，自己却背过身去，“七姐，多亏你来。不然老马一个人真正弄不过来。”“你怕光。”七姑奶奶说，“仍旧回到帐子里去吧！”罗四姐原是如此打算，不独畏光，也不愿让七姑奶奶看到她哭肿了眼睛，于是答应一声，仍旧上床，指挥接续而至的小大姐倒茶、预备午饭。“你不必操心。我来了也象回到家里一佯，要吃啥会交代他们的。”七姑奶奶在床前一张春凳上坐了下来，悄声说道：“到底为啥罗？”“心里难过。”“有啥放下开的心事？”罗四姐不作声，七姑奶奶也就不必再往下问，探手入帐去，摸她的脸，发觉她一双眼睛肿得有杏子般大，而且泪痕犹在。“你不能再哭了！”七姑奶奶用责备的语气说：“女人家就靠一双眼睛，身子要自己爱惜，哭瞎了怎么得了！”“哪里就会哭瞎了？”罗四姐顾而言他地问：“七姐，你从哪里来？”“从家里来。”七姑奶奶喊小大姐：“你去倒盆热水，拿条新手中来，最好是新的绒布。”这是为了替罗四姐热敷消肿。七姑奶奶一面动手，一面说话，说胡雪岩要回杭州去过节，就在这两三天要为他饯行，约罗四姐一起来吃饭。

“Is that Seventh Sister?” “Yes.” “Don't move. Let me get up and help you.” “No, no. I can see a little now.” Holding the doorframe, the Seventh Lady advanced slowly. “Be careful!” Luo was already up. She drew back a corner of the window curtain to let in some light, then turned her own face away. “Thank goodness you came. Old Ma really couldn't manage by himself.” “The light hurts your eyes. Go back behind your bed curtains.” That was what Luo had intended. Besides finding the light painful, she did not want her friend to see how swollen her eyes were. She agreed and returned to bed, telling the maid, who had followed them up, to bring tea and prepare lunch. “Don't trouble yourself. I feel as much at home here as in my own house. If I want anything, I shall tell them.” Sitting on a bench beside the bed, the Seventh Lady asked quietly, “What is the matter?” “I feel miserable.” “What is it that you cannot put aside?” Luo said nothing, and there was no need to ask further. Reaching through the curtains to touch her face, the Seventh Lady found her eyes swollen to the size of apricots, with traces of tears still on her cheeks. “You must stop crying,” she scolded. “A woman's eyes are everything to her. You must look after yourself. What if you cry yourself blind?” “How could I cry myself blind?” Changing the subject, Luo asked, “Where have you come from?” “Home.” The Seventh Lady called to the maid. “Bring a basin of hot water and a fresh towel—new flannel would be best.” She wanted to apply a hot compress to reduce the swelling. While doing so, she told Luo that Hu would soon return to Hangzhou for the festival. They would give him a farewell dinner in the next two or three days, and she wanted Luo to come.

“哪一天？”“总要等你眼睛消了肿，能够出门的时候。”“这也不过一两天事。”“那么，就定在大后天好了。”七姑奶奶又说：“你早点来！早点吃完了，我请你会看戏。”“我晓得了。”刚说得这一句，自鸣钟响了，罗四姐默数着是十二下，“我的钟慢，中午已经过了。”接着便叫小大姐：“你到馆子里去催一催，菜应该送来了。”“已经送来了。”“那你怎么不开口，菜冷了，还好吃？”罗四姐接着便骂小大姐。七姑奶奶在一旁解劝，说生了气虚火上升，对眼睛不好。罗四姐方始住口。“你把饭开到楼上来。”七姑奶奶关照，“我陪你们奶奶一起吃。”等把饭开了上来，罗四姐也起来了，不过仍旧背光而坐，始终不让七姑奶奶看到她的那双眼睛。““你到底是为啥伤心？”七姑奶奶说：“我看你也是蛮爽快的人，想不到也会这样想不开。”“不是想不开，是怨自己命苦。”“你这样的八字，还说命苦？”“怎么不苦。七姐，你倒想，不是守寡，就要做小。我越想越不服气！我倒偏要跟命强一强。““你的气好象还没有消，算了，算了。后天我请你看戏消消气。”

“On what day?” “We must wait until the swelling has gone down and you can go out.” “That will only take a day or two.” “Then let us make it three days from today. Come early. We can eat early, and afterwards I shall take you to the theatre.” “All right.” Just then the clock began to strike. Luo silently counted twelve. “My clock is slow. It is already past noon.” She called to the maid, “Go and hurry the restaurant. The food should have arrived.” “It has.” “Then why didn't you say so? Will it be any good once it is cold?” She began scolding the maid. The Seventh Lady intervened, saying that anger would make deficient fire rise and harm her eyes. Only then did Luo stop. “Bring lunch upstairs,” the Seventh Lady instructed. “I shall eat with your mistress.” When the meal was brought up, Luo got out of bed, but still sat with her back to the light, never allowing her friend to see her eyes. “What has upset you so much? I thought you were a very straightforward person. I never imagined you could brood like this.” “It is not brooding. I resent my miserable fate.” “With a horoscope like yours, you call your fate miserable?” “How can I not? Think, Seventh Sister: either I remain a widow or I become a concubine. The more I think about it, the less I can accept it. I am determined to defy my fate.” “You still seem angry. Let it go. I shall take you to the theatre the day after tomorrow to cheer you up.”

“戏我倒不想看，不过，我一定会早去。”“只要你早来就好。看不看戏到时候再说。”七姑奶奶问道：“小爷叔回杭州，你要不要带信带东西？”“方便不方便？”“当然方便。他又有人，又有船。”七姑奶奶答说：“船是他们局子里的差船，用小火轮拖的，又快，又稳当。”罗四姐点点头，不提她是否带信带物，却问到胡雪岩的“局子”。七姑奶奶便为她细谈“西征”的“上海转运局”。“克复你们杭州的左大人，你总晓得罗？”“晓得。”“左大人现在陕西、甘肃当总督，带了好几万军队在那里打仗，那里地方苦得很，都靠后路粮台接济，小爷叔管了顶要紧的一个，就是‘上海转运局’。”“运点啥呢？”“啥都运。顶要紧的是枪炮，左大人打胜仗，全靠小爷叔替他在上海买西洋的枪炮。”“还有呢？”“多哩！”七姑奶奶屈着手指说：“军装、粮食、药……”“药也要运了去？”罗四姐打岔问说。“怎么不要？尤其是夏天，藿香正气丸、辟瘟丹，一运就是几百上千箱。”

“I don't particularly want to see a play. But I shall certainly come early.” “As long as you do. We can decide about the theatre then. With Little Uncle going to Hangzhou, would you like him to take a letter or anything else?” “Would it be convenient?” “Of course. He has servants and a boat. It belongs to his bureau and is towed by a small steamer, so it is fast and steady.” Luo nodded. Instead of saying whether she had anything to send, she asked about Hu's bureau. The Seventh Lady explained the Shanghai Transport Bureau that served the western campaign. “You know Lord Zuo, who recovered your Hangzhou?” “Yes.” “He is now Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu, with tens of thousands of troops fighting there. Conditions are very harsh. They depend entirely on the rear commissariats for supplies. Little Uncle manages one of the most important, the Shanghai Transport Bureau.” “What does it send?” “Everything. The most important things are guns and cannon. Lord Zuo's victories depend entirely on the Western weapons Little Uncle buys for him in Shanghai.” “What else?” “A great deal.” The Seventh Lady counted on her fingers. “Uniforms, food, medicines…” “Medicines have to be sent too?” Luo interrupted. “Of course. Especially in summer. Huoxiang Zhengqi Pills and Biwen Dan are sent by the hundreds and thousands of cases.”

“怪不得。”罗四姐恍然有悟。“怎么？”“那天他同我谈，说要开药店。原来‘肥水不落外人田’。”“肥水不落外人田的生意还多。不过，他也不敢放手去做。”“为啥？”罗四姐问。“要帮手。没有帮手怎么做？”“七姐夫不是一等一的帮手？”“那是外头的。内里还要个好帮手。”七姑奶奶举例以明，“譬如说，端午节到了，光是送节礼，就要花多少心思，上到京里的王公大老棺，下到穷亲戚，这一张单子开出来吓坏人。漏了一个得罪人，送得轻了也得罪。”“送得重了也要得罪人。”罗四姐说，“而且得罪的怕还不止一个。”“一点不错。”七姑奶奶没有再说下去。

“No wonder!” Luo suddenly understood. “What?” “He told me the other day that he wanted to open a medicine shop. So the rich water is not to flow into someone else's fields.” “There are plenty of other businesses where he could keep the profits in his own hands. But he doesn't dare give them free rein.” “Why?” “He needs people to help him. How can he manage without them?” “Isn't Brother-in-Law Gu a first-rate assistant?” “In outside affairs. He needs a good assistant at home too.” The Seventh Lady gave an example. “Take the coming Dragon Boat Festival. Think of the trouble involved in sending the gifts alone. From princes and great officials in Beijing down to poor relations, the list is enough to frighten you. Leave one person out, and you offend them. Give too little, and you offend them too.” “Give too much, and you can also cause offence,” Luo said. “And perhaps offend more than one person.” “Exactly.” The Seventh Lady said no more.

到了为胡雪岩饯行的那一天，七姑奶奶刚吃过午饭，罗四姐就到了。一到便问：“七姐，你有没有工夫？”“啥事情？”“有工夫，我想请七姐陪我去买带到杭州的东西。还有，我想请人替我写封家信。”七站奶奶心想，现成有老马在，家信为什么要另外请人来写？显见得其中另有道理。当时便不提购物，只淡写信。“你要寻怎样的人替你写信？”“顶好是……”罗四姐说：“象七姐你这样的人。”“我肚子里这点墨水，不见得比你多，你写不来信，我也写不来。”七姑奶奶想了一下说：“这样，买东西就不必你亲自去了，要买啥你说了我叫人去办。写信，应春就要回来了，我来抓他的差。”“这样也好。”于是，七姑奶奶把她的管家阿福叫了来，由罗四姐关照，吃的、用的，凡是上海的洋广杂货，在内地都算难得的珍贵之物，以至于阿福不能不找纸笔来开单子。“多谢管家。”罗四姐取出一张五十两的银票，刚要递过去，便让七姑奶奶拦住了。“不必，我有折子。”罗四姐说。阿福不肯接，要看主妇的意思。七姑奶奶已猜到她所说的那个取货的折子，必是胡雪岩所送。既然她不肯用，又不愿要别人送，那就不必勉强了。“好了，随你。”有她这句话，阿福才接了银票去采办。

On the day of Hu's farewell dinner, Luo arrived just after the Seventh Lady had finished lunch. “Have you any time to spare?” she asked at once. “What is it?” “If you have, I should like you to come with me to buy things to send to Hangzhou. And I want someone to write a letter home for me.” Old Ma was readily available, the Seventh Lady thought. Why did Luo want someone else to write her letter? Plainly there was a reason. She said nothing about shopping and asked only about the letter. “What sort of person are you looking for?” “Preferably…” Luo hesitated. “Someone like you.” “I have hardly more learning than you. If you cannot write a letter, neither can I.” She thought for a moment. “There is no need for you to go shopping yourself. Tell me what you want, and I shall send someone. Yingchun will be home soon. I shall press him into service to write the letter.” “That will do.” The Seventh Lady summoned her steward, A’fu, and Luo gave him her instructions. Foodstuffs and household articles, all the foreign and southern merchandise sold in Shanghai, were rare and precious in the interior. The list grew so long that A’fu had to fetch paper and brush. “Thank you, steward.” Luo took out a fifty-tael banknote, but as she was about to hand it over, the Seventh Lady stopped her. “There is no need. I have a shop account book,” Luo said. A’fu would not take the money without his mistress's permission. The Seventh Lady guessed that the account book for collecting goods must have been a gift from Hu. Since Luo did not wish to use it, or accept presents from anyone else, there was no reason to insist. “Very well. As you wish.” Only then did A’fu accept the note and go to make the purchases.

恰好古应春亦已回家，稍微休息一下，便让七姑奶奶“抓差”，为罗四姐写家信。“这桩差使不大好办。”古应春笑道：“是象测字先生替人写家信，你说一句我写一句呢？还是你把大意告诉我，我写好了给你看，不对再改。”“哪种方便？”“当然是说一句写一句来得方便。”“那么，我们照方便的做。”“好！你请过来。”到得书房里，古应春铺纸吮笔，先写下一句：“母亲大人膝下敬禀者”，然后抬眼看着坐在书桌对面的罗四姐。“七姐夫，请你告诉我娘，我在上海身子很好，请她不要记挂。她的肝气病好一点没有？药不可以断。我寄五十两银子给她，吃药的钱不可以省。”“嗯，嗯。”古应春写完了问：“还有。”“还有，托人带去洋广杂物一网篮，亲戚家要分送的，请老人家斟酌。糖食等等，千万不可让阿巧多吃……““阿巧是什么人？”古应春问。“是我女儿。”

Gu happened to return just then. After a brief rest, his wife conscripted him to write Luo's letter. “This is not an easy assignment,” he said with a smile. “Shall I work like a character-diviner who writes letters for people, putting down each sentence as you dictate it? Or will you give me the general sense, and I shall write it out for you to read and correct?” “Which is easier?” “Taking it down sentence by sentence, naturally.” “Then let us do it the easy way.” “Good. Come with me.” In the study, Gu spread out a sheet of paper and moistened his brush. He first wrote, “Respectfully submitted at the feet of my honoured mother,” then looked up at Luo across the desk. “Brother-in-Law Gu, please tell my mother that I am well in Shanghai and she need not worry. Is her liver-qi trouble any better? She must not stop taking her medicine. I am sending her fifty taels. She must not economize on medicine.” Gu wrote it down. “Yes. What else?” “I am also sending a basket of foreign and southern goods with someone. Will she decide what to distribute among our relatives? She must be sure not to let A’qiao eat too many sweets…” “Who is A’qiao?” “My daughter.”

“托什么人带去要不要写？”“不要。”“好。还有呢？”“还有。”罗四姐想了一下说，“八月节，我回杭州去看她。”“还有？”“接到信马上给我回信。”罗四姐又说：“这封信要请乌先生写。”“古月胡，还是口天吴？”“不是。是乌鸦的乌。”“喔。还有呢？”“没有了。”古应春写完念了一遍，罗四姐表示满意，接下来开信封，他问：“怎么写法？”“请问七姐夫，照规矩应该怎么写？”“照规矩，应该写‘敬烦某某人吉便带交某某人’，下面是‘某某人拜托’。”“光写‘敬烦吉便’可以不可以？”当然可以。古应春是因为她说不必写明托何人带送，特意再问一遍，以便印证。现在可以断定，她是特意不提胡雪岩的名字。何以如此。就颇耐人寻味了。

“Should I mention who is bringing the things?” “No.” “Very well. Anything else?” “Yes.” Luo thought for a moment. “I shall go back to Hangzhou to see her at the Mid-Autumn Festival.” “Anything else?” “She must reply as soon as she receives this letter. And she must ask Mr Wu to write the reply.” “Hu, written with ‘ancient’ and ‘moon,’ or Wu, with ‘mouth’ and ‘heaven’?” “Neither. Wu as in ‘crow.’” “I see. Anything else?” “No.” Gu finished and read the letter aloud. Luo was satisfied. When he came to address the envelope, he asked how she wanted it written. “What is the proper form, Brother-in-Law Gu?” “The usual form is, ‘Respectfully troubling So-and-so to deliver this to So-and-so at a convenient opportunity,’ with ‘Entrusted by So-and-so’ below.” “Could we simply write, ‘Respectfully requesting delivery at a convenient opportunity’?” Of course they could. Gu had asked again because she had already said there was no need to identify the bearer, and he wanted confirmation. He could now be certain that she was deliberately avoiding Hu's name. Her reason for doing so was intriguing.

罗四姐一直到临走时，才说：“胡大先生，我有一封信，一只网篮，费你的心带到杭州，派人送到我家里。”她将信递了过去。“好！东西呢？”“在我这里。”七姑奶奶代为答说。“胡大先生哪天走？”“后天。”“那就不送你了。”罗四姐说。“不客气，不客气。”胡雪岩问：“要带啥回来？”“一时也想不起。”“想起来写信给我。或者告诉七姐。”

Only when she was about to leave did Luo speak to Hu. “Mr Hu, I have a letter and a basket. Would you be so kind as to take them to Hangzhou and send someone to deliver them to my family?” She handed him the letter. “Certainly. Where are the things?” “I have them,” the Seventh Lady answered for her. “When are you leaving, Mr Hu?” “The day after tomorrow.” “Then I shan't come to see you off.” “Please don't trouble yourself. What would you like me to bring back?” “Nothing comes to mind just now.” “Write to me if you think of anything. Or tell Seventh Sister.”

等送罗四姐上了车，七姑奶奶一走进来，迫不及待地问她丈夫：“罗四姐信上写点啥？”“原来是应春的大笔！”胡雪岩略显惊异他说：“怪不得看起来字很熟。”“我做了一回测字先生。”古应春说：“不过，我也很奇怪，这样一封信，平淡无奇，她为什么要托我来写。平常替她写家信的人到哪里去了？”“当然有道理在内。”七姑奶奶追问着，“你快把信里的话告诉我。”那封信，古应春能背得出来，背完了说：“有一点，倒是值得推敲的，她不愿意明说，信和网篮是托小爷叔带去的。”“她有没有说，为啥指明回信要托乌先生写？”“没有。”胡雪岩要问的话，另是一种，“她还有个女儿？”他说：“她没有告诉过我。”“今天就是告诉你了。不过是借应春的嘴。”“啊，啊！”古应春省悟了，“这就是她故意要托我来写信的道理。”

Once they had seen Luo into her carriage, the Seventh Lady hurried back inside and asked her husband, “What did she say in her letter?” “So Yingchun wielded the brush!” Hu said, a little surprised. “No wonder the handwriting looked familiar.” “I played the character-diviner for once. But I found it curious too. Why should she ask me to write such an entirely ordinary letter? What has become of whoever normally writes her letters home?” “There is certainly a reason. Tell me what was in it.” Gu could recite the whole letter from memory. When he had done so, he added, “One point is worth considering. She did not want to say explicitly that Little Uncle was bringing the letter and basket.” “Did she explain why she specifically wanted Mr Wu to write the reply?” “No.” Hu's question was different. “She has a daughter? She never told me.” “She has told you today, through Yingchun.” “Ah!” Gu understood. “So that is why she deliberately asked me to write it.”

“道理还多呢！”七姑奶奶接口，“第一，要看小爷叔念不念旧？她娘，小爷叔从前总见过的，如果念旧，就会去看她。”“当然！”胡雪岩说：“我早就想好了，信跟东西亲自送去。过节了，总还要送份礼。”“这样做就对了。”七姑奶奶又说：“小爷叔，她还要试试你，见了她女儿怎么样？”“嗯！”胡雪岩点点头，不置可否。“还有呢？”古应春这天将这三个字说惯，不自觉地滑了出来。“指明信要托乌先生写，是怕测字先生说不清楚，写不出来，马马虎虎漏掉了，只有乌先生靠得住。”胡雪岩觉得她的推断，非常正确，体味了好一会，感叹他说：“这罗四姐的心思真深。”“不光是心思深，还有灵。我说送礼送得轻了得罪入，他说送得重了，也要得罪，而且得罪的不止一个。”七姑奶奶接下来说：“小爷叔，你要不要这个帮手，成功不成功，就看乌先生写信来了。”胡雪岩心领神会，回到杭州先派人去办罗四姐所托之事，同时送了一份丰厚的节礼。然后挑了个空闲的日子，轻装简从，满荷洒洒地去看罗四姐的母亲。胡雪岩仍旧照从前的称呼，称她“罗大娘”，但罗大娘却不大认得出他了，陌生加上受宠若惊，惶恐不安。胡雪岩了解她的心情，跟她先谈罗四姐的近况，慢慢地追叙旧事，这才使得罗大娘的心定了下来。这心一定下来，自然就高兴了，也感动了，不断地表示，以胡雪岩现在的身分，居然降尊纤贵，会去看她，是她想都不敢想的事。

“There are other reasons,” the Seventh Lady said. “First, she wants to see whether Little Uncle remembers old ties. You must have met her mother in the old days. If you remember them, you will go and see her.” “Of course. I had already decided to deliver the letter and things myself. With the festival coming, I must take a present too.” “That is the right thing to do. And she wants to test how you react when you see her daughter.” “Mm.” Hu nodded without committing himself. “Anything else?” Gu had used the phrase so often that day that it slipped out unconsciously. “She specified Mr Wu because she was afraid a character-diviner might not explain things clearly or write them properly, and might carelessly leave something out. Only Mr Wu can be relied upon.” Hu thought her reasoning entirely correct. After considering it for a while, he said with feeling, “Sister Luo's mind works very deeply.” “Deeply and quickly. I said that giving too little could cause offence; she said that giving too much could offend more than one person. Little Uncle, if you want this helper, whether the match succeeds will depend on the letter Mr Wu writes.” Hu understood. Back in Hangzhou, he first sent someone to attend to Luo's commission, adding a generous festival gift. Then, on a free day, he dressed simply, took few attendants and went in an easy manner to visit her mother. He addressed her by the old name, Auntie Luo, but she could scarcely recognize him. His unfamiliarity, added to her astonishment at the honour, made her extremely uneasy. Understanding her feelings, he began with news of her daughter, then gradually recalled old times. Only then did Auntie Luo relax. Once at ease, she naturally became both pleased and moved, repeatedly saying that she would never have dared imagine a man in his present position lowering himself to visit her.

第六章 曲折情关｜CHAPTER SIX: A WINDING ROAD TO MARRIAGE

十天以后，罗四姐接到了家信，罗大娘照她的话，是请乌先生代写的。这乌先生是关帝庙的庙祝，为人热心，洞明世事，先看了罗四姐的来信，心头有个疑问，何以回信要指写他来写。再听罗大娘眉飞色舞地谈胡雪岩来看她的情形，恍然大悟，罗四姐大约不能确定，胡雪岩会不会亲自来看罗大娘，所以信中不说信件等物托何人所带。不过胡雪岩的动静，在她是很关心的，既然如此，就要详详细细告诉她。她之指明要自己替罗大娘写回信，也正是这个道理。这完全猜对了罗四姐的心思，因此，她的信也就深副她的期待了。乌先生的代笔，浅显明白，罗四姐先找者马来念给她听过，自己也好好下了一番工夫，等大致可以看得懂了，才揣着信去看七姑奶奶。“七姐，”她说。“我有封信，请你给我看看。”“哪个的信？”“我娘的信，我一看信很长，当中好象提到胡大先生，我怕有要紧话在里头，不方便叫老马给我看。”“我比你也好不了多少，你看不明白，我也未见得看得懂。不过，不要紧，一客不烦二主，当初你是托应春替你写的现在仍旧叫他来看好了。”“七姐夫在家？”“在家。”七姑奶奶答说： “有个洋人要来看他，他在等。”

Ten days later, Luo Sijie received a letter from home. As she had requested, her mother had asked Mr Wu to write it. Mr Wu was the keeper of the Temple of Lord Guan, a warm-hearted man with a thorough understanding of the world. Reading Luo’s letter first, he had wondered why she had specifically requested him as the writer of the reply. Then, listening to Auntie Luo’s delighted account of Hu’s visit, he understood. Her daughter probably had not been certain whether Hu would call in person, which explained why she had omitted the name of the man carrying her letter and gifts. Yet his actions mattered greatly to her. Mr Wu must therefore tell her everything in detail: that was precisely why she had asked him to write. He had guessed her intention perfectly, and the letter fully met her expectations. His language was plain and clear. She first had Old Ma read it aloud, then worked carefully through it herself. Once she could understand most of it, she put it inside her clothes and went to see the Seventh Lady. “Seventh Sister, I have a letter. Would you look at it for me?” “From whom?” “My mother. It is very long, and Mr Hu seems to be mentioned in the middle. I am afraid there may be something important that I ought not to ask Old Ma to read.” “I am not much better than you. If you cannot make it out, I may not be able to either. But never mind. One guest need not trouble two hosts. You asked Yingchun to write before; let him read this one too.” “Is Brother-in-Law Gu at home?” “Yes. A foreigner is coming to see him, and he is waiting.”

于是将古应春找了来，拿信交了给他。他一面看，一面讲：“东西都收到了，胡大先生还送了一份很厚的礼，一共八样，火腿、茶叶、花雕……”“这不要念了。”七姑奶奶插嘴问道：“他信里称小爷叔，是叫胡大先生？”“是啊！杭州人之中，尊敬小爷叔的，都是这样叫他的。”“好！你再讲下去。”“五月初七胡大先生去看你母亲，非常客气，坐了足足有一个时辰，谈起在上海的近况……”讲到这里，古应春笑笑硕住了。“咦！”七姑奶奶诧异地问：“啥好笑？”“信上说。你母亲知道你认识了我们两个，说是‘欣遇贵人’。”古应春谦虚着，“实在不敢当。”“我娘的话不错。你们两位当然是我的贵人。”罗四姐问道：“七姐夫，信上好象还提到我女儿。”“是的。你母亲说，胡大先生很喜欢你女儿，问长问短，说了好些话。还送了一份见面礼，是一双绞丝的金镯子。““你看！”罗四姐对七姑奶奶说，“大先生对伢儿们，给这样贵重的东西，不过，七姐，我倒不大懂了，大先生怎么会将这双镯子带在身边？莫非他去之前，就晓得我有个女儿？”“不见得。”七姑奶奶答说，“我们小爷叔应酬多，金表杂七杂八的东西很多，遇到要送见面礼，拿出来就是。”“原来这样子的。”罗四姐的疑团一释，“七姐夫，请你再讲。”

Gu was summoned and given the letter. He read and explained as he went. “Everything arrived. Mr Hu also sent a very substantial gift, eight things in all: ham, tea, Huadiao…” “You need not read those out,” the Seventh Lady interrupted. “Does the letter call Little Uncle Mr Hu?” “Yes. That is how Hangzhou people who respect him address him.” “Go on, then.” “On the seventh day of the fifth month, Mr Hu called on your mother. He was extremely courteous and stayed two full hours, talking about your recent life in Shanghai…” Gu smiled and stopped. “What is amusing?” his wife asked in surprise. “Your mother says she was pleased to learn that you had met the two of us. She calls it ‘the happy encounter with benefactors.’ That is far more than we deserve.” “My mother is right. You are certainly my benefactors.” Luo asked whether the letter also mentioned her daughter. “It does. Your mother says Mr Hu liked her very much, asked all sorts of questions, and talked with her at length. He also gave her a present at their first meeting: a pair of twisted-wire gold bracelets.” “Just think, Seventh Sister! Such costly things for a child. But I do not quite understand. Why did he have those bracelets with him? Did he know before going that I had a daughter?” “Not necessarily. Little Uncle has so many social obligations that he keeps gold watches and all sorts of other things. When a present is needed, he can simply produce one.” “So that is the explanation.” Her doubt resolved, Luo asked Gu to continue.

“你娘说，你说要回去，她也很想念你，如果你抽不出工夫。或者她到上海来看你。”罗四姐还未开口，七姑奶奶先就喊了出来，“来嘛！”她说，“把你娘接了来歇夏，住两三个月再回去。““上海是比杭州要凉快些。”罗四姐点点头：“等我来想想。”“后面还有段话，是乌先生‘附笔’，很有意思！”古应春微笑着，“他说，自从胡大先生亲临府上以后，连日‘庙中茶客议论纷纷’，都说胡大先生厚道。照他看，胡大先生是你命中的‘贵人’，亦未可知。”这话触及罗四姐心底深处，再沉着也不同得脸一红，七姑奶奶非常识趣，故意把话扯了开去，“什么‘庙中茶客’？”她问：“什么庙？”“关帝庙，就在我家邻近。替我娘写这封信的乌先生，是那里的庙祝，靠平常摆桌子卖茶、说大书，关帝庙的香火才有着落。”正谈到此处，洋人来拜访古应春了。在他会客时，罗四姐与七姑奶奶的话题未断，她也很想接她母亲来往，苦无便人可以护送。七姑奶奶认为这根本算不了一回事，写信给胡雪岩就是。“不好！”罗四姐只是摇头，却不说为何不好，及至七姑奶奶追问时，她才答说：“我欠他的情大多了。”“已经多了，何妨再欠一回。”“我怕还不清。”“那也有办法……”七姑奶奶想一想，还是不必说褥大露骨。罗四姐也没有再问，这件事就暂且搁下来了。

“Your mother says you mentioned coming home, and she misses you very much. If you cannot spare the time, perhaps she might come to Shanghai instead.” Before Luo could answer, the Seventh Lady exclaimed, “Let her come! Bring her here for the summer. She can stay two or three months before going back.” Luo nodded. “Shanghai is cooler than Hangzhou. Let me think about it.” “There is another passage, a postscript from Mr Wu. Quite interesting.” Gu smiled. “He says that since Mr Hu’s personal visit, the tea drinkers at the temple have talked of little else for days. Everyone calls him a generous and loyal man. Mr Wu thinks he might even be the benefactor destined to enter your life.” The words touched the deepest part of Luo’s heart. Composed as she was, she could not help blushing. With great tact, the Seventh Lady deliberately changed the subject. “What tea drinkers? What temple?” “The Temple of Lord Guan, near our house. Mr Wu, who wrote this letter for my mother, is its keeper. He sets out tables and sells tea, with storytellers performing. That is how the temple’s worship and incense are supported.” At this point Gu’s foreign visitor arrived. While he received him, the two women continued talking. Luo would very much like her mother to stay, but had no suitable person to escort her. The Seventh Lady thought that no difficulty at all: she need only write to Hu. “No, that would not do.” Luo kept shaking her head, and only when pressed explained, “I owe him too much already.” “Then what harm in owing him one kindness more?” “I am afraid I could never repay him.” “There is a way of doing that too…” On reflection, the Seventh Lady decided not to speak too plainly. Luo asked no further question, and the matter was left for the time being.

谈了些闲话，到了上灯时分，七姑奶奶提议，早点吃晚饭，饭后去看西洋来的马戏。罗四姐答应在她家吃饭，但不想去看马戏，因为散戏已晚，劳她远送回家，于心不安。“那还不好办？你住在我这里好了。我们还可以谈谈。”罗四姐想了一下，终于接受邀约。饭后看马戏回来，古应春也刚刚到家。“阿七，请你替我收拾收拾行李。”他说：“今天来的洋人。是德国洋行新来的总管。他说要专程到杭州去拜访小爷叔，顺便逛逛西湖，我只好陪他走一趟。”“怎么？”七姑奶奶高兴他说：“你要到杭州！好极，好极！你把罗四姐的老太太带了来。”古应春愣了一下，想到罗大娘信中的话，方始会意，欣然答说：“好，好！我一走办到。”他们夫妇已经这样作了决定，罗四姐除了道谢，别无话说。接着便谈行程，古应春计算，来去约需半个月。七姑奶奶便又出了主意。“你索性搬到‘大英地界’来往，我们来去也方便。”她说：“寻房带搬家，有半个月尽够了。”“嗯，嗯。等我想一想。”“你不必想。等我来替你想。”七姑奶奶是在想，有什么熟人的房子，或租，或买，一切方便，思索了一会，想到了，“老宓不是在造‘弄堂房子’？她问，“完工了没有？”“老早完工了。”“他那条弄堂，一共二十四家，算是条很长的弄堂。我想一定有的。”“那好。”七姑奶奶转脸对罗四姐说：“老宓是阜康的二伙，现在也发财了。是他的房子，只要一句话，就可以搬进去住。”

They chatted until the lamps were lit. The Seventh Lady proposed an early dinner followed by a visit to a Western circus. Luo agreed to dine but declined the circus: it would finish late, and she would feel guilty at making her hostess escort her so far home. “That is easily settled. Stay here. We can talk some more as well.” After considering it, Luo accepted. When they returned from the circus after dinner, Gu had just arrived home too. “A’qi, please pack my things. Today’s visitor is the new manager of a German trading house. He wants to make a special journey to Hangzhou to see Little Uncle and take the opportunity to visit West Lake. I have no choice but to accompany him.” “You are going to Hangzhou? Wonderful! Bring Sister Luo’s mother back with you.” Gu paused, then remembered the letter and understood. “Gladly. I shall certainly arrange it.” With husband and wife having decided between them, Luo could do nothing but thank them. They discussed the journey, which Gu reckoned would take about half a month there and back. His wife had another idea. “Why not move into the British settlement? It would be easier for us to visit each other. Half a month is quite enough to find a house and move.” “Let me think.” “You need not. Let me think for you.” She considered whose house might conveniently be rented or bought, and an idea came. “Wasn’t Old Mi building a row of houses in a lane? Are they finished?” “Long ago.” “There are twenty-four houses in that lane—a long one,” Gu continued. “I am sure some must be available.” “Then that is settled.” Turning to Luo, the Seventh Lady explained, “Old Mi is Fukang’s deputy manager. He has made a fortune too. If the houses are his, one word is all it will take for you to move in.”

“看看，看看！”罗四姐急忙否定，“我想另外寻，比较好。”“为啥呢？”罗四姐不答，只是摇头，七姑奶奶终于想到了，在此她跟胡雪岩的关系，正当微妙的时刻，她是有意要避嫌疑，免得太着痕迹。七姑奶奶觉得罗四姐人虽精明能干，而且也很重义气交情，但不免有些做作。她是个心直口快的人，遇到这种情形，有她一套快刀斩乱麻的手法，是罗四姐所做不到的。“我不管你那颗玲珑七巧心、九弯十转在想点啥？总而言之，言而总之一句话，你搬家是搬定了。房子呢，或租、或典、或买下来，我来替你作主，你不必管。”罗四姐反到服帖了，“七姐，”她说：“我就听你的话，一切不管，请你费心。”于是七姑奶奶独断独行，为她买了阜康钱庄二伙老宓新造的“弄堂房子”。这条弄堂名叫富厚里，二十四户，望衡对宇，两面可通，七姑奶奶挑定的一户，坐北朝南，楼下东西厢房，大客厅，后面是“灶披间”、下房、储藏室。扶梯设在中间，楼上大小五个房间，最大的一个，由南到北，直通到底，是个套房，足供藏娇。另外四间，一间起坐、一间饭厅、两间客房，家具摆饰，亦都是七姑奶奶亲自挑选，布饰得富丽堂皇，着实令人喜爱。前后不过十天工夫，诸事妥帖，七姑奶奶自己也很得意。第十一天早上，派马车将罗四姐接了来，告诉她说：“房子我替你弄好了。现在陪你去看看。”一看之下，罗四姐又惊又喜，兴奋之情，溢于言表，不断他说：“太好了，太好了。只怕我没有福气，住这么好的房子。”七姑奶奶不理她这话，光是问她还有什么不满意之处，马上可以改正。罗四姐倒也老实说了，还应该加上窗帘。

“There, you see!” Luo hastily rejected the suggestion. “I think it would be better to find somewhere else.” “Why?” She would only shake her head. At last the Seventh Lady understood. At this delicate stage in Luo’s relations with Hu, she wished to avoid suspicion and leave no obvious sign. The Seventh Lady found her shrewd, capable, and loyal to her friends, yet also somewhat affected. A frank woman herself, she had a way of cutting through complications that Luo could not manage. “I don’t care what twists and turns that wonderfully clever mind of yours is taking. To sum it up, and sum it up again: you are moving. Whether we rent, acquire the house under a redeemable pledge, or buy it, I shall decide. You need not concern yourself.” Luo yielded. “Then I shall do as you say, Seventh Sister. I leave everything to you.” Taking full charge, the Seventh Lady bought her one of the new houses built by Old Mi, Fukang’s deputy manager. The lane was called Fuhou Lane. Its twenty-four houses faced one another across a passage open at both ends. She chose one facing south. Downstairs were side rooms to east and west, a large reception room, and, at the back, a kitchen, servants’ quarters, and storeroom. The stairs were in the middle. Upstairs were five rooms of different sizes. The largest was a suite running the full depth of the house from south to north, ample accommodation for a beauty in seclusion. The other four were a sitting room, a dining room, and two guest rooms. The Seventh Lady personally selected all the furniture and ornaments, arranging them with an attractive richness and splendor. Everything was ready in only ten days, and she was thoroughly pleased with herself. On the eleventh morning she sent the carriage for Luo. “I have arranged your house. Come and see.” Luo was astonished and delighted. “It is wonderful! I only fear I lack the good fortune to live in such a house.” Ignoring this, the Seventh Lady asked what she disliked; anything could be changed at once. Luo frankly mentioned that curtains were still needed.

“窗帘已经量了尺寸，叫人去做了，明天就可以做好。”七姑奶奶接着又问：“你哪天搬？”“慢点！”罗四姐拉着她并排坐下，踌躇了一下说道：“七姐，说实话，房子我是真欢喜。不过，我怕力量办不到，房子连家具，一起在内，总要四千银子吧？”“四千不到。我有细帐在那里。”七姑奶奶说：“你现在不必担心买不起。这幢房子现在算是我置的，白借给你住，到你买得起了，我照原价让给你。”“世界上有这样的好事吗？”“你不相信，我自己郡不相信呢！”七姑奶奶笑道：“看起来，吴铁口的话要应验了。”罗四姐记得很清楚，吴铁口断定她要“做小”，如果“偏要做大”，就会“嫁一个克一个”。假使不愿“做小”，又不能“做大”，本身就会遭殃，性命不保。倘或如此，八字中前面那四个字的“财”、“官”、“印”，自然都谈不到了。所以只有心甘情愿“做小”，才会有福气。这样一想，七姑奶奶话中的意思，也就很明显了。话虽如此，罗四姐却不愿表示承认，可也不愿表示否认。这一来，唯一的办法便是装作未听清楚而忽略了她的弦外余音，故意言他。

“The windows have been measured, and the curtains are being made. They will be ready tomorrow. When will you move?” “Wait.” Luo drew her down to sit beside her and hesitated. “To tell the truth, I love the house. But I am afraid it is beyond my means. House and furniture together must cost four thousand taels?” “Less than four thousand. I have a detailed account. You need not worry about affording it now. For the moment, regard it as my property, lent to you to live in free of charge. When you can afford it, I shall let you have it at the original price.” “Can such good things happen in this world?” “You don’t believe it? I hardly believe it myself!” The Seventh Lady laughed. “It looks as though Wu Tiekou’s words are coming true.” Luo remembered them perfectly. He had insisted she must become a concubine. If she insisted on being a principal wife, she would bring death to one husband after another. If she would neither accept the lesser position nor occupy the higher one, disaster would overtake her own life. In that case, the Wealth, Officer, and Seal represented in the first four of her birth characters would count for nothing. Only by willingly becoming a concubine could she enjoy good fortune. The Seventh Lady’s meaning was therefore plain. Yet Luo would neither acknowledge nor reject it. Her only course was to pretend she had not quite heard, ignore the implication, and deliberately change the subject.

“七姐，搬家是件蛮麻烦的事，恐怕……”“你用不着顾前想后。这里家具摆设都有了，你那里的木器，能送人的送人，没人可送，叫个收旧货的来，一脚踢。收拾收拾衣服、首饰、动用器具，不过一天的工夫，有啥麻烦？““我那班客户呢？”“这倒比较麻烦。”七姑奶奶沉吟了一会说：“我劝你也不必再做了……”“不！”罗四姐抢着说道：“不光是为我自己。人家也是养家活口的一项行当，我不能不管。”“那也容易，你找个能干的人，做你的替手。说不走，还可以要一笔‘顶费’。”七姑奶奶又说：“新旧交替，难免接不上头，老马可以慢慢搬过来。或者老马投了新东家，你就更加省事了。“听七姑奶奶为她的打算，简捷了当却又相当周到，罗四姐实在无话可说了，“七姐，我真服了你了。”她说，“如今只剩下一件事：挑日子。”“对。”七姑奶奶说，“到我那里去，一面挑日子。一面再好好商量。”

“Moving is a troublesome business, Seventh Sister. I am afraid…” “There is no need to worry about every possibility. The furniture and fittings are all here. Give away what you can of your old furniture, and have a secondhand dealer take the rest in one lot. Packing clothes, jewelry, and household utensils cannot take more than a day. Where is the trouble?” “What about all my customers?” “That is more difficult.” After a pause, the Seventh Lady said, “I advise you to give up the business…” “No!” Luo interrupted. “It is not only for my own sake. This is a livelihood by which other people support their families. I cannot simply abandon them.” “That is easily managed too. Find someone capable to take your place. You might even receive a payment for handing over the business. The change between old and new management is bound to leave loose ends, so Old Ma can come to the new house later. Or he might stay with the new proprietor, which would save you still more trouble.” Her arrangements were so simple and decisive, yet so considerate of the details, that Luo could find nothing more to object to. “I truly admire you, Seventh Sister. There is only one thing left now: choosing a day.” “Exactly. Let us go back to my house, choose a day, and discuss everything further.”

回到古家，略为息一息，七姑奶奶叫人取了皇历来挑日子。很不巧，一连八、九天都不宜迁居，最快也得十天以后。“那时候老太太已经来了。”七姑奶奶说：“我的想法是：顶好这三、四天以内就搬停当，老大太一来就住新房子，让她老人家心里也高兴，而且也省事得多，四姐，你说呢？”“话自然不错。不过，日子不好，没有办法。”七姑奶奶想了一下说，“有办法。俗语道得好：拣日不如撞日。撞到哪天是哪天，你说好不好？”“怎么撞法？”“以老太太到上海的那天，就算你撞到的日子。老太太到了，先在我这里歇一歇脚，马上进屋，你也把要紧东西先搬运了来，晚上摆两桌酒，叫一班髦儿戏，热闹热闹，顺便就算替老太太接风，不是一举两得。”罗四姐觉得这样安排也很好，便即问道：“七姐夫不晓得哪天回来？”“快了。大概还有四、五天工夫。”

After a short rest at the Gu house, the Seventh Lady had the almanac brought. Unluckily, none of the next eight or nine days was suitable for moving. The earliest favorable date was ten days away. “Your mother will be here by then. I think it would be best to have everything settled within three or four days, so that she can go straight into the new house when she arrives. It would please her and save a great deal of trouble. What do you say?” “Of course that would be best. But if the days are unfavorable, there is nothing we can do.” The Seventh Lady thought for a moment. “Yes, there is. As the saying goes, better to take the day you happen upon than labor over choosing one. Whatever day comes our way will be the day. How about that?” “How are we to happen upon it?” “Take the day your mother reaches Shanghai. She can rest briefly at my house and then go straight to yours. Move your essential things beforehand. In the evening, give a dinner for two tables and engage a troupe of mao’er opera performers to make it lively. It will welcome your mother at the same time. Two purposes served by one arrangement.” Luo approved. “When will Brother-in-Law Gu be back?” “Soon. Probably in another four or five days.”

古应春回来了。使得罗四姐深感意外的是：她的母亲没有来，倒是乌先生来了。那乌先生有五十多岁，身材矮胖，满头白发，长一个酒糟鼻子，形容古怪，但那双眼睛极好，看人时，眼中两道光芒射过来，能把人吸引住，自然而然地觉得此人可亲且可信赖，因此，七姑奶奶一会便对他有好感。在古应春引见以后，自然有一番客套，七姑奶奶问到罗四姐的母亲何以不来，乌先生乘机道明了来意。“罗四姐的娘因天气大热，又是吃‘观音素’，到上海来作客，种种不方便，所以不来。不过她娘倒有几句要紧话，要我私下限她说，所以沾古先生的光，携带我到上海来开开眼界。”“蛮好，蛮好。”七姑奶奶说：“罗四姐，我跟她一见如故，感情象亲姐妹一样，乌先生是她敬重的人，到了这里，一切不必客气。现在，乌先生看，是把罗四姐接了来呢？还是你去看她。”“她娘还有点吃的、用的东西给罗四姐，还是我去好了。”“那么，我来送你去。”“不敢当，不敢当，决不敢当。”“乌先生，你不要客气。为啥要我亲自送你去呢？这有两个缘故。”说到这里，七姑奶奶转眼看着丈夫说：“你恐怕还不晓得，罗四姐搬家了，是老窗的房子，我一手替她料理的。““好快！”古应春说了这一句，便又对乌先生说：“罗四姐的新居在哪里，我都不知道，那就非内人送你去不可了。”“我送了乌先生去，顺便约一约罗四姐，今天晚上替乌先生接风，请她作陪。”听得这么说，乌先生除了一再道谢以外，再无别话，于是舍车坐轿，一起到了罗四姐那里。七姑奶奶把人带到，又约好罗四姐晚上陪乌先生来吃饭，随即匆匆忙忙赶回家，因为她急于要听古应春谈此行的经过。

Gu returned, but to Luo’s astonishment, her mother had not come. Mr Wu had arrived instead. He was in his fifties, short and stout, with a head of white hair and a red, bulbous nose. His features were odd, but his eyes were excellent. Their penetrating brightness held anyone he looked at and naturally inspired both affection and trust. The Seventh Lady took to him at once. After Gu’s introductions and the customary courtesies, she asked why Luo’s mother had not come. Mr Wu used the question to explain his visit. “The weather is very hot, and her mother is observing a vegetarian fast for Guanyin. A visit to Shanghai would be inconvenient in several ways. But she has some important things she wants me to tell her daughter privately. Thanks to Mr Gu, I have been brought along to broaden my experience of Shanghai.” “Excellent. Sister Luo and I became close at once, like true sisters. Since you are someone she respects, please stand on no ceremony here. Shall we send for her, or would you prefer to call on her?” “Her mother has sent a few things to eat and use. I had better take them to her.” “Then I shall take you.” He protested repeatedly that he could not accept such an honor. “There is no need for formality. I have two reasons for taking you myself.” She turned to her husband. “You probably haven’t heard that Sister Luo has moved. Into Old Mi’s house. I arranged everything.” “So quickly!” Gu turned to Mr Wu. “I don’t even know where her new home is. My wife really must take you.” “And while I am there, I can invite her to accompany you to dinner tonight, when we welcome you properly.” Mr Wu could only keep thanking her. They took sedan chairs instead of the carriage and went to Luo’s house. After delivering him and arranging for them both to come to dinner, the Seventh Lady hurried home, eager to hear Gu’s account of the journey.

“他是女家的‘大冰老爷’……”原来胡雪岩一回杭州，略得清闲，便与老母妻子谈罗四姐的事。本来娶小纳妾，胡雪岩原是自己可以做主的，但罗四姐的情形不同，好些有关系的事，都要预先谈好，最要紧的，第一是虚名，第二是实权。杭州官宦人家的妾侍，初进门称“新姑娘，一年半载亲党熟悉了，才会称姓，假如姓罗，便叫”罗姑娘“，三年玉载以后，才换称”姨奶奶“的称呼。至于熬到”姨太太“总要进入中年，儿女成长以后。可是胡雪岩却为罗四姐提出要求，一进门就要称”太太“。“那么，”胡老太太问道：“你的元配呢？这个也是‘太太’，那个也是‘太太’，到底是叫哪个？”“一个叫‘二太太，好了。”胡老太太沉吟了一会道：“她怎么说呢？”胡老太太用手遥指，这“地”是指胡太太。“我还没有跟她谈到这上头。先要娘准了，我再跟她去说。”胡老太太知道，媳妇贤惠而软弱，即使心里不愿，亦不会公然反对，但她作为一家之主，却不能不顾家规，所以一时不便轻许，只说：“我要好好儿想一想，总要在台面上说得过去才可以。”“台而上是说得过去的。为啥呢”胡雪岩正好谈“实权”，他说：“目下这种场面，里头不能没有一个人来‘抓总’，媳妇太老实，身子又不好。以至于好些事，还要老太太来操劳，做儿子的心里不安。再说句老实话，外头的情形，老太太并不清楚，有时候想操心，也无从着力。我想来想去，只有把罗四姐讨了来当家。既然当家，不能没有名分，这是所谓‘从权办理’。台面上说得过去的。“

“He is the bride’s matchmaker…” Soon after returning to Hangzhou, Hu had found time to discuss Luo with his mother and wife. Ordinarily, he could decide for himself to take a concubine, but Luo’s circumstances were different. Several consequential matters had to be settled beforehand, above all her title and her actual authority. In Hangzhou official households, a concubine was first called the New Miss. After six months or a year, when relatives and friends knew her, her surname would be used: Miss Luo, for instance. Several years might pass before she became yinainai, or Auntie. The more dignified title yitaitai, or Aunt-Madam, generally came only in middle age, after her children had grown. Hu, however, requested that Luo be addressed as Madam from the moment she entered the household. “Then what of your principal wife?” Old Madam Hu asked. “One is Madam and the other is Madam. How is anyone to know which is meant?” “Call one of them Second Madam.” His mother considered this. “What does she say?” She pointed vaguely in his wife’s direction. “I haven’t discussed that part with her yet. I wanted your approval before speaking to her.” Old Madam Hu knew her daughter-in-law was kind and weak. Even if reluctant, she would not openly oppose him. As head of the family, however, she herself had to consider its rules and could not agree lightly. “I must think carefully. Whatever we do must be defensible before others.” “It is defensible.” This gave Hu his opening to discuss authority. “With the establishment we now maintain, someone must take overall charge indoors. Your daughter-in-law is too unassertive, and her health is poor. You still have to attend to so much, which makes me feel a failure as a son. To be frank, you don’t fully understand affairs outside the house. Sometimes, even when you want to help, you cannot see how. I have thought it over endlessly. The only answer is to marry Sister Luo and put her in charge. If she manages the household, she must have the standing to do so. This is a special arrangement to meet the circumstances. It can be justified.”

“你要她来当家，这件事，我就更加要好好想一想了。你总晓得，当家人是很难做的。”“我晓得。罗四姐极能干，这个家一定当得下来。”“不光是能干。”胡老太太说：“俗语说：”不痴不聋，不做阿家翁。‘做当家人要吃得起哑巴亏。丫头老妈子、厨子轿班，都会在背后说闲话，她有没有这份肚量，人家明明’当着和尚骂贼秃‘，她只当没有听见，脸上有一点懊恼的神气都没有？““这一点……”胡雪岩说：“我当然要跟她说清楚，她一定会答应的。”胡老太太大摇其头，“说归说，答应归答应，到时候就不同了。”她说：“泥菩萨都有个土性，一个忍不住闹了起来，弄得家宅不和，那时候你懊悔嫌迟了。”这是各人的看法不同。胡老太太以前也见过罗四姐，但事隔多年，是何面貌都记不清楚了，当然只就一般常情来推测。胡雪岩心想，这不是一下子可将老母说服的，惟有多谈一谈罗四姐的性情才具，渐渐地让母亲有了信心，自然水到渠成。

“If you want her to manage the household, I must consider it still more carefully. You know how hard it is to be the person in charge.” “I do. She is exceptionally capable. She can certainly manage it.” “Ability is not everything. As the saying goes, ‘Unless you can play the fool and turn a deaf ear, you cannot be the elder of a household.’ The person in charge must bear injuries without complaint. Maids, older women servants, cooks, and chair bearers will all gossip behind her back. Has she the generosity to hear an insult aimed plainly at her—like cursing bald-headed scoundrels in front of a monk—and pretend she heard nothing, without the slightest displeasure showing on her face?” “As for that… I shall explain it clearly. She is sure to agree.” His mother shook her head emphatically. “Words and promises are one thing; the moment itself is another. Even a clay bodhisattva has a temper. If she loses patience and makes a scene, disrupting the household, you will regret it when it is too late.” Their perspectives differed. Old Madam Hu had met Luo years before, but could no longer remember even her appearance and could judge only by ordinary human behavior. Hu realized that he could not persuade his mother all at once. He must tell her more about Luo’s character and abilities. Once confidence grew, agreement would follow naturally.

就在这时候，古应春陪着洋人到了杭州，谈妥公事，派人陪着洋人去逛六桥三竺，古应春才跟胡雪岩详谈罗四姐所托之事。以及乌先生代笔信中的内容，认为事机已成熟，可以谈嫁娶了。“我门老太太还有顾虑。”胡雪岩说，“老太太是怕她只能任劳，不能任怨。”“那么，小爷叔，你看呢？”“这要先看我们怎样子待人家，”胡雪岩说：“罗四姐不肯拉倒，如果肯了，她总也知道，我不能拿元配休了，讨她做大太太，而只有做小。做小称太太，又让她掌权，她只要这样想一想，就算有闲言闲语难听，一口气咽得下去，自然心平气和了。”“小爷叔的话很透彻。”古应春自告奋勇，“我来跟老太太说。”

It was at this point that Gu arrived in Hangzhou with the foreign visitor. After their business was settled, someone else was sent to accompany the foreigner around the Six Bridges and Three Tianzhu Temples. Gu could then speak fully with Hu about Luo’s requests and Mr Wu’s letter. He thought the time was ripe to discuss marriage. “Mother still has doubts. She is afraid Sister Luo can bear hard work but not unfair criticism.” “What do you think, Little Uncle?” “That depends first on how we treat her. If she refuses, there is nothing more to say. If she agrees, she must understand that I cannot divorce my principal wife to make her First Madam. She can only enter as a concubine. Yet if she has the title of Madam and authority over the household, surely reflecting on that will make it easier to swallow unpleasant gossip and remain at peace.” “You have put it very clearly. Let me speak to your mother.”

说当然有个说法，根本不提胡雪岩，只谈七姑奶奶跟罗四姐如何投缘，以及罗四姐如何识好歹，因为七姑奶奶待她好，所以言听计从，情如同胞姐妹。胡老太太很尊重患难之交的古应春夫妇，对七姑奶奶更有份特殊的感情与信心，当时便说：“七姐中意的人，一定不会错的。这个媒要请七姐来做，我也要听了七姐的话才算数。”一桩好事，急转直下，看来成功在望了。但古应春心思细密，行事谨慎，觉得乐观的话以少说为宜。“老太太也不要太高兴，人家肯不肯，还在未知之数。”古应春接下来细谈七姑奶奶陪罗四姐去算命，几乎与吴铁口吵架的趣事，当然，他决不会透露，这是他们夫妇事先跟吴铁口说通了的秘密。胡老太太听得很仔细，而且越听笑意越浓，“原来她有这样的一副好八字，看来真是命中注定了。”她接着又说：“这种人的脾气是这样的，要嘛不肯，要肯了，说的话，一定有一句，算不句。”“小爷叔，”古应春又想到一件事：“不知道婶娘的意思怎么样？”“她肯的。”胡老太太接口，“我跟她谈过了，她要我作主，现在，七姐夫，这桩事情，我就拜托你了。”

Gu had his own approach. He did not mention Hu at all, speaking instead of how well his wife and Luo suited each other, and how Luo knew when she was being treated well. Because the Seventh Lady had been kind to her, Luo listened to everything she said; the two were like sisters. Old Madam Hu held the Gus, her friends through adversity, in great respect, and felt particular affection and confidence toward the Seventh Lady. “Anyone Seventh Sister approves of must be sound. She must arrange this match. I must hear what she has to say before deciding.” Matters had suddenly taken a favorable turn, and success seemed near. But Gu was thoughtful and cautious, and saw little reason to encourage excessive optimism. “Please do not be too pleased yet. Whether the other party will agree is still unknown.” He told her how his wife had taken Luo to have her fortune read and how Luo had almost quarreled with Wu Tiekou. Naturally, he concealed their advance arrangement with the fortune-teller. Old Madam Hu listened closely, smiling more and more. “So she has such excellent birth characters. It really does seem destined. People of that temperament either refuse outright or, once they consent, keep every word they give.” Gu thought of another point. “Little Uncle, what does your wife think?” “She agrees,” Old Madam Hu answered. “I have spoken to her. She leaves the decision to me. Now, Brother-in-Law Gu, I entrust the matter to you.”

“只要老太太作主，婶娘也不会埋怨，我同阿七当然要尽心尽力把这件事办圆满来。”于是古应春为胡雪岩策划，男家的媒人是七姑奶奶，女家的媒人不妨请乌先生承担。胡雪岩自然同意，便发了一份请帖，请乌先生吃饭。这在乌先生自有受宠若惊之感，准时到胡家来赴宴。做主人的介绍了古应春与其他的陪客，敬过一杯酒，托辞先离席了。席间闲谈，不及正事，饭罢到客座喝茶，古应春才将乌先生邀到一边，笑着说道：“乌先生，你我神交已久。”乌先生愕然，及至古应春提到彼此为罗四姐一家代笔的事，乌先生方始明白，人虽初识，笔迹早熟，这就是神交，因为如此，一切都好谈了。

“If you give your approval and your daughter-in-law will not resent us, A’qi and I will do everything we can to bring it to a satisfactory conclusion.” Gu proposed that the Seventh Lady act as matchmaker for Hu, while Mr Wu might represent the bride. Hu agreed and sent Mr Wu a dinner invitation. Naturally overwhelmed by the honor, the temple keeper arrived punctually. His host introduced Gu and the other guests, drank a cup with him, and then excused himself from the table. Conversation over dinner remained general; the real business was not mentioned. Only afterward, over tea, did Gu draw Mr Wu aside. “We have been acquaintances in spirit for a long time.” Mr Wu was puzzled until Gu explained their respective roles in writing letters for Luo’s family. Though they had never met, each already knew the other’s handwriting. That was their acquaintance at a distance, and it made everything easy to discuss.

“照此看来，事情已经定局了。”七站奶奶很高兴他说，“这乌先生看起来很关心罗四姐，不晓得他看了她的新房子，心里是怎么想？”乌先生等七姑奶奶一走，从房子看到摆饰，在他心目中无一不新，无一不精，想不到她如此阔气，只以有七姑奶奶这个初会面的堂客在，不便现于形色，怕人家笑话他没有见过世面，此时就不再需要任何矜持了，毫不掩饰地显出艳羡惊异的神态。“罗四姐，我真没有想到，你年纪轻轻一个女人家，会闯出这样一个场面来！上海我也来过两回，说实话，这样漂亮的帚子，我还是头一回见。”他紧接着又说：“古家当然是有身分的人家，房子虽比你的大，不过没有你的新，摆饰家具也比你多，可惜有细有粗，有好有坏，不比你的整齐。”听他这样夸赞，罗四姐心里有种说不出的舒服，人生得意之事，无过于从小相亲的熟人，看到此人肯争气、有出息，青云直上，乱目相看。她此时的心情，亦大有衣锦还乡之感，不过紧接着而来的感觉，却是美中不足的空虚。“房子、家具都不是我的，我哪里就到得了能这样子摆场面的地步？”

“Then the matter is settled!” the Seventh Lady said happily. “Mr Wu seems very concerned about Sister Luo. I wonder what he thinks of her new house.” Once she had left him there, Mr Wu had examined the house and its furnishings. Everything seemed new and exquisite. He had not imagined that Luo was so wealthy. With a woman he had only just met present, he had concealed his reaction for fear of appearing ignorant of the world. Now restraint was unnecessary, and his admiration and amazement showed without disguise. “I never expected a young woman like you to establish herself so splendidly. I have visited Shanghai twice before, but this is the first house of such beauty I have seen. The Gus are plainly people of standing. Their house is larger, but not as new. They have more furnishings, but fine pieces are mixed with ordinary ones, good with bad. Yours are so consistent throughout.” His praise gave Luo an indescribable pleasure. Few satisfactions could equal being seen by someone who had known one from childhood as a person of ambition and achievement, risen far enough to deserve new respect. She felt almost as though she had returned home in glory. Yet an emptiness followed: the glory was incomplete. “Neither house nor furniture is mine. How could I have risen far enough to maintain such a display?”

这话在乌先生并不觉得全然意外，略想一想说道：“就算是胡大先生替你置的，即使用了，就算是你的了。”“也不是他，是七姑奶奶的。”“七姑奶奶？”乌先生诧异，“你们罗家哪里跑出来这样一位姑奶奶？”“乌先生你缠到哪里去了？”罗四姐笑道：“就是古太太，娘家姓尤，行七，大家都叫她七姑奶奶，我叫她七姐。”“啊，啊，原来是她。”乌先生眨着眼想，越想越糊涂，“那么，古家两夫妇，怎么叫胡大先生‘小爷叔’？上海人叫叔叔叫‘爷叔’，胡大先生怎么会是他们的小叔叔？”其中有个缘故，我也是前几天才听七姑奶奶谈起，她的哥哥行五……“罗四姐告诉他说，尤五是松江漕帮的当家。尤五的师父跟胡雪岩是朋友，交情很厚，清帮中人，极重家规，所以尤五年龄虽比胡雪岩大，却尊他为长辈，七姑奶奶和古应春亦都跟着尤五叫胡雪岩为小爷叔。“照七姑奶奶说，松江的潜帮称为‘疲帮’。他们这一帮的漕船很多，是大帮，不过是个空架子，所以当家的带帮很吃力，亏得胡大先生帮他们的忙。为此，胡大先生在杭州到上海的这条水路上很吃得开，就因为松江漕帮的缘故。”

Mr Wu was not entirely surprised. “Even if Mr Hu bought them for you, once you use them, they are yours.” “It wasn’t he. They belong to the Seventh Lady.” “The Seventh Lady? Where did such a married aunt suddenly appear in your Luo family?” Luo laughed. “How have you got so confused? I mean Mrs Gu. Her maiden name is You, and she is seventh in her family. Everyone calls her the Seventh Lady; I call her Seventh Sister.” “Ah, so it is she.” The more he thought, the more confused he became. “Then why do the Gus call Mr Hu Little Uncle? Shanghai people use that word for an uncle. How can he be their young uncle?” Luo explained what she herself had learned only days before. The Seventh Lady’s brother, You Laowu, led the Songjiang Grain Transport Brotherhood. His master was Hu’s close friend. The Green Gang placed great weight on its rules of seniority, so although You was older than Hu, he honored him as an elder. His sister and Gu followed his usage. “Seventh Sister says the Songjiang group is called an exhausted brotherhood. It is large and has many grain boats, but little substance behind the name. Leading it is difficult, and Mr Hu has helped them greatly. That is why he has so much influence along the water route between Hangzhou and Shanghai.”

乌先生听得很仔细，一面听，一面在心里想他自己的事。他虽受托来做媒，但仔细想想；不是什么明媒正娶，他这个媒人也没有什么面子，所以一路上抱定一个主张，如果罗四姐本人不甚愿意，或者胡雪岩的为人，在杭州以外的地方，风评不佳，那就说不得打退堂鼓了。此刻看来，自己一路上的想法，似乎都不切实际了。既然如此，就不妨谈正事了，“罗四姐，”他说：“你晓不晓得，我这趟为啥来的？”这佯问法，罗四狙不免有些发窘，不过这是自己的终身大事，不能因为羞于出口，以致弄成误会，所以很沉着他说：“是不是我娘有什么话，请乌先生来跟我说。”“是的。我原来的意思，你娘即使不能来，写信给你，也是一样，你娘不赞成。她的话也有道理，写信问你，等你的回信，一来一去个把月，倒不如我来一趟，直接问个明白。”“娘要问我的是什么话？”“问你对胡大先生怎么样？”这一下，罗四姐的脸有些红了，“什么怎么样呢？”她用埋怨来遮掩羞涩，“乌先生你的话，说得不清不楚，叫我怎么说？”乌先生在关帝庙设座卖茶，一天见过三教九流的人不知多少，阅历甚丰，不过做媒人却是第一次，因而有时不免困惑，心想，大家都说“媒人的嘴”是最厉害的，成败往往在一句活上，到底如何是一言丧邦、一言兴邦，却始终无法模拟，不想，此时自然而然就懂了，他在想：只要答一句：“胡大先生要讨你做小。”罗四姐必然既羞且恼，一怒回绝，好事就难谐了。“如果乌先生对胡雪岩的印象不佳，他就会那样说，但此刻已决心来牵这根红线，便要拣最动听的话来说：“罗四姐，胡大先生要请你去当家。”

Mr Wu listened closely while considering his own position. He had agreed to act as matchmaker, but this was not a marriage to a principal wife through the full formal rites, and there was little distinction in arranging it. On the journey he had resolved that if Luo was not particularly willing, or Hu’s conduct outside Hangzhou had earned him an unfavorable reputation, he would have to withdraw. What he now saw made those earlier reservations seem unrealistic. He might as well turn to business. “Sister Luo, do you know why I have come?” The question embarrassed her. But this concerned the rest of her life; she must not let reluctance to speak create a misunderstanding. She answered steadily, “Has my mother asked you to tell me something?” “Yes. I thought that if she could not come herself, a letter would do just as well. But she disagreed, with reason. A letter to you and a reply would take a month or so between them. Better for me to come and ask you directly.” “What does she wish to ask?” “How you feel about Mr Hu.” Luo blushed. “Feel about him in what way?” She covered her shyness with a complaint. “You are being so vague. How can I answer?” Serving tea at the temple brought Mr Wu into contact with every sort of person, and his experience was considerable. Matchmaking, however, was new to him. People always spoke of a matchmaker’s formidable tongue: one sentence could make or ruin a match. He had never understood quite how a word could save a kingdom or destroy it, but now the meaning came naturally. If he simply said, “Mr Hu wants to take you as a concubine,” she would surely be angry and ashamed, refuse in indignation, and destroy the prospect. Had he thought poorly of Hu, that was what he would have said. Since he had now decided to join the pair, he chose the most pleasing words. “Mr Hu would like you to take charge of his household.”

这话让她心里一跳，但却不大敢相信，“哪里有这回事？”她说：“大家都叫胡大先生是‘财神’，他家那佯子大的排场，我怎么当得了他的家。”“罗四姐，我劝你不要客气，你的能干，从小就看得出来的，胡大先生向来最识人，他说要请你去当家，当然看准了你挑得起这副担子。”看来不象是随口玩笑的话，罗四姐不由得问一句：“真的？”“当然是真的。没有这句话，我根本不会来。”乌先生说：“名分上你已经吃亏了，没有别的东西来弥补，你想我肯不肯来做这个媒？”乌先生的话说得很巧妙，用“名分上已经吃亏了”的说法，代替听者刺耳的“做小”二字，罗四姐不知不觉便在心里接受了。“你的意思到底怎么样？”乌先生催问着，“如果你没有话，晚上我就要跟古太太去谈了。当然，我是女家的媒人，一定会替你争。”“怎么？为啥要跟七姑奶奶去谈？”罗四姐问“莫非她是……”“她是男家的媒人。”“我娘的意思呢？”“你娘情愿结这门亲的。”罗四姐心潮起伏，思前想后，觉得有些话是连在乌先生面前都难出口的，考虑了好一会说，“乌先生，你晓得的，七姑奶奶跟我象同胞姐妹一样，我看，我自己来问问她。”

Her heart leapt, but she hardly dared believe him. “Can that be true? Everyone calls him the God of Wealth. With such a grand establishment, how could I manage his household?” “There is no need for modesty. Your ability was evident from childhood. Mr Hu has always been an excellent judge of people. If he asks you to manage his house, he is certain you can bear the responsibility.” It did not sound like an idle joke. “Really?” “Of course. Without that undertaking, I would never have come. You would already be making a sacrifice in formal status. Without anything to compensate for it, do you think I would agree to arrange the match?” His wording was skillful. In place of the offensive word “concubine,” he spoke of a sacrifice in formal status, and Luo accepted the idea inwardly almost without noticing. “What do you think, then?” he urged. “If you have nothing further to say, I shall speak to Mrs Gu this evening. As your side’s matchmaker, I shall certainly press your interests.” “Why speak to the Seventh Lady? Is she…” “The matchmaker for his side.” “What does my mother think?” “She favors the marriage.” Luo’s feelings surged as she considered it from every angle. Some things were difficult to say even to Mr Wu. After a long pause, she replied, “You know that the Seventh Lady and I are like sisters. I think I had better ask her myself.”

“让我做个现成媒人，那再好都没有了。”乌先生说：“不过，罗四姐，你娘是托了我的，你自己跟古太太谈的辰光，不要忘记了替你娘留一条退路。”何谓“退路”？罗四姐不明白，便即问说：“乌先生，我娘是怎么跟你说的？”乌先生有些懊悔，“退路”的话是不应该说的。所谓“退路”是以罗四姐将来在胡家的身分，她母亲不会成为“亲家太太”，也就不会象亲戚那样往来，这样，便需为她筹一笔养老的款子，才是个“退路”。但看目前的情形，且不说罗四姐，即便是胡雪岩也一定会想到他那句话便是多余的了。因此，他就不肯再说实话，只是这样回答：“你娘没有说什么，是我想到的，养儿防老，积谷防饥，你要替你娘打算打算。”“原来是这一层！”罗四姐很轻松地答说：“我当然有打算的。”“那好，我也放心了。等下到了古家，你自己跟古太太去谈好了。”

“If I need only arrange a match you have settled yourselves, nothing could be better. But your mother has entrusted me with this, Sister Luo. When you speak to Mrs Gu, do not forget to leave your mother something to fall back on.” Luo did not understand. “What did my mother say to you?” Mr Wu regretted mentioning a safeguard. With the position Luo would occupy in the Hu household, her mother would not become a recognized fellow mother-in-law or visit on the footing of an ordinary relative. A fund should therefore be provided for her old age: that was the safeguard he meant. But in the present circumstances, surely not only Luo but Hu himself would think of it. The remark had been unnecessary. Unwilling to state his full meaning, he merely answered, “Your mother said nothing. It was my own thought. One raises children against old age and stores grain against hunger. You must make provision for her.” “So that is what you mean!” Luo answered readily. “Naturally, I have plans for that.” “Then I am reassured. When we reach the Gu house, speak to Mrs Gu yourself.”

为了替乌先生接风，古应春稍微用了些心思。乌先生既是生客，跟七姑奶奶又是第一次见面，应该照通常的规矩，男女分席，但主客一共四个人，分做两处，把交情都拉远了，而且说话也不方便，因此古应春决定请乌先生“吃大菜”。在人家家里“吃大菜”，乌先生还是第一回。幸好做主人的想得很周到，“吃大菜”的笑话见得多，刀子割破舌头虽是故甚其词，拿洗手指的水当冷开水喝，却非笑话，至于刀叉乱响，更是司空见惯之事，所以古应春除了刀叉以外，另备一双筷子。选的菜，第一，避免半生的牛排，第二，凡是肉类都先去骨头，第三，调味少用西洋的佐料。不过酒是洋酒，也不分饭前酒、饭后酒，黄的、白的、红的，摆好了几瓶，请乌先生随意享用。“乌先生！”七姑奶奶入座时就说：“自己人，我说老实话，用不惯刀叉，用筷子好了。”“是！是！恭敬不如从命，我就老实了。”乌先生欣然举著。“乌先生看见罗四姐的新房子了？”七姑奶奶有意将“子”字念得极轻，听去象“新房”。在她是开玩笑，乌先生却误会了，以为将来罗四姐会长住上海，她目前的新居，将来便是双栖之处。心想，如果是这样子，又怎么让罗四姐去当家？心里有些疑问，却不暇细思，因为要回答七姑奶奶的话，“好得很。”他说：“我听罗四姐说，是古太太一手经理的。”“乌先生，”罗四姐不等他话完，便即说道：“你叫七姐，也叫七姑奶奶好了。”“好！七姑奶奶，真是中帼英雄！”“怎么会想出这么一句话来？”罗四姐笑道：“恭维嘛，也要恭维得象才是。七姐又不是‘白相人嫂嫂’，怎么叫中帼英雄？”乌先生自己也觉得拟于不伦，便即说道：“我来之前，‘大书’说岳传，正说梁红玉擂鼓破金兵，‘中帼英雄’这句话听得多了，才会脱口而出。”

Gu gave some thought to the dinner welcoming Mr Wu. As a new guest meeting his wife for the first time, he should, by ordinary custom, dine separately from the women. But there were only four of them. Dividing the company would create distance and make conversation awkward. Gu therefore decided on a Western dinner. Mr Wu had never eaten one in a private house. Fortunately, his host had considered the difficulties. There were many stories of mishaps at Western meals. Cutting one’s tongue with a knife was an exaggeration, but drinking the finger-bowl water as though it were plain drinking water was no joke; clattering knives and forks were commonplace. Gu provided chopsticks as well as Western cutlery. He avoided underdone beef, had every meat dish boned, and used few Western seasonings. The drinks, however, were foreign. Instead of distinguishing between those served before or after food, he set out several bottles—yellow, white, and red—for Mr Wu to choose. As they sat down, the Seventh Lady said frankly, “We are among friends. If you are not used to knives and forks, use chopsticks.” “Very well. Obedience is better than ceremony. I shall be frank too.” He happily picked up his chopsticks. “Have you seen Sister Luo’s new house?” The Seventh Lady softened the last part of the Chinese word, making it sound like “bridal chamber.” She was joking, but Mr Wu misunderstood. He thought Luo would remain in Shanghai and her present home would become the couple’s shared residence. How, then, could she manage Hu’s household? He had no time to examine the doubt, for he must answer. “It is excellent. Sister Luo tells me you arranged it all, Mrs Gu.” Before he could finish, Luo said, “Please call her Seventh Sister, or the Seventh Lady.” “Very well. Seventh Lady, you are a heroine among women!” “How did you think of that?” Luo laughed. “Even a compliment must fit. Seventh Sister isn’t some adventurer’s wife. Why call her a heroine?” Mr Wu himself felt the comparison was misplaced. “Before I came, the storytellers were performing the tale of Yue Fei. They had reached Liang Hongyu beating the war drums to defeat the Jin. I heard ‘heroine among women’ so often that it slipped out.”

“乌先生喜欢听大书，明天我陪你。”古应春爱好此道，兴致勃勃他说：“城隍庙的两档大书，一裆‘英烈’，一档‘水浒’，都是响档。乌先生不可错过机会。”“苏州话，”罗四姐说，“乌先生恐怕听不懂。”“听得懂、听得懂。”乌先生接着用生硬的苏白说道：“阴立，白坐。”大家都笑了。“乌先生不但懂。”古应春说：“而且是内行。”原来“阴立、白坐”是“英烈、白蛇”的谐音，是书场里挖苦刮皮客的术语，有的阴阴地站在角落，不花一文听完一回书。名为“阴立”，有的大大方方坐在后面，看跑堂的要‘打钱“了，悄悄起身溜走，名为”白坐“。由于彼此同好，皆有喜遇知音之感，大谈“大书”，以及说书人的流派。罗四姐见此光景，轻轻向七姑奶奶说道：“乌先生这顿酒会吃到半夜，我们离桌吧！”

“If you enjoy storytelling, I shall take you tomorrow.” Gu, a devotee himself, spoke eagerly. “Two performances at the City God Temple, one of Tales of Heroes and the other of Water Margin, are both celebrated. You must not miss the chance.” “They speak Suzhou dialect,” Luo pointed out. “Mr Wu may not understand.” “I understand, I understand.” In stiff Suzhou speech, he added, “Yinli, baizuo.” Everyone laughed. “He not only understands,” Gu said. “He knows the business.” The expressions were puns on Yinglie, Tales of Heroes, and Baishe, White Snake. Story-house patrons used them to mock freeloaders. Some stood furtively in a corner and heard an entire episode without paying a copper: “shadow standing,” yinli. Others sat quite openly at the back, then slipped away as soon as the attendant came to collect payment: “free sitting,” baizuo. Discovering their shared enthusiasm, Gu and Mr Wu felt the pleasure of meeting a kindred spirit and talked at length about storytelling and its different schools. Luo watched them, then said quietly to the Seventh Lady, “Mr Wu will be drinking until midnight. Let us leave the table.”

七姑奶奶亦正有此意。找个空隙，打断他们的谈锋，说了两句做女主人应有的门面话，与罗四姐双双席席。七姑奶奶将她带到楼上卧室。这间卧室一直为罗四姐所欣赏，因为经过古应春设计，改成西式，有个很宽敞的阳台，装置很大的玻璃门，门上加两层帷幕、一层薄纱、一层丝绒，白天拉开丝绒那一层，阳光透过薄纱，铺满整个房间，明亮华丽，令人精神一爽。晚上坐在阳台上看万家灯火，亦别有一番情趣，尤其是象这种夏天，在阳台上纳凉闲谈，是最舒服不过的一件事。“你是喝中国茶，还是喝洋茶？”所谓“喝洋茶”是英国式的奶茶。七姑奶奶有全套的银茶具，照英国规矩亲自调制，而且亲自为客人倒茶，颇为费事。罗四姐此刻要谈正事，无心欣赏“洋茶”，便即说道：“我想吃杯菊花茶。”黄白“杭菊花”可以当茶叶泡来喝，有清心降火之功，七姑奶奶笑着问道：“你大概心里很乱？”“也不晓得啥道理，心里一直烦躁。”“我们到阳台上来坐。”七姑奶奶挑到阳台上去密谈，是替罗四姐设想，因为谈到自己的终身大事，她难免腼腆，阳台上光线幽暗，可以隐藏妞促的表情，就比较能畅所欲言了。

The Seventh Lady had been thinking the same thing. Finding a pause, she interrupted the men's flow of talk with a few of the gracious remarks expected of a hostess, and the two women left the table. She took Luo Sijie upstairs to her bedroom, which Luo had always admired. Gu Yingchun had redesigned it in the Western style, with a spacious balcony and large glass doors hung with two layers of curtains, one gauze and the other velvet. When the velvet curtains were drawn back by day, sunlight passed through the gauze and filled the room, making it bright, splendid, and wonderfully refreshing. At night, the sight of countless lights from the balcony had a charm of its own. In summer, especially, nothing could be more comfortable than sitting there in the cool air and talking. “Will you have Chinese tea or foreign tea?” Foreign tea meant English tea with milk. The Seventh Lady had a complete silver tea service and followed the English custom of preparing the tea herself and pouring it for her guests, a rather elaborate business. Luo, intent on discussing serious matters, had no mind to appreciate it. “I'd like a cup of chrysanthemum tea.” The yellow and white Hangzhou chrysanthemums could be brewed like tea to calm the mind and dispel internal heat. “Is your mind rather unsettled?” the Seventh Lady asked with a smile. “I don't know why, but I've been feeling restless all this time.” “Let's sit out on the balcony.” She chose the balcony out of consideration for Luo. Discussing her own marriage was bound to make her shy; in the dim light she could conceal her embarrassment and speak more freely.

等小大姐泡了菊花茶来，背光坐着的罗四姐幽幽地叹口气说：“七姐只怕我真的是命中注定了。”“喔，”七姑奶奶问道：“胡家托乌先生来作媒了，他怎么说？”“他说的话也不晓得是真是假？说胡大先生的意思，要我去替他当家。”“不错，这话应春也听见的。”“这么说，看起来是真的！”罗四姐心里更加踏实，但心头的疑虑亦更浓重，“七姐，你说。 我凭啥资格去替他当家？”七姑奶奶心想，胡雪岩顾虑者在此，罗四姐要争者亦在此，足见都是厉害角色，不开口则已，一开口必中要害。不过，她虽然已从古应春口中摸透了“行情”，却不愿轻易松口，因为不知道罗四姐还会开什么条件，不能不谨慎行事。于是她试探地问道：“四姐，你自己倒说呢？要啥资格，才好去替他当家。”“当家人的身分，身分不高，下人看不起，你说的话他左耳进、右耳出，七姐，你说，这个家我怎么当？”“是的。这话很实在。我想，我们小爷叔，不会不懂这个道理，他总有让下人敬重你的办法。”

When the maid had brought their chrysanthemum tea, Luo, sitting with her face turned away from the light, gave a soft sigh. “Seventh Sister, perhaps it really is my destiny.” “Oh? The Hu family has asked Mr Wu to act as matchmaker. What did he say?” “I don't know whether to believe him. He said Mr Hu wanted me to run his household.” “That's true. Yingchun heard him say it too.” “Then it seems he really means it!” Luo felt more assured, yet her misgivings grew stronger. “Tell me, Seventh Sister, what standing would I have to run his household?” This, the Seventh Lady reflected, was precisely what troubled Hu Xueyan and what Luo meant to fight for. They were both formidable people: once either of them spoke, the words went straight to the heart of the matter. Although Gu had already told her exactly how things stood, she was unwilling to commit herself too readily. She did not know what further conditions Luo might put forward, so caution was necessary. “What do you think yourself?” she asked tentatively. “What standing would you need to manage the household?” “It is the housekeeper's position that matters. If your rank is low, the servants look down on you. Everything you say goes in one ear and out the other. Tell me, how could I run a household like that?” “Yes, that's a very practical consideration. I don't suppose Little Uncle fails to understand it. He will find some way to make the servants respect you.”

“啥办法？”罗四姐紧接着问，“七姐夫怎么说？”“他说，胡老太太托我来做媒。不过，我还不敢答应。”罗四姐又惊又喜，“原来是胡老太太出面？”她问：“胡太太呢？”“他们家一切都是老太太作主。胡太太最贤惠不过，老太太说啥就是啥，百依百顺的。”听得这一说，罗四姐心头宽松了些，不过七姑奶奶何以不敢答应做媒？这话她却不好意思问。“我为啥不敢答应呢？”七姑奶奶自问自答他说：“因为我们虽然一见如故，象同胞姐妹一样，到底这是你的终身大事，你没有跟我详详细细谈过，我不晓得你心里的想法，如果冒冒失失答应下来，万一做不成这个媒，反而伤了我们感情。”“七姐，这一层你尽管放心。不管怎么样，你我的感情是不会伤的。”“有你这句话，我的胆就大了。四姐，除了名分以外，还有啥？请你一样一样告诉我。看哪一样是我可以代为答应下来的，哪一样我能替你争的，哪一样是怎么样也办不到的。”

“What way?” Luo asked at once. “What did Brother-in-Law Gu say?” “He said Old Madam Hu had asked me to act as matchmaker. But I haven't dared agree yet.” Luo was both startled and delighted. “So Old Madam Hu herself is behind this? What about Mrs Hu?” “The old lady decides everything in their household. Mrs Hu is as virtuous as can be. Whatever the old lady says, she accepts; she obeys her in everything.” Luo felt easier on hearing this. But why had the Seventh Lady not dared accept the commission? She was too embarrassed to ask. “Why haven't I dared agree?” the Seventh Lady went on, answering her own question. “Though we felt like old friends from the moment we met, as close as real sisters, this is still your marriage, a matter for your whole life. You haven't talked it over with me in detail, so I don't know exactly what you want. If I rashly agreed and then failed to arrange the match, it might end by hurting our friendship.” “Seventh Sister, you can put that fear aside. Whatever happens, it will never hurt the friendship between us.” “That gives me courage. Sister Luo, apart from your formal status, what else is there? Tell me everything, one thing at a time. Then we can see what I can agree to on their behalf, what I can try to obtain for you, and what cannot possibly be done.”

“怎么佯办不到的事，我也不会说。”罗四姐想了一下说：“七姐，我顶为难的是我老娘。”她老娘何以会成为难题？七姑奶奶想一想才明白，必是指的当亲戚来往这件事。以她的看法，这件事是否为难，主要的是要看罗四姐自己的态度？倘或她坚持要胡老太太叫一声“亲家太太”，这就为难了！否则胡家也容易处置。谈到这里，话就要明说了，“四姐，你的意思我懂了。”她说：“还有啥，你一股脑儿说出来，我们一样一样来商量。”“还有，你晓得的，我有个女儿。”“你的女儿当然姓她老子的姓。”七姑奶奶说：“你总不见得肯带到胡家去吧？”“当然，那算啥一出？”“既然不带到胡家，那就是你自己的事，不管你怎么安排，胡家都不便过问的。这件事可以不必谈，还有啥？”

“I wouldn't ask for anything impossible.” Luo thought for a moment. “My mother is my greatest difficulty.” Why should her mother present a difficulty? After a little thought, the Seventh Lady understood: Luo must mean whether the two families would acknowledge each other as relatives by marriage. In her view, whether this became a problem depended chiefly on Luo's own attitude. If she insisted that Old Madam Hu address her mother as a fellow mother-in-law, that would indeed be difficult. Otherwise, the Hu family could easily manage it. At this point, they had to speak plainly. “I understand what you mean. What else is there? Tell me everything, and we'll discuss the points one by one.” “Then there's my daughter, as you know.” “Your daughter naturally bears her father's surname,” said the Seventh Lady. “Surely you wouldn't want to take her into the Hu household?” “Of course not. What sort of arrangement would that be?” “Since you won't be bringing her into their household, she is your own concern. Whatever arrangements you make, the Hu family would have no business interfering. We needn't discuss that. What else?”

“还有，我只能给老太太一个人磕头。”“是不是！”七姑奶奶马上接口，“我不敢答应，就是怕你有这样的话，叫我说都不便去说的。”罗四姐自己也觉得要求过分了一些，不过话既已出口，亦不便自己收回，因而保持沉默。当然，在七姑奶奶看，这就是不再坚持的表示，能商量得通的。“四姐，我现在把人家的意思告诉你：第一是称呼，下人部叫你太太，第二进门磕一个头，以后都是平礼，第三生了儿子着红裙。这三洋，是老太大交代下来的。”罗四姐考虑了一会，觉得就此三事而言，再争也争不出什么名堂来，不如放漂亮些，换取对方在他处的让步。于是她说：“七姐这么说，我听七姐的。不过，我进他家的门，不晓得是怎么个进法？”

“One more thing: I can kowtow to the old lady, but to no one else.” “There!” the Seventh Lady replied immediately. “That is just why I was afraid to agree. I feared you might say something like this, a condition I couldn't even bring myself to put to them.” Luo herself felt she had asked a little too much. Having said it, however, she could hardly withdraw it of her own accord, so she remained silent. To the Seventh Lady, this naturally meant that she was no longer insisting and could be persuaded. “Now let me tell you what the family proposes. First, the form of address: all the servants will call you Madam. Second, you will make the required kowtow when you first enter the household; after that, all greetings will be exchanged as between equals. Third, once you have borne a son, you may wear a red skirt. These three instructions come from the old lady herself.” Luo considered them for a while. She felt that, on these three points, no amount of argument would gain her anything further. Better to concede gracefully and obtain concessions elsewhere. “If that is what you say, Seventh Sister, I'll accept your advice. But how exactly am I to enter their household?”

七姑奶奶心想，这是明知故问。妾侍进门，无非一乘一轿抬进门，在红烛高烧之下，一一磕头定称呼。罗四姐问到这话，意思是不是想要坐花轿进门呢？当然，照一般的办法，是太委屈了她，但亦决无坐花轿之理。七姑奶奶觉得这才真的遇见难题了。想了又想，七姑奶奶只能这佯回答：“这件事我来想办法，总归要让你面子上看得过去。你明天倒问问乌先生，看他有啥好办法？”正事谈到这里，实在也可以说是很顺利了。做媒本来就要往返磋商，一步一步将双方意见接近来，罗四姐也很明白事缓则圆的道理，因而很泰然地答说：“事情不急，七姐尽管慢慢想。”“你是不急，小爷叔恐怕急着要想做新郎官。”七姑奶奶笑着将她的脸扳向亮处，“不晓得你装扮成新娘子，是个啥样子？”这话说得罗四姐心里不知是何滋味？说一句：“七姐真会寻开心。”一闪站起身来，“乌先生不知道吃好了没有？”“我们一起下去看看。”

The Seventh Lady thought that Luo knew the answer perfectly well. A concubine was carried into the house in an ordinary sedan chair and, before the blazing red candles, made the kowtows that established her rank and the proper forms of address. Was Luo asking because she wanted to arrive in a decorated bridal chair? Certainly the ordinary procedure would be too humiliating for her, but there could be no question of the bridal chair either. Here, the Seventh Lady felt, was a real difficulty. After much thought, she could only say, “I'll try to find a way. Whatever we do, it must preserve your dignity. Ask Mr Wu tomorrow and see whether he has a good idea.” Their discussion had, in fact, gone very smoothly. Matchmaking always required negotiation back and forth, bringing the two sides closer step by step.
