Luo understood that patience gave matters time to come right. “There's no hurry,” she answered calmly. “Take your time thinking it over.” “You may not be in a hurry, but Little Uncle is probably eager to become a bridegroom.” With a smile, the Seventh Lady turned Luo's face toward the light. “I wonder what you'll look like dressed as a bride.” Luo could hardly have described the feelings this stirred in her. “You do love teasing me!” she said, springing to her feet. “I wonder whether Mr Wu has finished his dinner.” “Let's go down together and see.”

两人携着手夏回楼下，只见古应春陪着乌先生在赏鉴那些西洋小摆设。七姑奶奶少不得问些吃饭了没有之类的客气话，然后间到乌先生下榻之处。“客栈已经定好了。”古应春问道：“不知道罗四姐今天晚上，是不是还有事要跟乌先生谈？”“今天太晚了。”罗四姐答说：“有事明天也可以谈。”“那么，我送乌先生回客栈。明天一早我会派人到客栈陪了乌先主到罗四姐那里。下午我陪乌先生到各处逛逛。”等古应春送客回来，七姑奶奶还没有睡，等着要将与罗四姐谈论的情形告诉他，最后谈到罗四姐如何“进胡家的门”。“一顶小轿抬进门，东也磕头，西也磕头，且不说罗四姐委屈，我们做媒人的也没有面子。”“为小爷叔，没有面子也就算了。”古应春说：“你不要把你的想法也摆进去，那一来事情就越发摆不平了。”“好！那么罗四姐，总要让他的面子过得去。”“这有点难办。又有里子，又要面子，世界上恐怕没有那么便宜的事。”七姑奶奶也觉得丈夫的话不错，不过已经答应罗四姐要让她“面子上过得去。”所以仍在苦苦思索。“睡吧！我累了。”古应春旅途劳顿，一上床，鼾声即起，七姑奶奶却无法合眼，最后终于想到了一个办法，而且自己觉得很得意，很想唤醒古应春来谈，却又不忍，只好闷在心里。

Hand in hand, they went downstairs, where Gu Yingchun was showing Mr Wu his little Western ornaments. The Seventh Lady made the customary inquiries about whether their guest had eaten enough, then asked where he was staying. “His room at the inn has already been booked,” Gu said. “Does Sister Luo have anything else she wants to discuss with Mr Wu tonight?” “It's too late tonight. Anything we need to discuss can wait until tomorrow.” “Then I'll take Mr Wu back to his inn. First thing tomorrow, I'll send someone there to accompany him to your house. In the afternoon, I'll show him around.” When Gu returned from seeing their guest home, the Seventh Lady was still awake, waiting to tell him about her conversation with Luo. She ended with the question of how Luo was to enter the Hu household. “To be carried in in a little chair and made to kowtow here, there, and everywhere—quite apart from the humiliation to Sister Luo, it would do us matchmakers no credit.” “For Little Uncle's sake, we can put up with losing a little face,” Gu said. “Don't add your own feelings to the problem. That will only make it harder to settle.” “Very well! But at least Sister Luo must be allowed to keep her dignity.” “That's rather difficult. To get both the substance and all the outward honours—I'm afraid there are few bargains as good as that in this world.” The Seventh Lady knew her husband had a point, but she had promised Luo a dignified arrangement and went on searching for a solution. “Go to sleep. I'm tired,” Gu said. Exhausted by his journey, he began to snore as soon as he was in bed. She could not close her eyes. At last she hit upon an idea of which she was particularly proud. She wanted to wake him and discuss it, but could not bear to disturb him, so she kept it to herself.

第二天一早，古应春正在漱洗时，七姑奶奶醒了，掀开珠罗纱的帐子，探头说道：“不要紧了！我有法子了。”没头没脑一句话，说得古应春愣在那里，好一会才省悟，“你是说罗四姐？”他问。“对。”七姑奶奶起床，倦眼惺松，但脸上别有一种兴奋的神情，“他们的喜事在上海办，照两头大的办法，一样可以坐花轿、着红裙。”她问：“你看呢？”“小爷叔在杭州有大太大的，无人不知，人家问起来怎么说？”“兼桃！”七姑奶奶脱口回答：“哪个去查他们的家谱？”“这话倒也是。不知道小爷叔肯不肯？”“肯不肯是他自己的事，我们做媒人的，是有交代了。”七姑奶奶又说：“我想他也不会不肯的。”古应春考虑了一会，同意了她的办法，只问：“回到杭州呢？”“照回门的办法，先到祖宗堂磕头，再见老太太磕头。”“这不是哈回门的办法，是‘庙见’，这就抬举罗四姐的身分了。”古应春深深点头：“可以！”“你说可以就定规了。下半天，你问问乌先生，看他怎么说。”“能这样，乌先生还有什么话说？至到你说‘走规’，这话是错了，要小爷叔答应了才能定规。”“你这么说，那就快写信去问。”古应春觉得不必如此匆促。不过，这一点他觉得也不必跟爱妻去争，反正是不是写了信，她也不会知道，所以答应着说：“我会写。”

Early the next morning, while Gu was washing, the Seventh Lady awoke, drew aside the gauze bed curtains, and poked out her head. “It's all right now! I've found a way.” Gu stared, bewildered by this announcement without preamble. After a moment he understood. “You mean Sister Luo?” “Yes.” She got out of bed, her eyes still heavy with sleep but her face alight with excitement. “They can hold the wedding in Shanghai, with two wives of equal standing in separate households. Then she can have both the decorated bridal chair and the red skirt. What do you think?” “Everyone knows Little Uncle already has a principal wife in Hangzhou. What will they say when people ask?” “He can be heir to two family branches!” she answered at once. “Who's going to investigate their genealogy?” “There's something in that. I wonder whether Little Uncle would agree.” “That's for him to decide. We matchmakers will at least have offered a solution. Besides, I don't think he'll refuse.” Gu considered the idea and agreed to it, asking only, “What happens when she goes back to Hangzhou?” “Treat it like a bride's return visit to her parents: first she kowtows in the ancestral hall, then she meets the old lady and kowtows to her.” “That isn't a return visit to her parents. It's the formal presentation at the ancestral shrine. That would raise Sister Luo's standing.” Gu nodded emphatically. “It could work.” “If you think so, it's settled. Ask Mr Wu this afternoon and see what he says.” “If it can be arranged that way, what objection could he have? But you're wrong to say it's settled. It can only be settled when Little Uncle agrees.” “Then write quickly and ask him.” Gu thought there was no need for such haste. He also thought there was no need to argue with his beloved wife over it: she would not know whether he had written or not. “I'll write,” he said.

乌先生上午去看了罗四姐，下午由古应春陪着他，坐了马车去观光，一圈兜下来，乌先生自己提出要求，想到古家来吃晚饭，为的是谈罗四姐的亲事。“我跟她谈过了，她说她的意思，七姑奶奶都晓得。不过，既然我是媒人，她说有些话，要我跟七姑奶奶来商量。““是的。乌先生你说。”第一件，将来两家是不是当亲戚来往，现在暂且可以不管。不过，她的女儿，要胡太太认做子女儿，将来要到胡家来的，下人要叫她‘干小姐’。““胡太太的儿女，还要叫她妹妹。”七姑奶奶补充着，极有把握他说：“这件事包在我身上。”“第二件比较麻烦，她说七姑奶奶答应了她的，要我请问七姑奶奶，不晓得是啥办法？”“办法是想到一个，不过，还不敢作主。这个办法，一定要胡大先生点了头才能算数。”“是的，做媒本来要双方自己愿意，象七姑奶奶这样爽快有担当，肯代胡大先生作主，真是难得。”乌先生可说：“不过，先谈谈也不要紧。”

Mr Wu visited Luo that morning. In the afternoon, Gu took him sightseeing by carriage, and when they had completed their tour, Mr Wu himself asked to dine at the Gu house so that they could discuss the marriage. “I've talked to her. She says the Seventh Lady knows what she wants. Still, since I'm acting as matchmaker, she has asked me to discuss a few points with you.” “Yes, Mr Wu. Please go ahead.” “First, whether the two families will deal with each other as relatives by marriage can be left aside for now. But she wants Mrs Hu to take her daughter as a god-daughter. The girl will be visiting the Hu house, and the servants must address her as the family's young god-daughter.” “And Mrs Hu's children must call her their younger sister,” the Seventh Lady added with complete confidence. “Leave that to me.” “The second point is more difficult. She says you made her a promise, and she has asked me to find out what arrangement you have in mind.” “We have thought of one, but I can't commit us to it yet. Mr Hu must approve it before it can be agreed.” “Of course. In matchmaking, both parties must consent. It is rare to find someone so decisive and ready to take responsibility on Mr Hu's behalf as you are. But there can be no harm in discussing it first.”

这件事很有关系，七姑奶奶心想，倘或自己说错了一句话，要收回或更改就不漂亮了，不如让她丈夫去谈，自己在一旁察言观色，适时加以纠正或者补充，比较妥当。于是古应春便在她授意之下，讲他们夫妇这天清早商量好的办法。讲得一点不错，七姑奶奶认为无需作何修正。倒是乌先生的态度，让她奇怪，只见他一面听，一面锁紧眉头，她不知道这是乌先生在用心思索一件事时，惯有的样子，只当他对这样的办法还不满意，心里不免大起反感。于是等古应春讲完了，她冷冷地问：“乌先生觉得这个办法，还有啥欠缺的地方？”“不是欠缺，我看很不妥当。”这就连古应春都诧异了，“乌先生，请你说个道理看。”他问“何以不妥当。”“胡大先生现在是天下闻名的人，佩服他、赞成他的人很多，妒忌他、要他好看的人也不少。万一京里的御史老爷参上一本，不得了。”“参上一本？参胡大先生？”“这我就不懂。”七姑奶奶接着也说，“犯了啥错？御史要参他。”“七姑奶奶，请你耐耐心，听我说……”

The matter was consequential. If she herself said something wrong, the Seventh Lady thought, it would look awkward to withdraw or alter it. Better to let her husband explain while she watched Mr Wu's expression and supplied a correction or addition at the right moment. At her prompting, Gu described the plan they had discussed that morning. He explained it perfectly, and she felt no need to amend anything. Mr Wu's manner, however, puzzled her. As he listened, his brows drew together. She did not know this was simply his customary expression when thinking hard; she supposed that he was dissatisfied with their proposal and began to resent it. When Gu had finished, she asked coldly, “What does Mr Wu find lacking in this arrangement?” “It isn't a matter of something lacking. I think it is very inappropriate.” Now even Gu was astonished. “Please tell us why. What is inappropriate about it?” “Mr Hu is famous throughout the country. Many people admire and support him, but plenty are jealous and would like to teach him a lesson. If one of the censors in the capital submitted an impeachment, it could cause serious trouble.” “An impeachment? Against Mr Hu?” “I don't understand either,” the Seventh Lady put in. “What wrong would he have committed for a censor to impeach him?” “Seventh Lady, please be patient and let me explain.”

原来乌先生的先世是杭州府钱塘县的刑房书办，已历四代，现在由乌先生的长兄承袭，《大清律例》是他的家学，对“户婚律”当然亦很熟悉，所以能为古应春夫妇作一番很详细的解释。他说，以“兼祧”为取“两头大”的借口，是刁俗如此，而律无明文，不过既然习俗相沿，官府亦承认的，只是兼祧亦有一定的规矩，如俗语所说的“两房台一子”，方准兼桃，这在胡雪岩的情形，显然不合。“你们两位请想，即称‘胡大先生’及有‘胡二先生’，好比合肥李家，有‘李大先生’李瀚章，就一定有‘李二先生’李鸿章。胡大先生既然有兄弟，就可以承继给他无子的叔伯，何用他来兼祧？”“这话说得有道理，‘胡大先生’这个称呼，就摆明了他是有兄弟的。”古应春对他妻子说：“兼桃这两个字，无论如何用不上。”“用不上就不能娶两房正室。一定要这么办，且不说大清律上怎么样，论官常先就有亏了，这叫做‘宠妾灭妻’，御史老爷一本参上去，事实俱在，逃都逃不了的。”

Mr Wu's forebears had served as clerks in the criminal section of the Qiantang county office in Hangzhou Prefecture for four generations. His eldest brother had now inherited the post. The Great Qing Code was a family field of learning, and he was naturally familiar with its provisions on households and marriage. He could therefore give the couple a detailed explanation. Using succession to two family branches as a pretext for taking two wives of equal standing, he said, was a crafty practice established by custom, with no explicit basis in the code. Since the custom had long been followed, the authorities did recognize it, but only under certain conditions. As the saying went, there must be “one son between two branches” before he could serve as heir to both. Hu Xueyan's case plainly failed to meet that requirement. “Consider his title. If there is an Eldest Mr Hu, there is also a Second Mr Hu. It is like the Li family of Hefei: where there is an Eldest Mr Li, Li Hanzhang, there must be a Second Mr Li, Li Hongzhang. Since Mr Hu has brothers, one of them could be adopted as heir by a childless uncle. Why should he himself have to carry on two branches?” “That makes sense. Calling him Eldest Mr Hu shows plainly that he has brothers.” Turning to his wife, Gu said, “Whatever else we do, we cannot invoke succession to two branches.” “And without that, he cannot take two principal wives. If he insists, quite apart from what the Qing code may say, he will already have violated the standards expected of an official. This is called favouring a concubine at the expense of one's wife. A censor need only submit an impeachment: the facts would be there, with no way of evading them.”

一听这话，七姑奶奶吓出一身冷汗，“真是亏得乌先生指点，”她说，“差点做错了事情，害我们小爷叔栽个筋斗。”“筋斗倒也栽不大，不过面子难看。”乌先生又说：“讲老实话，胡大先生还在其次，我先要替罗四姐想一想，倘或因为她想坐花轿、穿红裙，弄出来这场麻烦，胡老太太、胡大先生一定很不高兴，说风凉知的人就会说：‘一进门就出事，一定是个扫帚星。’七姑奶奶你倒想，罗四姐以后还好做人？”“乌先生，你想得真周到，见识真正高人一等。”七姑奶奶由衷的佩服，“而且人家本来不知道罗四姐是啥身分，这一来‘妾’的名声就‘卖朝报’了。”“卖朝报”是句杭州的俗话，还是南宋时候传下来的，老百姓的名字忽然在“朝报”上出现，一定出了新闻，“卖朝报”的人为广招徕，必然大声吆喝，以至大街小巷，无人不知。如果胡雪岩因为“宠妾灭妻”而奉旨申斥，上谕中就会有罗四姐的名字。清朝的“宫门抄”就是南宋的“朝报”，所以七姑奶奶的这个譬喻，十分贴切。“是啊！”乌先生说，“那一来，不但杭州上海，到处都知道了，真正叫做‘求荣反辱’。我想我只要一说明白，罗四姐一定也懂的。”“是，是！”古应春忽忙接口，“那就拜托先生跟罗四姐婉言解释。只要讲一层讲通了，我想我们的这个媒就做成功了。”

The Seventh Lady broke into a cold sweat. “It's fortunate you explained this, Mr Wu. I nearly made a mistake that could have brought Little Uncle down.” “The fall would not be very serious, but it would look bad. To tell the truth, Mr Hu is my second concern. I must think of Sister Luo first. If her wish for a decorated bridal chair and a red skirt brought on all this trouble, Old Madam Hu and Mr Hu would certainly be displeased. Those inclined to sneer would say, ‘Trouble the moment she enters the house! She must bring bad luck.’ Think how hard her life would be after that.” “You have considered everything, Mr Wu. Your judgement is truly exceptional.” The Seventh Lady's admiration was sincere. “Besides, people might not originally have known her status. Then the fact that she was a concubine would be hawked about like the Court Gazette.” “Hawking the Court Gazette” was a Hangzhou expression handed down from the Southern Song. If an ordinary person's name suddenly appeared in the gazette, something newsworthy must have happened. The sellers would shout it out to attract customers until everyone in every street and alley knew. If Hu were reprimanded by imperial decree for favouring a concubine at his wife's expense, Luo's name would appear in the edict. The Qing Palace Gate Bulletin corresponded to the Southern Song Court Gazette, making the Seventh Lady's comparison especially apt. “Exactly,” Mr Wu said. “Then people everywhere would know, not just in Hangzhou and Shanghai. She would truly have sought honour and gained disgrace. I think she'll understand once I explain it clearly.” “Yes, yes!” Gu put in hastily. “Then please explain it to her tactfully. If we can settle this one point, I think our match will be made.”

罗四姐自然能够体谅其中的苦衷，但总觉得快快有不足之意，不过对七姑奶奶极力帮她讲话出主意，非常感激，因而也就更觉得可以说知心话，所以反而拿乌先生向她解释的话，来跟七姑奶奶商量。“四姐，我想劝你一句话，英雄不怕出身低，一个人要收缘结果好，才是真正的风光。你不是心胸不开阔的人，不要再在这上头计较了。”七姑奶又说：“我当你陪嫁的奶妈，送了你去，你看好不好？”江浙风俗，富家小姐出阁时，贴身的侍女、哺育的乳母，往往都陪嫁到夫家，而且保留着原来的称呼。罗四姐听七姑奶奶用这样的说法，表示就算委屈，她亦愿意分担，这份情意，求之于同胞姐妹，亦未见得必有，应该能够弥补一切了。“七姐，”罗四姐眼圈红红他说：“我也不知道前世敲破了多少木鱼，今生才会认识你。”“认识我没有啥了不得，倒是你嫁我们小爷叔，真是前世修来的。”七姑奶奶说：“做个女人家，无非走一步帮夫运，天大的本事，也是有限制的，丈夫是个阿斗太子，哪怕你是诸葛亮，也只好叹口气。我们小爷叔的本事，现在用出来的，不过十之二三，你能再把他那七、八分挖出来，你就是女人家当中第一等人物，何在乎名分上头？”

Naturally Luo could appreciate the difficulty, but she still felt disappointed and dissatisfied. At the same time, she was deeply grateful to the Seventh Lady for speaking up for her and trying so hard to find a solution. Feeling all the more able to confide in her, she brought Mr Wu's explanation back for discussion. “Let me offer you a little advice,” the Seventh Lady said. “A hero need not fear a humble beginning. It is a good outcome that brings real honour. You aren't a narrow-minded woman; don't keep dwelling on this. I'll be your dowry wet nurse and go with you to your new home. How would that be?” In Jiangsu and Zhejiang, when a girl from a wealthy family married, her personal maid and the wet nurse who had brought her up often accompanied her to her husband's home, retaining their old titles. In putting it this way, the Seventh Lady was saying that, if there was humiliation to endure, she was willing to share it. Such affection was not always to be found even between sisters of the same blood; it ought to make up for everything. “Seventh Sister,” Luo said, her eyes reddening, “I wonder how many wooden prayer fish I must have worn out in a previous life to earn the chance of knowing you in this one.” “Knowing me is nothing remarkable. Marrying Little Uncle is the blessing you earned in a former life. A woman can only help her husband prosper; however great her abilities, they have their limits. If her husband is an incapable Prince Adou, even a Zhuge Liang can do nothing but sigh. Little Uncle has so far used only two or three tenths of his ability. If you can bring out the remaining seven or eight tenths, you will rank among the finest of women. Why worry about formal status?”

听这一说，顿时激起罗四姐的万丈雄心，很兴奋他说：“七姐，我同你说心里的话，我自己也常在想，我如果是个男的，一样有把握创一番名堂出来，只可惜是个女的。如今胡大先生虽说把个家交给我，我看他倒也并非一定只限制我把家当好了就好了，在生意上头，如何做法，他也会听我的，我倒很想下手试一试。”“是的。”七姑奶奶很婉转他说：“不过，这到底在其次，你出了主意，是好的，他一定会听，那就等于你自己在做，并不一定要你亲自下手。照我看，你的顶大的一桩生意是开矿，开人矿。这话你懂不懂？”“不懂。七姐，”罗四姐笑道：“你的花样真多。”“我是实实在在的话，不是耍花佯。我刚刚说道，你要把我们小爷叔没有用出来的七、八分本事，把它挖出来。如果你做得到，你就是开着了一座金矿！别的都算小生意了。”罗四姐先当七姑奶奶是说笑话，听完了细细思量，方始逐渐领悟，庄容说道：“七姐，你的这番道理我懂了。不过，以前我没有想到这一点，只想到要逞自己的本事，现在才晓得，我要逞本事，一定要从胡大先生身上去下功夫。”“对啊！”七姑奶奶高兴地拍着手说：“你到底聪明，想得透，看得透。”

These words awakened boundless ambition in Luo. “Seventh Sister, I'll tell you what I really think,” she said excitedly. “I've often thought that, if I were a man, I could certainly make something of myself. It's just my misfortune to be a woman. Mr Hu says he is putting the household in my hands, but I don't think he necessarily means to limit me to keeping it in order. He will listen to my ideas about business too. I'd very much like to try my hand at it.” “Yes,” the Seventh Lady said tactfully, “though that comes second. If your ideas are good, he will certainly take your advice, and that amounts to doing the work yourself; you needn't carry it out with your own hands. In my view, your greatest enterprise will be mining—mining a man's abilities. Do you understand?” “No.” Luo laughed. “You have so many tricks, Seventh Sister.” “I'm quite serious. This isn't a trick. As I just said, you must dig out the seven or eight tenths of Little Uncle's ability that he hasn't yet used. If you can do that, you'll have opened a gold mine. Every other business will be a small affair beside it.” At first Luo had thought she was joking. Now she considered the words carefully and gradually understood. “I see what you mean,” she said gravely. “It hadn't occurred to me before. I thought only of showing what I could do myself. Now I understand that, to demonstrate my own ability, I must devote my efforts to bringing out Mr Hu's.” “Exactly!” The Seventh Lady clapped her hands with pleasure. “You are clever, after all. You can think things through and see to the heart of them.”

除了“迎亲”的花轿以外，其余尽量照“六礼”的规矩来办，先换庚帖，然后下聘，聘礼是两万现银，存在杭州阜康钱庄生息，供罗四姐为老娘养老之用，当然还有一座房子，仍旧置在螺狮门外。罗四姐在上海的新居，亦已过户在她名下，七姑奶奶所垫的房价及其他费用，自然是由胡雪岩结算。聘礼最重首饰，只得四样，不过较之寻常人家的八样，还更贵重，新穿的珠花、金刚钻的镯子、翡翠耳环、红玉簪子，其实是罗四姐自己挑的。胡雪岩关照古应春，请七姑奶奶陪罗四姐去选定了，叫珠宝店直接送到上海阜康钱庄，验货收款。

Only the decorated bridal chair for bringing her to her new home was omitted; in all other respects, the arrangements followed the Six Rites of marriage as closely as possible. First they exchanged cards bearing the birth dates and hours; then came the betrothal gifts. The monetary gift was twenty thousand taels of ready silver, deposited with Fukang Bank in Hangzhou to earn interest for Luo to support her mother. There was a house as well, again bought outside Luosimen. Luo's new home in Shanghai had also been transferred into her name, and Hu naturally settled the purchase price and other expenses advanced by the Seventh Lady. Jewellery was the most important part of the betrothal gifts. There were only four kinds, but they were more valuable than the eight kinds commonly given: newly strung pearl flowers, diamond bracelets, jade earrings, and red jade hairpins. Luo had chosen them herself. Hu had told Gu to ask the Seventh Lady to accompany her in making her selection, then have the jeweller deliver the pieces directly to the Shanghai branch of Fukang Bank for inspection and payment.

“四姐，应春昨天跟我说：你们情同姐妹，这一回等于我们嫁妹子，应该要备一份嫁妆。这话一点不错。”七姑奶奶说：“我想，仍旧你自己去挑，大家的面子，你尽管拣好的挑，不要客气。说老实话，几千两银子，应春的力量还有。”罗四姐心想，只要嫁到胡家，将来一定有许多机会帮古应春的忙，借为补报，所以不必说客气话。不过，也不好意思让他们多破费，因而这样答说：“七姐跟姐夫这番意思，我不能不领。不过，东西也不在乎贵重，只要欢喜就好，你说是不是？”“正是。”七姑奶奶说：“先挑木器。明天你空不空。”“空。”“那就明天下半天。仍旧到昌发去好了。”昌发在南市，是上海最大的一家木器行，罗四姐新居的家具，就是在那里买的，“好！就是昌发。”罗四姐说，“今天家里会有客人来，我要走了。”等七姑奶奶用马车将她送到家，罗四姐立即关照老马，另雇一辆马车，要带小大姐到南市去办事。

“Yingchun said to me yesterday that, since we're as close as sisters, this is like marrying off a sister of our own, and we ought to provide a dowry. He's quite right,” the Seventh Lady told Luo. “I think you should choose that yourself too. For all our sakes, pick the best and don't stand on ceremony. To be frank, Yingchun can still afford a few thousand taels.” Once she was married into the Hu family, Luo thought, there would be plenty of opportunities to help Gu and repay his kindness. There was no need for polite refusals. Still, she was embarrassed to let them spend too much. “I can't refuse such kindness from you and Brother-in-Law Gu. But things needn't be expensive. What matters is that one likes them, wouldn't you say?” “Exactly. Let's choose the furniture first. Are you free tomorrow?” “Yes.” “Then tomorrow afternoon. We may as well go to Changfa again.” Changfa Furniture Shop, in Nanshi, was the largest furniture firm in Shanghai. Luo had bought the furnishings for her new home there. “Good. Changfa it is. I'm expecting a visitor at home today, so I must go.” The Seventh Lady sent her home in her carriage. As soon as she arrived, Luo told Old Ma to hire another carriage: she wanted to take her maid to Nanshi on an errand.

到得南市在昌发下车，老板姓李，一见老主顾上门，忽忙亲自迎了出来招呼：“罗四小姐，今天怎么有空？请里面坐，里面坐。”“我来看堂木器。”“喔，喔！”李老板满脸堆笑，“是哪里用的？”“房间里。”所谓“房间里”是指卧房，首要的就是一张床，但既称“一堂”，当然应该还有几椅桌凳之类，李老板便先间材料，“罗四小姐喜欢红木，还是紫檀？”“当然是紫檀。”“罗四小姐，你既然喜欢紫檀，我有一堂难得的木器，不可错过机会。”“好！我来看看。”

When she alighted at Changfa in Nanshi, the owner, Mr Li, recognized his regular customer and hurried out to greet her himself. “Miss Luo, what brings you here today? Do come inside. Please, come in.” “I've come to look at a set of furniture.” “Ah, yes!” Mr Li was all smiles. “What room is it for?” “The bedroom.” A bedroom set meant, first and foremost, a bed, but since she wanted a whole set, it should naturally include tables, chairs, and stools as well. Mr Li began by asking about the material. “Would you prefer hongmu rosewood or zitan, Miss Luo?” “Zitan, of course.” “If you like zitan, I have a remarkable set. You mustn't miss the opportunity.” “Very well. Let me see it.”

李老板将她领入后进一个房间，进门便觉目眩，原来这些紫檀木器，以螺甸嵌花，有耀眼的反光，以致眩目。细细看去，华丽精巧，实在可爱，“这好象不是本地货色。”罗四姐说：“花样做法部不同。”“罗四小姐，到底是顶瓜瓜的行家，”李老板说：“一眼就只透了。这堂木器是广东来的，广东叫酸枝，就是紫檀。光是广东来的不稀奇，另外还有来历，说出来，罗四小姐，你要吓一跳。”“为啥？”“这本来是进贡的……”“进贡的？”罗四姐打断他的话说：“你是说，原来是皇帝用的。”“不错。”“李老板，”罗四姐笑道：“你说大话不怕豁边？皇帝用的木器，怎么会在你店里？”“喏，罗四小姐，你不相信是不是？其中当然有个道理。你请坐下来，等我讲给你听。”

Mr Li led her into a room at the back. The moment she entered, she was dazzled: the zitan furniture was decorated with mother-of-pearl inlay, which caught the light in brilliant flashes. On closer inspection, the pieces were splendid, delicately worked, and very appealing. “This doesn't look like local work,” Luo said. “The designs and workmanship are different.” “You really are a first-rate judge, Miss Luo. You saw it at a glance. This set came from Guangdong. They call the wood suanzhi there; it's what we call zitan. But coming from Guangdong is nothing extraordinary. It has a history that will astonish you.” “Why?” “It was originally made as tribute—” “Tribute?” she interrupted. “You mean it was originally for the emperor?” “Exactly.” “Mr Li,” she said with a laugh, “aren't you afraid a boast like that will burst at the seams? How could furniture meant for the emperor end up in your shop?” “You don't believe me, do you? There is naturally an explanation. Please sit down and let me tell you.”

李老板请罗四姐在一张交椅上坐了下来，自己在下首相陪。他很会做生意，用的伙计、徒弟亦很灵活，等罗四姐刚刚坐定，现泡的盖碗茶与四个高脚果碟，已经送了上来。罗四姐存心要来买木器，生意一定做得成，所以对昌发的款待，但然接受，连道声谢都没有。“罗四小姐，请你先仔细看看东西。”她原有此意。因为所坐的那张交椅，小巧玲珑，高低正好，靠背适度，一坐下来双时自然而然地搭在扶手上，非常舒服，本就想仔细看一看，所以听得这话，便低头细细赏鉴，工料两精，毫无瑕疵。看完交椅，再看椅旁的长方套几，一共三层，推拢了不占地位，拉开了颇为实用，一碗茶，四只果碟摆在上面，一点都不湿得挤。“东西是好的。”罗四姐说：“不过花样不象宫里用的，宫里用的应该是龙凤，不应该是‘五福捧寿，。”

Mr Li invited her to sit in an armchair and took a lower place beside her. He was an able businessman, and his clerks and apprentices were quick to act. She had scarcely sat down before freshly brewed tea in a covered bowl and four stemmed fruit dishes were brought in. Luo had come intending to buy furniture, and a sale was certain, so she accepted Changfa's hospitality without ceremony or even a word of thanks. “First, please take a good look at the pieces, Miss Luo.” She had intended to do just that. The armchair was compact and elegant, at exactly the right height, with a well-proportioned back. As soon as she sat down, her elbows rested naturally on the arms; it was extremely comfortable. Now she bent her head to examine it closely. Both the material and the craftsmanship were excellent, without a flaw. After the chair, she studied the rectangular nesting tables beside it. There were three, taking up little space when pushed together and proving very useful when drawn out. The tea bowl and all four fruit dishes stood on them without the least crowding. “The pieces are good,” Luo said. “But the design doesn't look like palace furniture. Surely palace pieces should have dragons and phoenixes, not ‘Five Blessings Supporting Longevity.’”

“罗四小姐，你驳得有道理，不过你如果晓得用在哪里，你就不会驳了。宫殿有各式各样的宫殿，何止三宫六院？看地方，看用场，陈设大不相同，通通是龙凤的花佯，千篇一律，看都看厌了。你说，是不是呢？““话倒也不错。那么，这堂木器是用在哪里的呢？”“是要用在圆明园的……”“李老板，你真当我乡下人了！ 哪个不晓得，” 洋鬼子把圆明园烧掉了。““烧掉了可以重造啊。当然，真的重造了，这堂木器也不会在我这里了。”

“Your objection is reasonable, Miss Luo. But if you knew where the furniture was intended to go, you would not object. There are all sorts of palaces, far more than the familiar Three Palaces and Six Courts. The furnishings differ greatly according to the place and its purpose. If everything had the same dragons and phoenixes, people would grow tired of looking at them. Wouldn't you agree?” “There is something in that. Where was this set to be used, then?” “At the Yuanmingyuan…” “Mr Li, you really do take me for a country bumpkin! Who doesn't know that the foreign devils burned the Yuanmingyuan down?” “What has been burned can be rebuilt. Of course, if it really had been rebuilt, this furniture would not be here.”

据李老板说，有班内务府的人，与宫中管事的太监，因为洪杨起义已经失败，捻军亦部打败了，不足为患，因而怂恿慈禧太后说：“再过三，四年，皇帝成年，‘大婚’、‘亲政’两桩大典一过，两宫太后应该有个颐养天年的地方，大可以将颐和园恢复起来。大后‘以天下养’，修个花园，不为过分。”慈禧太后心动了，十二、三岁的小皇帝更为起劲，风声一传，有个内务府出身、在广东干了好几任肥缺的知府，得风气之先，特制酸枝嵌螺甸的木器进贡，而在由海道北运途中，事情起了变化。原来这件事，在私底下已经谈了好几个月，当政的恭亲王大不以为然，不过不便说破，只是在两宫太后每天例行召见时，不断表示，大乱初平，百废等举，财政困难，意思是希望慈禧太后自动打消这个念头。哪知恭王正在下水磨功夫时，忽然听说有定样一个知府，居然进贡木器，准备在颐和园使用，不由得大为光火，授意一个满洲的御史，肿列这个知府贪污有据的劣迹，狠狠参了一本，恭王面请“革职查办”，慈禧太后不便庇护，准如所请，那知府就此下狱。贡品自然也就不必北运了，押运的是那知府的胞弟，将木器卸在上海变卖，是这样归于昌发的。

According to Mr Li, some men from the Imperial Household Department and the eunuchs in charge of palace affairs had argued that, since the uprising of Hong and Yang had been defeated and the Nian armies crushed, there was no longer any cause for concern. They had therefore urged Empress Dowager Cixi: “In another three or four years, the emperor will come of age. Once the two great ceremonies of his marriage and assumption of personal rule are over, the two empress dowagers ought to have somewhere to spend their later years in comfort. The Yiheyuan could perfectly well be restored. Her Majesty is supported by the whole empire. Building a garden is hardly excessive.” Cixi was tempted, and the young emperor, then twelve or thirteen, was even more enthusiastic. When word spread, a prefect who had come from the Imperial Household Department and served several lucrative terms in Guangdong was quick to seize the opportunity. He commissioned a special set of suanzhi furniture with mother-of-pearl inlay as tribute. While it was being shipped north by sea, however, circumstances changed. The scheme had been discussed privately for several months. Prince Gong, who was directing the government, strongly disapproved but could not say so openly. At the two empress dowagers' regular daily audiences, he therefore kept stressing that the great disorders had only just been suppressed, countless neglected affairs needed attention, and the treasury was in difficulty. He hoped Cixi would abandon the idea herself. While he was pursuing this patient campaign, news arrived of a prefect sending furniture as tribute for use at the Yiheyuan. Furious, he instructed a Manchu censor to impeach the man with a detailed account of proven corruption. Prince Gong personally asked for his dismissal and investigation. Cixi could hardly protect him and granted the request. The prefect was imprisoned. Naturally, there was no longer any reason to ship the tribute north. His younger brother, who was escorting it, unloaded it in Shanghai and sold it. That was how it had come to Changfa.

“木器一共三堂，一堂客厅，一堂书房，都卖掉了。现在剩下这一堂，前天有个江西来的候补道来看过，东西是欢喜得不得了，银子带得不够，叫我替他留十天，他没有下定洋，我就不管他了。罗四小姐，你要中意，我特别克己。”李老板又说：“我再说句老实话，这堂木器，也没有啥人用得起，你们想，房间里用这样子讲究的木器，大厅、花厅、书房应该用啥？这就是我这堂木器，不容易脱手的道理。罗四姐心想，照他的话看，这堂木器似乎也只有胡雪岩家用得起。不想居然也还有那么一个阔气的江西候补道，转念又想，胡雪岩也是江西候补道，莫非是他叫人来看过？于是她问：“那个江西候补道姓啥？看来他倒也是用得起的。”“姓朱。”李老板又说：“朱道台想买这堂木器也不是自己用，是打算孝敬一位总督的老太太的。”罗四姐心中一动，随即问说：“你这堂木器啥价钱？”“照本卖，一千五百两银。其实照本卖，已经把利息亏在里头了。好在另外两堂，我已经赚着了，这一堂亏点本也无所谓。”

“There were three sets in all: one for a reception hall, one for a study, and this one. The first two have been sold. An expectant circuit intendant from Jiangxi came to see this set the day before yesterday. He loved it, but hadn't brought enough money and asked me to keep it for ten days. Since he paid no deposit, I need not consider him. If you like it, Miss Luo, I shall give you an especially modest price. To tell you the truth, very few people can afford to use furniture like this. If a bedroom is furnished so splendidly, what must the main hall, garden drawing room and study contain? That is why this set is so difficult to sell.” Luo thought that, by his account, perhaps only Hu's household could use it. She had not imagined that an expectant circuit intendant from Jiangxi might be equally wealthy. Then it occurred to her that Hu himself held that designation. Could he have sent someone to look at it? “What is this gentleman's surname? He must be able to afford it.” “Zhu. But Circuit Intendant Zhu was not buying it for himself. He meant to present it to a governor-general's mother.” An idea stirred in Luo's mind. “What is your price?” “Fifteen hundred taels, at cost. In fact, even selling at cost means losing the interest on the money tied up in it. Still, I have made my profit on the other two sets. I don't mind losing a little on this one.”

“李老板，我还你一个整数。”“罗四小姐，”李老板苦笑着说：“三分天下去其一，你杀价也杀得太凶了。”“本来漫天要价，就地还钱，‘对折拦腰掼’的生意还多的是。”“罗四小姐，听你口音是杭州人？”“不错。你问它作啥？”“你们杭州人杀价厉害，‘对折拦腰掼’四分天下去其三，世界上哪里有这种生意。罗四小姐，你总要高升、高升吧？”高升又高升，讲定一千二百两银子。罗四姐是带了银票来的，取了一张四百两的，捏在手中，却有一番话交代。“李老板，你要照我的话，我们这笔交易才会成功，明天我带个人来看，问你啥价钱，你说八百两银子。”“这为啥？”“你不要管。”罗四姐说：“你要一千二百两，今天我付你四百，明天再付你八百，一文不少。”罗四姐又说：“你要在收条上写明白，一定照我的话，不照我的话，交易不成，加倍退定洋。”“是，是！我照办。”于是李老板收下定洋，打了收条。等罗四姐走后不久，又来了一个老主顾。

“I will offer you a round thousand, Mr Li.” He smiled wryly. “Miss Luo, you are taking away a third of the price. That is ruthless bargaining.” “The seller asks for the sky; the buyer offers the ground. Plenty of bargains are made by halving the price and then halving it again.” “From your accent, are you from Hangzhou?” “Yes. Why do you ask?” “You Hangzhou people bargain hard. Halving it twice means taking away three quarters. Where in the world can anyone do business like that? You must raise your offer a little, Miss Luo.” After several increases, they settled on twelve hundred taels. Luo had brought banknotes. Taking out one for four hundred taels and holding it in her hand, she laid down a condition. “This sale can go through only if you do as I say. Tomorrow I shall bring someone to look. If you are asked the price, say eight hundred taels.” “Why?” “Never mind that. You want twelve hundred. I shall pay you four hundred today and another eight hundred tomorrow, not a cash less. But you must state clearly on the receipt that you will follow my instructions. If you don't, the sale is cancelled and you must return double the deposit.” “Certainly. I shall do as you say.” Mr Li accepted the deposit and wrote the receipt. Shortly after Luo left, another regular customer arrived.

“唷，唷！古太太，我财神又临门了。今天想看点啥？”“看了再说。”李老板领着她一处处处看，看到那堂螺甸酸枝木器，站住脚问：“这堂木器啥价钱？”“对不起，古太太，刚刚卖掉了……”七姑奶奶大失所望，却未死心，“卖给哪个？”她说，“哪有这么巧的事？”见此光景，李老板心里在转念头，他原来的话，还有一句：“就是罗四小姐买的。”哪知话未说完，让“古太太”截断了，看她的样子，有势在必得之意，如果说破“罗四小姐”，她一定会跟人家去商量情让，那一来事情就尴尬了。“罗四小姐”人很厉害，少惹她为妙。打定了这个主意，便不答腔，七姑奶却是越看越中意，就越不肯死心，“你卖给人家多少钱？”她问。“既然卖掉了，古太太也就不必问了。”“咦，姨！”七姑奶奶放下脸来，“当场开销，”她说：“问问怕啥，李老板你是生意做得大，架子也大呢？还是上了年纪，越老越糊涂？做生意哪有你这个做法的，问都问不得一句！”“古太太你不要骂我。”李老板灵机一动，顿时将苦笑收起，平静地问道：“我先请教古太太两句话，可以不可以？”

“Mrs Gu! Here is my God of Wealth again. What would you like to see today?” “Let me look around first.” Mr Li showed her from one area to another. When they reached the suanzhi set with mother-of-pearl inlay, she stopped. “How much is this?” “I am sorry, Mrs Gu. It has just been sold…” Deeply disappointed but unwilling to give up, the Seventh Lady asked, “To whom? What an unlucky coincidence!” Mr Li considered the situation. He had intended to add, “Miss Luo has just bought it,” but Mrs Gu had cut him short. She looked determined to have it. If he named Luo, she would certainly ask her to yield it, and that would make things awkward. Miss Luo was formidable; the less he provoked her, the better. Having reached this conclusion, he said nothing. But the more the Seventh Lady looked, the more she liked the furniture and the less willing she was to let it go. “What price did you sell it for?” “Since it has been sold, there is no need to ask, Mrs Gu.” Her face hardened, and she began to give him a dressing-down on the spot. “What is wrong with asking? Has your business grown so large that you have become too grand for us, Mr Li? Or are you growing more muddle-headed with age? Who ever heard of doing business like this, when a customer may not even ask a question?” “Please don't scold me.” An inspiration came to him. His rueful smile vanished, and he asked calmly, “May I first ask you a couple of questions?”

“可以啊！有什么不可以？”“古太太想买这堂木器，是自己用，还是送人？”“送人。”“送哪个？”“你不要管。”“古太太，你告诉我了，或许有个商量。”“好。”七姑奶奶说：“喏，就是上回我同她来过的那位罗四小姐。”这下，李老板会意了，“罗四小姐”所说要带个人来看，此人就在眼前。于是他笑着道：“古太太，你说巧来真是巧！刚刚那个买主，就是罗四小姐。”七姑奶奶大感意外，心想：“她来过了？”她急急问说：“买了你这堂木器？多少钱？”“八百两。”七姑奶奶点点头，“这个价钱也还公道。”她又问：“付了多少定洋？”“没有付。”“没有付？”七姑奶奶气又上来了：“没有付，你为啥不卖给我？”“做生意一句话嘛！罗四小姐是你古太太的来头，我当然要相信她。”七姑奶奶觉得他这两句话很中听，不由得就说了实话，“李老板，我老实跟你说了吧！罗四小姐要做新娘子了，我买这堂木器陪嫁，她大概不愿意我花钱，所以自己来看定了。这样子，明天我陪她来，你不要收她的银子，要收我的。”

“Of course. Why not?” “Do you want this furniture for yourself or as a gift?” “A gift.” “For whom?” “Never mind.” “If you tell me, perhaps something can be arranged.” “Very well. For the Miss Luo who came here with me last time.” Now Mr Li understood. This was the person Luo intended to bring. Smiling, he said, “What a coincidence indeed! The customer who has just bought it was Miss Luo herself.” The Seventh Lady was astonished. So Luo had been here? “She bought this set?” she asked quickly. “For how much?” “Eight hundred taels.” She nodded. “A fair enough price. How much deposit did she leave?” “None.” “None?” Her temper rose again. “Then why wouldn't you sell it to me?” “In business, a promise must count. Miss Luo came through you, Mrs Gu. Naturally, I trust her.” The Seventh Lady liked the sound of that and told him the truth. “Mr Li, Miss Luo is going to be a bride. I am buying the furniture for her dowry. She probably didn't want me to spend the money, so she came to choose it herself. Tomorrow I shall bring her here. Don't accept her money. Take mine.”

“是，是！”“还有，你答应她八百两，当然还是八百两，不过我要杀你的价。杀价是假的，今天我先付你二百两，明天我杀价杀到六百两，你就说老主顾没办法，答应下来。这样做，为的是怕她替我心痛，你懂不懂？”“懂啊！怎么不懂？罗四小姐交到你这种朋友，真正前世福气，买木器陪嫁她，还要体谅她的心。这样子厚道细心的人，除了你古太太，寻不出第二个。”七姑奶奶买了这堂好木器，已觉踌躇满志，听了他这几句话，越发得意，高高兴兴付了定洋回家，将这桩称心如意的事，告诉了古应春。第二天，罗四姐来了，七姑奶奶一开口就说：“你昨天到昌发去过了？”罗四姐不知她何以得知？沉着地答说：“是的。”“你看中了一堂木器，价钱都讲好了？”“是的。讲定八百两银子。”“那再好都没有。”七姑奶奶说：“你真有眼光！我们走。”

“Certainly.” “One more thing. You promised her eight hundred taels, and eight hundred it must remain. But I shall bargain with you. It will only be pretence. I shall pay you two hundred today. Tomorrow, when I bargain you down to six hundred, say that you cannot refuse an old customer and agree. I don't want her to feel bad about my spending so much. Do you understand?” “Of course! Miss Luo must have earned the blessing of a friend like you in a previous life. You buy her dowry furniture and still take care to spare her feelings. No one could be more generous and considerate, Mrs Gu.” The Seventh Lady was already pleased with herself for securing such fine furniture. His praise made her happier still. She paid the deposit and went home in high spirits, telling Gu Yingchun how satisfactorily everything had worked out. When Luo arrived the next day, her first words were, “You went to Changfa yesterday?” Luo had no idea how she had found out, but answered composedly, “Yes.” “You chose a set of furniture and settled the price?” “Yes. Eight hundred taels.” “Then nothing could be better. You have a very good eye. Let us go.”

于是一车到了昌发。李老板早已茶烟、水果、点心都预备好了。略坐一坐，去看木器。“罗四小姐说，价钱跟你讲好了，是不是？”“是的。”“那是罗四小姐买，现在是我买。”七姑奶奶说：“李老板，我们我年往来，你应该格外克己，我出你六百两银子。”“古太太，我已经亏本了。”“我晓得你亏本，无非多年往来的交情，硬杀你二百两。”“下回我一定讲交情。这一回，”李老板斩钉截铁他说：“我的价钱，讲出算数，决不能改。”如此绝情，七姑奶奶气得脸色发白，真想狗血喷头骂他一，但一则是喜事，不宜吵架，二则也是舍不得这堂好木器，只好忍气吞声，连连冷笑道说：“好，好！算你狠。”说完，取出八百两银子的银票，往桌上一摔。“古太太，你请不要生气，我实在有苦衷，改天我到府上来赔罪。”“哪个要你来赔罪。我告诉你，这回是一闷棍的生意。”说完掉头就走，李老板追上来要分辩，七姑奶奶不理他，与罗四姐坐上马车回家，一路气鼓鼓的，话都懒得说，罗四姐也觉得好生无趣。

They drove to Changfa together. Mr Li had tea, tobacco, fruit and refreshments ready. After sitting for a little while, they went to inspect the furniture. “Miss Luo says she has settled the price with you. Is that right?” “Yes.” “That was when Miss Luo was buying. Now I am the buyer. We have dealt with each other for years, Mr Li. You ought to make a special concession. I offer six hundred taels.” “Mrs Gu, I am already losing money.” “I know. I am forcing another two hundred off the price only because we have been dealing with each other for so long.” “Next time I shall certainly show consideration. This time, however, my quoted price must stand. It cannot be changed.” His refusal was absolute. The Seventh Lady turned pale with fury. She wanted to give him a thorough tongue-lashing, but this was a wedding purchase, no occasion for a quarrel; besides, she could not bear to lose such fine furniture. Swallowing her anger, she laughed bitterly. “Very well. You win.” She took out banknotes for eight hundred taels and flung them onto the table. “Please don't be angry, Mrs Gu. I have a real difficulty. I shall come to your house another day to explain and apologize.” “Who wants your apology? Let me tell you, this is the last chance you will have to fleece me.” She turned and left. Mr Li hurried after her to explain, but she ignored him. She and Luo drove home, the Seventh Lady so angry that she scarcely spoke. Luo found the whole affair deeply unpleasant too.

一到家，在起坐问中遇见古应春。他一看爱妻神色不怡，便含笑问道：“高高兴兴出门，回来好象不大开心，为啥？”“昌发的李老板不上路！”七姑奶奶的声音很大，“以后再也不要作成他生意了。你说要带洋人到他那里定家具，省省！挑别家。”“怎么不上路？”“ 他，”七姑奶奶想一想说：“硬要我八百两银子。”“你照付了没有呢？”“你倒想！”七姑奶奶预先付过“差价”，是告诉过古应春的，他心里在想，李老板的生意做得很大，而且人虽精明，却很讲信用，似乎不至于硬吞二百两银子，其中或者另有缘故，只是当着罗四姐，不便深谈，只好沉默。

At home they found Gu in the sitting room. Seeing his wife's unhappy expression, he smiled and asked, “You went out so cheerfully. Why do you look so displeased now?” “Mr Li of Changfa doesn't know how to behave!” she declared loudly. “Never give him any more business. You said you would take a foreigner there to order furniture. Don't bother. Choose another shop.” “What did he do?” “He…” She paused. “He insisted on eight hundred taels.” “Did you pay?” “What do you think?” She had told Gu about paying the difference in advance. He knew that Mr Li had a large business and, though shrewd, was reliable. It seemed unlikely that he would simply pocket an extra two hundred taels. Perhaps there was another explanation. With Luo present, however, Gu could not pursue the matter and remained silent.

于是罗四姐便劝七姑奶奶说：“七姐，东西实在是好的，八百两银子是真正不贵。你先消消气，我要好好跟你商量，这堂木器有个用法。”七姑奶奶正要答话，让小大姐进来打断了。她是来通报，李老板来了，要见七姑奶奶。“不见。”“我见。”古应春接口，“等我来问他。”去了不多片刻，古应春笑嘻嘻地回进来，手里拿着个红封套，七姑奶奶接过来一看，封套签条上写“贺仪”二字，下面是李老板具名，贺仪是一张二百四十两的银票。“这算啥？”“不是送你的。”古应春说：“你不是告诉我，罗四姐要做新娘子了，人家是送喜事的贺礼。“听这一说，七姑奶奶与罗四姐相顾愕然，事出突兀，都用眼色催古应春说下去，但古应春却是一副忍俊不禁的神气。“你笑啥？”七姑奶奶白了丈夫一眼，“快说啊！”“怎么不要好笑？这种事也只有你们心思用得深的人，才做得出来。”

Luo tried to soothe her friend. “The furniture really is good, Seventh Sister. Eight hundred taels is very reasonable. Calm down first. I want to discuss a use I have in mind for it.” Before the Seventh Lady could reply, the maid came in to announce that Mr Li had arrived and wished to see her. “I won't see him.” “I will,” Gu said. “Let me question him.” He returned shortly afterwards, smiling broadly and carrying a red envelope. The Seventh Lady took it. On the label were the words “Wedding Gift,” with Mr Li's name below. Inside was a banknote for two hundred and forty taels. “What is this supposed to mean?” “It is not for you,” Gu said. “You told me Miss Luo was to be a bride, didn't you? This is his wedding present.” Taken completely by surprise, the two women exchanged bewildered looks, then urged him with their eyes to go on. But Gu seemed barely able to contain his laughter. His wife gave him a sharp look. “What are you laughing at? Tell us!” “How could I not laugh? Only people who think as deeply as you two could manage something like this.”

古应春看了罗四姐一眼，向妻子说道：“你晓得这堂木器多少钱？一千二百两。”“晴！”罗四姐叫了起来，“七姐夫，李老板告诉你了？”“当然告诉我了，不然，他另外收了二百两银子的定洋，硬不认帐，这话怎么交代呢？”“啊？”罗四姐问说：“七姐，你已付过他二百两？”七姑奶奶愣了一下，弄明白是怎么回事了，反问一句：“你先付过他四百两？”“是的。”“为啥？”“我不愿意你太破费。”“两个人走到一条路上来了。”七姑奶奶哈哈大笑，“我晓得你不愿意我太破费，所以预先付了他二百两。我道呢，哪里有这么便宜的东西！”罗四姐也觉得好笑，“七姐夫说得不错，心思用得太深，才会做出这种事来。你瞒我，我瞒你，大家都钻到牛角尖里去了。不过，”她说：“李老板也不大对，当时他就让二百两好了，何苦害七姐白白生一场气。”“他也有他的说法。”古应春接口答道：“我拿李老板的话照佯说一遍。他说：那位罗四小姐，看起来是很厉害的角色，我不能不防她，收条上写明白，报价只能报八百两，改口的话，加倍退还定洋，万一我改了口，罗四小姐拿出收条，一记‘翻天印，打过来，我没话说，所以我当时不松口，宁可得罪了古太太，事后来赔罪。“

Gu glanced at Luo, then told his wife, “Do you know what the furniture costs? Twelve hundred taels.” “Oh!” Luo exclaimed. “Brother-in-Law Gu, he told you?” “Of course. How else could he explain taking a further two hundred as deposit and then flatly refusing to acknowledge it?” “You had already paid him two hundred, Seventh Sister?” The Seventh Lady stared for a moment, then understood. “And you had paid four hundred first?” “Yes.” “Why?” “I didn't want you to spend too much.” The Seventh Lady burst out laughing. “We both took the same road! I knew you didn't want me to spend too much, so I paid him two hundred beforehand. I was wondering how such fine things could be so cheap.” Luo found it amusing too. “Brother-in-Law Gu is right. Only people who think too hard would do this. I kept it from you; you kept it from me; we both reasoned ourselves into a corner. Still, Mr Li was not quite right either. Why didn't he simply take two hundred less at the time, instead of making you angry for nothing?” “He has an explanation,” Gu replied. “Let me repeat his words. He said, ‘That Miss Luo looks a very formidable woman. I had to be on my guard. The receipt expressly says I must quote eight hundred taels, and if I change my words I must return double the deposit. Suppose I altered the price, and she produced the receipt and struck me with it like the Heaven-Overturning Seal? I would have no defence. That is why I would not give way. I preferred to offend Mrs Gu and come afterwards to apologize.’”

七姑奶奶前嫌尽释，高兴地笑道：“这个人还算上路，还多送了四十两贺礼。”说着将红封套递给罗四姐。“我不要。”罗四姐不肯接，“不是我的。”“莫非是我的？”七姑奶奶开玩笑：“又不是我做新娘子。”罗四姐窘笑着，仍旧不肯接，七姑奶奶的手也缩不回去，古应春说：“交给我。二百两是退回来的定洋，四十两送的贺礼，我叫人记笔帐在那里。”于是七姑奶奶将红封套交了给古应春，接着便盛赞那堂酸枝嵌螺甸的家具，认为一千二百两银子，实在也不算贵。

The Seventh Lady's resentment vanished. “He does know how to behave, after all,” she said happily. “He has even added forty taels as a wedding gift.” She handed the red envelope to Luo. “I don't want it. It isn't mine.” Luo refused to take it. “Then is it mine? I am not the one becoming a bride!” the Seventh Lady joked. Luo smiled in embarrassment but still refused, leaving her friend's hand suspended between them. “Give it to me,” Gu said. “Two hundred is the returned deposit, and forty is the wedding gift. I shall have them entered in the accounts.” His wife handed him the envelope, then began praising the suanzhi furniture with its mother-of-pearl inlay. Even twelve hundred taels, she thought, was not too much for it.

由此便谈到这堂木器的来历，它之贵重，已经不能拿银子多寡来论了。罗四姐因此有个想法，觉得自己用这堂木器，虽说出于“陪嫁”，亦嫌过分，难免遭人议论；因而私下跟七姑奶奶商量，打算把这堂木器，孝敬胡老太太。“我这个念头，是听了李老板的一句话才转到的，他说：有个江西的未道台，想买这堂木器孝敬一位总督的老太太。我心里就在想，将来我用这堂木器，胡老太太用的不及我，我用了心里也不安。倒不如借花献佛，做个人情。七姐，你不会怪我吧？”“哪里，哪里：”七姑奶奶异常欣慰地，“说实话，你这样子会做人，我就放心了。胡家人多口杂，我真怕你自己觉得行得正、坐得正，性子太直了，会得罪人。”“得罪人是免不了的。只要有几个人不得罪就好了。譬如胡老太太，一定要伺候得好。”七姑奶奶暗暗点头，心里在想，罗四姐一定懂。挟天子以令诸侯‘的道理，不但会做人，还会做“官”，替她担心，实在是多余的。

They went on to discuss the furniture's history. Its value could no longer be measured simply in silver. Luo had therefore formed a plan. Even if it were part of her dowry, such a set seemed too grand for her own use and might attract criticism. She privately proposed to the Seventh Lady that she present it to Old Madam Hu. “It was something Mr Li said that gave me the idea. A Circuit Intendant Zhu from Jiangxi had wanted to buy it for a governor-general's mother. I thought: if I use it and Old Madam Hu's furniture is not as fine, I shall feel uncomfortable. Better to offer borrowed flowers to the Buddha and turn it into a gift. You won't blame me, will you, Seventh Sister?” “Of course not.” The Seventh Lady was deeply pleased. “To tell the truth, seeing how well you understand people sets my mind at rest. There are so many people and so much gossip in the Hu household. I was afraid you might feel that, since you had done nothing wrong, you could be too outspoken and offend them.” “One cannot avoid offending people. As long as certain people are not offended, that is enough. Old Madam Hu, for instance, must be very well attended to.” The Seventh Lady nodded inwardly. Luo must understand the principle of holding the emperor in one's power to command the feudal lords, she thought. Luo knew not only how to deal with people but how to practise the art of government. Worrying about her had been quite unnecessary.

第七章 帮夫运｜CHAPTER SEVEN: A WIFE WHO BRINGS HER HUSBAND PROSPERITY

自从罗四姐嫁到到胡家，真是走了一步帮夫运，胡雪岩的事业如《红楼梦》上所形容的“鲜花着锦”般兴旺。当然，兴旺的由来是他恃左宗棠为靠山，左宗棠视他为股肽，只要左宗棠西征，节节胜利，所请在朝廷无有不准，胡雪岩水涨船高，亦就事事顺手了。原来从道光年问开始，君暗臣愚，激出内忧外患，西北的回民起义，亦是贪官污吏激荡而成。其时所谓“甘回”共有西、南北三大支，三大首领，西面的叫马朵之，驻扎在青海的西宁，南面的叫马占鳌，以甘肃与青海的河州，也就是临夏为根据地，北面叫马化龙，是三大首领中最厉害的一个，势力范围在宁夏、灵武一带，根据地名为金积堡，这个地方就是“黄河百害，惟富一套”的河套的起点，擅茶、马之利以外，东面有个盐池叫花马池，更是一大财源。金积堡周围有五百多个寨子，众星拱月般环卫着马化龙的金积堡。此人对宁夏将军穆图善很恭敬。左宗棠看到了此人的底蕴，所以西征的第一目标就是攻下金积堡。

Once Luo Sijie married into the Hu household, she truly entered upon a fortune that advanced her husband. Hu Xueyan's enterprises flourished like “fresh flowers upon brocade,” as Dream of the Red Chamber puts it. Their prosperity, of course, rested on Zuo Zongtang's support, while Zuo regarded Hu as his indispensable right hand. As the western campaign advanced from victory to victory and the court granted every request Zuo made, Hu rose with the tide and found everything going smoothly. Since the Daoguang reign, benighted rulers and foolish ministers had provoked troubles at home and abroad. The Muslim uprisings in the northwest had likewise been stirred up by corrupt officials. The forces then known as the Gansu Muslims fell into three main divisions, western, southern and northern, with three principal leaders. In the west was Ma Duozhi, based at Xining in Qinghai. In the south was Ma Zhan'ao, whose base was Hezhou, also called Linxia, in the Gansu–Qinghai region. The northern leader, Ma Hualong, was the most formidable of the three. His influence extended over Ningxia and Lingwu, and his stronghold was Jinjibao. It stood at the beginning of the Hetao region, the great bend of the Yellow River celebrated in the saying, “The Yellow River brings a hundred troubles; only its bend grows rich.” Besides controlling the profits from tea and horses, he had a major source of wealth in Huamachi, a salt lake to the east. More than five hundred fortified villages encircled Jinjibao like stars surrounding the moon. Ma was extremely respectful towards Mutushan, the general at Ningxia. Zuo saw what lay beneath this behaviour, and the first objective of his western campaign was to capture Jinjibao.

在攻金积堡之前，先要隔断捻军与甘回的联系。捻军分为两大股，称为“东捻”、“西捻”。曾国藩解释捻军之捻说：“捻纸燃脂，故谓之捻”，凡是用薄纸搓成条状，如吸水烟用的纸煤等等，都叫做捻子。捻军的特性在于易聚易散，但看起来象乌合之众，而流转不定，飘忽千里，令人疲于奔命，亦很厉害。僧格林沁的黑龙江马队，追奔逐北，捻军见了就澈，但一停下来，周围不知如何，就会冒出无数捻军来，僧王就是这样阵亡的。僧王打的是东捻，西捻的首领叫张宗禹，自河南至陕西，由河南横渡黄河，直上延安、米脂，南北战线拉长到一千多里，目的就是希望与马化友由西往东，也有千把里的这条战线交会。只要一接上头，西捻不复可制，回民起义亦不知何时才能镇压下去，所以左宗棠西征的初步战略，就在隔离西捻与甘回不让他们“会师”。罗四姐嫁到胡家时，正当西捻初平，两宫太后召见左宗棠，天语褒嘉，左宗棠自陈五年可以镇压回民起义之时。

Before attacking Jinjibao, however, he had to sever the link between the Nian armies and the Gansu Muslim forces. The Nian were divided into two main groups, the Eastern and Western Nian. Explaining their name, Zeng Guofan wrote, “Paper is twisted to burn in oil; hence the name nian.” Anything made by twisting thin paper into a strip, such as the spills used for lighting water pipes, was called a nianzi. The Nian armies could gather and disperse with equal ease. Though they looked like an undisciplined rabble, their unpredictable movements over a thousand li left pursuers exhausted and made them formidable opponents. Sengge Rinchen's Heilongjiang cavalry chased them relentlessly. Whenever they saw it coming, they withdrew. Yet as soon as the cavalry halted, innumerable Nian soldiers would somehow appear all around it. That was how Prince Sengge Rinchen had met his death. He had been fighting the Eastern Nian. Zhang Zongyu, leader of the Western Nian, moved between Henan and Shaanxi, crossing the Yellow River from Henan and pressing north towards Yan'an and Mizhi. His north–south front stretched over a thousand li. He hoped to join Ma Hualong's front, which extended a similar distance from west to east. Once the two linked up, the Western Nian would be beyond control, and there would be no telling when the Muslim uprising could be suppressed. Zuo's initial strategy was therefore to keep them apart and prevent a junction. When Luo married into Hu's household, the Western Nian had just been defeated. The two empress dowagers received Zuo with gracious praise, and he declared that he could suppress the Muslim uprising within five years.

左宗棠最初驻军西安，然后往西北逐步推进，大营先移乾州，再移甘肃境内的泾川，然后往北打，攻克镇原、庆阳，收容降众及饥民十七万人，行屯垦之法，种子、农具，都由胡雪岩的转运局采办好了，运到甘肃。及至左宗棠的前锋逼进灵武，马化龙看根据地有被剿之虞，于是“上书言抚”，抚是安抚，表示愿意投降，部众或者收编为清军、或者遗散、或者为他们谋个生计。有此化干戈为玉帛的结果，本来是最理想的办法，但造反起义的，就抚而又反复音，不知多少。左宗棠阅历极丰，而马化友又有善于翻覆的名声，他可以玩弄穆图善，而左宗棠决不会受他的愚，所以置之不理，备妥三月行粮，进攻金积堡。

Zuo first stationed his army at Xi'an, then advanced gradually northwest. Headquarters moved first to Qianzhou, then to Jingchuan in Gansu. Turning north, he captured Zhenyuan and Qingyang, took in 170,000 surrendered people and famine refugees, and established agricultural settlements for them. The seeds and farming implements were all procured by Hu's Transport Bureau and shipped to Gansu. When Zuo's advance troops approached Lingwu, Ma Hualong saw that his base was in danger of destruction and submitted a letter asking for pacification. That meant he was willing to surrender: his followers might be absorbed into the Qing army, dispersed, or provided with some means of livelihood. Turning weapons into peaceful relations would have been the ideal outcome. But countless rebels had accepted pacification only to rise again. Zuo was deeply experienced, and Ma had a reputation for repeated reversals. He might play tricks on Mutushan, but Zuo would not be fooled. Ignoring the appeal, he prepared three months' provisions and advanced on Jinjibao.

指挥此役的大将是刘松山。此人是曾国藩的小同乡，行伍出身，积功升至总兵。咸丰十年，英法内犯，僧格林沁提兵勤王，东南没有这一支膘悍的马队，战局大受影响。那时太平军李秀成，刚开始为洪秀全所重用，在芜湖召集军事会议，分道进兵，李秀成本人自率大军，由芜湖南下，攻占皖南黟县，另外太平军悍将李世贤、黄文金、李继远等，相继陷宁国、下徽州，又占江西浮梁、都昌、饶州。驻节祁门的曾国藩，西面来自湖北的接济，因江西粮道中断而绝，东面则有二李亲领的骄兵相逼，重重围困，听从幕宾建议，反攻徽州，以期打开通浙江的运道。于是曾国藩侈军祁门以东、徽州以西的休宁；有一天太平军夜袭，诸营皆贵，只有刘松山在月下列队迎敌，太平军不敢相逼，其余溃散各营，月夜看不真切，以为太平军拦截，掉头要逃，及至刘松山打出真号，大家才知道大营未夫，“老帅”无恙，惊魂始定。祁门一役，是曾国藩靖港兵败，投水遇救以后，另一次的大危机，他连遗书都写好了，结果转危为安，都由刘松山之功，从此以国士相待。

The general commanding the attack was Liu Songshan, a man from Zeng Guofan's own immediate home district. He had risen from the ranks to become a brigade commander through distinguished service. In the tenth year of Xianfeng, when British and French forces invaded, Sengge Rinchen had taken his troops to defend the emperor. The removal of that fierce cavalry force from the southeast greatly affected the war there. Li Xiucheng, just beginning to enjoy Hong Xiuquan's confidence, convened a military conference at Wuhu and divided the Taiping forces for an advance on several routes. He himself marched south from Wuhu and captured Yi County in southern Anhui. Other formidable Taiping commanders, Li Shixian, Huang Wenjin and Li Jiyuan, successively took Ningguo and Huizhou, followed by Fuliang, Duchang and Raozhou in Jiangxi. Zeng, based at Qimen, was cut off from his Hubei supplies to the west because the route through Jiangxi had been broken. From the east, confident troops led personally by the two Lis pressed upon him. Encircled, he accepted his advisers' proposal to counterattack Huizhou and reopen a supply route to Zhejiang. He therefore moved his army to Xiuning, east of Qimen and west of Huizhou. One night the Taipings attacked, and every camp broke except Liu's. Liu formed his men in the moonlight to meet the enemy, who dared not approach. Troops fleeing from the other camps, unable to see clearly, mistook his ranks for a Taiping blocking force and turned to run. Only when Liu displayed the proper recognition signals did they realize that headquarters still held and the old commander was safe. Their terror subsided. Since his defeat at Jinggang, when he had thrown himself into the water and been rescued, this had been Zeng's next great crisis. He had even written his last letters. His escape was entirely due to Liu, whom he thereafter treated as a man of exceptional national worth.

及至左宗棠受命西征，这是一场大战役，非地方性的军务可比，各军理当协力，曾国藩将他最重视的刘松山一军，交给左宗棠指挥。左宗棠本由曾国藩所提携，以后由于争饷而存意见，复以曾国荃破金陵，纵容洪秀全之子逃遁，直言讦奏，因而失和，不通音问已久，到这时，左宗棠才知道，谋国之忠，知人之明，自愧不如元辅“。将刘松山一军交他节制，比作曾国藩”嫁女“，对刘讼山的重用，自不待言。刘松山真亦不负曾国藩的知遇及左宗棠的期许，打西捻、甘回，几乎战无不胜、攻无不克。他从军以前，在家乡就已定下亲事，聘而未娶，在军中十几年，只因招兵，回过一次家乡，直到西捻既败，方在洛阳成婚，新郎新娘都三十多岁了。蜜月只得十天，刘松山便即入陕，肃清榆、延、绥、鄜四州以后，进军灵武，一战而克。马化龙力战无功，一面再次言抚，一面四处求援，但西宁、河州、临洮、靖远各地的回民军，震于刘松山的威名，都不敢妄运，于是刘松山大举进攻。同治九年正月，攻金积堡外围一个寨子，中炮坠马，因而阵亡，所部由他的侄子刘锦棠率领，同年十一月，终于攻克了金积堡。

When Zuo received command of the western expedition, its scale demanded cooperation from all the armies; this was no merely local operation. Zeng placed his most valued force, Liu Songshan's, under Zuo's command. Zuo had originally owed his advancement to Zeng, but they had later quarrelled over military funds. When Zeng Guoquan captured Jinling and allowed Hong Xiuquan's son to escape, Zuo openly denounced the matter in a memorial. Their relations broke down, and they had long ceased corresponding. Only now did Zuo acknowledge, “In loyalty to the country's interests and discernment of men, I am ashamed to fall short of the Grand Secretary.” He compared Zeng's placing Liu under his orders to giving a daughter in marriage. Needless to say, he entrusted Liu with important duties. Liu fully justified both Zeng's recognition and Zuo's expectations, winning almost every engagement against the Western Nian and the Gansu Muslim forces. Before enlisting, he had become engaged at home but had not married. In more than ten years of service, he returned home only once, to recruit men. Not until the Western Nian were defeated did he finally marry at Luoyang. Bride and groom were both over thirty. After a honeymoon of only ten days, he entered Shaanxi. Clearing the four districts of Yu, Yan, Sui and Fu, he advanced on Lingwu and took it in a single battle. Unable to defeat him, Ma Hualong again sought pacification while appealing everywhere for help. But the Muslim armies at Xining, Hezhou, Lintao and Jingyuan, overawed by Liu's reputation, dared not move rashly. Liu launched a major assault. In the first lunar month of the ninth year of Tongzhi, he was struck by cannon fire while attacking a fortified village outside Jinjibao, fell from his horse and died. His nephew Liu Jintang took command. In the eleventh month of that same year, Jinjibao finally fell.

西征军能够胜多败少，着着进展，是因为器械利、士气旺、纪律好。胡雪岩得古应春之力，西洋凡有新式枪械，以及其他精巧的军事装备，只要能用得上的，不必向左宗棠请示，先就办了来，加以补给适时，从无粮饷不断之虞，士气自然就旺盛了。这是西征军将士都佩服，也感激胡雪岩的，但纪律好亦应归功于胡雪岩，就只有左宗棠最明白了。从成丰未年，同治皇后阿鲁待氏的祖父赛尚武丧师失律，浪掷了一笔发自部库的二百万两银子的军饷以后，仗都是地方上自己在打，因此有楚军、湘军、淮军、浙军、粤军等等名号，都称之为“官军”，这些官军，来源不一，“回乡招募”的子弟兵固占多数，但也不个是土匪或者别处投过来的，出身不同，队官的作风各异，军纪就大有区别。湘军中以彭玉鳞部下纪律最严，鲍超一军最糟糕，这就是带兵的看法不同之故，不过鲍超骁勇善战，是曾国藩的“爱将”，所以诸事宽容。左宗棠所部，亦是杂牌军队，但都能格守纪律，一半是左宗棠治军较严，一半亦由于心悦诚服，不忍违犯纪律，论心悦诚服之所起，就不能不推服胡雪岩了，“湖湘子弟满天下”而无后顾之忧，都由于胡雪岩靠他广设钱庄、通汇便利，按时得能接济官兵家属。至于阵亡将士，恤死养生，不用左宗棠关照，他就派人去做了，大家都道“侯爷”如此爱护部下，何忍犯他的军纪？却不知是胡雪岩在助“候爷”维持纪律。

The western army won more often than it lost and advanced steadily because its weapons were superior, its morale high and its discipline good. With Gu Yingchun's help, Hu bought any new Western firearms or ingenious military equipment that could be useful, without first asking Zuo for instructions. Supplies arrived on time; the troops never feared an interruption in provisions or pay. Naturally, morale was high. Officers and men admired Hu for this and were grateful. But only Zuo fully understood that their discipline too owed much to him. Since the closing years of Xianfeng, when Saishang’a, grandfather of the Tongzhi emperor's empress of the Aludai clan, had lost his army and squandered two million taels of military funds from the ministry treasury, the provinces had been fighting their own wars. Hence the various Chu, Hunan, Huai, Zhejiang and Guangdong armies, all called government troops. They came from many sources. Men recruited in their commanders' home districts formed the majority, but there were also bandits and men transferred from elsewhere. Their backgrounds differed, as did their officers' methods, and discipline varied greatly. Within the Hunan Army, Peng Yulin's men were the best disciplined and Bao Chao's the worst, reflecting their commanders' differing views. But Bao was brave and skilful, a favourite of Zeng's, and was indulged in many things. Zuo's forces were equally mixed, yet they all observed discipline. Half the credit belonged to his strict command; the other half to their wholehearted devotion, which made them unwilling to disobey. For that devotion, Hu deserved acknowledgement. Hunan men served all over the empire without anxiety for those at home because his extensive network of banks and convenient remittances supported their families regularly. When officers or soldiers died, he sent men to provide death benefits and support the survivors without waiting for Zuo's instructions. Everyone thought: the marquis cares so much for us; how could we bear to violate his discipline? They did not know that Hu was helping the marquis maintain it.

胡雪岩能够公私兼顾，钱庄。典当、丝号一家接一家开张，生意越做越大，“财神”的名气越来越响，从胡老太太起始，都认为是“螺蛳太太”的功劳，原来为了避免用“二太太”之名，却又想不出更合适的称呼，有个通人说：“顺治年间‘江左三大家’之一的龚芝麓，娶了秦淮出身的顾眉生，龚芝麓的元配称她为‘顾太太’，仿照这个例子，拿‘罗四姐，的’姐，字改为‘太太’，有何不可？于是，‘罗四太太，就此叫开了。下人不明其理，只当她娘家住在螺蛳门外的缘故，叫成’螺蛳太太“。但最为乡党称道，而且使得胡雪岩自觉对螺蛳太太有愧，既爱且敬的是，她有个“大贤大德”的名声，为胡雪岩娶了十一房姨太太。

Hu managed to attend to public duties and private business alike. Banks, pawnshops and silk firms opened one after another, his enterprises expanded, and his reputation as the God of Wealth grew ever louder. Everyone, beginning with Old Madam Hu, attributed it to Madam Luosi. That title had arisen because they wished to avoid calling her Second Madam but could think of nothing more suitable. A learned man had offered a precedent: “In the Shunzhi reign, Gong Zhilu, one of the Three Great Masters of the Lower Yangtze, married Gu Meisheng, who came from the Qinhuai courtesan quarter. Gong's principal wife addressed her as Madam Gu. Why not follow that example and replace the ‘Sister’ in ‘Luo Sijie’ with ‘Madam’?” Thus she became Madam Luo Si. Servants who did not understand the reasoning assumed the title came from her family home outside Luosi, or Snail, Gate, and it became Madam Luosi. What most impressed their neighbours, however, and made Hu feel indebted to her, loving and respecting her all the more, was her reputation for extraordinary virtue: she arranged for him to take eleven more concubines.

约莫嫁后一年，螺蛳太太向到杭州三天竺来烧香的七姑奶奶诉苦。原来胡雪岩精力过人，只她一个人“当夕”，有些力不从心，因而也就觉得乐不敌苦了。于是胡雪岩不免留连花丛，本来欢场中应酬，在胡雪岩几乎是每天的例课，以前仅止于“吃花酒”，渐渐地以勾栏为行馆，经常整夜不归，其至在“堂子”里接见宾客，料理公事，这件事就可忧了。“七姐，”螺蛳太太说：“他现在正在风头上，这步桃花运走不得，第一，伤身体，第二，耽误正事，第三，名声不好听，还有第四，伙计们看东家的样，个个狂嫖滥赌，怎么得了？就算不学他的样，也会灰心，辛辛苦苦帮他创业，哪知道他是这样子不成材！”七姑奶奶知道最后两句话，是她“夫子自道”的牢骚，不过，她也有些怀疑，“小爷叔对这个‘色，字看不破，是大家都晓得的。不过，”她问；“又何至于’好‘到这个程度呢？”“喏，”螺蛳太太不免有怨言，“都是我们那位刘三叔！”

About a year after her marriage, Madam Luosi confided her troubles to the Seventh Lady, who had come to Hangzhou to offer incense at the Three Tianzhu Temples. Hu had exceptional sexual energy. Being his sole nightly companion had become more than she could manage, and the pleasure no longer outweighed the strain. Hu consequently began lingering among the courtesans. Entertaining at their houses had long been an almost daily duty for him, but previously he had confined himself to dining and drinking there. Gradually he began treating the brothels as residences, frequently staying all night and even receiving visitors and transacting official business there. That was cause for concern. “Seventh Sister, he is riding high now. He cannot afford this run of romantic adventures. First, it harms his health. Second, it delays important business. Third, it damages his reputation. And fourth, what if every employee follows his example, whoring and gambling without restraint? Even if they don't imitate him, they will be discouraged. They work so hard to help him build his enterprises, only to discover that he is such a disappointment.” The Seventh Lady knew that these last words expressed her friend's own resentment. Still, she was puzzled. “Everyone knows that Little Uncle has never overcome his weakness for women. But why should it have reached such a degree?” Madam Luosi could not suppress a complaint. “It is all the fault of our Third Uncle Liu!”

原来胡雪岩决定开办药店，他本早有此心，恰好又受了气，去年夏天胡老大大受暑发痧，土法子是拿铜钱刮瘀，刮出一条鲜红的血痕，病势顿去。胡老太太的痧刮得很透，本来已经不要紧了，只是胡雪岩不放心，请“郎中”来看了以后，开方打药，一再关照下人要快！仍旧去了两个时辰才回来，胡雪岩对有关老母的事异常认真，当下大发了一场难得一见的脾气。下人等他骂完，方始声诉：原来这年时疫流行，打药的人排着队等，一等等了个把时辰，他忍不住挤上前去，象看病“拔号”似的，要求先配他的方子。“请你快点。我们老太太等在那里要吃呢！”“哪家没有老太太？”药店伙计答说：“你要快，不会自家去开一爿药店？”挨了骂的那人，一股怨气发泄在药店伙计头上，加油添酱地形容了一番，将胡雪岩的火气挑拨了起来，当时顿一顿足说：“好！我就开一爿给他看。”于是刘不才受命筹备，即日北上到直隶去采办药材，顺便带回来几百帖“狗皮膏药”，供胡雪岩试用。

Hu had decided to open a medicine shop. He had long wished to do so, and an affront had finally prompted him. The previous summer, his mother had suffered an attack of sha after exposure to the heat. The traditional remedy was to scrape the skin with a copper coin, producing a bright red streak, after which the symptoms promptly subsided. Old Madam Hu had been thoroughly scraped and was already out of danger, but her son remained anxious. He sent for a physician, then had the prescription taken to be made up, repeatedly telling the servant to hurry. Even so, the man did not return for two double-hours. Hu was exceptionally particular about anything concerning his mother, and he flew into one of his rare tempers. Only after the scolding ended did the servant explain. An epidemic was spreading that year, and customers had to queue for medicines. After waiting for more than a double-hour, he had lost patience and squeezed to the front, hoping to have his prescription filled out of turn, as people sometimes did when seeking a consultation. “Please hurry. Our old lady is waiting to take it.” “Who doesn't have an old lady at home?” the shop assistant replied. “If you are in such a hurry, why don't you open your own medicine shop?” The scolded servant now vented his resentment on the assistant, embellishing the account until he rekindled Hu's anger. Stamping his foot, Hu declared, “Very well! I shall open one and show him.” Liu Bucai was ordered to make the preparations and set off that very day for Zhili to buy medicinal ingredients. Along with them, he brought back several hundred dogskin plasters for Hu to try.

这“狗皮膏药”是“房中药”的一种。刘不才在采买药材时，由于他的豪爽风趣，结识了好些朋友，酒酣耳热之际，少不得谈谈风月。其中有个苏州人，谈起上一科的状元，现任河北学政的洪钧，说他最近写信回苏州，托人买妾，信中说得很坦率，娶妾无非及时行乐，用不着找什么理由，没有儿子，一定说是“不孝有三，无后为大”，单身在外，说是没有人照料起居，这些话、无非自欺欺人而已。他说：及时行乐，这句话，要分做两面来谈，一面是及时，娶妾就要娶得早，人到中年，渐形衰颓，美色当前，力不从心，不但自误，而且误人，一面是行乐，当然要娶美妾，才有乐趣而言。大家听他说得诚恳，亦以诚恳相待，终于替他觅到了一个上海的名妓，国色天香的赛金花作妾。于是另有一人感叹：说少年创业，精力过人，就是没有钱，及至创业已成，钱是有了，精力却嫌不足，姬妾满眼，广田自荒，说不定还会戴上绿帽子，人生憾事，莫过于此。这些话提醒了刘不才，想起胡雪岩或许亦有此憾。因而打听，有没有好春药，只壮阳，不伤身。当时便有人指点，北京鼓楼有一家小药店，可以买到外用的“狗皮膏药”，药性王道，不似内服的春药，竭泽而渔那样霸道。不过这家小药店的主人，颇以制售此药为耻，须有跟他交情很深的人介绍，而且只特制，不零售。刘不才的人缘不错，居然找到了适当的介绍人，出重金订制了一批。胡雪岩试用之下，床第之间，便就此放纵了。

These dogskin plasters were a kind of sexual stimulant. While buying medicines, Liu's generosity and humour had won him many friends. Over wine, their conversation inevitably turned to women. One man from Suzhou mentioned Hong Jun, the top graduate of the previous imperial examination and now Education Commissioner of Hebei. Hong had recently written home asking someone to find him a concubine. His letter was frank: the purpose of taking a concubine was to enjoy life while one could. There was no need for excuses such as “Of the three failures in filial duty, having no heir is the greatest,” when a man lacked a son, or “There is no one to look after me,” when he lived away from home. Such claims merely deceived oneself and others. Enjoying life while one could, he said, had two sides. First, one must be timely: take a concubine early, for by middle age strength begins to decline. To face beauty with insufficient vigour was to disappoint not only oneself but another person. Second came enjoyment, which naturally required a beautiful concubine. His listeners responded to such frankness with equal sincerity and eventually found him a celebrated Shanghai courtesan of exceptional beauty, Sai Jinhua. Another man lamented that in youth, while building a career, one had ample energy but no money. Once established, one had money but insufficient energy: concubines everywhere, broad fields lying untilled, and perhaps the risk of being cuckolded. What greater regret could life offer? This reminded Liu that Hu might feel the same. He asked whether there was a good aphrodisiac that strengthened virility without harming the body. Someone directed him to a small medicine shop near Beijing's Drum Tower. It sold externally applied dogskin plasters, said to act gently, unlike internal stimulants that exhausted a man like draining a pond to catch its fish. The proprietor, however, was ashamed of making and selling them. A close friend's introduction was required, and they were prepared only to order, never sold over the counter. Liu's popularity enabled him to find a suitable intermediary. He paid heavily for a batch. After trying them, Hu gave free rein to himself in bed.

“这是没法子的事。”七姑奶奶说：“除非你想得开，”这意思是，螺蛳太太可能容许胡雪岩另外纳妾来分她的宠？她心里想，自己是半正半侧的身分，老太太固然宠信有加，大太太也能相安无事，但做当家人难免为下人憎厌，倘或娶进一房夷太太来。为人厉害，又为下人撺掇，联络大太太，不顾先进门为大“这个规矩，明枪暗箭，处处作对，虽不见得怕她，但免不了常常生气，这却是不可不虑的事。正在沉吟之时：七姑奶奶又开口了：“去年秋天，应春生了一场伤寒，病好调养。不能出门，在家也实在无聊不过，请了个说书的，出堂会，来解闷，每天下半天两个钟头，说的一部书叫做《儿女英雄传》讲女人家吃醋，实在有点道理。”“喔！”螺蛳太太问道：“说书的怎么说？”“他说：吃醋分会吃、不会吃两种，每种又分三等。不会吃醋的，吃得可笑、可怜、可怕，譬如……”“七姐，”螺蛳太太打断她的话说：“不会吃的，就不要去谈它了。”“好，讲会吃的，也分三等，叫做常品，能品、神品。常品，也不必谈，先说能品，譬如说象你，一等一的人材，小爷叔再娶了一个来，就算能胜过你，只要你宽宏大量，声色不动，而且照样处处关心小爷叔的饮食起居，他心里存了个亏欠你的心，依旧是你得宠。这就是会吃醋的能品。”

“There is no remedy,” the Seventh Lady said, “unless you can accept the situation generously.” She meant: could Madam Luosi allow Hu to take another concubine and share his favour? Madam Luosi considered her position, halfway between principal wife and concubine. The old lady trusted and favoured her, and she lived peacefully with the principal wife, but managing the household inevitably earned servants' resentment. Suppose a formidable new concubine arrived and, egged on by servants, allied herself with the principal wife, disregarding the rule that earlier entry conferred seniority and opposing her openly and covertly at every turn. She might not be afraid, but she would constantly be angry. That danger could not be ignored. As she reflected, the Seventh Lady spoke again. “Last autumn Yingchun had a fever. During his convalescence he couldn't go out and was dreadfully bored, so we hired a storyteller to perform at home for two hours every afternoon. The book was Tales of Heroic Sons and Daughters. Its account of women's jealousy made considerable sense.” “What did the storyteller say?” “He divided jealous women into those who manage jealousy well and those who don't, with three grades in each. Those who don't are laughable, pitiable or terrifying. For example…” “Never mind those who don't,” Madam Luosi interrupted. “Very well. Those who manage it well are also divided into three grades: ordinary, skilful and divine. We can leave out the ordinary. Take the skilful. A first-rate woman like you might see Little Uncle marry someone who surpassed even you. Yet if you remained generous, showed no disturbance and cared as attentively as ever for his food and daily comforts, he would feel indebted to you and you would retain his favour. That is skilful jealousy.”

螺蛳太太在想，照此说来，大太太就是个能品。只不知神品以是如何？心里转着念头，口中便问了出来。“你问神品，说穿了也没有啥稀奇，象你这样能干，做起来也不费事，一句话，恩威并用！她安分守己，是好的，你比小爷叔还要宠她，她有不守规矩的地方，你尽管说她、管她。将来有了儿女，你比她生母还要知痛痒，还要会教训。那一来，上上下下哪个不服你？哪个不说你贤惠？这样子吃醋，真吃得神了！”七姑奶奶的话，句句打入螺蛳太太心坎，而且别有领会。如今一家的主人，第一是“老太太”，第二是“老爷”，第三是“太太”，第四才轮到她，除了下人，只有管她的，而没有她管的。倘或亲自经手挑选，替胡雪岩多娶几房姨太太，照七姑奶奶所说的，拿“恩威并用”四个字来调教，叫她们心服口服，那时才真正显得出当家人的威风气派。这样想着，不自觉地在脸上绽开了笑容。七姑奶奶便也笑道：“怎么样？四姐，你也想吃一吃这种看不出来是吃醋的醋？““只伯我不会吃。”螺蛳太太说：“七姐，你也帮我留意留意。”一听这话，七姑奶奶知道她决心照她的话去做了。本来是闲谈，即令有为她策划的意思，亦需从长计议，不道她从善如流，立刻就听信了！实在出人意外。

By that account, Madam Luosi thought, the principal wife belonged to the skilful grade. What, then, was the divine? She asked aloud. “Nothing particularly extraordinary, once explained. With your ability, it would not be difficult. In a word, combine kindness with authority. If she behaves properly, treat her well; cherish her even more than Little Uncle does. If she breaks the rules, speak to her and keep her in order. When she has children, understand their needs better than their own mother and be better at bringing them up. Then who in the whole household will not respect you? Who will not call you virtuous? That is truly divine jealousy.” Every word went straight to Madam Luosi's heart, and she saw a further implication. In the household hierarchy, the old lady came first, the master second, the principal wife third, and she herself only fourth. Apart from the servants, there were people to govern her but nobody for her to govern. If she personally selected several more concubines for Hu and trained them through kindness and authority until they sincerely acknowledged her, she would at last display the full dignity and power of the household's manager. A smile appeared on her face without her noticing. The Seventh Lady smiled too. “Well, Sister Luo? Would you like to practise this jealousy that does not look like jealousy?” “I only fear I may not know how. Keep an eye out for someone for me, Seventh Sister.” The Seventh Lady realized that she had decided to act on the advice. It had begun as casual conversation; even if meant as a plan, it would require long consideration. She had never expected such immediate acceptance.

转念到此，她顿感肩头沉更，俗语说的“若要家不和，娶个小老婆”，象螺蛳太太这样的情形，实在少而又少，再说罗四姐是胡雪岩自己看中的，即令进门以后不如意，也怪不到她头上。现在不同了，竞完全象是她出的主意，将来倘有风波，从胡老太太起，都会怨她。因而不能不好好替螺蛳太太想一想。“四姐，”她想到就说：“凡事想得蛮好，做起来不太容易。小爷叔如果要讨堂子里的人，你不可以许他，堂子里的人有习气，难管。”“是的。要讨总要讨好人家的女儿。”螺蛳太太又说：“我要先同大先生说明白，他尽管自己去物色，人一定要让我看过。”她紧接着又说，“其实用不着他自己去物色，我先托人替他去挑。”螺蛳太太说到做到，三、四年工夫，陆续物色，加上胡雪岩自己选中的，一共娶了十一房姨太太，连她自己在内，恰好凑成十二金钗之数。

At that thought, the Seventh Lady suddenly felt a weight on her shoulders. As the saying went, “If you want discord at home, take a concubine.” Women like Madam Luosi were exceedingly rare. Besides, Hu had chosen Luo for himself. Even if things had gone badly after she entered the household, the Seventh Lady could not have been blamed. This was different: it now seemed entirely her proposal. If trouble followed, everyone, beginning with Old Madam Hu, would resent her. She must therefore think carefully on her friend's behalf. “Sister Luo, things sound fine in the planning but are not so easy to carry out. If Little Uncle wants to marry someone from a courtesan house, you must refuse. Such women have habits that make them difficult to manage.” “Yes. She must be a girl from a respectable family. I shall make it clear to him first: he may look for someone himself, but I must see her. In fact, there is no need for him to look. I shall ask people to choose someone for him.” She did as she said. Over three or four years, the women she found, together with those Hu chose himself, made eleven additional concubines. Including her, they numbered exactly twelve, like the Twelve Beauties of the novel.

眷属一多，又加上生意发达，不断添人，原有的房子虽然一再扩充，始终不敷所需，到后来基地所限，倘非彻底翻造，就得另辟新居。胡雪岩便与螺蛳太大商量，打算另外觅地建一所住宅，将他的两个胞弟，连同各式办事人等一起迁了出去，空出来的房子拆掉，改做花园，另外要造一座“走马楼”，将“十二金钡”集中一起。螺蛳太太对造一座走马楼，倒颇赞成，但对另建新宅却有异议。“请二老爷、三老爷搬出去，会伤老太太的心，亲戚也会说闲话。这件事，老爷还要斟酌。”听说会伤老母之心，胡雪岩立即打消了原议，不过，“房子不够住，总要想法子。”他问：“你有啥好主意？”“我听说间壁刘家的房子要卖，后门口米店老板死掉了，两个儿子分家争产，米店归哪个管，一直在吵，也想卖了房子分现款。不如拿这两家的地皮买过来，打通围墙，不是可以联在一起？”这下又激起了胡雪岩好摆排场的意兴。恰好这年丝价大涨。胡雪岩操纵“洋庄”，结算下来三个月的工夫，赚了四十万银子，‘决定大治园林。“譬如我没有挣到这笔款子，”他这样对螺蛳太太说：“我照你的意思来做，不过范围要做得大，前后左右都要临街，方方整整一大片，象王府的气派才好。”这是有面子的事，螺蛳太太当然高兴。于是胡雪岩派人到周围人家去游说，动以厚利，其中除了两家，都愿意迁让。

With more family members and an expanding business continually bringing new personnel, the house proved inadequate despite repeated extensions. Eventually the limits of the site meant either complete rebuilding or finding another home. Hu discussed it with Madam Luosi. He proposed buying land and building a new residence elsewhere, moving his two younger brothers there along with the various people who worked for him, and demolishing the vacated buildings to make a garden. He also wanted a gallery-lined residence where his Twelve Beauties could live together. Madam Luosi approved of the latter but objected to the separate house. “Asking Second Master and Third Master to move out will hurt your mother. The relatives will gossip too. You ought to reconsider.” At the thought of hurting his mother, Hu abandoned the proposal at once. “But there isn't enough room. We must do something. Have you a better idea?” “I hear the Liu house next door is for sale. The owner of the rice shop behind us has died, and his two sons keep quarrelling over the division of the estate and who should run the shop. They also want to sell the building and divide the cash. Why not buy both properties and break through the walls to join them to ours?” This revived Hu's appetite for grand display. Silk prices happened to rise sharply that year. Through his control of the silk trade with foreign houses, he made four hundred thousand taels in three months. He decided on a grand garden. “Let us pretend I never earned that money. I shall follow your suggestion, but on a larger scale. Streets must bound it on all four sides, making one great, regular block, with the grandeur of a prince's mansion.” Madam Luosi was naturally pleased by such distinction. Hu sent men to persuade the surrounding households, offering substantial inducements. All but two agreed to move and sell.

这两家一家是酒栈，说存酒搬运不便，无法出让，态度虽然坚决，说话却很客气。另一家就不同了。这一家是个极小的剃头店，位置恰好在元宝街与望仙桥直街转角之处，为出入所必经，整片房子，在此交通要道上缺了一块，而且是家破破烂烂的剃头店，就象绝色美人，瞎了一只眼那样令人难以忍受。“好是啥意思？”胡雪岩说：“她如果想卖好价钱，尽管说。要多少就多少好了。”她，是指剃头店的“崔老太婆”。老板是她的儿子，脾气虽然也很犟，但经不住胡家人三天两头去说好话，又看在钱的分上。意思倒有些活动了。

One holdout was a wine warehouse. It said the stored wine was too difficult to move and refused to sell, firmly but politely. The other was different. It was a tiny barbershop at the corner of Yuanbao Street and Wangxianqiao Straight Street, a place everyone had to pass when entering or leaving. To have a gap in the estate at such an important junction—and a dilapidated barbershop at that—was as intolerable as a peerless beauty with one eye blind. “What does she want?” Hu demanded. “If she wants a good price, let her name it. Whatever she asks, she can have.” “She” was Old Mrs Cui, the proprietor's mother. Her son was stubborn too, but the Hu household's frequent visits and courteous persuasion, together with the prospect of money, had begun to move him.

可是崔老大婆执意不允，原来她是年轻守寡，孤苦无依，好不容易将儿子抚养成人，也只是个剃头匠，她不怨自己当初不该叫儿子去学了这一行，只说老天无眼，慢慢养成了乖僻的脾气，最恨有钱人，越有钱越恨。因此，胡雪岩说到“要多少就多少”这句话，恰恰犯了她的忌。“你同你们东家去说，他是财神，我们是穷鬼，打不上交道。他发财是他的，他又不是阎王、判官，我也用不着怕他。”去打交道的是胡雪岩门下的一个清客，名叫张子洪，以脾气好出名，此时也忍不住生气，说了一句：“他虽不是阎王判官，不过是个道台。”“道台莫非不讲王法？”崔老太婆答说：“我们娘儿两个两条命，随便他好了。”这番话传到胡雪岩耳朵里，气得一天没有吃饭。门下清客，帐房、管事，还有听差打杂的，议论纷纷，而且出了好些主意，有的说请县里的差役来跟她说话，有的说放火烧掉她的房子再说，有的说造张假契约跟她打官司，但胡雪岩终觉不忍，螺蛳太太也怕逼出人命案子来，约束下人，不准胡来。以至于一直到巨宅落成，元室街也重新翻修过，那家剃头店始终存在。

His mother, however, refused absolutely. Widowed young and left without support, she had struggled to bring him up, only to see him become a barber. Rather than blame herself for choosing that trade for him, she accused Heaven of blindness. Over time she had grown contrary and bitter, hating the wealthy in proportion to their wealth. Hu's promise to pay whatever she asked touched precisely her sore point. “Tell your employer that he may be the God of Wealth, but we are paupers. We have no dealings with him. Let him make his fortune. He is neither the King of Hell nor a judge in the underworld. I have no reason to fear him.” The negotiator was Zhang Zihong, a literary hanger-on in Hu's household, famous for his mild temper. Even he lost patience. “He may not be the King of Hell or an underworld judge, but he is a circuit intendant.” “Does that put him above the law? My son and I have only our two lives. Let him do as he pleases.” When Hu heard this, he was so angry that he ate nothing all day. His household retainers, accountants, managers and servants proposed all kinds of measures: send the county bailiffs, burn down the house, or forge a deed and sue her. Hu could not bring himself to do it. Madam Luosi also feared that coercion might lead to a death and restrained the servants from any rash act. Even after the great mansion was completed and Yuanbao Street repaved, the barbershop remained.

落成之日，大宴宾客，共分三日，第一天是“三大宪”，杭州府、仁和、钱塘两县，以及候补道，邀约在籍的绅士作陪，入席之前，主人亲自引导游园，曲曲折折，转过假山，只见东南方树木掩映之中，矗起一座高楼，华丽非凡，令人不解的是，四周雕栏，金光闪耀，远远望去，谁也猜不透是何缘故。“雪翁，”巡抚杨昌浚问道：“那是个什么所在？”“是内人所住的一座楼。”听说是内眷住处，杨昌浚不便再间，私下打听，才知道那座楼名为“百狮楼”。栏杆柱子上，用紫檀打磨出一百个狮子，突出的狮目，是用黄金铸就，所以映日耀眼，令人不可逼视。“太太们住的地方，怎么叫百狮楼，莫非‘河东狮吼’这句话，他都不懂。”“不是。因为那位太太称为螺蛳太太，所以胡大先生造了这座楼给她住。”杨昌浚再问“螺蛳太太”之名如何而起，是何出身。打听清楚了觉得未免过分，便悄悄写了一封信给在肃州的左宗棠，颇有微词。

The completion was celebrated with three days of banquets. On the first day, the guests were the three principal provincial authorities, the prefect of Hangzhou, the magistrates of Renhe and Qiantang, and expectant circuit intendants, with local gentry invited to keep them company. Before the meal, Hu personally led them through the garden. Following its winding paths around a rockery, they saw an extraordinarily splendid tower rising among the trees to the southeast. What puzzled them was the gold light flashing from the carved railings all around it. At that distance, nobody could account for it. “Mr Hu,” Governor Yang Changjun asked, “what is that building?” “The residence of my wife.” Hearing that it belonged to the women's quarters, Yang could not inquire further, but private questions brought the explanation. It was called the Hundred Lions Tower. One hundred lions carved and polished from zitan stood on the railing posts. Their protruding eyes were cast in gold and glittered in the sunlight so brightly that one could scarcely look at them. “Why call the ladies' residence Hundred Lions Tower? Does he not know the saying about the lioness of Hedong roaring?” “No, that isn't it. The lady is called Madam Luosi, and he built the tower for her.” Yang asked how she had acquired the name and what her origins were. Once informed, he felt that Hu had gone rather too far and quietly wrote to Zuo at Suzhou in Gansu, expressing some criticism.

哪知左宗棠对他的看法，颇不以为然，只是不便明言，恰巧他的长子来信，亦批评了胡雪岩，正好借题发挥，说一个人的享用，求其相称，胡雪岩的功劳，世人不尽了解，他很清楚，西征军事之能有今日，全亏得有胡雪岩，享用稍过，自可无愧。他又提到他的儿女亲家，也是平生第一知己的陶澍，在两江总督任上时，他的女婿胡林翼，以翰林在江宁闲住，每天选歌征色，花的都是老丈人的“养廉银”，内帐房有一次向陶演表示，胡林翼挥霍无度，是否应该稍加节制？陶澎告诉他说：“尽管让他花！他将来要为国家出力，有钱亦没有工夫去花。”胡雪岩跟胡林翼的情形虽有不同，但个人的享用，比起为国家所谋的大利来，即令豪奢亦不足道。这些活辗转传到浙江，胡雪岩感激在心，对左宗棠自然越发尽忠竭力，但螺狮太太却心生警惕，与七姑奶奶私下谈起来，都认为“树大招风”，应该要收敛了。可是胡雪岩只问一句：“怎么收法？”螺蛳太太却又无词以对。因为胡雪岩所凭借的是信用，信用是建立在大家对他的信心上面，而信心是由胡雪岩的场面造成的。场面只能大，不能小，否则只要有人无意间说一句：“胡大先生如今也不比从前了。”立刻就会惹起无数猜测，原来有仇恨的、无怨无仇只是由于妒嫉的，都将推波助澜，大放谣言，那一来信用就要动摇，后果不堪设想。

Zuo disagreed considerably with Yang but could not conveniently say so outright. As it happened, his eldest son also wrote to criticize Hu, giving him a suitable occasion to express his view. A man's enjoyments, he said, should be proportionate to his deserts. The world did not fully understand Hu's services, but he did. The western campaign owed its present success entirely to Hu; a little excess in his pleasures need give him no shame. He cited Tao Shu, his closest lifelong friend and the father of his child's spouse.
