They must prepare their response, or a disturbance would break out at once. “We must first win people over,” Wu said. “There must be some respectable gentlemen among the crowd outside. Let us invite them in, ask Your Excellency to reason with them personally, and have them take the lead in persuading the others. At the same time, we can post a red proclamation explaining the arrangements. That combined approach would be safer.” “An excellent stratagem!” Dexin nodded. “But while we enlist respectable gentlemen, we must also pacify the troublemakers who seize on every disturbance. You and I should divide the work.” Xie sent two capable employees quietly into the neighbouring shops on either side. From their upper windows, they could examine the crowd and identify people who should be invited in. There were three categories: respectable gentlemen; troublesome scholars accustomed to stirring up a crowd; and the habitually unruly fellows whom Hangzhou people called liaoguier—idlers who did no honest work and welcomed disorder as a chance to fish in troubled waters, men little different from local ruffians.

当这两名伙计分头出发时，德馨与吴世荣已经商定，由杭州府出面贴红告示，这种告示，照例用六言体，吴世荣是带了户房当办来的，就在阜康帐户拟稿呈阅。告示上写的是：“照得阜康钱庄，信誉素来卓著，联号遍设南北，调度绰绰有余，只为时世不靖，银根难得宽裕，周转一时不灵，无须张皇失措，兹奉宪台德谕：市面必求平静，小民升头应顾，阜康照常开门，银票亦可兑付，千两以下十足，逾千另作区处，阜康主人回杭，自能应付裕如，为期不过三日，难关即可度过，切望共体时艰，和衷共济应变，倘有不法小人，希冀浑水摸鱼，或者危言惑众，或者暗中煽动，一经拿获审实，国法不贷尔汝。本府苦口婆心，莫谓言之不须！切切此谕。”

As the two employees set out separately, Dexin and Wu agreed that the red proclamation should be issued by the Hangzhou prefectural office. Such notices were conventionally written in lines of six characters. Wu had brought a clerk from the revenue section, who drafted it in Fukang’s accounts room for their approval: “Whereas Fukang Bank has long enjoyed a distinguished reputation, with affiliated establishments throughout north and south and ample means of transferring funds, present disorders alone have tightened the supply of silver and caused a temporary difficulty in meeting payments. There is no need for alarm. By instruction of His Excellency Treasurer De: the marketplace must remain tranquil, and the livelihoods of ordinary people must be considered. Fukang shall open as usual and its notes shall be redeemable. Those for a thousand taels or less shall be paid in full; those exceeding a thousand shall be dealt with separately. When the proprietor returns to Hangzhou, he will be able to meet his obligations with ease. Within no more than three days, the difficulty can be overcome. All are earnestly requested to recognise the hardships of the time and cooperate in meeting this emergency. Should lawless persons seek to profit from confusion, spread alarming falsehoods or secretly incite disturbance, once apprehended and found guilty they shall receive no indulgence from the law. This prefecture counsels you earnestly and patiently. Let none say that he was not warned. Take heed and obey.”

德馨与吴世荣对这通六言告示的评价不同，德馨认为写得极好，但有两点要改，一是提存与兑银相同，皆以一千两为限，二是银很大紧，到处都一样，不独沪杭为然。但吴世荣一开头就有意见，说阜康信誉卓著，说胡雪岩一回来，必能应付裕如之类的话，不无过甚其词，有意袒护之嫌，倘或阜康真的倒闭了，出告示的人难免扶同欺骗之咎，因而主张重拟，要拟得切实，有什么说什么，才是负责的态度。“世荣兄！此言差矣！”德馨答说：“如今最要紧是稳定民心。不说阜康信誉卓著，难道说它摇摇欲坠？那一来不等于明告杭州百姓，赶紧来提存兑现？而且正好授人以柄。如果阜康真的挤倒了，胡观察会说：本来不过一时周转不灵，只为杭州府出了一张告示，才起的风潮。那时候，请问你我有何话说？”吴世荣无以为答，只勉强答说：“府里总觉得满话难说，将来替人受过犯不着。“

The two officials differed in their judgement of this six-character proclamation. Dexin thought it excellent, but wanted two amendments: withdrawals of deposits should be subject to the same thousand-tael limit as the redemption of notes, and it should state that money was tight everywhere, not only in Shanghai and Hangzhou. Wu, however, objected from the outset. To praise Fukang’s reputation and declare that Hu could meet every obligation as soon as he returned seemed exaggerated and unduly protective. If Fukang really failed, those who issued the notice might be held responsible for assisting a fraud. He wanted it redrafted to state only what was known; that was the responsible course. “Brother Shirong, you are mistaken!” Dexin replied. “What matters most now is restoring confidence. If we do not say Fukang’s reputation is excellent, are we to say it is tottering? Would that not tell every person in Hangzhou to hurry and withdraw deposits or redeem notes? Worse, it would put a weapon into other people’s hands. If the run really brought Fukang down, Hu could say, ‘It was merely a temporary shortage of funds until the prefectural office issued its proclamation and started the panic.’ What answer could you or I make then?” Wu had none. He could only say reluctantly, “I still feel that sweeping assurances are dangerous. There is no reason to take the blame for someone else later.”

“现在还谈不到个人犯得着，犯不着这一层。如今最要紧的是把局面稳下来。胡雪岩号称‘财神’，‘财神’落难，不是好事，会搞成一路哭的凄惨景象。世荣兄，你要想想后果。”“是。”吴世荣越发没话说了，而德馨却更振振有词。“就事论事，说阜康‘信誉素来卓著’，并没有错，他的信用不好，会大半个天下都有他的联号？所以要救阜康，一定要说胡雪岩有办法。老实说，阜康不怕银栗兑现，只伯大户提存，如果把大户稳住了，心里就会想，款子存在阜康，白天生利息，晚上睡觉也在生利息，何必提了现银，摆在家里？不但大钱不会生小钱，而且惹得小偷强盗眼红，还有慢藏海盗之忧。世荣兄，你说我这话是不是？““是！是！”吴世荣完全为他说服了，尤其是想到“慢藏海盗”这一点，出了盗案，巡抚、按察使以下至地方官，都有责任，唯有藩司不管刑名，可以置身事外。照此看来，德馨的警告，实在是忠告。

“This is no time to consider whether you or I should take a personal risk. We must stabilise the situation. Hu is known as the God of Wealth. If the God of Wealth falls into distress, the consequences will be dreadful—lamentation everywhere. Think of that, Brother Shirong.” “Yes, sir.” Wu had still less to say, while Dexin grew more emphatic. “On the facts alone, it is not wrong to say Fukang ‘has long enjoyed a distinguished reputation.’ Could it have affiliated banks across more than half the country without good credit? To save Fukang, we must insist that Hu has a solution. Frankly, note redemption is not the real danger; withdrawals by large depositors are. Keep them calm and they will reflect that money in Fukang earns interest by day and even while they sleep. Why bring silver home? It would earn nothing and attract the envy of thieves and robbers. Carelessly kept wealth invites theft. Am I not right?” “Indeed, indeed!” Wu was completely persuaded, especially by that last consideration. When a robbery occurred, everyone from the provincial governor and judicial commissioner down to the local officials bore responsibility. Only the provincial treasurer, who did not handle criminal matters, could stand apart. Seen in that light, Dexin’s warning was friendly advice.

于是传言告示定稿，谢云青叫人买来上等梅行纸，找了一个好书手，用碗口大的字，正楷书写。告示本应用印，但大印未曾携来，送回衙门去铃盖，又嫌费时，只好变通办法，由吴世荣在他自己的衔名之下，画了个花押，证明确是杭州府的告示。其时奉命去邀客的两个伙计，相继回店复命，却是无功而返，只为没有适当的人可邀，倒是有自告奋勇，愿意来见藩台及知府的，但争先恐后，请这个不请那个，反而要得罪人，只好推托去请示了再说。从他们的话中听得出来，挤兑的人群中，并没有什么有地位的绅士，足以号召大众，而争先恐后想来见官府的，都是无名小卒。既然如此，无足为虑。德馨想了一下，看着吴世荣跟谢云青问道：“有没有口才好的人？声音要宏亮，口齿要清楚，见过大场面，能沉得住气的。”吴世荣尚未开口，谢云青却一叠连声他说：“有，有，就是大人衙门里的周书办。”“周书办。”德馨问道：“是周少棠不是？”“是，是！就是他。”“不错，此人很行。他怎么会在这里？”“他跟我们东家是早年的朋友，今天听说阜康有事，特为来帮忙的。

Orders were therefore given to finalise the proclamation. Xie sent out for fine-quality paper and found a skilled copyist, who wrote it in regular script with characters as large as the mouth of a bowl. The official seal should have been affixed, but it had not been brought along, and sending the notice back to the office would waste time. Wu improvised by putting his personal flourish beneath his own name and title, certifying that this was indeed a proclamation of the Hangzhou prefectural office. Meanwhile, the two employees sent to invite people in returned one after the other, empty-handed. They had found nobody suitable. Some people had volunteered to meet the Treasurer and prefect, but they competed so eagerly that to invite one and not another would only give offence. The employees could merely say they must ask for instructions first. Their report made it clear that there was no gentleman of standing in the crowd who could command the others’ attention. Those clamouring to see the officials were all nobodies. There was therefore little to fear. After a moment’s thought, Dexin looked at Wu and Xie. “Is there anyone who speaks well? He must have a strong voice, clear diction, experience of large gatherings and the ability to keep his head.” Before Wu could reply, Xie said eagerly, “Yes, sir! Clerk Zhou from your own office.” “Do you mean Zhou Shaotang?” “Yes, precisely.” “An able man. What is he doing here?” “He is an old friend of our employer’s. When he heard of the trouble today, he came specially to help.”

其实，此人是谢云青特为请来的。原来各省藩司衙门，都“有包办上下忙钱粮的书办，俗称”粮书“，公文上往往称此辈为”蠹吏“，所谓”钱粮“就是田赋，为国家主要的收入，其中弊端百出，最清廉能干的地方大吏，亦无法彻底整顿，所以称之为“粮糊涂”。但是这些“蠹吏”另有一本极清楚的底册，这本底册，便是极大的财源，亦只有在藩司衙门注册有案的粮书，才能获得这种底册。粮书是世袭的职务，父死子继，兄终弟及以外，亦可以顶名转让，买这样一个书办底缺，看他所管的县分而定，象杭州府的仁和、钱塘两县的粮书，顶费要十几万银子，就是苦瘠山城，亦非两三万两莫办。这周少棠原是胡雪岩的贫贱之交，后来靠胡雪岩的资助，花了五万银子买了个专管嘉兴府嘉眷县的粮书，只有上下忙开征钱粮的时候，才到嘉善，平时只在省城里专事结交，生得一表人才，能言善道。谢云青跟他很熟，这天因为阜康挤兑，怕应付不下来，特为请了他来帮忙，这时候正好派上用场了。

In fact, Xie had specially sent for him. Every provincial treasury office had clerks who handled the two seasonal collections of land tax. They were popularly known as grain-tax clerks, and official documents often called them corrupt vermin. Land tax was the state’s principal source of revenue, yet the system contained so many abuses that even the most honest and capable provincial authorities could not thoroughly reform it. Hence its reputation as an unfathomable muddle. These “vermin,” however, possessed another set of perfectly clear underlying registers. Those registers were a source of immense wealth, accessible only to grain-tax clerks officially registered at the provincial treasury. The posts were hereditary: sons succeeded fathers and younger brothers succeeded elder brothers. They could also be transferred to buyers who took over the registered name. The price depended on the county concerned. A post for Renhe or Qiantang, in Hangzhou prefecture, cost over a hundred thousand taels; even a poor mountain county required twenty or thirty thousand. Zhou had known Hu in the days when both were poor. With Hu’s financial support, he had later paid fifty thousand taels for the grain-tax clerkship responsible for Jiashan County in Jiaxing prefecture. He went to Jiashan only for the two seasonal collections. The rest of the time he stayed in the provincial capital, devoting himself to making connections. Good-looking and eloquent, he was well known to Xie. Fearing that he could not cope with the run on Fukang, Xie had invited him to help. Now his talents would come into use.

当时将周少棠找了来，向德馨及吴世荣分别行了礼，然后满面赔笑的肃立一旁，听候发落。“周书办，我同吴知府为了维持市面，不能不出头来管阜康的事。现在有张告示在这里，你看了就知道我们的苦心了。”“是，是！两位大人为我们杭州百姓尽心尽力，真正感激不尽。胡大先生跟两位大人，论公是同事，论私是朋友，他不在杭州，就全靠两位大人替他作主了。”“我们虽可以替他作主，也要靠大家顾全大局才好。说老实话，胡观察是倒不下来的，万一真的倒下来了，杭州的市面大受影响，亦非杭州人之福。我请你把这番意思，切切实实跟大家说一说。“

Zhou was summoned. After paying his respects to Dexin and Wu in turn, he stood deferentially to one side with a broad, obliging smile, awaiting their commands. “Clerk Zhou, Prefect Wu and I must intervene in Fukang’s affairs to preserve order in the marketplace. Here is a proclamation. Once you read it, you will understand our intentions.” “Indeed, indeed! You are sparing no effort for the people of Hangzhou. We cannot thank you enough. Mr Hu is your colleague in public affairs and your friend in private. While he is away, he must rely entirely on you to act for him.” “We can act for him, but everyone must also consider the larger situation. Frankly, Circuit Intendant Hu is not going to fail. If he did, it would seriously damage trade throughout Hangzhou and bring the people no good. I want you to explain this to them thoroughly.”

周少棠答应着，往后退了几步，向站在客座进口处的谢云青，使了个眼色，相偕到了柜房，阜康几个重要的伙计，以及拟六言告示的户房书办都在。周少棠一进门就说：“老卜，你这支笔真刮刮叫！”说着，大拇指举得老高。“老卜是叫户房书办，他们身分相同，走得极近，平时玩笑开惯的，当下老卜答说：”我的一支笔不及你的一张嘴，现在要看你的了。““你不要看我的笑话！倒替我想想看，这桩事情，要从哪里下手？”“要一上来就有噱头，一噱把大家吸住了，才会静下来听你吹。”老卜说道：“我教你个法子，你不是会唱‘徽调儿’？搬一张八仙桌出去，你在上面一站，象‘徐策跑城’一样，捞起皮袍子下摆，唱它一段‘垛板’，包你一个满堂彩。这一来，什么都了说了。”明明是开玩笑，周少棠却不当它笑话，双眼望着空中，眼珠乱转乱眨了一阵，开口说道：“我有办法了，要做它一篇偏锋文章。来，老谢，你叫人搭张八仙桌出去。”“怎么？”老卜笑道：“真的要唱‘徐策跑城’？一张桌子跑圆场跑不转，要不要多搭一张桌子？”

Zhou agreed, stepped back a few paces and caught Xie’s eye at the entrance. They went together to the accounts room, where several senior employees and the revenue clerk who had drafted the proclamation were waiting. “Bu, your pen is truly formidable!” Zhou exclaimed, raising his thumb. The revenue clerk he called Bu was his equal in rank and a close acquaintance. They often joked together. “My pen is no match for your tongue,” Bu replied. “Now it is your turn.” “Do not just wait to laugh at me. Help me work out how to begin.” “You need a trick at the outset to seize everyone’s attention. Then they will quieten down and listen to your bluster. Here is an idea: you can sing Hui opera, can you not? Put a square table outside and stand on it. Hitch up your fur robe like Xu Ce in Xu Ce Runs Along the City Wall and give them a rapid-fire passage. I guarantee a round of applause. After that, you can say anything.” This was plainly a joke, but Zhou did not treat it as one. He looked into the air, his eyes darting and blinking. Then he said, “I have it. We must approach this from an unexpected angle. Xie, have a square table carried outside.” “What?” Bu laughed. “Are you really going to perform Xu Ce Runs Along the City Wall? You cannot make a proper circuit on one table. Shall we put out another?”

“你懂个屁！”周少堂转脸对谢云青说：“这开门去贴告示，就有学问，没有预备，门一开，人一挤，马上天下大乱。现在这样，你叫他们从旁门搭一张桌子出去，贴紧排门，再把桌子后面的一扇排门卸下来。这一来前面有桌子挡住，人就进不来了。”“你呢？”老卜接口，“你从桌子后面爬出去？”“什么爬出去？我是从桌子后面爬上去。”“好！好！”谢云青原就在为一开门，人潮汹涌，秩序难以维持发愁，所以一听这话，大为高兴，立即派人照办。

“You know bugger-all!” Zhou turned to Xie. “Opening the doors to post that proclamation takes some thought. Without preparation, the moment they open, the crowd will rush in and all hell will break loose. Have the table taken through the side door and placed right against the shutters. Then remove the shutter behind it. The table will block the entrance and keep people out.” “And you?” Bu interposed. “You crawl out from behind the table?” “Not out. Up onto it.” “Excellent!” Xie had been worrying about just this problem: how to control the crowd once the doors opened. Delighted, he immediately ordered the arrangement made.

等桌子一抬出去，外面鼓噪之声稍微安静了些，及至里面排门一卸，先出去两名差役，接着递出红告示去。大家争先恐后往前挤，大呼小叫，鼓噪之声变本加厉了。“不要挤，不要挤！”周少棠急忙跳上桌子，高举双手，大声说道：“杭州府吴大人的告示，我来念。”接着他指挥那两名差役，将红告示高高举了起来，他就用唱“徽调”念韵白似地，“照得”云云，有板有眼地念了起来。念完又大声喝道：“大家不要乱动！”他这蓦地里一喝，由于量大声宏，气势惊人，别有一股慑入的力量，居然不少人想探手入怀的，手在中途停了下来。“为啥叫大家不要乱动？扒儿手就在你旁边！你来不及想摸银票来兑现，哪晓得银票摆在哪里，已经告诉扒儿手了。铜钱是你的总归是你的，阜康的银票，就是现银，今天不兑，明天兑，明天不兑后天兑，分文不少，哪天都一样。不过人家阜康认票不认人，你的银票叫扒儿手摸了去，朝我哭都没有用。“

As soon as the table appeared, the uproar outside subsided a little. When the shutter behind it was taken down, two runners went out first, followed by the red proclamation. Everyone tried to push forward at once, shouting and calling more loudly than before. “Do not push! Do not push!” Zhou hurriedly climbed onto the table, raised both hands and called out, “A proclamation from Prefect Wu of Hangzhou! I shall read it.” He directed the runners to hold it high. Then, like an actor delivering rhythmic speech in Hui opera, he began, “Whereas…” and read the notice in measured cadences. When he finished, he suddenly shouted, “Nobody move!” His voice was so powerful and commanding that many people whose hands were reaching inside their clothes stopped halfway. “Why do I tell you not to move? Because there may be a pickpocket beside you! In your hurry to get out your banknote and redeem it, you show him exactly where you keep it. Your money is yours. A Fukang note is as good as silver. Redeem it today, tomorrow or the day after: not a fraction will be missing, whichever day you come. But Fukang honours the note, not the person. If a pickpocket takes yours, crying to me will do you no good!”

夹枪带棒一顿排摈，反而将人声压了下去，但人丛中却有人放天嗓子说道：“周少棠，你是唱‘徽调儿’，还是卖梨膏糖？”此言一出，人丛中颇有笑声。原来周少棠早年卖过梨膏糖，这一行照例以唱小调来招揽顾客，触景生情，即兴编词，开开无伤大雅的玩笑，不但要一条极好的嗓子，而且要有一点捷才，周少棠随机应变的本事，便是在卖梨膏糖那两年练出来的。尽管人讪笑，他却神态自若，游目四顾，趁此机会动动脑筋。等笑声停住，他大声说道：“黄八麻子，你不要挖我的痛疮疤！我周少棠，今天一下唱徽调儿，二不卖梨膏糖，是来为大家打抱不平的。”最后这句话，又引起窃窃私议，但很快地复归于平静，那黄八麻子又开口了。“周少棠，你为哪个打抱不平？”“我为大家打！”周少棠应声而答。“打哪个？”“打洋鬼子！”他说：“洋鬼子看我们中国好欺侮，娘卖×的法国人，在安南打不过刘永福，弄两只灯笼壳的铁甲火轮船，在吴淤口外晃啊晃。上海人都是不中用的‘铲头’，自己吓自己，弄得市面大乱，连带金字招牌的阜康都罩不住。说来说去，是法国人害人！不过，法国人总算还是真小人，另外杀人不见血，还有比法国更加毒的洋鬼子。”说到这里，他故意停下来，看看反应，只听一片“哪一国，哪一国”发问的声音。“要问哪一国，喏，青竹蛇儿口，黄蜂尾上针，两样都不毒，最毒英国人。”

His mixture of warning and mockery actually quietened the crowd. Then someone bawled, “Zhou Shaotang, are you singing Hui opera or selling pear-syrup sweets?” Laughter rippled through the gathering. Zhou had once sold pear-syrup sweets, a trade in which sellers attracted customers by singing popular tunes, improvising verses about whatever they saw and making harmless jokes. It demanded not only a fine voice but a quick wit. His two years in that trade had taught him to think on his feet. He remained unruffled by the laughter, looking about while he used the pause to think. When it stopped, he called, “Huang Bamazi, do not reopen my old sores! Today I am neither singing Hui opera nor selling sweets. I am here to speak up against injustice on everyone’s behalf.” This brought another murmur, which quickly died away. Huang, the pockmarked man, spoke again. “Whose injustice are you speaking up against?” “Everyone’s!” “And who are you taking on?” “The foreign devils!” Zhou declared. “They think China is easy to bully. Those bloody French bastards cannot beat Liu Yongfu in Annam, so they bring a couple of ironclad steamships, flimsy as paper lanterns, to hover outside the Wusong. The useless fools in Shanghai frighten themselves into a panic and throw the whole market into disorder. Even Fukang’s golden reputation cannot withstand it. When all is said and done, the French are to blame! But at least they are open villains. There are other foreign devils more poisonous still, who kill without spilling blood.” He paused deliberately to judge the response. Voices called from every side, “Which country? Which country?” “You want to know? The green snake’s mouth, the wasp’s sharp sting—neither is as poisonous as the British!”

对这两句话，大家报以沉默。此一反应不大好，因为广济医院的梅藤更，颇获杭州人的好感，而此人是英国人。“你们只看见梅藤更，”周少棠把大家心里的疙瘩抓了出来，“梅藤更是医生，医家有割股之心，自然是好的。另外呢？第一个是赫德，我们中国的海关，归他一把抓，好比我们的咽喉给他卡住了！”说着他伸手张开虎口，比在自己脖子上作个扼喉的姿势，“他手松一松，中国人就多吃两口饭，紧一紧就要饿肚皮！这个娘卖×的赫德，他只要中国人吃‘黑饭’，不要中国人吃白饭。”说到这里，恰好有个涕泗横流的后生，极力往外挤，引起小小的骚动，给了周少棠一个借题发挥的机会。“你看你，你看你！”他指着那后生说：“年纪轻轻不学好，吃乌烟！瘾头一来，就是这副鬼相。不过，“他提高了声音，”也不要怪他，要怪杀人不见血的英国人！没有英国人，今天阜康没有事。““周少棠，你不要乱开黄腔，旱康显原形，跟英国人啥相千？屙不出屎怪茅坑，真正气数。”责问的是黄八麻子，词锋犀利。周少棠不慌不忙地答道：“你说我开黄腔，我又不姓黄。”

The crowd greeted these words with silence. This was not a favourable reaction: Mei Tenggeng of Guangji Hospital was well liked in Hangzhou, and he was British. “You are thinking only of Mei Tenggeng,” Zhou said, putting his finger on their objection. “He is a doctor, with a physician’s readiness to cut flesh from his own thigh to save another. Naturally, he is a good man. But what of the others? Take Hart first. He has all our Chinese customs in his grip, as though he were holding us by the throat.” Zhou spread the thumb and fingers of one hand and held them against his own neck in a gesture of strangulation. “If he loosens his hand, we Chinese get a few more mouthfuls of rice; if he tightens it, we go hungry. That bastard Hart wants the Chinese to eat only ‘black food,’ never white rice!” Just then, a young fellow with tears and mucus streaming down his face forced his way towards the edge of the crowd. The small commotion gave Zhou something else to exploit. Pointing at him, he cried, “Look at you! So young, and already taking to bad ways—smoking opium! See what a creature it makes of him when the craving comes! But,” he raised his voice, “do not blame him. Blame the British, who kill without spilling blood! Without the British, nothing would be wrong with Fukang today.” “Zhou, stop that ‘yellow talk’—spouting nonsense! What have the British to do with Fukang showing its true colours? You cannot shit, so you blame the privy. Infuriating!” The challenge came from Huang Bamazi, and it was sharp. Zhou replied calmly, “You accuse me of ‘yellow talk,’ but my surname is not Huang—Yellow!”

话一出口，立刻引起一阵爆笑，还有拍手顿足，乐不可支的。这又给周少棠一个机会，等笑声咯停，大声向黄八麻子挑战。“黄八麻子，你说屙不出屎怪茅坑，是要怪茅坑不好，你敢不敢同我辩一辩？”“别人怕你的歪理十八条，我姓黄的石骨铁硬的杭铁头，偏要戳穿你的西洋镜。”“你是杭铁头，莫非我是苏空头？放马过来！”大家一看有好戏看了，自动让出一条路来，容黄八麻子挤到前面，便有人喊：“上去！上去！”更有人将他抬了起来。周少棠很有风度，伸手拉了他一把，自己偏到一边，腾出地方来让他对立。经此鼓舞的黄八麻子，信心更足了，“周少棠，我辩不过你输一桌酒席。”他问：“你输了呢？”“我输了，一桌酒席以外，当场给大家磕头赔不是。”“好！你问我答，我问你答，答不出来算输。你先问。”周少棠本就想先发问，如下围棋的取得“先手”，所以一听黄八麻子的话，正中下怀，当即拱拱手说：“承让，承让！”“不必客气，放马过来。”黄八麻子，人高马大，又站在东面，偏西的阳光，照得他麻子粒粒发亮，只见他叉手仰脸，颇有睥睨一世的气概。

The retort brought a burst of laughter. Some people clapped and stamped their feet in delight. This gave Zhou another opening. When the laughter eased, he challenged Huang loudly. “You say a man who cannot shit blames the privy. Well, sometimes the privy is to blame. Dare you argue it out with me?” “Other people may fear your eighteen varieties of crooked reasoning. I am a Hangzhou Iron Head, bone of stone and iron. I shall expose your tricks!” “You are an Iron Head? Do you take me for a Suzhou Empty Head? Come on, then!” Anticipating a good show, the crowd made way for Huang. “Up you go!” people shouted, and some lifted him onto the table. Zhou, with great courtesy, gave him a hand and moved aside to make room for him to stand opposite. Encouraged, Huang grew still more confident. “Zhou, if I cannot beat you in argument, I shall pay for a banquet. What if you lose?” “I shall pay for a banquet too, and kowtow here and now to everyone in apology.” “Good. You ask, I answer; I ask, you answer. Whoever cannot answer loses. You ask first.” Zhou had wanted the first question, just as a player seeks the initiative at go. The offer suited him perfectly. He clasped his hands. “You are too kind!” “No need for courtesy. Come on!” Huang was a tall, imposing fellow. Standing on the eastern side of the table, he faced the declining western sun, which lit up every pockmark. With his arms folded and chin raised, he looked as though he scorned the whole world.

“请问，现在有一种新式缫丝的机器，你晓得不晓得？”“晓得。”黄八麻子看都不看地回答。“这种机器，一部好当一百部纺车用，你晓得不晓得？”“晓得。”“既然一部机器，好当一百部纺车用，那么，算他每家有五部纺车，二五得十，加十倍变一百，就有二十家人家的纺车没用处了，这一点你晓得不晓得？”“晓得。”“二十家的纺车没有用处，就是二十家人家没饭吃。这一点，你当然也晓得。”周少棠加了一句：“是不是？黄八麻子请你说。”“这有啥好说的？”黄八麻子手指着周少棠说：“这件事同阜康要上排门，有啥关系？你把脑筋放清楚来，不要乱扯。”“你说我乱扯就乱扯，扯到后来，你才晓得来龙去脉，原来在此！那时候已经晚了，一桌酒席输掉了。”“哼哼！”黄八麻子冷说，“倒要看看是我输酒席，还是你朝大家磕头。”

“Tell me, do you know about the new silk-reeling machines?” “I do,” Huang answered without even looking at him. “Do you know that one machine can do the work of a hundred spinning wheels?” “I do.” “Then suppose each household has five spinning wheels. Twice five makes ten; multiply by ten and you have a hundred. That means twenty households’ wheels become useless. Do you understand that?” “I do.” “Twenty households with useless wheels means twenty households with nothing to eat. You understand that too, of course.” Zhou added, “Do you not? Please answer, Huang Bamazi.” “What is there to answer?” Huang pointed at him. “What has any of this to do with Fukang putting up its shutters? Keep your head clear and stop wandering off the subject.” “Call it wandering if you like. Once I reach the end, you will understand how it all connects. But by then it will be too late: you will have lost your banquet.” “Hmph!” Huang sneered. “We shall see whether I lose a banquet or you kowtow to everyone.”

“好！言归正传。”周少棠问：“虽然是机器，也要有茧子才做得出丝，是不是？”“这还用你说！”“那么，没有茧子，他的机器就没有用了，这也是用不着说的。现在，我再要问你一件事，他们的机器是哪里来的？”“当然是外洋来的。”“是哪个从外洋运来的？”“我不晓得，只有请教你‘万宝全书缺只角’的周少棠了。”“这一点，倒不在我‘缺’的那只‘角’里面，我告诉你，怡和洋行，大班是英国人。”周少棠这时变了方式，面朝大众演说：“英国人的机器好，就是嘴巴大，一部机器要吃掉我们中国人二十家做给人家的饭。大家倒想，有啥办法对付？只有一个办法，根本叫他的机器饿肚皮。怎么饿法，不卖茧子给他。”这时台底下有些骚动了，“嗡嗡”的声音出现在好几处地方，显然是被周少棠点醒了，有些摸到胡雪岩的苦衷了。

“Very well! Back to the point,” Zhou said. “Even a machine needs cocoons before it can make silk. Correct?” “That goes without saying!” “Then it is equally obvious that, without cocoons, the machine is useless. Now another question: where do these machines come from?” “Abroad, naturally.” “Who brought them here?” “I do not know. I must ask you, Zhou Shaotang, the encyclopaedia with one corner missing.” “That happens not to be in my missing corner. I shall tell you: Jardine Matheson. Its chief is British.” Zhou now changed his method and addressed the crowd. “The British machines are good, but they have huge mouths. One machine swallows the rice that feeds twenty Chinese households. Think about it: what can we do? There is only one answer. Starve their machines from the outset. How? Sell them no cocoons!” A stir ran through the audience. Buzzing conversations broke out in several places. Evidently, Zhou had opened their eyes, and some were beginning to understand Hu’s difficulties.

这样的情况不能继续下去，否则凝聚起来的注意力一分散，他的话就说不下去了，因此找到一个熟人，指名发问。“喂，小阿毛，你是做机坊的，你娘是‘湖丝阿奶’，你倒说说看！”在家络丝，论件计酬，贴补家用的妇女，杭州人称之为“湖丝阿奶”，小阿毛父子都是织造衙门的织工，一家人的生计都与丝有关，对于新式缫丝厂的情况相当清楚，当即答说：“我娘先没有‘生活’做，现在又有了。”“是啥辰光没有‘生活’做？”“上海洋机厂一开工，就没有了。”“现在为啥又有了呢？”“因为洋机厂停工。”“洋机厂为啥停工？”“我不晓得。”“你晓不晓得？”周少棠转脸问黄八麻子，但不等他回答，自己说了出来，“是因为不卖茧子给它。”然后又问：“养蚕人家不卖茧子，吃什么？茧子一定要卖，不卖给洋鬼子，总要有人来买？你说，这是哪一个？“黄八麻子知道而不肯说，一说就要输，所以硬着头皮答道：“哪个晓得？”“你不晓得我告诉你！喏！”周少棠半转回身子，指着“阜康钱庄”闪闪生光的金字招牌说：“就是这里的胡大先生，”

He could not let that continue. Once the attention he had gathered dispersed, he would be unable to go on. Spotting an acquaintance, he called on him by name. “Xiao A’mao! You work at the looms, and your mother is a ‘husi granny.’ Tell us what you know!” In Hangzhou, women who wound silk at home, paid by the piece to supplement the household income, were called husi grannies. Xiao A’mao and his father were both weavers employed by the Imperial Weaving Office. The whole family depended on silk and knew a good deal about the new reeling factories. He answered at once, “My mother had no work before. Now she has some again.” “When did she lose her work?” “When the foreign machine factory in Shanghai began operating.” “Why has she work again now?” “Because the foreign factory has stopped.” “Why did it stop?” “I do not know.” “Do you know?” Zhou turned to Huang, but answered his own question before Huang could reply. “Because nobody will sell it cocoons. But if the silkworm rearers do not sell their cocoons, how are they to eat? The cocoons must be sold. If not to the foreign devils, someone else has to buy them. Who is it?” Huang knew, but would not say: to answer would be to lose. He brazened it out. “Who knows?” “If you do not, I shall tell you!” Zhou half-turned and pointed at the shining gold characters of Fukang’s sign. “Mr Hu, of this very bank!”

“周少棠，你又要捧‘财神’的卵泡了！”黄八麻子展开反击，“胡大先生囤的是丝，茧子没有多少，事情没有弄清楚，牛皮吹得哗打打，这里又没有人买你的梨膏糖。”“我的梨膏糖消痰化气。你倒想想看，那时节，只要你晚上出去赌铜钱到天亮不回来，你娘就要来买我的梨膏糖吃了。”这是周少棠无中生有，编出来的一套话，气得黄八麻子顿足敦指地骂：“姓周的，你真不要脸，乱说八道，哪个不晓得我姓黄的从来不赌铜钱的！”这时人丛中已有笑声了，周少棠却故意开玩笑说：“你晚上出去，一夜不回家，不是去赌铜钱，那就一定去逛‘私门头’。这一来，你老婆都要来买我的梨膏糖了。”台下哄然。黄八麻子咬牙切齿却无可奈何。周少棠仍是一副惫懒的神情，相形之下，越发惹笑。“你不要生气！”周少棠笑道：“大家笑一笑就是消痰化气。老弟兄寻寻开心，犯不着认真；等一息，我请你吃‘皇饭儿’。现在，”他正一正脸色：“我们话说回头。”

“Zhou, you are cradling the God of Wealth’s balls again!” Huang counterattacked. “Mr Hu is hoarding silk, not many cocoons. You have not got your facts straight, yet you boast away as though a drum were beating. Nobody here is buying your pear-syrup sweets!” “My sweets clear phlegm and soothe ill temper. Think back: whenever you went out gambling and stayed away till dawn, your mother used to come and buy some from me.” This was a complete invention. Furious, Huang stamped his feet and jabbed his finger at Zhou. “You shameless liar! Who does not know that I never gamble?” Laughter had already begun in the crowd, but Zhou deliberately pressed the joke. “If you stayed out all night and were not gambling, you must have been visiting a private brothel. Then your wife would need my sweets too.” The audience roared. Huang ground his teeth, helpless, while Zhou remained cheerfully shameless. The contrast made it funnier still. “Do not be angry!” Zhou laughed. “A good laugh clears everyone’s phlegm and temper. We are old acquaintances having a little fun. No need to take it seriously. I shall treat you at Huangfan’er shortly. Now,” he resumed a serious expression, “let us return to the matter in hand.”

接下来，周少棠又诉诸群众了，他将胡雪岩囤丝，说成是为了维护养蚕做丝人家的利益，与洋商斗法。他说，洋商本来打算设新式缫丝厂，低价收买茧子，产丝直接运销西洋，“中国人只有辛辛苦苦养蚕，等‘蚕宝宝上山，结成茧子，以后，所有的好处，都归洋鬼子独吞了！”他转脸问黄八麻子：“你们说，洋鬼子的心肠狠不狠？你有啥话好帮他们说？”这句话惹火了他的对手，“周少棠，你不要含血喷人，我哪里帮洋鬼子说过好话？只有你，捧‘财神’的卵泡！”黄八麻子指着他说：“你有本事，说出阜康收了人家的存款，可以赖掉不付的道理来，我佩服你。”“黄八麻子，你又乱开黄腔了！你睁开眼睛看看红告示，我们杭州府的父母官说点啥，藩台大人又说点啥？胡大先生手里有五万包丝，一包四百两，一共两千万，你听清楚，两千万两银了，五十两一个的大元宝，要四十万个，为啥要赖客户的存款。“

Zhou appealed to the crowd again. He presented Hu’s hoarding of silk as a struggle against the foreign merchants to protect the interests of those who reared silkworms and produced silk. The foreigners, he said, had intended to set up modern reeling factories, buy cocoons cheaply and ship the silk straight to the West. “The Chinese would do all the hard work of raising the silkworms. Once the little creatures climbed onto their frames and spun their cocoons, every bit of profit would be swallowed by the foreign devils!” Turning to Huang, he asked, “Are they not ruthless? What can you possibly say in their defence?” This enraged his opponent. “Do not slander me, Zhou! When have I ever spoken up for foreign devils? You are the one cradling the God of Wealth’s balls!” He pointed at Zhou. “If you can explain why Fukang is entitled to take people’s deposits and then refuse to pay them back, I shall admire you.” “There you go with your ‘yellow talk’ again! Open your eyes and read the red proclamation. What does our parent-official, the Prefect of Hangzhou, say? What does His Excellency the Treasurer say? Mr Hu holds fifty thousand bales of silk. At four hundred taels a bale, that is twenty million. Listen carefully: twenty million taels! In fifty-tael ingots, that would be four hundred thousand ingots. Why would he refuse to repay his depositors?”

“不赖，那么照付啊！”黄八麻子从怀中取出一叠银票在空中扬一扬说：“你们看，阜康的银票，马上要‘擦屁股，嫌罪过’了。”他这一着，变成无理取闹，有些泼妇的行径了。周少棠不慌不忙地将手一伸：“你的银票借我看看！你放心，当了这么多人，我不会骗你、抢你的。”这一下，黄八麻子知道要落下风了，想了一下硬着头皮将银票交了过去，“一共五张，两千六百多两银子，看你付不付，”他心里在想，周少棠绷在情面上，一定会如数照付，虽然嘴上吃了亏，但得了实惠，还是划算的。“周少棠不理他的话，接过银票来计算了一下，朝后面喊道：“兑一千四百四十两银子出来！听到没有？”谢云青精神抖擞地高声答应：“听到。”“对不起！现在兑不兑不是阜康的事情了，藩台同杭州府两位大人在阜康坐镇，出告示一千两以下照付，一千两以上等旱康老板回来，自会理清楚，大人先生的话，我们只有照听不误。”他捡出一张银票递了回去，“这张一千二百两的，请你暂时收回，等胡大先生回来再兑，其余四张，一共一千四百四十两，赌，来了！”

“If he is not refusing, let him pay!” Huang pulled a wad of banknotes from inside his clothes and waved them in the air. “Look! Fukang notes! Soon they will hardly be fit to wipe your arse with.” He was now becoming unreasonable, behaving almost like a quarrelsome shrew. Zhou calmly held out his hand. “Let me see your notes. Do not worry. In front of all these people, I shall neither cheat you nor rob you.” Huang knew he was losing ground. After a moment’s thought, he steeled himself and handed them over. “Five notes, over two thousand six hundred taels altogether. Let us see whether you will pay.” He thought Zhou, caught by the need to save face, would surely have them paid in full. He might lose the verbal contest, but the practical gain would make it worthwhile. Ignoring this challenge, Zhou counted the notes and called over his shoulder, “Bring out one thousand four hundred and forty taels! Did you hear?” “I heard!” Xie replied loudly, full of vigour. “I am sorry,” Zhou told Huang. “Whether these notes can be redeemed is no longer Fukang’s decision. The Treasurer and the prefect are here in person. Their proclamation says that notes for a thousand taels or less will be paid; anything above that must wait for Fukang’s owner to return and settle matters. We can only obey Their Honours.” He selected one note and handed it back. “Please keep this one for twelve hundred taels until Mr Hu returns. The other four come to one thousand four hundred and forty. Look! Here it is!”

阜康的伙计抬上来一个箩筐，将银子堆了起来，二十八个人元宝，堆成三列，另外四个十两头的元丝。都是刚出炉的“足纹”，白光闪闪，耀眼生花。“先生，”谢云青在方桌后面，探身出来，很客气他说：“请你点点数。”“数是不要点了，一目了然。不过，”黄八麻子大感为难，“我怎么拿呢？”“照规矩，应该送到府上。不过，今天兑银票的人多，实在抽不出人。真正对不住，真正对不住！“说着，谢云青连连拱手。“好了，好了！”人丛中有人大喊：“兑了银子的好走了，前客让后客！大家都有分。“这一催促提醒了好些原有急用、要提现银的人。热闹看够了，希望阜康赶紧卸排门开始兑银，所以亦都不耐烦地鼓噪，黄八麻子无可奈何，愤愤地向周少棠说：“算你这张卖梨膏糖的嘴厉害！银子我也不兑了，银票还我！”“对不起，对不起！”谢云青赔笑说道：“等明天稍为闲一闲，要用多少现银，我派‘出店，送到府上。暗，这里是原票，请收好了。”

Fukang’s employees carried out a wicker basket and piled up the silver: twenty-eight large ingots in three rows, with four smaller ingots of ten taels each. All were freshly cast silver of full standard purity, dazzlingly white. Leaning out from behind the square table, Xie said very politely, “Sir, please check the amount.” “There is no need. It is plain at a glance. But…” Huang was in difficulty. “How am I to carry it?” “Normally, we ought to deliver it to your house. Today, however, so many people are redeeming notes that we really cannot spare anyone. We are most sorry, most sorry!” Xie repeatedly clasped his hands in apology. Someone in the crowd shouted, “That is enough! If you have your silver, move along! Let the next customer come forward. There is enough for everyone!” This reminded others that they needed ready money for urgent purposes. They had seen enough entertainment and wanted Fukang to take down the shutters and begin paying out. Their impatient clamour grew. With no alternative, Huang said angrily to Zhou, “I admit that sweet-seller’s tongue of yours is formidable! I shall not take the silver. Give me back my notes!” “We are very sorry,” Xie said with an apologetic smile. “When things are a little quieter tomorrow, I shall send our outside clerk to your house with whatever silver you need. Here are your original notes. Please put them away safely.”

“八哥，八哥！”周少棠跳下桌，来扶黄八麻子，“多亏你捧场。等下‘皇饭儿’你一定要赏我个面子。”周少棠耍了一套把戏。黄八麻子展示了一个实例，即便是提一千两银子，亦须有所准备，一千两银子五十五斤多，要个麻袋，起码还要两个人来挑，银子分量重，一个人是提不动的。这一来，极大部分的人都散去了，也没有人对只准提一千两这个限额，表示异议，但却有人要求保证以后如数照兑，既不必立笔据，无非一句空话，谢云青乐得满口答应。不过要兑现银的小户，比平常是要多得多，谢云青认为应该做得大方些，当场宣布，延时营业，直到主顾散光为止，又去租来两盏煤气灯，预备破天荒地做个夜市。偌大一场风波，如此轻易应付过去，德馨非常满意。周少棠自然成了“英雄“，上上下下无不夸奖。不过大家也都知道，风潮只是暂时平息，”重头戏“在后面，只待”主角“胡雪岩一回来便要登场了。

“Brother Eight! Brother Eight!” Zhou jumped down and helped Huang off the table. “Thank you for helping the performance along. You must do me the honour of coming to Huangfan’er later.” Zhou had played a neat trick, and Huang had supplied a practical demonstration. Even withdrawing a thousand taels required preparation. A thousand taels of silver weighed more than fifty-five jin. One needed a sack and at least two men to carry it; the weight was too much for one man to lift. Most of the crowd now dispersed. Nobody objected to the thousand-tael limit, though some wanted an assurance that they would eventually be paid in full. Since no written undertaking was required, it amounted to no more than words, and Xie readily promised everything. There were nevertheless far more small customers seeking silver than usual. Feeling that the bank should act generously, he announced on the spot that business would continue until the last customer had left. He also rented two gas lamps, preparing to open at night for the first time. Dexin was thoroughly satisfied that so great a disturbance had been handled with such ease. Zhou naturally became the “hero,” praised by everyone from top to bottom. Yet all knew that the crisis had only been quietened for the moment. The main act was still to come, waiting for its leading player, Hu Xueyan, to return and take the stage.

第四章 夜访藩司｜CHAPTER FOUR: A NIGHT VISIT TO THE PROVINCIAL TREASURER

胡雪岩船到望仙桥，恰正是周少棠舌战黄八麻子，在大开玩笑的时候，螺蛳太太午前便派了亲信，沿运河往北迎了上去，在一处关卡上静候胡雪岩船到，遇船报告消息。这个亲信便是乌先生。他在胡家的身分很特殊，即非“师爷”，更非“管事”，但受胡雪岸或螺蛳太太的委托，常有临时的差使。这个人当螺蛳太太与胡雪岩之间的“密使”，自然是最适当的人选。“大先生，”，他说：“起暴风了。”不说起风波，却说“起暴风”，胡雪岩的心一沉，但表面不露声色，只说：“你特为赶了来，当然出事了。什么事？慢慢说。”“你在路上，莫非没有听到上海的消息？”等乌先生将由谢云青转到螺蛳太太手里的电报，拿了出来，胡雪岩一看色变，不过他矫情镇物的功夫过人，立即恢复常态，只问：“杭州城里都晓得了？”“当然。”“这样说，杭州，亦会挤兑？”“罗四姐特为要我来，就是谈这件事……”乌先生遂将谢云青深夜报信，决定卑康暂停营业，以及螺蛳太太亲访德馨求援，德馨已答应设法维持的经过，细说了一遍。

When Hu Xueyan’s boat reached Wangxian Bridge, Zhou Shaotang was in the midst of his verbal battle with Huang Bamazi, making jokes at his opponent’s expense. Before noon, Madam Luosi had sent a trusted man north along the canal to wait at a checkpoint and report the news as soon as Hu’s boat arrived. That man was Mr Wu. His position in the Hu household was unusual: he was neither a secretary nor a steward, but Hu or Madam Luosi often entrusted him with particular errands. No one could have been better suited to serve as their confidential messenger. “Sir,” he said, “a violent storm has broken.” He had said a violent storm, not merely a disturbance. Hu’s heart sank, but his face betrayed nothing. “Since you have come all this way, something must have happened. Tell me what it is. Take your time.” “Have you heard nothing of the news from Shanghai on your journey?” Mr Wu produced the telegram that Xie Yunqing had passed to Madam Luosi. Hu changed colour as he read it, but his ability to command his expression and steady others was exceptional. He recovered at once and asked only, “Does everyone in Hangzhou know?” “Of course.” “Then there will be a run here too?” “That is exactly why Sister Luo sent me…” Mr Wu gave a full account of Xie’s visit late at night, the decision to suspend business at Fukang, Madam Luosi’s personal appeal to Dexin, and the treasurer’s promise to do what he could to keep matters under control.

胡雪岩静静听完，第一句话便问：“老太太晓得不晓得？”“当然是瞒牢的。”“好！”胡雪岩放心了，“事情已经出来了，着急也没有用。顶要紧的是，自己不要乱。乌先生，喜事照常办，不过，我恐怕没有工夫来多管，请你多帮一帮罗四姐。”“我晓得。”乌先生突然想起：“罗四姐说，大先生最好不要在望仙桥上岸。”胡雪岩上船下船，一向在介乎元宝街与清河坊之间的望仙桥，螺蛳太太怕惹人注目，所以有此劝告。但胡雪岩的想法不同。“既然一切照常，我当然还是在望仙桥上岸。”胡雪岩又问：“罗四姐原来要我在啥地方上岸？”“万安桥。轿子等在那里。”乌先生答说：“这样子，我在万安桥上岸，关照轿子仍旧到望仙桥去接。”

Hu listened quietly to the end. His first question was, “Does the old lady know?” “Naturally, it has been kept from her.” “Good!” Hu felt relieved. “What has happened has happened. Worrying is no use. Above all, we must not lose our heads. Mr Wu, the wedding is to go ahead as usual, but I am afraid I shall have little time to attend to it. Please give Sister Luo all the help you can.” “I understand.” Mr Wu suddenly remembered something. “Sister Luo says it would be better if you did not go ashore at Wangxian Bridge.” Hu invariably boarded or left his boat there, between Yuanbao Street and Qinghefang. Madam Luosi had made the suggestion because she feared attracting attention, but he thought differently. “If everything is to proceed as usual, I must go ashore at Wangxian Bridge as usual. Where did she intend me to land?” “At Wan’an Bridge. Your sedan chair is waiting there,” Mr Wu replied. “In that case, I shall get off there and tell the bearers to go on to Wangxian Bridge to meet you.”

胡雪岩的一乘绿呢大轿，华丽是出了名的，抬到望仙桥，虽然已经暮色四合，但一停下来，自有人注目。加以乌先生了解胡雪岩的用意，关照来接轿的家人，照旧摆出排场，身穿簇新棉“号褂子”的护勇，码头上一站，点起官衔灯笼，顿时吸引了一大批看热闹的行人。见此光景，胡雪岩改了主意。往时一回杭州，都是先回家看娘，这一次怕老娘万一得知沪杭两处钱庄挤兑，急出病来，更加不放心。但看到这么多人在注视他的行踪，心里不免设身处地想一想，如果自己是阜康的客户，又会作何想法？只要一抛开自己，胡雪岩第一个念头便是：不能先回家！多少人的血汗钱托付给卓康，如今有不保之势，而阜康的老板居然好整以暇地光顾自己家里，不顾别人死活，这口气是咽不下的。因此船一靠岸，他先就询问：“云青来了没有？”谢云青何能不来？不过他是故意躲在暗处，此时闪出来疾趋上前，口中叫一声：“大先生！”“好，好！云青，你来了！不要紧，不要紧，阜康仍旧是金字招牌。”他特意提高了声音说，“我先到店里。”

Hu’s large green-cloth sedan chair was famous for its splendour. Though dusk had fallen by the time it reached Wangxian Bridge, its arrival inevitably drew attention. Understanding Hu’s purpose, Mr Wu told the household men to make their usual display. Guards in brand-new padded livery took their places on the landing and lit the lanterns bearing his official titles. A large crowd of passers-by soon gathered to watch. At this sight, Hu changed his mind. Whenever he returned to Hangzhou, he normally went home first to see his mother. Now he was all the more anxious to do so, fearing that news of the runs on the Shanghai and Hangzhou banks might have reached her and made her ill. But with so many people watching his movements, he could not help putting himself in their place. What would he think if he were a Fukang customer? The moment he set himself aside, his first thought was that he must not go home first. So many people had entrusted their hard-earned money to Fukang. Now it was in danger, yet the owner was calmly attending to his own household, regardless of what happened to anyone else. Who could swallow that? As soon as the boat touched the bank, he asked, “Has Yunqing come?” How could Xie have stayed away? He had deliberately kept in the shadows, but now stepped out and hurried forward. “Sir!” “Good, good! You are here, Yunqing. Nothing to worry about! Fukang still has its golden reputation.” Raising his voice deliberately, Hu added, “I shall go to the bank first.”

店里便是阜康。轿子一到，正好店里开饭，胡雪岩特为去看一看饭桌，这种情形平时亦曾有过，但在这种时候，他竟有这种闲情逸致，就不能不令人惊异了。“天气冷了！”胡雪岩问谢云青说：“该用火锅了。”“年常旧规，要冬至才用火锅。”谢云青说：“今年冬至迟。”“以后规矩改一改。照外国人的办法，冬天到寒暑表多少度，吃火锅，夏天，则多少度吃西瓜。云青，你记牢。”这是稳定“军心”的办法，表示阜康倒不下来，还会一年一年开下去。谢云青当然懂得这个奥妙，一叠连声地答应着，交代“饭司务”从第二天起多领一份预备火锅的菜钱。“阜康的饭碗敲不破的！”有人这样在说。

When his sedan chair reached Fukang, the staff were just sitting down to their meal. Hu made a point of inspecting the dinner table. He had done so before, but that he should have leisure for such things at a moment like this was astonishing. “The weather has turned cold,” he said to Xie. “You ought to be having hotpot.” “Our standing rule is to start at the winter solstice. It falls late this year.” “Change the rule from now on. Follow the foreigners’ practice: in winter, serve hotpot when the thermometer falls to a certain temperature; in summer, serve watermelon when it rises to a certain temperature. Remember that, Yunqing.” This was his way of steadying his troops. It told them that Fukang would not fall, but would carry on year after year. Xie understood perfectly. Agreeing at once, he told the cook to draw an extra allowance for hotpot ingredients from the following day. “No one is going to smash our rice bowls at Fukang!” someone said.

在听谢云青的细说经过时，胡雪岩一阵阵胃冷中，越觉得侥幸，越感到惭愧。事业不是他一人能创得起来的，所以出现今天这种局面，当然也不是他一个人的过失，但胡雪岩虽一想起宓本常，就恨不得一口唾沫当面吐在他脸上，但是，这种念头一起即消，他告诉自己，不必怨任何人，连自己都不必怨，最好忘记掉自己是阜康的东家，当自己是胡雪岩的“总管”，颇雪岩已经“不能问事”，委托他全权来处理这一场灾难。他只有尽力将得失之心丢开，心思才能比较集中，当时紧皱双眉，闭上眼睛，通前彻后细想了以后说：“面子就是招牌，面子保得住，招牌就可以不倒，这是一句总诀。云青，你记牢！”“是，我懂。”

As Xie described what had happened, chills ran through Hu. He felt increasingly fortunate, and increasingly ashamed. He had not built the business single-handed, and its present predicament could not be his fault alone. Whenever he thought of Mi Benchang, he wanted to spit in the man’s face. Yet the thought vanished almost as soon as it arose. He told himself not to blame anyone, not even himself. Best of all would be to forget that he owned Fukang and imagine himself as Hu Xueyan’s chief steward, entrusted with full authority to handle this disaster because Hu himself could no longer attend to his affairs. Only by setting his personal hopes and fears aside could he concentrate. He closed his eyes, his brows tightly knitted, and thought the matter through from beginning to end. Then he said, “Our standing is our reputation. Preserve that standing, and the name need not fall. That is the key to it all. Remember it, Yunqing.” “Yes. I understand.”

“你跟螺蛳太太商量定规，今天早晨不开门，这一点对不对，我们不必再谈。不过，你要晓得，拆烂污的事情做不得。”“我不是想拆烂污……”“我晓得。”胡雪岩摇摇手阻止他说：“你不必分辩，因为我不是说你。不过，你同螺蛳太太有个想法大错特错，你刚才同我说，万一撑不住，手里还有几十万款子，做将来翻身的本钱。不对，抱了这种想法，就输定了，永远翻不得身。云青，你要晓得，我好象推牌九，一直推得是‘长庄’，注码不管多少都要，你输得起，我赢得进，现在手风不顺，忽然说是改推‘铲庄’，尽多少铜钱赌，自己留起多少，当下次的赌本，云青，没有下次了，赌场里从此进不去了！“谢云青吸了口冷气，然后紧闭着嘴，无从赞一词。

“You and Madam Luosi decided not to open this morning. There is no need to discuss now whether that was right or wrong. But you must understand: we cannot simply shirk our responsibilities and leave a mess behind.” “I did not mean to—” “I know.” Hu raised a hand to stop him. “You need not defend yourself. I am not accusing you. But you and Madam Luosi have one idea that is utterly mistaken. You told me just now that, if we could not hold out, we would at least have several hundred thousand taels left as capital for a fresh start. Wrong! Think that way, and we are certain to lose. We shall never recover. Yunqing, imagine me keeping the bank at pai gow. I have always played with an unlimited bank: whatever the stake, I take it. If you can afford to lose it, I can accept the winnings. Now my luck turns against me, and I suddenly announce that I am limiting the bank: I shall risk only so much and keep the rest for another game. Yunqing, there will be no other game! I shall never be allowed into the gambling house again.” Xie drew a sharp breath, then pressed his lips together. He could not add a word.

“我是一双空手起来的，到头来仍旧一双空手，不输啥！不但不输，吃过、用过、阔过，都是赚头。只要我不死，你看我照样一双空手再翻起来。”“大先生这样气概，从古到今也没有几个人有。不过，”谢云青迟疑了一下，终于说了出来：“做生意到底不是推牌九。”“做生意虽不是推牌九，道理是一样的，‘赌奸赌诈不赌赖’。不卸排门做生意，不讲信用就是赖！”“大先生这么说，明天照常。”“当然照常！”胡雪岩说：“你今天要做一件事，拿存户的帐，好好看一看，有几个户头要连夜去打招呼。”“好。我马上动手。”“对。不过招呼有个打法，第一，一向初五结息，现在提早先把利息结出来，送银票上门。”“是。”“第二，你要告诉人家年关到了，或者要提款，要多少，请人家交代下来好预备。”“嗯、嗯、嗯。”谢云青心领神会地答应着。

“I began with empty hands. If I end with empty hands, what have I lost? Nothing! Everything I have eaten, enjoyed and spent in grand style has been a gain. So long as I live, you will see me rise again with nothing.” “Few men in any age have had your spirit, sir. But…” Xie hesitated, then finally said it. “Business is not quite the same as keeping the bank at pai gow.” “It may not be, but the principle is the same: you may gamble with cunning and deception, but never welsh on a bet. Keeping the shutters up and refusing to honour your word is welshing!” “Then, as you say, we open as usual tomorrow.” “Of course! There is one thing you must do tonight. Go carefully through the depositors’ accounts. There are several customers we must approach before the night is out.” “Very well. I shall begin at once.” “Good. But there is a way of approaching them. First, interest is normally settled on the fifth. Settle it early this time and send notes for the amount to their homes.” “Yes.” “Second, tell them the year’s end is approaching. Perhaps they will need to withdraw money. Ask them to let us know how much, so that we can have it ready.” Xie nodded repeatedly, understanding exactly what Hu meant.

能将大户稳定下来，零星散户，力能应付，无足为忧。胡雪岩交代清楚了，方始转回元宝街，虽已入夜，一条街上依旧停满了轿马，门灯高悬，家人排班，雁行而立，仿佛一切如常，但平时那种喧哗热闹的气氛，却突然消失了。轿子直接抬到花园门口，下轿一看，胡太太与螺蛳太太在那里迎接，相见黯然，但只转瞬之间，螺蛳太太便浮起了笑容，“想来还没有吃饭？”她问：“饭开在哪里？”这是没话找话，胡雪岩根本没有听进去，只说：“到你楼上谈。”他又问：“老太太晓得不晓得，我回来了。”“还没有禀告她老人家。”“好！关照中门上，先不要说。”“我晓得。不会的。”胡家的中门，仿佛大内的乾清门一般，禁制特严，真个外言不入，螺蛳太太早已关照过了，大可放心。到得螺蛳太太那里，阿云捧来一碗燕窝汤，一笼现蒸的鸡蛋糕，另外是现沏的龙井茶，预备齐全，随即下楼，这是螺蛳太太早就关照好了的。阿云武守在楼梯口，不准任何人上楼。

If the large depositors could be kept steady, the scattered small withdrawals were within their means and gave no cause for fear. Only after giving these instructions did Hu return to Yuanbao Street. Night had fallen, but the street was still packed with sedan chairs and horses. Lanterns hung high at the doors, and household attendants stood in orderly ranks. Everything seemed as usual, except that the customary bustle and cheerful noise had suddenly disappeared. His chair was carried straight to the garden entrance. When he alighted, the First Madam and Madam Luosi were waiting for him. Their meeting was sombre, but within a moment Madam Luosi produced a smile. “I suppose you have not eaten? Where shall dinner be served?” She was merely finding something to say. Hu scarcely heard her. “Let us talk upstairs in your rooms. Does the old lady know I am back?” “She has not been told yet.” “Good. Tell the people at the inner gate not to say anything for the moment.” “I know. They will not.” The household’s inner gate was guarded by restrictions as strict as those at the Gate of Heavenly Purity in the imperial palace: no word from outside was allowed through. Madam Luosi had already given her orders, and he could be easy on that score. Upstairs, A’yun brought a bowl of bird’s-nest soup, a steamer of freshly made egg cakes and newly brewed Longjing tea. Once everything was ready, she went downstairs, as Madam Luosi had instructed beforehand, and stood guard at the foot of the stairs to keep everyone else away.

“事情要紧不要紧？”胡太太首先开口。“说要紧就要紧，说不要紧就不要紧。”胡雪岩说： “如今是顶石臼做戏，能把戏做完，大不了落个吃力不讨好，没有啥要紧，这出做不下去，石臼砸下来，非死即伤。”“那么这出戏要怎样做呢？”螺蛳太太问说。“要做得台底下看不出我们头上顶了一个石臼，那就不要紧了。”“我也是这样关照大家，一切照常，喜事该怎么办，还是该怎么办。不过，场面可以拿铜钱摆出来的，只怕笑脸摆不出来。”“难就难在这里。不过，”胡雪岩加重了语气说：“再难也要做到，场面无论如何要好好儿把它绷起来，不管你们用啥法子。胡太太与螺蛳太太相互看了一眼，都将这两句话好好地想了一下，各有会心，不断点头。“外头的事情有我。”胡雪岩问说：“德晓峰怎么样？”“总算不错。”螺蛳太太说：“莲珠一下午都在我这里，她说：你最好今天晚上就去看看德藩台。”“晚上，恐怕不方便。”“晚上才好细谈。”“好，我等一下就去。”

“Is it serious?” the First Madam asked first. “You could call it serious, or you could call it nothing,” Hu replied. “We are performing a play with a stone mortar balanced on our heads. If we can finish it, the worst that happens is that we work hard and get no thanks. That is nothing. But if we cannot carry the performance through, the mortar falls, and we are killed or injured.” “Then how are we to perform it?” Madam Luosi asked. “So that the audience never sees the mortar on our heads. Then we shall be all right.” “That is what I told everyone too. Everything as usual: the wedding is to be conducted exactly as it should be. But money can provide the grand display. It may not provide the smiling faces.” “That is precisely the difficulty. Still”—Hu spoke with added force—“however difficult it is, it must be done. Whatever means you use, you must keep up the display.” The two women looked at each other. Both considered his words carefully, understood them in their own ways and nodded. “Leave the outside affairs to me. How has De Xiaofeng behaved?” “Well enough,” Madam Luosi said. “Lianzhu spent the whole afternoon here. She says you would do best to see Treasurer De tonight.” “Would it not be inconvenient at night?” “Night is the best time for a proper conversation.” “Very well. I shall go shortly.”

胡雪岩有些踌躇，因为这时候最要紧的事，并不是去看德馨，第一件是要发电报到各处，第二件是要召集几个重要的助手，商量应变之计。这两件事非但耽误不得，而且颇费功夫，实在抽不出空去看德馨。“有应春在这里就好了。”胡雪岩叹口气，颓然倒在一张安乐椅，头软软地垂了下来。螺蛳太太大吃一惊，“老爷！老爷！”她走上前去，半跪着摇撼着他双肩说：“你要撑起来！不管怎么样要撑牢！”“胡雪岩没有作声，一把抱住她，将头埋在她肩项之间，”罗四姐，“他说，“怕要害你受苦了，你肯不肯同我共患难？“怎么不肯？我同你共过富贵，当然要同你共患难。”说着，螺蛳太太眼泪掉了下来，落在胡雪岩手背上。“你不要哭！你刚才劝我，现在我也要劝你。外面我撑，里面你撑。”“好！”螺蛳太太抹抹眼泪，很快地答应。“你比我难。”胡雪岩说：“第一，老太太那里要瞒住，第二，亲亲眷眷，还有底下人，都要照应到，第三，这桩喜事仍旧要办得风风光光。”螺蛳太太心想第一桩还好办，到底只有一个人，第二桩就很吃力了，第三桩更难，不管怎么风光，贺客要谈煞风景的事，莫非去掩住他们的嘴？正这样转着念头，胡雪岩又开口了，“罗四姐，”他说：“你答应得落答应不落？如果答应不落，我……”

Hu hesitated. Calling on Dexin was not the most urgent business before him. First he had to send telegrams to various places; then he must bring his principal assistants together to discuss how to meet the emergency. Neither task could wait, and both would take time. He really could not spare any to visit Dexin. “If only Yingchun were here!” With a sigh, he sank dejectedly into an armchair, his head drooping. Madam Luosi was alarmed. “My dear! My dear!” She hurried over and half knelt before him, shaking his shoulders. “You must hold yourself together. Whatever happens, you must!” Without a word, he clasped her and buried his face between her neck and shoulder. “Sister Luo,” he said, “I am afraid I may bring suffering upon you. Will you share my troubles?” “How could I refuse? I have shared your prosperity. Of course I shall share your troubles.” Her tears fell onto the back of his hand. “Do not cry. You were encouraging me just now; now I must encourage you. I shall hold things together outside. You must do the same within.” “I will!” She wiped her eyes and answered at once. “Your task is harder than mine. First, you must keep the old lady from knowing. Second, you must look after the relatives and all the servants. Third, the wedding must be as splendid as ever.” The first task was manageable, she thought: after all, it concerned only one person. The second would be taxing, and the third harder still. However splendid the wedding, how could she stop the guests discussing things that would spoil it? Cover their mouths? While she was thinking, Hu spoke again. “Sister Luo, can you undertake it or not? If you cannot, I…”

等了一会不听他说下去，螺蛳太太不由得要问：“你怎么样？”“你撑不落，我就撑牢了，也没有意思。”“那么，怎么样呢？”“索性倒下来算了。”“瞎说八道！”螺蛳太太跳了起来，大声说道，“胡大先生，你不要让我看不起你！”胡雪岩原是激励她的意思，想不到同时也受了她的激励，顿时精神百倍地站起身来说：“好！我马上去看德晓峰。”“这才是。”螺蛳太太关照：“千万不要忘记谢谢莲珠。”“我晓得。”“还有，你每一趟外路回来去看德藩台，从来没有空手的，这回最好也不要破例。”

She waited, but he said no more. “You will do what?” she asked. “If you cannot hold things together, there is no point in my holding on.” “Then what?” “We may as well let everything collapse.” “Nonsense!” She sprang to her feet and cried, “Mr Hu, do not make me despise you!” He had meant to stir her courage. Unexpectedly, she had stirred his as well. Suddenly full of energy, he rose. “Very well! I shall go and see Mr Xiaofeng at once.” “That is more like it. Whatever you do, do not forget to thank Lianzhu.” “I know.” “And whenever you come home from a journey and call on Treasurer De, you never go empty-handed. It would be best not to make an exception this time.”

这下提醒胡雪岩，“我的行李在哪里？”他说：“其中有一只外国货的皮箱，里头新鲜花样很多。”“等我来问阿云。”原来胡雪岩每次远行，都是螺蛳太太为他收拾行李，同样地，胡雪岩一回来，行李箱亦照例卸在她这里，所以要问阿云。“有的。等我去提了来。”那只皮箱甚重，是两个丫头抬上来的，箱子上装了暗锁，要对准号码，才能打开。急切间，胡雪岩想不起什么号码，怎么转也转不开，又烦又急，弄得满头大汗。“等我来！”螺蛳太太顺手捡起一把大剪刀，朝锁具的缝隙中插了下去，然后交代阿云：“你用力往后扳。”阿云是大脚，近尺莲船抵住了皮箱，双手用足了劲往后一扳，锁是被撬开了，却以用力过度，仰开摔了一交。“对！”胡雪岩若有所悟地自语：“快刀斩乱麻！”一面说，一面将皮纸包着的大包小包取了出来，堆在桌上，皮箱下面铺平了的，是舶来品的衣料。

That reminded Hu. “Where is my luggage? There is a leather trunk of foreign goods, with all sorts of novelties in it.” “Let me ask A’yun.” Madam Luosi always packed for his journeys, and when he returned the luggage was invariably brought to her rooms, so A’yun was the person to ask. “Yes, it is here. I shall fetch it.” The trunk was heavy enough to require two maids to carry it upstairs. It had a combination lock that would open only when the numbers were correctly aligned. In his haste, Hu could not remember the combination. However he turned it, the lock would not open. Frustration and anxiety brought the sweat pouring from his forehead. “Let me!” Madam Luosi picked up a large pair of scissors and thrust a blade into a gap in the lock. “Pull it back hard, A’yun.” A’yun had unbound feet. Planting one, almost a chi long, against the trunk, she pulled back with both hands. The lock gave way, but she had used so much force that she fell backwards onto the floor. “Exactly!” Hu murmured, as though something had dawned on him. “Cut through the tangle with one stroke!” As he spoke, he took out parcels large and small, wrapped in tough paper, and piled them on the table. Imported cloth lay flat at the bottom of the trunk.

“这个是预备送德晓峰的。”胡雪岩将一个小纸包递给螺蛳太太，又加了一句：“小心打碎。”打开来一看，是个乾隆年间烧料的鼻烟壶，配上祖母绿的盖子。螺蛳太太这几年见识得多，知道名贵，“不过，”她说：“一样好象太少了。”“那就再配一只表。”这只表用极讲究的皮盒子盛着，打开来一看，上面是一张写着洋文的羊皮纸，揭开来，是个毫不起眼的银表。“这只表……”“这只表，你不要看不起它，来头很大，是法国皇帝拿破仑用过的，我是当古董买回来的。这张羊皮纸是‘保单’，只要还得出‘报门’不是拿破仑用过，包退还洋，另加罚金。”“好！送莲珠的呢？“只有一个金黄寇盒子。如果嫌轻，再加两件衣料。”

“This was intended for Mr Xiaofeng.” Hu handed Madam Luosi a small parcel and added, “Careful. It may break.” Inside was a glass snuff bottle made in the Qianlong reign, with an emerald stopper. She had seen enough fine things in recent years to recognize its value. “But one item seems rather little.” “Then add a watch.” The watch came in an exquisite leather case. When she opened it, she found a sheet of parchment covered in foreign writing. Beneath it lay a thoroughly unremarkable silver watch. “This watch…” “Do not look down on it. It has a very distinguished history. Napoleon, the Emperor of France, used it. I bought it as an antique. This parchment is the guarantee: anyone who can produce proof that Napoleon did not use it gets a refund, with a penalty payment besides.” “Very well. And for Lianzhu?” “There is only a gold box. If that seems too slight a gift, add two lengths of cloth.”

从箱子下面取出几块平铺着的衣料出来，螺蛳太太忽生感慨，从嫁到胡家，什么绫罗绸缎，在她跟毛蓝布等量齐观，但一摸到西洋的衣料，感觉大不相同。这种感觉形容不出。她见过的最好的衣料是“贡缎”，这种缎子又分“御用”与“上用”两种，“御用”的贡缎，后妃所用，亦用来赏赐王公大臣。皇帝所用，才专称为“上用”。但民间讲究的人，当然亦是世家巨族，用的亦是“上用”的缎子，只是颜色避免用“明黄”以及较“明黄”为暗的“香色”，“明黄”只皇帝、太上皇帝能用，“香色”则是皇子专用颜色，除此以外，百无禁忌，但争奇斗妍，可以比“上用”的缎子更讲究，譬如上午所着与晚间所着，看似同样花样的缎袍，而暗花已有区分，上午的花含苞待放，下午的花已盛开。这些讲究，已是“不是三世做官，不知道穿衣吃饭”的人家所矜重，但是，比起舶来品的好衣料来，不免令人兴起绚烂不如平淡之感。

As she lifted out several lengths laid flat beneath the other things, Madam Luosi was suddenly moved. Since marrying into the Hu household, she had come to regard every kind of silk and satin as no more remarkable than coarse blue cotton. Yet the touch of Western cloth gave her quite a different feeling, one she could not describe. The finest material she had known was tribute satin, divided into two categories: “imperial use” and “the sovereign’s use.” The former was used by the empress and imperial consorts, and was also bestowed on princes and high officials. Satin for the emperor himself was specifically designated “the sovereign’s use.” Discerning private households—naturally, the great families of generations’ standing—also used satin of this quality. They merely avoided bright yellow and the darker shade known as incense colour. Bright yellow was reserved for the emperor and a retired emperor; incense colour was for imperial princes. Apart from those colours, there were no restrictions. In their rivalry for novelty and beauty, private households could be more exacting even than the sovereign’s wardrobe. A satin robe worn in the morning might appear to have the same pattern as one worn in the evening, yet the subtly woven designs would differ: the morning flowers were buds about to open, while those for the afternoon were in full bloom. Such refinements were cherished in families of whom it could be said, “It takes three generations in office to learn how to dress and dine.” Yet compared with fine imported cloth, they prompted the thought that splendour could not equal simplicity.

螺蛳太太所拣出来的两件衣料，都是单色，一件藏青、一件玄色，这种衣料名叫“哔叽”，刚刚行销到中国，名贵异常，但她就有四套哔叽袄裤，穿过了才知道它的好处。这种在洋行发售，内地官宦人家少见，就是上海商场中，也只有讲时髦的阔客才用来作袍料的“哔叽”，在胡家无足为奇。胡雪岩爱纤足，姬妾在平时不着裙子，春秋佳日用“哔叽”裁制夹袄夹裤，稳重挺括，颜色素雅，自然高贵。她常说：“做人就要象哔叽一样，经得起折磨，到哪里都显得有分量。”此时此地此人，想到自己常说的话，不由得凄然泪下。幸好胡雪岩没有注意，她背着灯取手绢醒鼻子，顺便擦一擦眼睛，将拣齐了的礼物，关照阿雪用锦袱包了起来，然后亲自送胡雪岩到花园的西侧门。“

The two lengths she selected were plain colours, one navy blue and the other black. The fabric was called serge. It had only just begun to be sold in China and was exceptionally precious, yet she already had four suits of serge jackets and trousers. Only by wearing it had she discovered its virtues. Sold through the foreign trading houses, it was seldom seen among official families inland. Even in Shanghai’s commercial circles, only rich men with a taste for fashion had it made into robes. In the Hu household, however, it was nothing unusual. Hu loved slender feet, so his concubines did not ordinarily wear skirts. On fine spring and autumn days, they wore lined jackets and trousers made of serge: dignified and crisp, sober in colour, with a natural distinction. She often said, “One should be like serge: able to withstand wear and carry weight wherever one goes.” Remembering her own words at this moment, in these circumstances, she could not help weeping. Fortunately, Hu did not notice. Turning away from the light, she took out her handkerchief to blow her nose and wiped her eyes at the same time. She told A’xue to wrap the chosen gifts in a brocade cloth, then personally escorted Hu to the western side gate of the garden.

这道门平时关闭，只有胡雪岩入夜“微行”时才开，坐的当然也不是绿呢大轿，更没有前呼后拥的“亲兵”，只有两个贴身小跟班，前后各擎一盏灯笼，照着小轿直到藩司衙门。由于预先已有通知，德馨派了人在那里等候。胡雪岩下了轿，一直就到签押房。“深夜过来打搅晓翁，实在不安。胡雪岩话是这么说，态度还是跟平时一样，潇洒自如，毫不显得窘迫。“来！来！躺下来。”刚起身来迎的德馨，自己先躺了下去！接过丫头递过来的烟枪，一口气抽完，但却用手势指挥，如何招待客人。他指挥丫头，先替胡雪岩卸去马褂，等他侧身躺下来，丫头便将他的双腿抬到搁脚凳上，脱去双梁鞋，然后取一床俄国毯子盖在腿上，掖得严严的，温暖无比。“雪岩，”德馨说道：“我到今天才真佩服你！”没头没脑的这一句话，说得胡雪岩唯有苦笑，“晓翁，”他说：“你不要挖苦我了。”

This gate was normally kept shut and opened only when Hu went out privately at night. Naturally, he did not use the large green-cloth sedan chair, nor did a crowd of guards precede and follow him. Only two personal attendants accompanied the little chair, one before and one behind, each holding a lantern to light the way to the provincial treasurer’s office. Notice had already been sent, and Dexin had someone waiting. Hu alighted and went straight to the private office. “I am very sorry to disturb you so late, Mr Xiaofeng.” Despite his words, his manner was as easy and composed as ever, without a trace of embarrassment. “Come, come! Lie down.” Dexin had risen to greet him, but lay down again first. He took the opium pipe a maid handed him and smoked it in one breath, directing his guest’s reception by gestures. The maid first removed Hu’s riding jacket. When he lay on his side, she lifted his legs onto a footstool, took off his double-ridged shoes and covered his legs with a Russian blanket, tucking it closely around him. It was wonderfully warm. “Xueyan,” Dexin said, “only today have I truly come to admire you.” With no explanation for this sudden remark, Hu could only smile wryly. “Mr Xiaofeng, please do not mock me.”

“不是我挖苦你。”德馨说道：“从前听人说，孟尝君门下食客三千，鸡鸣狗盗，到了紧要关头，都会大显神通。你手下有个周少棠，你就踉孟尝君一样了。”周少棠大出风头这件事，他只听谢云青略为提到，不知其详，如今听德馨如此夸奖，不由得大感兴趣，便问一句：“何以见得？”好让德馨讲下去。“我当时在场，亲眼目睹，实在佩服。”德馨说道：“京里有个丑儿叫刘赶三，随机应变，临时抓限是有名的，可是以我看来，不及周少棠。”接着德馨眉飞色舞地将周少棠玩弄黄八麻子于股掌之上的情形，细细形容了一遍，胡雪岩默默地听着，心里在想，这周少棠以后有什么地方用得着他。“雪岩，”德馨又说：“周少棠给你帮的忙，实在不小。把挤兑的那班人哄得各自回家，犹在其次，要紧的是，把你帮了乡下养蚕人家的大忙，大大吹嘘了一番。这一点很有用，而且功效已显出来了，今儿下午刘仲帅约我去谈你的事，他就提到你为了跟英国人斗法，以至于被挤，说应该想法子维持。”刘仲帅是指浙江巡抚刘秉璋，他跟李鸿章虽非如何融洽，但总是淮军一系，能有此表示，自然值得珍视，所以胡雪岩不免有兴奋的语气。“刘仲帅亦能体谅，盛情实在可感。”

“I am not mocking you. I used to hear that Lord Mengchang kept three thousand retainers, and even those whose talents lay in crowing like cocks or thieving like dogs could work wonders in a crisis. With a Zhou Shaotang among your men, you are another Lord Mengchang.” Xie had briefly mentioned Zhou’s great performance, but Hu did not know the details. Such praise from Dexin naturally interested him. “How so?” he asked, inviting him to continue. “I was there and saw it myself. Truly admirable! There is a comic actor in Beijing called Liu Gansan, famous for his quick responses and improvised jokes, but in my judgement he is no match for Zhou.” With animated delight, Dexin described in detail how Zhou had made a plaything of Huang Bamazi. Hu listened silently, wondering where he might make use of Zhou in future. “Xueyan, the service he has done you is considerable. Talking the people demanding their money into going home was the lesser part of it. More important was his great account of how you helped the country people who raise silkworms. That is very useful, and it has already had an effect. Commander Liu asked me to discuss your affairs this afternoon. He mentioned that your struggle with the British had brought this pressure upon you, and said we ought to find a way to support you.” Commander Liu was Liu Bingzhang, the governor of Zhejiang. Although his relations with Li Hongzhang were not particularly close, he belonged to the Huai Army faction. Such words from him were therefore to be valued, and Hu’s voice betrayed some excitement. “Commander Liu understands my position too! His kindness is deeply appreciated.”

“你先别高兴，他还有话；能维持才维持，不能维持趁早处置，总以确保官款为第一要义。雪岩，”德馨在枕上转脸看着胡雪岩说：“你得给我一句话。”这句话自然是要胡雪岩提供保证，决不至于让他无法交代。胡雪岩想了一下说：“晓翁，我们相交不是一天，你看我是对不起人的人吗？”“这一层，你用不着表白。不过，雪岩，你的事业太大了，或许有些地方你自己都不甚了了。譬如，你如果对你自己的虚实，一清二楚的话，上海的阜康何至于等你一走，马上就撑不住了？”这番话说得胡雪岩哑口无言，以他的口才，可以辩解，但他不想那样做，因为他觉得那样就是不诚。“雪岩，你亦不必难过。事已如此，只有挺直腰杆来对付。”德馨紧接着说：“我此刻只要你一句话。”“请吩咐。”“你心里的想法，先要告诉我。不必多，只要一句话好了。”这话别具意味，胡雪岩揣摩了半天，方始敢于确定，“晓翁，”他说。“如果我真的撑不下去了，我一定先同晓翁讨主意。”这话的意思是一定会维护德馨的利益，不管是公、是私？“好！咱们一言为定。现在，雪岩，你说吧，我能替你帮什么忙？”

“Do not rejoice yet. He had more to say: support you if you can be supported; otherwise, make arrangements without delay. The first consideration must always be the safety of public funds.” Turning his face on the pillow towards Hu, Dexin added, “Xueyan, you must give me your word.” Clearly, he wanted a guarantee that Hu would not leave him unable to account for the money. Hu thought for a moment. “Mr Xiaofeng, we have known each other for years. Do you think I am a man who would let others down?” “You need not assure me of that. But your enterprises are so extensive that you may not fully understand every part of them yourself. If you knew your own position through and through, for instance, why did the Shanghai bank lose its footing the moment you left?” Hu had no answer. With his eloquence, he could have defended himself, but he did not wish to, because that would not have been honest. “There is no need to take it to heart. Things being as they are, you can only stand straight and face them. For the moment, I want just one word from you.” “Please tell me.” “You must let me know what you are thinking. Nothing more than one word is needed.” There was a particular meaning beneath this. Hu considered it for some time before he felt certain enough to reply. “If I really cannot hold on, I shall consult you first, Mr Xiaofeng.” What he meant was that he would protect Dexin’s interests, public and private alike. “Good! That is agreed. Now, Xueyan, tell me what I can do to help.”

“不止于帮忙，”胡雪岩说：“我现在要请晓翁拿我的事，当自己的事办。”这话分明一也很重，德馨想了一下说：“这不在话下。不过，自己的事，不能不知道吧？”“是，我跟晓翁说一句，只要不出意外，一定可以过关。”“雪岩，你的所谓意外是什么？”“凡是我抓不住的，都会出意外。”胡雪岩说：“第一个是李合肥。”说到这里，他不由得叹了一口报导，“唉！原以为左大人到了两江，是件好事，哪晓得反而坏了。”“喔。这一层，你倒不妨谈谈。”谈起来很复杂，也很简单，左宗棠一到两江，便与李鸿章在上海的势力发生冲突。如果左宗棠仍有当年一往无前笼罩各方的魄力，加上胡雪岩的精打细算，则两江总督管两江，名正言顺，李鸿章一定会落下风。无奈左宗棠老境颓唐，加以在两江素无基础，更糟糕的是对法交涉，态度软硬，大相径庭，而李鸿章为了贯彻他的政策，视左宗棠为遇事掣时、非拔除不可的眼中钉，而又以剪除左宗棠的党羽为主要手段，这一来便将胡雪岩看作保护左宗棠的盾牌，集矢其上了。

“I ask more than help,” Hu said. “I want you to treat my affairs as your own.” This too carried considerable weight. Dexin reflected. “That goes without saying. But one must know about one’s own affairs, must one not?” “Yes. Let me tell you this: provided nothing unforeseen happens, I can certainly get through.” “What do you mean by unforeseen?” “Anything beyond my control can produce a surprise. First of all, Li of Hefei.” He could not suppress a sigh. “I thought Lord Zuo’s coming to Liangjiang was a good thing. Who could have known it would turn out to be the opposite?” “Indeed? Tell me about that.” The explanation was at once complex and simple. As soon as Zuo came to Liangjiang, he clashed with Li Hongzhang’s power in Shanghai. Had Zuo retained the irresistible energy with which he once dominated every side, reinforced by Hu’s careful calculations, Li would certainly have had the worst of it. After all, the Governor-General of Liangjiang had every right to govern Liangjiang. But Zuo was declining with age and had no established base there. Worse still, their positions on negotiations with France—one hard, the other soft—were worlds apart. To carry out his own policy, Li regarded Zuo as an obstacle at every turn, a thorn that had to be removed. His principal method was to strip away Zuo’s supporters. Hu thus became the shield protecting Zuo, and all the arrows were directed at him.

“我明白了。”德馨说道：“冤家宜解不宜结，李合肥那方面要设法去打个照呼。这一层，我可以托刘仲帅。”“这就重就拜托了。”胡雪岩问：“刘仲帅那里，我是不是应该去见一见？”“等明天‘上院’见了他再说。”德馨又说：“你倒想一想，李合肥如果要跟你过不去，会用什么手段？”“别的我都不在乎，”胡雪岩说：“最怕他来提北洋属下各衙门的官款，提不到可以封我的典当，那一来就要逼倒我了。”“封典当，影响平民生计，果然如此，我可以说话。”“正要晓翁仗义执言。不过后说不如先后，尤其要早说。”“好！我明天就跟刘仲帅去谈。”“能不能请刘仲帅出面，打几个电报出去，就说阜康根基稳固，请各处勿为谣言所惑，官款暂且不提，免得逼倒了阜康。”“说当然可以说。不过，刘仲帅一定会问：是不是能保证将来各处的官款，分文不少？”德馨又加一句：“如果没有这一层保证，刘仲帅不肯发这样子的电报。”胡雪岩默然半晌，方始答说：“如果我有这样的把握，也就根本不必请刘仲帅发电报了。”

“I understand,” Dexin said. “Better to resolve enmity than create it. We must find some way to approach Li of Hefei. I can ask Commander Liu to do that.” “Then I entrust it to you most earnestly. Should I go and see Commander Liu myself?” “Let me see him at the official audience tomorrow first. Think, though: if Li of Hefei means to make trouble for you, what means will he use?” “Nothing else concerns me. What I fear most is that he will demand the public funds deposited by the offices under Beiyang. If I cannot repay them, he can seal up my pawnshops. That would force me under.” “Closing pawnshops affects ordinary people’s livelihoods. If it comes to that, I can speak out.” “That is precisely what I ask you to do. But it is better to speak beforehand than afterwards, and the sooner the better.” “Very well. I shall speak to Commander Liu tomorrow.” “Could he send out a few telegrams, saying that Fukang stands on firm foundations and asking the various offices not to be misled by rumours? They should refrain from withdrawing public funds for the moment, to avoid forcing Fukang into collapse.” “He can certainly be asked. But he will want to know whether you can guarantee that every office’s public money will ultimately be repaid in full. Without that guarantee, he will not send such telegrams.” Hu was silent for a long time before he answered. “If I could be that certain, there would be no need to ask him to send them in the first place.”

这下是德馨默然。一直等将烟瘾过足，方又开口：“雪岩，至少本省大小衙门存在阜康的官款，我有把握，在一个月之内不会提。”“只要一个月之内，官款不动，就不要紧了。”胡雪岩说：“我在天津的丝，可以找到户头，一脱手，头寸马上就松了。”“上海呢？”德馨问道：“你在上海不也有许多丝囤在那里吗？”“上海的不能动！洋人本来就在杀我的价钱，现在看我急需周转，更看得我的丝不值钱。晓翁，钱财身外之物，我不肯输这口气，尤其是输给洋人，更加不服。”“唉！”德馨叹口气，“大家都要象你这样子争气，中国就好了。”

Now it was Dexin’s turn to fall silent. He did not speak again until he had satisfied his craving for opium. “Xueyan, at least I can assure you that none of the public funds deposited with Fukang by the offices of this province, great or small, will be withdrawn for a month.” “If the public funds remain untouched for a month, we shall be all right,” Hu said. “I can find a buyer for my silk in Tianjin. Once it is sold, funds will immediately become easier.” “What about Shanghai? Have you not a great deal of silk stored there too?” “The Shanghai stock must not be touched! The foreigners were already beating down my price. Now that they see how urgently I need funds, they will value my silk even less. Mr Xiaofeng, money is only a worldly possession. I will not swallow this defeat—least of all at the foreigners’ hands.” Dexin sighed. “If everyone had your determination to stand their ground, China would be better off.”

正在谈着，闪出一个梳长辫子的丫头，带着老妈子来摆桌子，预备吃消夜。胡雪岩本想告辞，转念又想，应该不改常度：有几次夜间来访，到了时候总是吃消夜，这天也应该照常才是。“姨太太呢？”德馨问说，“说我请她。”“马上出来。”原来莲珠是不避胡雪岩的，这天原要出来周旋，一则慰问，再则道谢。

While they were talking, a maid with a long braid slipped in, followed by older women who set the table for a late supper. Hu Xueyan had been about to take his leave, but on reflection he decided that he ought to keep to his usual ways. On several previous evening visits he had stayed for supper when the time came; he ought to do the same tonight. “Where is your mistress?” Dexin asked. “Tell her I should like her to join us.” “She will be out directly.” Lianzhu did not observe the convention of avoiding Hu Xueyan. She had already intended to come out and entertain him that evening, both to express her concern and to thank him for his gifts.

及至胡雪岩刚刚落座，听得帘钩微响，扭头看时，莲珠出现在房门口，她穿的是件旗袍，不过自己改良过了，袖子并不太宽，腰身亦比较小，由于她身材颀长，而且生长北方，穿惯了旗装，所以在她手握一方绣花手帕，一摇三摆地走了来，一点都看不出她是汉人。“二太太！”胡雪岩赶紧站起来招呼。“请坐，请坐！”莲珠摆一摆手说：“胡大先生，多谢你送的东西，太破费了。”“小意思，小意思。”胡雪岩说：“初五那天，二太太你要早点来。”“胡大先生，你不用关照，我扰府上的喜酒，不止一顿，四姐请我去陪客，一前一后，起码扰你三顿。”原来杭州是南宋故都，婚丧喜庆，有许多繁文褥节，富家大族办喜事，请亲友执事，前期宴请，名为“请将”，事后款待，称为“谢将”。莲珠是螺蛳太太特为邀来陪官眷的“支宾”。

Hu Xueyan had scarcely taken his seat when he heard the faint clink of a curtain hook. Turning, he saw Lianzhu in the doorway. She was wearing a Manchu gown, though she had altered the design herself: the sleeves were less wide and the waist more closely fitted. She was tall and slender, had grown up in the north, and was accustomed to Manchu dress. As she approached with an embroidered handkerchief in her hand and a graceful swaying walk, there was nothing to suggest that she was Han Chinese. “Second Madam!” Hu rose at once to greet her. “Please sit down, please!” She waved him back to his seat. “Mr Hu, thank you for all those things you sent me. You have been far too extravagant.” “A mere trifle, a mere trifle,” Hu replied. “You must come early on the fifth, Second Madam.” “There is no need to remind me, Mr Hu. I shall be enjoying more than one wedding feast at your house. Fourth Sister has asked me to help entertain the guests. With the gatherings before and after the wedding, I shall be eating at your expense at least three times.” Hangzhou, the former capital of the Southern Song, retained many elaborate observances for weddings, funerals, and other family occasions. When a wealthy family held a wedding and enlisted relatives and friends to help, the preliminary banquet was called “inviting the generals,” and the feast afterwards, “thanking the generals.” Madam Luosi had specially invited Lianzhu to act as a hostess to the wives of officials.

“雪岩！”德馨问道：“喜事一切照常？”胡雪岩尚未答话，莲珠先开口了，“自然照常。”她说：“这还用得着问？”“你看！”德馨为姨太太所抢白，脸上有点挂不住，指着莲珠，自嘲地向胡雪岩说：“管得越严了，连多说句话都不得。”“只怕没有人管。”胡雪岩答说：“有人管是好事。”“我就是爱管闲事，也不光是管你。”莲珠紧接着又说：“胡大先生的事，我们怎么好不管，有件事我要提醒你，到了好日子那天，要约了刘抚台去道喜！”这正是胡雪岩想说不便说，关切在心里的一句话，所以格外注意德馨的反应，只听他答了一句：“当然非拉他去不可。”顿觉胸怀一宽。

“Xueyan,” Dexin asked, “is everything for the wedding going ahead as usual?” Before Hu could answer, Lianzhu spoke. “Of course it is. Do you even need to ask?” “There, you see!” A little embarrassed at being put down by his concubine, Dexin pointed at her and said to Hu with a self-mocking smile, “She keeps me under tighter control every day. I am not even allowed an extra word.” “The thing to fear is having no one to look after you,” Hu replied. “Having someone who does is a blessing.” “I do like to meddle, and you are not the only person I meddle with,” Lianzhu went on. “How could we stand aside when Mr Hu needs us? There is something I must remind you of: on the wedding day, you must arrange to go with Governor Liu and offer your congratulations.” This was precisely what Hu had been longing to ask but had felt unable to put into words. He watched Dexin's reaction with particular attention. When Dexin answered, “Of course I must drag him along,” a weight lifted from his heart.

“胡大先生，我特为穿旗袍给你看，你送我的哔叽衣料，我照这样子做了来穿，你说好不好看？”通家之好，到了这样的程度，似乎稍嫌过分，胡雪岩只好这样答说：“你说好就好。”“好是好，太素了一点儿。胡大先生，我还要托你，有没有西洋花边，下次得便请你从上海给我带一点来。”“有！有！”胡雪岩一叠连声地答说：“不必下一次。明天我就叫人送了来。”他接着又说：“西洋花边宽细都有，花式很多，我多送点来，请二太太自己挑。”“那就更好了。”“别老站着。”德馨亲自移开一张凳子，“你也陪我们吃一点儿。”于是莲珠坐了下来，为主客二人酌酒布菜，静静地听他们谈话。

“Mr Hu, I put on this Manchu gown especially to show you. I want to have the serge you sent me made up in this style. Do you think it would look well?” Even between families on such intimate terms, this seemed a little too familiar. Hu could only answer, “If you think it looks well, then it does.” “It would, only it would be a little too plain. There is something else I must ask you, Mr Hu. Can one get Western lace? Next time you have an opportunity, would you bring me some from Shanghai?” “Certainly, certainly!” Hu answered eagerly. “There is no need to wait until next time. I will have some sent over tomorrow. Western lace comes in broad and narrow widths, and in a great many patterns. I shall send a selection for you to choose from.” “That would be even better.” “Do not keep standing there,” Dexin said, moving a stool himself. “Sit down and have something with us.” Lianzhu sat down, poured wine and served food for host and guest, and quietly listened to their conversation.

“雪岩，我听说你用的人，也不完全靠得住。你自己总知道吧？”“过了这个风潮，我要好好整顿了。”胡雪岩答说：“晓翁说周少棠值得重用，我一定要重用。”“你看了人再用。”莲珠忍不住插嘴，“不要光看人家的面子，人用得不好，受害的是自己。”“是，是！二太太是金玉良言。”胡雪岩深为感慨，“这回的风潮，也是我不听一两个好友的话之故。”“其实你不必听外头人的话，多听听罗四姐的话就好了。”“她对外面的情形不大明白。这一点，比二太太你差多了。”听得这话，莲珠颇有知己之感，“胡大先生，你是明白的。不比我们老爷，提到外面的事，总说：“你别管‘。一个人再聪明，也有当局者迷的时候。刚才你同我们老爷在交谈的情形，我也听到了这一点儿。”说到这里，她突然问道：“胡大先生，上海跟杭州两处的风潮，左大人知道不知道？”

“Xueyan, I hear that not all the people you employ can be relied upon. You must know that yourself?” “Once this crisis is over, I shall put things thoroughly in order,” Hu replied. “You said Zhou Shaotang deserved to be given greater responsibilities, Mr Xiaofeng. I shall certainly see that he gets them.” Lianzhu could not resist intervening. “Judge the man for yourself before you employ him. Do not do it merely out of regard for someone else. If you choose badly, you are the one who suffers.” “Yes, yes! Those are words of gold, Second Madam.” Hu spoke with deep feeling. “This crisis, too, has come about because I failed to listen to one or two good friends.” “In fact, you need not listen to outsiders. You would do well enough if you listened more to Luo Sijie.” “She does not understand very much about affairs outside the household. In that respect she is a long way behind you, Second Madam.” Lianzhu felt that here, at least, was someone who appreciated her. “Mr Hu, you understand. Our master is quite different. Whenever I mention outside affairs, he says, ‘Keep out of it.’ However clever a person may be, there are times when being in the middle of things prevents him from seeing clearly. I caught something of what you and our master were discussing just now.” At this point she suddenly asked, “Does Lord Zuo know about the trouble in Shanghai and Hangzhou, Mr Hu?”

“恐怕还不晓得。”“你怎么不告诉他？”“告诉他？”胡雪岩有些茫然，多少年来，凡是失面子的事，他从不告诉左宗棠，所以阜康的风潮一起，他根本就没有想到过左宗棠。“为什么不告诉他？”莲珠说道：“你瞒也瞒不住的。”“说得不错。”德馨也说：“如果左大人肯出面，到底是两江总督部堂！”这个衔头在东南半壁，至高无上，但到底能发生什么作用，却很难说。哪知道莲珠别有深心，“胡大先生这会心很乱，恐怕不知道该跟左大人说什么好？”她随即提出一个建议：“是不是请杨师爷来拟个稿子看看？”那杨师爷是苏州人，年纪很轻，但笔下很来得，而且能言善道，善体人意，莲珠对他很欣赏。德馨只要是莲珠说好就好，所以对杨师爷亦颇另眼相看，此时便问胡雪岩：“你的意思怎么样？”“好是好！不过只怕太缓了。”“怎么缓得了？发电报出去，明天一早就到了。”“我密码本不在这里。”“用我们的好了。”莲珠接口。“对啊！”德馨说道，“请杨师爷拟好了稿子，就请他翻密码好了。小妾也可以帮忙。”“这，怎么好麻烦二太太？”“怕什么，我们两家什么交情！”真是盛情难地，胡雪岩只有感激的分儿。在请杨师爷的这段时间中，离座踱着方步，将要说的话都想好了。

“I am afraid he does not yet.” “Why have you not told him?” “Tell him?” Hu sounded rather bewildered. For many years he had never reported anything to Zuo Zongtang that would cost him face. When the trouble at Fukang broke out, Zuo had therefore never even entered his thoughts. “Why should you not tell him?” Lianzhu asked. “You cannot keep it from him in any case.” “Quite right,” Dexin agreed. “If Lord Zuo were willing to intervene—he is, after all, the Governor-General of Liangjiang!” In the southeastern half of the empire, no office stood higher. What practical effect its intervention could have, however, was another question. Lianzhu, as it happened, had a further purpose in mind. “Mr Hu's thoughts must be in turmoil at present. Perhaps he does not know what he ought to say to Lord Zuo?” She promptly made a suggestion. “Why not ask Secretary Yang to draw up a draft for us to look at?” Secretary Yang was a young man from Suzhou, an excellent writer, an accomplished speaker, and particularly good at understanding other people's wishes. Lianzhu thought highly of him. Since Dexin was content to approve anyone she approved of, he too treated the young secretary with special favour. “What do you think?” he now asked Hu. “It would be a good idea, only I am afraid it would take too long.” “How could it? Send a telegram and it will be there first thing tomorrow morning.” “I have not brought my codebook.” “Use ours,” Lianzhu put in. “Of course!” Dexin said. “Once Secretary Yang has drafted it, he can put it into code. My concubine can help him.” “But how could I trouble Second Madam with that?” “What trouble? Think how close our two families are!” Faced with such warmth, Hu could only feel grateful. While they sent for Secretary Yang, he left his seat and paced slowly about, arranging in his mind what he wished to say.

“杨师爷，拜托你起个稿子，要说这样子几点：第一，请左大人为了维持人心，打电报给上海道，尽力维持阜康。第二，请两江各衙门，暂时不要提存款。第三，浙江刘抚台、德馨台很帮忙，请左大人来个电报，客气一番。”“客气倒不必。”德馨说道：“要重重托一托刘抚台。”“是！是！”杨师爷鞠躬如也地问：“还有什么话？”“想到了，再告诉你。”莲珠接口说道：“杨师爷，你请到外面来写，清静一点儿。”莲珠很热心地引领着杨师爷到了外屋，悄悄嘱咐了一番。他下笔很快，不到半个钟头，便将稿子送了上来，除了照胡雪岩所要求的三点陈述以外，前面特为加一段，盛称德馨如何帮忙，得以暂度难关，实在令人感激，同时也说了些德馨在浙江的政绩。着墨不多，但措词很有力量，这当然是莲珠悄悄嘱咐的结果。

“Secretary Yang, may I trouble you to prepare a draft covering these points? First, to preserve public confidence, ask Lord Zuo to telegraph the Shanghai circuit intendant and instruct him to do everything possible to support Fukang. Second, ask the various government offices in Liangjiang to leave their deposits untouched for the time being. Third, Governor Liu and Treasurer Dexin here in Zhejiang have been most helpful; ask Lord Zuo to send a telegram expressing his appreciation.” “There is no need for compliments,” Dexin said. “But he ought to make a strong personal appeal to Governor Liu.” “Certainly, certainly!” Secretary Yang bowed deferentially. “Is there anything else?” “If we think of anything, we shall tell you,” Lianzhu interposed. “Come and write in the outer room, Secretary Yang. It will be quieter there.” She led him out with great solicitude and gave him some instructions in a whisper. He wrote quickly, and in less than half an hour brought back the draft. Besides setting out the three points Hu had requested, it opened with a special passage praising Dexin's assistance, which had enabled Hu to weather the immediate difficulty and deserved his profound gratitude.
