“In a foreign country—in America, Britain, even Japan—the authorities would certainly support a man in my position,” Hu continued. “I keep thinking that it would not matter if I took a loss, provided the benefit did not go abroad. If the court would put up four million five hundred thousand taels, I would sell my entire stock at half price. Or if it would undertake to settle all my public and private liabilities, I would willingly hand over every business I own. But… ah!” He shook his head and would say no more. “That would certainly be an open and honourable way to cut through the tangle!” Dexin said eagerly. “Why not ask Lord Zuo to submit it to the throne?” “It would be no use.” Hu shook his head. “The court's priority is raising money for the war. Besides, Lord Yan controls the Ministry of Revenue. His calculations are too exact; he would never agree.” Lord Yan was Yan Jingming, Assistant Grand Secretary, renowned for financial ability. His method consisted of matching expenditure to income and practising thrift. He had always deeply disapproved of Hu's princely way of life and would certainly not offer assistance now. “Then,” Dexin asked, puzzled, “if you do not want Lord Zuo to intervene, why are you going to see him?” “It is not that I do not want his help. I merely feel it would be useless. Naturally, I must hear what he thinks. You know that Lord Zuo is the mountain behind me. That mountain must not fall.” He then related Mr Wu's interpretation of the divinatory character.

不道德馨亦深好此道，立即问说：“乌先生在不在？”“不知道走了没有？”胡雪岩起身想找螺蛳太太去问，她已听见他们的话，自己走了进来说：“乌先生今天在这里，就不知道睡了没有？”“你叫人去看看。”“如果睡了，就算了。”德馨接口：“深夜惊动，于心不安。”其实这是暗示，即使睡了，也要惊动他起身。官做大了，说话都是这样子的。螺蛳太太识得这个窍门，口中答应着，出来以后却悄悄嘱咐阿云，传话客房，不论乌先生睡了没有，请他马上来一趟。

Dexin, it turned out, was also keenly interested in such matters. “Is Mr Wu here?” he asked at once. “I do not know whether he has left.” Hu rose to find Madam Luosi and ask, but she had heard their conversation and came in of her own accord. “Mr Wu is staying here tonight. I do not know whether he has gone to bed.” “Send someone to see.” “If he is asleep, leave him,” Dexin put in. “I should feel bad about disturbing him so late.” What this really meant was that Mr Wu should be woken even if he had retired. High officials always spoke in this fashion. Madam Luosi understood the convention. Aloud she agreed; once outside, she quietly told A’yun to send word to the guest rooms and ask Mr Wu to come immediately, whether he was asleep or not.

第六章 探骊得珠｜CHAPTER SIX: SEIZING THE DRAGON’S PEARL

乌先生却还未睡，所以一请就到，他是第一次见德馨，在胡雪岩引见以后，少不得有一番客套，德馨又恭维他测字测得妙，接下来便要向他“请教”了。“不敢当，不敢当！雕虫小技，不登大雅。”乌先生问：“不知道德大人想问什么？”“我在谋一件事，不知道有成功的希望没有？想请乌先生费心替我卜一下。”“是！请报一个字。”德馨略想一想说：“就是谋字吧。”一旁有现成的笔砚，乌先生坐下来取张纸，提笔将“谋”字拆写成“言”、“某”两字，然后搁笔思考。这时德馨与胡雪岩亦都走了过来，手捧水烟袋，静静地站在桌旁观看。“德大人所谋的这件事，要托人进‘言’，这个人心目中已经有了，没有说出来，那就是个‘某，。”乌先生笑道：“不瞒德大人说，我拆字是’三脚猫，，也不会江湖诀，不过就字论字，如果说对了，一路拆下去，或许谈言微中，亦未可知。”“是，是！”德馨很客气地：“高明之至。”“那么，请问德大人，我刚才一开头说对了没有？不对，重新来，请德大人不要客气，一定要说实话。”“是的，我一定说实话，你老兄一开头就探骊得珠了。”乌先生定睛细看一看他的脸色，直待确定了他是说的实话，方始欣慰地又说：“侥幸，侥幸。”燃后拈起笔来说道：“人言为信，这个人立在言字旁边，意思是进言的人要钉在旁边，才会有作用。”“嗯，嗯！”德馨不断点头，而且不断眨眼，似乎一面听，一面在体味。

Mr Wu had not yet gone to bed and came as soon as he was summoned. This was his first meeting with Dexin. After Hu Xueyan introduced them, the usual courtesies were exchanged. Dexin complimented him on his ingenious character divination, then proceeded to ask his advice. “You are too kind! A trifling skill, quite unworthy of serious company,” Mr Wu replied. “What would Your Excellency like to ask?” “I am pursuing a certain ambition and do not know whether there is any hope of success. Would you be kind enough to divine the outcome?” “Certainly. Please give me a character.” After a moment’s thought, Dexin said, “Let it be mou: ‘to scheme.’” Brush and ink were ready at hand. Mr Wu sat down, took a sheet of paper, and separated the character into its two components, yan, meaning “speech,” and mou, meaning “a certain person.” Then he laid down the brush to think. Dexin and Hu came over, each holding a water pipe, and stood quietly beside the table. “For what you are planning, Your Excellency, you need someone to speak on your behalf. You already have a person in mind but have not named him: hence ‘a certain person.’” Mr Wu smiled. “To be honest, I am only a dabbler at this. I know none of the professional diviners’ formulas. I simply consider the character itself. If I have begun correctly and continue taking it apart, perhaps I may stumble upon something pertinent.” “Yes, yes! Most perceptive,” Dexin said politely. “Then was my opening statement correct? If not, we must begin again. Please do not spare my feelings; you must tell the truth.” “I certainly shall. You have plunged straight to the dragon’s pearl.” Mr Wu studied his face until he felt sure the answer was sincere. “A fortunate guess!” he said with satisfaction, taking up the brush again. “‘Person’ beside ‘speech’ makes xin, ‘trust.’ The person standing beside the speech means that your spokesman must keep close at hand if he is to be effective.” Dexin nodded repeatedly, blinking as though weighing the words as he listened.

“现在看这个某字，加女为媒，中间牵线的要个女人。”“请教乌先生，这个牵线的女人，牵到哪一面？”“问得好！”乌先生指着“信”字说，“这里有两个人，一个进言，一个纳言，牵线是牵到进言的人身上。”“意思是，这个为媒的女子，不是立在言子旁边的那个人？”“不错。”“我明白了。”德馨又问：“再要请教，我谋的这件事，什么时候着手？会不会成功，能够成功，是在什么时候？““这就要看某字下面的这个木字了。”乌先生将“某”下之“木”涂掉，成了“甘”、“言”二字，这就不必他解释了，德馨便知道他所托的“某”人，满口答应，其实只是饴人的“甘言”。因此，他问：“要怎么样才会失掉这个木字？”

“Now look at the component mou, ‘a certain person.’ Add ‘woman,’ and it becomes mei, ‘a go-between.’ A woman must provide the connection.” “May I ask which party this woman connects with?” “A good question!” Mr Wu pointed to xin, “trust.” “There are two people here: one who speaks, and one who listens. The woman makes the connection with the one who speaks.” “You mean that the woman acting as go-between is not the person standing beside ‘speech’?” “Exactly.” “I understand. Now let me ask: when should I begin? Will I succeed? And if so, when?” “For that, we must consider the ‘wood’ beneath mou.” Mr Wu blotted out that lower component, leaving gan, “sweet,” and yan, “speech.” No explanation was necessary. Dexin understood that the person he relied on might promise everything, yet offer nothing more than soothing “sweet words.” “How would the ‘wood’ be lost?” he asked.

“金克木。”乌先生答说：“如果这件是在七、八月里着手，已经不行了。”“为什么呢？”“七月申月，八月西月，都是金。”“现在十一月，”胡雪岩插嘴：“十一月是不是子月？”“县的”胡雪岩略通五行生克之理，便向德馨说道：“子是水，水生木，晓翁，你赶快进行。”“万万来不及。”德馨说道：“今天十一月十六日，只半个月不到，哪来得及？”“而且水固生木，到下个月是丑月，丑为土，木克土不利。”乌先生接下来说：“最好开年正月里着手，正月寅，二月卯，都是木，三月里有个顿挫，不过到四、五月里就好了，四月已，五月午都是火……”“木生火。”胡雪岩接口，“大功告成。”“正是这话。”乌先生同意。“高明，高明！真是心悦诚服。”德馨满面笑容将水烟袋放下，“这得送润笑，不送就不灵了。”一面说，一面掀开“卧龙袋”，里面束着一条蓝绸汗巾作腰带，旗人在这条带子上的小零碎很多，他俯首看了一下，解下一个玉钱，双手递了过去。“不成敬意，留着玩。”乌先生接过来一看，倒是纯净无暇的一块羊脂白玉，上镌“乾隆通宝”四字，制得颇为精致，虽不甚值会，但确是很好的一样玩物，便连连拱手，口说：“谢谢，谢谢！”“这个不算，等明年夏天我谋的事成功了，再好好表一表谢意。”

“Metal overcomes Wood,” Mr Wu answered. “If you began in the seventh or eighth month, the venture would already be lost.” “Why?” “The seventh month is shen, the eighth you. Both belong to Metal.” “This is the eleventh month,” Hu put in. “Isn’t the eleventh month zi?” “Yes.” Hu knew something of how the Five Elements generated and overcame one another. “Zi is Water, and Water generates Wood. Mr Xiaofeng, you must begin at once.” “There is no possible way to do it in time. Today is the sixteenth of the eleventh month. Less than half a month remains. How could I manage it?” “Besides,” Mr Wu continued, “though Water generates Wood, next month is chou, which belongs to Earth. Wood overcomes Earth: an unfavorable relation. It would be best to begin in the first month of the new year. The first month is yin, the second mao, both Wood. There will be a setback in the third month, but all will be well by the fourth or fifth. The fourth is si, the fifth wu, both Fire…” “Wood generates Fire,” Hu supplied. “Complete success!” “Precisely,” Mr Wu agreed. “Wonderful! I am entirely convinced.” Beaming, Dexin put down his water pipe. “I must offer you a fee, or the prediction will not come true.” He lifted his sleeveless outer garment, revealing a blue silk kerchief serving as a sash about his waist. Bannermen carried many small accessories on such sashes. Looking down, he detached a jade coin and presented it with both hands. “A trifling token. Keep it to amuse yourself.” Mr Wu found it was a flawless piece of mutton-fat white jade, finely carved with the four characters for “Qianlong circulating treasure.” It was not particularly valuable, but made a charming object to handle. He repeatedly clasped his hands in thanks. “This hardly counts,” Dexin added. “When my plan succeeds next summer, I shall thank you properly.”

等乌先生告辞退出，胡雪岩虽然自己心事重重，但为了表示关怀好朋友，仍旧兴致盎然地动问，德馨所谋何事？“还不是想独当一面。我走的是宝中堂的路子，托他令弟进言。”德馨又说：“前年你不是邀他到南边来玩，我顺便请他逛富春江，约你作陪，你有事不能去。你还记得这回事不？”“嗯嗯。我记得。”胡雪岩问说：“逛富春江的时候，你就跟他谈过了？”“不！那时候我刚升藩司不久，不能作此非分之想。”德馨说道：“我们这位宝二爷看中了一个江山船上的船娘，向我示意，想藏诸金屋，而且言外之意，自备身价银子，不必我花费分文。不过，我刚刚到任，怎么能拉这种马，所以装糊涂没有答腔。最近，他跟我通信，还没有忘记这段旧情，而那个船娘，只想择人而事，我已经派人跟她娘老子谈过，只要两千两银子，宝二爷即可如愿。我一直还在犹豫，今晚上听乌先生这一谈，吾志已决。”这样去谋方面大员，胡雪岩心里不免菲薄，而且他觉得德馨的路子亦没有走对。既然是朋友，不能不提出忠告。“晓翁，”他问：“宝中堂跟他老的情形，你清楚不清楚？”“弟兄不甚和睦是不是？”“是的。”胡雪岩又说：“宝中堂见了他很头痛，进言只怕不见得效。”“不然。”德馨答说：“我跟他们昆仲是世交，他家的情形我知道。宝中堂对他这位令弟，一筹莫展，唯有安抚，宝二爷只要天天在他老兄面前罗嗦，宝中堂为了躲麻烦，只有听他老弟的活。”

After Mr Wu withdrew, Hu, despite his own heavy troubles, made a show of lively interest in his friend’s concerns and asked what he was planning. “What else but a post where I can take charge in my own right? I am working through Grand Secretary Bao, asking his younger brother to speak for me. You invited the brother south for a visit the year before last, remember? I offered to take him along the Fuchun River and asked you to join us, but you were too busy.” “Yes, I remember. Did you discuss it with him on that trip?” “No. I had only recently become provincial treasurer. I could hardly aspire beyond my station so soon. Our Second Master Bao took a fancy to a boatwoman on one of the Jiangshan boats and hinted that he wanted to install her in a secluded love nest. He also let me understand that he would supply the money himself: I need not spend a penny. But I had just taken office. How could I act as a procurer? I pretended not to understand. He has written to me recently and still hasn’t forgotten her. As for the woman, she wants to choose a suitable man to attach herself to. I’ve already sent someone to speak to her parents. For just two thousand taels, Second Master Bao can have his wish. I’ve been hesitating, but after listening to Mr Wu tonight, my mind is made up.” Hu could not help thinking little of such a way to seek a major provincial appointment. He also thought Dexin had chosen the wrong channel. As a friend, he ought to warn him. “Mr Xiaofeng, do you know how matters stand between Grand Secretary Bao and his brother?” “They don’t get on very well?” “Exactly. The grand secretary finds him a headache. I doubt his intercession would do much good.” “On the contrary. Our families are old friends, and I know their affairs. Bao can do nothing with his brother except placate him. If Second Master Bao nags him every day, he’ll have to listen simply to escape the nuisance.”

听得这一说，胡雪岩只好付之一笑，不过想起一件事，带笑警告着说：“晓翁，这件事你要做得秘密，让都老爷晓得了，参上一本，又出江山船的新闻，划不来。”所谓“又出江山船的新闻”，是因为一年以前在江山船上出过一件新闻，“翰林四谏”之一的宝廷，放了福建的主考，来去经由杭州，坐江山船溯富春江而入上闽，归途中纳江山船的一个船娘为妾，言官打算搏击，宝廷见机，上奏自劾，因而落职。在京的大名士李慈铭，做了一首诗咏其事，其中有一联极其工整：“宗室八旗名士草，江山九姓美人麻。”宝廷是宗室，也是名士，但加一“草”字，自是讥刺。下句则别有典故，据说江山船上的船户，共有九姓，皆为元末陈友谅的部将之后，朱元璋得了天下，为惩罚此辈，不准他们上岸居住，只能讨水上生涯。而宝廷所眷的船娘，是个俗语所说的“白麻子”，只以宝廷近视，咫尺之外，不辨人物，竟未发觉，所以李慈铭有“美人麻”的谐谑。这两句诗，亦就因此烩炙人口，腾为笑柄。德馨当然也知道这个故事，想起言官的气焰，不免心惊肉跳，所以口中所说“不要紧”，暗地里却接受了胡雪岩的警告，颇持戒心。

Hu could only smile at this. Then something occurred to him, and he added a smiling warning. “You must keep the business secret, Mr Xiaofeng. If the censors hear and submit an impeachment, there’ll be another Jiangshan boat scandal. It wouldn’t be worth it.” He was referring to a scandal of the previous year. Baoting, one of the “Four Hanlin Remonstrators,” had been appointed chief examiner in Fujian. Passing through Hangzhou on both journeys, he had taken a Jiangshan boat up the Fuchun River and into upper Fujian. On his return, he made one of the boatwomen his concubine. The censors prepared to attack him, but Baoting anticipated them and submitted a memorial impeaching himself, whereupon he lost office. Li Ciming, a celebrated man of letters in the capital, wrote a poem about it, including a particularly neat couplet: “Eight-Banner royal clansman, a scholar of grass; / Nine-Surname Jiangshan woman, a beauty with pockmarks.” Baoting belonged to the imperial clan and was indeed a man of letters, but the addition of “grass” was plainly satirical. The second line contained another allusion. The families living on Jiangshan boats were said to bear nine surnames, all descended from commanders who had served Chen Youliang at the end of the Yuan. After winning the empire, Zhu Yuanzhang punished them by forbidding them to live ashore: they could earn their living only on the water. The woman Baoting admired was what people called a “white-pockmarked woman.” Being so shortsighted that he could barely distinguish people and things even at close quarters, he had failed to notice. Hence Li Ciming’s joke about a pockmarked beauty. The lines became widely quoted, and the affair a laughingstock. Dexin naturally knew the story. Remembering the censors’ ferocity, he felt distinctly uneasy. Though he said there was nothing to worry about, privately he accepted Hu’s warning and resolved to be cautious.

一夜之隔，情势大变，浙江巡抚刘秉漳接到直隶总督北洋大臣李鸿章的密电，说有直隶水灾赈款六十万两银子，存在阜康福，被倒无着，电请刘秉漳查封胡雪岩所设的典当，备抵公款。于是刘秉璋即时将德馨请了去，以电报相示，问他有何意见？德馨已估量到会有这种恶劣的情况出现，老早亦想好了最后的办法，“司里的愚见，总以不影响市面为主。”他说，“如果雷厉风行，丝毫不留情面，刺激民心，总非地方之福，至于胡雪岩本人，气概倒还光明磊落，我看不如我去劝一劝他，要他自作处置。”“何以谓之自作处置？”“让他自已把财产目录，公私亏欠帐目开出来，捧交大人，请大人替他作主。”刘秉璋原以为德馨的所谓“自作处置”，是劝胡雪岩自裁，听了德馨的话，才知道自己误会了，也放心了。“好！你者哥多费心。”刘秉璋问：“什么时候可以听回音。”“总得明儿上午。”当夜德馨又去看胡雪岩，一见哽咽，居然挤出一副急泪，这就尽在不言中了。胡雪岩却很但然，说一声：“晓翁，说我看不破，不对，说我方寸不乱，也不对。一切都请晓翁指点。”于是德馨道明来意，胡雪岩一诺无辞。但提出一个要求，要给他两天的时间，理由是他要处分家务。德馨沉吟了好一会说：“我跟刘中丞去力争，大不了赔上一顶纱帽，也要把你这两天争了来。但望两夭以后，能把所有帐目都交了给他。”“一言为定。”

Overnight, the situation changed drastically. Liu Bingzhang, governor of Zhejiang, received a confidential telegram from Li Hongzhang, Governor-General of Zhili and Minister for the Northern Ports. Six hundred thousand taels of Zhili flood-relief funds had been deposited in Fukangfu and were now stranded by its collapse. Li asked Liu to seal Hu Xueyan’s pawnshops as security for the public money. Liu immediately sent for Dexin, showed him the telegram, and asked his opinion. Dexin had anticipated just such an adverse development and long since considered his last resort. “In my humble view, our principal concern must be to avoid disturbing trade,” he replied. “If we act with ruthless speed, showing no consideration, we shall alarm the public. That cannot benefit the province. As for Hu himself, his spirit is honorable and straightforward. I suggest that I speak to him and persuade him to make his own arrangements.” “What do you mean by that?” “Let him draw up an inventory of his property and accounts of his public and private debts, and place them in Your Excellency’s hands, asking you to act for him.” Liu had imagined that “make his own arrangements” meant persuading Hu to take his own life. Discovering his mistake, he felt relieved. “Very well. I must trouble you with this. When may I expect an answer?” “Tomorrow morning, at the earliest.” That night Dexin called on Hu again. At their meeting his voice caught, and he actually squeezed out a few anxious tears. They said everything. Hu, however, was quite calm. “It would be wrong to say I cannot face the truth, Mr Xiaofeng, but equally wrong to say I am untroubled. I leave everything to your guidance.” Dexin explained his purpose. Hu agreed without argument, asking only for two days to settle his household affairs. Dexin pondered for some time. “I shall fight for those two days with Governor Liu, even if it costs me my official cap. But I hope you can hand him all the accounts when they are over.” “Agreed.”

等德馨一走，胡雪岩与螺蛳太太关紧了房门，整整谈了一夜。第二天分头采取了几项行动，首先是发密电给汉口、镇江、福州、长沙、武昌各地的阜康，即日闭歇清理，其次是托古应春赶紧回上海，觅洋商议价出售存丝，第三是集中一批现银，将少数至亲好友的存款付讫，再是检点一批首饰、古玩，约略估价，抵偿德馨经手的一批存款。当然，还有最要紧的一件事是，开列财产目录。密密地忙到半夜，方始告一段落，胡雪岩累不可当，喝一杯人参浸泡的葡萄酒，正待上床时，德馨派专人送来一封信，信中写的是：“给事中邓承修奏请责令贪吏罚捐巨款，以济要需，另附一片，抄请察觉。”所附的抄件是：“另片奏：闻阜康银号关闭，协部大学士刑部尚书文煜，所存该号银数至七十余万之多，请旨查明确数，究所从来，等语，着顺天府确查具奏。”这封信及抄件，不是个好消息，但胡雪岩亦想不出对他还有什么更不利之处，因而丢开了睡觉。

After Dexin left, Hu and Madam Luosi shut themselves in and talked all night. The next day they took several steps. First, they sent confidential telegrams to the Fukang branches in Hankou, Zhenjiang, Fuzhou, Changsha, and Wuchang, instructing them to close immediately and begin liquidation. Next, they asked Gu Yingchun to hurry back to Shanghai and find foreign merchants with whom to negotiate the sale of the stored silk. Third, they gathered a quantity of ready silver and paid off the deposits of a small number of close relatives and friends. They also selected jewelry and antiques, valued them approximately, and used them to settle a group of deposits handled through Dexin. Most important of all, they drew up an inventory of their property. They worked quietly until midnight before reaching a stopping point. Utterly exhausted, Hu drank a glass of wine in which ginseng had been steeped and was about to go to bed when a special messenger brought a letter from Dexin. It read: “Supervising Censor Deng Chengxiu has memorialized, requesting that corrupt officials be ordered to contribute large sums as a penalty, to meet urgent needs. A supplementary memorial was attached. A copy follows for your information.” The enclosure read: “In a supplementary memorial he states: ‘I hear that Fukang Bank has closed, and that the sum deposited there by Wenyu, Assistant Grand Secretary and Minister of Punishments, amounts to more than seven hundred thousand taels. I request an imperial order to ascertain the exact amount and investigate its source.’ The Shuntian prefectural authorities are hereby ordered to investigate and report.” Neither letter nor enclosure brought good news, but Hu could not see how this might make his own position any worse. He put them aside and went to sleep.

一觉醒来，头脑清醒，自然而然地想到德馨传来的消息，同时也想到了文煜——他是满洲正蓝旗人，与恭王是姻亲，早在咸丰十一年就署理过直隶总督，但发财却是同治七年任福州将军以后的事。原来清兵入关，虽代明而得天下，但南明亡后，浙东有鲁王，西南有永历帝，海外有郑成功，此外还有异姓封王的“三藩”，手握重兵，亦可能成为心腹之患，因而在各省冲要枢纽之地，派遣旗营驻防，借以防备汉人反清复明。统率驻防旗营长官，名为“将军”，上加地名，驻西安即名之为西安将军，驻杭州即名之为杭州将军。

He awoke with a clear head and naturally thought of Dexin’s news, and of Wenyu himself. A Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner, related by marriage to Prince Gong, Wenyu had served as acting Governor-General of Zhili as early as the eleventh year of Xianfeng. His fortune, however, had begun only after he became Fuzhou Garrison General in the seventh year of Tongzhi. The Qing armies had entered the passes and won the empire from the Ming, but even after the Southern Ming fell, the Prince of Lu remained in eastern Zhejiang, the Yongli Emperor in the southwest, and Zheng Chenggong overseas. There were also the Three Feudatories, princes of other surnames commanding powerful armies who might become a grave internal threat. Banner garrisons were therefore stationed at strategic centers in the provinces to guard against Han attempts to overthrow the Qing and restore the Ming. Their commanders were styled generals, with the place name attached: the commander at Xi’an was the Xi’an Garrison General, the one at Hangzhou the Hangzhou Garrison General.

各地将军的权责不一，因地因时制宜，福建因为先有郑成功父子的海上舟师，后有耿精忠响应吴三桂造反，是用兵的要地，所以福州将军权柄特重，他处将军，只管旗营，只有福州将军兼管“绿营”，此外还有一项差使，兼管闽海关。起初只是为了盘查海船，以防偷渡或私运军械，到后来却成了一个专门收税的利薮，尤其是鸦片战争以后，海禁大开，英、法、美、日各国商人都在福州设有洋行，闽海关的税收大增，兼管海关亦就成了有名的美差。文烃从同治七年当福州将军，十年兼署闽浙总督，直至光绪三年内调，前后在福州九年，宦囊丰盈，都存在阜康银号。及至是京以后，先后充任崇文门正监督、内务府总管大臣，亦都是可以搞钱的差使，所以存在阜康的款子，总数不下百万之多，是胡雪岩最大的一个主顾。

Their authority and responsibilities varied with local conditions and circumstances. Fujian had first faced the fleets of Zheng Chenggong and his son, then Geng Jingzhong’s rebellion in support of Wu Sangui. As a strategic military region, it gave the Fuzhou Garrison General exceptional power. Elsewhere, generals commanded only Banner troops; the Fuzhou general alone also controlled Green Standard troops. He had a further duty: supervision of the Fujian Maritime Customs. Originally intended to inspect seagoing vessels and prevent illicit crossings or arms smuggling, this had gradually become a lucrative tax-collecting office. Especially after the Opium War, when the maritime restrictions were thrown wide open, British, French, American, and Japanese merchants established trading houses in Fuzhou. Customs revenue grew enormously, and its supervision became a famously profitable appointment. Wenyu became Fuzhou Garrison General in the seventh year of Tongzhi and concurrently acted as Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang from the tenth year. He remained until his transfer to the capital in the third year of Guangxu, spending nine years in Fuzhou. His official purse grew fat, and he deposited the money with Fukang. In the capital, he served successively as chief superintendent at Chongwen Gate and minister of the Imperial Household Department, both posts offering opportunities to make money. His deposits with Fukang totaled no less than a million taels, making him Hu’s largest customer.

这个主顾的存款，要查他的来源如何？虽与胡雪岩无关，但因此使得阜康的倒闭更成了大新闻，对他大为不利。但这亦是无可奈何之事，胡雪岩只有丢开它，细想全盘帐目交出以后的情形。帐都交了，清理亦无从清理起。不是吗？胡雪岩这样转着念头，突然精神一振，不可思议地、竟有一种无债一身轻之感。这道理是很明白的，交出全部帐目，等于交出全部财务，当然也就交出了全部债务，清理是公家的责任，当然，这在良心上还是有亏欠的，但事到如今也顾不得那许多了。不过，胡雪岩还存着万一之想，那就是存在上海、天津的大批丝货，能够找到一条出路。来偿还全部债务；这件事，虽托了古应春，但他的号召力不够，必得自己到上海，在古应春协助之下，才有希望。照这个想法来说，他交出全部帐目，债务由公家来替他抵挡一阵，等于获得一段喘息的时间，得以全力在丝货上作一番挣扎。这样一想，他的多日来的忧烦与萎靡，消失了一半，级着鞋，悄悄到房里去找螺蛳太太。

An investigation into the source of this customer’s money had nothing to do with Hu himself. Yet it would make Fukang’s collapse an even greater sensation, which was very bad for him. There was nothing he could do, however. He put it aside and considered what would happen once he had handed over all the accounts. With the books gone, there would be no way for him to conduct the liquidation himself—would there? As this thought took shape, his spirits suddenly lifted. Incredible as it seemed, he felt the lightness of a man freed from debt. The reasoning was plain: surrendering all the accounts meant surrendering all the finances, and therefore all the debts as well. Liquidation would become the authorities’ responsibility. Of course, his conscience would still be burdened, but at this stage he could no longer attend to every consideration. He also retained one faint hope: that some outlet might be found for the great stocks of silk in Shanghai and Tianjin, enabling him to repay every debt. He had entrusted the matter to Gu, but Gu lacked sufficient influence. There would be hope only if Hu went to Shanghai himself and worked with Gu’s assistance. Seen in that light, handing over the accounts would let the authorities hold off the creditors for a time, giving him breathing space to concentrate all his efforts on the silk. Half his recent anxiety and dejection vanished. Slipping his feet into his shoes, he quietly went to Madam Luosi’s bedroom.

她也忙了半夜，入睡不过一个多时辰。胡雪岩揭开皮帐子，一股暖香，直扑鼻观，螺蛳太太鼻息微微，睡得正酣，胡雪岩不忍惊醒她，轻轻揭开丝棉被，侧身睡下，不道惊醒了螺蛳太大，一翻身朝里，口中说道：“你真是不晓得死活，这里候还有心思来缠我。”胡雪岩知道她误会了，忍不住好笑，而且心境不同，也比较有兴来开玩笑了，便扳着螺蛳太太的依旧圆润温软的肩头说：“这就叫吃着黄连弹琴，苦中作乐。”“去！去！哪个同你作乐？”话虽如此，身子却回过来了，而且握住了胡雪岩的手。“我刚刚想了一想。”胡雪岩开始谈正事，“我见了刘中丞，请他替我一肩担待。我正好脱室身体到上海去想办法。你看我这个盘算怎么样？”听得这话螺蛳太太睁开双眼，坐起身来，顺手将里床的一件皮袄披在身上，抱着双膝，细细恩量。“他肯不肯替你担待呢？”“不肯也要肯。”胡雪岩说：“交帐就是交产，原封不动捧出去，请他看了办。”“你说交产？”螺蛳太太问：“我们连安身之处都没有了。”“那当然不是。”胡雪岩说：“我跟你来商量的，就是要弄个界限出来。”

She too had worked late into the night and had slept for only a little over two hours. Hu lifted the fur bed curtains, and a warm fragrance met him. Madam Luosi was sound asleep, breathing softly. Unwilling to disturb her, he gently raised the silk-wadded quilt and lay down on his side. But she woke, turned inward, and said, “You really have no idea what trouble you’re in! At a time like this, you still have a mind to pester me.” Realizing her mistake, Hu could not help smiling. His changed mood even gave him some appetite for a joke. Taking hold of her shoulder, still rounded, soft, and warm, he said, “It’s like playing music while chewing bitter coptis: finding pleasure in suffering.” “Go away! Who wants to find pleasure with you?” Yet she turned back and took his hand. “I’ve just been thinking,” Hu said, coming to business. “When I see Governor Liu, I’ll ask him to take the whole burden on his shoulders. That will leave me free to go to Shanghai and try to find a solution. What do you think?” At this, Madam Luosi opened her eyes and sat up. She put on a fur jacket lying on the inner side of the bed, clasped her knees, and considered carefully. “Will he be willing to take it on for you?” “He’ll have to. Handing over the books means handing over the property. I’ll surrender it intact and ask him to deal with it as he sees fit.” “The property? Then we won’t even have anywhere to live.” “Of course we will. What I’ve come to discuss is where to draw the line.”

“这个界限在哪里？”“在……”胡雪岩说：“在看这样东西，是不是居家过日子少不了的，如果是，可以留下来，不然就是财产，要开帐，要交出去。”“这哪里有一定的界限，有的人情茶淡饭，吃得蛮好，有的没有肉吃不下饭。你说，怎么来分？”“当然这里的伸缩性，也蛮大的。”螺蛳太太沉吟不语。她原来总以为只是胡雪岩的事业要交出去，私财除了金块、金条、金叶子以及现银以外，其他都能不动。照现在看，跟抄家也差不多了。一想到“抄家”，心里发酸，不过她也是刚强明达一路人，仍能强忍住眼泪想正经。只是想来想去，想不出一个头绪来，因为细软摆饰、动用家具、一切日常什物，诚如胡雪岩所说的伸缩性很大，似乎每一样东西都必须评估一番，才能区分。“这样一片家业，哪里是即时之刻，开得出帐目来的？”螺蛳太太说：“我看只有两个办法，一是同刘抚台声明，私财的帐目太琐碎，一时没法子开得周全，一个是只开大数，自己估个价，譬如说红木家具几堂，大毛皮统子多少件，每一项下面估个总数。”“我看照第二个办法比较好。”“不过，估价也很难，譬如说我们的住身房子，你倒估估看。”“这只有把造价开上去。数目也好看些。”为了求帐面好看，不但房子照造价开，其他一切亦都照买进的价钱开列。

“Where is the line?” “It depends…on whether something is indispensable to living our everyday lives. If it is, we can keep it. Otherwise it is property, and must be listed and handed over.” “How can there be a fixed line? Some people are perfectly happy with plain tea and simple food; others can’t eat a meal without meat. How do you distinguish between them?” “Of course, there is considerable room for interpretation.” Madam Luosi considered this in silence. She had always imagined that only Hu’s businesses would be surrendered; among their private possessions, only gold ingots, bars, and leaf, together with ready silver, would be touched. Now it seemed little different from having their home confiscated. The thought made her heart ache, but she was strong-minded and clear-sighted. Holding back her tears, she tried to consider the practical questions. Yet she could find no starting point. Jewelry and fine possessions, ornaments, furniture, everyday utensils—each item seemed to require a separate assessment before it could be classified. As Hu had said, the scope for interpretation was enormous. “How could an estate like this be inventoried in an instant?” she asked. “I can see only two ways. Either tell Governor Liu that the private property is too complicated to list completely in such a short time, or give only broad totals with our own valuations: so many sets of hongmu furniture, so many linings of heavy fur, and an estimated total under each heading.” “The second seems better.” “But valuation is difficult too. Take this house we live in. What would you put on it?” “We can only enter the cost of construction. That will make the figures look better.” To improve the appearance of the accounts, they listed not merely the house at its building cost, but everything else at its purchase price.

第二天又忙了大半天，诸事齐备，胡雪岩去看德馨，约期晋见巡抚刘秉璋。“最好是在今天晚上。”他说，“这不是啥有面子的事，最好少见人，而且，晚上可以穿便衣。”“我看不必，这是很光明磊落的事，没有什么见不得人。而且，刘中丞是翰袜出身，很讲究这些过节，晚上谈这件事，倒仿佛私相授受似的，他一定不愿意。准定明天上午上院吧。”“是。好！”胡雪岩只得答应。“穿便衣也不必。倒象有了什么罪过，青衣小帽负罪辕门似的。不过，雪岩，你的服饰也不必太华丽。”这是暗示，红顶花翎都不必戴。胡雪岩当然会意，第二天循规蹈矩，只按道员三品眼色穿戴整齐，带着从人上轿到佑圣观巷巡抚衙门。

They spent most of the following day at work again. When everything was ready, Hu went to Dexin to arrange an audience with Governor Liu Bingzhang. “Tonight would be best,” he said. “It’s hardly something to be proud of. The fewer people I meet, the better. Besides, I can wear informal clothes at night.” “I don’t think that is necessary. This is an entirely honorable proceeding, nothing to hide. Governor Liu comes from the Hanlin Academy and is particular about such conventions. Discussing it at night would make it look like a private bargain, which he certainly would not want. Let us fix the audience for tomorrow morning.” “Yes, very well.” Hu could only agree. “And there’s no need for informal clothes. That would make you look like a guilty man arriving at the yamen gate in a plain gown and little cap to confess. Still, Xueyan, you need not dress too splendidly.” The hint was that he should leave off the red finial and peacock feather. Hu understood. The next day, observing all the rules, he dressed simply according to the third-rank attire of a circuit intendant and set off by sedan, accompanied by his attendants, for the governor’s yamen in Youshengguan Lane.

其时德馨已先派了人在接应，手本一递进去，刘秉璋即时在西花厅延见，胡雪岩照官场规矩行了礼，刘秉璋很客气地请他“升炕”，平时他来看刘秉漳，本是在炕床上并坐的，但这天却再三谦辞，因为回头德馨要来，如果他升了炕，德馨只能坐在东面椅子上，未免委屈，所以他只坐在西面椅子上，留着上首的位子给德馨。此时此地，当然不必寒暄，胡雪岩开门见山他说：“职道没有想到今天。公私债务，无从料理，要请大人成全。““言重，言重！”刘秉璋说：“如今时局艰难，一切总以维持市面，安定人心为主。在这个宗旨之下，如果有可为雪翁略效绵薄之处，亦是我分内之事。”谈到这里，花厅外面有人高唱：“德大人到。”于是刘秉璋站了起来，而胡雪岩则到门口相迎。听差打开门帘，德馨人内，先向刘秉璋行了礼，然后转身道：“雪翁，你请这面坐！”说着，他占了胡雪岩原来的位置，将上首留给胡雪岩。“不，不！晓翁请上坐。”两人辞让了好一会，刘秉璋忍不住发话：“细节上不必争了。雪翁就坐在这面，说话比较方便。”听得这话，胡雪岩方始在靠迎刘秉璋的东首椅子上坐了下来，向对面的德馨问道：“我帐国已经带来了，是否现在就呈上刘大人？”“是，是，我看现在就上呈吧！”

Dexin had already sent someone ahead to receive him. As soon as Hu’s visiting card was presented, Liu Bingzhang admitted him to the western reception hall. Hu made the proper official salute, and Liu courteously invited him onto the kang. On ordinary visits they had sat together there, but today Hu repeatedly declined. Dexin would be coming shortly; if Hu occupied the kang, Dexin could only take the chair to the east, which would slight him. Hu therefore sat in the western chair, leaving the place of honor for Dexin. At such a time there was no need for small talk. Hu came straight to the point. “I never imagined I should reach this position, Your Excellency. I cannot settle my public or private debts and must ask your help.” “Please, there is no need to put it so strongly. These are difficult times. Our first concern must be to sustain trade and reassure the public. Whatever small service I can render you within that purpose, Mr Xueyan, is part of my duty.” Just then a voice outside announced, “His Excellency De!” Liu rose, while Hu went to the doorway to meet him. An attendant lifted the curtain. Dexin entered, first saluted Liu, then turned to Hu. “Mr Xueyan, please sit over here.” He took Hu’s former seat, leaving the place of honor to him. “No, no! That is your place, Mr Xiaofeng.” They exchanged courtesies for some time before Liu intervened. “No need to dispute over details. Sit on this side, Mr Xueyan. It will be easier to talk.” Hu finally took the eastern chair, nearer Liu, and asked Dexin opposite him, “I have brought the accounts. Shall I present them to His Excellency now?” “Yes, yes. I think you should.”

胡雪岩便起身将置在一旁的一厚叠帐簿，双手捧起，送上炕床，德馨也站起来帮着点交。帐傅一共六本，第一本是阜康钱庄连各地分号的总帐，第二本是二十九家当铺的档手及架本数目清帐，第三本是所有田地一万一千亩，座落的地点及田地等则的细帐，第四本是丝茧存货数量地点的清册，第四本是杂项财产，包括胡庆余堂药店在内的目录，第五本是私人财产清单，第六本便是存户名册。但各钱庄所开出的银票，列在第一本之内。刘秉璋只略翻一翻，便即搁下，等胡雪岩与德馨归座以后，他才问道：“雪翁这六本帐的收支总数如何？”“照帐面上来说，收支相抵，绰绰有余，不过欠人是实数，人欠就很难说了。”“所谓‘人欠’；包括货色在内。”德馨补充着说：“雪翁的丝茧，因为跟洋人斗法的缘故，将来只怕必须出之以‘拍卖，一途，能收回多少成本就很难说了。”

Hu rose, lifted the thick stack of account books placed beside him with both hands, and carried them to the kang. Dexin stood too and helped check them as they were handed over. There were six books in all. The first was the general ledger of Fukang Bank and all its branches. The second listed the managers and capital of the twenty-nine pawnshops. The third gave the locations and grades of all eleven thousand mu of land. The fourth inventoried the quantities and locations of the silk and cocoons in stock. The fourth listed miscellaneous property, including Hu Qingyu Hall. The fifth was an inventory of personal possessions, and the sixth a register of depositors. Notes issued by the various banks, however, appeared in the first book. Liu merely leafed through them and put them down. Once Hu and Dexin had resumed their seats, he asked, “What is the overall balance of these six books?” “On paper, there is far more coming to me than I owe. But what I owe is a definite sum; what is due to me is much less certain.” “‘What is due’ includes the goods,” Dexin explained. “Because of his struggle with the foreign merchants, Mr Xueyan may eventually have to sell his silk and cocoons by auction. How much of their cost he can recover is difficult to say.”

“何谓‘拍卖’？”“这是外国人的规矩。”胡雪岩说：“有意者彼此竞价。由底价叫起，只要有两个人出价，就一路往上叫，叫到没有人竟价，主持人拍一拍‘惊堂木，，就算敲定了。”“这样说，洋人可以勾通好，故意不竞价。”“不但故意不竟价，甚至不出价，那一来就只好把底价再往下压。”“照此而言，雪翁的丝茧值多少银子，根本无从估计？”“是！”“难。”刘秉璋转脸问道：“晓翁看，应该如何处理？”“只有先公后私，一步一步清理。”“也只好如此。”刘秉璋说：“现在朝廷的意思还不知道，我亦暂时只能在‘保管’二字上尽力。”他又问道：“雪翁，一时不会离开杭州吧？”

“What is an auction?” “A foreign practice,” Hu replied. “Those interested bid against one another. The bidding starts at a reserve price. So long as two people keep offering more, the price rises. When nobody bids further, the person presiding strikes a block of wood, like a magistrate’s desk block, and the sale is settled.” “Then the foreigners could agree among themselves and deliberately refrain from competing.” “They might not merely refuse to compete; they might refuse to bid at all. Then the reserve would have to be lowered.” “In that case, there is no way to estimate what your silk and cocoons are worth?” “Exactly.” “Difficult.” Liu turned to Dexin. “How do you think we should proceed, Mr Xiaofeng?” “Settle the public claims before the private ones, step by step.” “There seems no alternative. We do not yet know the court’s intentions. For now, I can only do my best to hold everything in safekeeping.” He added, “You won’t be leaving Hangzhou for the time being, will you?”

这句话问出来的暗含着有监视他的行踪的意味在内，胡雪岩略想一想，决定据实而陈。“回大人的话，职道想到上海去一趟，能够让丝茧不至于拍卖，于公于私，都有好处。”“呃，你要去多少时候？”“总得半个月。”刘秉璋微微颔首，视线若不经意似地转向德馨，却带着一种戒备与征询的神色。然后又转过脸来说：“雪翁，这半个月之中，万一有事一定要请你来面谈，怎么办？”胡雪岩还没有想到这一点，一时愣在那里，无从答言，不想德馨却代他回答了。“如果有这样的情形，请大人告诉我就是。”“好！”刘秉璋很爽快地答应：“雪翁，你干你的正经去吧！但望这半个月之中，你能料理出一个眉目来，只要公款不亏，私人不闹，我又何必多事？”“是，是。”胡雪岩站起身来，垂手哈着腰，“多仗大人成全。”“言重，言重！”说着，刘秉璋手已摸到茶碗上。

The question carried an implication that Hu’s movements were to be watched. After a moment’s thought, he decided to tell the truth. “Your Excellency, I should like to go to Shanghai. If I can prevent the silk and cocoons from being auctioned, it will benefit both the public and private interests involved.” “How long would you be away?” “At least half a month.” Liu nodded slightly, his eyes turning towards Dexin as if casually, though their expression was wary and inquiring. Then he looked back at Hu. “Suppose something arises during that half-month which requires me to speak to you in person. What then?” Hu had not considered this. He was momentarily nonplussed, unable to answer, but Dexin spoke for him. “If that happens, Your Excellency, please let me know.” “Very well!” Liu agreed readily. “Go about your business, Mr Xueyan. I only hope you can bring some order to matters within that half-month. So long as no public money is lost and private creditors make no trouble, why should I interfere?” “Yes, yes.” Hu rose, hands lowered, and bowed. “I am deeply indebted to Your Excellency’s kindness.” “Please, please.” As he spoke, Liu’s hand moved towards his teacup.

站在门口的戈会哈随即一面掀帘，一面向外高唱：“送客等胡雪岩一走，刘秉璋回到签押房，随即将一本由吏部分发到浙江的候补知县的名册取了出来，细细检阅，这本名册除了姓名、年龄、籍贯、出身、到省年月以外，另有两项记载，一项是曾派何差，如某年月派案某、某年月派解”京饷“之类，再一项便是此人的关系，是刘秉璋亲笔所注，如某中堂表亲、某年月日某尚书函托等等。刘秉璋现在要派二十九员候补知县的差使，根据四个条件来考虑。

The orderly at the doorway immediately raised the curtain and called out, “See the guest out!” Once Hu Xueyan had gone, Liu Bingzhang returned to his private office and took out the register of expectant county magistrates whom the Ministry of Personnel had assigned to Zhejiang. He examined it carefully. Besides each man’s name, age, native place, qualifications, and date of arrival in the province, the register contained two further kinds of information. One recorded previous assignments: an investigation undertaken in such-and-such a month and year, for instance, or the escorting of revenue silver to the capital. The other recorded his connections, in Liu’s own hand: a cousin of a certain grand secretary, or recommended by a particular minister in a letter of a certain date. Liu now had assignments for twenty-nine expectant magistrates and would make his choices according to four criteria.

第一个条件是出身，正途优先，假使是“榜下即用”的新科进士，一时无缺可补，甚至连署理都没有机会，当然毫不考虑地先派这个差使。一翻名册，这种情形只有三个人，当时在名册上一勾，还剩下二十六个人要派。两榜出身的进士以外，举人当然比军功保举及捐班来得占便宜，但须看第二个条件，即是其人的关系，如果曾有朝中大老的“八行”推毅，当然是在候选之列，但还要看第三个条件，最近派过差使没有？派的差使是苦是美？最近派过苦差使，为了“调剂”起见，不妨加以考虑，否则就要缓一缓了。费了好大的功夫，才将一张名单拟妥，即时派戈什哈个别通知，翌日上午到巡抚衙门等候传见。同时另抄一张全单，送交德馨作参考。

The first was qualifications, with priority going to men who had entered through the regular examination route. A newly successful jinshi designated for immediate appointment, but still unable to obtain a vacancy or even an acting post, would naturally receive one of these assignments without further consideration. Liu found only three such men in the register and marked their names, leaving twenty-six places to fill. After the jinshi, who had passed both the provincial and metropolitan examinations, provincial graduates naturally enjoyed an advantage over men recommended for military merit or admitted by purchase. But this depended on the second criterion: their connections. A letter of recommendation from a senior figure at court would certainly place a man among the candidates, though the third criterion still had to be considered. Had he received an assignment recently, and had it been onerous or lucrative? A man recently given an onerous task might be considered in the interests of balancing things out; otherwise, he would have to wait. It took considerable effort to complete the list. Liu then sent orderlies to notify the men individually that they were to await an audience at the governor’s office the next morning. A copy of the full list went to Dexin for his reference.

接到通知的二十九名候补州县官不敢怠慢，第二夭一大早，都备好了“手本”，齐集在抚院官厅待命。这天逢“衙参”之期，刘秉璋接见藩、桌二司及盐道、巡道、首府、首县——杭州知府及钱塘知县，一直到午牌时分，才轮到道班候补州县官进见，在座的还有德馨。知县见巡抚照例是有座位的，但人数太多，没有那么多椅子，值堂的差役去端了几张长条凳来，二十九位“大老爷”，挨挨挤挤地坐了下来，却还有两个人无处容身，一个赌气，退到廊下去听消息，一个做官善于巴结，看刘秉璋因为他还没有安顿好，不便开口，觉得让“宪台”久候，不好意思，便蹲了下来，臀部临空，双手按膝，仿佛已经落座似地。“今邀各位老哥来，有个差使要请各位分头去办。”刘秉璋说：“各位想必都已经从《申报》上看到了，胡观察的阜康银号倒闭，市面大受影响。阜康的存款之中，官款很多，不能没有着落。胡观察自愿拿他所开设的二十九家当铺，请我查封，备抵官款。现在就要请各位老哥，每人查封一家。“

The twenty-nine expectant department and county magistrates dared not neglect the summons. Early the next morning, with their formal visiting slips ready, they assembled in the waiting hall at the governor’s office. It happened to be a day for the regular official audience. Liu received the provincial treasurer and judicial commissioner, the salt and inspection circuit intendants, and the prefect and county magistrate of the provincial capital—the prefect of Hangzhou and the magistrate of Qiantang. It was noon before the expectant magistrates were admitted, with Dexin also present. County magistrates were ordinarily offered seats when they saw the governor, but there were too many men and too few chairs. The attendants brought in several long benches, and the twenty-nine “Your Honours” squeezed together. Even so, two men could find no room. One withdrew sulkily to the corridor to hear what happened; the other, more practised in ingratiating himself with his superiors, noticed that Liu was waiting for him to settle before beginning. Embarrassed to keep His Excellency waiting, he squatted down with his hands on his knees and his backside unsupported, as though he too were seated. “I have invited you gentlemen here because there is an assignment I wish each of you to undertake,” Liu said. “You have presumably read in the Shenbao that Circuit Intendant Hu’s Fukang Bank has failed, seriously disturbing the markets. Its deposits include a great deal of public money, which must be secured. Intendant Hu has voluntarily offered the twenty-nine pawnshops he owns for me to take into official custody as security for those funds. I now ask each of you to take charge of one.”

此言一出，无不诧异，却不敢发问，只有刚才虚蹲着的那人，因为双腿得无法忍受，正好装作发言，站起来舒舒筋骨。“回大人的话，这种差使，从来没有人当过，卑职不知道怎么样个当法？”“喔，”刘秉璋看了他一眼间道：“老哥贵姓？”“卑职姓马。“他叫马逢时，陕西人，刚至省不久。”德馨在一旁悄悄提示。刘秉璋点点头说：“马大哥的话不错，这种差使，我也是头一回遇到，不过，人不是生而知之的。各位莫非没有想到过，将来退归林下，也许会设典当谋生？收典当跟开典当是一样的，不外验资、查帐而已。”“再要请示。”马逢时又问：“验资、查帐以后，是不是封门。”“不是，不是。验资、查帐，如果毫无弊病，责成黄当管事，照旧经营。各位只要取具管事甘结，承认该典有多少资本，就可以交差了。“原来名为查封，其实是查而不封。接下来便由德馨主持抽签，马逢时抽到的，恰好是作为总号的公济典。

Everyone was surprised, but no one dared ask a question. Only the man suspended in his squat, whose legs had become unbearably painful, seized the chance to rise and stretch them under cover of speaking. “Your Excellency, no one has ever undertaken an assignment of this kind. I do not know how it is to be carried out.” “Oh?” Liu looked at him. “What is your surname, sir?” “Ma, Your Excellency.” “His name is Ma Fengshi, from Shaanxi. He arrived in the province only recently,” Dexin prompted quietly. Liu nodded. “Mr Ma is right. This is my first encounter with such an assignment too. But people are not born knowing everything. Have none of you considered that, when you eventually retire, you might open a pawnshop to support yourselves? Taking over a pawnshop is much the same as opening one. It amounts to verifying the capital and examining the accounts.” “May I ask further,” Ma said, “whether we are to seal the premises after verifying the capital and accounts?” “No, no. If the capital and accounts are found to be in order, hold the manager responsible for continuing the business as before. You need only obtain his written undertaking acknowledging the amount of capital held by the establishment, and your assignment will be complete.” So, though it was called sequestration, the premises were to be inspected rather than closed. Dexin then supervised the drawing of lots. Ma happened to draw Gongji Pawnshop, the principal establishment.

其时已在午后未未申初，当天查封，时间已不许可。马逢时领了公事回头，一个人坐着发愣，心里在想典当里又是帐目，又是“ 当头”，帐目则是那笔龙飞凤舞之字，比张旭、怀素的草书还要难识，“当头”则包罗万象，无所不有，自己一个人赤手空拳，如何盘查封存？而况公济典既然是总号，规模一定很大，倘或照顾不过来，查封之际出现了虚冒走漏等等情事，责任非轻。转念到此，愁眉不展，马太太不免困惑，一早兴冲冲上院，说有差使，看起来今年这个年是可以过得去了。不道一回来是这等神气，岂不可怪？

It was already about three in the afternoon, too late to carry out the inspection that day. Ma returned home with his official papers and sat alone, staring into space. A pawnshop meant both accounts and pledged articles. The accounts would be written in a flying scrawl harder to decipher than the cursive calligraphy of Zhang Xu or Huaisu; the pledges could include anything under the sun. How was he to inspect and secure it all single-handed, with no assistance? Gongji, being the principal shop, must be a large concern. If he failed to keep an eye on everything and fraudulent claims or concealed removals occurred during the takeover, his responsibility would be serious. His worried expression puzzled his wife. He had set off for the governor’s office so eagerly that morning, saying he had an assignment. It had looked as though they would be able to get through the New Year after all. Why had he returned in such a state?

这一来，少不得动问缘由，马逢时叹口气说：“派了个从来没有千过的差使，去查封胡财神的公济典。光是查帐验资，典当仍旧照常开门。你想，我连算盘都不会打，这个差使怎么顶得下来。”“马太太的想法不同，”到浙江来候补，只派过一个解饷的差使，靠当当过日子，朝奉的脸真难看。“她兴高彩烈他说：”想不到你会派这个差使，让我也出口气。“马逢时破颜一笑，“真正妇人之见。他说：”这个差使好处‘没有，倒霉有份。““怎么会倒霉？”“查帐，验资！如果我们动了手脚，将来责任都在我头上，吃不了，兜着走呢！”“我不懂你说的什么？”马太太想了一下说：“你何不去请教请教杨大哥？”

She had to ask. Ma sighed. “They have given me a task I have never done before: taking the God of Wealth Hu’s Gongji Pawnshop into official custody. I am only to examine the accounts and verify the capital; the shop is to remain open. Think of it—I cannot even use an abacus. How am I to manage?” His wife saw it differently. “Since we came to Zhejiang to wait for an appointment, you have had only that one assignment escorting revenue silver. We have lived by pawning things, and those pawnbrokers have given us such sour looks!” she said delightedly. “Who would have thought you would get this assignment? Now I can get a little of my own back.” Ma broke into a smile. “A woman’s view, indeed! This task offers no benefit, only a chance of trouble.” “How could it bring trouble?” “Examining accounts and verifying capital! If there has been any tampering, the responsibility will fall on my head. I shall have to bear all the consequences.” “I do not understand what you mean.” She thought for a moment. “Why not ask Brother Yang’s advice?”

这倒提醒了马逢时。原来这“杨大哥”是仁和县礼房的书办，住得不远，马逢时夫妇为人都很随和，并不看轻他的身分，平时“杨大哥、杨大哥”叫得很亲热。杨书办受宠若惊，也很照应马逢时，每年学台院试发榜，是他最忙的时候，有些土财主家的子弟中了秀才，请客开贺，总希望来几位有功名的贵客，壮壮门面，于是杨书办就会来通知马逢时，穿上官服，去当贺客，酒足饭饱，主人家还有一个红包，最少也有二两银子。一年象这样的机会总有七、八次，在马逢时也算受惠不浅了。因此，听了马太太的话，愁颜一展，唤他的儿子去请“杨伯伯”。杨书办这夭正好没有应酬，一请就到，动问何事。“我有个差使，不知道怎么办？还是内人有主意，说要请教杨大哥。“喔，马大老爷，”杨书办倒是按规矩来称呼：“是啥差使？”“查封当铺。”杨书办一愣，旋即笑道：“恭喜，恭喜！马大老爷，你好过个肥年了。”

This reminded Ma of a possibility. “Brother Yang” was a clerk in the rites section of the Renhe county office and lived nearby. Ma and his wife were easygoing people who did not look down on his position, always addressing him warmly as Brother Yang. Flattered by their kindness, the clerk did what he could for Ma. His busiest time came each year when the education commissioner posted the results of the qualifying examination. When the sons of wealthy country families won their first degree, their families gave celebratory banquets and hoped to attract a few distinguished guests with examination honours to lend the occasion prestige. Clerk Yang would notify Ma, who put on his official robes and attended. Besides being well fed and supplied with wine, he received a red envelope from the host containing at least two taels. There were usually seven or eight such opportunities a year, so Ma owed Yang a good deal. At his wife’s suggestion his face brightened, and he sent his son to invite “Uncle Yang.” The clerk happened to have no engagement that day and came at once, asking what was the matter. “I have an assignment I do not know how to carry out. My wife had the good sense to suggest asking your advice, Brother Yang.” “Oh, Your Honour”—Yang observed the proper form of address—“what sort of assignment?” “Taking a pawnshop into official custody.” Yang was startled, then smiled. “Congratulations! Congratulations! Your Honour, you will have a fat New Year.”

此言一出，马逢时的表情，顿时不同，又惊又喜地问：“杨大哥，你这话怎么说？”“我先请问，是不是查封胡大先生的当铺？”“是阿！”“哪一家？”“公济。”“嘿！那马大老爷，你这个年过得越发肥了。”马逢时心里越喜，但也越困感，搔搔头问：“我，我是看得到，吃不下。”“这话怎么说？”杨书办立即又是省悟的神情，“喔，马大老爷，你是说，不晓得怎么样下手，是不是？”“不错。”马逢时紧接着说：“要肥大家肥。杨大哥，你是诸葛亮，我是刘先生。”“不敢，不敢！等我想想，有个朋友，一定帮得上忙。”“杨大哥，你这位令友，今天找得找不到？你要知道，明天一早就要动手。”杨书办想起一个朋友，便是周少棠。从他的阜康门前“登台说法”，为胡雪岩解围以后，名气大为响亮，马逢时也知道有这样一个人，很乐意向他请教，但怕时间上来不及，因为查纣一事，次日上午便须见诸行动。“不要紧，不要紧！”杨书办看一看天色说：“这时候去正好，他在大井巷口隆和酒店吃酒。”大井巷在城隍山脚下，有口极大的甜水井，井的对面，就是隆和酒店，周少棠每天傍晚在那里喝酒，即令有饭局，也一定先到隆和打个照面，所以这时候去了，即令他不在，也会知道他的行踪。

Ma’s expression changed at once. Surprised and delighted, he asked, “Brother Yang, what do you mean?” “First let me ask: is it one of Mr Hu’s pawnshops?” “Yes.” “Which one?” “Gongji.” “Ha! Then your New Year will be fatter still.” Ma grew happier and more puzzled. Scratching his head, he said, “I can see the food, but I cannot get it into my mouth.” “What do you mean?” Understanding immediately dawned on Yang’s face. “Ah, Your Honour, you mean you do not know how to begin?” “Exactly.” Ma added at once, “If there is to be any fat, let us all share it. Brother Yang, you are Zhuge Liang, and I am Master Liu.” “You flatter me! Let me think. There is a friend who could certainly help.” “Can this friend of yours be found today? You see, I have to begin first thing tomorrow.” The friend Yang had in mind was Zhou Shaotang. Since his performance outside Fukang had relieved Hu’s predicament, Zhou’s reputation had grown considerably. Ma had heard of him and was very willing to seek his advice; he was only afraid there would not be time, since the takeover had to begin the following morning. “Do not worry.” Yang looked at the sky. “This is just the right time. He will be drinking at Longhe Tavern, by the entrance to Dajing Lane.” Dajing Lane lay at the foot of City God Hill and contained a very large well with sweet water. Longhe Tavern stood opposite it. Zhou went there for a drink every evening; even when invited to dinner elsewhere, he always put in an appearance first. If they went now, they could find out where he was even if he had already left.

当下安步当车，走到隆和，其实华灯初上，隆和正在上市。吃“柜台酒”的贩夫走卒，各倚着柜台，人各一碗，悠闲自在，其中识得杨书办的人很不少，纷纷招呼。杨书办一面答应，一面往里走——里面是一座敞厅，摆了十几张方桌，已上了七成座，杨书办站定看了一下，没有发现周少棠，便拉一个伙计问讯。“周先生来过走了。不过，停一停还要来。”伙计问道：“你老是等他，还是留话？”“我等他好了。”于是挑了一张位在僻处的桌子，两人坐了下来，要了酒慢慢喝着，喝到第三碗酒，周少棠来了。“少棠，少棠！”杨书办起身叫唤，将他拉了过来说道：“我们等你好半天了。我先来引见，这位是马大老爷，”周少棠是很外场的人，对马逢时很客气地敷衍了一阵。等酒到微酣，杨书办方始道明来意，马逢时随即举杯相敬：“我对当铺一窃不通，接了这个差使，不知道该怎么办？”他说：“全要仰仗周先生指点。”“好说，好说。”周少棠一面应答，一面在肚子里做功夫。他跟公济典的唐子韶，只是点头之交，但阜康的谢云青，却跟他很熟，最近的过从更密，从谢云青口中，知道了紧邻公济典的好些秘密，这当然也就是唐子韶的秘密。

They walked leisurely to Longhe. The lamps had just been lit, and business was getting under way. Hawkers and labourers drinking at the counter leaned there at their ease, each with a bowl. Many knew Clerk Yang and greeted him. Answering as he went, Yang made his way inside to an open hall containing more than a dozen square tables, about seven-tenths of them occupied. He stopped to look, saw no sign of Zhou, and caught a waiter to ask. “Mr Zhou has been and gone, but he will be back shortly. Would you like to wait or leave a message?” “I shall wait.” They chose a table in a quiet corner, ordered wine, and drank slowly. Zhou arrived as they were on their third bowl. “Shaotang! Shaotang!” Yang rose and drew him over. “We have been waiting ages. Let me introduce you. This is Magistrate Ma.” Zhou was adept in company and spent some time exchanging courtesies with Ma. Only when the wine had put them pleasantly at ease did Yang explain why they had come. Ma immediately raised his bowl in a toast. “I know nothing whatever about pawnshops. Now I have accepted this assignment, I have no idea how to carry it out. I must rely entirely on your guidance, Mr Zhou.” “You are very kind,” Zhou replied, while working things out in his mind. He and Gongji’s Tang Zishao were merely nodding acquaintances, but he knew Xie Yunqing of Fukang well and had seen a great deal more of him lately. From Xie he had learned quite a few secrets about neighbouring Gongji—and those, of course, were Tang’s secrets too.

周少棠很看不起唐子韶，同时因为与胡雪岩是贫贱之交，情分不同，所以对唐子韶在胡雪岩遭遇这样沉重的打击，不想想平日所受的提携，拿出良心来共患难，反而乘人于危，趁火打劫，在公济典中大动手脚，暗中侵吞，大为不平。如今恰有这样一个马逢时可以去查帐的机会，岂可错过。“马大老爷，人家都说我周少棠好说大话，做起事来不扎实。所以，查封公济典这件事，我不想多说啥，只有一句话奉告，马大老爷把我这句话想通摸透，包你差使办得漂亮。”周少棠停了一下说：“这句话叫做：”看帐不如看库，验资不如验货‘。“马逢时一愣，因为周少棠的两句话开场白颇为突兀，有点发牢骚的意味在内，因而嗫嚅着说：“周先生我们今天是初会，我从没有说过那些话……”“啊，啊，误会了误会了。马大老爷，我不是说你，也不是说杨大哥，不过因为今天正好有人这样子说我，顺便一提。”周少棠又说：“马大老爷，你不是要我指点？我刚才那两句话，就是把‘总筋’指点给你看，你要看清楚，想透彻。”原来刚才那种近乎牢骚的话，是周少棠为引起交谈对方注意的一种方式，经此折冲，马逢时已将“看帐不如看库，验资不如看货”十二个字深印入脑中，当即作出受教的神色说道：“周先生，你这两句话，从字面上说，就大有学问在里头，索性请你明明白白地开导一番。”

Zhou had a very low opinion of Tang. His own friendship with Hu dated from their days of poverty, which gave it a particular depth. Now that Hu had suffered such a heavy blow, Tang ought to have remembered all the help he had received and shown enough conscience to stand by him. Instead, he was taking advantage of Hu’s distress, manipulating Gongji’s affairs and secretly embezzling its funds. Zhou bitterly resented it. Here was an opportunity to have Ma examine the accounts; how could he let it pass? “Your Honour, people say I talk big and never do anything properly. So I shall not say much about taking Gongji into custody. I have just one piece of advice. Understand it thoroughly, and I guarantee you will carry out the assignment splendidly.” He paused. “It is this: ‘Better to inspect the storeroom than read the books; better to examine the goods than verify the capital.’” Ma was taken aback. Zhou’s opening had been abrupt and sounded rather like a complaint. “Mr Zhou,” he stammered, “this is our first meeting. I have never said anything of the kind...” “Ah, a misunderstanding! I did not mean you, Your Honour, or Brother Yang. Someone happened to say that about me today, so I mentioned it in passing.” Zhou continued, “Did you not ask for guidance? Those two phrases point out the central thread. You must see it clearly and think it through.” His almost aggrieved opening had merely been a device to seize the other man’s attention. After this exchange, those twelve Chinese characters were firmly imprinted on Ma’s mind. Looking duly receptive, he said, “Mr Zhou, even on the surface those words contain a great deal of learning. Please go further and explain them plainly.”

“言重，言重。”周少棠问道：“马大老爷，典当的规矩，你懂不懂？”“我刚才不说过，一窃不通。”“那就难怪了……”“老周，”杨书办忍不住了，“你不必城头大出丧，大兜大转了。马大老爷明天去查封，要留意哪几件事，请你细说一说。”“是的。”马逢时接口，“还有，一去要怎样下手？”周少棠心想，查封胡雪岩的典当，是为了备抵存在阜康的公款，能多保全一分，胡雪岩的责任即轻一分，因此，能将唐子韶在公济典侵吞的款子追出来，对胡雪岩就是最直接、也最切实的帮忙。转念到此，他决定插手干预。于是他问：“马大老爷去查封公济典，有没有委札？”“有。不过交代是抚台交代，委札是藩台所出。”“那一样，都是宪台。”周少棠又问：“领了封条没有？”“领了”“几帐？”“两张。”“怎么只领两张呢？”“我以为查封是封前后门，所以只领了两张。”马逢时又说：“后来想想不对，抚台交代，查封归查封，当铺还是照常取赎。既然如此，纣了门，岂非当主不能上门了。”“不独当主不能上门，公济的人也不能进出了。”周少棠想了一下说：“不过不要紧，马大老爷今天就去刻一个长条戳，上面的字是：”奉宪谕查封公济典委员候补知县马，。凭这个长条戳，马大老爷自己就可以封。“

“You are too kind,” Zhou said. “Do you understand pawnshop practices, Your Honour?” “Did I not say I knew nothing about them?” “Then it is no wonder...” “Old Zhou,” Yang interrupted impatiently, “stop leading us on a grand funeral procession round the city walls. His Honour has to take charge tomorrow. Tell him plainly what to watch for.” “Yes,” Ma added. “And how should I begin when I arrive?” Zhou reflected that Hu’s pawnshops were being taken into custody to secure the public money deposited with Fukang. Every additional sum preserved would reduce Hu’s liability. Recovering what Tang had embezzled from Gongji would therefore be the most direct and practical help he could offer Hu. He decided to intervene. “Have you an official warrant for this assignment?” “Yes. The instructions came from the governor, but the warrant was issued by the treasurer.” “That makes no difference. Both are your superiors. Have you collected any sealing strips?” “Yes.” “How many?” “Two.” “Why only two?” “I thought taking the premises into custody meant sealing the front and back doors, so I took only two. Afterwards I realised that could not be right. The governor said the shop was to continue allowing customers to redeem their pledges. If I sealed the doors, how could they come in?” “Nor could Gongji’s own people get in or out.” Zhou thought for a moment. “But that does not matter. Have an oblong stamp cut today, bearing the words: ‘By order of His Excellency: Commissioner Ma, Expectant County Magistrate, appointed to take Gongji Pawnshop into official custody.’ With that stamp, you can apply seals yourself.”

“嗯，嗯，”马逢时一面想一面点头：“我应该有这人权柄。”“当然有。”“周先生，，‘马逢时问道：”明天我去了，第一步做什么？第二步做什么？请你给我说一说。““这，这要看情形，现在很难说。”说着，周少棠望一望杨书办。一直很冷静在旁听的杨书办，知道该他说话了：“马大老爷，我看你要请少棠去帮忙。”“是啊，是啊！”马逢时一叠连声他说：“我就有这样一个打算，不过不知道合不合公事上的规矩？”“怎么会不合？譬如马大老爷你‘挂牌’放了实缺，起码要请刑名、钱谷两位师爷，现在请少常去帮忙，也是同样的道理。”“是，是！这个譬喻通极。”马逢时双手举起酒杯：“周先生，请你帮忙。不过，惭愧的是，现在还谈不到什么敬意，只有感激在心里。”于是商定几个步骤，其实也就是周少棠在发号司令，马逢时要做的是，连夜将长条戳刻好，第二天一早在开市以前，便须到达公济典，首行要贴出一张告示：“奉宪谕查封，暂停营业一天。”然后分头查村，最要紧的是库房跟银柜。“这就要看帐了。‘看帐不如看库，验资不如验货’，此话怎讲？因为帐是呆的，帐面上看不出啥。到库房看过，再拿帐来对照，真假弊病就一目了然了。”

“Yes, yes.” Ma nodded thoughtfully. “I ought to have that authority.” “Of course you do.” “Mr Zhou, what should I do first tomorrow, and what should I do next? Please tell me.” “Well, that depends on what we find. It is difficult to say now.” Zhou glanced at Yang. The clerk, who had been listening calmly, knew his turn had come. “Your Honour, I think you should ask Shaotang to help you.” “Yes, indeed!” Ma answered eagerly. “I had just that in mind, but I did not know whether it would conform to official practice.” “Why should it not? If you received a substantive appointment and opened your own office, you would engage at least two secretaries, one for legal affairs and one for revenue. Asking Shaotang to help now is the same sort of thing.” “Quite so! An excellent comparison.” Ma raised his bowl with both hands. “Mr Zhou, please help me. I am ashamed to say I cannot yet offer any token of appreciation—only my heartfelt gratitude.” They then agreed on several steps, though in fact Zhou was issuing the instructions. Ma was to have the oblong stamp cut that night and reach Gongji before business began the next morning. His first action would be to post a notice: “Taken into official custody by order of His Excellency. Business suspended for one day.” They would then divide up the inspection, concentrating above all on the storeroom and the silver chest. “Then we shall examine the books. Why did I say it was better to inspect the storeroom than read the books, and to examine the goods than verify the capital? Because the books are lifeless things; you cannot see much from the figures alone. Inspect the storeroom first, then compare it with the accounts, and truth, falsehood, and malpractice will be clear at a glance.”

“是，是。请教周先生，这姓唐的有哪些弊病？”马逢时间。“我也是听说，到底如何，要明天去看了才晓得。”周少棠说：“第一种是满当的货色上动脑筋，当本轻、东西好，这也有两种脑筋好动，一种是掉包，譬如大毛的皮统子，换成二毛的，还有一种……”“慢慢，周先生，请问这个弊病要怎么查？”“容易。一种是看帐，不过当铺里的帐，总是好的写成坏的，所以不如估价。”周少棠说：“朝奉的本事就在看货估价，决不会走眼，大毛是大毛的价钱，二毛是二毛的价钱，你拿同样的货色来比较，问它同样的当价，为啥一个大老，一个是二毛？他话说不清楚，里头就有弊病了。”“我懂了。请问还有一种呢？”“还有一种说是赎走了，其实是他占了满当的便宜。要查封这种弊病也不难，叫他拿销号的原票出来看，有，是真的赎走了，没有，就是当主根本没有来赎。”

“Yes, yes. What sort of malpractice has this Tang been guilty of, Mr Zhou?” Ma asked. “I have only heard reports. We shall not know exactly until we go tomorrow. The first kind concerns pledges whose redemption period has expired. If the loan is small and the article valuable, there are two tricks he can play. One is substitution: replacing a heavy fur lining with one of lighter fur, for example. The other...” “A moment, Mr Zhou. How do we detect that first trick?” “Easily. One way is to read the accounts, but pawnshop books always describe good things as poor ones, so valuation is better. A pawnbroker’s skill lies in judging and valuing goods; he will not get it wrong. Heavy fur commands one price and lighter fur another. Compare similar articles and ask why, if the loan amounts are the same, one pledge is heavy fur and the other light. If he cannot explain it, something is wrong.” “I understand. And the other trick?” “He says the pledge has been redeemed, when in fact he has appropriated the valuable article after its term expired. That is not difficult to detect either. Ask him to produce the original pawn ticket cancelled on redemption. If he has it, the pledge was genuinely redeemed. If not, the customer never came to redeem it at all.”

处理满当货的弊端，马逢时大致已经了解，但是否还有其他毛病呢？问到这一点，周少棠的答复是肯定的，而且词色之间，颇为愤慨。“这个姓唐的，真是狗彘不如！今日之下，他居然要趁火打劫，真正丧尽天良。”原来唐子韶从早康出事以后，认为胡雪岩之垮只是迟早间事，公济典当然也保不住了，既然如此，且趁眼前还能为所欲为之时正捞一笔。“他的手法很毒，不过说穿了一个钱不值，弄个破铜表来算是金表，一当十两、八两银子，马大老爷，你说，这是不是放抢？”“太可恶了！”马逢时亦是义形于色，“在满当货上动手脚，还可以说是取巧，因为东家的本息到底已经收回了，只不过没有占到额外的好处而已。象这样子，以假作真，以贱为贵，诈欺东家，是可以重办他的罪的。““当然应该重办。”周少棠冷笑一声：“他自以为聪明，假货要到满当没有人来赎，盘库日验货，才会发现，那时他已回徽州老家了，你就告他，他也可以赖，说当初原是金表，不晓得怎么掉包了。也没有想到，偏偏会遇到你马大爷，又遇到我，不等满当，就要办它一个水落石出，这叫‘人有千算，天只一算’。“

Ma now had a general understanding of the abuses involved in handling expired pledges. But were there others? Zhou’s answer was emphatically yes, and his voice and expression showed considerable indignation. “This Tang is worse than a beast! To plunder his employer at a time like this—he has no conscience left.” Since Fukang’s troubles began, Tang had believed Hu’s collapse only a matter of time. Gongji could not survive it either. He might as well seize what he could while he was still free to do as he pleased. “His method is vicious, though once explained it is worth nothing. He brings in a broken brass watch, treats it as a gold one, and advances eight or ten taels on it. Your Honour, is that not outright robbery?” “Abominable!” Ma too looked righteously indignant. “Tampering with expired pledges might at least be called sharp practice: after all, the proprietor has recovered his principal and interest and merely loses an additional profit. But passing off false goods as genuine and cheap goods as valuable to defraud the proprietor is an offence that can be severely punished.” “And severely punished it should be.” Zhou gave a cold laugh. “He thinks himself clever. The fake goods would not be discovered until the pledges expired without being redeemed and the storeroom was checked. By then he would be back home in Huizhou. Even if you prosecuted him, he could deny it: the watch had originally been gold, and he had no idea how it had been switched. He never expected to run into you and me, Your Honour. Before the pledges expire, we shall get to the bottom of it. As the saying goes, ‘A man may make a thousand calculations; Heaven needs only one.’”

谈到这里杨书办插嘴了，“唐子韶总还有同党吧？”他说，“朝奉是很爱惜名誉的，如果有为唐子韶勾结、欺骗东家这个名声在外，以后就没有人敢请教他，只好改行了。”“老杨，你问得好。唐子韶自然有同党；不过这个同党，同他的关系不同，是他一手提拔起来的外甥。”“嗯，嗯！这就是了。唐子韶预备卷铺盖了，当然也要带了他一起走。”“一点不错。”周少棠转脸说道：“马大老爷，你明天去了，就要着落在唐子韶的外甥身上，追究真相。要格外留心最近的帐，拿当得多的几笔，对帐验货，如果货帐不符，再问是哪个经的手？第一步只要这样就可以了，”“你是说当时不要追究？”“对，当时不要追究，因为当时一问，唐子韶一定有番花言巧语，打草惊蛇，不是聪明的办法？”“那么，怎么是聪明的办法呢？”“把唐子韶的外甥带走，另外找个地方去间。那些小生后经不起吓，一吓什么都说出来了。”周少棠又说：“最好到县衙门里惜两名差役带了去，威风更足，事情也就更容易办了。”“是，是，这倒容易，仁和县的王大老爷，我很熟。”马逢时越听越有兴趣，很起劲地问：“问出来以后呢？”是不是再传唐子韶来问。“

Yang spoke up. “Tang must have an accomplice. Pawnbrokers value their reputations. If a man became known for conspiring with Tang to cheat his employer, no one would engage him again; he would have to change his trade.” “A good question, Old Yang. Tang certainly has an accomplice, but the relationship is a special one: his sister’s son, whom he has advanced entirely through his own efforts.” “Ah, that explains it. If Tang is preparing to pack up and leave, he will naturally take the nephew with him.” “Exactly.” Zhou turned to Ma. “Tomorrow you must get at the truth through Tang’s nephew. Pay particular attention to the recent entries. Select several of the largest advances and compare the pledged goods with the accounts. If the goods do not match the entries, ask who handled the transactions. That is all you need do at first.” “You mean I should not pursue the matter on the spot?” “Exactly. If you ask then, Tang will have some plausible story ready. Alerting him before you are prepared is hardly wise.” “What would be wise, then?” “Take his nephew away and question him elsewhere. These youngsters cannot stand a fright; frighten them and they tell you everything.” Zhou added, “Better still, borrow two runners from the county office and take them with you. You will look more imposing, and it will make the work easier.” “Yes, that is easy. I know Magistrate Wang of Renhe well.” The more Ma heard, the keener he became. “And after we have the answers? Do we summon Tang for questioning?”

“用不着你去传他，他自己会到府上来求见。”“何以见得？”“这……”周少棠迟疑一下，说声：“我先同老杨说句话。”“他将杨书办拉到一边，悄悄问他跟马逢时的关系。杨书办据实以告，周少棠便另有话问了。“快过年了，马木老爷当然要弄几个过年盘缠是不是？”“当然。”杨书办问：“你的意思是要他敲唐子韶一笔？”“不错，不过，公私要兼顾，他可以同唐子韶提条件：条一，要他拿原当赎回去，这是公，第二，要弄几两银子过年，数目他自己同唐子韶去谈……或者，同你谈。如果唐子韶不就范，报上去请他吃官司。“杨书办盘算了一下，觉得其事可行，笑笑说道：“你对胡大先生倒是蛮够朋友。”“贫贱之交不可忘。”周少棠掉了句文，虽然有些不伦，却不能说他这句话不通。

“You will not need to summon him. He will come to your house and ask to see you.” “What makes you so sure?” “Well...” Zhou hesitated. “Let me have a word with Old Yang first.” Drawing the clerk aside, he quietly asked about his relationship with Ma. Yang told him truthfully, and Zhou asked another question. “The New Year is approaching. His Honour will naturally want to find a little money to see him through it?” “Of course. You mean he should squeeze something out of Tang?” “Exactly. But both public and private interests must be considered. He can give Tang two conditions. First, Tang must redeem the pledged articles himself: that protects the public interest. Second, he must provide a few taels for the New Year. His Honour can negotiate the amount with Tang—or you can. If Tang refuses, report him and let him face prosecution.” Yang considered it, decided the scheme was workable, and smiled. “You really are a good friend to Mr Hu.” “One must not forget the friends of one’s poverty,” Zhou replied, dropping into a literary phrase. The quotation was not altogether appropriate, but neither could one say it made no sense.

两人再深入地谈了一下，自然而然地出现了一种演变，即是襄助马逢时的工作，由周少棠移转到杨书办身上。不过周少棠仍在幕后支援，商定他在阜康钱庄对面的一家安利茶店喝茶，公济典近在咫尺，有事随时可以接头。等相偕回到原座，周少棠作了交代，“马大者爷，”他说：“你同杨书办很熟，明天请他陪了你去，有啥话说起来也方便。其中的窍门，我同杨书办说过了，这桩差使，一定可以办得漂亮。”说着起身告辞而去。其时已是万家灯火，酒客络绎而至，热闹非凡，说话轻了听不见，重了又怕泄漏机密，杨书办提议另外找个地方去喝酒。“到哪里？”“你跟我去，不过，”杨书办声明在行先，“马大老爷，到了那个地方，我不便用尊称，一叫马大者爷，露了相不好。”“不要紧，你叫我老马好了。”“最好连姓都不要用真的。你们老太太尊姓？”“姓李。”“我就叫你老李了。离这里不远，我们走了去。”

As they discussed the matter further, a change came about naturally: the task of assisting Ma passed from Zhou to Yang. Zhou would still support them from behind the scenes. They agreed that he would sit drinking tea at Anli Tea House, opposite Fukang Bank. Gongji was only a step away, so they could contact him whenever necessary. Returning to the table together, Zhou explained, “Your Honour, you and Clerk Yang know each other well. Ask him to accompany you tomorrow; it will be easier to discuss anything that arises. I have told him the essential points, and this assignment will certainly go well.” He then rose, said goodbye, and left. By now lights shone from every house, and drinkers were streaming into the tavern. It was extremely noisy. If they spoke softly they could not be heard; if loudly, they risked revealing their secrets. Yang suggested going elsewhere for another drink. “Where?” “Come with me. But I must say this first: when we get there, I cannot address you by your title. Calling you ‘Your Honour’ would give you away.” “Never mind. Call me Old Ma.” “Better not use your real surname either. What is your honoured mother’s surname?” “Li.” “Then I shall call you Old Li. It is not far. Let us walk.”

第七章 大封典铺｜CHAPTER SEVEN: THE MASS SEQUESTRATION OF THE PAWNSHOPS

杨书办惠了帐，带着马逢时穿过两条街，进入一条曲曲折折的小巷，在巷底有一家人家，双扉紧闭，但门旁有一盏油灯，微弱的光焰，照出一张退了色的梅红笺，上写“孙寓”二字。“这是什么地方？”马逢时有些不安地问。“马……”杨书办赶紧顿住，“老李，这个地方你不能告诉李大嫂。”一听这话，马逢时不再作声，只见杨书办举手敲门，三急三缓，刚刚敲完，大门呀地一声开了，一个半老徐娘，高举着“手照”说：“我道哪个，是你。算算你也应该来了。”接着，脸上浮满了笑容又问：“这位是……”“李老板。”杨书办紧接着问：“楼上有没有客人？”“没有。”“楼下呢？”“庆余堂的老朱同朋友在那里吃酒，就要走的。”“他们东家遭难，他倒还有心思吃花酒。”杨书办又说：“你不要说我在这里。”“多关照的。”那半老徐娘招呼“李老板”说：“请你跟我来。走好！”于是一行三人，由堂屋侧面的楼梯上楼，楼上一大两小三个房间，到了当中大房间，等主人剔亮了灯，杨书办方为马逢时引见。“她姓孙。你叫她孙干娘好了。”马逢时已经了然，这里是杭州人所说的“私门头”，而孙干娘便是鸨儿，当即笑嘻嘻地说道：“孙子娘的子女儿一定很多？”“有，有。”孙子娘转脸问杨书办：“先吃茶还是先吃酒？”“茶也要，酒也要，还要吃饭。”说着，杨书办拉着孙干娘到外房，过了好一会才进来。

Clerk Yang paid the bill and led Ma Fengshi across two streets into a winding lane. At its end stood a house with both doors shut. An oil lamp beside the entrance cast a feeble light on a faded rose-red slip of paper bearing the words “Sun Residence.” “What is this place?” Ma asked uneasily. “Ma…” Yang checked himself. “Old Li, you must not tell Mrs Li about this place.” Ma said no more. Yang knocked three times quickly and three times slowly. As he finished, the door creaked open. A middle-aged woman, still attractive, held up a hand lantern. “I wondered who it was. You! I thought it was about time you came.” Her face filled with smiles. “And this gentleman is…?” “Mr Li,” Yang answered, then asked at once, “Any guests upstairs?” “No.” “Downstairs?” “Old Zhu from Qingyu Hall is drinking with some friends. They will be leaving soon.” “His employer is in trouble, yet he still has a mind for courtesan parties! Do not tell him I am here.” “As if I needed reminding!” The woman turned to “Mr Li.” “Come with me, please. Mind your step.” The three of them went up the stairs beside the main room. Upstairs were three rooms, one large and two small. In the central room, once their hostess had brightened the lamp, Yang introduced her. “Her surname is Sun. You can call her Auntie Sun.” Ma now understood: this was what Hangzhou people called a private brothel, and Auntie Sun was its madam. Smiling broadly, he said, “You must have a great many daughters, Auntie Sun?” “Indeed I do.” She turned to Yang. “Tea first, or wine?” “Both—and we shall want a meal as well.” He drew her into the outer room and returned some time later.

“这个孙干娘，倒是徐娘半老，丰韵犹存。”马逢时说道。“怎么？你倒看中她了！我来做媒。”“算了，算了！我们先谈正事。”这话正好符合杨书办的安排，他已关照好孙干娘备酒备饭，要讲究，但不妨慢慢来，公便跟马逢时先谈妥了明日之事，再开怀畅饮。“你的事归我来接下半段。我先问你，你年底有多少帐？”马逢时一愣，约莫估计了一下说：“总要五六十两银子才能过关。”“我晓得了。”杨书办说：“明天我陪了你去，到了公济典，你看我的眼色行事。”何谓看眼色行事？马逢时在心里好好想了一会问道：“杨大哥……”“慢点，慢点。”杨书办硬截断了他的话，“明天在公济典，你可不能这样叫我。”“我明白。做此官，行此札，到那时候，我自然会官派十足地叫你杨书办，你可不要生气。”“不会，不会。这不过是唱出戏而已。”“这出戏你是主角。”马逢时问：“你认识不认识唐子韶。”“怎么不认识，不过没有什么交情。”“你认识最好，我想明天我做红脸，你做白脸，遇见有不对的地方，我打官腔，你来转圜，唐子韶当然就要找上你了，什么事可以马虎，什么事不能马虎，我都听你的语气来办。““一点不错。”杨书办很欣慰他说，“我们好好儿来唱他一出‘得胜回朝’。”

“Auntie Sun may be past her first youth, but she still has plenty of charm,” Ma remarked. “What? Have you taken a fancy to her? I shall be your matchmaker.” “Enough of that! Let us discuss our business first.” This suited Yang’s arrangements perfectly. He had instructed Auntie Sun to prepare good wine and a good meal, but to take her time, so he could settle tomorrow’s business with Ma before they drank freely. “Leave the rest of your business to me. First, how much do you owe at the year’s end?” Ma was taken aback. After a rough calculation, he said, “I shall need fifty or sixty taels to get through it.” “I understand. I shall go with you tomorrow. Once we reach Gongji Pawnshop, take your cue from my eyes.” What exactly did that mean? Ma pondered it for a while. “Brother Yang…” “Wait!” Yang cut him short. “You must not address me like that at Gongji tomorrow.” “I understand. When holding an office, observe its forms. I shall call you ‘Clerk Yang’ in my grandest official manner. Do not take offence.” “Of course not. We are only putting on a performance.” “You are the leading player. Do you know Tang Zishao?” “Naturally, though we are not close.” “Good. Tomorrow I shall play the stern red face and you the kindly white. If anything is wrong, I shall speak with official severity and you can smooth matters over. Tang will naturally turn to you. Whether something can be overlooked or must not be, I shall follow the tone you take.” “Exactly!” Yang said with satisfaction. “We shall give a fine performance of Returning to Court in Triumph.”

谈到这里，楼梯上有响声，只见帘启处，孙干娘在前，后面跟着女佣，手中端一个大托盘，四样酒菜，两副杯筷。“怎么只有两副？”杨书办问。“我怕你们要谈事情，不要旁人来打搅。“谈好了，再去添两副来。”杨书办问：“巧珍在不在？”“今天没有来。”孙干娘说：“阿兰在这里，不晓得李老板看得中，看不中？”杨书办心中一动，因为看到马逢时目不转睛地看着孙干娘，决心成全他们这一段露水姻缘，当即说道：“等一等再说。你先陪我们吃两杯。”于是又去添了杯筷来，孙干娘为客人布菜斟酒，颇为周到，马逢时不住地夸赞酒好菜好，杨书办只是微笑不语。看看是时候了，他问：“庆余堂的老朱还没有走吧？”“还没有？”“我下楼去看一看他。”杨书办站起身来，对孙干娘说：“你陪李老板多吃几杯，我的好朋友，你要另眼相看。”于是杨书办扬长下楼，叫相帮进去通知，床余堂的老朱，满脸通红地迎了出来，“老杨，老杨！”他拉着他的手说：“请进来吃酒。”“方便不方便。”“方便，方便。不是你的熟人，就是我的熟人。”进去一看，四个人中只有一个不认识，请教姓名，才知道是老朱的同事。杨书办之来闯席，一则是故意避开，好让马逢时有跟孙千娘勾搭的机会，再则便是打听庆余堂的情形，尤其使他困惑而又好奇的是，胡雪岩的全盘事业，都在风雨飘摇之中，何以老朱竟还兴高采烈地在这里寻欢作乐。

Footsteps sounded on the stairs. The curtain lifted, and Auntie Sun entered, followed by a maid carrying a large tray with four dishes and two sets of cups and chopsticks. “Why only two?” Yang asked. “I thought you had business to discuss and would not want to be disturbed.” “We have finished. Bring two more sets. Is Qiaozhen here?” “She has not come today. A’lan is here, though. I do not know whether Mr Li would care for her.” Noticing that Ma could not take his eyes off Auntie Sun, Yang decided to bring about a brief liaison between them. “We shall see later,” he said. “Have a couple of cups with us first.” More cups and chopsticks were brought. Auntie Sun served the guests attentively, and Ma kept praising the wine and food. Yang merely smiled. When he thought the time was right, he asked, “Old Zhu from Qingyu Hall has not left yet?” “Not yet.” “I shall go down and see him.” Rising, Yang told Auntie Sun, “Keep Mr Li company over a few more cups. He is a good friend of mine. You must treat him especially well.” He went downstairs and had an attendant announce him. Old Zhu came out, his face flushed scarlet. “Yang! Come in for a drink!” he said, taking his hand. “Would it be convenient?” “Certainly. Everyone is either a friend of yours or a friend of mine.” Inside, Yang knew three of the four men. On asking the fourth man’s name, he learned that he was Zhu’s colleague. Yang had joined the party partly to leave Ma an opportunity to make advances to Auntie Sun and partly to find out how Qingyu Hall was faring. What especially puzzled him was how Zhu could be enjoying himself so heartily when all Hu Xueyan’s businesses were in peril.

席间一一应酬过了，一巡酒下来有人提起阜康的风波，这是最近轰动南北的大新闻，凡是应酬场中，几乎无一处不资以为谈助。杨书办只是静静地听着，等到谈得告一段落时，他开口了。“老朱，你在庆余堂是啥职司？”“我管查验。”“查验？”杨书办问：“查验点啥？查验货色？你又不是药材行出身，药材‘路脚’正不正，你又不懂。”“货色好坏不懂，斤两多少还不会看？等看货的老先生说药材地道，过秤时就要请我了。”老朱又说：“不过，我顶重要的一项职司，是防备货色偷漏。”“有没有抓到过。”“当然抓到过，不过不多。”“你说不多；只怕已经偷漏了的，你不晓得。“不会。”老朱停了一下说：“老实说，你就叫人偷漏，你们也不肯。你倒想，饭碗虽不是金的、银的，至少也是铁的，一生一世敲不破；工钱之外有花红，遇到夏天有时疫流行，上门的主顾排长龙等药，另外有津贴。再说家里大人、小伢儿有病痛，用药不管丸散膏丹，再贵重的都是白拿，至于膏滋药、药酒，收是收钱，不过比成本还要低。如果贪便宜，偷了一两支人参，这些好处都没有了，你想划得来，划不来？“

After the greetings and a round of drinks, someone mentioned the crisis at Fukang. It was the great news of the day throughout the country, discussed at almost every social gathering. Yang listened quietly until there was a pause. “Zhu, what exactly is your job at Qingyu Hall?” “I handle inspections.” “Inspections of what? The quality of the goods? You did not start in the medicinal-herb trade. You cannot tell whether the ingredients come from the proper sources.” “I may not know their quality, but I can read a weight! Once the experienced men pronounce the herbs genuine, they call me to supervise the weighing. My most important duty, though, is preventing goods from being stolen or spirited away.” “Have you ever caught anyone?” “Of course, but not many.” “You say not many. Perhaps goods have disappeared without your knowing.” “No.” Zhu paused. “To be frank, even if you urged the men to steal, they would refuse. Think of it: their rice bowls may not be gold or silver, but they are at least iron, unbreakable for a lifetime. Besides wages, there are bonuses. When summer epidemics bring customers queuing for medicines, there is an extra allowance. If an adult or child at home falls ill, medicines—pills, powders, pastes or pellets—are free, however costly. They do pay for tonic pastes and medicinal wines, but at less than cost. Steal a root or two of ginseng out of greed, and all those benefits vanish. Would that be worth it?”

“你的话是不错，不过这回恐怕要连根铲了！”“你是说胡大先生的生意怕会不保？别的难说，庆余堂一定保得住。”“为啥？”“有保障。”老朱从从容容地说：“这回阜康的事情出来，我们的档手同大家说：胡大先生办得顶好的事业，就是我们庆余堂。不但挣钱，还替胡大先生挣了名声。如果说亏空公款，要拿庆余堂封了抵债，货色生财，都可以入官，庆余堂这块招脾拿不出去的。庆余堂是简称，正式的招牌是胡庆余堂，如果老板不姓胡了，怎么还好用庆余堂的招牌。所以官府一定不会封庆余堂，仍旧让胡大先生来当老板。大家要格外巴结，抓药要道地，对待客人要和气，这只饭碗一定捧得实，不必担心。”

“You have a point. But this time the whole thing may be uprooted!” “You mean Mr Hu’s businesses may not survive? I cannot speak for the others, but Qingyu Hall is certain to remain.” “Why?” “It has protection,” Zhu replied calmly. “When the trouble at Fukang began, our manager told us that Qingyu Hall was the best of all Mr Hu’s enterprises. It earns money and has earned him a reputation too. Suppose they say there is a shortage of public funds and seal Qingyu Hall to cover the debt. They can confiscate the stock and equipment, but they cannot take away its signboard. Qingyu Hall is only the short name. The full name is Hu Qingyu Hall. If the owner is no longer a Hu, how can they keep using that sign? So the authorities are certain not to seal it. They will let Mr Hu remain the owner. We must all work especially hard, dispense genuine medicines and treat customers courteously. Then our rice bowls will be secure. There is no need to worry.”

听到这里，杨书办心中浮起浓重的感慨，胡雪岩有如此大的事业，培植了不知道多少人材，是可想而知的事，但培植人材之始。如果只是为他自己找个不问手段，只要能替他嫌钱的帮手，结果不是宓本常，就是唐子韶，因为水涨船高，“徒弟”升伙计，伙计升档手，这时候的档手心里就会想：“你做老板，还不是靠我做徒弟的时候，洗尿壶、烫水烟袋，一步一步抬你起来的？伙计做到啥时候？我要做老板了。”一动到这个念头，档手就不是档手了，第一步是“做小货”，有好生意，自己来做，譬如有人上门求售一批货色，明知必赚，却多方挑剔，最后明点暗示，到某处去接头，有成交之望，其实指点之处就是他私下所设的号子。其次是留意人材，伙计、徒弟中看中了的，私下刻意笼络，一旦能成局面，不愁没有班底，最后是拉拢客户，其道孔多，但要拉拢客户，一定不会说原来的东家的好话，是一定的道理，否则客户不会“跳槽”。因此，只要有了私心重的档手，一到动了自立门户的念头，就必然损人以利己，侵蚀到东家的利益，即令是东家所一手培植出来的，亦不会觉得自己忘恩负义，因为他替东家赚过钱，自以为已经报答过了。

Yang was deeply moved by what he heard. With enterprises on so vast a scale, Hu must have trained more capable men than anyone could count. But if, at the beginning, he sought only assistants who would make money for him by whatever means, the result would be a Mi Benchang or a Tang Zishao. As the water rose, so did the boat: an apprentice became an employee, an employee became a manager. Then the manager would think, “How did you become the proprietor? When I was an apprentice, I emptied your chamber pot and rinsed your water pipe with hot water. I raised you up step by step. How long must I remain an employee? I want to be a proprietor myself.” Once that thought took hold, he ceased to be a true manager. First came private trading on the side. If a profitable transaction presented itself, he took it for himself. Someone might offer a consignment he knew would make money; he would find fault with it in every way, then openly or indirectly suggest another place where a deal might be struck. That place would be his own secret business. Next, he would watch for talent, privately cultivating promising employees and apprentices so that, when he could establish himself, he would have his staff ready. Finally came drawing away customers. There were many methods, but one thing was certain: to win them over, he would never speak well of his present employer. Otherwise, why would they change firms? A selfish manager who decided to set up on his own would inevitably profit at his employer’s expense. Even if the employer had trained him from the start, he would feel no ingratitude. He had made money for the man and believed that debt was already paid.

庆余堂的档手能够如此通达诚恳，尽力维持庆余堂这块金字招牌，为胡雪岩保住一片事业，这原因是可想而知的，胡雪岩当初创办庆余堂，虽起于西征将士所需要成药及药材，数量极大，向外采购不但费用甚巨，而且亦不见得能够及时供应，他既负责后路粮台，当然要精打细算，自己办一家大药店，有省费、省事、方便三项好处，并没有打算赚钱，后来因为药材地道、成药灵验、营业鼎盛，大力赚钱。但盈余除了转为资本，扩大规模以外，平时对贫民施药施医，历次水旱灾荒、时疫流行，捐出大批成药，亦全由盈余上开支，胡雪岩从来没有用过庆余堂的一文钱。

The reason Qingyu Hall’s manager could be so sincere and understanding, doing everything to preserve its reputation and one part of Hu’s business, was not difficult to imagine. Hu had founded the medicine shop because the troops on the western campaign required enormous quantities of prepared medicines and herbs. Buying them elsewhere was expensive and did not always ensure timely delivery. Responsible for the supply administration behind the army, he had to calculate carefully. A large shop of his own would save money, save trouble and make supply easier. He had not intended to earn a profit. Later, genuine ingredients and effective preparations brought flourishing trade and substantial earnings. But apart from profits reinvested to expand the business, the surplus paid for free medicines and treatment for the poor, and for large donations of prepared remedies during floods, droughts, famines and epidemics. Hu had never taken a single cash from Qingyu Hall for his own use.

由于当初存心大公无私，物色档手的眼光，当然就不同了，第一要诚实，庆余堂一进门，供顾客等药休息之处，高悬一幅黑漆金字的对联：“修合虽无人见，存心自有天知。”因为不诚实的人卖药，尤其是卖成药，材料欠佳，分量不足，服用了会害人。其次要心慈。医家有割股之心，卖药亦是如此，时时为病家着想，才能刻刻顾到药的品质。最后当然还要能干，否则诚实、心慈，反而成了易于受欺的弱点。这样选中的一个档手，不必在意东家的利润，会全心全力去经营事业，东家没有私心，也就引不起他的私心，加以待遇优厚，亦不必起什么私心。庆余堂能不受阜康的影响，细细考查来龙去脉，自有种善因、得善果的颠扑不破之理在内。念头转到这里，不由得对那连姓名都还不知道的余庆堂的档手，油然而起敬慕之心。于是在把杯闲谈之际，杨书办向老朱问起此人的生平，据说庆余堂的档手姓叶；当初是由胡雪岩的一个姓刘的亲戚去物色来的，性情、才干大致证明了杨书办的推断，这就更使他感到得意了。

Because his original purpose was entirely public-spirited, he had sought a different sort of manager. Honesty came first. Just inside the shop, above the place where customers waited and rested, hung a black-lacquered couplet in gold: “Though none may see your medicines prepared, Heaven knows the intentions in your heart.” A dishonest medicine seller, especially one selling ready-made preparations, could harm people by using poor ingredients or insufficient quantities. Compassion came next. A physician must have the heart to sacrifice his own flesh for another; a medicine seller should be the same. Only by constantly thinking of the sick could he constantly attend to quality. Finally, the man must be capable, or honesty and compassion might merely make him easy to deceive.
