Such a manager, free from concern for the proprietor’s personal profit, would devote himself wholeheartedly to the business. An unselfish employer would not awaken selfishness in him; generous treatment removed any need for it. Examined closely, Qingyu Hall’s escape from Fukang’s troubles exemplified the enduring truth that good causes bear good fruit. Yang felt a spontaneous admiration for its manager, whose name he did not even know. Over their drinks he asked Zhu about the man’s history. He learned that his surname was Ye and that a relative of Hu’s named Liu had originally found him. What he heard of Ye’s character and ability broadly confirmed his deductions, making Yang still more pleased with himself.

“你们的档手对得起胡大先生，也对得起自己，不比公济典的那个黑良心的唐子韶，我看他快要吃官司了。”“怎么？”老朱问道：“你这话是哪里来的？”这一问才使杨书办意识到酒后失言了。他当然不肯再说，支支吾吾地敷衍了一会，重回楼上。楼上的马逢时与孙干娘，还在喝酒闲谈，彼此的神态倒都还庄重，但谈得很投机，却是看得出来的，因而杨书办便开玩笑他说：“老李，今天不要回去了。”“你在同哪个说话？”孙子娘瞟眼过来问说。杨书办尚未开口，马逢时却先笑了，这一笑自有蹊跷在内，他就不作声了。“明明是马大老爷，你怎么说是李老板？”孙干娘质问：“为啥要说假话？”“对不起！”马逢时向杨书办致歉：“她说我不象生意人，又问我哪里学来的官派，所以我跟她说了实话。”“说了实话？”杨书办问：“是啥实话？除了身分还有啥？”“没有别的。”杨书办比较放心了，转脸对孙干娘说：“你要识得轻重，不要说马大老爷到你这里来玩过。”

“Your manager has done right by Mr Hu and by himself,” Yang said. “Not like that black-hearted Tang Zishao at Gongji. I think he will soon find himself facing charges.” “What?” Zhu asked. “Where did you hear that?” Only then did Yang realise that wine had loosened his tongue. Naturally, he would say no more. After some evasive replies, he returned upstairs. Ma and Auntie Sun were still drinking and talking. Their manner remained decorous, but they were plainly getting on very well. Yang joked, “Old Li, do not go home tonight.” “Whom are you speaking to?” Auntie Sun asked, glancing across. Before Yang could answer, Ma laughed. There was something behind that laugh, so Yang held his tongue. “He is Magistrate Ma. Why did you call him Mr Li?” Auntie Sun demanded. “Why tell a lie?” “I am sorry,” Ma apologised to Yang. “She said I did not look like a businessman and asked where I had acquired my official manner, so I told her the truth.” “The truth? What truth? Anything besides who you are?” “Nothing else.” Somewhat reassured, Yang turned to Auntie Sun. “You must understand the importance of this. Do not tell people Magistrate Ma has been here for pleasure.”

“这有啥好瞒的？道台大人都到我这里来吃过酒。”“你不要同我争，你要我常常带朋友来，你就听我的话。”杨书办又说：“今天要走了，马大老爷明天有公事，改天再来。”“哪天？”孙干娘问：“明天？”“明天怕还不行。”马逢时自己回答：“我等公事一完了，就来看你。”“条戳没有到，今天晚上也找不着人了，明天一早去请教刻字店。”杨书办说：“总要到中午，一切才会预备好，我看准定明天吃中饭去查封。”“好！一切拜托，我在舍间听你的信。”于是相偕离座出门，走在路上，杨书办少不得有所埋怨，而马逢时不断道歉，他也就不便多说什么了。

“What is there to hide? Even a circuit intendant has come here to drink.” “Do not argue. If you want me to keep bringing friends, listen to me.” Yang continued, “We must go now. Magistrate Ma has official business tomorrow. We shall come another day.” “When?” Auntie Sun asked. “Tomorrow?” “Tomorrow may still be impossible,” Ma answered for himself. “I shall come as soon as my business is finished.” “The rectangular stamp has not been made,” Yang said. “We shall find nobody to do it tonight. I shall go to an engraver first thing tomorrow. It will be noon before everything is ready. We had better settle on taking the shop into official custody at lunchtime.” “Very well. I leave everything to you and shall wait for word at home.” They rose and left together. On the way, Yang could not help reproaching Ma, but Ma apologised so persistently that he could hardly say more.

第二夭是“卯期”，杨书办照例要到“礼房”去坐一坐，以防“县大老爷”有什么要跟“学者爷”打交道的事要问，好及时“应卯”。礼房有现成的刻字匠，找了一个来，将一张马逢时的临时衔名条交了给他，不到一顿饭的工夫，已经刻好送来，看看无事，起身回家，预备伴随马逢时到公济典去查封。一进门跨进堂屋，便看到正中方桌上堆了一条火腿，大小四个盒子，门口又是五十斤重的一坛花雕，知道是有人送礼，便喊：“阿毛娘，阿毛娘！”阿毛是他儿子的乳名，“阿毛娘”便是叫他的妻子。杨太太应声而至，不等他开口便说：“有张片子在这里，是公济典的姓唐的。我们跟他没有来往，送的礼我也不敢动。“说着，杨太太递过来一张名片，一看果然是唐子韶，略一沉吟，杨书办问道：“他有什么话？”“说等等再来。”杨太太答说：“看他吞吞吐吐，好象有什么话，要说不肯说似的。”“我晓得了。这份礼不能收的。”杨书办坐了下来，一面喝茶一面想，唐子韶的来意，不问可知？他只奇怪，此人的消息，何以如此灵通，知道他会赔马逢时去查封公济？是不是已经先去看过马逢时，马逢时关照来找他的呢？倘是如此，似乎先要跟马逢时见个面，问一问他交谈的情形，才好定主意。

The next day was one on which attendance had to be marked. As usual, Yang went to sit in the rites section, so that if the county magistrate had questions about dealings with the education official, he would be on hand to answer the roll. An engraver was readily available there. Yang summoned one and handed him a slip bearing Ma’s temporary title. In less than the time it took to eat a meal, the stamp was cut and brought back. Finding nothing else to do, Yang went home to prepare to accompany Ma to Gongji. The moment he entered the main room, he saw a ham and four boxes of different sizes piled on the central table. By the door stood a fifty-jin jar of Huadiao wine. Someone had sent a gift. “A’mao’s mother!” he called. A’mao was his son’s childhood name; he was calling his wife. She came at once and spoke before he could. “Here is a card. The man is Tang from Gongji Pawnshop. We have no dealings with him, so I dared not touch the gifts.” She handed him the card. It was indeed Tang Zishao’s. After a moment’s thought, Yang asked, “What did he say?” “That he would come back shortly. He seemed hesitant, as though he had something to say but would not say it.” “I understand. We cannot accept these gifts.” Yang sat drinking tea and thinking. Tang’s purpose was obvious. What puzzled him was how the man had learned so quickly that Yang would accompany Ma to take Gongji into official custody. Had he already visited Ma and been told to come here? If so, Yang ought to see Ma first and find out what they had discussed before deciding how to act.

正这样转着念头，听得有人敲门，便亲自起身去应接。他跟唐子韶在应酬场中见过，是点头之交，开门看时，果然是他，少不得要作一番讶异之状。“杨先生，”唐子韶满脸堆笑地说：“想不到是我吧？”“想不到，想不到。请里面坐。”杨书办在前头领路，进了堂屋，指着桌子说：“唐朝奉，无归不肥禄，你这份礼，我决不收。”唐子韶似乎已经预知他会有这种态度，毫不在乎他说：“小事，小事，慢慢谈。”杨书办见他如此沉着，不免心生警惕，说声：“请坐。”也不叫人倒茶，自己在下首正襟危坐，是不想久谈的神情。“杨先生，听说你要陪马大老爷来查封公济典？”见他开门见山地发问，杨书办却不愿但然承认，反问一句：“唐朝奉，你听哪个说的？”“是辗转得来的消息。”辗转传闻，便表示他不曾跟马逢时见过面，而消息来源，只有两处，一是周少棠，一是庆余堂的老朱。细想一想，多半以后者为是。“请问，你是不是从庆余堂那边得来的消息？”这也就等于杨书办承认了这件事，唐子韶点点头说：“是的。”

While he was considering this, someone knocked. Yang went to answer the door himself. He and Tang were nodding acquaintances from social gatherings. Sure enough, Tang stood outside, and Yang had to make a show of surprise. “You did not expect me, did you, Mr Yang?” Tang asked with a broad smile. “Indeed I did not. Please come in.” Leading him into the main room, Yang pointed at the table. “Master Tang, I cannot accept a reward I have not earned. I certainly shall not accept these gifts.” Tang seemed to have expected this response and took it lightly. “A small matter. We can discuss it in due course.” His composure made Yang wary. “Please sit.” He did not call for tea, but sat stiffly upright in the lower seat, signalling that he did not intend a long conversation. “Mr Yang, I hear you are to accompany Magistrate Ma to take Gongji into official custody?” Faced with this direct question, Yang was unwilling to admit it outright. “Who told you, Master Tang?” “The news reached me indirectly.” If it was indirect news, he had not met Ma. There were only two possible sources: Zhou Shaotang or Old Zhu from Qingyu Hall. On reflection, the latter seemed more likely. “Did you hear it through Qingyu Hall?” That was itself an admission of the matter. Tang nodded. “Yes.”

“那么，老兄就是打听这一点。”“当然还有话要请教杨先生。”唐子韶问：“请问，预备什么时候来？我好等候大驾。““言重！言重！这要问马大老爷。”由于活不投机，唐子韶不能吐露真意，不过他送的那份不能算菲薄的札，始终不肯收回，杨书办亦无可奈何，心头不免有欠了人家一份人情，协助马逢时去查封公济时，较难说话的困惑。“杨先生，”唐子韶起身预备告辞时，忽然问出一句话来：“我想请问你，同周少棠熟不熟？”杨书办沉吟了一下，只答了一个字：“熟。”“他同马大老爷呢？”问到这句话，显得此人的交游很广、路子很多，也许前一天他与马逢时、周少棠曾在酒店中一起聚晤这件事，已有人告诉了他，然则用一句“不大清楚”来回答，便是故意说假话，受了人家一份礼，连这么一句话都不肯实说，唐子韶自然会在心里冷笑。以后如何是以后的事，眼前先让唐子韶这样的人对他鄙视，未免太划不来了。这样转着念头，不由得说了实话：“不算太熟。”唐子韶似乎对他的回答很满意，微笑着说：“打扰，打扰。改天公事完了，我要请杨先生、马大老爷好好叙一叙。”

“So you came only to find out about that?” “There are other things I should like to ask you, of course. When do you intend to come? I should like to be ready to receive you.” “You are too courteous. You must ask Magistrate Ma about that.” Finding the conversation unpromising, Tang could not disclose his real purpose. Yet he would not take back the gifts, which were by no means trifling. Yang could do nothing about it. He now felt uncomfortably indebted, and feared it would be harder to take a firm line when assisting Ma at Gongji. As Tang rose to leave, he suddenly asked, “Mr Yang, may I ask whether you know Zhou Shaotang well?” Yang considered, then answered simply, “Well.” “And how well does he know Magistrate Ma?” This question suggested extensive connections and many sources of information. Perhaps somebody had already told Tang that Yang, Ma and Zhou had met in the wine shop the previous day. To answer “I am not sure” would then be a deliberate lie. If, after receiving his gifts, Yang would not answer even that small question honestly, Tang would surely sneer inwardly. Whatever happened later, it was hardly worth earning the contempt of a man like Tang now. Without quite intending to, Yang told the truth. “Not particularly well.” Tang appeared satisfied. Smiling, he said, “I have taken up your time. Once the official business is finished, I should like to invite you and Magistrate Ma for a proper gathering.”

正当杨书办在马逢时家，准备出发去查封公济典时，他家里的女仆匆匆奔了来，请他回家，道是“太太有要紧事要商量”。杨书办还在踌躇，马逢时开口了，“你就先请回去吧！”他说：“商量好了马上请过来，我在这里等。”好在离得近，杨书办决定先回去一趟，到家一看，非常意外地是周少棠在等候，明明是他要请他来说话，却作了托辞，显然的，周少棠来看他，是不愿让马逢时知道的。“事情有了变化。”周少棠停了一下说：“我说实话吧，唐子韶来看过我了。”“喔，”杨书办问：“啥辰光？”“就是刚刚的事，他寻到阜康来的。”周少棠说：“他的话也有点道理，公济的事一闹出来，又成了新闻，对胡大先生不利。而且查封的事，一生枝节，官府恐怕对胡大先生有更厉害的处置。我想这两点也不错，投鼠忌器，特为来同你商量。”杨书办想了一下答说：“他先到我这里来过了，还送了一份礼。事情很明白了，他在公济确有毛病，而且毛病怕还不小。现在你说投鼠忌器，是不是放他一马，就此拉倒？”“那不太便宜他了？他亦很识相，答应‘吐’出来。”“怎么吐法？”“这就要看你了。”周少棠的意思是，杨书办陪了马逢时到公济典，细细查库、查帐，将唐子韶的毛病都找了出来，最好作成笔录，但不必采取任何行动，回来将实情告诉周少棠，由他跟唐子韶去办交涉。杨书办心想，这等于是一切由周少棠做主，他跟马逢对不过是周少棠的“伙计”而已。不过，只要有“好处”，做“伙计”亦无所谓。

Yang was at Ma’s house, preparing to set out for Gongji, when his maid hurried over to ask him to come home. “Madam has something urgent to discuss,” she said. While Yang hesitated, Ma spoke. “Go back first. Come straight over when you have finished. I shall wait here.” Fortunately, the houses were close. Yang decided to return briefly, only to find, to his great surprise, that Zhou was waiting for him. Clearly Zhou was the one who wanted to talk; the excuse about his wife meant he did not wish Ma to know of the visit. “Things have changed,” Zhou said. He paused. “I shall tell you frankly: Tang Zishao has been to see me.” “Oh? When?” “Just now. He found me at Fukang. There is something in what he says. If Gongji’s affairs cause a commotion, there will be another scandal, which will harm Mr Hu. And if complications arise during the proceedings to take the shop into official custody, the authorities may deal with him more severely. Both points are sound, I think. We must not smash the vessel while trying to strike the rat. That is why I came to consult you.” After a moment’s thought, Yang replied, “He came to see me first and brought gifts. The position is clear: something is wrong at Gongji, and probably something quite serious. Now you speak of sparing the vessel. Do you mean we should let him off and drop the affair?” “Would that not be letting him off too cheaply? He understands his position and has agreed to disgorge the money.” “How?” “That depends on you.” Zhou wanted Yang to accompany Ma to Gongji and examine the storeroom and accounts carefully, uncovering every irregularity. A written record would be best, but they need take no action. Yang should bring the facts back, and Zhou would negotiate with Tang himself. Yang thought this made Zhou master of the entire affair, with himself and Ma merely Zhou’s employees. Still, provided there was something in it for them, being employees did not matter.

当然，这不必等他开口，周少棠亦会有交代：“这样做法，不过是免了唐子韶吃官司，他再要想讨便宜，就是妄想。我们还是照原来的计划，一方面是帮胡大先生的忙，一方面我们三个，你、我、老马，弄几两银子过年。”“我倒无所谓。”杨书办说：“老马难得派个差使，而且这件事也要担责任，似乎不好少了他的。”“一点不错。你叫他放心好了。”“你做事，他也很放心的，不过，最好开个‘尺寸’给他。”尺寸是商场的切口，意指银数，周少棠答说：“现在有‘几尺水，还不晓得，这个尺寸怎么开法？”“几尺水”者是指总数。唐子韶侵吞中饱几何，能“吐”出来多少？目前无从估计，周少棠不能承诺一个确数，固属实情，但亦不妨先“派派份头”。等杨书办提出这个意见以后，周少棠立即说道：“大份头当然是归胡大先生。如果照十份派，胡大先生六份，老马两发，你、我各一份。怎么样？”杨书办心想，如果能从唐子韶身上追出一万银子，马逢时可得两千，自己亦有一千两进帐，这个年可以过得很肥了。于是欣然点头：“好的，就照这样子派好了。”

There was no need for him to raise the point. Zhou supplied the assurance himself. “This arrangement only saves Tang from a lawsuit. If he thinks he can profit from it as well, he is dreaming. We shall follow our original plan: help Mr Hu on the one hand, and find a few taels for the three of us—you, me and Ma—to see us through the New Year on the other.” “It does not matter so much about me,” Yang said. “Ma seldom gets an assignment, and this one carries responsibility. We ought not to stint his share.” “Exactly. Tell him he need not worry.” “He trusts you to handle it. Still, it would be best to give him a ‘measurement.’” In business slang, a measurement meant a sum of money. “We do not yet know how many ‘feet of water’ there are,” Zhou replied. “How can I give him a measurement?” The depth of the water meant the total amount. How much had Tang embezzled, and how much could be recovered? They could not yet estimate it. Zhou was right not to promise a definite sum, but they could at least agree on the shares. When Yang suggested this, Zhou immediately said, “The largest share must naturally go to Mr Hu. Divide it into ten parts: six for him, two for Ma, and one each for you and me. How does that sound?” If ten thousand taels could be recovered from Tang, Yang thought, Ma would receive two thousand and he himself one thousand. That would make a very comfortable New Year. He nodded happily. “Good. Let us divide it that way.”

由于事先已有联络，马逢时由杨书办陪着到了公济典，不必摆什么官派，只将预先写好的、暂停营业三夭的告示贴了出去，等顾客散尽，关上大门。开始封库查帐。唐子韶先很从容，看马逢时态度平和，杨书办语言客气，以为周少棠的路子已经走通了，及至看到要封库，脸色已有些不大自然，再听说要查帐，便无法保持常态了。“杨先生，你请过来。”他将杨书办拉到一边，低声问道：“今天中午，周少棠同你碰过头了？”“是的。”“他怎么说？”杨书办不免诧异；不过他的念头转得很快，知道周少棠下了一着狠棋，因而声色不动地问说，“你同他怎么说的？”原来唐子韶托谢云青居间，见到周少棠以后，隐约透露出，请他转托杨书办及马逢时，在查封公济典时，不必认真，同时许了周少棠三千银子的好处，“摆平”一切。复又央请谢云青作保，事过以后，三千银子分文不少。谢云青也答应了。但他不知道周少棠有意要助胡雪岩，并非为了他自己的好处，有为胡雪岩不平的意味在内，这就不关钱的事了。当时周少棠满口应承，实是一个“空心汤圆”，而犹一直不曾醒悟，只以为周少棠自己吞得太多，杨书办嫌少，故而有意刁难，说不得只好大破悭囊了。

Since contact had already been made, Ma needed no display of official importance when he arrived at Gongji with Yang. They simply posted the prepared notice suspending business for three days, waited for the customers to leave and shut the main doors. Then they began sealing the storeroom and examining the accounts. Tang was composed at first. Seeing Ma’s mild manner and hearing Yang’s courteous words, he thought his approach through Zhou had succeeded. When he saw that the storeroom was to be sealed, his expression became less natural. On hearing that the accounts would be examined, he could no longer keep calm. “Mr Yang, a word.” Drawing Yang aside, he asked quietly, “Did you meet Zhou Shaotang at noon today?” “Yes.” “What did he say?” Yang was surprised, but his mind worked quickly. He realised that Zhou had played a ruthless move. Without betraying his feelings, he asked, “What did you tell him?” Tang had met Zhou through Xie Yunqing. He had hinted that Zhou should ask Yang and Ma not to be too exacting in their inspection of Gongji, and had promised Zhou three thousand taels to settle everything. He had also asked Xie to guarantee that, once the affair was over, every cash of the three thousand would be paid. Xie had agreed. What Tang did not know was that Zhou intended to help Hu, not to pursue his own gain. He felt indignant on Hu’s behalf, so this was not a matter of money. His ready agreement had been an empty dumpling—a promise with nothing inside. Tang had still not grasped this. He merely assumed that Zhou had kept too much for himself and Yang, dissatisfied with his share, was making difficulties. There was nothing for it but to open his purse wider.

“杨先生，大家都是场面上的人，有话好说，不要做得太难堪。”情急之下，他口不择言了，“快过年了，大家都有帐要付，这一层我知道的。除了原来的以外，我另外再送两千银子，马大老爷那里，只要你老大哥摆平，我不说话。”什么是原来的？杨书办略想一想也就明白，不过还是要打听一下：“原来多少？”等将唐子韶与周少棠打交道的情形问清楚以后，杨书办觉得很为难。他为人比较忠厚，觉得唐子韶可怜兮兮的，不忍心象周少棠那样，虚与委蛇，让他吃个“空心汤圆”，当然，要接受他的条件，也是决不可能的事。“杨先生，”唐子韶近乎哀求他说：“你就算交我一个朋友。我知道你在马大老爷面前一言九鼎，只要你说一声，他就高抬贵手，放我过去了。”谈到“交朋友”。杨书办倒有话说了，“朋友是朋友，公事是公事。”他说，“只要马大老爷公事上，能过得去，我当然要顾朋友的交情。唐朝奉，我答应你一件事，今天决不会让你面子难看，不过，我只希望你不要妨碍公事。至于查封以后，如何办法，我们大家再商量。”这番话是“绵里针”，唐子韶当然听得出来，如果自己不知趣，不让马逢时查帐，变成“妨碍公事”，他是有权送他到县衙门的“班房”去收押的。好在还有以后再商量的话，好汉不吃眼前亏，先敷衍好了杨书办，再作道理。“杨先生，你这样子说，我不能不听，一切遵吩咐就是。”

“Mr Yang, we are all men who know the ways of society. Everything can be discussed. Do not make matters too embarrassing.” In his anxiety, Tang no longer chose his words carefully. “The New Year is coming. We all have debts to pay; I understand that. Besides the original amount, I shall give another two thousand taels. If you can settle matters with Magistrate Ma, I shall have nothing to say.” What original amount? Yang could guess, but still needed to find out. “How much was it originally?” Once he had learned the details of Tang’s dealings with Zhou, he felt deeply uncomfortable. Yang was comparatively kind-hearted. Tang looked so pitiful that he could not bear to string him along with an empty promise as Zhou had done. Yet accepting his terms was equally out of the question. “Mr Yang,” Tang said almost pleadingly, “do it for the sake of making a friend. I know your word carries enormous weight with Magistrate Ma. One word from you and he will show mercy and let me through.” Friendship gave Yang something to say. “Friendship is one thing, official business another. So long as Magistrate Ma can answer for his conduct of the assignment, I shall certainly consider our friendship. Master Tang, I promise you one thing: you will not be humiliated today. But I hope you will not obstruct official business. We can all discuss what to do after the inspection and sealing.” Tang recognised the needle hidden in the cotton. If he failed to take the hint and refused to let Ma examine the accounts, he would be obstructing official business. Ma could have him detained in the county office’s holding room. Fortunately, there was still the promise of later discussion. A sensible man did not invite immediate suffering. He would satisfy Yang first and consider the rest afterwards. “Since you put it that way, Mr Yang, I must listen. I shall follow every instruction.”

唐子韶也豁出去了，不但要什么帐簿有什么帐簿，而且问什么答什么，非常合作，因此查帐非常顺利。只是帐簿太多，这天下午只查了三分之一，至少第二天还要费一整天才能完事。等回到家，杨太太告诉丈夫：“周少棠来过了，他说他在你们昨天吃酒的地方等你。”“喔！”杨书办问：“光是指我一个人？”“还有哪个？”“有没有叫老马也去？”“他没有说。”“好。我马上就去。”杨书办带着一份记录去赴约。

Tang now committed himself. He supplied every ledger they requested and answered every question, cooperating so fully that the examination proceeded smoothly. There were simply too many account books. That afternoon they checked only a third; finishing would take at least the whole of the following day. When Yang returned home, his wife told him, “Zhou Shaotang came. He said he would wait for you where you were drinking yesterday.” “Oh? Did he mean only me?” “Who else?” “Did he ask Ma to go too?” “He did not say.” “Very well. I shall go at once.” Yang took a written record of the findings with him to the meeting.

“胡大先生怎么能不倒霉！”周少棠指着那份记录说：“光是这张纸上记下来的，算一算已经吞了三、四万银子都不止了。”“你预备怎么个办法？”“还不是要他吐出来。”周少棠说：“数目太大，我想先要同胡大先生谈一谈。”“这，”杨书办为马逢时讲话，“在公事上不大妥当吧？”“怎么不妥当？”周少棠反问“杨书办亦说不出如何不妥，他只是觉得马逢时奉派查封公济典，如何交差，要由周少棠跟胡雪岩商量以后来决定，似乎操纵得大过分，心生反感而已。“公事就是那么一回事，你老兄是‘老公事’，还有啥不明白的？”周少棠用抚慰地语气说，“总而言之，老马的公事，一定让他交代得过，私下的好处，也一定会让他心里舒服。至于你的一份，当然不会比者马少，这是说都用不着说的，”当然，周少棠的“好处”亦不会逊于他跟马逢时，更不待言。照此看来，唐子韶的麻烦不小，想起他那万般无奈、苦苦哀求的神情，不由得上了心事。“怎么？”周少棠问：“你有啥为难？”“我怎么不为难？”杨书办说：“你给他吃了个空心汤圆，他不晓得，只以为都谈好了，现在倒好象是我们跟他为难，他到我家里来过一次，当然会来第二次，我怎么打发他？”“那容易，你都推在我头上好了。”事实上这是唯一的应付办法，杨书办最后的打算亦是如此。此刻既然周少棠自己作了亏诺，他也就死心塌地，不再去多想了。

“How could Mr Hu escape misfortune?” Zhou said, pointing at the record. “Add up what is on this sheet alone, and the money swallowed already exceeds thirty or forty thousand taels.” “What do you intend to do?” “Make him disgorge it, of course. The amount is so large that I think I must speak to Mr Hu first.” Speaking for Ma, Yang said, “Would that be quite proper in official business?” “Why not?” Zhou countered. Yang could not explain exactly why it was improper. He merely felt resentful that Ma, officially commissioned to take charge of Gongji, should have to wait for Zhou and Hu to decide how he was to discharge his assignment. Zhou was exercising too much control. “Official business is what it is. You are an old hand at it—what is there that you do not understand?” Zhou spoke soothingly. “In any case, I shall make sure Ma can account satisfactorily for his assignment, and that the private benefit pleases him too. As for your share, it certainly will not be less than his. That goes without saying.” Naturally, Zhou’s own benefit would be no smaller than either man’s. Tang appeared to be in serious trouble. Recalling his helpless expression and desperate pleas, Yang grew troubled. “What is it?” Zhou asked. “Is something troubling you?” “How could it not? You gave him an empty dumpling, but he does not know it. He thinks everything has been settled. Now it looks as though we are deliberately making trouble for him. He has been to my house once and will certainly come again. How am I to deal with him?” “That is easy. Put it all on me.” In fact, this was the only possible answer, and Yang had already intended to use it in the end. Now that Zhou had offered the assurance himself, he accepted it wholeheartedly and ceased to worry further.

第二天仍如前一天那样嘴上很客气，眼中不容情，将唐子韶的弊端，一样一样，追究到底。唐子韶的态度，却跟前一天有异，仿佛对马逢时及杨书办的作为，不甚在意。只是坐在一边，不断地抽水烟，有时将一根纸煤搓了又搓，直到搓断，方始有爽然若失的神情，显得他在肚子里的功夫，做得根深。约莫刚交午时，公济开出点心来，请马逢时暂时休息。唐子韶便趁此时机，将杨书办邀到一边有话说。“杨先生，”他问：“今天查得完查不完？”一想把它查完。““以后呢？”唐子韶问道：“不是说好商量？”“不错，好商量。你最好去寻周少棠，只要他那里谈好了，马大老爷这里归我负责。”唐子韶迟疑了好一会说：“本来是谈好了，哪晓得马大老爷一来，要从头查起。语气中仿佛在埋怨杨书办跟周少棠彼此串通，有意推来推去，不愿帮忙。杨书办心想，也难怪他误会，其中的关键，不妨点他一句。“老兄，你不要一厢情愿！你这里查都还没有查过，无从谈起，更不必说啥谈好了。你今天晚上去寻他，包你有结果。“唐子韶恍然大悟，原来是要看他在公济典里弄了多少“好处”，然后再来谈“价钱”。看样子打算用几千银子“摆平”，是一种不切实际的妄想。“树倒猢狲散”，不如带着月如远走高飞，大不了从此不吃朝奉这一行的饭，后半世应可衣食无忧。就在这刹那间打定了主意，就更不在乎杨书办与马逢时了，不过表面上仍旧很尊敬，当天查帐完毕，要请他们吃饭。马逢时当然坚辞，杨书办且又暗示，应该早早去觅周少棠“商量”。

The next day the inspection continued as before: polite words, unsparing eyes. Tang Zishao’s irregularities were pursued one by one to the end. His own manner, however, had changed. He seemed scarcely concerned with what Ma Fengshi and Clerk Yang were doing, merely sitting to one side and smoking his water pipe. Sometimes he rolled a paper spill between his fingers again and again until it broke; only then did he look momentarily lost, revealing how deeply his mind was at work. Shortly after noon began, Gongji served refreshments and invited Ma to rest. Tang took the opportunity to draw Yang aside. “Mr Yang, can you finish the inspection today?” “We mean to try.” “And afterward? Didn’t you say we could discuss things?” “Certainly. You had better find Zhou Shaotang. Once you have settled matters with him, I’ll answer for His Honour Ma.” Tang hesitated for some time. “I thought we had settled things already. Who could have known His Honour would come and insist on examining everything from the beginning?” His tone suggested that Yang and Zhou were working together, deliberately passing him back and forth without helping. Yang thought the misunderstanding natural enough; he might as well give him a hint. “My dear fellow, don’t indulge in wishful thinking. Before we’ve even examined the place, there’s nothing to discuss, let alone settle. Go and see him tonight. I guarantee you’ll get a result.” Tang suddenly understood. They wanted to see how much he had taken from Gongji before naming their price. Expecting to settle everything for a few thousand taels was an absurd dream. When the tree fell, the monkeys scattered. Better to take Yueru and flee far away. At worst, he would never work as a pawnbroker again; he should still have enough to live comfortably for the rest of his life. The decision formed in an instant, leaving him even less concerned with Yang and Ma, though outwardly he remained respectful. When the day’s examination ended, he invited them to dinner. Ma firmly declined, while Yang again hinted that he should find Zhou early and “discuss matters.”

唐子韶口头上边声称“是”，其实根本无此打算，他要紧的是赶回家去跟月如商量。约略说了经过，随即向月如透露了他的决心。“三十六计，走为上让。你从现在起始，就要预备，最好三、五天之内料理清楚，我们开溜，”月如一愣，“溜到哪里？”她说：“徽州我是不去。”唐子韶的结发妻子在徽州原籍，要月如去服低做小，亲操井臼，宁死不愿，这一层意思表明过不止一次，唐子韶当然明白。“我怎么会让你到徽州去吃苦？就算你自己要去，我也舍不得。我想有三个地方，一个是上海，一个是北京，再有一个是扬州，我在那里有两家亲戚。”只要不让她到徽州，他处都不妨从长计议，但最好是能不走，上生上长三十年，从没有出过远门，怕到了他乡水土不服住不惯。

Tang repeatedly agreed, without the least intention of doing so. His urgent business was to get home and consult Yueru. After briefly describing what had happened, he revealed his decision. “Of the Thirty-Six Stratagems, running away is the best. Start preparing now. We should have everything ready in three to five days, then slip away.” Yueru stared. “Where to? I won’t go to Huizhou.” Tang’s first wife remained in his native Huizhou. Yueru would rather die than go there to take a subordinate place and do the household drudgery herself. She had made that clear more than once, and he knew it perfectly. “How could I send you to suffer in Huizhou? Even if you wanted to go, I couldn’t bear it. I have three places in mind: Shanghai, Beijing, or Yangzhou, where I have two sets of relatives.” Provided Huizhou was excluded, the choice could be discussed at leisure. Better still, though, would be not to leave at all. Yueru had lived here all her thirty years and had never traveled far. She feared that elsewhere the climate and water would disagree with her and she would not settle.

“不走办不到，除非倾家荡产。”“有这么厉害？”“自然。”唐子韶答说：“这姓周的，良心黑，手段辣，如今一盘帐都抄了去，一笔一笔照算，没有五万银子不能过门。”“你不会赖掉？”“把柄在人家千里，怎么赖得掉？”“不理他呢？”“不理他？你去试试看。”唐子韶说：“姓马的是候补县，奉了宪谕来查封，权力大得很呢！只要他说一句，马上可以送我到仁和县班房，你来送牢饭吧！”月如叹口气说：“那就只好到上海去了。只怕到了上海还是保不得平安。”“一定可以保！”唐子韶信心十足地说，“上海市场等于外国地方，哪怕是道台也不能派差役去抓人，上海县更加不必谈了。而且上海市场上五方杂处，各式各样的人都有，只要有钱，每天大摇大摆，坐马车、逛张园、吃大菜、看京戏，没有哪个来管你的闲事。”听他形容上海的繁华，月如大为动心，满腔离愁，都丢在九霄云外，细细盘算了一会说道：“好在现款存在汇丰银行，细软随身带了走，有三天工夫总可以收拾好，不动产只好摆在那里再说。不过，这三天当中，会不会出事呢？”

“We can’t stay, unless we’re prepared to lose everything.” “Is it as bad as that?” “Of course. This Zhou has a black heart and a ruthless hand. They have copied all the accounts. Once he adds them up item by item, it will take fifty thousand taels to get past him.” “Can’t you deny it?” “With the evidence in their hands?” “What if you ignore him?” “Try it! Ma is an expectant magistrate acting under his superior’s orders. He has enormous powers. One word from him, and I’m in the lockup at Renhe. You can bring me my meals there.” Yueru sighed. “Then it will have to be Shanghai. But even there, we may not be safe.” “We certainly will!” Tang declared confidently. “The foreign settlement is practically foreign territory. Even the circuit intendant can’t send runners in to arrest people, let alone the Shanghai magistrate. People come there from everywhere, every sort imaginable. So long as you have money, you can swagger about every day, ride in carriages, visit Zhang Garden, eat Western meals, and watch Beijing opera. Nobody will meddle in your affairs.” This picture of Shanghai’s pleasures thoroughly tempted Yueru. All her sorrow at leaving vanished. After careful thought, she said, “Fortunately, the cash is in HSBC. We can take our valuables with us and should be packed within three days. The property we can’t move will have to stay for now. But might something happen during those three days?”

“当然要用缓兵之计。杨书办要我今天晚上就去看周少棠。他一定会开个价钱出来，漫天讨价，就地还钱，一定谈不拢，我请他明天晚上来吃饭，你好好下点功夫……”“又要来这一套了！”月如吼了起来，“你当我什么人看。”“我当你大慈大悲、救苦救难的观世音菩萨看。”唐子韶说：“这姓周的请我吃空心汤圆，你要替我报仇。““报仇？哼，”月如冷笑，“我不来管你的事！你弄得不好‘赔了夫人又折兵’，我白白里又让人家占一回便宜，啥犯着？”“你真傻，你不会请他吃个空心汤圆？两三天一拖拖过去，我们人都到上海了，他到哪里去占你的便宜？”“万一，”月如问说：“万一他来个霸王硬上弓呢？”“你不会叫？一叫，我会来救你。”“那不是变成仙人跳了？而且，你做初一，他做初二。看起来我一定要去送牢饭了。”唐子韶不作声。月如不是他的结发妻子，而且当初已经失过一回身，反正不是从一而终了，再让周少棠尝一回甜头，亦无所谓。不过这话不便说得太露骨，只好点她一句。“如果你不愿意送牢饭，实在说，你是不忍心我去吃牢饭，那么全在你发个善心了。”月如亦不作声，不过把烧饭的老妈子唤了来，关照她明天要杀鸡，要多买菜。

“We must play for time. Yang told me to see Zhou tonight. He’s bound to name a price. He’ll ask the earth, and I’ll bargain him down. Naturally, we won’t agree. I’ll invite him to dinner tomorrow evening, and you must make a special effort…” “That trick again!” Yueru shouted. “What do you take me for?” “The compassionate Guanyin herself, saving those in distress. This Zhou fed me an empty dumpling. You must avenge me.” “Avenge you?” She gave a cold laugh. “I’ll have nothing to do with it. You may end up losing the lady as well as the troops, and I’ll have let another man take advantage of me for nothing. Why should I?” “Don’t be foolish. Can’t you give him an empty dumpling too? Drag it out for two or three days, and we’ll be in Shanghai. How will he take advantage of you then?” “Suppose he forces himself on me?” “Can’t you shout? I’ll come and rescue you.” “Then it becomes a blackmail set-up. And what you do to him one day, he’ll repay the next. It looks as though I’ll be bringing you prison meals after all.” Tang fell silent. Yueru was not his first wife, and she had already once slept with another man. Since lifelong fidelity was no longer in question, he thought, it would hardly matter if Zhou enjoyed her favors too. But he could not say so crudely and could only hint. “If you don’t want to bring meals to prison—if, in truth, you can’t bear to see me imprisoned—then everything depends on your showing a little compassion.” Yueru said nothing either. She merely called the serving woman who did the cooking and told her to kill a chicken and buy extra food for the following day.

周少棠兴冲冲地到了元宝街，要看胡雪岩，不道一说来意，就碰了一个钉子。“说实话，周先生，”胡家的门上说：“生病是假，挡驾是真。你老倒想想，我们老爷还有啥心思见客。我通报，一定去通报，不过，真的不见，你老也不要见怪。”“我是有正事同他谈。”“正事？”门上大摇其头，“那就一定见不着，我们老爷一提起钱庄、当店、丝行，头就大了。”“那么，你说我来看看他。”“也只好这样说。不过，”门上一面起步，一面咕哝着，“我看是白说。”见此光景，周少棠的心冷了。默默盘算，自己想帮忙的意思到了，胡雪岩不见，是没法子的事。唐子韶当然不能便宜他，不妨想想看，用什么手段卡住他的喉咙，让他把吞下去的东西吐出来：过年了，施棉衣、施米、做做好事，也是阴功积德。这一落入沉恩，就不觉得时光慢了，忽然听得一声：“周先生！”抬头看时，是门上在他面前，“我们老爷有请，”“喔，”周少棠定定神说：“居然见我了？”“原来周先生是我们老爷四十年的老朋友。”门上赔笑说道：“我不晓得！周先生你不要见气。”“哪里，哪里！你请领路。”

Zhou went eagerly to Yuanbao Street to see Hu Xueyan, only to meet a rebuff as soon as he explained his purpose. “To be frank, Mr Zhou,” the doorkeeper said, “illness is an excuse; the master is refusing visitors. Just think—what mood can he be in to receive anyone? I’ll announce you, certainly, but if he won’t see you, please don’t take offense.” “I have serious business to discuss with him.” “Business?” The man shook his head vigorously. “Then you definitely won’t see him. Mention the bank, pawnshops, or silk business, and his head begins to ache.” “Then say I’ve come to visit him.” “That’s all I can say. Still…” As he started off, the doorkeeper muttered, “I doubt it will do any good.” Zhou’s enthusiasm cooled. He reflected silently that he had done his part in wishing to help; if Hu would not see him, nothing could be done. Tang must not be let off, of course. He could think of some means of gripping the man by the throat and making him disgorge what he had swallowed. The New Year was coming. Distributing padded clothes and rice would do good and earn merit in the unseen world. Absorbed in these thoughts, he lost track of time, until a sudden “Mr Zhou!” made him look up. The doorkeeper stood before him. “The master asks you in.” “Oh!” Zhou collected himself. “So he will see me after all?” “I didn’t know you were his friend of forty years!” the man said with an apologetic smile. “Please don’t be offended.” “Not at all. Lead the way.”

门上领到花园人口处，有个大丫头由一个老妈子陪着，转引客人直上百狮楼。“周先生走好！”一上楼便有个中年丽人在迎接，周少棠见过一次，急忙拱手说：“螺蛳太太，不敢当，不敢当！”“大先生在里头等你。”说着螺蛳太太亲自揭开门帘，周少棠是头一回到这里，探头一望，目迷五色，东也是灯，西也是灯，东也是胡雪岩，西也是胡雪岩。灯可以有多少盏，胡雪岩不可能分身，周少棠警告自己，这里在镜子很多，不要象刘姥姥进了怕红院那样闹笑话。因此，进门先站住脚，看清楚了再说。“少棠！”胡雪岩在喊：“这面坐。”循声觅人，只见胡雪岩坐在一张红丝绒的安乐椅上，上身穿的小对襟棉袄，下身围着一条花格子的毛毡，额头上扎一条寸许宽的缎带，大概是头痛的缘故。“坐这里！”胡雪岩拍一拍他身旁的绣墩，指着头上笑道：“你看我这副样子，象不象产妇做月子？”这时候还有心思说笑话，周少棠心怀一宽，看样子他的境况，不如想象中那么坏。

At the garden entrance the doorkeeper handed him over to a senior maid accompanied by an older serving woman, who led him straight to the Hundred Lions Tower. “Mind your step, Mr Zhou!” A beautiful middle-aged woman greeted him upstairs. He had met her once before and hastily clasped his hands. “Madam Luosi! You are too kind!” “Mr Hu is waiting inside.” She lifted the curtain herself. This was Zhou’s first visit to these rooms. Looking in, he was dazzled: lamps to the east, lamps to the west; Hu Xueyan to the east, Hu Xueyan to the west. There might be any number of lamps, but Hu could not multiply himself. He warned himself that there were many mirrors here: he must not make a fool of himself like Granny Liu entering Yihong Court. He stopped just inside the doorway to get his bearings. “Shaotang! Sit over here.” Following the voice, he found Hu in a red-velvet armchair, wearing a short padded jacket buttoned down the front, with a checked woolen blanket around his lower body. A satin band about a cun wide was tied around his forehead, presumably for a headache. “Sit here.” Hu patted the embroidered stool beside him and pointed to his head with a smile. “Don’t I look like a woman resting after childbirth?” If he could still joke, Zhou thought with relief, perhaps things were not as bad as he had imagined.

于是闲闲谈起查封公济典的事，原原本本、巨细靡遗，最后谈到从唐子韶那里追出中饱的款子以后，如何分派的办法。“算了，算了。”胡雪岩说：“不必认真。”此言一出，周少棠愣住了，好半天才说了句：“看起来，倒是我多事了，”“少棠，你这样子一说，我变成半吊子了。事到如今，我同你说老实话，我不是心甘情愿做洋盘瘟生，不分好歹，不识是非，我是为了另外一个人。”“为了哪一个？”周少棠当然要追问。“唐子韶的姨太太。”“喔，喔！”周少棠恍然大悟，他亦久知胡雪岩有此一段艳闻，此刻正好求证：“我听说，唐子韶设美人局，你上了他的当？”“也不算上当，是我一时糊涂。这话也不必去说它了。”胡雪岩紧接着说：“昨天我同我的几个妾说：我放你们一条生路，愿意走的自己房间里东西都带走，我另外送五千银子。想想月如总同我好过。现在有了这样一个机会，我想放他一马。不过，这是马逢时的公事，又是你出了大力，我只好说一声：多谢你！到底应该怎么办？我也不敢多干预。”“原来你是这么一种心思，倒是我错怪你了。”同少棠又说：“原来是我想替你尽点心，你不忘记者相好，想这样子办，我当然照你的意思。至于论多论少，我要看情形办，而且我要告诉人家。”

He began casually describing the inspection of Gongji, recounting the whole affair without omitting the smallest detail. Finally he explained how the money was to be divided once recovered from Tang. “Let it go,” Hu said. “There’s no need to pursue it so seriously.” Zhou stared. Only after a long silence could he say, “It seems I’ve been meddling unnecessarily.” “Shaotang, that makes me sound a halfwit. Let me tell you the truth. I’m not willingly playing the gullible fool, unable to distinguish good from bad or right from wrong. I’m thinking of someone else.” “Who?” Zhou naturally asked. “Tang’s concubine.” “Ah!” Zhou understood at once. He had long known of Hu’s amorous adventure and now had a chance to confirm it. “I heard Tang laid a beauty trap and you fell into it?” “It wasn’t exactly that. I lost my head for a moment. There’s no need to discuss it now.” Hu went on, “Yesterday I told my concubines: ‘I’m giving you a way out. Any of you who wish to leave may take everything in your rooms, and I’ll give you five thousand taels besides.’ Yueru, after all, once shared my affection. Now that I have this opportunity, I’d like to let Tang off. But it is Ma Fengshi’s official business, and you have gone to such trouble. All I can do is thank you. I wouldn’t presume to interfere too much with how it is handled.” “So that is what you have in mind. I misjudged you. I only wanted to do something for you. If you remember an old lover and want it handled this way, naturally I’ll follow your wishes. As for how much or how little, I must judge by circumstances. And I shall tell them.”

“不必，不必！不必说破。”胡雪岩忽然神秘地一笑，“少棠，你记不记得石塔儿头的‘豆腐西施’阿香？”周少棠愣了一下，从尘封的记忆中，找出阿香的影子来——石塔儿头是地名，有家豆腐店的女儿，就是阿香，艳声四播。先是周少棠做了入幕之宾，后来胡雪岩做了他的所谓“同靴弟兄”，周少棠就绝迹不去了。少年春梦，如今回想起来，什么感觉都没有了，只是奇怪胡雪岩何以忽然提了起来？“当初那件事，我心里一直难过，‘兔子不吃窝边草’，我不该割你的靴腰子。现在顶好一报还一报。”胡雪岩放低了声音说：“月如是匹扬州人所说的‘瘦马，，你倒骑她一骑看。”听此一说，周少棠有点动心，不过口头上却是一叠连声地道：“笑话，笑话！”胡雪岩不作声，笑容慢慢地收敛，双眼却不断眨动，显然有个念头在转。“那么，少棠，我说一句决不是笑话的话，你要不要听？”“要的。”

“No, no! Don’t explain it.” Hu suddenly smiled mysteriously. “Shaotang, do you remember A’xiang, the ‘Tofu Beauty’ at Shita’ertou?” Zhou paused, retrieving her image from the dust of memory. Shita’ertou was a place name. A’xiang, the daughter of a tofu-shop owner there, had been famous for her beauty. Zhou had first become her lover; later Hu had become his so-called “brother sharing the same boots,” and Zhou had stopped visiting altogether. Looking back on that youthful dream of love, he felt nothing now. He only wondered why Hu had suddenly brought it up. “I’ve always felt bad about that. A rabbit shouldn’t eat the grass beside its own burrow. I shouldn’t have poached on you. Now it would be best to repay you in kind.” Lowering his voice, Hu said, “Yueru is what Yangzhou people call a ‘slender horse.’ Why don’t you try riding her?” Zhou felt a flicker of interest, though he repeatedly protested, “You must be joking!” Hu said nothing. His smile slowly faded, while his eyes kept blinking: plainly another thought was forming. “Then, Shaotang, would you like to hear something that is certainly no joke?” “Yes.”

“年大将军的故事，你总晓得罗？”“年大将军”是指年羹尧。这位被杭州人神乎其词他说他“一夜工夫连降十八级“的年大将军，在杭州大概有半年的辰光，他是先由一等公降为杭州将军，然后又降为”闲散章京“，满洲话叫做”拜他喇布勒哈番“，汉名叫做”骑都尉“，正四品，被派为西湖边上涌金门的城守尉，杭州关于他的故事极多，所以周少棠问说：”你是问哪一个？““是年大将军赠妾的故事。”这是众多年羹尧的故事中，最富传奇性的一个。据说，年羹尧每天坐在涌金门口，进出乡人，震于他的威名，或者避道而行，或者俯首疾趋，惟有一个穷书生，早晚进出，必定恭恭敬敬地作一个揖。这样过了几个月，逮捕年羹尧入京的上谕到了杭州，于是第二夭一早，年羹尧等那穷书生经过时，喊住他说：“我看你人很忠厚，我这番入京，大概性命不保，有个小妾想送给你，请你照料，千万不要推辞。”那个穷书生哪敢作此非分之想，一再推辞，年羹尧则一再相劝。最后，穷书生说了老实话，家徒四壁，添一口人实在养不起。“原来是为这一层，你无庸担心，明天我派人送她去。你住哪里？”问了半天，穷书生才说了他家的住址。下一天黄昏，一乘小轿到门，随携少数“嫁妆”。那轿中走出来一个风信年华的丽人，便是年羹尧的爱妾。穷书生无端得此一段艳福，自然喜心翻倒，但却不知往后何以度日。那丽人一言不发，只将带来的一张双抽屉的桌子，开锁打开抽屉，里面装满了珠宝，足供一生。

“You know the stories about General Nian, surely?” General Nian was Nian Gengyao. Hangzhou people told fantastic tales of his being “demoted eighteen ranks in a single night.” He had spent roughly six months in the city, first reduced from duke of the first class to Hangzhou Garrison General, then to an unattached officer—baitalabulehafan in Manchu, cavalry commandant in Chinese, of the regular fourth rank—and assigned as commander of the guard at Yongjin Gate beside West Lake. There were so many stories about him in Hangzhou that Zhou asked, “Which one?” “The story of General Nian giving away his concubine.” This was one of the most remarkable of the many Nian Gengyao legends. It was said that he sat every day at Yongjin Gate. Country people passing through, awed by his formidable reputation, either avoided him or hurried past with lowered heads. Only a poor scholar, who came and went morning and evening, always greeted him with a respectful bow. Several months passed. Then an imperial order arrived for Nian’s arrest and removal to the capital. Early the next morning, he stopped the scholar. “I can see that you’re an honest, kindhearted man. I doubt I shall survive this journey to the capital. I have a concubine I should like to give you. Please look after her, and do not refuse.” The poor scholar dared not entertain such an extravagant thought. He repeatedly declined, while Nian repeatedly urged him. Finally he admitted the truth: his house was bare, and he could not afford another mouth to feed. “So that is the difficulty! You needn’t worry. I’ll send her tomorrow. Where do you live?” Only after much questioning did the scholar reveal his address. At dusk the next day, a small sedan arrived, accompanied by a modest “dowry.” A beautiful woman in the bloom of her twenties stepped out: Nian’s favorite concubine. The scholar was overwhelmed with joy at this unexpected romantic good fortune, yet did not know how they would live. Without a word, the woman unlocked the two drawers of a table she had brought. They were full of jewels—enough for a lifetime.

“我现在跟年大将军差不多。”胡雪岩说：“我的几个妾，昨天走了一半，有几个说一定要跟我，有一个想走不走，主意还没有定，看她的意思是怕终身无靠。我这个妾人很老实，我要替她好好找个靠得住的人。少棠，你把她领了回去。”“你说笑话了！”周少棠毫不思索地说，“没有这个道理！”“怎么会没有这个道理。你没有听‘说大书’的讲过，这种赠妾、赠马的事，古人常常有的。现在是我送给你，可不是你来夺爱，怕啥？”周少棠不作声，他倒是想推辞，但找不出理由，最后只好这样说：“我要同我老婆去商量看。”

“I am much like General Nian now,” Hu said. “Half my concubines left yesterday. Some insist on staying with me. One has not decided whether to go; I think she fears having nobody to depend on for the rest of her life. She is a very honest woman, and I want to find someone trustworthy for her. Shaotang, take her home with you.” “You’re joking!” Zhou replied without thinking. “There can be no question of it.” “Why not? Haven’t you heard the storytellers? People in the old days often gave away concubines or horses. I’m offering her to you; you aren’t stealing my beloved. What is there to fear?” Zhou fell silent. He wanted to refuse but could find no reason. At last he could only say, “I must discuss it with my wife.”

第二天一大早，周少棠还在床上，杨书办便来敲门了。起床迎接，周少棠先为前一日晚上失迎致歉，接着动问来意。“唐子韶！”杨书办说：“昨天早晚就来看我，要我陪了他来看你。看起来此人倒蛮听话，我昨天叫他晚上来看你，他真的来了。”“此刻呢？人在哪里？”“我说我约好了你，再招呼他来见面，叫他先回去。你看，在哪里碰头？”“要稍为隐蔽一点的地方。”“那么，在我家里好了。”杨书办说：“我去约他，你洗了脸、吃了点心就来。”周少棠点点头，送杨书办出门以后，一面漱洗，一面盘算，想到胡雪岩昨天的话，不免怦然心动，想看看月如倒是怎么样的一匹“瘦马”？到得杨家，唐子韶早就到了，一见周少棠，忙不迭地站了起来，反客为主，代替杨书办招待后到之客，十分殷勤。“少棠兄，”杨书办站起来说：“ 你们谈谈，我料理了一桩小事，马上过来。中午在我这里便饭。”这是让他们得以密谈，声明备饭，更是暗示不妨详谈、长谈。

Early the next morning, while Zhou was still in bed, Clerk Yang knocked at his door. Zhou rose to receive him, apologized for having been out the previous evening, and asked why he had come. “Tang Zishao! He came to see me last night and asked me to accompany him to your place. He seems quite obedient. I told him yesterday to see you in the evening, and he really came.” “Where is he now?” “I said I’d arrange a meeting with you and let him know, then sent him home. Where shall you meet?” “Somewhere reasonably secluded.” “My house, then. I’ll fetch him. Come over when you’ve washed and had something to eat.” Zhou nodded. After seeing Yang out, he washed and considered his plans. Remembering Hu’s words the previous day, he could not help feeling tempted. He wanted to see what sort of “slender horse” Yueru might be. Tang was already at Yang’s house when Zhou arrived. He hastily stood and, behaving like the host rather than a guest, attended to the newcomer with great solicitude. “Brother Shaotang,” Yang said as he rose, “you two talk. I have a small matter to attend to and will be back shortly. Stay for a simple lunch.” He was leaving them to speak privately; mentioning lunch further suggested that they need not hurry and could discuss everything at length.

但实际上无须花多少辰光，因为唐子韶成竹在胸，不必抵赖，当周少棠出示由杨书办抄来的清单，算出他一共侵吞了八万三千多银子时，他双膝一跪，口中说道：“周先生，请你救救我。”“言重，言重！”周少棠赶紧将他拉了起来，“唐朝奉，你说要我救你，不管我办得到、办不到，你总要拿出一个办法来，我才好斟酌。”“周先生，我先说实话，陆陆续续挪用了胡大先生的架本，也是叫没奈何！这几年运气不好，做生意亏本，我那个小妾又好赌，输掉不少。胡大先生现在落难，我如果有办法，早就应该把这笔款子补上了。”“照此说来，你是‘铁公鸡，一毛不拔，？”“不是，不是。”唐子韶说，一我手里还有点古董、玉器。我知道周先生你是大行家，什么时候到我那里看看，能值多少？“唐子韶略停一下又说：”现款是没有多少，我再尽量凑。““你能凑多少？”“一时还算不出。总要先看了那些东西，估个价，看缺多少，再想办法。”原来这是唐子韶投其所好，编出来的一套话。周少棠玩玉器，在“茶会”上颇有名声，听了唐子韶的话信以为真，欣然答说：“好！你看什么时候，我去看看。”“就是今天晚上好不好，”唐子韶说：“小妾做的菜，很不坏。我叫她显显手段，请周先生来赏鉴赏鉴。”一听这话，周少棠色心与食指皆动，不过不能不顾到杨书办与马逢时，因而说道：“你不该请我一个。”“我知道，我知道。马大老爷我不便请他，我再请杨书办。”

In fact, little time was needed, for Tang had his plan ready and had no intention of denying anything. When Zhou produced Yang’s copied list and calculated that the total embezzled exceeded eighty-three thousand taels, Tang dropped to his knees. “Mr Zhou, please save me!” “Please, please!” Zhou hastily pulled him up. “Mr Tang, whether or not I can save you, you must first propose some course for me to consider.” “Let me tell the truth. I took money from Mr Hu’s capital little by little because I had no choice. My luck has been bad these past few years. I lost money in business, and my concubine loves gambling and has lost a great deal too. Now that Mr Hu is in trouble, if I had any means of doing so, I ought to have replaced the money long ago.” “So you’re an iron rooster, unwilling to part with a single feather?” “No, no! I still have a few antiques and jades. I know you are an expert. Perhaps you could come and see what they’re worth?” Tang paused, then added, “There isn’t much cash, but I’ll gather whatever I can.” “How much?” “I can’t say at once. First we must value the objects and see what is lacking; then I’ll try to find a way.” This was a story Tang had invented to appeal to Zhou’s tastes. Zhou’s interest in jade was well known in the collectors’ tea gatherings. Taking Tang at his word, he readily agreed. “Very well. When shall I come?” “Would this evening suit you? My concubine cooks very well. I’ll ask her to show what she can do, and you can judge her skill.” The invitation stirred both Zhou’s lust and his appetite. Still, he could not ignore Yang and Ma. “You shouldn’t invite only me.” “I understand. It would be awkward for me to invite His Honour Ma, but I’ll ask Clerk Yang as well.”

杨书办是故意躲开的，根本没有什么事要料理，所以发觉唐子韶与周少棠的谈话已告一段落，随即赶了出来留客。“便饭已经快预备好了，吃了再走。”“谢谢！谢谢！”唐子韶连连拱手，“我还有事，改日再来打搅。顺便提一声：今天晚上我请周少棠到舍下便饭，请你老兄作陪。”说成“顺便提一声”，可知根本没有邀客的诚意，而且杨书办也知道他们晚上还有未完的话要谈，亦根本不想夹在中间。当即亦以晚上有事作推托，回绝了邀约。送走唐子韶，留下周少棠，把杯密谈，周少棠将前一天去看胡雪岩的情形，说了给杨书办听。不过，他没有提到胡雪岩劝他去骑月如那匹瘦马的话。这倒并非是他故障隐瞒，而是他根本还没有作任何决定，即使见了动心，跃跃欲试，也要看看情形再说。“胡大先生倒真是够气概！”杨书办说：“今日之下，他还顾念着老交情！照他这样厚道来看，将来只怕还有翻身的日子。”“ 难！他的靠山已经不中用，他本人呢，锐气也倒了，哪里还有翻身的日子？”周少棠略停一下说：“闲话少说，言归正传，你看要唐子韶吐多少出来？”“请你作主。”周少棠由于对月如存着企图，便留了个可以伸缩的余地，“多则一半，少则两三万。”他说，“我们三一三十一。”

Yang had deliberately withdrawn and had nothing to attend to. Realizing that their conversation had ended, he immediately came out to urge them to stay. “Lunch is almost ready. Have it before you go.” “Thank you, thank you!” Tang clasped his hands repeatedly. “I have something to do. I’ll trouble you another day. By the way, I’ve invited Zhou to a simple dinner at my house tonight. Please join us.” The phrase “by the way” showed how little sincerity there was in the invitation. Yang also knew they had unfinished business to discuss and had no wish to come between them. Claiming an engagement that evening, he declined. After seeing Tang off, he kept Zhou for a confidential conversation over wine. Zhou described his visit to Hu the day before, omitting the suggestion that he ride Yueru, the “slender horse.” This was not deliberate concealment; he had simply made no decision. Even if the sight of her tempted him, he would first have to judge the circumstances. “Mr Hu has real generosity of spirit,” Yang said. “Even now he remembers old affections. A man as kindhearted as that may yet rise again.” “Hardly. His powerful patron is no longer any use, and his own spirit is broken. How can he rise again?” Zhou paused. “Enough of that. To business: how much should we make Tang disgorge?” “You decide.” Having designs on Yueru, Zhou left himself room to maneuver. “Half at most; twenty or thirty thousand at least. We three will divide it equally.”

唐子韶家很容易找，只要到公济典后面一条巷子问一声“唐朝奉住哪里？”自会有人指点给他看。是唐子韶亲自应的门，一见面便说：“今天很冷，请楼上坐。”楼上升了火盆，板壁缝隙上新糊了白纸条，外面虽然风大，里头却是温暖如春，周少棠的狐皮袍子穿不住了，依主人的建议脱了下来，只穿一件直贡呢夹袄就很舒服了。“周先生，要不要‘香一筒，？”唐子韶指着烟盘说。“你自己来。”周少棠说：“我没有瘾，不过喜欢躺烟盘。”“那就来靠一靠。”唐子韶令丫头点了烟灯，然后去捧出一只大锦盒来，放在烟盘下方说道：“周先生，你先看几样玉器。”两人相对躺了下来，唐子韶抽大烟，周少棠便打开锦盒，鉴赏玉器，那锦盒是做了隔板的，每一层上面三块汉玉，每一块的尺寸大致相仿，一寸多长，六七分宽，上面刻的篆字，周少棠只认得最后四个字。“这是‘刚卯’。”周少棠指着最后四个字说：“一定有这四个字：”莫我敢当‘。““喔，”唐子韶故意问说：“刚卯作啥用场？”“辟邪的。”“刚卯的刚好懂，既然辟邪，当然要刚强。”唐子韶说：“卯就不懂了。”“卯是‘卯金刀’，汉朝是姓刘的天下。还有一个说法，要在正月里选一个，所以叫刚卯。”“周先生真正内行。”“玩儿汉玉，这些门道总要懂的。”说着周少棠又取第二方，就着烟灯细看。

Tang’s house was easy to find. One had only to go into the lane behind Gongji Pawnshop and ask where Pawnbroker Tang lived; someone would point it out. Tang answered the door himself. “It’s very cold today. Come upstairs.” A brazier was burning there, and fresh strips of white paper covered the cracks in the wooden partitions. Though the wind outside was strong, the room was as warm as spring. Zhou could not bear to keep his fox-fur robe on. At his host’s suggestion, he removed it and was perfectly comfortable in his lined jacket of woolen satin. “Would you care for a fragrant pipeful?” Tang asked, indicating the smoking tray. “You go ahead. I have no craving, though I like reclining beside a smoking tray.” “Then make yourself comfortable.” Tang told a maid to light the opium lamp, brought out a large brocade-covered box, and placed it below the tray. “Have a look at a few jades first.” They lay facing each other. Tang smoked while Zhou opened the box to examine its contents. It was divided by removable trays. On the top lay three Han jades, each roughly the same size: a little over one cun long and six or seven fen wide. Zhou could recognize only the last four seal-script characters carved on them. “These are gangmao amulets,” he said, pointing. “They must have these four characters: ‘None dare confront me.’” “Oh?” Tang asked deliberately. “What are gangmao used for?” “Warding off evil.” “Gang means strong—that I understand. Naturally, something that wards off evil must be strong. But I don’t understand mao.” “Mao, together with ‘gold’ and ‘knife,’ gives the surname Liu. The Han was the Liu dynasty. Another explanation says the choice must be made in the first month of the year; hence the name gangmao.” “You really are an expert.” “Anyone who collects Han jade must know such things.” Zhou took up the second piece and examined it by the opium lamp.

“你看这三块刚卯，怎么样？”“都还不错。不过……”唐于韶见他缩口不语，便抬眼问道：“不过不值钱？”“也不好说不值钱。”周少棠没有再说下去。唐子韶当然明白，他的意思是，几万银子的亏欠，拿这些东西来作抵，还差得远，因而也就不必再问了，只伸手揭开隔板说道：“这样东西，恐怕周先生以前没有见过。”周少棠拿起来一看，确是初见，是很大的一块古色斑斓的汉玉，大约八寸见方，刻成一个圆环，再由圆环中心向外刻线，每条线的未端有个数目字，从一到九十，一共是九十条线，刻得极细极深极均匀。“这是啥？象个罗盘。”“不错，同罗盘差不多，是日规。”“日规？”周少棠反复细看，“玉倒确是汉玉，好象出土不久。”“法眼、法眼！”唐子韶竖起大拇指说：“出土不过三四年，是归化城出土的。”“喔，”周少棠对此物颇感兴趣，“这块玉啥价钱？”“刚刚出土，以前也没有过同样的东西，所以行情不明。”唐子韶又说：“原只要当一千银子，我还了他五百，最后当了七百银子。这样东西，要遇见识货的，可以卖好价钱。”“嗯。”周少棠不置可否，去揭第二块隔板，下面是大大小小七八方玉印。正取起一块把玩时，只听得楼梯上有响声，便即侧身静听。

“What do you think of these three gangmao?” “They’re all quite good. But…” When Zhou stopped, Tang looked up. “But they aren’t worth much?” “I wouldn’t say that.” Zhou went no further. Tang understood: against a debt of tens of thousands, objects like these would fall far short. There was no need to ask more. Lifting the partition, he said, “I doubt you have seen anything like this before.” Zhou picked it up. It was indeed new to him: a large piece of Han jade with a rich, mottled patina, about eight cun square, carved with a circular ring. Lines radiated outward from the center, each ending in a number, from one to ninety. There were ninety lines in all, exceptionally fine, deep, and evenly cut. “What is it? It looks like a compass.” “Yes, rather like one. It’s a sundial.” “A sundial?” Zhou examined it repeatedly. “The jade is certainly Han. It looks as though it was excavated recently.” “A discerning eye!” Tang held up his thumb. “Only three or four years ago, in Guihua City.” Intrigued, Zhou asked, “What is it worth?” “It’s only recently come to light, and nothing like it had been seen before, so there’s no established price. The owner originally wanted a loan of a thousand taels. I offered five hundred, and we finally settled on seven hundred. In the hands of someone who appreciates it, it could fetch a good price.” Zhou murmured without committing himself and lifted the second partition. Beneath it lay seven or eight jade seals of various sizes. He had just picked one up when footsteps sounded on the stairs. Turning onto his side, he listened.

“你去问问老爷，饭开在哪里？”语声发自外面那间屋子，清脆而沉着，从语声的韵味中，想象得到月如过了风信年华，正将步入徐娘阶段的年龄。这样在咫尺之外，发号施令，指挥丫头，是不是意味着她不会露面？转念到此，周少棠心头，不免浮起一丝怅惘之感。此时丫头进来请示，唐子韶已经交代，饭就开在楼上，理由仍旧是楼上比较暖和。接着，门帘启处，周少棠眼前一亮，进来的少妇，约可三十上下年纪，长身玉立，鹅蛋形的脸上，长了一双极明亮的杏眼，眼风闪处，象有股什么力量，将周少棠从烟榻上弹了起来，望着盈盈含笑的月如，不由得也在脸上堆满了笑容。“这是小妾月如。”在烧烟的唐子韶，拿烟签子指点着说：“月如，这是周老爷，你见一见。”“喔，是姨大大！”周少棠先就抱拳作揖。“不敢当，不敢当！”月如裣作礼，“周老爷我好象哪里见过。”“你自然见过。”唐子韶说：“那天阜康门口搭了高台，几句话说得挤兑的人鸦雀无声，就是周老爷。”

“Ask the master where dinner is to be served.” The voice came from the outer room, clear and composed. Its tone suggested that Yueru was past the first bloom of womanhood and approaching the age of mature charm. Giving orders to a maid from only a few steps away—did that mean she would not appear herself? A slight disappointment rose in Zhou. When the maid came to inquire, Tang ordered dinner served upstairs, again because it was warmer. Then the curtain lifted, and Zhou’s eyes brightened. The woman who entered was about thirty, tall and graceful, with an oval face and exceptionally bright almond-shaped eyes. As her glance swept towards him, some force seemed to spring him from the smoking couch. Looking at her gentle smile, he found his own face wreathed in smiles. “This is my concubine, Yueru,” Tang said, indicating her with his opium needle as he prepared another pipe. “Yueru, this is Mr Zhou. Make your greeting.” “Ah, Madam!” Zhou clasped his hands and bowed first. “You are too kind!” She curtsied. “Mr Zhou, I feel I’ve seen you somewhere.” “Naturally you have,” Tang said. “Remember the platform outside Fukang, and the few words that silenced everyone demanding their money? That was Mr Zhou.”

“啊！我想起来了。”月如那双眼睛，闪闪发亮，惊喜交集，“那天我同邻居去看热闹回来，谈周老爷谈了两三夭。周老爷的口才，真正没话说。这倒还在其次，大家都说周老爷的义气，真正少见。胡大先生是胡财神，平常捧财神的不晓得多少，到了财神落难，好比变了瘟神，哪个不是见了他就躲，只有周老爷看不过，出来说公道话。如今一看周老爷的相貌，就晓得是行善积德，得饶人处且饶人，有大福气的厚道君子。“这番话说得周少棠心上象熨过一样服帖，当然，他也有数，“得饶人处且饶人”，话中已经递过点子来了。“好说，好说！”周少棠说：“我亦久闻唐姨太太贤惠能干，是我们老唐的贤内助。唐子韶一听称呼都改过了，知道周少棠必中圈套，“随你奸似鬼，要吃老娘洗脚水”，心中暗暗得意，一丢烟枪，翻身而起，口中说道：“好吃酒了。”

“Ah, now I remember!” Her eyes sparkled with delighted surprise. “I went with our neighbors to watch. We talked about you for two or three days afterward. Your eloquence is beyond praise. But that is the lesser thing. Everyone says your loyalty is truly rare. Mr Hu was the God of Wealth; who knows how many people flattered him then? Once misfortune struck, he became a God of Pestilence, and everyone fled at the sight of him. Only you could not bear it and came forward to speak fairly. Now that I see you, I can tell you’re a blessed, kindhearted gentleman who does good, earns merit, and shows mercy wherever he can.” Her words soothed Zhou as though his heart had been gently ironed. Naturally, he recognized the hint conveyed by “shows mercy wherever he can.” “You are too kind. I too have long heard how capable and virtuous Mistress Tang is—a worthy helpmate to our Old Tang.” Hearing this change of address, Tang knew Zhou was certain to fall into the trap. “Cunning as a devil, yet you’ll drink the water a woman has washed her feet in,” he thought smugly. Tossing aside his pipe, he sprang up. “Time for wine!”

其时方桌已经搭开，自然是请周少棠上座，但只唐子韶侧面相陪。菜并非如何讲究，但颇为人味，周少棠喜爱糟臃之物，所以对糟蒸白鱼、家乡肉、醉蟹这三样肴馔，格外欣赏，听说家乡肉、醉蟹并非市售，而是月如手制，便更赞不绝口了。周少棠的谈锋很键，兴致又好，加以唐子韶是刻意奉承，所以快饮剧谈，相当投机。当然，话题都是轻松有趣的。“老唐，”周少棠间到唐子韶的本行，“天下的朝奉，都是你们徽州人，好比票号都是山西人，而且听说只有太谷、平遥这两三府的人。这是啥道理？”“这话，周先生，别人问我，我就装糊涂，随便敷衍几句，你老哥问到，我不能不跟你谈来历，不过，说起来不是啥体面的事？”“喔，怎么呢？”

The square table had been set. Naturally Zhou Shaotang was given the seat of honour, but only Tang Zishao sat beside him. The dishes were not particularly elaborate, yet they were delicious. Zhou liked foods preserved in wine or wine lees, and especially enjoyed the whitefish steamed with lees, the country-style cured pork, and the drunken crabs. On learning that the pork and crabs had been prepared by Yueru herself rather than bought, he praised them still more warmly. Zhou was an animated talker and in excellent spirits; Tang was deliberately flattering him. They drank freely, talked eagerly, and got on very well. Their subjects were naturally light and entertaining. “Old Tang,” Zhou asked, turning to his host’s trade, “all the pawnbrokers in the country seem to be Huizhou men, just as all the remittance banks belong to Shanxi men. I have heard that even those come from only two or three prefectures, such as Taigu and Pingyao. Why is that?” “Mr Zhou, if anyone else asked, I should pretend not to know and put him off with a few words. But since it is you, I must tell you the history. It is not a very creditable story, though.” “Oh? How so?”

“明朝嘉靖年间，我们徽州有个人，叫汪直，你晓得不晓得。”“我只晓得嘉靖年间有个‘打严嵩’的邹应龙，不晓得啥汪直。”“你不晓得我告诉你，汪直是个汉奸。”“汉奸？莫非象秦桧一样私通外国。”“一点不错。”唐子韶答说，“不过汪直私通的不是金兵，是日本人，那时候叫做倭寇。倭寇到我们中国，在江浙沿海地方一登了陆，两眼漆黑，都是汪直同他的部下做向导，带他们一路奸淫掳掠。倭寇很下作，放枪的时候，什么东西都要，不过有的带不走，带走了，到他们日本也未见得有用，所以汪直动了个脑筋，开爿典当，什么东西都好当，老百姓来当东面，不过是个幌子，说穿了，不过替日本人销赃而已。““怪不得了，你们那笔字象鬼画符，说话用‘切口’，原来都有讲究的。”周少棠说：“这是犯法的事情，当然要用同乡人。”“不过，话要说回来，徽州地方苦得很，本地出产养不活本地人，只好出外谋生，呼朋招友，同乡照顾同乡，也是迫不得已。”

“During the Jiajing reign of the Ming, there was a man from our Huizhou called Wang Zhi. Have you heard of him?” “I know only that there was a Zou Yinglong in the Jiajing reign—the man who attacked Yan Song. I know nothing about Wang Zhi.” “Then I shall tell you. Wang Zhi was a traitor.” “A traitor? You mean he conspired with foreigners, like Qin Hui?” “Exactly. But Wang Zhi’s allies were not the Jin troops. They were Japanese, what people then called the wokou pirates. When they landed on the Jiangsu and Zhejiang coast, they knew nothing of the country. Wang Zhi and his followers guided them as they raped and plundered their way inland. The pirates were a base lot: when looting, they took everything. Some things they could not carry away; others would be of little use in Japan even if they could. So Wang Zhi had an idea. He opened a pawnshop that would accept anything. Ordinary people bringing in their pledges were merely a cover. In plain language, he was disposing of stolen goods for the Japanese.” “No wonder your writing looks like a sorcerer’s charms, and you speak in special jargon. There was a reason for it all,” Zhou said. “Since it was illegal, you naturally had to use men from your own district.” “Still, one must remember how poor Huizhou is. What the district produces cannot support its own people. They have to go elsewhere for a living, calling in friends and helping fellow townsmen. They have little choice.”

“你们微州人做生意，实在厉害，象扬州的大盐商，问起来祖籍一大半是徽州。”周少棠说：“象汪直这样子，做了汉奸，还替日本人销赃，倒不怕公家抓他法办？”“这也有个原因的，当时的巡按御史，后来做了巡抚的胡宗宪，也是徽州人，虽不说包庇，念在同乡份上，略为高一高手，事情就过去了。官司不怕大，只要有交情，总好商量。”唐子韶举杯相邀：“来，来，周先生干一杯。”最后那两句话，加上敬酒的动作，意在言外，的然可见，但周少棠装作不觉，千了酒，将话题扯了开去，“那个胡宗宪，你说他是巡按御史，恐怕并没有庇护汪直的权柄。”他又问一句：“真的权柄这么大。”“那只要看三堂会审的王金龙好了。”“王金龙是小生扮的，好象刚刚出道，哪有这样子的威风？戏总是戏。”谈到这方面，唐子韶比周少棠内行得多了，“明朝的进士，同现在不一样。现在的进士，如果不是点翰林或者到六部去当司官，放出来不过是个‘老虎班’的知县，明朝的进士，一点‘巡按御史’赏上方宝剑，等于皇上亲自来巡查，威风得不得了。我讲个故事，周先生你就晓得巡按御史的权柄了。”

“You Huizhou men certainly know how to do business. Ask the great salt merchants of Yangzhou where their families came from, and more than half say Huizhou. But if Wang Zhi was both a traitor and a receiver of the Japanese pirates’ stolen goods, was he not afraid of being arrested?” “There was a reason for that too. Hu Zongxian, the inspecting censor who later became governor, was also a Huizhou man. One need not call it protection; he had only to be a little lenient towards a fellow townsman, and the matter passed. However serious a case may be, if there is friendship, something can always be arranged.” Tang raised his cup. “Come, Mr Zhou, let us drink.” The last two sentences, accompanied by the toast, plainly carried another meaning. Zhou pretended not to notice. He drained his cup and changed the subject. “You say this Hu Zongxian was an inspecting censor. I doubt he had the power to protect Wang Zhi. Was his authority really so great?” “You have only to look at Wang Jinlong in The Trial Before Three Judges.” “Wang Jinlong is played as a young man, apparently just beginning his career. How could he have such authority? A play is only a play.” Tang knew much more about this than Zhou. “Ming jinshi were different from those today. Nowadays, unless a jinshi enters the Hanlin Academy or becomes an official in one of the Six Ministries, he is sent out as no more than a county magistrate of the ‘tiger class.’ But a Ming jinshi appointed inspecting censor received an imperial sword of authority. He was as good as the emperor himself on a tour of inspection. His power was tremendous. Let me tell you a story, and you will understand.”

据说明朝有个富人，生两个女儿，长女嫁武官，次女嫁了个寒士，富人不免有势利之见，所以次婿受了许多委屈。及至次婿两榜及第，点了河南的巡按御史，而长婿恰好在河南南阳当总兵。御史七品，总兵二品，但巡按御史“代天巡狩”，地位不同，所以次婿巡按到南阳，第二天五更时分，尚未起身，长婿已来禀请开操阅兵，那次婿想到当年岳家待他们连襟二人，炎凉各异，一时感慨，在枕上口占一绝：“黄草坡前万甲兵，碧纱帐里一书主；于今应识诗文贵，卧听元戎报五更。”既“有诗为证”，周少棠不能不信，而且触类旁通，有所领悟，“这样说起来，‘三堂会审’左右的红袍、蓝袍，应该是藩司同臬司？”他问：“我猜得对不对？”“一点不错。”“藩司、桌司旁坐陪审，那么居中坐的，身分应该是巡抚？”“胡宗宪就是由巡按浙江的御史，改为浙江巡抚的。”“那就是了。”周少棠惋惜他说“胡大先生如果遇到他的本家就好了。”这就是说，胡雪岩如果遇见一个能象胡宗宪照顾同乡汪直那样的巡抚，他的典当就不至于会查封。唐子韶明白他的意思，但不愿意接口。

There was said to have been a rich man in the Ming with two daughters. The elder married a military officer, the younger a poor scholar. The father was somewhat snobbish, and the younger son-in-law suffered many slights. Eventually the scholar passed the provincial and metropolitan examinations and was appointed inspecting censor for Henan. His fellow son-in-law happened to be brigade commander at Nanyang in that province. A censor held the seventh rank, a brigade commander the second. But an inspecting censor toured on the emperor’s behalf, which gave him a different standing. When he reached Nanyang, the commander came before he was out of bed, during the fifth watch next morning, to request permission to parade the troops for inspection. Remembering how differently their father-in-law had treated them, the scholar was moved to compose a quatrain on his pillow: “Before the yellow-grass slope, ten thousand armoured men; behind green gauze curtains, a solitary scholar. Now you should know the worth of verse and prose: lying in bed, I hear the commander announce the fifth watch.” With a poem to prove the story, Zhou could hardly disbelieve it. He also drew a further conclusion. “Then the men in red and blue robes on either side in The Trial Before Three Judges must be the provincial treasurer and judicial commissioner. Am I right?” “Exactly.” “If those two sit beside him as fellow judges, the man in the centre ought to have the standing of a governor?” “Hu Zongxian went from inspecting censor for Zhejiang to governor of Zhejiang.” “That explains it.” Zhou sighed. “If only Mr Hu had encountered that namesake of his!” He meant that, had Hu Xueyan found a governor willing to protect him as Hu Zongxian had protected his fellow townsman Wang Zhi, his pawnshops would not have been taken into official custody. Tang understood but did not care to respond.

“周先生，”唐子韶忽然说道：“公济有好些满当的东西，你要不要来看着？”周少棠不想贪这个小便宜，但亦不愿一口谢绝，便即问说：“有没有啥比较特别、外面少见的东西？““有，有，多得很。”唐子韶想了一会说：“快要过年了，有一堂灯，我劝周先生买了回去。到正月十五挂起来，包管出色。”一听这话，周少棠不免诧异，上元的花灯、竹篾彩纸所扎，以新奇为贵，他想不明白，凭什么可以上当铺？因此，他愣了一下问道：“这种灯大概不是纸扎货？”“当然。不然怎么好来当？”唐子韶说：“灯是绢灯，样子不多，大致照宫灯的式样，以六角形为主。绢上画人物仕女，各种故事，架子是活动的，用过了收拾干净，折起包好，明年再用。海宁一带，通行这种灯。周先生没有看过？”“没有。”“周先生看过了就晓得了。这种灯不是哄小讶儿的纸扎走马灯，要有身分的人家，请有身分的客人吃春酒，厅上、廊上挂起来，手里端杯酒，慢慢赏鉴绢上的各家画画。当然，也可以做它多少条灯谜，挂在灯上，请客人来打。这是文文静静的玩法：象周先生现在也够身分了，应该置办这么一堂灯。”周少棠近年收入不坏，常想在身分上力争上流，尤其是最近为阜康的事，跟官府打过交道，已俨然在绪绅先生之列，所以对唐子韶的话，颇为动心，想了一下间道：“办这么一堂灯，不晓得要花多少？”

“Mr Zhou,” Tang said suddenly, “Gongji has quite a few unredeemed pledges whose terms have expired. Would you like to come and look?” Zhou did not want to take such a petty advantage, but neither did he wish to refuse outright. “Is there anything unusual, something one does not often see elsewhere?” “Yes, plenty.” Tang thought for a moment. “The New Year is approaching. There is a set of lanterns I advise you to buy. Hang them up on the fifteenth of the first month, and I guarantee they will be a splendid sight.” Zhou was puzzled. Lantern Festival lanterns were made of bamboo strips and coloured paper; novelty was their chief attraction. How could they be accepted as pledges? “These cannot be paper lanterns, I suppose?” “Of course not. How could they be pawned otherwise? They are silk lanterns, in a limited number of designs, mostly hexagonal, like palace lanterns. The silk is painted with figures, beautiful women, and all sorts of stories. The frames fold. After use, you clean them, fold and wrap them, and bring them out again next year. They are common around Haining. Have you never seen them?” “No.” “You will understand when you do. They are not revolving paper lanterns for amusing children. A respectable family gives a New Year dinner for distinguished guests and hangs them in the hall and corridors. With a cup in hand, one can study the paintings by different artists at leisure. One can also hang riddles from them for the guests to solve. It is a quiet, cultivated amusement. A man of your present standing ought to acquire a set.” Zhou’s income had been good in recent years, and he was eager to improve his social position. Since his dealings with the authorities over Fukang, he was by now virtually counted among the gentry. Tang’s suggestion appealed to him. “How much would such a set cost?”

“多少都花得下去！”唐子韶说：“这种灯，高下相差很大，好坏就在画上，要看是不是名家？就算是名家，未见得肯来画花灯，值钱就在这些地方。譬如说，当今画仕女的，第一把手的费晓楼，你请他画花灯，他就不肯。”“那么，你那里满当的那一堂灯呢？是哪个画的呢？”“提起此人大大的有名，康熙年间的大人先生，请他画过‘行乐图’的，不晓得多少。他是扬州人，姓大禹的禹，名叫禹之鼎，他也做过官，官名叫鸿胪寺序班。这个官、照规矩是要旗人来做的，不晓得他怎么会做这个官……”“老唐，”周少棠打断他的话说：“我们不要去管他的官，谈他的画好了。”于是唐子韶言归正传，说禹之鼎所画的那堂绢制花灯，一共二十四盏，六种样式，画的六个故事，西施沼吴、文君当垆、昭君出塞、文姬归汉、宓妃留枕、梅杨争宠，梅是梅妃，杨是杨玉环，所以六个故事，却有七大美人。“禹之鼎的画，假的很多，不过这堂灯绝不假，因为来历不同。”唐子韶又说：‘康熙年间，有个皇帝面前的大红人，名叫高江村，他原来是杭州人，后来住在嘉兴的平湖县，到了嘉庆年间，子孙败落下来，这堂灯就是高江村请禹之鼎画的，所以不假，周先生，这堂灯，明天我叫人送到府上。““不，不！”周少棠摇着手说：“看看东西，再作道理。”

“You could spend any amount,” Tang replied. “There are enormous differences in quality. It all depends on the paintings—whether they are by famous artists. Even a famous artist may not consent to paint lanterns; that is what makes them valuable. Take Fei Xiaolou, the foremost painter of beauties today. Ask him to paint lanterns, and he will refuse.” “Then who painted the set of expired pledges you have?” “An exceedingly famous man. Countless great officials of the Kangxi reign commissioned him to paint portraits of them at leisure. He came from Yangzhou. His surname was Yu, like Yu the Great, and his full name Yu Zhiding. He also held office as an usher in the Court of State Ceremonial. By regulation that post was for bannermen; I do not know how he came to hold it...” “Old Tang,” Zhou interrupted, “let us leave his office aside and talk about his paintings.” Tang returned to the point. Yu’s set comprised twenty-four silk lanterns in six designs, illustrating six stories: Xi Shi and the fall of Wu, Wenjun tending the wine shop, Zhaojun going beyond the frontier, Wenji returning to the Han, Fufei leaving her pillow, and Mei and Yang competing for favour. Mei was Consort Mei, and Yang was Yang Yuhuan. Thus the six stories contained seven beauties. “There are many counterfeit Yu Zhiding paintings, but these lanterns are certainly genuine. Their history is different. In the Kangxi reign there was a great imperial favourite called Gao Jiangcun, originally from Hangzhou. Later he lived in Pinghu County, Jiaxing. By the Jiaqing reign his descendants had fallen into poverty. Gao commissioned Yu Zhiding to paint this set, so there can be no doubt about it. Mr Zhou, I shall have it sent to your house tomorrow.” “No, no!” Zhou waved his hands. “Let me see it first; we can decide afterwards.”

唐子韶还要往下说时，只见一个丫头进来说道：“公济派人来通知，说‘首柜，得了急病，请老爷马上去。”典当司事，分为“内缺”、“外缺”两种，外缺的头脑，称为“首柜”，照例坐在迎门柜台的最左方，珍贵之物送上柜台，必经首柜镜定估价，是个极重要的职司，所以唐子韶得此消息，顿时忧形于色，周少棠也就坐不住了。“老唐，你有急事尽管请。我也要告辞了。”“不！不！我去看一看就回来。我们的事也要紧的。”接着便喊：“月如，月如！”等丫头将月如去唤了来，唐子韶吩咐她代为陪客，随即向周少棠拱拱手，道声失陪，下楼而去。面临这样的局面，周少棠自然而然地想起了胡雪岩中美人汁的传说，起了几分戒心。但月如却落落大方地一面布菜斟酒，一面问起周少棠的家庭情形，由周太太问到子女，因话搭话，谈锋很健，却很自然，完全是熟不拘札的闲话家常。在周少棠的感觉中，月如是个能干贤惠的主妇，因而对于她与胡雪岩之间的传说，竟起了不可思议之感。当然也少得谈到胡雪岩的失败，月如更是表现了故主情殷，休戚相关的忠捆。周少棠倒很想趁机谈一谈公济的事，但终于还是不曾开口。

Tang was about to continue when a maid came in. “Someone has come from Gongji. The chief counter appraiser has been taken suddenly ill. They ask you to go at once.” Pawnshop clerks held either internal or counter posts. The head of the latter was called the chief counter appraiser and ordinarily sat at the extreme left of the counter facing the entrance. Any valuable article brought in had to pass through his hands for examination and valuation. It was therefore an important position, and worry immediately appeared on Tang’s face. Zhou could no longer remain comfortably seated. “Old Tang, if you have urgent business, please go. I was about to take my leave.” “No, no! I shall go and look, then return. Our business is important too.” He called for Yueru. When the maid brought her, he told her to keep their guest company, saluted Zhou with clasped hands, and went downstairs. In this situation Zhou naturally remembered the story of Hu falling into a beauty trap, and became a little wary. But Yueru was entirely at ease. Serving food and pouring wine, she asked about Zhou’s family, moving from his wife to his children as one subject led naturally to another. She talked readily, with the unceremonious familiarity of an old acquaintance discussing household affairs. To Zhou, she seemed an able and virtuous housewife, making the stories about her and Hu almost impossible to believe. Inevitably Hu’s failure came up, and she showed deep loyalty to her former master, as though his fortunes were her own. Zhou was tempted to raise Gongji’s affairs, but in the end said nothing.

“姨太，”丫头又来报了，“老爷叫人回来说，首柜的病很重，他还要等在那里看一看，请周老爷不要走，还有要紧事谈。”“晓得了。你再去烫一壶酒来。”“酒够了，酒够了。”周少棠说，不必再烫，有粥我想吃一碗。““预备了香粳米粥在那里，酒还可以来一点。”“那就以一壶为度。”喝完了酒喝粥，接着又喝茶，而唐子韶却无回来的消息，周少棠有些踌躇了。“周老爷，”月如从里间走了出来，是重施过脂粉了，她大大方方地说：“我来打口烟你吃。”“我没有瘾。”“香一简玩玩。”说着，她亲自动手点起了烟灯，自己便躺了下去，拿烟签子挑起烟来烧。

“Madam,” the maid reported again, “the master has sent word that the chief appraiser is very ill. He must remain there a little longer to see how things develop. Mr Zhou is asked not to leave; there is still important business to discuss.” “Very well. Warm another pot of wine.” “I have had enough wine,” Zhou said. “There is no need for more. If there is congee, I should like a bowl.” “We have fragrant rice congee ready. You can still have a little more wine.” “Then let us stop after one pot.” After the wine they had congee, then tea. Still there was no word of Tang’s return, and Zhou began to feel uncertain. “Mr Zhou.” Yueru emerged from the inner room, her powder and rouge freshly applied. Quite openly she said, “Let me prepare you a pipe.” “I have no habit.” “Just enjoy one for amusement.” She lit the opium lamp herself, lay down, and lifted some opium on the needle to heat it.

丫头端来一小壶滚烫的茶，一盘松子糖，放在烟盘上，然后一言不发地退了出去。“烟打好了。”月如招呼：“请过来吧！”周少棠不由自主地躺在月如对面，两人共用一个长枕头，一躺下去便闻到桂花油的香味。魔障一起，对周少棠来说，便成了苦难，由她头上的桂花油开始，鼻端眼底，触处无不是极大的挑逗。“周少棠啊周少棠！”他在心中自语：“你混了几十年，又不是二三十岁的小伙子了，莫非还是这样子的‘嫩’？”这样自我警告着，心里好象定了些，但很快地又意乱神迷了，需要第二次再提警告，就这样一筒烟，还没有到口，倒已经在内心中挣扎了三四回了。月如终于打好了一个“黄、长、松”的烟泡，安在烟枪“斗门”上，拿烟签子轻轻地捻通，然后将烟枪倒过来，烟嘴伸到周少棠唇边，说一声：“尝一口看。”这对周少棠来说，无异为抵御“心中贼”的一种助力，他虽没有瘾，却颇能领略鸦片烟的妙处，将注意力集中在烟味的香醇上，暂时抛开了月如的一切。分儿口抽完了那筒烟，口中又干又苦，但如“嘴对嘴”喝一口热茶，把烟压了下去，便很容易上瘾，所以他不敢喝茶，只取了块松子糖送人口中。

The maid brought a small pot of piping-hot tea and a plate of pine-nut sweets, set them on the smoking tray, and withdrew without a word. “Your pipe is ready,” Yueru called. “Come over.” Almost against his will, Zhou lay down opposite her. They shared a long pillow, and he immediately caught the fragrance of her osmanthus hair oil. Once desire took hold, it became a torment. Beginning with that scent, everything that met his eyes or nostrils was an irresistible provocation. “Zhou Shaotang, Zhou Shaotang!” he told himself. “You have been about the world for decades. You are no youngster of twenty or thirty. Can you still be so green?” The warning steadied him a little, but soon he was bewildered again and had to repeat it. Before that single pipe reached his lips, he had struggled with himself three or four times. Yueru finally prepared a yellow, elongated, loosely rolled pellet, placed it over the pipe bowl’s opening, and gently pierced it with the needle. Turning the pipe, she brought the mouthpiece to his lips. “Try it.” To Zhou, this offered a means of resisting the thief within his heart. Though he was not addicted, he could appreciate opium’s attractions. Concentrating on its rich, mellow flavour, he temporarily forgot everything about Yueru. A few draws finished the pipe and left his mouth dry and bitter. But following it immediately with hot tea made addiction easy, so he dared not drink any and took a pine-nut sweet instead.

“周老爷，”月如开口了，“你同我们老爷，原来就熟悉的吧？”“原来并不熟，不过，他是场面上的人，我当然久闻其名。”“我们老爷同我说，现在有悠扬事，要请周老爷照应，不晓得是什么事？”一听这话，周少棠不由得诧异，不知道她是明知故问呢，还是真个不知？想一想，反问一句：“老唐没有跟你谈过？”“他没有。他只说买的一百多亩西湖田，要赶紧脱手，不然周老爷面上不好交代。”“怎么不好交代。”“他说，要托周老爷帮忙，空口说白话不中用。”月如忽然叹口气说：“ 唉，我们老爷也是，我常劝他，你有亏空，老实同胡大先生说，胡大先生的脾气，天大的事，只要你老实说，没有不让你过门的。他总觉得扯了窟窿对不起胡大先生，‘八个坛儿七个盖’，盖来盖去盖不周矣，到头儿还是落个没面子，何苦？”“喔，”周少棠很注意地问：“老唐扯了什么窟窿？”接下来，月如便叹了一大堆苦经，不外乎唐子韶为人外精明、内糊涂，与合伙做生意，吃了暗亏，迫不得已在公济典动了手脚。说到伤心处，该然欲涕，连周少棠都心酸酸地为她难过。

“Mr Zhou,” Yueru began, “you and my husband have known each other well for a long time, have you not?” “Not well, originally. But he is a man of standing, and of course I had long heard his name.” “He tells me there is something for which he needs your help. I do not know what it is.” Zhou was surprised. Did she really not know, or was she asking a question whose answer she knew already? After a moment he asked, “Has Old Tang not discussed it with you?” “No. He only said that we must sell the hundred-odd mu of land by West Lake as soon as possible, or he would find it difficult to face you.” “Why should he find it difficult?” “He says that asking your help with nothing but empty words would be no use.” She suddenly sighed. “Ah, that husband of mine! I have often told him: if you have a shortfall, tell Mr Hu frankly. With his temperament, however serious the matter, he will always let you through if you are honest. But my husband felt he had wronged Mr Hu by creating the deficit. Eight jars and seven lids—however he shifted them, he could not cover everything. He has lost face in the end all the same. Why go through it?” “Oh?” Zhou listened closely. “What sort of deficit did he create?” Yueru poured out a long tale of misery. Tang, she said, was shrewd on the surface but foolish underneath. He had suffered concealed losses in business partnerships and had been forced to tamper with Gongji’s funds. At the saddest points she seemed ready to weep, and even Zhou’s heart ached for her.

“你说老唐吃暗亏，又说有苦说不出，到底是啥个亏，啥个苦？”“周周老爷说说不要紧。”月如间道：“胡大先生有个朋友，这个姓很少见的，姓古，周老爷晓不晓得？”“听说过，是替胡大先生办洋务的。”“不错，就是他这位古老爷做地皮，邀我们老爷合股。当初计算得蛮好，哪晓得洋人一打仗，市面不对了。从前‘逃长毛’，都逃到上海，因为长毛再狠，也不敢去攻租界。一到洋人要开仗了，轮到上海人逃难了，造好的房子卖不掉，亏了好几十万。击老爷你想想，怎么得了？”月如又说：“苦是苦在这件事还不能同胡大先生去讲。”因为第一，唐子韶当年曾有承诺，须以全副精力为胡雪岩经营典当，自己不可私营贸易。这项承诺后来虽渐渐变质，但亦只属于与胡雪岩有关的生意为限，譬如收茧卖丝之类，等于附搭股份，而经营房地产是一项新的生意。“再有一个缘故是，古老爷是胡大先生的好朋友，如果说跟古老爷一起做房地产亏了本，告诉胡大先生，他一定会不高兴。为啥呢？”月如自问自答：“胡大先生心里会想，你当初同他一起合伙，不来告诉我，亏本了来同我说，是不是要我贴补呢？再说，同古老爷合伙，生意为啥亏本，有些话根本不便说，说了不但没有好处，胡大先生还以为有意说古老爷的坏话，反而会起误会。”“为啥？”周少棠问道：“是不是有不尽不实的地方？”

“You say Old Tang suffered concealed losses and could not speak of his troubles. What losses? What troubles?” “There is no harm in telling you. Mr Hu has a friend with an unusual surname—Gu. Do you know him?” “I have heard of him. He handles Mr Hu’s foreign business.” “Exactly. This Mr Gu invited my husband to join him in property development. The original calculations looked excellent. Then the foreigners went to war and the market changed. When people fled the Longhairs, they went to Shanghai; however savage the rebels were, they dared not attack the concessions. But once the foreigners were going to war, it was the people of Shanghai who had to flee. The completed houses would not sell, and they lost several hundred thousand taels. Think what that meant! And the worst of it was that he could not tell Mr Hu.” For one thing, Tang had originally undertaken to devote all his energies to managing Hu’s pawnshops and conduct no private trade of his own. Although this promise had gradually been diluted, his other ventures had remained confined to businesses connected with Hu, such as buying cocoons and selling silk. He was, in effect, taking subsidiary shares. Property development was a new business altogether. “There was another reason,” Yueru continued. “Mr Gu is Mr Hu’s close friend. If we said we had lost money in property with him, Mr Hu would be displeased. Why? He would think: you did not tell me when you joined him, but now you have lost money you come to me. Do you expect me to make it good? Besides, there were things about why the partnership lost money that could hardly be mentioned. Speaking of them would do no good. Mr Hu might think we were deliberately speaking ill of his friend, and there would be a misunderstanding.” “Why?” Zhou asked. “Was something not quite honest?”

月如不作声，因为一口烟正烧到要紧地方，只见她灵巧的手指，忙忙碌碌地一面烘一面卷，全神贯注，无暇答话，直待装好了烟，等周少棠抽完，说一声：“真的够了，我是没有瘾的。”月如方如搁下烟签子，回答周少棠的话。“周老爷你想，人在杭州，上海的行情不熟，市面不灵，怕胡大先生晓得，还不敢去打听，这种生意，如果说会赚钱，只怕太阳要从西面出来了。”这话很明显地表示，古应春有侵吞的情事在。周少棠对这话将信将疑，无从究洁，心里在转的念头是：唐子韶何以至今未回，是不是也有设美人局的意思？“这又是一大疑团，因而便问：“老唐呢？应该回来了吧？”“是啊！”月如便喊来她的丫头失照：“你走快点，到公济看老爷为啥现在还不回来？你说，周老爷要回府了。“丫头答应着走了。月如亦即离开烟榻，在大冰盘中取了个天津鸭梨，用一把象牙柄的锋利洋刀慢慢削皮，周少棠却仍躺在烟榻上，盘算等唐子韶回来了，如何谈判？

Yueru said nothing. She had reached a critical stage in preparing another pipe. Her nimble fingers heated and rolled the opium busily, her attention entirely absorbed. Not until she had filled the pipe and Zhou had finished it, saying, “That really is enough; I have no habit,” did she lay down the needle and answer. “Think, Mr Zhou. My husband was in Hangzhou. He knew little of Shanghai prices and had no reliable market information. Afraid that Mr Hu might find out, he did not even dare make inquiries. If that sort of business could make money, the sun would surely rise in the west.” Her words plainly suggested that Gu had been embezzling. Zhou half believed and half doubted her, with no means of getting to the truth. His mind turned instead to Tang’s prolonged absence. Was he too arranging a beauty trap? Here was another serious uncertainty. “Where is Old Tang? Surely he ought to be back by now?” “Yes, indeed.” Yueru called her maid. “Hurry to Gongji and ask why the master has still not returned. Tell him Mr Zhou wants to go home.” The maid agreed and left. Yueru rose from the smoking couch, took a Tianjin pear from a large platter, and began slowly peeling it with a sharp foreign knife with an ivory handle. Zhou remained on the couch, considering how to negotiate when Tang returned.

正想得出神时，突然听得“啊唷”一声，只见月如右手捏着左手拇指，桌上一把洋刀，一个快削好了的梨，不用说，是不小心刀伤了手指。“重不重，重不重？”周少棠奔了过去问说。“不要紧。”月如站起身来，直趋妆台，指挥着说：“抽斗里有干净帕儿，请你撕一条来。”杭州话的“帕儿”就是手绢。周少棠拉开抽斗一看，内有几方折得方方正正的各色纺绸手绢，白色的一方在下面，随手一翻，发现了薄薄的一本书。“这里还有本书。”周少棠顺口说了这一句，正要翻一翻时，只听得月如大声极叫：“不要看，不要看，”周少棠吓一大跳，急忙缩手，看到月如脸上，双颊泛红，微显窘色，想一想恍然大悟，那本不能看的书是什么。于是他微笑着抽出一条白纺绸手绢，拿剪刀剪一个口子，撕下寸许宽的一长条，持在手上，另一只手揭开粉缸，伸两指拈了一撮粉说道：“手放开。”等月如将手松开，他将那一撮粉敷在创口上，然后很快地包扎好了，找根线来缚紧，“痛不痛？”周少棠问，但仍旧握着她的手。“还好。”月如答说：“亏得你在这里，不然血一定流得满地。”说着，她在手上用了点劲想抽回去，但周少棠不放，她也就不挣扎了。

He was deep in thought when he suddenly heard a cry. Yueru was gripping her left thumb with her right hand. The knife and a nearly peeled pear lay on the table; plainly she had cut herself. “Is it bad?” Zhou hurried over. “It is nothing.” She rose and went straight to the dressing table, giving instructions as she went. “There are clean handkerchiefs in the drawer. Tear me a strip.” She used pa’er, the Hangzhou word for a handkerchief. Zhou opened the drawer and found several in various colours of spun silk, folded into neat squares. A white one lay underneath. Turning the others aside, he discovered a thin book. “There is a book here too,” he remarked casually. He was about to turn its pages when Yueru cried urgently, “Do not look! Do not look!” Startled, he drew his hand back. Her cheeks were flushed, and she looked slightly embarrassed. After a moment he understood what sort of book it must be. Smiling, he took the white handkerchief, made a snip with scissors, and tore off a long strip about a cun wide. Holding it in one hand, he opened the powder jar with the other and took a pinch between two fingers. “Let go of your hand.” When she did, he put the powder on the cut, quickly bandaged it, and found a thread to tie the dressing. “Does it hurt?” he asked, still holding her hand. “Not much. It is lucky you were here, or I should have bled all over the floor.” She gave a slight tug to withdraw her hand. When he would not release it, she stopped resisting.

“阿嫂，你这双手好白。”“真的？”月如问道：“比你太太怎么样？”“那不能比了。”“你的太太很年轻吗？”“她属羊的。”周少棠问：“你呢？”“我属牛。”“她比你大多了。”周少棠牵着她的手，回到中间方桌边，放开了手，各自落座。“ 梨削了一半……”“我来削。”周少棠说：“这个梨格外大，我们分开来吃。”“梨不好分的。”月如说道：“你一个人慢慢吃好了。梨，化痰清火，吃烟的人，冬天吃了最好。”“其实，我同你分不分梨无所谓。”周少棠说：“只要你同老唐不分梨就好了。”“梨”字谐音为“离”，彼此默喻，用以试探，月如抓住机会说了一句切中要害的话。“我同老唐分不分离，完全要看你周老爷，是不是阴功积德了。”“言重，言重。我哪里有这么大的力量。”“不必客气。我也听说了，老唐会不会吃官司，完全要看周老爷你肯不肯帮忙，你肯帮忙，我同老唐还在一起，你不肯帮忙，我看分离分定了。”

“Sister-in-law, what white hands you have.” “Really? How do they compare with your wife’s?” “There is no comparison.” “Is your wife very young?” “She was born in the Year of the Sheep. And you?” “The Ox.” “Then she is much older than you.” Holding her hand, Zhou led her back to the square table in the middle of the room, released it, and sat down opposite her. “The pear is only half peeled...” “I shall finish it. It is unusually large; we can share it.” “One should not divide a pear,” Yueru said. “Take your time and eat it yourself. Pears clear phlegm and internal heat. They are excellent for opium smokers in winter.” “It does not really matter whether you and I divide a pear.
