As long as you and Old Tang do not part, all will be well.” The word for pear, li, sounded like the word for parting. Both understood the play on words and used it to test the other. Yueru seized her chance. “Whether Old Tang and I part depends entirely on whether you will do a good deed and earn merit, Mr Zhou.” “You exaggerate. How could I have such power?” “There is no need for modesty. I have heard that whether Old Tang faces prosecution depends entirely on your willingness to help. If you help, we can remain together. If not, I fear we shall certainly be parted.”

周少棠这时才发现，她对唐子韶的所作所为，即使全未曾参预，定必完全了解，而且是唐子韶安排好来眼他谈判的人。然则自己就必须考虑了，要不要跟她谈，如果不谈，现在该是走的时候了。但一想到走，顿有不舍之意。这样就自然而然在思索，应该如何谈法？决定先了解了解情况再作道理。于是他问：“阿嫂，你晓得不晓得老唐亏空了多少？”“我想，总有三四万银子吧？”“不止，”“喔，是多少呢？”“起码加个倍。”一听这话，月如发愣，怔怔地看着周少棠——不知她心里在想什么主平最凄凉的事，居然挤出来一副“急泪”。周少棠大为不忍，“阿嫂，你也不必急，慢慢商量。我能帮忙，一定帮忙。”他问：“老唐眼前凑得出多少现银？”“现银？”月如想了一下说：“现银大概只有两三千，另外只有我的首饰。”“你的首饰值多少？”“顶多也不过两三千。“两个两三千，就有五六千银子了。”周少棠又问：“你们的西湖田呢？”“田倒值一万多银子，不过一时也寻不着买主。”“西湖田俏得很，不过十天半个月，就有买主。”“十天半个月来得及，来不及？”这句话使得周少棠大为惊异，因为问到这活，就显得她很懂公事。所谓“来得及，来不及”，是指“马大老爷”复命而言，。即受藩宪之委，当然要克服复命，如果事情摆不平，据实呈复，唐子韶立郎便有缧绁之灾。照此看来，必是唐子韶已彻底研究过案情，想到过各种后果，预先教好了她如何进言，如何应付。自己千万要小心，莫中圈套。

Only now did Zhou realise that, even if Yueru had taken no part in Tang’s doings, she must know all about them. Tang had arranged for her to negotiate with him. He therefore had to decide whether to discuss the matter with her. If not, it was time to leave. Yet the thought of leaving immediately filled him with reluctance, and he found himself considering how to begin. He would first learn a little more before deciding. “Sister-in-law, do you know how large Old Tang’s deficit is?” “Thirty or forty thousand taels, I suppose?” “More.” “Oh? How much?” “At least twice that.” She stared at him, stunned. Who knew what she summoned up as the most sorrowful experience of her life? Somehow she squeezed out a sudden flood of tears. Zhou could not bear it. “Do not be anxious. We can discuss it calmly. If I can help, I certainly shall. How much ready silver can Old Tang raise now?” “Ready silver?” She thought. “Probably only two or three thousand taels. Apart from that, there is only my jewellery.” “What is it worth?” “Two or three thousand at most.” “Two lots of two or three thousand make five or six thousand. What about your land by West Lake?” “That is worth over ten thousand, but we cannot find a buyer immediately.” “West Lake land is in great demand. Ten days or half a month should bring a buyer.” “Would ten days or half a month be in time?” The question astonished Zhou. It showed that she understood official procedure. “In time” referred to Magistrate Ma’s report. Having accepted the treasurer’s commission, he had to report back by the appointed deadline. If matters could not be settled and he reported the facts, Tang would immediately face imprisonment. Evidently Tang had studied the case thoroughly, considered every consequence, and coached her in what to say and how to respond. Zhou must take the greatest care not to fall into their trap.

于是他想了一下问说：“来得及怎么样，来不及又怎么样？”“如果来得及最好，来不及的话，要请周老爷同马大老爷打个商量，好不好把公事压一压，先不要报上去。”“这恐怕难。”就在这时，周少棠已经打定主意，由于发现唐子韶与月如，是打算用施之于胡雪岩的手法来对付他，因而激发了报复的念头，决定先占个便宜再说。“阿嫂，”他突然说道：“船到桥头自会直，你不必想太多。天塌下来有长人顶，等老唐来了，商量一个办法，我一定帮你们的忙。不过，阿嫂，我帮了忙，有啥好处？”“周老爷，你这话说得太小气了。”月如瞟了他一眼：“好朋友嘛，一定要有好处才肯帮忙？”“话不是这么说，一个人帮朋友的忙，总要由心里发出来的念头，时时刻刻想到，帮忙才帮得切实。不然，看到想起，过后就忘记了，这是人之常情，不是小气。”“那么，你说，你想要啥好处。”“只要阿嫂待我好就好了。想起阿嫂的好处，自然而然就会想起阿嫂交代给我的事。”说着，周少棠伸出手去，指着她的拇指问：“还痛不痛？”“早就不痛了。”“我看看。”周少棠拉住她的手，慢慢地又伸手探入她的袖筒，她只是微笑着。

After thinking for a moment, he asked, “What if it is in time? And what if it is not?” “If it is, so much the better. If not, would you discuss it with Magistrate Ma and ask him to hold the matter back, without reporting it yet?” “That may be difficult.” By now Zhou had made up his mind. Discovering that Tang and Yueru intended to use the same methods on him as they had on Hu had aroused his desire for revenge. He would take some advantage of the situation first. “Sister-in-law,” he said abruptly, “the boat will straighten itself when it reaches the bridge. Do not think too much. If the sky falls, there are tall people to hold it up. When Old Tang returns, we shall find a way. I shall certainly help you. But what do I get for helping?” “Mr Zhou, how petty that sounds!” She glanced at him. “Must good friends offer you a benefit before you will help?” “That is not what I mean. To help a friend properly, the wish must come from the heart. One must keep thinking of it. Otherwise one remembers while the friend is there and forgets afterwards. That is human nature, not pettiness.” “Then what benefit do you want?” “Only that you should be kind to me. Remembering your kindness will naturally remind me of what you have asked.” He reached out and pointed to her thumb. “Does it still hurt?” “It stopped hurting long ago.” “Let me see.” He took her hand and slowly slipped his other hand up her sleeve. She merely smiled.

“好不好？”她忽然问说。“什么好不好？”“我的膀子啊！摸起来舒服不舒服？”“舒服，真舒服，”“这就是我的好处。”月如说道：“想起我的好处，不要忘记我托你的事。”“不会，不会！不过，可惜。”“可惜点啥？”“好处太少了。”“你要多少好处？”说着，月如站起身来，双足一转，索性坐在周少棠的大脚上。这一下，周少棠自然上下其手，恣意轻薄。不过他脑筋仍旧很清楚，双眼注视着房门，两耳细听楼梯上的动静，心里在说：只要不脱衣服不上床，就让唐子韶撞见了也不要紧。话虽如此，要把握得住却不大容易，他的心里象火烧那样，一次又一次，想作进一步的行动的意念越来越强，到快要真的忍不住时，突然想到了一个法子，推开月如，将靠穿一张半桌上放着的一杯冷茶，拿起来往口中就倒，“咕嘟、咕嘟”一气喝完，心里比较舒服了。

“Is it nice?” she suddenly asked. “Is what nice?” “My arm. Does it feel pleasant?” “Very pleasant.” “That is the kindness I offer. When you remember it, do not forget what I have asked.” “I shall not. Only, it is a pity.” “What is?” “There is so little of it.” “How much kindness do you want?” Rising and turning on her feet, she simply sat on his lap. Zhou naturally began caressing and fondling her freely. His mind, however, remained clear. He watched the door and listened for sounds on the stairs, telling himself that, as long as he neither undressed nor went to bed with her, it would not matter even if Tang walked in. Keeping within that limit was another matter. He felt as though he were burning. Again and again the urge to go further grew stronger. Just when he could scarcely control himself, he thought of a way out. Pushing Yueru aside, he seized a cup of cold tea from a small table by the window and gulped it down without stopping. That made him feel somewhat easier.

但他不肯就此罢手，喘着气说：“阿嫂，怪不得胡大先生见了你会着迷。”“瞎说八道。”月如瞪起眼说：“你听人家嚼舌头！”“无风不起浪，总有点因头吧？”“因头，就象你现在一样，你喜欢我，我就让你摸一摸，亲一亲，还会有啥花样？莫非你就看得我那么贱？”“我哪里敢？”周少棠坐回原处，一把拉住她，恢复原样，但这回自觉更有把握了，“好，既然你说喜欢你就让我摸一摸、亲一亲，我就照你的话做。”说着，一手搂过她来亲她的嘴。月如很驯顺地，毫无挣扎之意，让他亲了一会，将头往后一仰问道：“我给你的好处，够不够多？”“够多。”“那么，你呢？”“我怎么？”“你答应我的事。”“一定不会忘记。”“如果忘记掉呢？”月如说道：“你对着灯光菩萨罚个咒。”赌神罚咒，在周少棠也很重视的，略作盘算以后说道：“阿嫂，我答应帮你的忙，暂时让马大老爷把你们的事情压一压，不过压一压不是不了了之。你不要弄错，这是公事，就算马大老爷是我的儿子，我也不能叫他怎么办，他也不会听我的。“

But he was unwilling to stop there. Breathing hard, he said, “Sister-in-law, no wonder Mr Hu was bewitched by you.” “Nonsense!” She widened her eyes. “You listen to people’s malicious gossip.” “There is no smoke without fire. There must have been something to start it.” “Something just like this. You like me, so I let you touch and kiss me. What else could there be? Do you really think me so cheap?” “How could I dare?” Zhou sat down again and drew her back onto his lap. This time he felt more in control. “Very well. Since you say that if I like you, I may touch and kiss you, I shall do as you say.” He slipped an arm around her and kissed her mouth. Yueru was quite compliant and made no attempt to resist. After letting him kiss her for a while, she leaned her head back. “Have I given you enough kindness?” “Plenty.” “And you?” “What about me?” “What you promised.” “I shall certainly not forget.” “And if you do? Swear before the Lamp-Light Bodhisattva to accept punishment if you forget.” Zhou took oaths invoking divine punishment seriously. After a brief calculation, he said, “Sister-in-law, I promise to help you by having Magistrate Ma hold back your case for a while. But a delay does not mean letting it disappear. Do not misunderstand. This is official business. Even if Magistrate Ma were my own son, I could not order him how to deal with it, nor would he obey.”

“这一层我明白，不过，我倒要问你，你打算叫他怎么办？”“我叫他打个折扣。”“几折？”“你说呢？”“要我说，最好大事化小，小事化无。如果你肯这样做，我再给你好处！”周少棠心中一动，笑嘻嘻地问道：“什么好处？”月如不作声，灵活的眼珠不断地在转。周少棠知道又有新花样了，很冷静地戒备着。突然间，楼梯上的响动打破了沉默，而且听得出是男人的脚步声，当然是唐子韶回来了。“周老爷，”月如一本正经地说：“等下当着我们老爷，你不要说什么风话。”接着，起身迎了过去。这一番叮嘱，使周少棠颇有异样的感觉，明明是他们夫妇商量好的一档把戏，何以月如又要在她丈夫面前假作正经，而且她又何以会顾虑到他在她丈夫面前可能会说“风话”？这都是很值得玩味的疑问，但一时却无暇细想，因为唐子韶已经回来了，他少不得也要顾虑到礼貌，起身含笑目迎。

“I understand that. But what do you intend to ask him to do?” “Allow a reduction.” “How much?” “What do you say?” “If it were up to me, I should want a big affair made small and a small affair made nothing. If you will do that, I shall give you more kindness.” Zhou was tempted. Smiling, he asked, “What sort?” Yueru said nothing, her lively eyes constantly moving. Knowing she had thought of another trick, he kept a cool watch. Suddenly footsteps on the stairs broke the silence. They were plainly a man’s: Tang had returned. “Mr Zhou,” Yueru said with perfect seriousness, “when my husband comes in, do not make any suggestive remarks.” She rose to meet him. Her warning gave Zhou a peculiar feeling. This was clearly a scheme the couple had arranged together. Why, then, must she pretend to be proper before her husband? And why was she worried that Zhou might say something suggestive in his presence? These were questions worth pondering, but there was no time. Tang was already there, and courtesy required Zhou to rise and greet him with a smile.

“对不起，对不起！”唐子韶抢步上前，抱拳致歉，“累你久等，真正不好意思。”“没有啥，没有啥！”周少棠故意说风话：“我同阿嫂谈得蛮投机的，削梨给我吃，还害得她手都割破了。”“是啊！”唐子韶转脸看着月如：“我刚刚一进门就看见了，你的手怎么割破的，要紧不要紧。”“不要紧。”月如关切地问：“赵先生怎么样了。”赵先生便是公济典得急病的“头柜”。唐子韶答说：“暂时不要紧了。亏得大先生给我的那支好参，一味‘独参汤’总算扳回来了。“接下来他又说：”你赶快烧两筒烟，我先过瘾要紧。来，来，周先生，我们躺下来谈。“于是宾主二人在烟盘两旁躺了下来，月如端张小凳子坐在两人之间，开灯烧烟，唐子韶便谈赵先生的病情，周少棠无心细听，支支吾吾地应着，很注意月如的神情，却看不出什么来。等两筒鸦片抽过，月如开口了，“刚刚我同周老爷叹了你的苦经，亏空也是没办法。”她说：“周老爷很帮忙，先请马大老爷把公事压一压，我们赶紧凑一笔钱出来，了这件事。”“是啊！事情出来了，总要了的。周先生肯帮我们的忙，就算遇到救星了。”“周老爷说，亏空很多，只好打个折扣来了。我们那笔西湖田，周老爷说，有十天半个月就可以脱手。你如今不便出面，只好请周老爷代为觅个头主。”月如又说：“当然，中人钱，我们还是要照送周老爷的。

“My apologies!” Tang hurried forward, saluting with clasped hands. “I am truly ashamed to have kept you waiting so long.” “Not at all!” Zhou deliberately made an insinuation. “Sister-in-law and I have got on very well. She even cut her hand peeling a pear for me.” “Yes!” Tang turned to Yueru. “I noticed as soon as I came in. How did you cut it? Is it serious?” “It is nothing. How is Mr Zhao?” Mr Zhao was Gongji’s chief counter appraiser, the man who had fallen suddenly ill. “Out of danger for the moment. Thanks to that fine ginseng Mr Hu gave me, a decoction of ginseng alone finally brought him round.” Tang continued, “Quickly prepare a couple of pipes. I must satisfy my craving first. Come, Mr Zhou, let us lie down and talk.” Host and guest reclined on either side of the smoking tray. Yueru drew up a small stool between them, lit the lamp, and prepared the opium. Tang described Mr Zhao’s illness. Zhou had little interest in listening and answered vaguely, watching Yueru’s expression closely without discovering anything. After the two pipes had been smoked, she spoke. “I have been telling Mr Zhou about your troubles. You had no choice about the deficit. He has been very helpful. First he will ask Magistrate Ma to hold back the official proceedings while we hurry to raise a sum to settle the affair.” “Yes, once a matter has come out, it must be settled. If Mr Zhou will help, we have found our saviour.” “He says the deficit is large and can only be settled at a reduction. He also says our West Lake land should sell in ten days or half a month. Since it is inconvenient for you to appear yourself, we must ask him to find a buyer. Naturally, we shall pay him the usual intermediary’s commission.”

谈来谈去，唐子韶方面变出来一个结果，他承诺在十天之内，凑出两万四千银子，以出售他的西湖田为主要财源，其次是月如的首饰，唐子韶的古董，如果再不够，有什么卖什么，凑够了为止。现在要轮到周少棠说话了，他一直在考虑的是，马逢时呈报顺利接收的公事一报上去，唐子韶的责任便已卸得干干净净，到时候他不认帐又将如何？当然，他可以要唐子韶写张借据，但“杀人偿命”，有官府来作主，“欠债还钱”两造是可以和解的，俗语说：“不怕讨债的凶，只怕欠债的穷。”唐子韶有心赖债，催讨无着，反倒闹得沸沸扬扬，问起来“唐子韶怎么会欠你两万四千银子，你跟庸子韶不过点头之交，倒舍得把大笔银子借给他？”那时无言以对，势必拆穿真相。变成“羊肉没有吃，先惹一身骚”，太犯不着了。由于沉吟不语的时间太久，唐子韶与月如都慢慢猜到了他的心事。唐子韶决定自己先表示态度。“周先生，你一定是在想，空口讲白话，对马大老爷不好开口，是不是？”既然他猜到了，周少棠不必否认，“不错，”他说：“我是中间人，两面都要交代。”

After considerable discussion, Tang made a commitment: within ten days he would raise twenty-four thousand taels. The principal source would be the sale of his West Lake land, followed by Yueru’s jewellery and his antiques. If those were insufficient, he would sell whatever else he had until the sum was complete. It was now Zhou’s turn to speak. He had been considering one difficulty throughout: once Ma reported that the takeover had proceeded satisfactorily, Tang would be entirely discharged from responsibility. What if he then repudiated the agreement? Zhou could, of course, demand an acknowledgement of debt. But whereas the authorities enforced the principle that a murderer must pay with his life, the two parties could reach a private settlement over a debt. As the saying went, “It is not the fierce creditor one fears, but the penniless debtor.” If Tang deliberately refused payment, demands might prove fruitless and merely create a public scandal. People would ask: “How did Tang come to owe you twenty-four thousand taels? You are no more than nodding acquaintances. Would you really lend him so large a sum?” Zhou would have no answer. The truth would inevitably emerge, and he would acquire all the stink of mutton without having tasted a morsel. It was not worth it. His silence lasted so long that Tang and Yueru gradually guessed his concern. Tang decided to state his position first. “Mr Zhou, you must be thinking that empty words give you nothing to put before Magistrate Ma. Is that it?” Since he had guessed, Zhou need not deny it. “Exactly. I am the intermediary. I must answer to both sides.”

“这样子，我叫月如先把首饰检出来，刚才看过的汉玉，也请你带了去，请你变价。至于西湖田，也请你代觅买主，我把红契交了给你。”凡是缴过契税，由官府铃了印的，称为“红契”。但这不过是上手的原始凭证，收到了不致另生纠葛，根本上买卖还是要订立契约，没有卖契，光有红契，不能凭以营业，而况唐子韶可用失窃的理由挂失，原有的红契等于废纸。唐子韶很机警，看周少棠是骗不倒的内行，立即又补上一句：“当然，要抵押给你，请老杨做中。”周少棠心中一动，想了一下说道：“这样吧，明天上午，我同老杨一起到公济来看你，商量一个办法出来。”“好，好！我等候两位大驾。”“辰光不早，再谈下去要天亮了。”周少棠起身说道：“多谢，多谢！明朝会。““这一盒玉器，你带了去。”“不，不！”周少棠双手乱摇，坚决不受。然后向月如说道：“阿嫂，真正多谢，今天这顿饭，比吃鱼翅席还要落胃。”“哪里，哪里。周老爷有空尽管请过来，我还有几样拿手菜，烧出来请你尝尝。”“好极，好极！”一定要来叨扰。“

“Then let me have Yueru sort out her jewellery first. Please take the Han jades you saw earlier too, and sell them for us. As for the West Lake land, I shall ask you to find a buyer and give you the red deed.” A deed on which the transfer tax had been paid and the official seal impressed was called a “red deed.” But it was only the original evidence of the previous acquisition. Obtaining it prevented certain later complications; fundamentally, a fresh contract was still required for a sale. Without a deed of sale, the red deed alone could not authorise a transaction. Moreover, Tang could report it stolen and have it invalidated, reducing the original to wastepaper. Quick-witted as he was, Tang saw that Zhou understood too much to be deceived and promptly added, “Naturally, I shall mortgage it to you, with Old Yang as intermediary.” Zhou was struck by an idea. After considering, he said, “Let us do this: tomorrow morning I shall come to Gongji with Old Yang, and we can work out an arrangement.” “Very good. I shall await you both.” “It is late. If we go on talking, dawn will be here.” Zhou rose. “Thank you for everything. Until tomorrow.” “Take this box of jades with you.” “No, no!” Waving both hands, Zhou firmly refused. He then turned to Yueru. “Sister-in-law, thank you indeed. This meal has suited my stomach better than a shark’s-fin banquet.” “You are too kind. Come whenever you have time. I have a few more special dishes I should like you to try.” “Excellent! I shall certainly trouble you again.”

第八章 赠妾酬友｜CHAPTER EIGHT: A CONCUBINE AS A GIFT TO A FRIEND

由于有事，回到家只睡了一会儿，周少棠便已醒来，匆匆赶到杨家，杨书办正要出门。“你到哪里去？”“想到城隍山去看个朋友……”“不要去了。”同少棠不等他话完，便即打断，“我有要紧事同你商量。”“于是就在杨家密谈。周少棠将昨夜的经过情形，细细告诉了杨书办，问他的意见。“卖田他自己去卖好了，月如为啥说唐子韶不便出面？”“对！我当时倒忘记问她了。”“这且不言。”杨书办问道：“现在马大老爷那里应该怎么办？”“我正就是为这一点要来同你商量。月如打的是如意算盘，希望先报出去，顺利接收，那一来唐子韶一点责任都没有了。不过，要等他凑齐了银子再报，不怕耽误日子？如今我倒有个办法，”周少棠突然问道：“你有没有啥路子，能借一笔大款子？”“现在银根紧。”杨书办问：“你想借多少？”“不是我借。我想叫唐子韶先拿他的西湖田抵押一笔款子出来，我们先拿到了手，有多少算多少。”杨书办沉吟了好一会说：“这是出典。典田不如买田，这种主顾不多，而且，手续也很麻烦，不是三两无能办好的。”

With business on his mind, Zhou Shaotang woke after only a little sleep at home and hurried to Yang’s house. Clerk Yang was just going out. “Where are you off to?” “I thought I would visit a friend on City God Hill…” “Do not go.” Zhou interrupted him before he could finish. “I have something urgent to discuss with you.” They held their private conference at Yang’s house. Zhou gave a detailed account of the previous night and asked for his opinion. “Let him sell his own land. Why did Yueru say Tang Zishao could not appear in the transaction himself?” “Exactly! I forgot to ask her that.” “Leave that aside for now. What should we do about Magistrate Ma?” “That is precisely what I came to discuss. Yueru has it all nicely worked out: she hopes we shall first report that the takeover went smoothly. Then Tang will be free of all responsibility. But if we wait until he has raised the silver before submitting the report, will we not hold things up? I do have an idea, though.” Zhou suddenly asked, “Do you know anyone who could arrange a substantial loan?” “Money is tight at present. How much do you want to borrow?” “It is not for me. I want Tang to raise a loan against his West Lake fields. Let us get the money into our hands first, however much it is.” Yang thought for some time. “That means putting the land in pledge. Taking land in pledge is less attractive than buying it outright. There are not many people willing to do it, and the formalities are troublesome. It cannot be settled in two or three days.”

周少棠爽然若失，“照此看来，”他说：“一只煮熟的鸭子，只怕要飞掉了。”“这也不见得。如果相信得过，不妨先放他一马。”“就是因为相信不过。”周少棠说：“你想他肯拿小老婆来陪我……”周少棠自知泄漏了秘密，要想改口，已是驷不及舌。杨书办笑笑问道：“唷，你‘近水楼台先得是月’，同月如上过阳台了？”“没有，没有。”周少棠急忙分辩：“不过嘴巴亲一亲，胸脯摸一摸。总而言之，唐子韶一定在搞鬼，轻易相信他，一定会上当。““我晓得了。等我来想想。”公事上到底是杨书办比较熟悉，他认为有一个可进可退的办法，即是由马逢时先报一个公事，说是帐目上尚有疑义，正在查核之中，请准予暂缓结案。“唐子韶看到这样子一个活络说法，晓得一定逃不过门，会赶紧去想法子。如果他真的想赖掉，我们就把他的毛病和盘托出。虽没有好处，至少马大老爷也办了一趟漂亮差使。”“好极！就是这个办法。”周少棠说：“等下我们一起到公济典，索性同唐子韶明说：马大老爷已经定规了。事不宜迟，最好你现在就去通知马大老爷。”

Zhou looked crestfallen. “Then it seems our cooked duck may fly away after all.” “Not necessarily. If we can trust him, we might give him some leeway first.” “The trouble is that we cannot trust him. Think of it: he was willing to let his concubine entertain me…” Zhou realized he had let out a secret, but it was too late to call back his words. Yang smiled. “Well! The tower nearest the water catches the moon first. Have you been to bed with Yueru?” “No, no!” Zhou hastened to explain. “Only kissed her lips and felt her breasts. In any case, Tang must be up to something. We shall certainly be taken in if we trust him too readily.” “I see. Let me think.” Yang, after all, knew more about official procedure. He proposed a course that would leave them room to advance or retreat: Ma Fengshi should first submit a report stating that there were still doubtful points in the accounts, that they were being investigated, and that permission was requested to defer closing the case. “Once Tang sees a report that leaves the matter open, he will know he cannot get away and will hurry to find a solution. If he really tries to evade payment, we shall disclose every one of his irregularities. We may gain nothing ourselves, but at least Magistrate Ma will have carried out his commission creditably.” “Excellent! That is the way.” Zhou added, “When we go to Gongji Pawnshop together, let us tell Tang outright that Magistrate Ma has already decided. We should lose no time. You had better inform him now.”

“他不在家，到梅花碑抚台衙门‘站班’去了。”原来巡抚定三、八为衙参之期，接着藩臬两司及任实缺、有差使的道员，候补的知县佐杂，都到巡抚衙门前面去“站班”，作为致敬的表示，目的是在博得好感，加深印象。这是小官候补的不二法门，有时巡抚与司道谈论公事，有个什么差使要派人，够资格保荐的司道，想起刚刚见过某人，正堪充任，因而获得意外机缘，亦是常有之事。“你同唐子韶约的是啥辰光？”“还早，还早。”周少棠说：“我们先到茶店里吃一壶茶再去。”“也不必到茶店里了。我有好六安茶，泡一壶你吃。”于是泡上六安茶，又端出两盘干点心，一面吃，一面谈闲天。杨书办问起月如，周少棠顿时眉飞色舞，不但毫不隐瞒，而且作了许多形容。

“He is not at home. He has gone to stand in attendance at the governor’s yamen at Meihuabei.” The governor held official audiences on days ending in three or eight. Following the provincial treasurer, the judicial commissioner and the circuit intendants holding substantive posts or special commissions, expectant county magistrates and subordinate officials would go to stand in attendance outside the governor’s yamen. This was a show of respect intended to win favour and strengthen the impression they made. For minor officials awaiting appointments, it was the surest road to advancement. Sometimes, while discussing business with the senior officials, the governor would need someone for a commission. A treasurer, commissioner or intendant entitled to recommend a candidate might remember a suitable man he had just seen. Such unexpected opportunities were by no means rare. “What time did you arrange to meet Tang?” “There is plenty of time yet,” Zhou said. “Let us have a pot of tea at a teashop first.” “No need to go out. I have some good Lu’an tea. I shall brew you a pot.” Yang made the tea and brought out two plates of dry pastries. They ate and chatted. When Yang asked about Yueru, Zhou grew animated at once. He concealed nothing and gave a wealth of description.

杨书办津津有味地听完，不由得问道：“如果有机会，月如肯不肯同你上床？”“我想一定会肯。其实昨天晚上，只要我胆子够大，也就上手了。”“你是怕唐子韶来捉你的奸，要你写‘伏辩’？”“不借。这是我们三个人的事，我不能做这种荒唐事，连累好朋友。”“少棠，你不做见色轻友的事，足见你够朋友。”杨书办说：“我倒问你，你到底想不想同月如困一觉？”“想是想，没有机会。”“我来给你弄个机会。”杨书办说：“等下，我到公济典去，绊住唐子韶的身子，你一个人闯到月如楼上，我保险不会有人来捉你们的奸。”“不必，不必！”周少棠心想，即令能这样顺利地真个消魂，也要顾虑到落一个话柄在杨书办手里。这种傻事决不能做，所以又加一句：“多谢盛情。不过我的胆还不够大，谢谢，谢谢。”杨书办倒是有心想助他成其好事，看他态度如此坚决，也就不便再说。只是付之一笑。

Yang listened with relish. “If you had the chance, would Yueru be willing to go to bed with you?” “I am sure she would. In fact, last night I could have had her if I had been bold enough.” “You were afraid Tang would catch you in the act and make you sign a confession?” “Exactly. This business concerns all three of us. I could not do anything so foolish and drag my friends into trouble.” “Shaotang, you would not put a pretty woman before your friends. That shows what a good friend you are. But tell me: do you want to sleep with Yueru or not?” “I do, but there is no opportunity.” “I shall make one for you. When we go to Gongji, I shall keep Tang occupied. You can go straight upstairs to Yueru. I guarantee that no one will catch you together.” “No need, no need!” Even if he could enjoy himself so easily, Zhou reflected, he would still have to consider the hold this would give Yang over him. He must never do anything so foolish. He therefore added, “Thank you for your kindness, but I am still not brave enough. Thank you, all the same.” Yang had genuinely meant to help him attain his desire. Seeing him so determined, however, he could hardly press the matter. He merely smiled.

“不过，你倒提醒我了，我还是可以到月如那里去一趟，问问你提出来的那句话。”“这样说，仍旧我一个人到公济？”“不错，你先去，我问完了话，随后就来。”“那么，”杨书办问：“我在唐子韶面前，要不要说破？”“不必，你只说我随后就到便是。”近午时分，两人到了公济典旁边的那条巷子，暂且分手。周少棠来到唐家举手敲门，好久没有回音，只好快快回身，哪知一转身便发现月如冉冉而来，后面跟着她家的丫头，手里挽个菜篮，主婢俩是刚从小菜场回来。“碰得巧！”周少棠说：“如果你迟一步，或者我早来一步，就会不到面。”“周老爷，你也来得巧，今天难得买得新鲜菌子，你在我那里吃了中饭走。”“不，不！杨书办在公济等我。”“那就请杨书办一起来。”“等一息再说。阿嫂，我先到你这里坐一坐，我有句话想问你。”其实丫头已经去开了大门，进门就在客堂里坐。月如请他上楼，周少棠辞谢了，因为他不想多作逗留，只说两句话就要告辞，觉得不必累人家费事。

“You have reminded me of something, though. I could still call on Yueru and ask her that question you raised.” “Then I am to go to Gongji alone?” “Yes. You go ahead. I shall follow as soon as I have asked her.” “Should I tell Tang about it?” Yang asked. “No need. Just say I shall be along shortly.” Towards noon they reached the lane beside Gongji Pawnshop and parted for the moment. Zhou went to Tang’s house and knocked. After a long wait without an answer, he turned away in disappointment. As he did so, he saw Yueru approaching at an unhurried pace, her maid behind her with a market basket on her arm. Mistress and maid had just returned from buying food. “What good timing!” Zhou said. “A moment later for you, or a moment earlier for me, and we should have missed each other.” “You have come at just the right time too, Mr Zhou. I was lucky enough to find fresh mushrooms today. Stay for lunch.” “No, no! Clerk Yang is waiting for me at Gongji.” “Then invite him too.” “We shall see in a moment. Sister-in-Law, let me sit with you first. There is something I want to ask.” The maid had already opened the door. They went in and sat in the reception room. Yueru invited him upstairs, but he declined. He meant to stay only long enough for a few words and felt there was no need to put her to any trouble.

“阿嫂，我想请问你，你昨天说卖西湖田，老唐不便出面。这是啥讲究？”不想问的是这句话，月如顿时一愣，同时也提醒她想起一件事，更加不安。看在周少棠眼里，颇有异样的感觉，尽头不由得疑云大起。“周老爷，你请坐一坐，我是突然之间想起有句话要先交代。”接着便喊：“阿翠，阿翠，你在做啥？客人来了也不泡茶。”“我在厨房里，烧开水。”阿翠高声答应着，走了出来。“你到桥边去关照一声，家里有客人，要他下半天再来。”阿翠发愣，一时想不起到“桥边”要关照什么人。“去啊！”“去，去，”阿翠嗫嚅着问：“去同哪个说？”“不是我们刚刚去过？叫他们老板马上来？”“喔，喔！”阿翠想起来了，“木器店、木器店。”说着，转身而去。“真笨！”月如咕哝着，转身说道，“对不起，对不起！周老爷，你刚才要问我的那句话，我没有听清楚。”

“Sister-in-Law, yesterday you said Old Tang could not appear in person to sell the West Lake fields. Why is that?” Yueru had not expected this question. She was taken aback, and it also reminded her of something else, making her still more uneasy. Zhou sensed something strange in her reaction, and suspicions began to cloud his mind. “Please sit for a moment, Mr Zhou. I have suddenly remembered an instruction I must give first.” She called, “A’cui! A’cui! What are you doing? We have a guest, and you have not even made tea.” “I am in the kitchen boiling water,” A’cui answered loudly, coming out. “Go to the bridge and tell him we have a guest. Ask him to come this afternoon instead.” A’cui stared blankly. For the moment she could not think whom she was to inform at the bridge. “Go on!” “Yes, yes,” she faltered. “Whom am I to tell?” “Did we not just go there and ask the owner to come at once?” “Oh, yes! The furniture shop, the furniture shop.” She turned and left. “What a fool!” Yueru muttered. Turning back, she said, “Forgive me, Mr Zhou. I did not quite catch your question.”

“老唐卖田，为啥不便出面。”月如原来是因为唐子韶突然要卖田，风声传出去，惹人猜疑，莫非他要离开杭州了，是不是回安徽老家？这一来会影响他们开溜的计划，所以不便出面。如今的回答，当然改过了。“公济典一查封，我们老爷有亏空，大概总有人晓得，不晓得也会问，为啥卖田。如果晓得卖田是为亏空，就一定会杀价，所以他是不出面的好。”理由很充分，语气亦从容，周少棠疑虑尽释，“到底阿嫂细心。”他站起身来：“我就是这句话，问清楚了要走了。”出了唐家往公济典，走不多远，迎面遇见阿翠，甩着一条长辫子，一扭一扭地走了过来，“周老爷，”她开口招呼：“要回去了。”“不，我到公济典去。”“喏，”阿翠回身一指，“这里一直过去，过一座小桥，就是公济典后门。”周少棠本来要先出巷子上了大街从公济典前门入内，现在既有捷径可通后门，落得省点气力，“谢谢你。”他含笑致谢：“原来还有后门。”“走后门要省好多路。”阿翠又加一句客气话：“周老爷有空常常来。”

“Why can Old Tang not show himself when selling the land?” Yueru’s real reason was that a sudden sale by Tang would start rumours and suspicions. Was he leaving Hangzhou? Was he returning to his old home in Anhui? Such talk would interfere with their plans to slip away, which was why he could not appear himself. Naturally, she now gave a different answer. “Since Gongji has been taken into official custody, some people probably know that our master has a shortfall in his accounts. Even those who do not will ask why he is selling land. Once they learn that he needs the money to make good a deficit, they are bound to force down the price. It is better for him to keep out of sight.” The reason was persuasive, and her tone composed. Zhou’s suspicions vanished. “You really do think of everything, Sister-in-Law.” He stood up. “That was all I wanted to ask. Now I understand, I must go.” He had not gone far towards Gongji when he met A’cui coming back, her long plait swinging as she walked with a sway. “Going home, Mr Zhou?” she greeted him. “No, I am going to Gongji.” “Look.” She turned and pointed. “Straight along here, over a little bridge, and you are at Gongji’s back entrance.” Zhou had intended to leave the lane, reach the main street and enter by the front. A shortcut to the rear would save him some effort. “Thank you,” he said with a smile. “So there is a back entrance too.” “It saves a good deal of walking.” She added politely, “Do come and see us often, Mr Zhou, whenever you have time.”

见她如此殷勤，周少棠想起一件事，昨夜在唐家作客，照便应该开发赏钱，因而唤住她说：“ 阿翠你等等。”说着，探手入怀，皮袍子口袋中，有好几块碎银子，摸了适中的一块，约莫三四钱重，递向阿翠。“周老爷，这作啥？”“这个给你。昨天我走的时候忘记掉了。”“不要，不要。”“不许说不要。”周少棠故意板一板脸：“没规矩。”于是阿翠笑着道了谢，高高兴兴地甩着辫子回去。周少棠便照她的指点，一直往前走，果然看到一座小石桥，桥边一家旧货店，旧木器都堆到路上来了。周少棠心中一动，站住脚细看了一会，并没有发现什么木器店。不由得奇怪，莫非月如所说的木器店，即是指这家旧货店？这样想着，便上前问讯：“老板，请问这里有家木器店在哪里？”“不晓得。”旧货店老板诧异，“从没有听说过这里有家木器店。哪个跟你说的？骗你来‘撞木钟’。”“是……”周少棠疑云大起，决意弄个水落石出，“只怕我听错了，公济典唐朝奉家说这里有家木器店，要同你买木器。”“你不是听错了，就是弄错了。不是买木器，是要卖木器，叫我去看货估价。““她为啥要……”周少棠突然将话顿住了，闲事已经管得太多了，再问下去，会惹人猜疑，因而笑一笑，说一声：“是我弄错了。”扬长而去。

Her attentiveness reminded Zhou of something. As a guest at Tang’s house the previous night, he should have given the servants a tip. “A’cui, wait a moment,” he called. Reaching inside his fur-lined robe, he felt among several pieces of silver in a pocket and chose one of a suitable size, weighing perhaps three or four tenths of a tael. He held it out. “What is this for, Mr Zhou?” “For you. I forgot when I left yesterday.” “No, no!” “You must not refuse.” He put on a stern face. “That would be bad manners.” A’cui smiled, thanked him and went happily on her way, swinging her plait. Zhou followed her directions. Sure enough, he came to a little stone bridge. Beside it stood a second-hand shop, with old wooden furniture piled out into the roadway. Something struck him. He stopped and looked carefully around but could see no furniture shop. Could Yueru have meant this second-hand dealer? He went over to ask. “Excuse me, where is the furniture shop around here?” “I have no idea,” the dealer answered in surprise. “I have never heard of one. Who told you that? Someone is sending you on a fool’s errand.” “It was…” Suspicion rose again, and Zhou resolved to get to the bottom of it. “Perhaps I heard wrongly. At Master Tang’s house—the pawnbroker from Gongji—they said there was a furniture shop here and they wanted to buy some furniture from you.” “Either you heard wrongly or you have got it wrong. They want to sell furniture, not buy it. They asked me to look it over and give them a price.” “Why does she want to…” Zhou broke off. He had meddled quite enough already. More questions would arouse suspicion. He smiled, said, “My mistake,” and strode away.

到了公济典，只见唐子韶的神气很难看，是懊恼与忧虑交杂的神情。可想而知，杨书办已将他们所决定的处置告诉他了。不过，看到周少棠，他仍旧摆出一副尊敬而亲热的神情，迎上前来，握着周少棠的手说，“老大哥，你无论如何要帮我一个忙。”“啥事情？”周少棠装做不知，一面问，一面坐了下来，顺便跟杨书办交换了一个眼色，相戒谨慎。“老杨告诉我，马大老爷预备报公事，说我帐目不清。”唐子韶的话说得很急：“公事上怎么好这样说？”“这也无所谓，你把帐目弄清楚，不就没事了吗？”“话不是这样说，好比落了一个脚印在那里。有这件案底在衙门里，我以后做人做事就难了。”“那么，你想怎么样呢？”“咦！”唐子韶手指着说：“周先生，你不是答应我的，请马大老爷暂时把公事压一压？”“压也不过是一天半天的事。”杨书办插了一句嘴。“一两天哪里来得及？”唐子韶说：“现在银根又紧。”“好了，我晓得了。”周少棠说：“老唐，外头做事，一定要上路，不上路，人家要帮忙也无从帮起。这样子，你尽快去想办法，我同老杨替你到马大老爷那里讨个情，今天晚上再同你碰头。”说完，他已经站了起来，准备离去。“

At Gongji he found Tang looking very unhappy, with an expression compounded of vexation and anxiety. Clearly Yang had told him what they had decided to do. Nevertheless, Tang greeted Zhou with a show of warmth and respect, coming forward to clasp his hand. “My dear elder brother, you must help me, whatever happens.” “What is it?” Zhou asked, pretending ignorance as he sat down. He exchanged a glance with Yang, warning him to be cautious. “Old Yang tells me Magistrate Ma intends to submit a report saying my accounts are not clear.” Tang spoke urgently. “How can he put that in an official report?” “What does it matter? Put the accounts in order, and that will be the end of it.” “That is not how it works. It is like leaving a footprint. With such a record against me at the yamen, it will be difficult for me to do anything or hold up my head afterwards.” “Then what do you want?” “Why, Mr Zhou!” Tang pointed at him. “Did you not promise to ask Magistrate Ma to hold the matter back for a while?” “Only for a day or half a day,” Yang put in. “What can I do in a day or two? Money is so tight now.” “All right, I understand,” Zhou said. “Old Tang, a man doing business must know how to behave. If you do not, others cannot help you even if they wish to. Let us do this: find a way as quickly as you can, while Old Yang and I plead with Magistrate Ma for you. We shall meet again this evening.” He had already risen to leave.

“不忙，不忙！”唐子韶急忙说道：“我已经叫人去叫菜了，吃了饭再走。”“饭不吃了。”周少棠灵机一动，故意吓他一吓，“说实话，我们到你这里来，已经有人在钉梢了，还是早点走的好。”这一下，不但唐子韶吃惊，也吓了杨书办，脸上变色，悄悄问道：“是哪里的人？在哪里？”“杭州府的人，你出去就看到了。”说着，往外就走，杨书办紧紧跟在后面。“两位慢慢！”唐子韶追上来问：“晚上怎么样碰头？”“我会来看你。”“好，恭候大驾。”于是周少棠领头扬长而去，出了公济典，不断回头看，杨书办神色紧张地问：“人在哪里？”周少棠“噗哧”一声笑了出来，“对不起，对不起，害得你都受惊了。”他说：“我们到城隍山去吃油蓑饼，我详详细细告诉你。”

“No hurry, no hurry!” Tang said hastily. “I have sent someone to order dishes. Have lunch before you go.” “We shall not stay for lunch.” A sudden idea occurred to Zhou, and he deliberately gave Tang a fright. “To tell the truth, someone has been watching us since we came here. We had better leave at once.” This alarmed not only Tang but Yang, whose face changed colour. “Whose men?” he asked quietly. “Where are they?” “Men from the Hangzhou prefecture. You will see when you go out.” Zhou started for the door, with Yang close behind. “Wait a moment, both of you!” Tang hurried after them. “How shall we meet this evening?” “I shall come to see you.” “Very well. I shall await your visit.” Zhou strode out in front. Once outside Gongji, he kept looking back. Yang asked anxiously, “Where are they?” Zhou burst out laughing. “Forgive me! I have even frightened you. Let us go up City God Hill for yousuobing cakes. I shall tell you everything.”

上了城隍山，在药师间壁的酒店落座，老板姓陈，是周少棠的熟人，也认识杨书办，亲自从帐桌上起身来招待。“这么冷的天气，两位倒有兴致上城隍山？难得、难得。”陈老板问：“要吃点啥？”“特为来吃油蓑饼。”周少棠说：“菜随便，酒要好。”“有一坛好花雕，卖得差不多了，还剩下来三斤，够不够？”“中午少吃点，够了。”“我上回吃过的‘一鸡四吃’，味道不错，”杨书办说：“照样再来一回。鸡要肥。”“杨先生放心好了。”于是烫上酒来，先用现成的小菜、发芽豆、茶油鱼干这类下酒。这时周少棠告诉杨书办，根本没有人钉梢，只是故意吓一吓唐子韶而已。

They climbed City God Hill and sat down in the tavern next to Yaoshi. Its owner, surnamed Chen, knew Zhou well and also knew Yang. He rose from his account desk to attend to them himself. “What brings you up City God Hill in such cold weather? A rare pleasure! What would you like?” “We came especially for yousuobing. Any dishes will do, but the wine must be good,” Zhou said. “I have a jar of fine Huadiao, almost all sold. Three jin remain. Will that be enough?” “We shall drink less at noon. That will do.” “Last time I had your ‘one chicken, four ways,’ and it was excellent,” Yang said. “Let us have it again. Make sure the chicken is fat.” “Leave it to me, Mr Yang.” The wine was heated, and they began with ready-made small dishes: sprouted beans, dried fish in tea-seed oil and the like. Zhou now told Yang that nobody had been watching them. He had merely meant to frighten Tang.

“不过，有件事很奇怪，月如不晓得在搞啥花样。”等周少棠细说了他发现唐家要卖木器的经过，杨书办立刻下了一个判断：“唐子韶要带了他的小老婆，逃之夭夭了。”周少棠也是如此看法，“逃到哪里呢？”他问：“不会逃到徽州吧？”“逃回徽州，还是可以抓回来的。只有逃到上海，在租界里躲了起来，只要他自己小心，不容易抓到。”杨书办又说：“我看他用的缓兵之计，卖田最快也要十天半个月，要开溜，时间上足足够用。”“嗯，嗯。那么，我们应该怎么办呢？”杨书办亦无善策，默默地喝了一会酒，突然之间，将酒杯放下，双手靠在桌上，身上前倾，低声说道：“我同你说实话，你刚刚开玩笑，说有人‘钉梢’，我当时心里心上八下，难过极了。俗语说得，‘日里不做亏心事，夜半敲门心不惊’。发横财也要命的，强求不来。这件事，我们作成马大老爷立一场功劳，关照他据实呈报；唐子韶自作自受，不必可惜。你看如何？”周少棠想了一下，点点头：“我同意。不过数目要打个折扣。”“为啥？”“咦！我不是同你讲过，胡大先生要报月如的情，我们原来预备分给他一份，他不要，算是送月如。所以唐子韶作弊的数目不能实报。”

“There is something very strange, though. I cannot make out what Yueru is up to.” Once Zhou had described his discovery that the Tangs meant to sell their furniture, Yang reached an immediate conclusion. “Tang is going to take his concubine and run away.” Zhou thought so too. “Where would he go? Surely not back to Huizhou?” “If he fled to Huizhou, they could still bring him back. His only chance is Shanghai. If he hides in the foreign settlements and takes care, he will not be easy to catch. I think he is playing for time. Selling land takes ten days or half a month at the very least. That would give him more than enough time to slip away.” “Yes, yes. Then what should we do?” Yang had no good answer either. They drank in silence for a while. Suddenly he set down his cup, rested both hands on the table and leaned forward. In a low voice he said, “I shall be honest with you. When you joked just now about someone watching us, I was in a terrible state. As the saying goes, do nothing shameful by day and you need not fear a knock at midnight. A windfall can cost a man his life. You cannot force it. Let us give Magistrate Ma a chance to earn some credit. Tell him to report the facts. Tang has brought this on himself; we need not pity him. What do you say?” Zhou considered, then nodded. “I agree. But the amount must be reduced.” “Why?” “Did I not tell you? Mr Hu wants to repay Yueru’s kindness. We had meant to give him a share, but he does not want it. He is making it a present to Yueru. So we cannot report the full amount Tang has embezzled.”

这段话中的“胡大先生”四字，不知怎么让陈老板听到了，便踱过来打听他的消息，少不得嗟叹惋惜一番。周少棠他们的座位临窗，窗子是碎锦格子糊上白纸，中间嵌一方玻璃，望出去一株华盖亭亭的不凋松，春秋佳日，树下便是极好的茶座，陈老板指着说道：“那株松树下面，就是胡大先生同王抚台第一次来吃茶、吃酒的地方。王抚台有一回来过，还特为提起，这句话十七八年了。”“王抚台如果晓得胡大先生会有今天这种下场，只怕他死不瞑目。”杨书办感慨不止，“这样子轰轰烈烈的事业，说败就败，真同年大将军一样。”“比年大将军总要好得多。”周少棠说：“至少，性命之忧是不会有的。”陈老板接口说道：“就算没有性命之忧，活得也没意思了。”“是啊！”杨书办深深点头：“爬得高，跌得重，还是看开点好。”

Somehow the words “Mr Hu” reached Chen’s ears. He strolled over to ask for news, and naturally there were sighs and expressions of regret. Zhou and Yang sat beside a window of intricate latticework covered in white paper, with a square of glass set into the middle. Through it they could see an evergreen pine, its lofty crown spreading like a canopy. On fine days in spring and autumn, the space beneath it made an excellent place for tea. Chen pointed. “Under that pine is where Mr Hu and Governor Wang sat the first time they came for tea and wine. Governor Wang mentioned it particularly on a later visit. That was seventeen or eighteen years ago.” “If Governor Wang knew how Mr Hu would end, I doubt he could rest in his grave,” Yang said with deep feeling. “Such a magnificent enterprise, gone just like that! Exactly like General Nian.” “Still, he is much better off than General Nian,” Zhou said. “At least his life is not in danger.” “Even if his life is safe,” Chen added, “what pleasure can there be left in living?” “True.” Yang nodded gravely. “The higher you climb, the harder you fall. Better to take things less to heart.”

就这样一直在谈胡雪岩，直到酒醉饭饱，相偕下山，周少棠方又提到唐子韶，“我答应过他，只算两万四千银子。”他说：“你同马大老爷去说，要报就报这个数目好了。”“好的。”杨书办说：“不过，你应该同胡大先生去说说清楚，现在是照他的意思，看在唐子韶小老婆分上，特为少报。我们三个人是随公事。不然，他只以为我们从中弄了多少好处，岂不冤枉。”他又加了一句：“这句话请你一定要说到。”由于杨书办的态度很认真，周少棠决走到元宝街去一趟。胡雪岩已经不会客了，但对周少棠的情分不同，仍旧将他请了进去，动问来意。“你说的那匹‘瘦马’我见过了，亦就是见一见，没有别的花样。”周少棠说：“他亏空至少有八万银子，照你的意思，打了他一个三折，公事一报上去，当然要追。追出来抵还你的官款，也不无小补。”

They went on talking about Hu until they had eaten and drunk their fill. Only as they walked down the hill together did Zhou return to Tang. “I promised him we would count only twenty-four thousand taels. Tell Magistrate Ma that if he submits a report, that is the figure he should use.” “Very well,” Yang said. “But you ought to explain it all to Mr Hu. We are reducing the amount out of consideration for Tang’s concubine, just as he wished. The three of us are simply following official procedure. Otherwise he may think we have made a fortune out of it. That would be unfair to us.” He added, “Please be sure to tell him that.” Yang spoke so earnestly that Zhou decided to visit Yuanbao Street. Hu was no longer receiving visitors, but his affection for Zhou was different. He had him shown in and asked what had brought him. “I have seen that ‘slender horse’ you spoke of. Only seen her—nothing more,” Zhou said. “Tang’s deficit comes to at least eighty thousand taels. In accordance with your wishes, we have cut it to thirty per cent. Once the report goes in, they will of course have to recover it. Whatever they collect can go towards repaying the government money you owe. It will be of some help.”

一听这话，胡雪岩的眼圈发红，“少棠，”他说：“有你这句话就够了。从出事到现在，再好的朋友，都是同我来算帐的，顶多说是打个折扣，少还一点，没有人说一句，我介绍来的那笔存款，不要紧，摆在那里再说，帮我去弄钱来的，可以说没有。其中只有两个人，一个是古应春，帮我凑了二三十万银子，应付上海的风潮；再一个是你。古应春受过我的好处，大家原是有往来的，象你，该当凭你本事弄来的外款不要，移过来替我补亏空，虽说杯水车薪，无济于事，不过，我看来这两万四千银子，比什么都贵重。““大先生，你不要这样说。从前我也受过你的好处。”周少棠又说：“今天中午，我们在城隍山吃油蓑饼，还提起你同王抚台的交情，只怕他听得你有这一场风波，在阴司里都不安心。”提到玉有龄，枨触前尘，怀念故友，胡雪岩越发心里酸酸地想哭，“真正是一场大梦！”他说：“梦终归是梦，到底是要醒的。”“一个人能够象你做这样一场梦，古往今来，只怕也不过数得出来的几个人。”

Hu’s eyes reddened. “Shaotang, those words alone are enough. Since my troubles began, even my closest friends have come to settle accounts with me. At most they offer to knock something off and let me repay a little less. Not one has said, ‘Never mind that deposit I brought you. Leave it there for now.’ As for helping me raise money, you could say there has been nobody. Only two exceptions: Gu Yingchun, who helped scrape together two or three hundred thousand taels to meet the panic in Shanghai, and you. Gu has benefited from me; we have always helped one another. But you are giving up money you could rightfully earn by your own abilities and diverting it to make good my deficit. A cup of water on a cartload of burning wood, perhaps—too little to save anything. Yet to me these twenty-four thousand taels are more precious than anything else.” “Mr Hu, you must not put it that way. I too benefited from you in the old days.” Zhou went on, “At noon today we were having yousuobing on City God Hill and spoke of your friendship with Governor Wang. If he heard of this disaster, I doubt he could be at peace even in the other world.” The mention of Wang Youling brought back the past and his lost friend. Hu felt still more painfully close to tears. “It has all been one great dream,” he said. “A dream is a dream. In the end one has to wake.” “From ancient times to the present, there can have been only a handful of men who ever dreamed a dream like yours.”

这话使得胡雪岩颇受鼓舞，忽然想到他从未想过的身后之名，“不晓得将来说书的人，会不会说我？”他问：“说我又是怎样子地说，是骂我自作孽，还是运气不好？”“说是一定会说的，好比年大将军一样，哪个不晓得？”这使得胡雪岩想起年大将军赠妾的故事，心中一动，便笑一笑说：“我哪里比得上年大将军？不讲这些了。老弟兄聊聊家常。少棠，你今年贵庚？”“我属老虎，今年五十四。”“嫂夫人呢？”“她属羊，”比我小五岁。“周少棠说：”照道理，羊落虎口，我应该克她，哪晓得她的身子比我还健旺。““你也一点都不象五十几岁的人。”胡雪岩说：“嫂夫人我还是年纪轻的时候见过。那时候，我看你就有点怕她。现在呢？”“都一把年纪了，谈啥哪个怕哪个？而况……”“怎么不说下去？”胡雪岩问。这是因为说到周少棠伤心之处了，不愿多谈，摇摇头说：“没有啥。”

These words encouraged Hu. Suddenly he thought of something that had never occurred to him before: his reputation after death. “I wonder whether storytellers will tell of me one day. And if they do, what will they say? That I brought ruin upon myself, or that my luck failed?” “They certainly will tell your story. Just like General Nian—who has not heard of him?” This reminded Hu of the story of General Nian giving away a concubine. An idea stirred in him. He smiled. “How could I compare with General Nian? Let us leave that aside and talk of family matters, as old friends should. Shaotang, how old are you this year?” “I was born in the Year of the Tiger. Fifty-four.” “And your wife?” “The Year of the Sheep, five years younger. In theory, with a sheep in a tiger’s jaws, my influence ought to harm her. Yet her health is even better than mine.” “You do not look in your fifties at all. I last saw your wife when we were young. I thought you were a little afraid of her then. What about now?” “At our age, what does it matter who fears whom? Besides…” “Why stop there?” Hu asked. Zhou had reached a painful subject and did not wish to speak of it. He shook his head. “It is nothing.”

“一定有缘故。少棠，你有啥苦衷，何妨同我讲一讲。”“不是有啥苦衷。”周少棠说：“我们的独养儿子……”周少棠的独子，这年正好三十，在上海一家洋行中做事，颇得“大板”‘的器重，当此海禁大开，洋务发达之时，可说前程如锦。哪知这年二月间，一场春瘟，竟尔不治。周太太哭得死去活来。周少棠本来要说的一句话是：“而况少年夫妻老来伴，独养儿子死掉了，我同她真正叫相依为命。”原来是提到了这段伤心之事，所以说不下去。胡雪岩便问：“你儿子娶亲了没有呢？”“没有。”“怎么三十岁还不成家？”“那是因为他学洋派，说洋人都是这样的，三十岁才成家。他又想跟他们老板到外国去学点本事，成了家不方便，所以耽误下来的。如今是连孙子都耽误了。“

“There must be a reason. Shaotang, if something is troubling you, why not tell me?” “It is not that. Our only son…” Zhou’s only son had been thirty that year. He worked for a foreign firm in Shanghai and was highly valued by its chief. With maritime restrictions lifted and foreign business flourishing, his prospects had seemed splendid. Then, in the second month, a spring epidemic had carried him off. Mrs Zhou had been beside herself with grief. What Zhou had begun to say was, “Besides, a young husband and wife become companions in old age. With our only son dead, she and I truly have no one but each other.” It was this painful memory that had stopped him. “Had your son married?” Hu asked. “No.” “Why was he still unmarried at thirty?” “He had taken to foreign ways. He said foreigners did not marry until thirty. He also wanted to go abroad with his employer and learn something useful. Marriage would have made that inconvenient, so he kept putting it off. Now that delay has cost us even a grandson.”

“是啊！不孝有三，无后为大。”胡雪岩说：“嫂夫人倒没有劝你讨个小？”“提过。我同她说……”周少棠突然顿住，因为他原来的话是：“算了，算了，‘若要家不和，讨个小老婆’。”话到嘴边，想起忌讳：第一，螺蛳太太就是“小老婆”；第二，胡雪岩家“十二金钗”，“小老婆”太多，或许就是落到今天这个下场的原因。总之，令人刺心的话，决不可说。于是他改口说道：“内人虽有这番好意，无奈一时没有合便宜的人，只好敬谢不敏了。”“这倒是实话，要有合适的人，是顶要紧的一桩。‘若要家不合，讨个小老婆’，大家总以为指大太太吃醋，其实不然！讨小讨得不好，看大太太老实好欺侮，自己恃宠而骄，要爬到大太太头上。那一来大太太再贤惠，还是要吵架。”周少棠没有想到自己认为触犯忌讳的那句俗语，倒是胡雪岩自己说了出来。不过他的话也很有道理，螺蛳太太固然是个现成的例子；古应春纳妾的经过，他也知道。都可以为他的话作注脚。

“Yes. Of the three offences against filial duty, leaving no heir is the worst,” Hu said. “Has your wife not urged you to take a concubine?” “She has. I told her…” Zhou stopped abruptly. What he had actually said was, “Forget it. If you want discord at home, take a concubine.” As the words reached his lips, he remembered how offensive they might be. First, Madam Luosi was herself a concubine. Second, Hu’s household had its “Twelve Beauties.” Perhaps having so many concubines was part of what had brought him to his present plight. In any event, words that would wound him must not be spoken. Zhou changed his answer. “My wife meant it kindly, but I could not find a suitable woman just then. I could only decline with thanks.” “That is true enough. Finding the right woman is the most important thing. ‘If you want discord at home, take a concubine.’ People always assume this means the principal wife grows jealous. It need not be so at all! Choose badly, and the concubine sees a quiet principal wife whom she can bully. Spoiled by her husband’s favour, she tries to climb over the wife’s head. Then there will be quarrels, however virtuous the wife may be.” Zhou had not expected Hu himself to quote the very saying he had thought too delicate to mention. Yet there was much truth in his words. Madam Luosi was a ready example; Zhou also knew what had happened when Gu Yingchun took a concubine. Both experiences could serve as footnotes to Hu’s argument.

“少棠，你我相交一场，我有力量帮你的时候，没有帮你什么……”“不，不！”周少棠插嘴拦住，“你不要说这话，你帮我的忙，够多了。”“好！我现在还要帮你一个忙，替你好好儿物色一个人。”“大先生！”周少棠笑道：“你现在倒还有闲工夫来管这种闲事？”“正事轮不到我管，有刘抚台、德藩台替我操心，我就只好管闲事了。”满腹牢骚，出以自我调侃的语气，正见得他的万般无奈。周少棠不免兴起一种英雄末路的苍凉之感。再谈下去，说不定会掉眼泪，因而起身告辞。胡雪岩握着他的手臂，仿佛有话要说，却两次欲言又止，终于松开了手说：“再谈吧！”

“Shaotang, we have been friends for so long. When I had the means to help you, I did very little…” “No, no!” Zhou interrupted. “Do not say that. You have helped me more than enough.” “Very well. Now I want to do you another service and find a suitable woman for you.” Zhou laughed. “Mr Hu! At a time like this, you still have leisure to concern yourself with such trifles?” “My serious affairs are no longer mine to manage. Governor Liu and Treasurer De worry about them for me. I can only occupy myself with trifles.” His self-mocking tone, beneath which lay so much resentment, revealed his utter helplessness. Zhou felt the desolation of a hero brought to the end of his road. If they talked much longer, he might weep. He therefore rose to take his leave. Hu grasped his arm as though he had something to say. Twice he almost spoke, then stopped. At last he released his hold. “We shall talk again.”

半夜里叩中门，送进来一封信，说是藩台衙门的专差送来的。螺蛳太太将胡雪岩唤醒了，拿一盏水晶玻璃罩的“洋灯”，让他看信。看不到几行，胡雪岩将信搁下，开口说道：“我要起来。”于是螺蛳太太叫起丫头，点起灯火，拨旺炭盆，服侍胡雪岩起身，他将德馨的信，置在桌上细看。一张八行笺以外，另有一个抄件，字迹较小，需要戴老花眼镜，才看得清楚。

At midnight there was a knock at the inner gate, and a letter was brought in, delivered by a special messenger from the provincial treasurer's yamen. Madam Luosi woke Hu and held a Western lamp with a crystal-glass shade for him to read it. Before he had gone through more than a few lines, he put it down. “I must get up.” She roused the maids, had the lights lit and the brazier stirred, and helped him dress. He laid Dexin's letter on the table for closer examination. Besides the sheet of eight-column stationery, there was a copy of another document, written so small that he needed his reading spectacles.

抄件是一道上谕：“谕内阁：给事中郎承修奏请，责令贪吏罚捐巨款，以济要需一折，据称该给事中所开赃私最著者，如已故总督瑞麟、学政何廷谦、前任粤海关监督崇礼及俊启、学政吴宝恕、水师提督翟国彦、盐运使何兆瀛、肇难道方浚师、广州府知府冯端本、潮州府知府刘湘年、廉州府知府张丙炎、南海县知县杜凤治、顺德县知县林灼之、现任南海县知县卢乐戌，皆自宫广东后，得有巨资，若非民膏，即是国帑等语，着派彭玉麟将各该员在广东居官声名苦何，确切查明，据实具奏。”这跟胡雪岩无关。

It was an imperial edict: “To the Grand Secretariat. Supervising Censor Deng Chengxiu has memorialized, requesting that corrupt officials be ordered to make substantial compulsory contributions to meet urgent needs. He lists as particularly notorious for illicit gains the late Governor-General Ruilin; Education Commissioner He Tingqian; former superintendents of the Guangdong Maritime Customs, Chongli and Junqi; Education Commissioner Wu Baoshu; Naval Commander Zhai Guoyan; Salt Transport Commissioner He Zhaoying; Circuit Intendant Fang Junshi of Zhaonan; Prefect Feng Duanben of Guangzhou; Prefect Liu Xiangnian of Chaozhou; Prefect Zhang Bingyan of Lianzhou; Magistrate Du Fengzhi of Nanhai; Magistrate Lin Zhuozhi of Shunde; and the present Magistrate Lu Lexu of Nanhai. All, he states, acquired great wealth after serving in Guangdong. Such wealth must have come either from the people's substance or from the public treasury. Peng Yulin is hereby directed to ascertain precisely the reputations of these officials during their service in Guangdong and report the facts.” This did not concern Hu.

另有一个附片，就大有关系了：“另片奏：闻阜康银号关闭，协办大学士刑部尚书文煜，所存该号银数至七十余万之多，请即查明确数，究所从来，据实参处等语，着顺天府确查具奏。”接下来再看德馨的亲笔信，只有短短的两行：“事已通天，恐尚有严旨，请速为之计。容面谈。”

The supplementary memorial, however, concerned him very closely: “The supplementary memorial states: ‘I hear that Fukang Bank has closed, and that Wenyu, Assistant Grand Secretary and Minister of Punishments, has more than seven hundred thousand taels deposited there. I request an immediate investigation to ascertain the exact sum and its source, followed by a report seeking appropriate disciplinary action.’ The Shuntian prefectural authorities are hereby ordered to investigate and report.” Dexin's own letter contained only two short lines: “The affair has reached the throne. Further severe orders may follow. Please make preparations without delay. We must discuss this in person.”

“你看！”胡雪岩将信递了给螺蛳太太，“话没有说清楚，‘容面谈’是他来，还是要我去？”“等我来问问看。”螺蛳太太将递信进来的丫头、由镜槛阁调过来的巧珠唤了来，关照她到中门上传话，赶到门房去问，藩司衙门来的专差，是否还在？如果已经走了，留下什么话没有？这得好一陈工夫才会有回话，胡雪岩有点沉不住气了，起身蹀躞，喃喃自语：“严旨，严旨！是革职还是抄家？”螺蛳太太一听吓坏了，但不敢现诸形色，只将一件大毛皮袍，一件贡缎马褂堆在椅子上，因为不管是德馨来，还是胡雪岩去，都要换衣服，所以早早预备在那里。“ ‘速为之计’，怎么‘计’法？”胡雪岩突然住足，“我看我应该到上海去一趟。“为啥？”“至少我要把转运局的公事，弄清楚了，作个交代，不要牵涉到左大人，我就太对不起人了。”“光是为这件事，托七姐夫就可以了。”“不！还有宓本常，我要当面同他碰个头，看看他把上海的帐目，清理得怎么样了。”商议未定之际，只见巧珠急急来报，德馨已经微服来访。胡雪岩急忙换了衣服，未及下楼，已有四名丫头，持着宫灯，前引后拥地将德馨迎上楼来。

“Look!” Hu handed the letter to Madam Luosi. “He has not made himself clear. Does ‘discuss this in person’ mean he is coming here, or that I am to go to him?” “Let me find out.” She called Qiaozhu, the maid who had brought in the letter and who had been transferred from Jingjian Pavilion. Qiaozhu was to send word through the inner gate to the gatehouse and ask whether the treasurer's messenger was still there. If he had gone, had he left any message? It would take some time for an answer to return. Hu could no longer sit still. He paced about, muttering, “Severe orders, severe orders! Dismissal from office, or confiscation of the household?” Madam Luosi was terrified, but dared not show it. She merely laid a heavy fur robe and a tribute-satin riding jacket on a chair. Whether Dexin came to Hu or Hu went to Dexin, he would need to change, and she wanted the clothes ready. “‘Make preparations without delay’—what preparations?” Hu suddenly stopped. “I think I must go to Shanghai.” “Why?” “At the very least I must put the Transport Bureau's official business in order and give a proper account. I cannot let Lord Zuo become involved. I would never forgive myself.” “If that is all, you can ask Brother-in-Law Gu to do it.” “No. There is Mi Benchang as well. I must meet him face to face and see how far he has got with settling the Shanghai accounts.” Before they had reached a decision, Qiaozhu hurried back: Dexin had arrived in plain clothes. Hu changed quickly. Before he could go downstairs, four maids with palace lanterns were already escorting Dexin up, some leading and others following.

胡雪岩在楼梯口迎着，作了一个揖，口中不安地说：“这样深夜，亲自劳步，真正叫我不知道怎么说了！”“自己弟兄，不必谈这些。”德馨进了门，还未坐定，便即说道：“文中堂怕顶不住了。”“文中堂”便是文煜，现任协办大学士刑部尚书，所以称之为“中堂”。他是八旗中有名的殷实大户，发财是在福州将军任上。海内冲要重镇，都有驻防的将军，位尊而权不重，亦谈不到什么入息，只有福州将军例外，因为兼管闽海关，五口通商以后，福州亦是洋商贸易的要地，税收激增，所以成了肥缺，文煜因为是恭王的亲戚，靠山甚硬，在这个肥缺上盘踞了九年之久，及至内调进京，又几次派充崇文门监督，这也是一个日进斗金的阔差，数十年宦囊所积，不下千万之多。在阜康，他是第一个大存户，一方面是利害相共，休戚相关；一方面他跟胡雪岩的交情很厚，所以从阜康出事以后，他一直在暗中支持，现在为邓承修一纸“片奏”所参，纸包不住火，自顾不暇，当然不能再替胡雪岩去“顶”了。“雪岩，”德馨又问：“文中堂真的有那么多款子，存在你那里？”“没有那么多。”胡雪岩答说：“细数我不清楚，大概四五十万是有的。”“这也不少了。”

Hu met him at the head of the stairs and bowed. “To trouble you to come in person at such an hour—I truly do not know what to say!” “We are brothers. There is no need to speak of that.” Dexin had scarcely entered and had not yet settled into his seat when he said, “I am afraid Lord Wen can no longer hold the line.” Lord Wen was Wenyu, the current Assistant Grand Secretary and Minister of Punishments, and was therefore addressed as a grand secretary. He was a famously wealthy man among the Eight Banners. His fortune had been made as Fuzhou Garrison General. Garrison generals were stationed in important strategic cities throughout the empire. Their rank was high, but their power modest, and their income generally unremarkable. Fuzhou was the exception because its general also supervised the Fujian Maritime Customs. After the five treaty ports opened, Fuzhou became a major centre of foreign commerce, customs receipts rose sharply, and the appointment grew lucrative. Related to Prince Gong and backed by powerful protection, Wenyu had occupied this profitable post for nine years. After his transfer to the capital, he had several times been appointed superintendent at Chongwen Gate, another office where wealth poured in by the day. Over decades in office he had accumulated no less than ten million taels. At Fukang he was the largest depositor. His interests were bound up with Hu's, and their personal friendship was close. Since the crisis began, he had supported Hu behind the scenes. Now Deng Chengxiu's supplementary memorial had impeached him. The fire could no longer be wrapped in paper. Preoccupied with protecting himself, he could naturally no longer shield Hu. “Xueyan,” Dexin asked, “does Lord Wen really have so much deposited with you?” “Not that much. I do not know the exact figure, but there must be four or five hundred thousand.” “That is no small sum either.”

“晓翁，”心乱如麻的胡雪岩，终于找到一句要紧话：“你看，顺天府据实奏报以后，朝廷会怎么办？”“照定制来说，朝廷就不会听片面之词，一定是要文中堂明白回奏。”“文中堂怎么回奏呢？”“那就不知道了。”德馨答说：“总不会承认自己的钱，来路不明吧！”“他历充优差，省吃俭用，利上滚利，积成这么一个数目；似乎也不算多。”“好家伙，你真是‘财神’的口吻，光是钱庄存款就有四五十万，还不算多吗？”胡雪岩无词以对，只是在想：文煜究竟会得到怎么一种处分？“文中堂这回怕要倒楣。”德馨说道：“现在清流的气焰正盛，朝廷为了尊重言路，只怕要拿文中堂来开刀。”胡雪岩一惊，“怎么？”他急急问道：“会治他的罪？”“治罪是不会的。只怕要罚他。”“怎么罚？罚款？”“当然。现在正在用兵，军需孔急，作兴会罚他报效饷银。数目多寡就不知道了。”德馨语重心长地警告：“雪岩，我所说的早为之计，第一步就是要把这笔款子预备好。”“哪笔款子？”胡雪岩茫然地问。“文中堂的罚款啊！只要上谕一下来，罚银多少，自然是在他的存款中提的。到那时你就变成欠官款了，而且是奉特旨所提的官款，急如星火，想拖一拖不都不成。”

At last Hu's confused thoughts yielded an essential question. “Mr Xiaofeng, once the Shuntian authorities have reported the facts, what do you think the court will do?” “Under the established procedure, the court will not listen to one side alone. It will certainly order Lord Wen to submit a clear explanation.” “What explanation can he give?” “That I cannot say. He will hardly admit that his money comes from a dubious source.” “He has held profitable posts for years, lived frugally, and let the interest accumulate. A sum like that hardly seems excessive.” “Good heavens, you really do speak like the God of Wealth! Four or five hundred thousand in bank deposits alone, and you call it nothing excessive?” Hu had no answer. He could think only of what punishment Wenyu might receive. “I fear Lord Wen is in for trouble,” Dexin continued. “The Pure Stream group is very much in the ascendant. To show respect for the right of remonstrance, the court may make an example of him.” Hu started. “What? Will he be convicted of an offence?” “Not that. But he may be penalized.” “How? A fine?” “Of course. We are at war, and military funds are urgently needed. He may be ordered to contribute to the war chest as a penalty. I cannot say how much.” Dexin's warning was earnest. “When I urged you to prepare early, Xueyan, the first thing I meant was that you must have this money ready.” “Which money?” Hu asked blankly. “Lord Wen's fine! Once the edict arrives, whatever sum he is required to pay will naturally be drawn from his deposit. Then it becomes public money that you owe—and public money demanded by a special imperial order. It will be as urgent as a spark in dry tinder. You will not be able to put it off for a moment.”

“喔！”胡雪岩心想，要还的公私款项，不下数千万，又何在乎这一笔？但德馨的好意总是可感的，因而答说：“晓翁关爱，我很感激，这笔款子我这回一到上海，首先把它预备好，上谕一到，当即呈缴。”“这才是。”德馨问道：“你预备什么时候动身？”“明天来不及，后天走。”“哪天回来？”“看事情顺手不顺手。我还想到江宁去一趟，看左大人能不能帮我什么忙？”“你早就该去了。”德馨紧接着说：“你早点动身吧！这里反正封典当这件事正在进行，公款也好，私款也好，大家都要看封典当清算的结果，一时不会来催。你正好趁这空档，赶紧拿丝茧脱手，‘讲倒帐’就比较容易。”“讲倒帐”，便是打折扣来清偿。任何生意失败，都是如此料理。但讲倒帐以前，先要准备好现款，胡雪岩一直在等待情势比较缓和，存货就比较能卖得比较好的价钱，“讲倒帐”的折扣亦可提高。但照目前的情势看，越逼越紧，封典当以后，继以文煜这一案，接下来可能会有革职的处分，那时候的身分，一落千丈，处事更加困难，真如德馨所说的，亟应“速为之计”。

“Oh!” Hu thought of the tens of millions he already owed in public and private funds. What difference could this one sum make? Still, Dexin's concern deserved gratitude. “I am very grateful for your care, Mr Xiaofeng. As soon as I reach Shanghai this time, I shall make preparing this sum my first task. When the edict comes, it can be submitted at once.” “That is the right approach. When do you intend to leave?” “I cannot manage tomorrow. The day after.” “When will you return?” “That depends on how smoothly things go. I also want to visit Jiangning and see whether Lord Zuo can help.” “You should have gone long ago,” Dexin said at once. “Leave as soon as you can. The sequestration of the pawnshops is proceeding here. Public and private creditors alike are waiting to see what it yields, and will not press you for the moment. Use the interval to dispose of the silk and cocoons quickly. Then it will be easier to negotiate a reduced settlement.” Such a settlement meant paying debts at a discount, the usual way of dealing with a failed business. But cash had to be ready before negotiations could begin. Hu had been waiting for conditions to ease so that his stocks might fetch a better price and creditors could be offered a larger proportion of what they were owed. Now the pressure was tightening. After the seizure of the pawnshops came Wenyu's case; dismissal from office might follow. If Hu's standing collapsed, everything would become harder. As Dexin said, preparations really must be made without delay.

因此，等德馨一走，胡雪岩跟螺蛳太太重作计议，“箭在弦上，不得不发了。”他说：“有句话叫做‘壮士断腕’，我只有自己斩掉一条膀子，人虽残废，性命可保。你看呢？”“都随你！”螺蛳太太噙着眼泪说：“只要你斩膀子，不叫我来动手。”“虽不叫你来动手，只怕要你在我的刀上加一把劲，不然斩不下来。这一点，你一定要答应我。”螺蛳太太一面流泪，一面点头，然后问道：“ 这回你以上海，预备怎么办？”“我托应春把丝茧全部出清，款子存在汇丰银行，作为讲倒帐的准备金。再要到江宁去一趟。请左大人替我说说话，官款即令不能打折扣，也不要追得那么紧，到底我也还有赚钱的事业，慢慢儿赚了来还，一下子都逼倒了，对公家也没有什么好处。“

After Dexin left, Hu discussed their plans afresh with Madam Luosi. “The arrow is on the bowstring. It must be released,” he said. “There is a saying about a brave man cutting off his wrist. I must cut off one of my own arms. I shall be crippled, but I shall live. What do you think?” “Whatever you decide.” Tears stood in her eyes. “Only cut off the arm yourself. Do not ask me to do it.” “I shall not ask you to wield the blade, but I may need you to add your strength to mine. Otherwise I shall never bring myself to cut. You must promise me that.” Weeping, she nodded, then asked, “What do you intend to do in Shanghai this time?” “Ask Yingchun to sell off all the silk and cocoons and put the proceeds in HSBC as a reserve for negotiating settlements. Then go to Jiangning and ask Lord Zuo to speak for me. Even if the public debts cannot be reduced, they need not be pressed so hard. I still have profitable businesses. Let them earn the money to repay gradually. Driving them all to ruin at once would do the authorities no good either.”

“怎么？”螺蛳太太忽有意会，定神想了一下说：“你是说，譬如典当，照常开门，到年底下结帐，赚了钱，拿来拉还公款，等还清了，二十几家典当还是我们的？“胡雪岩失笑了，“你真是一手只如意、一只手算盘，天下世界哪里有这么好的事？”他说，“所谓‘慢慢儿赚了来还’，意思是赚钱的事业，先照常维持，然后再来估价抵还公款。”“这有啥区别呢？迟早一场空。”螺蛳太太大失所望，声音非常凄凉。“虽然迟早一场空，还是有区别的。譬如说：这家典当的架本是二十万两，典当照常营业，当头有人来赎，可以照二十万两算；倘或关门不做生意了，当头只好照流当价来估价，三文不值两文，决不能算二十万两，不足之数，仍旧要我们来赔，这当中出入很大。这样子一说，你明白了吧？”“明白是明白。不过，”螺蛳太太问道：“能不能留下一点来？”“那要看将来。至少也要等我上海回来才晓得，现在言之过早。”

“Do you mean…” A thought struck her, and she considered it carefully. “For example, the pawnshops would stay open, and at the year-end reckoning their profits would go towards the public debts? Once those were paid, the twenty-odd pawnshops would still be ours?” Hu could not help laughing. “You have a wish-granting sceptre in one hand and an abacus in the other! Where could one find such a wonderful arrangement? By earning the money gradually, I mean keeping the profitable businesses running for the time being, then valuing them and handing them over against the public debts.” “What difference does that make? Sooner or later, everything is gone.” Her disappointment sounded desolate. “There is a difference, even if everything must go in the end. Suppose a pawnshop has capital of two hundred thousand taels. If it continues trading and customers come to redeem their pledges, it can be valued at two hundred thousand. If it closes, the pledges have to be valued at the prices they would fetch as unredeemed goods. What should be worth three cash may not fetch two. The shop certainly cannot be counted at two hundred thousand, and we must still make up the shortfall. That is a considerable difference. Do you understand now?” “I understand. But can we keep a little for ourselves?” “That depends on what happens. We shall know no sooner than my return from Shanghai. It is too early to say.”

螺蛳太太前前后后想了一遍，问出一番极紧要的话来：“从十月底到今天，二十天的工夫，虽然天翻地覆，总当做一时的风波，除了拿老太太搬城外去住以外，别的排场、应酬，不过规模小了点，根本上是没有变。照你现在的打算，这家人家是非拆散不可了？”听得这话，胡雪岩心如刀割，但他向来都是先想到人家，将心比心，知道螺蛳太太比他还要难过，眼泪只是强忍着不让它流下来而已。这样转着念头，便觉得该先安慰螺蛳太太，“我同你总归是拆不散的。”他说，“不但今生今世，来世还是夫妻。”螺蛳太太的强忍着的眼泪，哪禁得起他这样一句话的激荡！顿时热泪滚滚，倚着胡雪岩的肩头，把他的湖绉皮袍湿了一大片。“罗四姐，罗四姐，”胡雪岩握着她的手说：“你也不要难过。荣华富贵我们总算也都经过了，人生在世，喜怒哀乐，都要尝到，才算真正做过人。闲话少说，我同你商量一件事。“这件事，便是遣散姬妾。两个人秘密计议已定，相约决不让第三者知道，包括胡太太在内，都不能知道，只等胡雪岩上海回来，付诸实行。

Having considered everything, Madam Luosi asked a crucial question. “From the end of the tenth month until today, it has been twenty days. Everything has turned upside down, but we have still treated it as a passing storm. Apart from moving the old lady outside the city, our display and entertaining have merely been reduced a little. Nothing fundamental has changed. With the course you are proposing now, must this household really be broken up?” Her words cut Hu to the heart. Yet he always thought of others first. Putting himself in her place, he knew that she suffered still more and was holding back her tears by sheer effort. He felt that he must comfort her. “You and I will never be parted,” he said. “Not only in this life—we shall be husband and wife in the next.” How could the tears she had restrained withstand that assurance? They poured down. Leaning on his shoulder, she soaked a large patch of his Huzhou-crepe fur robe. “Luo Sijie, Luo Sijie.” He held her hand. “Do not grieve. We have had our share of wealth and splendour. To have truly lived, a person must taste joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure alike. But enough of that. There is something I must discuss with you.” It was the dispersal of his concubines. They settled the matter privately and agreed that no third person—not even Mrs Hu—was to know. They would put the plan into effect only after Hu returned from Shanghai.

“你看，”胡雪岩突然问道：“花影楼的那个，怎么样？”花影楼住的是朱姨太，小名青莲，原是绍兴下方桥朱郎中的女儿。朱郎中是小儿科，只为用药错误，看死了周百万家三房合一的七岁男孩，以致官司缠身，家道中落。朱郎中连气带急，一病而亡，周百万家却还不放过，以至于青莲竟要落入火坑。幸而为胡雪岩看中，量珠聘来，列为第七房姬妾。螺蛳太太不明白他的话，愣了一下问道：“你说她什么怎么样？没头没脑，我从哪里说起？”“我是说她的为人。”“为人总算是忠厚的。”螺蛳太太答说：“到底是郎中的女儿，说话行事，都有分寸。”“你看她还会不会生？”问到这话，螺蛳太太越发奇怪，“怎么？”她问：“你是不是想把她留下来？”“你弄错了。”胡雪岩说：“你光是说她会生不会生好了。”“只要你会生，她就会生。圆脸、屁股大，不是宜男之相？”“好！”胡雪岩说：“周少棠的独养儿子，本来在洋行里做事，蛮有出息的，哪晓得还没有娶亲，一场春瘟死掉了。周少棠今年五十四，身子好得出奇，我想青莲如果跟了他，倒是一桩好事。“

“What do you think of the one in Huaying Tower?” Hu suddenly asked. Huaying Tower housed Mistress Zhu, whose childhood name was Qinglian. She was the daughter of Doctor Zhu of Xiafangqiao in Shaoxing. Her father treated children, but a mistake in prescribing had killed a seven-year-old boy who was the common heir of three branches of the Zhou Millionaire's family. Lawsuits followed, and the doctor's fortunes collapsed. Overwhelmed by anger and anxiety, he fell ill and died. Even then the Zhou family would not relent, and Qinglian was on the point of being forced into prostitution. Fortunately Hu had taken a liking to her, paid a generous marriage settlement, and brought her into his household as his seventh concubine. Madam Luosi was puzzled. “What do you mean, what do I think of her? With no beginning or end to your question, where am I to start?” “I mean her character.” “She is a decent, honest sort. A doctor's daughter, after all. She knows how to conduct herself and what to say.” “Do you think she can still bear a child?” This puzzled Madam Luosi still more. “Why? Are you thinking of keeping her?” “You have misunderstood. Just tell me whether you think she can bear children.” “If you can father one, she can bear one. A round face and broad hips—is that not the look of a woman who will bear sons?” “Good. Zhou Shaotang's only son worked in a foreign firm and had excellent prospects. But before he had even married, a spring epidemic carried him off. Shaotang is fifty-four and remarkably strong. If Qinglian went to him, I think it would be a good thing.”

“你怎么想出来的？”螺蛳太太沉吟了一会说：“好事倒是好事，不过周太太愿意不愿意呢？”“愿意。”胡雪岩答得非常爽脆。“你问过他？”“是啊。不然怎么会晓得？”“这也许是嘴里的话。“不！我同少棠年纪轻的时候，就在一起，我晓得他的为人，有时候看起来油腔滑调，其实倒是实实惠惠的人，对我更不说假话。”“那好。”螺蛳太太说：“不过青莲愿不愿意，就不晓得了。等我来问问她看。”“我看不必问，一问她一定说不愿。”胡雪岩用感慨的声音说：“ ‘夫妻本是同林鸟，大限来时各自飞。’夫妻尚且如此，别的不必说了，到时候，她自会愿意。”

“How did that occur to you?” Madam Luosi pondered. “It might be a good thing, but would Mrs Zhou consent?” “She would,” Hu answered promptly. “Have you asked him?” “Of course. Otherwise how should I know?” “Perhaps that is only talk.” “No. Shaotang and I have known each other since we were young. I know his character. At times he seems glib and flippant, but in fact he is a thoroughly straightforward man, and he would never lie to me.” “Very well. But we do not know whether Qinglian would agree. Let me ask her.” “I do not think you need to. If you ask now, she will certainly refuse.” Hu's voice was full of feeling. “‘Husband and wife are birds of the same forest; when the final calamity comes, each flies away.’ If even spouses are like that, there is no need to speak of anyone else. When the time comes, she will agree of her own accord.”

胡雪岩是早就打算好了的，到了上海，哪里都不住，到城里找了一家小客栈住了下来，为的是隐藏行迹，租界上熟人太多，“仕宦行台”的茶房头脑，更是见多识广，岂能没有见过鼎鼎大名的“胡财神”？所以要遮掩真相，只有隐身在远离租界的小客栈中。安顿既定，派跟班去通知古应春来相会。古应春大出意外，但亦不难体会到胡雪岩的心境，所以尽管内心为他兴起一种英雄末路的凄凉，但见了面神色平静，连“小爷叔为啥住在这里”这么一句话都不问。“七姐怎么样？身子好一点没有？”“还好。”“我的事情呢？”胡雪岩问：“她怎么说？”“她不晓得。”“不晓得？”胡雪岩诧异：“怎么瞒得住？”“多亏瑞香，想尽办法不让她晓得。顶麻烦的是报纸。每天送来的《申报》，我总先要看过，哪一张上面有小爷叔的消息，就把这张报纸收起来，不给她看。”“喔！”胡雪岩透了一口气，心头顿感轻松，他本来一直在担心的是，见了七姑奶奶的面，不知道说什么话来安慰她，现在不必担心了。

Hu had already decided where he would stay in Shanghai. He went nowhere familiar, but found a small inn in the Chinese city and settled there to conceal his movements. He knew too many people in the foreign settlement. The head attendants at the inns catering to officials were particularly well informed; how could they fail to have seen the celebrated God of Wealth? His only way of hiding his circumstances was to disappear into a small inn far from the settlement. Once settled, he sent an attendant to fetch Gu. Gu was astonished, but could readily understand Hu's state of mind. Though inwardly moved by the desolation of a great man at the end of his road, he met him calmly and did not even ask why he was staying there. “How is Seventh Sister? Is her health any better?” “Fairly well.” “And what does she say about my affairs?” “She does not know.” “Does not know?” Hu was surprised. “How have you kept it from her?” “Thanks to Ruixiang. She has tried every possible means of keeping her from hearing. The greatest difficulty is the newspaper. Every day I read Shen Bao first, and if a page carries news of you, I put that sheet away so that she cannot see it.” “Oh!” Hu breathed out and felt immediately easier. He had been worrying about what he could say to comfort the Seventh Lady when they met. Now that concern was lifted.

接下来便谈正事。胡雪岩首先将他所作的“壮士断腕”的决定，告诉了古应春，当然也要问问他的看法。“小爷叔己下了决心，我没有资格来说对不对，我日日夜夜在想的是，怎么样替小爷叔留起一笔东山再起的本钱……”“应春，”胡雪岩打断他的话说：“你不要痴心妄想了。我胡某人之有今天，是天时、地利、人和，再加上两个可遇不可求、可一不可再的机会凑成功的。试问，天时、地利、人各，我还占得到哪一样？就算占全了，也不会再有那样两个机会了。”“小爷叔说的是两个机会是啥？一个大概是西征，还有一个呢？”“还有一个海禁大开。当时懂得跟外国人打交道的，没有几个，现在呢？懂洋务的不晓得有多少，同洋人打交道，做生意，不但晓得他们的行情，而且连洋人那套吃中国人的决窍都学得很精了，哪里还轮得到我来做市面？再说，中国人做生意要靠山。“胡雪岩摇摇头换了个话题，”你说要替我留一笔钱，我只好说，盛情可感，其实是做不到的。因为我的全部帐目都交出去了，象丝茧两样，都有细数，哪里好私下留一部分？“

They turned to business. Hu first told Gu of his decision to sacrifice an arm to save himself, and naturally asked his opinion. “Since you have made up your mind, Little Uncle, it is not for me to say whether you are right. What I think about day and night is how to preserve some capital for you to begin again…” “Yingchun,” Hu interrupted, “do not indulge in impossible hopes. What I achieved depended on favourable times, favourable circumstances, and the support of the right people, together with two opportunities that cannot be sought at will and never come twice. Which of those advantages do I still possess? Even if I had them all, those two opportunities would never return.” “Which two opportunities do you mean? The western campaign must be one. What was the other?” “The opening of the maritime trade. In those days very few people knew how to deal with foreigners. Now countless men understand foreign affairs. In trading with foreigners, they know not only their prices but also all their tricks for exploiting Chinese people. What place is left for me? Besides, a Chinese businessman needs a powerful patron.” Shaking his head, Hu changed the subject. “You say you want to save some money for me. I can only be grateful for the thought; it cannot be done. All my accounts have been handed over. The silk and cocoons are recorded in detail. How could I secretly hold back a portion?”

“办法还是有。”古应春说：“顶要紧的一点是，丝茧两项，小爷叔一定要坚持，自己来处理。”“我懂你的意思。不过现在一步都错不得，东西虽然在我手里，主权已经不是我的了。我们有户头，卖不卖要看刘抚台愿意不愿意，他说价钱不好，不卖，我们没有话说。”“价钱好呢？”“好到怎样的程度？”胡雪岩脱口相问，看古应春不作声，方又说道：“除非价钱好到足抵我的亏空有余，我马上可以收回，自己处理。无奈办不到，只有请刘抚台出面来讲折扣，那就只好由他作主了。”“不过，刘抚台一时也未见得找得到主顾。”“不错，我也晓得他找不到。我原来的打算是，他找不到，就拖在那里，拖它几个月，或者局面好转了，或者洋商要货等不及了，行情翻醒，或放我们可以翻身。不过照目前的情形看，再拖下去，会搞得很难看。”于是胡雪岩将言官参劾，可能由文煜的案子，牵连到他受革职处分的情形细说了一遍，接着又细谈此行的目的。

“There are still ways,” Gu replied. “The essential thing is that you must insist on handling the silk and cocoons yourself.” “I understand what you mean. But I cannot afford one wrong step now. The goods may still be in my hands, but the right to dispose of them is no longer mine. Even with a buyer of our own, the sale depends on Governor Liu's consent. If he says the price is too low and refuses, we have nothing to say.” “And if the price is good?” “How good?” Hu asked at once. Seeing that Gu remained silent, he continued, “Only if the price were high enough to cover my deficit with something to spare could I immediately recover control and handle matters myself. Unfortunately that cannot be done. I can only ask Governor Liu to negotiate reduced settlements, so the decision must be his.” “But Governor Liu may not be able to find a buyer immediately.” “True. I know he cannot. My original idea was to let the matter wait if he found none. After a few months, conditions might improve, or the foreign merchants might become too impatient for supplies. Prices could recover, and perhaps we could regain our footing. But in the present circumstances, further delay may end very badly.” He then explained in detail how the censors' impeachment of Wenyu might implicate him and lead to his own dismissal from office, before describing the purpose of his journey.

“我这趟来，第一件事，就是找丝茧的买主，你有没有？”“有。就是价码上下，还要慢慢儿磨。”“不要磨了。我们以掮客的身分，介绍这生意。刘抚台答应了，佣钱照样也要同他说明。”“那么刘抚台呢？”古应春问：“佣金是不是也要分他一份？”“当然，而且应该是大份。不过，这话不便同他说明，一定要转个弯。”“怎么转法？是不先跟德藩台去谈？”“不错，要先同德晓峰谈。我同他的关系，你是晓得的，既然你有了户头，我们马上打外电报给他。”“这要用密电。”“是的。”胡雪岩说：“临走以前，我同他要了一个密码本，而且约好，大家用化名。”“那就很妥当了。”

“My first business here is to find a buyer for the silk and cocoons. Have you anyone?” “Yes. Only the price still needs some patient bargaining.” “No more bargaining. We shall introduce the transaction as brokers. If Governor Liu agrees, we shall also explain the commission openly.” “And Governor Liu? Is he to have a share of the commission?” “Naturally, and the largest share. But we cannot put that to him directly. We must take a roundabout approach.” “How? Speak to Treasurer De first?” “Exactly. You know my relationship with De Xiaofeng. Since you have a buyer, let us telegraph him at once.” “It must be a confidential cable.” “Yes. Before leaving, I obtained a codebook from him. We also agreed to use assumed names.” “Then everything is in order.”

接下来，古应春便细细地谈了他所接洽的户头，有个法国的巨商梅雅，开的条件比较好。胡雪岩听完以后，又问了付款的办法、担保的银行，认为可以交易，但仍旧追问一句：“比梅雅好的户头还有没有？”“没有。”“好！就是他。”胡雪岩又说：“至于佣金，你的一份要扣下来，我的一份，归入公帐。”“我的也归公帐。”“不必，不必！我是为了显我的诚心诚意，你又何必白填在里头？如果说，折扣打下来，不足之数仍旧要在我身上追，你这样做，让我少一分负担，犹有可说，如今总归是打折了事，你这样做，于我没啥好处，连我都未必见你的情。至于旁人，根本不晓得你不要佣金，就更不用谈了。”“我是觉得我应该同小爷叔共患难……”“好了，好了！你不必再说了。”胡雪岩拿他的话打断，“铜钱掼到水里还听个响声，你这样牺牲了都没有人晓得，算啥？”“好吧！”古应春另外打了主意，不必说破，只问：“电报什么时候打？”

Gu went through the buyers he had approached in detail. A wealthy French merchant named Meiya offered comparatively favourable terms. Having heard them, Hu asked about the method of payment and the bank providing the guarantee. He considered the transaction acceptable, but pressed one further question. “Is there any buyer better than Meiya?” “No.” “Good. Then he is the man. As for the commission, deduct your share. Mine is to go into the general settlement account.” “Mine can go into it too.” “No, no! I am doing it to show my sincerity. Why should you put your money in for nothing? If, after a reduced settlement, I still had to make up the balance, you could reasonably say that your sacrifice lightened my burden. But the whole matter is to be settled at a discount. Your contribution would do me no good. Even I might scarcely appreciate the favour. Others would not know that you had forgone your commission, so there is no question of their gratitude.” “I feel that I ought to share your hardship…” “Enough, enough!” Hu cut him short. “Even a copper coin thrown into the water makes a sound. If you sacrifice this money and no one knows it, what is the point?” “Very well.” Gu formed a different intention but kept it to himself. “When shall we send the telegram?”

“现在就打，你先起个稿子看。”古应春点点头，凝神细想了一会说：“佣金的话，怎么说法？”“这先不必提，你只报个价，叙明付款办法，格外要强调的是，没有比这个价钱更好的了。如果刘抚台有意思，由你到杭州同他当面接头，那时候再谈佣金。”“小爷叔，你自己回去谈，不是更妥当吗？”“不！第一，我要到江宁去一趟；第二，这件事我最好不要插手，看起来置身事外，德晓峰才比较好说话。”“好！我懂了。”于是唤茶房取来笔砚，古应春拟好一个电报稿，与胡雪岩斟酌妥当，然后取出密码本来，两人一起动手，翻好了重新誊正校对，直到傍晚，方始完事。“我马上去发，否则，电报局要关门了。”古应春问：“小爷叔是不是到我那里去吃饭，还是苦中作乐，去吃一台花酒？”“哪里有心思去吃花酒？”胡雪岩说：“我们一起出去逛逛，随便找个馆子吃饭，明天再去看七姐。”“也好。”于是胡雪岩连跟班都不带，与古应春一起出了客栈，先到电报局发了密电，安步当车，闲逛夜市。

“Now. Draft it first and let us look at it.” Gu nodded and thought carefully for a while. “How shall I put the matter of the commission?” “Do not mention it yet. Give only the price and explain the terms of payment. Stress that no better price can be obtained. If Governor Liu is interested, you can go to Hangzhou and discuss it with him in person. That will be the time to speak of the commission.” “Would it not be more suitable for you to go back and negotiate yourself, Little Uncle?” “No. First, I must go to Jiangning. Second, it would be better for me to keep out of this. If I appear uninvolved, De Xiaofeng will find it easier to speak.” “I understand.” They called for the inn attendant to bring writing materials. Gu prepared a draft, which they considered and revised together. They then took out the codebook, encoded the message, copied it afresh, and checked it. By the time they finished, evening had come. “I shall send it at once, or the telegraph office will close,” Gu said. “Will you dine at my house, Little Uncle, or shall we find pleasure in adversity and have a courtesan dinner?” “How could I be in the mood for that? Let us go out for a walk and find somewhere to eat. I shall see Seventh Sister tomorrow.” “Very well.” Leaving even Hu's attendant behind, they went out together, first sent the confidential telegram at the telegraph office, and then walked leisurely through the night market.

第九章 少年绮梦｜CHAPTER NINE: YOUTHFUL DREAMS OF LOVE

走过一家小饭馆，胡雪岩止住了脚，古应春亦跟着停了下来。那有饭馆的金字招牌，烟熏尘封，已看不清是何字号，进门炉灶，里面是一间大厅，摆着二三十张八仙桌，此时已将歇市，冷冷清清的，只有两桌客人，灯火黯淡，益显萧瑟。古应春忍不住说：“小爷叔，换一家吧，或者到租界上去，好好找家馆子。这家要打烊了。”“问问看。”说着，举步踏了进去。跑堂的倒很巴结，古应春亦就不好意思打断人家的生意了。“两位客人请坐，吃饭还是吃酒。”“饭也要，酒也要。”胡雪岩问道：“你们这家招牌，是不是叫老同和？”“是的。老同和。”“老板呢？”胡雪岩问：“我记得他左手有六个指头。”“那是我们老老板，去世多年了。”“现在呢？小开变老板了？”“老老板没有儿子，只有一个女儿，现在是我们的老板娘。”“啊！”胡雪岩突然双眼发亮，“你们老板娘的小名是不是叫阿彩？”“原来你这位客人，真正是老客人了。”跑堂的说道：“现在叫得出我们老板娘名字的，没有几个人。”接着，便回过去，高声喊道：“老板娘，老板娘！”看看没有回音，古应春便拦住他说：“不必喊了。有啥好东西，随意配几样来，烫一斤酒。”

Passing a small restaurant, Hu Xueyan stopped, and Gu Yingchun stopped with him. Smoke and dust had so obscured the gold lettering on its sign that the name was no longer legible. The cooking range stood just inside the entrance; beyond it was a large room containing twenty or thirty square tables. The restaurant was about to close. Only two tables were occupied, and the dim lights made the deserted room seem still more forlorn. “Little Uncle, let us try somewhere else,” Gu said. “Or go to the settlement and find a proper restaurant. This one is closing.” “Let us ask.” Hu stepped inside. The waiter was so eager to oblige that Gu could hardly deprive him of their custom. “Please sit down, gentlemen. Will you be eating or drinking?” “Both. Is this place called Laotonghe?” Hu asked. “Yes, sir. Laotonghe.” “Where is the proprietor? I remember he had six fingers on his left hand.” “That was our old proprietor. He died years ago.” “And now? Has the young master taken over?” “He had no son, only a daughter. She is our mistress now.” “Ah!” Hu's eyes suddenly brightened. “Was her childhood name A’cai?” “You really are an old customer! Very few people still know our mistress's name.” The waiter turned and shouted for her. When there was no answer, Gu stopped him. “Never mind calling. Bring us a few of whatever dishes are good, and warm a jin of wine.”

等跑堂离去，胡雪岩不胜感慨地说：“二十多年了！我头一回到上海，头一顿饭就是在这里吃的。”“小爷叔好象很熟嘛！连老板女儿的小名都叫得出来。”“不但叫得出来……”胡雪岩摇摇头，没有再说下去。这种欲言双止的神态，又关涉到一个“女小开”，很容易今人想到，其中必有一段故事。如此寒夜，如此冷店，听这段故事，或者可以忘忧消愁。就这样一转念间，古应春便觉得兴致好得多了。等跑堂端来“本帮菜”的白肉、乌参，一个“糟钵头”的火锅，看到熊熊的青焰，心头更觉温暖，将烫好的酒为胡雪岩斟上一杯，开口说道：“小爷叔，你是什么都看得开的，吃杯酒，谈谈当年在这里的情形。”正落入沉恩中的胡雪岩，啜了一口酒，夹了一块白肉送入口中，咀嚼了一会说：“不晓得是当年老板的手艺好，还是我的胃口变过了，白肉的味道，大不如前。”“说不定两个原因都有。”古应春笑道：“还说不定有第三个原因。”“第三个？”“是啊！当年还有阿彩招呼客人。”“她不管招呼，坐帐台。那时我在杭州钱庄里的饭碗敲破了，到上海来寻生意，城里有家钱庄，字号叫做源利，有个得力的伙计是我一起学生意的师兄弟，我到上海来投奔他，哪晓得为他兄弟的亲事，他回绍兴去了，源利的人说就要回上海的，我就住在一家小客栈里等。一等等了十天，人没有等到。盘缠用光了，只好在小客栈里‘孵豆芽’。”

When the waiter had gone, Hu said with deep feeling, “More than twenty years! The first meal I ever ate in Shanghai was here.” “You seem to know the place well, Little Uncle. You even remember the proprietor's daughter's childhood name.” “More than remember it...” Hu shook his head and said no more. His hesitation, involving a young heiress to a business, readily suggested a story. On such a cold night, in such a chilly, empty restaurant, hearing it might help them forget their cares. The thought lifted Gu's spirits. The waiter brought boiled pork and dark sea cucumber, both local specialties, and a hotpot flavored with wine lees. Its vigorous blue flame warmed Gu's heart as well. He poured Hu a cup of the heated wine. “You have always been able to take things in your stride, Little Uncle.
